title: Add /autobuilder-loop and /plan-deliverables skills
body:
## What this adds

Two skills that work as a unit, plus the supporting fixes they depend on.

### `/autobuilder-loop`

Plan-driven build loop. Resolves an approved plan, freezes the milestone set, and drives it to completion with model-routed subagents (the orchestrator never reads source, diffs, or logs — subagents return compact envelopes). Every milestone must pass a **mandatory gate** before it counts as done:

- `/plan-eng-review` + `/review`, each in a subagent that reads its own skill file and returns findings-only (fixes stay routed dispatches).
- An **adversarial cross-model forum** — Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` at `ultra` effort and Grok `grok-build`, read-only. A `[P1]` from **either** model fails the gate. If both are unavailable it degrades to a single Claude adversarial subagent tagged `[single-model]` rather than silently passing.
- Local Docker verification (a crashed app returning 500 is a FAIL, never a pass; `NO_SERVER` is a FAIL of "functional").

A bounded deferral valve allows batching **at most one** small, non-sensitive milestone's gate forward — never security/auth/migrations/public interfaces, and never the final milestone.

### `/plan-deliverables`

Authors **per-milestone acceptance criteria** — each measurable and paired with the check that validates it (the deliverable) — into the design doc.

This closes a real gap in the pipeline: `/autobuilder-loop` re-reads per-milestone `{next_milestone, acceptance_criteria}` from the plan on every iteration, but **nothing upstream authored that field**. `/office-hours` writes a single prose `## Success Criteria` blurb, `/plan-eng-review` audits proposed test coverage, and `/spec`'s Definition of Done is issue-level (epics only).

Runs after `/office-hours`, before the plan reviews. Per-piece loop:

> draft criteria → default-on cross-model gap-check (Codex + Grok, honoring the existing `codex_reviews` / `grok_reviews` kill-switches) → probe the user for judgment calls → pair each criterion with a **repo-native** validating check (or an explicit `manual-verification` when no automated check can honestly prove it) → write the block.

Idempotent and resume-safe: re-running reads existing progress and processes only what's missing.

### How the two connect

`<!-- status: pending | built-gate-pending | complete -->` milestone markers. `/plan-deliverables` writes `pending`; `/autobuilder-loop` step 1.0 selects the first `pending` milestone, and step e / the deferral valve write status back. That's an explicit handoff contract instead of inferring "next" from unchecked checkboxes at both ends.

## Hardening

`/plan-deliverables` was put through an adversarial audit (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` ultra + Grok `grok-build` + independent verification agents) before this PR. Fixed:

- A gap-check block that **never wrote its prompt file** — both external models caught it independently; it would have sent an empty prompt to both CLIs on every milestone.
- `mktemp "…-XXXXXXXX.txt"` — the `.txt` after the X-template means **zero randomization on BSD/macOS** (collisions between concurrent runs).
- `BRANCH=$(git … | tr … || echo no-branch)` — without `pipefail` the pipeline exits 0 on `tr`, so the fallback never fires and `BRANCH` ends up empty.
- Missing idempotency/resume guards; section insert landing below the doc's closing section; prompt-injection fencing for doc-derived text; probe model availability once and run the two CLIs in parallel instead of sequentially.

Three findings were verified as false-positive / convention-consistent and deliberately **not** "fixed" (e.g. the markdown format is the shape autobuilder-loop's LLM parse subagent was co-designed for).

## Validation

- `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all` → clean; `--dry-run` freshness gate → **0 stale**.
- `bun run skill:check` → all hosts fresh; `gstack-plan-deliverables` OK across hosts.
- ⚠️ `skill:check` reports `❌ claude/SKILL.md — generated file missing`. This **pre-exists on `main`** (upstream `claude/` contains only `SKILL.md.tmpl`) and is unrelated to this branch.

## Notes for review

- Commit 1 also carries the `gen-skill-docs` and test-suite fixes that `/autobuilder-loop` depends on to generate and validate.
- Happy to split this into two PRs, trim scope, or take the skills separately — whatever's easiest to review.

Gstack now requires each project to approve a specific Codex profile before Codex can run.

## How it works

title: Windows: setup can never pass its own browse gate (BROWSE_BIN misses .exe) — skills silently never install while VERSION reports the new version
body:
## Summary

On Windows (MSYS2/Git Bash), `./setup` **can never succeed**. `BROWSE_BIN` is hardcoded without the `.exe` suffix, but `bun build --compile` emits `browse.exe` on Windows. The gate at `setup:436` is an **executable-bit** test, not an existence test, so it always fails and the script `exit 1`s.

Because that gate sits *before* skill installation, the user is left with a half-install whose failure is silent by consequence: `gstack/VERSION` reports the **new** version while `~/.claude/skills/*` still holds the **old** skill files. The version file reports a success the skills never received.

I hit this upgrading 1.43.1.0 → 1.60.1.0 (global git install). My installed skills were dated **May 22** while `VERSION` read 1.43.1.0 — so this had been failing silently across multiple upgrades. `/diagram` and `/spec` (new in 1.60) were present in the repo but never installed.

## Root cause

`setup:20` sets the path with no extension:

```sh
BROWSE_BIN="$SOURCE_GSTACK_DIR/browse/dist/browse"   # setup:20 (and again at :245)
```

Windows *is* detected — but only at `setup:28`, after the assignment, and `IS_WINDOWS` is never applied to `BROWSE_BIN`:

```sh
IS_WINDOWS=0
case "$(uname -s)" in
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) IS_WINDOWS=1 ;;
```

The build then produces `browse.exe`, so the two `-x` tests on the extensionless path both misfire:

- `setup:379` — `[ ! -x "$BROWSE_BIN" ]` is the **staleness** check, so Windows rebuilds the binary on *every* run (~10s wasted each time).
- `setup:436` — the same test is a hard gate: `exit 1`.

```
  [353ms] compile  browse/dist/browse.exe        <- build emits .exe
gstack setup failed: browse binary missing at /c/Users/.../browse/dist/browse
```

`ls` confirms the mismatch — the built artifact and the tested path are different files:

```
-rwxr-xr-x  98519552  browse.exe     <- freshly built, executable
-rw-r--r-- 103963473  browse         <- stale leftover, NOT executable -> -x fails
```

## Reproduce

On Windows / Git Bash, from a clean clone: `./setup` → exits 1 at the gate, `~/.claude/skills/` is never updated, `VERSION` reads new regardless.

## Proposed fix

Apply the suffix once Windows is known (and at `:245`, which duplicates the assignment):

```sh
BROWSE_BIN="$SOURCE_GSTACK_DIR/browse/dist/browse"
[ "$IS_WINDOWS" -eq 1 ] && BROWSE_BIN="$BROWSE_BIN.exe"
```

This requires moving the assignment below the `IS_WINDOWS` detection at `setup:28`, or re-applying it there.

Worth noting: the extensionless PE **does** execute under Git Bash — after `cp -f browse.exe browse`, `./browse/dist/browse status` returns `Status: healthy`. So the skills' documented `browse/dist/browse` invocation path is fine; only the exec-bit test is wrong. Pointing `BROWSE_BIN` at `.exe` also fixes the redundant per-run rebuild at `:379`.

### Workaround (for other Windows users landing here)

```sh
cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack/browse/dist
cp -f browse.exe browse && chmod +x browse
cp -f find-browse.exe find-browse && chmod +x find-browse
cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup    # now exits 0 and installs skills
```

⚠️ This workaround degrades the *next* upgrade from a loud failure into a silent one. `browse/dist/` is gitignored, so the copied `browse` survives `git reset --hard`; on the next upgrade the rebuild refreshes `browse.exe` while the stale `browse` still passes `-x`. Setup then reports success while skills invoke the **stale** binary. Re-run `cp -f browse.exe browse` after every upgrade until this is fixed properly.

## Related

- #1901 / #1902 — same symptom class (setup aborting before skills/hooks/migrations land). The proposed phase reorder would **not** fix this one: the browse gate is Phase B, still ahead of skill linking, and on Windows it can never pass regardless of ordering. This needs the `.exe` fix itself.
- #2124 — also concerns `browse.exe` on Windows (Smart App Control / signing).

title: team-init required mode: generated hook emits flat permissionDecision, so the deny never fires
body:
I was setting up team mode for a repo and wanted to check that `required` actually blocks before rolling it out, so I had Claude Code test the generated hook. Turns out the deny doesn't work.

`bin/gstack-team-init required` generates `.claude/hooks/check-gstack.sh`. When gstack is missing it prints:

```json
{"permissionDecision":"deny","message":"gstack is required but not installed. See stderr for install instructions."}
```

For PreToolUse hooks, Claude Code only reads `permissionDecision` from inside a `hookSpecificOutput` object (see the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)). A flat `permissionDecision` isn't a documented field at any event, so this JSON gets ignored. The script also exits 0, which means the exit-code-2 blocking path doesn't apply either. Net result: the Skill call goes through and `required` mode doesn't enforce anything.

The odd part is that gstack already does this correctly elsewhere. `hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts:105-115`:

```ts
function deny(reason: string): void {
  process.stdout.write(
    JSON.stringify({
      hookSpecificOutput: {
        hookEventName: 'PreToolUse',
        permissionDecision: 'deny',
        permissionDecisionReason: reason,
      },
    }),
  );
  process.exit(0);
}
```

So it looks like the generator in `bin/gstack-team-init:130` just drifted from the schema the other hooks use.

## Repro

```bash
cd $(mktemp -d) && git init -q
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-team-init required
# simulate a machine without gstack
FAKE=$(mktemp -d); HOME="$FAKE" bash .claude/hooks/check-gstack.sh
```

Prints the flat JSON above.

## Impact

The CLAUDE.md that team-init writes still works, since the agent follows those instructions as text. But the hook is supposed to be the hard gate and it isn't. A team that turns on `required` will assume enforcement they don't have.

## Fix

One line in `bin/gstack-team-init:130`:

```bash
echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"gstack is required but not installed. See stderr for install instructions."}}'
```

I patched my generated hook locally and verified both paths: denies when gstack is absent, still prints `{}` when present. `test/team-mode.test.ts` only asserts the hook exists and is registered, so nothing there breaks. Can open a PR if you want.

## Environment

- gstack 1.60.1.0 (`a325940`)
- Windows 11, Git Bash (MSYS2)
- Claude Code

Found on Windows but the generated line is the same on every platform.

title: gstack-diff-scope reports every scope false on uncommitted work, and can't set two categories for one file
body:
# `gstack-diff-scope` reports every scope false on uncommitted work, and can't set two categories for one file

**Version:** 1.60.1.0
**File:** `bin/gstack-diff-scope`

Two independent bugs. Both fail silently — `SCOPE_*` comes back `false` rather than erroring, so the consuming skill just skips a reviewer and prints nothing. I hit the first one during a `/ship` and only noticed because I knew the diff was frontend-only.

---

## Bug 1 — uncommitted work is invisible, so `/ship` skips reviewers

`git diff BASE...HEAD --name-only` exits **0 with empty output** when the branch has no commits yet. The `||` fallback is therefore never reached:

```bash
# bin/gstack-diff-scope:10
FILES=$(git diff "${BASE}...HEAD" --name-only 2>/dev/null || git diff "${BASE}" --name-only 2>/dev/null || echo "")
```

`FILES` is empty, the early-exit block at :12-23 prints all-false, and every scope-gated reviewer is skipped.

This is not an edge case for `/ship`. `/ship` detects scope in **Step 9 (Pre-Landing Review)**, which runs **before** it commits in **Step 15**. So the common flow — start work, run `/ship` with changes still in the working tree — hits this every time.

### Repro

```bash
git checkout -b feat/x            # no commits yet
echo "// x" >> src/Button.jsx     # uncommitted frontend change
gstack-diff-scope main
# SCOPE_FRONTEND=false   ← expected true
# ...all false
git add -A && git commit -m x
gstack-diff-scope main
# SCOPE_FRONTEND=true    ← same diff, different answer
```

### Impact

In `ship/sections/review-army.md`, specialist dispatch is gated on these flags:

- `SCOPE_FRONTEND` → design specialist
- `SCOPE_AUTH` / `SCOPE_BACKEND` → security specialist
- `SCOPE_MIGRATIONS` → data-migration specialist (tagged `[NEVER_GATE]`, i.e. meant to run even when silent)

An uncommitted migration or auth change silently skips the specialist that exists specifically to catch it. Step 1 also uses `SCOPE_FRONTEND` to decide whether to recommend `/design-review`, so that recommendation never fires either.

### Suggested fix

Union the committed diff with the working tree and untracked files:

```bash
COMMITTED=$(git diff "${BASE}...HEAD" --name-only 2>/dev/null || true)
WORKING=$(git diff HEAD --name-only 2>/dev/null || true)
UNTRACKED=$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard 2>/dev/null || true)
FILES=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$COMMITTED" "$WORKING" "$UNTRACKED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
```

Untracked matters too: a brand-new `.jsx` component or test file is exactly the kind of thing a reviewer should see, and `/ship` commits it in Step 15 regardless.

---

## Bug 2 — one `case` for nine independent flags makes categories mutually exclusive

Lines :35-83 classify every file through a **single** `case`. `case` is first-match-wins, so each file can only ever set **one** category, even though the nine `SCOPE_*` values are independent booleans.

`*.jsx` (:39) precedes `*.test.*` (:53), so:

```bash
gstack-diff-scope main   # diff contains only src/Button.test.jsx
# SCOPE_FRONTEND=true
# SCOPE_TESTS=false      ← it is unambiguously a test file
```

The asymmetry is visible within the same run: `util.test.ts` sets `TESTS` (because `*.test.*` at :53 precedes `*.ts` at :81) while `Button.test.jsx` sets `FRONTEND` and not `TESTS`. Same intent, opposite result, purely from arm ordering.

### Suggested fix

One `case` per category so the flags are genuinely independent.

`BACKEND` is the one that must stay exclusive — the `# Backend: everything else that's code (excluding views/components already matched)` comment at :76 shows it currently relies on fall-through to avoid claiming `.tsx`/`.jsx`. Make that explicit with a per-file frontend flag:

```bash
f_frontend=false
case "$f" in
  *.tsx|*.jsx|*.vue|*.svelte|*.astro) f_frontend=true ;;
  # ...remaining frontend patterns
esac
[ "$f_frontend" = true ] && FRONTEND=true

# ...independent case blocks for PROMPTS / TESTS / DOCS / CONFIG /
#    MIGRATIONS / API / AUTH

if [ "$f_frontend" = false ]; then
  case "$f" in
    *.rb|*.py|*.go|*.rs|*.java|*.php|*.ex|*.exs) BACKEND=true ;;
    *.ts|*.js|*.mjs|*.cjs|*.mts|*.cts) BACKEND=true ;;
  esac
fi
```

### Known behaviour change

With independent flags, `util.test.ts` sets `BACKEND` **and** `TESTS` where it previously set only `TESTS`. Backend-test-only PRs can then trip the security specialist via the `SCOPE_BACKEND=true AND DIFF_LINES>100` gate. That errs toward more review rather than less, but it's a real change and worth a deliberate call.

---

## Verification

I patched both locally and checked 15 cases:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| uncommitted `.jsx`, no commits | *(all false)* | `FRONTEND` |
| untracked new `.jsx` | *(all false)* | `FRONTEND` |
| `Button.test.jsx` | `FRONTEND` | `FRONTEND TESTS` |
| `Button.spec.tsx` | `FRONTEND` | `FRONTEND TESTS` |
| `util.test.ts` | `TESTS` | `BACKEND TESTS` |
| `A.jsx` | `FRONTEND` | `FRONTEND` |
| `server.ts` | `BACKEND` | `BACKEND` |
| `app.mjs` | `BACKEND` | `BACKEND` |
| `db/migrate/001_x.rb` | `BACKEND MIGRATIONS` | `BACKEND MIGRATIONS` |
| `src/api/users.ts` | `BACKEND API` | `BACKEND API` |
| `src/lib/auth.ts` | `BACKEND AUTH` | `BACKEND AUTH` |
| `README.md` | `DOCS` | `DOCS` |
| `package.json` | `CONFIG` | `CONFIG` |
| clean tree, no changes | *(all false)* | *(all false)* |

Happy to open a PR if useful.

### Minor

`*.module.css|*.module.scss` at :38 are unreachable — they sit in the same arm as `*.css|*.scss`, which already match them.

title: setup fails on Linux: build-node-server.sh uses unescaped { in perl regex (fatal on perl ≥5.26)
body:
# setup fails on Linux: `build-node-server.sh` uses unescaped `{` in perl regex (fatal on perl ≥5.26)

## Summary

`./setup` aborts on a fresh Linux install because `browse/scripts/build-node-server.sh` runs a perl substitution whose pattern contains an **unescaped literal `{`**. Perl 5.26+ treats an unescaped `{` in a regex as a fatal error, so perl exits non-zero, and because the script runs under `set -e`, the entire gstack setup aborts.

Notably this is a **Windows-only** build step (Node.js server bundle, per the script header), so it should never block setup on Linux/macOS at all.

## Environment

- OS: AlmaLinux 8.10 (Cerulean Leopard), x86_64
- perl: v5.26.3
- bun: 1.3.14

## Offending line

`browse/scripts/build-node-server.sh:35`

```sh
perl -pi -e 's|import { Database } from "bun:sqlite";|const Database = null; // bun:sqlite stubbed on Node|g' "$DIST_DIR/server-node.mjs"
```

## Error

```
Unescaped left brace in regex is illegal here in regex; marked by <-- HERE in m/import { <-- HERE Database } .../ at -e line 1.
```

This surfaces to the user as:

```
script "build" exited with code 255
gstack setup failed
```

## Root cause

In perl 5.26.0 the previously-deprecated unescaped literal `{` inside a regex pattern became a hard error. The `{` / `}` in `import { Database }` are parsed as a (malformed) quantifier and rejected.

## Fix

Escape the braces in the pattern (behavior-preserving):

```sh
perl -pi -e 's|import \{ Database \} from "bun:sqlite";|const Database = null; // bun:sqlite stubbed on Node|g' "$DIST_DIR/server-node.mjs"
```

## Secondary issue (worth considering)

This bundle step is documented as Windows-only, yet it runs unconditionally during `setup` and, under `set -e`, a failure here kills the whole install. Consider either:
- guarding the Node/Windows bundle build behind an OS/platform check, or
- not letting a failure in this optional step abort the top-level setup.

That would make setup resilient even if a future regex/tooling incompatibility resurfaces.

title: gstack-redact-prepush: no allowlist plumbing (engine supports it) + unchunked scan fail-closes on >1 MiB diffs — both push users onto GSTACK_REDACT_PREPUSH=skip, which skips all scanning
body:
Two defects in `bin/gstack-redact-prepush` (observed on gstack 1.60.1.0, macOS, bun) that together train users to reach for `GSTACK_REDACT_PREPUSH=skip` — and that valve skips ALL scanning, which defeats the guard exactly when it matters. Related but distinct from #1946 (fail-open on git errors, which the current hook already fixes with `gitStrict`).

## Defect 1 — the hook never passes the engine's `allowlist` option, so synthetic fixtures hard-block pushes

`lib/redact-engine.ts` supports value-exact suppression:

```ts
export interface ScanOptions {
  /** Extra allowlist entries (exact strings) that suppress a matched span. */
  allowlist?: string[];
  ...
}
```

…but the hook calls `scan(added, { repoVisibility: "private" })` with no allowlist and no way for a repo to provide one. Any repo whose committed docker-compose / test files contain a synthetic DB URL like `postgresql://booking:booking@localhost:5432/booking` gets a HIGH `db.url_with_password` on every push that touches those lines (the `booking:booking` password is not caught by `isPlaceholderSpan`). There is no remediation path other than the skip valve, so the valve becomes routine — we counted the skip in 14 of 38 working transcripts in one project before intervening.

**Suggested fix:** read an optional repo-level allowlist file (e.g. `.gstack-redact-allowlist` at the repo root — one literal span per line, `#` comments) and pass it through to `scan()`. Value-exact spans only; the engine already does `allow.has(span)` so no engine change is needed.

## Defect 2 — added lines are scanned as ONE string, so >1 MiB diffs fail closed with `engine.input_too_large`, and the only relief valve disables scanning entirely

The engine's 1 MiB `maxBytes` fail-closed cap is correct for a single scan call, but the hook concatenates all added lines per ref and scans once. Feature-branch pushes with big lockfiles/docs/generated files routinely exceed 1 MiB, producing:

```
HIGH  engine.input_too_large  Input too large to scan safely (N > 1048576 bytes) — blocking fail-closed
```

The push is blocked on SIZE, not on a finding — and the documented escape (`GSTACK_REDACT_PREPUSH=skip`) then performs zero scanning on exactly the largest, riskiest pushes.

**Suggested fix:** chunk the added-lines text on line boundaries under `maxBytes` (a single line larger than the chunk size can be sliced with a few KB of overlap so a token spanning the cut is still seen whole), scan each chunk, and aggregate findings. In our downstream copy of this approach, a 3.96 MB added-lines diff scans in 6 chunks in ~340 ms, and a single planted credential inside such a diff is still caught.

## Why filing instead of patching

We run the fix as a repo-local `pre-push.local` leg (same engine, allowlist + chunking + fail-closed watchdog) because hand-editing the managed binary gets clobbered by upgrades. Happy to share the implementation if useful.

title: setup omits lib/ beside bin/, breaking gstack-learnings-log runtime imports
body:
## Summary

The installer/runtime registration omits the shared `lib/` directory, while `bin/gstack-learnings-log` imports `../lib/jsonl-store.ts`. After a setup/refresh, the installed runtime can fail with:

```
Cannot find module .../lib/jsonl-store.ts
```

This prevents gstack learning entries from being written.

## Reproduction

1. Run `./setup` for a Codex/Claude/OpenCode runtime.
2. Invoke the installed `gstack-learnings-log` with valid JSON:

```bash
gstack-learnings-log '{"skill":"investigate","type":"investigation","key":"smoke-test","insight":"test","confidence":10,"source":"observed"}'
```

3. Observe the missing `lib/jsonl-store.ts` module error when the runtime sidecar does not contain `lib/`.

## Root cause

The setup flow copies/links runtime assets such as `bin`, `browse`, `review`, and `qa`, but does not consistently copy/link `lib` beside `bin`. However, `bin/gstack-learnings-log` depends on:

```ts
import { hasInjection } from "../lib/jsonl-store.ts";
```

## Suggested fix

Include `lib` in the sidecar asset list and link/copy it into every runtime root that receives `bin` (Codex, Factory, OpenCode, Kiro, and other supported hosts). Add setup validation tests asserting that `bin` and `lib` are installed together.

I applied this locally and verified:

- `gstack-learnings-log` smoke test succeeds.
- `bun test test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts`: 403 passed, 0 failed.

Environment: macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.14, gstack `a325940` (VERSION `1.60.1.0`).

title: fix(gbrain): honor GBRAIN_HOME as workspace root, not state dir
body:
## Summary
- `gstack-gbrain-detect`, `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts`, and `lib/gbrain-exec.ts` all resolved `$GBRAIN_HOME/config.json` (flat) when `GBRAIN_HOME` was set, but fell back to `$HOME/.gbrain/config.json` (nested) when unset.
- The real `gbrain` CLI always nests state under a `.gbrain` dir inside `GBRAIN_HOME` regardless of whether it's set or defaulted — confirmed empirically: pointing `GBRAIN_HOME` straight at the `.gbrain` dir breaks the CLI with "No brain configured".
- Net effect for anyone with a relocated `GBRAIN_HOME` (not the default `~/.gbrain`): `gstack-gbrain-detect` always reported `gbrain_config_exists: false` and `gbrain_local_status: "missing-config"` even with a fully working gbrain install pointed elsewhere. Every `/sync-gbrain` and `/setup-gbrain` invocation hit this, and `buildGbrainEnv` silently never seeded `DATABASE_URL` for spawned gbrain calls in this setup either.

## Fix
Always join `GBRAIN_HOME` (or the `userHome` fallback) with `.gbrain` before appending `config.json`, in all three places — matching the real CLI's own resolution.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced: `GBRAIN_HOME=/custom/path` with real config at `/custom/path/.gbrain/config.json` → `gstack-gbrain-detect` reported `gbrain_config_exists: false`, `gbrain_local_status: "missing-config"` before the fix
- [x] After fix: same setup reports `gbrain_config_exists: true`, `gbrain_engine: "postgres"`, `gbrain_local_status: "ok"`
- [x] Verified from two different working directories/repos, not just one
- [x] `git diff --stat` confirms only the 3 intended files changed, rebased cleanly onto latest `main` (no conflict with the recent `engine-locked` classification commit, which added a new function calling the same broken helper)

title: retro/ship test-file count scans untracked build output: reports 623 vs 17 real (37x) on a Rails repo
body:
## Summary

The test-file counting command used by `/retro` and `/ship` scans the whole working tree with `find`, so it counts untracked build artifacts as test files. On a Rails repo with bundled gems it over-reports by **37x** (623 vs 17).

`/retro` reports this number directly as "Total test files: N", so the number in the retro is simply wrong. `/ship` uses it for a before/after delta in the PR body, so its delta stays roughly right but both absolute numbers are inflated.

## The command

```bash
find . -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -name '*_test.*' -o -name '*_spec.*' 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | wc -l
```

Locations (v1.60.1.0):

| File | Line(s) | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `retro/SKILL.md.tmpl` | 200 | source |
| `ship/sections/test-coverage.md` | 39, 177 | source |
| `scripts/resolvers/testing.ts` | 225, 433 | source |
| `openclaw/skills/gstack-openclaw-retro/SKILL.md` | 63 | source |
| `retro/SKILL.md` | 1029 | generated |
| `test/fixtures/golden-ship-claude.md` | 1090, 1250 | fixture |
| `test/fixtures/golden/codex-ship-SKILL.md` | 1390, 1528 | fixture |
| `test/fixtures/golden/factory-ship-SKILL.md` | 1392, 1530 | fixture |

## Reproduction

Any Rails repo with `bundle install --path vendor/bundle`. Measured on a Rails 8 app (17 real test files under `test/`):

```
$ find . -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -name '*_test.*' -o -name '*_spec.*' 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | wc -l
623

$ git ls-files | grep -E '(\.test\.|\.spec\.|_test\.|_spec\.)' | wc -l
17
```

Where the 623 comes from:

```
433  vendor/bundle/ruby/3.4.0/gems/...     bundled gem test suites
189  .claude/worktrees/agent-*/            agent worktree copies
  4  nested node_modules                   e.g. vendor/.../axe-core-api-4.11.1/node_modules
 17  test/                                 the real answer
```

## Two separate defects

**1. `grep -v node_modules` only removes literal path matches.** It catches `./node_modules/...` but the filter is doing string matching on output lines, not tree pruning — so `find` still descends into every `node_modules` on disk and pays the walk cost. More importantly it does nothing about `vendor/`, `.claude/worktrees/`, `tmp/`, `coverage/`, or any other untracked tree.

**2. No exclusion list can be complete.** `vendor/bundle` is Ruby, `.claude/worktrees/` is gstack's own feature, and every ecosystem adds more (`target/` in Rust, `.venv/` in Python, `Pods/` in iOS). Enumerating them is a losing game.

## Proposed fix

Count tracked files instead:

```bash
git ls-files 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(\.test\.|\.spec\.|_test\.|_spec\.)' | wc -l
```

- Untracked build output is excluded by definition, no exclusion list to maintain
- Respects the repo's own `.gitignore` for free
- Much faster (no full-tree walk)
- Both `/retro` and `/ship` already require a git repo and run `git log origin/<default>` in the same step, so this adds no new dependency

Note `.claude/worktrees/` is untracked in the parent repo, so this also fixes the worktree inflation without special-casing gstack's own directory.

## Tradeoff

Brand-new test files that are written but not yet `git add`-ed stop counting. For `/retro` that is correct (it reports on merged history). For `/ship`'s before/after delta it slightly changes semantics — if that matters, `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` includes untracked-but-not-ignored files while still honoring `.gitignore`.

PR incoming.

title: /browse daemons bind OS-assigned ephemeral ports on 127.0.0.1 and can silently hijack local test-suite traffic (phantom 404s)
body:
## Summary

The `/browse` terminal agent (`browse/src/terminal-agent.ts`) starts with
`Bun.serve({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port: 0 })` and keeps that OS-assigned port for its whole
lifetime (days/weeks). `port: 0` hands out a port from the OS **ephemeral range**
(49152–65535 on macOS) — the same pool every short-lived test server draws from. Because the
daemon answers `404 "not found"` to everything it doesn't recognize, it can silently absorb
traffic meant for ephemeral test servers, producing "impossible" phantom 404s in any Node test
suite on the machine.

On this machine two gstack daemons were squatting the ephemeral range:

```
$ lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P | grep 127.0.0.1
bun ... 127.0.0.1:49197 (LISTEN)   ← browse terminal-agent, alive since 2026-07-10
bun ... 127.0.0.1:54221 (LISTEN)
```

## The hijack mechanism (verified end-to-end)

1. supertest (and many test helpers) start one ephemeral server per request with
   `app.listen(0)` — **no host**, so Node binds the wildcard `::` (dual-stack). The bind is
   handed a port by the kernel.
2. On macOS, a **specific tcp4 bind** (`127.0.0.1:49197`, the daemon) and a **v6 wildcard
   bind** (`:::49197`, the test server) **coexist** — the kernel happily assigns the test
   server the daemon's port number. Verified:

   ```js
   // with the gstack daemon alive on 127.0.0.1:49197
   http.createServer(...).listen(49197)          // → SUCCESS, address = { address: '::', port: 49197 }
   http.get('http://127.0.0.1:49197/ping')       // → 404 "not found"  ← answered by the DAEMON
   ```

3. supertest connects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. For v4 traffic, the daemon's **more
   specific** bind wins. Every request of that unlucky test goes to the daemon → its 404.

With ~2 squatted ports out of ~16,384 and thousands of `listen(0)` calls per full-suite run,
the per-run collision probability lands at the ~10-30% we measured. The result is a flake with
a rotating victim test, never reproducible in isolation, insensitive to jest workers/CPU — it
cost us multiple engineering days across two incident investigations before instrumentation
traced the 404s to a constant foreign port.

## Suggested fixes (any one of these kills the class)

1. **Bind a port outside the ephemeral range.** E.g. scan a small fixed window in the
   registered range (say 8531–8599) instead of `port: 0`, keeping the existing port-file
   discovery. Long-lived daemons and `port: 0` are a bad pairing: the OS assumes ephemeral
   ports are returned quickly.
2. Alternatively, make the port configurable (env var) and document the interference so
   affected users can move it.
3. At minimum: respond to unknown routes with something distinctive (e.g. a
   `Server: gstack-browse` header or a JSON body naming the daemon). A greppable fingerprint
   would have turned days of debugging into minutes.

## Workaround we shipped on our side

Client-side: patch supertest's `Test.prototype.serverAddress` in `jest.setup.js` so tests
connect via `http://[::1]:<port>` (pure IPv6 loopback) — a tcp4-bound daemon can never receive
that traffic. (Binding the test servers to `127.0.0.1` instead is NOT viable: supertest reads
`server.address()` synchronously after `listen(0)`, and passing a host makes the bind async via
`dns.lookup`.)

## Environment

- gstack 1.60.1.0, browse terminal-agent started via `bun run .../browse/src/terminal-agent.ts`
- macOS (darwin 25.2.0), Bun ≥ 1.x, Node 22.22.3 test suite (jest 30 + supertest 7)
- Diagnosis one-liner for affected users:
  `lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P | grep 127.0.0.1` → any port ≥ 49152 held by a daemon is a
  potential phantom-404 source for local test suites.

title: review skill: Claude Code install path still never copies checklist.md/specialists/ (fresh repro on v1.60.1.0, follow-up to #1499)
body:
Follow-up to #1499, which was closed with:

> Setup linker hardening shipped in v1.38.0.0 via `_link_or_copy` and the static-invariant test (`test/setup-windows-fallback.test.ts`). Closing — if specific review sibling files (checklist.md, specialists/) are still unreachable on latest, please reopen with a fresh repro.

Reproduced fresh on **v1.60.1.0** (latest), Windows/Git Bash. I don't have permission to reopen #1499 myself (not the author or a collaborator), so filing this as the requested fresh repro instead.

## Repro

1. Fresh `./setup` targeting Claude Code (no `--local`).
2. Inspect `~/.claude/skills/review/`:

```
$ ls ~/.claude/skills/review/
SKILL.md
```

Only `SKILL.md` is present. `checklist.md`, `design-checklist.md`, `greptile-triage.md`, `TODOS-format.md`, and `specialists/` are all missing, even though they exist in the source checkout at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/review/`.

3. Running `/review` fails at "Step 2: Read the checklist" (`Read .claude/skills/review/checklist.md`) because the file was never copied into the flattened skill dir.

## Root cause

The v1.38.0.0 fix hardened `_link_or_copy`'s Windows fallback (real copy vs symlink), but it never taught the **Claude Code install path** to actually copy the `review` skill's extra runtime asset files. `link_claude_skill_dirs()` in `setup` (~line 540) only ever copies `SKILL.md` and, if present, a `sections/` subdir for each skill:

```bash
_link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/SKILL.md" "$target/SKILL.md"
if [ -d "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" ]; then
  ...
  _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" "$target/sections"
fi
```

Every *other* host installer in the same `setup` script (`create_codex_runtime_root`, `create_factory_runtime_root`, `create_opencode_runtime_root`, and the Kiro install block) explicitly loops over `checklist.md design-checklist.md greptile-triage.md TODOS-format.md` (and, for OpenCode, `specialists/`) to copy them into the flattened runtime dir. The Claude Code path was simply never given the equivalent step, so it's the one host where `/review` has always been missing these files on a fresh install.

## Suggested fix

Add a `review`-specific branch to `link_claude_skill_dirs()` mirroring what the other hosts already do:

```diff
       if [ -d "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" ]; then
         if [ -e "$target/sections" ] || [ -L "$target/sections" ]; then rm -rf "$target/sections"; fi
         _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/sections" "$target/sections"
       fi
+      # review/ runtime assets: SKILL.md reads checklist.md and
+      # greptile-triage.md via a relative path resolved against this
+      # flattened dir. Codex/Kiro/Factory/OpenCode installers already copy
+      # these; mirror that here so /review doesn't 404 on Claude.
+      if [ "$dir_name" = "review" ]; then
+        for f in checklist.md design-checklist.md greptile-triage.md TODOS-format.md; do
+          if [ -f "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/$f" ]; then
+            if [ -L "$target/$f" ]; then rm -f "$target/$f"; fi
+            _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/$f" "$target/$f"
+          fi
+        done
+        if [ -d "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/specialists" ]; then
+          if [ -e "$target/specialists" ] || [ -L "$target/specialists" ]; then rm -rf "$target/specialists"; fi
+          _link_or_copy "$gstack_dir/$dir_name/specialists" "$target/specialists"
+        fi
+      fi
       linked+=("$link_name")
```

Applied and verified locally (Windows/Git Bash) — a re-run of the linker now populates `~/.claude/skills/review/` with all five items and `/review` proceeds past Step 2.

title: fix(hooks): question-preference-hook must not emit permissionDecision 'defer' (merges #2165 + #1924)
body:
Picking up the handoff from #2165. @time-attack asked there on 2026-07-15:

> Please rewrite this version to include the accurate documentation and strict output coverage from PR 1924. Its implementation is otherwise the best current foundation.

Neither PR has moved since, so this branch does that merge. Credit belongs to @dpnascimento (#2165) and @jacksondc (#1924); every commit here carries both as co-authors. If either of them would rather carry it forward, I am happy to close this in favour of theirs.

## The bug

`hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts` emitted `permissionDecision: "defer"` on its no-opinion path. `defer` is a real Claude Code value meaning "pause this tool call and hand control back", and it is honored in print/non-interactive mode. So in any non-interactive session, every `AskUserQuestion` the hook did not auto-decide got parked and never executed. On my machine one such call was replayed several times across resumes, and no `tool_result` was ever written for it.

## What changed

- `defer()` becomes `passThrough()`: silent `exit 0`, or `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` alone when plan-tune has context to inject. No `permissionDecision` on that path.
- The `deny` paths (never-ask auto-decide, Conductor prose redirect) are untouched.
- Spike doc corrections, going a little beyond #1924: it restores the `deny > ask > allow` precedence fact that #1924 deleted outright, moves "No output" out of the `permissionDecision values:` list where it is not a value, and rewrites the Auto-decide example from the never-implemented `allow` + `updatedInput` to the `deny` + reason shape the hook actually emits.
- Tests: `expectNoDecision` (from #1924) now covers about ten pass-through cases, plus two cases #1924 lacked. One is `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` with no preference, which is the exact shape the bug reports fire on. The other asserts `hookEventName === 'PreToolUse'` on the `additionalContext`-only output.

## Scope

Fixes the root cause behind #2006, #2035, #2292 and #2310.

#2207 is not fixed here. That one is the Conductor auto-install of the hook, owned by #2208. An early commit body on this branch listed #2207 among the root-cause issues; that wording was too broad, and this PR body is authoritative on claim surface.

## Verification

```
bun test test/question-preference-hook.test.ts test/memory-cache-injection.test.ts
  28 pass / 0 fail / 67 expect()      (upstream/main: 27 pass / 52 expect)

bun run test
  2 failures: spec-template-sync, session-runner observability
  Both also fail on untouched upstream/main. Zero new failures.

bun run slop:diff
  no new findings in 5 changed files
```

## Two things I could not verify

The cathedral e2e assertion never executed locally. `test/skill-e2e-plan-tune-cathedral.test.ts` is `EVALS=1`-gated. Forcing it with `EVALS_ALL=1 EVALS=1` gives 0 pass / 5 fail, because the fixture scaffold does not copy `lib/`, so the hook dies with `Cannot find module '../../../lib/is-conductor'` at `expect(res.status).toBe(0)`, before the pass-through assertion runs. That fixture gap predates this branch and is not fixed here. Gate coverage for this behaviour is the two unit test files above.

The Conductor deny reason carries a premise I could not confirm. In Conductor the hook still denies with a prose redirect whose reason cites the MCP variant being flaky. That premise was tied to the same `defer` path this PR removes, and I have not re-proven it under current Claude Code. The behaviour is deliberately unchanged, since it is out of scope, but that wording is now a historical claim this PR does not confirm.

I can rebase or reshape this however suits the review.

title: question-preference-hook: permissionDecision 'defer' hangs AskUserQuestion on Claude Code >= 2.1.21x
fix(preamble): probe gbrain engine liveness before recommending it
body:
## Problem

The gbrain block in the skill preamble decides whether to tell the agent "prefer `gbrain search` over Grep". Today it checks three things:

1. `~/.gbrain/config.json` exists
2. `gbrain --version` responds
3. the worktree has a `.gbrain-source` pin

All three can pass while the engine is completely unreachable — **none of them opens a connection**. They prove gbrain is *installed*, not that it *works*.

So when the engine goes down (disk full, container stopped, pooler unreachable, autopilot wedged), every skill preamble keeps printing:

> GBrain configured. Prefer `gbrain search`/`gbrain query` over Grep for semantic questions…

The agent then reaches for a tool whose every query fails, instead of falling back to Grep. Nothing errors, nothing is surfaced — the guidance actively asserts health it never verified, so the outage is silent and can persist indefinitely.

I hit exactly this: the local Postgres engine was crash-looping on a full Docker disk for well over a day. The preamble recommended gbrain the entire time.

## Fix

Add a bounded liveness probe and branch on the result:

```bash
_GBRAIN_ALIVE=0
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 5 gbrain sources list >/dev/null 2>&1 && _GBRAIN_ALIVE=1
else
  gbrain sources list >/dev/null 2>&1 && _GBRAIN_ALIVE=1
fi
```

When it fails, the preamble now says so and redirects to Grep:

```
GBrain DOWN — this worktree is pinned, but a probe query failed, so
the engine is unreachable. Do NOT rely on `gbrain search`/`code-def`
this session; use Grep instead. Diagnose with `gbrain doctor --fast`.
```

Design notes:

- **Bounded.** `timeout 5` means a hung engine can't stall the preamble of every skill. Falls back to an unbounded call only where `timeout` isn't available (rare on macOS/Linux; the alternative is skipping the check entirely).
- **Engine-agnostic.** Points at `gbrain doctor --fast` rather than assuming any particular backend (PGLite / Postgres / Supabase).
- **Zero cost when gbrain isn't in play.** The probe runs only inside the existing "pin is present" branch, so non-gbrain users and unpinned worktrees are untouched.
- **Cheap.** One `sources list` per skill invocation.

## Changes

- `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-brain-sync-block.ts` — the actual change
- 49 generated `SKILL.md` files — regenerated via `bun run gen:skill-docs`

Insertions only; no existing lines modified.

## Verification

Tested against a genuinely stopped engine, from a pinned worktree:

| engine state | preamble output |
|---|---|
| up | normal "prefer `gbrain search`" guidance |
| **stopped** | **`GBrain DOWN` + use Grep + diagnose hint`** |
| restarted | normal guidance again |

Also confirmed the unpinned-worktree branch still prints its existing "isn't pinned yet" message and never runs the probe.

title: fix(hooks): don't emit invalid permissionDecision 'defer' — it swallows the AskUserQuestion widget
body:
## The bug

`question-preference-hook` returns `{"permissionDecision":"defer"}` on its no-opinion path, intending "let the permission flow continue."

`defer` is **not** in Claude Code's PreToolUse schema, which accepts only `allow` / `deny` / `ask`. As of **Claude Code 2.1.14** the unrecognized value is interpreted as *defer the tool call*: the call is dropped and logged as a `hook_deferred_tool` attachment. It never executes.

For `AskUserQuestion` this means **the question widget never renders**. The user sees nothing at all, and the agent is left waiting on an answer that can never arrive.

Captured in a real transcript:

```
tool_use          AskUserQuestion  toolu_01PWVYTunnejtJTZv3SF6Bsw
hook_success      PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion
                  stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"defer"}}
hook_deferred_tool  AskUserQuestion   <-- call swallowed here
user              "questions are not loading"
```

## Blast radius

This is not limited to users with plan-tune preferences configured. `defer()` is the **default** path for every non-auto-decidable question:

- no preference set
- recommendation marker missing
- `always-ask` preference
- one-way-door safety override
- empty/unparseable stdin (crash safety)
- non-AUQ tool names (defensive)

So `AskUserQuestion` is broken for essentially every user on Claude Code 2.1.14 with gstack installed.

## The fix

Omit `permissionDecision` entirely in `defer()`. That is the correct "no opinion" signal — normal permission flow continues, and `additionalContext` (the memory-cache injection) is still delivered.

The `deny()` paths are untouched: never-ask auto-decide and the Conductor prose redirect still enforce exactly as before.

## Docs

`docs/spikes/claude-code-hook-mutation.md` documented `"defer" — let permission flow continue` as a valid value. That stale assumption is how this got written, so it's corrected here to prevent reintroduction.

## Tests

Defer-path assertions changed from `toBe('defer')` to `toBeUndefined()`, matching the corrected contract.

```
bun test test/question-preference-hook.test.ts \
         test/memory-cache-injection.test.ts \
         test/gstack-question-log.test.ts

 51 pass
 0 fail
 101 expect() calls
```

Verified end-to-end on Claude Code 2.1.14: with the patch applied, `AskUserQuestion` renders and returns answers normally. Both PostToolUse AUQ hooks (`question-log-hook`, `auq-error-fallback-hook`) were also checked and are unaffected.

title: v1.61.0.0 feat: /garygoal — goal-to-production orchestrator with a deterministic, resumable state machine (v1.61.0.0)
body:
## Summary

`/garygoal` — a goal-to-production orchestration skill (v1.61.0.0, MINOR). One objective in, evidence-gated delivery out:

```
/garygoal Build the hashtag discovery system described in docs/hashtag-spec.md
```

It conducts the pipeline the suite already has — repository audit → objective contract → `/spec`/`/office-hours` only when the objective is vague → `/autoplan` (premise gate respected) → TDD implementation → `/review` → `/cso --diff` → `/design-review` + `/qa` → `/devex-review` → `/benchmark` → `/codex` → `/ship` (stop-loop handled) → CI repair → review-thread repair → `READY_TO_MERGE`. Only under explicit `--merge` **and** `garygoal_autonomous_merge: true`: merge-check → merge → `/land-and-deploy` → `/canary` with rollback handling.

**Thin conductor, not another specialist.** Every phase loads the real specialist skill from disk via `{{INVOKE_SKILL}}` and executes it at full depth. The specialists stay the source of truth.

**Deterministic state, not prose.** `bin/gstack-garygoal` + `lib/garygoal-state.ts` (same audited `jsonl-store`/`redact-engine` plumbing as the decision store) enforce:

- 29-state machine with per-state evidence requirements (`PR_OPEN` needs a real PR number + head SHA; `VERIFIED` needs deployed SHA + HEALTHY canary)
- gates tied to commit SHAs, with a deterministic diff→invalidation matrix (docs-only commits don't re-run browser QA; auth changes re-run tests + security + QA)
- merge-check derives **mandatory** review gates from the PR diff itself — an auth diff with no `security_review` gate refuses even if routing was talked out of `/cso`
- MERGING unreachable outside merge/repair-pr modes, with a READY_TO_MERGE head-SHA cross-check
- fail-closed repair budgets clamped to policy (3 CI hypotheses/check, 3 review cycles, 5 ship reruns → BLOCKED with an investigation report)
- session-anchored branch locks (same-owner supersede, rename-steal reclaim, pid≤0 DoS guard); `init` refuses to twin an incomplete run (no budget laundering; `--abandon-incomplete` is the audited escape)
- untrusted-derived free text travels via `--evidence-file`/`--text-file`, is deeply injection/secret-scanned at write time, and is datamarked on render; O_EXCL atomic state writes
- runs resume across sessions (`--resume`), with fail-safe refusal on corrupt or unknown-schema state

## Review

title: security: keep ngrok authentication tokens out of agent chat
body:
## Summary

The canonical `pair-agent/SKILL.md` tells users with an unauthenticated ngrok installation to return an ngrok authentication token in chat, then places that token in a model-visible command. Provider authentication credentials should never enter an agent transcript or tool call.

No credential value was inspected or included in this report. The short-lived setup key generated specifically for agent pairing is a separate, documented handoff credential and is not the subject of this issue.

## Recommended remediation

- Direct the user to run ngrok authentication themselves in a private terminal.
- Ask only for confirmation that local authentication completed.
- Never request, receive, display, compare, transform, or place the ngrok authentication token in a model-visible command.
- Add a static skill-source guard against instructions to paste or provide API keys, provider tokens, passwords, cookies, or secrets to the agent.

## Duplicate check

No matching open issue or visible draft repository security advisory was found.

/sync-gbrain --dream: classifyDreamOutcome false-positives 'pack does not extract code symbols' on every base-pack brain
body:
## Summary

`classifyDreamOutcome` in `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts` (~line 1381) decides the dream stage failed for pack-capability reasons by string-matching the cycle log:

```ts
if (/does not declare this phase/i.test(out)) {
  return "dream ran, but this source's schema pack does not extract code symbols, ...";
}
```

But in gbrain (0.42.26.0), the only emitters of `"active pack does not declare this phase"` are the **content** phases — `extract_atoms` (`src/core/cycle.ts:1686`) and `synthesize_concepts` (`src/core/cycle.ts:1800`). Neither has anything to do with code symbols. On `gbrain-base` / `gbrain-base-v2` (the default packs, which legitimately don't declare those creator-pack phases), every dream cycle log contains the matched string, so `/sync-gbrain --dream` reports the WARN even when the call-graph build worked.

**Versions:** gstack 1.60.1.0, gbrain 0.42.26.0, PGLite engine.

## Observed

Dream cycle log from a real run (base-v2 pack, TS repo):

```
  - extract_atoms  extract_atoms: active pack does not declare this phase (run `gbrain dream --phase extract_atoms --drain` to drain a backlog)
  ✓ resolve_symbol_edges  6001 chunk(s) walked; resolved 0, ambiguous 0, unmatched 0
  - synthesize_concepts  synthesize_concepts: active pack does not declare this phase
```

`resolve_symbol_edges` ran (✓) — yet the stage summary came out as:

```
WARN  dream  dream ran, but this source's schema pack does not extract code symbols, so the call graph stays empty. Switch this source to a code-aware schema pack (`gbrain schema use <pack>`) ...
```

## Why it matters

- The WARN's remediation ("switch schema packs") is wrong and costly — no bundled gbrain pack even declares a code-symbol phase, so a user following it churns packs for nothing.
- It masks the real diagnosis. In my case the graph was empty because of a genuine gbrain bug (edges written with NULL `source_id` — filed as garrytan/gbrain#3379); the false pack-capability WARN sent debugging in the wrong direction first.
- The `/sync-gbrain` SKILL.md Step 3.5/Step 5 wording propagates the same claim ("on a non-code-aware pack --dream completes but the graph stays empty"), so the agent-facing docs reinforce the misdiagnosis.

## Suggested fix

1. Anchor the match to the phase that actually builds the graph, e.g. only WARN on pack capability if the log lacks a `resolve_symbol_edges` completion line, or match `/(resolve_symbol_edges|extract_code_symbols)[^\n]*does not declare/i` instead of the bare phrase.
2. When `resolve_symbol_edges` completes with `resolved 0`, prefer the existing 0-edge WARN branch ("resolved 0 edges — no code symbols matched yet") over the pack-capability one; the ordering comment says pack-capability "wins", but it currently wins on unrelated evidence.
3. Update the SKILL.md wording once the classifier is fixed.
