title: ios-qa: guard DebugBridgeTouch.m on DEBUG, not just TARGET_OS_IOS
body:
## The problem

`DebugBridgeTouch.m` and its header both promise the code never ships:

> `Uses these private UIKit selectors (DEBUG-only; never shipped to App Store)`
> `DEBUG-only — never link in Release.`

Nothing enforced it. The only guard was `#if TARGET_OS_IOS`, so a **Release** build for iOS compiles the whole implementation in — private API included.

Measured on a real app, `nm -j` against an iOS Release binary:

| | count |
|---|---|
| `DebugBridge` symbols | **15** |
| `IOHIDEventCreateDigitizer` | 2 |
| `AXSSetAutomationEnabled` | 1 symbol, 2 strings |
| `IOKit.framework` | 4 strings |

Including `+[DebugBridgeTouch sendTapAtPoint:inWindow:]` and `_OBJC_CLASS_$_DebugBridgeTouch`.

That is a Guideline 2.5.1 private-API exposure in a shippable binary, and it fails `Package.swift`'s own stated CI invariant:

```
nm -j build/Release/<binary> | grep -q DebugBridge && exit 1
```

## Why the documented guard doesn't cover it

`Package.swift` describes the protection as `.when(configuration: .debug)` on the consuming target's dependency. That works for **SwiftPM consumers**.

It cannot be expressed by an app integrating DebugBridge as a local package inside an **`.xcodeproj`**. Xcode's Filters column under *Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content* offers platform conditions only — iOS, macOS, visionOS — never build configuration. So for xcodeproj consumers the documented guard silently does nothing, which is exactly the case measured above.

The Swift targets were already safe: all four `.swift` files are `#if DEBUG` guarded and `Package.swift` defines `DEBUG` for them via `swiftSettings`. Only the Objective-C target — the one that actually links private API — was unguarded.

## The fix

1. `DebugBridgeTouch.m.template` branches on `#if !defined(DEBUG)` first and emits **nothing** in Release, falling through to the existing iOS / non-iOS branches only in Debug.
2. `Package.swift.template` declares `DEBUG` explicitly for the ObjC target:
   ```swift
   cSettings: [.define("DEBUG", .when(configuration: .debug))]
   ```
   The two Swift targets already did this. Relying on SwiftPM's implicit `DEBUG` for C-family targets isn't worth betting a private-API exposure on.

Putting the guard in the source means it holds regardless of how the package is integrated, rather than depending on the consumer getting it right.

## Verification

Compiled the generated file for iOS both ways:

```
xcrun -sdk iphoneos clang -c DebugBridgeTouch.m -arch arm64 -I include -fobjc-arc [-DDEBUG=1]
```

| config | DebugBridge symbols | private-API symbols | object size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Release (no `-DDEBUG`) | **0** | **0** | 448 B |
| Debug (`-DDEBUG=1`) | 7 | 6 | 13,104 B |

The harness is unchanged in Debug. Release emits an empty translation unit.

## Note for maintainers

The comments in both templates now record the measured failure, so the guard isn't removed later as redundant. Happy to adjust wording or split the two changes if you'd prefer them separately.

title: fix(test): hermetic-wiring skill-seeding tripwire can never pass on default ~/.claude installs
body:
## Problem

The tripwire `skill seeding stays under runRoot and reads the live repo tree, never operator ~/.claude` asserts every seeded symlink target must NOT start with `~/.claude` — and then that it MUST resolve into the live repo tree. On the default global-git install the repo itself lives at `~/.claude/skills/gstack`, so every **correct** symlink carries the banned prefix: the two assertions can never both hold.

## Evidence

Pristine `c118e240` (v1.64.1.0), verified 2026-08-15 on macOS arm64:
- worktree under `~/.claude/skills/` → the seeding test **fails** (`pair-agent: symlink escapes to .../pair-agent/SKILL.md`)
- worktree anywhere else → **passes**

CI never sees this because dev checkouts don't live under `~/.claude` — but every user following the README install path who runs the suite does.

## Fix

Targets that `realpath` into the resolved repo ROOT are exempted **before** the operator-`~/.claude` ban (both sides realpath'd, so a symlinked $HOME can't dodge the tripwire). Genuine escapes — a target under `~/.claude` but outside the repo — still fail with the specific escape message.

## Verification

`bun test test/hermetic-wiring.test.ts`: 5/5 pass both at `~/.claude/skills/gstack` and at a non-`~/.claude` worktree of this branch.

title: fix(brain-cache): honest 'missing' instead of fabricated-empty digests on gbrain failure
body:
## Problem

`fetchRecentDecisions` and `fetchSalience` in `bin/gstack-brain-cache` return hardcoded empty digests (`_No prior skill runs recorded._` / `_No salient pages in last 14d._`) when `!result?.pages` — i.e. when the gbrain call **failed**, not when it genuinely returned zero rows. `refreshEntity()` then caches that digest and stamps `last_refresh`, so a gbrain-unreachable failure becomes a 'successful' empty answer that survives every TTL cycle, indistinguishable from real emptiness.

## Fix

- Both fetchers return `null` on `!result?.pages`, letting `cmdGet`'s existing missing/stale-fallback machinery report the true state — the same polarity `fetchGoals`/`fetchSimplePage` already have.
- Genuine `pages.length === 0` still renders the honest empty digest.
- New `Array.isArray(result.pages)` guard: a malformed payload (`{pages: {}}`) classifies as failure instead of throwing inside `refreshEntity` (which has no try/catch) and crashing the CLI `get`.

## Verification

`bun test test/brain-cache-roundtrip.test.ts test/brain-cache-stale-but-usable.test.ts`: 33/33 pass; `bun bin/gstack-brain-cache --help` smoke-tested.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(security): guard brain-sync arithmetic against injected .brain-last-pull content; sanitize _GBRAIN_HOST
body:
## Problem

The generated brain-sync preamble bash (every host, every skill) feeds the raw file content of `~/.gstack/.brain-last-pull` straight into `$(( ))` arithmetic. Bash arithmetic evaluates array subscripts and command substitution, so a writable state file is an execution vector — e.g. content like `x[$(cmd)]` runs `cmd` at preamble time. `_GBRAIN_HOST` is likewise interpolated unsanitized into the trusted status line.

## Fix

- `case "$_BRAIN_LAST" in ''|*[!0-9]*) _BRAIN_LAST=0 ;; esac` before the arithmetic — non-numeric content degrades to 0 instead of evaluating.
- `_GBRAIN_HOST` normalized via `head -1 | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-'`.
- Existing `quoteSafePath()` behavior preserved; all host SKILL.md outputs regenerated (49 files) and the three ship golden fixtures re-blessed in the same commit.

## Verification

`bun run gen:skill-docs --host all --dry-run`: 0 STALE. `bun test test/host-config.test.ts test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts test/brain-sync.test.ts`: 503/503 pass.

title: fix(test): repair three browse test files stranded by the v1.63–v1.64.1 refactors
body:
## Problem

Three browse test files fail deterministically on pristine `c118e240` on any machine that actually runs them (24 failures total):

1. **compare-board.test.ts** (16 fails): the v1.64 signature-bridge wrapper for `handleReadCommand` drops its 4th argument, so the now-unconditional JS-origin assertion TypeErrors on `bm.hasCookieImports()`. The sibling write bridge two lines down passes it correctly.
2. **extension-sender-auth.test.ts** (2 fails): the behavioral "gate answers" loops iterate `sidebar-command`, which `background.js` no longer routes (dropped from `ALLOWED_TYPES` with the chat rip) — the listener goes silent on unknown types before the sender gate ever runs.

The first test waits 15s for a `data-status` that never arrives, and bun's timeout handler SIGTERMs the **shared** `beforeAll` browser (exit 143), cascading "browser has been closed" into every later test.

CI never sees #3 because the file self-skips wherever Playwright chromium isn't installed.

## Fix

- compare-board: forward `b` through the read bridge (one argument).
- sender-auth: behavioral loops iterate routed types; `sidebar-command` keeps a nothing-usable-leaks check and stays in the sender-auth policy as defense-in-depth.
- sidepanel: replaced the five stranded tests with pins of the current contract (shield exists, stays hidden, stays undriven) plus a tombstone documenting what was removed, why it can never pass, and how to resurrect the old cases if the shield is ever re-driven.

title: fix(redact): parcel IDs are not phone numbers
body:
## The problem

A county tax-map parcel ID (APN) reads as a national-format phone number to `pii.phone.e164` — the same collision class as the digit-only UUID that `insideUuid` already guards.

```
parcel_id: "12-3456789.000"   →  MEDIUM pii.phone.e164
norm:      "123456789000"     →  MEDIUM pii.phone.e164
```

The regex is deliberately loose to catch international formats, and an APN satisfies it in both its punctuated and normalized forms.

This isn't a rare edge. Land, title and property-tax repos carry APNs by the hundred — one title branch tripped 2 MEDIUM findings on nothing but synthetic fixtures, and the same shape recurs in every fixture, mart and smoke in the domain. A guardrail that cries wolf on the domain's primary identifier is one people learn to wave through, which is how a real HIGH finding eventually gets ignored. That's the reason to fix it rather than live with the noise.

## The guard

`looksLikeParcelId(span, match)`, wired into the existing `validate` alongside `insideUuid` and `looksLikeCompactTimestamp`, following the same context-window approach `insideUuid` uses. Two deliberately separate tiers:

1. **Dotted form, exempt on shape.** No phone convention puts a dot before a trailing 3–4 digit group after a 4–8 digit middle, so this cannot swallow a real number. Hyphen-only variants (`22-0001-000`) are **not** shape-exempted — those genuinely are phone-shaped.

2. **Digits-only form, exempt only on evidence.** A bare digit run is phone-shaped in isolation, so it must be the exact digit-normalization of a punctuated APN within a 400-char window. Fixtures and marts always carry the pair; a real phone number has no such twin nearby. This reads the document's own evidence instead of guessing from digits.

## Verification

**A/B against the unmodified engine** over inputs spanning every rule family — AWS key, PEM, GitHub PAT, email, public IP, credit card, SSN, compact timestamp, UUID, and nine phone formats. Exactly **one** behavior changed: the APN pair. Everything else byte-identical.

**New test pins both directions** (`test/redact-parcel-id-false-positive.test.ts`, 15 cases):
- 9 real phone shapes stay flagged — US dashed/parens/dotted, E.164 US/UK/DE/PT, bare 11-digit
- 3 APN shapes clean
- 3 narrowness controls, including the load-bearing one: **a bare digit run with no punctuated APN nearby is still flagged**

**Proven red under mutation.** Stubbing the guard to `return true` — the dangerous blanket-exemption failure, which would quietly gut the pattern — fails 12 of 15. Stubbing to `return false` fails 3. Restored: 15/15 with the source byte-identical.

**Existing suites green:** `redact-pattern-lint` 49/49, `gstack-config-redact-keys` 6/6, `browse/proxy-redact` 8/8.

HIGH detection is untouched — PEM, GitHub PAT and Slack token all still block.

title: fix(redact-prepush): don't re-scan commits a catch-up merge brought in
body:
## The problem

`remoteSha..localSha` is "everything new on this branch", which is not the same as "everything new to the remote". Merge `origin/main` into a feature branch and every commit main gained since that branch's last push becomes an added line — content that is already published, already scanned, and not this push's doing.

Two consequences, both observed in practice:

- **False HIGH findings.** A placeholder connection string in a fixture someone else had already merged blocked an unrelated push as `db.url_with_password`, telling the operator to rotate a credential over a file they had never touched. A guard that cries wolf on catch-up merges is one people learn to bypass reflexively — which is exactly how a real secret eventually gets through.
- **Oversized scans.** The `SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES` comment already records a 1,146,782-byte diff from "a feature branch catching up to a busy main" blowing the engine's 1 MiB cap. Same root cause, treated there as a size problem and solved by slicing. Narrowing the range fixes the size too.

A two-dot range cannot express this: after merging main, neither the remote tip nor the merge-base with main is an ancestor of the other, so no single base excludes both.

## The fix

The narrowed range is `rev-list localSha --not remoteSha --remotes`, with two guards that matter more than the narrowing itself:

**`remoteSha` stays the base.** It is what git *tells* the hook the remote has, and it is authoritative in a way `--remotes` is not — tracking refs can be absent (fresh clone that never fetched, a remote with no tracking ref) or stale. Using `--remotes` alone excludes nothing in a repo without them, so every commit ever made reads as "new". That is the same false positive from the other direction, and it is precisely what the existing test `only NEW content is scanned (remote..local), not pre-existing` catches.

**When excluding tracking refs changes nothing, defer to the plain range.** Such a push has no catch-up commits, so the existing range already describes it exactly. This keeps every non-catch-up push on the original `gitStrict` diff path — the one `#1946`'s fail-closed regression test exercises. Without this guard that test still *passes*, because the new path never invokes `git diff` and so the test's stub never fires: it would have gone green forever while testing nothing. A narrowing that silently retires a security regression test is a worse trade than the false positives it set out to fix.

Each commit is diffed alone. A merge's combined diff shows only content present in no parent, so a secret introduced while resolving a conflict is still caught, while an ordinary merge contributes nothing. Falls back to the existing range logic for a fresh repo, an absent remote object, or a >500-commit rewrite.

## Verification

- **22/22 existing `redact-prepush-hook` tests pass**, including both `#1946` fail-closed cases.
- **Both new guards proven load-bearing by mutation:** dropping the `remoteSha` base fails 2 tests; dropping the defer-to-plain-range guard fails 1. Restored: 27/27.
- **5 new tests** (`test/redact-prepush-scan-range.test.ts`) build real repositories on disk, because the behaviour under test *is* the git plumbing — a mocked `git` would test the mock. They pin both directions: a catch-up merge no longer re-scans published content (and the old two-dot range demonstrably did), and secrets in new commits, in merge resolutions, and in repos with no remote are all still scanned.
- Other redact suites green: `redact-pattern-lint` 49/49, `gstack-config-redact-keys` 6/6, `browse/proxy-redact` 8/8.
- End-to-end against the real hook: a fresh commit containing an AWS key still exits 1 with `aws.access_key`.

One note for reviewers: `--cc` is passed explicitly on the per-commit `git show`, but it is self-documenting rather than load-bearing — `git show` already defaults to a combined diff for merges, so no test can pin it. The merge-resolution test pins the *coverage*, not the flag. Called out in a comment there so nobody over-trusts it later.

title: v1.66.0.0 feat: test/evals/CI speedup — 90s truthful free suite, diff-billed evals, required Linux lane
body:
## Summary

Test/evals/CI speedup pass (v1.66.0.0). ~85 bisected commits vs main, +7.3K/−5.5K across 84 files.

**Free suite: 454s → ~90-100s, and it stopped lying.** `scripts/test-free-shards.ts` runs the full ~7,000-test suite as up to six concurrent shard processes (serial within each) with strict per-shard output classification: exit-0-without-bun's-terminal-summary is a FAILURE, a wedged shard is SIGKILLed at a size-scaled deadline and named, and the quiet console contract prints per-shard status + `✗ file — test name` epilogues with the full stream in a per-run log. Tree-mutating tests and tree-measuring ratchet readers run in a serial phase after the parallel shards so measurements never race regeneration. 12 orphaned test files wired in; the 3,372-line dead `skill-e2e.test.ts` monolith deleted with 4 never-run tests revived out of it; 5 pre-existing env failures quarantined individually with receipts.

**Paid evals bill by diff.** Three-file selection split (`touchfiles-data.ts` pure literals + `test-selection.ts` logic + `touchfiles.ts` facade, with literal-only + export-parity + duplicate-key tripwires), map-diff selection for edits to the data file itself (old version evaluated via `git show` + a bun child; fail-closed with named reasons), uncommitted/untracked work included in selection, parent-side shard skipping with a `skipped-by-diff` taxonomy and selection banner, `EVALS_JOBS` split from `EVALS_CONCURRENCY`, preflight API ping once per run (fail-fast on missing binary/timeout/exit-127), `--retry 1` on retry-bearing paid paths, detach timeouts floor-enforced against the live shard census.

**CI.** New REQUIRED secretless `free-tests.yml` lane (first-ever Linux coverage for ~420 free-test files; least-privilege token, PR-number concurrency, failure-log artifact, main-push runs). Docker cache key trio ends version-bump image rebuilds; Bun 1.3.13; `skill-e2e-review` split into three matrix shards (741s job → 3 × ≤250s); actionlint digest-pinned prebuilt image; five jobs right-sized; lint/skill-docs double-runs ended; Windows lane caches bun installs and runs the curated suite.

**Eval semantics (D1a/D2a/D3a).** SDK capture default Opus → Sonnet via centralized `lib/eval-model.ts`; judge default STAYS Sonnet after a live A/B regression (below); 4 posture tests demoted to periodic; 9 fixture-extraction commits (SKILL.md sections instead of 1,800-line copies, 58-97% cuts); the 0-for-26 context-save-list test fixed.

**Review-army fix wave (18 commits).** Everything the ship review surfaced and verified, including: cancellation now terminates paid runs (signal forwarders schedule parent exit + launch guards), per-origin classifier buffers (interleaved pipes can't shear a `(fail)` line), phantom `TREE_MUTATING` key replaced with the real carve-guard readers + census pin tests, win32 tree-kill via `taskkill /T`, DSN password percent-encoding, redact placeholder calibration hardened (lowercase `password`/`pass` and bare `$word` at URL-password position block; fully-braced `${...}` interpolations don't), retro E2E requires its report on disk, fork same-name-branch concurrency cancellation closed across three workflows.

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (subagent, diff-scoped): **45/54 paths tested (83%)** — gate PASS (target 80%). Tests: 498 → 508 files (+11 new, −1 monolith). The one REGRESSION-GAP it found (browser-manager `close()` SIGKILL branch untested) was closed in this PR with four unit tests on an injectable race window. Remaining gaps are tracked in TODOS.md follow-ups (evals.yml matrix census tripwire, buildPaidShardArgs pin, `main()` full-suite path self-exercise).

## Pre-Landing Review

5 reviewers (checklist pass + testing/maintainability/security/performance specialists) + red team + Claude adversarial + Codex adversarial: **26 findings, all triaged; every confirmed critical fixed in-branch.** Highlights: 3 testing criticals (phantom TREE_MUTATING key, vacuous destructive-actions guard, classifier line-shear), red team's fork-concurrency cancel vector + evaporating CI failure logs, Codex adversarial's 3 P1s (cancellation didn't stop paid runs — repro'd; `admin:` + lowercase-password URL passing the redact HIGH gate — verified; DSN corruption on reserved password chars). One deliberate rejection: preflight stays fail-open on generic non-zero exits (pinned by test — a flaky preflight must not block a runnable suite); it now fail-fasts on spawn error/timeout/127. Codex structured review timed out at 540s (exit 124) — that pass contributed NO findings and is missing coverage, not a clean bill; the completed passes above cover the diff.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped (the only `browse/src` change is process-lifecycle code in `browser-manager.ts`; diff-scope's frontend flag was a false positive from workflow/test files).

## Eval Results

- **Partial-diff rehearsal (live, $0.67):** scratch edit to `qa/SKILL.md.tmpl` → selection banner `selected 17 of 177 tests -> running 4 of 45 shards, reason: diff`; 41 shards reported `skipped-by-diff`; /qa E2E passed (quick $0.54 + bootstrap $0.13).
- **Judge A/B (drove a decision):** Haiku scored 2/2/2 vs Sonnet's 4/3/4 on the identical health-rubric prompt → judge default reverted to Sonnet per D1a's pin-on-regressors clause; `GSTACK_EVAL_MODEL_JUDGE` override added. Receipts in `test/helpers/llm-judge.ts`.
- **Full gate matrix runs on THIS PR** (the touchfiles change forces full selection) — that is the planned forced-full validation for the remaining model change (capture → Sonnet). A periodic re-baseline (`eval:bg:periodic`) is scheduled post-merge; regressors get Opus pins per D1a.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: **CLEAN.** All 84 files trace to plan items; the two `lib/` collaterals are item 7's bash→TS port and the redaction calibration that port triggered on push, both test-pinned.

## Plan Completion

**46 plan items — 37 done, 5 changed, 4 deferred (3 of 4 were declared stretch).** Changed: parallelism shipped as N shard processes after a `--parallel` probe hit three Bun 1.3.13 worker pathologies (receipts in the runner header); detach timeouts are static-above-floor with the census-derived floor enforced by test; judge default reverted per D1a's own regressor clause; final full-gate + CI validation routed to this PR's checks (V6/V7). Deferred → TODOS.md: gbrain-detect DI refactor, git-fixture helper (stretch), dynamic fromJSON select matrix (stretch), fail-fast dead shards (stretch).

## Verification Results

Plan verification V1-V5 complete (post-merge re-measure, failing canary, timing ×2, $0 selection checks, live partial-diff rehearsal). V6/V7 run on this PR's CI: the required free-tests lane's first Linux run + the full gate eval matrix + the cache-trio second-push tag hit. /qa-only auto-verification skipped — no dev server (CLI project).

## TODOS

- Completed: "P1: Free suite exit code is untrustworthy" → moved to Completed at v1.66.0.0.
- Filed: 12 review-army follow-ups (LPT shard balancing, EVALS_SELECTION_JSON propagation, evals.yml matrix census tripwire, dep-list self-registration sweep, paid-runner log spooling, image freshness tripwire, detach-floor runtime self-check, eval-store model recording, SECURITY_BENCH periodic lane, shared child-lifecycle helper, gbrain-detect DI, coverage-audit assertion tightening).

## Documentation

**Doc sync commit:** 9b9bc84b — docs: sync docs for v1.66.0.0 (test/evals/CI speedup)

- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: all suite-level `bun test` references → `bun run test`; Tier 1 timing corrected to ~90-100s for the full ~7,000-test suite; strict shard runner documented (`--verbose`, `--wall-timeout`); sharded paid-runner paragraph documents diff-based shard skipping and the `EVALS_JOBS` vs `EVALS_CONCURRENCY` split; `GSTACK_EVAL_MODEL_JUDGE` documented.
- **AGENTS.md**: build-commands block updated to `bun run test` (strict shard runner, ~90-100s).
- **ARCHITECTURE.md**: two "Tier 1 runs on every `bun test`" sentences updated to `bun run test`.
- **CHANGELOG.md / CLAUDE.md / TODOS.md / VERSION**: updated on this branch; verified consistent (v1.66.0.0 across CHANGELOG, VERSION, package.json).

### Documentation Debt

- The doc audit's one CONFIRMED code-vs-CHANGELOG gap (free-tests.yml missing the PR-number concurrency + artifact step that its commit message claimed) was fixed in-branch (`b831f9b2`) — the workspace-revert incident during the ship caught that file between edits.
- Advisory: pre-existing cost-claim tension (CLAUDE.md's ~$4/run vs the pre-selection ~$38 full-suite figure) needs one measured number; `GSTACK_EVAL_MODEL_<KIND>` overrides and `--shards N --shard i` CI mode have no how-to coverage (`/document-generate` can fill these).

## CI validation record (post-open triage, all resolved)

Opening this PR was the forced-full validation moment, and it delivered. Ten CI rounds, every failure root-caused and fixed in-branch:

- **Cache trio first-run**: the default buildx `docker` driver can't export registry cache — `setup-buildx-action` added at all three build sites; the tag-hit fast path verified on the following round.
- **First Linux run of the free suite (7 failure classes)**: two real product bugs (`isOurXvfb` substring-matched the whole cmdline, so the test runner itself was identified as our Xvfb — the sibling-kill class the identity check exists to prevent; the failure reporter misattributed under GHA `::group::` wrappers and bun's headerless recap, inventing a phantom failing file) plus five environment classes (no DISPLAY → `xvfb-run`; missing bun on a deterministic PATH; a claude-binary assumption on the secretless lane; make-pdf gates hard-requiring off-platform; missing xterm vendoring).
- **A never-run suite exposed**: `security-sidepanel-dom` had never executed anywhere (no local chromium, no Linux CI) and rotted through three contract changes, ending with the v1.14 sidebar rewrite that removed the UI it asserts on — deleted with receipts.
- **Eval flake pair**: `pty-plan-smoke` (rotating members) and `e2e-workflow` (document-release) failed attempt 2 across rounds while passing on three-attempt branches — per-row `retries: 2` override for exactly those two rows; every other row keeps `--retry 1`.
- **Expanded Windows lane (13 → ~230 files)**: reached its green fixed point over four curation rounds (a shard-truncating wedge had been hiding successive strata); every exclusion carries a receipted reason, the census pin keeps the list honest, and the lane now uploads shard logs on failure.

## Known risks / watch on this PR

- **Retry 1** raises visible flake rate by design — flakes become fix-work.
- Judge/capture model defaults changed; eval:compare across this boundary conflates model swap with skill drift until the periodic re-baseline lands (TODOS: record effective models in the eval store).

## Test plan

- [x] Full free suite green on final HEAD via `bun run test` (strict runner, exit 0; ~3.5 min under load, ~90-100s dedicated)
- [x] All review-fix test files green (262 tests across the 12 affected files)
- [x] Live partial-diff rehearsal: 4/45 shards, 41 skipped-by-diff, /qa E2E passed ($0.67)
- [x] This PR's CI: **all 29 checks green** — required free-tests lane green 4 consecutive rounds, full gate eval matrix green 2 consecutive full rounds, cache-trio tag hit verified, expanded Windows lane green

Updates `actions/download-artifact` from 4 to 8
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

title: gstack
`gstack-version-bump repair` writes a fabricated `0.0.0.0` into package.json when it cannot find VERSION — and the package.json path cannot be configured to avoid it
body:
Two related defects in `bin/gstack-version-bump`, verified against `origin/HEAD` (v1.66.0.0, 410b4928); first hit on 1.62.0.0.

Related but distinct: #2462 is the same `readVersionFile`-swallows-a-miss root cause applied to the **base** version. This one is about the **current** version, and unlike #2462 it ends in a **write**. #2567 touches the same two functions but is about `package-lock.json` staleness.

Layout throughout: `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root, `package.json` in `app/`.

## 1. `repair` writes a version it invented

`readVersionFile` folds "file missing" into `DEFAULT` (`0.0.0.0`):

```ts
// line 67
function readVersionFile(p: string): string {
  try { const v = readFileSync(p, "utf-8").replace(/[\r\n\s]/g, ""); return v || DEFAULT; }
  catch { return DEFAULT; }
}
```

`cmdRepair` then propagates that value into `package.json` without ever establishing that the file it read from exists:

```
package.json BEFORE: 0.1.0.0
root VERSION is:     0.2.0.0

$ cd app && bun run gstack-version-bump repair
{"repaired":"0.0.0.0"}          # exit 0

package.json AFTER:  0.0.0.0
```

`package.json` is now **below where it started**, at a version present nowhere in the repo, and the command reported success. The guard at line 184 does not fire because `0.0.0.0` is a structurally valid 4-digit version — it is well-formed and wrong, which is exactly what a shape check cannot see.

This is reached through the documented happy path, not a misuse: `classify` returns `DRIFT_STALE_PKG`, and the Step 12 dispatch table says `DRIFT_STALE_PKG` → run `repair`.

```
$ cd app && bun run gstack-version-bump classify --base main
{"state":"DRIFT_STALE_PKG","baseVersion":"0.1.0.0","currentVersion":"0.0.0.0","pkgVersion":"0.1.0.0","pkgExists":true}
```

`currentVersion: 0.0.0.0` is already fabricated at this point — the real root `VERSION` says `0.2.0.0`.

## 2. The package.json path cannot be configured, which is what forces you into that cwd

`VERSION` resolves three ways — `--version-path`, a `.gstack/version-path` pin, then a default (line 56). `package.json` resolves exactly one way, in both readers and writers:

```ts
// line 78 (readPkgVersion) and line 97 (writePkgVersion)
const pkgPath = join(cwd, "package.json");
```

So when the two files are not siblings there is no cwd that satisfies both, and each choice breaks a different half:

**From the repo root** — `VERSION` resolves, `package.json` does not, and `cmdWrite` treats absent as nothing-to-do:

```ts
// line 164
if (existsSync(join(cwd, "package.json"))) { writePkgVersion(cwd, version!); }
// exits 0 either way
```

```
$ bun run gstack-version-bump write --version 0.2.0.0
{"wrote":"0.2.0.0","packageJson":false}      # exit 0
$ cat app/package.json                        # still 0.1.0.0 — drifted, silently
```

`pkgExists: false` on every run also means both drift branches in `classifyState` (lines 125, 129) are unreachable, so the tool's hand-edit detection is dead for the whole repo — it cannot catch a genuine hand-edit either.

**From `app/`** — `package.json` resolves, `VERSION` does not, and you are in the corruption above.

## Repro

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/r/app && cd /tmp/r && git init -q && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init
printf '0.1.0.0\n' > VERSION
printf '{"name":"x","private":true,"version":"0.1.0.0"}\n' > app/package.json
git add -A && git commit -qm v && git branch -M main
git remote add origin . && git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD

bun run <gstack>/bin/gstack-version-bump write --version 0.2.0.0
# {"wrote":"0.2.0.0","packageJson":false}  exit 0, package.json untouched

cd app && bun run <gstack>/bin/gstack-version-bump classify --base main
# currentVersion 0.0.0.0  (root VERSION actually says 0.2.0.0) -> DRIFT_STALE_PKG

bun run <gstack>/bin/gstack-version-bump repair
# {"repaired":"0.0.0.0"} -> package.json regressed to 0.0.0.0
```

## Suggested fix

1. **Distinguish "file missing" from "file empty" in `readVersionFile`.** A `VERSION` the tool cannot find should stop `repair`, not become `0.0.0.0` and get written to disk. This is the one that turns a wrong reading into a wrong write, and it also underpins #2462.
2. **`--pkg-path` flag plus a `.gstack/pkg-path` pin**, mirroring `resolveVersionPath()`.
3. **In `cmdWrite`, separate *absent by configuration* from *absent unexpectedly*.** If a pkg path was configured and the file is missing, error; the unconditional `exit 0` is why the drift is silent.

Happy to send a PR if that shape sounds right.

## Workaround, for whoever lands here first

Run the version step with `cwd` set to the directory holding `package.json`, plus a `.gstack/version-path` there pointing back at the root `VERSION` (`../VERSION`). Both halves then resolve:

```
{"state":"ALREADY_BUMPED","baseVersion":"0.0.0.0","currentVersion":"0.9.0.0","pkgVersion":"0.9.0.0","pkgExists":true}
```

Two caveats. `.gstack/` is commonly gitignored, so unless you carve out that one file the fix works on one clone and silently nowhere else — the same failure shape as the bug. And it depends on always invoking from the right cwd, so it is worth pairing with a CI check asserting the two files agree; that catches drift regardless of cause, including a hand-edit.

## Environment

- gstack `1.66.0.0` (`origin/HEAD`, 410b4928); first hit on `1.62.0.0`
- Windows 11, git-bash, bun
- `VERSION` + `CHANGELOG.md` at repo root, `package.json` in `app/`

Diff-selected paid evals ran (89 E2E + 4 LLM-judge selected): all real executions passed, including ship/land/review/plan gate E2E and the ship + land workflow judges. No item silently dropped.

Rotating single-test failures in earlier runs were triaged with receipts: every one passed standalone, none in a branch-touched file, one class proven base-inherited on a clean v1.65 control worktree. Naming/style gates green; `git grep` for the excluded reference terms: clean.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR. Five new follow-ups added (eval-run evidence records, spawn outcome ledger, merge-SHA custody, default-if-silent escalations, staleness-grading E2E eval).

title: v1.67.1.0 fix: external-contributor security sweep — 6 findings hardened, regression-pinned
body:
## Summary

This PR is the outcome of an explicit security sweep of all external-contributor code merged in the last two months (the 7 directly-merged `time-attack` PRs, the v1.63/v1.65 fork-port squash waves, and the ~50 absorbed community PRs — ~38K lines across ~500 files, audited by 72 read-only agents with two adversarial verifiers per finding, plus a 4-specialist pre-landing review).

**Sweep verdict: no backdoor, no exfiltration path, no live secret leak.** The external contributions are net security-strengthening. This PR hardens the six real findings the sweep confirmed and pins each behind a regression guard. Supply-chain inputs (`basic-ftp@5.3.1`, `diff@9.0.0`) were verified against the live npm registry (integrity hashes match, advisories real).

**Security fixes**
- `fix(redact)`: the pre-push HIGH gate blocks real all-caps URL passwords again (v1.66 had widened the placeholder skip to any all-caps shape); the `USER:PASSWORD` doc convention still suppresses. Anchored exact-match set, never substring.
- `fix(browse)` config: the browse state dir writes a self-contained `.gitignore` (`*`) unconditionally at creation, so persisted session cookies (`session-state.json`) and token-bearing logs can never be git-committed, regardless of the project's `.gitignore`.
- `fix(ios-qa)`: the private-API touch bridge (`_touchesEvent`, `IOHIDEventCreateDigitizer*`, `_AXSSetAutomationEnabled`) compiles out of Release builds — `#if TARGET_OS_IOS && DEBUG` plus the missing `cSettings` DEBUG define. Lands the safety half of closed PR #2269.
- `fix(ship)`: the App Store Connect upload key is scoped to the app being released (`allAppsVisible:false` + explicit `apps` relationship) instead of all apps on the team, and the exit report discloses the key + revocation path.
- `harden(browse)`: constant-time bearer-token comparison in `validateAuth`.

**Reliability restore**
- `fix(browse)` polyfill: re-lands the v1.64 `Bun.spawn` contract (`exited` promise, eager drain, 16MB per-stream cap) that the v1.65 fork-port squash silently reverted, plus its five deleted pinning tests. Live callers `await proc.exited` on the Windows Node fallback and were silently getting `undefined`.

**Docs**
- `docs(egress)`: `gstack-egress verify` documents that ledger tail-truncation/deletion are out of scope (forensic observability, not an exfiltration control).

**Regression guards (from the pre-landing review)**
- `test:` static tripwire for the constant-time `validateAuth` (a revert to `===` keeps accept/reject green while restoring the timing side-channel); table-driven suppression test over the exported placeholder set; unconditional-write proof for the state-dir ignore; POSIX signal-exit (128+n) coverage for the polyfill.

Governance findings from the sweep (zero-review collaborator merges, ruleset gaps, dormant push collaborators) are settings-level and tracked separately with a runbook — not code in this PR.

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (subagent): **96%**, 1 minor gap (closed by the signal-exit test added in the final test commit).

```
C1 redact urlPasswordIsPlaceholder      [***] both directions + substring-cant-rescue + full-set table
C2 bun-polyfill exited/drain/cap        [***] 7 tests incl. spawn-failure, 1MB drain, cap, signal 128+n
C5 config self-contained .gitignore     [***] happy path + no-nesting + git-already-ignores placement proof
C4 validateAuth constant-time           [** ] static tripwire (timingSafeEqual + length gate + null guard)
C6 ios Release compile-out              [** ] static tripwire both halves; nm/strings proof = device tier
DOCS egress/apple                        --  prose, no code path
```

Tests: 4 test files extended + 1 new tripwire file (+13 tests net). No regressions: every pre-existing pinned behavior (placeholder suppression, project-.gitignore fallback, auth accept/reject) still asserted.

## Pre-Landing Review

4 specialists + adversarial challenge (Codex unavailable — required MCP unreachable; Claude subagents used):
- **Security: NO FINDINGS** (verified: exact-match set cannot leak on substring; the config write is into an owner-only 0700 dir with fixed content; the cap handles negative/NaN; the length short-circuit cannot throw).
- **Performance: NO FINDINGS** (drain is O(1) amortized + capped; the redact change is a strict speedup).
- **Maintainability: 2 informational, both accepted** (dead `truncated` field is inherited verbatim from the restored v1.64 block — fidelity over cleanup; placeholder-vocabulary overlap is documented intent).
- **Testing: 4 gaps — all fixed** in the `test:` commit above.
- **Adversarial: NO ADDITIONAL ISSUES** (probed false-positive regressions, embedder import side-effects, listener leaks/double-resolve, the SPM target graph in Release, header shapes, golden-fixture drift — all hold).

## Design Review

No UI-facing changes (the frontend scope flag triggers on `browse/` paths; the changes are server/CLI/template) — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

Free suite: green for the branch across 3 full runs (~7,100 tests each). Each run had exactly one failure on merged non-branch code (a different test each time), every one passing standalone twice — the known parallel-load flake class.

Paid E2E (diff-selected, full run under 25-way concurrency): **58 pass, 322 skipped (not selected), 1 fail** — `review-dashboard-via` timed out with 0 turns / 0 tokens / $0.00 (the `claude -p` child never started; FAIL-to-FAIL vs the prior baseline). Re-run isolated for a clean receipt: **PASS** (4 turns, 148s, $0.25). The failure was API starvation under concurrency, not a code regression.

## Plan Completion

All 6 approved remediation items (D1-D6 from the eng-reviewed fix plan) delivered, plus 1 of 2 optional Tier C hardening items (constant-time compare; the hermetic-env per-provider allowlist was assessed and deliberately deferred — it refactors the harness that gates all E2E, failing the "low-risk only" bar).

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR (the fixes came from the fresh security sweep, not the backlog).

## Documentation

Post-ship doc sync for v1.67.1.0 (`/document-release`, commits `bae7dd6f` + `be15895b`):

- **ARCHITECTURE.md** — egress receipt ledger section now states `gstack-egress verify`'s scope (detects in-place edits, reordering, and mid-chain deletion; tail-truncation and deletion of the ledger itself are out of scope for a forensic log), mirroring the disclosure shipped in `bin/gstack-egress`.
- **README.md** — `gstack-egress` tools-table row carries the same verify scope clause.
- **docs/howto-ios-testing-with-gstack.md** — Release-build guard section documents the second layer this branch added: `DebugBridgeTouch.m` compiles out behind `#if TARGET_OS_IOS && DEBUG` (DEBUG defined only in the debug configuration via `cSettings`), emitting an empty translation unit in Release. Also fixed "three Swift targets" → "three SwiftPM targets" (DebugBridgeTouch is Objective-C).
- **CHANGELOG.md** — v1.67.1.0 entry preserved as written; VERSION matches.

### Documentation Debt

- Pre-existing, verified by cross-model review: docs claim a `.when(configuration: .debug)` dependency condition makes SwiftPM refuse to link `DebugBridge*` in Release (docs/howto-ios-testing-with-gstack.md:81, ios-qa/SKILL.md.tmpl:133/244, ios-qa/templates/Package.swift.template:15-17). No template or fixture implements a conditional dependency — only DEBUG build-setting defines. The real guards are the `#if DEBUG` compile-out plus the CI `nm -j` invariant. Needs a coordinated template + SKILL.md.tmpl + regen fix.
- `GSTACK_SPAWN_MAX_BUFFER` (per-stream byte cap, default 16MB) has reference coverage only in CHANGELOG/source — no user doc.
- The apple-release exit disclosure's "delete `~/.gstack/apple/api-key.json` locally" is local cleanup, not server-side revocation; the app-scoped key can later be re-associated to another app by design.

## Test plan
- [x] Free suite green for the branch (3 full runs, ~7,100 tests; flakes on non-branch code proven standalone-green)
- [x] Paid E2E: 58 pass + the 1 timeout re-run isolated to a clean PASS
- [x] All 4 pre-landing specialist reviews + adversarial challenge clean

title: fix(redact-prepush): scan the pushed range, not the whole repo, on a new ref
body:
## The bug

Pushing a **new branch** can fail with `HIGH engine.input_too_large`, reported under the heading "credential(s) in the pushed diff". The only documented way past it is `GSTACK_REDACT_PREPUSH=skip`.

On a new ref there is no remote SHA to diff against, so the hook approximated the branch point as `merge-base(local, origin/HEAD)`. In a repo whose default branch has drifted from the branch it actually ships from, that base sits hundreds of commits below the real branch point.

Measured in a repo that ships from a long-lived release branch while `origin/main` sits 200 commits behind it:

```
commits in the approximated range = 201        (real range: 1)
added-line bytes handed to scan() = 3,652,518
engine cap                        = 1,048,576   -> 3.48x over
```

The push itself was **2,141 bytes**. Input size tracked the repo, not the diff.

## Why this is worse than a false alarm

A new ref that **genuinely contained a credential** produced the same size error, so the credential was never scanned at all.

The chain is: a capacity bug manufactures a bogus "credential in the pushed diff" finding, the only escape is the documented skip flag, and the resulting habit of skipping then lets a real secret through. The operator believes a guard ran when none did. A guard that fails closed and hands out a bypass in the same breath ends up weaker than one that fails open.

## The fix

Three changes. None of them reduces detection.

**1. Correct base — `pushedRangeBase()`.** Replaces the merge-base guess with `git rev-list --boundary <local> --not --remotes=<remote>`, which asks git directly which commits this push adds to *this* remote. Falls back to octopus merge-base, then the old merge-base, then the empty tree; every fallback scans **more**, never less. The remote name comes from `process.argv[2]`, which git already passes and the managed wrapper already forwards.

This is a sizing fix rather than a detection reduction: the bytes it stops scanning are bytes the remote **already holds and this push does not send**, which is exactly what the existing-ref path (`remote..local`) has always excluded. Everything the push introduces is still scanned byte for byte.

**2. Chunked scanning.** The engine's 1 MiB fail-closed cap is untouched, so any other caller still fails closed. The hook slices added lines into 512 KiB chunks with 16 KiB overlap and scans **every** chunk, deduping findings by global line and column. A single added line larger than a chunk (minified bundle, base64 blob) is split into overlapping windows rather than skipped. No threshold was raised, no file is skipped, no severity downgraded. A 3.4 MiB scan takes 0.44 s.

**3. Honest messaging.** Size is no longer printed under "rotate the credential". If a region genuinely cannot be scanned, a separate `UNSCANNED` block names the byte count and line offset, says plainly that nothing was found because nothing was read, and **still exits 1**.

## Verification

All cases run by invoking the hook with synthetic stdin. No push was made and no remote branch was created or deleted during testing.

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| new ref, all-zeros remote SHA | **exit 1** `engine.input_too_large` | **exit 0**, clean |
| existing ref, small diff | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| new ref **containing** fabricated credentials | **exit 1** `engine.input_too_large`, secret never scanned | **exit 1**, names `db.url_with_password` and `aws.access_key` |

The third row is the one that matters: it is the proof the fix did not gut the guard.

Supporting cases, same method: a 3.4 MiB clean push (was blocked, now passes); a credential 3.2 MiB deep, past the old cap (was invisible, now named); one 1.6 MiB single added line (found via windowing).

Test secrets are fabricated and point at `example.invalid`. No real credential was read or written.

**Suite: 185 pass, 0 fail across the 8 redact test files** (up from 176). 5 of the 9 new tests fail against the pre-fix binary, so they genuinely pin the behaviour.

## Known limits, documented in the source

- The 64 MiB `maxBuffer` on the diff call is a second, much rarer ceiling that still ends in block-plus-bypass. Post-fix it needs a >64 MiB single push. Fixing it properly means streaming the diff through a temp file; left alone to keep this change narrow.
- The new-ref base trusts `refs/remotes/<remote>/*`. After a force-push or branch deletion since the last fetch, it may believe the remote holds a commit it no longer does. Not a regression — the old merge-base path read the same stale refs more coarsely.
- Pushing commits the remote already holds under a **new branch name** is now deliberately not re-scanned. That matches this hook's documented scope as a pushed-diff scanner rather than a history scanner, but it is a conscious narrowing rather than an accident.

title: fix(plan-tune): reject never-ask on one-way ids at --write
body: ## Why (in your own words) I set `never-ask` on `plan-eng-review-arch-finding` and `--stats` said it worked. The next `--check` still asked, with a note that one-way doors ignore that pref. So the file lied: it stored a preference that can never fire. `--write` is what I want to stop. If the id is one-way, refuse `never-ask` and `ask-only-for-one-way` (exit 1, name the door type, don't touch the file). `--stats` should say `INERT_ONE_WAY` for leftovers already on disk, not `NEVER_ASK: 1`. `always-ask` on a one-way id is fine — that matches what `--check` already does. **Fixes #2488.** Related: #2489 (closed — registry path made this easier to hit), #2490 (product split, out of scope), #2390 / #2429 (same `--write` function, unknown-source exit 2, already on tip). ### Why this shape Issue author asked for reject-at-write plus honest `--stats` for prefs written before the fix. Storing the value and labeling it INERT is the weaker pair — not done. CONTRIBUTING's wave rule: if two PRs fix the same thing, keep the smaller one. This is 2 files, on current `main`. Fine to absorb into a wave. ### What it does - `--write never-ask` / `ask-only-for-one-way` on a one-way id exits 1, names `door_type: one-way`, does not write, does not append an event. - `--write always-ask` on a one-way id still succeeds. - Origin gate still runs first: a poisoning source on a one-way id exits 2, not 1. - `--stats` counts leftover one-way suppressing prefs as `INERT_ONE_WAY`. Working `NEVER_ASK` is only prefs that `--check` would actually `AUTO_DECIDE`. - `--check` tests that still need a planted one-way pref write the file directly, because `--write` now refuses them. ### What it deliberately does not do - Split `plan-eng-review-arch-finding` (#2490) - Change `ask-only-for-one-way` alias semantics - Reject `--write` on `*-split-*` ids (that carve-out stays `--check`-only) - Keyword-net `--write` (no summary on the write path) - Hooks, registry, skill templates, `VERSION` / `CHANGELOG` / README - A migration (schema unchanged; `--stats` is honesty for old files) - `/ship` (wave stamps version) AI was used for assistance. ## Live evidence Same isolated `GSTACK_HOME`, same payload, `cwd` = repo: ``` {"question_id":"plan-eng-review-arch-finding","preference":"never-ask","source":"plan-tune"} ``` **Before** (`upstream/main` binary): ``` $ bin/gstack-question-preference --write '{"question_id":"plan-eng-review-arch-finding","preference":"never-ask","source":"plan-tune"}' OK: plan-eng-review-arch-finding → never-ask (source: plan-tune) $ bin/gstack-question-preference --read { "plan-eng-review-arch-finding": "never-ask" } $ bin/gstack-question-preference --stats TOTAL: 1 ALWAYS_ASK: 0 NEVER_ASK: 1 ASK_ONLY_ONE_WAY: 0 $ bin/gstack-question-preference --check plan-eng-review-arch-finding ASK_NORMALLY NOTE: one-way door overrides your never-ask preference for safety. ``` **After** (this branch): ``` $ bin/gstack-question-preference --write '{"question_id":"plan-eng-review-arch-finding","preference":"never-ask","source":"plan-tune"}' gstack-question-preference: cannot set never-ask on one-way question "plan-eng-review-arch-finding" (door_type: one-way) $ bin/gstack-question-preference --read {} $ bin/gstack-question-preference --stats TOTAL: 0 ALWAYS_ASK: 0 NEVER_ASK: 0 ASK_ONLY_ONE_WAY: 0 INERT_ONE_WAY: 0 ``` Planted leftover file (a pref written before this reject existed): ``` $ bin/gstack-question-preference --stats TOTAL: 1 ALWAYS_ASK: 0 NEVER_ASK: 0 ASK_ONLY_ONE_WAY: 0 INERT_ONE_WAY: 1 $ bin/gstack-question-preference --check plan-eng-review-arch-finding ASK_NORMALLY NOTE: one-way door overrides your never-ask preference for safety. ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** `bin/gstack-question-preference`, `test/gstack-question-preference.test.ts` - **Verified live by:** the transcripts above, plus `bun test test/gstack-question-preference.test.ts` (52 pass) - **Did NOT test:** Tier 2/3 evals. title: fix(redact): a typo'd subcommand no longer exits 0 having done nothing
body:
## The bug

`main()` in `bin/gstack-redact` recognises exactly two subcommands and lets everything else fall through to the stdin scan. On empty stdin that prints `(no findings)` and exits 0:

```console
$ gstack-redact install-prepush-hooks    # plural typo
gstack-redact scan — repo UNKNOWN
  (no findings)
  HIGH=0 MEDIUM=0 LOW=0 WARN=0
$ echo $?
0
$ ls .git/hooks/pre-push
ls: .git/hooks/pre-push: No such file or directory
```

No hook was installed, and the operator has every reason to believe the credential guard is armed. A guard that silently no-ops must never exit 0 — this is the failure mode the guard itself exists to prevent, in the tool that installs it.

## Two smaller faults in the same dispatch

Both of them lead people into the first one.

**No `--help` handler.** `gstack-redact --help` fell through to the scanner, so piping a credential to it scanned the secret and exited 3 rather than printing help.

**No TTY guard.** With nothing piped in and no `--from-file`, `readInput()` blocks on `readSync(fd 0)` waiting for an EOF an interactive terminal never sends. It prints nothing at all, so it reads as a hang rather than as "this is a filter, feed it something". That is how I arrived here: I ran `gstack-redact scan`, watched it sit for three minutes, and assumed the scanner was wedged.

## What changed

- `--help` / `-h` / `help` → usage, exit 0
- unrecognised positional → names the offender on stderr, exit 1
- stdin is a TTY and no `--from-file` → usage instead of blocking
- `scan` stays accepted, because the human output header reads `gstack-redact scan — repo …` and that is what people type. Rejecting it would break that muscle memory for no gain.

Usage errors exit **1**, deliberately not 2 or 3. Those mean MEDIUM and HIGH findings and callers gate dispatch on them (per the exit-code table at the top of the file), so a usage error exiting 2 would be read as "medium findings — prompt the user". There is a test pinning that.

`install-prepush-hook` and `uninstall-prepush-hook` are unchanged, as is the piped filter path.

## Tests

Four tests written failing first, in `test/gstack-redact-cli.test.ts`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| typo'd subcommand | exit 0, "no findings" | exit 1, `unknown subcommand` |
| unknown positional | clean scan report | no scan, exit 1 |
| `--help` with a credential piped in | scanned it, exit 3 | usage, exit 0 |
| `scan` alias, `--json`, flags | pass | pass (unchanged) |

The TTY guard is not unit-tested — spawned stdin is a Buffer, never a TTY. Verified manually under a pty:

```console
$ script -q /dev/null bun bin/gstack-redact
gstack-redact — scan text for secrets/PII/legal content.
...
```

Suites: `test/gstack-redact-cli.test.ts` 15 pass / 0 fail; the nine redact-related files 133 pass / 0 fail; full `bun run test` **7,722 pass / 0 fail** across 7/7 shards.

## Note on the diff's own scan

`git show <branch> | gstack-redact --repo-visibility public` reports 2 HIGH. Both are `AKIA1234567890ABCDEF`, the fixture this test file already ships at lines 31, 40 and 62 — the added test follows the existing convention rather than introducing a new secret.

title: Fix: gstack-config get returns "" with exit 0 for keys that have no default
body:
## Why (in your own words)

Four config keys that skill preambles read every run — `question_tuning`,
`team_mode`, `transcript_ingest_mode`, `repo_mode` — are missing from
`lookup_default`'s table, so they hit the `*) echo "" ;;` catch-all and come
back as an empty string with **exit 0**.

That exit code is the whole bug. Every preamble reads config with the same
pattern:

```bash
_QUESTION_TUNING=$(gstack-config get question_tuning 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
```

`|| echo` only fires on a **non-zero** exit. A catch-all that prints `""` and
exits 0 means the fallback never runs and the variable is left empty — so the
written default is unreachable, and the skill branches on `""` instead of on
`false`/`off`/`unknown`. Nothing errors; the setting simply reads as blank
forever. I hit this on `question_tuning`, where a documented default of `false`
never reached the skill that gates on it.

Two changes, and they are deliberately separate:

1. Add the four missing keys to the table, using the values the callers already
   assume in their own `|| echo "<default>"` fallback — so behaviour is
   unchanged for anyone whose fallback happened to work.
2. Make the **unknown-key** path `return 1` instead of printing `""` with exit
   0, so the caller's fallback can fire at all.

Change 2 is scoped strictly to the unknown-key catch-all. The keys whose default
is *intentionally* empty (`cross_project_learnings`, `salience_allowlist`,
`user_slug_at_*`, `redact_repo_visibility`) keep exit 0, because `""` is their
real answer and their callers depend on it — `cross_project_learnings` uses
empty-vs-set to trigger the first-time prompt, and flipping it would re-prompt
every existing user.

## Live evidence

Reproduced against `origin/main` at v1.67.0.0 (`ae8914a`), unmodified, then
against this branch. `gstack-config-before` below is literally
`git show origin/main:bin/gstack-config`.

```
########## BEFORE (origin/main @ v1.67.0.0) ##########
  get question_tuning        -> '' (rc=0)   | pattern '|| echo FALLBACK' -> ''
  get team_mode              -> '' (rc=0)   | pattern '|| echo FALLBACK' -> ''
  get transcript_ingest_mode -> '' (rc=0)   | pattern '|| echo FALLBACK' -> ''
  get repo_mode              -> '' (rc=0)   | pattern '|| echo FALLBACK' -> ''

########## AFTER (this branch) ##########
  get question_tuning        -> 'false'   (rc=0)
  get team_mode              -> 'false'   (rc=0)
  get transcript_ingest_mode -> 'off'     (rc=0)
  get repo_mode              -> 'unknown' (rc=0)
```

Note the BEFORE line that matters most: the `|| echo FALLBACK` column is empty.
The caller's own documented fallback does not fire, which is why this is
invisible rather than noisy.

Non-regression, run with an isolated `GSTACK_HOME` so the user's own config
cannot mask the defaults:

```
########## intentionally-empty defaults -- must stay rc=0 ##########
  get cross_project_learnings -> '' (rc=0)
  get salience_allowlist      -> '' (rc=0)
  get redact_repo_visibility  -> '' (rc=0)

########## unknown key -- must be rc=1 so the fallback arms ##########
  get totally_unknown_key                      -> '' (rc=1)
  get totally_unknown_key || echo "FALLBACK"   -> 'FALLBACK'
```

Test suite added with the fix:

```
$ bun test test/gstack-config-defaults.test.ts
bun test v1.3.14 (0d9b296a)
 4 pass
 0 fail
 11 expect() calls
Ran 4 tests across 1 file. [2.63s]
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-config` (+23/-2) — four keys added to
  `lookup_default`, unknown-key catch-all returns 1, and `get` propagates that
  non-zero exit. New `test/gstack-config-defaults.test.ts` (+137).
- **Verified live by:** running the unmodified `origin/main` copy of
  `bin/gstack-config` side by side with the patched one (output above), on
  Windows 11 / git-bash, gstack at v1.67.0.0; plus the new test file, and the
  four-key behaviour through the real `|| echo` pattern the preambles use.
- **Did NOT test:** macOS and Linux — the change is pure POSIX shell with no
  platform-conditional code, but I only have a Windows/git-bash box. I also did
  not audit every caller of `gstack-config get` across all skills for one that
  might *rely* on an unknown key exiting 0; I checked the preamble pattern,
  which is the dominant caller, and the four keys above.

## Liveness proof (required)

✅ Attached in a follow-up comment on this PR: `GSTACK PR 2611` typed live into my
PowerShell prompt. Unedited, cropped only. Say the word if you want a wider frame
showing the typed command and the window chrome, and I will re-shoot it.

To be explicit about how this PR was produced, since the section exists to
establish exactly that: I am a human (Benjamin Bérès), this is my account, and I
directed the work. The investigation, the diff, and the evidence above were done
with Claude Code in my terminal — which is also how the bug surfaced, on my own
Windows box. Close this if the workflow does not meet your bar; I would rather say
how it was made than have you find out.

## Checklist

- [x] Liveness screenshot attached: `GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface (not edited onto the image)

title: Fix issues #2600, #2394, #2402, #2441
body:
## Summary

Four independent fixes for gstack:

### #2600 — `gstack-version-bump repair` writes fabricated `0.0.0.0`
When the VERSION file is missing or empty, `readVersionFile` folded it into `DEFAULT ("0.0.0.0")`, which passed the shape check and was written into package.json, regressing the version. 
- `cmdRepair` now fails with exit 2 when the VERSION file is missing OR unparsable

### #2394 — `--probe` counts didn't match actual ingest
`probeMode` counted all files in the window but `preparePages` applies an attribution filter (skips transcripts with no git remote). Probe now applies the same filter and reports `skipped_unattributed`.
- New `transcriptIsAttributable()` helper
- `ProbeReport` gains `skipped_unattributed`

### #2402 — learnings auto-capture rarely fired
The "Operational Self-Improvement" preamble block was conditional ("if you discovered..."), so models skipped it. Made it a direct instruction with an explicit negative acknowledgment ("say 'no learnings this run'").

Added untrusted-content warnings to `/scrape` (SKILL.md + tmpl) and `browser-skills/hackernews-frontpage`.

Closes #2600, #2394, #2402, #2441

title: session-update: lock records the parent $$ from a backgrounded subshell, so the stale-lock branch lets every concurrent session in
body:
### Summary

`bin/gstack-session-update` records its lock holder with `echo $$` from **inside** the backgrounded subshell. In bash, `$$` does not change in a subshell — it stays the parent shell's PID. The parent here is the hook script itself, which exits immediately by design, so the PID written to the lock belongs to a process that is gone milliseconds later. Every subsequent session then classifies the lock as stale, removes it, and re-acquires. The guard admits exactly the callers it exists to exclude.

### The code

```bash
(
  # ... entire update body runs here ...
  if ! mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
    if [ -f "$LOCK_DIR/pid" ]; then
      LOCK_PID=$(cat "$LOCK_DIR/pid" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
      if [ "$LOCK_PID" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && ! kill -0 "$LOCK_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
        rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null          # <- treated as stale, re-acquired
        mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || { log_entry "SKIP lock_contested"; exit 0; }
      else
        log_entry "SKIP locked_by=$LOCK_PID"; exit 0
      fi
    else
      log_entry "SKIP locked_no_pid"; exit 0
    fi
  fi
  echo $$ > "$LOCK_DIR/pid" 2>/dev/null          # bin/gstack-session-update:76
  trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
  # ... git pull --ff-only --autostash, then ./setup -q ...
) >/dev/null 2>&1 &

exit 0
```

The script's own header states the intent that makes the recorded PID short-lived:

> The entire update runs in background (forked). The hook itself exits immediately so session startup is never delayed.

### Reproduction

The bash behaviour on its own:

```
$ echo "parent $$"; ( echo "subshell $$"; echo "BASHPID $BASHPID" ) & wait
parent 167666
subshell 167666
BASHPID 167678
```

And on a live install, immediately after a real run, the PID recorded in `$LOCK_DIR/pid` is already dead:

```
$ kill -0 "$(cat "$STATE_DIR/.setup-lock/pid")" || echo "already dead"
already dead
```

### Observed consequence

Two Claude Code sessions starting close together both ran the update body concurrently. Neither logged the `SKIP locked_by=` that a holding lock produces, and both failed:

```
PULL_FAILED exit=128 reason=fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.
PULL_FAILED exit=128 reason=fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.
```

Two concurrent `git pull`s in one checkout race on `FETCH_HEAD`: git truncates it, then reopens it to append merge candidates, so a second fetch interleaving can leave more than one merge-marked line, and `--ff-only` aborts with exactly that message.

I want to be precise about how far this is proven. Repository configuration was ruled out as the cause: a single `git pull --ff-only --autostash` in the same tree exits 0, `branch.<name>.merge` is a single ref, `fetch.all` and extra merge targets are absent, and a second remote with a wildcard refspec is not consulted by an argument-less `git pull`. But the log alone, without a `FETCH_HEAD` snapshot and timing, does not prove those two hook processes were the only competitors — any other concurrent fetch in the same checkout would produce the same state. So: the lock defect is directly demonstrated; the `FETCH_HEAD` race is its expected consequence and the most likely explanation of these two lines, not a conclusively isolated one.

The practical effect either way is that auto-upgrade silently skips whenever sessions start together, and the install drifts behind until a session happens to start alone. It is silent because the subshell sends all stdio to `/dev/null` — deliberately, to avoid SIGPIPE once the hook exits — so the only trace is the analytics log.

### On the fix

`$BASHPID` is the semantically correct value (the subshell's own PID), but I do not think it is safe as a portable one-line patch: `BASHPID` was introduced in Bash 4.0, and the system bash on older macOS is 3.2, where it expands to nothing and the lock file would be written empty. That lands in the `SKIP locked_no_pid` branch rather than anything dangerous, but it would disable auto-upgrade outright on those hosts.

Two options that avoid that, whichever fits your intent:

- Re-invoke the script in an explicit worker mode (e.g. an internal flag) so the update body runs as its own process and its `$$` is genuinely its own PID. No version dependency.
- Use `$BASHPID` and declare Bash 4+ a requirement for this path, with a fallback that keeps the current behaviour rather than writing an empty PID file.

Observed on 1.67.0.0. Happy to send a PR for whichever shape you prefer.

On a macOS/ARM machine where gbrain is installed in `/opt/homebrew/bin` (the issue reporter's environment), the wireup test's "--strict + gbrain missing on PATH: exits 2" case saw the real gbrain through the fixture's leaked PATH and exited 0 instead of 2 — the test could not fail where the bug existed, so tier 1 gave contributors no signal on that machine class. title: fix(slug): a dot-prefixed project slug silently blocks memory-ingest forever
body: ## Why (in your own words) If you turn on artifacts sync, `~/.gstack` becomes a git repo. From that moment, running any `gstack-*` bin with a cwd inside it makes `gstack-slug` resolve `basename(PROJECT_ROOT)` to `.gstack`, and gstack creates a project directory literally named `~/.gstack/projects/.gstack/`. That name is legal today: the sanitizer filters to `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]`, which keeps a leading dot. But the slug is used as a **path component** — both for `~/.gstack/projects//` and, via `gstack-memory-ingest`, as a directory inside the staging tree handed to `gbrain import`. A leading dot makes that component a hidden directory, and markdown collectors skip hidden entries while walking. The pages are staged, never collected, and the accounting guard in `ingestPass` then refuses to advance state — permanently, on every subsequent run. The user-visible result is transcript ingest that errors on every skill start and never progresses. The error message points at `.gitignore`, which is a dead end. `.` and `..` survived the old filter too. As path components those resolve to the parent directory. ## Live evidence Reproduced on a fresh install (gstack v1.67.1.0, gbrain 0.46.15.0, local PGLite). **Before — every run, forever:** ``` $ bun run bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts --incremental --quiet [memory-ingest] ERR: gbrain import accounted for 1 of 3 staged page(s) (imported=0, unchanged=1). gbrain collected 1 file(s) from the staging dir. Refusing to advance state — the unaccounted pages would be marked ingested without landing in the brain. If the count is 0, check whether /Users/tim/.gstack/.staging-ingest-63033-... is inside a git repo that ignores it (gbrain import honours .gitignore). [memory-ingest] 0 written, 3 failed in 997ms ``` **Isolating it.** I patched `cleanupStagingDir` locally to keep the staging tree, then listed it. All 8 files exist with unique paths, so this is not a slug collision: ``` learnings/.gstack/2026-08-17-learnings.md <-- hidden dir learnings/tim/2026-08-17-learnings.md timelines/.gstack/2026-08-17-timeline.md <-- hidden dir timelines/tim/2026-08-17-timeline.md transcripts/claude-code/_unattributed/2026-08-17-1ba1a088-fa9.md transcripts/claude-code/_unattributed/2026-08-17-9301781b-fa0.md transcripts/claude-code/_unattributed/2026-08-17-95fc9439-339.md transcripts/claude-code/_unattributed/2026-08-17-ae9c0a35-c6e.md ``` Exactly 2 hidden-directory pages, exactly the 2 the guard reports missing. **Ruling out the message's own suggestion.** `.gitignore` is not the cause. A controlled `gbrain import` against an identical tree, once outside any git repo and once inside `~/.gstack` (whose `.gitignore` is `*`), collects everything both times: ``` $ gbrain import --no-embed --json Found 3 markdown files {"status":"success","imported":0,"skipped":3,"errors":0,"total_files":3} ``` **After — same machine, after removing the dot-named project dir:** ``` $ bun run bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts --bulk --quiet written: 6 failed: 0 $ bun run bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts --incremental --quiet (no output — nothing left to do) ``` **Regression tests fail without the fix.** 4 new tests in `test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts`: ``` $ git stash push bin/gstack-slug && bun test test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts 3 pass 4 fail <-- the new tests $ git stash pop && bun test test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts 7 pass 0 fail ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** `bin/gstack-slug` strips leading dots from the resolved slug before it is cached or emitted (root fix). `bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts` adds `safeSlugComponent()` and applies it in `repoSlug()` and to the `projects//` match in `buildArtifactPage()` (defense in depth, because components also arrive from git remotes and from directories created before this fix). `test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts` gains 4 regression tests. - **Verified live by:** reproducing the permanent-failure loop on a real install, isolating the two hidden-directory pages out of the staging tree, ruling out `.gitignore` with a controlled `gbrain import`, then confirming a clean `written: 6 / failed: 0` and a quiet incremental run afterwards. - **Did NOT test:** Windows path handling. Non-PGLite (Supabase) engines. Whether gbrain's collector should also be taught to descend into hidden directories when given an explicit root — that is a gbrain-side call and is deliberately not part of this PR. ### Pre-existing test failures (with receipts) `bun run test` reports 5 failures on this branch, all in `browse/test/` (`commands.test.ts`, `path-validation.test.ts`, `data-platform.test.ts`) around path-traversal validation. They are not from this change. Stashing all three changed files and running the same three files on clean `main` reproduces exactly the same 5: ``` $ git stash push bin/gstack-slug bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts test/gstack-slug-sanitize.test.ts $ bun test browse/test/commands.test.ts browse/test/path-validation.test.ts browse/test/data-platform.test.ts 283 pass 5 fail ``` Every other shard passes. ## Liveness proof (required) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached: `GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface (not edited onto the image) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) — N/A - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction is in "Live evidence" above; no existing issue found

title: Team mode's auto-update silently never runs if gstack is installed under a path with a space — no error, ever
body:
**Impact:** Team mode's entire value proposition is that everyone on a team stays on the same gstack version automatically. If gstack is installed under any path with a space in it, that auto-update hook silently never registers correctly — and nothing tells you. No error during `setup`, no error at session start, no error anywhere. You believe team mode is on and syncing; it isn't. Over time this produces exactly the failure mode team mode exists to prevent: team members silently drifting onto different gstack versions, each seeing different behavior, with no signal pointing at the cause.

This isn't a rare edge case — spaces in install paths are common in exactly the environments most likely to run gstack in team mode: Windows usernames (`C:\Users\Jane Doe\...`), OneDrive/iCloud-synced folders, and any org-mandated folder naming convention with a space in it.

**Root cause:** `setup` builds the hook command as an unescaped string and writes it straight into `~/.claude/settings.json` (`setup:1859-1863`, `bin/gstack-settings-hook:81-83`). The space breaks the command when Claude Code runs it, and the failure is swallowed.

**To reproduce:** install gstack under a path containing a space, run `./setup --team`, start a new session, and confirm the hook never actually runs.

**Fix:** escape the path before writing it into the hook command. `test/setup-windows-fallback.test.ts:59` currently asserts the unescaped form, which is why this was never caught.

title: ios-qa: drop the app name from the DebugBridge release-guard comment

title: fix(setup): quote the install path in the team-mode SessionStart hook command
body:
## Why (in your own words)

Team mode promises that everyone on a team stays on the same gstack version automatically. But if gstack is installed under a path with a space (Windows `C:\Users\Jane Doe\...`, OneDrive/iCloud folders), `setup --team` writes the SessionStart hook command unquoted into `~/.claude/settings.json`. The shell splits it at the space, the hook exits 127 every session, and nothing ever reports it — `setup` discards the registration's stderr and the hook runner's failure is invisible. The team believes auto-update is on; it silently never runs. This change quotes the path where the command is built, and makes re-running `./setup --team` heal an already-broken registration in place instead of dedupe-skipping it.

Fixes #2619.

## Live evidence

Before (main, `c86e647`) — build `HOOK_CMD` exactly as `setup:1862` does under an install at `.../space dir/gstack`, register via the real `gstack-settings-hook add`, execute the stored string the way the hook runner does:

```
$ bash -c "$STORED_CMD"
bash: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/space: No such file or directory
exit=127
```

After (this branch) — same install path, same flow:

```
$ bash -c "$STORED_CMD"
exit=0
$ cat hook.log
HOOK_RAN
```

Self-heal — seed a settings.json holding the old unquoted entry, re-run `gstack-settings-hook add` with the corrected command:
