title: gstack-evidence reports false test results in any repo with a .env.local: Bun auto-loads dotenv and Bun.spawn inherits it
body:
## Summary

`gstack-evidence run` reports **false test failures** in any repo that has a
`.env.local`. It is a Bun script, Bun auto-loads dotenv files from the cwd into
`process.env`, and `Bun.spawn` inherits that polluted environment into the
child test runner. The tool whose entire job is trustworthy verification
silently returns the wrong verdict.

## Mechanism

`bin/gstack-evidence:1` is `#!/usr/bin/env bun`. Bun's runtime loads `.env`,
`.env.local` and `.env.<NODE_ENV>` from the cwd into `process.env` before user
code runs. Then at `bin/gstack-evidence:192`:

```ts
proc = Bun.spawn(spawnArgv, { stdin: "inherit", stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
```

No `env` key is passed, so the child inherits `process.env` — already carrying
the repo's secrets and config. For the common single-token form the argv is
`["bash", "-c", cmd]` (`:170`), and it flows straight through to `npm` and the
test runner.

There is no env sanitisation anywhere in the file; the only `process.env` read
is `GSTACK_HOME` at `:95`.

## Observed

On a Next.js repo whose `.env.local` defines `PHOTO_RESERVATION_SECRET` and
`NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, two unrelated suites went red under the wrapper and
green everywhere else:

```
gstack-evidence run --label vitest -- 'npm run test:once'   ->  2 files RED
npm run test:once                                           ->  green
CI=true npm run test:once                                   ->  green
```

Both suites assert behaviour that only holds when those vars are **unset** (a
capability degrades to `null`; a URL falls back to `http://localhost`). The
injected production values flipped both. Nothing in the diff was wrong.

Two-line confirmation that the runtime, not the repo, is responsible:

```
$ bun  -e 'console.log(process.env.PHOTO_RESERVATION_SECRET, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL)'
<secret> https://app.example.com
$ node -e 'console.log(process.env.PHOTO_RESERVATION_SECRET, process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL)'
undefined undefined
```

## Why this one matters more than the usual env-leak bug

- It is **silent**. The run completes and records a verdict; it just records the
  wrong one. Both directions are possible — a false red as above, or a false
  green where an injected value masks a real failure.
- It affects **every repo with a `.env.local`**, which is most JS repos.
- It lands specifically on the evidence ledger, which exists to be believed.

`gstack-evidence` is the only script under `bin/` that runs user-supplied repo
commands, so it is the whole blast radius — the other `Bun.spawn` call sites in
`bin/` are fixed-argv tool invocations.

## Suggested fix

Subtract the keys Bun parsed from `.env*` in the cwd before spawning, and pass
an explicit `env` to `Bun.spawn`. That keeps the developer's real environment
(which the child legitimately needs) while removing exactly what the runtime
injected behind the user's back.

Worth noting `test/helpers/hermetic-env.ts` already implements a full allowlist
(`buildHermeticEnv`, `hermeticChildEnv`), but it is drop-everything-else and
lives under `test/`. That is too aggressive here: `gstack-evidence run` executes
arbitrary developer commands that may need `PATH` extensions, credentials, or
tool config. The narrow subtraction is the right shape.

A `--clean-env` opt-out flag would be a reasonable escape hatch for anyone who
genuinely wants dotenv values passed through.

title: Nothing reclaims per-repo .gstack state — browse-audit.jsonl is append-only by design and bin/ has no cleanup verb
body:
Ran a full disk audit on a box with gstack installed across seven repos and noticed there's no way to reclaim the per-repo `.gstack/` state short of deleting the directory by hand.

`browse/src/audit.ts:6` states the intent plainly:

> restarts and is never truncated by the server

That's a reasonable default for an audit log, but nothing else rotates it either, so it's monotonic for the life of the repo:

```
472K  2026-08-06  /root/ArceHubBot/.gstack/browse-audit.jsonl
 28K  2026-07-12  /root/read-only/.gstack/browse-audit.jsonl
  8K  2026-07-28  /root/.claude/.gstack/browse-audit.jsonl
```

`browse-network.log` and `browse-console.log` sit beside it with the same shape. And `.gstack/tmp/` collects codex scratch — `codex-err-*.txt`, `codex-review-iter*.{err,out}` — which is pure byproduct:

```
8.3M  /root/ArceHubBot/.gstack   (8.0M of it in tmp/)
```

I'm not going to pretend this is urgent. Busiest repo here is 8 MB after six weeks. The reason I'm filing is the structural bit: `bin/` has 76 commands and the only two that remove anything are `gstack-uninstall` and `gstack-brain-uninstall`, both all-or-nothing. There's no `gstack-clean`, and `/browse` gives you no way to say "keep the audit trail, drop the console spam."

What would cover it:

A `gstack-clean` verb, dry-run by default, scoped to `.gstack/` in the current repo. Delete `tmp/codex-*` past some age, truncate `browse-{network,console}.log` over a size threshold, and rotate `browse-audit.jsonl` keeping a retention window rather than truncating it — the audit log is the one file in there with a reason to survive.

Liveness gates worth having before it removes anything: no `codex` process, no browse daemon listening, file mtime older than an hour. Cheap to check and it makes the command safe to run from a cron.

Environment: gstack 1.60.1.0, Ubuntu 22.04, Claude Code 2.1.220.

title: fix(evidence): subtract Bun-auto-loaded dotenv keys from the child environment
body:
## Why (in your own words)

`gstack-evidence` exists to be believed — it's the mechanical arm of /ship's "no completion claims without fresh verification evidence." But in any repo with a `.env.local` (most JS repos), it records the wrong verdict: the script runs under Bun, Bun auto-loads dotenv files from the cwd into `process.env` before user code runs, and the `Bun.spawn` call passed no `env`, so the child test runner inherited values the developer never exported. Suites that assert behavior when those vars are *unset* go falsely red; injected values can equally mask a real failure as a false green. This change subtracts exactly the keys those dotenv files define and passes an explicit `env` — the developer's real environment (PATH, credentials, tool config) still flows through untouched. The helper never throws, per the file's transparency invariant.

Fixes #2624.

## Live evidence

Repro repo containing `.env.local` with `INJECTED_SECRET=oops`; the wrapped command asserts the var is unset.

Before (main, `c86e6472`):

```
$ gstack-evidence run --label repro -- 'test -z "$INJECTED_SECRET" && echo CLEAN || { echo "POLLUTED: $INJECTED_SECRET"; exit 1; }'
POLLUTED: oops
gstack-evidence: recorded label=repro exit=1 log=.../logs/2026-08-18T18-31-53-777Z-repro-....log
wrapper-exit=1
```

After (this branch, same command, same repo):

```
CLEAN
gstack-evidence: recorded label=repro exit=0 log=.../logs/2026-08-18T18-39-13-589Z-repro-....log
wrapper-exit=0
```

Red-green on the new test: with the fix stashed (main's binary), `dotenv keys Bun auto-loaded from the cwd do not reach the child` fails; with the fix, `bun test test/evidence.test.ts` → 26 pass, 0 fail.

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-evidence` — new `childEnv()` helper (parses only the *keys* from `.env`, `.env.<NODE_ENV>`, `.env.local`, `.env.<NODE_ENV>.local` in the cwd, subtracts them from a copy of `process.env`; wrapped in try/catch so it can never turn a run red) and `env: childEnv()` on the `Bun.spawn` call. Plus 2 regression tests.
- **Verified live by:** the before/after repro above on macOS, driving the real `gstack-evidence run` entry path; full `test/evidence.test.ts` suite (26 pass).
- **Did NOT test:** Windows; repos using non-standard dotenv filenames (out of scope — the subtraction targets exactly the set Bun auto-loads). I deliberately did not add a `--clean-env`/opt-out flag to keep the diff minimal — easy follow-up if you want the escape hatch.

title: v1.68.1.0 fix: phantom AskUserQuestion hooks — canonical-only registration + self-healing settings.json
body:
## Summary

Fixes the phantom AskUserQuestion hooks that spammed `No such file or directory` errors on every question: gstack installs were baking ephemeral Conductor worktree paths (`biarritz-v3`, `taipei-v2`, ...) into `~/.claude/settings.json`, and nothing ever cleaned them up.

Root cause was a three-bug pileup:

- **Conductor auto-opt-in overrode dev-setup's guard.** `setup` upgraded `--plan-tune-hooks=prompt` to `yes` whenever Conductor env vars were set, so every new workspace registered hooks non-interactively.
- **Hook paths were baked from the setup-time tree** (`pwd -P` of the running worktree), so deleting the workspace left dead absolute paths behind.
- **Dedupe degraded to append-forever.** Claude Code strips the unknown `_gstack_source` key on its own rewrites, so each worktree's differently-pathed hook appended a fresh entry. No pruning existed anywhere.

What ships:

- **`bin/gstack-settings-hook` rewritten around a KNOWN_HOOKS identity table** (6 hook identities: basename + relpath suffix + event + matcher). Ownership is decided per hook ITEM; entry tags never claim foreign items; a user's co-located hook is never collateral damage.
- **New `prune-stale [--repoint <root>] [--all]` self-healer.** Every `./setup` heals first: dead gstack entries pruned, stale ones re-pointed at the stable `~/.claude/skills/gstack` install, duplicates collapsed — one visible log line only when something changed.
- **Canonical-only registration.** `_hook_command_path` resolves against `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/skills/gstack` only; the ephemeral-tree fallback is gone. A missing canonical hook means "don't register," never "bake the running tree's path."
- **`PT_EXPLICIT` consent provenance** via new `gstack-config has <key>`: the Conductor auto-opt-in fires only on the true silent fall-through (no flag, no env, no config key present). dev-setup's no-mutation guarantee now actually holds.
- **Mutation safety:** mkdir lock with owner token + atomic stale takeover, unique tmp/backup names, backup-on-change with mtime-based keep-10 rotation, fail-closed parse (a corrupt settings.json is never clobbered — exit 3), 0600 mode preservation, and a `gsMain` fail-loud umbrella (bun `-e` swallows post-require uncaught exceptions and exits 0 — verified on 1.3.13 — so every script body now converts a runtime throw into stderr + exit 4). Lock give-up exits 5 and setup reports the skipped registration honestly.
- **`gstack-uninstall` ordering fix:** hook cleanup ran AFTER the install root was deleted — from inside that root — so a real uninstall silently no-op'd. Cleanup now runs first, plus a full identity sweep (auq-error-fallback, verify-gate, untagged strays).
- **`--no-team` teardown** removes the AskUserQuestion trio and sweeps identities while excluding the user-registered verify-gate opt-in (`GSTACK_SWEEP_EXCLUDE_SOURCES`).

Local box verified: 11 hook entries healed to 5 canonical ones, idempotent on re-run, zero dead-worktree paths remaining.

## Test Coverage

Ship coverage dashboard: **87%** of changed behaviors pinned by free-tier tests.

| Area | Tests |
|------|-------|
| `gstack-settings-hook` behavioral (identity healer, per-item safety, lock, fail-closed, rollback, rotation, escape round-trip) | `test/gstack-settings-hook-schema-aware.test.ts` — 51 tests incl. an incident facsimile seeding the exact live-box corruption (6/3/2 entries → 2/1/1 canonical) |
| Adversarial regressions | wrong-shape hooks value → loud exit 4 + file untouched; `toString`-basename foreign hook survives `--all`; verify-gate sweep exclusion; fresh-foreign-lock exits 5 |
| Setup wiring tripwires (canonical-only, heal-first ordering, prelude concatenation, matcher drift, unsuppressed heal) | `test/setup-hook-canonical-paths.test.ts` (new) |
| Consent provenance | `test/setup-plan-tune-hooks-noninteractive.test.ts` — PT_EXPLICIT + Conductor condition pins |
| Uninstall ordering | `test/uninstall.test.ts` — behavioral test runs the INSTALLED copy from inside the deleted root |
| Windows + locale | `test/setup-windows-fallback.test.ts`, `test/gstack-config-key-locale.test.ts` |

Uncovered (documented, accepted): interactive-TTY setup paths and the live `~/.claude` heal itself (exercised manually on this box instead).

## Pre-Landing Review

| Pass | Findings | Fixed | Notes |
|------|----------|-------|-------|
| Plan reviews (CEO + Eng + 2 Codex outside-voice rounds) | 41 | all folded into the approved plan | pre-implementation |
| Review army (pre-landing `/review`) | 26 | 12 | rest rejected with reasons or documented |
| Red team | 8 | 6 | verify-gate identity row, single quoting authority, Windows path normalization |
| Claude adversarial (Codex unavailable: MCP auth failure — informational gate) | 12 | 8 | verified-critical F1: bun `-e` swallows uncaught exceptions → gsMain umbrella |

Notable rejected/deferred findings, on the record: PID-aware lock takeover deferred (owner file already carries the pid if it becomes worth it); Claude Code itself doesn't honor the mutation lock — lost updates against a live session remain possible and convergent (next heal repairs); consent posture: heal may prune/re-point but never ADDS entries.

## Eval Results

Diff-selected paid E2E: **8/8 passed** ($0.93, 178s). All other eval categories selected zero tests for this diff (no skill-behavior changes). Free suite green via the strict sharded runner; late singleton flakes in untouched areas (browse watchdog, make-pdf render, design daemon) were each verified green standalone and traced to a saturated box (sibling worktree running its own eval suite, load avg 25+).

## Scope Check

CLEAN — every change traces to the approved plan (`fluttering-graham` plan file, NO UNRESOLVED DECISIONS) or to a review finding logged against it.

## Plan Completion

47/50 plan items DONE. The 3 remaining are documented deferrals, not gaps: PID-aware lock takeover, `setup:1601` CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR alignment (new TODO), and Windows bash-prefix on plan-tune/Stop add-events (new TODO).

- Added: Windows bash-prefix on plan-tune/Stop add-events; `setup:1601` CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR alignment; bool-parsing/`validate_key` centralization (P3).

## Documentation

- **README.md**: setup hooks section documents canonical-only hook registration (hook commands point at the stable `~/.claude/skills/gstack` install, never the running tree) and the heal-first `prune-stale --repoint` pass (visible one-liner + backup only when something changed). The manual-uninstall note now covers every gstack hook identity — SessionStart auto-update, the AskUserQuestion PreToolUse/PostToolUse trio, and the Stop hooks (timeline, verify-gate) — not just timeline-stop-hook.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: records PT_EXPLICIT provenance (Conductor auto-opt-in fires only on the true silent fall-through, checked via `gstack-config has`) and the stated repair exception to dev-setup's no-mutation guarantee: heal may prune dead entries and re-point existing ones to canonical, never register new ones.
- **CHANGELOG.md**: v1.68.1.0 release summary with the incident-facsimile numbers.

Claude Code keeps listing them. `cleanup_old_claude_symlinks` could not see them: it listed names from the payload, and a missing payload matches nothing. Scan `$skills_dir` instead. Only delete dirs whose `SKILL.md` (or the dir itself) is a symlink with an anchored gstack path — not a user skill whose target merely contains the substring `gstack`. **Fixes #2204.** Related: #954 (absolute vendored links — distinct), #896 (prefixed uninstall leftovers — `cleanup_prefixed_claude_symlinks`, out of scope), #1882 (hardcoded `~/.claude/skills/gstack/` in skill prose — distinct). title: install-prepush-hook: fs.mkdirSync(recursive) throws EEXIST on Windows (bun) when .git/hooks exists
body:
## Summary

`gstack-redact install-prepush-hook` throws `EEXIST` on Windows (bun runtime) when the target `.git/hooks` directory already exists, and the hook is never written.

## Environment

- gstack: **1.67.2.0**
- bun: **1.3.12** (Windows x64)
- OS: **Windows 11** (`MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200`), running under Git Bash
- Global git install (`~/.claude/skills/gstack`)

## What happened

Enabled the hook globally (`gstack-config set redact_prepush_hook true`) and installed it into several existing repos. On one repo the install crashed:

```
function installPrepushHook(): void {
  const dir = hooksPath();
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });   // <-- throws here
          ^
EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.git\hooks'
    path: ".git\hooks",
 syscall: "mkdir",
   errno: -17,
    code: "EEXIST"
      at installPrepushHook (…/bin/gstack-redact:58:6)
```

The hook file was not created, so that repo was left unprotected until I copied the managed hook in by hand.

## Root cause

`bin/gstack-redact` → `installPrepushHook()`:

```ts
const dir = hooksPath();
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
```

Per Node semantics, `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` is a no-op when `dir` already exists. Under **bun on Windows** it instead throws `EEXIST`. Since almost every real repo already has a `.git/hooks` directory, the install is fragile on Windows. (In my run it failed on 1 of 4 repos — the other three, which also already had `.git/hooks`, happened to succeed, so the behavior looks nondeterministic under bun/Windows.)

## Suggested fix

Make the mkdir defensive so an existing directory is never fatal:

```ts
// Option A — ignore EEXIST
try {
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
} catch (e: any) {
  if (e?.code !== "EEXIST") throw e;
}

// Option B — guard on existence
if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
```

The same pattern likely applies anywhere else the codebase relies on `recursive: true` being a no-op on Windows.

## Workaround (for other Windows users hitting this)

Copy the managed hook from a working repo:

```bash
cp <working-repo>/.git/hooks/pre-push <broken-repo>/.git/hooks/pre-push
chmod +x <broken-repo>/.git/hooks/pre-push
```

The hook is generic (points at the global `gstack-redact-prepush` binary and chains `pre-push.local`), so copying is safe.

title: fix(evals): the GITHUB_ prefix no longer admits operator credentials into hermetic children
body:
## Why (in your own words)

CONTRIBUTING promises that when you run evals locally, "your operator `~/.claude`
config, MCP servers, skills, `~/.gstack` decision logs, and `CONDUCTOR_*` env never
leak into the child, so local eval signal matches CI". `test/helpers/hermetic-env.ts`
enforces that with an allowlist, and it deliberately drops operator credentials —
`GH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` are named in the module doc and pinned
by `hermetic-env.test.ts`.

But the allowlist also has prefix rules, `ALLOW_PREFIXES = ['EVALS_', 'GITHUB_']`,
and `GITHUB_` is there for CI metadata (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITHUB_SHA`,
`GITHUB_WORKSPACE`). That same prefix matches the credentials developers actually
export in their shells: `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`,
`GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. So `GH_TOKEN` was blocked and its sibling walked straight
through, and every locally-spawned eval child — `claude -p`, the PTY runner, the
Agent SDK runner, codex, gemini — ran with the operator's GitHub *write* credential
in its environment.

This is also precisely a CI-equivalence failure, which is the module's whole reason
to exist: no workflow in `.github/workflows/` sets an env var named `GITHUB_TOKEN`
(the job token is passed as `GH_TOKEN`, which the allowlist already drops), so CI
children never had it. Only local children did. The repo already treats this exact
variable as a hazard elsewhere — `test/free-tests-workflow-wiring.test.ts` pins
`persist-credentials: false` because "a default-grant GITHUB_TOKEN persisted into
.git/config by checkout would hand that code whatever the repo default allows."
Handing it to the eval child directly is the same threat, one layer over.

The fix screens prefix admissions by name shape instead of adding names to a
denylist, so a future `GITHUB_*_TOKEN` needs no edit.

## Live evidence

**1. On my real shell — before and after.** Names only, no values printed. I have
`GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` exported, like a lot of people do.

```
$ bun .probe/real-env.ts            # on main
kept from THIS shell: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, HOME, PATH, SHELL, TERM
credential-shaped among them: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN

$ bun .probe/real-env.ts            # on this branch
kept from THIS shell: HOME, PATH, SHELL, TERM
credential-shaped among them: (none)
```

**2. Synthetic operator env — the leak and the metadata that must survive it.**

```
$ bun .probe/leak-repro.ts          # on main
dropped  GH_TOKEN
KEPT     GITHUB_TOKEN                    <-- operator write credential
KEPT     GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN    <-- operator PAT
KEPT     GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY          <-- app private key
KEPT     GITHUB_ACTIONS
KEPT     GITHUB_SHA
KEPT     GITHUB_PATH
KEPT     GITHUB_WORKSPACE

$ bun .probe/leak-repro.ts          # on this branch
dropped  GH_TOKEN
dropped  GITHUB_TOKEN
dropped  GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
dropped  GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
KEPT     GITHUB_ACTIONS
KEPT     GITHUB_SHA
KEPT     GITHUB_PATH                     <-- PATH, not PAT: the near-miss holds
KEPT     GITHUB_WORKSPACE
```

**3. Red / green on the new tripwires.** Reverting only the screen (keeping the
exported predicate so the file still imports) turns the new tests red:

```
$ bun test test/helpers/hermetic-env.test.ts     # screen reverted
(fail) prefix rules never admit credential-shaped names > GITHUB_ credentials are dropped even though GITHUB_ is an allowed prefix
(fail) prefix rules never admit credential-shaped names > extraAllow still re-admits a runner credential — screen is prefix-rule only
 22 pass
 2 fail

$ bun test test/helpers/hermetic-env.test.ts     # branch as submitted
 24 pass
 0 fail
 131 expect() calls
```

**4. No regressions in the hermetic surface.** Every test file that touches the
module, main vs branch, same machine, back to back:

```
$ bun test test/helpers/hermetic-env.test.ts test/hermetic-wiring.test.ts \
      test/hermetic-skills-seeding.test.ts test/pty-skill-seeding-wiring.test.ts \
      test/helpers/session-runner.test.ts test/helpers/gemini-session-runner.test.ts

main    45 pass, 2 fail
branch  49 pass, 2 fail      (+4 = the new tests)
```

The 2 failures are identical on both sides and pre-existing on Windows —
`EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink` in `hermeticSkillsConfigDir`, which needs
Developer Mode or an elevated shell. Untouched by this change.

## Scope

- **Changed:**
  - `test/helpers/hermetic-env.ts` — prefix admissions are screened by
    `isCredentialShapedName()` (new, exported). The last `_`-delimited segment of the
    name is checked against the credential vocabulary the shipped scanner already uses
    (`ENV_KV_SUFFIX` in `lib/redact-patterns.ts`), plus `PAT`. Screened for the
    module's own `ALLOW_PREFIXES` only — an `ALLOW_EXACT` entry (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`)
    or an `opts.extraAllow` entry (codex's `OPENAI_API_KEY`, gemini's `GEMINI_*`) is a
    deliberate per-runner admission and still wins, so the documented opt-in keeps
    working.
  - `test/helpers/hermetic-env.test.ts` — 4 tests: the credentials are dropped and no
    credential *value* survives under any name; the full documented GitHub Actions
    runner-env set plus the `EVALS_*` knobs still survive the screen; `extraAllow`
    still re-admits `GEMINI_API_KEY` without re-opening the `GITHUB_` hole;
    `isCredentialShapedName` matches the tail segment, not a substring
    (`GITHUB_PATH`, `GITHUB_TOKENIZER`, `GITHUB_KEYRING` all stay allowed).
  - `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the "Hermetic by default" paragraph claims credentials never
    leak; it now says so explicitly and states the prefix-vs-exact rule.

- **Verified live by:** running the reproduction above on my own shell (Windows 11,
  Git Bash, bun 1.3.14) against main and against this branch; red/green on the new
  tripwires; before/after comparison of every hermetic-touching test file.

- **Did NOT test:** a paid eval run. This changes only which variables reach the
  child, and no test helper, runner, or workflow in the repo reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` —
  `grep -rn GITHUB_TOKEN test/ scripts/ lib/ bin/` returns nothing outside
  `.github/workflows/`, where it appears only as `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` passed to
  `password:` or to a `GH_TOKEN:` env. Windows note: I could not use the full
  `bun run test` suite as a gate — it reports ~1100 pre-existing failures on a clean
  clone here (#2597), so I compared the affected file set directly instead.

## Liveness proof (required)

`GSTACK PR` typed live at a real PowerShell prompt on my machine — the shell's own
`CommandNotFoundException` is the proof it was parsed, not painted on.

![GSTACK PR typed live into Windows PowerShell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntdatt812/gstack/liveness-asset/pr-liveness.png)

the three files above.</sub>

title: fix(scripts): stop heredoc bodies deadlocking under Homebrew bash
body:
## The bug

`./setup --help` can hang forever on macOS. No output, no error, no way to tell it apart from a slow install. Ten more scripts carry the same latent hang.

bash 5.2+ delivers a heredoc body of 64KiB or less through a pipe. The forked child writes the whole body before `exec`, and nothing reads the other end until the command starts. Under macOS pipe-KVA pressure the kernel hands a fresh pipe a 512-byte buffer instead of the usual 16 to 64KiB, so any body of 512 bytes or more blocks `write()` permanently. The runtime capacity check bash would need to notice this (`F_GETPIPE_SZ`) is Linux-only, so it never fires.

`#!/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to Homebrew bash on a Mac with brew on PATH, which is most of them. Apple's `/bin/bash` 3.2 predates the pipe path and is unaffected, so the bug is invisible to anyone testing with the system shell. It is pressure-dependent, which is why it reads as "worked on my machine": the same script runs fine all day and then wedges.

Reproduction on any bash 5.2+:

```bash
probe() { [ -p /dev/stdin ] && echo PIPE || echo TEMPFILE; }
probe <<EOF
$(printf 'x%.0s' $(seq 1 1000))
EOF
```

On Homebrew bash 5.3.15 that prints `PIPE`. Prefix it with `BASH_COMPAT=50` and it prints `TEMPFILE`.

## The fix

`BASH_COMPAT=50` in each affected script, which restores the pre-5.2 tempfile path.

Deliberately **not** a `#!/bin/bash` shebang swap:

* That pins the script to whatever bash lives at `/bin`, which is 3.2 on macOS and absent on some Linux distributions.
* It is bypassed entirely by `bash script.sh` call sites. The variable survives those.

Other properties:

* Not exported, so child processes keep their own compat level.
* Placed below any `--help` `sed` range that reads `$0`, so usage output is unchanged. Verified on all eleven.
* Every guarded script is bash-3.2-clean (no associative arrays, case conversion, or `mapfile`), so compat level 50 costs them nothing.

## Scope

Eleven scripts, one guard each, no behaviour change:

`setup`, `bin/gstack-brain-sync`, `bin/gstack-artifacts-init`, `bin/gstack-jsonl-merge`, `bin/gstack-team-init`, `bin/gstack-distill-free-text`, `bin/gstack-brain-restore`, `bin/gstack-settings-hook`, `gstack-upgrade/migrations/v1.27.0.0.sh`, `gstack-upgrade/migrations/v1.37.0.0.sh`, `scripts/build-app.sh`

## Test

`test/heredoc-pipe-deadlock.test.ts` does two things:

1. Scans every tracked shell script for a heredoc body in the 512B to 64KiB window and fails without the guard, so a new one cannot land unguarded.
2. Proves the mechanism at runtime on bash 5.2+ by asserting the body moves from `PIPE` to `TEMPFILE`. Skipped on older bash, where the pipe path does not exist.

`bun run test:free` is green except three failures that reproduce identically on a pristine `main` checkout here: the `path-validation` symlink case, `touchfiles` `detectBaseBranch`, and the `codex-hardening` watchdog (flaky roughly 2 runs in 3 on stock main).

## Related

Split out of #1696 so each piece can be reviewed on its own merits. This one is a pure bug fix and stands alone.

title: fix(redact): tolerate EEXIST from recursive mkdir in install-prepush-hook on bun/Windows
body:
**Linked issue**: #2635

## Why (in your own words)

On Windows, bun's `fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` throws `EEXIST` when the directory already exists - Node treats the same call as a no-op. Since virtually every real repo already has a `.git/hooks` directory, `gstack-redact install-prepush-hook` crashes on Windows before writing the hook, leaving the repo without the credential-scan guard while the operator believes it is armed (#2635). This change makes that one mkdir defensive: `EEXIST` is tolerated only when the path is confirmed to be an existing directory; a regular file occupying the path, a stat failure, or any other errno still throws, so real collisions still fail loudly.

## Live evidence

`bun --preload` fixture (committed as `test/helpers/emulate-bun-windows-eexist.ts`) emulates bun-on-Windows `mkdirSync` semantics - recursive mkdir on an existing directory throws EEXIST - so the exact crash path runs on any platform. Transparent emulation; no other fs behavior is altered.

Before (baseline `main` @ 9da66929, in a repo with pre-existing `.git/hooks` + a non-managed `pre-push`):

```
$ bun --preload test/helpers/emulate-bun-windows-eexist.ts bin/gstack-redact install-prepush-hook
EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.git/hooks'
 code: "EEXIST"
      at installPrepushHook (bin/gstack-redact:58:6)
exit=1            # hook never written; repo left unguarded
```

After (this fix, same repo setup):

```
$ bun --preload test/helpers/emulate-bun-windows-eexist.ts bin/gstack-redact install-prepush-hook
gstack-redact: preserved existing hook as pre-push.local (chained).
gstack-redact: installed pre-push hook at .git/hooks/pre-push
exit=0            # managed hook written; original preserved as pre-push.local
```

Committed regression test (`test/fs-utils.test.ts`) reproduces the above at test level and fails on baseline / passes on the fix; unit tests additionally pin that a regular file occupying the mkdir path still throws `EEXIST`.

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-redact` (`installPrepushHook` uses the new helper), `lib/fs-utils.ts` (new `mkdirpSync`), `test/fs-utils.test.ts` + `test/helpers/emulate-bun-windows-eexist.ts` (new tests).
- **Verified live by:** the before/after CLI run above; `bun test test/fs-utils.test.ts` (4/4); `bun test test/redact-prepush-hook.test.ts test/gstack-redact-cli.test.ts` (41/41, install/uninstall/chaining unchanged); full free suite `bun run test` - no new failures (5 pre-existing `browse/test/*` failures reproduce on clean `main`, browser-launch environmental).
- **Did NOT test:** a real Windows machine (none available). The Windows crash path is exercised through the transparent `--preload` emulation above; the issue reporter's stack trace matches it frame-for-frame.

## Checklist

- [x] Not a generated-file-only diff(pure source + tests)
- [x] No ETHOS.md edits, no voice / founder perspective / YC changes
- [x] No new public command / external service / host adapter(N/A)
- [x] Linked issue: #2635

## Notes

- Deliberately scoped to the one call site from #2635. The same bare `mkdirSync(recursive)` pattern exists elsewhere (e.g. #2048's `browse`/`mkdirSecure`, and open PR #2329 adds a `mkdirpSync` under `scripts/` for the doc generators) - if you'd rather unify, `lib/fs-utils.ts` is a natural home and I'm happy to extend it in a follow-up.

title: v1.68.2.0 fix: tunnel revoke exists and revokes everything — setup keys included, verified live
body:
## Why (in your own words)

Revoking a paired agent was a lie twice over. `revokeToken` deleted only the first Map entry for a clientId, and the spent setup key kept for connection retries always sat first in line: `DELETE /token/<agent>` returned 200 while the live session kept driving the browser, a leftover unspent setup key could mint a brand-new session for a "revoked" agent inside the key's 5-minute window, and a second DELETE returned 200 again. The documented way out, `$B tunnel revoke`, did not exist — the CLI forwarded it to the daemon as `Unknown command: 'tunnel'`. And the pairing docs still promised a read+write sandbox ("Cannot execute arbitrary JavaScript, read cookies, or access storage") three releases after b73f3644 deliberately made pairing full-access, so a user following the skill believed they granted a sandboxed session and actually granted JS execution on their logged-in browser.

This PR makes revocation total and verified, makes the documented CLI real, pins the pairing default in one shared constant, and rewrites the docs to the truth. Along the way it closes four adjacent traps found during review: bare `--restrict` silently granted FULL access (the opposite of intent), a scopes list could smuggle in the `control` scope, scope typos surfaced as a misleading error to the remote agent at `/connect`, and `rateLimit: 0` (documented "unlimited") silently became 10 on the `/pair` path.

## Live evidence

BEFORE — origin/main @ 9da66929, `BROWSE_HEADLESS_SKIP=1` daemon, `mallory` paired + connected, second setup key pending:

```
$ DELETE /token/mallory
HTTP 200
$ GET /agents
{"agents":[{"clientId":"mallory","scopes":["read","write","admin","meta"],...}]}   # still listed
$ POST /command with the 'revoked' token
HTTP 403                                                                            # NOT 401 — token still authenticates
$ POST /connect with the leftover setup key (within its 5-min window)
{ "token": true, "scopes": ["read","write","admin","meta"] }                        # new session minted post-revoke
$ DELETE /token/mallory (second call)
HTTP 200                                                                            # false 200, again
```

AFTER — this branch, same ceremony:

```
$ browse tunnel agents
mallory  scopes=read,write,admin,meta  domains=any  expires=2026-08-21T04:04:40.869Z  commands=0
mallory  (pending setup key)  scopes=read,write,admin,meta  domains=any  expires=2026-08-20T04:09:40.872Z  commands=0
$ browse tunnel revoke mallory
Revoked "mallory" (3 tokens).
Verified: not in the active agent list.
$ GET /agents
{"agents":[]}
$ POST /command with the revoked token
HTTP 401
$ POST /connect with the leftover setup key
HTTP 401
$ browse tunnel revoke mallory (second call)
No paired agent named "mallory".
No agents are currently paired.
exit: 1
$ POST /pair with a scope typo
{"error":"Invalid scope: raed. Valid: read, write, admin, meta, control"}
$ POST /pair smuggling control in scopes
{"error":"The control scope requires the control flag (--control); it cannot be granted via a scopes list."}
```

Fail-first: the shape a/b regression tests run against origin/main fail (0 pass, 2 fail — session survives revoke; leftover key re-connects); on this branch the committed versions pass.

```
(fail) fail-first: revoke-all shapes on origin/main > shape a: revoke kills the session shadowed by a spent setup key
(fail) fail-first: revoke-all shapes on origin/main > shape b: unspent setup key dies with the revoke (no re-grant)
 0 pass
 2 fail
```

Targeted suite on the branch: `bun test browse/test/token-registry.test.ts browse/test/pair-agent-e2e.test.ts browse/test/tunnel-revoke-cli.test.ts browse/test/server-auth.test.ts browse/test/tab-isolation.test.ts browse/test/skill-token.test.ts` → 178 pass, 0 fail. `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all` → zero drift. `bun run build` → clean.

## Scope

- **Changed:** `browse/src/token-registry.ts` (revoke-all + count, `DEFAULT_PAIR_SCOPES`, `InvalidScopeError`, shared option validation, `listTokens({includeSetup})`, invariant comment), `browse/src/server.ts` (`/pair` control gate + typed 400s, `/agents` pending keys, `DELETE /token` decode + `tokens_deleted`, 403 hint), `browse/src/cli.ts` (`tunnel revoke`/`tunnel agents` with post-revoke verify, `validatePairAgentFlags`, explicit scopes), `browse/src/skill-token.ts` (Boolean wrap), docs (`pair-agent/SKILL.md.tmpl` + regenerated `SKILL.md`, `docs/REMOTE_BROWSER_ACCESS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`), tests (35 new cases incl. a subprocess CLI harness with stub daemons pinning the version-skew net and every CLI error branch), VERSION/CHANGELOG.
- **Verified live by:** the before/after transcript above, the fail-first run on origin/main, the 178-test targeted loop, the gen-skill-docs drift gate, `bun run build`, and a pre-push adversarial review (4 lenses, refute-style verification: 13 raw findings, 7 refuted, 6 confirmed and fixed in the final commit — including an `--restrict=read` equals-form bypass of the new validation).
- **Did NOT test:** the live ngrok tunnel path (needs an authtoken; the tunnel allowlist code is unchanged — `TUNNEL_PATHS` still `/connect` + `/command`). The full free suite in my sandbox has pre-existing environment failures OUTSIDE `browse/` (relink/session-update/skill-validation fail identically or worse on untouched origin/main there — missing `file` binary, symlink collisions with a live gstack install); all `browse/` shards pass locally, and the authoritative full run is this PR's `free-tests.yml` lane.

Notes for the reviewer:
- The "Revocation incomplete" CLI branch doubles as a deliberate version-skew net: a NEW CLI pointed at a still-running OLD daemon (first-match revoke bug) gets caught by the post-revoke `/agents` re-read, exits 1, and suggests re-running (which converges on old daemons) or `stop`. Pinned by a stub-daemon test.
- `POST /token` (root direct mint) intentionally still accepts explicit `control` in scopes — root minting explicit scopes is the deliberate path; only the `/pair` ceremony gates it behind the control flag.
- The re-grant hole is time-boxed by the setup key's 5-minute expiry; the transcript's leftover-key step ran inside that window.

## Liveness proof (required)

Maintainer-authored PR, prepared by Claude Code in a cloud sandbox at the owner's request — there is no human screen in the loop to photograph. @garrytan: attach a `GSTACK PR` screenshot from your machine if you want the ritual observed for maintainer PRs, or waive it.

title: fix(evidence): stop bun's dotenv autoload from reaching the spawned command
body:
`bin/gstack-evidence` has a `#!/usr/bin/env bun` shebang, and **bun auto-loads `.env`, `.env.<NODE_ENV>` and `.env.local` from the cwd into `process.env`**. The wrapper spawned the command with no `env` override, so everything run through `gstack-evidence run` inherited those variables — and a repo `.env.local` routinely holds production credentials.

Reproduce in three lines:

```bash
mkdir t && cd t
printf 'SECRET_PROBE=leaked\n' > .env.local
printf 'Bun.spawnSync(["bash","-c","echo child SECRET_PROBE=$SECRET_PROBE"],{stdout:"inherit"})\n' > c.ts
bun c.ts        # -> child SECRET_PROBE=leaked
```

## Two problems, and the second is worse than the leak

1. **Secrets reach a child that would not otherwise have them.** `npm test` run by hand in the same shell sees none of them; the same command through the wrapper sees all of them.
2. **The command under test behaves differently, so the ledger certifies a run that is not the run CI performs.** Observed in a Next.js repo on 2026-08-20: four tests failed **4/4** through the wrapper and passed **5/5** without it, because app code branched on env vars only the wrapper supplied. It reads exactly like a flake, and nearly an hour went into chasing one — the measuring instrument was the bug. `gstack-evidence` exists to record trustworthy evidence, so silently altering the environment defeats its purpose.

## The fix, and why the detection is exact rather than heuristic

The child env is now `process.env` minus the keys bun injected. Verified on **bun 1.3.11**: a dotenv file does **not** override a variable the shell already exported — the shell's value wins.

```
$ SECRET_PROBE=from_shell bun p.ts
SECRET_PROBE=from_shell          # .env.local said "leaked"
```

So a key whose live value equals the dotenv file's value was injected by bun, and dropping it restores the environment the user's own shell would have given the command. A key whose live value **differs** is genuinely the caller's and survives untouched.

`BUN_DOTENV_FILES()` mirrors bun's precedence, including that `.env.local` is skipped when `NODE_ENV` is `test` (measured: `NODE_ENV=test` loads `.env` but not `.env.local`). Scrubbing a key bun never loaded would strip a variable the caller legitimately provided.

- **Escape hatch:** `GSTACK_EVIDENCE_KEEP_DOTENV=1` restores the old pass-through behaviour.
- When keys are scrubbed the wrapper warns with the **key names only**, so the diagnostic cannot become the leak it prevents.
- A key that fails to parse (multi-line values) is left in the child env — the safe direction.

## Tests

Six cases in `test/evidence.test.ts`, **mutation-verified**: removing `env: spawnEnv` reddens exactly the two leak tests, restoring it gives 30/30. The three control tests correctly stay green under that mutation, since they guard against over-reach rather than testing the scrub.

⚠️ Worth knowing for anyone extending these: `bun test` sets `NODE_ENV=test`, so **the first version of these tests passed vacuously** against a `.env.local` bun had never loaded. Every leak test now asserts the scrub warning fired, so a fixture bun ignores fails instead of passing silently. One test pins the `NODE_ENV=test` skip behaviour deliberately.

Verified so far: `bun test test/evidence.test.ts` → **30 pass / 0 fail**, plus the mutation run above. The full suite is running as I open this; I'll confirm in a comment rather than claim it here.

title: gstack-memory-ingest: colliding path-derived slugs overwrite in staging, then fail the whole batch
body:
## What breaks

`gstack-memory-ingest` derives a page slug from lossy inputs:

- transcripts: `transcripts/<agent>/<repo>/<date>-<session_id[:12]>`
- artifacts:   `<type>s/<repo>/<date>-<baseName>`

Two distinct source files can therefore collapse to one slug (a session resumed under the same `session_id` on the same day, or two sessions whose `session_id` shares a 12-char prefix on the same day).

`writeStaged()` names each staged file `${slug}.md`, so the second file **overwrites** the first on disk. `written` still counts both, but only one file lands in the staging dir. gbrain's batch `import` then collects fewer files than were staged, and the staged-vs-collected reconciliation guard refuses to advance state:

```
[memory-ingest] ERR: gbrain import accounted for 21 of 22 staged page(s) (imported=7, unchanged=14).
gbrain collected 21 file(s) from the staging dir. Refusing to advance state ...
[memory-ingest] 0 written, 22 failed
ISSUE [transcripts]: gstack-memory-ingest exit 1
```

The guard is correct (no silent loss), but the batch fails on **every run** until the colliding inputs age out of the window. Note the message's `.gitignore` hint is a red herring for this case: the ingester already passes `--include-gitignored` and sets `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, and a gitignore drop collects 0 files, not 21 of 22.

## Reproduction

Two prepared pages with the same path-derived slug and distinct `source_path` values. `writeStaged()` writes 2 but only 1 file exists on disk; the reconciliation guard then fails the batch.

## Proposed fix

Disambiguate colliding slugs in `preparePages()` before staging: keep the first page's slug, give each later collider a stable per-source suffix `-<sha8(source_path)>`. Deterministic across runs (same source -> same slug -> gbrain sees it unchanged, no churn), unique because `source_path` is unique per prepared page. Mutate `slug` and `page_slug` together to preserve the `stagedRelPath()` single-source-of-truth contract (staging path, #1802 resume reconstruction, and state recording stay in lockstep).

PR to follow.

title: browse (Windows): daemon children spawn without windowsHide, opening a console window per child
/land-and-deploy §4a-postfail recovers the merge but never deletes the remote branch, silently dropping the --delete-branch half
body:
## Summary

`/land-and-deploy` Step 4 merges with `gh pr merge --auto --delete-branch` (SKILL.md:1478) or `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` (SKILL.md:1487). When `gh` exits non-zero *after* GitHub has already merged, §4a-postfail correctly recovers the merge, cleans up stale worktrees, and continues. But nothing in that recovery path deletes the remote branch, so the `--delete-branch` half of the original command is silently lost. The user is left with a merged PR and a surviving remote branch, and no message says so.

## Reproduction

Ship from a secondary worktree while the base branch is checked out in the primary working tree. This is the normal worktree layout, so it reproduces every time.

1. Primary tree has `main` checked out.
2. Create a worktree on a feature branch, open a PR from it.
3. Run `/land-and-deploy` from the worktree.

`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` merges server-side, then its local cleanup phase runs `git checkout main`, which fails:

```
fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree at /path/to/primary
```

`gh` exits non-zero. The remote branch is never deleted, because `gh` aborts its cleanup after the checkout failure.

## What the skill does right

§4a-postfail (SKILL.md:1496) handles the hard part correctly and should not change:

- The universal invariant fires: query authoritative PR state, never retry `gh pr merge`.
- `state == "MERGED"` is recognized, with the accurate "possibly completed before the local cleanup phase failed" framing.
- The non-destructive candidate-based worktree cleanup at SKILL.md:1511 offers to remove the stale worktree.

This all worked as designed in the run that surfaced this. The gap is only the remote branch.

## The gap

The `state == "MERGED"` branch (SKILL.md:1500 through 1523) covers merge SHA capture and worktree cleanup, then goes straight to §4a. There is no step reconciling the branch deletion that `--delete-branch` was supposed to perform. Compare the success path at SKILL.md:1489, which tells the user "The branch has been cleaned up." On the postfail path that statement would be false, and it is simply not made, so the discrepancy is invisible.

## Suggested fix

In the `state == "MERGED"` branch, after capturing the merge SHA, reconcile the branch:

```bash
gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/<branch>" --silent 2>/dev/null && echo "REMOTE_BRANCH_EXISTS"
```

If it still exists, delete it (or offer to, matching the worktree block's confirm-first posture):

```bash
git push origin --delete <branch>
```

Then adjust the user-facing message so the postfail path states the branch outcome explicitly rather than staying silent about it.

Deleting the local branch has the same problem for the same reason, and is worth covering in the same step.

## Environment

- gstack v1.61.0.0 (commit 94993f7)
- gh version 2.89.0
- Related upstream: cli/cli#3442, cli/cli#13380, already cited at SKILL.md:1496

title: /review Step 2 reads `.claude/skills/review/checklist.md`, a path the installer never creates
body:
## Summary

`/review` Step 2 instructs the agent to read `.claude/skills/review/checklist.md` behind a hard stop, but nothing in the install creates a file at that path. The checklist exists, just somewhere else.

Version 1.60.1.0, macOS, Claude Code.

## What the skill says

`~/.claude/skills/gstack/review/SKILL.md:1095`

```
## Step 2: Read the checklist

Read `.claude/skills/review/checklist.md`.

**If the file cannot be read, STOP and report the error.** Do not proceed without the checklist.
```

## What the install actually looks like

`~/.claude/skills/review/` contains a single symlink and nothing else:

```
SKILL.md -> /Users/<user>/.claude/skills/gstack/review/SKILL.md
```

The real `checklist.md` sits next to the symlink target, in `~/.claude/skills/gstack/review/`, together with `design-checklist.md`, `greptile-triage.md` and `specialists/`. None of those are linked into `~/.claude/skills/review/`.

So neither reading of the path resolves. As `~/.claude/skills/review/checklist.md` it does not exist, because only `SKILL.md` is linked. As a repo-relative `<repo>/.claude/skills/review/checklist.md` it does not exist either, at least not in a repo that has no local gstack checkout.

## Why this looks like a defect rather than a choice

Line 1335 of the same file references its sibling correctly, with an absolute gstack path:

> Use the existing design review checklist at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/review/design-checklist.md`

Two references to two files in the same directory, written two different ways, one of which resolves.

The path is hardcoded in `review/SKILL.md.tmpl:51`, so it is not a failed template substitution. `ship/SKILL.md` carries the same `Read \`.claude/skills/...\`` pattern, so a fix probably wants to cover both.

## Effect

Taken literally, Step 2 aborts every `/review` run. In practice the model usually recovers by searching for the file, so this surfaces as inconsistent behaviour rather than a clean failure, which makes it easy to miss: a hard gate that silently degrades into a soft one.

## Possible fixes

1. Change the reference to the absolute path, matching how `design-checklist.md` is already referenced on line 1335.
2. Or have the installer symlink the sibling files into `~/.claude/skills/review/` alongside `SKILL.md`.

Option 1 looks smaller and matches existing precedent in the file.

title: gstack-gbrain-source-wireup: first sync uses sync --repo without --source, silently repoints the default gbrain source
body:
## Summary

`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` runs `gbrain sync --repo "$WORKTREE"` (line ~325) without `--source "$SOURCE_ID"`. On gbrain 0.46.x, `sync --repo` resolves the sync to the brain's **default** source when the given repo path does not match any registered source's `local_path`, and then **rewrites that default source's `local_path` anchor to the worktree path** (gbrain `sync.ts` `writeSyncAnchor(engine, opts.sourceId, 'repo_path', anchorPath)`).

The result: the pre-existing primary source (e.g. `gbrain-main` pointing at the user's real knowledge repo) is silently repointed at the gstack worktree, and the sync then "heals" pages into the wrong repo. The newly registered gstack source itself never gets a real first sync (0 files).

## Repro

1. Have a gbrain with an existing federated default source `gbrain-main` whose `local_path` is repo A.
2. Run `gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` which registers `gstack-brain-<host>` with a fresh worktree B, then calls `gbrain sync --repo B`.
3. Inspect `sources` table: `gbrain-main.local_path` is now B (wrong), `last_sync_at` updated; worktree B received a normalized copy of a page from repo A's DB state.

Observed on gbrain 0.46.24.0 with gstack latest-stable, macOS, PGLite engine.

## Expected

The wireup helper should sync the **newly registered** source, i.e. `gbrain sync --source "$SOURCE_ID"`, or at minimum assert that the resolved source id equals the one it just registered and abort otherwise.

## Impact

Silent cross-source path corruption on the primary knowledge repo registration. Recoverable (sources remove + re-add with correct path, then `gbrain sync --source`), but only if the operator notices — the helper's own output reports success.

## Suggested fix

- Change the first-sync call to `gbrain sync --source "$SOURCE_ID"` (gbrain CLI supports `--source`), or
- After the sync, verify `sources` row for the new id advanced and the default source's `local_path` was NOT modified; fail loudly otherwise.

Happy to provide full logs if useful.

title: v1.68.3.0 fix(pairing): re-pair to narrow revokes the old grant on the spot
body:
## Why (in your own words)

Tightening a paired browser agent is supposed to be one re-pair away, and it wasn't. `POST /pair` minted a fresh setup key but never touched the agent's live session, so `pair-agent --client codex --restrict read` on an agent that had already connected (or whose new 5-minute key just expired unexchanged) left the original full-access session — `eval` over the tunnel included — alive for up to 24 hours. Two more holes sat next to it: revoke never released tab ownership, so an agent re-paired under a reused name inherited the previous one's authenticated tabs; and because `root` is the sentinel every scope/domain/rate/tab check uses for the omnipotent caller, `--client root` minted a "scoped" token that skipped all enforcement. This change makes a reducing re-pair revoke the old session (and free its tabs) immediately, keeps a broaden/refresh working with no outage, and reserves the `root` client name.

## Live evidence

Before/after against a `BROWSE_HEADLESS_SKIP=1` daemon on each side (same script, `main` at v1.68.2.0 vs this branch). `status` on a valid own-only token that hasn't claimed a tab returns **403** (still a valid token, tab-denied); a **revoked** token returns **401** — so 403→401 is the revoke signal.

```
### BEFORE — main v1.68.2.0
1. paired broad + connected. old-token /command status BEFORE re-pair: 403
2. re-paired --restrict read, WITHOUT exchanging the new key. superseded = undefined
3. old-token /command status AFTER narrowing re-pair: 403   <- still VALID = BUG (wide session survived)
4. shadow-key: narrow re-pair BEFORE connect, then exchange the OLD broad key -> 200   <- BUG (stale broad key live)
5. broaden re-pair, old-token status: 403   (session kept)
6. --client root -> 200   <- BUG (bypass token minted)

### AFTER — fix-pairing-scope-revoke
1. paired broad + connected. old-token /command status BEFORE re-pair: 403
2. re-paired --restrict read, WITHOUT exchanging the new key. superseded = {"tokens_deleted":2,"tabs_released":0}
3. old-token /command status AFTER narrowing re-pair: 401   <- REVOKED = FIXED
4. shadow-key: narrow re-pair BEFORE connect, then exchange the OLD broad key -> 401   <- FIXED (stale key dead)
5. broaden re-pair, old-token status: 403   (session kept, no outage; superseded = undefined)
6. --client root -> 400   <- FIXED (reserved)
```

Targeted regression suite (green on this branch; these tests fail on main):

```
$ bun test browse/test/token-registry.test.ts browse/test/pair-agent-e2e.test.ts \
    browse/test/skill-token.test.ts browse/test/pty-session-lease.test.ts \
    browse/test/server-factory.test.ts browse/test/server-auth.test.ts \
    browse/test/tab-isolation.test.ts
 240 pass  0 fail  716 expect() calls

$ bash browse/scripts/build-node-server.sh
 Node server bundle ready: browse/dist/server-node.mjs   # type/import check clean

$ bun run gen:skill-docs --dry-run                        # zero drift
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `browse/src/token-registry.ts` (ReservedClientIdError + assertValidClientId; revokeSetupKeys/getClientSession/grantReducesAccess), `browse/src/server.ts` (/pair supersede, DELETE /token unconditional tab release, typed 400s), `browse/src/browser-manager.ts` (releaseClientTabs), `browse/src/cli.ts` (--client root fast-fail, supersede notice, no-`--client` hint), regression tests, `pair-agent/SKILL.md(.tmpl)` + `docs/REMOTE_BROWSER_ACCESS.md`, VERSION → 1.68.3.0, CHANGELOG.
- **Verified live by:** the before/after transcript above; 240 targeted tests; node-server bundle build; an adversarial diff-review workflow that surfaced 4 issues (validate-before-revoke regression, an expired-session tab-inheritance gap on `/pair`, and 2 missing tests), all fixed and re-verified.
- **Did NOT test:** the live ngrok tunnel path (needs an authtoken; `TUNNEL_PATHS` unchanged). The full `test:free` suite wasn't run clean locally — this sandbox has no `xvfb`, so headed-browser shards fail for environment reasons unrelated to the diff; the fix's own files are pure token/tab bookkeeping and are fully covered above. Tabs are released on revoke but not closed (the authenticated page stays open, root-only) — deliberate; close-vs-release is deferred.
