title: Deferred review finding: careful/bin/hook-extract.sh:123 — On a POSIX host the shared normalizer rewrites c:/x and C:\x
body:
Filed by /ship's pre-landing review of garrytan/gstack#3758 (head 2034fbb61d8b). The finding is in code that PR did not change, so it was deferred here instead of being fixed there (review scope frozen after pass 1).

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Where:** `careful/bin/hook-extract.sh:123`
- **Finding:** On a POSIX host the shared normalizer rewrites c:/x and C:\x to /c/x on every platform (the #2876 contract, test E1), but Linux and macOS write 'c:/x' as a file named 'c:' under cwd. A POSIX freeze boundary under a one-letter top-level directory (/c/...) therefore allows a drive-letter path that lands outside it. Needs a decision on whether the cross-platform contract should hold on POSIX hosts.

title: fix(design): exits ease out, never ease in
body:
## Summary

The design checklist (`scripts/resolvers/design.ts`, rendered into `/design-review`) and the DESIGN.md template `/design-consultation` writes both tell agents to use ease-in for exits. That puts ease-in on dismissals, menu closes and toast exits. Ease-in starts slow at the moment the user is watching, so the exit reads as lag. This PR switches both to ease-out for exits.

## Evidence

- Emil Kowalski's animation guidance (author of Sonner and Vaul), in his [`animate` skill](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills/blob/main/skills/animate/SKILL.md): the curve table maps "Entering or exiting" to `ease-out`, followed by "Never `ease-in` on UI. It starts slow, delaying the exact moment the user is watching."
- The two sources reinforce each other downstream. A project whose DESIGN.md came from `/design-consultation` carries `exit(ease-in)`, and `/design-review` checks against the same rule, so an exit that lags never gets flagged. I found this auditing a project built with gstack.

## Changes

- `scripts/resolvers/design.ts`: the first Motion & Animation item now says to use ease-out for entering and exiting, to keep exits shorter than entrances, and to flag ease-in on any UI element.
- `design-consultation/sections/proposal-and-preview.md.tmpl`: `exit(ease-in)` becomes `exit(ease-out)`.
- Regenerated `design-review/SKILL.md` and `design-consultation/sections/proposal-and-preview.md` with `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all`.

Left alone on purpose: the repo's own `DESIGN.md:122` (gstack's own design system, your call) and two test fixtures that are recorded captures (`test/fixtures/design-consultation-section-design-md.md`, `test/fixtures/design-md-legacy.md`). No new test, because this is prompt wording no software reads, which the test value bar says not to pin.

## Verification

- `bun run skill:check`: exit 0 (2032 artifacts). With the old `design-review/SKILL.md` planted back, it exits 1 with `STALE: design-review/SKILL.md`.
- `bun run typecheck`: exit 0.
- Focused tests (`design-craft-resolvers`, `gen-skill-docs`, `design-consultation-contract`, `design-consultation-command-contract`, `design-checklist-sync`): 553 pass, 1 fail. The failure (`the extraction recipe prevents the actual CLI automatic DESIGN.md write...`, line 98) fails the same way on a clean `origin/main` at 9514b7609 in my checkout, before the template is read, so it is environmental and unrelated.

title: Deferred review finding: lib/review-exclude.ts:346 — Fix #3 keeps an attribute-binary file through the secret-line rule,
body:
Filed by /ship's pre-landing review of PR #3902 (head 78c09eea9d98). The finding is in code that PR did not change, so it was deferred here instead of being fixed there (review scope frozen after pass 1).

- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Where:** `lib/review-exclude.ts:346`
- **Finding:** Fix #3 keeps an attribute-binary file through the secret-line rule, but readers still cannot see the credential line. reviewExclude now reads those files' added lines with `git diff --text`, so the file gets reason secret-line or code and goes back into the keep pathspecs. readSelection, the only diff gstack-review-dispatch hands readers (bin/gstack-review-dispatch:165), still runs `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff` with no --text, for both the main command and the keep command. Git honours the branch's checked-out .gitattributes there, so every reader gets 'Binary files ... differ' for the kept file. Reproduced in a scratch repo: numstat `-\t-`, the reader-style diff prints 'Binary files differ', and `--text` shows the line. The changelog line 'A branch's .gitattributes cannot hide a credential line' is therefore not true end to end, and the new test checks the classification, not what readers receive. Only the visible .gitattributes hunk itself is left to tip off a reviewer.
- **Suggested fix:** For kept paths that are binary only by attribute (claimed, not in `binary`), have readSelection read them with `--text --no-textconv --no-ext-diff`. Give them their own literal-pathspec command, or put them on the keep command, so real NUL binaries do not flood readers' bytes. Add an assertion that the reader text for the kept file contains the added line. Otherwise, soften the changelog and ship-policy wording to say the file is kept but readers see it as binary.
- **Found by:** red-team

<!-- gstack-deferred-finding: lib/review-exclude.ts:346:red-team -->

**Candidate: do not merge until the GST-1089 measurement passes and GStack Minder confirms the crew behavior change.** This is the after pin for GST-1088. It changes /review's prompts, so the crew no-loss rule applies (2026-10-30). It never boards a train on its own.

## What changed

![/review Step 4: every CRITICAL finding now needs a floor reason and proof, or it is reported as INFORMATIONAL](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/5P7x06BTtFCI36NSg8XlBRyoLKctwiBnbh9eBJvUzoQ.png)

/review Step 4: every CRITICAL finding now needs a floor reason and proof, or it is reported as INFORMATIONAL. The marker paragraph pins the `Dispatching` lines that evals count.

![/investigate drops its learnings search and the investigation learnings log](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/UGdYaYcL8OwkLK_nsEeQqRk31ex9jqfkF2sfmFWx0QE.png)

/investigate drops its learnings search and the investigation learnings log: 21,242 to 17,838 always-loaded bytes against v1.94.24.0.

/investigate loads about 3.4 KB less and /review about 3.3 KB less, and every blocking /review finding must now prove itself.

- **Skill-scoped R56 cuts.** `modules/cuts.json` is a new cut ledger. Each entry is a `part:<skill>/<name>` module id that `gstack-modules list` shows with status `cut`. A cut applies in every loadout, `full` included, and on every host, but only to its own skill. `modules/loadouts.json` is unchanged, so no other skill loses anything. One cut, /review's repo-ownership section, is a preamble piece; `preambleSections()` drops it for /review alone. The rest are deleted from the two templates.
- **/review blocker proof (plan decision 5, CREW rule 23).** A CRITICAL finding gets a floor reason (`fails a test`, `breaks production`, `loses data or secrets`, or one of the Sideways sweep's forced-CRITICAL classes) and proof: a repro with its output, a failing test, or a cited `file:line` with its consequence. /review verifies a forwarded finding (specialist, QA, adversarial or bot) and appends both itself, so the pinned reviewer briefs don't change. A CRITICAL nobody proves is INFORMATIONAL at Step 5, whatever its `Blocks:` line. The rule is in the Step 4 critical pass and in the review-only branch of the pre-emit verification gate (`scripts/resolvers/confidence.ts`).
- **Fixed dispatch lines.** Specialist selection always prints one `Dispatching N specialists:` line, small diffs included, and the native adversarial pass prints `Dispatching adversarial pass: native` before its Agent call. These are for eval counting. The `adversarial-pass` contract item stays gated by `match` alone, exactly as on main. This PR adds no `marker:` to the frontmatter and doesn't touch the contract resolver. `review/sections/review-army.md`, `review/sections/adversarial.md` and their resolvers are unchanged, so the pinned reviewer briefs and /ship keep their bytes.
- **Ratchet.** `test/cut-ledger.test.ts` fails when a cut piece comes back in its skill, its sections or the shared preamble file on any host, when a pinned size moves, when a cut names a skill other than /investigate or /review, or when review-only text shows up in any other skill.

## Why

Opus 5.5 read these skills in full and still skipped their required steps (Run D, gstack-evals#140). The forced full /review caught 67.2% of blocking bugs but raised 2.71 false blockers per PR per pass (gstack-evals#120). The cuts take out text that nothing measured shows is doing work. The blocker-proof rule targets the false-blocker rate. GST-1089 (GEVA-214) decides whether either one keeps.

## Blast radius

**Durable scope test.** `test/cut-ledger.test.ts` renders every host twice, once from the tree and once from a copy whose `modules/cuts.json` has no cuts, and asserts that every file outside the investigate and review trees is byte-identical. As a negative control, a cut added to the office-hours preamble failed it on all 12 non-Claude hosts. A second test checks that no preamble cut comes back through the shared `sections/preamble.md` on any host. As its negative control, appending `## Repo Ownership` to `review/sections/preamble.md` failed it.

**Pins** (all lowered to measured at 9386a27, no headroom):
- `modules/cuts.json:72-73`: investigate 17838, review 56716.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts:493`: /review `maxSkeletonBytes` 60,014 to 56,716. `:496`: `maxSizeRatio` 1.3283 to 1.2979 (140,849 / 108,523 = 1.29788). `:898`: /investigate `minUnionBytes` 55,000 to 54,778.
- `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json:9-55`: nine `*/gstack-review` pins lowered to measured. The values are agy 101,780, codex 100,964, copilot 101,398, cursor 119,875, factory 122,253, gemini 101,225, kiro 119,713, opencode 120,462 and slate 119,794.
- Fixed caps unchanged: the 5,315-token context budget, DRIVER.md 12,288 B (now 12,245), the global skeleton cap of 61,420 (`carve-guards.ts:164`), module size 800 and PART_MAX 24,576.

**Sibling trial merges (CREW rule 25 with the 2026-11-03 addendum), at 9386a27:**
- **#3837 at 95437450:** only `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` conflicts, and `docs/skills.md` merges cleanly. The resolution keeps this PR's review and investigate pins and #3837's other pins. On the merged tree, `bun run typecheck` exits 0 and 49 focused test files ran 1,766 tests with no failures. Sizes are unchanged: review 56,716, investigate 17,838, ratio 1.29788.
- **Lane B bin-path, #3957 at 3129fe82:** `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` and the allowlist conflict, because both PRs re-pin the same lines. The resolution takes this PR's side and re-pins up to the combined measurement. That gives review 56,772 and investigate 17,894 (both +56 bytes), ratio 1.2984 (140,905 / 108,523 = 1.29839) and every `*/gstack-review` allowlist pin +24. On the merged tree, `bun run typecheck` exits 0, `gen:skill-docs` is fresh, and 44 focused test files ran 1,668 tests with no failures. title: /codex: the filesystem boundary's bare `agents/` makes Codex skip a repository's own agents/ folder
body:
## What happens

The filesystem boundary that /codex puts in front of every `codex exec` prompt (codex/SKILL.md, "Filesystem Boundary") reads:

> IMPORTANT: Do NOT read or execute any files under ~/.claude/, ~/.agents/, .claude/skills/, or agents/. ...

The first three entries are the skill install paths. The last one, `agents/`, is relative to the repository, so it also matches a repository's own `agents/` folder when that folder is reviewed code (for example a repo that keeps agent prompt files in `agents/` and tests them).

Seen on v1.91.162.0 (the text is unchanged in v1.91.350.0), Codex consult mode, reviewing a diff that changed `agents/planner.md`:

- Codex left the changed `agents/planner.md` out of its review.
- It wrapped the repo's documentation test suites in a read guard, and the suites that read `agents/` were blocked (4 of 12 in one run; 3 of 3 that read it in a later run whose diff didn't touch `agents/` at all).
- Its verdict was "Can't verify".

It isn't consistent: an earlier run in the same session, with the same boundary, ran all 12 suites. The workaround is one extra sentence in the task text saying the repository's `agents/` folder is reviewed code and may be read.

## Expected

The boundary keeps Codex out of skill definitions without hiding repository content that happens to share the folder name.

## Suggestion

Name the exact install paths the boundary protects (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, and the generated `agents/openai.yaml` it already names), not a bare `agents/`. Or add a sentence saying the reviewed repository's own folders are always readable. A test prompt for a repo with an `agents/` folder in its diff would pin it.

title: Plan-review task lists never close: /ship and /land-and-deploy don't mark shipped tasks done
body:
## What happened

`/plan-ceo-review`, `/plan-eng-review` and `/plan-design-review` write an Implementation Tasks list to `~/.gstack/projects/<slug>/tasks-<phase>-*.jsonl` (via `bin/gstack-tasks add`). Nothing else ever reads those lists back or closes them.

On my machine, after about two months of normal use across 6 projects:

- 54 task list files, 584 task rows, 512 unique titles
- 383 of the 584 are P1
- disposition rows (`done` / `dropped`) exist in only one project, and only because the same review happened to be rerun on the same branch

Many of those P1s shipped weeks ago. Their lists still show them as open, so the lists can't answer "what's left?" at all.

On origin/main (1.94.15.0) the code does this:

- `bin/gstack-tasks` and `lib/tasks-prior.ts` are the only writers. `git grep task-dispositions` finds writers only and no readers.
- `/ship` Step 14 item 4 ("Detect completed TODOs", ship/SKILL.md.tmpl:338) already moves proven completions in TODOS.md to Completed. It doesn't do the same for the review's task list.
- A review rerun forces the agent to re-decide every task from the previous list (lib/tasks-prior.ts:111-113). It doesn't check whether a task was already closed. So a task closed elsewhere comes back on the next rerun.
- Lists written before a repo existed (branch `unknown`/`none`) never match a later branch, so they never get reconciled.

Expected: a task the review wrote should close when the work that finishes it merges.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `/plan-eng-review` on a plan; it writes `tasks-eng-review-<branch>-<ts>.jsonl`.
2. Implement task T1 and run `/ship`, then `/land-and-deploy`.
3. T1 is still open in the task list, and no disposition row was written. The only way to close it is to rerun the same review on the same branch.

## Proposed fix (no new skill)

I read #1343 and its closing note on skill-list cost, so this proposal adds no skill. It only extends `bin/gstack-tasks` and two existing skill steps:

- `gstack-tasks open [--all-projects] [--json]`: open tasks = non-superseded rows minus closed ones, across all branches of a project.
- `gstack-tasks close` / `sweep`: append disposition rows using the format `add` already writes, plus `pending` (with a repo-qualified PR) and `reopened`.
- `/ship`, next to Step 14 item 4: tasks named in a `Task: <run_id>/<id>` commit trailer (same style as the existing `Fixes: #<n>` trailer) become `pending` on that PR. Other closures the agent proposes need confirmation, and uncertain ones stay open, mirroring the TODOS.md rule.
- `/land-and-deploy`: after a verified merge, `sweep` turns `pending` into `done`. A PR closed unmerged reopens its tasks. A Step 8 rollback reopens the tasks that PR closed.
- Task identity follows `carried_from` back to the first ref, so a carried task stays one task. Readers replay rows through a small transition table and ignore rows that are illegal at that point, so concurrent runs can't overwrite a newer decision. No locks.
- `prior` treats closed and pending tasks as already decided (fixes the rerun re-ask).

All of it lands in one new `lib/tasks-lifecycle.ts` behind the existing bin, with a table-driven test, plus the two template steps with their goldens, a gate-tier E2E and a `changelog.d` fragment.

I'm happy to send the PR if this direction works for you. If you'd rather solve it differently, or you think it isn't needed, I'd like to know before I write it.

## Readiness report

Not an install problem: the behavior above comes from reading origin/main at 1.94.15.0, so I left the doctor output out. (My install is on 1.94.15.0. Its doctor fails on the unrelated macOS bash 3.2 parse error already tracked in #3601.)

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.317
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.2.0)

Closes the gap described in #3924.

## What changed

The `Filesystem boundary` that `/codex` puts in front of every `codex exec` prompt named a bare `agents/` next to the skill install paths:

```
> IMPORTANT: Do NOT read or execute any files under ~/.claude/, ~/.agents/, .claude/skills/, or agents/.
```

That last entry is relative to the working directory, so it also matched a *reviewed repository's* own `agents/` folder. title: fix(free-ci-health): a split shard's overrun compares wall time with its per-job prediction (#3851)
body:
Closes the gap described in #3851.

## What changed

`--ci-verify`'s shard-overrun warning compared two different units. `plan.shards[].predictedMs` is the shard's **serial** seed sum (the packing load), while `outcome.elapsedMs` is the shard's **wall** clock. At `--shard-jobs k` the k sub-shards run in parallel and `mergeSubShardOutcomes` records the group's wall time, so a healthy shard finishes in about `predictedMs / k`. At k=4 the 1.5x factor therefore only fired after roughly a 6x slowdown, and the signal was blind exactly where shard splitting is used.

- `shardOverruns` takes an optional `jobs` and measures `elapsedMs` against `predictedMs / max(1, jobs)`.
- `ciHealthSummary` passes the plan shard's `jobs` through, so the `--ci-verify` job summary uses the same wall expectation.
- `overrunWarning` names the parallel job count, so the number it prints is the wall time it compared. k=1 output is byte-identical.
- `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` states the wall-time rule next to the 1.5x / 30 s thresholds.

No behavior change when a plan has no `jobs` (k=1), which is the default and every plan written before `--shard-jobs`.

## Verification

```
bun test test/free-seed-ratchet.test.ts   # 12 pass — two new cases: k=4 warns at 1.6x wall, stays quiet at 1.2x
bun test test/shard-jobs.test.ts test/test-free-shards.test.ts test/free-tests-workflow-wiring.test.ts   # 126 pass
bun run typecheck                          # clean
bun run typecheck:test                     # 812 known diagnostics, none new
```

The new cases fix the reported failure mode: a 400 s serial seed over 4 parallel jobs that takes 160 s (1.6x its 100 s wall prediction) now warns, where before it needed 600 s.

`--ci-verify`'s shard-overrun warning now measures a shard's wall time against its seed prediction divided by the shard's parallel job count. `shardOverruns` and `overrunWarning` in `scripts/lib/free-ci-health.ts` use `predictedMs / jobs`, `ciHealthSummary` passes the plan shard's `jobs` through, and the warning says `across N parallel jobs` when k > 1. No network, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies are touched. ## Credit Rewritten on main from @indraoverflow's #4051 (read as text only, not checked out), credited with a Co-authored-by trailer on 5e2964d. ## Tests Two new cases in `test/free-seed-ratchet.test.ts`: `shardOverruns` at jobs = 1 and jobs = 4 (written first; the jobs = 4 case failed on main), and `ciHealthSummary` carrying a plan's jobs = 4. The full free suite is carried from CI run 42249997890/1 (1613 files). Locally the three focused files were green, `bun run typecheck` was clean, and `bun run typecheck:test` showed no new diagnostics against the baseline. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch capy/gst-1653-shard-overrun-jobs. ## Summary A split CI shard is now judged against the share of the seed it actually runs, so a stale duration seed shows up in the job summary again. One commit (5e2964d) changes the comparison, its message, two tests and one docs sentence, plus a changelog.d fragment. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage (deterministic map: the one changed runtime file has a changed test naming it). Two new cases in `test/free-seed-ratchet.test.ts`: `shardOverruns` at jobs = 1 and jobs = 4 (the jobs = 4 case failed on main), and `ciHealthSummary` carrying a plan's jobs = 4. Tests ran: free 1613 (files, carried from CI run 42249997890/1) ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=0 fixed=0 scope=frozen ledgers_read=2 dispatches=1 est_input_tokens=2735 Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Outside review: completed (openai/gpt-6.1-sol as host subagent): approve with a follow-up, nothing blocking. Native adversarial (claude-opus-5-5): ship as-is. ## Review notes None of these would fail a test, break production or lose data or secrets, so under the crew's blocking floor they ship as notes and were not fixed in this PR. - **Expected wall time assumes balanced, fully parallel sub-shards** (`scripts/lib/free-ci-health.ts:36`; red-team, adversarial and outside voice agree). `assignSubShards` packs whole files into k groups and runs `SLOW_UNDER_LOAD` files in a trailing serial sub-shard, so the true floor is the largest packed group plus the serial tail, not sum/k. Today `SLOW_UNDER_LOAD` is empty and `TREE_MUTATING` files sit in the exclusive k = 1 shard; on the real seed at 10 shards x 4 jobs each shard's largest group matches sum/4, so a seed-accurate run raises no false warning. A very imbalanced shard (for example one 60 s file plus three 1 s files) or a future `SLOW_UNDER_LOAD` entry would warn falsely. Follow-up: carry a per-shard expected wall time in the plan at `--ci-plan` time from the same packer plus the serial sum. - **k comes from the plan, not the result** (`ciHealthSummary`). It runs before `verifyFreeCiResults` rejects a result whose `jobs` disagrees with the plan, so only the diagnostic of an already-failing run can be misleading. Follow-up: use the result's `jobs`. - **Runner contention may make the 4-job threshold noisy** (investigate). If four sandboxed children run more than about 50% slower per file than the seed recording, every shard would warn. Unmeasured here; compare one recent free-suite run's shard `elapsedMs` with sum/4. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `shardOverruns`/`overrunWarning` (2 probes, both pass, verdict pass): a 4-job shard at 160 s vs 100 s warns with `across 4 parallel jobs` while 140 s does not; `jobs: 0` and a missing `jobs` fall back to serial with no divide-by-zero, the 30 s floor still applies, and a 40 s shard split 4 ways that takes 40 s warns. Limits: `ciHealthSummary` end to end is covered by the committed unit test, not probed; the serial tail was not probed (`SLOW_UNDER_LOAD` is empty). ## Issues Fixes #3851 Refs #4051 ## Verification Results No plan is bound to this branch, so there are no Step 8.1 obligations to verify. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Scope:** the committed diff against 8d7091ac (the free-CI shard-overrun prediction now accounts for split shards). Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. **Result:** current. `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` already says that a shard split by `--shard-jobs k` is predicted as its serial seed sum divided by k, which matches `scripts/lib/free-ci-health.ts`. No other doc covers this behavior. **Debt:** none. ## Test plan - [x] `bun run test` (free lane): carried from CI run 42249997890/1 at tree b51619a4dd6f, 1613 files - [x] `gstack-pregate --allow-repo-commands`: pass (secrets, strays, literals, timing, guards typecheck/module-size/conflict-markers, 24 of 24 selected files reused from the CI run) - [x] `bun test test/free-seed-ratchet.test.ts test/shard-jobs.test.ts test/test-free-shards.test.ts`: green before /ship (focused files, all cases); `bun run typecheck` clean

title: fix(ship-queue): keep land's merged checks out of the checkout's git config and hooks (GST-1747)
body:
**Parked.** This PR is parked at 59b7b26 by the Captain's ruling; GST-1766 continues from this branch.

## What changed

- `gstack-ship-queue land --pin --allow-repo-commands` records the guarded git paths of the checkout before `land.merged_checks` run: `config`, `config.worktree`, `hooks/`, `commondir` and `gitdir` in the checkout's git directories, the checkout's `.git` entry, and every hop of a symlink among them.
- When a check changed or added any of them, land restores nothing. It refuses with `QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS` and names each changed path. It makes no further git call in the checkout, so it does not merge, remove the worktree or push the lock release, and the land lock stays held. The `LOCK:` line names the release command: once the named paths are restored from a trusted copy (or an added hook is deleted), `gstack-ship-queue land --pr <n> --pin <sha>` without `--allow-repo-commands` refuses with `REPO_COMMANDS_NOT_ALLOWED` and releases the lock without running the checks.
- Land's own `rev-parse HEAD` and `status` in the merged tree now run with the checks' scrubbed environment, before the after-snapshot, followed by a stray-process sweep on Linux.
- `lib/ship-queue-gate`'s `git()`, the runner behind every queue, lock, notes and train call, runs with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false` through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, appended after any count the caller already sets.
- docs/ship-policy.md#land-direct, docs/troubleshooting.md and the docs/captain.md result table describe the refusal and the release step.

## Why

The merged checks run with a scrubbed environment (GST-1421) so land's tokens never reach repo commands, but they share the checkout's `.git` through the worktree, and land's later git calls run with its full environment. Land now stops instead of trusting a git directory the checks changed, and leaves the lock held so a person checks the checkout before any further git call there.

## Blast radius

- Only `land` with `--allow-repo-commands` on a moved base takes the snapshot. A merged check that writes the shared `.git/config` or installs a hook now stops land and holds the lock until someone restores the paths and runs the release command.
- Every `gstack-ship-queue` git call stops running hooks and fsmonitor.
- The same-user residual is documented and not sandboxed. The checks run as land's user, so they can still write the linked `node_modules`, other files in the checkout, the user's global git config and directories on `PATH`, and on macOS read land's starting environment through `ps -E`. Pass `--allow-repo-commands` only for PRs you trust to run.

## Approvals

Approved: yes (record r-32e4bf46e427). The full approval record stays private: this repository is public or its visibility is unknown.

## Test Coverage

- Changed tests in test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts: a check that changes hooks and config is refused with each path named, runs no hook and pushes no lock release, and the release command frees the lock without running the checks; a hook under the checkout's `core.hooksPath` never runs and land still merges; a repointed `commondir` is refused with the lock held; a repointed middle link of a symlinked `.git/config` chain is detected.
- Focused at the final code: test/gstack-clean-producers, gstack-ship-policy, gstack-ship-queue, land-direct-recovery-isolation and ship-queue-land-direct, 107 pass, 0 fail; typecheck clean; module-size ratchet and conflict-marker checks pass. CI is the full run.

## Pre-Landing Review

Pass 1 (specialists, red-team) found 4 issues, all fixed. Pass 2 found 3 blocking issues in the fix round, all fixed. Step 11's voices (adversarial-native, outside voice gpt-6.1-sol, targeted) found 3 blocking issues in the restore code; the granted fix-check round replaced the restore with the refusal above. The fix-check found one blocking issue, which the owner ruled a disclosed note (below).

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=8 deferred=0 noted=6 fixed=10 scope=frozen unbound=3 ledgers_read=4 fix_checks=1 dispatches=8

Ruled note: lib/land-merged-checks.ts:62:fix-check at d8efd242bb1d ruled by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36), 2026-11-07 at 2026-11-07T08:11:29.416Z: ships as a disclosed note: a checkout whose .git is reached through a symlink chain is not re-located after the checks; GST-1766 moves merged-tree checks to a separate clone (approval a-0530ca53a87c)

Gate edits: 3 listed, 2 read, 0 findings — 0 kept, 0 restored, 0 open

Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol (outside voice) reviewed; its two blocking findings were resolved by the fix-check round.

## Review notes

- A checkout whose `.git` is reached through a symlink chain is not re-located after the checks (ruled note above; GST-1766 follows up by running the checks in a separate clone).
- Files pulled in through `[include]` or `includeIf` in the checkout's config are not among the guarded paths.
- On macOS, a stray process a check leaves running is not swept, so it can change the config after the snapshot.
- The `QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS` `fix:` text still says to merge main and push, which does not match the hold-and-inspect detail for changed git paths.
- The release command assumes the earlier land checks still pass, and its line does not mention `--break-lock`.
- No test covers a FIFO among the guarded paths.
- `git()`'s global hooks-off setting also skips the managed pre-push guard on train, stamp and notes pushes; whether to scope it to land is a design question for the Captain.
- A same-content hard-link swap of a guarded file is not detected.
- `refs/replace` in the shared object store was already reachable before this PR.
- A refused land leaves a stale worktree registration until `git worktree prune`.

## Issues

**Status:** updated. Two downstream docs now describe land's git-directory guard.

**Scope:** the 6 selected committed files (base 5862765..d8efd242): lib/land-merged-checks.ts, lib/ship-queue-gate.ts, lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts, docs/ship-policy.md, changelog.d/capy-gst-1747-land-git-dir.md, test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts.

title: ship: base_merge leaves a clean moved base unmerged on merge-queue repos (GST-1772)
body: /ship Step 3 currently merges origin/ into the branch whenever the base has moved, even when nothing conflicts. A repo that lands through a merge queue (qm, on GitHub's) gets nothing from that merge, since the queue tests the exact merge commit anyway. What the merge does do is change the head, restart CI and the PR's report, and, on a stack, force a merge-up through every child (qm #3186, #2878). - **New policy key `base_merge: auto | on-conflict | always`** (default `auto`). Under `on-conflict`, or under `auto` when `gh api graphql` reports a `mergeQueue` on the base branch, Step 3 checks the moved base with `git merge-tree`. If it merges cleanly, Step 3 leaves it unmerged: `MERGE: skipped (origin/ is N commit(s) ahead and merges clean; …)`. A conflict still merges and stops as before. When `auto` can't tell (a local origin, or a failed or empty gh answer) or merge-tree fails, Step 3 merges and a `BASE_MERGE:` line says why. - **finish recheck.** The release commit (a claim-at-open VERSION or CHANGELOG write) can make a skipped base conflict. `gstack-ship-release finish` rechecks any head that lacks origin/ against a fresh `fetch --refmap=`, so origin/ doesn't move, and stops with the conflicted files if the base no longer merges. - **Receipt.** An optional `base_merge: { base, behind, mergeable }` is written whenever the receipt's head lacks origin/. - **Preflight warning.** `ORIGIN_HEAD:` warns when the local refs/remotes/origin/HEAD names neither the base nor the remote's default branch. Fix: `git remote set-head origin --auto`. Plan approved by Garry ("Do it", via GStack Minder) on autoplan run autoplan-20261107090351. Unchanged: how gstack itself lands (stamp-at-merge still never merges at Step 3), and the land and merged-tree checks.

title: Close and sweep shipped plan-review tasks across reruns (#3943)
body:
Closes shipped plan-review tasks when a pull request merges and sweeps prior-run task files during reruns so completed items do not remain stuck in todo state. This keeps task lists accurate across review and deploy workflows.

## Details
- **Disposition reader & lifecycle transitions (`lib/tasks-lifecycle.ts`)**: Follow `carried_from` back to the root `<run_id>/<id>` identity and replay `task-dispositions-<phase>-*.jsonl` in chronological order (`timestamp`, filename, line order) so a later transition (`done`, `dropped`) overrides an earlier `todo` record. Added `closeShippedRunTasks` and `sweepShippedTasksFromGitHistory`.
- **CLI (`bin/gstack-tasks-lifecycle`)**: Added `close-shipped` and `sweep-shipped` subcommands and wired `sweep-shipped` into `extract` before carrying forward prior runs.
- **Skill templates (`ship/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `land-and-deploy/SKILL.md.tmpl`)**: Close shipped tasks when landing or shipping a pull request.
- **Tests (`test/tasks-lifecycle.test.ts`)**: Added unit tests covering chronological disposition override, closing shipped tasks across `carried_from` chains, and sweeping shipped tasks from git history.

Fixes #3943

title: fix(pr-shots): resolve the real base for before-images (#3733)
body: ## Why (in your own words) A clone whose local `origin/HEAD` names the pushed feature branch makes `gstack-pr-shots --path` read that feature head as its own before-image. Committed PR changes then disappear from the comparison: with no extra uncommitted edit, both sides are identical and generation refuses with `PR_SHOTS_IDENTICAL`. Use the real resolved base branch and its merge base with HEAD, so the comparison includes the committed PR changes. **Fixes #3733.** The shared default-base work from #3718/#3795 landed earlier, but #3718 explicitly deferred this pr-shots consumer. This does not duplicate that completed resolver work. > Validation status: full free CI passed on the final head `daa6a2400` (29 checks passed, 14 skipped; [Free Tests run](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42424544313)). 96 focused checks also pass locally, including the push-guard test that failed CI on the intermediate commit `d883966ec` (explained below). The selected paid lane remains pending: fork PRs skip the eval jobs, and skipped jobs are not passes. One local real-browser case was filtered out because of the host's sandbox restriction; it receives no pass credit. ### Why this shape The existing `gate-diff/git` helpers already implement the common default-base policy, remote-tracking precedence and merge-base calculation. Reusing them removes the separate raw `origin/HEAD` loop without introducing another resolver or a production test seam. The shared selector deliberately keeps naming a stale remote HEAD (a missing branch, or history HEAD does not share), so the gates refuse instead of guessing a base; `test/ship-release.test.ts` pins that for the push guard. pr-shots only renders a before/after image, so when the shared default is unusable it falls back to `main` as its old loop did, then `master`. That fallback lives in `lib/pr-shots.ts`, not in the shared resolver. CONTRIBUTING's wave process prefers the smaller change when two PRs solve the same thing. This is four files: one pr-shots production fix, existing-owner regressions, a CLI help correction and a changelog fragment. Fine to absorb into a wave. ### What it does - Resolves the real base when local `origin/HEAD` incorrectly points at the feature branch, including a non-main default. - Keeps the branch fork point rather than using the base's latest tip. - Prefers the remote-tracking base over a stale local branch. - Falls back to `main` (as pr-shots did before), then `master`, when local `origin/HEAD` names a missing branch or unrelated history. - Preserves explicit `--base`, local-only repository behavior and structured missing-base refusal. - Adds nine Git-fixture cases to existing `test/pr-shots.test.ts`, not a new standalone test file. - Updates the CLI help to describe the resolved-base default. ### What it deliberately does not do - No browser selection, rendering, layout, installation or sandbox changes. No captured file content is executed. - No new public exports, flags, dependencies or generated files. - No change to the shared `lib/default-base.ts` resolver, so the gates keep refusing a stale `origin/HEAD`. No new remote writes, fetch/merge policy or competing base resolver. The existing resolver's bounded PR-base/remote-HEAD metadata reads remain its own behavior. - No `VERSION`, package-version, released `CHANGELOG.md`, README or ETHOS edits. Release documentation is one entry-text-only branch fragment. - No `/ship` workflow changes or manual release stamp; the repository's merge/release process assigns the version. ## Live evidence Bun 1.4.2 on Linux. The reproductions use existing local Git-fixture helpers, a local bare origin and the real `defaultBase`, `pathSides` and `buildPage` functions. The remote's real default remains main; only the working clone's local origin/HEAD is changed. No browser, live model or GitHub service is needed by the fixtures. ### Feature-branch `origin/HEAD` (the reported bug) Before the production edit, the diagnostic fixture printed: ```text REMOTE DEFAULT ref: refs/heads/main HEAD MISPOINTED LOCAL origin/HEAD: isFeatureHead=true isRealBase=false before="feature\n" after="feature\n" result=PR_SHOTS_IDENTICAL CONTROL origin/HEAD=main: isFeatureHead=false isRealBase=true before="before\n" after="feature\n" result=comparison generated ``` Those fields are the recorded fixture result with ephemeral SHAs omitted. The original production module was unchanged between the initial base and refreshed `5f9b7ef20`. The new owner-test cases also failed before the production edit: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/pr-shots.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'default base' ... (fail) default base > a local origin/HEAD naming feature still compares against main [231.79ms] ... (fail) default base > a local origin/HEAD naming feature still compares against develop [213.19ms] ... (fail) default base > a moved remote base still compares from the branch fork point, not its tip [265.56ms] ... (fail) default base > a self-referential remote HEAD with no resolvable base does not fall back to itself [267.19ms] 3 pass 11 filtered out 4 fail 16 expect() calls Ran 7 tests across 1 file. [1445.00ms] ``` After the fix, the same mispointed-HEAD production-function scenario returned: ```json { "localRemoteHead": "origin/feature", "choseRealBase": true, "choseFeatureHead": false, "before": "before\n", "after": "feature\n", "result": "comparison generated" } ``` The branch was then fast-forwarded to current main at `5f9b7ef20`, with the patch verified byte-identical before and after the refresh. ### Stale `origin/HEAD` (found in review) Review of the first commit found a second case: when local `origin/HEAD` names a missing branch or unrelated history, the shared selector still names it, so pr-shots refused where its old loop fell back to `origin/main`. The two new cases failed before the fallback: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/pr-shots.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'an unusable origin/HEAD' --timeout=30000 ... Received: { code: "PR_SHOTS_INPUT_NOT_FOUND", message: "no merge base with the resolved base branch; pass --base ", } ... (fail) default base > an unusable origin/HEAD (dangling) falls back to main [239.65ms] ... (fail) default base > an unusable origin/HEAD (unrelated) falls back to main [223.56ms] 0 pass 18 filtered out 2 fail 4 expect() calls Ran 2 tests across 1 file. [553.00ms] ``` The first attempt at that fix, `d883966ec`, changed the shared resolver instead. CI caught that the push guard relies on the resolver to refuse a dangling `origin/HEAD`; the same failure reproduces locally: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/ship-release.test.ts --timeout=30000 --test-name-pattern 'a base that exists on origin but is not fetched' ... Expected substring or pattern: /^GUARDS: refused / Received: "GUARDS: fail (regen no registry (origin/main@9565de98536f (no .gstack/generated.json)); guards 1 guard(s) failed: housekeeping)" ... (fail) push: the pre-push housekeeping guards (GST-1138) > a base that exists on origin but is not fetched, a mistyped --base, a dangling origin/HEAD and an unreadable policy stop the push [2671.80ms] ``` `daa6a2400` restores `lib/default-base.ts` byte-for-byte and keeps the fallback in pr-shots. The whole push-guard file passes again: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/ship-release.test.ts --timeout=30000 23 pass 0 fail 200 expect() calls Ran 23 tests across 1 file. [70.03s] ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** four files, +142/-11 against `main` at `5f9b7ef20`: `lib/pr-shots.ts`, `test/pr-shots.test.ts`, the existing CLI's help line, and `changelog.d/fix-3733-pr-shots-default-base.md`. No VERSION, released CHANGELOG or generated-file changes. Three commits: the second (`d883966ec`) fails the push-guard test on its own, and the third reverts its shared-resolver change, so the series is meant to be squashed. - **Verified live by:** the failed-before/working-after runs above; full free CI on `daa6a2400` (29 passed, 14 skipped); 96 focused tests on the final head; strict product typecheck; test-type ratchet (812 known diagnostics, none new); CLI help; changelog prose lint; `git diff --check`; exact staged-diff redaction scans with zero findings. - **Did NOT test:** the full free suite locally (it passed in CI), the selected paid lane, native Windows/macOS execution, or a full `/ship` review/verification run. The one filtered real-browser capture case was not run locally. No browser sandbox override or global tool change was used. Focused checks on the final head, under Bun 1.4.2 with `umask 022`, `LC_ALL=C` and isolated `HOME`, `GSTACK_HOME` and `TMPDIR`: | Check | Pass | Filtered | Fail | |---|---:|---:|---:| | pr-shots owner cases: base selection, comparison, browser-free CLI | 19 | 1 | 0 | | `test/ship-release.test.ts`, including the dangling-`origin/HEAD` push-guard refusal | 23 | 0 | 0 | | Shared resolver and gate-diff CLI: `test/default-base.test.ts`, `test/gate-diff-cli.test.ts` | 38 | 0 | 0 | | Test-layout, subprocess-timeout and egress-wiring guards | 16 | 0 | 0 | | **Total** | **96** | **1** | **0** | The commands were: ```bash bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/pr-shots.test.ts --timeout=30000 --test-name-pattern 'default base|diff and hunks|path mode|working-tree fingerprint|secret in a capture|outside the repository' bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/ship-release.test.ts --timeout=30000 bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/default-base.test.ts test/gate-diff-cli.test.ts --timeout=30000 bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/test-of-test-ratchet.test.ts test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts test/egress-receipt-wiring.test.ts --timeout=30000 ``` The paid selector is intentionally reported, not reduced: the shared pr-shots references reach 252 registered cases. For this four-file diff, the PR profile selects **108 paid behaviors**, no dedicated quality judges, and defers **144 broad behaviors** to scheduled/release coverage. None of those unrun cases receives pass credit. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface). - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff; source and existing owner tests are changed, with no generated outputs needed. - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references. - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked: N/A. - [x] Linked issue and reproduction: #3733. ## Test plan - [x] Reproduce the wrong before-image and PR_SHOTS_IDENTICAL with a committed/pushed feature change. - [x] Show the new cases fail before the fix, then pass after it. - [x] Cover main/develop defaults, normal-head and explicit-base controls, a moved base, stale local base, local-only fallback and unresolved self-reference. - [x] Cover a dangling or unrelated `origin/HEAD` falling back to `main`, with the shared resolver unchanged so the push guard still refuses that case. - [x] Refresh to current main at `5f9b7ef20` while preserving the patch byte-for-byte. - [x] Rerun focused checks on the final head: 96 pass, 1 filtered, 0 fail. - [x] Run product typecheck and the test-type debt ratchet. - [x] Check CLI help, changelog prose, whitespace and outgoing-diff redaction. - [x] Complete full free acceptance on this PR's head (CI on `daa6a2400`: 29 passed, 14 skipped). - [ ] Complete required selected paid coverage or record maintainer-run fork-PR coverage. - [ ] Complete remaining shipping reviews/verification before merging. Fork PRs do not receive upstream eval secrets. Skipped paid CI jobs are not passes; a maintainer must run the required paid coverage on an upstream branch before merge. Broad-profile deferrals remain scheduled/release coverage, not PR passes. Fixes #3733.

title: Move the tools only Capy crews use into a crew/ folder (GST-1833)
body:
Moves the tools that only Capy crews use to merge and release gstack into a `crew/` folder, along with their tests. Nothing changes for anyone who installs gstack, so the public install stays small and fast for outside users. **Do not land before the scheduled stable cut on Sun 2026-11-08 14:00Z finishes.** This PR moves files the release path runs (`weekly-release.yml`, `release-gate.yml`, the release-cut script and the release-gate command). ## What changed ![Capy-crew-only commands and modules move from bin/, lib/ and scripts/ into crew/](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/fbO_0ndR7qMkhyWiup1W1f37ephAxuqWVDhCyoewMoQ.png) Capy-crew-only commands and modules move from `bin/`, `lib/` and `scripts/` into `crew/`, so the public tree holds only what outside users run.
Before/after as text: Capy-crew-only commands and modules move from bin/, lib/ and scripts/ into crew/ ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output $ ls bin/gstack-release-gate bin/gstack-coauthor-trailers lib/ship-queue-train.ts scripts/release-cut.ts +cannot access 'bin/gstack-release-gate': No such file or directory +cannot access 'bin/gstack-coauthor-trailers': No such file or directory +cannot access 'lib/ship-queue-train.ts': No such file or directory +cannot access 'scripts/release-cut.ts': No such file or directory -bin/gstack-coauthor-trailers -bin/gstack-release-gate -lib/ship-queue-train.ts -scripts/release-cut.ts $ ls crew +README.md bin docs lib scripts test -(no crew/ folder on main) ~~~
- 43 modules and their 26 test files moved: `gstack-release-gate` and `gstack-coauthor-trailers` to `crew/bin/`; the merge-train and wave modules, release gate, release cut and cadence, gate-cost reports and the train and backstop eval scripts to `crew/lib/`, `crew/scripts/` and `crew/test/`. - The Captain guides now live in `crew/docs/`. The old paths `docs/captain.md` and `docs/recommended-harness.md` keep a one-line pointer. - `gstack-flaky`, `lib/flaky-run.ts` and `lib/factory-scorecard.ts` stay public, because `docs/flaky.md` tells outside users to run `bin/gstack-flaky`. - Every free test run still runs every crew test. The earlier plan to skip crew tests when a pull request leaves `crew/` alone was taken out of this PR and comes back in a later one. ## Why Garry approved keeping the crew tools in this repo under `crew/` and loading them only on Capy machines, so everyone else gets gstack without them. This PR does the move with no behavior change. Later phases unhook the few public modules that still import `crew/`. ## Blast radius The move touches every workflow, import, doc and test fixture that named an old path. Free Tests at b7da0b7 (run 42426000235, 36,305 tests at tree 98d620a95bcb) passed with every crew test planned. Two install paths needed more than a rename: - Setup builds each host's install folder (Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini and others) by linking `bin/` and `lib/`, or by copying them on Windows. Root commands such as `gstack-ship-receipt` and `gstack-pregate` now import `crew/lib/`, so setup copies `crew/lib/` beside them. A copied folder from this branch failed with `Cannot find module '../crew/lib/...'` before the fix. A new test in `test/env-host-runtime-assets.test.ts` builds a Windows-style copied folder and starts both commands; it failed before the fix and passes after it. - The release bisect checks out older commits and runs the train-gate script from them, so it now uses `scripts/train-gate.ts` when a commit predates the move. On a Capy machine the launch file adds `crew/bin` to PATH after `bin`, so `gstack-release-gate` and `gstack-coauthor-trailers` still work by bare name; a test covers it. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-99e90e0c8eb1). The full approval record stays private: this repository is public or its visibility is unknown. title: Replace remaining array push spreads with loops to prevent stack overflow (#3989)
body:
Replaces the remaining array push argument spreads across test selection and dependency graph helpers with iteration loops so large input arrays cannot overflow the V8 call stack. This completes the stack-safety cleanup for large repository runs.

## Details
- `lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts`: Replace `why.push(...prov)` with a `for (const p of prov)` loop.
- `lib/pregate/lanes.ts`: Replace `.push(...)` spreads on `reverseDirEdges`, `existing`, and `uncoveredChanged` with `for` loops.
- `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts`: Replace `.push(...walkDir(full))` and `.push(...specs)` recursive/spec spreads with `for` loops.
- `lib/pregate/regen.ts`: Replace `out.push(...walkTrackedFiles(root, rel))` recursive spread with a `for` loop.
- `lib/pregate/context.ts`: Replace `files.push(...untracked)` spread with a `for` loop.
- `test/pregate-lanes.test.ts`: Add regression test verifying large provenance and changed-file arrays (>150,000 items) do not throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

Fixes #3989

title: gstack-learnings-log and peers cannot resolve ../lib/*.ts on kiro host install (curated lib subset + nested lib/lib symlink)
body:
# Bug: `gstack-learnings-log` (and peers) cannot resolve `../lib/*.ts` on the kiro host install

## Summary

On the **kiro** host install, several `bin/` scripts import library modules via
`$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/<module>.ts`, but the installed top-level
`<install>/lib/` directory contains only a **curated subset (13 files)** of the
library. The full library (**274 files**) is reachable only one level deeper,
through a nested symlink `<install>/lib/lib -> <checkout>/lib`. As a result,
modules such as `jsonl-store.ts` are at `lib/lib/jsonl-store.ts`, not the
expected `lib/jsonl-store.ts`, and the scripts fail at runtime.

Reproduced on a fresh upgrade from 1.96.0.0 to 1.98.0.0; the layout is identical
in both versions, so the upgrade does not fix it.

## Environment

- gstack version: 1.98.0.0 (HEAD `118207f`)
- Host / tier / scope: `kiro` / `experimental` / `global`
- Install root: `/home/appadmin/.kiro/skills/gstack`
- Checkout (source): `/home/appadmin/gstack`
- State root: `/home/appadmin/.gstack` (durable)
- Bun: 1.4.4 (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
- OS: Linux x64
- Doctor: `11 ok, 1 warn, 2 not configured, 0 fail` — does NOT flag this.

## Reproduction

```
$ ~/.kiro/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-learnings-log '{"type":"tooling","key":"x","insight":"y","confidence":8,"source":"user-stated"}'
error: Cannot find module '/home/appadmin/.kiro/skills/gstack/bin/../lib/jsonl-store.ts' from '/home/appadmin/[eval]'
Bun v1.4.4 (Linux x64)
```

## Root cause

The script constructs the import path from `$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib`:

```bash
# bin/gstack-learnings-log (lines ~57-58)
VALIDATED=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | GSTACK_LIB_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib" bun --no-env-file --config="${GSTACK_BUN_CONFIG:-/dev/null}" -e "
const { hasInjection } = await import(process.env.GSTACK_LIB_DIR + '/jsonl-store.ts');
```

So it imports the literal path
`/home/appadmin/.kiro/skills/gstack/bin/../lib/jsonl-store.ts`.

But the installed lib layout is:

```
<install>/lib/                 <- REAL directory, 13 curated files
  agent-model.ts
  claude-bin.ts
  claude-code-windows-job.ts
  claude-code.ts
  gate-outcomes.ts
  model-catalog.ts
  model-policy-cli.ts
  model-policy-notice.ts
  model-policy.ts
  outside-consent.ts
  outside-review-result.ts
  state-root.ts
  lib -> /home/appadmin/gstack/lib   <- nested symlink to the FULL lib (274 files)
```

`jsonl-store.ts` exists only at `<install>/lib/lib/jsonl-store.ts`. The script
looks for `<install>/lib/jsonl-store.ts`, which is absent, hence the failure.

Note: `stat <install>/bin/../lib/jsonl-store.ts` misleadingly prints success
(it echoes the requested name), but `find -L` and Bun both confirm the real
file is at `lib/lib/jsonl-store.ts`.

## Blast radius

Every `bin/` script that imports from `../lib` is affected the same way.
Scripts found referencing `GSTACK_LIB_DIR` / `../lib/`:

- `gstack-learnings-log`   (imports `jsonl-store.ts`) — CONFIRMED broken
- `gstack-question-log`    (imports `jsonl-store.ts`) — same pattern
- `gstack-evidence`        (references `jsonl-store`)  — same pattern
- `gstack-brain-sync`
- `gstack-review-read`
- `gstack-telemetry-log`
- `gstack-review-log`
- `gstack-retro-metrics`

These back the `/learn`, question-tuning, telemetry, review, and retro flows,
so the kiro host is effectively unable to persist learnings / question prefs /
review logs until the layout is fixed.

## Expected

`<install>/lib/` should contain the full library flat (or be a single symlink
to `<checkout>/lib`), so that `$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/<module>.ts` resolves for all
274 modules — not just the 13 curated ones.

## Likely fix (for maintainers)

The kiro installer vendors a curated subset into `<install>/lib/` and then adds
a nested `lib/lib` symlink for the remainder. Either:

1. Make `<install>/lib` a single symlink to `<checkout>/lib` (matching what the
   bin scripts assume), or
2. Have the installer flatten the full lib into `<install>/lib/`, or
3. Change the bin scripts to resolve lib through a host-aware resolver that
   knows about the nested `lib/lib` layout.

Doctor should also gain a check that `../lib/jsonl-store.ts` resolves from
`bin/`, since this passed as healthy while the flow was broken.

## Workaround (not applied)

A top-level `<install>/lib/jsonl-store.ts` re-exporting from `./lib/jsonl-store.ts`
unblocks `learnings-log`, but it is a modification to the managed install that
`./setup` would overwrite, and it would need repeating for every affected
module. Not applied; filing upstream instead.

title: Make setup replace an existing real directory with a symlink instead of nesting one inside it
body:
This change makes setup's non-Windows linking helper replace an existing real directory at the destination, so the symlink lands at the destination itself instead of being nested inside it. That restores the library layout the kiro host's bin scripts expect, which fixes the runtime failures described in #4153.

## The bug

`_link_or_copy` runs `ln -snf "$src" "$dst"` to make `$dst` a symlink to `$src`. But `ln -snf SRC DST` does not replace `DST` when `DST` is an existing real directory — it creates the link inside it as `DST/$(basename SRC)`.

On the kiro host, a re-install where `$KIRO_GSTACK/lib` already existed as a real directory produced a curated-subset `lib/` plus a nested `lib/lib -> <checkout>/lib` symlink. So `jsonl-store.ts` lived at `lib/lib/jsonl-store.ts`, while bin scripts import `$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/<module>.ts`. The result was `Cannot find module '<install>/bin/../lib/jsonl-store.ts'` in `gstack-learnings-log`, with the same latent break in `gstack-question-log`, `gstack-evidence`, `gstack-brain-sync`, `gstack-review-read`, `gstack-telemetry-log`, `gstack-review-log`, and `gstack-retro-metrics`. `gstack-doctor` reported the install healthy, so it slipped through.

## The fix

Before `ln -snf`, remove a real (non-symlink) directory at `$dst` so the symlink lands at `$dst` itself. An existing symlink at `$dst` is still replaced atomically, so the normal re-link path is unchanged.

A guard (added after review) skips the removal when `$src` and `$dst` resolve to the same real directory, so the helper never deletes the source and leaves a self-referential dangling link.

## Tests

`test/setup-link-or-copy-nested.test.ts` (same extract-and-run harness as `test/setup-link-ownership.test.ts`), all red-green verified against the pre-fix code:

- Existing real directory at the destination is replaced by a symlink; no nested `DST/basename`; stale file gone.
- Existing symlink at the destination is replaced atomically.
- Absent destination gets a fresh symlink.
- Source and destination are the same path: no deletion, source survives.
- Destination resolves to the source via a symlinked parent: no deletion, source survives.

## Verification

- `bun test test/setup-link-or-copy-nested.test.ts` passes (5 tests).
- `bun test test/setup-link-ownership.test.ts test/setup-staged-copy.test.ts test/runtime-root-assets.test.ts test/setup-codex-design-pdf-runtime.test.ts` passes with no regressions (45 tests total).
- End to end: re-ran `./setup --host kiro`; the install's `lib` is now a symlink to the checkout lib, the nested `lib/lib` is gone, and `gstack-learnings-log` writes and reads back a learning.

## Suggested follow-up (not in this PR)

Add a `gstack-doctor` check that `../lib/jsonl-store.ts` resolves from `bin/`, since the broken layout passed as healthy.

title: autoplan guard: name the fix when a phase report's declaration is buried mid-sentence
body:
## Problem

On Claude Code 2.1.319 (Opus 5.5), `/autoplan` stopped after Phase 1 twice in one day with
`publication_missing`, even though a filled Phase 1 report had been sent in its own message
with only the `true autoplan-published ceo` no-op.

What happened in the session journal:

- The report was not saved as a `text` block. Claude Code journaled the prose between tool
  calls as a `thinking` block whose signature is tagged `narration`, holding a **paraphrased
  summary** of the prose, not the prose itself.
- The guard already reads narration blocks (`lib/claude-journal-records.ts`,
  `publicNarrationText`), so this part works as designed.
- The report message opened with a verification sentence before `**Phase 1 complete.**`. The
  summary merged the two:

  > I checked the packet against the plan and all four edits are in place, with the native
  > reviewer's hash matching. Phase 1 is complete with 9 native issues and no outside review,
  > so the work moves on to Phase 2.

- `phaseDeclaration` accepts a declaration only at the start of a line, so this does not count,
  and the guard said `publication_missing`. That reads like "the report is not there", which
  sent the agent (and the user) looking for dropped text, and the run was abandoned.
- Re-sending the report with no preface worked: the summaries became
  "Phase 1 is complete: the outside review was unavailable…" and
  "Phase 1 is done: outside review was unavailable…", and both count.

I ran the guard's own `recordEvents` + `autoplanPhaseCompletions` over the journal to confirm.
The first message gives no hit; both re-sends give a Phase 1 hit.

## Change 1: the phase-close procedure says the report must open the message

`autoplan/sections/phase-close.md.tmpl`, step 6, adds:

> The message starts with the report's `**Phase <report.number> complete.**` line: no preface,
> status or verification sentence before it. Claude Code may journal prose between tool calls as
> a paraphrased summary, and a preface gets folded into the declaration so the guard cannot count
> it. Say anything else in an earlier message.

`phase-close.md` is regenerated with `bun run gen:skill-docs`. No other generated file changed.

## Change 2: a specific denial, `publication_buried`

When no report counts but a message after the close Read mentions the phase's completion
somewhere other than the start of a line, the guard denies with `publication_buried` instead of
`publication_missing`. The text names the fix.

- **Same gate strength.** It is still a denial. The new check only picks which corrective text
  to show, and it never counts a buried mention as a report.
- `lib/autoplan-phase-publication.ts`: new `buriedPhaseDeclaration(text, phase)`. It matches
  `Phase N [(name)] [is] complete|completed|done|finished|wrapped up` at a position > 0 on a line,
  skips fenced code, ignores negations ("is not complete"), and keeps `2` and `2.5` apart.
- `autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts`: picks between the two codes where
  `publication_missing` used to fail.
- `autoplan/bin/guard-reasons.ts`: new corrective reason. It doesn't advise a retry, and it
  includes the publish-separately instruction.
- `docs/autoplan-guard-troubleshooting.md`: `#publication-buried` anchor (the reason-inventory
  test requires one per code).

## Why not count paraphrased or thinking text more loosely

- Accepting a declaration anywhere in a sentence would let a summary like "…before Phase 1 is
  complete, …" or a quoted plan line pass.
- Reading untagged thinking would treat private reasoning as a published report, which defeats
  the "visible parent text" rule.
- The narration channel is a summary by design, so the reliable fix is making the declaration
  survive summarizing: open the message with it.

## Tests

`test/autoplan-publication-buried.test.ts`:

- The real summaries from the failing session: the buried one is not counted and is flagged as
  buried; the opening one is counted and not flagged.
- Negative controls: another phase, a negation, a fenced template, and `2` vs `2.5`.
- Hook replay with the existing guard fixture: a report with a preface gives `publication_buried`
  with the fix in the text. Controls: no report stays `publication_missing`, and a normal
  `publish()` is allowed.
- `test/autoplan-guard-reasons.test.ts` still passes (code inventory, no-retry rule, anchors).

## Verification

- `bun test test/autoplan-publication-buried.test.ts test/autoplan-guard-reasons.test.ts`: 9 pass, 0 fail.
- Wider run of `test/autoplan-*.test.ts`, `test/*publication*.test.ts` and `test/skill-docs*.test.ts` on Windows 11, before and after this change: 51 failures each, and 50 of them are the same tests. The two that differ are timing flakes. `autoplan-review-discovery` "canonical global path in copy installations" passed 2 of 3 isolated runs on this branch, and `autoplan-token-efficiency` "below the cap" failed before this change and passes after. The 50 shared failures are Windows environment issues unrelated to this change (paths, spawning bun by PATH name).

title: Stop review planning from reading canned usage replies and look-alike client names as risky code (GST-1888)
body:
Review planning no longer sends a pull request to the full review panel just because it contains a canned model-API usage reply or a JavaScript variable named `requests` or `got`.

## What changed

- **Canned usage replies.** A usage object whose API usage-count keys (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, cache creation and read tokens, `_count` and `_details`, snake_case or camelCase) are numeric constants no longer reads as money. Token caps, prices and `_usd` keys still do.
- **Look-alike client names.** In JavaScript, TypeScript and the other C-syntax languages, a `requests` or `httpx` call counts as security only when it is one of the client's own functions (`requests.post(`, `httpx.stream(` and the rest) or the changed lines import the client. An import of either, inline ones and ones after an escaped newline included, is security on its own. `got` counts on an import or on a `got(` or `got.<verb>(` call.
- Security still reads every changed line, comments included. Money still reads comments and strings, as on main.

## Why

gbrain-evals#387, an eval write-up whose only code was a local stub for a model API, planned risk:money and risk:security because of its canned usage replies and a `requests.filter(` call on a JavaScript array. That cost a full review panel on a change with no money or network code.

## Blast radius

`lib/review-risk.ts` (matchRisk) only, plus its tests, `docs/review-policy.md`, a changelog fragment and the review pin. No-loss replay against main over 2,919 files: 6 files lose security and 12 lose money, and nothing is gained. Every lost security line is a JavaScript `requests` or `got` name on an array or string, and every lost money line is a canned usage-count literal.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- Status: **parked at 19698d1** by the /ship run (Captain rule: a fail-open finding after the fix round parks the PR). Step 11 voices found fail-open cases in the canned-usage rule (a spread of real usage beside a zero default, a token cap under a usage-limit name, a reservation-shaped constant) and `got.default(url)` losing security. Not fixed in this run.
- Earlier rounds: comment skipping was tried twice and dropped after review found fail-open bypasses.
- /ship round 1 (red-team) found Python embedded in a TypeScript string losing security; fixed in 19698d1 (the client's module functions count in every file, and the import anchor accepts an escaped newline).
- Listed fail-closed notes: any comment that names a call reads as security; `.vue` and `.svelte` `requests.filter(` reads as security; a zero usage literal in a catch block no longer reads as money (ruling a); a JavaScript `import requests from './requests'` now reads as security.
- Tripwire fix: the exec fixture in test/review-risk-mentions.test.ts gained a timeout (ca6f38e) after CI's sync-spawn tripwire failed at 07d37cb.
- Flaky: the local focused lane timed out once on review-plan-cli "scratch under .gstack/tmp/ is ignored" (5011 ms against a 5000 ms limit) at 07d37cb; one rerun at the same tree passed.

</details>

title: Stop the secrets check flagging code that reads an environment variable (GST-1894)
body:
The preflight secrets check stops failing a branch for code that reads an environment variable, or for a self-describing fixture label in a test file. That keeps the safety check honest, so people trust it when it does fail. ## What changed ![Env reads that end the expression now pass; a literal fallback still fails (QA captures 001 and 002)](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/RgF7q94kIyDRGxkGXMBrs7pvx7uFexLblPly7lxOFrM.png) Env reads that end the expression now pass; a literal fallback still fails (QA captures 001 and 002).
Before/after as text: Env reads that end the expression now pass; a literal fallback still fails (QA captures 001 and 002) ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +env.kv findings per line shape (branch c44d6348) +env member read, ends with ; 0 passes +getenv call, ends with ) 0 passes +member read with ?? literal fallback 1 still fails +getenv call with literal default 1 still fails +fallback wrapped to the next line 1 still fails -env.kv findings per line shape (main d479c5bf) -env member read, ends with ; 1 fails pregate -getenv call, ends with ) 1 fails pregate -member read with ?? literal fallback 1 -getenv call with literal default 1 -fallback wrapped to the next line 1 ~~~
## Why "The preflight secrets check fails on `token = opts?.env?.AGENT_API_TOKEN;`": yc-software/qm hit this on a test file that only reads an environment variable and names a fixture `"personal-secret"` (GST-1894). Those lines now pass. A line with a fallback or a second argument gets no new exemption, so a hardcoded secret written as a default still fails. ## Blast radius Only the `env.kv` rule in `lib/redact-patterns.ts` changes, and every `gstack-redact` caller shares it: pregate, PR-body scans and decision-log scans. It's safe because the wider env-read exemption applies only when the line has no `??`, `||`, `or` or `:`, has no second argument, and ends the expression with `;`, `,` or `)`. Every other line keeps exactly the #2912 exemption main has. We checked this by running the scanner on main and on this branch (QA captures 001 to 004), and CI run 42455675573 passed at this tree. ## Summary Pregate blamed ordinary code for holding a credential. `process.env.X` already passed, but `opts?.env?.X;`, `ctx.env.X;`, `import.meta.env.X;`, `process.env["X"];` and `System.getenv("X");` all failed it. Now an `env` member read by an ALL-CAPS name, or an indexed or call read whose argument is a quoted ALL-CAPS name, passes when the line holds no fallback and ends the expression. In test-named files, a value made only of lowercase words with a credential word among them passes as a fixture label. The branch first added a next-line reader and a shared backtick change, then removed both, so a fallback on the next line or in backticks is simply not exempted. The changelog fragment now says a quoted name that isn't ALL-CAPS in `os.environ[...]` fails where it used to pass. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. The Step 7 audit mapped 10 of 10 changed paths at three stars across test/redact-context-exemptions.test.ts and test/pregate-secrets-source-context.test.ts. Tests: 1760 → 1760 (+0 new) Coverage: 100% value-weighted (100% including 0 weakly covered paths) Test value: 0 tests written, 2 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered (weak = ★, gate-failing or unrated). Tests ran: tests 1641 ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted. The fix round then corrected the changelog half of that finding (c44d6348), and the one scoped fix-check found nothing blocking. title: Run checks for files that still name deleted tests (#3536)
body: Removing or renaming a test now runs checks for files that still name its old path, even when another test was already selected. This catches stale test lists before they slip through the local checks. ## Why (in your own words) Pregate, the local pre-push test check, can report success after a test is deleted while skipping a remaining curation-list test that would fail on the stale filename. This happens when the deleted test already maps to another test, either through `dependencies` or a surviving test's path reference: `selectLanes` takes its mapped-test early return before checking other files that still name the removed path. This addresses #3536. Merged parent #3534 explicitly left that early-return case as a known limit; this is the deferred follow-up, not a repeat of the parent fix. **Validation status:** [Full free CI passed](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42453607997) on head `45701d4c4`. The 165 focused local checks and both typechecks also pass. Required selected paid coverage and remaining shipping reviews are still pending; skipped fork jobs are not passes. ### Why this shape Reuse the existing remaining-file coverage logic through a private helper. Call it before the mapped-test early return, without moving the entire removal-waiver path or changing its import and ownership checks. The policy's own `dependencies` keys intentionally map removed paths, so treating those keys as stale uses would reject otherwise valid mappings. Only those keys are excluded from that policy-file scan. Dependency test targets and other policy fields still count, with regressions against exempting the whole policy or all dependency contents. Five files, one commit, no new public exports, settings or dependencies. The diff stays bounded for maintainer integration. It does not include #4150's separate array-spread cleanup, even though that work touches the same module. ### What it does - Applies remaining-file coverage to both mapped deletions and rename old names. - Preserves the originally selected tests and adds the tests for remaining non-Markdown files that name the removed test. - Refuses an uncovered reference instead of silently passing; preserves intentional empty dependency declarations. - Keeps valid dependency-map keys while checking dependency targets and other policy references. - Adds eight regression/control cases in the existing `test/pregate-removed-paths.test.ts` owner file. - Updates `docs/pregate.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` to distinguish reference checks from unmapped-removal waivers. ### What it deliberately does not do - No broader removed-source waivers (#3535), runner-script/target discovery (#3537), or Markdown/tracked-symlink changes (#3538). - No array-spread cleanup, new flags, policy keys, packages, exports or test-only production seams. - No `VERSION`, package-version, released `CHANGELOG.md`, README or ETHOS edits. Release notes are one entry-text-only `changelog.d/` fragment. - No skill-template, generated-output, `/ship` workflow, release-stamping or deployment changes. ## Live evidence Bun 1.4.2 and Node 20.20.2 on Linux, with `umask 022`, `LC_ALL=C`, private HOME/state/TMPDIR and local bare Git origins. No browser, cloud VM or live model was used. ### Actual CLI before and after The fixture uses the existing `makeFixtureRepo`, `commit` and `runBin` helpers. It invokes the real command with `--base main --allow-repo-commands --stage tests`, requires an actual `lanes` record, and extracts the following fields. Both sides intentionally retain the same stale curation entry. **Before: unchanged main production code at `d479c5bf1`:** ```json { "source": "base-d479c5bf1", "exit": 0, "laneStatus": "pass", "code": null, "detail": "1 tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0", "ran": "ran: node --test 'test/retry.test.js'" } ``` **After: the production code committed as `45701d4c4`:** ```json { "source": "working-fix", "exit": 1, "laneStatus": "fail", "code": "PREGATE_LANE_FAILED", "detail": "local lane exited 1 (1 failed of 2 ran; 2 files; pipefail)", "ran": "ran: node --test 'test/curation.test.js' 'test/retry.test.js'" } ``` The repaired gate now runs the missing curation check and rejects the stale entry. It does not repair the fixture's list or drop the originally mapped retry test. ### Failing-first regressions and controls The final eight new cases were also copied into an isolated detached worktree at `d479c5bf1`, without changing its production code. That control produced **7 failures and 1 passing control**, with 47 unrelated cases filtered out: - Four stale-curation failures: dependency mapping or surviving-test reference, each with deletion or rename. - Two policy-reference failures: runner command and dependency test target. - One uncovered-namer failure. - The intentional no-test declaration remains the passing control. On the repaired implementation, the complete owner file passes all **55 cases**, including those eight and the existing removal/import/source/owning-suite controls. ### Focused checks Commands ran with the isolated environment described above. Counts below do not double-count the separate new-case runs or the failing base control. | Command | Pass | Fail | |---|---:|---:| | `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test test/pregate-removed-paths.test.ts --timeout=30000` | 55 | 0 | | `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test test/pregate-selection.test.ts test/pregate-policy-lane-verdicts.test.ts --timeout=30000` | 73 | 0 | | `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test test/test-of-test-ratchet.test.ts test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts test/egress-receipt-wiring.test.ts --timeout=30000` | 22 | 0 | | `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test test/changelog-fragments.test.ts --timeout=30000` | 15 | 0 | | **Total** | **165** | **0** | No skipped or filtered cases in those four runs. Product `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run typecheck:test` reports `812 known diagnostics, none new.` The committed source/test bytes match the passing inputs. Runtime docs were updated after those runs, and the later release fragment passed its own suite. Plain-title and changelog prose checks, whitespace checks, and exact staged/committed patch redaction scans pass with zero redaction findings. ## Scope - **Changed:** five files, +106/-17 against base `d479c5bf1`: `lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts`, the existing removed-path owner test, two runtime docs, and one branch fragment. One commit: `45701d4c47acae31d1bebdd0eca1f95bd43a4ab3`. - **Verified live by:** actual CLI before/after above, the unchanged-base regression control, 165 focused passing checks, both typechecks, [full free CI on this head](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42453607997), and exact-byte publication checks. - **Did NOT test:** the full `bun run test` suite locally, required selected paid coverage, or a complete `/review` and `/ship` certification. Local reproduction and owner checks ran on Linux. Full free CI passed remotely; this is not a claim of running the owner suite natively on every platform. The free paid-coverage planner (`bun run eval:select --base upstream/main --json`) reaches 252 registered cases through this shared module. The PR profile selects **108 behaviors**, no dedicated quality judges, and defers **144 broad behaviors** to scheduled/release coverage. None was run locally; none receives pass credit here. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface). - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff; production source and existing owner tests are changed. - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references. - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked: N/A, none added. - [x] Linked issue and reproduction: #3536. ## Test plan - [x] Reproduce the mapped deletion falsely passing while the curation test is skipped. - [x] Prove the new regression cases fail against unchanged main production code. - [x] Cover dependency and surviving-test mappings, deletion and rename, uncovered references and intentional empty declarations. - [x] Keep policy runner and dependency-target references checked rather than exempting the whole policy. - [x] Pass the complete owner suite, adjacent selection/policy controls, source/test guards and fragment checks. - [x] Pass strict product types and the unchanged test-type debt limit. - [x] Check the plain title, release-fragment prose, whitespace and exact outgoing patch for sensitive content. - [x] Complete full free acceptance on this PR head. - [ ] Complete required selected paid coverage, with maintainer-run fork-PR coverage where needed. - [ ] Complete remaining shipping reviews and verification before merge. Fork PRs do not receive upstream eval secrets. Skipped paid jobs are not passes; required maintainer-run coverage remains necessary before merge. Broad-profile deferrals are scheduled/release coverage, not PR passes. Fixes #3536.
