title: /office-hours spec review: reviewers return invented sha256 in OFFICE_HOURS_VERDICT receipt, so genuine verdicts fail `check`
body:
## What happened

On gstack **1.98.0.0** (`91009308`, main tip), an `/office-hours` independent spec review failed at the receipt check even though both reviewer verdicts were genuine. The reviewers returned their `OFFICE_HOURS_VERDICT round=N sha256=<hash> path=...` line before their `Seal:` command had finished, so the `sha256` in each receipt was made up instead of copied from what `seal` printed. `gstack-office-hours-review check --receipt` then failed with:

```
receipt hash does not match the saved verdict bytes
```

The verdict JSON files on disk were valid. Only the reported hashes were wrong. Under `office-hours/sections/design-and-handoff.md` ("A missing, malformed, or mismatched receipt fails the check: that attempt is a failed review"), a mismatched receipt counts as a failed review, so the round's real work gets thrown away and the user is told the review failed, with nothing wrong in the design doc.

The /office-hours session's own diagnosis, verbatim:

> "Both reviewer verdicts are genuine, but their reported hashes were invented before seal finished, so the check caught the mismatch and this is a gstack contract bug rather than a problem with your doc."
>
> "ELI10: Both round-2 reviewers handed back a made-up receipt before their seal command finished, so the check failed. The seal tool's own output, saved in each reviewer's transcript, matches the verdict file on disk exactly, so the verdict is genuine. I can run the check using that tool-generated receipt instead of the reviewer's wrong one, and note the substitution in the doc. Or I can rerun again, which will likely fail the same way,"

## Why this looks like a contract bug, not bad luck

The check itself is correct (`verifyOfficeHoursVerdictReceipt`, `lib/office-hours-review.ts:212-220`), and it rightly refuses. The fragile part is the contract: the reviewer must copy a 64-hex-character hash into its final response exactly, and must not answer until `seal` has printed it (`lib/office-hours-review.ts:252-253`). When a model gets ahead of the tool output, or fills in a plausible hash, the whole attempt is lost.

gstack has already hit this exact failure in its own test suite. The changelog entry "The autoplan-guard-pty eval no longer fails when its test actor mistypes a hash" says a Haiku actor "made up a tail for the Design dispatch's hash". That was fixed by replacing the hash with a short declared token (`DISPATCH ceo`) and letting the harness substitute the exact value. The fix only went into the eval harness; the production `/office-hours` reviewer contract still asks the model to copy a 64-char hash.

## Repro (probabilistic)

1. Run `/office-hours` through to the independent spec review.
2. The reviewer subagent Writes its verdict, is told to run `Seal:`, and must return the printed receipt line as its whole response.
3. Every so often the reviewer returns an `OFFICE_HOURS_VERDICT` line whose `sha256` doesn't match `sha256(verdict file)`, either because it answered before `seal` returned or because it reconstructed the hash instead of copying it.
4. `check --receipt` fails, and the round counts as a failed review.

## Suggested fix

Don't make the model copy the hash. For example:

- Have `seal` record its receipt in a sidecar next to the verdict (e.g. `<verdict>.receipt`, written only by `seal`) and have the reviewer return a short token such as `OFFICE_HOURS_SEALED round=N`. `check` then reads the sidecar and verifies it against the saved bytes. The binding still proves `seal` validated these exact bytes, and the model never transcribes a 64-char value. This is the same approach as the eval fix above.
- Or, at minimum, tell the parent how to recover when the hash mismatches but the path and round match: re-run `seal` itself on the unchanged verdict file and, if it validates, accept that receipt instead of failing the round. (This is weaker, since it no longer proves the reviewer ran `seal`, so the sidecar approach seems better.)

Either way, a test with a reviewer response whose hash is wrong but whose verdict file is valid would pin the behaviour.

## Environment

- gstack 1.98.0.0, global git install, `main` channel
- Claude Code (VS Code extension), macOS

title: Field report: 63 skills, 2 ran — an honest ledger from a no-remote WeChat mini-program shop (plus 4 questions)
body:
# Field report: 63 skills, 2 ran — an honest ledger from a no-remote WeChat mini-program shop (plus 4 questions)

## Context

One-person shop: a non-coder product owner directing AI agents (Claude Code) to build a WeChat mini-program (payment flows inside). Windows, **no git remote** (local-only), Chinese workflow, UI via the local WeChat component ecosystem. We kept a usage ledger of the suite, audited after two days of work, and we're sharing it as a data point for Earn Its Place.

## The ledger (2026-11-07 → 11-08, one project)

- **Actually ran: 2 of 63.** `autoplan` partially (design-doc check + preamble + plan persisted; the four phases did not run — requirements were already user-approved line by line and UI is platform-native, so we rerouted to a plan-eng-review-style independent-subagent review), and `plan-eng-review` as a lightweight run without the preamble/decision-brief toolchain. That lightweight run surfaced **8 real pre-build issues** (physically infeasible hardware feature; payment-architecture one-way door; incomplete order state machine; missing order snapshot; missing tenant isolation; sequencing risk on real payment/print integration) — all converted into design revisions before implementation. Plus `/captain` as the discipline source: our no-remote crew adaptation (lanes never merge; READY = branch + full SHA + tree hash + named check evidence; controller-only merge trains; mechanical READY validator) delivered 11+ lanes with zero process accidents.
- **Absorbed as text, never executed: 7** (guard family / health / retro / document-release / test-audit / verify — replaced by our own full-check gate: 281 automated tests, all-green before every merge — / gstack-upgrade pending).
- **Inapplicable:** the web design line, iOS line, browser line, deploy/canary/PR lines, web benchmark — the platform is a mini-program and the repo is local-only. Browser-style QA replaced by mini-program automation plus a browser MCP.

## Honest debts

- `cso` never ran and the app carries payment flows. We read ETHOS §9 — safety skills don't do cost-benefit triage. Scheduled before real gateway integration; we consider it already overdue.
- guard hooks not installed. "Pending install" with no date means never, we know.
- Our full-check gate is AI-written; the owner cannot read code and no human has verified it. Fault-injection drills (planted bugs on a throwaway branch) are planned.

## Questions

1. For a no-remote, non-web platform, which parts of the suite would you actually keep on? Our current cut: plan reviews (eng at minimum), the captain lineage, cso, health, retro, document-release, guard — and nothing else. Is that the right cut, or are we wrong in either direction?
2. Does §9's "safety stays on" reasoning generalize beyond careful/freeze/guard/unfreeze/cso — e.g. document-release before a real-money launch?
3. Our autoplan reroute (prerequisites yes, phases no, eng-review-style subagent instead): defensible adaptation, or a violation we should stop rationalizing?
4. What legitimately builds human trust in AI-authored gates for owners who cannot read the code?

Business specifics redacted. Happy to share the generic crew templates and the READY validator script.

title: Give a clear error when Chromium's sandbox can't start, and make design-build preflight launch the browser (GST-1906)
body:
On Linux hosts that block Chromium's sandbox (stock Ubuntu 23.10+ under AppArmor, non-root Docker), gstack's browser now stops with one clear error that names both fixes, and `/design-review --build` finds the problem before it starts work. This serves the README's promise that gstack's own browser works out of the box on Linux. ## What changed ![design-build preflight on a host that blocks Chromium's sandbox: it used to say ok, now it stops with BROWSER_SANDBOX and the fix](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/cYSjeDW7dUEGCVHYGmwlf0xiv9LSGJIKbaINHJig4VM.png) design-build preflight on a host that blocks Chromium's sandbox: it used to say ok, now it stops with BROWSER_SANDBOX and the fix.
Before/after as text ~~~text Before (main 9740bfd, user.max_user_namespaces=0): $ gstack-design-build preflight --inventory inv.json PREFLIGHT: ok engine=browse states=1 targets=loopback mutations=unknown exit=0 After (this branch, same host): $ gstack-design-build preflight --inventory inv.json DESIGN_BUILD: unrendered code=BROWSER_SANDBOX (Chromium could not start its sandbox: this Linux host does not let unprivileged users create user namespaces ... or set GSTACK_CHROMIUM_NO_SANDBOX=1 to run Chromium without its sandbox. Use that only for pages you trust ... No usable sandbox! ...) | fix: allow unprivileged user namespaces, or set GSTACK_CHROMIUM_NO_SANDBOX=1 only if every page in the run is trusted, then rerun /design-review --build exit=4 ~~~
- **One error for a sandbox that can't start.** When Chromium aborts with "No usable sandbox!", browse fails with a single message naming both fixes. You can allow user namespaces (the Ubuntu AppArmor setting), or set `GSTACK_CHROMIUM_NO_SANDBOX=1`, which is only for pages you trust. Chromium's own line stays below it. The same text reaches the headed handoff error and design-build preflight. - **No automatic retry without the sandbox.** The only new host signal is Docker's `/.dockerenv`, which now counts as a container, the same as `CONTAINER`. - **Preflight launches the browser it found.** It opens and closes one tab through the same path render uses, including the lazy Chromium install. A sandbox failure stops the run with `DESIGN_BUILD: unrendered code=BROWSER_SANDBOX`, and any other launch failure stops it with `NO_BROWSER`. ## Why "Server failed to start" followed by a wall of Playwright log was all a user on stock Ubuntu 24.04 or in non-root Docker got, and `gstack-design-build preflight` still printed `PREFLIGHT: ok` before the run died later. Now the first command that touches the browser says what is wrong and how to fix it, and gstack never decides on its own to drop the sandbox on a host it hasn't classified. ## Blast radius The four Playwright launch sites in `browse/src/browser-manager.ts` gain one `.catch(explainSandboxFailure)`, which rethrows every error that is not a sandbox abort unchanged, so XProtect and custom-Chromium handling keep their behavior (read at `browse/src/chromium-sandbox.ts:49-52`). `renderWithBrowse` keeps its tab-open path, now shared with `launchBrowse`; the existing fake-browse tests in `test/aside-render.test.ts` still pass over it, and the real sandbox failure was reproduced on this host with `user.max_user_namespaces=0` (repro and Exploratory QA below). ## Summary On a host that denies unprivileged user namespaces, Chromium aborts with "No usable sandbox!" and gstack showed a raw Playwright log; preflight did not start the browser at all, so `/design-review --build` died mid-run. This PR maps that abort to one actionable error at every launch site, with no retry and no automatic sandbox-off, and makes preflight do a real launch so the run stops at the start with `BROWSER_SANDBOX`. A follow-up commit only rewords the changelog fragment. ## Test Coverage Step 7 audit (audit-only, no tests generated): 15 of 18 changed paths tested (83%), value-weighted 83%. Quality: 9 paths at three stars, 6 at two, 0 at one. Tests: 1762 files before and after (the new and changed tests landed in the original commit: `browse/test/chromium-sandbox.test.ts` new; `browse/test/browser-manager-unit.test.ts` and `test/design-build.test.ts` extended). Fail-first: 6 of the 7 new tests fail on main 9740bfd; the seventh, "no signal keeps the sandbox on", guards against an automatic sandbox-off being added. Test value: 0 tests written, 1 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. Gaps left as proposed tests: - `explainSandboxFailure` passes a non-sandbox launch error through unchanged (only sandbox aborts are tested). - Preflight with the Aside engine skips `launchBrowse` (every preflight test stubs launch or uses browse). - The extension launch path's `explainSandboxFailure` wiring (rejected: same helper already covered through `launch()` and `handoff()`). Tests ran: focused 65 Tests ran: free carried from CI (see Test plan) ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 2 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 2 asked (0 fixed, 2 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted Both are below the blocking floor (a finding blocks only if it would fail a test, break production, or lose data or secrets) and stay unfixed here: - [INFORMATIONAL] (confidence: 6/10, red-team) `browse/src/chromium-sandbox.ts:22`: counting `/.dockerenv` as a container turns the sandbox off for non-root Docker users even where it would have worked. Kept: this is the lane's ruled design (`/.dockerenv` counts as a container); raised for the owner to confirm. - [INFORMATIONAL] (confidence: 8/10, core) `docs/troubleshooting.md:1700`: the sentence "gstack never turns the sandbox off on its own: it already does so for root, CI, CONTAINER and Docker's /.dockerenv" contradicts itself; it should say gstack turns it off on its own only for those hosts. Gate edits: none detected (7 listed, 5 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Outside review: completed (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, host subagent), VERDICT: FINDINGS with 1 Low, Blocks: no. Native adversarial review: 5 findings (1 Medium, 4 Low), all Blocks: no. Targeted gate reader: no findings. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `browse/src/chromium-sandbox.ts:22` /.dockerenv turns the sandbox off in every Docker container with no opt-back-in (duplicate of red-team#1, multi-source) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/design-build.ts:220` Any non-sandbox preflight launch failure is labeled NO_BROWSER with the gstack-browser-ensure fix - INFORMATIONAL `lib/design-build.ts:217` Preflight now starts the browse daemon (may run gstack-browser-ensure up to 600 s) before the UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET check; design-build-e2e daemon outlives its temp repo - INFORMATIONAL `browse/src/browser-manager.ts:701` Sandbox error replaces the GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH message; the binary name survives only in cause - INFORMATIONAL `browse/src/browser-manager.ts:2262` Cosmetic: multi-line framing of the handoff and browseRunner error text - INFORMATIONAL `lib/aside-render.ts:600` launchBrowse ignores closetab's result, so a failed close leaves the probe tab open while preflight reports success ## Exploratory QA Functional (CLI) smoke on this host (uid 1001, no `/.dockerenv`, no CI or CONTAINER), owned loopback fixture on 127.0.0.1:5611. `user.max_user_namespaces` was set to 0 for probes 2 and 3 and restored to 64045 afterwards. - Probe 1 pass: preflight on a sandbox-capable host prints `PREFLIGHT: ok engine=browse`, exit 0. - Probe 2 pass: with namespaces denied, preflight prints `DESIGN_BUILD: unrendered code=BROWSER_SANDBOX` with the actionable error, exit 4, before any URL check. - Probe 3 pass: with namespaces denied, `browse goto` exits 1 with the one sandbox error after `Server failed to start:` and does not navigate, so there is no retry without the sandbox. Verdict: pass. Limits: smoke budget only (3 probes, 32 s); probe 1 finished in 0.8 s, so it alone does not prove a cold Chromium start (probe 2 does prove the launch path is real); `browse/dist/browse` was built from HEAD's browse source (mtimes, clean tree), not rebuilt for this run. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results Evals not run. No prompt, template or judge changed, but `lib/design-build.ts` is a derived reference, so the PR selector picks 108 behavioral probes (the gate-tier touchfile plan selects 18 tests in 7 shards). title: generic harness: the router description's `: ` makes SKILL.md invalid YAML, so strict loaders (Pi) drop the skill
body:
## What happened

`gstack-harness register generic` (the "any other harness" target, `docs/hosts.md`) writes a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is **not valid YAML**: the router description contains an interior `": "` (`... Load first for any coding task: lists every gstack skill ...`) and is emitted as a plain scalar, so a strict YAML loader reads it as a nested mapping and rejects the file.

A harness that parses frontmatter with a real YAML parser then **drops the skill silently**, so `register` reports success and the skill never appears:

```text
gstack-harness: any other harness: 60 gstack skills reachable through one router skill at <dir> (installed, 1 files written)
```

…and in Pi, `~/.agents/skills/gstack/SKILL.md` is never listed, with no error the user can act on (Pi documents malformed `SKILL.md` files as "not loaded").

This is the same class of bug as #1778 (`generated SKILL.md descriptions with colons are invalid YAML`), which was fixed in `scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts` by quoting with `toYamlInlineScalar`. That helper stayed local to the generator, and the two frontmatter writers in `lib/harness-register.ts` never got it:

- `routerSkill()` → `'description: ' + ROUTER_DESCRIPTION` (router mode, the failing one)
- `flatFrontmatter()` → `'description: ' + desc` (`--skills all` for Claude-render targets: any skill description with a colon breaks the same way)

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gstack && cd gstack
bun install
./bin/gstack-harness register generic --skills-dir /tmp/repro-skills
head -3 /tmp/repro-skills/gstack/SKILL.md
```

Then parse the frontmatter with a strict YAML loader (any: `yaml`, `js-yaml`, PyYAML, or the loader the target harness uses):

```bash
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),{parse}=require("yaml");
const m=/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---/m.exec(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));
try{const o=parse(m[1]);console.log("OK name="+o.name)}catch(e){console.log("REJECTED: "+e.message.split("\n")[0])}' \
  /tmp/repro-skills/gstack/SKILL.md
```

## Real output

Before (current `main`, base commit for this report `6042f6a`, VERSION `1.98.0.0`):

```text
REJECTED: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:

description: Use to review a diff or PR, debug a bug or failing test, QA test a…
             ^
```

After quoting the same value with `toYamlInlineScalar` (PR linked below):

```text
OK name=gstack descLen=229
```

The description parses back to exactly `ROUTER_DESCRIPTION`, so nothing is lost or rewritten — only the encoding changes.

## Expected

Frontmatter written by `gstack-harness register` parses as YAML for every target, including harnesses that use a strict loader (Pi, QM), and the register output is a skill the harness actually lists.

## Impact

`--skills-dir` registration with `generic` produces a skill that YAML-strict harnesses never load. Pi is the case I hit; `~/.agents/skills` is Pi's documented skill location, so the natural install path is exactly this one. `--context` / `--print` are unaffected (no frontmatter), and the Claude/Codex/Cursor/Gemini routers are unaffected (their committed description has no colon).

Interim workaround: after `register`, quote the value by hand (`description: "<text>"`), or register a `--context` block instead. Both are overwritten by the next `register` / `--refresh-registered`.

## Readiness report

```text
doctor (paths shortened to ~; 2 warns and 1 not-configured are unrelated to this issue)
gstack doctor 1.98.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: opencode global current (1.98.0.0), cursor global current (1.98.0.0), agy global current (1.98.0.0), gemini global current (1.98.0.0), codex global current (1.98.0.0), claude global current (1.98.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.2 at ~/.bun/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              windows bash    C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe (chosen by git --exec-path)
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.166.0; self-locate ok
warn            codex probe     not probed; Codex readiness is unverified until a skill or --live runs it
not configured  artifacts sync  off; cross-machine artifacts sync is unavailable
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.98.0.0
ok              claude code     2.1.319 (Claude Code)
ok              session journal no session journals for this project
ok              guard log       no guard decisions logged
13 ok, 2 warn, 1 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host: `generic` target (Pi 0.x, skills root `~/.agents/skills`), also affects any harness with a strict YAML frontmatter loader
- OS: Windows 11, Git for Windows bash, Bun 1.4.2, Node v26.12.1
- gstack: VERSION `1.98.0.0` installed; reproduced on `main` at `6042f6ad48774504f918ab1391908c1ccdb11fe0`

Fix: PR to follow (extracts `toYamlInlineScalar` into `lib/yaml-scalar.ts`, uses it at both `harness-register.ts` emission sites, with tests).

title: prefix install: ./setup --status reports "1 of 114 broken" and exits 1, though the doc's own prefixed path resolves
body:
## What happened

On a **prefix** install (`--prefix`, skills land as `gstack-review`, `gstack-qa`, …), `./setup --status` reports a broken section link for the Claude host and exits **1** — but nothing is actually broken. Every prefix install fails this self-check permanently.

```text
$ ./setup --status; echo "exit=$?"
Install checks:
  opencode global: router is a real file; section links: 75 checked, all resolve
  cursor global: router is a real file; section links: 75 checked, all resolve
  agy global: router is a real file; section links: 75 checked, all resolve
  gemini global: router is a real file; section links: 75 checked, all resolve
  codex global: router is a real file; section links: 74 checked, all resolve
  claude global: router is a real file; section links: 1 of 114 broken (first: gstack-review/SKILL.md names ../qa/sections/exploratory.md). Fix: cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup --host claude
gstack: an install has broken section links (see Install checks above); exit 1
exit=1
```

Re-running the suggested `./setup --host claude` reproduces it byte for byte, so the "Fix:" hint cannot clear it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/garrytan/gstack ~/gstack && cd ~/gstack && ./setup --host claude --prefix --global` (any prefix install does it; the Claude host is the only one that ships the relative pointers)
2. `./setup --status; echo $?` → `1 of 114 broken`, exit `1`
3. Drop `--prefix` (`./setup --host claude --no-prefix --global`) → `114 checked, all resolve`, exit `0`

## Why it is a false positive

The installed `gstack-review/SKILL.md` states both layouts itself, one line apart:

```markdown
- If the caller directory is `review`, Read `../qa/sections/exploratory.md` in full.
- If the caller directory is prefixed `gstack-review`, use `../gstack-qa/sections/exploratory.md` instead and read it in full.
```

`_status_install_checks()` (in `setup`) walks every `` Read `<path>/sections/<f>.md` `` pointer and resolves `../*` literally:

```bash
          ../*) path="$dir/$tok" ;;
```

On a prefix install `$dir` is `…/gstack-review`, so `../qa/sections/exploratory.md` points at `…/qa/sections/…`, which does not exist — while the very next line of the same doc tells the agent to use `../gstack-qa/sections/…`, which does. The checker counts the first pointer as broken before ever reading the second.

## Expected

`./setup --status` reports `114 checked, all resolve` and exits 0 on a prefix install, because every pointer the doc offers resolves in the layout the doc itself describes.

## Suggested fix

Either is enough, and neither touches installed content:

1. **Resolve the prefixed sibling** in the `../*)` arm — if `$dir/$tok` is unreadable, retry with the first path segment prefixed (`../qa/…` → `../gstack-qa/…`) when that file exists.
2. **Rewrite body pointers in prefix mode** next to the existing `name:` patch (`bin/gstack-patch-names`), so the installed doc carries only the path that exists in that layout.

## Impact

`--status` is the readiness gate used in `docs/hosts.md` and quoted by the bug template; on a prefix install it returns a hard failure (`exit 1`) that no re-run clears, so any script or human gating on it learns to ignore it. Skill behavior is unaffected — the doc's second line is what actually gets used.

## Readiness report

```text
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: opencode/cursor/agy/gemini/codex/claude global current (1.98.0.0)
ok              bun             1.4.2 at ~/.bun/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              windows bash    C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe (chosen by git --exec-path)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
13 ok, 2 warn, 1 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.319 (the only host whose render carries the relative pointers), 6 global installs registered
- OS: Windows 11, Git for Windows bash, Bun 1.4.2
- gstack: `1.98.0.0` (`9740bfd`); `setup` is byte-identical to `main` at `6042f6ad48774504f918ab1391908c1ccdb11fe0`, where `_status_install_checks` has the same `../*) path="$dir/$tok"` line

title: Quote the harness router description so strict YAML loaders keep the skill (#4163)
body:
## Why (in your own words)

`gstack-harness register` writes its own `SKILL.md`, and the router description it writes ends `... Load first for any coding task: lists every gstack skill and where to read it.` Both frontmatter writers in `lib/harness-register.ts` emitted that as a plain scalar. To a YAML parser an interior `": "` is a nested mapping, so a harness that parses frontmatter with a real YAML loader — Pi does — rejects the file and **drops the whole skill as malformed**, while `register` still prints "installed, 1 files written". A user gets a successful-looking install and no skill.

#1778 fixed exactly this for the doc generator, and the fix was a helper local to it (`toYamlInlineScalar` in `scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts`). The harness renderer was never covered. This PR moves that helper to `lib/yaml-scalar.ts` (the generator re-exports it, so nothing that imports it changes) and applies it at both emission sites: `routerSkill()` — router mode, the path that failed — and `flatFrontmatter()` — `--skills all`, where any skill description containing a colon broke the same way.

Values that are already valid plain scalars pass through untouched, so no other host's render changes and no committed `SKILL.md` changes bytes.

Fixes #4163.

## Live evidence

Reproduced on `main` at `6042f6ad48774504f918ab1391908c1ccdb11fe0` (VERSION `1.98.0.0`), Windows 11, Git for Windows bash, Bun 1.4.2. Strict parse is the `yaml` package Pi uses.

**Before** (base commit, same commands):

```text
$ ./bin/gstack-harness register generic --skills-dir /tmp/repro-before
gstack-harness: any other harness: 60 gstack skills reachable through one router skill at /tmp/repro-before (installed, 1 files written)

$ head -3 /tmp/repro-before/gstack/SKILL.md
---
name: gstack
description: Use to review a diff or PR, debug a bug or failing test, QA test a site, plan or review architecture, ship 
...

$ node -e '<parse frontmatter with yaml>'
REJECTED: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:

description: Use to review a diff or PR, debug a bug or failing test, QA test a…
             ^
```

Pi's own loader, pointed at that directory, lists 76 skills and no `gstack`:

```text
$ node -e 'loadSkillsFromDir({dir:"/tmp/repro-before"})'
gstack: NO
```

**After** (this branch):

```text
$ ./bin/gstack-harness register generic --skills-dir /tmp/repro-after
gstack-harness: any other harness: 60 gstack skills reachable through one router skill at /tmp/repro-after (installed, 1 files written)

$ node -e '<parse frontmatter with yaml>'
name=gstack description.length=229
```

The description reads back exactly (229 chars = `ROUTER_DESCRIPTION.length`), i.e. the encoding changed and nothing was lost. In Pi's loader the same directory now lists the skill:

```text
$ node -e 'loadSkillsFromDir({dir:"/tmp/repro-after"})'
技能总数: 77 | gstack: YES | gstack 相关诊断: 0
```

Repo checks on this branch:

```text
$ bun run typecheck
$ tsc -p tsconfig.json                  # no output, exit 0

$ bun run typecheck:test
test typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new.

$ bun run scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts --dry-run
exit 0                                   # generated docs byte-identical

$ bun test test/catalog-trim.test.ts
23 pass, 0 fail                          # toYamlInlineScalar still reachable from the generator

$ bun test test/harness-register.test.ts -t "generic: the router frontmatter"
1 pass                                   # new test
$ bun test test/harness-register.test.ts -t "flat frontmatter quotes only"
1 pass                                   # new test
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `lib/yaml-scalar.ts` (new — the helper, moved and re-exported), `lib/harness-register.ts` (import + 2 call sites), `scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts` (helper removed, import + re-export), `test/harness-register.test.ts` (2 tests), `changelog.d/fix-harness-yaml-scalar.md`.
- **Verified live by:** the before/after runs above, real `register generic --skills-dir` on this machine, and Pi's `loadSkillsFromDir` pointed at the written directory.
- **Did NOT test:** Linux/macOS (this box is Windows). The two new tests are pure string/parse assertions with no platform dependency, but CI is the first non-Windows run. I also did not verify harnesses beyond Pi that parse frontmatter strictly (QM was not run: no `GSTACK_QM_URL` here).

Full `test/harness-register.test.ts` on this Windows box: 23 failures both before and after this change, `comm` over the two failing-test lists shows no test that passes before and fails after. They are environment, not code: `--install-root must be an absolute path ... (got "C:\\...")` from the Bun renderer (14 occurrences, see #3498), `could not render hermes/openclaw skills` (the same), `EPERM` creating symlinks without Developer Mode, and `EINVAL ... open() while reading config "/dev/null"` (the `#!/usr/bin/env -S bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null` shebang) — that last one also fails on the base commit when run alone, so it is not from this change.

## Liveness proof (required for external contributors)

Not attached yet. **@NekoCCN** will add the screenshot of `GSTACK PR` typed live into a real terminal on this machine before this PR leaves draft. Everything else in the checklist below is done from the agent side.

title: Stop counting a finished command as a failed QA capture on macOS
body: ## Why (in your own words) On macOS, `gstack-qa-evidence capture` sometimes records a successful command as `status: incomplete`, `exitCode: 2`. The QA chain then refuses `--after` on that capture, so /ship's exploratory QA stalls on a command that worked. The cause is the cleanup kill in `runQaDeadlineCommand`: after the child exits, it signals the process group and treats everything except `ESRCH` as a containment failure. While an exited group is still being torn down, macOS can answer `EPERM`. This change treats `EPERM` on macOS the same as `ESRCH` for that kill. Every other error, and `EPERM` on other platforms, still fails closed. ## Live evidence The kill error, measured directly: 14 runs of a multi-threaded Rust CLI that exits 0, with the same detached spawn and `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL')` on the `exit` event: ``` darwin v26.3.0 {"exit0:ESRCH":1,"exit0:EPERM":3,"exit0:ok":10} ``` The same program through `gstack-qa-evidence capture --public --deadline ...` (the program itself exits 0 when run directly): ``` # upstream main 6042f6ad4, 12 runs 9 "status":"complete" "exitCode":0 3 "status":"incomplete" "exitCode":2 # this branch, 16 runs 16 "status":"complete" "exitCode":0 ``` The new test was red first (`processGroupAlreadyGone` in place, still only accepting `ESRCH`), then green: ``` # before the fix (fail) a process group that already exited on macOS is not a containment failure # test/qa-deadline.test.ts on this Mac upstream main: 39-40 pass, 4-5 fail (two runs) this branch: 46 pass, 0 fail ``` The 4-5 failures on main are existing `qa-deadline` tests (timeout and interruption closing the owned process tree). They pass with this change, so they appear to hit the same `EPERM`. ## Scope - **Changed:** - `lib/qa-deadline.ts`: new `processGroupAlreadyGone(code, platform)`, used by the group kill. - `test/qa-deadline.test.ts`: `EPERM` is tolerated on macOS only; other errors and other platforms still fail closed. - `changelog.d/fix-qa-deadline-macos-group-kill.md`: the changelog fragment. - **Verified live by:** the capture runs above on macOS 26 (Apple Silicon, Bun 1.x); `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run typecheck:test` "812 known diagnostics, none new"; `bun run build` passes. - **Did NOT test:** - Linux or Windows behaviour (the new branch is macOS-only). - The full free suite: `gstack-checks` reported the selection as too broad (1711 files), so I ran the qa-deadline and qa-evidence tests. - `test/qa-evidence*.test.ts` still has 5 failures on this Mac. All 5 also fail on clean main, which has 7 there. - **Known trade-off:** on macOS, a group member owned by another user that survives the child's exit is now not reported, since `EPERM` cannot be told apart from teardown. - **Not changed:** `lib/claude-code.ts:100` has a similar group kill with the same `ESRCH` check. I did not reproduce a failure there. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction above 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix three flaky test causes found in the 2026-11-08 harvest (GST-1912)
body:
Three flaky-test causes are fixed, and `./setup` no longer tells people their healthy hooks are broken when Bun crashes during the hook check. This serves gstack's goal of a test suite and setup you can trust: a red run or a setup error should mean something is really wrong. ## What changed ![A Bun crash during the hook check no longer reports healthy hooks as broken](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/j0N1DMkEnCC94K5_fnTzlIsrf9VIVnZI4fXuoc4-E_k.png) A Bun crash during the hook check no longer reports healthy hooks as broken.
Before/after as text: A Bun crash during the hook check no longer reports healthy hooks as broken ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ GSTACK_HOOK_CHECK_BUN= bin/gstack-hook-check . # this branch +gstack-hook-check: bun was killed by signal 11 while bundling the TypeScript hook entries, so they cannot be checked -$ GSTACK_HOOK_CHECK_BUN= bin/gstack-hook-check . # main ok bin/gstack-session-update +ok careful/bin/check-careful.sh +ok freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh +exit 3 -fail hosts/claude/hooks/question-log-hook /workspace/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/question-log-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry -fail hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook /workspace/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry -fail hosts/claude/hooks/auq-error-fallback-hook /workspace/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/auq-error-fallback-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry -fail hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook /workspace/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry -fail hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook /workspace/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry -... -exit 1 ~~~
**Hook check when Bun crashes (Free Tests 42327570347 shard 8).** Bun segfaulted in the one-process bundle probe, and the check reported four healthy hooks as "does not parse", so setup exited 1 with "this is a gstack bug". Now the rows Bun printed before the crash still count: a reported failure still fails its hook, an ok row still feeds the merge-marker scan, and the shell parse checks still run. Only an entry Bun never reported is unchecked, and the check exits 3 (unavailable, the same as a missing Bun) only when such an entry exists and nothing else failed. A Bun that exits normally without a report still fails every entry it left out. **gbrain prune test (Free Tests 42448270551 shard 3).** `test/gbrain-prune-gone-worktrees.test.ts` saw a parallel shard's live `gbrain autopilot` process through `pgrep -f`, so the removal refused. The fixture now stubs `pgrep` to "no match", as `test/gstack-gbrain-sync.test.ts` already does. **plan-ceo-finding-floor overwrite binding (census 42252633016 slice 7).** The floor actor did not recognize Claude Code's cropped "Do you want to overwrite …?" diff for its own working plan, so the menu waited out `PERMISSION_UNANSWERED_MS`. The binding now handles an overwrite like a cropped Create: it binds to the sole pending owned Write and checks every visible row against the current file bytes and the pending content. The cases live in `test/plan-count-file-permission.test.ts`, the owner test the test-of-test ratchet names. The third-party-actions defer change this PR first carried is gone: review found it counted "I will not mark this step as blocked on you" as a defer option, so those two files are back to main and that flake gets its own fix. ## Why These were open entries in the crew's flaky ledger. Each one failed a PR or census check on a correct run, or (setup) told users healthy hooks were broken. Now those runs pass, and setup refuses only hooks that really fail. ## Blast radius `bin/gstack-hook-check` changes behavior only when its Bun process dies by a signal, and its three consumers stay fail-closed. Setup refuses every hook with a fail line, and `bin/gstack-session-update` holds the update on exit 3 or an incomplete report (walked in `hook_report`, and the signal cases run in `test/setup-hook-syntax-gate.test.ts`). Everything else is test helpers and fixtures. ## Summary Flaky reds on correct runs cost every lane a rerun and hide real failures. This branch removes three causes with a failing-first test each, moves the new overwrite cases into their owner test so the ratchet stays green, and makes the hook check keep what Bun already reported when Bun crashes. ## Test Coverage Coverage: deterministic (each changed runtime file has a changed test naming it). Regression proof: "a failure bun reported before it was killed still fails its hook" fails at d174289 (expected 1, received 3) and passes at 38ef0ad; the crash-plus-broken-shell assertion fails on the original script (expected 1, received 3) and passes after the fix. Tests ran: targeted 257 Tests ran: tests (bun run test) carried from CI at the final head ## Pre-Landing Review Pass 1 fixed one finding (a crash skipped the shell checks), pass 2 found nothing to fix, and Step 11's outside voice found two blockers: a pre-crash fail row was discarded (fixed in 38ef0ad under a granted fix-check) and the widened defer rule accepted a negated mark (reverted to main in 17edf5b under a second grant). Both fix-checks were clean. The last outside voice at 17edf5b: CLEAN. Gate edits: none detected (13 listed, 4 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-doctor:202` still words exit 3 as "bun not found", which misdiagnoses a Bun crash. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-session-update:104` after a Bun crash with a broken shell hook, the hold names hook-check-unavailable instead of the broken file (the update still holds). - INFORMATIONAL `setup:4364` in the crash-plus-real-failure case, setup's lists leave out the TypeScript hooks it registers unchecked, and the "registered unchecked" warning does not print. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-hook-check:205` after a late crash the check can exit 0 while stderr still says the entries cannot be checked. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-hook-check:262` a signal landing between two ok rows of one entry leaves its later imports unscanned for merge markers. - Low: on native Windows a Bun crash may exit at or below 128, so the crash path may never fire there (unverified; that falls back to main's fail-closed behavior). - Low: on the first auto-update after this lands, a crash under the old installed checker can hold the update with a misleading reason. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `bin/gstack-hook-check` at b0336fb (3 probes, all pass): the real checkout exits 0 with an ok per hook; a Bun killed by SIGSEGV exits 3 with no fail lines; a Bun that exits 0 with no report exits 1 with a fail line per TypeScript hook. After the fix, a Bun that prints a fail row and then crashes exits 1 with that fail line (scripted repro and test). ## Eval Results Test-harness files changed. The focused paid runs at 429777e: tpa-present PASS 1/1 ($0.08) and plan-ceo-finding-floor PASS 1/1 (cost not printed). tpa-present's harness change was later reverted to main. The 54-test PR profile was not run (over the $10 focused cap); this is a known gap for a --no-screen READY. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). Daily flaky pass, exempt from planning. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed. **Scope:** 6 commits from 6042f6a to a1e7432 on `fix-flaky-tests-2026-11-08`, 8 committed files and no working-tree changes. The only user-facing change is in `bin/gstack-hook-check`: when Bun is killed by a signal during bundling, the rows it already reported still count, the shell checks still run, and the check exits 3 only when a hook went unreported and nothing else failed. The rest is test fixes plus the changelog.d fragment. **Documentation health:** - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The `auto-update-hook-check-unavailable` entry already counts a crash as an unavailable reason, and the setup refusal entry still describes real parse failures correctly. - `bin/gstack-hook-check` header comment: current. It documents the new exit-3 crash case. - `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`: current. No surface they describe changed. **Coverage debt:** setup's existing warning, "the hook parse check could not run (exit N); hooks are registered unchecked", has no troubleshooting entry. Only reference coverage exists, in the script header and the changelog fragment. This gap predates the branch, and the change now makes the warning reachable after a Bun crash. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Test plan - [x] bun test (targeted: prune, plan-count-file-permission, setup-hook-syntax-gate, third-party-actions, test-of-test ratchet, free-fixtures, session-update hook hold): 257 tests, exit 0 - [x] bun run test: carried from Free Tests at the final head 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
Agent notes Refs GST-1912 ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-ce7fab9a6a7b). The full approval record stays private: this repository is public or its visibility is unknown. Plan: exempt: flaky REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=2 deferred=0 noted=6 fixed=2 scope=frozen unrecorded=1 ledgers_read=8 fix_checks=2 dispatches=8 Gate edits: none detected (13 listed, 4 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Review-loop grants: a-357b0f3ee235 (fix-check at d174289), a-1a987d0e4fd4 (fix-check at 38ef0ad, split). ```gstack-ship-receipt { "schema_version": 1, "pr": 4167, "head": "a1e743245d9b15db0a91f73bf229c57b6e4832e1", "version": "1.98.0.0", "base": "main", "gate": { "tests": { "pass": 1643, "fail": 0, "skip": 0 }, "targeted": { "pass": 257, "fail": 0, "skip": 0 } }, "ci_carried": [ { "lane": "tests", "run": 42494190452, "attempt": 1, "tree": "a23b4ab125c911925178a2b64853c0ccf7496113" } ], "session_kind": "unattended", "head_tree": "a23b4ab125c911925178a2b64853c0ccf7496113", "product_patch_id": "adff9d6c30a1e7f54a87b82b20446944ee69c04f", "gstack_version": "1.98.0.0", "review_depth": { "depth": "full", "class": "gate", "runtime_lines": 21, "rules": "c6a079fdf812f479", "base": "6042f6ad48774504f918ab1391908c1ccdb11fe0", "registry": "6042f6ad48774504f918ab1391908c1ccdb11fe0", "gate_scan": { "tagged": 0, "head": "a1e743245d9b15db0a91f73bf229c57b6e4832e1" }, "reasons": [ "gate-class", "runtime=21" ], "risk": [], "mode": "panel" }, "pregate": "requires-remote cleared @a23b4ab125c9 (8 checks, current for a1e743245d9b)", "requires_remote": [ "free-tests.yml/macos-named-regressions: https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42494190452/attempts/1", "pregate.json/remote_gate: remote-gate tree=a23b4ab125c9 tests=36501 skipped=90 runs=42494190452/1 profiles=ci-reuse/free-tests heads=a1e743245d9b verified=2026-11-08T15:29:22.122Z" ], "issues": { "fixes": [], "refs": [], "flakes": [] }, "docs": { "status": "current", "scope": "AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md and docs/ (troubleshooting.md checked against the hook-check change)" }, "review_loop": { "passes": 2, "blocking_found": 2, "deferred": 0, "noted": 6, "fixed": 2, "scope": "frozen", "fix_checks": 2, "rounds": 4, "unrecorded": 1, "ledgers_read": 8, "dispatches": { "specialist": 6, "red-team": 2 } } } ```

title: A 5-minute video walkthrough of gstack for new users
body:
When people learn a new tool, the biggest cost is communication: someone has to explain what it is and how the pieces fit before anyone can put it to work. To speed that up, I made a 5-minute narrated video so anyone who wants to use gstack gets the high-level picture first: what gstack is, one sprint from `/office-hours` to `/retro`, and how to install it and run a first session.

[![gstack, explained: 5-minute walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flowos-official/gstack-explained/main/thumbnail.jpg)](https://github.com/flowos-official/gstack-explained/releases/tag/v1.0)

**Watch:** [MP4, 5:08, 1080p](https://github.com/flowos-official/gstack-explained/releases/download/v1.0/gstack-explained-1080p60.mp4) · [subtitles (.srt)](https://github.com/flowos-official/gstack-explained/releases/download/v1.0/gstack-explained.en.srt) · [chapters](https://github.com/flowos-official/gstack-explained#chapters)

Commands, roles and facts were checked against `main` at `d479c5b` (8 Nov 2026), and the example app is the one in the README. It is CC BY 4.0, so feel free to link it from the README or docs, or re-cut it. If anything is wrong or out of date, say so here and I will fix it and re-render.

title: /sync-gbrain skips transcript staging when local status is thin-client, though consent is recorded and memory-ingest can stage without a local engine
body:
## What happened

On a machine that is a pure thin client of a remote gbrain (remote-HTTP MCP, gbrain's `remote_mcp` config marker, no local engine), I answered the `/sync-gbrain` transcript question with `new@<UTC time>`. The answer was stored, but the memory stage did not run:

```
SKIP  memory       skipped — local engine thin-client — thin client (remote-HTTP MCP brain, no local engine by design, #2051); code indexing runs on the brain server, memory syncs via the remote brain's artifacts pull — nothing to do locally (0.1s)
```

The skip message says the remote brain's artifacts pull covers this, but the pull only has what this machine stages into `~/.gstack/transcripts/`, and the stage that stages it is the one being skipped. So on this setup the user is asked for transcript consent, sees the destination named as the artifacts repo, and while the status stays `thin-client`, no session can be staged by this command. (This machine has older pages from 2026-10-21/22, before its current gbrain config of 2026-11-02, and none since. My one real run came right after the cutoff, so it had no eligible new session; the point is that the stage did not run at all.) In a real run, the notice that the skill tells the agent to repeat ("The sync prints what it will ingest, in words") does not print, because the skip returns before `printTranscriptNotice`; a dry run does print it.

I expected one of two things:

1. the memory stage stages pages for the pull, as the docs below describe for remote-http mode; or
2. if a pure thin client is deliberately outside transcript export, `/sync-gbrain` says so: no consent question, or a message saying that transcripts are not exported from this machine.

Which of the two is right is a design call; the docs below currently say different things.

### What the code and docs say, at `6417abf7a6f88a54fea523dd885f9be654092f7b` (these files are byte-identical at the installed e75a69c9, 1.97.0.0)

- `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:1551-1560`: the pre-flight skips memory on any local status but `ok` or `timeout`. A gbrain OAuth thin client cannot reach `ok`: `lib/gbrain-local-status.ts:471-476` returns `thin-client` for any config with `remote_mcp`. Its comment gives the reason: "gstack-memory-ingest shells out to `gbrain import` which targets the LOCAL engine". The skip text is at `:1032-1035`, and `printTranscriptNotice` is at `:1573`, after the skip.
- `bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts:2209-2217`: in remote-http mode that binary stages to `~/.gstack/transcripts/` and skips `gbrain import`, so on this path the comment's reason does not apply.
- Docs that promise staging in remote-http mode: `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md:143`, `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl:114-117`, `setup-gbrain/memory.md:42`, `setup-gbrain/SKILL.md:694-698`. `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md:68` describes Path 4 as wanting "the cross-machine memory benefit without standing up a local database". The Step 4d question (`setup-gbrain/sections/brain-init.md:195-198`) says "Transcripts and artifacts continue routing through the artifacts repo" before offering the local PGLite, whichever way it is answered.
- Docs that say it skips: `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl:143-146` ("no local engine BY DESIGN, so the code, memory, and dream stages will SKIP"), and `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md:141` ("only brain-sync runs" when the local engine is missing in Path 4). `brain-init.md:241-243` says answering No at Step 4d ends at `missing-config` or `no-cli` and mentions only the code stage skipping; the current classifier returns `thin-client` when config is absent but a remote-only MCP entry exists (`lib/gbrain-local-status.ts:460`). All of these statuses skip memory.
- `setup-gbrain/SKILL.md:511-517` (Step 7.5) says Path 4 skips the gate because transcript ingest "shells out to the local `gbrain` CLI which Path 4 doesn't install", that a brain admin pulls from the artifacts repo, and that "`/sync-gbrain` asks".
- `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl:235`: the consent step names the artifacts repo as the destination, with no thin-client exception.

The one route to staging I can find in the docs is answering Yes at Step 4d: by my reading of `brain-init.md` that replaces the config with a local PGLite, the status becomes `ok`, and the memory stage then stages (`bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts:2252`). I did not run that case. It means replacing the CLI's thin-client config with a local database described as code-only, while the remote MCP registration stays. I found no flag, env var or config key that opens the gate otherwise. `--sources` selects types and does not bypass it.

I understand #2051 and #1792 added the thin-client state so that healthy thin clients stop reading as broken, and I am not asking to undo that. The question here is only the memory stage's gate. #3539/#3552 made a loopback serve count as local, which is a different case: here the brain really is on another machine.

## Steps to reproduce

A minimal repro of the gate, in a throwaway `HOME`. It sets `recent` rather than `new@`, disables brain-sync, and does not cover the consent question or anything downstream. The thin-client branch returns before the local-engine probe and does not probe remote reachability. Needs gstack, gbrain, `bun` and `jq` on `PATH`.

```bash
GS=~/.claude/skills/gstack
SB=$(mktemp -d); cd "$SB"
run() { env -i HOME="$SB" GBRAIN_HOME="$SB" GSTACK_HOME="$SB/.gstack" PATH="$PATH" "$@"; }
mkdir -p .gbrain .gstack demo
echo '{"engine":"postgres","remote_mcp":{"issuer_url":"https://brain.invalid","mcp_url":"https://brain.invalid/mcp","oauth_client_id":"sandbox","oauth_client_secret":"sandbox"}}' > .gbrain/config.json
echo '{"mcpServers":{"gbrain":{"type":"http","url":"https://brain.invalid/mcp"}}}' > .claude.json
run "$GS/bin/gstack-config" set transcript_ingest_mode recent
git -C demo init -q
git -C demo -c user.email=a@example.com -c user.name=a commit -q --allow-empty -m init
git -C demo remote add origin https://github.com/example-org/demo-repo.git
P=".claude/projects/$(echo "$SB/demo" | sed 's#[/.]#-#g')"; mkdir -p "$P"
TS=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z); SID=11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555
cat > "$P/$SID.jsonl" <<EOF
{"type":"user","parentUuid":null,"cwd":"$SB/demo","sessionId":"$SID","version":"2.1.316","gitBranch":"main","message":{"role":"user","content":"add a hello function"},"uuid":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","timestamp":"$TS"}
{"type":"assistant","parentUuid":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","cwd":"$SB/demo","sessionId":"$SID","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"done"}]},"uuid":"aaaaaaaa-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","timestamp":"$TS"}
EOF
cd demo
run "$GS/bin/gstack-gbrain-detect" | jq -c '{gbrain_mcp_mode,gbrain_local_status}'
run bun run "$GS/bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts" --no-code --no-brain-sync
ls "$SB/.gstack/transcripts" 2>/dev/null | wc -l
run bun run "$GS/bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts" --incremental --sources transcript
find "$SB/.gstack/transcripts" -type f
```

What I got on this setup:

```
{"gbrain_mcp_mode":"remote-http","gbrain_local_status":"thin-client"}
SKIP  memory       skipped — local engine thin-client — thin client (remote-HTTP MCP brain, no local engine by design, #2051); ...
0
.gstack/transcripts/run-<pid>-<ts>/transcripts/claude-code/example-org-demo-repo/2026-11-08-11111111-222.md
```

So the orchestrator stages nothing while `gstack-memory-ingest`, run directly, stages the session without any local engine. I ran that direct call only to test the gate and did not adopt it as a route. I did not check the brain-side pull or anything after staging. The same skip showed on my real machine.

A possible fix, if option 1 is the intended design: let `runMemoryIngest` proceed for `thin-client` when the MCP entry is remote, since that path never calls `gbrain import`, and word the skip accordingly elsewhere. If option 2 is intended: have the consent step and the skip text say that transcripts are not exported from a pure thin client, and align the docs above.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.97.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.97.0.0), codex global current (1.97.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at ~/.bun/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           14 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.167.0; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 16m ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 0)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.97.0.0 (e75a69c9e151)
ok              claude code     2.1.316 (Claude Code) at ~/.local/bin/claude
ok              session journal largest of 6: 350,6 KiB
ok              guard log       no guard decisions logged
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host and version: Claude Code 2.1.316
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu 26.04)
- gstack 1.97.0.0 (e75a69c9), code checked at `main` 6417abf7a6f8 as well; gbrain CLI 0.60.614.0 as a thin client of a remote brain
- Related: #2051, #1792 (thin-client state), #3539 (loopback serve is not Path 4)

title: Stop macOS EPERM marking a finished QA capture as incomplete
body:
On macOS, `gstack-qa-evidence capture` no longer records a command that exited 0 as an incomplete capture, so /ship's exploratory QA stops stalling on commands that worked. This serves gstack's goal of a QA loop you can trust unattended: a capture still fails closed whenever the command's process group has a live member. ## What changed ![Before, any group-kill error except ESRCH failed the capture; after, a macOS EPERM fails it only if the group still has a live member](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/HLtell0qUn4CIo7DyWk0jlT4XufAM0zH63n2FfMSpy8.png) Before, any group-kill error except ESRCH failed the capture; after, a macOS EPERM fails it only if the group still has a live member.
Before/after as text: Before, any group-kill error except ESRCH failed the capture; after, a macOS EPERM fails it only if the group still has a live member ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +function processGroupEmpty(pgid: number): boolean { + try { process.kill(-pgid, 0); } catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ESRCH') return true; } + const listing = spawnSync('ps', ['-A', '-o', 'pgid=,stat='], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5_000 }); + if (listing.status !== 0) return false; + return !listing.stdout.split('\n').some(line => { + const [group, state = ''] = line.trim().split(/\s+/); + return Number(group) === pgid && !state.startsWith('Z') && !state.includes('E'); + }); +} + + ... - const kill = () => { if (!child.pid) return; try { if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGKILL'); else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch (error) { + const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code; + if (code !== 'ESRCH' && !(code === 'EPERM' && process.platform === 'darwin' && processGroupEmpty(child.pid))) outcome = 2; - if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') outcome = 2; } }; ~~~
Before: an `EPERM` from the cleanup kill of an exited command's process group meant `incomplete`, exit 2, on every platform. After, on macOS only: an `EPERM` makes the capture check the group itself. The group counts as gone when `kill(-pgid, 0)` returns `ESRCH`, or when `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` lists no member of that group except zombies (state starting with `Z`) or members that are exiting (the `E` flag). A live member, a failed `ps`, or any other error still fails closed. On Linux and every other platform, `EPERM` fails closed exactly as on main. The macOS teardown state is inferred from XNU and `ps`, not measured: this PR was never run on a Mac. If captures on macOS still come back `incomplete` after a command exits 0, @vilano93, please reopen #4166 or comment here with the capture receipt. ## Why "`gstack-qa-evidence capture` sometimes records a successful command as `status: incomplete`, `exitCode: 2`. The QA chain then refuses `--after` on that capture, so /ship's exploratory QA stalls on a command that worked" (#4166, which measured 3 of 12 captures failing on main and 0 of 16 with a fix). Finished commands now record as complete on macOS, and a group that still has a live member is still reported. ## Blast radius `runQaDeadlineCommand`'s group-kill error path is shared by `lib/qa-evidence.ts:232` (QA captures) and `lib/dx-error-capture.ts:405`. Only the `EPERM`-on-macOS branch changed, and it can only turn a failure into a pass after `ps` shows no live member, so Linux and Windows behave as on main (read at lib/qa-deadline.ts:160-168; the off-macOS test fails without the platform check). The check spawns `ps` (found through PATH) synchronously with a 5 s timeout, only on that path. No network, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies change. ## Summary The QA capture recorded finished macOS commands as incomplete because it treated a teardown `EPERM` like a containment failure. The fix checks the group directly on macOS. Review then narrowed it twice. The check runs only on macOS, so a Linux member hidden from `ps` can't turn a failure into a pass, and the `ps` state parsing now matches macOS, where `E` (exiting) is a trailing flag and `X` means traced. title: Count an autoplan phase report that starts after a preface sentence (GST-1916)
body:
/autoplan no longer stops after Phase 1 when Claude Code saves the phase report as a summary that opens with another sentence. This keeps unattended /autoplan runs on Claude Code going past their first phase.

## What changed

![The guard now counts the captured Phase 1 summary; quoted and example forms still don't count](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/0BuTF_Mbhs6Jl6NGr2VwEzMLUf63CrCijG8Kt1CBouQ.png)

The guard now counts the captured Phase 1 summary; quoted and example forms still don't count.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The guard now counts the captured Phase 1 summary; quoted and example forms still don't count</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+counted Phase 1  <-  I checked the packet against the plan and all four edits are in place, with the native ...
-not counted (publication_missing)  <-  I checked the packet against the plan and all four edits are in place, with the native ...
 not counted (publication_missing)  <-  The template says "Done. Phase 1 is complete. Next." for this step.
 not counted (publication_missing)  <-  Example: Done. Phase 1 complete.
~~~

</details>

## Why

"/autoplan stops after Phase 1 with publication_missing" (#4155, found and diagnosed by @mstormo). Claude Code can save the prose between tool calls as a paraphrased summary, and when the report opened with a check sentence the summary folded that sentence in front of "Phase 1 is complete". The guard only looked at the start of a line, so it denied a report that was really there. It now also reads a declaration that starts a sentence in a plain prose line, so the run moves on to Phase 2.

## Tests

`test/autoplan-publication-mid-sentence.test.ts`, written first. On main (15a35ff) it fails 3 of 25: the captured summary, other sentence-start forms, and the guard replay, which returns `publication_missing`. With the fix, 25 of 25 pass. Negative controls that stay rejected: a declaration inside double, curly or single quotes or inline code, "did not declare Phase 1 complete", "Phase 1 is not complete", "with no outside review", "will be complete", a subordinate "before Phase 1 is complete", Phase 4 and Phase 2.1, list, numbered, heading and quote lines, an example introduced on the previous line or earlier on the same line, and a fenced block. In the guard replay, a quoted, a negated and a Phase 2 summary each stay `publication_missing`.

## Blast radius

Only the autoplan publication detector changes: `autoplanPhaseCompletions`, read by the phase-publication hook (autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts:473) and the autoplan test observers. Compared with main it accepts more reports and never fewer, because the new sentence check only runs where main already returned nothing; the 23 test files that use the detector, the hook or its fixtures ran 686 pass, 0 fail on the fixed tree.

## Summary

A report like "I checked the packet... Phase 1 is complete with 9 native issues and no outside review, so the work moves on to Phase 2." used to stop the run. The detector now checks each sentence start in a plain prose line. A sentence inside quotes or inline code, one after an example or template introduction on the same line, list, heading, table and quote lines, negated or future forms and other phase numbers still don't count. A "with" result is rejected for "no" only when it opens with "no", so "with 9 native issues and no outside review" counts. Review added the same-line example check.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage: test/autoplan-publication-mid-sentence.test.ts names the changed file (deterministic coverage map, no audit reader).
Regression proof: the new test fails 3 of 20 on main (15a35ff) and passes on this branch; review added 3 rejected cases that return [1] at e12449f and [] now.
Tests ran: focused, 23 files, 686 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail (bun test on the fixed tree).

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked (0 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 8 noted.
- [AUTO-FIXED] lib/autoplan-phase-publication.ts:45 a declaration after a same-line unquoted example introduction ("Example: Done. Phase 1 complete.") counted → the sentence check now rejects a preface that names an example, template, marker or expected-output introduction (red-team checklist, confirmed by QA capture 002).
- Fix-check and the native adversarial pass found nothing blocking; their notes are below.

Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

Outside review: not dispatched (review plan: code class, no numeric claims).

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- The same-line example guard matches its word list anywhere in the preface, so a real report whose preface mentions "source", "marker", "sample" or "template" ("I read the source files. Phase 1 complete.") is not counted and the guard asks for the report again. Main already rejected every mid-line report, so this is no regression from main; it narrows the gain. Raised by both the fix-check and the adversarial pass. A narrower trigger (only the last sentence before the boundary, or a word followed by ":" or "reads/says") is the likely follow-up.
- Same-line introducers outside the word list ("E.g. Phase 1 complete.", "For instance. Phase 1 complete.") still count.
- A line starting with an HTML comment or an "(a)" enumerator ("<!-- draft. Phase 1 complete. -->") still counts.
- Withdrawals still match only at line start while declarations now also match mid-line; main already behaved this way for line-start declarations.
- The per-boundary prefix recount is quadratic: a 340 KB line with 20,000 boundaries took about 13 s. Real lines are far smaller.
- "complete with results: no." now counts; contrived.
- The boundary lookahead is case-sensitive and accepts only a space or tab, so "phase 1" and non-breaking-space forms are not counted (fails closed).

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke on the detector through a one-line CLI wrapper (report: .gstack/tmp/qa-reports/run-20261108T162343Z/functional/report.md, verdict pass). A preface plus a real Phase 1 report counts ([1], capture 004). "Example: Done. Phase 1 complete." returned [1] before the review fix (capture 002) and [] after (replay 003). The guard hook path is covered by the test file's guard replay tests, not probed here.

No eval: this is a detector fix, and the new test replays the captured summary through the real guard hook as a narration-journaled report (R56).

The candidate has no staged, unstaged or untracked files. The banned-terms check returned none.

title: StateServer comments/docs say loopback-only, but the IPv6 listener accepts all of fc00::/7 (plus open /healthz and a == bearer check)
body:
Hi! I've been using ios-qa on a real iPhone and read through `StateServer.swift.template` (gstack v1.91.93.0, `e23f7b8`). Nothing here looks like an exploit, and the bearer check held when I poked at it. A few things seemed worth tightening, mostly because the comments and docs say one thing and the code does another.

**1. Comments say loopback-only, but the code accepts all of `fc00::/7`**
Line 4 says "Loopback-only", lines 120-121 say never bind `::`, and the howto says "loopback-only always" (lines 27 and 31). But the IPv6 listener binds the wildcard and filters per connection (lines 154-169, 178), and `isLoopbackPeer` lets in anything in `fc00::/7` (line 227). I get why: the CoreDevice tunnel peers have to get through. But that range is a lot wider than the tunnel. It also covers Tailscale's IPv6 addresses (`fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`) and the ULA prefixes many home routers hand out. Line 191 also mentions an "interface gate" that I couldn't find.

**2. `/healthz` needs no token** (lines 310-321)
It returns `version`, `build`, `accessor_hash` and `bundle_id` to any peer that passes the filter. The daemon only reads `bundle_id` and `boot_token_error` (`tunnel-bootstrap.ts:272-283`, `:440`), and it calls `/healthz` before it has the boot token, so it can't just require auth there.

**3. Bearer compared with `==`** (lines 363, 371)
Not constant-time. The tokens are long and random, so this is hardening more than anything.

**What I saw** (iPhone 11, iOS 27.0, wired, local-USB mode)
- Over the CoreDevice tunnel: `/healthz` gave 200 with no token, and `/state/snapshot` gave 401.
- From the same Mac but not through the tunnel (Wi-Fi addresses, link-locals, etc.): I couldn't connect at all. The phone wasn't answering ICMP or neighbour discovery either, so that fails before TCP and doesn't tell us much either way.
- I didn't test a Tailscale or LAN-ULA peer. I can't say for sure it gets in, only that the code looks like it would.

**Ideas, take or leave**
- Tighten the peer check, e.g. reject Tailscale's `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`, or limit by interface type (I haven't checked what type the tunnel reports).
- Have `/healthz` return only `bundle_id` / `boot_token_error` without a token, and put the rest behind the bearer.
- Use a constant-time compare for the bearer.
- Update the comments and docs to match what the code does.

Happy to test a patch on the device if that helps.

title: Open findings and results write-ups with two or three plain takeaways
body:
Findings, results and investigation write-ups in gstack now open with two or three plain takeaways, what works first. - **We learned that a findings file is most useful when its first lines say what a builder should do.** Every findings file, investigation write-up and results README in gstack now opens with two or three plain takeaways ("We learned X. You should do X."), with what works first. - **What didn't work comes right after, stated plainly with its number.** A null becomes the lesson its data supports, and no number is rounded in our favour or caveat dropped. - **You should name the public lesson before an experiment runs.** /eval-plan's preregistration now asks for a `lesson:` line under Bars. ## What changed - **ETHOS.md, Explain the Number** gains one paragraph with the rule: takeaways first, what works then what didn't, internal mechanics last, each experiment names its public lesson, cost shown only when it is part of the lesson (for example cost per correct answer between two setups), and a repo, dataset or tool opened only with a stated reason (helping builders, or letting others reproduce a published finding). One anti-pattern line is added. - **/eval-plan**: the Bars row of the preregistration table and the `prereg --init` template comment ask for `lesson:` first; Step 5 says the results file opens with the takeaways and points to ETHOS.md for the rest. - **docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md** adds a short "Writing it up" paragraph beside its results reporting guidance, linking ETHOS.md. ![The preregistration's Bars row now asks for the public lesson first](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/LZ5RI4xz7X_Y7r_erzARk8LtfZziR0gfJ21TzBGanUo.png) The preregistration's Bars row now asks for the public lesson first, so the lesson is named before the run.
Before/after as text: The preregistration's Bars row now asks for the public lesson first ~~~diff --- Before · eval-plan/SKILL.md.tmpl § Step 1: Preregistration at 1e25057 · source text +++ After · eval-plan/SKILL.md.tmpl § Step 1: Preregistration on this branch · source text @@ ⋯ 3 unchanged ⋯ @@ | Section | What it holds | |---|---| +| Bars | `lesson:` the public lesson the run is after, then one line per metric: name, pass bar, direction, what a miss means for the decision | -| Bars | one line per metric: name, pass bar, direction, what a miss means for the decision | | Arms | one line per arm: the arm identity first (`` or `#`), settings, per-item cost from Step 1b | | Comparison | `stack: loaded` when any arm loads gstack or another skill stack; otherwise `stack: none` and a `why:` line | | Decoys | inputs the scorer must reject or score low; how many, how they were made, what a decoy pass proves | ~~~
## Why Garry, 2026-11-08: "each markdown file we try to write around an investigation should have up top bullet points that are the two or three big takeaways", "when we discover that something doesn't work, we should just state it plainly", and "this is a gift". His same-day amendment adds that findings don't publish what they cost by default and that private is the default for repos, datasets and tools. gstack is where agents read how to write these files, so the rule lives here rather than only in crew notes. ## Blast radius Prose only, plus one template comment string in `lib/eval-plan.ts` (`prereg --check` already ignores `` guidance, so no check changes). eval-plan/SKILL.md grows by about 75 tokens, so its context-budget ceiling moves from 5,107 to 5,700, the value the capture script computes for it (5,181 × 1.10). No other ceiling moves. ## Summary - One commit: the writing rule in ETHOS.md, its pointers in /eval-plan and docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, the eval-plan context-budget ceiling, and a changelog fragment. ## Test Coverage Coverage: 3 of 4 changed runtime files have no changed test naming them (ETHOS.md, eval-plan/SKILL.md, eval-plan/SKILL.md.tmpl). All three are prose. The parity, context-budget and eval-plan tests pass at this tree, and the coverage audit wrote no new test. ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 0 auto-fixed, 0 asked (0 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 1 noted The review found nothing at the blocking floor (a failing test, a production break, or lost data or secrets). These notes stay open for a follow-up: - **The `lesson:` line is asked for but not checked.** `prereg --check` (`checkPrereg`, lib/eval-plan.ts:131) only requires Bars to be non-empty, so a preregistration without `lesson:` still prints `PREREG: ok`, as QA probe 002 shows. The testing specialist and the adversarial reader both raised this. Making the check enforce it would be new check behavior, outside this writing-rule change. - **Cost in the eval-plan results file.** Step 5 gates the results file before any number leaves the run, and the new paragraph says cost appears there only as part of a lesson. It doesn't say whether that file is a public findings file or an internal report (raised by the adversarial reader). - **No test pins the new `lesson:` text** in the template comment or the skill (raised by the coverage audit). ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `gstack-eval-plan prereg` at tree 856126b692f8: 3 probes, verdict pass. A filled preregistration with `lesson:` passes `prereg --check`.
