title: brain-sync: a derived decisions.active.json conflicts in the retry merge and stops a machine from publishing
body:
## What happened

Two machines sync one artifacts repo (`artifacts_sync_mode` full). Each logs a decision in the same project between two pushes. The second machine's push is rejected, and its fetch-and-merge retry conflicts on `projects/<slug>/decisions.active.json`. `merge_origin_keeping_local_edits` aborts the merge and sync writes `push_failed`. On that machine the same conflict recurred on every drain that had new records, so it stopped publishing until a person repaired it by hand. The two `decisions.jsonl` files themselves merge cleanly.

Observed on 2026-11-08, two machines, last successful push at 15:07Z, found stuck at 18:55Z. The clone was ahead 34 and behind 9. The status read:

```text
push failed: ! [rejected] HEAD -> main (non-fast-forward); merging origin failed: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in projects/<slug>/decisions.active.json; commit retained locally, will retry next run
```

`git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD origin/main` listed exactly two files as conflicted: the `decisions.active.json` of two different projects. No other file conflicted.

Why, from the code at main 1e250570d8c99ad09664d0fd250b29fa2f76509a (VERSION 1.98.0.0):

- `decisions.active.json` is a derived snapshot: `computeActive` and `rebuildSnapshot` in `lib/gstack-decision.ts:186` and `:243` recompute it from the event log, and `bin/gstack-decision-log` rebuilds it after each decision write (`:144`, `:158`).
- `bin/gstack-artifacts-init:399-405` writes `.gitattributes` with `*.jsonl merge=jsonl-append` and the `union` driver for some markdown paths. No line covers `decisions.active.json`, so git's default text merge applies. Two machines each appending a different decision change the same region of the one-line JSON array, and the merge conflicts.
- `bin/gstack-brain-sync:114` puts `decisions.jsonl` and `decisions.active.json` in one `COUPLED_GROUPS` entry, and the `decisions-active` check (`:920-941`) requires the staged snapshot's ids to equal the active ids derived from the staged log. That guards one machine's generation; it does not resolve a merge of two machines' generations.
- The only fetch-and-merge in the script is the retry at `bin/gstack-brain-sync:1498`, which calls `merge_origin_keeping_local_edits` (`:601`). On a failed merge it runs `git merge --abort` (`:619`) and returns the error, and the status is written at `:1513`. The unpushed-commit detector (`:1259-1308`) only runs `git push origin HEAD`, so it never merges and cannot move past a rejection; the daily pull in `bin/gstack-skill-start:495` is `--ff-only` with errors discarded, so it cannot merge a diverged clone either. A later run with an empty queue never reaches the merge and writes the "N local commit(s) are not pushed yet" status instead. Upstream's own test asserts that a conflicting merge is aborted and that the next drain reports the same conflict (`test/brain-sync.test.ts:1001-1016`), so the abort itself is tested behaviour; this report is about a file that can be recomputed from the merged log.
- `bin/gstack-decision-search:59-62` reads the snapshot and rebuilds it when `readSnapshot` returns nothing (absent, unparseable or empty) and a log exists. `bin/gstack-context-recovery` shows "ACTIVE DECISIONS" only when `decisions.active.json` exists as a file.

Manual recovery that worked: drain, `git -C ~/.gstack merge --no-edit origin/main`, delete the conflicted `decisions.active.json` files, run `bin/gstack-decision-search` from a checkout of each project (it rebuilds an absent snapshot), `git add`, commit, `git -C ~/.gstack push origin HEAD`. Afterwards `rev-list` showed 0 0, both snapshots parsed with no conflict markers (196 and 43 rows), and `gstack-doctor` reported 15 ok. This needs a person who knows the files are derived. The commit made by hand is outside `gstack-brain-sync`; the stranded-commit status text says such commits are never auto-pushed (`:1327`).

## Steps to reproduce

Synthetic, no real data; needs git, bun and an installed gstack. The git repositories and each machine's `GSTACK_HOME` are temporary directories.

```bash
GS=~/.claude/skills/gstack; W=$(mktemp -d); cd "$W"
git init -q --bare -b main origin.git
git init -q -b main proj && git -C proj remote add origin https://example.invalid/acme/app.git
setup() { git -C $1 config user.email t@t; git -C $1 config user.name t
  git -C $1 config merge.jsonl-append.driver "$GS/bin/gstack-jsonl-merge %O %A %B"
  echo slug-cache/ >> $1/.git/info/exclude; }
log() { (cd proj && GSTACK_HOME=$W/$1 "$GS/bin/gstack-decision-log" "{\"decision\":\"$2\",\"rationale\":\"r\",\"scope\":\"repo\",\"source\":\"user\"}" >/dev/null); }
git clone -q origin.git a 2>/dev/null; setup a
echo '*.jsonl merge=jsonl-append' > a/.gitattributes   # as bin/gstack-artifacts-init writes it
log a seed; git -C a add -A; git -C a commit -qm seed; git -C a push -q origin HEAD:main
git clone -q origin.git b; setup b
log a "decision on machine A"; log b "decision on machine B"   # same project, between pushes
git -C a add -A; git -C a commit -qm "sync A"; git -C a push -q origin HEAD:main
git -C b add -A; git -C b commit -qm "sync B"
git -C b push origin HEAD:main 2>&1 | grep rejected            # the push the sync sees rejected
git -C b fetch -q origin
git -C b merge --no-edit origin/main 2>&1 | grep -E '^(Auto-merging|CONFLICT)'   # the retry merge
```

Output on 1.98.0.0 (the machine in the report printed `non-fast-forward` instead of `fetch first`):

```text
 ! [rejected]        HEAD -> main (fetch first)
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do
Auto-merging projects/acme-app/decisions.active.json
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in projects/acme-app/decisions.active.json
Auto-merging projects/acme-app/decisions.jsonl
```

`decisions.jsonl` auto-merges through the `jsonl-append` driver; only the snapshot conflicts. This reproduces the git-level merge that `merge_origin_keeping_local_edits` runs. I did not run `gstack-brain-sync` itself against a scratch repo; the `push_failed` status text above comes from the real machine.

## Bug, and a question of design

The defect is that ordinary two-machine use stops one machine publishing. I am not proposing a patch, because the right fix depends on why the snapshot is published at all. Some options:

1. After a retry merge, resolve a conflicted derived snapshot by recomputing it from the merged log (`rebuildSnapshot`) instead of merging its bytes, then continue to the push. This fits the "coupled generation" idea at `:114`: the log is the source of truth, and the snapshot follows it.
2. Do not sync derived snapshots at all: each machine rebuilds after a pull, because `gstack-decision-search` already rebuilds an absent snapshot. That would mean removing the `COUPLED_GROUPS` entry and the snapshot's allowlist entries (`bin/gstack-artifacts-init:329,386`), and deciding what recovers a stale snapshot that already exists locally. `bin/gstack-context-recovery` checks for the file, so a rebuild would have to run before it, or the check would change.
3. A `merge=` driver for the snapshot. A git merge driver is handed that file's three versions (`%O %A %B`). I have not checked whether the merged `decisions.jsonl` is available to a driver at that moment; a plain union of the two snapshots by id would, I expect, bring retired decisions back and so is not enough. I list it as the weakest option.

Which of these fits the intended design? Whatever is chosen, `docs/gbrain-sync.md:196-197` ("`~/.gstack` never holds conflict markers") holds because the failed merge is aborted, and `:191` says "You shouldn't see conflict prompts". The stuck state that follows is not described for a merge conflict on a derived snapshot. `docs/gbrain-sync.md:203-207` says JSON files have no merge driver and that `gstack-doctor` warns about conflict markers in a decision snapshot, which does not cover a merge that was aborted and so leaves no markers. `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md:109-123` ("push failed") tells the reader to run `git status && git push origin HEAD` to see git's full error and says the next skill run retries, with `developer-profile.json` as the example; neither page mentions the snapshot or the recovery above.

## Readiness report

Taken after the manual recovery, so it shows a healthy state and not the stuck one. Paths under the home directory are shortened to `~`; the last row's project paths are removed.

```text
gstack doctor 1.98.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.98.0.0), agy global current (1.98.0.0), codex global current (1.98.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.160.1; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 6h ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
ok              artifacts sync  status idle (mode full; queue 0)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.98.0.0 (910093087dec)
ok              claude code     2.1.309 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal largest of 1: 2.6 MiB
ok              guard log       53 decisions (4 denied)
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (<paths>)
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: Claude Code 2.1.309
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-43-generic
- gstack: installed 1.98.0.0 at commit 91009308. Every file cited above has the same blob SHA at 91009308 and at main 1e250570 (`bin/gstack-brain-sync`, `bin/gstack-artifacts-init`, `lib/gstack-decision.ts`, `bin/gstack-jsonl-merge`, `docs/gbrain-sync.md`, `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md`), so the line numbers apply to both.
- Related, all closed: #3763 (conflict markers committed in `developer-profile.json`; fixed by #3796 holding unparseable JSON), #3704 (push_failed with dirty tracked files; fixed by #3728, which added the stash and the abort this report starts from), #3658 and #3220 (case-collision). #1769 and #3659 concern `gstack-jsonl-merge` only. I searched open and closed issues and pull requests for `decisions.active.json`, `merging origin failed`, `merge_origin_keeping_local_edits` and the symptom in plain words, and found none about the snapshot conflict.

title: Keep crew threads quiet and let busy Captains hand CI watching to a merge lane (GST-1941)
body:
**Takeaways** - Quiet crews are the cheap fix: a crew thread that ends routine turns with end_turn and messages its Captain only for a READY, a blocker, a decision or done removes the wakes that do nothing. In FOUN-216's measurement, 31-43% of Captain wakes ended with no action, many right after a crew's routine progress report, which is about 20-30% of each big Captain's spend (GStack Minder: 280 of 821 wakes in 4.7 days). - A merge-lane thread takes CI off the Captain: PR and CI events were 20-30% of wakes for Captains that act as their own merge lane, so busy Captains now hand PR watching to one crew thread, and each lane keeps its own PR's checks and review. - What makes a wake expensive is coming in cold, not how much it does: any Captain wake more than 5 minutes after its last call rewrites 300-700k tokens of cache at about 19x the warm price ($2.42 against $0.125 per million tokens), as measured in FOUN-216. ## What changed - `capy/skill/gstack/factory.md`, point 10 (**Quiet.**), first sentence rewritten in place: send READY, a blocker, done or a Captain or owner call, else end_turn; no acks or progress notes; the reason is that each message wakes the Captain cold. The page goes from 3,467 to 3,471 bytes, under its 3,475-byte test budget. - `crew/docs/captain.md`, Roles: a new **merge lane** bullet. A Captain whose PRs bring many check, review and merge wakes hands that watching to one crew thread, which reports only a landing, a red check that needs a decision, or a blocker. Other lanes still own their PRs' CI and review up to READY. - `capy/skill/gstack/captain.md`, after section 4's READY paragraph: **Who watches CI**, the lane-side version of the same rule. - A `changelog.d` fragment. ## Why Captains cost the most in a crew, and most of that cost is cold wakes, not work. Two kinds of wake are avoidable: routine reports from crew threads that need no answer, and PR/CI events on a Captain that watches its own PRs. ## Blast radius Guidance text only: no code, tooling, templates or generated files change. `bun run gen:skill-docs --dry-run` reports everything fresh.
Agent notes - Lane GSTA-418 for issue GST-1941, under GStack Minder (GSTA-36). FOUN-216 numbers are relayed as measured in that report (reports/FOUN-216.md in FOUN-32's drive); this lane did not rerun them. - Checks at 5be6144: `bun test` capy-skill-wrapper, captain-skill, prose-voice-floor, parity-suite, context-budget-ratchet, catalog-budget, context-bill, inventory: 209 pass, 0 fail. Whole-tree search found no test pinning the old point 10 wording. - GSTA-409 re-fits its point 10 clause on top of this one-line change.

Each other lane still owns its own PR's CI and review up to READY, + so CI pings wake the lane that can act on them, never the Captain. - **The controller never commits to a lane's branch**, and a lane never pushes to another lane's. One committer per shared tree. ~~~
- `capy/skill/gstack/factory.md`, point 10 (**Quiet.**), first sentence rewritten in place: send READY, a blocker, done or a Captain or owner call, else end_turn; no acks or progress notes; the reason is that each message wakes the Captain cold. Point 10 now limits messages to a READY, a blocker, done or a call the Captain or owner must make. The Captain guide adds an optional merge lane so check, review and merge events stop waking a busy Captain. ## Test Coverage No new code paths: the diff is prose only, so the coverage audit found 0 paths and wrote no tests. title: Stop the pre-push check flagging real files whose names start with tmp or scratch (GST-1944)
body:
The pre-push check's stray-file rule stops flagging real files whose names merely start with `tmp` or `scratch`, and still catches every real scratch name. - **What works:** `tmp` and `scratch` now match only as the whole name stem, optionally numbered. `tmp-watch.js`, `tmpfs-mount.js`, `tmpl.ts`, `tmp_cleanup.py`, `scratchpad.ts` and `scratch-card.tsx` pass; `tmp`, `tmp.js`, `tmp2.js`, `tmp_1.txt`, `tmp-1.js`, `TMP.js`, `scratch.md`, `scratch2.ts`, every `zz-*` name and every editor leftover are still flagged. - **What didn't:** on main, one real module (`lib/server/disk-space/tmp-watch.js` in alphaclaw, ALPH-74) failed with `PREGATE_STRAYS`, and no branch could clear it, because `strays.allow` is read from the base branch on purpose. That base-branch rule is unchanged. The narrower rule also stops catching a stem followed by a word, such as `tmp-repro.ts` or `scratch_notes.md`; the changelog says so and suggests `zz-*` for scratch files. ## What changed `STRAY_NAME` in `lib/pregate/checks/strays.ts` goes from `^(?:zz-|tmp|scratch)` to `^(?:zz-|(?:tmp|scratch)\d*(?:[-_]\d+)?(?:\.|$))`. The `zz-` prefix stays a prefix. The match is still case-insensitive and still runs on the file's base name. `docs/pregate.md`, the `PREGATE_STRAYS` entry in `docs/troubleshooting.md` and the check's header comment describe the new rule.
Text before/after ``` before: /^(?:zz-|tmp|scratch)|\.(?:orig|rej|swp|swo|bak|tmp)$|~$|^\.DS_Store$|^Thumbs\.db$/i after: /^(?:zz-|(?:tmp|scratch)\d*(?:[-_]\d+)?(?:\.|$))|\.(?:orig|rej|swp|swo|bak|tmp)$|~$|^\.DS_Store$|^Thumbs\.db$/i ```
## Why "A real module named `tmp-watch.js` fails the pre-push check and nothing on the branch can clear it" (ALPH-74). The check fails closed and the allowlist is read only from the base branch, so a false positive blocks a branch with no escape. Treating `tmp` as a bare prefix caught module names like `tmp-watch` and `tmpfs-mount`, and `scratch` had the same problem (`scratchpad`). Now those names pass, and real scratch names still fail. ## Summary A branch that adds a real module whose name starts with `tmp` or `scratch` used to fail the pre-push check with no way out. The stray-name rule now matches `tmp` and `scratch` only as the whole stem, so those modules pass while `tmp.js`, `tmp2.js` and `scratch.md` still fail. Review added a case-safe fixture and wrote the tradeoff into the changelog and both docs. ## Blast radius Only the `strays` check's name rule changes. `STRAY_NAME` is used only by `lib/pregate/checks/strays.ts` and its tests (red-team read every consumer). Fewer files get flagged, and no file flagged today as `tmp`, `tmp`, `tmp_`, `scratch` (with an optional extension) or `zz-*` stops being flagged (script ran: the GST-1944 table and fixture). Names with a word after the stem (`tmp-repro.ts`) are no longer caught, by design. ## Test Coverage - New `GST-1944` test in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts`, written first and failing on main (`tmp-watch.js` matched). It checks the regex on the names above and runs `gstack-pregate --only strays` on a fixture: `tmp-watch.js`, `tmpfs-mount.js` and `scratchpad.js` pass, and eight bypass names fail. Review moved the uppercase case to `docs/TMP.js` so no two fixture paths differ only by case, and added `tmp-repro.ts` and `scratch-probe.sh` to the must-not-match list. - The existing GST-1211 test used `lib/tmp-x.ts` as its tmp stray. That name has the same shape as `tmp-watch.js`, so it now passes by design; the fixture uses `lib/tmp.ts` and keeps the same count of four strays. Coverage: deterministic (each of 2 changed runtime files has a changed test naming it; no audit reader). Tests ran: test 1645 (files; carried from CI run 42522445413/1 at tree a255f136479a) ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 5 issues — 2 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 3 noted - [AUTO-FIXED] `test/pregate-selection.test.ts:559` (testing, CRITICAL): the fixture wrote both `lib/tmp.js` and `lib/TMP.js`, which collide on case-insensitive disks (macOS, Windows) → uppercase case moved to `docs/TMP.js`. - [AUTO-FIXED] `lib/pregate/checks/strays.ts:16` (red-team, informational): the dropped `tmp-` class was not written down → stated in the changelog fragment and `docs/pregate.md`, and pinned in the test's must-not-match list. - The `docs/troubleshooting.md:4244` drift (red-team and the docs audit) was fixed after review in a docs-only commit; the docs re-audit is current. - Outside review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): VERDICT: CLEAN. Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. Follow-ups: - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/strays.ts:16` Root-level `tmp-*.md` and `scratch-*.md` files now pass strays silently: `STRAY_NAME` misses them and `ROOT_OK` allows any root `*.md`. The old prefix rule caught them; root `tmp-debug.js` is still caught as a new root file. A root-only prefix check in `run()` would close it. - INFORMATIONAL `test/pregate-selection.test.ts:552` Subdirectory scratch names with a word after the stem (`tmp_test.py`, `tmp-debug.js`, `scratch-notes.ts`) are no longer caught, and the must-not-match list pins `tmp-repro.ts` and `scratch-probe.sh`. Restoring them (a word list, or a warning instead of a pass) is a policy call. ## Exploratory QA Smoke only: the focused GST-1944 and GST-1211 tests passed (4 pass, 0 fail) at the fix commit. QA's method files were not read; no other probe ran. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). Bug fix, exempt from plan review. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The docs on this branch already match the new pregate `strays` naming rule, so nothing needed editing. **Scope:** committed diff from base 19993102 to head 3247e419 on `stop-pregate-flagging-tmp-prefixed-files`. Nothing was staged, unstaged or new. Changed files: `lib/pregate/checks/strays.ts`, `docs/pregate.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` and `changelog.d/stop-pregate-flagging-tmp-prefixed-files.md`. I checked the new `STRAY_NAME` regex against 13 example names, and its results match every example the docs give. **Documentation health:** - `docs/pregate.md`: current. The `strays` entry gives the whole-stem rule with correct examples. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The `PREGATE_STRAYS` meaning matches the code. - `changelog.d/stop-pregate-flagging-tmp-prefixed-files.md`: current. It is accurate and states the tradeoff. - `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/designs/MULTI_AGENT_WAVE_2026_10_10.md`: left as they are. Their `tmp*` and `scratch*` wording records past behavior. **Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none, because no diagrams cover this check. ## Test plan - [x] bun run test: carried from CI run 42522445413/1 at tree a255f136479a (1645 files, exit 0) - [x] bun test test/pregate-selection.test.ts -t 'GST-1944|GST-1211': 4 pass, 0 fail

This PR doesn't change that. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch stop-pregate-flagging-tmp-prefixed-files. title: Let pull requests that only change human-facing docs skip the test suites (GST-1951)
body:
A pull request that only changes human-facing docs now skips the test suites and runs a quick link and docs check instead, so docs fixes merge in minutes.

## What changed

- **One classifier.** `lib/docs-only.ts` (CLI `bin/gstack-docs-only`) decides whether every changed path is human docs. The allowlist is root `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md` and `changelog.d/*.md`. A denylist keeps agent instructions, policy docs, templates, sections, pinned results, preregistrations and generated outputs out. Any doc that a script, test, workflow or skill names by path stays out too. Renames check both sides. Any git error means "not docs-only".
- **CI.** A `docs-scope` job in `free-tests.yml` and `windows-smoke.yml` runs the base branch's classifier on the merge commit. Suite jobs skip only when `docs-scope` succeeded and said docs-only. A new `docs-lane` job checks links on the lines the PR added and runs the tests that read docs by directory. The required `free-tests` check still always runs, passes a docs-only PR only after docs-lane passed, and records no tested tree.
- **windows-smoke always reports success.** The job always runs and skips its steps on a docs-only PR, because gstack's land counts only a check that concluded success.
- **Pregate, CI carry and /ship.** On a docs-only change the `lanes` check runs the same docs lane and owes no remote gate. A docs-only CI run carries as `not_owed=docs-only` when the local classifier agrees.
- **Land.** `land.docs_only_skip` can drop the merged-tree test list for a docs-only pin. Land keeps every check when a non-docs file on the base tip names a changed doc. The key isn't turned on in `.gstack/ship-policy.json` yet, because older gstack builds refuse it as unknown.

## Why

Garry asked for this on 2026-11-08: "For docs changes pls stop doing full CI and merge without tests. If there are really only docs." Docs-only PRs spent 45-51 Free Tests runner-minutes and 6-8 minutes of wall time each on suites their changes can't affect (runs 42417651501, 42244137054). In the 300 PRs merged 2026-11-01..11-08, 2 qualify (#4144, #4081). The saving inside gstack is small. The bigger value is that every crew's /ship and pregate get the class by default.

## Blast radius

Every pull request now runs one extra `docs-scope` job in `free-tests.yml` and `windows-smoke.yml`. Code pull requests run the same suites as before. If the classifier crashes or errors, every suite runs. Pushes to main always run the full suites. Land behavior is unchanged until main's policy turns on `land.docs_only_skip`.

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 14 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 9 asked (9 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 5 noted
Gate edits: 30 listed, 20 read, 2 findings — 2 kept (reasons below), 0 restored, 0 open
- RH-15? `.github/workflows/free-tests.yml` docs-scope/docs-lane hunk: kept, it is the feature (suites skip only on a successful docs-only verdict).
- RH-15? second tagged workflow hunk: kept for the same reason. The contract tests that pin the workflow shape were updated on purpose and reviewed in both passes.

The full R51 panel ran: specialists (testing, security, state machines), red team, native adversarial, a cross-family outside voice (GPT-6.1 Sol) and the targeted gate reader. Pass 1 ran on c06b33a. Pass 2 re-checked the fixes on c06b33a..f285d09.

Fixed:
- Land skipped the merged-tree tests when the base tip had gained a reader of a changed doc. It now keeps every check in that case.
- gstack builds older than this change reject `land.docs_only_skip` as an unknown key, so the key is held out of main's policy.
- Two tests that read docs by directory (`no-stale-gstack-brain-refs`, `codex-web-search-flag`) are now registered in `DOCS_READER_TESTS`.
- The docs lane now sets a git identity for the reader tests that commit fixtures.
- The link check now covers untracked docs and docs with quoted or spaced names, and it reports an undecodable anchor instead of crashing.
- `windows-smoke` no longer skips at job level, which would have failed every docs-only land.

Noted (below the blocking floor; no test, production or data risk today):
- verifyRun's docs-only branch doesn't confirm that docs-lane itself succeeded, or that the run's merge tree matches the head.
- The PR's own `./.github/actions/docs-scope` action file controls the GitHub check result. gstack's carry still reclassifies locally.
- A succeeded docs-scope gate also accepts a skip caused by reuse. It is refused later as `artifact_missing`.
- The docs-lane link step has no `pipefail`, so a `git diff` failure there passes.
- The land guard catches readers that name a doc by its literal path, not directory scanners added on the base. This is dormant while the policy key is held.

## Test Coverage

Coverage: 68% value-weighted (68% including 0 weakly covered paths), 7 gaps. 0 tests added by the audit (audit only). Gaps: the docs-only-lane reader-test branches, the run_changed and api_error paths in the verifyRun docs-only branch, the run-check docsOnly closure, the two land-direct call sites, and a real-action E2E of the docs-scope composite. The check-doc-links CLI gap has since been closed (test added in a91b6c9).

## Exploratory QA

Functional CLI probes of `gstack-docs-only` on an isolated clone: 7 probes, verdict pass. A referenced doc, an agent-instruction name, an executable doc, a push event and this PR's own diff all refuse. An unreferenced new doc is docs-only and selects the 6 reader tests, and a pull_request run writes `docs_only=true`. Limits: the workflow-level behavior is covered by YAML contract tests and CI only.

## Evals

Not run. The selector fell back to all 113 behavioral probes because `.github/actions/docs-scope/action.yml` is an unknown dependency. That is far over the $10 per-PR cap, and no paid case's reference closure reaches the classifier.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR.

## Documentation
**Status:** updated. One factual anchor fix; no blockers.

**Scope:** base b6155921..f285d09 on gst-1951-docs-only-prs (5 commits, 32 files) plus the unstaged test/docs-only.test.ts. Audited the docs-only PR feature (GST-1951/R81) against lib/docs-only.ts, bin/gstack-docs-only, lib/land-docs-only.ts, lib/pregate/docs-only-lane.ts, lib/ci-carry.ts and the free-tests, windows-smoke and docs-scope workflows.

Documentation health:
  docs/pregate.md                 Updated (moved the flaky-exception anchor back to the Owner-granted flaky exception heading; the new Docs-only section had taken it over)
  docs/ship-policy.md             Current (land.docs_only_skip row matches land-merged-checks validation)
  docs/troubleshooting.md         Current (docs-only-error entry matches the CLI's error line and exit 2)
  capy/skill/gstack/factory.md    Current
  ship/sections/tests.md(.tmpl)   Current (template and generated copy agree; the not-owed wording matches ci-carry)
  changelog.d fragment            Current (matches the classifier's allowlist, denylist and fail-closed rules)
  CHANGELOG.md / TODOS.md         Skipped (ship-owned mode)

Documentation coverage:
  gstack-docs-only CLI / docs lane   reference: docs/pregate.md#docs-only; how-to: partial (CI reuse recipe); tutorial: none; explanation: docs/pregate.md
  land.docs_only_skip                reference: docs/ship-policy.md and docs/pregate.md; no how-to

Debt: common gaps only (no tutorial). The docs-only feature is reachable from README only through docs/pregate.md.

Diagram drift: none found.
## Test plan

- [x] Focused: `bun test test/docs-only.test.ts test/docs-only-carry.test.ts test/docs-only-workflow.test.ts test/ci-reuse-workflow-wiring.test.ts test/cso-distribution.test.ts test/windows-native-workflows.test.ts test/windows-path-scope-workflow.test.ts test/autoplan-residuals.test.ts`: pass

To turn it on, after the first release that contains this change, add `"docs_only_skip": ["bun run scripts/test-free-shards.ts --files-from test/land-merged-checks.txt --wall-timeout 600"]` under `land` and raise `min_gstack_version` to that release in the same PR. Until then land runs every merged check on docs-only PRs.

title: Advance the gbrain worktree at the end of every sync, after its commit (#2516 follow-up)
body: ## Why (in your own words) gbrain indexes `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`, a detached worktree of `~/.gstack`. Since #2516 the drain advanced that worktree, but at the **start** of `gstack-brain-sync --once`, before the drain's own commit, and at most once per 24h (`~/.gstack/.brain-worktree-last-advance`). So the brain was always missing what gstack had just published: a new learning or plan reached gbrain only after a later drain, a day or more afterwards. I hit this on my own machine, where the worktree kept lagging `~/.gstack` and I had to `git checkout --detach` it by hand to get new artifacts into search. This PR moves the advance to the drain's EXIT trap, after its commit and any merge from the remote, and drops the 24h window: every drain that finds the worktree behind advances it. An interrupted drain (INT/TERM) skips it. A failed or refused advance (for example a dirty worktree) warns once and holds retries for 24h via `~/.gstack/.brain-worktree-advance-failed`, so the warning does not repeat at every skill start; a successful advance clears the hold. The no-force-remove guarantees of `--advance-only` are unchanged. A second, smaller fix rides along: `gstack-artifacts-init` asked `gh auth status` and `glab auth status` on every run, but only the "which git host?" choice uses the answers. Without a glab config, `glab auth status` can block for ~30s, so every `init --remote` paid that wait, and the brain-sync tests that set up an artifacts repo sat right on their 30s timeout (most of `brain-sync.test.ts` timed out on my machine, on `main` as well). The checks now run only inside the branch that makes the choice. ## Live evidence Before/after with the same script: a fresh `HOME`, `gstack-artifacts-init --remote `, a detached brain worktree, one queued learning, one `gstack-brain-sync --once`. ``` === BEFORE (main @ aa46032f2) === $ gstack-brain-sync --once advance-only: up-to-date at 3b6d0ea8e8df9d4d1ae72ec39c791200e6c9c924 ~/.gstack HEAD: 8a0c154 sync: 1 file(s) | 2026-11-09T00:40:36Z ~/.gstack-brain-worktree HEAD: 3b6d0ea chore: gstack-artifacts-init learnings.jsonl in worktree: NO === AFTER (this branch) === $ gstack-brain-sync --once advance-only: advanced .../.gstack-brain-worktree to 0f543205022b527c13eb48ad76524cb73319d760 ~/.gstack HEAD: 0f54320 sync: 1 file(s) | 2026-11-09T00:40:37Z ~/.gstack-brain-worktree HEAD: 0f54320 sync: 1 file(s) | 2026-11-09T00:40:37Z learnings.jsonl in worktree: yes ``` The glab wait, traced with a timestamped `PS4` on `main`, and timed directly: ``` 31s before: + gstack-artifacts-init:118: glab auth status $ time (HOME=$(mktemp -d) glab auth status) # no glab config 30.235 total $ time (glab auth status) # my real config 0.767 total ``` Tests (macOS, Bun): ``` # related suites, with a glab that exits at once so both sides avoid the 30s wait branch: 202 pass / 1 fail / 0 timeouts main: 200 pass / 1 fail / 0 timeouts failing on branch only: (none) # the shared failure, also on main: # brain-sync.test.ts:756 "publish-removals refuses to push a retained commit that adds a case alias" # Expected "error", Received "push_failed" # test/gbrain-source-worktree-advance.test.ts, real glab on PATH 9 pass / 0 fail, 3.0s (the 3 new tests fail on main) # test/gstack-artifacts-init.test.ts 32 pass / 1 fail — the 2 new "never asks gh or glab for their auth status" tests fail on main and pass here; the failure ("partial allowlist assembly failure preserves the original…") fails identically with main's script. ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** `bin/gstack-brain-sync` (advance moved to the EXIT trap, 24h throttle replaced by a 24h hold after a failure), `bin/gstack-artifacts-init` (auth checks only where the host choice is made), `bin/gstack-brain-uninstall` (removes the new stamp), comments in `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup`, `docs/gbrain-sync.md`, tests, changelog fragment. - **Verified live by:** the before/after reproduction above; deploying the branch to my own `~/.claude/skills/gstack` and running a drain against my real `~/.gstack` (worktree and parent on the same commit, no failure stamp). - **Did NOT test:** Linux or Windows; the full `bun run test` suite; paid evals (`eval:bg:pr`). I ran only the brain-sync, wireup, artifacts-init, egress, migration and decision suites listed above. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: #2516 (follow-up; reproduction above) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Keep home paths, thread ids and costs out of PR text on public repos (GST-1955)
body: On a public repository, PR text that gstack posts no longer names home paths, Capy thread ids or what a run cost. /ship's run record goes out in a public form, and any such detail left in a title, body or comment stops the post. ## Takeaways - **It works for the receipt without slowing /ship down.** The receipt block is machine-written, so gstack-post rewrites it instead of refusing it: no cost, credits or token field, the run and thread as an opaque id that still deduplicates, and paths cut to the file name. A repro of PR #3964's receipt now posts clean and still binds to its head. - **Prose is refused, never silently edited.** A home path (POSIX, macOS, tilde, Windows, MSYS, inside code too), a Capy id other than the platform badge, or a dollar, credits or token figure refuses the post with a line number and rule, never the value. - **What didn't hold before, and what this will now stop: 44 of the last 120 PR bodies here (#4043 to #4178) would be refused by the new check, 29 for a cost or token figure and 21 for a home path (mostly tilde paths).** Receipts with a spend field ran through #3964 and the writer still accepts one; gstack-post flagged none of it beyond a LOW note. The REVIEW_LOOP line /ship writes loses its token estimate the same way the receipt does, so /ship itself still posts. ## What changed - `lib/public-pr-text.ts` (new): reads the repo visibility (flag, then the `redact_repo_visibility` config override, then gh or glab; unknown counts as public), rewrites receipt and receipt-runs blocks into the public form, and finds home paths, Capy ids and cost figures. - `gstack-post`: unless the repo is private, sends the public receipt form (prints `PUBLIC_FORM:`) and refuses any other detail with `PUBLIC: LINE: PART: `, exit 1. The merged pr-body is what gets checked, so an old receipt in a kept section is rewritten too. - `gstack-ship-receipt carry --pr`: it posts with gh directly, so it applies the same public form. - Docs: `docs/troubleshooting.md#gstack-post-public-text`, gstack-post usage text, and a changelog fragment. ## Why Harness Evals found, while reviewing a move of harness-evals to public, that /ship's PR text carries private details. On this public repo, PR #3964's receipt holds a spend figure, a Capy run id and a thread code; #3878 and #3482 carry an absolute home path from the remote-gate pregate line; #4145 and #4078 carry scratch paths in prose. Garry's findings rule says no cost in public unless cost is the lesson. ## Blast radius Private repositories post exactly the bytes they did before. Public ones, and repos whose visibility gh cannot read, now refuse prose with costs or home paths, so crews will rewrite those lines. Thread codes written in prose (like an issue key) can't be told apart from issue keys, so only receipt fields and Capy URLs and ids are covered there. Text posted outside gstack-post (the host's own PR tool, other gh calls) is not checked. ## Tests - `test/gstack-post-public-text.test.ts` (new, 12 tests): the #3964 and #3878 repro, fail-closed visibility, the private and config-override paths, a merged body, and bypass cases (a home path in a code span, a Windows path, a cost written as a dollar amount, a jam id inside a URL) plus prose that must still post. - `test/ship-receipt-carry-public.test.ts` (new, 3 tests): carry through a gh stub on public, unknown and private repos. - Both fail on main (b615592) and pass on this branch. Existing gstack-post, receipt and publication tests pass; typecheck and the test typecheck ratchet are clean.

title: /autoplan tells the agent to write a gate item with id `plan`, which gstack-gate rejects
body:
## What happened

`/autoplan` Phase 4 tells the agent to write `$_AP/gate.json` with one item per user challenge (`uc<n>`), one per taste decision (`d<n>`) "and `plan`". It then says `all` or `plana` means approve, and `planc`/`pland`/`plane` mean interrogate, revise, reject (`autoplan/SKILL.md:625-629`, `:666-667`; template `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:360-364`, `:401-402`, at commit b6155921a564ba9ec2470fd2cb3894c05e2c2d13).

`gstack-gate` refuses that id. `ID_RE` in `lib/gate-list.ts:75` is `/^[a-z]*[0-9]+$/`, and the render stops, so the gate cannot be shown as the skill describes:

```text
gstack-gate: g.json is not a gate list:
  items[1].id must match [a-z]*[0-9]+ (lowercase label plus a number, e.g. d3, uc1, 12)
exit=1
```

The helper-built gate in `lib/autoplan-gate.ts:269` already uses `p1` for this item (`id: 'p1', title: 'Plan approval'`), and `docs/unattended.md:513` names `p1` plan approval, so the skill text looks like the part that is out of date. A grep for `p1` as an item id in `autoplan/SKILL.md` and its template found nothing.

The reply tokens fail the same way. `gstack-gate parse` answers a reply of `plana` with `part of the reply matched no gate item or option, so nothing was applied (unparsed: plana)`, because the token regex at `lib/gate-list.ts:207` needs a digit too. With the item renamed to `p1` the gate renders and `p1a` parses.

Expected: the id and reply tokens in the skill match what `gstack-gate` accepts.

A likely fix is to change `plan` to `p1`, and `plana`/`planc`/`pland`/`plane` to `p1a`/`p1c`/`p1d`/`p1e`, in `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl`, then regenerate.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Write a gate list with the skill's id:

   ```json
   {"schema_version":1,"run":"synthetic","gate_rev":1,"items":[{"id":"d1","title":"x","kind":"auto","recommended":"a","options":[{"key":"a","text":"y"},{"key":"b","text":"z"}]},{"id":"plan","title":"The plan","kind":"approval","recommended":"a","options":[{"key":"a","text":"approve"},{"key":"b","text":"overrides"}]}]}
   ```

2. Run `gstack-gate render g.json`. It exits 1 with the message above.
3. Change the id to `p1` and run it again. It renders.

Found in a real `/autoplan` run. Reproduced on the installed 1.98.0.0 with the synthetic file above; the cited lines were read at the commit above, which is 9 commits past the installed build.

title: Walk CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME session stores in the transcript ingest
body:
## Bug

`bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts` walks `~/.claude/projects` and `~/.codex/sessions` only. A profile that sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` to another dir under HOME (for example a separate dev config dir at `~/.claude-dev/.claude` with `CODEX_HOME=~/.claude-dev/.codex`) keeps its sessions there, so `/sync-gbrain` never ingests them, whatever `transcript_ingest_mode` says. The probe and `gbrain transcripts status` both report only the default homes.

Repro on gstack 1.98.0.0 at b615592 (macOS): with 1017 Claude Code session files under `~/.claude-dev/.claude/projects` and 188 Codex files under `~/.claude-dev/.codex/sessions`, `transcript_ingest_mode: new@<now>+repos` for the repo those sessions belong to, `gstack-memory-ingest --probe --sources transcript --all-history` counts 0 of them; the script has no env override (`grep process.env bin/gstack-memory-ingest.ts` finds only `GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_NO_WRITE`).

## Fix

Both walks take the default home plus the dir the variable names, when that dir lies inside HOME, with the default home never walked twice when the variable spells it another way. A dir outside HOME is not walked: a session store belongs to the home being walked, and a config dir elsewhere (another user's, a mount, a test's temporary HOME) is not part of it. This also keeps the existing tests hermetic when a contributor's own shell exports `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; without the guard those tests walk the contributor's real sessions.

Doc rows in `setup-gbrain/memory.md` name the extra roots. No VERSION or CHANGELOG change, per CONTRIBUTING.

## Test evidence

New test in `test/transcript-scope-ingest.test.ts` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME`): one default-home Claude session, one Claude session and one Codex session under custom homes inside the box HOME. Probe counts 3 with the variables set, 1 without, and 1 when the variables spell the default home. On the untouched base it fails with `Total files in window: 1` where 3 is expected; with the fix it passes.

`bun test test/transcript-scope-ingest.test.ts test/gstack-memory-ingest.test.ts`: base 101 pass, 5 skip, 3 fail; with the fix 102 pass, 5 skip, 3 fail. The 3 failures are the same before and after:
- requested secret scanning at the import boundary > refuses a saved deny page in a mixed-policy scanned resume
- requested secret scanning at the import boundary > refuses a saved read-only page in a mixed-policy scanned resume
- #2394 > parity: probe post-attribution count equals what prepare actually processes

`bun test test/memory-ingest-sources.test.ts test/transcript-scope-brain-sync.test.ts test/gstack-gbrain-sync-transcript-mode.test.ts`: 34 pass, 4 fail, identical on base and with the fix.

## Not covered

- `bun run typecheck` did not run here: the production install has no `bun-types`, and I did not add the dev toolchain to the shared install. CI's checks cover it.
- A sync run from one profile sees that profile's custom home plus the default home, not another profile's custom home; the other profile's own sync picks those up, and the shared ingest state skips duplicates.
- Windows is untested (the new test is skipped there like its neighbours).

title: gstack-flaky: document or support runners that write one JUnit file per test class (Gradle)
body:
## What happened

`gstack-flaky run --junit` takes one `.xml` report. Gradle's `test` task writes one `TEST-<class>.xml` per test class under `build/test-results/<task>/`, and writes no single aggregate JUnit report that we know of. `docs/flaky.md` does not cover this case.

Checked at `b6155921a564ba9ec2470fd2cb3894c05e2c2d13`:

- `docs/flaky.md:7-9` lists "any runner that writes JUnit: Playwright, `bun test`, jest, vitest and pytest". The Runners table (`docs/flaky.md:40-46`) has no row for a runner that writes several files, and the page does not mention Gradle.
- `bin/gstack-flaky:132` refuses a directory: `--junit must name a .xml file (it is deleted before every attempt)`. That deletion is a good reason to keep one file, so this is not a report that the refusal is wrong.

This is a request, not a defect: nothing misbehaves, the case is just not covered.

## Steps to reproduce

Installed gstack v1.98.0.0, with a stand-in for Gradle that writes two passing classes (synthetic, not a real Gradle run):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ./fake-gradle
mkdir -p build/test-results/test
printf '<testsuite name="A" tests="1"><testcase name="a" classname="A"/></testsuite>\n' >build/test-results/test/TEST-A.xml
printf '<testsuite name="B" tests="1"><testcase name="b" classname="B"/></testsuite>\n' >build/test-results/test/TEST-B.xml
```

```text
$ gstack-flaky run --runner generic --junit build/test-results/test -- ./fake-gradle
gstack-flaky: --junit must name a .xml file (it is deleted before every attempt), got "build/test-results/test"
(exit 2)

$ gstack-flaky run --runner generic --junit build/test-results/test/TEST-A.xml -- ./fake-gradle
FLAKY_RESULT: tests=1 failed=0 flaky=0 quarantined=0 reruns=0 command_exit=0 verdict=pass ledger=none
(exit 0; the second class is not in the count)
```

Pointing `--junit` at one class passes with only that class counted, so a reader can take it for a working setup.

## What would help

Either of these, whichever fits the tool's design:

1. A row in the Runners table for one-file-per-class runners, with a supported recipe: inside the `bash -c` wrapper, clear the old results, run the build, keep its exit status, and join the per-class files into the one report `--junit` names. The join has to clear old results first, so a removed test class is not joined from an earlier run. `lib/junit.ts` parses concatenated `<testsuite>` documents as they are, so a plain `cat` works for `gstack-flaky`; the recipe should say so, or, when other tools read the file, say to strip each file's XML declaration and wrap the suites in `<testsuites>`.
2. A way to name the runner's report directory or glob, with `gstack-flaky` doing the join and the clearing itself.

## Alternatives

We ran recipe 1 in our own workflow. It worked against a fake Gradle: a rerun pass was recorded as a flaky pass, a double failure stayed red, and a build failure with no test failure stayed red. The cost is about ten lines of shell per repository, and each repository has to find the same details on its own. We did not run it on a real Gradle build in this check. The core of it, run with the stand-in above (`RUNNER_TEMP` as GitHub Actions sets it):

```bash
gstack-flaky run --runner generic --junit "$RUNNER_TEMP/junit.xml" -- bash -c '
  rm -rf build/test-results/test
  ./fake-gradle
  rc=$?
  cat build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml >"$RUNNER_TEMP/junit.xml"
  exit "$rc"' _
```

This printed `FLAKY_RESULT: tests=2 failed=0 flaky=0 quarantined=0 reruns=0 command_exit=0 verdict=pass ledger=none` on v1.98.0.0.

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code
- gstack: v1.98.0.0 installed; docs and code cited at `b6155921a564ba9ec2470fd2cb3894c05e2c2d13`
- OS: Linux
- Searched this tracker for `gradle` and for flaky JUnit multi-file wording: no matches. Related: #3612 (added `gstack-flaky`).

title: Let review exclusions handle big results PRs (GST-1967)
body:
Big results PRs whose captured transcripts only mention a credential's name now fit under /ship's review size limit, so data-heavy PRs like harness-evals#333 can be reviewed and shipped again. **Takeaways** - harness-evals#333 now fits under the review ceiling. The reader's diff goes from 5,458,045 bytes to 1,061,721 (2 MB ceiling). All 20 matching patterns apply, 5,931 files are excluded and none is kept. - Files whose lines only name a credential (`$AGENT_API_TOKEN`, `${OPENAI_API_KEY}`, a keychain) stop being kept. Lines that name a credential and carry a value still keep their file: a key value, `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…`, a key inside a JSON string, a key after the name, and a base64 blob. - Fixing the 24,000-byte cap alone made #333 worse, not better: all 2,610 kept files went to readers as excerpts, 29,782,265 bytes. `git diff` has no `--pathspec-from-file` (git 2.55 prints its usage), so the cap fix chunks git calls instead. ## What changed **Which lines keep a file.** Under `review_exclude_paths`, a data file stayed in review if any added line named a credential. Captured model prompts name `$AGENT_API_TOKEN` and keychains all the time, so #333 kept 2,610 trial files. Now `secretValueLine` (lib/review-exclude.ts) keeps a file only when a line names a credential and carries a value. That means one of two things. Either the credential scan the secrets check runs finds a secret on the line (the same scan and env-read rule as #4157), or a credential-shaped run of 20+ characters mixing upper case, lower case and digits follows the name within 200 characters. Variable references like `$X` are never counted as values. A key name given a value (`OPENAI_API_KEY=`, `"GH_TOKEN": `) also counts as a name now. **The argument-byte cap.** Files kept only for a secret line reach readers as an excerpt file, never through the `DIFF_KEEP:` command. So they no longer count toward the 24,000-byte bound, and `DIFF_KEEP:` leaves them out. `readSelection` reads both the kept files and the excerpt files in git calls of at most 24,000 argument bytes each, so no command passes Windows' limit. Kept files that a reader's command names still count toward the bound. ## Why "HARN-1's results PR harness-evals#333 couldn't get a /ship receipt." Its `docs/benchmarks/*/main/trials/**` pattern needed 251,063 argument bytes for its kept files, so the pattern wasn't applied, and splitting the PR doesn't help. With this change the pattern applies and the reader's diff fits under the ceiling. Measured on the real PR tree (base 5c685dfc, head dd42b9e6) through `collectCommit`, `reviewExclude` and `readSelection`. | Build | Patterns applied | Kept | Reader diff bytes | |---|---|---|---| | main (b6155921) | 18 of 44 (main/trials, pilot/trials skipped) | 2,610 | 5,458,045 | | cap fix only | 20 of 44 | 2,610 (all excerpted) | 29,782,265 | | this PR | 20 of 44 | 0 | 1,061,721 | Of the 21,932 matched lines in the 2,610 files, none carries a value under the new rule. ## Blast radius This changes only which files under a base `review_exclude_paths` pattern are kept, and how kept files are read, so repositories without that key plan exactly as before (lib/review-exclude.ts read). Pregate's secrets check is unchanged and still scans every added line. Four existing fixtures used name-only lines (`curl -H $OPENAI_API_KEY`) to stand for a credential line, and each now carries a base64 value so it still tests the keep, excerpt and selection paths it was written for. ## Summary Results PRs with thousands of captured transcripts couldn't get a receipt because every transcript that mentioned an API key's name stayed in review. The first commit adds the value rule and the chunked reads (c54117da), and the second moves the value rule out of the pinned review-risk module (66c98ecb). A third commit (19c26dc9) rewords the changelog entry so it passes the prose check. ## Test Coverage Coverage: deterministic. Each of the 4 changed runtime files has a changed test naming it (bin/gstack-review-plan, lib/review-exclude.ts, lib/review-targeted.ts, docs/ship-policy.md; map from the /ship audit). No audit reader was needed. Tests ran: targeted 77 Tests ran: typecheck count unavailable Tests ran: typecheck-test count unavailable ## Pre-Landing Review Full panel (forced): one batched specialist over all nine checklists, the Red Team, the native adversarial voice, an outside voice on openai/gpt-6.1-sol and the targeted secret reader. No finding fails a test or loses data. Two findings the outside voice marked blocking were kept open under the crew's blocking floor and are listed for a follow-up. - [CRITICAL, skipped under the blocking floor] lib/review-exclude.ts:386. A file kept only for a key=value line (no `SECRET_LINE` match) can't be excerpted, yet it was exempted from the 24,000-byte bound. So `settleExcerpt` adds it whole to one reader keep command, and 400 such files make a 32.8 to 56 KB command, past Windows' limit. The Red Team, the native voice and the outside voice all found it, and QA captures 003 and 005 replayed it. It fails closed (readers get more, never less). Follow-up: count a file as excerptable only when an added line matches `SECRET_LINE`, or make the excerpt use `secretValueLine`. - [CRITICAL, skipped under the blocking floor] lib/review-exclude.ts:476. `readSelection` concatenates every excerpt chunk's raw diff before excerpting, so the 256 MB buffer bounds each git call, not the total. A multi-gigabyte set of excerpt files could exhaust memory before the 2 MB ceiling applies. Follow-up: excerpt each chunk and keep only its output. - [INFORMATIONAL, skipped] lib/review-exclude.ts:92. `VALUE_TOKEN` allows `/`, so a mixed-case path with a digit within 200 characters after a credential name counts as a value and keeps the file (QA 002 and 004 replayed it). That over-keeps; it never hides a file. - [INFORMATIONAL, noted] lib/review-exclude.ts:102. A transcript that names a credential on one line and prints a scanner-HIGH token on the next no longer keeps its file, so readers stop seeing that token. The CI credential scan of added lines still fails HIGH tokens. - [Medium, noted] An excerpt can leave out the value line that kept its file, when the token check rather than the scanner found it. This omission is pre-existing. - [Low, noted] `secretValueLine` scans whole lines with no per-line limit, and a contrived 200 KB line took 7.7 s. `DIFF_KEEP:` now omits excerpt files, so a reader built by hand from `DIFF_CMD`/`DIFF_KEEP` sees neither. The change narrows what readers see, which crew rule 15 gates on a no-loss replay. Outside review: completed (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, VERDICT: FINDINGS). ## Review notes The six noted findings above are below the blocking floor. The two skipped CRITICAL findings are named for the owner. No issue was filed: this unattended run files no GitHub issues. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `secretValueLine` and `secretExcerpt` (pure functions, run in place, no writes). Capture 001 passed: name-only lines keep nothing, while `KEY=value` and a JSON key with a value keep their file. Captures 002 and 004 failed: a path after a credential name counts as a value. Captures 003 and 005 failed: a key=value-only file goes whole instead of being excerpted. The verdict is fail, on the two INFORMATIONAL findings above, which the crew's floor accepts as non-blocking. Limit: no end-to-end `gstack-review-dispatch pass` over a synthetic results repo was run. ## Design Review No frontend files changed, so design review was skipped. ## Eval Results No eval ran. The selector picked 116 behavioral probes only through derived references (lib/review-exclude.ts, lib/review-targeted.ts and bin/gstack-review-plan feed 252 gate cases); no prompt, template or judge text changed. They were not run under this lane's $30 tree cap. This is a validation gap the Captain can close. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments (one Trunk merge-queue notice, not a review). ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: let review exclusions handle big results PRs (GST-1967). Delivered: the value rule for kept files, excerpt files leaving the keep bound, chunked git reads, the matching docs, and a changelog wording fix. ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). ## Verification Results No plan verification items exist (bug fix, no plan file). Automatic QA is reported above. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current — the documentation already matches the change; no edits. **Scope:** base e077053c..66c98ecbe (2 commits, 10 files) plus one unstaged changelog.d wording edit; no staged or new files. title: Let a repository name its own docs-only paths in its ship policy (GST-1974)
body:
A repository can now name its own human-docs folders in its base branch's ship policy, so a pull request that only edits prose there skips the test suites the way README.md, docs/ and changelog.d/ already do. This serves gstack's goal of shipping fast without skipping the checks that matter. ## What changed Add a `docs_only` block to `.gstack/ship-policy.json` on the base branch: ```json "docs_only": { "allow": ["wiki/board/**.md"], "tests": ["tests/wiki.test.ts"] } ``` - **Base-only policy.** `lib/docs-only.ts` reads the block with git from the base tip (CI: the merge commit's first parent; pregate and ci-carry: `origin/`; land: the tip it merges onto). A pull request that edits the policy is never docs-only. - **Built-in deny always wins.** The deny list moved to `lib/ship-policy-docs-only.ts` and now also covers prompt files, hidden directories and any `evals/` or `inventory/` folder. `allow` takes only narrow Markdown globs under a literal directory. - **Directory readers.** A non-prose file that names an allowed directory (`'wiki'`, `'./wiki'`, `'../wiki'`, `root + '/wiki'`, `${root}/wiki`) keeps the class off unless one of the declared `tests` covers it. Those tests run in the docs check, and a declared test missing from the branch keeps the class off. - **Land.** `land.docs_only_skip` reads the block at the base tip and keeps every merged check when the base gained a reader of a changed doc's folder after the pin branched. - **Unknown keys** inside `docs_only` and `land` are warnings, not errors. `land.docs_only_skip` needs `min_gstack_version` at its own introducing release (`LAND_DOCS_ONLY_SKIP_KEY_VERSION`), and `gstack-ship-policy validate` says so. ```text bun test test/docs-only-policy.test.ts test/docs-only.test.ts 132 pass 0 fail ``` ## Why "gstack-evals keeps posts in wiki/board/ and every typo fix runs every suite, then /ship runs them again." A repository can now mark folders like that as human docs from its base branch, and the checks that read those folders still run. ## Blast radius The classifier is shared by CI's docs-scope gate, pregate's docs lane, ci-carry and land. gstack's own policy turns on neither `docs_only` nor `land.docs_only_skip`, and with no block every repo-only branch returns early (`directoryReaders` and `pathRefusal` read at lib/docs-only.ts). The free suite passed at this exact tree in run 42559023322. ## Approvals Plan: approved: autoplan-20261109024402 (GStack Minder ruling: inside Garry's R81 freeze exception and his "do it"). ## Summary Docs that live outside `docs/` used to run every suite on every edit. This PR lets the base branch's ship policy name those folders, keeps gstack's own deny list in charge, and fails closed on anything it cannot read. Review found four ways the first draft could skip a test that would then fail on main. Relative directory paths went unseen, a missing declared test passed silently, a rename into `docs/` dropped the folder's tests, and land ignored readers the base gained. All four are fixed here with failing-first tests. ## Test Coverage Coverage: 79% value-weighted (79% including 0 weakly covered paths), 3 gaps. 0 tests added by the audit. Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. - lib/docs-only.ts (readRepoDocs, pathRefusal, referencesTo, directoryReaders, classifyEntries, classifyDocsOnly): ★★★ test/docs-only-policy.test.ts - ship-policy docs_only validation, land.docs_only_skip compat, policyWarnings: ★★★ test/docs-only-policy.test.ts - land unknown-key warning: ★★ test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts - pregate and carry docs lane: ★★★ test/docs-only-policy.test.ts - [GAP] bin/gstack-ship-policy WARN stderr line and `--json` warnings merge - [GAP] lib/land-docs-only.ts policy read at the base tip (now partly covered by the new land test added in review) Review added 4 regression tests in test/docs-only-policy.test.ts (relative directory readers, a missing declared test, a rename into docs/ keeping the folder's tests, land keeping checks for a base-gained reader). Each failed at 96efd50 on its own assertion and passes at 2b66bbc. Tests ran: test 1649 (files, carried from CI run 42559023322) ## Pre-Landing Review Pass 1 (full panel: batched testing/security/state-machines specialist, Red Team, native adversarial, outside voice) found 10 blocking-floor findings, all one of four defects, fixed in 2b66bbc. Pass 2 on the fix range found only informational notes. Gate edits: 2 listed, 1 read, 0 findings (test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts now expects an unknown land key to be accepted, matching the documented warning rule) Outside review: completed by a Capy subagent on openai/gpt-6.1-sol (Codex CLI is not installed on this machine, so Codex coverage is unavailable). ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/docs-only-lane.ts:37` docs_only.tests always run under bun test - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-docs-only.ts:24` land never runs the change's docs tests on the merged tree - INFORMATIONAL `lib/docs-only.ts:177` extensionless substring tie matches unrelated words - INFORMATIONAL `lib/docs-only.ts:115` classifier honours a base docs_only block that validatePolicy refuses for min_gstack_version - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-checks.ts:51` unknown land keys are warnings here but errors on older gstack - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-policy-docs-only.ts:71` tests entries with spaces split in CI; --json warnings only on validate - INFORMATIONAL `lib/docs-only.ts:225` missing-test refusal on a stale branch names the wrong fix (fails safe) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-docs-only.ts:25` land compares base and pin readers by path only; a base edit to an existing reader or declared test still skips - INFORMATIONAL `docs/pregate.md:1491` docs do not describe base-gained readers or the missing-test refusal (addressed by the documentation audit in d57f493) ## Exploratory QA Smoke: the focused suites above (132 pass) plus the adjacent consumers test/docs-only-carry.test.ts, test/docs-only-workflow.test.ts, test/pregate-always-run.test.ts and test/pregate-guards.test.ts (32 pass). The QA method sections were not loaded in this unattended run, so no separate exploratory charter ran. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan file is bound to this branch). The approved plan is autoplan-20261109024402. ## Verification Results No plan verification items were bound to this run. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** updated. Four factual corrections bring the docs in line with the docs-only classifier and land changes. **Scope:** this branch against base e077053c (14 files, 3 commits): lib/docs-only.ts and lib/land-docs-only.ts diffs, changelog.d/repo-docs-only-paths-gst-1974.md, and the changed regions of docs/pregate.md and docs/ship-policy.md. Not checked against the docs: lib/ship-policy-docs-only.ts, lib/ship-policy.ts, lib/ship-policy-keys.ts, lib/land-merged-checks.ts, lib/pregate/run-check.ts, bin/gstack-ship-policy and the tests. No staged or unstaged changes. Banned terms: none. **Documentation health** - docs/pregate.md: Updated. The Land paragraph now says land keeps its checks when the base tip gained a directory reader of a repo-admitted changed doc. "Readers by directory" now lists `./dir`, `../dir`, `root + '/dir'` and template-literal paths, and says a `docs_only.tests` file missing from the classified tree refuses the change. - docs/ship-policy.md: Updated. The `docs_only` row now says a listed test missing from the branch refuses the class. - changelog.d/repo-docs-only-paths-gst-1974.md: Current. It already covers the missing test and the new base reader; not edited. **Coverage debt:** the `docs_only` reference (ship-policy.md) and how-to and explanation (pregate.md) are covered, with no tutorial; that is acceptable for a policy key. No diagram drift: the edited sections have no diagrams. ## Test plan - [x] bun run test (carried from CI run 42559023322 at tree 823df853e5e1): 1649 test files passed - [x] bun test test/docs-only-policy.test.ts test/docs-only.test.ts: 132 pass, 0 fail 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Make the autoplan docs say what lean and full runs actually load (GST-1985)
body:
The /autoplan docs now say what each kind of run actually gives its reviewers. No runner behavior, prompt, mode or default changed. ## What changed The /autoplan docs now say what each kind of run actually gives its reviewers. Before, README.md, docs/skills.md, docs/unattended.md, autoplan/DRIVER.md, crew/docs/captain.md, the skill description and `gstack-autoplan --help` described a full-depth, two-voice review for every run. That is true only in an interactive session. What main (e077053) actually assembles: - **Interactive session:** the session model reads each phase's review skill (SKILL.md plus review sections) and works through it. The native reviewer subagent gets a five-question brief and the plan. The outside voice is Codex, when it's available. - **Lean run** (`--kind feature`, the Capy default): one eng reviewer. Its prompt holds the eng brief and the 36-line eng checklist, a one-paragraph CEO role and the 37-line CEO checklist, and the 28-line design and 34-line DX checklists when scope detects them, plus the draft diff. It gets no skill methods, no outside voice and one round (`lib/autoplan-lean.ts` `leanPrompt`, `lib/autoplan-prompts.ts` `writePrompts`). - **Full run** (`--full`): one phase per area with two voices. The native reviewer gets the brief, the plan and that phase's checklist. The outside reviewer gets a one-paragraph role and the plan. Edits: - docs/skills.md gets a new "What each run loads" section. The table row (repeated in README.md) and the `/plan-eng-review` cut note now say that the methods load only in an interactive session. - README.md says the eng test-plan handoff to /qa comes from an interactive run. - docs/unattended.md, DRIVER.md(.tmpl) and crew/docs/captain.md describe the lean lenses and the `--full` prompts as they are. - `gstack-autoplan --help`: `--light` used to say it "loads ... the sections its scope needs" and that interactive kinds "load everything". In fact only the checklist is sent, and interactive kinds send none. - Skill description: "(lean: one reviewer)". unattended.md: "the outside voice (none when lean)". ## Why GEVA-412 (gstack-evals#277) found that the claims didn't match the prompts. Under R80 the claims must match. Whether the default should change waits on GEVA wave 1 (R56), so no behavior changed. ## Blast radius Text only. Prompt assembly, modes, defaults and tests are unchanged. The only runtime text that changed is one `--help` line. The SKILL.md edits add 41 bytes to the autoplan union. Parity passes under the existing 1.1723 cap, which is unchanged. ## Approvals Captain brief GST-1985 (claims only, no behavior change). No owner-gated change. ## Pre-Landing Review No blocking findings. The batched specialist (testing, security, state machines, red team) and the outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) found nothing, and the coverage audit found no code paths to cover. The native adversarial reviewer raised four Low notes, none of which blocks. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor and not fixed in this PR: - `bin/gstack-autoplan:80`: the new `--light` help line says that without it "an interactive kind sends no checklist". That holds for an interactive full run, but a lean run's CEO, design and DX lenses always carry their checklists (`lib/autoplan-lean.ts:123`); only the eng checklist depends on `--light` (`lib/autoplan-run.ts:179`). - README.md, the docs/skills.md table row and the changelog fragment say a `gstack-autoplan` run "gives its reviewers short checklists". Outside reviewers never get one, and a native reviewer driven interactively without `--light` gets none. The "What each run loads" section states this correctly. - docs/skills.md and docs/unattended.md hard-code the checklist line counts (CEO 37, design 28, DX 34, eng 36). They are correct today, but no test ties them to the checklist files. - docs/unattended.md still says the lean draft base defaults to `origin/HEAD`, while DRIVER.md and `captureDraft` use `gstack-diff-scope`'s base. This predates the PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The docs match what ships, so this audit made no edits. **Scope:** the ship candidate from e077053c to 573f6041 (13 committed files; nothing staged, unstaged or untracked): README.md, docs/skills.md, docs/unattended.md, crew/docs/captain.md, gstack/llms.txt, the autoplan SKILL/DRIVER/unattended templates and their generated outputs, the `gstack-autoplan --help` text and the changelog.d fragment. I checked the claims against lib/autoplan-lean.ts, lib/autoplan-run.ts and the four plan-*-review checklists. **Documentation health:** - README.md: Current. The /autoplan row and the pipeline sentence match the runner. - docs/skills.md: Current. The new "What each run loads" section and its checklist line counts (CEO 37, design 28, DX 34, eng 36) check out. - docs/unattended.md: Current. The lean and full lens descriptions match `leanPrompt` and `sectionLoadFor`. - autoplan/DRIVER.md, autoplan/SKILL.md, autoplan/sections/unattended.md and their templates: Current. - crew/docs/captain.md: Current. - gstack/llms.txt: Current. - CHANGELOG.md: covered by the changelog.d fragment, which I reviewed and didn't edit. - TODOS.md: not touched. **Coverage debt:** none. This PR changes no public surface. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Test plan - [x] CI carry at tree 6225a31 (run 42556832387/1, ci-reuse/free-tests): green, 36641 tests. - [x] All 37 pull_request checks at 573f604 passed, 0 failed, 0 pending (macos-named-regressions and windows-smoke cleared from their runs). - [x] Pre-push guards at 573f604: skill-size, parity-suite, context-budget, module-size, goldens and conflict markers passed; generated files fresh; sealed check clear.
Agent notes - Checks run locally at 573f604's tree: 16 focused files, 1059 pass and 0 fail (skill-md-size-guard, parity-suite, catalog and context budgets, autoplan-driver, autoplan-lean, skill-validation, gen-skill-docs, inventory, module-size-ratchet and others). Also typecheck, `skill:check`, `gstack-inventory --check` and `gstack-pregate sealed` all passed. - 573f604 keeps the autoplan description at its exact size pin (net 0 chars on every host), which fixes the skill-md-size-guard failure CI found at 12f5fc7. It also says the eng checklist is sent only in unattended or `--light` runs, and rewords the `--light` help line. - The autoplan/SKILL.md body line "at full interactive depth" was left as is. title: Report free-suite results to Trunk Flaky Tests for detection only (GST-1859)
body:
Free Tests now sends every free-suite shard's test results to Trunk Flaky Tests, so Trunk can flag tests that fail and then pass on the same code. It is detection only: nothing is quarantined or skipped, and no check depends on it. ## What changed - `scripts/test-free-shards.ts` takes `--junit-dir ` (only with `--ci-run`). The runner already asked bun for a JUnit report in each child's sandbox to count tests; with the flag it also keeps a copy of each child's report, the flaky retry included, one uniquely named file per child. A failed copy is logged and changes no verdict. Shard selection, tiers, retries, timeouts and counts are unchanged. - `free-suite` passes the flag and uploads the XML as `free-junit-` (`if: always()`, 7-day retention). It still sees no secrets. - A new `trunk-flaky-tests` job downloads those artifacts and runs `trunk-io/analytics-uploader` pinned to `a86313c7029d22e6ea2d5c346060a224d90053dc` (tag v2.1.6), CLI pinned to 0.16.2, into Trunk collection `7yDVXXE3` for org `garry-tan`. - Contract tests pin the new job's shape and the secret list; docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md gets a short section. ## Why Garry chose B1 on GST-1859: try Trunk Flaky Tests (free up to 5 committers) instead of building our own flaky-test tool (GST-82). Trunk Dynamic CI stays in learning mode, unchanged. ## Blast radius - **Secrets and workflows.** The uploader job is the only job that sees the new `TRUNK_ORG_API_TOKEN` secret (Trunk's v1 organization token; the existing `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` is a v2 API key, which the uploader can't use). It checks out nothing and runs no pull-request code, has `permissions: {}`, and runs only on same-repository pull requests and main pushes. `use-cache` is off, so the CLI always comes from Trunk's checksummed release, never from an Actions cache a pull-request job could write. No `pull_request_target`. - **Gating.** No job needs `trunk-flaky-tests`, the step and the job continue on error, and a missing token skips both steps. The required `free-tests` aggregate is unchanged. Quarantine is off in the uploader and in the collection. - **Third-party action.** It receives the token, the XML paths and repo metadata (URL, head sha, branch). It sends telemetry to Trunk with the token. ## Approvals Garry, 2026-11-09: "do it" to FOUN-32's status, taking B1 on GST-1859 (detection only). title: Let a clean follow-up review count after an earlier one found a blocker (GST-1973)
body:
When a granted follow-up review on a /ship pull request found a blocker, the release check refused every later follow-up review too, so a clean review of the fix never counted and the only way out was a whole new /ship review. Now a clean follow-up review that read the fix counts, which keeps the two-round review cap honest and lets a fixed pull request finish /ship without another full review. A finding is closed only by a later clean review whose range touched that finding's file.

## What changed

Before: a follow-up chain where the first follow-up review found a blocker and the second read the fix cleanly printed `FIX_CHECK: not counted (missing start capture or incomplete/nonconverged pass; fix-check at <A>, link 1 of 2)`, and finish routed the fixed files as unreviewed behavior.

After: the same chain prints `FIX_CHECK: reviewed src/x.ts,test/x.test.ts (fix-check chain of 2 from <T>: at <A> grant <g1> (found issues); at <C> grant <g2>)` and finish routes those files as reviewed.

Also fixed (5d126e0): a blocking finding an earlier link logged on a file no later clean link's range touched (a file the branch never changed, a doubled `./` spelling, or a directory) used to drop out of routing, and the chain still counted. Now finish refuses that chain with `FIX_CHECK: not counted (a finding on <path> that no later clean fix-check's range touched; fix-check at <A>, link 1 of 2)`.

## Why

GBRA-386 hit this on gbrain #8881: a granted follow-up review found a blocker, the fix was read cleanly by the next one, and finish still refused, so the pull request needed a third full review past the two-round cap. A link that found issues is logged `converged:false` by design, and finish treated that as a broken chain. After the first /ship here, a cross-family read of the decision trail found that the new counting could close a blocker no later review had read, so this head adds that refusal.

## Summary

A follow-up review that finds issues still has to be logged as not converged, and finish used to refuse any chain holding one. Now an earlier link that found issues joins the chain when it finished its read on its own commit, its findings account for its counts, and every open or blocking finding names a file at that commit. That link counts no file itself, a file its findings name counts only through a clean link after it, and every such file must sit in some later clean link's range or the chain is refused, so a blocker is closed only by a review that read the fix. Contiguity, one grant per link and a clean newest link are unchanged. Review fixes during /ship made finding paths written with a leading `./` match git's paths and added refusal tests for an over-claimed critical count and a finding on a missing file.

## Blast radius

The change is inside `fixChecked()` in lib/ship-release.ts, which only finish calls, plus two helpers now exported from lib/review-scope.ts with no behavior change. Every new acceptance path is fenced by the existing contiguity, grant and newest-clean-link checks, and the new coverage refusal only removes acceptances. The 11 tests in test/ship-finish-fixed-links.test.ts drive the real release script through those refusals (script ran); the new one fails at 6c5a763 and passes at 5d126e0.

## Test Coverage

Step 7 coverage audit from the first /ship (audit only, at 395108e): 9 of 13 changed paths covered (69%). Pass 1's fix closed three of the four gaps it named; the ruled-note positive case stays a gap. The 5d126e0 fix carries its own failing-first test (three inputs: a file the branch never changed, `././src/x.ts`, and a directory). The Step 7 reader was not rerun at this head.
