title: Use p1 instead of plan for the final approval gate item in /autoplan
body:
Phase 4 of `/autoplan` instructed the agent to write the final approval gate item with id `plan` and reply tokens `plana`, `planc`, `pland`, and `plane`, which `gstack-gate` rejects because gate item ids require a trailing number. Updating the template and generated skill doc to use `p1` and `p1a`/`p1c`/`p1d`/`p1e` matches `lib/autoplan-gate.ts` and passes `gstack-gate` validation.

## Summary

- Replace `and \`plan\` (approval: ...)` with `and \`p1\` (approval: ...)` and replace `plana` / `planc`/`pland`/`plane` with `p1a` / `p1c`/`p1d`/`p1e` in `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `autoplan/SKILL.md`.
- Add a regression test in `test/gate-list.test.ts` verifying that `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `autoplan/SKILL.md` specify `p1` and `p1a`/`p1c`/`p1d`/`p1e` and that `validateGateList` and `parseReply` accept them.

Fixes #4181

title: Resolve prefixed sibling section links in setup --status
body:
Running `./setup --status` on a `--prefix` install reported 1 of 114 section links broken and exited 1 because `gstack-review/SKILL.md` documents both `../qa/sections/exploratory.md` and `../gstack-qa/sections/exploratory.md` while `_status_install_checks` resolved `../` pointers literally without checking the `gstack-*` prefixed sibling directory. Falling back to `../gstack-<rest>` when an installed skill directory is prefixed lets `./setup --status` resolve the documented prefixed sibling and exit 0.

## Summary

- In `_status_install_checks()` (`setup`), when `${dir##*/}` is prefixed (`gstack-*`) and `$dir/$tok` is not readable for a `../*` pointer, check `$dir/../gstack-${tok#../}` before counting the pointer as broken.
- Mirror the prefixed sibling fallback in `brokenSectionPointers` and add a conformance test in `test/host-conformance.test.ts` covering `./setup --host claude --prefix` followed by `./setup --status`.

Fixes #4164

title: Make the /autoplan approval gate render and accept plan replies (#4181)
body: /autoplan's final approval gate now renders, and its plan-approval replies parse. The skill told the agent to name that item `plan` and to read replies like `plana`, which `gstack-gate` refuses. ## Why (in your own words) `/autoplan` Phase 4 tells the agent to write `$_AP/gate.json` with one item per user challenge (`uc`), one per taste decision (`d`), and a plan-approval item named `plan`. It then says `plana` approves and `planc`/`pland`/`plane` interrogate, revise or reject. `gstack-gate` accepts only a lowercase label followed by a number (`ID_RE` in `lib/gate-list.ts:75`), so a gate written as the skill says fails to render, and none of the `plan` replies can ever match an item. The owner's approval step breaks on the text the skill itself supplies. This addresses #4181, reported with the exact lines by @exGeni. **Validation status:** [Full free CI passed](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42571358998) on head `34a0b6904` (32 checks passed, 20 skipped, none failed), including all eleven free-suite shards, typecheck, macOS named regressions and Windows smoke. Locally, the full free suite ran once and every failing file was rerun on unchanged main (below): the only failure this change caused was a size pin, fixed in this commit. Required selected paid coverage and remaining shipping reviews are still pending; skipped fork jobs are not passes. ### Why this shape `p1` is already the id everywhere except the skill text. The helper-built gate writes `{ id: 'p1', title: 'Plan approval' }` (`lib/autoplan-gate.ts:269`), and `docs/unattended.md:513` calls the item `p1` plan approval. The skill prose is the stale side, so the change renames three tokens on three template lines and leaves the grammar, which is a parsed contract, alone. Three lines in one template, its regenerated `SKILL.md`, twelve exact size pins the rename moved, one test case in the existing gate-grammar owner file, and one changelog fragment. Fine to absorb into a wave. ### What it does - Names the plan-approval item `p1` in the Phase 4 gate.json instructions. - Teaches `p1a` (approve) and `p1c`/`p1d`/`p1e` (interrogate, revise, reject) as the reply tokens. - Regenerates `autoplan/SKILL.md`; `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all` changes no other file. - Lowers the twelve `*/gstack-autoplan` pins in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` by 10 characters each. Those renders are over the 100,000-character limit and pinned at their exact size, and the rename shortens each by 10, which `test/skill-md-size-guard.test.ts` reports with the exact values to set. - Adds one case to `test/gate-list.test.ts` that reads the template's plan-approval id and its reply tokens, then checks them with the real `validateGateList` and `parseReply`. It reads the tokens from the template rather than pinning a sentence, so a later rewording that keeps a valid id still passes. ### What it deliberately does not do - No change to `lib/gate-list.ts`, `lib/autoplan-gate.ts` or `bin/gstack-gate`; the grammar stays as it is. - No change to the `uc` / `d` wording, `all`, or any other part of Phase 4. - Nothing for #3322 (the publication guard on Windows VS Code), which is a separate autoplan issue. - No `VERSION`, package-version, released `CHANGELOG.md`, README or ETHOS edits. Release notes are one entry-text-only `changelog.d/` fragment. ## Live evidence Bun 1.4.4 and Node 22.23.4 on Linux, `LC_ALL=C`, private `HOME` and `GSTACK_HOME`. No browser or live model was used. The gate file holds one auto item (`d1`) and the plan-approval item with options a to e, written exactly as each version of the skill describes. ### Actual CLI before and after **Before: the item named `plan`, as the skill says on main at `a229e2580`:** ```text $ gstack-gate render gate.json gstack-gate: gate.json is not a gate list: items[1].id must match [a-z]*[0-9]+ (lowercase label plus a number, e.g. d3, uc1, 12) exit=1 $ gstack-gate parse gate.json --reply "plana" --gate-rev 1 --json gstack-gate: gate.json is not a gate list: items[1].id must match [a-z]*[0-9]+ (lowercase label plus a number, e.g. d3, uc1, 12) exit=1 ``` **After: the item named `p1`, as the skill says on this branch:** ```text $ gstack-gate render gate.json GATE: run=r gate_rev=1 items=2 page=1/1 1. [d1] Taste decision (auto; recommended: a) d1a) keep (recommended) d1b) change 2. [p1] Plan approval (approval; recommended: a) p1a) approve as-is (recommended) p1b) with overrides p1c) interrogate p1d) revise p1e) reject ... exit=0 $ gstack-gate parse gate.json --reply "p1a" --gate-rev 1 --json {"valid":true,"gate_rev":1,"reply":"p1a","choices":[{"id":"d1","chosen":"a","kind":"auto","how":"auto_default"},{"id":"p1","chosen":"a","kind":"approval","how":"recommended"}],"pending":[],"unparsed":[],"mode":"tokens"} exit=0 $ gstack-gate parse gate.json --reply "p1c" --gate-rev 1 --json {"valid":true,"gate_rev":1,"reply":"p1c","choices":[{"id":"d1","chosen":"a","kind":"auto","how":"auto_default"},{"id":"p1","chosen":"c","kind":"approval","how":"override"}],"pending":[],"unparsed":[],"mode":"tokens"} exit=0 ``` Control: the old token against the same valid gate is still refused, so the reply half of the bug is real on its own, not only a side effect of the render failure. ```text $ gstack-gate parse gate.json --reply "plana" --gate-rev 1 --json {"valid":false,"gate_rev":1,"reply":"plana","choices":[],"pending":[],"unparsed":["plana"],"error":"GATE_REPLY_UNPARSED"} exit=1 ``` ### Failing-first regression The new case was written before the template edit and run against the unchanged template: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/gate-list.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'autoplan gate text' error: expect(received).toEqual(expected) - title: Fix five small browse and question-hook bugs
body:
This fixes five small bugs in gstack's browser commands and its question hooks, so `browse scroll`, the PDF and diagram renderer, per-project domain skills and never-ask preferences behave the way the docs say. It serves the README's goal of skills a person can rely on without babysitting.

## What changed

![A question marker with a malformed signal hint used to lose its id (left, main); it now keeps the lowercased id and drops only the bad hint (right)](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/kmd8sJcfwNBA3QBiUWC82A2SMPugcaC346oPd_sTnjM.png)

A question marker with a malformed signal hint used to lose its id (left, main); it now keeps the lowercased id and drops only the bad hint (right).

<details><summary>Before/after as text: A question marker with a malformed signal hint used to lose its id (left, main); it now keeps the lowercased id and drops only the bad hint (right)</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 $ parseQidMarker("<gstack-qid:Ship-X;signal=scope_appetite> Ship now?")
+{"id":"ship-x","stripped":"Ship now?"}
-null
 
~~~

</details>

1. `browse scroll <selector>` keeps its selector when `--wait` is absent. The old parser read the first argument as the `--wait` value, so `scroll footer` scrolled to the page bottom (browse/src/write-commands.ts).
2. The renderer skips a `browse` on PATH whose real file has another name, such as Debian and Ubuntu's `/usr/bin/browse` link to xdg-open, instead of launching a desktop opener (lib/aside-render.ts).
3. On installs without `~/.claude`, the browse daemon gives each project its own domain-skill file. It tries the checkout's own `gstack-slug`, then the Claude install's, then the git remote rule, instead of one shared "unknown" bucket (browse/src/project-slug.ts).
4. A question marker with a malformed `;signal=` hint keeps its id and drops only the hint (scripts/qid-marker.ts).
5. The never-ask hook reads the lowercased marker id, as the log hook and stored preferences already do (hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts).

## Why

Each fix comes from a bug the crew hit: "scroll footer" replied "Scrolled to bottom", a Debian machine opened a desktop app instead of rendering, a Codex install mixed every repository's domain skills, and a silenced question was asked again because its marker had capitals or a bad hint. After this, those commands and preferences do what they say. Review found that widening the marker pattern let text inside a marker skip the one-way door check, so two follow-up commits keep that text in the check, spaced apart from the next word.

## Blast radius

The scroll parser, the PATH lookup and the slug lookup are each one function with their own tests. The marker change reaches both Claude hooks through `parseQidMarker`, and the never-ask gate and the spawned deny path now classify the marker's tail text too, so any change there only makes the hook ask more often; the red/green tests in test/question-preference-hook.test.ts and a probe of `classifyQuestion` showed that (script ran). Security read: the slug fix runs a local `gstack-slug` script (the checkout's own `bin/gstack-slug`, then `~/.claude`'s) through `execFileSync` with no shell and a 2 s timeout; there is no network use, no credentials, and no install, upgrade or workflow change. One small risk in fix 2: a PATH wrapper whose real file has another name is now skipped, and the renderer reports that no browser was found.

## Summary

Five one-commit bug fixes, each with a test that fails on main, plus two review fixes to the one-way door check and a docs note on where domain skills live. This is crew work.

## Test Coverage

Coverage: deterministic (each of 5 changed runtime files has a changed test naming it; no audit reader).
Regression proof: each fix's test fails on main 10fc9b1 and passes on this branch. The two review-fix tests failed on the hook before each fix and pass after it.
Tests ran: free (carried from CI; see Test plan)

## Pre-Landing Review

Pass 1 (full panel, gate class): 3 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 2 asked (0 fixed, 2 skipped), 0 deferred, 1 noted. The Step 11 targeted reader found one blocker, fixed in "Keep a marker's tail in the one-way door check". Pass 2 (full panel on the range): clean, 3 notes. Its Step 11 voices found one blocker in that fix (the tail joined the next word), fixed in "Keep a marker's tail apart from the next word in the one-way door check" and checked by one granted fix-check reader plus the targeted reader: no findings.

Gate edits: none detected (7 listed, 2 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol as a host subagent. Pass 1: VERDICT: CLEAN. Pass 2: one finding, fixed.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. Follow-ups:

- Option labels and the marker id never reach the never-ask gate's keyword check. `<gstack-qid:adhoc-x> Proceed?` with `A) Force-push to main (recommended)`, or an unregistered id like `force-push-main`, can still auto-decide under a never-ask preference. This already happens on main; it is the same class as the fixed tail bug.
- The Codex session importer (bin/gstack-codex-session-import:141) keeps its own copy of the old strict marker regex and does not lowercase the id, so a malformed hint still loses its id on that path.
- No test covers a destructive marker tail on the spawned-session deny path (hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook.ts:518); its code matches the tested never-ask gate.
- The auto-decided question log still drops the marker tail text (the `qText` at :475 and :517).
- When no `gstack-slug` runs (native Windows, or a 2 s timeout), the slug fallback uses `getRemoteSlug()` rather than `slugFromEnvironment()` from lib/bin-context.ts, so it ignores `.gstack-project` markers and the outer-root walk; no test reaches that branch.
- Domain skills saved before this change stay in `~/.gstack/projects/unknown/learnings.jsonl`; the changelog and docs/domain-skills.md say so, and nothing moves them.
- The PATH check looks only at the first `browse` on PATH and checks only its file name.
- The first slug lookup can block the daemon for up to about 6 s (two 2 s script calls plus git), once per daemon.

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke (report-only, 3 of 12 probes, 300 s budget): all pass on current inputs. The qid marker keeps the lowercased id with a malformed hint and keeps a valid hint; a PATH `browse` linked to xdg-open resolves to nothing while a real `browse` still resolves; with no `~/.claude`, a repository with origin acme/widgets gets the slug `acme-widgets`. Not run live: `browse scroll` (needs a browser; covered by browse/test/commands.test.ts) and the never-ask hook end to end (covered by its tests).

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. eval:select's dependents profile lists probes through scripts/qid-marker.ts references; none were run.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: CLEAN

## Plan Completion

Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). Bug fixes skip plan review; each carries a failing-first test.

## Verification Results

No plan verification items. Exploratory smoke: 3 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED.

## TODOS

Completed: the plan-tune qid marker follow-ups item (#3442 review notes) is removed from TODOS.md, since fixes 4 and 5 ship it.

## Documentation
**Status:** updated. One factual edit, no blockers.

**Scope:** base 10fc9b1e to head 67df8225 on `five-small-browse-and-question-hook-fixes` (8 commits, 12 files: browse scroll parsing, the PATH browse check in the renderer, per-project browse slug, qid-marker hint parsing, and never-ask hook id lowercasing). There were no staged, unstaged or untracked changes.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/domain-skills.md`: Updated. Storage now says how the project slug is resolved and where rows saved by older builds sit (`projects/unknown`).
- `BROWSER.md`: Current. The scroll command row matches the fixed behavior.
- `browse/sections/command-list.md`: Current.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: Current. It does not describe the PATH browse lookup.
- `changelog.d/five-small-browse-and-question-hook-fixes.md`: Reviewed and consistent with the code; not edited.
- `TODOS.md`: Reviewed. The removed qid-marker item matches the fix; not edited.

**Coverage debt:** no critical gaps. One common gap: the renderer rule that skips a PATH `browse` whose real file has another name (for example Debian and Ubuntu's xdg-open link) is documented only in source comments and the changelog. The qid-marker and hook changes are internal. There is no architecture diagram drift.
## Test plan
- [x] `bun run test` (free suite): carried from Free Tests run 42570140462 at this tree (tree bfc52c392e04, head 79b69fe), 1651 files, exit 0 (EVIDENCE: FRESH).
- [x] Focused at c73852a: `bun --no-env-file test test/question-preference-hook.test.ts test/qid-marker.test.ts test/hook-log.test.ts`: 55 pass, 0 fail. `bun run typecheck`: exit 0.
- [x] Focused at 095e1fd (parent): aside-render, project-slug, qid-marker, question-preference-hook and neighbors 147 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail; browse/test/commands.test.ts under xvfb 256 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] windows-smoke run 42570921595 at 79b69fe: success. macOS jobs in run 42570140462: success.

title: Stop SSE streams leaking on cancel, keep network capture to its own session, and read code fences like GitHub in the docs link checker
body:
Live activity and inspector streams now release their subscriptions as soon as a client goes away, network capture keeps each session's responses to itself, and the docs link checker reads code fences the way GitHub renders them. That keeps the browser sidebar from leaking connections and keeps the docs link gate from reporting false broken links.

## Why (in your own words)

Three places in gstack keep running after the thing they belong to has ended.

- **Live activity and inspector streams leak.** If the sidebar closes or the client cancels a stream, `createSseEndpoint` only cleaned up on the request's abort signal. A cancelled stream kept its subscription and heartbeat. A request that was already aborted still subscribed. A subscriber whose `unsubscribe` threw stopped the stream from closing.
- **Network capture mixes sessions.** A response whose body was still loading when you ran `network --capture stop`, or started a new capture, was pushed into the buffer afterwards.
- **The docs link checker misreads fences.** It closed a code block on a shorter fence or on a fence followed by text, and opened one on a line of inline code that starts with backticks. It also gave repeated headings anchors that can collide (`# A`, `# A`, `# A-1`), and reported a file named like `..notes.md` as outside the repository.

The fix ties each listener and subscription to its own session and cleans up on every way a stream can end. The link checker now follows CommonMark and github-slugger.

## Live evidence

The new regression tests against `origin/main`'s source for `lib/doc-links.ts`, `browse/src/sse-helpers.ts` and `browse/src/network-capture.ts`, and then on this branch:

```
$ bun test test/doc-links-regressions.test.ts browse/test/state-machine-regressions.test.ts   # main's source
(fail) heading IDs remain unique when a natural suffix collides with a duplicate
(fail) shorter fences and backticks followed by text do not close a code block
(fail) a backtick line with backticks after the marker is inline code, not a fence
(fail) a repository filename beginning with two dots is not an escape
(fail) pending response cannot cross stop
(fail) pending response cannot cross restart
(fail) pending response cannot cross clear
(fail) stale listener cannot start work after stop; invalid filter preserves active session
(fail) SSE cancellation releases subscription immediately and once
(fail) already aborted SSE request never subscribes or replays
(fail) abort during subscribe releases returned disposer exactly once
 0 pass
 11 fail

$ bun test test/doc-links-regressions.test.ts browse/test/state-machine-regressions.test.ts   # this branch
 11 pass
```

title: Stop the focused-test tag from keeping run data in review (GST-2006)
body:
The gate scan's focused-or-skipped-test check (RH-1) now skips data and log files, so a model reply that says "don't fit (the gap never drops below one space)" in a committed results `.jsonl` no longer keeps that whole file in the reviewers' diff under `review_exclude_paths`. On harness-evals#333 at a229e258 the gate scan tagged `docs/benchmarks/2026-11-06-qm-s1-edition/main/turns.jsonl` as RH-1, review-exclude re-kept it as `gate-tagged`, and the reader's diff went back to 5,120,181 bytes against the 2 MB ceiling (`REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`). ## What changed Before: RH-1 matched skip and focus idioms in every file that was not prose or generated, so English "fit (" in run data tagged the file and kept it in review. After: RH-1 skips `.json`, `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.log` and `.out` files unless they were renamed from another kind of file. Every other file, in a test folder or not, keeps RH-1, and every other gate tag still reads data files. No image: this is a gate-scan rule with no visible surface. The two smoke probes under Exploratory QA show the before/after behavior as command output. ## Why "`/ship` stopped with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`" on a results PR whose run data was already excluded from review, because a model reply in that data said "fit (". Results PRs now keep their run data out of the reviewers' diff, while a skipped or focused test in code under the same excluded path is still tagged and kept. ## Blast radius The change touches only RH-1 inside `tagHunk` (`lib/gate-diff/tags.ts`) and passes the old path of a rename from `lib/gate-diff/index.ts`; review-exclude and the other tags are unchanged. It is safe because the rule now fails toward tagging. Only the seven data and log extensions lose RH-1, which the new tests and two smoke runs of `gstack-gate-diff` on throwaway repositories confirm (script ran). ## Summary A results PR with a 5 MB transcript hit the reviewers' 2 MB ceiling even though the transcript sat under `review_exclude_paths`, because RH-1 read English "fit (" as a focused test. RH-1 now skips data and logs. Review then found that the first version, an allowlist of code extensions, also dropped RH-1 from an HTML browser suite, unlisted languages such as Crystal, and a test-folder file renamed to data, so the rule became a short denylist of data and log formats with a bypass test written first. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage: `test/gate-diff.test.ts` "RH-1 reads only files a test runner can execute (GST-2006)" (6 tests, including the review bypass case, red at 7dda9ea and green at 76c3f84) and `test/review-exclude.test.ts` "the gate scan keeps code but not run data under a pattern (GST-2006)". Tests ran: free 1650 (files, carried from CI run 42579796201/1 at tree 3165c7df1daf) ## Pre-Landing Review Pass 1 (full panel: batched testing/security/state-machines specialist, Red Team, native adversarial, outside voice openai/gpt-6.1-sol, targeted gate reader) found five blocking reports of two bypasses, all fixed in 76c3f84: an HTML browser suite with `describe.skip` outside a test path lost RH-1, and a test-floor file with an unlisted extension renamed to data with its declarations removed lost RH-1. Pass 2 on the fix range found only notes. One informational finding was skipped by design: extensionless run output and test-folder report formats (xml, yaml, html) still carry RH-1; exempting them would reopen the HTML bypass. Gate edits: 3 listed, 3 read, 0 findings — 0 kept, 0 restored, 0 open Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol, completed (2 findings, both fixed). ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/gate-diff/tags.ts:262` RH-12/13/14/16 still match quoted shell/lint text inside run data, so a big transcript can still be gate-tagged and kept - INFORMATIONAL `lib/gate-diff/tags.ts:37` a results file renamed from .md or .txt to .jsonl regains RH-1 through the rename clause - INFORMATIONAL `lib/gate-diff/tags.ts:35` Postman/Newman collection .json files run embedded JS tests; a pm.test.skip added there no longer carries RH-1 ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `gstack-gate-diff` in two owned throwaway repositories: a test file and an extensionless script with focus markers tag RH-1 while `results/turns.jsonl` with #333's replies tags nothing; a test renamed to `.jsonl` that drops its declaration still tags RH-1. Both passed at 7dda9ea and again at 76c3f84 after the review fix. Verdict: pass, 2 of 12 smoke probes used. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). title: Stop /ship picking a version another git worktree already holds
body: When /ship picks a version, it now notices every parallel git worktree of the repo, so two branches in progress stop taking the same number. ## Why (in your own words) Today `gstack-next-version` only looks in `///`, the layout Conductor creates. I work in worktrees that Claude Code puts under `.claude/worktrees`, and pointing `workspace_root` there does nothing, because the scan then looks for `.claude/worktrees//`. The config comment says any directory holding parallel worktrees will do, but it silently finds none. This change asks `git worktree list`, which knows every linked worktree wherever it lives, and still reads the workspace root because that is how separate clones are found. ## Live evidence A temp repo with `main` at 0.1.66.0 and one worktree outside the Conductor layout holding 0.1.67.0, run from the main checkout with `--base main --bump micro --current-version 0.1.66.0`: ``` installed 1.98.0.0: {"version": "0.1.66.1", "reason": "no collision; clean bump from base"} siblings: 0 active: 0 this branch: {"version": "0.1.67.1", "reason": "bumped past active sibling 0.1.67.0"} siblings: 1 active: 1 this branch, --workspace-root null: {"version": "0.1.66.1", "reason": "no collision; clean bump from base"} siblings: 0 active: 0 ``` The same comparison on my real project, which has 17 worktrees (the main checkout plus 16 linked ones), run from the main checkout: ``` installed 1.98.0.0: siblings 0 active 0 this branch: siblings 14 active 2, and the pick moved past the highest active sibling ``` The two tests for the new behaviour were red before the fix: ``` (fail) sibling scan finds git worktrees wherever they live > a worktree outside any workspace root still holds its version (fail) sibling scan finds git worktrees wherever they live > run from a linked worktree, it lists the others and never itself 3 pass 2 fail ``` The other three tests guard behaviour that must not change, so they pass before the fix too. I broke the code on purpose in four ways to confirm the tests can fail: | Sabotage | Test that went red | |---|---| | `null` no longer disables the scan | workspace root null still turns the whole scan off | | current worktree not excluded | run from a linked worktree, it lists the others and never itself | | no de-duplication | a worktree inside the Conductor layout is counted once | | workspace root scan removed | a separate clone in the Conductor layout is still found | After the fix: ``` bun test 222 pass 0 fail Ran 222 tests across 10 files. gstack-checks run CHECK typecheck PASS CHECK build PASS CHECK tests TOO_BROAD (1720 test files selected, left to CI) ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** - `bin/gstack-next-version`: the sibling scan takes the union of `git worktree list` and the workspace root layout, compares real paths, and excludes the current checkout by its top level. - `bin/gstack-config`: the `workspace_root` comment now says what the setting does, and drops the claim that any directory of worktrees works. - `test/gstack-next-version.test.ts`: five tests against real temp repos and worktrees. - `changelog.d/fix-next-version-sees-git-worktrees.md`: the changelog fragment. - **Verified live by:** the runs above on macOS 26 (Apple Silicon, Bun 1.4.3). - **Did NOT test:** - Linux or Windows. - Real Conductor workspaces. The Conductor layout is covered by the tests with a directory of the same shape. - The full free suite locally (see `TOO_BROAD` above). CI runs it on this PR. - The paid evals. This change adds no prompt text. - **Behaviour change to weigh:** repos with parallel worktrees outside Conductor now get the "bumped past active sibling" path for the first time, so a version can skip a number while another worktree has a fresh unshipped bump with no open PR. That is what the check is for, and it applied only to Conductor users until now. - **Not changed:** the `/landing-report` template still labels this list "Sibling Conductor worktrees". It is cosmetic, and changing it means regenerating skill files. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction above 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Stop reading ship receipt CI run ids as phone numbers (GST-2047)
body:
## What changed `gstack-post` no longer holds a PR body because its ship receipt carries GitHub Actions run ids. Run ids in the receipt's run-id fields (`ci_carried[].run`, `flaky_exception[].runs`, `issues.flakes[].run`) pass the `pii.phone.e164` check when the block is one the receipt writer rendered: a closed `gstack-ship-receipt` fence whose JSON passes the receipt schema and is byte-identical to `renderReceiptBlock`'s output. Only those value positions are exempt. ## Why Each carried CI entry held as a phone number, so every ship tail with carried CI needed `--confirm` (seen on garrytan/gstack-evals#289). Routine confirmation trains crews to wave through holds they should read. ## Blast radius `lib/gstack-post.ts` only: the exemption filters `pii.phone.e164` findings after the scan, by line and column of the parsed receipt's run-id values. `lib/redact-patterns.ts` and every other caller of the shared phone pattern are unchanged. Still held (tested): an E.164 or bare 11-digit number in prose, a carried run id copied into prose, the same number under any other receipt key (`thread`, `attempt`, `lane`, `issues.flakes[].issue`), a number on the line before or after the block, and a number inside a schema-invalid, hand-written one-line, malformed-JSON or unclosed receipt block. Mutation checks: dropping the schema check, dropping the byte-identity check, or exempting one extra key each fails the new test.
Agent notes Failing-first: the new test failed on main 68b1d056 with four `pii.phone.e164` findings, one per carried run. Docs: one bullet added under the existing `redact-run-id-as-phone` troubleshooting anchor (anchor unchanged). Changelog fragment added.

~~~diff
-APPROVAL_RECORD_SECRET field ask: pii.phone.e164
 
~~~

</details>

- **CI run numbers in /ship's summary block.** `gstack-post` no longer reads GitHub Actions run numbers in the run fields of a `gstack-ship-receipt` block (`ci_carried[].run`, `flaky_exception[].runs`, `issues.flakes[].run`) as phone numbers. Only a block exactly as the writer renders it qualifies (closed fence, schema-valid, byte-identical to `renderReceiptBlock`), only those values, and only when the value is 11 to 20 digits with an optional `/attempt`.
- **Autoplan run ids on approval import.** `gstack-approvals import` skips `pii.phone.e164` and `pii.cc` findings that start inside a minted autoplan run id's time stamp, or the thread number right before it, at the two places import writes the id. A phone number in the rest of the name, the row's words or plan title, or the same id typed into `add`, still refuses.
- **Versions next to a VERSION file or a semver.** `pii.ip_public` skips a four-part quad a short punctuation gap (or the word `to`) away from a `VERSION` file name or path, or from a three-part version, on the same line, and a `VERSION` file holding only the quad. This is the shared scanner, so it applies to `gstack-post`, the pregate secrets check and the push hook alike.
- **LOW findings.** A home path already only notes in `gstack-post` and only warns in pregate; new tests pin that.

## Why

Garry asked to "reduce the extreme privacy holds and false positives". CI run numbers in /ship's summary block cost extra confirmation stops on every ship with carried CI, a `VERSION` write warned as a public IP, and an approval import refused an autoplan run id. Those stops now go away, and the real cases still hold.

## Blast radius

The change narrows three detectors shared by `gstack-post`, `gstack-approvals`, the pregate secrets check and the push hook. Every exemption is bound to an exact position and shape, and each still-held case has a test. Those cases are a key anywhere (refused, inside the summary block too), a phone number in prose, beside the block, under another key, in a forged or broken block, as a 10-digit or text run value, in an approval's words, title or the name half of a run id, and a public IP with no version beside it (tests ran: the four focused files, 376 pass, and CI's free suite carried at this tree).

## Summary

The privacy scan held PRs and approvals on numbers gstack itself wrote. This PR teaches the three detectors those exact shapes, at their exact positions, and nothing else. Review found and closed two holes in the first version (a phone-shaped string in a run field, and a phone number in a run id's name half), then a 10-digit run value, each now pinned by a test.

title: Keep local paths out of the approvals table and add render --redacted (GST-2048)
body:
`gstack-approvals render` no longer prints local filesystem paths in the approvals table of a PR body, and `--redacted` forces the public form on any repository.

## What changed
- The Asked, Covers and Still pending columns show each local path as `…/<file name>`, and a bare home directory as `~`. That covers absolute and home paths (`~/`, `~user/`, `$HOME/`, `/home/…`, `/Users/…`), Windows-drive, UNC and `file:` paths in any case, Drive-relative `.capy/drive/…` paths, and paths glued onto a `:` or `-` such as `ledger:/home/…`. Only a `://` scheme prefix keeps a slash path as written. Exact words stays verbatim because it is the owner's quote, and `gstack-approvals list` keeps the full record.
- `render --redacted` prints the same bytes a public repository gets. `--redacted` with `--full` is a usage error (exit 2) with nothing on stdout.
- The redacted line now ends "The full approval record stays private." so it stays true when `--redacted` is used on a private repository.

## Why
On a private repository `render` printed the full table with each row's text as recorded. On garrytan/gstack-evals#289 that put a ledger path under `/home/<user>/.capy/drive/…` into 102 spend-cap rows. gstack-post flags that as `internal.user_path`, and because a PR description keeps its edit history, the path would stay readable after the repository went public.

## Blast radius
`pathLabels` has one production caller, `renderRecord`, and the table stays display only: `lib/ship-receipt-prose.ts` finds the block by its header and footer and never parses cells, and labels never add a `|`. The ship-receipt-prose, plan-record and module-size tests pass on this head (51/0 with the spawnSync tripwire).

## Review notes
These are below the blocking floor and are recorded here, not fixed in this PR.
- Accepted: Asked and Still pending now get the same labels as Covers. Known false positive: a non-local slash path in those columns is relabelled too, for example `/api/v1/users` becomes `…/users`.
- Known false positive from the last fix: a URL whose path has a segment ending in `-` or `:`, such as GitLab's `https://gitlab.com/g/p/-/merge_requests/12`, renders as `…/12` after that segment.
- `~2/3` style approximations render as `…/3`.
- A home folder containing a space keeps the words after the space, for example `C:\Users\Garry Tan\x.md` becomes `~ Tan\x.md`.
- Mount-relative Drive paths without `.capy/drive/` (`project-user-<project>-<person>/x.md`) and paths that end at a Drive scope or `/var/home/<name>` folder keep that folder name; `~user` is ASCII only.
- Exact words is never labelled, by design.
- Codex outside review was unavailable (Codex CLI not installed on the review machine).

## Documentation
**Status:** current. No documentation changes were needed.

**Scope:** base 68b1d056..6f58ad11 (3 commits). Changed files: `bin/gstack-approvals`, `lib/approval-record.ts`, `test/approval-record.test.ts`, `docs/skills.md` and `changelog.d/keep-local-paths-out-of-approvals-render.md`. There were no staged, unstaged or new files. I searched every doc and template that mentions `gstack-approvals render`.

**Documentation health:**

**Coverage debt:** `render --redacted` is covered in reference docs (`docs/skills.md` and the CLI help) but has no how-to guide. That is a common gap, not a critical one.

title: Stop /autoplan getting stuck between phases after a long session is compacted
body: /autoplan now keeps working after Claude Code compacts a long session, so a run no longer gets stuck between two phases. ## Why (in your own words) In a long /autoplan run on Claude Code 2.1.317, the design phase closed normally and the next phase could never start. Every entry was refused with `cross_phase_batch` ("one message enters two phases"), even when the Read was alone in its message, and retrying could not help. The cause is the compaction, not the message. Its boundary named a `logicalParentUuid` that never reaches the session file, while the preserved tail stays in place. The tail no longer equals the logical parent, so the 2.1.300 handling did not apply, the boundary was orphaned, and every record after it was silently dropped. The guard then took the last Reads before the compaction for the current message. The change continues such a boundary from the preserved tail. I do not know why Claude Code leaves that record out; the reader only stops depending on it. ## Live evidence Regression tests before the fix, on a boundary of that shape: ``` $ bun test test/autoplan-compaction-preserved-segment.test.ts (fail) ... a boundary whose logical parent was never written continues from the preserved tail (fail) ... the next phase entry passes after a compaction whose logical parent was never written "permissionDecision": "deny" ... (code close_incomplete, Claude Code 2.1.292) 11 pass 2 fail ``` That run had 13 tests; review added 4 more, see Scope. After the fix, rebased on current main: ``` $ bun test test/autoplan-compaction-preserved-segment.test.ts 17 pass 0 fail ``` Replay of the real 2.1.317 session journal, cut just before the first refused Read and evaluated with `evaluatePayloadPublication`. Only counts and tool names are shown, the journal itself stays private: ``` BEFORE (installed guard) events 200 last: Read methodology.md (design phase) allow=false AFTER (this branch) events 260 last: Bash `true autoplan-published design` no cross_phase_batch ``` The AFTER run first returned allow=true. Repeated on the final commit it returns `close_stale`, the same as on the commit before the review fixes: the plan file changed after the journal cut, so the guard correctly refuses a stale packet. The refusal this PR fixes is gone in both. The boundary in that journal: `logicalParentUuid` occurs nowhere in the file, `preservedSegment.tailUuid` equals the last entry of `preservedMessages.uuids` and is a node written before the boundary. ## Scope - **Changed:** `preservedUuids` accepts a list whose last entry is the segment's tail, without requiring the tail to be the logical parent. `ownedCausalOrder` resumes from the preserved tail when the logical parent is absent from the file. A logical parent that is the list's own tail may be unflushed and still supplies no ownership, covered by a test. A cycling boundary whose list omits its logical parent stays refused, and a resumed fork that begins with the boundary stays a genesis root; both were widened by the first commit and restored after review, each with a test seen red first. A mismatched tail and a list with no record in the file are also covered; the mismatch test fails when the tail check is removed. Adds a CHANGELOG fragment. - **Verified live by:** the journal replay above, the eight guard and transcript test files compared with and without the fix (the same six tests fail on both in my scratch checkout, none only with the fix), `bun run typecheck`. - **Known limit:** a logical parent that is not the list's tail and is merely late is treated as never written until it lands, then the boundary re-attaches to it. The trace stays ordered and no record is lost. - **Did NOT test:** a fresh live /autoplan run through a new compaction with this branch installed. `bun run test:quick` fails locally in areas this change does not touch (browse, CSO and Bun resolution tests, from a checkout under `/private/tmp` with no built binaries), so the fork CI is the full free-suite signal. The /ship test lane did not pass locally: it hit the 600 s pregate limit, and CI carry does not accept fork runs. The setup was a manual `bun install --frozen-lockfile` rather than `bin/dev-setup`, and this branch was not symlinked as the live install. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction above 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Refuse agent words on owner-only autoplan answers
body:
An agent's own words can no longer settle a user challenge at the /autoplan gate. Only the owner's words can, and the gate stays open until they arrive.

## What changed

- `gstack-autoplan answer` now refuses, with `OWNER_REPLY_REQUIRED`, a reply given in an agent's own words (`--words-by agent:<id>`) that would choose a `uc` approval item not already settled at this revision. That covers `rec`, `as-is` and explicit `uc` tokens. The error names each item and asks for the owner's words, and nothing is written.
- The agent can still answer the `d` items in its own words and leave the `uc` items to the owner.
- A new shared predicate, `agentWords` in `lib/gate-list.ts`, replaces the inline `words_by` checks in `lib/approval-citations.ts` and `lib/autoplan-carry.ts`, so the rule lives in one place.
- `docs/unattended.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` and the `OWNER_REPLY_REQUIRED` summary describe the new case.

## Why

Only the owner may settle a user challenge or a round-cap approval. Before this change, an agent that answered with `--words-by` could choose one on its own authority, and the gate recorded it as settled. Carry-forward and plan citations already refused agent words; the answer path did not.

## Blast radius

The change touches only `gstack-autoplan answer` when `--words-by` names an agent. Owner replies, carried answers and agent answers to `d` items behave as before. A Captain that relays the owner's words without `--words-by` is unaffected.

## Documentation

**Status:** current. The branch's docs already describe the change, and none needed edits.

**Scope:** 10 committed files selected by the candidate at base 68b1d056 and head 2edd0c28; nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. Docs that mention `--words-by` were searched across the tracked tree.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/unattended.md`: Current. It describes the `uc` refusal for agent words, which matches `answerGate`.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Current. The `OWNER_REPLY_REQUIRED` entry covers the new case and matches `lib/result-codes.ts`.
- `changelog.d/refuse-agent-words-on-user-challenges.md`: Current, and accurate against the code.
- `crew/docs/captain.md`: Current, and consistent with the change.
- `autoplan/DRIVER.md`: Current. It is consistent, but see the coverage debt below.

**Coverage debt:** The `answer` line in `autoplan/DRIVER.md` doesn't say that `--words-by` replies can't settle `uc` items. It is prompt prose, so it is left to the parent.

title: Keep quoted file names with secrets in review (GST-1451)
body:
A data file whose name git quotes in patch headers no longer slips past the secret-line keep rule in `review_exclude_paths`, so a credential value in such a file reaches every reviewer like any other. ## What changed **Before:** on a base policy of `{"review_exclude_paths":["r/**"]}`, a branch adding `r/q"x.json` with a credential value had that file excluded from every reader's diff. The same content at `r/s.json` was kept. **After:** both are kept as `secret-line`. A quoted or UTF-8 name with no secret is still excluded. - **The collector decodes quoted patch headers.** `core.quotePath=false` only stops git escaping bytes of 0x80 and above. git still C-quotes a `---`/`+++` header when the name holds a `"`, a backslash, a tab or another control byte, and `-z` doesn't change patch output, so the -U0 parser stored added lines under the quoted header text. `lib/review-collect.ts` now decodes those headers byte by byte (octal escapes, `\"`, `\\`, `\t` and the rest, then UTF-8). It also pins `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/` so a user's `diff.noprefix` or `diff.mnemonicPrefix` can't shift the slice, and records an empty added-lines entry for every file section it parsed. - **The exclusion fails closed.** In `reviewExclude`, a matched file that no rule keeps but that the collector has no record of (no per-path entry, or a text file with changed lines and no added-lines entry) is kept as `consumer-scan-unavailable` instead of being excluded. - **The new tests skip on Windows.** Windows cannot create file names holding a quote, a tab or a control byte, so the quoted-name block runs on Linux and macOS only; the rest of the file still runs everywhere. ## Why Credential values in excluded data files would never reach any reviewer, and only the file name decided whether they did. ## Blast radius The change is limited to `readDiff` in `lib/review-collect.ts` and the reason loop in `reviewExclude`. Every `reviewExclude` caller (`gstack-review-plan`, `ship-receipt-depth`) passes collector output, so the fail-closed check only fires when collector keys and git's listing disagree; two reviewers read every consumer of the added-lines map and found that the new empty entries change none of them (file:line read). The kept-reason set and the receipt schema are unchanged, and names without special characters parse exactly as before. ## Tests - New in `test/review-exclude-secret-value.test.ts`: the collector keys added lines by the real path for five quoted names and a UTF-8 name. Quoted and UTF-8 names with a value line are kept, while quoted and UTF-8 names without one are excluded, and so are a deletion-only edit and a whole-file deletion, both through `collectCommit`+`reviewExclude` and through `gstack-review-plan --json` on the live tree. A matched file with no collector entry is kept as unread. - Failing first on 350d419: 3 of the new tests failed. The UTF-8-only case already passed there, because `core.quotePath=false` covers it, and it stays as a guard. - Focused suite run locally: review-exclude, review-collect, review-secret-excerpt, review-reader-selection, review-exclude-secret-value, review-plan-cli and module-size-ratchet, 129 pass and 0 fail. `bun run typecheck` is clean.
Agent notes - I chose decoding over `-z`/`core.quotePath=false` because neither changes how patch headers are quoted, so decoding is required for patch output. Mapping sections to numstat order would also work but couples two outputs. - On a branch that isn't valid UTF-8, the names come out as U+FFFD in both the numstat and the decoded headers, so the keys still agree. - The repro line from the issue (`curl -H $OPENAI_API_KEY` alone) only names a variable, and GST-1967 deliberately doesn't keep files for that, so the tests use a line that carries a value.
## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage: each of the 3 changed runtime files has a changed test naming it (deterministic coverage map, no audit reader). - Failing first on 350d419: 3 of the new tests in `test/review-exclude-secret-value.test.ts` failed; the UTF-8-only case already passed there and stays as a guard. - Tests ran: free carried from CI (see Test plan). ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue, 1 fixed after the outside voice, 0 deferred, 2 noted. - Pass 1 (specialists testing, security and state machines, plus red team): no findings. Pass 2 on the fix range: no findings. - Outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, certified configuration): one blocking finding, verified against CI. The new quoted-name tests could not create their fixture files on Windows, and `windows-scoped-shard` failed with ENOENT on `receipts/q"plain.json` (run 42587806615). Fixed in 84447ed by skipping that describe block on win32. - Native adversarial voice: no blocking findings; its two notes are listed below. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-exclude.ts:370`: the new `p in text.added` check also matches inherited object keys, so a root-level path named `constructor` or `toString` would read as seen. It can't be reached in practice, because such an extensionless name counts as code and is never excludable. `Object.hasOwn` would close it. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-collect.ts:127` (pre-existing at the base): a root-level file named `__proto__` makes the collector throw. It fails loudly, so nothing is excluded silently. Building the maps with `Object.create(null)` would close it. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `gstack-review-plan --json` in an owned fixture repo (3 probes, pass): - A plain data edit under `receipts/**` is excluded (capture 001). - `receipts/q"x.json` with a credential value is kept as `secret-line`, and `receipts/tabplain.json` with no secret is excluded (capture 002). - Negative control: the installed base build (350d419) excludes all three on the same fixture, which reproduces the bug (capture 003). Octal-escaped and control-byte names are covered by the unit tests, not probed. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. The eval selector lists dependents of `lib/review-collect.ts` and `lib/review-exclude.ts` as scheduled and release coverage, not PR passes. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix, exempt from plan review. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match the change, so no edits were made. **Scope:** committed diff 350d4196..84447ed9 on capy/keep-quoted-file-names: lib/review-collect.ts (decodes C-quoted patch-header paths and pins the a/ and b/ prefixes), lib/review-exclude.ts (keeps a matched text file whose changed lines the collector holds no lines for, as consumer-scan-unavailable), a new test, docs/ship-policy.md and a changelog.d fragment. Nothing is staged, unstaged or untracked. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-policy.md: current. The branch updated the `consumer-scan-unavailable` row of the kept-reasons table for the new fail-closed case. - docs/review-policy.md: current. Its review_exclude_paths reader section is not affected. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. No reason-code text changed. - changelog.d/keep-quoted-file-names-with-secrets-in-review.md: present and accurate. The parent owns it. **Coverage debt:** none. The change is internal collector behavior, and its only public surface, the kept reason, is covered by the reference table in ship-policy.md. **Diagram drift:** none. No diagrams reference the collector or the exclusion. ## Test plan - [x] `bun run test` (free lane): carried from CI run 42595036747/1 at tree 58140858799f, 1652 files, 36767 tests, green - [x] `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=30000 test/review-exclude-secret-value.test.ts`: 8 pass, 0 fail - [x] `bun run typecheck:test`: 812 known diagnostics, none new
Agent notes - Refs GST-1451 - /ship fixed two CI failures at earlier heads: the test-code type-debt ratchet (TS2769 on an untyped kept reason, fixed in 215c6e0) and windows-scoped-shard (fixed in 84447ed). - The free-tests pull_request run hit tree_mismatch after main moved, so free-tests.yml was dispatched on the branch (run 42595036747) and carried. - Locally, test/review-collect.test.ts and test/review-exclude.test.ts hung past 580 s on this 4-core machine; two reviewers saw one 5 s timeout there that also fails at base 350d4196. CI passed them. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch capy/keep-quoted-file-names. <details><summary>Before/after as text: the No orphaned work section</summary>

The section is new on this branch (not present at a7968dc). It says a Captain archives or rotates a thread only once a live successor owns its open PRs and issues, puts successor triggers on an issue rather than in notes, sweeps for orphaned PRs and issues on every wake, and closes a crew PR only as landed, superseded or dropped.

</details>

- **No orphaned work** is a new section in `crew/docs/captain.md`, and the daily issue sweep now re-owns issues whose assignee is archived instead of closing or backlogging them.
- **Waves:** one open queue PR per lane, follow-ups ride that PR or the area's next wave, and the section says when to move from direct landing to waves.
- **Outside PRs are bug reports.** Each gets a recommendation within 7 days, posted under the bot identity, and "not a bug" or "out of scope" needs the maintainer's word. A real bug is rewritten from main with credit, so no contributor commit enters the tree. `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("How a contributor's PR lands"), `captain/templates/CREW.md` rule 18, `crew/docs/captain.md`, `docs/review-policy.md` and the Contributor PRs row in `crew/docs/recommended-harness.md` say the same.
- **Credit check:** the credit recipe fetches the contributor's PR head with a `+` refspec, lists the authors first, and drops any author whose lines the commit does not carry before `gstack-coauthor-trailers --message` adds trailers.
- The report and brief templates carry an **Open work** line.

## Why

Garry, 2026-11-09: "we want to help future software factories NOT do this and that means gstack." gbrain's merge queue reached 220 open PRs partly because finished work lost its owner when a thread was archived. These rules make the next crew re-own that work instead of letting it rot.

## Summary

Crews kept losing finished PRs when the thread that owned them was archived, and outside PRs had no clear path. This PR writes down the rules. A Captain hands work to a live owner before archiving, sweeps for orphans, and lands outside fixes as rewrites with credit. title: Let the docs audit repair a badly shaped final line without using an attempt
body:
The /ship docs audit now tells a badly shaped final line apart from a failed audit, so a formatting slip no longer uses up its one re-audit. A repair can fill in a missing or misnamed field, but it can never supply the audit's identity or its outcome.

## What changed

/ship Step 14.5's docs audit now separates a shape-only fault in the audit child's last line from a real failure. When the last line is one JSON object whose only faults are its keys, types or the documentation section (a missing field, or a misnamed field holding `"x"`), `gstack-docs-candidate result` prints `FORMAT_REPAIR:` instead of `RETRY_NOTE:`. The step then asks once for just that line, using no attempt:

- `gstack-docs-candidate repair-prompt <output> --audit-id <id>` prints the request: the schema, the problems, and the child's own output as data. It goes to one fresh agent with no tools, never the writer child.
- `gstack-docs-candidate result <reply> ... --repair-of <output>` checks the reply. It passes only when every value the first line already gave correctly is unchanged, and each audit gets one repair. A failed or second repair prints `RETRY_NOTE:` and goes to Blocked recovery as before.

These still count as a failed attempt and get no repair: a missing, wrong or repeated audit id; a missing, unknown or repeated status; a `files_updated` or `blockers` list that is present but malformed; a status that contradicts the file lists; and a last line that is not JSON at all. A `--repair-of` that names an output with no repair is refused without using up the audit's repair.

## Why

gbrain-evals #356 (2026-11-03): both allowed docs-audit attempts returned an invalid last line, the first missing `documentation_section`, the second a misnamed key set to `"x"`. The second audit had found the docs current, but the run had spent both attempts on formatting, so an unattended /ship stopped and needed an owner-named risk or a fresh /ship.

## Blast radius

Only Step 14.5's result check: `lib/ship-docs-result.ts`, the `result` and `repair-prompt` commands in `bin/gstack-docs-candidate`, the section's Collect step, and the `DOCS_RESULT_INVALID` fix text in the result-code registry and the troubleshooting doc. A valid line produces exactly the same output and files as before. No other /ship step changed, and neither did the review-army or pr-body sections.

## Test Coverage

`test/docs-audit-result.test.ts` was written first on main and failed there (9 failures), then passed. Each review fix also got its tests first, and they failed at the previous head: 4 at b8aad9a and 5 at 4b4fe32. The file now covers both reported shapes repairing without an attempt, a valid line passing unchanged, nine content failures that still count (no repair offered, `repair-prompt` refuses), a missing blocker list staying repairable, a repair that changes `status` or `files_updated` being refused, one repair per audit, and a `--repair-of` that names a content failure not using up the repair: 41 pass, 0 fail. Step 7 coverage audit (read-only): 10 of 14 changed paths have a test; the gaps are a wrong-type status or schema_version row, the 24,000-character truncation, and whether a real child follows the repair prompt (eval).

## Pre-Landing Review

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=2 deferred=0 noted=3 fixed=6 scope=frozen ledgers_read=5 fix_checks=2 dispatches=3

Pre-Landing Review: 14 issues — 6 auto-fixed (plus 1 duplicate folded into a fixed one), 0 asked, 0 deferred, 7 noted.

The full pass (testing, security and state-machine checklists, then the Red Team) raised 4 findings, all fixed: a missing or unknown status was repairable, a missing audit id was repairable, `--repair-of` used up the repair before checking the original, and the re-ask went to the writer child. Step 11's outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) found two blocking holes: a malformed blocker list could be repaired into an empty one, and a repeated status key let the repair choose the outcome. The owner granted one scoped fix-check for those, and both are fixed. The fix-checks found nothing blocking.

## Exploratory QA

Inconclusive. The success probe passed (a valid line gives `DOCS_RESULT: ok`). The riskiest-edge probe failed: a line with no audit id was offered a format repair. It was replayed, fixed in 4b4fe32 and covered by a regression test, but the post-fix capture did not run because the 300-second smoke clock had expired.

## Eval Results

Not run in this /ship. `scripts/eval-select.ts` selects 113 behavioral probes through `lib/ship-docs-result.ts`, including the `ship-docsync-*` cases. That is well over the lane's $10 paid-eval cap, so it is left to the READY screen.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:64` Same root as outside-voice#1: a wrong-type blockers or files_updated skips the status invariants.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-docs-candidate:332` The one-repair limit and kept-value check apply only when the parent passes --repair-of with the record dir.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:91` Child output containing the AUDIT_OUTPUT>>> marker can close the repair prompt's data fence early.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-docs-candidate:340` A crash between the marker write and the result write uses up the repair.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:41` A repeated `blockers` or `files_updated` key (as opposed to a malformed one) is still repairable. So a line like `"blockers":["X"]," blockers":[]` with status current could be repaired to `blockers: []`, which loses a reported blocker: the same kind of loss this PR closes, reached a rarer way. The follow-up is to count any repeated outcome-field key as a content failure; the Captain will decide on it after this lands.
- INFORMATIONAL `docs/troubleshooting.md:6855` The entry's parenthetical "keys, types or the section" is broader than the tool now is: a malformed outcome list or a repeated id or status gets `RETRY_NOTE:` (fix-check after the granted fix; the docs audit judged the sentence still correct).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:38` A repeated status key (fix-check after the first fix round; closed by the granted fix).

title: Carry the owner's autoplan answer across fix-only gates
body:
When an autoplan run's phases were at their round cap, the owner could be asked to approve the same plan twice. In run autoplan-v0-20261109012507 the owner answered gate_rev 1 with "do it". `revise` at the cap wrote gate_rev 2 with unreviewed-delta items, and its delta check found Highs. The Highs were fixed and revise ran again, which wrote gate_rev 3 with `CARRY: no (gate_rev 2 was not answered)`. The fixes answered the owner's first "do it", but the owner had to approve again. **Carry across fix-only gates** (`lib/autoplan-carry.ts`) - When the gate before the new one was never answered, the carry now walks back to the owner's last answered gate. It only skips gates that are unanswered, were never relayed, and hold only `p1`, items decided at an earlier gate, or post-cap deltas recommending accept. Anything else refuses with its own reason. - When gates are skipped, the delta check always runs. It reads every edit since the answered gate (`plan-at-gate.r.md`), and a High or Critical still leaves the gate for the owner. `CARRIED:` says `across unrelayed gate_rev `, and the journal records `skipped_gate_revs`. - `finishGate` overwrites gate.json at a capped regate, so each gate list is now kept as `gate-at-gate.r.json`. That lets the walk read the earlier gates. - A revise since the answer that put a new axis in scope refuses the carry. That covers `ui`, `dx`, or code beyond a docs-only plan, which `plan_revised` records as `scope_widened`. **One retry per owner answer**: once two skipped gates have dispatched a delta check against the same answer, the next gate goes to the owner. That holds whether those checks failed or were voided by a revise while pending, `--unavailable`, or a stale result. If a voided check's result file exists, its reservation settles as unknown in `spend.json` instead of being released. **What counts as relayed**: every owner-facing render now journals `gate_relayed`: `gstack-owner-brief render` (both forms) and `gstack-gate render` of a gate in a run directory. A gate with such a row, or with a `recommend`, is never skipped. If a gate was rendered but never sent, the run falls back to asking the owner, which is how it behaved before this change. **Saying it up front** (`lib/autoplan-revise.ts`, `bin/gstack-autoplan`): `NEW_GATE:` says a plan edit at the round cap reopens no reviewer and goes to a new gate, and whether that gate can carry the owner's answer. It is printed in the NEXT lines after an answer that leaves accepted changes, at the top of the `revise` output, and after a delta check that found a High. A Captain can read it before promising the owner a single review pass. **Checkpoint folder** (`lib/autoplan-checkpoint.ts`): if `GSTACK_AUTOPLAN_CHECKPOINT_DIR` points at one run's folder, the checkpoint is skipped and nothing is written. One run's folder means a run directory, a `/` checkpoint folder, or a folder named after the run. The skip line names the folder to use instead, so the checkpoint no longer silently nests a copy inside it. Tests: `test/autoplan-carry-across-gates.test.ts` has the repro, which fails on main. It also has one refusal test each for an intervening user challenge, a relayed gate, a High across gates, and new scope, plus the `NEW_GATE` forecasts. `test/autoplan-checkpoint.test.ts` covers the folder-skip case. All eight new tests fail on main. Removing the relay, item, or scope guard makes its test fail. Further tests cover the retry limit, and each of the three void kinds counting toward it and staying in the spend.
Agent notes - Bug fix, so no /autoplan. The repro was written first and fails on main 350d419 and on 5164353. - `lib/autoplan-gate.ts` and `gstack-autoplan answer` are not touched. The lines #4201 changed in `assess` are kept intact, and this branch is built on main after #4201 landed (5164353). - Focused local runs: 74 related files, 1662 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail, run before #4201 landed. After moving onto 5164353, the carry, approval-class and checkpoint files all pass. `test/review-plan-targeted-delta.test.ts` times out at 5 s on this machine, and it does the same on clean 5164353, so this change didn't cause it. - **Review at bf8c1e5 is clean; no SHIP_RECEIPT yet.** Rounds 1 and 2 plus fix-check 1 ran in an earlier /ship (fixes in 19fb623 and 83352ec). The granted fix-check on 83352ec..bf8c1e5 (grant a-aea3dddb2fef) found nothing blocking: the fix-check reader and the targeted money reader both returned clean, with `REVIEW_SCOPE: policy=frozen pass=2 findings=3 note=3 blocking=0`. title: Keep deferred review findings on the PR instead of filing issues
body:
/ship and the crew docs stop filing deferred review findings as GitHub issues. A blocking finding in code a PR did not change now stays on that PR, in the body's `## Deferred findings` section, so the issue tracker only holds follow-up work someone owns. ## What changed ![Step 9.4 no longer files an issue for a deferred finding; it stays on the PR](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/kUovxOY3xXtCtvldj6p0UyWyTun88HVW4Uxpi0Kto5s.png) Step 9.4 no longer files an issue for a deferred finding; it stays on the PR.

It files one issue per `scope: defer` finding, - reusing an open issue that carries the finding's marker, scanning the issue text - as the PR body is scanned, and prints `DEFERRED:` lines; `unfiled ()` - keeps the finding deferred when gh cannot file it or the scan refuses the text, - and the command still exits 0: the PR body carries the reason. Then `gstack-review-scope render --deferred --findings ` prints the `## Deferred findings` and `## Review notes` sections: save them for Step 19's PR body. Deferred and noted findings are never edited. @@ ⋯ 1 unchanged ⋯ @@ queued adversarial finding after this pass's items 5–6 were logged, append one row under its own skill (a tokenless `review` row would read UNVERIFIED): `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-log '{"skill":"review-late-defer","via":"ship","timestamp":"TIMESTAMP","status":"issues_found","issues_found":0,"critical":0,"informational":0,"pass":PASS,"review_scope":"SCOPE","findings":FINDINGS_JSON}'` + with `findings` holding only the deferred records (`action: "deferred"`, - with `findings` holding only the deferred records (`action: "deferred"`, `issue`, `locus`, `kind`, `blocking`, `ledger_id` as in item 6) and no `--finish` token. title: pregate secrets: env.kv flags the Django idiom `session = self.client.session` as a credential
body:
## What happened

`/ship` (gstack 1.98.0.0) stopped at Step 5: the pre-gate's secrets check failed with

```
PREGATE: fail
PREGATE_DETAIL: gstack-pregate: secrets: 1 credential finding(s) in added lines (env.kv); fix: rotate and remove the credential from the added lines (history included); secrets cannot be downgraded (...) (PREGATE_SECRETS)
```

The only flagged added line is the standard Django test-client idiom in a test file:

```python
        session = self.client.session
```

Running the branch diff through `gstack-redact --json` gives five `env.kv` MEDIUM findings, all on that same line shape (`preview: 'self********…'`, col at the start of `self.client.session`); one is an added line, the rest are context/removed lines.

## Why it is a false positive

`session` matches `ENV_KV_NAME` as a bare credential suffix (rule ii in `isCredentialShapedEnvName`), and `self.client.session` passes the entropy gate. But the value is a dotted Python attribute reference, not a literal. The name-shape calibration rejects `cacheKey:`/`monkey:`, yet there's no equivalent check on the value side for identifiers or attribute access, so any `session = obj.attr.chain` (or `token = request.auth`, etc.) in Python trips it.

## Impact

- `/ship` hard-stops. `gstack-no-stop` cannot downgrade secrets, so the only remedy is editing the per-machine allowlist in `<state root>/projects/<slug>/pregate.json`. In an auto-mode session the agent can't make that edit, since it's (reasonably) treated as weakening a security gate. That leaves a human to edit policy for what is plainly not a secret.
- Every future test that uses this idiom will trip it again (the repo already has 15 such lines; it only fires on added lines).

## Suggested fix

Skip `env.kv` when the matched value is an unquoted identifier or dotted attribute chain (e.g. `^[A-Za-z_][\w]*(\.[A-Za-z_][\w]*)+$`, optionally followed by `()`/`[...]`) in a source file. A quoted literal or an `.env`/YAML value would still be scanned.

## Repro

1. In any Python repo, add a line `        session = self.client.session` to a test file.
2. `git diff | gstack-redact --repo-visibility private --json` → `env.kv` MEDIUM.
3. `gstack-pregate --allow-repo-commands` → `PREGATE_SECRETS` fail.

Workaround used: an allowlist entry `{"finding":"env.kv","paths":["**/tests/**/*.py"],"pattern":"self\\.client\\.session", ...}`.

title: Stop concurrent browse tunnel starts from leaking an ngrok session (GST-2117)
body:
Starting the browse tunnel from two places at once no longer leaves a public ngrok tunnel that the daemon can't close, and a failed start no longer keeps an idle daemon running forever. This serves gstack's goal of a browser that agents can share remotely without exposing more than you asked for. ## What changed ![The new tunnel test fails on main (two ngrok sessions; idle daemon never exits) and passes with this fix](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/6CYWWy7V0xbTQArih7tJITznRJZcMmSjUmtWc0v6xtg.png) The new tunnel test fails on main (two ngrok sessions; idle daemon never exits) and passes with this fix.
Before/after as text: The new tunnel test fails on main (two ngrok sessions; idle daemon never exits) and passes with this fix ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ bun test browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts # this PR ab195de +(pass) two concurrent tunnel starts share one ngrok session and URL [356.44ms] +(pass) a tunnel start that fails after ngrok opens leaves the daemon idle-stoppable [321.56ms] + 2 pass + 0 fail -$ bun test browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts # origin/main c25580e -[browse] Tunnel listener bound on 127.0.0.1:41969, ngrok → https://session-2.invalid -"session-2", -Received: 0 -(fail) two concurrent tunnel starts share one ngrok session and URL [361.53ms] -(fail) a tunnel start that fails after ngrok opens leaves the daemon idle-stoppable [366.83ms] - 0 pass - 2 fail ~~~
- **Concurrent tunnel starts share one session.** `ctx.tunnel.start` in `browse/src/server.ts` is now single-flight. A `POST /tunnel/start` that arrives while another start is running waits for the same `startTunnel()` promise and returns the same URL, instead of opening a second ngrok session. - **A failed start leaves the daemon idle-stoppable.** When `startTunnel()` fails after `ngrok.forward()` (for example, the state-file write throws), the catch now clears `tunnelServer`, `tunnelUrl` and `tunnelActive` along with `tunnelListener`, so `idleCheckTick` can shut an idle daemon down again. ## Why Two quick `/tunnel/start` calls opened two ngrok sessions. The daemon kept the second, so the first stayed public on the user's ngrok account until the process exited, and closing the tunnel never reached it. A start that failed after ngrok opened also left the daemon convinced a tunnel was live, so a headless daemon and its Chromium never stopped on idle. Both were found by GEVA-449's pstack verification. ## Tests `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts` drives the real `/tunnel/start` route through `buildFetchHandler().fetchLocal` with `@ngrok/ngrok` mocked. Each case runs in a child `bun test` (same pattern as `pty-inject-scan.test.ts`) so the module mock and the module-level tunnel state can't leak into other shard files. Both cases fail on origin/main (`c25580e`: `opened` was `["session-1","session-2"]`; idle tick never exited) and pass with the fix. `dual-listener.test.ts`'s source guard marker now matches the single-flight line; its assertion is unchanged. ## Blast radius The product change is 4 lines in `browse/src/server.ts`: the factory's `tunnel.start` callback and `startTunnel`'s catch block. The `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1` auto-start in `start()` still calls `startTunnel()` directly, so it shares the catch fix but not the single-flight slot (see Review notes; pre-existing on main, not widened here, read at server.ts:2128). No network, secrets, permissions, workflow, install-script or dependency changes. ## Summary A pair-agent caller that hit `/tunnel/start` twice could leak a public tunnel, and a failed start could pin the daemon awake. Route-level starts now coalesce into one in-flight start, and the failure path resets all of the tunnel state, so the idle timer works again. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts` drives the real `/tunnel/start` route through `buildFetchHandler().fetchLocal` with `@ngrok/ngrok` mocked, each case in a child `bun test` so the module mock and module-level tunnel state can't leak into other shard files. Both cases fail on origin/main c25580e (`opened` was `["session-1","session-2"]`; the idle tick never exited) and pass at ab195de. `dual-listener.test.ts`'s source-guard marker now matches the single-flight line; its assertion is unchanged. Tests ran: test 1653 (files, carried from CI run 42607749960/1 at tree 1d192cd69b8a) ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 2 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 1 noted. Adversarial (in-host, Claude): 5 findings, all below the blocking floor and noted. title: Find the RSpec spec for a Rails file in pregate lanes
body:
Rails loads classes by name, so a spec never requires the file it tests, and pregate gave every `app/` file in a Rails repo no test lane.

- A spec at `spec/<path>_spec.rb` now selects `app/<path>.rb`, and `spec/lib/<path>_spec.rb` selects `lib/<path>.rb`, when that file exists. It sits beside the existing `bin/<name>` convention.
- Example from a real Rails app: touching `app/services/plugins/netatmo_weather_station/api.rb` used to report no lane, and the starter drafted 10+ unrelated specs that mention "api". It now selects `spec/services/plugins/netatmo_weather_station/api_spec.rb` (convention).
- Test: `test/pregate-rspec-convention.test.ts`, including the case where no spec exists.
