title: Make the browse tunnel auto-start share the start lock (GST-2117)
body:
A browse daemon started with `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1` no longer leaks a second public ngrok tunnel when a `/tunnel/start` call arrives while its own auto-start is still opening. This serves gstack's goal of a browser that agents can share remotely without exposing more than you asked for. ## What changed ![The new auto-start overlap test opens two ngrok sessions on main and one with this fix](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/AL4ipymgM4Uc8Hsu_Cr9sUdCDG1G5P2SiGNwolnBFFs.png) The new auto-start overlap test opens two ngrok sessions on main and one with this fix.
Before/after as text: The new auto-start overlap test opens two ngrok sessions on main and one with this fix ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ bun test browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts # this PR c473d8b +(pass) two concurrent tunnel starts share one ngrok session and URL [434.70ms] +(pass) a route start that overlaps the BROWSE_TUNNEL=1 auto-start shares its ngrok session [722.13ms] +(pass) a tunnel start that fails after ngrok opens leaves the daemon idle-stoppable [384.38ms] + 3 pass + 0 fail -$ bun test browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts # origin/main ba2289e -(pass) two concurrent tunnel starts share one ngrok session and URL [401.57ms] -[browse] Tunnel listener bound on 127.0.0.1:, ngrok → https://session-1.invalid -[browse] Tunnel listener bound on 127.0.0.1:, ngrok → https://session-2.invalid -(fail) a route start that overlaps the BROWSE_TUNNEL=1 auto-start shares its ngrok session [697.01ms] -(pass) a tunnel start that fails after ngrok opens leaves the daemon idle-stoppable [316.57ms] - 2 pass - 1 fail ~~~
- **One start lock for both callers.** In `browse/src/server.ts` the single-start lock now lives in `startTunnel`, which wraps `openTunnel` (the old body). The `/tunnel/start` route and the `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1` auto-start in `start()` both go through it, so an overlapping start waits for the one in flight and gets the same URL. - **Changelog wording.** The unreleased fragment from #4210 now names both overlap paths. ## Tests `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts` gains a case that runs the real `start()` (headless Chromium, mocked `@ngrok/ngrok`, `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1`) in the same child `bun test` probe, holds the auto-start inside `ngrok.forward()`, and sends `POST /tunnel/start` to the daemon's real port. It fails on main ba2289e (`opened` is `["session-1","session-2"]`) and passes here. The `dual-listener.test.ts` source-guard marker returns to `start: (authtoken) => startTunnel({`. ## Blast radius The product change is 8 lines in `browse/src/server.ts`: `startTunnel` becomes a wrapper that holds the lock, and the factory's `tunnel.start` callback calls it instead of holding its own. Every throw in `openTunnel` sits inside its `try` and `.finally` always clears the lock, so a failed start can't leave it stuck (read at server.ts:404-411, confirmed by the adversarial reader). No network, secrets, permissions, workflow, install-script or dependency changes. ## Why The #4210 review noted that the `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1` auto-start "still calls startTunnel() directly", outside the lock. A `/tunnel/start` that arrived during that start opened a second ngrok session that closing the tunnel never reached. Now there is one session, whichever path starts first. ## Summary The auto-start and the route share one in-flight tunnel start, a new test drives the real `start()` to prove it, and the changelog fragment says so. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. The new case in `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts` runs the real `start()` with `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1` and `@ngrok/ngrok` mocked, holds the auto-start's forward open, sends a `/tunnel/start` and checks one session and one URL. It fails on origin/main ba2289e (`opened` was `["session-1","session-2"]`) and passes at c473d8b. `dual-listener.test.ts`'s source-guard marker is back to the original call line; its assertion is unchanged. ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted. Adversarial (in-host, Claude): no findings in the range, one older note outside it. Outside voice (GPT-6.1 Sol): clean. - Skipped: `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts:113` (the probe sleeps 100 ms before releasing the held forward). Below the blocking floor: if the route request were late, the probe would fail loudly, never pass falsely, and the same pattern from #4210 has run green in CI. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `browse/test/tunnel-start-state.test.ts:113` The overlap probe relies on a fixed 100 ms sleep for the routed `/tunnel/start` to join the in-flight auto-start before `release()`; a deterministic join signal would remove the timing dependency. - Low (pre-existing, outside the range) `closeTunnel()` does not wait for an in-flight `openTunnel`, so a close during a start is a no-op and the start then marks the tunnel active. Same at ba2289e1; it does not leak an ngrok session. ## Exploratory QA Not run: no required probe for this change. I grepped the tunnel docs in README.md, BROWSER.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/REMOTE_BROWSER_ACCESS.md and docs/BROWSER_INTERNALS.md for start-lock and concurrency wording. **Documentation health:** - README.md: current (the /pair-agent row's tunnel auto-start note is still accurate) - BROWSER.md: current (the `BROWSE_TUNNEL` variable table is unchanged) - ARCHITECTURE.md: current (the dual-listener lifecycle is unchanged) - docs/REMOTE_BROWSER_ACCESS.md: current (the `BROWSE_TUNNEL=1 $B restart` setup is still valid) - docs/BROWSER_INTERNALS.md: current **Coverage debt:** none new. title: Say one open pull request per agent thread and never archive a thread that owns work, on the factory page (GST-2077)

The page is now 3,626 bytes, rounded up to the next 25 as the test's own comment asks. - A changelog fragment describes the change.

title: Lines removed by /learn prune come back after a sync merge: gstack-jsonl-merge keeps every base line
body:
## What happened

`/learn prune` tells the agent to remove an entry by deleting its lines from `learnings.jsonl` (`learn/SKILL.md.tmpl:49`). With artifacts sync on, those lines can come back with no warning when a later merge or stash pop invokes the JSONL merge driver and its base or other side still holds them. A clone that only fast-forwards and has no local edits takes the removal correctly, because the driver does not run.

The cause is the merge driver. `bin/gstack-jsonl-merge:13` says "Concatenate base + ours + theirs", and the loop at lines 57-85 reads all three files into one set. A line that one side deleted is still in the base, so it is always in the result. Git reports a clean merge (exit 0).

Two sync paths reach the driver, both described in `docs/gbrain-sync.md:194-195` and implemented in `bin/gstack-brain-sync` (lines 609, 616, 622):

1. A push is rejected and the sync merges `origin/<branch>`. The local clone's commits are built on a base that still has the line.
2. A file the merge would change has local edits. The sync stashes it, merges, and pops the stash. The pop goes through the driver too, with a base that still has the line. The line is back in the working tree, and the next drain commits it as an ordinary one-parent commit that only adds lines. The same pop also undoes a prune the machine made itself and has not committed yet, if another machine first pushed a change to the same file: the stash then holds the removal, and the driver adds the line back from the base.

Expected: a line removed on one side and unchanged on the other stays removed, as in any three-way merge. Appends from both sides still survive.

This is already known: `TODOS.md:5525` lists it as "P2 — brain-sync resurrects removed learnings". I found no issue or pull request for it, so this gives it a tracker entry with a reproduction and the two sync paths. The header of the driver calls these files append-only, and that holds for most of them. `/learn prune` is a documented writer that removes lines; its `update` is not affected because the latest entry wins at read time. `docs/gbrain-sync.md` at this commit covers removal of whole files ("Removed and moved files", line 120) and does not cover removal of lines inside a synced JSONL file. `test/jsonl-merge.test.ts` has no case for a line removed on one side.

We saw this on our own artifacts repo, synced between machines. A prune removed 206 lines from one project's `learnings.jsonl`. Nine days later a one-parent sync commit added 191 lines and removed none; 158 of them matched removed lines byte for byte. That is the shape of path 2. We did not trace it on the machine that made the commit, so treat it as consistent with this bug and not as proof of it. The reproduction below is the proof.

## Steps to reproduce

Run this in an empty directory. It uses only git and the driver.

```bash
DRIVER=~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-jsonl-merge
git init -q --bare -b main origin.git
git clone -q origin.git a 2>/dev/null
setup() { git -C "$1" config user.email t@t; git -C "$1" config user.name t
          git -C "$1" config merge.jsonl-append.driver "$DRIVER %O %A %B"; }
setup a
echo '*.jsonl merge=jsonl-append' > a/.gitattributes
printf '%s\n' '{"ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","key":"kept"}' '{"ts":"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z","key":"pruned"}' > a/learnings.jsonl
git -C a add .gitattributes learnings.jsonl; git -C a commit -qm base; git -C a push -q origin main
git clone -q origin.git b; setup b
git clone -q origin.git c; setup c

# Machine a prunes and pushes.
sed -i '/"pruned"/d' a/learnings.jsonl; git -C a commit -qam prune; git -C a push -q origin main

# Path 1: machine b committed an append before it saw the prune.
echo '{"ts":"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z","key":"b-new"}' >> b/learnings.jsonl; git -C b commit -qam b-append
git -C b fetch -q origin; git -C b merge --no-edit origin/main; echo "merge exit $?"; cat b/learnings.jsonl

# Path 2: machine c has an uncommitted append when the sync merges.
echo '{"ts":"2026-01-04T00:00:00Z","key":"c-new"}' >> c/learnings.jsonl
git -C c stash push -q -- learnings.jsonl; git -C c fetch -q origin; git -C c merge --no-edit origin/main
git -C c stash pop -q; echo "pop exit $?"; cat c/learnings.jsonl
```

`sed -i` is the GNU form. On macOS use `sed -i ''`.

Result, with the driver at the commit below:

```text
merge exit 0
{"ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","key":"kept"}
{"ts":"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z","key":"pruned"}
{"ts":"2026-01-03T00:00:00Z","key":"b-new"}
pop exit 0
{"ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","key":"kept"}
{"ts":"2026-01-02T00:00:00Z","key":"pruned"}
{"ts":"2026-01-04T00:00:00Z","key":"c-new"}
```

Both results contain `pruned`, and each has its own new line, which is correct.

## Possible fix

`TODOS.md:5525` proposes a removal marker that the driver and every raw reader honour. A smaller option is worth weighing first: keep a base line only when it is still in both ours and theirs. Lines new on either side are kept as they are today, so appends from two machines still survive, and sorting and dedup do not change. The rule is symmetric in ours and theirs, so both machines still converge, and readers need no change because a removed line is simply gone.

The limit: the driver is registered for every `*.jsonl`, so any other writer that rewrites or rotates a synced JSONL file would start propagating its removals too. I did not audit those writers. A marker also covers one case this does not: a clone that re-adds the same line later.

The workaround today is to prune again after every machine has pulled, and to repeat it whenever the lines return. Nothing warns you that they did.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.98.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.98.0.0), agy global current (1.98.0.0), codex global current (1.98.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.160.1; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 11h ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 17)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.98.0.0 (910093087dec)
ok              claude code     2.1.309 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal no session journals for this project
ok              guard log       75 decisions (5 denied)
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: Claude Code 2.1.309
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 12, Linux 7.0.0-43-generic; git 2.39.5, Python 3.11.2
- gstack: running 1.98.0.0; code and docs cited at `main` ba2289e1cd9f2387d069b3b6c51b404d56c4a1e9. `bin/gstack-jsonl-merge` has the same blob at both (4a7074186955).
- Related, different problems in the same sync: #4174 (a derived snapshot conflicts in the retry merge), #3704 (the retry merge itself), #3659 (driver encoding on Windows). A tracker search for "gstack-jsonl-merge", "learn prune", "pruned learnings" and "merge driver deleted lines" found no issue on this. The neighbouring `TODOS.md` entry "learnings.jsonl has no writer lock" is about a different race in the same prune step.

title: /learn prune reads only the top 100 learnings and does not say it skipped the rest
body:
## What happened

`/learn prune` builds its list with `gstack-learnings-search --limit 100` (`learn/SKILL.md.tmpl:40` at bfa36fe59354a5dc8d21e11ef64a011d30cbd959) and flags stale and conflicting entries from that list. A project with more than 100 unique learnings is only partially checked, and the search output prune reads does not disclose the cut.

Why the part left out matters, all at the same commit:

- With no query, `bin/gstack-learnings-search:212-217` sorts by effective confidence, then recency, and line 221 cuts to the limit.
- Lines 155-160 take 1 point off `observed` and `inferred` entries per 30 days, so decay can push older entries of those sources below the cut. Those are plausibly the entries that name a file that is gone.
- The notice "N more matched, raise --limit to see them" (line 236) only prints when a query was given, and `test/gstack-learnings-search.test.ts:203` pins that. Prune passes no query, so the summary line reads `LEARNINGS: 100 loaded (...)`, the same as for a project that holds exactly 100.

The CONFLICT check has the same limit: it needs both rows of a key to be on the list, and a key whose other row was cut is not seen.

I expected prune to check every entry, or to say how many it did not check. `docs/skills.md:1284` describes prune as removing "stale entries (when referenced files no longer exist)"; the docs at this commit do not mention a cap.

Two of our project stores hold 286 and 373 unique learnings, so most of each never reaches prune. This report is about prune, where a skipped entry means a stale entry stays; `show` and `export` use smaller limits too (`--limit 20`, `--limit 50`), but they are a view, not a cleanup.

## Steps to reproduce

Synthetic store: 110 fresh entries, plus one 90-day-old entry that names a deleted file. This runs the command the prune row uses, not the skill itself. I ran it on the installed 1.98.0.0 (91009308), where `bin/gstack-learnings-search` and `learn/SKILL.md.tmpl` are byte-identical to bfa36fe; I did not run it on a bfa36fe checkout.

```bash
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/state" "$T/repo"
git -C "$T/repo" init -q -b main
git -C "$T/repo" remote add origin https://github.com/example/prune-demo.git
mkdir -p "$T/state/projects/example-prune-demo"
python3 - "$T/state/projects/example-prune-demo/learnings.jsonl" <<'EOF'
import json, sys, datetime as d
now = d.datetime.now(d.timezone.utc)
stamp = lambda t: t.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
row = lambda k, t, **x: json.dumps({"skill": "demo", "type": "pitfall", "key": k, "insight": k, "confidence": 9, "source": "observed", "ts": stamp(t), **x})
with open(sys.argv[1], 'w') as f:
    for i in range(110):
        f.write(row(f"fresh-{i}", now) + "\n")
    f.write(row("old-points-at-deleted-file", now - d.timedelta(days=90), files=["src/deleted.ts"]) + "\n")
EOF
cd "$T/repo"
S=~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-learnings-search
GSTACK_HOME="$T/state" "$S" --stats | head -2
GSTACK_HOME="$T/state" "$S" --limit 100 | head -1
GSTACK_HOME="$T/state" "$S" --limit 100 | grep -c '^- \[old-points-at-deleted-file\]'
GSTACK_HOME="$T/state" "$S" --limit 1000 | grep -c '^- \[old-points-at-deleted-file\]'
```

Output:

```text
TOTAL: 111 entries
UNIQUE: 111 (after dedup)
LEARNINGS: 100 loaded (100 pitfalls)
0
1
```

The one entry that prune should flag is not on the list it reads, and the summary line gives no sign of that.

That costs context on a large store, which may be why the limit exists. The alternative is for prune to state how many entries it did not check, which the skill can do from `--stats` without changing the search's query-only notice. The current workaround is parsing `learnings.jsonl` directly.

Related: #2762 (closed), a query pushing the exact match off the list, is where a query's cut got its handling; #4214 is a different prune defect, removed lines coming back after a sync merge.

title: /test-audit Step 1 reads $BRANCH without setting it, so it misses the eng-review test plan
body:
## What happened

`/test-audit` Step 1 looks for the eng-review test plan of the current branch, so it can use the plan's `## Tests to Retire` entries as seed candidates. With `BRANCH` unset, the lookup matches only plans for branches whose names end in `-`, whatever the current branch is. If no such plan exists, no `SEED_PLAN:` line is printed, even when the current branch has a plan, and the skill takes its "Without it, run full discovery" path with no sign that a plan was missed.

The lookup is `test-audit/SKILL.md.tmpl:60` (line 166 of the generated `test-audit/SKILL.md`):

```bash
ls -t "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT"/projects/$SLUG/*-"$BRANCH"-eng-review-test-plan-*.md 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/^/SEED_PLAN:/'
```

Nothing sets `BRANCH` in that block, and the generated `test-audit/SKILL.md` has no `BRANCH=` assignment outside `DEFAULT_BRANCH=`. With `BRANCH` empty the pattern becomes `*--eng-review-test-plan-*.md`. The writer names plans `{user}-{branch}-eng-review-test-plan-{datetime}.md` (`scripts/resolvers/testing.ts:511`), so only a branch name ending in `-` produces the `--` that pattern needs. Such a plan matches from any branch, so another branch's plan can be picked up. `2>/dev/null` hides the failed `ls`.

Expected: when a plan exists for the current branch, Step 1 prints `SEED_PLAN:<path>` and its `## Tests to Retire` entries (written at `scripts/resolvers/testing.ts:532`) become seed candidates, as `test-audit/SKILL.md.tmpl:66-67` says.

The `BRANCH:` line from `gstack-skill-start` does not fill the gap if an agent substitutes it by hand. It keeps `/` (`bin/gstack-skill-start:155`), while the writer's value from `gstack-slug` turns `/` into `-` (`bin/gstack-slug:625`), so a branch like `feat/x` misses either way. The reproduction below shows that too.

The writer already has the right line (`scripts/resolvers/testing.ts:503`). The same line before the `ls` fixes the lookup, as the last case below shows:

```bash
BRANCH=$(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-slug --get BRANCH 2>/dev/null)
```

The `/test-audit` section of `docs/skills.md` does not cover the seed, so Step 1 is the only statement of this behaviour that I found.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a scratch repo on branch `feat/x`, create a plan where the writer would put it. I set `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT` to a temp directory.
2. Run the Step 1 `ls` line in a fresh shell: as written, with the `BRANCH:` value from skill start, and with the writer's `BRANCH=` line first.

```bash
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q -b feat/x repo && cd repo
git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -q --allow-empty -m init
export GSTACK_STATE_ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"
B=~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin
SLUG=$("$B/gstack-slug" --get SLUG 2>/dev/null)
W=$("$B/gstack-slug" --get BRANCH 2>/dev/null)
mkdir -p "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/projects/$SLUG"
touch "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/projects/$SLUG/alice-$W-eng-review-test-plan-20261109-120000.md"
look='ls -t "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT"/projects/$SLUG/*-"$BRANCH"-eng-review-test-plan-*.md 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed "s/^/SEED_PLAN:/"'
export SLUG
echo "as written:";  env -u BRANCH bash -c "$look"
echo "skill-start value:"; BRANCH=feat/x bash -c "$look"
echo "with the writer's line:"; env -u BRANCH bash -c "BRANCH=\$($B/gstack-slug --get BRANCH 2>/dev/null); $look"
```

Output (temp path shortened):

```text
as written:
skill-start value:
with the writer's line:
SEED_PLAN:<tmp>/projects/repo/alice-feat-x-eng-review-test-plan-20261109-120000.md
```

An agent can work around this by setting `BRANCH` itself, which is how I noticed. An agent that runs the block as written, with `BRANCH` unset, gets a clean-looking result: full discovery that silently ignores the plan's retire list, or, when a plan exists for a branch ending in `-`, that plan's list, whichever branch it was written for.

title: [feature] /test-audit: check stronger_proof with a behavior-breaking edit before a test is retired
body:
## What is missing

A `/test-audit` retirement card has a `stronger_proof` field, and no step runs it before deletion. The field can be filled from reading alone. So a test can be retired as a duplicate of a stronger test that does not fail on the same regression, and the suite stays green while the protection is gone.

A new regression test has to show executed evidence: it fails at HEAD in its own assertion, and a load or environment failure does not count (`scripts/resolvers/test-value.ts:151`, shape at `docs/test-value-bar.md:130`). A test being deleted has no equivalent.

Checked at gstack `bfa36fe`:

- `test-audit/SKILL.md.tmpl:99-102` requires the card to be complete. Step 3 tells the agent to read the test, its owner, the callers and the overlapping tests.
- `validation` and Step 6.3 (`:141`, "Run the owner and sibling tests") run after approval and after the deletion, against unbroken production code. A green run there says nothing about the regression the deleted test caught.
- `docs/test-value-bar.md:49-51` lists the card fields. Its sample at `:142` is prose: `stronger_proof: test/refund.test.ts covers refund reasons through refundPayment`.
- Step 6.2 (`:139-140`) already asks for an executed check in a scratch worktree, after approval, before production code is removed. Retiring a test has no such check.
- The docs at this commit do not cover probing a retirement.

gbrain has a stricter rule for its own repo. `docs/TESTING.md:364-376` at gbrain `8af65c1`, "Retiring a test": "make a behavior-breaking edit to the production code (or, for a vacuous assertion, show that such an edit passes), run the test and the surviving owner, then revert." Step 3 there also requires the survivor to run at the same or a more frequent cadence with an equal or stronger failure gate. This request asks for the probe part only.

## What happened to us

In a private deployment repo, a `/test-audit` run retired one test of about 20 grep assertions over a bash supervisor as a duplicate of its behaviour tests. Its `/review` caught and restored a different row from the same PR, and this one passed.

Five days after that landed, a later run tried the mutation by hand, on a copy of the tree at private commit `9159d63` with one line deleted, using `bats <file>` on the two owning test files:

- `trap '' TERM INT` removed from the stop handler: rc=0 for both files, 27 and 19 tests ok, none failed or skipped. Without that line a second TERM re-enters the handler and logs the stop twice. The retired test, at the commit before its removal, passed unmodified and failed on this same edit, in its own assertion, so its removal lost this protection.
- The same trap removed from each of the two helpers the handler calls: rc=0 on the 10 stop tests, each time.

The same later run found a second case in a card from a report-only run: a probe was named as the stronger proof for a test that pins three `COPY` lines. The probe failed on a changed destination but passed when the lines were deleted. That cut had not been applied.

This was one repo and a few rows. It is one example, not a measured rate.

**Against this request:** the first case did not need a new rule to be caught. A comment in the surviving test said the parent-level trap in the handler "is guarded by the static scripts.bats row, not by this one", and that row was the one retired. Step 3 requires reading overlapping tests, and the retention bar keeps source inspection when it is the cheapest independent guard. The agent missed it. We are not reporting a bug. We are asking for a mechanical backstop, because in this case a careful read did not happen.

## Proposal

A probe in Step 6, after a batch is approved and before 6.1 makes the edits, in a scratch worktree like Step 6.2. This keeps the boundaries at `:37-42`: discovery stays read-only, edits happen only to an approved batch, and spawned and headless sessions stay report-only. The probe edits and runs only in the scratch worktree, never in the checkout, so `:44` ("Never edit source or tests while a test runner is running in the checkout") holds too.

For each retirement whose card names a surviving test:

1. Confirm the retired test and the surviving test both pass without the edit.
2. Make the behavior-breaking edit for each behaviour the card says the survivor covers. A test with many assertions gets one edit per distinct behaviour, not one per assertion.
3. Run both tests on each edit. The probe holds, and the candidate stays in the batch, when the retired test fails and the survivor fails in its own assertion. A load, syntax or environment failure does not count, as with regression proof: if that happens, or if either test fails in step 1, record `probe: not run (<reason>)`.
4. Record it on the card, for example `probe: <edit> → <test> failed in assertion`.

When the retired test fails on an edit and the survivor stays green, the survivor does not cover that behaviour, so the candidate leaves the batch and goes back to the user. It may still be retired for another stated reason (an obsolete requirement, an implementation detail the survivor rightly does not pin), but not as a duplicate. When a probe cannot run (Docker, a live stack, paid calls), the card says `probe: not run (<reason>)` and the user decides.

When the retired test itself stays green on the edit, the probe is inconclusive: the edit may be wrong, or the test may simply miss that regression. The candidate goes back to the user. Calling a test vacuous needs its own evidence.

This checks the behaviours the card names. It does not prove that all coverage survives.

It adds run time per candidate, after the 8-minute discovery budget at `:68`. If you would rather have the result on the card at approval time, a scratch-worktree run during discovery depends on how you read `:37`, which is your call.

## Alternatives

- What we do now: run the mutation by hand on each card and add the step to our own process. It works only for a session that remembers it.
- Mark such a test with `gstack:test-value keep reason="..."`. That protects a test someone already knows is special, and this one looked like a plain duplicate.
- Rely on reading and `/review` of the card. Those caught one row in this PR and missed another.

## Environment

- gstack 1.98.0.0 at `9100930`, Claude Code on Linux. Claims about the skill and docs were read at `bfa36fe` on `main`.
- Searched open and closed for `test-audit`, `retirement card`, `stronger_proof`, `test value bar mutation`, and found no issue on this. #4216 is open on `/test-audit` Step 1, a different problem.

title: Stop the review collector reading severity words in prose as findings (GST-2122)
body:
The review collector no longer stops /ship when a reader returns `NO FINDINGS` or writes a sentence that denies a severity. Prose outside a clean reply collects exactly as it did before.

## What changed

The review collector (`parseFindings` in `lib/review-ledger.ts`, run by `gstack-review-dispatch collect`) no longer stops /ship on a reader's clean reply or on a sentence that denies a severity.

- **Before:** #4208's pass-2 red team returned `NO FINDINGS` but quoted `CRITICAL (the reviewer wrote …)` in a coverage bullet, and it collected as `p2/red-team#1` CRITICAL. An alphaclaw fix-check wrote "No fix introduced a CRITICAL defect", which collected as CRITICAL too. Judge may not drop or lower a collected finding, so `gstack-review-plan` printed `NEXT: stop` on both.
- **After:**
  - **Clean replies:** a reply that says `NO FINDINGS` keeps only its structured findings, which still collect at their label. Those are JSON objects (malformed ones included), lead labels, label headings, numbered finding headings, `Severity` fields, `Blocks: yes`, the native voice's FIXABLE or INVESTIGATE tag, and anything naming a file:line. Its other prose collects nothing.
  - **Denials:** "No fix introduced a CRITICAL defect" and its variants (none of the fixes caused, added or left a High regression) are no-defect clauses, read by the existing GST-435 closing-summary grammar. That holds after a bold, unlabelled lead too, such as `**1. Coverage:** …` or `- **Callers:** …`.
  - **Everything else:** prose outside a clean reply collects exactly as before. A real prose blocker such as #4075's "Neither fix clears the P0." still blocks, and every earlier pinned expectation is unchanged.

## Why

A reader reporting a clean result, or saying a fix introduced nothing severe, was enough to stop /ship. That stopped this repo's #4208 and garrytan/alphaclaw#385/#386 (GST-2122).

## Blast radius

This changes only the collector's reading of clean replies, plus one new denial phrase class. Judge, the blocking count and reader briefs are unchanged. The one bypass is unstructured, unlocated prose inside a `NO FINDINGS` reply, which now collects nothing. `test/review-prose-severity.test.ts` pins it.

## Tests

- **New test file:** `test/review-prose-severity.test.ts`, written first. At this head it covers:
  - #4208's raw reader reply, as a fixture.
  - The alphaclaw sentence, verbatim. Its reply was not kept, so the text around it is rebuilt in the fix-check brief's shape.
  - A `NO FINDINGS` reply with severity words in its prose.
  - Documented-format CRITICALs for every role.
  - Structured or malformed findings next to `NO FINDINGS`.
  - #4075's prose blocker, which still blocks.
  - The bypass pin.
  - The readers' three bold-lead denial controls.
  - Native relaxed-parse alignment and numbered headings.
- **Focused checks at this head:**
  - Parser and dispatch suites: 125 pass.
  - review-collect, review-scope and review-plan: 194 pass.
  - Parity-suite, module-size-ratchet and the spawnsync tripwire: 11 pass.
  - `bun run typecheck` is clean.

## Documentation
**Status:** current. The docs already describe this branch's review-collector change, so I made no edits.

Scope: the diff from base `bfa36fe` to head `fa6abab` on `stop-review-collector-reading-prose-severity`. It touches `lib/review-ledger.ts`, `docs/review-policy.md`, a changelog.d fragment and tests. There were no staged, unstaged or new files.

Documentation health:
- `docs/review-policy.md`: current. It describes how a `NO FINDINGS` reply keeps only its structured findings, the new denial clause and the bold-lead handling (GST-2122), and that wording matches the code.
- `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/unattended.md`, `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `review/SKILL.md.tmpl`: current. They mention `NO FINDINGS` but not how prose is parsed.

Coverage debt: none. Diagram drift: none.

## Pre-Landing Review

/ship ran two full review rounds and one granted fix-check (a-efb05cd1606d).
- Fixed in round 1 (d460378): the relaxed native parse fell out of line with the main parse under `NO FINDINGS` (p1/specialist-batched#1), and numbered finding headings lost their label (p1/red-team#2).
- Fixed in the granted round (fa6abab): a numbered or bold-led heading that only denies a severity collected at it under `NO FINDINGS` (p2/adversarial-native#2, p2/red-team#1).
- Open notes, none blocking:

  - p1/red-team#3: a coverage note that quotes `Severity:`/`Blocks:` fields or cites a file:line still collects at its label beside `NO FINDINGS`.
  - p1/red-team#4: `**NO FINDINGS**` in bold is not read as the clean marker.
  - p3/fix-check#1: the bold-lead strip skips the lead's file:line, exception and Severity-field guards, so `- **auth.ts:9:** No CRITICAL issues.` and `**Severity:** nothing CRITICAL.` after a located finding now collect nothing.
  - p3/fix-check#2: the new denial clause accepts any short subject, so "No null check left a CRITICAL bug." reads as a denial.

title: Make autoplan's plan-approval gate item p1 so gstack-gate accepts it (#4181)
body:
/autoplan's final approval gate now renders, and replies to its plan-approval item parse. The skill told the agent to name that item `plan`, which gstack-gate refuses, so the whole gate failed before anyone could answer it.

## What changed

- `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` (and the regenerated `autoplan/SKILL.md`) names the plan-approval gate item `p1` instead of `plan`, and lists its replies as `p1a`, `p1c`, `p1d` and `p1e` instead of `plana`, `planc`, `pland` and `plane`.
- `test/gate-list.test.ts` adds "the /autoplan Phase 4 gate as documented (#4181)": it builds the gate from the template's own text and runs `bin/gstack-gate render` and `parse` for every documented reply.
- `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` lowers 12 autoplan size pins by the 10 characters the rename saves.
- `changelog.d/autoplan-gate-accepts-plan-approval-replies.md` adds the release note.

## Why

"gstack-gate render exits 1" on the gate /autoplan Phase 4 tells the agent to write (#4181, reported by @exGeni). gstack-gate only accepts an item id made of a lowercase label and a number (`ID_RE` at lib/gate-list.ts:75, and the reply-token pattern at :207), so `plan` failed validation and `plana` never matched. `p1` is the id gstack's own gate builder (lib/autoplan-gate.ts) and docs/unattended.md already use, so the skill now agrees with the tool.

## Blast radius

Only /autoplan's Phase 4 prose and its test and size pins change; no code path changes. The new test builds the gate from the template text itself, so a future rename that breaks the id fails CI (rung: script ran; failing first on main 6473a17, where render and all four parses exit 1 with "items[2].id must match [a-z]*[0-9]+"). The change touches no network, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies.

Outside credit: @ElNeMeR70 (#4189) and @szsunyuan (#4191) proposed the same rename. Their code was read as text only and never checked out or run; this change was written on main, and the commit credits both with Co-authored-by trailers.

title: Rebuild the decision snapshot from the merged log when two machines' syncs conflict (#4174)
body:
Two machines that each log a decision between pushes no longer stop one of them from syncing, so gbrain-sync keeps every machine's decision memory in step without a hand repair. ## What changed Before, the second machine's push was rejected, its fetch-and-merge retry conflicted on `projects//decisions.active.json`, and `gstack-brain-sync` aborted the merge and wrote `push_failed` on every later drain until someone repaired the clone by hand. Now the merge finishes and the push goes out, with a snapshot rebuilt from the merged `decisions.jsonl`. - `bin/gstack-brain-sync`: when a stopped retry merge's only conflicts are `projects/*/decisions.active.json` files whose `decisions.jsonl` merged cleanly, each snapshot is rebuilt from the merged log, staged, and the merge is committed. The rebuild runs only when every line of the log at the merge base is still on both sides. The log merge driver takes the union of both sides, so a log that lost lines on one side (`--compact` expunging a redacted decision) would get them back; that merge aborts as before. A conflict in any other file, a log that did not merge cleanly, a missing bun or a failed rebuild also still aborts. - `bin/gstack-decision-log --rebuild-snapshot `: rewrites one project's snapshot from its log with the same `rebuildSnapshot` every decision write uses. It refuses an empty slug, a path, `.`/`..`, or a project with no log. - `bin/gstack-artifacts-init`: new repositories get `projects/*/decisions.active.json merge=binary` in `.gitattributes`, so a merge run by hand leaves no conflict markers in the snapshot. The brain-sync fix does not depend on this line. - `docs/gbrain-sync.md` says how the snapshot is resolved, when brain-sync still aborts, and how to finish a hand-run merge. ## Why "Two machines' syncs conflict and one of them stays push_failed for good" (#4174). The snapshot is derived from the event log, and the log already merges through the jsonl-append driver, so rebuilding from the merged log is the one correct resolution, as long as neither side deleted log lines. ## Blast radius Only brain-sync's retry merge after a rejected push, and only when every conflict is a decision snapshot. The stash recovery path after that merge is unchanged from main, so a mismatched log and snapshot there stay held by the decisions-active coupled-group check (tested). A clone whose peer ran `--compact` since they last agreed still aborts, as on main. ## Test Coverage - `test/brain-sync.test.ts`, the #4174 block, 6 tests: two machines each log a decision (current and pre-fix `.gitattributes`), a clone already holding a conflicting commit recovers, a merge that would bring back a redacted and compacted decision still aborts, a decision log that stash pop brings back with an expunged decision stays held and never reaches the remote, and a conflict in another file still aborts. - Failing first: on main 6473a17 three of the original four went red with `push_failed` and `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in projects/acme-app/decisions.active.json`. The redaction test was red without its guard (status `ok`, expected `push_failed`). The hold test was red with the reverted stash-pop rebuild put back (status `ok`). - `test/gstack-decision-bins.test.ts` covers `--rebuild-snapshot` and its refusals; all 26 green. - CI: free-tests run 42653255504 green at this tree (1654 files carried). ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 3 blocking found across 2 full passes and 1 fix-check, all fixed; 4 noted, 0 deferred. - The first pass's red team (CRITICAL, fixed): a retry merge after another machine's `--compact` rebuilt the snapshot from the union log and republished a redacted decision. Fixed by the base-line guard. - Step 11 adversarial and outside voice (CRITICAL, fixed): a stash-pop snapshot rebuild added in pass 1 made a decision brought back by stash pop consistent and publishable. Reverted to main's stash path, with a hold test. - Notes, below the floor: a peer's compaction keeps that case stuck as on main; the jsonl-append driver brings back compacted lines on clean merges (predates this PR); after the hold, the next ordinary decision on that machine rebuilds the snapshot from the brought-back log (predates this PR); criss-cross merge bases and a missing bun are edge cases. Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 0 read). ## Exploratory QA Smoke only through the failing-first repro tests above; the QA method sections were not run. ## Documentation **Scope:** I audited the 7 selected files in the candidate (base 324135dfb150, head fa756304d, 4 commits, with nothing staged, unstaged or untracked) against reviewed tree 68807149491999a53fd125c0207a11ffdb9640ff. **Result:** The docs are current, and I made no edits. `docs/gbrain-sync.md` already describes the snapshot rebuild, the exception for logs that lost lines, the `merge=binary` attribute and the manual `--rebuild-snapshot` recovery. All of it matches `bin/gstack-brain-sync`, `bin/gstack-decision-log` and `bin/gstack-artifacts-init`. The banned-terms check found nothing, and there are no blockers. **Debt:** The new `--rebuild-snapshot` flag is documented only in the CLI usage text and in `docs/gbrain-sync.md`. The decision-log CLI has no reference doc. ## Test plan - [x] `bun test test/brain-sync.test.ts -t 4174`: all 6 green - [x] `bun test test/gstack-decision-bins.test.ts`: all 26 green - [x] free-tests CI run 42653255504 at fa756304dfe8: green ## Issues Refs #4174
Agent notes Lane GSTA-445 for GStack Minder. Decision trail: reports/GSTA-445-decisions.tsv in the Captain drive. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-26365ae18dad). The full approval record stays private. Plan: exempt: bug fix REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=3 deferred=0 noted=4 fixed=4 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 fix_checks=1 dispatches=4

title: gstack-post holds a READY block with carried CI: the SHIP_RECEIPT line's run ids read as phone numbers
body:
## What happened

`gstack-ship-queue ready` printed a READY block whose `SHIP_RECEIPT:` line ends in `ci_carried=tests:<run id>/1,e2e:<run id>/1`. Posting that block with `gstack-post pr-comment` stopped with exit 2 and `RULE: pii.phone.e164`, once for each run id occurrence on that line. `crew/docs/recommended-harness.md:157` says to post the READY block as a PR comment. It does not name a tool, and `gstack-post` was our choice. The block comes from gstack's own command, so I expected it to pass.

#4198 (GST-2047) fixed the same false hold for the JSON `gstack-ship-receipt` block in a PR body. The one-line summary of that receipt was not part of that change. The receipt writer builds the summary at `lib/ship-receipt.ts:190` and `ready` prints it. The `ci_carried=` field itself gives none of the recognized contexts:

- `receiptRunIdSpans` (`lib/gstack-post.ts:519`) reads only the fenced JSON block.
- `CI_RUN_LIST` (`lib/redact-patterns.ts:405`) needs `run=` or `runs=` directly before the id.
- `CI_RUN_WORD_BEFORE` (`lib/redact-patterns.ts:407`) needs a run word directly before the id. Here the id follows `tests:`, a lane name, and the lane name varies by repo.

The section at `docs/troubleshooting.md:2979` lists the exempt positions, and this line is not one of them. Its fallback for anything else is `--confirm`. The doc's rule that a phone number elsewhere must still report is good, so this asks for the exact shape only, not for looser matching.

This is a false hold, not a leak. A READY comment with carried CI hits this hold when its run ids have no other recognized context in the comment, and the only route the message offers is to ask the user to confirm. This leaves the symptom of #4198 in the one-line summary, outside the fenced JSON that #4198 covers. We hit it on a private repo, where the post also stopped.

Workaround we used: add a true line `ci_carry: runs=<run id>/1` to the comment. `receiptDigitTokens` then allowlists that exact token for the whole text, so the `SHIP_RECEIPT:` line passes unchanged. `captain/templates/READY.md` allows the lane's own lines after the block, and a line placed there works too. The doc's fix is to write the id next to a run word. Here that means adding context around the tool's printed line, and it helps only because the allowlist works by token across the whole text.

A possible fix: add a `ci_carried=<lane>:<id>/<attempt>[,...]` shape beside `CI_RUN_LIST`, with its bounds (11 to 12 digits, attempt required), so every scan caller gets it. A bare number or `+14155552671` elsewhere on the line would still report.

## Steps to reproduce

Run at `324135d` on `main`, in a scratch git repo whose `origin` is an unreachable GitHub URL, with a synthetic run id. A post that passes the scan would then stop at `gh`, not reach anything.

1. Write a body file:
   ```text
   READY #1 abc STAMP_VERSION=unstamped
   SHIP_RECEIPT: pr=1 head=abc123abc123 version=1.0.0.0 base=main ci_carried=tests:42000000001/1,e2e:42000000001/1
   ```
2. Run `gstack-post pr-comment 1 --repo-visibility private --body-file body.md`.

Result, exit 2:

```text
RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 2 PART: body
RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 2 PART: body
gstack-post: MEDIUM findings; nothing was posted. Ask the user about each finding; to post these exact bytes, rerun with --confirm <token>. Any edit needs a new scan.
```

Adding a line `ci_carry: runs=42000000001/1` above or below the `SHIP_RECEIPT:` line gets past the scan: exit 3 from `gh`, on the unreachable repo.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.98.0.0
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

Trimmed to the summary: every row is `ok`, and none of them touches this path.

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.309
- OS: Linux 7.0.0
- gstack installed: 1.98.0.0 at `9100930`, where we first hit it on a real READY block. The three cited files differ between that commit and `main`, so the reproduction above was rerun at `324135d`.
- Related: #4197 and #4198 (GST-2047). Searched open and closed for `ci_carried pii.phone`, `SHIP_RECEIPT phone`, `gstack-post READY comment MEDIUM`, and found no issue on this line.

title: Test Framework Bootstrap detection misses a runtime whose package.json is not at the repo root
body:
## What happened

In a repo whose only `package.json` is two directory levels down (`site/code/package.json`, with a `"test"` script), the detection block of the Test Framework Bootstrap in `/qa`, `/design-review` and `/ship` prints no runtime and no test script. Every runtime and script marker check is a root-relative `[ -f <marker> ]` or an `ls` of the root, so a Node project that lives two levels down is invisible. The skill's own text then has nothing to go on, and likely falls to its "Unknown runtime" prompt (`:33`) instead of recognising node.

Checked at gstack `main` e487cd40f81a51af26fbf402181957aa7fb63d24 (VERSION 1.98.0.0, the version I run):

- `qa/sections/test-bootstrap.md:10-15` loops over `package.json`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, ... with `[ -f "$marker" ]` in the current directory; `:21` tests `[ -f package.json ] && grep -q '"test"...'`; `:33` says "Unknown runtime: AskUserQuestion ... Monorepo: ask which first, or both sequentially."
- `design-review/sections/test-bootstrap.md:15,29` and `ship/sections/tests.md:17,31` use the same root-only `[ -f package.json ]`.
- Scope: `:5` limits `/qa` bootstrap to browser /qa and lets a documented test command in CLAUDE.md/TESTING.md skip it, so this only bites repos with neither.
- The `TESTFILES` count (`qa/sections/test-bootstrap.md:24`) uses `git ls-files | grep`, which is recursive, so test files are found at any depth while runtime and script markers are not.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `git init` an empty repo; create `site/code/package.json` containing `{"name":"x","scripts":{"test":"vitest"}}`.
2. Run the bash block of `qa/sections/test-bootstrap.md` from the repo root. Output: `TESTFILES:0` only.
3. Add a root `package.json` and run it again: now `RUNTIME:node` appears.

(I ran the extracted block directly; I did not run a full `/qa` on this synthetic repo, so the prompt behaviour above is inferred from the skill text, not observed.)

## Expected

A runtime marker below the root (a `site/code/` or `app/` style layout) is reported with its directory, or at least the "Unknown runtime" prompt offers the directories where markers were found, so the monorepo sentence at `:33` has something to ask about.

## Readiness report

Not applicable to the detection logic itself; the behaviour is in the skill text above. I found no mention of nested runtime markers in these three skill files at the commit above.

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code, gstack 1.98.0.0
- Related, not the same: #1069 (`/ship` hardcodes `bin/test-lane` + `npm run test` regardless of detected framework, closed).
- This is a request to widen detection, not a defect in the root-only case; I know the root-only form may be deliberate to keep the probe cheap. A bounded search (for example `find . -maxdepth 3 -name package.json -not -path '*/node_modules/*'`, which also sees untracked files) would keep that cost small.

title: Fix seven test and eval checks that misread correct work or raced their neighbours (GST-2131)
body:
Seven gstack test and eval checks no longer fail on correct work or race the tests beside them. A red check in the free suite or the paid gate points at a real problem again, which serves the README's goal of a review and release workflow you can trust unattended.

## What changed

No screen or prompt changed, so this shows the check output before and after instead of an image.

- codex-review's skill excerpt: main's version left 3 helper paths pointing at an install the eval never seeds. This branch points every one of them, `bin/` helpers and the `lib/outside-review-result.ts` script alike, at the checkout, and a free check now fails if any excerpt path cannot run without an install.
- tpa-present's consent check: `D) Do it later. I'll mark this step as waiting on you.` was missed before and now counts as the defer option. Refusals and conditions such as `I refuse to mark this step as blocked on you` and `Otherwise this step is blocked on you` still do not count.
- scrape-prototype-path now credits browse's own `Navigated to <fixture URL> (2xx)` line, so a run that navigated through `$PWD` passes.

## Why

"Seven checks failed on correct work or raced other tests in the same shard" (daily flaky pass, census run 42571575838 and Free Tests 42547259416, 42560717406 and 42555737357). Each red cost a rerun or a misdiagnosis. Each repair changes how the check reads the result or isolates its fixture, so real failures still fail.

## Blast radius

Only test helpers, test files, one captured fixture, two harness pins and one Windows curation entry change, and no product code ships. The new helpers are called only from the changed case files: I read every caller, and the focused files pass 120 of 120 at this head (QA capture 001).

## Summary

Contributors saw eval and free-suite reds that came from the checks, not the work. The checks now read what the model actually did, such as browse's navigation line, a file:line inside the right function or a defer option in its own words. Two free-suite races are gone. The handoff test takes a race-safe X display, and the AUQ fixture turns off git's background maintenance. The Windows curated lane skips one more test that spawns shebang scripts. title: Make the behind= trailer and rebase rules agree across gstack docs (GST-2136)
body:
Agents now get one answer when gstack's install check says their copy is behind (run the fix it prints before the next workflow), and the unattended docs now say a branch whose base moved is merged, never rebased. That keeps crews on current gstack and keeps reviewed branches intact. ## What changed - **Behind trailer (C20).** Every place the install-trailer rule is written now says the same thing. `behind=1` or more means run the trailer's fix before the next workflow. Two things still hold the checkout where it is: a pin with a recorded reason (a `stale=h (pinned: )` note, or a `fix:` starting `unset GSTACK_CAPY_`, which is skipped while the reason is recorded), and an install that was refused (`upgrade skipped: … ()`). Files: capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md, capy/skill/gstack/lane-card.md, docs/capy-install.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, a comment in bin/gstack-capy-install, a test comment in test/capy-skill-wrapper.test.ts, and the UPGRADE_SKIPPED fix string in lib/result-codes-capy.ts. - **Merge, never rebase (C5).** docs/unattended.md now says a moved base is merged in, never rebased, and no longer names "the slot call" as a reason to rebase. The rule it points to is docs/ship-policy.md, section "Carrying a receipt across a base merge or a test-only fix" ("Merge main into a reviewed branch; never rebase it"), which crew/docs/captain.md L442 repeats. - A changelog fragment, changelog.d/fix-behind-trailer-and-rebase-docs.md. VERSION, package.json and CHANGELOG.md are untouched; the merge stamps them. ## Why The Capy skill said both "run the fix" and "`behind=` alone is informational" about the same trailer, so most lanes took the second reading and kept working on an old gstack. FOUN-35's audit found 113 of 150 follow-up trailers at the same or an older revision than the first one. The rebase wording was a second contradiction: docs/unattended.md let a slot call rebase a reviewed branch, while ship-policy.md says to merge. ## Blast radius Only prose changed, plus one comment, one test comment and one fix string. No runtime logic moved, so every install, upgrade and pin behaves as before. The pin case was checked against bin/gstack-capy-session L139-176 and L229-241 (file:line read): a reasoned pin still holds, because the docs now tell agents to skip the `unset GSTACK_CAPY_` fix while a reason is recorded. The Drive copy of the Capy skill does not update itself, so the owner recopies it after merge. ## Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues remain. The one blocker (outside voice, openai/gpt-6.1-sol: following the new rule would unset a deliberate pin under 24 hours old) was fixed in 8e64a8a. A scoped fix-check the Captain granted past the round cap reviewed that fix and found nothing blocking. Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 1 read). Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol at 0e737b3 found 1 blocker, now fixed and fix-checked at 8e64a8a. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - Low `bin/gstack-capy-session:244` The stale message still says "run the fix before the first workflow", while the docs now say "next workflow". Tests at test/capy-skill-wrapper.test.ts:797 and :1226 pin the string. - Low `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md` step 2 The "behind=1 or more" rule does not say it applies only to `gstack: ok for=` trailers, not `for=none` ones. - Low `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md` step 2 The rule does not say whether the fix runs once per session or once per workflow. - Low `docs/unattended.md` The closing sentence names only a plan-named rebase and drops the `/modernize` disposition the bullet above it allows. - INFORMATIONAL `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md:13` The skip clause for a `fix:` starting `unset GSTACK_CAPY_` does not restate its condition (a recorded reason) as a check the agent runs; docs/capy-install.md:143 does. - INFORMATIONAL `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md:13` Step 2's reason list names GSTACK_PIN_REASON and gstack.pinReason, not `--revision` or `gstack.contributor`, which the wrapper also counts. - INFORMATIONAL `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md:13` The skip clause is not limited to ok trailers. A `fail revision` trailer with AUTO_UPGRADE=0 and a recorded reason would skip its only fix; this fails closed. - INFORMATIONAL `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md:13` Step 2 now says a thread older than a day reruns the check before its next workflow, dropping "once its last check is over 24h old". ## Test Coverage No changed executable paths, so there are no coverage gaps. ## Eval Results No paid evals ran. eval:select picked dependency-derived behaviors from a bin comment and a lib fix string, and that selection was over the $10 per-PR cap. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. title: Make autoplan's rec and all replies apply every recommended plan change (GST-2139)
body:
/autoplan now treats `rec` (and its alias `all`), the one-word default reply at the plan gate, as "take every recommendation", so recommended plan changes are applied instead of the plan being approved as first written. This keeps the plan you approve the same as the decisions gstack records.

## What changed
/autoplan's Phase 4 reply table now says what `gstack-gate parse` and `gstack-autoplan answer` actually do.

- **`rec` / `all`** are the one-word default and take every recommendation, recommended plan changes included. A chosen plan-changing option goes to B (a `d<n>`) or B2 (a `uc<n>`), so the change is applied and the affected phases rerun before the gate comes back. `as-is` stays "the plan as first written". Before, `all` went straight to A ("approve as written") while the gate had already recorded every plan-changing recommendation, and `rec` had no row at all.
- **An explicit override still changes the plan.** A chosen option marked `changes_plan: true`, or an override of an option with no flag, goes to B or B2. That is the same rule `answerGate` uses (`changes_plan ?? how === 'override'`), so `p1a d2b` no longer approves the plan and drops the owner's `d2b`.
- **Every `uc<n>`/`d<n>` option now sets `changes_plan`** in a hand-written gate.json, `true` when it changes the plan and `false` otherwise. Without the flag, `rec` could not tell a plan change from a keep.
- **`p1a` with a user challenge pending** approves nothing. The skill waits for the owner's own answer to the `uc<n>` and re-parses their whole reply.
- **The `p1` item** recommends `b` (take the recommended changes) when a recommended option changes the plan, otherwise `a`.
- No gate code changed. lib/gate-list.ts and lib/autoplan-gate.ts already behave the way the new table describes.

## Why
Garry's standing rule is that the recommended reply, which accepts every recommended plan change, is the one-word default, and `all` is never offered as the plan as first written. The old table broke that rule and let decisions.jsonl and the approved plan disagree.

## Summary
An owner who answered `all` at the /autoplan gate got the plan approved as first written, even though gstack had recorded each recommended plan change as accepted. Now `rec` and `all` route recommended plan changes through the affected-phase rerun, explicit overrides keep counting as plan changes, and a test checks the skill's reply table against what `gstack-gate parse` returns.

## Blast radius
Only autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl Phase 4 and its regenerated SKILL.md change, and the routing they describe matches `answerGate` in lib/autoplan-gate.ts:451, which was read and traced for every reply case (script-ran: test/gate-list.test.ts parses each reply through bin/gstack-gate). To stay under the generated-size pins without raising one, other Phase 4 lines were shortened (the owner-brief parenthetical, the A close note, the D wording, the Cross-Phase "none" text, a repeated "Eng still runs last", one repeated "carry forward" sentence and one Decision Audit Trail clause), and every autoplan size pin drops by 35 characters.

## Test Coverage
All new code paths have test coverage. test/gate-list.test.ts adds three cases that read the template's reply table and check it against `bin/gstack-gate parse`: `all`/`rec` with plan-changing recommendations (expects B and B2, never A), bare `p1a` with a pending `uc1` (expects no approval), and `p1a d1b` on options with no flag (expects B). On main (1b96d9f) the first two fail, and the override case fails on 1bc1b7a; all pass at this head.
Tests ran: test 1654 (files, carried from CI run 42655104573 at tree 3e93bd33e373)

## Pre-Landing Review
Pass 1 (full panel: batched specialists, Red Team) found two blocking issues in Phase 4, both fixed in f36c2b8: the skill never told a hand-written gate.json to set `changes_plan`, and the new table sent an override of an unflagged option to A. Pass 2 on the fix range and Step 11 (native adversarial and an outside voice, openai/gpt-6.1-sol) found nothing blocking.
Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)
Outside review: CLEAN (openai/gpt-6.1-sol via a host subagent).

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:423` Dropped 'Carry forward unchanged accepted requirements.' from the amendment paragraph; another line ('On a rerun, carry forward unchanged accepted requirements') may or may not cover amendments.
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:406` Hand-written re-presented gates have no carried/prior exclusion like answerGate, so a repeated applied decision could route rec back to B/B2; B2 has no cycle cap.
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:365` changes_plan on every uc/d option is prose only; validateGateList never checks it, so an unflagged plan-changing recommendation under rec still approves as written (answerGate agrees; tooling follow-up, freeze applies).
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:406` One rec reply can route to both B and B2; the skill does not say to rerun the union of affected phases with Eng once, last.
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:413` With rec as default, the 3-cycle cap's end state (approve, stop or escalate) is undefined.
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:404` Pending uc items take precedence over p1c/p1e, so the owner cannot reject or interrogate until every user challenge is answered (matches answerGate).
- INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:423` Size trim dropped reminders (Carry forward unchanged accepted requirements, Eng still runs last, draft-direction close note); meaning survives elsewhere.

## Exploratory QA
Smoke probes for a prose change: each new test case was run against the pre-fix template (fails) and the fixed one (passes), and `bin/gstack-gate parse` was driven for `all`, `rec`, `p1a` and `p1a d1b`. No browser surface.

## Eval Results
No eval selected: the change is skill prose checked by free tests and guards; no paid eval was run.

## Plan Completion
Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix exempt from plan review (R65), with failing-first tests.

**Status:** current — no documentation edits needed.

**Scope:** base 1b96d9f8..HEAD on `capy/make-autoplans-rec-and` plus staged changes (changelog fragment rename): `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` (gate reply table: `rec`/`all` take every recommendation, `as-is` keeps the plan, `p1` recommends `b` when a recommended option changes the plan, `changes_plan` on every `uc`/`d` option, bare `p1a` with a pending `uc` approves nothing), its generated `autoplan/SKILL.md`, `test/gate-list.test.ts`, the size allowlist, and the changelog fragment.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/unattended.md` — Current (already documents `rec` alias `all`, `as-is`, `p1b`, and the pending-`uc` rules)

**Coverage debt:** the gate reply grammar has reference and how-to coverage in `docs/unattended.md`; `docs/skills.md` does not mention `rec`/`as-is` for interactive users (common gap, reference-only). **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Keep /autoplan working after a Claude Code 2.1.317 compaction
body:
/autoplan no longer gets stuck between phases after Claude Code 2.1.317 compacts a long session. This keeps the planning workflow usable on the current Claude Code release.

## What changed

![The three 2.1.317 compaction tests fail on main (119ed92) and pass on this branch; the hold cases pass on both](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/CqSCzEpP8NwE6eaNGYfhxTzB6TnjGX4wgxY9RpG9Kbk.png)

The three 2.1.317 compaction tests fail on main (119ed92) and pass on this branch, and the hold cases pass on both. The before counts cover the preserved-segment file only (20 tests). The after counts also include the 2.1.293 copies file (31 tests).

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The three 2.1.317 compaction tests fail on main (119ed92) and pass on this branch; the hold cases pass on both</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+(pass) records written after the boundary stay owned
+(pass) the next phase entry passes once the close packet is read in full after the compaction
+(pass) three such compactions in one session stay owned and the next phase entry passes
-(fail) records written after the boundary stay owned
-(fail) the next phase entry passes once the close packet is read in full after the compaction
-(fail) three such compactions in one session stay owned and the next phase entry passes
 (pass) a 2.1.300 tail that is the logical parent and not flushed yet still supplies no ownership
 (pass) a preserved list whose last entry is not the segment tail does not continue the boundary
 (pass) a preserved list naming no record of this file does not continue the boundary
@@ ⋯ 1 unchanged ⋯ @@
 (pass) a boundary with an absent logical parent and no compactMetadata still drops what follows
 (pass) a 2.1.300 boundary that cycles back but whose list omits its logical parent is still reported as an unrecognized shape
 (pass) a resumed fork that opens with such a boundary stays a genesis root
+ 31 pass
+ 0 fail
- 17 pass
- 3 fail
~~~

</details>

On 2.1.317, a compaction's boundary names a parent record (`logicalParentUuid`) that is never written to the session file. Its `compactMetadata.preservedMessages.uuids` list ends with the last record kept in place (`preservedSegment.tailUuid`). The journal reader in `lib/claude-journal-records.ts` required that tail to equal the logical parent, so it ignored the list. The boundary became an orphan and every record after the compaction was dropped without a word. The guard then judged each phase entry against stale history and refused it on every retry. The fixture shows `close_incomplete`, and the reporter's real session showed `cross_phase_batch`.

- `preservedUuids` now reads a list of native uuids whose last entry is `preservedSegment.tailUuid`. It no longer requires that tail to be the logical parent.
- `ownedCausalOrder` continues such a boundary from the last listed record that belongs to this file and does not descend from the boundary. It does this only when the logical parent is missing from the file and the boundary is not the file's first record.
- `docs/autoplan-guard-troubleshooting.md` now says the guard reads the preserved segments of both 2.1.300 and 2.1.317. This came from /ship's documentation audit.

## Why

"/autoplan gets stuck after compaction on Claude Code 2.1.317" (@vilano93, #4200). After a long session compacted, every later phase entry was refused, and retrying didn't help. Now the reader picks up from the record the compaction kept, so phase entries pass as they did on 2.1.300.

## Blast radius

The change only touches the owned journal reader behind the /autoplan publication guard (`lib/claude-journal-records.ts`, read through `lib/claude-owned-journal.ts`). The 2.1.300 path is unchanged: when the list's tail is the logical parent, the boundary still continues only if it cycles back through itself. The anchor search now scans the whole list, but in that case the tail descends from the boundary and is excluded, so it picks the same record as before (file:line read, and the hold tests ran). The new branch fires only for lists that main used to reject. Hold tests pin today's outcome for an unflushed 2.1.300 tail, a list whose last entry is not the tail, a list naming no record of this file, a subagent tail, a boundary with no `compactMetadata`, a 2.1.300 cycle whose list omits its logical parent, and a resumed fork that opens with such a boundary. The change adds no network calls, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies.

Known limit, kept from #4200: a logical parent that is missing but only late, and not the list's tail, is treated as never written until it lands. When it lands, the boundary reattaches to it.

## Summary

People on Claude Code 2.1.317 hit a stuck /autoplan after any compaction. This PR fixes the journal reader so it follows the 2.1.317 compaction layout. It also updates one sentence in the troubleshooting guide to match. The fix is a rewrite on current main of @vilano93's report and fix in #4200, with credit.

## Test Coverage

Every new code path has test coverage. The one changed runtime file has a changed test that names it (deterministic coverage audit; no audit reader).

title: Pregate skips test files the vitest or jest config excludes (GST-2146)
body:
Pregate's lanes check no longer fails on test files that the repo's own vitest or jest config leaves out. Before this change, a selected file in a directory the config excludes was handed to `npx vitest run`, which exits 1 on "No test files found". The lane reported `fail` and /ship could not get a receipt. In alphaclaw#386, 51 `tests/live` and `tests/container` files hit this. Those directories run only when `OPENCLAW_LIVE_E2E=1` is set. When such a file sat beside other files, vitest skipped it silently and the lane counted it as run. **What changes** - Before the local lane runs a `vitest run` or jest group, it asks the runner which of the selected files its config would run in the lane's environment (`vitest list --filesOnly --json=`, `jest --listTests --json`). The runner evaluates its own config, so env-gated and spread-built `include`/`exclude` (or `testMatch`/`testPathIgnorePatterns`) resolve the same way they would in a real run. vitest's file-only listing does not import test files or run `globalSetup`. - Each file the runner does not list goes on a `not applicable:` line with the reason. It is not run, it is not counted as covered, and it never fails the lane. If every file is left out, the lane passes, or stays `requires-remote` when it has obligations, with the detail "no selected file runs under the runner's config here". This follows the precedent of files a declared runner can't run. - Fallback: if a vitest run still exits non-zero with no test summary on its own "No test files found", and every file it was given exists, the run is read as not applicable. The reason quotes the include and exclude lines vitest printed. vitest matches file arguments as path substrings, so that message means the config excluded the files. Jest's "No tests found" stays a failure, because a regex argument can match nothing even when the config includes the file. A missing file still fails. A real failure in any other run of the lane still fails it (hold test). - Jest is listed with `jest --listTests --json` and no file arguments, and the selection is checked against the full list. jest reads a file argument as a regex, or as a path under `--runTestsByPath`, so passing the files would get either an `app/[id]/` path or an escaped path wrong. Runner names match as whole command words, so `bun test --preload ./jest.setup.ts` gets no jest probe. A package manager's preamble around jest's JSON (yarn classic) no longer hides the listing. - Nothing else changes. Other runners (bun, node --test, pytest, playwright, cargo, dart, dispatchers) behave as before, and so do the remote gate, CI carry and `--from-run`. If a listing fails, times out or prints nothing readable, every file runs as before. **Evidence** - Repro on main 119ed92 with real vitest 4.1.12, in a fixture whose config excludes `tests/live/**` unless `LIVE=1`: - A `tests/live`-only selection: `PREGATE: tests fail — lanes: local lane exited 1 (? failed of ? ran; 1 files; pipefail)`. - A mixed selection: `1 tests ran in 2 file(s)`. - With this branch: - The `tests/live`-only selection: `pass — no selected file runs under the runner's config here; 1 selected file(s) not applicable here (… \`vitest list --filesOnly\` does not list them in this environment): tests/live/a.test.js`. - The mixed selection: `1 tests ran in 1 file(s)`, with the live file named as not applicable. - With `LIVE=1`, the live file runs. - Real jest 30 with `testPathIgnorePatterns` gives the same result. With real jest 30, the listing names the ignored file under both `npx jest` and `npx jest --runTestsByPath`, with a `tests/unit/[id]/` file in the selection. - New tests (`test/pregate-runner-config.test.ts`, 8 tests): four of them fail on main's `lanes.ts`. The focused suite passes: `test/pregate-*.test.ts`, carry, ubicloud pregate, module-size ratchet, parity suite, spawnSync tripwire, bun isolation, changelog fragments and plain title, 551 pass and 0 fail. `bun run typecheck` and `typecheck:test` are clean.
Agent notes GST-2146, lane GSTA-451 under GStack Minder. This is a crew-blocker fix allowed under the tooling freeze. The new module `lib/pregate/runner-config.ts` is registered in the module-size ratchet, and `lanes.ts` is 704 lines. Docs: the `runner` row in docs/pregate.md. Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/pregate-skips-files-the-runner-config-excludes.md`. The hold test's `1 failed of 1 ran` count is new: on main the same case fails as `? ran`, because the excluded run's missing summary nulled the sum. The first /ship review (pass 1, at 08fa0f3) raised three below-floor findings: unescaped jest regex arguments, `jest` matched inside `./jest.setup.ts`, and a yarn preamble breaking `JSON.parse`. All three were fixed at 8b85ab6. Pass 2 found that escaping jest arguments broke `--runTestsByPath` runners (a zero-test pass). Under the Captain's grant a-d439bb5c3f9a, b9fb0d7 replaces the escaping with an argument-free jest listing, keeps jest's no-tests exit as a failure, and adds shim tests for both cases.

title: Stop the secret check from blocking on Django's self.client.session (#4209)
body:
Python and Dart projects can now run /ship on code like Django's `session = self.client.session` without the secret check stopping them, while real secrets still stop it. This serves gstack's promise that /ship runs end to end without someone hand-editing an allowlist. ## What changed ![env.kv now passes Django's self.client.session in Python source; the same value in a docstring or .env still reports](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/ZdVp1phcPIU7pa_gvBk8Cczd65vUM-KDI1y_h0UrZaY.png) env.kv now passes Django's self.client.session in Python source; the same value in a docstring or .env still reports.
Before/after as text: env.kv now passes Django's self.client.session in Python source; the same value in a docstring or .env still reports ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ scan at this branch (bba4d30) +tests/test_views.py Django test client read env.kv passes -$ scan at main (119ed92) -tests/test_views.py Django test client read env.kv REPORTS tests/conftest.py same line in a docstring env.kv REPORTS .env same value in .env env.kv REPORTS ~~~
In Python and Dart source, an unquoted dotted name chain that is the whole right-hand side of an `=` assignment (`self.client.session`, `request.auth`) now reads as an attribute, not a value. Everything else env.kv reports is unchanged. ## Why "/ship hard-stops on `session = self.client.session`" (#4209). env.kv matches any name ending in `session`, `token` or `key`, and `self.client.session` looks random enough to pass its entropy check. The secrets stage can't be downgraded, so the only way past it was a hand-edited allowlist on each machine, which an unattended agent rightly refuses to write. Now that line passes, and a quoted value, a random token, the same line inside a string and every .env or config file still stop the check. ## Blast radius The change adds one validator to env.kv (`isAttributeReference` in `lib/redact-patterns.ts`), so every caller of the redact engine sees it, but it only exempts a value when the scan has a `.py`, `.pyi` or `.dart` path. The pregate secrets check passes those files to the scanner whole, so the string check can see a `"""` opener (read at `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts` by the red-team reviewer, and proven by the pregate-level fixture in `test/pregate-secrets-source-context.test.ts`). Two review-side callers scan fragments with a `.py` path; see Review notes. ## Notes left on this PR - **docs/pregate.md needs one sentence (not edited here; that file is outside this lane).** The Allowlist section's env.kv bullet for Python and Dart (around line 1778) lists only the #3630 forms. The docs audit suggests adding, after "Python's keyword form … still reports": a plain `=` assignment whose whole right-hand side is an unquoted, name-shaped dotted chain (`session = self.client.session`) is an attribute read (#4209); anything after the value on the line except a comment, a random-looking segment, the line inside a string, and non-Python/Dart files still report. Its example `password=request.password` also now passes when it ends the line with no comma. - Review-side fragment scans (`lib/review-exclude.ts:102`, `lib/review-secret-excerpt.ts:76`) could drop `sourcePath` for `.py`/`.dart` the way `bin/gstack-redact-prepush` does; a follow-up, not a lost secret, because pregate scans whole files. - Python's keyword-argument form with a trailing comma (`password=request.password,`) still reports. Lifting it is a separate, wider change. - The pre-push hook scans added lines without a file path, so it may still warn (MEDIUM, non-blocking) on this line, as docs/pregate.md already says. Reported by @dgrant in #4209, who also suggested the shape of the fix. No code was carried over. ## Summary Django tests that grab the test client's session failed the secrets check nobody can downgrade (#4209). The fix teaches env.kv that, in Python and Dart source, a dotted chain of name-shaped segments alone on the right of `=` is an attribute read. Hold tests were written first (c6f6fcf, red on main for the Django cases only) and prove quoted literals, high-entropy tokens, env and config files, strings and trailing literals still report. One pinned case from #3419, `password = request.password`, was a labeled known false positive of the same shape, so it moved from must-fire to exempt; the keyword form `password=request.password,` still fires. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage (each changed runtime file has a changed test naming it). Tests ran: targeted 138 ## Pre-Landing Review No issues found.
