title: Stop the merge queue from landing a stacked PR's unreviewed parent commits (GST-2153)
body:
The merge queue now refuses to land a stacked pull request whose parent is still open, so a parent's commits can't reach main without their own review. This keeps gstack's promise that nothing merges without a /ship review of the exact change being landed.

## What changed

![A stacked child's receipt reviewed against its open parent: accepted on main, refused with QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH on this branch](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/x3IdkbSCp_o8NdrQdCtEwiblyq--F2Nl8sGJIRMVNf0.png)

A stacked child's receipt reviewed against its open parent: accepted on main, refused with QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH on this branch.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: A stacked child's receipt reviewed against its open parent: accepted on main, refused with QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH on this branch</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
-$ bindReceipt(child receipt base=parent, queue base=main)  # at main b51925e
-{"ok":true,"line":"SHIP_RECEIPT: pr=7 head=aaaaaaaaaaaa version=- base=parent"}
+$ bindReceipt(child receipt base=parent, queue base=main)  # this branch
+{"ok":false,"code":"QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH","message":"PR #7's ship receipt was reviewed against parent, not main, so it covers only the change since parent; land the parent (parent) first, merge main into this branch and push, then gstack-ship-receipt carry --pr 7 --base main moves the receipt to main"}
~~~

</details>

## Why

A child PR shipped against its parent branch has a review that covers only the child's own change. If someone pointed that child at main while the parent was still open, `ready` and `land --pin` accepted it, and the parent's commits landed with no review of their own. The new tests showed it on main at b51925e: `ready` exited 0 and `land --pin` merged the child. Now the queue refuses it and tells you to land the parent, merge main into the child and push, then carry the review over.

## Blast radius

`ready`, `land --pin` and train build all bind through `bindShippedReceipt`, which now passes the queue's base; a review written against main, including a stacked child reviewed against main, binds exactly as before, and a PR that already merged skips the check (read at lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:503, walked with 116 passing targeted tests). Callers that pass no base, the receipt tool's own terminal line and train verify, are unchanged.

## Summary

Stacked PRs could carry their parent's commits past the queue on the child's review. The queue now compares the base a review was written against with the base it is landing onto, and refuses a mismatch with a fix that tells you the next three steps. Along the way the review added a train build test, kept the older "base contains head" diagnostic ahead of the new check so its test still passes, made the base comparison work for any git remote name, and listed the new refusal in the land refusal tables in docs/ship-policy.md.

## Test Coverage

Step 7 audit (non-blocking): the core behavior is covered. `ready` and `land --pin` each have a test where a mismatched base refuses and a matching base proceeds, and train build now has one too (crew/test/ship-queue-train.test.ts, red without the fix, green with it). Remaining gaps, proposed as follow-up tests: the `refs/remotes/<remote>/` normalization, a merged resume skipping the check, the doctor anchor row for the new code, and a receipt that is both conditional and mismatched.

Coverage: 50% value-weighted at the audit (5 of 10 paths), before the train test was added.
Test value: 1 existing test extended (train build), 0 tests written by the audit.

Tests ran: targeted 116
Tests ran: free carried from CI at the pushed head (see Agent notes)

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 8 issues — 1 auto-fixed, 3 fixed under the owner's grant of one scoped fix-check, 0 deferred, 4 noted.

- Fixed: the train build path had no test for the new refusal (testing specialist).
- Fixed (Step 11 outside voice, GPT-6.1 Sol): an existing test in test/default-base.test.ts failed because the new check ran before the "base contains head" guard; the base comparison stripped only the `origin` remote; and the printed fix left out merging main into the child, so following it looped.
- The scoped fix-check after those fixes found nothing blocking.

Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol at medium (certified configuration), 3 blocking findings, all fixed and checked.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue-land.ts:347`: the refusal call sites print a generic "rerun /ship" NEXT for this code instead of land, merge, carry; the crew captain refusal table (crew/docs/captain.md) also has no row for it yet.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt.ts:112`: the check trusts the base field the receipt reports about itself; a hand-edited body could still claim main. Enforcing it needs the carry's patch-id comparison, a tooling change outside this fix.
- INFORMATIONAL `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-verify.ts:274`: train verify's pre-merge read passes no base; train land rechecks it.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt.ts:114`: the message assumes the other branch is a stack parent; a review written against an unrelated branch by mistake needs /ship against main instead.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt-depth.ts:503`: a receipt that is both paused on a red base and reviewed against a parent now reports the red-base pause first; it is still refused.

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke, 6 captures against `bindReceipt` with synthetic receipts (no network, no repo state), verdict pass: a main review binds under main; a parent review is refused with QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH; the train's `refs/remotes/origin/main` and `origin/main` forms bind; callers that pass no base bind as before; a non-origin remote ref was refused at the time of the probe (fail closed), and the later fix now normalizes it. Limits: the CLI paths are covered by the targeted lane and CI, not these captures; a merged resume was not probed.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR.

## Documentation
**Scope:** this audit covered the change from b51925e3 to b5d84115 (the new `QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH` refusal in `ready`, `land --pin` and train build). It reviewed `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `lib/result-codes-release.ts` and `lib/ship-receipt.ts`, plus `crew/docs/captain.md`, which was read-only.

**Result:** the docs are current. The ship-policy carry paragraph, the land refusal list and the land table row describe the new code and link to the new troubleshooting anchor, and they match the code's result-code entry and receipt-binding message. This audit made no edits.

**Debt:** the result-code table in `crew/docs/captain.md` has no `QUEUE_RECEIPT_BASE_MISMATCH` row. That file holds agent instructions, so the row needs a follow-up PR with its own review.

## Test plan
- [x] bun test test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts test/default-base.test.ts crew/test/ship-queue-train.test.ts: 116 tests ran, exit 0
- [x] bun run typecheck: clean
- [x] Free suite (bun run test): carried from CI at the pushed head

title: Accept a verbatim phase declaration and read numbered severity headings
body:
**Two /autoplan failures from one real run, both fixed here.** The publication guard refused a correctly published phase report, and the outside-review checker could not read Codex's severity labels.

## 1. `publication_missing` after a correct report

**Cause.** With Claude Code's thinking-display "updates" mode (`tengu_thinking_display_updates: true`, Claude Code 2.1.319), text written before a tool call is journaled only as a paraphrased `thinking` block, not the literal text. In one run the Phase 2 report began "**Phase 2 complete.**", but the journal held "...Two judgment calls go to the gate, and I'm passing to Phase 2.5 DX Review next." The declaration was gone, so `requirePublication()` found no report and refused DX entry twice, including a resend in the exact template. Phase 1 passed only because its paraphrase happened to start "Phase 1 is done:". #4155 handles a paraphrase that keeps the declaration mid-sentence; this is the case where it is dropped.

**Fix.** Bash commands are journaled verbatim, so the publication no-op may carry the declaration, quoted:

```
true autoplan-published design 'Phase 2 complete.'
```

- `autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts`: a declaring no-op after the close read counts as the report. It must name this phase and declare this phase, checked with `autoplanPhaseCompletions`, so negated, future-tense and other-phase declarations do not count.
- `lib/autoplan-stop-gate.ts`: `PUBLISHED` accepts the optional quoted declaration, and a declaring no-op satisfies the "report before it" check through the same parser.
- `phase-close.md.tmpl` step 6, the guard's reason text and the troubleshooting doc now show the declaring form.
- The bare no-op after a literal report still works.

## 2. `untagged_review` for completed Codex reviews

**Cause.** `lib/outside-review-result.ts` allowed one prefix before a severity label: a heading, a bullet or a number. Codex writes findings as `### 1. High` plus a title (a heading and a number), so no severity was read. Three completed reviews in the run came back `VERDICT: unverified, REASON: untagged_review`, and under the review gate the same shape classified as clean.

**Fix.** `LABEL_START`, the severity-word label pattern, `CODE_LABEL_BEFORE` and `NUMBERED_ITEM` allow an optional heading followed by an optional bullet or number. Re-running the checker on the run's three real outputs now gives P0, P1 and P1.

## Tests

- `test/autoplan-publication-mid-sentence.test.ts`: a paraphrase that dropped the declaration plus a declaring no-op is allowed (single and double quotes). Bare no-op, wrong phase, wrong phase name, negated, future-tense, `echo`-wrapped and chained commands stay `publication_missing`.
- `test/autoplan-stop-gate.test.ts`: the same cases through `checkRun`.
- `test/outside-review-severity.test.ts`: numbered headings with High, Critical, Medium and `[P1]`, plus a "high-level" prose negative control.
- `test/autoplan-publication-payload.test.ts`: the reason text expectation now includes the declaration.

|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bun test` on stop gate, guard reasons, skill gates, all `autoplan-publication-*`, all `outside-review-*`, gen-skill-docs (3 files) | 1183 pass, 6 skip, 0 fail |
| 2 | `bun run typecheck` | exit 0, 0 errors |

title: `ship-queue ready --fixes-base-red` can't name a test case that contains a comma or `>`, so the fixer's train reads as red on main
body:
## Summary

`gstack-ship-queue ready --fixes-base-red <cases>` can't declare a failing case whose name contains a comma. It can declare a case whose name contains `>`, `<`, `&` or a quote only if you type the name XML-escaped. The train compares the declared list with T0's red cases as an exact set. So in both situations T0 reads as red on main (`QUEUE_TRAIN_RED_ON_MAIN`), and the fix-forward path that base-red trains exist for is closed.

The `>` case covers most Vitest suites. Vitest's JUnit reporter names a test inside a `describe` block `suite > test` and writes `>` as `>`. So nearly every nested Vitest test is stored with `>` in its id.

Seen on gstack 1.98.0.0. The four files below are the same on `main` at e9de3a9d8be13422bb60190fee5b3a64ebc7f4b0.

## What happens

1. **The flag value is split on every comma.** `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-cli.ts:186` runs `fixes?.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)`. `flag()` (line 74) returns only the first occurrence, so you can't repeat the flag. There is no file form and no escape. A case named `totals > rounds 1,5 up to 2` becomes two entries: `totals > rounds 1` and `5 up to 2`.
2. **JUnit attribute values aren't decoded.** `parseTestRecord` (`crew/lib/ship-queue-train-gate.ts:149`) reads `classname` and `name` with a regex and joins them with `.`. It never decodes XML entities. A testcase `name="totals > sums line items"` is stored as `cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items`. Any name holding `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` or `'` is stored in its escaped form. JSON records aren't affected by this part.
3. **The comparison is an exact set.** `classifyPrefixes` (line 114) returns `red-on-main` unless slot 1's `fixes_base_red` equals T0's red list exactly (`sameSet`, line 100). A split entry or an unescaped `>` never matches.
4. **The output hides the split.** The READY line prints the list joined with `", "` (`crew/lib/ship-queue-train-ready.ts:300`). The train's `SLOT:` line joins it with `","` (`crew/lib/ship-queue-train.ts:473`). Both read back like the string that was typed, so a `--dry-run` looks right even when the list is wrong.

## Reproduction

This uses made-up test names and calls the two library functions the train uses. The CLI split is copied from `ship-queue-train-cli.ts:186`.

```ts
// repro.ts: bun run repro.ts
import { parseTestRecord, classifyPrefixes } from '<gstack checkout>/crew/lib/ship-queue-train-gate.ts';

const xml = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<testsuites><testsuite name="cart.test.ts" tests="3" failures="2">
<testcase classname="cart.test.ts" name="totals > rounds 1,5 up to 2"><failure message="expected 1 to be 2"/></testcase>
<testcase classname="cart.test.ts" name="totals > sums line items"><failure message="expected 3 to be 4"/></testcase>
<testcase classname="cart.test.ts" name="totals > empty cart is zero"/>
</testsuite></testsuites>`;
const rec = parseTestRecord([{ name: 'unit.xml', text: xml }])!;
console.log('T0 red cases:', JSON.stringify(rec.failed));

const cli = (v: string) => v.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean); // ship-queue-train-cli.ts:186
const verdict = (fixes: string[], red = rec.failed) =>
  classifyPrefixes([{ outcome: 'RED', red }, { outcome: 'GREEN', red: [] }], [{ pr: '12', fixes_base_red: fixes }]).kind;

const a = 'cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1,5 up to 2,cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items';
console.log('A typed as the runner shows it ->', JSON.stringify(cli(a)), '->', verdict(cli(a)));
const b = 'cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1,5 up to 2,cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items';
console.log('B typed with > ->', JSON.stringify(cli(b)), '->', verdict(cli(b)));
console.log('C the stored list itself ->', verdict(rec.failed));

const one = ['cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items'];
console.log('D one case, no comma, typed with > ->', verdict(cli('cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items'), one));
console.log('E one case, no comma, typed with > ->', verdict(cli('cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items'), one));
console.log('display:', cli(a).join(', '));
```

Output on 1.98.0.0:

```
T0 red cases: ["cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1,5 up to 2","cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items"]
A typed as the runner shows it -> ["cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1","5 up to 2","cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items"] -> red-on-main
B typed with > -> ["cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1","5 up to 2","cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items"] -> red-on-main
C the stored list itself -> green
D one case, no comma, typed with > -> red-on-main
E one case, no comma, typed with > -> green
display: cart.test.ts.totals > rounds 1, 5 up to 2, cart.test.ts.totals > sums line items
```

The CLI behaves the same way. `gstack-ship-queue ready --pr <n> --no-screen --fixes-base-red '<case A>,<case B>' --dry-run` exits 0 and prints a `FIXES_BASE_RED:` line that looks whole, and the train then reads T0 as red on main.

## Expected

A fixer can declare exactly the cases T0 is red on, under the names the test runner prints, whatever characters they contain. If a declared case can't match, `ready` says so before the train runs.

## Proposed fix

1. **Take the list without splitting on commas.** Make `--fixes-base-red <case>` repeatable and collect every occurrence. Add `--fixes-base-red-file <path>` with one case per line, or a JSON array. Keep the comma form for compatibility if needed, and document that it can't carry a comma.
2. **Decode XML entities in `parseTestRecord`.** Decode `< > & " '` and numeric references (`&#NN;`, `&#xNN;`) in `classname` and `name` before building the id. Records written by older versions still hold escaped ids, so `sameSet` could compare decoded forms on both sides.
3. **Check the list at READY time.** When the base's latest test record is readable, refuse a declared case that isn't in its red set, and name the closest stored ids. Print the cases one per line, quoted, with a count (`FIXES_BASE_RED: 2 cases`), so a split shows up in the dry run.
4. **Tests.** Add case names with a comma, with `>` and with `&`, for both the CLI parse and `parseTestRecord`.

## Workaround today

For a name with no comma, type it XML-escaped (`>` for `>`), as in E above. A name that contains a comma has no workaround: in our case the fixer had to land outside the train.

title: /ship: a review record fingerprints the tree when its row is logged, not when its readers return, so fixing things in the "wrong" order voids reviews and costs extra granted passes
body:
## Summary

We run /ship unattended on Capy (gstack 1.97 and 1.98). Over about ten PRs we kept paying for review passes that read nothing new: a second Step 11 voices pass, or another fix-check that the review cap turns into an owner's grant. Every case traces to how a review record binds to a tree:

- A pass's end is fingerprinted when its row is logged, not when its readers return.
- Step 11's records bind only to the exact current tree, and only a full voices rerun can re-bind them.
- An edit between the last fix-check and Step 11 can't be bound, and only `--post-review` planning says so.
- A PR bot's finding has no row, so its fix can't be bound either.

We now work around these with five local rules for our agents (listed near the end). Each rule tells the agent what order to do things in, and getting the order wrong costs a pass.

Code references are to `main` at e9de3a9d8be13422bb60190fee5b3a64ebc7f4b0. The cited files are unchanged from 1.98.0.0.

Related: #2803 (closed) added the start capture that made late edits visible. This issue is about the end side of that binding. #3857 (open) is about the review-loop exception's scope; one item in section 5 touches the same record.

## 1. A pass's end is fingerprinted at log time, not when its readers return

- `bin/gstack-review-log:72` computes `WTREE` with `gstack-wtree --review` when the logger runs, and exports it as `GSTACK_STAMP_WTREE` (line 87).
- `bindReview` (`lib/review-evidence.ts:266`) uses that as the pass's end (`const end = env.GSTACK_STAMP_WTREE`, line 305). If it differs from the start that `--start` captured, `review_binding.state` is `changed`.
- `reviewFreshness` then reports `STALE: content changed during review ... so the record cannot bind` (line 363). `docs/troubleshooting.md#review-content-changed` says logging the same results again can't repair it.
- Yet gstack already records what each reader read. `collect` (`lib/review-ledger.ts:355`) writes `tree`, `reported_tree` and `tree_ok` on every reader output in the dispatch ledger.

So an edit made after every reader has returned, but before the row is logged, is treated like an edit made while readers were reading. That includes an uncommitted edit, and one you later revert. Nothing warns at log time. What it costs depends on the pass:

- **A Step 9 pass:** the documented repair (log `converged:false` with the fix as `fixed`) keeps the cost to the normal fix-check.
- **A Step 11 voice:** the voice has to run again on a frozen tree.
- **A fix-check after the review cap:** it takes another fix-check, which needs the owner's grant.

**Repro**

1. Run /ship to a review pass. The pass program dispatches readers on tree T1, and they return. The ledger shows `tree_ok: true` at T1 for each reader.
2. Edit a file to fix one finding. Don't commit.
3. Log the pass row.
4. `gstack-review-read` shows `review_binding.state: "changed"` and `review_freshness: STALE content changed during review: the tree moved from T1 to T2`.

**Expected:** the row binds to T1, the tree every reader reported. The edit then routes as a post-pass fix, the same as when the row is logged first.

## 2. Step 11's records bind only to the exact current tree, and only a full voices pass can re-bind them

- `reviewFreshness` returns STALE whenever `rec.wtree !== currentWtree` (`lib/review-evidence.ts:370`). So any commit after the voices read voids their records, a test-only commit included.
- `fixRangeBase` refuses a narrowed (fix-range) re-read once a Step 11 row follows the latest pass, with the message "a Step 11 review followed the latest pass" (`lib/review-evidence.ts:187`).

PR review bots often comment after the push that Step 11 read. Answering one of those comments with a one-line test fix then costs a second full voices pass. This happened to us on two PRs.

**Expected:** a commit after Step 11 is re-read at the size of its own diff (a fix-range read, or a fix-check over the new commits), not by rerunning every voice over the whole diff.

## 3. An edit between the last fix-check and Step 11 can't be bound, and only `--post-review` planning says so

**Sequence**

1. A fix-check is logged clean on tree A.
2. At Step 10, a bot comment is fixed with a test-only commit, giving tree B.
3. In-loop planning (`gstack-review-plan ... --last fix-check`) answers `NEXT: done` for that edit.
4. Step 11's voices read B, and their rows are logged on B.
5. Step 11.5 can't bind, because the last Step 9 record is on A. Finish's post-review plan (`gstack-review-plan --post-review`) stops for the owner's grant of another fix-check. That follows `lib/review-depth.ts:405`: "Edits after the review bound (`postReview`) that follow a fix-check are a new stop".

For the same history, the two planner modes give different answers. So the agent learns it needs a grant only after it has paid for the voices. The voices did read B, so B's change was reviewed. The record just has no way to count it.

**Expected,** either of:

- In-loop planning gives the same answer as `--post-review` (stop for a grant) as soon as an edit lands after the last fix-check, so the ask comes before Step 11.
- Or Step 11.5 accepts Step 11 records on the current tree as covering a below-floor change since the last fix-check.

## 4. A PR bot's finding has no row, so its fix can't be bound

- A fix commit can carry a `Review-Finding: <id> reader=<role>` trailer. When the finding came from a PR bot, the trailer names nothing in the run's rows or ledgers, and `summarizeReviewLoop` reports it as `unbound` (`lib/review-scope.ts:477`). There is no row type for an outside reviewer's finding, so the fix counts as an edit after the review bound (see section 3).
- `parseFixTrailers` silently drops a trailer without `reader=` (`lib/review-scope.ts:378`). The blocker it fixed then shows as `unrecorded` on the receipt, with no warning at commit time or at `summary`.

**Expected:** a way to log a bot's finding and what was done about it as a row (for example a `review-external` row with the bot as the reader), so its trailer binds and the fix counts inside the loop. Also a warning for a `Review-Finding:` trailer that doesn't parse.

## 5. Smaller items in the same area

- **The pass folder's name decides the pass kind.** `ledgerPass` (`lib/review-scope.ts:368`) treats a ledger as a fix-check only if a `fix-check` reader output holds findings or a clean marker. Otherwise a folder named `pN` makes it full pass N, and a pass N with no review row is listed as `unbound`. On 1.97, a clean fix-check run into `p3` showed `unbound=1` on the receipt. On current `main` this looks limited to a fix-check reply with neither findings nor a clean marker, but we haven't retested it there. Taking the kind from the dispatch step, not the folder name, would close it.
- **The review-loop exception and a removed test line.** After a fix-check chain was cut short at the cap, finish's `--review-loop-exception` didn't accept a test file whose only change was one removed line, so a second grant was needed. We saw this but didn't trace the routing. #3857 covers the same exception's scope from the other direction.
- **The reading meter counts waiting time.** The pass program measures a pass's reading as the driving thread's meter, from its first dispatch to its collection. A pass left uncollected while the agent waits for the owner counts the wait as review reading. On one PR, the measured reading came to about 40% more than the readers' own costs. Summing the readers' own costs, or closing the window when the last reader settles, would fix it. This item has a different cause from sections 1 to 4, and we can split it out.

## The local rules these force

1. Log each pass's row before you commit its fixes, and name a fix-check's output folder `fc`, never `pN`.
2. Settle and commit every bot comment before Step 11's voices read the tree.
3. Commit every bot fix before the fix-check runs too, and run the post-review plan before Step 11.
4. Collect a pass before you stop to wait for the owner's word. When a chain was cut short at a cap, ask in one go for everything the finish will need.
5. Log a fix-check's row before you fix its finding.

The tool could enforce each of these by refusing or warning at the step where the order goes wrong. Better, it could make the order not matter: bind to what the readers reported (section 1), and let smaller re-reads re-bind (sections 2 and 3).

## Proposed fix

1. **Bind at read time.** When a pass has a dispatch ledger, take its end fingerprint from the ledger: the tree that every reader output reported with `tree_ok: true`, or a `collected_wtree` the dispatcher stamps when the last reader settles. Keep `changed` for an edit that landed while a reader was still reading. Any later edit is then an ordinary post-pass fix.
2. **Warn at log time.** If the working tree differs from the pass's start tree when `gstack-review-log` runs, say so and offer the bind-to-ledger path, instead of quietly writing a row that can't be repaired.
3. **Re-bind after Step 11 at the size of the change.** Allow a fix-range read, or a fix-check over the commits after Step 11, instead of only a full voices rerun.
4. **One answer from the planner.** For the same history, in-loop and `--post-review` planning agree, or in-loop planning prints at Step 10 that this edit will need a grant at finish.
5. **Rows for outside findings,** plus a warning for a `Review-Finding:` trailer that doesn't parse.
6. **The smaller items** in section 5: take the pass kind from the dispatch step, and measure reading cost from the readers.

title: Stop the merge queue from calling a head green while a check on it failed (GST-2167)
body:
The merge queue no longer calls a pull request's CI green while one of its checks actually failed. This serves the goal of only ever merging work whose tests passed.

## What changed
The queue's CI read, on three real heads where verdicts changed (from a live probe over 65 recent heads):

<details><summary>Before and after, as text</summary>

Before (main):
```
ci: green at fa756304dfe8 (passed=34 failed=0 pending=0 skipped=17)
ci: red at e9de3a9d8be1 (passed=9 failed=1 pending=0 skipped=0)
ci: none at 1cc98fc92ecb (passed=0 failed=0 pending=0 skipped=0)
```
After (this branch):
```
ci: red at fa756304dfe8 (passed=34 failed=1 pending=0 skipped=17)
ci: red at e9de3a9d8be1 (passed=9 failed=6 pending=0 skipped=0)
ci: red at 1cc98fc92ecb (passed=0 failed=7 pending=0 skipped=0)
```
</details>

## Why
gstack-evals#303 went READY at `6b30aae` with `passed=1 failed=0` while its `checks` job had failed. The queue now sees failed runs that GitHub's default list hides, so a head like that stays red and `land` refuses it.

## Blast radius
`ready`, `land`, train land, wave and the post-merge watch all read CI through `ciAtHead` in `lib/ship-queue.ts`, so they all change together and nothing else does. A live probe ran the old and new read over 65 real heads, and only three verdicts changed, each to a correct red (script ran).

## Summary
GitHub's check-runs list shows only each workflow run's newest attempt by default. On #303 the `ci` run was rerun, the second attempt created no jobs, and the failed `checks` run from the first attempt dropped out of the list. The read now asks for every attempt, judges each check suite by its latest attempt that ran jobs, and keeps the newest run per check name as before.

A workflow run that ends before starting any job has no check run at all. The read now also lists the head's workflow runs. A failed run with no jobs counts as a failed check named `<workflow> (run <id>, no jobs)` unless a later run of the same workflow replaced it. A run cancelled before any job isn't counted. An unreadable list makes the result unknown, never green. docs/ship-policy.md now describes this.

## Test Coverage
New ready cases use the #303 shape and its cancelled, timed_out and action_required versions. They also cover a jobless failure with and without a later run, a run cancelled before any job, a stale matrix job, an empty failed rerun and an unreadable runs list. Hold cases check that a green head, a pending check, a skipped check and a rerun that later passed read as before. A land case shows `land --pin` merged the #303 shape before this change and now refuses with QUEUE_LAND_CHECKS.
Regression proof: the #303 fixture read green and merged on main b51925e. The stale-matrix fixture read `ci: red at 1d506e90fa40 (passed=2 failed=1 …)` and the empty-failed-rerun fixture read `ci: green at e208720cb0a6 (passed=2 failed=0 …)` on 7036ee1. All pass after the fix.
Tests: 218 pass, 0 fail across 9 focused files.
Tests ran: tests 1655

## Pre-Landing Review
Round 1 found one blocking defect (a run cancelled before any job read as failed), which was fixed with its test. Round 2 and the Step 11 voices found nothing blocking. One granted fix-check found nothing. After review, one scoped reader checked the docs/ship-policy.md edit and found it clean.
REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=1 deferred=0 noted=3 fixed=3 scope=frozen unbound=3 fix_checks=1 dispatches=8
Gate edits: UNAVAILABLE — this run's record did not keep Step 9's line.
Outside review: GPT-6.1 Sol outside voice completed; its notes are listed below.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue.ts:167` No test pins that a completed-cancelled jobless rerun does not replace an earlier jobless failure.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue.ts:169` A workflow run not finished and with no jobs yet adds nothing to the verdict (neither pending nor failed); same as main before this PR.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue.ts:158` A run cancelled before any job at the judged PR head is dropped rather than read as not-run; main before this PR also never saw it.
- INFORMATIONAL A jobless skipped or neutral run can act as a replacement.
- INFORMATIONAL Replacement is ordered by created_at, which a rerun keeps.
- INFORMATIONAL New unknown paths: Actions read scope, the 1000-run cap, and a third strict list.
- INFORMATIONAL Three paged API calls per poll instead of two.

## Exploratory QA
Not run: no user-facing surface. The live probe over 65 real heads stands in for it.

## Design Review
No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results
No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Review bot comments
No review bot comments.

## Issues
Refs v1/outside-voice#1
Refs v1/outside-voice#2

## Verification Results
Not run: no Step 8.1 obligations were declared for this bug fix.

## TODOS
No TODO items completed in this PR.

## Documentation
Scope: repair re-audit (attempt 2) of attempt 1's blocker, the ci: counting paragraph in docs/ship-policy.md, checked against lib/ship-queue.ts ciAtHead at a6a32e3.

Result: updated. The paragraph now says ci: reads every attempt of each check suite, judges a suite by its latest attempt that has jobs (earlier attempts only when the latest has none), and keeps the newest run per check name with the existing tie-break, two-apps and commit-status rules. A workflow run that failed with no jobs counts as a failed check `<workflow> (run <id>, no jobs)` unless a later run of the same workflow replaced it, a run cancelled before any job is not counted, and an unreadable list is unknown, never green.

Debt: none known from this edit. The unreadable-list wording was taken from the brief and not traced in code this round.

## Test plan
- [x] bun run test: CI free-tests run 42707259055 passed (1655 test files) at 718218b

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- Repro on origin/main b51925e: ready printed `ci: green at … (passed=1 failed=0 pending=0 skipped=0)` for the #303 fixture, and land exited 0 (merged).
- Live read with the fix: gstack-evals#303 at 6b30aae is `red (passed=1 failed=2)`: `checks=failure` and `sealed (run 42671854799, no jobs)=failure`.
- Live probe over 65 heads: fa756304 (#4220, Plain title startup_failure after a pass), e9de3a9d and 1cc98fc9 (jobless failures) changed; all three are correct reds.
- train-ops ran in CI only.
- Open review notes (below the floor): p2/specialist#1, p2/red-team#1, p2/red-team#2, v1/adversarial-native#2 to #5, as listed under Review notes.
- Follow-up (Captain): `gstack-pr-wait` (`parseHeadChecks` in lib/gh-poll.ts via `fetchChecks` in lib/pr-wait-github.ts) and `ci-gate` (`gh pr checks`) still read only each workflow run's latest attempt, the same blind spot `ciAtHead` had.
- The main merge after #4229 landed (c8679c9) was granted by the Captain after the fact; the #4229 trial merge was clean (typecheck plus 108 tests passing).
- Fix-check grant a-b66db3338a66 (scope 'review_loop_grant 7036ee1 on #4235'); the fix-check returned no findings.
- Scoped reader after review: SCOPED_REVIEW: clean by anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (docs/ship-policy.md)
- Lane: GSTA-459.

## Approvals

Approved: yes (record r-5a351186a754). The full approval record stays private.
Plan: exempt: bug fix
Plan check: exempt bug fix

title: Keep a numbered review finding's closing paragraph on that finding after a nested list (GST-2174)
body:
/ship's review gate no longer blocks a merge on a Low finding just because the native reviewer wrote it as a numbered item with a nested list and a closing paragraph. This serves gstack's goal of a review loop that stops only on real blockers.

## What changed

![Before: the closing paragraph split off and the Low finding blocked /ship as CRITICAL. After: one Low record, no blocker.](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/0FvWK7U6V8rwqTtjV-3E1sAZdr73Cp6Q6zrrWE0vXfU.png)

Before: the closing paragraph split off and the Low finding blocked /ship as CRITICAL. After: one Low record, no blocker.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Before: the closing paragraph split off and the Low finding blocked /ship as CRITICAL. After: one Low record, no blocker.</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 $ collect adversarial-native reply (numbered FIXABLE item, nested list, closing "Severity: Low. Blocks: no.")
+records: 1
+  Low          1. **FIXABLE. The retry queue drops a job on shutdown** (`queue.ts`). 
-records: 2
-  CRITICAL  <- blocks /ship  1. **FIXABLE. The retry queue drops a job on shutdown** (`queue.ts`). 
-  Low          So a job queued in the last second is lost, which is rare. Severity: L
 
~~~

</details>

## Why

An alphaclaw /ship run stopped on a finding its own reviewer rated "Severity: Low. Blocks: no." The reviewer wrote six findings and the gate collected nine, because the closing paragraph of each numbered item split off into its own record and left the item's FIXABLE label to count as CRITICAL. Now that paragraph stays on its finding, so a Low FIXABLE collects at Low and /ship keeps going.

## Blast radius

Only `parseLabelled` in lib/review-ledger.ts changed, and every reviewer's output goes through it. The new join runs only for the native reviewer's numbered items with no fields of their own and stops after the first closing paragraph, so other readers' output parses exactly as on main. The 22 test files that import the ledger pass (216 tests in the 14-file collector lane, run at 3159fbe and again at the final tree), and the new test fails on the previous head.

## Summary

The native reviewer often writes a finding as `1. **FIXABLE. …**`, a short sub-list, then a closing paragraph that holds `Severity` and `Blocks`. The collector treated that paragraph as a new finding, so the item kept no fields and its FIXABLE label made it a blocker. The collector now keeps the indented lines and the first closing paragraph on the numbered item, so the paragraph's fields bind to it.

The first review round found three ways the first version of that join could hide a real blocker. It took in a separate bold-led finding, it kept absorbing later paragraphs, and it applied to every reader and could lower an item that names CRITICAL. The join is now narrow. It applies only to the native reviewer, ends after the first closing paragraph, never takes in a bold-led paragraph or a verdict line, and never lowers an item that names CRITICAL or P0. A new test covers each case.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage (deterministic coverage audit: the one changed runtime file has a changed test naming it).
Regression proof: test/review-native-nested-list.test.ts fails at main f75ce6f (2 of 2), and its third test fails at 1109bf5, the head before the review fixes. All three pass now.
Tests ran: collector 216

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 9 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 3 asked (3 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 6 noted

Round 1 (full panel: batched testing/security/state-machines specialist and Red Team) found three blockers in the join, all fixed in 3159fbe:
- a bold-led margin paragraph that starts a separate finding was absorbed, so its `Severity: Low` and `Blocks: no` lowered the FIXABLE blocker;
- the join applied to every reader and could lower an item that names CRITICAL to an absorbed paragraph's Severity;
- the join kept absorbing later paragraphs until a field came, so a separate finding's fields bound to the item.

Round 2 (the same panel on the fix range) found no blocker. The Step 11 voices (native adversarial reviewer, outside voice on openai/gpt-6.1-sol and the targeted money-path reader) ran on the final code tree.

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=8 deferred=0 noted=9 fixed=3 scope=frozen ledgers_read=4 dispatches=8

Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

Outside review: completed (host subagent, openai/gpt-6.1-sol), 1 finding, listed under Review notes. Targeted reader: NO FINDINGS.

## Review notes

These are open notes, shipped after the two-round cap. None would fail a test, break production or lose data; the first two can make the gate block on a finding that is not real (it fails closed), and none can hide a real blocker.

- `lib/review-ledger.ts:281` (outside voice, native reviewer): an indented paragraph after the nested list uses up the one allowed join, so fields in a later margin paragraph split off and the item collects a false CRITICAL. The suggested fix (`afterGap && !indented`) reopens round 1's fail-open case and fails test/review-native-nested-list.test.ts, so it was not taken.
- `lib/review-ledger.ts:278` (native reviewer): a closing section of two margin paragraphs before own-line fields splits again, as it did before 1109bf5. Picking the better default needs a replay of real native outputs.
- `lib/review-ledger.ts:183` (native reviewer, round 2 Red Team): the comment says an item naming CRITICAL is never lowered, but `Severity` and `Blocks` on their own lines still lower it through the existing field-line path and ruling A's relaxed pass. That behaviour is unchanged since main; only inline fields in the joined paragraph are pinned.
- `lib/review-ledger.ts:279` (round 2 Red Team): the verdict-line exclusion also applies to indented lines, so an indented verdict inside an item splits off and takes the item's later field lines (a false CRITICAL, fail-closed).
- `lib/review-ledger.ts:301` (native reviewer): non-native readers no longer get the join, by design after round 1; their output parses as on main.
- Collector artifacts: three reviewer prose paragraphs (round 2 Red Team scope note, native scope and closing notes) were collected as CRITICAL records; they state no defect.
- Round 1 Red Team limit: one plain paragraph right after the nested list that carries its own `Severity` and `Blocks: no` still binds to the item; no parser rule can tell it from the intended shape.

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke, 3 probes on `parseFindings` against synthetic reviewer replies (verdict: pass):
- the intended case (numbered FIXABLE, nested list, closing `Severity: Low. Blocks: no.`) collects one Low record: pass;
- a second paragraph after the closing one stays its own finding and the FIXABLE stays CRITICAL: pass;
- a specialist's numbered item naming CRITICAL is never joined to a later Low paragraph: pass.
Limit: collect and ledgerBlockers are covered by the unit test, not by a QA capture.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Review bot comments

No review bot comments.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: CLEAN

## Plan Completion

Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). Fix: add "Plan: <path>" to the PR body, or run /autoplan.

## Verification Results

No plan obligations: 0 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED, 0 NOT RUN.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR.

## Documentation
**Status:** updated. One factual edit to docs/review-policy.md, no blockers.

Scope: base f75ce6fd to head 3159fbec on capy/keep-a-numbered-review. Audited lib/review-ledger.ts, test/review-native-nested-list.test.ts and the new changelog.d/capy-keep-a-numbered-review.md fragment. Nothing was staged or unstaged.

Documentation health:
- docs/review-policy.md: Updated. It now says the native reviewer's numbered item with a nested list keeps its first closing paragraph, so that paragraph's Severity and Blocks bind to the item (ALPH-93).
- docs/troubleshooting.md: Current. Its 'Numbered findings' section is about verdict counting, not the collector.
- changelog.d/capy-keep-a-numbered-review.md: Current (reviewed only).

Coverage debt: none. The collector rule is internal and has reference coverage in docs/review-policy.md. Diagram drift: none.
## Test plan

title: design: Gemini default image model returns image/jpeg, every generate fails ("not a PNG")
body:
## Summary

With the Gemini provider, `$D setup` (and any image command) fails after a successful, billed generation:

```
Smoke test FAILED: Gemini returned image/jpeg, not a PNG; nothing was saved.
Check your Gemini key and its quota in Google AI Studio.
```

The default image model `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` (`GEMINI_DEFAULT_MODELS.image` in `design/src/models.ts`) answers with `inlineData.mimeType: "image/jpeg"`. `readImage()` in `design/src/provider.ts:127` rejects anything but `image/png`:

```ts
if (mime !== "image/png") throw new DesignImageError(`Gemini returned ${mime}, not a PNG; nothing was saved.`, false);
```

The request in `imageRequest()` (`provider.ts:70-73`) sets only `responseModalities` and `imageConfig.aspectRatio`, so nothing asks Gemini for PNG output. The result: the Gemini path cannot produce an image with the default model, and each attempt is still billed.

## Environment

- gstack 1.98.0.0 (checkout 350d4196c344; `main` at f75ce6fdcc14 has the same `provider.ts` check)
- macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), global git install
- Gemini key from Google AI Studio, billing enabled on the project
- No OpenAI key configured; no `GSTACK_DESIGN_*` overrides set

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save a Gemini key to `~/.gstack/gemini.json` (billing enabled).
2. Run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/design/dist/design setup`.
3. Smoke test fails with the error above.

## Expected

The smoke test passes and the image is saved as PNG.

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. Accept `image/jpeg` (and `image/webp`) and convert to PNG before saving, e.g. with `sips -s format png` on macOS, or a small decoder/encoder in Bun.
2. Ask Gemini for PNG in the request, if the model supports an output MIME option in `imageConfig`.
3. Save the native format and report the real extension in the output JSON (larger contract change, since callers read `*.png`).

## Smaller related papercut

After this failure, the generic hint "Check your Gemini key and its quota in Google AI Studio." is printed (`design/src/cli.ts:155-157`). It's misleading here: the key and quota were fine. It could be printed only for auth/quota failures.

title: design setup: rejects new-format Gemini API keys ("AQ…"), only accepts "AIza…"
body:
## Summary

Google AI Studio now issues Gemini API keys that start with `AQ`. `$D setup --provider gemini` rejects them:

```
Invalid key. A Gemini key starts with 'AIza'.
```

The check is in `design/src/cli.ts`:

```ts
const KEY_PREFIX: Record<ProviderName, string> = { openai: "sk-", gemini: "AIza" };   // line 95
...
if (!key || !key.startsWith(KEY_PREFIX[provider])) {                                    // line 136
```

The key itself is valid. Writing it straight to `~/.gstack/gemini.json` (`{"api_key": "AQ…"}`), which `auth.ts` loads without a prefix check, lets Google accept it: requests go through and are billed.

Provider auto-detection has the same assumption (`cli.ts:135`): with no `--provider`, an `AQ…` key is classified as OpenAI and rejected for not starting with `sk-`.

## Environment

- gstack 1.98.0.0 (checkout 350d4196c344; same code on `main` at f75ce6fdcc14)
- macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new key at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey (it starts with `AQ`).
2. Run `$D setup --provider gemini` and paste it.

## Expected

The key is saved and the smoke test runs.

## Suggested fix

Accept both prefixes for Gemini (`AIza` and `AQ`), or drop the hard prefix check when `--provider` is given and let the smoke test validate the key. For auto-detection, treat `AIza…`/`AQ…` as Gemini.

The setup prompt and `auth.ts` comments that say Gemini keys look like `AIza…` would need the same update.

title: Keep crew threads on their PR to the end and cap finished PRs at 10 before new fix threads (GST-2192)
body:
Agent threads that work on a pull request now keep it until it merges or closes, and no new fix thread starts in a repo while more than 10 finished pull requests wait there to merge. This is a wording change to gstack's own rules pages; no tool changes.

## What changed
- **factory.md** (read by every gstack session on Capy): point 12 drops "past 500M tokens, rotate" for every thread. A thread keeps its PR until it merges or closes and hands off only then, never mid-PR on a token count, and checks in with its Captain once past 1B own tokens. Standing threads that wake on every event (merge lanes, watchers) still rotate at 500M tokens or 3 days. New point 14: no new fix thread in a repo while more than 10 finished PRs (green, reviewed, waiting only to merge) sit in its queue; severe hotfixes (security, data loss, red main, a broken install) are exempt. Its byte budget in `test/capy-skill-wrapper.test.ts` rises from 3,650 to 4,200 for these two rules, with the reason recorded beside it as for earlier rule additions.
- **crew/docs/captain.md**: a "Keep the PR to the end" bullet under Lane context and a "Finish before starting" paragraph under New threads join the crew.
- **lane-card.md**: the same keep-the-PR line for lanes.
- **/runaway-stopper** (template and generated SKILL.md): the limits now apply rotation to standing threads only; a ROTATE or own-tokens WARN on a crew thread holding a PR needs no action; Step 3 rotates standing threads only; Step 4 gains the keep-the-PR brief line. Subagent limits (look past 100M, never reuse one across PRs) are unchanged.
- **README.md, docs/skills.md**: the /runaway-stopper summaries say the same.

## Why
Per-thread token stops forced handoffs in the middle of a PR. One PR went through four threads in eight hours and is still a draft. Every handoff wakes the Captain, whose tokens cost about 1.7 times a crew thread's, and handoffs are where orphaned PRs came from. The cap on finished PRs keeps them from piling up behind new fix threads.

## Blast radius
Prose only. `gstack-runaway scan` (lib/runaway.ts) still flags every non-Captain thread past 500M as ROTATE and warns at 400M. The skill now tells the reader how to act on that for a crew thread, and the tool is untouched under the tooling freeze.

title: Stop gstack-uninstall deleting a repo's committed .gstack files and unsaved worktrees (GST-2197)
body:
Running `gstack-uninstall` from inside a repo deleted the repo's whole `.gstack/` folder and every `.gstack-worktrees/` checkout, even with `--keep-state`. Since ship policy landed, `.gstack/` holds committed files (`ship-policy.json`, `pregate.json` and others), so an uninstall-and-reinstall repair left `git status` showing them deleted, and a worktree's uncommitted work was gone for good. This PR makes uninstall safe for users' data. It fixes GSTA-461 audit item 9.

## What changed

- `--keep-state` now keeps the repo's `.gstack/` and every `.gstack-worktrees/` entry.
- Without `--keep-state`, uninstall never deletes git-tracked files under `.gstack/`. When the folder holds tracked files, uninstall removes only what git ignores, which covers all of browse's runtime state, and says it kept the tracked files. When the folder has no tracked files, uninstall removes it whole, as before. If git can't list the tracked files, uninstall keeps the folder.
- Uninstall checks each top-level checkout under `.gstack-worktrees/` before it removes anything. It stops with exit 2, naming each checkout and the fix, when a checkout has uncommitted changes (whatever `status.showUntrackedFiles` says), has commits no branch or tag holds, isn't a worktree registered to this repo, or can't be read by git. The fix is to commit or stash, re-run with `--keep-state`, or pass the new `--force-worktrees` to delete them anyway.
- A symlinked `.gstack-worktrees` is only unlinked, as before. Uninstall never follows the link, so the folder it points at and any worktrees there are kept and stay registered.
- Git runs inside a checkout only after the checkout matches the repo's own worktree list, with `core.fsmonitor` and hooks disabled. Checkouts it removes leave `git worktree list`; other worktrees' registrations are never touched.
- docs/uninstall.md and the changelog fragment describe all of this.

## Why

Uninstall is the repair path we tell people to use, and it was destroying committed files and unsaved work. This keeps the repair path safe for user data.

## Blast radius

Only `bin/gstack-uninstall`, its tests, docs/uninstall.md and one changelog.d fragment. Uninstall can now refuse (exit 2) where it used to delete; `--keep-state` and `--force-worktrees` are the ways past it.

## Approvals

- Review-loop grant a-ceae0db5a103 (GStack Minder, Captain): one scoped fix on top of e5aca18, a symlinked `.gstack-worktrees` is unlinked and never followed, plus one fix-check reader.
- Docs exception (GStack Minder, GSTA-36, 2026-11-09): "I accept the docs/uninstall.md:65 manual-removal risk on #4241. main has the same line, and a follow-up lane fixes it after #4241 lands. I rule outside-voice#3 (git status running the user's own filter drivers) a note, not a regression."

## Known limitations

These fail safe: uninstall refuses them, and `--force-worktrees` gets past the refusal.
- A worktree with an initialized submodule.
- A worktree whose branch was deleted after a squash-merge.

A worktree created inside another checkout under .gstack-worktrees/ is not checked and is deleted with its parent. main deletes it too; a follow-up PR fixes it. Repro: `repro-nested-worktree.sh`.

<details><summary>repro-nested-worktree.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repro for PR #4241 pass-2 red-team finding: a dirty worktree nested inside a clean gstack lane is deleted.
# Usage: repro-nested.sh <path to gstack-uninstall> <scratch dir>
set -euo pipefail
U="$1"; F="$2"; rm -rf "$F"; mkdir -p "$F/home/.claude/skills/gstack" "$F/home/.gstack"
echo test > "$F/home/.claude/skills/gstack/SKILL.md"; : > "$F/gitconfig"
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$F/gitconfig" GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
g() { git -c user.name=fixture -c user.email=fixture@example.com -c commit.gpgsign=false "$@"; }
mkdir "$F/proj"; cd "$F/proj"; g init -q -b main
printf '.gstack-worktrees/\n' > .gitignore; echo v1 > f.txt; g add .gitignore f.txt; g commit -q -m seed
g worktree add -q --detach .gstack-worktrees/run1/lane HEAD
g -C .gstack-worktrees/run1/lane worktree add -q --detach .gstack-worktrees/run2/inner HEAD
INNER="$F/proj/.gstack-worktrees/run1/lane/.gstack-worktrees/run2/inner"
echo 'unsaved edit' >> "$INNER/f.txt"
echo "inner status: $(g -C "$INNER" status --porcelain)"
echo "outer lane status: [$(g -C .gstack-worktrees/run1/lane status --porcelain)]"
set +e
env HOME="$F/home" GSTACK_DIR="$F/home/.claude/skills/gstack" GSTACK_SETTINGS_FILE="$F/home/settings.json" GSTACK_HOME= GSTACK_STATE_ROOT="$F/home/.gstack" GSTACK_STATE_DIR= CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA= bash "$U" --force >"$F/out" 2>"$F/err"
echo "uninstall exit=$?"; sed 's/^/  stderr: /' "$F/err"
[ -e "$INNER/f.txt" ] && echo "inner edit KEPT: $(tail -1 "$INNER/f.txt")" || echo "inner edit DELETED"
echo "worktree list:"; g worktree list | sed 's/^/  /'
```
</details>

## Documentation

Status: blocked, with the owner exception above. The audit (docs-4241d-1, at 15e2281) found docs/uninstall.md:65, the manual removal steps, still says `rm -rf .gstack .gstack-worktrees`, which main also says; a follow-up lane fixes it. docs/state-root.md, README.md, docs/hosts.md, docs/install.md and ARCHITECTURE.md are current.

## Tests

`test/uninstall.test.ts` gains fixture cases in a throwaway repo, with HOME and the state root in a temp dir. Each fix has a test that failed first: the original cases on origin/main f75ce6f, three symlink cases on efc9b03, and five symlink cases on e5aca18 (including a link to a folder inside the repo holding a clean worktree with an ignored `.env`). Targeted lane at 15e2281: `bun test test/uninstall.test.ts`, 39 tests, 0 failures. CI runs the full suite.

Plan: exempt: bug fix

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- Rulings: the bin/gstack-uninstall:174 stale-path case (git and a filter driver can run in another repo sitting at a prunable worktree path) is a note under the outside-voice#3 ruling. docs/uninstall.md:65 is an accepted risk with a follow-up lane after this lands; outside-voice#3 (`git status` in a registered worktree can run the user's own configured clean or process filter) is a note, not a regression.
- Review: full depth (risk: security). Pass 1 red-team found the symlink deletion (fixed in e5aca18); pass 2 found the in-repo link case (fixed in c473a72, link-only removal under grant a-ceae0db5a103); the fix-check found no regression. Specialists found nothing. Step 11 ran adversarial-native and an outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol). Cold /ship run ship-4241d at 15e2281 (tree 4f1e53434e0e) reviewed once with no fixes: specialists none, red team 2 informational (the :174 stale-path case and the locked worktree), adversarial-native 5 and outside voice 6 (a Claude Opus 5.5 reader; Codex CLI not installed), all below the floor or shared with main. Exploratory QA passed 3 probes.
- Notes that main shares (main deletes in every case):
  - A `.gstack/` with nothing tracked is still deleted whole, untracked files included.
  - The confirmation preview still lists `.gstack-worktrees/` when it is a link, though only the link goes.
  - A git-tracked `.gstack-worktrees` link is removed without the ls-files check.
  - The check runs before the prompt; a checkout that becomes dirty while the prompt waits is deleted.
  - Edits hidden by assume-unchanged or skip-worktree, and ignored files such as `.env`, don't count as changes.
  - A locked worktree is deleted and its registration is left behind; stale registrations for nested or missing lanes stay (no data cost).
  - `$(_real …)` strips a trailing newline, so an unregistered checkout named `lane-1<LF>` can match a registered `lane-1`.
  - There's no test for the ls-files-failure branch.
  - A `.gstack/` that is its own git repo is deleted with its unpushed commits.
  - An untracked, unignored file in a `.gstack/` with nothing tracked is deleted.
  - `--force` can now exit 2 when a worktree is at risk (intended and documented).
  - Smaller: a REMOVED entry is recorded even if `git clean` fails; gstack's detached test leftovers can block uninstall (fails safe).
- Lane GSTA-472, issue GST-2197.
</details>

title: Read the merge queue's notes in one git process so land and ready stay fast (GST-2198)
body:
`gstack-ship-queue land --pin` and the first `ready` on a head now read the merge queue's notes with one git process instead of one per note. This keeps the merge step fast and stops it from drifting toward the command timeout, which serves the goal of a merge queue crews can rely on. ## What changed Rebuilding local queue state from `refs/notes/gstack-trains` (`rebuildFromNotes` in crew/lib/ship-queue-train-record.ts) ran `git cat-file blob` once per note. It now feeds every note blob to a single `git cat-file --batch` process and splits the output by byte size before decoding, so notes with multibyte text come back intact. Each note still goes through the same `parseNote`, in the same order, so the same records are restored. Malformed, empty and wrong-schema notes are still skipped. Measured on the live 1,442 notes (a bare fetch of `refs/notes/gstack-trains`, same 4-core machine): | | first rebuild (empty state) | later rebuilds | |---|---|---| | before | 14,781 ms | 15,435 ms, 14,103 ms | | after | 505 ms | 137 ms, 118 ms | Both runs restored 1,442 records, and the restored state directories hash the same (`ac7b69ad8ba24d70`). ## Why Every land and every first READY paid that 14 to 15 s cost, and it grew about 8 s a week as notes piled up. At that rate it would pass the 120 s git command timeout in about three months, and a land killed there leaves the land lock held (reports/GSTA-461.md item 4). ## Blast radius One function in crew/lib/ship-queue-train-record.ts, plus `parseNote` is now exported so the test can run the old per-note read as its oracle. No output, result code or record format changed. One behaviour is stricter. If that single read fails, times out or overruns its buffer, the rebuild now reports the notes as not read (`fetched: false`), so `land --repair` and the freeze lock refuse instead of acting on an empty queue. ## Tests New crew/test/ship-queue-notes-batch.test.ts, on a fixture of several hundred notes that includes a malformed note, an empty note, a wrong-schema note, a multibyte note, a note whose text looks like a `cat-file` header, and a duplicated record: - The batch reads all notes with one `git cat-file` process. This failed on main with 411 processes. - The batch restores exactly the records the per-note read restores. - A newer local record is kept, a repeat rebuild restores nothing, and an origin with no notes reads nothing. - A failed batch read reports `fetched: false` and restores nothing (failed before the fix in c089deece).
Agent notes Lane GSTA-469 for GStack Minder (GSTA-36), issue GST-2198. /ship by its /ship subagent at head 29cdc707dee3. Pass 2: no issues in the diff, notes below. - Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) - Adversarial (Step 11): native adversarial issues_found (3 notes below, none blocking); outside voice openai/gpt-6.1-sol CLEAN. - Exploratory QA: pass. A failed `git cat-file --batch` was reproduced reporting fetched:true with 0 of 51 notes read; after the fix it reports fetched:false and writes no record. #### Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:161` A normal direct land (land-direct:161/173) and newTrain (train.ts:404-405) ignore rebuildFromNotes().fetched and read the freeze from local JSON, so a failed notes read (fetch or, now, the batch) lets a non-repair land past a remote-only freeze. title: Catch secrets in files git treats as binary before they are pushed (GST-2195)
body:
This PR keeps credentials out of pushes. It covers files that git treats as binary: a file with a NUL byte, UTF-16 text, or a file that a `.gitattributes` line marks `-diff`. Before, git printed "Binary files differ" for these files instead of the added lines, so a GitHub token inside one passed both the pre-push hook and pregate's `secrets` check unscanned. Now both guards read those files and block the token.

## What changed

- Both guards now run git's diff with `--text`, so the added lines of a binary file reach the scanner. That covers `bin/gstack-redact-prepush`, which runs `git diff` and `git show`, and `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts`.
- A new helper, `scannableText`, reads each line of such a file three ways. First as plain bytes, where every run of control or non-UTF-8 bytes becomes one space. Then as little-endian and as big-endian UTF-16 with the NUL bytes removed. A token is found in whichever reading keeps it whole, including UTF-16 text that is mostly Cyrillic or CJK.
- In a binary file, only credential findings count. A run of digits in a compressed image is no longer reported as a phone number, and this repo's own PNG, JPEG, GIF and ICNS files add no finding.
- Pregate now treats a merge-base diff that git did not finish as `PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT`, never a pass. That covers an error, a kill or a full buffer.
- The pass line names the files read: `12 added lines clean in 3 files (1 binary)`.
- The added-line parser now runs in linear time. A 200,000-line diff used to take about 75 s and now takes under 2 s.
- `docs/pregate.md` and the changelog fragment describe all of this. The fragment also says which layouts are not caught yet.

## Why

A credential pushed once is compromised. GST-2195 showed three ordinary ways a token could pass both guards. They were a NUL byte in the file, UTF-16 text, and a `-diff` attribute added in the same branch. This PR closes all three for a token on one line.

## Blast radius

- **Behaviour change: oversized binaries now fail closed.** Before, they passed unscanned. A file whose scanned text is over the scanner's 16 MiB limit now fails pregate's `secrets` check, and a push whose diff is over the hook's 64 MiB buffer is blocked. Git LFS is the way past both, because its small pointer files scan as text.
- **Compiled executables.** An executable that contains a literal OpenSSH private-key header gives `pem.private_key`, just as text would. The allowlists handle such a case, and this repo stores no executables.
- **Scope.** The PR touches only the two guards, their two test files, `docs/pregate.md` and one changelog fragment.

## Open advisory notes

None of these is a regression against main. Each is a gap or rough edge left after this PR.

1. **Known gap: a keyword and its value split across lines in UTF-16 text.**
   - **What leaks.** Take a UTF-16LE file whose first line is `aws_secret_access_key:` and whose second line holds the 40-character key. It still passes both guards.
   - **Repro.** The file `le.txt` holds the bytes `FF FE`, then the UTF-16LE encoding of `aws_secret_access_key:\n  <40-character synthetic key>\n`. It was committed as `creds.yml` in a scratch repo with a bare remote. Results:

     | File | Head `3a82baa` hook / pregate | Base `f75ce6f` hook / pregate |
     |---|---|---|
     | plain.txt (UTF-8, same text) | blocked / fail (`aws.secret_key`) | blocked / fail (`aws.secret_key`) |
     | le.txt (UTF-16LE, key on the next line) | **exit 0 / pass** (`3 added lines clean in 1 file (1 binary)`) | exit 0 / pass (`no added lines`) |
     | le1.txt (UTF-16LE, key on the same line) | blocked / fail (`aws.secret_key`, `env.kv`) | exit 0 / pass (`no added lines`) |

   - **Cause.** In `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts:95-98`, the three readings are joined on one line. So the keyword line ends with the letter-spaced plain reading, and the `aws.secret_key` next-line rule loses its keyword. The outside voice also reports that UTF-16BE `PASSWORD=…` loses its `env.kv` (MEDIUM) finding the same way. That one was not reproduced here.
   - **Fix.** Scan each reading as its own text with the same line numbers, then merge the findings. A follow-up PR will make this fix after #4243 lands.
2. **Known limit: deleted or replaced binaries count toward the hook's 64 MiB buffer.** With `--text`, the old bytes of a deleted or replaced binary fill the hook's buffer. Removing an already-pushed 70 MB binary, or replacing a 40 MB one with another 40 MB one, blocks the push, while base let it through. The push fails closed, and its message (`git diff failed (status=killed/overflow)`) doesn't say why. A move to Git LFS (delete the blob, commit the pointer) is affected too. Pregate is not affected: it skips deletions and has a 256 MiB buffer. A follow-up will add `--irreversible-delete` and a clearer message.
3. **Pregate shows a misleading message for oversized files.** A file whose scanned text is over 16 MiB gets "HIGH finding(s) … rotate the credential" instead of "too large to scan". Because the three readings grow UTF-16 text about 2.46 times, this now happens for UTF-16 files from about 6.8 MB and for binaries from about 24 MB.
4. **One NUL byte drops privacy findings for the whole file.** Binary status is decided per file, so a single NUL silences email, hostname and legal warnings on every line of it. Before this PR the file wasn't scanned at all.
5. **Some layouts are still not read.** UTF-32 text, compressed containers (zip, docx, xlsx, PDF Flate streams, PNG zTXt) and packed string tables are not read. In a packed string table, such as Go `-X` values, a token sits next to letters or digits, so the `\b` anchors fail.
6. **A token can be reported twice,** because more than one reading of a line can hold it.
7. **The third reading roughly doubles the scanned text for UTF-16 files.** This is the earlier fix-check's informational note.
8. **The new parse-speed test checks wall-clock time.** It asserts under 2,000 ms with no `gstack-timing-ok` comment, so a heavily loaded CI runner could fail it.
9. **Large untracked files are still skipped.** Pregate skips untracked files over 4 MiB, binaries included. That rule predates this branch.

## Exploratory QA

title: Refuse to archive a thread that holds an open PR, and close a landed PR's issue (GST-2188)
body:
A thread that still has an open pull request can no longer be archived, and the issue a merged pull request names now closes in the same step. This serves the crew goal that no PR or issue is left with nobody to wake it.

## Summary

`gstack-archive-check thread` runs right before a Captain archives a crew thread. The Captain writes the raw thread and open-issue reads to a file, and the check re-reads every PR the thread holds from GitHub. It refuses while any PR is open, successor or not (R91), or while an issue in a working state is still assigned to the thread. It refuses stale, truncated, header-only or unparsable reads and failed gh reads. Every run prints a handoff stub for a successor brief. `gstack-archive-check landed --pr <n>` names the tracker codes in a merged PR's title so the Captain closes those issues in the same program.

## What changed

- New `bin/gstack-archive-check` and `lib/archive-check.ts`, with five `ARCHIVE_*` result codes and troubleshooting sections.
- `crew/docs/captain.md`, `capy/skill/gstack/factory.md` item 12, `/captain`, `/runaway-stopper` and the successor brief now say a thread with an open PR stays until that PR merges or closes.
- `docs/skills.md` says the same for the runaway-stopper Stop step.

## Why

A 6-hour sweep found orphans hours after they happened: 24 archived threads with open PRs in the first sweep, then 14 more plus 12 live issues. Checking at archive time stops them before they exist.

## Blast radius

Captains archiving crew threads and the land step. The check fails closed, so a bad read blocks an archive instead of allowing one. `gstack-ship-queue` is unchanged.

## Documentation
Re-audit after rebasing onto main 6088c86 (#4240). Scope: the two files with rebase conflicts, `capy/skill/gstack/factory.md` item 12 and the `docs/skills.md` /runaway-stopper Stop bullet, plus cross-reference checks against `crew/docs/captain.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md`. Result: current, with no edits. Both conflict files keep #4240's PR-scoped handoff and 1B check-in wording and add this branch's rule never to archive a thread that holds an open PR (R91), enforced through `gstack-archive-check thread`. The `gstack-archive-check` docs and troubleshooting codes agree with that wording. Debt: none found. The rest of the docs were covered by the first audit (ship4244-docs1).

Documentation exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-09 via Captain reply relayed by GSTA-462 at head 4ae42d87bd3c77604ce3dc47af3b706e68b1f6cd: runaway-stopper/SKILL.md step 3 was trimmed by 2 lines after docs re-audit ship4244-docs2, to fit the context budget; the trim was reviewed by the granted fix-check (no findings above the floor). Accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36), 2026-11-09.

## Test plan

- `test/archive-check.test.ts`: written failing first, then extended by the review fixes (stub truncation, `landed` CLI, header-only issue lists, case-insensitive codes).
- Focused set on the rebased tree: 495 pass, 0 fail, typecheck clean; CI run 42702356486 green at 4ae42d8.

title: Keep Free Tests planning under its job cap when the duration seed goes stale (GST-2193)
body:
## What changed Free Tests no longer fails to plan when the test-duration seed falls behind, and the seed is current again. - **Fresh seed.** `scripts/free-test-durations.json` is re-recorded from run [42691699570](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42691699570) on main: 1,661 files, 0 failed while recording. The old seed (2026-10-31) was missing 196 files, and every Free Tests shard job carried a 77-minute timeout. With the fresh seed the planner prints no unseeded warning and the shard timeout is **48 minutes**. That is the real figure, not the ~38 the audit estimated, because the 196 new files take 1,510 s together. The 1,465 files both seeds share moved from 5,154 s to 5,769 s, with a per-file median ratio of 1.008, so the recording is consistent with the last one. - **Unseeded files can't push a plan over the cap.** Files missing from the seed are still packed at the seed's 99th percentile. When that estimate would push a shard's job past the 90-minute cap, `--ci-plan --job-setup-seconds` now cuts that shard's prediction back to the cap, instead of throwing `FREE_JOB_TIMEOUT_OVER_CAP` for every PR and main. The runner wall and the GitHub job timeout both read the capped prediction from the plan, so GitHub still never kills a job before the runner can name a hung file. Recorded durations are never cut: a shard whose seeded files alone need more than 90 minutes still fails the plan. Plans under the cap are byte-for-byte unchanged. - **Closed seed PRs raise a blocker.** When the weekly recorder's seed PR (`bot/free-duration-seeds`) is closed without merging, `free-durations-record.yml` opens (or comments on) a GitHub issue titled "Blocker: free-suite duration seed PR closed unmerged" and turns that run red. A seed PR that merges closes the issue. The trigger is `pull_request: closed` filtered to PRs touching the two seed files, and the recording jobs skip that event. - **Eight new slow files admitted.** The fresh seed records eight files over the 60 s ceiling. Each becomes an annotated exception in `scripts/free-test-seed-allowlist.json` (todo: "split or speed up; post-11-21 slow-test pass"), as the ratchet's shrink-only rule requires. ## Why The audit (GSTA-461, item 1) measured new test files arriving at about 22 a day. About 60 more unseeded files would have made the planner throw on every PR and on main, roughly 3 days from 11-09. The last two weekly seed PRs were closed unmerged (#3452, #3835), and the 11-09 scheduled recording opened none. ## Blast radius Free Tests planning (`scripts/test-free-shards.ts` `createFreeCiPlan` / `--ci-plan`), the duration seed and its allowlist, and the weekly recorder workflow. The Windows lane plans without `--job-setup-seconds` and is unchanged. No merge-check, pregate, ship-queue or receipt code changed. ## Tests Written first on f75ce6f and failing there: - `test/test-free-shards.test.ts`: a shard over the cap only because of unseeded files now plans at 90 min, and the real `--ci-plan` CLI with a stale seed exits 0 with every timeout ≤ 90. - `test/free-durations-record-workflow.test.ts`: the blocker step, run against a stub `gh`: it creates the issue, comments on an existing one, closes it on merge, and stays quiet on a merge with no open issue. Hold tests that pass before and after: a plan under the cap is identical with or without the cap, and recorded durations over the cap still throw. `test/free-tests-workflow-wiring.test.ts` now plans the same way the CLI does. ## Documentation Documentation exception: accepted by GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-09 via Captain ruling relayed by lane GSTA-464 on the /ship cap raise: docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md is outside this lane: record the two corrections as a follow-up and do not edit that file **Status:** blocked. The read-only audit found two factual corrections needed in docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md; no files were edited. **Scope:** committed diff f75ce6fd..465e8467 on capy/free-seed-unseeded-cap (3 commits, 8 files: free-durations-record.yml, test-free-shards.ts, the duration seed, the seed allowlist, a changelog fragment and 3 tests). Nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. **Documentation health:** - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: needs update. The CI job-timeout paragraph overstates FREE_JOB_TIMEOUT_OVER_CAP: the plan now caps unseeded overestimates and fails only when recorded durations exceed 90 minutes. The duration-seed section lacks the closed-unmerged seed PR blocker issue. - changelog.d/free-seed-unseeded-cap.md: current (matches the code). - .github/workflows/free-durations-record.yml header comment: current. - scripts/free-test-seed-allowlist.json annotations: current. - README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md: current (they don't cover this behavior). **Coverage debt:** `maxPredictedMsUnderJobCap` and the capped-prediction behavior of `--ci-plan --job-setup-seconds` have reference coverage only in code comments and the changelog fragment until TESTING_INTERNALS is corrected. The seed-PR blocker issue has no reference docs outside the workflow comment. Eight new allowlist exceptions carry a 'post-11-21 slow-test pass' todo, so that is tracked debt. **Diagram drift:** none; no diagrams reference the shard planner or the seed recorder.
Agent notes - Review note 1 (below the floor, not fixed): if the bot seed PR is closed because the seed landed some other way, such as a hand-recorded seed PR or a wave merge, the new job still raises the blocker issue and a red run. The issue body says to close it by hand in that case. - Review note 2 (below the floor, not fixed): GitHub may hold the closed-event run on a PR the workflow token opened, so the blocker job could fail to run. No run has shown this. The `pull_request_target` alternative was declined as a security trade-off. - Docs follow-up 1: `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` (around lines 215-217) still says any shard over 90 minutes fails the plan with `FREE_JOB_TIMEOUT_OVER_CAP`. With `--job-setup-seconds`, the plan now cuts the unseeded estimate back to the cap and fails only when recorded durations alone pass it. - Docs follow-up 2: the "Free suite duration seed" section of `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` (around lines 1583-1632) doesn't mention the new `pull_request: closed` trigger or the blocker issue it opens and closes. Both docs fixes are outside this lane; the documentation exception was accepted by GStack Minder (GSTA-36). - Plan: exempt: bug fix (kind fix), failing-first test shown on f75ce6f - Likely regression, not just slow files: `test/review-pass.test.ts` went from 24 s (2026-10-31 seed) to 221 s (about 9x), and `test/review-exclude.test.ts` (new to the seed) records 126 s. Not investigated here; flagged for the post-11-21 slow-test pass. - The 11-09 scheduled recorder run (42560745759) proposed nothing because its Windows recording was cancelled at the 30-minute job timeout and `propose` needs both artifacts. Not changed here. - Recorder run 42691699570 was dispatched for this lane on main; its Linux artifact is the committed seed. The Windows seed is not part of this PR. - Thread GSTA-464, issue GST-2193, source audit reports/GSTA-461.md item 1.
