title: Let ci-carry verify a rerun Actions attempt by reading its jobs in pages of 50 (GST-2215)
body:
gstack can again reuse a GitHub Actions run as test evidence after that run has been rerun, so a green rerun of a known flaky test no longer forces /ship to run the whole test suite again on the agent's machine. This serves the project goal of CI being the one full test run.

## What changed

![ghRunDeps.jobs: one 100-job page per request (502 past the proxy's ~10 s cutoff on rerun attempts) becomes 50 per page, with one whole-list reread at 25 after a 5xx](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/5SM5-2SbEBH33Yz5MGwtMmYztsEo17gd51Rm0ADh8zI.png)

The job list for one run attempt is now read 50 jobs per page instead of 100, and a server error (5xx) rereads the whole list once at 25 per page.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: ghRunDeps.jobs: one 100-job page per request (502 past the proxy's ~10 s cutoff on rerun attempts) becomes 50 per page, with one whole-list reread at 25 after a 5xx</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
   return {
     run: id => json<ApiRun>(`repos/${repo}/actions/runs/${id}`),
     runsForHead: (workflow, sha) => all<ApiRun>(`repos/${repo}/actions/workflows/${workflow}/runs?head_sha=${sha}&per_page=100`, 'workflow_runs'),
+    // A long rerun attempt's 100-job page can outlast a proxy's ~10 s cutoff (GST-2215): read 50 per page, and after a 5xx read the whole list once more at 25. A failed page throws, so a partial list never counts.
+    jobs: (id, attempt) => {
+      const read = (n: number) => all<ApiJob>(`repos/${repo}/actions/runs/${id}/attempts/${attempt}/jobs?per_page=${n}`, 'jobs');
+      try { return read(50); } catch (e) { if (!/\bHTTP 5\d\d\b/.test((e as Error).message)) throw e; return read(25); }
+    },
-    jobs: (id, attempt) => all<ApiJob>(`repos/${repo}/actions/runs/${id}/attempts/${attempt}/jobs?per_page=100`, 'jobs'),
     artifact: (id, name) => {
 
~~~

</details>

## Why

"`gstack-ci-carry find` returned `no_verified_run: test: run <id>: api_error` for any run whose newest attempt is a rerun" (gbrain #8940). On a rerun attempt GitHub took about 11 seconds to answer a 100-job page for gbrain's 86-job Test workflow, and the proxy that Capy machines reach GitHub through cuts requests off at about 10 seconds with a 502. Smaller pages answer well inside that limit, so a rerun attempt verifies again and its green CI result carries instead of the suite running locally.

## Blast radius

Only the jobs read inside `ghRunDeps` (lib/run-evidence.ts:335-339) changes; every caller of `ghRunDeps` (`gstack-ci-carry`, `gstack-pregate --from-run`, `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts`) gets the same complete job list it got before, now in more pages. It stays safe because a failed page still makes `gh` exit non-zero, which throws, so a partial list never counts. The negative-control test walked that failure path, and a live read of gbrain run 42670157276 attempt 4 (the run that answered 502 before) returned all 86 jobs.

## Summary

A rerun Actions attempt could not be verified as test evidence. Reading its job list 100 at a time timed out behind the proxy, so every rerun came back `api_error` and /ship fell back to the full local suite even after a green rerun of a flaky test. The jobs read now asks for 50 per page (gh follows every page) and, on a 5xx, rereads the whole list once at 25. A non-5xx error (a 404, say) does not retry, and any failed page still leaves the run unverified.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage. Three tests at the end of test/run-evidence.test.ts drive `ghRunDeps(...).jobs` through a stub `gh` on PATH that pages an attempt-2 list of 86 jobs and answers 502 past a page-size limit: 50 per page across every page, one 5xx retry at 25, and a negative control where page 2 fails (stays `api_error` after exactly one retry) plus a 404 that does not retry. They were red on f75ce6f and are green at this head.

## Pre-Landing Review

No issues found by the core checklist or the batched specialist (testing, security, state machines, red team). The adversarial reader raised two notes below the blocking floor, listed under Review notes; the outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) returned CLEAN.

Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

Outside review: CLEAN (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, completed).

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:338` The 25-per-page retry fires only when gh's stderr carries 'HTTP 5xx'; with --jq, gh prints a JSON-parse error instead when a 5xx body is HTML, plain text or empty, so those 5xx answers skip the retry and stay api_error (fails closed, no regression)
- INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/capy-ci-carry-reads-rerun-attempt-jobs-in-pages-gst-2215.md:4` Changelog says any server error (5xx) triggers the 25-per-page reread; per finding 1 that holds only when the 5xx body is JSON

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke, CLI surface, read-only against GitHub through the live proxy (budget 300 s, 3 captures):

- Checkpoint 002: pass. `ghRunDeps('garrytan/gbrain').jobs('42670157276', 4)`, the rerun attempt that answered 502 at 100 per page before this change, returned 86 of 86 jobs in 18.9 s.
- Checkpoint 003: pass. A run id that does not exist (`garrytan/gstack` run 1) throws `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` in 0.6 s instead of yielding an empty or partial list.
- Capture 001 failed on the probe script's own import path, not product code, and is superseded by 002 on the same inputs.
- Limit: the retry count on a live 5xx is not observable without a failing proxy; the stub tests cover it.

title: Stop learnings, timeline events and brain sync from storing Stripe, Slack, npm and database secrets (GST-2196)
body:
Learnings, timeline events and brain sync no longer store or push Stripe live keys, Slack tokens, npm tokens or database URLs with a real password. This serves gstack's goal of never leaking a user's secrets into synced memory.

## What changed

- `gstack-learnings-log` and `gstack-timeline-log` now refuse any row whose keys or string values hold a HIGH-tier secret found by lib/redact-engine. They exit 1, name the rule and never print the value. This is the same check `gstack-decision-log` already used.
- Brain sync's push-time scanner now also holds Stripe live and restricted keys, Slack tokens, npm tokens and database URLs with a password. It keeps redact-engine's placeholder rules, so `${DB_PASSWORD}`, `PASSWORD` and the local `postgres:postgres@localhost` default still sync.
- The timeline logger also gets the Windows cygpath fix the learnings logger already had.

## Why

Before this change, `gstack-learnings-log` stored a database URL with its password and exited 0, and `gstack-timeline-log` had no secret check at all. Brain sync then pushed those rows to the user's sync repo, because its scanner knew only six families.

## Summary

Four commits. The failing tests came first (bcd1c35), then the writer and scanner change (9f2b4b2), then two fixture fixes (4a20a78, cd89e8c).

## Blast radius

The loggers now fail closed when they run from a bin/ with no lib/ beside it, so six test fixtures that run them from a shadow bin changed:

- test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts and test/skill-end-completion-durability.test.ts get a read-only lib symlink.
- test/skill-e2e-bws.test.ts, test/skill-e2e-session-intelligence.test.ts, test/skill-e2e-context-skills.test.ts and test/skill-e2e-skillify.test.ts are paid agent tests, so they get a copy of lib/. A copy is used because a live agent could write through a symlink into the real checkout.

Real installs always ship bin/ and lib/ together. Nothing else calls the loggers from a bare bin/.

## Documentation

Documentation exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-09 via Captain reply to GSTA-480, 2026-11-09: GStack Minder (GSTA-36), 2026-11-09: I accept the docs/gbrain-sync.md risk on #4247 (the secret-family list and 'the hook runs the same scan' are stale, below the floor). It's disclosed in the PR's Documentation section, and the follow-up fixes it with decode-before-scan and the context-lines false hold.
**Status:** blocked. Read-only audit found 2 factual corrections that are needed in docs/gbrain-sync.md.

**Scope:** base f75ce6fd to head cd89e8cd, 4 commits and 13 files. `gstack-learnings-log` and `gstack-timeline-log` now refuse HIGH-tier secrets, and `gstack-brain-sync` now holds four more secret families. Nothing is staged, unstaged or untracked.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/gbrain-sync.md: needs update. The 'Secret protection' list is missing Stripe live or restricted keys, Slack tokens, npm tokens and database URLs with a password. Its claim that the pre-commit hook runs the same scan is now inaccurate.
- docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md: current.
- docs/gbrain-quick-tour.md: current (short list, advisory).
- USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md: current.
- docs/troubleshooting.md: current. No entry covers the new secret refusals (debt).
- changelog.d fragment: present (not audited for edits).

**Coverage debt:** the refusal of learnings and timeline rows that hold secrets has no reference or how-to coverage outside the changelog fragment. The four new brain-sync families have no reference coverage until docs/gbrain-sync.md is updated.

**Diagram drift:** none found.
## Open notes

These are follow-ups. None of them is fixed here.

- Brain sync also scans context and removed diff lines. So a file that already holds a pushed database URL is held on every later edit, even the edit that removes it, until `--skip-file`. It is a false hold that fails safe. The fix is to scan only added lines.
- Brain sync scans the raw JSONL text, so a hand-written row with JSON-escaped secrets (a database URL with `\/` separators, or an npm token starting `\u006e`) passes the new rules. Main has no such rule at all, and rows written through the two loggers are scanned after decoding. The fix is to decode before scanning.
- The db-url rule counts JSON escapes such as `\n` as part of the password, so sync can falsely hold a row the writers accepted.
- Sync is looser than redact-engine on Markdown: quotes, a trailing backslash, and NFKC and zero-width forms.
- The hand-copied placeholder lists have no parity test against redact-engine.
- A row over 1 MiB fails closed, but the message calls `engine.input_too_large` a secret.
- The artifacts-init and brain-restore pre-commit hooks still have only six patterns.
- `gstack-timeline-log` writes the raw input when `ts` is present, so a secret in an earlier duplicate JSON key is not scanned. No repo caller sends `ts` or duplicate keys.
- `gstack-skill-start` and `gstack-skill-end` discard the timeline logger's exit 1, so a refused event disappears silently.
- Python's `\b` treats Unicode letters as word characters and JavaScript's does not, so brain sync can miss a token next to an accented letter in a file no writer gates.

## Review notes

title: Stop a merge check from passing a test that was weakened after review (GST-2204)
body:
A receipt carry no longer lets a test that was weakened after review merge without anyone reading it. This closes a hole in the merge checks (GSTA-461 audit item 6). ## What changed - `gstack-ship-receipt carry` used to treat every edit under `test/` as harmless. After /ship, a lane could change `expect(a).toBe(1)` to `expect(typeof a).toBe('number')`, carry the receipt as a "test-only change", and land with CI green and no reviewer. Now a carry whose test diff removes or changes an assertion line (an `expect`, `assert` or matcher, or a `test(...)`/`it(...)` line) refuses with `RECEIPT_CARRY_TEST_WEAKENED`. The refusal names each hunk as `path:line` and writes a packet for one scoped fix-check. The carry goes through once `--test-review ` holds a clean verdict bound to that head and the packet's sha256. - New tests and new assertions still carry as a test-only change. An assertion the base changed on its own, merged in, still carries as a base merge. A skipped test or a deleted test file still refuses through the review-depth check, which runs first. - `test/land-merged-checks.txt` (the list land runs on a moved base) and the touchfile maps under `test/helpers/` now count as product for a carry. Emptying or editing them is `RECEIPT_CARRY_PRODUCT_CHANGED`, not a test-only change. - New troubleshooting entry (`#receipt-carry-test-weakened`), a row in docs/ship-policy.md's carry table, a `gstack-ship-preflight` route line and a changelog fragment. ## Tests `test/ship-receipt-carry-weakened-test.test.ts` was written first from the audit repro. On main, the repro carried and the gate-path and parser cases failed (6 of 9 failed). On this branch all 9 pass. The negative controls are a pure test addition, a base-side assertion change and `test.skip`.
Agent notes - Detection is in `lib/ship-carry-tests.ts`. It reads removed lines in the zero-context diff from the reviewed head to HEAD, minus lines the base removed itself, plus lines the branch's current patch drops that its reviewed patch didn't (an assertion a base merge brought in that the branch then removed). - The new refusal is placed after the depth recheck, so `test.skip` and deleted tests keep their stronger refusal (/ship). - Gate test paths are compared path by path (`comparePath`) because the product patch-id pathspec can't re-include a path under an excluded `test/**` glob. `planCarry` now refuses whenever `changedProduct` is non-empty, even when the patch-ids match. title: Stop the runaway scan from telling Captains to rotate crew threads that hold a PR (GST-2226)
body:
`gstack-runaway scan` no longer tells you to rotate or warn about an agent thread that still has an open pull request. Only threads marked as long-running get rotation advice, and only after every pull request they hold is merged or closed. ## What changed - Crew threads (every thread not marked standing) get no `ROTATE` and no own-token `WARN`. Past 1 billion own tokens they get one `FLAG: CHECK_IN` line, and they keep their PR. - Standing threads (a merge lane, a watcher, an automation's standing thread) still get `FLAG: ROTATE` at 500M own tokens or 3 active days, with the 400M warn line. - A standing thread that holds an open PR gets `DEFER: holds an open PR; rotate after every PR merges or closes (R91)` instead of `ROTATE`. A file whose `pull_requests` list is missing or shorter than `pull_requests_total` counts as holding one. - `SWEEP:` gains a `check_in=` count. /runaway-stopper's fetch program gets a `standing` list, its line table gets a `CHECK_IN` row, and `--help` and docs/skills.md say the same. The skill stays inside its 3,841-token context budget. ## Why The scan was pointing Captains at rotating crew threads that still held unmerged PRs, which the archive rules forbid. This keeps the factory's own tooling in line with those rules. ## Blast radius The change is limited to the scan's printed advice in lib/runaway.ts and the /runaway-stopper skill text. The scan never acts on its own, and archive-check (#4244) still refuses to archive a thread with an open PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. title: Make the archive check refuse unknown PR states, cut-short issue rows and a missing title policy (GST-2241)
body:
The pre-archive check (`gstack-archive-check`, added in #4244 so a Captain never archives a thread that holds an open PR) had four places where it could say "clean" or "close this" without proof. Each now fails closed. This serves R91: a thread with an open PR is never archived. **Unknown PR states.** The check treated every state other than `OPEN` as closed, so an empty or unknown `state` from `gh pr view` let a thread archive while its PR might still be open. Now only `OPEN`, `CLOSED` and `MERGED` are accepted. Anything else exits 3 with the new code `ARCHIVE_PR_STATE_UNKNOWN`, in both `thread` and `landed` (where it used to exit 1, "not merged", which was also a guess). **Cut-short issue rows.** A row like `- GST-1 · Backlog` with no assignee, title or age passed as a complete issue. The parser now requires the real `tools.issue.read` row shape: code, state, optional markers (priority, `blocked`), an `@assignee` list or `unassigned`, a title, an optional `n/m sub-issues closed`, and an age like `5h`. I checked this against 300 live rows: every one fits. A row that doesn't is `ARCHIVE_READS_UNPARSED`. Titles that contain ` · ` are now kept whole in the handoff stub. **CI read failures.** When the CI read at the PR's head fails, the ORPHAN line now says `ci=unknown (CI read failed: )` instead of a bare `ci=unknown`. The open PR still refuses the archive. **Missing title policy.** `landed` with no `.gstack/plain-titles.json` (or an invalid one, or one with no `codes`) treated every code-shaped ref in the title as an issue to close. It now exits 3 with the new code `ARCHIVE_POLICY_UNREADABLE`, naming the file and the parse error, before it reads GitHub. Both new codes are registered in `lib/result-codes-capy.ts` with entries in docs/troubleshooting.md, and the `--help` exit-code text says when exit 3 happens. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/archive-check.ts:148` multi-line gh error or empty head sha bypasses the 'CI read failed' label; the PR still refuses (cosmetic output) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/archive-check.ts:35` AGE accepts only Nm/Nh/Nd; a future wider age format would make thread checks refuse (fails closed, never archives wrongly) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/archive-check.ts:177` landed refuses (exit 3) outside a checkout with .gstack/plain-titles.json; intended and documented, issues stay open - INFORMATIONAL `lib/archive-check.ts:66` pre-existing: a 100-row list's '[More issues. Pass cursor=...]' line is unrecognized, so the check refuses (fails closed) ## Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual doc correction was made, with no blockers. **Scope:** the 7 committed files from base 01e39805 to head 3694eb44 (gstack-archive-check now fails closed on unknown PR states and on an unreadable plain-titles policy), plus the authored docs that describe the archive check and the land step. **Documentation health** - crew/docs/captain.md: Updated. The diff already added the ARCHIVE_PR_STATE_UNKNOWN and ARCHIVE_POLICY_UNREADABLE anchors, and they match lib/result-codes-capy.ts. - captain/SKILL.md.tmpl: Current. - runaway-stopper/SKILL.md.tmpl: Current. - docs/skills.md: Current. - changelog.d/archive-check-fails-closed-on-unknown-pr-states.md: Current and accurate. **Coverage debt:** none. Every new result code has a troubleshooting anchor and a doctor mapping. **Diagram drift:** none, since no diagrams cover this path. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-8b77b5c3ba13). title: Stop hook times out on Windows: detached --repair child keeps the hook's process tree alive
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the timeline Stop hook intermittently fails with:

```
Hook failed: bash /c/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook (stop): timed out after 14s
```

The hook itself is fast (~0.2s warm) and fail-open by design, so the timeout cannot come from the foreground path. The cause is the **detached `--repair` child** that `spawnRepair()` launches on a slug-cache miss.

## Root cause

`spawnRepair()` (hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook.ts) spawns:

```ts
spawn(process.execPath, [...bunIsolationArgs(), file, '--repair', cwd], {
  detached: true, stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true,
})
```

The child runs `backgroundRepair()` → `runBin('gstack-slug', ..., { timeout: REPAIR_SLUG_TIMEOUT_MS /* 30s */ })` through Git Bash, then repairs.

Claude Code on Windows waits for the **entire process tree** of a hook, not just the direct child — `detached: true` does not remove the grandchild from that tree (same class of bug as anthropics/claude-code#24206, "Stop hook timeout does not kill child process tree", and the Windows orphan/suspended-process reports #77078, #100399).

So every slug-cache miss keeps the Stop hook's tree alive for the child's full lifetime:

- typical `gstack-slug` through Git Bash: ~1–3s (borderline vs. the 5s hook budget once bash+ bun startup is counted),
- degraded cases: up to the 30s `REPAIR_SLUG_TIMEOUT_MS`.

`~/.gstack/hook-errors.log` on this machine shows real `gstack-slug: ETIMEDOUT` repair failures, i.e. the slow path is exercised in practice. Miss markers are per-cwd with a 5-minute TTL, so every new working directory re-arms the spawn.

## Reproduction

1. Windows, Git Bash hook shell, bun on PATH.
2. In Claude Code, stop a session whose `cwd` has **no versioned slug-cache entry** (any fresh directory works).
3. The hook returns immediately, but the detached `bun --repair` child keeps the hook's process tree alive until `gstack-slug` exits; with a slow/failed resolve this exceeds the hook timeout and Claude Code reports `Hook failed: ... timed out`.

Verified locally: with the spawn skipped on `process.platform === 'win32'`, the miss path completes in ~0.13s with zero lingering `bun` processes; the cache-hit path is unchanged at ~0.16s.

## Suggested fixes (any one)

1. **Skip `spawnRepair` on win32** — the inline path already repairs every cache hit; a miss just retries next Stop. Cheapest and matches the hook's fail-open contract. Trade-off: uncached directories never get background slug resolution on Windows.
2. **Spawn through a tree-escaping mechanism on Windows** — e.g. WMI `Win32_Process.Create` or `Start-Process`, so the repair child is not a descendant Claude Code waits on. Preserves the feature fully.
3. **Bound the child's worst case harder on win32** — e.g. a much smaller slug timeout; reduces but does not eliminate the timeout window.

## What I run locally

Option 1 as a two-line guard plus a test seam:

```ts
if (process.platform === 'win32' && process.env.GSTACK_TIMELINE_REPAIR_CHILD !== '1') return;
```

and `test/timeline-stop-hook-slug.test.ts` sets `GSTACK_TIMELINE_REPAIR_CHILD=1` in the hook env so the miss→child→repair path stays covered on every platform (all 4 slug tests + 2 stdin tests pass on Windows; the 4 pre-existing `timeline-stop-hook wiring` failures reproduce on unmodified HEAD and are unrelated).

Happy to open a PR with this if the direction looks right.

## Environment

- Windows 11, Git Bash (`OSTYPE=msys`), bun 1.4.4
- Claude Code 2.1.293
- gstack main @ a58e6e27c (2026-11-09)

title: Keep the session timeline hook from timing out on Windows
body:

## Summary

- On Windows, Claude Code waits on a Stop hook's **whole process tree**; the detached `--repair` child spawned on a slug-cache miss still counts, and it runs `gstack-slug` for up to `REPAIR_SLUG_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s). Every miss could hold the hook past its timeout → `Hook failed: ... timed out`.
- `spawnRepair()` now returns early on `process.platform === 'win32'` unless `GSTACK_TIMELINE_REPAIR_CHILD=1`. The inline path still repairs every cache hit; a miss just retries next Stop (same fail-open semantics the hook already has for every other failure mode).

title: Make ship-queue ready refuse when its READY note doesn't reach origin (GST-2242)
body:
`gstack-ship-queue ready` now refuses when its READY note never reaches origin, so a pull request is no longer reported ready to merge when the merge step would refuse it. This keeps the merge queue's READY signal trustworthy, which is what lets PRs merge on green without a human checking each one.

## What changed

- After pushing `refs/notes/gstack-trains`, the notes writer fetches origin's ref back. It reports `notes pushed` only when origin's tip is the local tip or contains it. A push that exits 0 while origin still lacks the note now counts as a failure and goes through the same three tries.
- Under a train policy (gstack's own), `ready` and `ready --base-red` refuse with the new `QUEUE_READY_NOTE_UNPUSHED` (exit 3) when the note isn't on origin after those tries. The local receipt is kept, so rerunning `ready` once the push works keeps `ready_at` and pushes the receipt.
- New troubleshooting entry `#queue-ready-note-unpushed`, a line in docs/ship-policy.md's train READY section, the regenerated doctor component list, and a changelog fragment.

## Why

`ready` used to exit 0 and print `notes pushed` even when the note never reached origin. The lane then sent READY, and `land --pin` refused the pin with `QUEUE_NOT_READY` because origin had no note. That cost #4245 a land round. Now the failure shows up at `ready`, where the lane can fix the push, instead of at land time.

## Blast radius

Every caller of `persist()` in crew/lib now pays one extra fetch per write and can get `pushed: false` for a push that exited 0. Callers that already check `pushed` get the stricter answer, and callers that ignore it behave as before; both reviewers checked every `persist()` call site (file:line read). The non-train `ready` path in lib/ship-queue.ts is unchanged.

## Test Coverage

`crew/test/ship-queue-ready-notes-push.test.ts` drives the real `bin/gstack-ship-queue ready` against a bare fixture origin. A pre-receive hook that rejects `refs/notes/*` makes ready refuse with the new code; that case failed on main (exit 0) before the fix. A post-receive hook that deletes the ref after accepting it makes ready refuse too. A normal push succeeds with origin's notes tip equal to the local tip, and a rerun after the hook is removed succeeds.

Coverage: 70% of changed paths (7 of 10), audit-only. The gaps are the ancestor branch of the read-back (another writer moved origin past the local tip), a read-back fetch failure other than a missing ref, and the refusal on the base-red path.

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 3 issues in pass 1, all below the blocking floor: 1 fixed in docs, 1 skipped, 1 noted. Pass 2 (full, on the fix range) found 2 more below-floor notes; the adversarial voice found 3 low or medium non-blocking notes, and the outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) returned CLEAN.
REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=3 fixed=2 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 dispatches=6
Gate edits: none detected

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor. Pass-1 #1 and #2 are open notes; #3 was fixed in docs.

- INFORMATIONAL `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-ready.ts:230` No test drives the base-red `conditionalReady` refusal or its NEXT command. Open note: below the floor; the plain path's tests cover the shared `recordReceipt`.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-queue.ts:298` The non-train `ready()` still ignores `p.pushed` and exits 0 on an unpushed note, for repos with `merge: direct` and no `train` block. Open note, tracked in GSTA-486: #4235 owns lib/ship-queue.ts, so this is a Captain-owned follow-up after #4235 lands. The changelog fragment now says the fix covers train policies; commit 6a3fd04's `Review-Finding: p1/red-team#1` trailer covers only that changelog half of the finding, not the code path.

title: Test that a stamped PR keeps its review after moving its entry to a changelog fragment (GST-2245)
body:
This PR adds an end-to-end test proving that a stamped PR keeps its /ship review after one commit moves its version stamp and CHANGELOG entry into a changelog fragment, and that the PR then lands through `gstack-ship-queue land --pin`. It serves the direct-merge goal: open PRs from the stamp-at-/ship era can switch to fragments without a fresh /ship each.

## Why

When a repo switches to `merge: direct`, open PRs still carry their own VERSION, package.json version and CHANGELOG entry, and `land --pin` refuses them with `QUEUE_LAND_STAMPED`. Rerunning /ship on each one is slow and costly. The receipt carry already handles a commit that only changes release metadata, but nothing proved it end to end.

## Summary

- New test `test/ship-receipt-carry-unstamp-land.test.ts` covers three carry paths (no base merge, a clean base merge, a conflicted base merge) through `land --pin`, plus a control where a code edit in the same commit refuses.
- The land-direct gh shim helpers moved unchanged into `test/helpers/land-direct-fixture.ts`.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`'s `QUEUE_LAND_STAMPED` fix now gives the carry order: commit and push, run the pregate at the new head, carry with `--pregate`, then ready. Base-merge conflicts keep the PR's own package.json changes.
- `scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts` excludes the new test, which uses the same extensionless gh shim as land-direct.

## Blast radius

Tests and docs only. No product code changed.

title: Make the ship queue fetch the latest main before it checks a pull request (GST-2232)
body:
## What changed `gstack-ship-queue ready` now fetches `origin/` before it reads the base policy or checks any field of the PR's /ship receipt. Before this, it used whatever copy of the base the lane's clone last fetched. If that copy was a few landings old, ready measured the PR from an older merge base, counted excluded files that belong to PRs that had already landed, and refused a good receipt with a false `RECEIPT_INVALID field=review_exclude`. That stopped gbrain #8991, whose clone held origin/master at d253ec0f while the real master was 310da193. - When the fetch fails, `ready` refuses with a new code, `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED`, and compares nothing. The stamp path of `land` used to ignore a failed fetch and keep going; it now refuses with the same code. `land --pin` (direct merges) already fetched and refused. - No change to how the review_exclude selection is measured. It was already the PR's own files, diffed from the merge base. A new test pins that: a file another PR lands on the base after this PR forked does not change the selection. ## Why This unblocks the gbrain merge queue (GBRA-108): lanes were being sent to rerun /ship's review for receipts that were correct. ## Blast radius `ready` makes one extra `git fetch` of the base branch per run. The new refusal only fires when that fetch fails, and in that case ready would otherwise have compared the receipt against a ref it couldn't refresh. The train paths are unchanged, because train ready already fetched. ## Tests - New file test/ship-queue-ready-fresh-base.test.ts. In its first test, the lane's origin/main is behind the remote after a stacked parent landed. Before the fix, ready refused with `RECEIPT_INVALID … source=origin/main@`; after it, the receipt binds. The same test checks that an unreachable origin refuses with `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED`. The second test checks that a base which moved under the exclusion leaves the selection unchanged; it fails if the selection is changed to a two-dot diff. - One test added to test/ship-queue-land.test.ts: an unfetchable base refuses before the receipt check, and nothing is pushed. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. Review ran once at 620f102 (specialists, red team, adversarial and an outside voice); none of these would fail a test, break production or lose data under this repo's `merge: direct` policy. - `lib/ship-queue-land.ts:344`: the stamp path of `land` fetches with a bare `git fetch -q origin `, which leaves `origin/` stale in a single-branch or narrowed-refspec clone, and `land()` loads its policy before that fetch. Not reachable here: under `merge: direct`, `land()` refuses at line 330 before it fetches. A follow-up could use the same explicit refspec as `ready`. - `bin/gstack-ship-queue:200`: the CLI picks the train or plain `ready` route from the policy before `ready` fetches, so a repo whose train setting changed since its last fetch could take the wrong route. This repo has no train block. - Two `ready` runs in one clone can race on the `origin/` ref lock and report `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED`; a rerun clears it. - The refusal echoes git's first stderr line (capped at 200 characters); git redacts credentials there, and an existing path already prints it. - `ready` fetches `origin` and ignores `ctx.remote`, matching the rest of `ready()`. ## Exploratory QA Pass. Two smoke probes against an isolated fixture: a stale `origin/main` is refreshed to the remote tip by `ready`, and an unreachable origin refuses with `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED` (exit 3) and leaves the ref untouched. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The release docs match the code at 620f102, and no edits were needed. **Scope:** 3 commits from a5bcbc4 across 10 files: lib/ship-queue.ts, lib/ship-queue-land.ts, lib/result-codes-release.ts, bin/gstack-doctor-components.sh, scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts, two tests, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and a changelog.d fragment. Nothing is staged, unstaged or untracked. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-policy.md: current. It describes the base fetch in ready and the stamp-path refusal of land; land --pin still uses QUEUE_NOT_READY, which the code confirms. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. The new queue-base-unfetched entry matches the anchor in the result code. - changelog.d/ship-queue-ready-fetches-base-gst-2232.md: current. - README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/pregate.md: current, with no change needed. **Coverage debt:** none. QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED has a reference entry and a fix entry. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch ready-fetches-base-before-receipt-check. title: Stop gstack-pr-wait, the land gate and the release cut from calling a head green while a check on it failed (GST-2252)
body:
gstack-pr-wait, the land gate (gstack-ci-gate) and the stable release cut no longer call a commit green while a check on it failed, because they now see a failed run hidden behind a jobless rerun the way the merge queue does.
This serves the merge-check goal: no gate in gstack passes a head the merge queue would refuse.

<details><summary>What changed and why</summary>

## Summary

gstack-evals#303 went ready with its `checks` job red, because GitHub's rollup (`gh pr checks`) and its default check-runs list only show each check suite's latest attempt. A rerun that creates no jobs hides the failed run before it, and a workflow run that fails before creating a job never appears as a check run. #4235 fixed this for the merge queue (`ciAtHead`). This PR fixes the same blind spot in gstack-pr-wait (`lib/pr-wait-github.ts` `fetchChecks`), gstack-ci-gate (`lib/ci-gate.ts`) and the release cut (`crew/scripts/release-cut.ts` `gateVerdict`). All three now also read CI at the commit through `ciAtHead`, via a small adapter, `lib/ci-head-checks.ts`, and keep the worse answer per check name. A rerun that passed still reads green, and an unreadable read is an error, never a pass. The release cut sets its own "Cut the release" run and the never-gating workflows aside by run id, so it no longer waits on itself.

## Blast radius

The change touches the three readers above and their tests. It is safe because each reader only adds rows and keeps the worst bucket per name, so no check that gated before stops gating. Three probes run against b86d26d confirm that an unreadable read is never green (script ran). pr-wait and the cut make more GitHub REST reads per poll, which is noted below as deferred.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests, review and docs</summary>

## Test Coverage

Coverage: 1 of 5 changed runtime files have no changed test naming them (docs/ship-policy.md). Step 7's test-writing reader was not run, because this head was shipped read-only.
Tests ran: free 1672 (files), carried from CI run 44048079219 at tree a562f654d396.

## Pre-Landing Review

No blocking findings. One read-only full review ran at b86d26d (specialists, red-team, adversarial, a second-model review on openai/gpt-6.1-sol and the targeted gate reader).
Second-model review: CLEAN, no findings.
Gate edits: 1 listed, 1 read, 0 findings — 0 kept, 0 restored, 0 open

## Deferred findings

All below the blocking floor. Each fails closed and none gives a false green. They stay on this PR.
- crew/scripts/release-cut.ts:166 (testing): gateVerdict's branch that fails closed on an unreadable every-attempt read has no test. A probe confirms it returns "cannot read its check runs".
- lib/pr-wait-github.ts:195 (testing): fetchChecks' transient GhError on an unknown read has no test. A probe confirms transient is true.
- lib/pr-wait-github.ts:195 (red-team, and adversarial #4 separately): permanent errors such as more than 1000 entries are retried as transient, so pr-wait spends about 10 minutes before it stops. A probe reproduces it.
- lib/ci-gate.ts:191 (adversarial): ci-gate returns ERROR on a short read inside its --wait window instead of retrying, and its FIX line points at gh auth.
- lib/pr-wait-github.ts:193 (adversarial): about 6 list reads per poll instead of 2.
- crew/scripts/release-cut.ts:164 (adversarial): the cut spends more of the workflow token's hourly limit per commit, which could delay stable.
- crew/scripts/release-cut.ts:169 (adversarial): a third-party commit status stuck at pending holds the cut. The changelog says this is intended.

## Exploratory QA

Three probes run against b86d26d (scratch, not committed), 3 passed: the release cut fails closed on an unreadable read; pr-wait throws a transient GhError on an incomplete read; an over-cap workflow-run list also throws a transient GhError.

## Documentation

**Status:** blocked. **Scope:** release diff be73938..b86d26d: docs/releases.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and the changelog fragment (docs roots docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md)

title: Stop the pre-merge check from accepting a half-finished run (GST-2194)
body:
The pre-merge check no longer accepts a record from a half-finished run. This serves the goal of only merging work whose secret scan and tests actually passed on the code that lands. ## What changed - `verifyPregate` refuses `PREGATE_INCOMPLETE` unless the record holds every registered check. Because `gstack-ship-queue ready` and `gstack-ship-receipt write` call it, they refuse too. The message names what is missing: `pregate.json holds checks=1 of 8 (missing: regen, secrets, …)`. Fail, incomplete, environment and uncleared-remote records still refuse under their own codes first. - The `PREGATE:` line prints `checks=N of M`. - A `--only` or `--stage preflight|tests` run keeps the checks it skipped from the record it replaces when head, tree, base commit, policy and registry all match, and prints `PREGATE_MERGED: kept …`. So the documented order (a full run, then `--stage tests --remote` at the same head) still verifies, and a same-tree rerun can no longer drop an earlier `secrets` failure. Guards-stage runs never merge, and nothing merges from the by-tree mirror (any probe run overwrites it). - docs/pregate.md describes the completeness rule and the same-tree merge (`#same-tree-checks`). docs/troubleshooting.md now names the missing-checks refusal under `PREGATE_INCOMPLETE` and says a fix commit needs a full run. The clone-lane mirror now stands in only for a complete record: run the full `gstack-pregate --remote` in the clone, or `clear --receipt`. ## Why The GSTA-461 audit (item 2) reproduced it. After a full run failed on `secrets` (`github.pat`), following pregate's own "rerun `--stage tests`" hint gave `PREGATE_VERIFY: ok` with the token still in HEAD. `gstack-pregate --only strays` (checks=1) also verified as a full pass. docs/pregate.md already called such runs "not evidence", but the code didn't enforce it. ## Blast radius Anything that verifies a pregate record: `gstack-pregate verify`, `gstack-ship-queue ready` (its own record and the by-tree mirror), `gstack-ship-receipt write`/carry, and the remote-gate stand-in. A record from a standalone `--stage tests --remote` with no full run at that head is now refused, which is the hole being closed. Test fixtures that wrote fake one-check records now write the full check list, including the crew queue tests (crew/test/ship-queue-train, -train-ops, -wave), which CI run 42718782737 showed failing at dbad74c (file:line read and the three files run 55 pass, 0 fail). ## Tests - New: test/pregate-partial-record.test.ts. Before the rebase, an inventory of 131 related files ran green apart from the fixtures updated here. ## Open notes (review round 1 at 24b3c73, all below the blocking floor, deferred) 1. `lib/ship-queue.ts`: `mirrorGap` and its comment still describe a tests-only mirror as enough. `ready` treats the missing-checks refusal as final and doesn't say why a mirror stopped standing in (red-team and adversarial agree). 2. `lib/pregate/index.ts`: `mergeSameTreeChecks` needs an exact base-commit match, so a moved origin/main keeps nothing and verify asks for a full rerun (fails closed). `coordinator-contract.ts:22` and `autoplan/DRIVER.md:157` still describe a staged rerun. 3. Repair hints in `lanes.ts:583`, `result-codes.ts:405/415`, `guards.ts:101` and troubleshooting.md still say to rerun one stage. After a fix commit that alone is refused, so they should name a full run. 4. No test yet for the obligation carry on a preflight rerun or for the base/policy mismatch guard. 5. Verify checks against the installed registry, so an upgrade that adds a check fails in-flight records closed. title: Stop a main merge from counting as the PR's own change, so a retake no longer needs a second full review (GST-2229)
body:
A base merge no longer counts as the PR's own change in two merge checks. This keeps a mechanical retake from costing a full second /ship, which serves the goal of cheap, trustworthy merge checks for every crew.

## What changed

**The receipt carry's scoped-review cap counts only the branch's own lines.** On founderstar#802, a base merge changed only the context lines around the PR's 22 reviewed, unchanged hunks in `scripts/core/game.gd` (+66/-11 at both heads). The scoped-review packet counted those context lines and the hunk headers toward its 200-line section cap, so the section came to about 205 lines and `gstack-ship-receipt carry` refused with `RECEIPT_CARRY_PRODUCT_CHANGED`. 1.94.39.0 (GST-1226) had stopped counting the base's +/- lines, but not the context lines inside the branch's hunks or in the base's change. Now `contextPacket` counts only the branch's own +/- lines in "Reviewed hunks" and "Current hunks", and nothing in "The base's change" until it passes the existing 2,000-line ceiling. All of it is still shown to the reader. A section whose branch +/- lines pass 200 still takes the full loop. This applies to carry and to `gstack-ship-release finish`, which share the packet.

**The review fix range counts only the PR's own change since `--range-base`.** On harness-evals#354, `gstack-review-plan` measured the fix range as `--range-base` to HEAD. A main merge had brought a 68-line bootstrap script and a `.gstack/pregate.json` edit into that range, so it read as gate class and the owner's grant printed `next=voices` instead of the one targeted-only read. The PR's own change was a changelog fragment, one docs line and one manifest line. The fix range, its gate scan, and the check for gate-class or executable edits after the last fix-check now read the commit `ownChangeSince` builds. That's the PR's own change after `--range-base`, the same change `gstack-ship-receipt write` already reads for targeted records (GST-1593). A gate-class edit in the PR's own change still escalates.

Why `ownChangeSince` rather than a merge's first parent or a blob match against main: it compares the PR's patch against its own merge base at both ends, so it gives the same answer whatever the number and order of merges and fixes in the range. It also replays main's change three-way for files both sides touched. A first-parent diff removes only one merge, and a blob match misses files both sides changed. One limit: it works per path, so in a file both main and the PR changed after the range base, main's lines still count.

## Why

"A base merge that only moves lines around a reviewed change forced a second full /ship" (founderstar#802), and on harness-evals#354 a main merge made the PR's tiny docs fix read as gate class, so the owner's grant re-reviewed code main had already shipped. Now both checks measure only what the PR itself changed, so a mechanical retake after a main merge gets the cheap path it was meant to get, while a PR's own large or gate-class edit still takes the full loop.

## Blast radius

Two callers change behaviour: `gstack-ship-receipt carry` and `gstack-ship-release finish` (they share `contextPacket` in lib/ship-patch.ts), and `gstack-review-plan`'s `--range-base` fix range and its `--post-review` carry check. Both only stop counting lines and paths that main already merged; when `ownChangeSince` can't build the PR's own change, the fix range reads as unread and the plan falls back to a full pass (bin/gstack-review-plan, read and confirmed by the red team and the native adversarial reviewer), and a section whose branch +/- lines pass 200 still refuses (test/ship-rereview-triggers.test.ts, run at a129c39c).

## Tests

- `test/ship-rereview-triggers.test.ts`:
  - The founderstar#802 shape: 22 unchanged hunks with both hunk sections over 200 lines. On main, carry refuses with the reported message.
  - 30 scattered base edits next to 4 branch hunks, whose context lines pass 200 in the base section. This also fails on main.
  - Both now reach `RECEIPT_CARRY_SCOPED_REVIEW`.
  - Hold: 60 hunks whose own +/- lines pass 200 are still refused.
- `test/review-plan-merged-range.test.ts`:
  - The harness-evals#354 shape. On main it prints `NEXT: stop`, the gate-class stop. Now it prints `NEXT: targeted` with one targeted reader.
  - Hold: the PR's own `pregate.json` edit after the merge still escalates.

## Places that still diff a range against HEAD, left unchanged

- `gstack-review-dispatch`: the scoped reader and the Red Team read `git diff <range-base>`, so after a merge they see main's content too. Changing that changes a review packet, which needs a preregistered no-loss replay first.
- `gstack-review-scope classify`: range hunks come from `range-base` to the working tree. This only decides where findings go, not escalation.
- `gstack-ship-receipt carry`: the re-check packet includes `git diff <receipt head> HEAD` for changed paths. It's packet text, not a decision.
- `gstack-ship-release finish`: the loop exception's `touchedPaths(fix_check.head, now)` can only widen which paths are accepted.
- `gstack-no-stop` already merges the base into `range-base` before it diffs.

Docs: `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` and `docs/review-policy.md` describe the new counting.

## Test Coverage

Coverage audit (Step 7, audit only, no tests generated): 5 of 7 changed code paths covered (71%), every covered path at ★★★.
- Covered: fix range excludes main's merged gate files (review-plan-merged-range.test.ts), the PR's own pregate.json edit still escalates, contextPacket ignores moved context lines and the base's change, own +/- over 200 still refused (ship-rereview-triggers.test.ts, 'GST-2229, founderstar#802').
- Gaps: `--post-review` carry after a base merge (rawSince/gateTagsOf on the own commit) has no test; the `ownChangeSince` null branch needs a seam (rejected).
Tests: 1778 → 1778 test files (+0 new from this run; the PR's own failing-first tests were already in the branch).
Tests ran: test carried from CI (free-tests at a129c39c; see Agent notes).

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 6 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 6 asked (0 fixed, 6 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted. None is above the blocking floor (no test failure, production break, or data/secret loss); all were skipped unattended with the reasons below and are open notes.

title: Let an owner's ruling clear new blockers that an extra review round found, so /ship can finish (GST-2251)
body:
When a granted fix-check finds a new blocker and the owner decides to ship it as a disclosed note, `/ship` can now finish. Before this, the owner's ruling was recorded but `gstack-ship-release finish` ignored it, so the only way out was another fix-check, which R51's two-round cap had already ruled out. This serves the shipping goal: an owner's decision at the round cap should end the loop without extra review rounds or hand edits around a gate. **What was broken.** The ship policy says an owner's ruling (`gstack-approvals rule`) closes a finding on a fix-check, and the fix-check then counts ([ship-policy.md#ruled-notes](docs/ship-policy.md#ruled-notes)). In practice a fix-check that finds a CRITICAL logs it `open` and the row `converged:false`, because the review skill sends a CRITICAL to the owner stop (review-army decision 3.5 → 2). Finish then refused that row in two ways. First, `reviewFreshness` rejected any non-converged row before it applied rulings. Second, rulings could close only `skipped`, `noted` or `deferred` findings, never `open` ones. So a ruling could never clear the stop it was built for. harness-evals#361 hit this with two CRITICALs the owner had accepted. **What changed.** - A ruling can now close an `open` finding as well as `skipped`, `noted` and `deferred` ones. Gate findings are still excluded. - A fix-check that stopped on findings binds at the one tree it read, as a clean read, once approved rulings cover every blocking finding on it. "Read one tree" means its binding is `incomplete` with the same start and end tree. Finish then routes the paths it read as `fix_checked` and prints every `RULED_NOTE:`. The receipt and PR body keep listing each `Ruled note:` line as before. - Any unruled finding marked blocking keeps the fix-check from binding, whatever its action, so ruling one open CRITICAL can't wave through a skipped blocker beside it (cross-family audit fix, f76ac74). - When a fix-check is not counted and still has unruled blocking findings, finish prints `FIX_CHECK_OPEN:`. That line names the fingerprints, the fix-check's commit and the `gstack-approvals rule` command, and says that a review-loop exception accepts edits after a fix-check, never its findings. #361 reached for that exception because nothing pointed at rulings. - These cases still refuse: a finding with no ruling, the lane's own claim in its review-log row, a ruling at a head outside the fix-check's range (listed as `not applied`), and any edit made after the fix-check head (it routes as behavior unless an exception accepts it). - Docs: ship-policy.md (ruled notes), review-policy.md (fix-check binding), a new troubleshooting entry `FIX_CHECK_OPEN`, and a changelog fragment. **Tests.** `test/ship-finish-ruled-notes.test.ts` adds four cases built from #361's sequence: a round-2 stop, a granted fix-check, two new `open` CRITICALs logged `converged:false`, the owner's exception at that head, and then the rulings. The tests cover binding after both rulings, staying unbound with one ruling of two, the lane's own claim and an out-of-range ruling closing nothing, and an edit after the fix-check head still stopping. All four failed before the fix. A fifth case, added in the review fix round (0115690b), shows that an open INFORMATIONAL finding next to two ruled CRITICALs keeps the fix-check from counting, names that finding, and lets the fix-check bind once it is ruled. A sixth case, added after a cross-family audit (f76ac74), shows that an unruled skipped blocking finding beside a ruled open CRITICAL keeps the row unbound and is named; it failed before the fix. The file passes 23/23 in finish's targeted lane at f76ac74. Full CI (free-tests run 42735521760) is green at this head. **Open notes (non-blocking, shipped as disclosed).** - When finish doesn't count a fix-check, `FIX_CHECK_OPEN` prints for every link in the chain, including earlier links that were handed on and fix-checks that failed for reasons other than unruled findings (for example a missing grant). The output is noisy but never wrong about what blocks. Raised in review pass 2 (red-team) and in pass 1 (red-team#2, adversarial-native#4). - The rule command that `FIX_CHECK_OPEN` prints contains the placeholder `--words ''`. Inside single quotes, `\'` doesn't escape the quote, so pasting the placeholder as-is breaks the shell line. The owner replaces it with their own words anyway. Raised in review pass 2 (red-team). - A ruling made at a chain boundary (`--head` set to link N's commit) also falls inside link N+1's range, so it can clear that link as well. Shipped as a note on the Captain's call (pass 1, adversarial-native#5). - A `converged:false` fix-check row that claims `action:"fixed"` on an unchanged tree can bind as a ruled stop. Shipped as a note on the Captain's call (pass 1, adversarial-native#6). - Some things still hold a row open without being named by `FIX_CHECK_OPEN`: gate findings, CRITICALs whose action is outside the rulable set, and an `issues_found` count above the number of logged findings. This predates the change (pass 2, red-team, informational). - A finding logged `fixed` or `auto-fixed` still carries `blocking:true`, and gate findings that were kept or restored do too. If such a finding has no ruling, it now keeps a fix-check row unbound. Nobody can rule on it, and `FIX_CHECK_OPEN` doesn't name it, so finish prints only the generic reason. It fails closed. Shipped as is on the Captain's call, and narrowing it goes to GST-2273, with harness-evals#361's row as the test case (fix-check reader on f76ac74, informational). - Review freshness compares only the end trees, so an edit that is made and then undone (tree A, then B, then A again) reads as unchanged. This predates the change. It's a note only, routed to GST-2273 (cross-family audit, Q5). ## Approvals Plan: exempt: bug fix with failing-first tests; R65 says bug fixes need no plan review
Agent notes - Lane GSTA-485 (GST-2251, for HARN-65 and HARN-1). gstack 1.98.0.0, base 01e3980. - Scope: `lib/review-evidence.ts` (`RULABLE`, `reviewFreshness`) and `lib/ship-release.ts` (`fixChecked`). This PR doesn't touch lib/review-depth.ts, lib/review-grant.ts, the ship skeleton's Step 11.5 or bin/gstack-review-plan. Only finish passes rulings to `reviewFreshness`; `gstack-review-read` and Step 11.5 call it without them, so their behavior doesn't change. - Focused local checks: typecheck clean, plus 146/148 adjacent review and ship tests and 384/384 troubleshooting-anchor and changelog-fragment tests. The 2 failures hit the 5 s per-test timeout on this 4-core machine. `shared-libs-snapshot-check` "nonconverged passes…" also times out on unchanged main (5100 ms). `review-notes-only-pass` "negative controls" passed on main at 4637 ms. CI is the full run. - Review: plan printed full depth after `--declare-risk policy`. Pass 1 ran the batched specialist (testing, security, state machines), the red team, adversarial-native and the outside voice openai/gpt-6.1-sol (CLEAN). One fix round, 0115690b: `unresolvedFinding` now drives the `FIX_CHECK_OPEN` listing, the full rule command is printed, and one test was added. It fixes adversarial-native#1–#3, specialist-batched#1 and red-team#1. Pass 2 ran the specialist (no findings) and the red team (informational notes only, listed above). - Cross-family audit hold (Q1) on 004f843: fixed in f76ac74 (`holdsOpen` in lib/review-evidence.ts, used by finish's clearing check and `FIX_CHECK_OPEN`), with a failing-first test. One scoped fix-check on that delta under the Captain's rule-11 grant a-56a2b6ddaabe (plan: `next=fix-check dispatches=1`). One reader returned a single informational finding, listed above, and the row is logged clean and bound at f76ac74. Docs re-audit ship-4260-docs-2 at f76ac74: current, no edits.

title: Catch secrets split across lines in UTF-16 files and stop deleted binaries from blocking pushes (GST-2261)
body:
This closes two gaps #4243 left in the secret check and the pre-push hook. Both are security fixes that serve the project's goal of never pushing a credential.

## What changed

**Secrets split across two lines of UTF-16 text are now caught.** #4243 reads a file git calls binary three ways (as bytes, and as little- and big-endian UTF-16) but put all three readings side by side on each line. So the line holding `aws_secret_access_key:` ended with the letter-spaced byte reading, and the rule that looks for the key on the next line lost its keyword. An AWS secret key under its YAML key in a UTF-16LE or UTF-16BE file passed both guards (the repro table in #4243's "Open advisory notes", item 1). `scannableText` becomes `scannableReadings`, which returns each distinct reading as a whole text with the file's line breaks. Pregate's `secrets` check runs gstack-redact once per reading, and the hook scans one part per reading, both keeping the file's line numbers. Plain-text files still have one reading and are scanned once, as before. A token that several readings of one file find is reported once.

**Deleting a large binary no longer blocks a push.** With `--text`, a deleted binary's old bytes filled the hook's 64 MiB diff buffer, so removing an already-pushed 70 MiB file (or moving it to Git LFS) failed with `git diff failed (status=killed/overflow)`. The hook's `git diff` and per-commit `git show` now pass `--irreversible-delete`, so a deleted file prints only its header. A delete can't add a secret. Adding a binary over the limit still blocks. A *replaced* binary's old bytes still count: git has no flag that drops a modification's preimage (`-B` merges the broken pair back into a rewrite that prints the old lines), so that stays a documented limit. Pregate already skipped deletions and is unchanged there.

No screenshots: this change has no visible surface, and the tests below show the behavior.

## Why

An AWS secret key stored under its YAML key in a UTF-16 file got past both the pre-push hook and pregate, which is the leak these guards exist to stop. Separately, deleting a large binary that was already pushed made the hook fail, so people could not clean up their repository. Now the split key is blocked in every encoding and the delete pushes clean.

## Blast radius

The change touches the secret check in lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts and the pre-push hook bin/gstack-redact-prepush, which imports it; lib/pregate/index.ts is untouched. Plain-text files still get exactly one reading, so their scan is the same as before, and the new tests fail on main at 76e2d3f and pass here (script ran, plus the carried CI run 42731728299).

## Summary

The secret check and the pre-push hook let a key slip through when a UTF-16 file split it across two lines, and they blocked the push that deletes a large binary. Each reading of a binary file is now scanned as its own text with its line breaks, so the key and its value stay together. Deleted files leave the hook's diff, so removing a big binary no longer fills the buffer. A token that several readings find is listed once, and an allowlisted token never hides a different one.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage. The tests were written first and failed on main at 76e2d3f:
- `test/pregate-secrets-source-context.test.ts`: the split AWS pair fails in plain text, UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE.
- `test/redact-prepush-hook.test.ts`: the same pair blocks the push in all three encodings; adding a 70 MiB binary still blocks on the buffer limit, and deleting it pushes clean.

Tests ran: test 1658 (files, carried from CI run 42731728299/1 at tree 54dc12485f73)

## Pre-Landing Review

Full panel (security change): two passes, a fix-check on the round-2 fix and a targeted secret-class read. Every blocking finding was fixed on the branch; each fix commit names its finding in a `Review-Finding:` trailer. The targeted secret read at 6bd89e1 found nothing. Outside review: CLEAN.

Pre-existing on main; the scan still runs.

title: Make gstack's shell locks hold when mkdir reports a race it lost (GST-2247)
body:
gstack's shell locks now hold on Ubuntu 26.04, where `mkdir` can report success after another process has already created the directory. Every lock now goes through one helper, so the kernel lets exactly one process take it.

## Summary

- A new sourced helper, `gstack_lock_take` in `bin/gstack-lock.sh`. It runs `mkdir` only to make the directory and ignores its exit status. The holder is whoever creates the owner file with the shell's noclobber redirect, which opens it with O_EXCL. It returns 0 when taken, 1 when held, 2 when the directory can't be created, and 3 when the owner file can't be written. On 3 the file and the directory are removed again.
- All 26 places that used `mkdir` as a lock now call the helper. Each keeps its own waiting, stale-lock recovery and release.
- The Claude Code wrapper's copied runtime ships the helper, and `bin/gstack-render-claude.sh` sources it itself.
- New tests cover the change. A race test uses a `mkdir` shim that behaves like the uutils one. A disk-full case runs under `ulimit -f 0`. A source guard fails on any new lock that trusts a bare `mkdir`.

## Why

Ubuntu 26.04 ships Rust coreutils (uutils) as `mkdir`, and GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` does too from 2026-11-09. That `mkdir` exits 0 even when another process created the directory a moment earlier, so two processes could both think they held a lock. With the real uutils 0.8.0 `mkdir`, the old pattern let two holders in on 132 of 300 races. The helper let in exactly one on every race. Eight parallel `gstack-config set` calls lost keys on main in 2 of 5 trials, and in 0 of 5 with this change.

## Blast radius

This covers every gstack shell path that takes a lock. Those are the session-start updater, `gstack-upgrade`, `./setup`, `gstack-config`, the Claude render, leases, freeze, brain sync, the Codex probe and /setup-gbrain. With GNU `mkdir` the behavior doesn't change, and no caller's stale-lock rules changed.
**Status:** current. Every authored doc changed since base 18652ccc matches the new `gstack_lock_take` helper, so no edits were needed.

**Scope:** committed, staged, unstaged and new content on `capy/shell-locks-hold-when-mkdir-lies-gst-2247`, compared with base 18652ccc after the merge of main. Checked against `bin/gstack-lock.sh`, `bin/gstack-upgrade`, `bin/gstack-session-update` and `bin/gstack-lease`.

**Documentation health:**
- `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md`: Current. The `.setup-gbrain.lock.d` row correctly describes the O_EXCL pid-file lock, and the merge with main is clean.
- `docs/capy-install.md`: Current. The lease lock description matches `gstack-lease`.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Current. The new `#shell-locks` section and the `.setup-lock` recovery note match the helper and the refusal text in `gstack-upgrade`.
- `setup-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl`: Current. The lock snippet sources the helper and releases with `rm -rf`. The generated `SKILL.md` matches it.
- `changelog.d/capy-shell-locks-hold-when-mkdir-lies-gst-2247.md`: Current. Read only; not edited.

**Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none, since no diagrams are affected.

## Test plan

- [x] CI free-tests run 42747053716 at efac08c passed: 1660 files, carried by the ship gate.
- [x] macOS and Windows lanes at efac08c passed in runs 42747053716, 42737904127 and 42737903818.
- [x] Locally, the gstack-lock-race, gstack-ff-update pin and mkdir-lock-guard tests passed: 42 pass, 0 fail.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/windows-setup-e2e.yml:47` setup now hard-requires bin/gstack-lock.sh and exits 1 when it is missing. It is also the single arbiter for every install-path lock on Git Bash: the setup Chromium and deps locks, gstack-config, the install registry, the render lock, settings-hook and session-update. But it is missing from both the `paths:` trigger list and the install-files PATHS list that decide whether the Windows setup e2e jobs run. Its consumers are all listed, so this PR triggers the jobs. A later PR that changes only the helper, for example its noclobber or MSYS behaviour, would skip the Windows install e2e and be covered only by windows-smoke.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-lock.sh:40` Under zsh the new 3> owner-file open prints 'file exists' to stderr when the take loses a real race (rc stays 1); bash, dash and busybox stay quiet.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-browser-ensure:89` Empty or missing pid is taken over at once, so a holder between mkdir and its pid write loses the lock (same overlap rate as main).
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-browser-ensure:91` Loop spins forever on rc 2/3 because continue precedes the tries counter.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-developer-profile` During an upgrade, old releases' rmdir cannot clear the new takeover and .break locks, which now hold a pid file.

- Skipped under approval a-efc6d50031d4: `test/gstack-lease.test.ts:555`. The `chmod a-w` setup doesn't block writes for root, so the test would fail when run as root.
- Skipped under approval a-efc6d50031d4: `bin/gstack-browser-ensure:89`. The wait loop treats return codes 2 and 3 as contention and never reaches its timeout. Return code 2 behaves the same on main.
- `bin/gstack-ff-update` must run standalone, so it carries a byte-identical inline copy of `gstack_lock_take`. A test in `test/gstack-ff-update.test.ts` fails if the two drift.
- Five tests that hooked into the old `mkdir` call now observe the same behavior through the new path: codex-probe-cache, gstack-settings-hook-symlink, gstack-lease, session-update-autostash and setup-gbrain-fixture.
- 17 test fixtures that copy single bin scripts now also copy `bin/gstack-lock.sh`.
- Follow-up after the freeze: `windows-setup-e2e.yml` paths should list `bin/gstack-lock.sh`.

title: Brain sync catches JSON-escaped secrets, and its pre-commit hook checks every family (GST-2263)
body:
Brain sync's secret scan now catches secrets hidden behind JSON escapes, and the pre-commit hook in `~/.gstack` checks the same secret families as the sync. This serves gstack's goal of never pushing a user's credentials to their artifacts repo. ## What changed - **Escaped secrets are held.** A hand-written learnings or timeline row could hide a Stripe key behind `\u` escapes, or an auth header inside an escaped JSON string, and the scan pushed it. The scan still reads the whole staged diff as before (file names, unchanged lines around each edit, added and removed lines), and now also scans each added line with every escaped JSON string decoded in place (so an escaped key or an escaped `Bearer` still lines up with its value), and again for each decoded string on its own, including a JSON document stored as a string value. The scan's `git diff` calls pass `--no-color --no-ext-diff`. - **One scanner for sync and the pre-commit hooks.** The scanner moved out of `bin/gstack-brain-sync` into `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py`. `gstack-artifacts-init` and `gstack-brain-restore` copy it into `.git/hooks/` beside the pre-commit hook they write, and the hook runs that copy. A manual `git commit` of a Stripe live key, a Slack or npm token, or a database URL with a password is now refused, where the old hook knew only six families. The hook refuses the commit when its scanner is missing or fails, where the old one let a commit through when `git diff` failed. - **Docs.** `docs/gbrain-sync.md` lists all ten families, says the scan reads the whole staged diff and decodes JSON strings in added lines, and says how to refresh a hook written by an older gstack. ## Tests Written first and failing before their fixes: an escaped Stripe key row and an escaped auth-header row are held (0b1c484, failing on main 97b796e), each hook refuses a Stripe live key, and a key renamed to `authorization` above an unchanged Bearer value and a file named after an AWS key are held (3d1f03b, failing at c4f2f86 and passing on main). The test that an edit next to an already-pushed database URL syncs was dropped with the added-lines-only scan. The existing hook test checks that both bins call the shared scanner, and its Bearer-header commit is still refused. ## Blast radius The change touches the brain-sync scan call sites, the hook bodies that `gstack-artifacts-init` and `gstack-brain-restore` write, and the new scanner file; brain sync's own commits run the hook, so the hook keeps a scanner copy beside it rather than a path into the install, which a test proves by deleting the install that wrote the hook and committing (script ran). Hooks already on users' machines keep their old body until `gstack-artifacts-init` runs again. No network, permission, workflow, install-script or dependency changes. ## Why These are gaps #4247 left open, plus the hooks that #4247's lane flagged: a secret could reach the user's artifacts remote by being escaped, and a manual commit in `~/.gstack` skipped four of the ten families. An earlier version of this PR also scanned only added lines; an audit showed that let a key renamed above an unchanged value, or a secret in a file name, through, so the whole-diff scan main already had is kept. ## Summary Someone who pasted a Stripe key into a learnings row with `\u0051` in place of one letter, or kept an auth header inside an escaped JSON string, had it pushed to their artifacts repo, because the scan only read raw text. Now escaped secrets are held, and the pre-commit hook in `~/.gstack` refuses the same secrets the sync does. It keeps its own copy of the scanner, so moving or upgrading gstack does not break brain sync's own commits. A file that already holds a flagged line is still held on every edit, as on main. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. New tests in `test/brain-sync.test.ts`, each failing before its fix: a `\u`-escaped Stripe key and an auth header inside an escaped JSON string are held; an escaped auth key and an escaped `Bearer` prefix are held; a key renamed to `authorization` above an unchanged Bearer value is held; a file named after an AWS key is held; each hook refuses a Stripe live key; each hook refuses a commit when its scanner is missing or fails; the hook still scans after the install that wrote it is deleted. Tests ran: bun run test 1658 (files; carried from CI run 42747093393) ## Pre-Landing Review Gate class, full depth, as `gstack-review-plan` printed it: pass 1 (specialists, red-team, adversarial, outside voice, targeted), one fix-check, then one fix round granted by the Captain after two High Step 11 voices, closed by a scoped fix-check. A later audit found that scanning only added lines missed a renamed key and a secret file name; the Captain granted one more scoped fix-check at 3d1f03b (approval a-b99494c1df99), which came back clean. No blocking findings remain. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=2 deferred=0 noted=8 fixed=3 scope=frozen unbound=2 ledgers_read=6 fix_checks=3 dispatches=4 Gate edits: none detected (3 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Outside review: completed (openai/gpt-6.1-sol); its one High finding is fixed in 9bc00ca. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `docs/gbrain-sync.md:167` The doc says a held file stays held "until you remove the line or skip the file", but removing the line does not clear the hold, because removed lines are scanned too; only `--skip-file` clears it (same as main). - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py:133` In gate mode the decoded forms of added lines are joined across files, so a contrived pair of lines in two files can hold the whole sync without naming a file. It fails closed. - INFORMATIONAL Scanning unchanged lines means a file that already holds a flagged line is held on every edit until `--skip-file`, as on main. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-sync:585` A merge commit that rebuild_conflicted_snapshots concludes runs the wider hook against remote-side lines, so a new-family secret already on the remote can stall the merge-retry path. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py` The JSON-string regex is quadratic on a line with thousands of unterminated quotes. - INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d` Nothing migrates hooks written by an older gstack; rerunning `gstack-artifacts-init` refreshes one, and the scanner copy beside the hook updates only then. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py` A doubly escaped key inside a JSON document stored as a string is still not matched; in-place decoding does not run inside the nested decode. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py` Decoding uses strict JSON, so a string holding a raw tab or an invalid escape is scanned raw only. ## Exploratory QA Gate-mode smoke on the scanner at 9bc00ca: a clean line exits clean, a `\u`-escaped Stripe key is held, and an auth header inside an escaped string is held. The context-line probe from that run no longer applies, since unchanged lines are scanned again. ## Eval Results Paid evals skipped: `eval:select` picked about 118 behavioral probes through `bin/gstack-brain-sync` and `bin/gstack-brain-restore`, far over this PR's $10 cap, and no paid case references the new scanner. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Issues Refs v1/adversarial-native#1 Refs v1/outside-voice#1 ## Documentation **Scope:** brain-sync secret-scan changes on `fix/brain-sync-scan-escaped-secrets-and-added-lines`: the new `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py`, the whole-diff scan with JSON strings in added lines decoded, and the pre-commit hook that `gstack-artifacts-init` and `gstack-brain-restore` install. The docs1 audit covered `docs/gbrain-sync.md`, `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/gbrain-quick-tour.md`, the top-level docs and the changelog fragment at c4f2f86; the audit fix at 3d1f03b then changed `docs/gbrain-sync.md` and the fragment. Documentation exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-10 via GST-2263: docs/gbrain-sync.md and the changelog fragment changed after the docs1 audit; the lane rechecked both against the shipped scan behavior **Debt:** `docs/gbrain-sync.md:167` overstates how a hold clears (see Review notes). `docs/gbrain-quick-tour.md` gives a short list of blocked secret types that doesn't name the new families. ## Test plan - [x] bun run test: 1658 test files passed in CI run 42747093393 at this tree (carried) - [x] Targeted brain-sync tests at 3d1f03b: 120 pass, 0 fail; the renamed-key and AWS-file-name repros fail at c4f2f86 and pass on main - [x] Trial merge with #4179: clean merge of #4179 at 4d6a9357 onto 3d1f03b (merge base aa46032f, 0 conflicts, tree 4a8a7ae8), typecheck 0, focused brain-sync, artifacts-init, worktree-advance and removals tests 149 pass, 0 fail
