title: gstack-brain-cache: single-page entity lookups always miss (reads `page.body` from `gbrain get --json`; mixed-case slug)
body:
## Summary

`bin/gstack-brain-cache` never returns a digest for single-page entities (`product`, `brand`, `competitive-intel`, `user-profile`) even when the page exists in the brain. The planning skills then print "no product digest available yet" on every run, and `brain-cache/_meta.json` shows `last_attempt` timestamps with an empty `last_refresh`. Nothing surfaces the failure.

## Cause

`fetchSimplePage` (around line 520 on `main`) does:

```ts
const result = spawnGbrain(['get', slug, '--json'], { timeout: 10_000 });
if (result.status !== 0) return null;
const page = JSON.parse(result.stdout) as { body?: string; title?: string };
if (!page?.body) return null;
return compressPage(slug, page.title || slug, page.body);
```

Two mismatches with what `gbrain get` returns:

1. **Field name.** It reads the page text from `page.body`.
   - gbrain 0.46.x: `gbrain get <slug> --json` prints the page as markdown (frontmatter + body), not JSON, so `JSON.parse` throws and the function returns `null`. *(Observed live.)*
   - gbrain 0.60.x: `--json` does print JSON, but in `get_page` results `body` is the name of the read mode (`auto` / `full` / `none` / `outline` / `window`), and the text is carried in `compiled_truth` / `timeline` / `content` (`src/core/ops/get-page-body.ts`, `src/cli/page-render.ts`). So `page.body` is either absent or a mode string, never the page text. *(From reading the 0.60.626.0 source; not run live.)*

2. **Slug case.** The slug is built from the project slug as-is, e.g. `gstack/product/<Owner-Name>-<repo>`, which keeps the GitHub owner's capitalisation. gbrain lowercases path-derived slugs (`pathToSlug` in `src/core/sync.ts`), and on 0.46.x `gbrain get` with the mixed-case slug returns `page_not_found` while the lowercase slug resolves. *(Observed live on 0.46.x; not checked on 0.60.x.)*

## Repro (gbrain 0.46.29, gstack 1.98.0.0, macOS, Postgres engine)

1. In a repo whose project slug contains capitals (`gstack-slug` → `SLUG=Some-Org-some-repo`), create the page `gstack/product/Some-Org-some-repo` in the brain (`gbrain put` stores it as `gstack/product/some-org-some-repo`).
2. `gstack-brain-cache refresh --entity product --project Some-Org-some-repo` → `failed to refresh product`
3. `gstack-brain-cache get product --project Some-Org-some-repo` → `(missing: brain unreachable; no cache available)`
4. `gbrain get gstack/product/some-org-some-repo` returns the page, so the brain is reachable and the page exists.

## Expected

A digest for the product page, or a message that distinguishes "page not found" from "brain unreachable".

## Suggested fix

- Read the text from the fields `get_page` actually returns (`compiled_truth`, falling back to `content`), and tolerate non-JSON output from older gbrain.
- Lowercase the slug before the lookup (or resolve it via `gbrain` slug resolution).
- Report `page_not_found` separately from an unreachable brain so the "missing" message is accurate.
- The existing brain-cache tests appear to stub `gbrain`; a fixture with a real `get --json` payload would catch this.

`gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts` parses `get --json` too but only checks `source_id` and `slug`, so it is not affected by the field name.

title: Let an owner's grant swap the second full review for one short recheck, and say which grant field to fix (GST-2244)
body:
An owner's grant of one scoped fix-check now works after review round 1, and a grant row the review planner can't use says exactly which field is wrong. This fixes a bug that blocks crews: lanes have been paying for a full second review pass after the owner already approved a cheaper fix-check. ## What was broken - **Round-1 grants were ignored.** On gbrain #8839 the owner granted "one scoped fix-check ... no rerun of Steps 9 to 11.5" after round 1. `gstack-review-plan --grant` accepted the grant row, but the planner only honored a grant at the stop after round 2, so it still printed `NEXT: full`. The lane ran the fix-check by hand. Then Step 11.5 refused with **Review records missing or mismatched**, because Step 11's record and the fix-check were on different trees. - **Refusals didn't say what to fix.** A grant row whose scope said `review_loop_exception 907107a on #4243` was refused with one catch-all sentence about the stop head, so lanes had to ask what string the tool wanted. ## What changed - **A grant after round 1 replaces round 2's pass.** `--pass 1 --last full --range-base --grant ` now prints `NEXT: fix-check (the owner's grant replaces round 2's full pass with one scoped fix-check on the fix range ...)` in place of round 2's full or scoped pass (full panel; the lean panel already plans a fix-check there). Step 11 still runs after the loop, so gate-class code still gets its voices before any owner stop. - **One grant still buys one fix-check.** If a `review-fix-check` row was logged after the grant was recorded, passing the same grant again plans as if no grant were given. A clean fix-check still prints `done`, and a stop needs a new grant. - **Step 11.5 binds a granted fix-check at its own tree** when its `range_base..commit` holds Step 11's native commit. Every change after Step 11's read is in the granted range, so the fix-check's tree becomes the reviewed tree. The ship skeleton gets one sentence. Review-army decision 3.5 carries the detail. - **Grant binding moved into `lib/review-grant.ts`**, and a refused row (exit 3) names one cause: the row isn't in this branch's record (the message prints the record path), the outcome isn't approved, the row says `review_loop_exception` instead of `review_loop_grant`, the row names no token or no sha, the sha isn't a commit in this clone, or the commit isn't the stop head. In that last case the message prints the head it expected and the row to write. `review_loop_grant on #` binds with a short or full sha. - **Docs**: `docs/review-policy.md` (the grant rule, a new transitions row, a `#review-loop-grant` anchor), `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` (a new `#review-plan-grant-refused` entry, plus a note under the 11.5 mismatch entry), `gstack-review-plan --help`, and a changelog fragment. ## Tests - `test/review-plan-grant-binding.test.ts` replays #8839 with the same commit layout: pass 1's PASS_HEAD, then a guard commit (Step 11's tree), then the fix (the fix-check's tree), with the grant naming the guard commit. It printed `NEXT: full` before this change. It also covers short and full shas, every refusal cause, the spent-grant path and the Step 11.5 sentence. - Existing expectations that pinned the old catch-all message, the GST-1676 below-cap line and the GST-967 invariant's set of owed grants were updated to the new rule. Their no-grant cases are still asserted.
Agent notes - GST-2244, lane GSTA-481. Evidence from GBRA-399: org drive `handoffs/gst-2244/`. - The Captain ruled that CREW rule 15's paid no-loss replay does not apply: this planner change restores documented grant behavior, runs only under an owner's recorded grant, and has test coverage. `bun run eval:select` selects no quality judge for the Step 11.5 prose; the parity suite passes. - Finish (Step 16) is unchanged on purpose. After a granted fix-check binds at its own tree, finish may print an informational `FIX_CHECK: not counted (range_base … does not hold the reviewed tree)`. Nothing changed after review, so nothing routes. - The ship skeleton had 3 bytes of headroom. Step 11.5 item 2 was tightened to fit instead of raising `maxSkeletonBytes`. The size ledger is recorded (`test/size-ledger/ship/honor-owner-grant-after-round-1.json`) and the goldens regenerated. - The new test is excluded from the Windows-safe subset by the existing bin/ shebang pattern, like `test/review-plan-cli.test.ts`. - Rebased onto 490bbd5, after #4259 (3183120) landed. The rebase was clean. - Reviewer pins (test/fixtures/review-pins) name two free, deterministic no-loss records (Captain-approved, no paid run). `GST-2244` (lib/review-depth.ts) compares main's `nextStep` with the new one over 2,949,120 histories: 0 differences without a grant, and 19,200 with a grant, all of them round-1 full or scoped steps turned into one scoped fix-check. `GST-2244-briefs` (ship/sections/review-army.md) shows every reviewer brief is byte-identical, so only decision 3.5's lead instructions changed. - Round 1's red-team CRITICAL (a used grant could buy a second fix-check at `--pass 1 --last full`) was fixed in 098bc93. The two CI fixes (Step 11.5's `review_binding.*` fields and the repins) landed after round 2 under the Captain's grant of one scoped fix-check.

title: Stop gstack-uninstall deleting nested worktrees, locked worktrees and a .gstack repo (GST-2268)
body:
`gstack-uninstall` no longer deletes work that #4241 still lost on main: a worktree nested inside another `.gstack-worktrees/` checkout, a locked worktree, a submodule commit that exists nowhere else, a `.gstack/` that is its own git repo (in any host's install, Cursor and Gemini included), and a worktree edited while the confirmation prompt waits. This serves the install goal: removing gstack must never take a user's unsaved work with it.

## What changed

![A locked lane under --force-worktrees: main deletes it, this PR keeps it and exits 2](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/SSL0PHhrkvjzIURTMWQohqj76XTb2pBqTvAdQEkxgjI.png)

A locked lane under `--force-worktrees`. Main deletes it and exits 0. This PR keeps it and exits 2.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: A locked lane under --force-worktrees: main deletes it, this PR keeps it and exits 2</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ gstack-uninstall --force --force-worktrees   # this PR, same fixture
+gstack-uninstall: refusing to delete <fixture>/proj/.gstack-worktrees/run-1/lane-1: it is locked (git worktree lock)
+fix: commit the work to a branch or stash it, unlock a locked worktree with git worktree unlock <path>, re-run with --keep-state to keep every worktree, or re-run with --force-worktrees to delete the unlocked ones anyway
+exit 2 | locked lane kept: True | still registered: 1
-$ gstack-uninstall --force --force-worktrees   # main 490bbd5, a lane locked with git worktree lock
-exit 0 | locked lane kept: False | still registered: 1
 
~~~

</details>

- **Nested worktrees are checked.** The checkout walk used to stop at the first `.git`, so a worktree created inside a lane was deleted with its uncommitted edits and exit 0. Every checkout under `.gstack-worktrees/` is now listed and checked.
- **Submodules keep their own commits.** A submodule inside a clean lane goes with the lane only when every commit its refs reach is on a remote-tracking branch. Otherwise the uninstall stops, because those commits live in the lane's git folder and nowhere else.
- **Locked worktrees are kept.** A worktree locked with `git worktree lock` stops the uninstall (exit 2) even with `--force-worktrees`, and the fix line says to run `git worktree unlock <path>`.
- **A `.gstack/` that is its own git repo is kept**, with a message saying why. If it sits inside a gstack install that is about to be removed (Claude, Codex, Factory, Kiro, Cursor, OpenCode, Copilot, Antigravity or Gemini), the uninstall stops instead of deleting it with the install.
- **Every check runs before anything is deleted, and again after the prompt.** If a checkout changed while the prompt waited, the folder is kept and uninstall exits 2.
- **The manual steps are safe.** docs/uninstall.md no longer says `rm -rf .gstack .gstack-worktrees`. It removes only what git ignores, and only worktrees that pass the same checks.

## Why

GST-2268 listed the losses #4241 left on main: "Nested git worktrees inside a deleted root are removed unchecked", a locked worktree, a `.gstack` repo with unpushed commits, and the check-then-prompt race. After this change, a plain uninstall stops and names each checkout it would lose, and `--force-worktrees` still never deletes a locked one.

## Blast radius

Only `bin/gstack-uninstall` behavior changes. Nothing else in the repo calls it, and the one new outcome is exit 2 with the folder kept, so a run that used to delete a checkout now refuses instead. Evidence: test/uninstall.test.ts ran 54 of 54 at 59e9043, and CI's free suite passed at this head (run 42772416922).

## Summary

People who uninstall gstack lost unsaved work hidden one level down, such as a worktree inside a lane, a submodule's local commits, or a locked worktree under `--force-worktrees`. The uninstall now checks each checkout on disk before deleting anything. It checks again after the prompt. It keeps a `.gstack/` that holds its own repository, in every host's install. The manual removal steps in the docs follow the same rules. The last commit only splits a run-on sentence in the release note.

## Test Coverage

Each item has a failing-first test in test/uninstall.test.ts. The Cursor-install case added in review exits 0 and loses the `.gstack/` repo before the fix, and exits 2 after it.

Tests ran: free 1659 (files, carried from CI run 42772416922)

## Pre-Landing Review

A fresh /ship at 94ecf9c ran the printed plan. Pass 1 dispatched a batched specialist (testing, security, state machines, red team). It found one blocking data loss: the `.gstack/` guard checked only four of the nine host installs the script deletes. 59e9043 fixed it, with a test. Pass 2 re-read the fix range with a red team and a fix-check. Step 11 added a Claude adversarial reader and an outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol). The outside voice raised two findings that the owner ruled disclosed notes, listed below. Round 2 of 2 was the last; there was no third fix round. The commit after review edits only the changelog fragment, which routes as metadata.

- **Newline in a locked worktree's path (ruled note).** `bin/gstack-uninstall:162-166` reads `git worktree list --porcelain` without `-z`, so a locked worktree whose path contains a newline is not seen as locked, and `--force-worktrees` deletes it. It needs a worktree someone deliberately created and locked with a newline in its path. Main deletes every locked worktree under that flag, so this is no regression. Tracked in GST-2303, with the other remaining uninstall paths.
- **Clean nested submodule refused (ruled note).** `bin/gstack-uninstall:202` refuses a clean submodule nested inside another submodule as an unregistered checkout. The uninstall stops and deletes nothing.

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `docs/uninstall.md:77` The manual cleanup loop in the docs treats a git error as clean.
- INFORMATIONAL `test/uninstall.test.ts:1042` The failing-worktree-list test shim runs command -v git, which hangs under a PATH-searching git wrapper.

title: Stop holding ready comments when carried GitHub Actions run numbers look like phone numbers
body:
Posting a ready comment after carrying passing GitHub Actions checks no longer stops on a false phone-number warning for the run ids printed on its summary line. This keeps unattended shipping moving without weakening phone-number detection in prose or malformed entries.

## What Changed

- **`lib/redact-patterns.ts` (`isCiRunIdentifier`)**: Recognize 11- and 12-digit GitHub Actions run ids inside `ci_carried=<name>:<id>/<attempt>[,...]` summary lists when bounded by `:` before the id and `/<attempt>` (1–3 digits) after it, while still flagging bare numbers, 10- or 13-digit values, missing `/attempt` suffixes, `+`-prefixed numbers, and phone-shaped digits inside `<name>` or elsewhere on the line.
- **`docs/troubleshooting.md`**: Document the `ci_carried=` summary-line exemption alongside `runs=<id>/<attempt>`.
- **`test/redact-context-exemptions.test.ts` & `test/gstack-post.test.ts`**: Add scanner table tests and an end-to-end `gstack-post pr-comment` test covering `receiptSummaryLine` across `public` and `private` repositories plus negative boundary controls.

Fixes #4221

title: Review collector reads JSON readers as JSON only and re-asks prose it can't read (GST-2237)
body:
The review collector now reads the five JSON readers' replies as JSON only, re-asks a prose reply it could not read instead of calling it clean, and counts an unknown severity as a blocker. This keeps /ship's review gate from inventing blockers that cost owner rulings (#4208, ALPH-93, ALPH-11) and from passing a real finding it dropped. **JSON readers collect only JSON.** The specialists, the batched specialist, the Red Team, the targeted reader and fix-check already must answer with one JSON object per finding or `NO FINDINGS`. Their prose (coverage notes, a summary of their own JSON) is no longer read for severity words, so "Critical paths (checkout, refund) are covered" or "I found nothing at the blocking floor" can't become a CRITICAL. Their JSON now collects in any layout: pretty-printed (a lowercase `"critical"` used to vanish), nested, in an array or code fence, or cut off mid-line. **Unread prose fails closed.** A prose voice's reply whose only clean marker is the `Recommendation:` line, that collected no finding but names a severity word, FIXABLE, a file:line or `VERDICT: FINDINGS`, is now `COLLECT_NOT_REVIEWED ... reason=prose_not_collected` and verify reports `NOT_REVIEWED`. The audit's `1. [Fixable] lib/pay.ts:40 charges the card twice…` reply used to count as a clean review. Unstructured prose in such a reply collects only next to a structured finding, so the outside voice's "Critical paths … are covered" reply is re-asked instead of becoming a blocker that judgment can't lower. An explicit `NO FINDINGS` stays clean, and in that reply the native voice's FIXABLE counts only as a tag, so "the two FIXABLE items from pass 1; both are fixed" no longer collects a CRITICAL. **What blocks.** A label no vocabulary ranks (`CRITICAL (blocks shipping)`, the brief's own wording, or `BLOCKER`) counts as CRITICAL in the ledger count and in judge, replacing `rank(label) ?? 0`. The outside voice's High and P1 block, as its brief says. `Blocks: no` keeps its GST-1031 meaning. No reviewer prompt or brief changed. docs/review-policy.md's collector paragraph describes the new contract. **Replay of the saved ledgers.** 92 of the 95 drive ledger directories have a ledger, holding 219 reader outputs. 178 of those have their raw reply saved and were collected with main (dcebc44) and with this branch. 3 verdicts change: GSTA-189 red-team (a prose summary row dropped, still a review, 0 blockers), GST-986 r2 fix-check (phantom CRITICAL "I found nothing at the blocking floor" dropped, blockers 1 → 0), and #4212 p1 adversarial-native ("NO FINDINGS. Range…" with a "(not a finding, Low, Blocks: no)" note is now re-asked instead of collecting a Low). The 41 outputs with no saved raw reply can't be replayed. Their merged rows hold 3 more JSON-reader prose rows (GSTA-197 run2), one of them the second phantom CRITICAL. No saved row carries an unranked label or an outside-voice High or P1.
Agent notes - GST-2237, GSTA-461 item 3. Failing-first: test/review-collector-gst2237.test.ts fails all 10 on main and passes on this branch. - Existing tests that used fix-check or red-team to exercise the prose parser now use the outside voice, which parses prose the same way on main. Each JSON reader's own case is pinned to its new JSON-only result. The GST-976 invariant checks JSON readers against their JSON objects' severities and keeps main as the floor for the prose voices. #4237's nested-list cases, GST-1657, GST-2122 and #3901 hold. - bin/gstack-review-dispatch: one message change so COLLECT_NOT_REVIEWED prints `reason=prose_not_collected` instead of "no finding and no clean marker". No new reason code. - Local, on the 33 review test files: 511 pass, 3 fail. Two of the failures also fail on main at dcebc44 on this machine (review-dispatch "an output event edited to look refused…", review-plan-targeted-delta "#225 shape"). The third ("verify re-derives each merged row") timed out at 5 s under load and passed when rerun once.

title: Warn when a branch-only run hides a red PR check, and make ready refuse when its note or base is missing (GST-2205)
body:
This PR fixes three gaps in gstack-ship-queue — the shared merge queue's protocol steps (docs/ship-policy.md#run-a-shared-merge-queue)

  ready --pr <n> [--pregate <file>] [--gate-exit <rc> --gate-log <file>]
                                           READY #<n> <head> STAMP_VERSION=<X|unstamped>, CI at that head, PREGATE, gate state,
                                           SHIP_RECEIPT (refused unless the PR body carries /ship's receipt for that head)
  stamp --pr <n> --version <X> --expect-gated <sha> --expect-base <sha> [--expect-order <pr,...>] [--allow-repo-commands]
        [--gate-exit <rc> --gate-log <file>]
                                           restamp, commit and prove: QUEUE_STAMP: <pr> <X> head= gated= tree= receipt=
  verify --pr <n> --gated <sha> | --record <file> [--receipt <sha256>] [--expect-head <sha>] [--ref <ref>] [--no-fetch]
        [--gate-exit <rc> --gate-log <file>]   (full_e2e: --gated needs the lane's passing gate run on that head)
                                           the coordinator's check from the PR's pushed head: VERIFY: ... and MERGE_CONDITION
  gate-ahead --after <pr> --pr <n> [--predecessor-ref <ref>] [--allow-repo-commands]
                                           prepare an attempt: merged, stamped worktree, gated sha and the gate command
  gate-ahead --record --pr <n> --attempt <id> --exit <rc> --log <file>
                                           bind the gate result to that attempt's gated tree; removes its worktree
  gate-ahead --list --pr <n>               attempts for a PR, newest last (the current one)
  verify --pr <n> --screen                 (train policy) the PR head's screen verdict read from its run (SCREEN_VERDICT)
  verify --post-merge <sha> [--timeout <s>] wait for every check run at a merged commit to settle: POST_MERGE: green|red|pending
                                           and one CHECK: line per workflow; resumable, default timeout 2700 s
  land --pr <n> --pin <sha> [--repair] [--dry-run] [--allow-repo-commands] [--break-lock]
                                           merge: direct: merge the PR at its own green head (receipt and READY at the pin, no stamp
                                           files, checks green, mergeable clean), verify the tree, write a land note; a stale base
                                           runs land.merged_checks, repo commands, only with --allow-repo-commands (never --dry-run);
                                           it holds the land lock from the re-fetch to the merge (--break-lock: a stale one);
                                           --repair: while frozen, land the one repair PR the freeze admits (recorded under the lock)
  land --pr <n> [--dry-run] [--no-wait] [--timeout <min>] [--break-lock [--break-train-lock]] [--allow-repo-commands]
                                           the merge step: lock, merge the base, stamp (fragments folded), push the stamp commit,
                                           wait for its checks, squash with --match-head-commit, confirm the base tree; resumable
  land --pr <n> --repair                   after QUEUE_LAND_DRIFT: open the PR that gives the merge outside land its own
                                           release; /ship and land it, which releases the lock
  land --census                            what land would do with every open PR (read-only)
  train build|status|verdict|bisect|rebuild|watch|prune ...
                                           merge trains, when the base policy declares a train block (train --help;
                                           docs/ship-policy.md#run-a-merge-train); ready then takes --screen|--no-screen
  wave plan|build|status|settle ...        wave PRs under a train policy: 3-6 same-area PRs in one slot and one version
                                           (wave --help; docs/ship-policy.md#wave-prs)

--base <branch>: base branch (default: origin/HEAD unless it names the checked-out branch, else the PR's base, origin/main). Nothing here pushes, except land (the stamp commit and the
refs/notes/gstack-land lock), ready under changelog_fragments (its READY receipt note) and merge trains.
Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 fail · 2 usage · 3 refused or needs a flag, the command that marks a pull request ready to merge and then merges it. It makes sure a pull request never merges while a check on it quietly failed.

## What changed

- **A warning when a red check was replaced by a run from another check suite.** `ready` and `land` judge each check by its newest run. When a `pull_request` run goes red and the lane dispatches `free-tests.yml` on its branch, the branch-only run (which never tested the merge with main) replaces the red one and CI reads green with no word about it. Both commands now print `CI_SUPERSEDED: <check> red run <id> replaced by <id> (suite <a> → <b>)` under their CI line. It is a warning only and changes no verdict; a rerun in the same check suite prints nothing.
- **Plain `ready` refuses when its READY note never reached origin.** Without a train policy, under `changelog_fragments`, `ready` exited 0 even when pushing its note to `refs/notes/gstack-trains` failed, so `land --pin` later refused `QUEUE_NOT_READY`. It now refuses `QUEUE_READY_NOTE_UNPUSHED` with the train path's message (#4254), shared through one helper.
- **`ready` fetches the base before it picks the train or plain path.** The command read the base policy to choose train or plain `ready` before #4256's fetch inside `ready()` ran, so a clone with no (or a stale) `origin/main` ran plain `ready` under a train policy and skipped the screen, conflict and READY-receipt steps. The fetch now runs first. If it fails, a train policy still goes to the train path, which refuses `POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` on its own fetch; otherwise `ready` refuses `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED`.

## Why

Our own direct land refused `QUEUE_NOT_READY` on 2026-11-09 because a READY note never reached origin, and 16.5% of PR heads go red with lanes routinely dispatching a branch-only run afterwards (reports/GSTA-461.md items 7 and 19). The routing gap came from the #4256 decision-trail read.

## Blast radius

`lib/ship-queue.ts` (`ciAtHead`, `ready`), `bin/gstack-ship-queue` (ready routing), `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts` and `lib/ship-queue-land.ts` (one printed line each), `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-record.ts` and `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-ready.ts` (the shared refusal message). Verdicts are unchanged for CI; the only new refusals are a plain `ready` whose note did not reach origin and a plain `ready` that cannot fetch its base before routing.

## Documentation

Scope: a read-only /document-release audit of branch warn-superseded-ci-refuse-unpushed-ready-note against 00cb80c. It covered 12 changed files, including docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, the changelog.d fragment, and the ship-queue code paths for ready and land (direct and stamp). The working tree had no staged, unstaged or untracked changes.

Result: the docs are current. The CI_SUPERSEDED warning (printed by ready and by both land paths; a warning only, with no change to the verdict), the QUEUE_READY_NOTE_UNPUSHED refusal for plain ready under changelog_fragments, and the fetch of the base before ready picks its train or plain path are all described accurately, with matching troubleshooting anchors. No edits were needed or made.

Debt: none found.

## Tests

- `test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts`: `free-tests` red in suite 1 and green in suite 3 prints the line right after `ci:` and stays green; controls cover a second superseded check, a same-suite rerun, pass over pass and a red newest run.
- `test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts`: `land --pin` prints the line under `CI:` and merges; with origin rejecting `refs/notes/*` plain `ready` refuses, and after the hook is removed a rerun pushes the note and `land --pin` (separate state root, so only origin has the note) merges.
- `test/ship-queue-ready-fresh-base.test.ts`: with `refs/remotes/origin/main` deleted under a train policy, `ready` takes the train path and records its receipt.

All three failed on main before the fix. Free Tests passed at this head in run 42734518357.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor and not fixed in this PR:

- `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:161`: `land --pin` can read a local-only READY receipt from the same state root (older behavior).
- `bin/gstack-ship-queue:200`: `ready` fetches the base in the bin and again in `ready()`; a train block landing between the two yields a plain success that `land` later refuses (fails closed).
- `lib/ship-queue.ts:165`: `CI_SUPERSEDED` treats cancelled as red and skipped as a passing replacement; warning only.
- `docs/ship-policy.md`: the docs say `land` prints the line; train land, wave and post-merge do not.
- `lib/ship-queue-land.ts:443`: the stamped-commit CI check drops the line on a resumed stamped landing.
- The changelog fragment's third bullet says a failed fetch refuses `QUEUE_BASE_UNFETCHED` without naming the train-path split described above.



## Approvals

No approvals recorded for branch warn-superseded-ci-refuse-unpushed-ready-note.

title: Let an owner ruling close findings on a full pass and a Step 11 voice, as the review policy says (GST-2273)
body:
An owner's ruling now closes a finding on a round-2 full pass and on a Step 11 voice, the way docs/review-policy.md already says it does, instead of only on an extra review round the owner granted. This unblocks three crew PRs (#4248, #4266, #4257) and harness-evals#361, which all stopped with the owner's ruling recorded but ignored. ## Why The docs promised that a loop at its round cap finishes with "an owner-ruled note … closed and listed", but only finish's fix-check chain read rulings. Crews parked PRs at the cap with the owner's ruling recorded and nothing to apply it. ## Blast radius Review-binding code: `lib/review-evidence.ts`, `lib/ruled-notes.ts`, `lib/review-scope.ts`, `lib/ship-release.ts` (fix-check chain), `lib/approval-record.ts` (read roots), `bin/gstack-review-read`, `bin/gstack-review-scope`. The binding rules from #4260 stay: a ruling outside the reviewed range closes nothing, the lane's own row fields rule nothing, gate findings are never ruled, and an edit after the bound head still needs review. What counts as blocking does not change. The negative controls in test/ship-ruled-full-pass.test.ts and test/ship-finish-ruled-notes.test.ts hold on both main and this branch (script ran). ## Summary - **Full-pass rows.** `gstack-review-read` now applies each approved `gstack-approvals rule` row whose head lies inside the range the row reviewed (`range_base..commit`, or the row's own commit when it names no range_base). A round-2 full pass whose only blocker is ruled reads `CURRENT`, so Step 11.5 can bind it (#4248's shape). - **Step 11 voice findings.** `gstack-review-scope summary` counts a ruled blocker that no row records, such as a Step 11 voice's ledger-only finding, as `noted` instead of `unrecorded` (#4266, #4257). It reads rulings only from the run's newest row. A ruling names a finding by fingerprint, or a ledger-only finding by `:`. - **Fixed findings on a fix-check.** A finding the fix-check itself read as `fixed` or `auto-fixed` no longer holds the row open (harness-evals#361's real row). `FIX_CHECK_OPEN` now also names findings no ruling can close, such as a gate finding, instead of leaving only the generic nonconverged reason. - **One-tree binding for stopped reads.** A stopped read (an `incomplete` binding) is promoted by rulings only if it read one committed tree: the start capture now records its commit, and the row must end there. Rows logged before this change must end at a commit made before the read began. title: Make gstack agents lead every report with what failed, what's unverified and what else changed (GST-1455)
body:
gstack agents now open every status report with what failed, what they didn't verify and what else they changed. This serves gstack's trust-but-verify goal: a builder reading an agent's report should see the skipped test or unchecked claim first, not dig for it. ## What changed - **The shared closer** (`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-voice-directive.ts`, tier 2 and up; every `sections/preamble.md` regenerates from it). It used to say "report in at most a few short lines". Now a status report (after work or when asked) stays under 250 words and opens with three lines, `Failed or skipped:`, `Unverified:` and `Also changed:`, each naming every item or saying none. Lists longer than 10 show the top 10, a count of the rest and an offer to list them. The closer is 4 B smaller than before. Ship's size ledger records -4 B. - **Capy crews** follow the same shape. factory.md point 10 carries the three-line rule and points findings write-ups at ETHOS.md section 8. The lane report Outcome gains `Failed or skipped:` and `Also changed:` lines, and READY's lane lines gain the same two. The existing `Unverified:` lines stay where the controller reads them. - **factory.md's byte budget** rises from 4,200 to 4,400. The page is 4,396 B. The clause is the exact wording the eval measured, so it wasn't trimmed to fit. ## Behavior changes - Every tier-2+ skill's closing report now opens with the three lines, and the old "few short lines" guidance is gone. - Capy lane reports, replies and READY blocks carry `Failed or skipped:` and `Also changed:` lines. ## Evidence These are dev numbers from GEVA-2's preregistered trust-but-verify eval, on Claude Opus 5.5, comparing round 3 (gstack f83eba4) with the old closer at 641d622. Recall is the share of key facts disclosed in a report's first 250 words. - Skill layer: 0.520 against 0.442 for the old closer (+7.6 points, 95% CI [+0.9, +14.2]) and 0.489 for no gstack (+2.7 [-5.1, +10.6]). The dev MDD is 13.1 points. - Capy lane reports: 0.604 against 0.552 (old) and 0.489 (no gstack). - The marker lines appeared in 32 of 40 investigate reports, 38 of 40 ship reports and 35 of 40 Capy reports. - What didn't move: reports still run long (74 of 80 over 250 words), and unsupported claims in the skill layer stay at the old level (4.75 per report, against 3.02 with no gstack). Capy unsupported claims fell from 4.80 to 3.90. - The sealed held-out read (P f83eba4, C acbc88d) is GEVA-2's and hasn't been reported here. Dev numbers aren't the result. /investigate's three DEBUG REPORT rows were part of the measured round but aren't ported, because main retired /investigate (#4110). ## Why A builder reading an agent's report kept finding the skipped test or the unchecked claim near the end, or not at all. Leading with three fixed lines puts what failed, what wasn't verified and what else changed where a reader looks first, and the dev eval measured more key facts in a report's first 250 words. ## Blast radius The closer regenerates into every tier-2+ skill's `sections/preamble.md` and its SKILL.md preamble id, plus the four ship golden files. That is safe because the change is prose only, and no code reads the new READY lines (grep over `lib/` and `bin/`, read by the adversarial reviewer), and CI's free suite passed at this tree (run 44046230530, 1,672 files). ## Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues found. One read-only full review ran at b447538 (Captain ruling A1), with a batched specialist, an adversarial reviewer on Claude and an outside voice on openai/gpt-6.1-sol. The specialist and the outside voice found nothing. The adversarial reviewer raised six findings, all below the blocking floor, and each ships as a disclosed note without a fix. Outside review: clean (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, completed). ## Review notes Below the blocking floor. These are recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - Medium, adversarial #1, `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-voice-directive.ts:34`: the closer drops "never the deliverable" and narrows the mandated-report exemption to a closed list, so the findings lists of /review, /cso, /qa and /ship could be read as status reports and cut to the top 10. - Medium, adversarial #2, same file: the closer's "opens with `Failed or skipped:`" competes with the Completion Status Protocol and with caller-required first lines such as `REVIEWED_TREE:`, and nothing says which comes first. - Low, adversarial #3, `captain/templates/report.md`: it orders the lines Failed, Also changed, Unverified, while factory.md point 10 and the closer say Failed, Unverified, Also changed. - Low, adversarial #4, same closer: the new example is labelled plain `Good:` beside the voice section's own Good/Bad pair, and the bad-closer example is gone. - Low, adversarial #5, `capy/skill/gstack/factory.md`: the page is 4,396 bytes against the new 4,400 budget, so the next edit needs another raise. - Low, adversarial #6, `changelog.d/gstack-reports-lead-with-failures.md`: the changelog's dev numbers (0.442 to 0.520, 0.552 to 0.604) carry no run ids in the checkout. - Round 1, note 1: the closer drops the completion-status exemption and doesn't place its three lines relative to STATUS. - Round 1, note 2: factory.md's "open with" ordering differs from READY.md and report.md. - Round 1, note 3: no unit test pins the three labels. The four Captain manuals that still name only `Unverified:` get a docs-only follow-up PR after this one merges. ## Documentation Status: blocked. A read-only audit (docs-4273-1) covered docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, capy/skill/gstack and captain/templates at b447538. It found that crew/docs/captain.md, captain/SKILL.md.tmpl, captain/templates/CREW.md and capy/skill/gstack/captain.md still list only the `Unverified:` line. The owner accepted that named risk, and the docs-only follow-up fixes it. Documentation exception: accepted by GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-17 via Captain ruling A3 relayed by the parent lane: A3. title: Let the CI carry accept a run where only an unrelated job was rerun (GST-2284)
body:
When one job of a green CI run is rerun on its own (a flaky export job, for example), the CI carry now still accepts the run. That keeps gstack's flaky-rerun rule usable for every crew that carries CI results: rerun the one failed job, note it as flaky, and the carry goes through. ## What changed - **A run where only an unrelated job was rerun now verifies.** GitHub numbers the run's newest attempt 2, but a job that wasn't rerun keeps the `tree.json` it uploaded in attempt 1. Run verification now works out which attempt each profile job actually ran in: GitHub relists a job it didn't rerun under the new attempt with its old start and finish times, so a job listed the same way one attempt earlier was carried from there. `tree.json` is checked against that attempt. - **Rerunning the checks job too no longer refuses.** That leaves one same-named artifact per attempt, which used to refuse as `artifact_missing`. The verifier now downloads each by id and reads the one that records the uploading job's newest attempt, and no other. - **Old evidence can't be made fresh by an unrelated rerun.** A run's age now comes from the profile's own jobs, so rerunning another job days later doesn't let week-old test results pass the 24-hour freshness check. - **Nothing else got looser.** Head, merge commit, tree, event and job conclusion are still compared exactly, and an artifact from an older attempt with a different tree still refuses (`tree_mismatch`). - **A clearer message when dependencies are missing.** When the pregate's skipped-tests command fails with `Cannot find package` or `Cannot find module`, the refusal now says the checkout has no installed dependencies. ## Why harness-evals#364 (HARN-56) was blocked by both refusals at 9595abe3. Run 42724981450 had `public-export` rerun alone, and `accept` refused with `artifact_mismatch`; rerunning `checks` as a workaround then refused with `artifact_missing`. ## Blast radius `lib/run-evidence.ts` (`verifyRun` and `ghRunDeps.artifact`), used by `gstack-ci-carry`, `gstack-pregate clear --run` and `--from-run`, the flaky-exception reader and the CI reuse job. A run with no reruns reads what it read before. A job listing without start and finish times falls back to the run's newest attempt, the old behaviour. **Status:** updated. One factual edit; no blockers. **Scope:** release diff from b1702ee to b9e42c1, plus the unstaged changelog.d fragment edit. The diff touches lib/run-evidence.ts, lib/pregate/index.ts, docs/pregate.md and tests. Documentation health: docs/pregate.md Updated (the `skipped_failed` refusal now notes when the checkout has no installed dependencies; the attempt resolution and profile-job dating were already documented on this branch) changelog.d/ci-carry-accepts-unrelated-job-rerun.md Current (covers the rerun fix, freshness dating and the dependency hint) README.md / AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md Current (no affected claims) docs/ship-policy.md / docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md Current (no affected claims) Coverage: all shipped behavior is documented; there is no new public surface. Diagram drift: none. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/flaky-exception.ts:202` readRunFailures still dates a red run by every job's completed_at, so rerunning a non-profile job on a days-old red run makes it look fresh on the flaky-exception path (pre-existing on main; same class as the pass-1 fix). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:178` A rerun of one free-suite shard reruns the free-tests aggregator, which uploads a new tree.json and re-dates the run (behaviour unchanged from main); the new docs/pregate.md sentence holds only for jobs no profile job depends on. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:179` When no profile job reports completed_at the date falls back to run.updated_at, which an unrelated rerun moves; reachable only when every profile job lacks a completion time (missing or all-skipped jobs), which other checks refuse or which records no tests. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/flaky-exception.ts:202` readRunFailures still dates a red run by every job (same as p2/red-team#1). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/index.ts:458` Errors that only mention node_modules (an ENOENT on node_modules/.bin/) no longer get the install hint; message text only, the refusal is unchanged. - INFORMATIONAL `docs/pregate.md:874` The new docs/pregate.md lines 874-875 are not wrapped like the rest of the file (cosmetic).

title: Keep review commands working after copied installs refresh
body:
Copied-host installations can load the review commands after a refresh. This keeps the existing review workflow usable across supported hosts without adding a new command or dependency.

## Summary

Both `gstack-review-plan` and `gstack-review-scope` import the shared `scripts/resolvers/fix-check.ts` module, but the runtime asset list did not stage it. Copied installations therefore failed at module loading before either command could handle input. Add that existing module to the shared list.

The regression creates an owned copied runtime through setup's actual staging helper, then checks native help and invalid-input handling. Its fixture supplies the existing `crew/lib` assets used by current upstream. A branch-named changelog fragment follows the repository's stamp-at-merge policy; VERSION, package version and released CHANGELOG sections are untouched.

## Blast radius

One installer asset-list entry, one test file and one changelog fragment. The shared quoted/staged copy path is unchanged. No new CLI, provider, credential, network, release or deployment path is introduced.

## Test Coverage

The changed asset-staging behavior is covered by two native CLI-contract regressions. On Windows/Bun, the focused suite passed 10 tests with 4 existing platform skips; both new tests execute. The same new test was copied into an owned checkout of the untouched upstream base: both cases fail specifically because the shared module is absent. With the installer fix, both pass.

Current hosted Windows curation excludes the new test because its fixture contains bin-path handling, so local Windows execution is separate evidence from Windows Smoke. Linux free-suite and other hosted gates are checked on this draft's actual head; no all-host certification is claimed from local tests.

## Pre-Landing Review

No actionable findings from the core checklist, testing/security/state-machine/Red Team checklists or separate native adversarial pass. Full source/test inspection was performed by the core reader; native adversarial test/fixture coverage was summary-only. The reviewer snapshots match the final content; the subsequent commit only records that same content. Outside-model reviews and review-bot triage were disabled.

## Exploratory QA

Two bounded functional probes verified the positive candidate and the missing-module negative control. The control intentionally exits with two failures at the untouched base; it is not counted as passing product tests. Private receipts and the causal checkpoint are retained locally. No browser, live model, real data or deployment was exercised.

## Verification Results

- Focused copied-runtime/setup/timeout-tripwire tests: 10 passed, 4 existing platform skips, 0 failed.
- New regression tests alone: 2 passed, 0 failed; untouched-base control: 0 passed, 2 expected missing-module failures.
- Product typecheck: passed.
- Test-code typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new.
- Bash setup syntax and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Mechanical preflight: generated-input selection, secrets, stray/literal/policy/timing checks and applicable typecheck/conflict-marker guards passed.
- Changelog prose and plain-title checks: passed.
- Hosted CI inspected at head `bf50266d15466424d47f92caad39019754559fdc` and base `56c5aa62ea5f10c6593ec9a643e8027559b153bd`: ten fork workflows report `action_required` and await upstream maintainer approval. [Free Tests](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42752949674) has zero jobs executed; Windows Smoke and the other approval-gated workflows have not run. [Plain title](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42752949594) passed independently. No full-suite pass is claimed. Provider-secret eval jobs have not executed; after approval, their expected fork skips remain excluded from passing eval coverage. No paid workflow was dispatched.

## Plan Completion

No formal plan is bound to this small packaging repair; plan-completion audit was not run. Scope matches the installer defect and its regression coverage.

## Documentation

**Status:** current. Read-only installer documentation audit completed with no required corrections and no edits.

Audited the isolated publication candidate on `codex/fix-review-runtime-module-pr`: the installer/test patch at `2c4122071efcd0886911514ca9e11718115bf515`, its selected current-upstream fixture adaptation and the unversioned changelog fragment, against `56c5aa62ea5f10c6593ec9a643e8027559b153bd`. This restores an existing shared module in copied runtime assets; it introduces no command, flag, setting, skill or new user workflow. Eight relevant authored documentation/metadata files were read, with the installer, module imports and regression fixture cross-checked.

title: Brain sync scans binary files and split authorization values for secrets (GST-2292)
body:
Brain sync no longer pushes a credential hidden in a file git treats as binary, or an auth value added on the line under an unchanged `"authorization":` key. It keeps the promise that brain sync never publishes a secret from `~/.gstack` to your notes remote. ## What changed ```text Before (main at 6afe390) After (this PR) printf '\0AKIA…\n' > projects/p/ceo-plans/note.md gstack-brain-sync --once -> pushed to remote -> held: aws-access-key, not pushed "authorization": + "Bearer abcdef…" -> pushed to remote -> held: bearer-token-json same, in UTF-16 text or with diff.context=0 -> pushed -> held ``` - **Binary files are scanned by their bytes.** The sync and the pre-commit hook now scan two readings of the staged diff: git's plain diff as you see it (your `diff.context` and any textconv driver apply), and a `--text --no-textconv -U3` reading, so a file with a NUL byte or UTF-16 text arrives as its bytes. A match in either reading holds the file. Each line holding a NUL byte is also read as UTF-16 (both byte orders and alignments, with JSON escapes decoded) and with its NULs removed. A section the text reading still sees as "Binary files … differ" or a "GIT binary patch" is held as `binary-not-scanned`. A clean binary still syncs. - **A key and a value split across an unchanged line and an added line are matched.** The scanner also scans each hunk's new text (unchanged and added lines without their markers) as one block, read plainly, with JSON strings decoded, as UTF-16 and with NULs removed. `-U3` keeps the key line in the text reading even when a user sets `diff.context=0`. - **The scan's temporary diff files are private.** They now carry binary bytes, so the sync creates them with mode 0600. - **Docs.** docs/gbrain-sync.md describes the two readings, and docs/gbrain-sync.md and docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md say plainly that a secret already committed in `~/.gstack` stays held after you delete it, because it sits on a removed line of the next diff, and only `--skip-file` clears it. If it was pushed, treat it as exposed. ## Why A cross-family audit of #4264 found that an AWS key inside a note with one NUL byte was enqueued, synced and published to the notes remote, because git prints "Binary files differ" instead of the content. It also found that a Bearer value added under an existing `"authorization":` line was missed, because the added line's `+` broke the pattern's whitespace match. Both leaks were reproduced on main by failing-first tests through `gstack-brain-sync --once` with a local bare remote. ## Blast radius The change touches the scanner, the two scan diffs in bin/gstack-brain-sync and the hook diff written by gstack-artifacts-init and gstack-brain-restore. Main's plain diff reading is kept as one of the two readings, so nothing main catches is dropped; the whole test/brain-sync.test.ts file passes at 9c0444e (135 tests) and CI's free suite passed at this head. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. Tests added to test/brain-sync.test.ts, each failing first on main or on the earlier head: - an AWS key in a file with a NUL byte, in UTF-16LE and in UTF-16BE is held and never reaches the remote; - an AWS key added to a clean binary that already synced is held; - a Bearer value added under an unchanged authorization key is held, also in UTF-16 text and under `diff.context=0`; - a secret only the user's `diff.context` or a textconv driver shows is still held (the plain reading); - a `\u`-escaped key in a UTF-16 JSON file is held, and the scan's diff files are private to the user; - the pre-commit hook from init and from restore refuses a binary AWS key; - the scanner flags a "Binary files … differ" or "GIT binary patch" section, and not a text line that mentions binary files. Tests ran: tests 1662 ## Pre-Landing Review Full panel (gate class): batched testing, security and state-machines specialist, Red Team, native adversarial pass and outside voice. Round 1 found two blocking leaks (a split value in UTF-16 text, and a split value under `diff.context=0`) and one wording issue; all three are fixed with failing-first tests. Round 2 found only notes. A cross-family audit at 201c6a0 then found two regressions against main (the plain diff reading and a textconv-only secret), fixed in 0c114fb. Step 11's voices on that fix found two critical issues (a `\u`-escaped key in UTF-16 JSON, and binary bytes in a 0644 temp file), fixed in 9c0444e. The granted fix-check and the targeted reader at 9c0444e found nothing blocking. Review-loop exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-10 via Captain ruling to GSTA-503 (A, ship): Owner decision, Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36): the fix-check's edits to gate-class paths bin/gstack-brain-sync, bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py and bin/gstack-artifacts-init are named and accepted. A cross-family re-audit (GPT-6.1 Sol) of 201c6a0..9c0444e returned LAND with test/brain-sync.test.ts 135/135 (handoffs/GSTA-498/sol-audit-9c0444e.md). The 4 INFORMATIONAL notes ship in the PR body. (fix-check at 9c0444e58129, 4 findings) Gate edits: bin/gstack-brain-sync, bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py and bin/gstack-artifacts-init, edited by the fix round and named in the exception above. Outside review: unavailable (Codex is not installed); the outside voice ran as a Claude subagent. ## Exploratory QA Surface: functional (the brain secret scanner behind the pre-commit hook), in throwaway git repos. Verdict: pass. Before the fix, a UTF-16 split value and a split value under `diff.context=0` passed (rc=0); after it, both are held (rc=3), the UTF-8 split value is still held, and a non-secret control still passes (rc=0). ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN Intent: stop brain sync pushing secrets in binary files and split authorization values. Delivered: the scanner, both scan diffs in sync, both hook copies, docs and tests for those cases. ## Documentation **Status:** blocked, with the owner's exception. The audit at 1009286 found the docs current; the docs/gbrain-sync.md paragraph changed in 0c114fb was not re-audited because the audit attempt budget was spent. It matches the shipped behaviour: main's plain git diff reading plus a raw --text --no-textconv reading with three context lines. No third audit. ## Test plan - [x] bun test test/brain-sync.test.ts at 9c0444e: 135 pass, 0 fail (local, git wrapper removed from PATH) - [x] CI free suite at 9c0444e: run 42764940522 attempt 2 green (attempt 1 lost free-suite (3) to a runner dpkg lock during the Playwright install, before any test ran) - [x] macos-named-regressions at 9c0444e: green in run 42764940522 ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-38f34f941fb3). The full approval record stays private. Plan: exempt: bug fix (R65) Plan check: exempt bug fix Refs GST-2292 ## Summary Brain sync's secret scan saw only what `git diff` printed, so a binary file or a value split from its key could reach the remote. The scan now reads binary content beside git's plain diff, matches a key on an unchanged line with a value added under it, holds anything it still cannot read, keeps its temporary diff files private, and the docs explain how a committed secret's hold is cleared. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `test/brain-sync.test.ts:635` the diff.context=0 test's GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 override replaces the free shard runner's inherited maintenance.auto/gc.auto pairs for that test's git calls, a possible isolation flake; appending the pair after the inherited ones avoids it - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-sync:1043` GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0 in the environment overrides -U3 on all four scan diffs, so a Bearer value added under an unchanged authorization key passes the gate; pre-existing at the base, reachable only with that variable set (native and outside voice: Medium, Blocks: no) - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py:139` hunk-level nul_readings re-decode a large binary's bytes: a 20 MB binary went from 0.91 GB / 22.6 s to 1.44 GB / 31.6 s peak; fails closed (sync blocks) on very large files - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py:243` a staged file whose textconv output doesn't change appears in --name-only but not in the plain diff, so attribution exits 4 and the sync holds the queue; main does the same (exit 4 at 6afe390), and nothing is lost - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-brain-sync:1045` the coupled-group blob file (`$scan.blobs`) is still created under the user's umask; the same exposure exists on main - INFORMATIONAL `test/brain-sync.test.ts:707` the private-files test resolves realGit with `command -v git`, which recurses when git is itself a PATH wrapper (seen on a Capy machine; CI uses /usr/bin/git); lines 824 and 937 use the same pattern ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Plan Completion Plan: exempt (bug fix with failing-first tests). ## Verification Results Every blocking finding fixed has a test that failed before the fix and passes after it. No obligation is unresolved. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Agent notes - Issue: GST-2292. Lanes GSTA-498 and GSTA-503 under GStack Minder (GSTA-36). Security fix allowed during the tooling freeze. - Size limit: the brain-sync scan path on main has no size limit, so there was none to keep. With `--text`, git diffs files above `core.bigFileThreshold` and files marked `-diff` as text, and any section that still arrives without bytes is held as `binary-not-scanned`. - Sibling PR #4179 (outside contributor) touches bin/gstack-brain-sync, bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py, docs/gbrain-sync.md and test/brain-sync.test.ts. A text-only trial merge (`git merge-tree`, no checkout or run, per the untrusted-code rule) with its head 4d6a935 is clean at the final head 9c0444e (merged tree 71a7021). Typecheck and tests were not run on the merged tree, because that would run outside code. - Out of scope: UTF-32, compressed formats (zip, PDF streams) and `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0` (see Review notes) are not handled. - CI: free-suite (3) attempt 1 at 9c0444e failed on a runner dpkg lock in "Install Playwright Chromium" before the suite ran; the failed jobs were rerun once, green. title: Count a fix-check whose range starts after a docs-only commit (GST-2294)
body:
When a docs-only commit sits between the reviewed commit and a granted fix-check, `gstack-ship-release finish` now counts that fix-check instead of refusing it. This unblocks crew PRs whose Step 14.5 docs commit landed before the owner granted the fix-check, so the fix-check's range started at the docs commit (harness-evals#361 is the live case). It serves the shipping goal: a reviewed, granted fix should reach a receipt without a third review round. ## What changed - **finish bridges a docs-only gap.** Before, `fixChecked` in `lib/ship-release.ts` required the oldest fix-check's `range_base` to hold the reviewed tree, or to be an earlier fix-check's commit. Anything else printed `FIX_CHECK: not counted (range_base does not hold the reviewed tree)` and the fixed code routed as unreviewed behavior. Now, at exactly that gap, finish walks `range_base`'s first parents (off the base) back to the nearest commit holding the reviewed tree. It accepts the range only when every commit after that one, `range_base` included, has a single parent and touches only paths finish already routes as release metadata or authored docs (not test code, not bookkeeping). It prints `FIX_CHECK_DOCS_BRIDGE: range_base follows the reviewed commit by docs or release metadata only ()`. Those docs paths still take the docs route and its recheck, because they sit outside the fix-check's read. - **Still refused:** a code or test commit in between (alone or after a docs commit), a merge commit in between, a `range_base` that the reviewed commit descends from (so `range_base` comes before it), and a `range_base` on another branch. The equal-tree case is unchanged. No other part of `fixChecked` changed: grants, freshness, ruled notes, the chain walk through earlier rows and the per-path read test are as before. - **Docs.** `docs/ship-policy.md#fix-check-docs-bridge` describes the rule and says to pass `--reviewed-tree` as the tree the bound review read, never the fix-check's own tree. `docs/review-policy.md` links it. ## Why Three parked PRs printed the same refusal. Only one of them needs this change. The diagnosis for each: | Case | Reviewed tree's commit | range_base | Commits between | How finish routes them | Covered | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | harness-evals#361 | e5584cb6 (tree 0009a8ff) | 5e1c1555 | 5e1c1555 only (docs/README.md, docs/canary.md; parent e5584cb6) | docs (`ROUTE: … docs=2`) | Yes, by this change | | gstack #4267 | 1baf586 (tree f3f3352d, the tree finish 1 to 3 used) | d19cf6f | d19cf6f only (docs/uninstall.md, changelog.d fragment) | docs plus release metadata (`ROUTE: … docs=1 metadata=1`) | Yes, once finish gets the reviewed tree | | gstack #4270 | 5afaeb3 (tree 9adf2a8d) | 5afaeb3 | none | n/a (equal tree) | Already counted on main, once finish gets the reviewed tree | The #4267 and #4270 refusals came from the arguments, not the rule. Their last finish runs passed `--reviewed-tree` as the fix-check's own tree (7c0a53dd at 94ecf9c, and 08c09c25 at ddf1918; both print `ROUTE: reviewed= current=`). With that argument, `range_base` is an ancestor of the "reviewed" commit, and this change correctly keeps refusing. Rerun with the bound review's tree (f3f3352d40fad4d06919a63bda078f868a1b2bcd for #4267, 9adf2a8d4f83c63eac02a1069cbfa03104063a0e for #4270). GST-2274 (a null `range_base` on round-1 fix-checks) is unaffected: a null or off-branch `range_base` exits the walk before the bridge runs, so those rows still refuse with `the row names no range_base commit on this branch`.

title: Count a granted follow-up review whose range starts after a docs-only commit (GST-2294)
body:
When /ship's docs commit lands between the reviewed commit and a follow-up review the owner granted, `gstack-ship-release finish` now counts that follow-up review instead of refusing it, so a fix reviewed under the owner's grant reaches its ship record without a third review round. harness-evals#361 is the live case: its granted review's range started at the docs commit.

## What changed

- **finish bridges a docs-only gap.** Before, `fixChecked` in `lib/ship-release.ts` required the oldest fix-check's `range_base` to hold the reviewed tree, or to be an earlier fix-check's commit. Anything else printed `FIX_CHECK: not counted (range_base <sha> does not hold the reviewed tree)` and the fixed code routed as unreviewed behavior. Now, at exactly that gap, finish walks `range_base`'s first parents (off the base) back to the nearest commit holding the reviewed tree. It accepts the range only when every commit after that one, `range_base` included, has a single parent and touches only paths finish already routes as release metadata or authored docs (not test code, not bookkeeping).
- **The bridge uses the router's own rule for release metadata.** It asks the same per-path question `route` asks, so on a stacked branch whose parent already landed it uses the stricter list there too. A docs commit that edits a declared stamp path or release output there is not bridged.
- **The bridge line prints only when the chain counts.** `FIX_CHECK_DOCS_BRIDGE: range_base <sha12> follows the reviewed commit <sha12> by docs or release metadata only (<commits>)` no longer appears beside a refused chain. The docs paths still take the docs route and its recheck, because they sit outside the fix-check's read.
- **Still refused:** a code or test commit in between (alone or after a docs commit), a merge commit in between, a `range_base` that comes before the reviewed commit, and a `range_base` on another branch. The equal-tree case is unchanged, and so are grants, freshness, ruled notes, the chain walk through earlier rows and the per-path read test.
- **Docs.** `docs/ship-policy.md#fix-check-docs-bridge` describes the rule and says to pass `--reviewed-tree` as the tree the bound review read, never the fix-check's own tree. `docs/review-policy.md` links it.

## Why

Three parked PRs printed the same refusal. Only one of them needs this change. The diagnosis for each:

| Case | Reviewed tree's commit | range_base | Commits between | How finish routes them | Covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| harness-evals#361 | e5584cb6 (tree 0009a8ff) | 5e1c1555 | 5e1c1555 only (docs/README.md, docs/canary.md; parent e5584cb6) | docs (`ROUTE: … docs=2`) | Yes, by this change |
| gstack #4267 | 1baf586 (tree f3f3352d, the tree finish 1 to 3 used) | d19cf6f | d19cf6f only (docs/uninstall.md, changelog.d fragment) | docs plus release metadata (`ROUTE: … docs=1 metadata=1`) | Yes, once finish gets the reviewed tree |
| gstack #4270 | 5afaeb3 (tree 9adf2a8d) | 5afaeb3 | none | n/a (equal tree) | Already counted on main, once finish gets the reviewed tree |

The #4267 and #4270 refusals came from the arguments, not the rule. Their last finish runs passed `--reviewed-tree` as the fix-check's own tree, so `range_base` is an ancestor of the "reviewed" commit, and this change correctly keeps refusing. Rerun them with the bound review's tree (f3f3352d40fad4d06919a63bda078f868a1b2bcd for #4267, 9adf2a8d4f83c63eac02a1069cbfa03104063a0e for #4270).

## Blast radius

Only the `range_base` gap clause of finish's fix-check walk. A chain that counted before still counts with the same line. A chain that refused before now counts only in the docs-only shape. GST-2274 (a null `range_base` on round-1 fix-checks) is unaffected: a null or off-branch `range_base` exits the walk before the bridge runs.

## Test Coverage

`test/ship-finish-fixed-links.test.ts` covers the bridge: one docs commit, a docs commit plus a CHANGELOG stamp, and the refusals (code or test commit in between, merge, non-descendant, other branch, equal tree). The fix round added six cases: a stamp path and a release output on a landed stack parent, each in the rewrite and append shapes, two controls, and the refused chain that must not print the bridge line. Five of those failed before the fix; the controls passed. Two narrow refusal clauses still have no test of their own: a docs file that matches a `bookkeeping` glob, and a Markdown file that matches a `test_code` glob.

Tests ran: test 1662

## Pre-Landing Review

Two review passes ran. Pass 1 found no blocking issue and left three notes. The fix round at faf5c7d fixed two of them (the bridge's broad release list on a landed stack parent, and the bridge line printing beside a refused chain). Pass 2 reviewed that fix (batched specialist plus native adversarial), found nothing blocking, and left the three notes below, none fixed in this PR.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- CRITICAL `.gstack/tmp/pr-body-top.md` draft PR body (gitignored, not in the diff) still lists as open review notes two issues faf5c7d fixes: the bridge using the broad release list on a landed stack parent, and FIX_CHECK_DOCS_BRIDGE printing beside a refused chain
- Low `lib/ship-release.ts` the bridge is safe only because a path it accepts can never become a fix-check candidate (behavior, tests, context, bounded); route enforces this today but nothing pins it, so a later route change could reopen the partly-read-path hole outside the shapes the new tests cover
- CRITICAL `docs/ship-policy.md` docs/ship-policy.md#fix-check-docs-bridge does not say the bridge line now prints only when the chain counts

## Documentation
**Status:** blocked, with a named risk accepted. The Step 14.5 audit at a70c72a found the docs current. The fix round at faf5c7d then changed lib/ship-release.ts, which the audit had hashed, so the audit no longer covers it. Instead of a second audit, the Captain accepted the docs delta as a named risk:

Documentation exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-10 via GSTA-499 ruling: Named risk, Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36): the lib/ship-release.ts change a70c72a..faf5c7d makes the bridge use route's own per-path metadata closure and print FIX_CHECK_DOCS_BRIDGE only when the chain counts. docs/ship-policy.md#fix-check-docs-bridge (lines 1916-1928 at faf5c7d) already says finish accepts commits 'whose every path it routes as docs or release metadata, printing' the line, so the fix makes the code match the doc and needs no doc change. The pass-2 docs note stays open on the PR.

**Scope audited:** docs/ and README.md (140 docs files; reviewed docs/ship-policy.md, docs/review-policy.md, the changelog fragment against lib/ship-release.ts). The a70c72a audit found docs/ship-policy.md, docs/review-policy.md and the changelog fragment current, and noted that FIX_CHECK_DOCS_BRIDGE has no docs/troubleshooting.md entry.

title: QM edition no longer ships the review skill (GST-2306)
body:
QM's default gstack skills no longer include `gstack-review`; the QM edition now ships one skill, `gstack-plan`. This keeps the QM edition to skills that measurably help people who use gstack inside QM.

## What changed
- `hosts/qm.ts` no longer lists `gstack-review`, and the edition is regenerated: `qm/sandbox/skills/gstack-review/` is gone and `qm/edition.json` lists only `gstack-plan`.
- The review skill's first-step script (`hosts/qm/scripts/diff-base.sh`), its `qmScriptCommand` helper and the script's tests are removed, since nothing else used them.
- `test/qm-edition.test.ts` and `test/context-budget-ratchet.test.ts` use `gstack-plan` where they named the review skill.
- `qm/README.md` and `docs/hosts.md` describe the one-skill edition. A changelog fragment tells QM deployments to delete their `sandbox/skills/gstack-review/` folder and run `qm up`.
- `.gstack/pregate.json` maps the deleted sandbox script to `test/qm-edition.test.ts`, the test that used to check it, so the pre-merge check accepts its removal.

## Why
The Harness Evals benchmark of the QM edition (harness-evals #333) found that `gstack-review` flagged too many problems without making the reviewed work any better, and named it a cut candidate. Garry decided to cut it, so QM users now get only the planning skill by default.

## Blast radius
Only the QM edition's generated files, its spec, its tests and two docs change; gstack's own `/review` skill and every other host are untouched. That is safe because `gen-qm-edition --check` reports the edition fresh and the full free suite passed in CI at this head (run 42777061972).

## Summary
QM users were getting a review skill that over-flagged without helping. The edition now ships only `gstack-plan`, the generator output and tests follow, and the docs say why review was cut and how an existing QM deployment removes it.

## Test Coverage
All remaining code paths have test coverage; this PR only removes code and the tests that covered it.

title: Windows: `./setup --status` run from the gstack checkout reports the checkout's own Codex sidecar as a separate unregistered project install and suggests moving it
body:
## What happened

On Windows 11 (Git Bash, no Developer Mode), running `./setup --status` from inside the gstack checkout reports the checkout's generated Codex runtime sidecar as a separate, unregistered Codex project installation:

```text
  codex     experimental     project  unregistered 1.99.0.0                    ~/.claude/skills/gstack/.agents/skills  (source: ~/.claude/skills/gstack/.agents/skills/gstack)
            installed before the registry, and the gstack checkout lives in this host's runtime root (~/.claude/skills/gstack/.agents/skills/gstack), so ./setup --host codex would replace it; move it first: mv ~/.claude/skills/gstack/.agents/skills/gstack ~/gstack && cd ~/gstack && ./setup --host codex (docs/troubleshooting.md#setup-runtime-root-contains-checkout)
```

`~/.claude/skills/gstack/.agents/skills/gstack` is the generated runtime target that `create_agents_sidecar` builds inside the checkout (setup:3033). The global Codex install uses it (setup:4214-4219). It is not a separate installation and not a source checkout: it has `VERSION` but no `setup`. Following the printed fix would move the sidecar away from the path the global Codex skills use, and the `./setup --host codex` that follows would fail because the sidecar has no `setup`.

This is the directory the docs send users to. troubleshooting.md:26-27 and README.md:291 say to run `./setup --status` "in your gstack checkout" for hosts other than Claude. troubleshooting.md:7295 says "Run `./setup --status` from your gstack checkout". README.md:67 shows it right after `cd ~/gstack && ./setup --host auto`.

Run from another repository that has no project-local gstack install, the same command prints only the real rows: agy, codex and claude global, all `current`. Expected: the checkout's own generated sidecar is not reported as an independently installed, unregistered Codex project installation, and no move is suggested for it.

Cause, from reading main at 4685fa9:

- `gstack_install_known_roots` (bin/gstack-install-registry.sh:244, row at line 263) adds `codex project $proj/.agents/skills/gstack`. `$proj` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of the current directory, so run from the checkout the candidate is the checkout's own sidecar.
- `_gstack_install_source` (line 221) resolves the candidate's source. The candidate has no `setup`, so the function takes its second branch, `cd "$1/bin" && pwd -P` (lines 225-227). On Windows the sidecar's `bin` is a real copy, not a symlink (setup:3051-3053, the #2444 `IS_WINDOWS` branch), so the source resolves to the sidecar itself.
- `_gstack_status_rows` (line 269) prints the candidate as `unregistered`, because only `~/.codex/skills/gstack` is in the registry. `gstack_install_move_hint` (line 40) then finds the source within the root (they are the same path, line 44) and adds the move command (lines 304-305).

We only observed this on Windows. Where the sidecar's `bin` symlinks resolve to the source checkout, the move hint seems unlikely to appear. The duplicate `unregistered` row and its "register it" advice may still appear there. We did not test that.

Suggested direction: when discovering project installs, don't count the source checkout's own generated sidecar as a separate project install, and keep discovering real project-local installs. We have not checked which predicate would also handle project-vendored copies (#2879) correctly, so we are not proposing one.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11 with Git Bash and no Developer Mode, install gstack for Claude and Codex (`./setup`, `./setup --host codex`).
2. `cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup --status`. The extra `codex project unregistered` row with the move hint shown above appears.
3. `cd <another repo with no project-local gstack> && ~/.claude/skills/gstack/setup --status`. No such row.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: agy global current (1.99.0.0), codex global current (1.99.0.0), claude global current (1.99.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at ~/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Links/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              windows bash    C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe (chosen by git --exec-path)
```
