title: Windows (Git Bash): every `./setup` re-spells the hook commands between `C:/...` and `/c/...` and calls them stale
body:
## What happened

On Windows 11 under Git Bash, every `./setup` run prints these two lines, including a second run straight after the first with no change in between:

```text
  healed hook registrations: removed 0, repointed 4 (backup: settings.json.bak.<ts>; ...)
  re-pointed Stop hook to bash /c/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/gstack/hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook (previous registration held a stale path)
```

For these registrations the hook target never moved. Setup only rewrites the command between two spellings of the same hook path, so the "(previous registration held a stale path)" message is wrong. The heal step and the registration steps write the same hooks in different spellings, and every run undoes the run before it. The `settings.json.bak.*` files from one run show the heal writing every gstack hook as `bash C:/Users/<user>/.claude/skills/gstack/...`, then the later registration steps writing four of them back as `bash /c/Users/<user>/...`. The next run starts from `/c/` and does the same again. Each run rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` several times and leaves several backups. On this machine that came to 10 backups from three runs in one morning.

Expected: a second `./setup` heals nothing and re-points nothing.

This happened on every repeated default `./setup` we ran on this machine. The conversion described below is specific to Git Bash/MSYS. We did not test other platforms.

Cause, from reading main at 4685fa9:

- `setup` heals with `"$SETTINGS_HOOK" prune-stale --repoint "$CANONICAL_GSTACK_ROOT"` (setup:4385). `bin/gstack-settings-hook` passes the root to Bun as an environment variable, `GSTACK_REPOINT_ROOT="$REPOINT_ROOT" bun ...` (bin/gstack-settings-hook:773), and builds `root + "/" + row.relpath` from it (line 827).
- When MSYS starts a native Windows program, it converts environment values that look like POSIX paths. Bun therefore receives `C:/Users/...`, and the heal writes that spelling.
- The registration steps pass `--command "bash $CANONICAL_GSTACK_ROOT/..."`. Examples: the Stop hook at setup:4876-4878, with its `ensure-event` call at setup:4916. A value that starts with `bash ` is not converted, so these keep `/c/Users/...`. `ensure-event` treats the existing entry as the same gstack hook, sees a different command string, re-points it and logs the "stale path" line (setup:4926, and setup:4996 for the other hooks).
- Both sides start from the same `CANONICAL_GSTACK_ROOT` (setup:4327). The only difference is how the root reaches them: an environment variable for the heal, an argument for registration.

The two paths should agree on how they spell a command, or should treat equivalent path spellings as unchanged. `gsWinPath` (bin/gstack-settings-hook:171-174) already separates filesystem normalization from stored command spelling: "stored commands keep the form the firing shell expects". bin/gstack-path-spelling.sh:2-6 names this class of bug: "Comparing two spellings as strings is the bug class behind #3088, #3100 and #3101". Neither the heal nor `ensure-event` uses those helpers.

The conversion is easy to show on its own:

```console
$ X=/c/Users/me/x bun -e 'console.log(process.env.X)'
C:/Users/me/x
$ MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL=X X=/c/Users/me/x bun -e 'console.log(process.env.X)'
/c/Users/me/x
```

Both spellings run under Git Bash, so the hooks keep working. The harm is the settings churn, the build-up of backups, and log lines that describe an equivalent path as stale.

Possible fixes:

- Exclude `GSTACK_REPOINT_ROOT` from MSYS environment conversion for this one Bun call, keeping any exclusions already set in `MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL`.
- Or, in both the heal and `ensure-event`, compare the path inside each command in one spelling (the `gstack_path_shell` / lib/path-spelling.ts helpers), and keep the wrapper, arguments and quoting as they are.

We searched the docs and code at 4685fa9 for an existing setting or guard. We found none: `MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL`, `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` and `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` do not appear in setup or bin/gstack-settings-hook.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11 with Git Bash, install gstack for Claude: `cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && ./setup`.
2. Run `./setup` again and save the output. It shows `healed hook registrations: ... repointed 4` and `re-pointed Stop hook ... (previous registration held a stale path)`.
3. Run it a third time. The same two lines appear, and `ls ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.*` shows several more files than after step 2.

title: Stop gstack-uninstall deleting unpushed or kept work under any folder it removes (GST-2303)
body:
gstack-uninstall now checks every folder it is about to delete for git work that exists nowhere else, and stops instead of deleting it. This serves gstack's goal of being safe to install and remove: uninstalling should never cost you unpushed commits or kept state.

## What changed
- Before deleting anything, uninstall looks for git checkouts inside each host's gstack install (global and project-local), the gstack-made Claude per-skill folders and `~/.gstack`. A checkout with uncommitted changes, commits no remote holds, or a locked worktree stops the uninstall with exit 2 and names the checkout.
- `--keep-state` no longer deletes the state it promised to keep. An install that holds kept state is refused instead.
- A stable-channel install that was updated with `git fetch origin stable` still uninstalls cleanly, including through a `url.insteadOf` rewrite. A commit that only a local fetch (`git fetch . HEAD`) wrote is still treated as unpushed.
- On git older than 2.36, which cannot list worktrees safely, uninstall now refuses rather than guessing.
- The manual removal steps in docs/uninstall.md use the same checks, and docs/troubleshooting.md explains each refusal.

## Why
Uninstall used to check only the repo you ran it from. An unpushed `.gstack` repo inside `~/.claude/skills/gstack`, an edited project-local install, or a notes repo under `.agents/skills/gstack-*` was deleted without warning, and `--keep-state` run from inside the gstack checkout deleted the very lanes it was told to keep.

## Blast radius
Only bin/gstack-uninstall and its docs change, and every new path fails closed: when git cannot prove a checkout is safe, the folder is kept and uninstall exits 2. The 73 uninstall tests (including the docs-helper replays and an old-git shim) pass, and CI free-tests run 42789222890 is green at this head.

## Documentation
**Status:** updated. One factual fix in docs/troubleshooting.md, with no blockers.

Scope: the 5 committed files between 6c23638d and 8eb11739 (bin/gstack-uninstall, test/uninstall.test.ts, docs/uninstall.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and the GST-2303 changelog.d fragment), plus the README.md and docs/install.md links to the uninstall doc. Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked.

- docs/troubleshooting.md: Updated. The git-cannot-read list now includes the `has worktrees git cannot list (gstack-uninstall needs git 2.36 or later)` message and its fix.
- changelog.d/uninstall-checks-every-folder-it-deletes-gst-2303.md: Current.
- README.md and docs/install.md: Current. Both still link to docs/uninstall.md.

Coverage: all shipped features have adequate documentation. The new refusals have reference coverage in docs/uninstall.md and how-to fixes in docs/troubleshooting.md. No diagrams drifted, so there is no documentation debt.

title: Accept AQ. Gemini keys in setup
body:
## Why (in your own words)

Google AI Studio now issues Gemini auth keys that start with `AQ.` (`AQ.Ab...`). `setup` still required `AIza`, so a valid key was rejected before the smoke test. Leave off `--provider` and the same key was classified as OpenAI, then rejected for not starting with `sk-`. This accepts both prefixes. The live Gemini check also redacts an `AQ.` key if an error body echoes it.

## Live evidence

On current main the gate is still one prefix. A fixture that starts with `AQ.` fails before any request:

```
Invalid key. A Gemini key starts with 'AIza'.
```

After this change, same kind of fixture, temp home, no stub:

```
Key saved to ~/.gstack/gemini.json (0600 permissions).

Running smoke test (generating a simple image)...
Smoke test FAILED: Gemini API error (401, model gemini-nano-banana-2.1, key from ~/.gstack/gemini.json): API key not valid.
```

The saved file is mode 0600 and the stored prefix is `AQ.`. Google rejected the fixture. That is the right failure for a fake key. The prefix gate did not fire, and the fixture was not printed.

`bun test design/test/gemini-provider.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail.

## Scope

- **Changed:** the setup prefix gate and its prompt (`design/src/cli.ts`), the auth comment (`design/src/auth.ts`), the live-check redactor (`design/scripts/live-gemini-check.ts`), and the tests (`design/test/gemini-provider.test.ts`).
- **Verified live by:** `setup --provider gemini --key-stdin` with an `AQ.` fixture, plus the Gemini provider test file.
- **Did NOT test:** a real billed AI Studio key. Gemini returning JPEG instead of PNG is separate (#4238).

## Liveness proof (required for external contributors)

No screenshot in this PR. I am not attaching a generated image.

title: Fix six test and eval checks that misread correct work or raced their own fixtures (GST-2338)
body:
This fixes six test and eval checks that failed on correct work or raced their own fixtures, found by the 2026-11-10 daily flaky-test pass (harvest window 2026-11-09T14:00Z to 2026-11-10T14:00Z). It serves the goal of keeping CI red only for real defects, so crews stop rerunning flaky checks. Only tests, fixtures and detectors change; no product code, threshold, trial count, case kind or retry. **Paid eval checks** - **ship-docsync-store** (census 42748129558, main b1702eea): /ship's documentation step has asked models to count each audit launch with `gstack-docs-candidate attempt --state ` since #4192, but the docsync fixture's command interface never listed that call. The model followed the interface, refused to run the undeclared command and stopped before launching any audit. The interface now declares `attempt --state ` and `attempt --help`, and the observer admits exactly that shape. Negative controls stay refused: a state file in the repo, a non-JSON state, a state under the installed skills, a child output inside the repo, a missing or misplaced `--state`, extra flags and the tilde path. - **tpa-absent-darwin** (same census): the model offered "I drive it in gstack's own visible browser (recommended, since Aside isn't available)", and the Aside-drive detector counted it because the option contains the word Aside and a drive verb. A mention that says Aside is missing ("isn't available", "was not detected", "is unavailable", "with no Aside installed") no longer makes an option an Aside drive. The captured render now replays to zero Aside drives; options that also name Aside as the browser they use still count. - **tpa-present defer check** (open note from #4223's /ship): "Until then the step stays blocked on you" and "The step is waiting on you" after another instruction counted as a defer offer. A status line (stays, remains, is blocked or waiting on you) now counts only when an earlier part of the same option puts the step off ("later", "not yet", "not now"; not "not later"). The "I'll mark this step as ..." form, which is what choosing the option does, is unchanged, and every earlier negative control stays false. - **scrape-prototype-path** (outside-voice#1 on #4223): the navigation check credited only browse's "Navigated to (2xx)" line, so `$B goto "" >/dev/null && $B html` would fail a correct run. It now also credits a goto whose stdout goes to /dev/null when the call proves it exited 0: no `Exit code N`, tool error, `Error` or `net::ERR_` line, and every command after the goto is joined by `&&`. The target must be the fixture URL itself or `$PWD` under the case's working directory (followed through literal `cd`). `;`, `||`, `&`, a trailing `; echo`, single-quoted `$PWD`, `cd` elsewhere and a goto quoted inside `echo` stay uncredited. **Free tests** - **test/cso-snapshot-state.test.ts** "equal ticket decisions use token order..." (Free Tests 42779334663 shard 10, #4282): the contender child wrote its result file with a plain `writeFileSync`, and the parent read it as soon as it existed, so it could read it empty (Expected "INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY", Received ""). The child now writes a temp file and renames it into place. A standalone writer/reader loop read an empty file 2,315 and 2,210 times out of 3,000 with the plain write and 0 of 3,000 with the rename. - **test/cso-registry-socket.test.ts** "deadline cleanup removes the whole per-call socket root..." (Free Tests 42772387147 shard 3, #4267): the test gave the watchdog a deadline 150 ms out. The watchdog takes whole seconds and cleans up as soon as the deadline passes, so on a slow start the deadline passed inside the ~1 s startup handshake and the product correctly failed closed ("Registry socket watchdog failed its startup handshake" after 1,024 ms). The deadline is now 2 s out. With the watchdog start delayed 400 ms, 6 of 30 handshakes failed with the 150 ms deadline and 0 of 30 with 2 s. The harness pin for test/helpers/session-runner.ts is re-recorded as non-behavioral: browseNavigatedTo's only caller is the changed scrape-prototype-path case file.

title: Stop /ship's docs audit halting when the child writes prose after its result (GST-2349)
body:
/ship's documentation audit no longer spends an attempt, or stops for an owner sign-off, when the audit writes text after its JSON result. It gets one free re-ask instead, and a "blocked" verdict can never turn into "current" along the way.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Text after the result line gets one free re-ask instead of a spent attempt.** When an audit's output has text after a JSON line carrying its audit id, `gstack-docs-candidate result` doesn't accept it. It prints `FORMAT_REPAIR:` and re-asks once for the whole result line without using one of the two attempts.
- **The re-ask only works one way.** If any JSON line with the audit id said "blocked" or listed a blocker, the reply must stay blocked and keep every one of those blockers (it may add more), and the re-ask prompt says so. A later correction or a fenced "current" example can't turn a blocked audit into a passing one.
- **Content problems still count.** If any of those lines has a missing status, a wrong audit id, or "current" with files listed as edited, the output spends an attempt as before. Output with no JSON line carrying the audit id does too.
- **The audit is told the format plainly.** The re-ask and the retry note both say to put the documentation section inside the JSON as a string and write nothing after the line.
</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

In founderstar #837 and harness-evals #393 the audit concluded "current, no edits" and then restated its section in prose after the JSON. Because the last line was prose, gstack treated the result as unreadable and skipped its free format re-ask. Each rejection spent an attempt, and after both, /ship stopped for an owner sign-off though nothing was wrong. A second-model review of an earlier version showed that ignoring trailing text let a "blocked" verdict flip to "current", and a later review found that a re-ask judged with nothing carried over could do the same. This version keeps the blocked verdict through the re-ask.
</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the documentation audit's result parser (`lib/ship-docs-result.ts`), its re-ask and retry texts, the help comment and one output line in `bin/gstack-docs-candidate`, one sentence in `ship/sections/documentation.md` and the troubleshooting entry. No other check, receipt or review behavior changes.
</details>

title: Keep /review and /ship working in copied Windows installs (GST-2347)
body:
On Windows, /review and /ship stopped at their first step under Codex, Cursor and the other non-Claude hosts. This change makes setup copy the three source files those commands need, so both start again, which keeps gstack's install and core workflows working on every supported platform. ## What changed ![From a copied Windows install, the review planner used to stop on a missing module; with the three files copied it starts](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/S2RIQ7Fbc7U2L2H1dKq2pkmCwPg_obmXfR0x7ycWvDU.png) From a copied Windows install, the review planner used to stop on a missing module; with the three files copied it starts.
Before/after as text: From a copied Windows install, the review planner used to stop on a missing module; with the three files copied it starts ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ gstack-review-plan --help # copied Windows codex root, setup on this branch +gstack-review-plan — the review depth of the next /ship step (docs/review-policy.md#review-depth) -$ gstack-review-plan --help # copied Windows codex root, setup before this PR -error: Cannot find module '../scripts/resolvers/fix-check' from '~/.codex/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-review-plan' + --base the base branch (merge base with HEAD is the diff base); required + --pass full review passes already run in this invocation (default 0) + --last none|full|fix-check the step that just finished (default none: plan pass 1) +exit=0 -Bun v1.4.4 (Linux x64) -exit=1 ~~~
- `setup` now copies `scripts/resolvers/fix-check.ts`, `scripts/discover-skills.ts` and `scripts/lib/ci-history.ts` into each non-Claude host's runtime folder, next to the `bin/` and `lib/` copies it already makes. - `test/runtime-root-assets.test.ts` gains one check per host that follows the static imports of the commands that host's skills run and fails when one resolves outside the runtime folder. It also builds a copied (Windows-style) Codex folder and runs `gstack-review-plan --help` from it. - `test/setup-production-deps.test.ts` moves one sentinel: setup now names `scripts/discover-skills.ts`, so that check scans it as a root file, and its import-walk proof now points at `scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts` instead. - `TODOS.md` records what stays deferred, and a changelog fragment describes the fix for users. ## Why A Windows user running /review under Codex got `Cannot find module '../scripts/resolvers/fix-check'` before any review started. On Windows, setup copies `bin/` and `lib/` instead of linking them, so a module they import only loads if setup copied it too, and it left out `fix-check.ts`; the commands behind /retro and /write-skill had the same gap through the other two files. Now all three are copied, and a test fails CI when a new static import points outside the runtime folder. ## Blast radius This touches the install script (`setup`) and makes it copy three more source files into each non-Claude host's runtime folder; no network access, secrets, permissions, CI workflows or dependencies change. Claude Code installs and linked (non-Windows) installs already reach these files through links, so they behave the same. The copy logic is shared bash (`_link_or_copy` with `IS_WINDOWS=1`), so Linux CI exercises it: on dbb4b50 the new tests fail 8 of 18 with that exact error, and on this branch all 18 pass (script ran). ## Credit The fix was first proposed in outside draft PR #4275 by @SatriaSuriaAriffin. It was rewritten on current main rather than taken from their branch, and the commit carries a Co-authored-by trailer for them. ## Summary Copied Windows installs were missing three `scripts/` modules that `bin/` and `lib/` import, so /review and /ship could not start there. Setup now copies them, a per-host import check guards the copy list, and one existing dependency check was adjusted because setup now names one of those files. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage: the per-host import checks and the copied-root start test in `test/runtime-root-assets.test.ts`. Tests ran: runtime-root-assets 18 Tests ran: tests 1662 (files, carried from CI run 42861319483) ## Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues found. Two passes ran: the first on the whole diff, the second on the follow-up test fix; neither found anything at or above the blocking floor. ### Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/keep-review-working-in-copied-windows-installs.md:4` Changelog says the new test follows every import, but importsOutsideRoot follows static import statements only; dynamic import()/require() (bin/gstack-evidence -> scripts/lib/shard-engine, caught; lib/pregate/flaky-exception.ts -> shard-engine) are unchecked. INVESTIGATE, Blocks: no. - INFORMATIONAL `TODOS.md:428` The edited TODOS entry reads as if the remedy covers only ship-measure, and the line is overlong. FIXABLE, Blocks: no. Gate edits: none detected (5 listed, 3 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## Exploratory QA Pass: two smoke probes on a copied (`IS_WINDOWS=1`) Codex root built from setup's own functions. `gstack-review-plan --help` exits 0, and a real `gstack-review-plan --base main` run exits 0 with the same plan as the source install. Linux bash stands in for Git Bash; there was no native Windows run beyond CI's Windows Smoke and Windows Setup E2E lanes. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. title: pregate secrets: env.kv flags a TypeScript template literal made of ${…} slots and a fixed word
body:
## What happened

`gstack-pregate`'s `secrets` check (gstack-redact, finding `env.kv`, "secret-named assignment, high entropy") fails on an added TypeScript line whose value is a template literal built only from interpolations and a fixed word:

```ts
key: `${over.day}|${over.groomerId}|over_tough|`,
```

The value is a cache/list key, not a credential: every character outside the `${…}` slots is a literal (`|over_tough|`). The same shape on lines already on the base isn't reported, only because those lines aren't added.

## Why it matters

`secrets` can't be downgraded, so the only way through is an `allowlist` entry, which must first land on the base. One false positive on an ordinary TypeScript line costs a separate PR and a review cycle.

## Suggestion

Treat a TypeScript/JavaScript template literal's `${…}` slots as code, the way Python f-string fields and Dart `${…}` are already read as code (GST-738), and the way TypeScript dict entries that read a name are exempt (#3630). A template literal whose non-interpolated text is short or low-entropy and has no credential-shaped run could then be exempt from `env.kv`, while a literal containing a real key shape (`sk-…`, `AKIA…`) still reports.

Seen on gstack 1.99.0.0. The repository is private, so no link to the PR.

title: setup's umask 077 also applies to bun install, so bun's shared package cache gets owner-only files that later installs of other projects hardlink
body:
## What happened

`setup` sets `umask 077` on line 5 for the whole script (`umask 077  # Restrict new files to owner-only (0o600 files, 0o700 dirs)`, added for M9 of #783 to protect gstack's state and log files). The same umask is still in effect when `install_runtime_deps` runs `bun_cmd install` (lines 1913, 1917 and 1920 at f0cd9f8c4b453c1eadd714e4149174ee01179eae), and when setup runs `bun_cmd x playwright install chromium` (lines 2480 and 2482).

Bun extracts each package it downloads into its global install cache (`~/.bun/install/cache` by default). As observed with bun 1.4.4 (reproduction below), the extracted files take the umask of the extracting process, so under setup's umask a package downloaded by gstack's `bun install` lands in the cache with its group and other permission bits removed (in the reproduction: 0600 files in 0700 directories). On Linux, bun installs by hardlinking from that cache by default (bun's `docs/pm/global-cache.mdx`), so when the same user later runs `bun install` in an unrelated project with a normal umask, that project's `node_modules` gets the same 0600 inodes.

We hit this as a failure for a second Unix user. The owning user's separate Bun project (a gbrain checkout) had `node_modules/qs/*` `-rw------- root root`, while the published `qs-6.16.1.tgz` has 0644 entries. A second Unix user on the machine that runs that project then failed with:

```text
error: Cannot find module '<checkout>/node_modules/qs' from '/tmp/[eval]'
note: Cannot read file "<checkout>/node_modules/qs/": EACCES
```

On this machine, 388 of the 572 top-level entries in `~/.bun/install/cache` are 0700, and 17,582 cache files are 0600. We did not trace which process created the qs cache entry; the timing is consistent with gstack's setup: `qs@6.16.1@@@1` was created at 2026-10-26 11:03Z, about 20 minutes after gstack commit a1487458 (2026-10-26 10:44Z) added `qs@6.16.1` to gstack's `bun.lock`. The reproduction below shows the mechanism independently of that history.

Expected: the owner-only umask protects the files setup writes for gstack itself (state and logs) and does not leak into bun's package cache, which is shared by every Bun project of that user. One possible shape: run the bun calls (`install_runtime_deps`, `bun x playwright`) in a subshell with `umask 022`, and check that the state and log files M9 protects keep their owner-only modes. Restrictive cache permissions otherwise propagate into later installations of unrelated projects and can prevent access by another Unix user. We considered reporting this to bun instead, but the restrictive umask is set by setup.

## Steps to reproduce

Bun 1.4.4 on Linux, with a throwaway cache so the real one is untouched:

1. ```bash
   export BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=$PWD/cache
   mkdir a b
   for p in a b; do echo '{"name":"'$p'","version":"0.0.0","dependencies":{"qs":"6.16.1"}}' > $p/package.json; done
   (cd a && umask 077 && bun install)   # what setup does
   (cd b && umask 022 && bun install)   # an unrelated project, normal umask
   stat -c '%a %h %i %n' cache/qs@6.16.1@@@1/lib/index.js a/node_modules/qs/lib/index.js b/node_modules/qs/lib/index.js
   ```
2. Output: all three paths show mode `600`, link count `3` and the same inode number (one filesystem), so project `b` gets the owner-only file through the shared hardlinked inode, although it was installed with umask 022.

Local repair: `chmod -R a+rX <checkout>/node_modules/qs`. Because the files are hardlinks, this also changes the cache copy. The other 0600 cache entries remain until the next install that pulls them into a project another user reads.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.99.0.0), agy global current (1.99.0.0), codex global current (1.99.0.0)
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
...
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: Claude Code 2.1.309
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), Linux 7.0.0
- gstack: 1.99.0.0 installed (9ab50347); claims checked against `main` at f0cd9f8c4b453c1eadd714e4149174ee01179eae
- bun: 1.4.4
- Related: #783 (security audit, M9 asked for `umask 077` at the top of `setup`; this issue keeps that intent and only asks that it not reach bun's package cache). The gstack docs at f0cd9f8 do not cover the umask's effect on bun's cache.

title: redact env.kv: Python settings reads and camelCase field-path constants are false positives; concat and comments are missed
body:
The `env.kv` pattern in `lib/redact-patterns.ts` (~line 965) produces recurring false positives on Python code, and has two blind spots. A downstream repo has added four path- and pattern-scoped pregate allowlist entries for these false positives so far. Found on gstack `1.91.369.0` (`34c65288b`). We reproduced each case with the real `redact-engine.scan` and `pregate/allowlist.applyAllowlist`, and the `gstack-redact --from-file --json` CLI gave the same results.

## 1. False positive: Python attribute reads of settings

```python
aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY,
```
This fires `env.kv` (MEDIUM, blocking). `isBareEnvRead` (#2912) exempts `os.environ[...]`, `os.getenv(...)` and `process.env.X`, but not `settings.X`, `config.X` or `conf.X`. `isSourceExpression` is TS-only (~line 684).

Suggested fix: when the whole value is an unquoted dotted name ending in an UPPER_SNAKE attribute, with nothing but `,`, `;` or `)` after it, treat it as a read, the same way `isBareEnvRead` does. A one-line `ENV_READ_SPAN` extension passed the existing engine suites in a local copy. It still let through `password=settings.DB_PASSWORD; token=<S>`, so the fix needs that case as a regression test.

## 2. False positive: a bare `KEY` constant holding a dotted camelCase field path

```python
KEY = "form.section.fieldName"
```
This fires because a bare `KEY` counts as credential-shaped (`isCredentialShapedEnvName` rule ii) and camelCase dotted paths pass the entropy ≥ 3.0 threshold. `isSchemaFieldIdentifier` only exempts `<word>_key` names with lowercase snake values. The same happens for `field_key="form.section.fieldName",` when the value is camelCase.

## 3. Missed detection: a short first token followed by a concatenated secret

```python
KEY = "form.x" + "Qx9vL2mZp8Rt4Kw7Yn3Bh2Jd"
```
This gives **no finding**. The regex captures only the first token, which falls below the entropy threshold, and the rest of the line is never checked.

## 4. Blind spot: comment text

```python
x = 1  # API_KEY = "Qx9vL2mZp8Rt4Kw7Yn3Bh2Jd"
```
This gives no `env.kv` finding because the regex is anchored at `^[ \t]*`. A secret in a trailing comment is caught only when the code before it happens to fire. So an allowlist entry for that code silently hides the comment as well. (Provider-shaped tokens like AKIA, `ghp_` and `sk_live_` still fire under their own ids.)

## Regression cases

`<S>` is a 24–32-character mixed-case alphanumeric literal.

| Line | Expected |
|---|---|
| `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY,` | no finding |
| `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY)` | no finding |
| `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY or "<S>",` | env.kv |
| `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY + "<S>",` | env.kv |
| `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY.replace("a", "<S>"),` | env.kv |
| `password=settings.DB_PASSWORD; token="<S>"` | env.kv |
| `SECRET_KEY=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY` in a `.env` file | env.kv (not Python) |
| `KEY = "form.section.fieldName"` | no finding |
| `field_key="form.section.fieldName",` | no finding |
| `KEY = "form.<S>"` | env.kv |
| `KEY = "form.x" + "<S>"` | env.kv (currently no finding) |
| `x = 1  # API_KEY = "<S>"` | env.kv (currently no finding) |

Allowlist note, for anyone writing entries in the meantime: `patternHits` only forbids `[\w-]` after the match (`pregate/allowlist.ts:37`). A pattern without an end-of-line lookahead therefore also allowlists `<benign> or "<secret>"` on the same line. It may be worth documenting this in `docs/pregate.md#allowlist`.

title: Keep browser checks and question preferences working in copied installs
body:
Copied installations can check browser readiness and read question preferences again, keeping the existing one-install workflow working across host runtimes.

## Summary

A copied runtime omits `package.json` and dependencies. `gstack-browser-ensure` therefore reports missing Playwright even when the checkout recorded in `.source-path` has working dependencies. Use that checkout only when the runtime has no package manifest and the pointer names a directory containing both the package manifest and the gstack helper. Preserve source installs and invalid-pointer behavior, including read-only `--check`.

The runtime asset list also omits `one-way-doors.ts` and `psychographic-signals.ts`, which the Bash question helper imports dynamically. Copy those two existing modules so `--check` and `--signal-keys` start successfully.

## Blast radius

Only browser dependency-root selection and copied runtime assets change. Regression tests execute native helper processes and setup's own copied-root functions; the browser cases use a local Playwright stub. No new public flags, dependencies or installation steps are introduced.

## Validation

- Linux owner suites: 38 passed, zero failed, 161 assertions.
- Linux adjacent setup/isolation/timeout checks: 45 passed, zero failed. Product typecheck passed; test typecheck reported no new diagnostics.
- Native Windows copied-source cases: seven passed, zero failed. The three valid-pointer cases fail against the base helper; the copied question case fails against the base asset list.
- Native Windows isolation file: ten passed, zero failed with the repository's documented 30-second test timeout. The initial cold run using Bun's default five-second timeout failed; no test threshold, assertion or skip was changed.
- Bash syntax, whitespace, preflight, secret scan, typecheck, module-size and conflict-marker guards passed. Independent source and adversarial reviews found no issues.

Eight regression cases extend two existing test files, covering normal paths, spaces, CRLF pointers, empty/stale/non-gstack pointers, source-install precedence and actual copied question commands.

Required contributor checks, including `free-tests` and `windows-smoke`, passed at exact head `98eee100c99f6e170a57cc559ca6fd06cf4b4d40`. [Free Tests run 42957652364](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/42957652364) recorded 37,110 tests across 1,668 files on Linux, macOS and Windows, with six explicitly skipped files. Expected secret-dependent fork jobs were skipped; they are not reported as passes.

The internal CI-carry verifier intentionally rejects fork runs (`fork_run`). That protects maintainer checkout/queue evidence and is distinct from GitHub review readiness. This PR follows [the outside-contributor process](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/f0cd9f8c4b453c1eadd714e4149174ee01179eae/CONTRIBUTING.md#how-a-contributors-pr-lands): the maintainer crew reviews the report, rewrites the repair and verifies its own branch. No internal queue receipt, paid-eval pass or merge acceptance is claimed.

## Documentation

**Status:** current — no documentation corrections were required for the selected copied-runtime repair.

Audited scope: base `f0cd9f8c4b453c1eadd714e4149174ee01179eae`, branch `codex/copied-runtime-followup`; four unstaged source/test files and the selected changelog fragment. The change redirects browser readiness checks to a valid recorded source checkout when the copied runtime lacks `package.json`, and includes two existing question-classifier modules in setup's runtime assets. No public command, flag or configuration option was added.

Documentation health:
- README.md — Current (installation and Windows copy-refresh guidance remain accurate).

- docs/troubleshooting.md — Current for the relevant browser-bootstrap and copied-runtime entries; unrelated diagnostic entries were outside this scoped review.
- changelog.d/codex-copied-runtime-followup.md — Current (accurately describes both repairs; protected bytes preserved).
- CHANGELOG.md — Current for the release-heading consistency check (1.99.0.0 matches the existing version source; no voice or content edit performed).

Documentation coverage:
- Browser readiness in copied runtimes — existing reference and recovery how-to in docs/troubleshooting.md, installation guidance in README.md/docs/install.md, and the existing source-checkout explanation cover the repaired behavior. No separate tutorial is needed for this internal repair.
- Question classifiers in copied runtimes — restoration of existing runtime assets, with no new public interface; existing host/setup references remain accurate.

Documentation debt: no critical or common gap introduced by the selected changes. Diagram drift: none found in the reviewed architecture, contributor and host diagrams. This was a static documentation/source audit; runtime results supplied by the parent were not independently rerun here.

## Test plan

- [x] Focused copied-runtime regressions and adjacent setup checks.
- [x] Product/test typechecks, source review, bounded CLI smoke and documentation audit.
- [x] Full free-suite CI and Windows smoke on this exact PR head.

## Why (in your own words)

Copied Codex runtimes on Windows could not start two prerequisite checks: browser readiness looked in a dependency-free runtime, and question preferences could not load their classifiers. This was encountered while using the installed skills in a real project. The repair lets those existing commands start using the dependencies and modules setup already owns.

Fresh native Windows reproduction used two isolated copied-runtime fixtures with identical source pointers to the existing checkout and no local package manifest or dependencies. The before helper came from base `f0cd9f8c`; the after helper is byte-for-byte the PR helper. These commands launch the real installed Chromium through Playwright, rather than the regression tests' stub. Paths are shown relative to the checkout for readability.

title: Let browser checks and question preferences work from non-Claude hosts' gstack folders (GST-2442)
body:
Browser skills and question preferences work again from the gstack folders that setup gives Codex, Cursor and the other non-Claude hosts. This keeps install, startup and the core workflows working on every supported host.

## What changed

![gstack-browser-ensure in a Codex gstack folder: before it looked for Playwright only in that folder; now it uses the recorded checkout's](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/Wl_ATchEKvtev9-M7Ek14AlQUUJWUbQAond25If6gKI.png)

gstack-browser-ensure in a Codex gstack folder: before, it looked for Playwright only in that folder; now it uses the recorded checkout's dependencies.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: gstack-browser-ensure in a Codex gstack folder: before it looked for Playwright only in that folder; now it uses the recorded checkout's</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 $ gstack-browser-ensure --check   # from a Codex-style gstack folder
+BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE Chromium did not launch via node (browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1254/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell)
+fix: /workspace/gstack/bin/gstack-browser-ensure (installs Chromium; ~115 MiB) (BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE; https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#browser-ensure-failed)
+# Playwright now resolves from the recorded checkout; this test machine has no Chromium download yet
-BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE playwright is not installed under ~/.codex/skills/gstack/node_modules
-fix: cd ~/.codex/skills/gstack && ./setup (BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE; https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#browser-ensure-failed)
 
~~~

</details>

## Why

A user on Codex reported (#4290) that every browser skill stopped with `BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE playwright is not installed` even though their gstack checkout had Playwright, and that the question-preference helper failed with `Cannot find module './scripts/one-way-doors.ts'`. Host folders have no `package.json` or `node_modules` of their own and record the checkout in `.source-path`, so the browser helper now follows that pointer under strict checks, and setup now copies the two scripts the question helper loads at run time.

## Blast radius

The pointer is followed only when the host folder has no `package.json`, `.source-path` is a regular file holding an absolute path, and its real directory holds gstack's own regular `package.json` and `bin/gstack-browser-ensure`; anything else keeps today's behaviour, and `--check` still never writes (bin/gstack-browser-ensure:30-46 read; walked by test/gstack-browser-ensure.test.ts and two QA probes). Setup's change only adds two files to the runtime asset list, pinned by test/runtime-root-assets.test.ts on linked and copied roots (script ran: 44 pass).

## Summary

Codex, Cursor and Factory users hit a browser skill that said Playwright was missing when it wasn't, and a question helper that could not start. The browser helper now uses the checkout setup recorded, and only when every check on that pointer holds, so a missing, relative, stale, linked or non-gstack pointer changes nothing. Setup now ships the two classifier scripts the question helper imports inside its `bun -e`, which the existing import walk cannot see. This is a crew rewrite of outside PR #4290 on current main; that branch was read as text only.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage: test/gstack-browser-ensure.test.ts covers valid, linked, relative, empty, stale and non-gstack pointers, a root's own package.json winning, and `--check` writing nothing; test/runtime-root-assets.test.ts covers the question helper's `--check` and `--signal-keys` from linked and copied (Windows) runtime roots.

title: Stop the doctor floor test failing on every release that adds no policy key (GST-2441)
body:
Release PRs stop going red on a test bug, so the daily stable cut can ship again. Any release that adds no new ship-policy key, such as the v1.99.1.0 release PR #4291, used to fail free-tests on one doctor test.

## What changed

At VERSION 1.99.1.0 (a release stamp that adds no policy key), main's floor-row test fails and this PR's version passes. The before/after image was not rendered: the screenshot tool's secret scanner reads the version numbers as public IP addresses and refuses the capture, so the text version follows.

## Why

The test took its expected version from the repo's VERSION, while the doctor correctly reads policies as the newest policy key it knows. The test now computes that newest key from the same table validatePolicy reads, so it expects what the doctor prints at any VERSION.

## Blast radius

Only test/policy-floor-stable.test.ts and one changelog.d fragment change; no product code moved, so no caller or host can change behavior. The doctor's own rule at bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh:513-523 (read) prints the "reads policies as" suffix only when the newest key is newer than VERSION, which is the exact condition the new expectation uses, and the test passed at both VERSION 1.99.0.0 and 1.99.1.0 (script ran).

The doctor floor-row test assumed the repo's VERSION always equals the newest policy key. That holds only on a release that adds a key, so every other release stamp failed it. The expected version now comes from the policy key table, and the first PASS line expects the suffix only when that key is newer than VERSION.

title: gstack-approvals: no way to retire approvals after a crew resets its rules
body:
## What happened

A Captain rebuilt its crew's rules from the current templates in one sitting: a new CREW.md and AGENTS.md, and a new `CONTRACT_DATE`. The owner's principle for the reset was that no earlier approval carries over, whether a standing merge word, a standing spend grant or a plan approval.

`gstack-approvals` has no way to express that. It reads every approval root (the machine-local record, the Captain drive's `approvals/` mirror and the `READ_ALSO` roots; `lib/approval-record.ts` unions them and can mirror rows back). So a standing row written before the reset still renders in a PR body and still resolves in `plan-check` as if it were current. Moving old files into an archive folder only works partly, because a lane machine's local record can carry them back, and nothing marks a row as retired.

## What we did meanwhile

We added a crew-specific CREW.md rule: rows dated before `CONTRACT_DATE` grant nothing, and a lane asks through the controller instead. crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're filing it here.

## Suggestion

An approval epoch. For example, `gstack-approvals retire --before <ISO time> --words <owner's words> --by <who> --reason <why>` writes one retirement row that `render`, `plan-check` and resolution honour: earlier rows show as history and never as authority. It would help if `CONTRACT_DATE` carried a time, so rule 20's stale READYs and the epoch use the same instant. A date alone can't separate a morning receipt from an afternoon reset.

## Environment

- Host: Capy (claude-code threads), Captain workflow
- gstack: 1.99.0.0 (main at 554390da387d97c8b93dc2337c2ab41d4271e9f4)

title: Captain: nothing checks that a crew's CREW.md and AGENTS.md still match the templates
body:
## What happened

Rules drifted in a crew's files over a few weeks: a Captain's rule files grew to several hundred KB of local rules before the crew reset them from the templates. After the reset, nothing in gstack checks that they stay aligned.

- `gstack-doctor` checks the install, runtime and hooks.
- `gstack-ship-queue train doctor` checks the merge setup.
- `gstack-skill-contract` checks skill contracts against Claude Code transcripts.

None of them compares a crew's CREW.md and AGENTS.md with `captain/templates/` at a known SHA.

## Suggestion

A read-only check, for example `gstack-crew-check --crew <drive dir> --base <policy>`, that a Captain can run in the daily issue sweep and after each gstack upgrade:

1. Rules 1–24 match the template at the checked SHA, and every Home path exists.
2. Every parameter is filled and agrees with the base policy and the live branch rules (reusing `train doctor`).
3. Every crew-specific rule carries an owner date and the owner's words; one without them is reported as the controller's call.
4. No rule or open issue points at a path that is missing or archived.
5. The files' sizes, with a warning when they grow past a threshold, since growth is how the drift showed up.

It would report findings only and never rewrite rules. A missing input would print as unavailable, never as a pass.

## Environment

- Host: Capy (claude-code threads), Captain workflow
- gstack: 1.99.0.0 (main at 554390da387d97c8b93dc2337c2ab41d4271e9f4)

title: captain.md and the AGENTS.md template say the Captain's AGENTS.md reaches the crew; on Capy it doesn't
body:
## What happened

`crew/docs/captain.md` (the Captain drive layout: "Scope instructions in the drive root (`AGENTS.md`, `CREW.md`) apply to every thread in the crew") and `captain/templates/AGENTS.md` both say the Captain's AGENTS.md reaches every crew thread.

On Capy it doesn't. Capy's docs (Captains, the Captain drive table) say AGENTS.md holds "The Captain's own rules ... Crew threads don't read it", and CREW.md holds "Rules that every crew thread reads on every turn".

The result: an owner's standing word recorded only in AGENTS.md, which is where the template keeps the decisions log, never reaches the lanes. They either ask the owner again or act without it.

## Suggestion

In captain.md and the AGENTS.md template, say that on Capy AGENTS.md reaches the Captain alone. Have the template put every owner word a lane must cite into CREW.md's standing-approvals table, which the template already starts. Keep AGENTS.md for what only the Captain needs.

title: Stop the stable cut counting its own check runs against the commit it cuts (GST-2463)
body:
The daily stable release no longer blocks itself on its own check run, so a commit the release gate passed can reach stable the same day. This serves the stable channel's promise that important fixes reach users within a day.

## What changed

`gateVerdict` in `crew/scripts/release-cut.ts` now sets aside the check runs that the stable-release workflow produced itself, whether running or finished. Every other check run is judged exactly as before.

**How it recognises its own check runs.** The lookup runs only when a candidate has a check run that is still going or red. It reads the commit's workflow runs (`GET repos/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>`) and keeps the runs whose `path` is `.github/workflows/weekly-release.yml` (`CUT_WORKFLOW`). For each of those it lists every job, re-run attempts included (`GET repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{id}/jobs?filter=all`). It then drops only the check runs whose `id` is one of those job ids, because an Actions job's id is its check run's id. That was checked live: job 130716281605 is the "Cut the release" check run on 19ed2ac5. A job name like "Cut the release" can be reused by any workflow, so the name is never the key.

**Why not the check suite.** The first version of this PR matched on `check_suite.id`. Two reviewers pointed out that GitHub files a check run that a workflow creates through the API with `GITHUB_TOKEN` under some github-actions check suite on that commit, and the creator can't choose which. The `main-backstop` check runs from `release-gate.yml` and `evals-main-backstop.yml` are created exactly that way. So a red `main-backstop` could land in the cut's suite, be set aside, and let the cut release past a failed backstop. Matching by job id leaves API-created check runs alone.

**Fails closed to today's behaviour.** If the workflow-runs or jobs read fails, nothing is set aside, so the verdict is what it was before this change. A clean commit makes no extra API call.

**Permissions.** Both jobs in `weekly-release.yml` gain `actions: read` (read-only) for the lookup.

**Lines that change gate behaviour** (`crew/scripts/release-cut.ts` at the final head): line 79, `export const CUT_WORKFLOW = '.github/workflows/weekly-release.yml';`, and lines 126-136, the `if (runs.some(c => c.status !== 'completed' || RED.has(c.conclusion ?? '')))` block that builds `own` from the jobs of the cut's workflow runs and ends with `runs = runs.filter(c => !(typeof c.id === 'number' && own.has(c.id)));`. Everything after it (required check, backstop, train and release-record evidence, red and running checks) is unchanged and runs over the remaining check runs. The freeze and the RED release-record hold live in `readTrainNotes`, which this doesn't touch.

## Why

"Stable has been stuck on v1.99.0.0." The daily cut runs on main's newest commit, so its own "Cut the release" job lands a check run on the very commit it might release. While the cut runs, that commit looks unfinished and is skipped. When a cut fails, its red check run keeps the commit out of every later cut. On 2026-11-11 the release gate passed 19ed2ac5 (v1.99.1.0). The 18:16Z cut (run 43076123863) skipped it because its own job was still going, failed with NO_RELEASE_PR, and left a red "Cut the release" check run on 19ed2ac5. With this change, the live `release-cut.ts --dry-run --daily` plans 19ed2ac5.

## Blast radius

This touches only the stable cut's commit selection (`gateVerdict`, whose one production caller is `planRelease`) and the read-only permissions of `weekly-release.yml`. It's safe because the set-aside is limited to check runs whose id matches a job of a `weekly-release.yml` run on that commit. A failed lookup sets nothing aside. That was confirmed by reading release-cut.ts:126-136 and by tests that fail on the old code and pass here.

## Summary

The cut was deadlocking on itself, because its own running or failed job counted as a not-green check on the commit it was cutting. It now recognises its own jobs through the workflow file and those runs' job ids, and ignores them. The review turned up the check-suite flaw described above, so matching moved from check suites to job ids. `docs/releases.md` now explains the set-aside, the `actions: read` it needs and the fail-safe.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage. These tests in `crew/test/release-cut.test.ts` (describe "the cut sets aside its own check runs (GST-2463)") fail against the earlier versions of `release-cut.ts` (main's, and the check-suite version) and pass here:
- The cut's own in-progress, queued or failed check run, on a commit with a GREEN release record, is green.
- Still not green: a red run from another workflow beside the cut's own; a "Cut the release" job from another workflow's run; a running check run that isn't one of the cut's jobs; a red API-created `main-backstop` filed under the cut's check suite; a running `free-tests`; no gate evidence; an unreadable workflow-runs API.
- The 11-11 state: head with its backstop and the cut still running, a release-gated commit carrying the failed cut's red run, and stable on the released commit before it. The cut picks the gated commit, and a RED release record on it still refuses.

`test/weekly-release-workflow.test.ts` expects `actions: read` on both jobs.

Tests ran: free 1662 (files, CI run 43082282390 attempt 2)

Pre-Landing Review: 5 issues — 2 auto-fixed (one defect, found by the Red Team and the native adversarial pass), 0 asked, 0 deferred, 3 noted. The suite-membership defect (`p1/red-team#1` = `p1/adversarial-native#1`) is fixed in 505dbe1c. The first item in Review notes below is that same finding, now fixed. title: autoplan phase publication is unverified when a Remote Control bridge_status record is the journal root
body:
## What happened

In a Claude Code 2.1.309 session where Remote Control is active before the first prompt, guarded reviewer Agent calls of `/autoplan` pass, but the publication hook prints:

```text
PreToolUse:Agent says: [autoplan] phase publication was NOT verified for this session (journal shape unrecognized_shape:preamble:system:bridge_status): This Claude Code journal shape is not recognized (unrecognized_shape:preamble:system:bridge_status). Phase-report enforcement was skipped for this call. (code unrecognized_shape:preamble:system:bridge_status, Claude Code 2.1.309).
```

Phase-publication enforcement is skipped on each of these calls. Our guard log (`~/.gstack/analytics/autoplan-guard.jsonl`) holds 21 `unverified` decisions with this code from one day, and no other disposition for it. `docs/autoplan-guard-troubleshooting.md` (lines 62-74 at 19ed2ac5) describes this code as usually a Claude Code journal format change and asks for the detail and version, which is this report.

The allow-with-warning is the documented fail-open path for unknown shapes, and it works as designed here. The request is to recognise this shape, so a session with Remote Control active from the start is verified like a plain interactive session instead of degrading.

### Cause

When Remote Control is active, Claude Code writes a `system` record with subtype `bridge_status` as the conversation root (`parentUuid: null`), and the first user message is its child. The journal head, with values omitted:

```text
{"type":"mode"}
{"type":"permission-mode"}
{"type":"bridge-session", ...}                       # bridgeSessionId, sessionId, ...
{"type":"system","subtype":"bridge_status","parentUuid":null,"isMeta":false,
 "content":"/remote-control is active · Continue here, on your phone, or at https://claude.ai/code/session_…",
 "url":"…","uuid":"A","cwd":"…","version":"2.1.309", ...}
{"type":"user","parentUuid":"A","uuid":"B", ...}       # first user turn
{"type":"attachment","parentUuid":"B", ...}            # SessionStart hook attachments follow
```

In `lib/claude-journal-records.ts` at 19ed2ac5, `ownedCausalOrder` only accepts SessionStart hook attachments before the first message (line 387):

```ts
const preamble = top.slice(0, turn).find(n => !n.sessionStart);
```

`sessionStartRecord` (line 244) matches only `type: 'attachment'` with `attachment.hookEvent === 'SessionStart'`. So the `bridge_status` root becomes `preamble:system:bridge_status` (line 389), and `autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts` (lines 760-762) turns the second identical read into an unverified allow. The record carries the Remote Control status line (`content` above) and is the parent of the first user message.

We saw this root form in two journals. In a third, `bridge_status` sits mid-file with a non-null parent (after a `stop_hook_summary`), as an ordinary chain node, so the preamble check does not apply there.

### Proposed fix

Accept a `system` record with subtype `bridge_status` and `parentUuid: null` as a preamble node, the way a SessionStart attachment is accepted, and nothing broader: every other unknown preamble record (for example the `preamble:system:local_command` shape the tests pin) stays an `unrecognized_shape`. Add a fixture with this head to the guard tests. In the root-uniqueness check (`candidates` and `carriesTurn`, lines 372-383), message-less root candidates and the walk through their descendants recognize only SessionStart records, so the fix should also be tested against a competing root next to a `bridge_status` head, for example a second null-parent user record.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Claude Code 2.1.309 session in which Remote Control is already active before the first prompt, in a repo where gstack is installed. Our two affected sessions were started through Remote Control; we have not tried other ways to reach this head.
2. Run `/autoplan` on any plan, or anything that dispatches a guarded reviewer Agent call.
3. Guarded Agent calls print the `unrecognized_shape:preamble:system:bridge_status` warning above. The session's journal under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` starts with the head shown in "Cause".

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.0.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.99.0.0), agy global current (1.99.0.0), codex global current (1.99.0.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.160.1; self-locate ok
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 0)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.99.0.0 (9ab50347ac37)
ok              claude code     2.1.309 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal no session journals for this project
ok              guard log       90 decisions (5 denied)
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

(Trimmed: two `codex` model/probe lines. Doctor ran from a different checkout than the affected sessions.)

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: Claude Code 2.1.309, Remote Control (bridge) session
- OS: Linux 7.0.0
- gstack: installed 1.99.0.0 (9ab50347). The code cited above was checked on `main` at 19ed2ac5, where it reads the same.
- Related: earlier autoplan guard journal fixes landed in #3069 and #3209. We found no open or closed issue for `bridge_status` or `unrecognized_shape`.

title: Let an owner's recorded approval close a gate finding in unattended /ship (GST-2491)
body:
An unattended /ship can now finish a PR whose gate change the owner approved, so an owner's recorded decision is carried through by the tooling instead of handed back to the owner as a step to type. Until now an unattended run forced every loosened-gate finding open and nothing could close it, which stopped founderstar#906 after Garry had approved its test-gate change.

## What changed

- **A new recording path.** `gstack-approvals gate --finding <fingerprint> --gate-id <gate_id> --head <stop head> --reason '<the gate change>' --words '<the owner's exact words>' --by '<who recorded>'` writes one approved row with scope `gate_disposition <fingerprint> <gate_id> <head>`. It refuses a missing gate id, empty or multi-line words, a multi-line reason, a head that isn't a commit, a `--by` naming gstack, and any call while this checkout holds an open /ship run's marker. `gstack-approvals add` refuses the scope, and `gstack-approvals dispositions` prints the `Gate disposition: …` line for each row.
- **Where it counts.** A disposition closes a gate finding only on a review row with that exact fingerprint and gate id, whose `range_base..commit` holds the head (a first pass: only the row's own commit). So a later, different loosening of the same line stays open. `gstack-review-read` then shows the finding as `kept` with the disposition's id and reason and grades the row CURRENT, so the existing /ship gate rules read it as kept. finish applies the same test to granted fix-checks. The review log itself is unchanged and still says `open`; rulings and anything the lane writes on its own row still close nothing.
- **Nothing is hidden.** finish prints `GATE_DISPOSITION: <fp> [gate <gate_id>] at <head12> by <who> at <time>: <reason> — "<words>" (approval <id>)`, marked not applied when no review row's range holds it. `gstack-ship-receipt write` records `gate_dispositions` and refuses a body that doesn't carry each `Gate disposition: …` line word for word, and the READY block prints each one. A disposition row can't stand in for a plan approval.
- **Docs.** A new gate dispositions section in docs/ship-policy.md beside ruled notes, a troubleshooting entry for an unattended stop on an open gate finding, and the PR-body section names the new line.

## Why

The owner's approval should be recorded once and carried through by the tooling, not handed back to the owner as a step to type (R82). The trust model is the one ruled notes already use, with the owner's words in the approval record and the row written outside the lane's own run.

## Blast radius

Only runs whose review logged an open gate finding and whose owner then recorded a `gstack-approvals gate` row behave differently. Every other review row, ruling, receipt and READY is unchanged. As with rulings, a review row derived from a findings file is not cleared by a disposition. `test/ship-gate-dispositions.test.ts` fails on main and passes with the fix, and covers the negative controls: no row, another fingerprint or gate id, a head outside the range, a row recorded while the /ship marker is held, a ruling, empty words, and the lane's own review-log claim.
## Documentation

**Status:** blocked: one factual doc correction is needed, and this read-only audit could not make it.

**Scope:** 3 commits (d8fcbc430, 7a7384b52, b25284969) on `owner-approved-gate-changes-finish-unattended-ship` against base 0ead11c8, plus the unstaged change to `docs/troubleshooting.md`. 18 files are selected; the authored docs among them are `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl` (with its generated `pr-body.md`) and one changelog fragment.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/ship-policy.md`: Current. The new Gate dispositions section matches `gstack-approvals gate` and `dispositions`, `lib/gate-dispositions.ts`, the review-read view, finish output, the receipt and the READY line.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Needs update. The new `gate-finding-open-unattended` entry and the unstaged receipt-write line are accurate, but the check-prose entry (line 7047) does not list `Gate disposition: …` among the required lines never read as claims.
- `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl` / `pr-body.md`: Current. Both carry the `Gate disposition:` line, and the generated file matches its template.
- `changelog.d/owner-approved-gate-changes-finish-unattended-ship.md`: Current. It is consistent with the code; voice is not audited in this mode.

**Coverage debt:** `gstack-approvals gate` and `dispositions` have reference coverage (ship-policy, the CLI help) and how-to coverage (troubleshooting). There is no tutorial, and the explanation is inline in ship-policy. Neither gap is critical.

**Diagram drift:** none. No diagram names the changed modules.

Documentation exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-11 via agent message to GSTA-518, 2026-11-11: Accepted: the two troubleshooting.md lines adding `Gate disposition:` to the RECEIPT_INVALID required-body list and the never-read-as-claims list were made after the last docs audit and aren't re-audited; the Captain's pre-land cross-family audit covers them.

## Pre-Landing Review

The full panel ran on pass 1 (specialists, red team, coverage audit, adversarial and an outside voice on GPT-6.1 Sol), and the one fix round bound the disposition to the gate id, made the reader show a closed finding as kept, and kept an unreadable disposition store from crashing the reader. The second pass over the fix range came back clean.

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=2 deferred=2 noted=10 fixed=1 unbound=5
Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

## Deferred findings

- Deferred: rows derived from a findings file (`status_source: derived`) can't use a disposition, the same limit rulings have. The Captain (GSTA-36) accepted keeping it to mirror rulings; docs/ship-policy.md#gate-dispositions says so.
- Deferred: the Step 19 draft rule in `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl` keys on `open`; the reader's kept view now covers it.

## Review notes

- A disposition can't be withdrawn, and one finish marks not applied is still listed in the receipt (same as rulings).
- `gate` can be run from a sibling worktree with `--branch`; the PR-body disclosure is the control, as for rulings.
- SHA-256 repositories are ignored.
- A gate finding with no gate id matches `--gate-id undefined`; a wrong gate id makes finish name the fingerprint instead.
- The reader shows a dispositioned finding as kept on a derived row too, though the row is not cleared.
- Missing tests: the kept-reread branch in finish, the reader's unreadable-store fallback, the plan-record exclusion.

## Approvals

title: Let the sealed-output guard check pull requests larger than 256 MiB (GST-2494)
body:
The check that keeps sealed eval answers out of public pushes can now read pull requests of any size. This unblocks crews whose PRs carry millions of generated fixture lines, which the guard used to refuse every time. ## What changed - The two large reads, the text check over each commit's added lines and the check for patches that already landed on the base, now write git's output to a private temporary file and read it one line at a time, only after git exits 0. A partial output never reaches a verdict. - What the guard finds, skips and refuses is unchanged. Rules, policy and refusal codes are untouched. - A git failure still refuses, and the message now says what failed, for example `git diff-tree -p failed (exit 128): fatal: ...`, `(killed by SIGKILL)`, `(timed out after 120 s, SIGTERM)` or `(could not run git: ...)`. docs/troubleshooting.md#sealed-output-refused explains each one. No screenshot: this is a library change with no visible surface. The terminal output from the QA probes is under Exploratory QA. ## Why it's safe `test/sealed-stream.test.ts` carries a verbatim copy of the old buffered code and runs it beside the new code on fixtures with renames, copies, a merge resolution, binary files, CRLF, invalid UTF-8 and cherry-picks at an offset. Findings and skipped commits match exactly at read sizes from 1 byte up. The same file shows the old code refusing with an empty error when its buffer is small, and the new code giving the right answer on the same commits. Negative controls cover a non-zero exit, a process killed mid-output, a timeout, a missing git and an unreadable object; each one refuses and names the cause. A synthetic repository (not in CI) with 4.05 million generated lines, 352 MB of text-check output and 509 MB of landed-check output: the new guard finished in 8.4 s at 61 MB peak memory, with 4 landed commits skipped and the 3 planted markers found. The old guard refused in 5.0 s at 1.39 GB. ## Blast radius Only `lib/sealed-guard.ts` changes, and only repos that set a `sealed` policy run it. `test/sealed-stream.test.ts` runs a verbatim copy of the old buffered code beside the new code and gets the same findings and skipped commits at read sizes from 1 byte up (script ran), and the free suite passed at this head in CI run 43110512097. The temporary file needs free space about the size of the patch in the system temp directory. ## Why Harness Evals' PR with about 4 million lines of fixtures refused every push with `SEALED_OUTPUT_REFUSED` and an empty `git diff-tree -p failed:`, because the guard held all of git's output in memory under a 256 MiB limit. Now the guard reads the patch from disk in pieces, so a big PR gets the same verdict a small one would. ## Summary A synthetic repository (not in CI) with 4.05 million generated lines produced 352 MB of text-check output and 509 MB of landed-check output. The new guard finished in 8.4 s at 61 MB peak memory, with 4 landed commits skipped and the 3 planted markers found. The old guard refused in 5.0 s at 1.39 GB. A follow-up commit loosens one test's expected error text, because Bun on Windows says "Executable not found in $PATH" where Linux says ENOENT. ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. `lib/sealed-guard.ts` is the one changed runtime file, and `test/sealed-stream.test.ts` names it (deterministic coverage map, no audit reader). It covers parity with the old code, a non-zero exit after partial output, a process killed mid-stream, a timeout, a missing git binary, temp-file cleanup and an unreadable object. The fake-git cases skip on Windows. Tests ran: test 37128 (carried from free-tests run 43110512097 at tree a4ed874d0f68) ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 2 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 1 noted. Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Outside review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): CLEAN. Native adversarial review: 4 low-severity notes, recommendation "ship as-is". ## Review notes None of these would fail a test, break production, or lose data or secrets, so none was fixed: - lib/sealed-guard.ts:104 (testing, advisory, skipped): `GitStreamOptions` and its `bin` override are seams only the tests use. The reviewer notes they are the cheapest way to test the fail-closed paths. - lib/sealed-guard.ts:121 (red-team, noted): on Windows, a cleanup error in `finally` could replace the verdict with a raw EBUSY message. It still refuses. Not reproduced. - lib/sealed-guard.ts:106 (adversarial, noted): a run killed mid-read leaves the spooled patch in a 0600 file inside a 0700 temp directory. - changelog and docs (adversarial, noted): where `/tmp` is a RAM-backed tmpfs, the spool uses memory, and a small container fails closed with a git exit. - lib/sealed-guard.ts:252 (adversarial, noted): the findings list has no cap. It already had none for patches under 256 MiB. - lib/sealed-guard.ts readLines (adversarial, noted): a `chunkBytes` of 0 or less reads no lines. Only tests can set it. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on an owned fixture repository (59 MB commit, 2 million generated lines), running `bin/gstack-pregate sealed` from this branch: 2 of 2 passed. - A clean push gives `SEALED: clear findings=0 commits=1`, exit 0. - A sealed answer marker in a commit after the large one gives `sealed.answer leak.txt:2` and `SEALED_OUTPUT_REFUSED`, exit 1. Limits: the fixture is smaller than the old 256 MiB limit (the over-limit case is the synthetic run above). A first smoke run pointed its first probe at the installed gstack instead of this branch and ended inconclusive, so it was replaced. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix, exempt from plan review. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The documentation already matches this change, and no edits were needed. **Scope:** 3 commits from 0ead11c8 to 4815d5d2 on `sealed-guard-stream-large-diffs`, touching `lib/sealed-guard.ts`, `test/sealed-stream.test.ts`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` and `changelog.d/sealed-guard-stream-large-diffs.md`. Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. I checked the sealed-guard docs (`docs/troubleshooting.md#sealed-output-refused` and `docs/pregate.md#sealed`) against the new streamed `git diff-tree` reads. **Documentation health:** - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The branch adds a paragraph on the new `git diff-tree -p failed ()` error. Its error format, 120 s timeout, temp-file streaming, free-disk-space note and the old 256 MiB limit all match the code. - `docs/pregate.md`: current. The sealed section never described the in-memory size limit, so nothing in it is stale. - `changelog.d/sealed-guard-stream-large-diffs.md`: read and accurate, not edited. - `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`: no change needed. **Coverage debt:** none. title: Stop /ship counting a reviewer's "nothing blocks" summary as a blocking finding (GST-2495)
body:
/ship no longer turns an adversarial reviewer's "nothing blocks" summary into a blocking finding. This serves the shipping goal directly: a false blocker stops a crew's /ship receipt from going green when nothing in the review blocks. **What went wrong.** On founderstar#926 the native adversarial reader opened its review with "I found nothing that blocks. There are three Low findings, all FIXABLE, and none can change outcomes, draws or save replay." The review ledger had a special case for this kind of verdict line, but it only recognised a few spellings of "nothing blocks", and only when the line named no severity besides FIXABLE. This line missed on both counts ("nothing that blocks", and "Low"). The general closing-summary reader refuses any line with FIXABLE in it, so the line fell through to the default rule, where the native reader's FIXABLE means CRITICAL. Lead judgment may not lower a CRITICAL row, so the receipt said `blocking_found=1` with nothing blocking. **What changed** (`lib/review-ledger.ts`, the verdict-line rule only): - The no-blocker clause now covers the common phrasings: "nothing that blocks", "nothing blocking", "none of which would block", "none of them is a blocker", "no finding that would block", "no blockers", "nothing here blocks", alongside the old ones. - A verdict line may now count its findings at a severity ("three Low findings", "one Medium and two Low findings"). It collects at the most severe count it states (Low here, High if it says High, CRITICAL if it says CRITICAL), never lower and never raised to CRITICAL by its FIXABLE tag. - On the relaxed review class the same line used to be raised to CRITICAL after collection. It now stays at its collected label there too; the existing #3901 verdict line ("…all FIXABLE, and none blocks.") changes from CRITICAL to FIXABLE on that class for the same reason. **What stays strict.** A line is still collected as CRITICAL when it also says something blocks ("I found one blocker", "One finding blocks the merge", a `Blocks:` naming a finding), adds an exception ("nothing that blocks except the token leak", "apart from…", a "but" after the denial), names a file and line, carries its own Severity or Blocks field, or uses FIXABLE outside a count or an "all/both/are FIXABLE" tag ("The cache key drops the tree, FIXABLE."). That last one was quietly accepted before when the line said "nothing blocks"; it's now a blocker, which is the fail-closed direction. Real findings under the summary parse exactly as before. **Evidence.** The new tests in `test/review-ledger-verdict-line.test.ts` use the captured founderstar verdict text and fail on main (4 of 8 tests). Every captured reader fixture and pinned input the ledger corpus holds (`test/fixtures/review-ledger/main-labels.json` with its generated shapes, plus every reader output under `test/fixtures/review-ledger`, `outside-review-severity` and `codex-review`, each under four reader roles on both review classes: 3,874 parses, 4,818 rows, 1,666 CRITICAL) gives identical labels on main and on this branch.
