title: The lander must accept each owner-approved gate change before a PR merges (GST-2491)
body:
An unattended /ship can now finish a PR whose gate change the owner approved, and the person who lands the PR has to accept each such approval by id before it merges. This keeps crews shipping without a human in the loop while the merge decision stays with a separate actor, which is what Founderstar's lander asked for. This supersedes #4299 and builds on it: #4299 added `gstack-approvals gate`, the owner's recorded answer that closes one gate finding. Credit to that PR for the recorder, the matcher and the disclosure lines, all kept here. ## What changed - **The lander decides.** `gstack-ship-queue land --pin` works out the gate dispositions the approval store applies at the pin, prints each as a `GATE_DISPOSITION:` line, and merges only when the lander passes `--accept-gate-disposition ` for every one. It refuses with the new `QUEUE_GATE_DISPOSITION` code when one isn't accepted, when an accepted id names nothing, or when the receipt or PR body leaves one out or invents one. It never trusts the receipt for this. - **A check for landers that merge another way.** `gstack-ship-queue verify --pr --pin [--accept-gate-disposition ]...` runs the same function as land, read-only, and exits 0 only when every disposition is accepted. - **ready cross-checks too.** `ready` prints the dispositions it works out and refuses a receipt or body that differs from the store. - **The writer is harder to misuse.** `gstack-approvals gate` refuses while a /ship run is open on the branch in any worktree of the repository, and it checks and appends under a lock in the git common dir that /ship's preflight also takes. It refuses `--gate-id undefined`, and a gate finding without a gate id is never closed. - **Hand-made rows are ignored.** A disposition counts only with every field the writer writes, `source: gate`, the store's own branch and a digest over those fields. The digest catches edits; it isn't authentication. - **Disclosure can't be skipped.** `gstack-ship-receipt write` refuses to write a receipt while a disposition applies at HEAD unless `--body` carries each line. ## Why A lane runs as the same user as everything else on its machine, so no local file is out of its reach. It could write a disposition row itself, or record one from a sibling worktree. That was the blocking finding in the cross-family audit of #4299. The real boundary is the separate actor who lands the PR. The hardening makes casual self-approval fail, and the lander's explicit acceptance is what authorizes the rest. ## Blast radius Only PRs with an owner gate disposition are affected; land, verify and ready print nothing new when the store holds none. A store that can't be read now stops ready and land instead of reading as empty. A lander that merges through the REST API runs `verify --pin` first. ## Test Coverage New tests in test/ship-gate-dispositions.test.ts (sibling-worktree writer, malformed and edited rows, literal undefined gate id, receipt write without --body) and test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts (end to end: owner row, unattended review reads CURRENT, ready, land refuses until accepted, verify agrees; a hand-appended row; receipt and body mismatches). The focused lane ran 72 tests, all passing; the free suite carried from CI run 43119721034. ## Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues found. Below-floor notes, recorded and not fixed here: - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:84`: a parked /ship's marker refuses `gstack-approvals gate` on that checkout. This is intended, because the owner records from their own session. - `bin/gstack-approvals:197`: `--by` with leading or trailing spaces records a row that never counts (fails closed). - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:28`: a U+2028 or U+2029 in the reason records a row that never counts (fails closed). - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:73`: no command withdraws a disposition, so an obsolete one still has to be accepted. - `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:274`: the receipt and land read the store's current contents, not what finish applied. - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:104`: the stale-lock takeover is check-then-remove. - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:11`: a same-user lane can still author a well-formed row; the lander's acceptance is the boundary (documented). - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:66`: `verify --pin` checks the receipt and dispositions only, not READY, CI, mergeability or a freeze. - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:200`: land checks dispositions before it takes the land lock. - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:25`: heads must be 40 hex, so a SHA-256 repository records rows that never count. - `lib/gate-dispositions.ts:90`: a leftover marker in a detached worktree refuses `gate` on every branch. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=0 fixed=0 scope=frozen ledgers_read=2 dispatches=4 Gate edits: none detected (4 listed, 0 read) ## Exploratory QA Smoke in an isolated clone with its own state root and approval directory: 5 of 5 probes passed. They covered listing; refusal while a run is open, with nothing written; a malformed `--accept-gate-disposition` as a usage error; recording and listing once the run closes; and a literal `undefined` gate id refused. ## Issues Refs #4299 ## Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match the change, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** the authored docs touched by the owner-gate-disposition change (base 0ead11c8, head ab73c3fd, 26 committed files, nothing uncommitted): the new `gstack-approvals gate` and `dispositions` commands, `gstack-ship-queue land --accept-gate-disposition`, the new `verify --pin`, and the `Gate disposition:` lines required in the receipt and PR body. **Documentation health** - `docs/ship-policy.md`: current. It covers gate dispositions, who authorizes a disposition, and the `QUEUE_GATE_DISPOSITION` land check. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. It covers `QUEUE_GATE_DISPOSITION`, the open gate finding in an unattended run, and the receipt and prose rules for `Gate disposition:` lines. - `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl`: current. It lists `Gate disposition:` lines, and the generated copies match. - `changelog.d/owner-approved-gate-changes-finish-unattended-ship.md`: present. Reviewed only, not edited. - `docs/captain.md`, `captain/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `docs/releases.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG_STYLE.md`: current. The change doesn't affect them. **Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Test plan - [x] Focused lane: test/ship-gate-dispositions.test.ts and test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts (72 tests pass) - [x] Free suite carried from CI run 43119721034 at this tree - [x] macOS and Windows remote lanes cleared from green runs at ab73c3f

title: Let a repo keep its tier-only test folders out of /ship's local test run (GST-2500)
body:
A pull request that touches tier-only tests (alphaclaw's `tests/live/**` and `tests/container/**`, which its test runner skips unless a tier flag is set) made pregate select those tests, plus the tests that import their helpers, and run them in /ship's local lane. The runner found no test files, the lane failed, and /ship wrote no receipt. This unblocks alphaclaw's /ship receipts. **What changed** - A `[]` declaration in `.gstack/pregate.json` on a folder inside a test directory (`tests/live/**`; the directory is `test/`, `tests/`, `spec/` or `__tests__/`) now keeps every selected test under that glob out of the local lane, whether the test was touched or picked through an import. A `[]` on the whole directory (`test/**`, which repos already use to clear helpers) changes nothing. Always-run tests still join, and a remote platform lane that selects the test still owes it. Before, `[]` only cleared a file no test mapped to, and a test always maps to itself, so the declaration did nothing for test files. - Nothing is hidden: the `lanes` result gets one line per glob, `declared test tree : N test file(s) not run in the local lane (declared [] in ; the repo runs them in their own tier)`, printed and recorded in the pregate record with the other lanes lines. `--explain` names each skipped test, and when nothing is left for the local lane the detail says how many were left out. - Nothing loosens by default. Without such a declaration selection is unchanged; a `[]` on any other glob never skips a test; a test outside the glob that imports a file inside it still runs. As with every `[]`, a new one counts only once it is on the base branch (`--policy-from head` still refuses it). The Dart `integration_test/` handling is untouched. - Docs: the `dependencies` row in docs/pregate.md says a declared test tree is the repo's statement that those tests run in their own tier, not in /ship's local lane. Changelog fragment marked `important: blocker`. **Tests** `test/pregate-declared-test-tree.test.ts` builds a fixture repo with `tests/live/x.test.js` importing `tests/live/fixture.js`. On main the three declared cases fail (the tier test runs, `PREGATE_LANE_FAILED`); with this change they pass. Controls: no declaration, a non-matching `tests/container/**` glob and a whole-directory `tests/**` still run the tier test; touching only a tier test still runs the always-run tests; a branch-only `[]` is refused under `--policy-from head`; a `[]` on `scripts/**` still runs `scripts/z.test.js`; `test/outside.test.js` importing the live fixture still runs. **Open notes (below the blocking floor; review at 5239196c)** - Remote platform lanes still owe a dropped tier test: in a repo whose profiled macOS or Windows job also skips its tier tests, `gstack-pregate clear --remote --run-url` could refuse with `tests_uncovered`. Remote lanes are out of scope here and the docs state this behavior (red team, confidence 4, lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:308). - When one lane's tests are all dropped and another lane keeps tests, the `Tiers ran:` evidence line can still name the dropped lane's tier. Only that line is affected (red team, confidence 6, lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:324). ## Approvals Plan: exempt: bug fix that unblocks a crew; bug fixes need no plan review

title: The lander must accept each owner-approved gate change before a PR merges (GST-2491)
body:
An unattended /ship can now finish a PR whose gate change the owner approved, and the person who lands the PR has to accept each such approval by id before it merges. This keeps crews shipping without a human in the loop while the merge decision stays with a separate actor, which is what Founderstar's lander asked for.

This supersedes #4302 and #4299 and builds on both. #4299 added `gstack-approvals gate`, the owner's recorded answer that closes one gate finding; credit to it for the recorder, the matcher and the disclosure lines. #4302 added the lander's acceptance, `verify --pin`, the writer hardening and the receipt's always-recorded set; credit to it for all of that. This PR carries #4302's head unchanged and adds the two fixes its last review found.

## What changed

- **The lander decides.** `gstack-ship-queue land --pin` works out the gate dispositions the approval store applies at the pin, prints each as a `GATE_DISPOSITION:` line, and merges only when the lander passes `--accept-gate-disposition <approval id>` for every one. It refuses with `QUEUE_GATE_DISPOSITION` when one isn't accepted, when an accepted id names nothing, or when the receipt or PR body leaves one out, changes one or invents one. It never trusts the receipt for this.
- **A check for landers that merge another way.** `gstack-ship-queue verify --pr <n> --pin <sha> [--accept-gate-disposition <id>]...` runs the same function as land, read-only, and exits 0 only when every disposition is accepted.
- **The receipt always carries the applied set.** `gate_dispositions` is always written, as `[]` when none applies, so a merger reading another state root, or a store that lost a row after the receipt, refuses instead of reading as nothing to accept. `ready` prints the dispositions it works out and refuses the same mismatches.
- **A rewritten branch no longer strands itself.** In a full clone, a row whose head commit is gone (the branch was rewritten and garbage-collected, or the name reused) just doesn't apply, because the pin's history is all present and can't contain it. A pin missing from the clone refuses, and a shallow clone that can't prove a row's ancestry refuses and says to deepen it.
- **The writer is harder to misuse.** `gstack-approvals gate` refuses while a /ship run is open on the branch in any worktree, checks and appends under a lock in the git common dir that /ship's preflight also takes, and refuses `--gate-id undefined`.
- **Hand-made rows are ignored.** A disposition counts only with every field the writer writes, `source: gate`, the store's own branch and a digest over those fields. The digest catches edits; it isn't authentication.
- **Disclosure can't be skipped.** `gstack-ship-receipt write` refuses while a disposition applies at HEAD unless `--body` carries each line.

## Why

A lane runs as the same user as everything else on its machine, so it could write a disposition row itself. The real boundary is the separate actor who lands the PR: the hardening makes casual self-approval fail, and the lander's explicit acceptance authorizes the rest.

## Blast radius

Only PRs with an owner gate disposition are affected; land, verify and ready print nothing new when the store holds none. A store that can't be read stops ready and land instead of reading as empty. A lander that merges through the REST API runs `verify --pin` first.

## Test Coverage

test/ship-gate-dispositions.test.ts and test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts cover the writer, malformed rows, the receipt's disclosure and the lander's acceptance end to end. New here: a branch rewritten and garbage-collected so a recorded row's head is gone, where ready, verify, land and receipt write keep working with that row not applied; a pin missing from the clone refuses; a shallow clone refuses and says to deepen. test/gstack-ship-receipt-docs.test.ts now expects `gate_dispositions` as the receipt's last key.

## Pre-Landing Review

## Review notes (below the blocking floor)
- Outside voice #1 (deferred): under train or legacy merge routes a disposition still clears a gate finding, but only `land --pin` and `verify --pin` enforce `--accept-gate-disposition`. gstack runs `merge: direct`, so this repository is not exposed; repositories on trains are.
- Receipt write now refuses on a detached HEAD (no approval-store branch), where ruled notes treat it as none.
- `verify --pin` does not check that `--pr` is numeric the way `land` does.
- Acceptance trusts text the lane can write (design question; the docs already say the digest is not authentication).
- The open-run refusal is reported under APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID, whose summary talks about a missing field.
- Coverage gaps: stale-lock reclaim, lock timeout, a malformed accept id, a missing pin.
- Pass 2: a live /ship run past its 120-minute lease, or one resumed after a Capy machine sleep (capy-server restarts, so the lease reads stale), no longer counts as open, so its own runner could record a disposition; the lander's acceptance stays the boundary.
- Pass 2: the 60 s lease-check timeout under the gate lock can outlast the lock's 60 s stale window.

title: Let a repo keep its tier-only test folders out of /ship's local test run (GST-2500)
body:
A repo can now mark a test folder that only runs in its own separate setup, such as alphaclaw's `tests/live/**`, so /ship stops trying to run those tests on your machine before a merge. Before this, touching those tests made /ship run them locally, the repo's test command found nothing to run, and /ship could not finish.

This supersedes #4303, which it builds on, and fixes the three problems a cross-family review found there.

## What changed

- A `[]` declaration in `.gstack/pregate.json` on a folder inside a test directory (`tests/live/**` or `tests/live/*`, where the directory is `test/`, `tests/`, `spec/` or `__tests__/`) keeps every selected test under that glob out of the local lane, whether it was touched or picked through an import. A `[]` on the whole directory (`test/**`) or on a single test file changes nothing.
- The exclusion is local-only. A test that `.gstack/always-run.json` names still runs. The remote gate, the `test_backend` runner with its `PREGATE_FILES_FILE`, and any remote platform lane still receive every selected test.
- Only a trusted policy counts, meaning the base branch's `.gstack/pregate.json` or the user's own policy file. A new `[]` on a branch is still refused under `--policy-from head`, and a bootstrap head policy drops nothing.
- The `lanes` result prints and records one `declared test tree <glob>: N test file(s) not run in the local lane` line per glob, and `--explain` names each skipped test.

## Why

alphaclaw's /ship could not write a receipt for any PR that touched its tier-only tests, because the local lane ran tests its own runner refuses to run. The declaration gives the repo a plain way to say those tests run in their own tier, without hiding them from the remote gate.

## Summary

- Declared test trees stay out of the local lane, with always-run tests kept and remote obligations unchanged.
- A trusted policy is required, so a branch cannot use the declaration to skip its own tests.
- The changelog fragment was reworded into plain sentences after review (prose-lint).

## Blast radius

Only repos whose base or user policy already has a `[]` on a folder inside a test directory see a change, and gstack's own policy has none. Without such a declaration, lane selection is unchanged. The change touches lib/pregate lane selection and the lanes check, and nothing else in /ship.

## Test Coverage

The coverage audit rated 10 of 11 changed behaviors as tested (91%, 82% at two stars or better). One gap remains, the `--from-run` filter on `gateTests`, which has no test.

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 3 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 3 asked (0 fixed, 3 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted
Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

The full plan ran once at full depth with the specialists (testing, security, state-machines), Red Team, a native adversarial reader and an outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, CLEAN). No finding reached the blocking floor.

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke, 2 probes, pass. `bun test test/pregate-declared-test-tree.test.ts` and the adjacent `bun test test/pregate-selection.test.ts` both exited 0.

## Issues

None.

## TODOS

No TODOS.md changes.

## Documentation
**Status:** current. The branch's documentation already matches the change, so no edits were needed.

**Scope:** 8 committed files plus 1 unstaged file between base 842fef1f and head 0f36e241. The change lets a `[]` declaration on a folder inside a test directory (for example `tests/live/**`) keep the selected tests under it out of /ship's local pregate lane. The remote gate, `test_backend` and platform lanes still cover those tests, tests named in always-run still run, and a head-bootstrap policy's `[]` drops nothing.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/pregate.md: current. The `dependencies` and `runner` rows describe the declared test tree rule, its limits and the `declared test tree` output line.
- changelog.d/declared-test-trees-skip-local-lane.md: current. Its unstaged rewording matches the code.
- docs/test-impact.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, docs/ship-policy.md: current. None of them cover this behavior.

**Coverage debt:** The declared test tree is documented only as a reference entry in pregate.md's policy table. There is no how-to, such as a worked `tests/live/**` example in its own section. This is a common gap, not a critical one.

**Diagram drift:** none found.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/pregate-declared-test-tree.test.ts` (9 pass, local lane in preflight and finish)
- [x] CI free tests carried from run 43139175050 at 7aee41f
- [x] macOS named regressions cleared by run 43139175050; Windows smoke cleared by run 43138319683

## Open notes

- **Remote obligation depends on core count.** On a machine with 8 or more cores, a diff that touches only declared-tree tests passes with nothing owed, because no remote obligation is created there. Under 8 cores with a remote gate or a non-local test backend, the remote gate still owes those tests. This is the settled design for this PR; whether a declared tree should be out of every lane is a product call.
- **Existing `[]` entries gain a meaning.** A downstream policy that already has `"test/helpers/**": []` will now also keep test files under that folder out of the local lane, with only an informational line.
- **The provenance line names `.gstack/pregate.json`** even when the declaration came from the user policy (the printed lanes line names the right policy).
- **A diff with only tier tests reports `REPO_COMMANDS_NOT_ALLOWED`** when run without `--allow-repo-commands`, although nothing would run locally.
- An extglob glob such as `tests/!(unit)/**` passes the folder check, but pregate's glob matcher reads it literally, so it matches nothing.

title: Count a test-dir runner and skip engine sidecars in the retro test census
body:
`/retro` on a Godot repo whose whole suite is `tests/run.gd` (run with `godot --headless -s tests/run.gd`) reported `TEST_FILES_TOTAL: 0`, while `TEST_FILES_CHANGED: 2` counted the `tests/run.gd.uid` sidecar Godot writes next to every script.

**Changes (`bin/gstack-retro-metrics`)**
- **`TEST_FILES_TOTAL` fallback:** the filename-convention census runs first, as now. Only when it finds 0 does it count code files under `tests?/`, `specs?/` and `__tests__/`, minus prose and `.uid`/`.import`/`.meta`. Repos that follow a convention keep today's number, so the existing "dir-homed helpers do not count" case (`tests/utils.py`) still passes.
- **`is_test`:** `.uid`/`.import` (Godot) and `.meta` (Unity) sidecars return 0 like prose, so they leave `TEST_FILES_CHANGED` and `TEST_INSERTIONS`.

**Test (`test/gstack-retro-metrics.test.ts`)**
New fixture: `games/brick.gd`, `tests/run.gd`, `tests/run.gd.uid`, `tests/README.md` → `TEST_FILES_TOTAL: 1`, `TEST_FILES_CHANGED: 1`, `TEST_INSERTIONS: 1`. Seen failing before the change (0, then 2), passing after.

title: Ask which skills to register at first setup, and name added or removed skills at upgrade
body:
## What I'd like

`disabled_skills` (#1206) works well for dropping skills I don't use, and it already covers every host. But it is hard to find: README.md and docs/ don't mention it, only `bin/gstack-config`'s comments and the changelog do. I found it after turning off dozens of skills one project at a time in Claude Code's `skillOverrides`. Two prompts built on it would make it part of setup:

1. **First setup asks once.** Following setup's existing first-run prompts (skill naming, the plan-tune hooks, the credential push guard: only with an interactive terminal and no `--quiet`, a time-bounded read with a safe default, the answer saved so it isn't asked again): "Register all skills, or choose?" The default is all, which is today's behaviour. Choose lists the skills in groups (planning and review, QA and browser, design, deploy, iOS, gbrain, other hosts), one line each, and writes the rest to `disabled_skills`. Scripted installs need no new flag: they set `disabled_skills` before `./setup`, and a set value skips the prompt.

2. **Upgrade names what changed in the skill list.** After an upgrade, list by name the skills added and removed since the old version. Example: 1.99 removes `/plan-eng-review` and `/investigate`, which I only learned by reading the changelog; "What's new" summarizes it in 5 to 7 bullets, so a removal can get lost. For added skills, ask: register them, choose, or leave them off. A config key could set the default for later upgrades, e.g. `new_skills: ask | register | leave_off`, with `register` (today's behaviour) when there's no terminal.

Open question: in `--team` mode, should the picker be skipped so the shared repo's install decides?

## Why

Each registered skill's description is in every request's skill list, so unused ones cost tokens and can be picked by mistake (the iOS skills on a Windows machine). Today new skills arrive registered without notice at upgrade, so a trimmed list grows back.

## Environment

gstack 1.96.0.0 (behaviour checked against main at b9bbc31c, 1.99.1.0), Claude Code 2.1.306, Windows 11 with Git Bash.

title: Disabling open-gstack-browser leaves its installed connect-chrome alias registered
body:
## What happened

`gstack-config set disabled_skills ios-clean,ios-design-review,ios-fix,ios-qa,ios-sync,setup-gbrain,sync-gbrain,codex,open-gstack-browser,pair-agent,runaway-stopper,ubicloud` relinked ("Relinked 51 skills") and removed the other disabled skills, but `~/.claude/skills/connect-chrome/SKILL.md` (the backwards-compatible alias copy that setup wrote before the skill was disabled) is still there, so `/connect-chrome` still shows in Claude Code.
```text
$ gstack-config set disabled_skills ...,connect-chrome,...
Error: unknown skill 'connect-chrome' in disabled_skills. Did you mean 'context-restore'? Existing value left unchanged.
```

title: troubleshooting: no entry for a gate-sweep run whose steps finished green but whose job stays in_progress
body:
Seen on gstack 1.99.1.0 (Capy cloud lanes).

A promotion PR's gate-sweep workflow run finished every step green, but GitHub kept the job in_progress. Cancel and rerun were both refused, and new Actions runs queued behind it. About 90 minutes passed before we found a workaround.

What worked: converting the PR to draft and back to ready. That started a fresh gate-sweep run, which went green in about 5 minutes. The dead run stayed listed as queued.

troubleshooting.md has no entry for this symptom. Suggest adding:
- how to recognise it: steps complete, job in_progress, cancel refused
- the draft-to-ready workaround
- whether the sweep or the land step should treat a run whose steps are all complete as finished, rather than waiting on the job status.

title: pregate literals: raising a two-digit constant flags every unrelated occurrence of the old value
body:
Seen on gstack 1.99.1.0.

PREGATE_LITERALS blocked a one-line change that raised an exported numeric constant from 10 to 11. The check treated the old value's bare literal as changed or relevant in about 194 lines across 11 unrelated files, so the only way through was waiver markers on all of them. We shipped without the raise instead.

Expected: compare the constant's own declaration, and the places that use its identifier, rather than every bare occurrence of the old number. Short numbers like 10 appear everywhere, so the false positives grow with the number of digits removed.

title: ship docs audit: the result validator reads bracketed Next.js route paths as globs (DOCS_RESULT_INVALID)
body:
Seen on gstack 1.99.1.0, in unattended /ship runs.

At Step 14.5, the docs-audit child returned status current. Its reviewed-files list included Next.js dynamic route paths such as `app/api/items/[id]/route.ts`. The result validator treats the square brackets as a glob character class, matches nothing, and refuses the result with DOCS_RESULT_INVALID.

Both audit attempts fail the same way, because every attempt lists the same paths. So the run stops at Blocked recovery and needs an owner exception, even though the audit found nothing wrong. We hit this twice in one night, on two separate PRs.

Expected: validate listed paths literally, or escape glob metacharacters before matching. Next.js, SvelteKit and other file-routed frameworks all use bracketed segments.

title: Give a tests-only change one reviewer in the /ship review plan (GST-2547)
body:
A pull request that changes only test files now gets one independent reviewer in /ship. Before, `gstack-review-plan` printed a plan with zero readers for such a diff, so the only review was the author re-reading its own work.

## What changed

- A tests-only diff's first pass now dispatches one batched reader on the Testing checklist (`DISPATCH: specialist batched effort=medium checklists=testing`). It leaves any docs in the diff out of what it reads. A clean pass, or below-floor fixes that change no runtime lines, still ends the loop after that one round.
- The same holds under `review.panel off` and `review.panel risk`, where tests used to get only the author's core read.
- A diff whose only code is registered generated outputs (no runtime lines) gets one batched reader on the code checklists over the whole diff, so no non-docs diff plans zero readers on its first pass.
- If a forced specialist already reads a tests diff, it stays its own reader, as on main, and no batched Testing reader is added.
- A docs-only diff still plans no reader (R81), and the plans for code, gate-class and security diffs are unchanged. `docs/review-policy.md` and the CLI help say so.

## Why

Review depth follows risk (R51): docs, tests and write-ups get one reviewer and one round, never none. A tests-only change could pass /ship with nobody but its author reading it.

## Blast radius

The change is inside `planReview` and `leanPlan` in `lib/review-depth.ts`, which every /ship review consumer reads (`gstack-review-dispatch pass`, finish, the receipt and ready). A deterministic no-loss replay over 186,624 plan cases found 0 plans that got lighter and 2,392 that gained exactly one batched reader, all on tests-only or outputs-only diffs. The review-depth pin is updated with that replay (`test/fixtures/review-pins/replays/GST-2547.json`).

## Test Coverage

title: Remove the /connect-chrome alias when /open-gstack-browser is disabled (#4308)
body: Disabling `/open-gstack-browser` now takes its backwards-compat alias `/connect-chrome` off too. Before, `gstack-config set disabled_skills open-gstack-browser` removed the skill's own entry and left the alias in Claude Code's skill list. ## Why (in your own words) setup installs `/connect-chrome` as a second entry for `/open-gstack-browser`: a copy of that skill's SKILL.md with `name:` rewritten, written by `_install_alias_skill_md` into `~/.claude/skills/connect-chrome` (`gstack-connect-chrome` with `skill_prefix`). `disabled_skills` reaches a Claude install through `bin/gstack-relink`, which walks the checkout's skill directories and cleans the entries named after each disabled skill. The alias never comes up in that walk. The loop skips the symlinked `connect-chrome` source dir on purpose (#2201), and a checkout made without symlinks has no such dir at all. So the alias outlives the skill it points at, and `/connect-chrome` still loads a skill the user turned off. This addresses #4308, reported with reproduction steps by @dipbazz. The issue left one thing unchecked, whether the next full `./setup` clears the alias. It does not (transcript below). setup's alias installer returns early for a disabled skill, which keeps a fresh install clean but removes nothing that is already there. **Validation status:** [Full free CI passed](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/43213839652) on head `4398d0d18` (35 checks passed, 21 skipped, none failed), including all eleven free-suite shards, typecheck, macOS named regressions, Windows setup and Windows smoke. The three new cases fail on unchanged main and pass with the fix. Locally, 199 focused checks pass on the final tree, and the full free suite ran once with every failing file rerun alone on this head and on unchanged main (below): none of the failures comes from this change. Required selected paid coverage and remaining shipping reviews are still pending; skipped fork jobs are not passes. ### Why this shape `gstack-config set disabled_skills` runs `gstack-relink`, not setup, so the removal has to live in relink for the command to take effect when the user runs it. relink already has the function for the job. `_cleanup_skill_entry` removes an entry only when it can prove gstack owns it, and it already recognizes a copy whose `name:` line was rewritten to the entry's own name, which is what the alias is. The fix is two calls to it in the branch that handles a skill kept off. The two alias names are spelled out because a checkout without symlinks gives relink nothing to discover them from. setup and `bin/gstack-uninstall` already spell out the same names. Nine lines in one script, two cases in relink's owner test file, one case in the `disabled_skills` setup suite, and one changelog fragment. Fine to absorb into a wave. ### What it does - When `open-gstack-browser` is kept off, `gstack-relink` also cleans `~/.claude/skills/connect-chrome` and `~/.claude/skills/gstack-connect-chrome`, through the same ownership gate as every other entry. - A user's own skill named `connect-chrome` is reported and left byte-identical, like any other entry gstack cannot prove is its own. - Adds two cases to `test/relink.test.ts`. One removes both alias names on a checkout with no symlinked alias dir, and checks that an enabled skill keeps its alias. The other keeps a user's own `connect-chrome` skill. - Adds one case to the `disabled_skills (#1206)` block of `test/setup-install-registry.test.ts`. It runs the real `./setup` and follows the alias through disable, setup, enable and setup. ### What it deliberately does not do - No change to `setup`. Its alias installer already skips a disabled skill and writes the alias back on its next run once the skill is enabled. `gstack-relink` still never creates this alias (#2201 keeps that in setup), so after re-enabling, `/connect-chrome` returns with the next `./setup`, not with the config command. The first commit added a two-line comment to `setup`; the second takes it out, because any edit to `setup` switches the paid-eval planner to its full fallback. - No change to which names `disabled_skills` accepts. Naming `connect-chrome` itself is still refused on a checkout without symlinks (the reporter's second message, reproduced below) and still accepted with no effect on a checkout with them. With the alias following its skill, the only thing left for that name to do is hide the alias alone, which is a new option, not this bug. - Nothing for the alias left under its old name after a `skill_prefix` flip (`gstack-connect-chrome` stays after a switch to flat names). It showed up while testing, it is the same on unchanged main, and it is separate from #4308. - Nothing for #4307 (choosing skills at first setup) or for `setup --status` (#4190). - No `VERSION`, package-version, released `CHANGELOG.md`, README or ETHOS edits. Release notes are one entry-text-only `changelog.d/` fragment. ## Live evidence Bun 1.4.4 on Linux, `LC_ALL=C`, private `HOME` and `GSTACK_HOME`. No browser or live model was used. The transcripts come from the real `./setup` and `gstack-config`, run against a throwaway `HOME` by the repo's install fixture (the real checkout files with stubbed binaries). The listings are filtered to the two names involved, and setup's own output is left out. ### Actual CLI before and after **Before, on main at `bc858ffc6`:** ```text $ ./setup --host claude --no-prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome open-gstack-browser $ gstack-config set disabled_skills open-gstack-browser Router: disabled skills left out of ~/.claude/skills/gstack/SKILL.md Relinked 59 skills as flat names Disabled (gstack-config disabled_skills, not registered): open-gstack-browser exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome $ ./setup --host claude --no-prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome ``` The last two commands are the step the issue left unchecked. A full `./setup` leaves the alias in place too. **After, on this branch:** ```text $ ./setup --host claude --no-prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome open-gstack-browser $ gstack-config set disabled_skills open-gstack-browser Router: disabled skills left out of ~/.claude/skills/gstack/SKILL.md Relinked 59 skills as flat names Disabled (gstack-config disabled_skills, not registered): open-gstack-browser exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' (nothing) $ ./setup --host claude --no-prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' (nothing) $ gstack-config set disabled_skills "" Relinked 60 skills as flat names exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' open-gstack-browser $ ./setup --host claude --no-prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome open-gstack-browser ``` **A prefixed install where the user owns a skill named `connect-chrome`, on this branch.** gstack's `gstack-connect-chrome` goes, and the user's skill stays byte-identical and is reported: ```text $ ./setup --host claude --prefix exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' gstack-connect-chrome gstack-open-gstack-browser # the user adds their own skill named connect-chrome $ gstack-config set disabled_skills open-gstack-browser Router: disabled skills left out of ~/.claude/skills/gstack/SKILL.md Relinked 59 skills as gstack-* Disabled (gstack-config disabled_skills, not registered): open-gstack-browser Skipped 1 foreign entry (not gstack-managed, left untouched): connect-chrome skipped connect-chrome: existing entry is not gstack-managed (foreign skill with the same name) — left untouched exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills | grep -E 'chrome|open-gstack' connect-chrome ``` **The reporter's checkout shape, on this branch.** The reporter is on Windows, where a checkout without symlink support has `connect-chrome` as a plain file. A small install built that way on Linux gives the reporter's second message word for word, and disabling the skill then removes the alias: ```text $ gstack-config set disabled_skills connect-chrome Error: unknown skill 'connect-chrome' in disabled_skills. Did you mean 'context-restore'? Existing value left unchanged. exit=1 $ ls ~/.claude/skills connect-chrome context-restore open-gstack-browser ship $ gstack-config set disabled_skills open-gstack-browser Relinked 2 skills as flat names Disabled (gstack-config disabled_skills, not registered): open-gstack-browser exit=0 $ ls ~/.claude/skills context-restore ship ``` ### Failing-first regression The three new cases were written before the fix and run against unchanged `bin/gstack-relink`: ```text $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/relink.test.ts -t '#4308' 1308 | expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(skillsDir, 'connect-chrome'))).toBe(false); error: expect(received).toBe(expected) Expected: false Received: true (fail) gstack-relink: a disabled skill takes its alias with it (#4308) > disabling open-gstack-browser removes its connect-chrome alias under both names, and an enabled skill keeps it 1325 | expect(out).toContain('skipped connect-chrome'); error: expect(received).toContain(expected) Expected to contain: "skipped connect-chrome" Received: "Relinked 1 skills as flat names\nDisabled (gstack-config disabled_skills, not registered): open-gstack-browser" (fail) gstack-relink: a disabled skill takes its alias with it (#4308) > a user's own connect-chrome skill is reported and left byte-identical 0 pass 63 filtered out 2 fail $ bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test test/setup-install-registry.test.ts -t '#4308' 201 | expect(existsSync(alias)).toBe(false); error: expect(received).toBe(expected) Expected: false Received: true (fail) disabled_skills (#1206) > disabling open-gstack-browser takes /connect-chrome with it, across setup runs, until the skill is enabled again (#4308) 0 pass 16 filtered out 1 fail ``` The second relink case fails on main only at its last line. Nothing there looks at the alias name, so the user's skill is safe but also never reported. Its file-content assertions are the guard for this change. After the fix all three pass (3 pass, 24 `expect()` calls). ### Focused checks Commands ran under the isolated environment above, on the final tree. | Check | Pass | Fail | |---|---:|---:| | `test/relink.test.ts` (relink owner file, including the two new cases) | 65 | 0 | | `test/setup-install-registry.test.ts` (real `./setup`, including the new case) | 17 | 0 | | relink, alias and ownership suites: `relink-disabled-router`, `retired-skills`, `crew-skills-on-capy`, `setup-alias-name-uniqueness`, `setup-link-ownership`, `plan-mode-preamble-render`, `uninstall-windows-copies` | 80 | 0 | | `test/test-of-test-ratchet.test.ts`, `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts`, `test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts`, `test/egress-receipt-wiring.test.ts` | 22 | 0 | | `test/changelog-fragments.test.ts` | 15 | 0 | | **Total** | **199** | **0** | Each run was `bun --no-env-file --no-load-bunfig test --timeout=300000`. Product `bun run typecheck` exits 0. `bun run typecheck:test` reports `812 known diagnostics, none new.` `gstack-plain-title check` on the title, branch, commit subjects, fragment and this body prints `PLAIN_TITLE: ok`; `gstack-prose-lint --gate` on the fragment prints `PROSE_LINT: ok`; `git diff --check` is clean; `gstack-redact --repo-visibility public` on the exact outgoing patch reports zero findings. One earlier run of `test/setup-install-registry.test.ts` had a failure in an existing case, `a second checkout never silently replaces the global Claude install`. The same case failed the same way on unchanged main, because this container's `claude` CLI wrote its own policy files into the fixture's `~/.claude` between the two snapshots the case compares. It did not recur in the run counted above. ### Full free suite and base control `bun run test` ran once locally on the tree of the first commit, which differs from this head only by the two-line `setup` comment the second commit removes. All five shards reported failures, 345 failing tests in 91 files by the runner's count. That is 90 repo test files and one `probe.test.ts` that a browser test generates. This container's Playwright browsers are Chromium build 1243, while the repo pins Playwright 1.65.0 (build 1254), so every browser launch fails here; 41 of the 90 files are under `browse/test/`. The other 49 are spread over /cso, iOS QA, Ubicloud runner and other suites. They were not diagnosed one by one, only compared with main. Neither test file this PR changes is among the 90. Every failing file was then rerun on its own, with the same flags, on this head (`4398d0d18`) and on unchanged main at `bc858ffc6`: | Result | Files | Fails on this branch | Fails on unchanged main | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Fails on main as often or more | 86 | 363 | 365 | | Passes alone on both | 3 | 0 | 0 | | Fails equally once nothing else is running | 1 | 5 | 5 | - **The three that pass alone** are `test/harness-register.test.ts`, `test/qa-browser-deadline-evidence.test.ts` and `test/plan-count-timeout.test.ts`. The last one failed 1 of 2 on the branch in the first rerun pass, which ran four files at a time, and passes 2 of 2 on both sides with nothing else running. - **`browse/test/chromium-profile-isolation.test.ts`** failed 6 on the branch and 5 on main in that first pass, and 5 on each side with nothing else running. ## Scope - **Changed:** four files, +102/-0 against `main` at `bc858ffc6`: `bin/gstack-relink`, `test/relink.test.ts`, `test/setup-install-registry.test.ts` and `changelog.d/fix-4308-disabled-skill-alias.md`. Two commits: `d42a0d83a69b844d025b5e3c197085e849f7ff6d` (the fix, its cases and the fragment) and `4398d0d1852b2ecf4a63ae3b26ed07322536b31f` (takes the `setup` comment back out). - **Verified live by:** [full free CI on this head](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/43213839652), the real `./setup` and `gstack-config` before and after in a throwaway `HOME`, the reporter's checkout shape rebuilt on Linux, the failing-first runs of the three new cases, 199 focused passing checks, the full free suite with a per-file base control on unchanged main, both typechecks, and exact-patch lint and redaction scans. - **Did NOT test:** this fix on native Windows or macOS (CI's Windows setup, Windows smoke and macOS named-regressions jobs passed on this head, but it was not confirmed that any of them disables a skill that has an alias; the reporter's checkout shape was rebuilt on Linux instead), a green full free suite locally (this container cannot launch the pinned Chromium; CI ran it green on this head), a live Claude Code session listing its skills, or any paid lane. The free paid-coverage planner (`bun run eval:select --base upstream/main`) selects **two behavioral probes** for this diff in the PR profile, `gstack-upgrade-happy-path` and `skillmd-setup-discovery`, **no quality judges**, and defers nothing. Neither probe was run; neither receives pass credit here. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface). - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff; no generated file is changed. - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references. - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked: N/A, none added. - [x] Linked issue and reproduction: #4308. ## Test plan - [x] Reproduce the alias surviving `disabled_skills` with the real `./setup` and `gstack-config`, and show that a later `./setup` keeps it. - [x] Prove the three new cases fail on unchanged main. - [x] Show the alias leaving with the skill, staying off across `./setup`, and returning once the skill is enabled and setup runs again. - [x] Show the prefixed alias name removed and a user's own `connect-chrome` skill left byte-identical. - [x] Rebuild the reporter's checkout shape (no symlinked alias dir) and show the fix there. - [x] Pass the relink owner suite, the `disabled_skills` setup suite, the alias and ownership suites, ratchets and layout guards. - [x] Run the full free suite once and rerun every failing file on this head and on unchanged main. - [x] Pass strict product types and the unchanged test-type debt limit. - [x] Check the plain title, fragment prose, whitespace and the exact outgoing patch for sensitive content. - [x] Complete full free acceptance on this PR head (CI on `4398d0d18`: 35 passed, 21 skipped). - [ ] Complete required selected paid coverage, with maintainer-run fork-PR coverage where needed. - [ ] Complete remaining shipping reviews and verification before merge. Fork PRs do not receive upstream eval secrets. Skipped paid jobs are not passes; required maintainer-run coverage remains necessary before merge. Fixes #4308.

title: docs: troubleshooting links ship-policy.md#approval-classes, which doesn't exist
body:
Running gstack 1.99.1.0 (checkout 0ead11c), `docs/troubleshooting.md:6715` says "See [Approval classes](ship-policy.md#approval-classes)". `docs/ship-policy.md` has no heading with that anchor, so the link goes nowhere. Someone fixing an `approval-classes-invalid` refusal can't find the class format or the rules for citing approvals.

Expected: an "Approval classes" section in ship-policy.md covering the format of .gstack/approval-classes.json and `gstack-approval-classes init / validate / check`, plus how a change in a declared class cites an owner approval. Or the link should point to wherever that is documented now.

Found while wiring approval classes into a consuming repo.

title: Stop /ship's docs audit from refusing Next.js bracketed route paths (GST-2554)
body:
/ship's documentation audit (Step 14.5) now accepts file-routed paths such as `app/api/items/[id]/route.ts`, so unattended /ship runs on Next.js and SvelteKit projects stop halting at Blocked recovery when the audit found nothing wrong. This serves the goal of unattended /ship runs finishing without an owner exception (fixes #4313). ## Why The result check refused any listed path containing `*`, `?`, `[` or `]` as a glob, before looking at anything else. A Next.js dynamic route (`[id]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...opt]]`) or a SvelteKit route (`src/routes/blog/[slug]/+page.svelte`) in `files_reviewed` or `files_updated` therefore failed with `DOCS_RESULT_INVALID`. The retry produced the same list and failed the same way, so the run stopped. ## What changed - `lib/ship-docs-result.ts`: a path holding one of those characters still counts as a glob, unless that exact file exists. The other path rules (no absolute paths, backslashes, empty, `.` or `..` segments, no duplicates) run first and are unchanged. - `bin/gstack-docs-candidate`: `result` and `repair-prompt` look the path up literally from the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to the working directory outside a repository), so running from a subdirectory works too. - Patterns stay refused: `docs/*.md` and `docs/[ab].md` are refused even when a file they would match exists, and a bracketed path that names no file is refused as before. ## Tests `test/docs-audit-result.test.ts` adds cases for `[id]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...opt]]`, a route group around a dynamic segment, a SvelteKit route, a file named with `*` and `?` (skipped on Windows, where such names are invalid), a bracketed `files_updated` entry, and a run from a repository subdirectory. All 8 fail on main and pass here. The controls (a bracketed path with no file, `docs/*.md`, `docs/[ab].md`, the existing glob case, and `app/(group)/page.tsx`, which was never refused) behave the same on main and here. ## Blast radius Only /ship's Step 14.5 result check changes. A listed path with `*`, `?`, `[` or `]` that names an existing file now passes; every other path rule runs first and is unchanged, and `checkDocsResult` keeps the old strict default for any caller that passes no file lookup. If the repository root can't be found, the lookup falls back to the working directory, which refuses as before. ## Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual fix and no blockers. **Scope:** base 990315d to 9a9fc1c (one commit, four files: `bin/gstack-docs-candidate`, `lib/ship-docs-result.ts`, `test/docs-audit-result.test.ts`, `changelog.d/docs-audit-accepts-bracketed-route-paths.md`). Nothing is staged, unstaged or new in the working tree. **Documentation health** - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Updated. The `DOCS_RESULT_INVALID` entry now says that duplicate, absolute or glob paths are refused, and that a path holding `*`, `?`, `[` or `]` passes when that exact file exists, as with `app/api/items/[id]/route.ts`. - `ship/sections/documentation.md.tmpl`: Current. The 'not globs' wording is still accurate. - `document-release/sections/audit-scope.md.tmpl`: Current. - `changelog.d/docs-audit-accepts-bracketed-route-paths.md`: Current. **Coverage debt:** the bracketed-path acceptance in the result check now has reference coverage in troubleshooting and the changelog fragment. It has no how-to, and none is needed. title: Stop the transcript-scope brain-sync tests timing out on local runs (GST-2555)

A bare local `bun test` of `test/transcript-scope-brain-sync.test.ts` no longer times out: the file now gives each test the same 30-second budget that CI and gstack's pre-merge test runner already use. This keeps gstack's free test suite trustworthy, so a red test on a local or trial-merge run means a broken change rather than a slow machine.

With the pre-push transcript scan disabled in a scratch worktree, both scan cases failed on their assertions 4 of 4 times with main's file and 4 of 4 times with this one (script ran).

The four transcript-scope brain-sync tests timed out on bare local runs because bun's 5-second default is shorter than the push-retry cases need on a 4-core machine. The file now sets the 30-second default CI already uses, so local runs and CI agree. A changelog fragment records the fix.

title: browse: handoff window opens with a stray about:blank tab that browse can't close
body:
## What happens

Opening GStack Browser (`/open-gstack-browser`, `/connect-chrome`, or a headed `/browse` launch) opens a Chromium window that sits on a blank `about:blank` page instead of the GStack welcome page or the page the agent was asked to open.

## Expected

The headed window should land on the welcome page (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/welcome`) or the requested URL, never on a bare `about:blank` window.

## Environment

- gstack v1.92.61.0
- Windows 11 (Git Bash / PowerShell host)
- Headed mode (`launchHeaded`, extension-loaded persistent context)

## Where it likely comes from

- `browse/src/browser-manager.ts` (~L1029): the persistent context's default page is adopted as the first tab. That page starts on `about:blank`.
- `browse/src/server.ts` (~L1990-2003): after `Bun.serve`, the server navigates that tab to `/welcome` only if it is still on `about:blank`, with a 3 s timeout. Any failure is only a `console.warn`, so the user is left looking at `about:blank` with nothing on screen saying why.
- If something later creates a second page (e.g. `newTab()` or a `goto` into a new tab) while the adopted default page stays put, the user also ends up with an extra `about:blank` window next to the real one.

## Suggested fix

1. Launch the persistent context straight onto the welcome URL (or navigate the adopted default page before the window is shown), so `about:blank` is never what the user sees.
2. If the welcome navigation fails or times out, retry once and surface the error in the CLI output rather than only a server-log warning.
3. When the agent's first command opens a URL, reuse the adopted default `about:blank` tab instead of leaving it behind as an empty window.
4. Add a headed-launch test asserting no page stays on `about:blank` after launch plus the first `goto`.

title: Stop gstack-doctor flagging gstack's own CLAUDE.md as a pasted skill list
body: Running gstack-doctor from inside a gstack checkout no longer warns about gstack's own CLAUDE.md, so the readiness report flags only skill lists someone actually pasted. ## Why (in your own words) I ran `gstack-doctor` from inside my install (`~/.claude/skills/gstack`) and its CLAUDE.md row warned that the gstack section there lists 25 skills. That file is gstack's own development guide, not a skill list I pasted. It opens with `# gstack development`, so the check reads the whole file as one gstack section and counts every `/skill` it mentions. The fix line says to replace that section with a two-line block, which would replace the entire guide. Anyone who runs the doctor from their gstack folder sees this. A `cd && ./setup` fix line leaves you in that folder, and the bug template has users of other hosts run the doctor from there. This change skips a CLAUDE.md at the root of a gstack tree (setup, VERSION and bin/gstack-relink, the markers setup already uses to recognize one) and names the skipped file in the row. A real skill list in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or in another project's CLAUDE.md still warns. ## Live evidence Before, main at 0ead11c (`check_claude_md` is unchanged at 4414f4c), run from the checkout root. Doctor output here shows only the CLAUDE.md row and the summary line, with paths shortened. ``` $ ./bin/gstack-doctor warn CLAUDE.md the gstack section in /CLAUDE.md lists 25 skills; Claude Code lists installed skills itself, and a pasted list goes stale with each release fix: replace that section with this short block (https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#claude-md-skill-list): ## gstack Use /browse from gstack for all web browsing. Never use mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools. 8 ok, 4 warn, 3 not configured, 0 fail ``` My real install (1.99.0.0) shows the same row when the doctor runs from inside `~/.claude/skills/gstack`, and an ok row when it runs from another folder: ``` warn CLAUDE.md the gstack section in ~/.claude/skills/gstack/CLAUDE.md lists 25 skills; ... ok CLAUDE.md no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) ``` After, this branch, same checkout: ``` $ ./bin/gstack-doctor ok CLAUDE.md no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, skipped gstack's own /CLAUDE.md) 9 ok, 3 warn, 3 not configured, 0 fail ``` The new test, first with main's `bin/gstack-doctor` (4414f4c), then with this branch's: ``` $ bun test test/gstack-doctor-launch.test.ts -t "gstack.s own guide at the root" --timeout=30000 --max-concurrency=1 # main warn CLAUDE.md the gstack section in /gstack/CLAUDE.md lists 9 skills; ... Expected: "ok" Received: "warn" (fail) CLAUDE.md: gstack's own guide at the root of a gstack checkout is skipped and named in the row; the same text in another project and a list in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md still warn # this branch 1 pass 0 fail $ bun test test/gstack-doctor-launch.test.ts --timeout=30000 --max-concurrency=1 15 pass 5 skip 0 fail Ran 20 tests across 1 file. ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** `check_claude_md` in `bin/gstack-doctor` skips a CLAUDE.md at the root of a gstack tree and names it in the row. One test in `test/gstack-doctor-launch.test.ts`, one sentence under `docs/troubleshooting.md#claude-md-skill-list`, and a changelog fragment. - **Verified live by:** the doctor runs and tests above, on Windows 11 with Git Bash and Bun 1.4.4. - **Did NOT test:** macOS or Linux, the full free suite, or `typecheck` locally. CI's free-tests runs them. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction under Live evidence above

title: Two shell helpers still read ~/.gbrain/config.json and ignore GBRAIN_HOME (follow-up to #2521)
body:
## What happened

When `GBRAIN_HOME` is set, gbrain keeps its config at `$GBRAIN_HOME/.gbrain/config.json`. gbrain's `configDir()` appends `.gbrain` to the override (`src/core/config.ts:1973-1985` at gbrain `752ecbd0`), and `docs/architecture/topologies.md:262-265` documents setting `GBRAIN_HOME` per worktree. #2521 moved gstack's config reads to that contract. `lib/gbrain-exec.ts:86-88` now says "Every gstack-side gbrain-config read MUST resolve through this helper", and `bin/gstack-skill-start:445-450` follows the same rule. Two shell helpers on `main` (`4414f4cc`) still hard-code `$HOME/.gbrain/config.json`:

1. **`bin/gstack-skill-start:394`** sets `_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"`. Lines 395-414 print the `/sync-gbrain` context-load hint ("GBrain configured…" or "…this worktree isn't pinned yet") only when that file exists. Take an install whose config is under `GBRAIN_HOME`, with nothing at `~/.gbrain`. The preamble prints no hint there, though `gbrain` is on PATH and configured. Line 450 of the same script already reads `"${GBRAIN_HOME:-$HOME}/.gbrain/config.json"`.
2. **`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:58`** sets `GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"`. Lines 104-119 use it for the URL lock: the script reads the file's `database_url` and exports it as `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` for every child `gbrain` call. Line 351 uses it for the ZeroEntropy advisory (#2365). The header at lines 30-37 says the lock exists so that a config rewrite "can't redirect us at a different brain mid-stream". gbrain lets a set `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` override the file's `database_url` (`config.ts:683`, merge at `:748-753`).
   - When `~/.gbrain/config.json` is absent and both URL variables are empty, no URL is captured and the advisory's check is silent. gbrain then uses the `GBRAIN_HOME` config.
   - Now put a second brain's config, one with a `database_url`, at `~/.gbrain`. The lock exports that URL, and the wireup's database calls (`sources list`, `sources add`, `sync`) go to that brain. Without a `database_url` there, the same calls go to the `GBRAIN_HOME` brain. So the target depends on a file `GBRAIN_HOME` was meant to override.
   - The split-topology guide (`topologies.md:274-276`) places the artifact brain at the default config with `GBRAIN_HOME` unset. The helper mixes the default config's URL with an inherited `GBRAIN_HOME` config. Should callers clear `GBRAIN_HOME`, or should the helper honor it throughout? `lib/gbrain-sources.ts` (its header says it mirrors this helper) passes the caller-supplied environment unchanged, or inherits the process environment when none is supplied, and selects cwd through `gbrainChildCwd`. It does not itself read `~/.gbrain/config.json`.
   - This branch is the documented path: `setup-gbrain/SKILL.md:498` runs the helper with both URL variables emptied. The other callers (`gstack-brain-restore:247`, the daily `gstack-brain-sync --advance-only` at `:1247`, the v1.17.0.0 migration) set no URL variable themselves.

Expected: both helpers use the parent-directory convention that line 450 of `gstack-skill-start` already uses, `${GBRAIN_HOME:-$HOME}/.gbrain/config.json`. For a valid absolute `GBRAIN_HOME` without surrounding whitespace, this matches gbrain's `configDir()`. gbrain also trims whitespace and validates the value; the shell form does not.

Scope: I checked these two shell helpers only. I did not audit TypeScript or skill prose; `lib/checks.ts:166` and `setup-gbrain/sections/brain-init.md:217` show the same `$HOME/.gbrain` pattern.

## Steps to reproduce

The hint (1). Run this from a gstack checkout at `4414f4cc` whose toplevel has no `.gbrain-source`. Set `GBRAIN_HOME` to a directory that holds `.gbrain/config.json`, have `gbrain` on PATH, and leave `~/.gbrain` absent:

```bash
S=$(mktemp -d)
sed -n 394,414p bin/gstack-skill-start > "$S/asis.sh"
sed '1s|.*|_GBRAIN_CONFIG="${GBRAIN_HOME:-$HOME}/.gbrain/config.json"|' "$S/asis.sh" > "$S/fixed.sh"
bash "$S/asis.sh"     # prints nothing
bash "$S/fixed.sh"    # GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run `/sync-gbrain --full` ...
env -u GBRAIN_HOME bash "$S/fixed.sh"   # prints nothing: unset GBRAIN_HOME still means ~/.gbrain
```

On the same install, the full preamble (`gstack-skill-start --skill gstack --model claude`) prints no `GBrain configured` line.

The URL lock (2), with two synthetic configs. The snippet makes no database call; it shows that the helper exports `brain_a`'s URL while `GBRAIN_HOME` names the config with `brain_b`. A child `gbrain` that inherits that URL uses it over the `GBRAIN_HOME` config's `database_url` (`config.ts:683`, `:748-753`).

```bash
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/home/.gbrain" "$T/b/.gbrain"
echo '{"engine":"postgres","database_url":"postgresql://localhost/brain_a"}' > "$T/home/.gbrain/config.json"
echo '{"engine":"postgres","database_url":"postgresql://localhost/brain_b"}' > "$T/b/.gbrain/config.json"
{ echo 'warn(){ echo "WARN: $*" >&2; }'
  sed -n 58p bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup
  sed -n 97,125p bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup
  echo 'echo "$GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL"'; } > "$T/lock.sh"
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$T/home" GBRAIN_HOME="$T/b" bash "$T/lock.sh"
# postgresql://localhost/brain_a
```

## Readiness report

The doctor output has no gbrain row. Complete output, with the home directory shortened to `~` and the project path replaced:

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.2.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.99.2.0), agy global current (1.99.2.0), codex global current (1.99.2.0)

ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
```
