Validation parity with gbrain's trim, absolute-path and `..` checks (`config.ts:1976-1984`) is outside this change.

title: Skill start and the source wireup read gbrain's config under GBRAIN_HOME (#4325)
body: Skill start and the gbrain source wireup now find gbrain's config under `GBRAIN_HOME`. Users who keep gbrain's home outside `$HOME` get the `/sync-gbrain` hint, and the wireup's URL lock pins the brain gbrain itself uses. ## Why (in your own words) When `GBRAIN_HOME` is set, gbrain keeps its config at `$GBRAIN_HOME/.gbrain/config.json`. Two gstack helpers still looked only at `~/.gbrain/config.json` (#4325): - `gstack-skill-start` never printed its `/sync-gbrain` hint on such an install. - In `gstack-gbrain-source-wireup`, with no explicit or environment URL and no `~/.gbrain/config.json`, no URL was captured, and the ZeroEntropy advisory's config check was silent. When no explicit or environment URL was set and another brain's config with a non-empty `database_url` sat at `~/.gbrain`, the lock exported that brain's URL to every `gbrain` call the wireup makes. This change makes both helpers read `${GBRAIN_HOME:-$HOME}/.gbrain/config.json`. That is the parent-directory convention of gbrain's `configDir()`, and `gstack-skill-start` already uses it for its own engine check (line 450 on `main`). Under the split topology this means the wireup now follows `GBRAIN_HOME`, the intent question #4325 raises, which is also what `lib/gbrain-sources.ts` does. ## Live evidence Before and after, run as `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME= GSTACK_HOME=/gstack GBRAIN_HOME=

title: [feature] gstack-decision-search --semantic: let GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID name the memory source
body:
## What happens

`gstack-decision-search --query KW --semantic` adds its "Related from memory" block only when it finds the curated-memory source by path. That means a gbrain source whose `local_path` ends in `.gstack-brain-worktree`. A source that holds the same artifacts repo under another directory is never found, and the block is absent. Please extend source resolution while keeping the scoped search and the silent fallback.

Checked at `4414f4cc9377a9df06c7847433fe567ba6398aa8` (main):

- `lib/gstack-decision-semantic.ts:46-50` keeps only rows whose `local_path` ends with `BRAIN_WORKTREE_SUFFIX` (`:24`). `:85-89` returns `null` when there is none, "rather than searching UNSCOPED", and `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts:116-127` pins that. The module reads no environment variable or config key. That includes `GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE`, so moving the worktree with the wireup's own override (`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:50`) also loses the block unless the new directory keeps the same name.
- The two other readers of the artifacts source accept an explicit id. `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:151-153` takes `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` as the source id. `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:274-275` uses it ahead of its path match (`isArtifactsSourceRow`, `:248-262`, which also honors `GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE` and the state root).
- The docs do not say `--semantic` needs the worktree layout. `CLAUDE.md:570-571` and `CHANGELOG.md:12236` say it appends related hits "from gbrain memory when it's up". The search-guidance block (`sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl:497-498`) answers "What did we decide last time?" with `gbrain search "<terms>" --source gstack-artifacts-<user>`, by id.

Our layout: the agent machine is also the brain host. The artifacts repo is registered as a host-side clone with the id gstack derives itself (`derive_source_id`, wireup `:160-164`). gstack prints this kind of registration for a separate brain host (`bin/gstack-artifacts-init:504-523`, `docs/gbrain-sync.md:46-49`); the same-host case is close to #3539 and #3727. Ids and paths below are renamed:

```text
$ gstack-gbrain-source-wireup --probe
source_id=acme-gstack-artifacts
worktree=~/.gstack-brain-worktree
worktree_status=absent
gbrain=ok (0.60.675.0)
source_status=registered (different path)

$ gstack-decision-search --query "<a word in several checkpoints>" --semantic
- <one decision line from the file store>
$                                   # no "Related from memory" block

$ gbrain search "<the same word>" --source acme-gstack-artifacts
[0.52] projects/.../checkpoints/20261016-... -- ## Working on: ...
```

## Steps to reproduce

Hermetic, in the style of `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts`: a fake `gbrain` on `PATH` reports one federated source, and only its `local_path` changes.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
GSTACK_ROOT="${GSTACK_ROOT:-$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack}"
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/shim"
cat > "$T/shim/gbrain" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "sources" ]; then
  echo "{\"sources\":[{\"id\":\"acme-gstack-artifacts\",\"local_path\":\"$SRC_PATH\",\"federated\":true}]}"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$1" = "search" ]; then
  echo "[0.52] projects/acme/checkpoints/20261016-example -- Working on: example"
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
SH
chmod +x "$T/shim/gbrain"
cat > "$T/probe.ts" <<TS
const m = await import("$GSTACK_ROOT/lib/gstack-decision-semantic.ts");
console.log("  resolveMemorySourceId:", m.resolveMemorySourceId());
console.log("  semanticRecall:", JSON.stringify(m.semanticRecall("example")));
TS
run() { PATH="$T/shim:$PATH" bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null "$T/probe.ts"; }
echo "A. source is a clone elsewhere on the host"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= SRC_PATH=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts run
echo "B. same source at the wireup worktree path"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= SRC_PATH="$HOME/.gstack-brain-worktree" run
echo "C. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID set"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID=acme-gstack-artifacts SRC_PATH=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts run
rm -rf "$T"
```

Output on gstack 1.99.2.0, whose `lib/gstack-decision-semantic.ts` is byte-identical to `4414f4cc`:

```text
A. source is a clone elsewhere on the host
  resolveMemorySourceId: null
  semanticRecall: null
B. same source at the wireup worktree path
  resolveMemorySourceId: acme-gstack-artifacts
  semanticRecall: [{"score":0.52,"slug":"projects/acme/checkpoints/20261016-example","snippet":"Working on: example"}]
C. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID set
  resolveMemorySourceId: null
  semanticRecall: null
```

A is the gap; C shows the override is not read.

## What would help

1. Let `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` name the source, with the same precedence `gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:274-275` uses. When it is set, use it if a source with that id is registered, and otherwise return `null`. When it is unset, keep the worktree match. The search stays scoped, and the operator who sets the variable is responsible for naming the curated-memory source. The companion pull request (#4328) carries this change and two tests (named source wins over a worktree source; an unregistered id gives `null`). With it, case C returns the same single hit as B, and A and B are unchanged.
2. Optional, so that no setting is needed, also accept the row whose id equals what `derive_source_id` yields from the artifacts repo's `origin`.
3. The comment at `lib/gstack-decision-semantic.ts:33-35` says "the caller then searches unscoped", which contradicts `:85-89`. The PR corrects it.

## Alternatives

- `gbrain search "<terms>" --source <id>` works today. It is the route the search-guidance block gives; only the `--semantic` flag misses it.
- Re-registering through the wireup would move the source to `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`. With `--probe` reporting `registered (different path)` and a different directory name, its drift branch runs `gbrain sources remove <id> --yes` and `gbrain sources add <id> --path <worktree> --federated` (`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:330-337`). Registering the clone under a directory named `.gstack-brain-worktree` would also pass the suffix check, but gbrain has no `sources update`, so it means the same remove and add. Another process on this host maintains that checkout, so re-registering it is a larger change than one lookup.

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.309; OS: Linux
- gstack 1.99.2.0 installed (`bc858ffc`); code and docs cited at `4414f4cc`
- gbrain 0.60.675.0
- `gstack doctor 1.99.2.0`: 15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
- Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `gstack-decision-search --semantic`, `gstack-decision-semantic`, `resolveMemorySourceId`, `semanticRecall`, `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID`, `gstack-brain-worktree`, "artifacts source id", "wireup different path". No issue about how `--semantic` finds its source. Related: #2516, #3810, #3539, #3727.

title: gstack-decision-search --semantic honors GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID
body: Users can now set `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` to point `gstack-decision-search --semantic` at a registered artifacts source outside `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`, and its matching memory hits are appended to the decisions. Issue: #4327. ## Why (in your own words) The semantic lookup found the curated-memory source only by a `local_path` that ends in `.gstack-brain-worktree`. A source that holds the same artifacts repo elsewhere, such as a clone on a machine that is also the brain host, was never found, and the block was silently absent. `gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` and `gstack-gbrain-sync` already accept `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID`, but the semantic lookup did not read it. This change gives the variable the precedence `gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:274-275` uses: - When it is set, `resolveMemorySourceId` returns that id if a source with it is registered, and `null` otherwise. - When it is unset, the worktree match is unchanged. The search stays scoped. An unregistered id degrades to the file results, never to an unscoped search, so the design `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts` pins still holds. The doc comment that said "the caller then searches unscoped" is corrected, and the module header and the `semanticRecall` comment now describe the named source. ## Live evidence The two new tests fail on `main` and pass on this branch. Output trimmed to the result lines: ``` $ bun test test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts # main's lib/, new tests (fail) end-to-end with a fake gbrain shim > GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID names a source outside the worktree and wins over it (fail) end-to-end with a fake gbrain shim > an unregistered GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID degrades to null (no fallback, no unscoped search) 10 pass 2 fail $ bun test test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts # this branch 12 pass 0 fail ``` On a real install whose artifacts source is a host-side clone, run from this branch's checkout (the decision text and slugs are replaced): ``` $ GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= bin/gstack-decision-search --query "" --semantic - $ GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= bin/gstack-decision-search --query "" --semantic - Related from memory (gbrain semantic recall): [0.52] projects//checkpoints/: ## Working on: ... [0.49] projects//checkpoints/: ## Working on: ... [0.49] projects//checkpoints/: ## Working on: ... ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** - `lib/gstack-decision-semantic.ts`: two lines in `resolveMemorySourceId`, and the three comments that describe how the source is found; - two tests in `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts`; - `test/gstack-decision-bins.test.ts`: its `--semantic` helper drops an inherited `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID`, which would otherwise bypass the shim's worktree source on a developer machine that exports it; - the fragment `changelog.d/semantic-source-id.md`. - **Verified live by:** - the run above on gbrain 0.60.675.0; - the 8 decision test files (`bun test test/*decision*.test.ts`: 235 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, both with the variable unset and with `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID=zzz` exported); - `bun run typecheck:test` (no new diagnostics); - `bun run typecheck`; - `bin/gstack-prose-lint` on the fragment. - **Did NOT test:** - the full free suite, which is left to CI; - macOS and Windows. - **Behavior change:** a set but unregistered `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` now gives no related block, where it used to be ignored in favor of the worktree source. This matches `gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:275`. - **Not changed:** - matching the source by the id `derive_source_id` yields without a setting (option 2 in the issue); - `GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE`, which the semantic lookup still does not read. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: #4327 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Nothing in skill start runs gstack-brain-context-load, though memory.md and the 1.26.0.0 notes say skills auto-load brain context
body:
## What happened

Three places say skills get the context of `bin/gstack-brain-context-load.ts` at skill start, but on `main` (`4414f4cc9377a9df06c7847433fe567ba6398aa8`) I found no code path that runs the helper:

- `bin/gstack-brain-context-load.ts:5`: "Called from the gstack preamble at every skill start."
- `setup-gbrain/memory.md:264-271`: "At every gstack skill start, the preamble runs `gstack-brain-context-load` which: ..." and `:273-282`: when you run `/office-hours`, "the model context automatically includes" `## Prior office-hours sessions in this repo` and three more sections.
- `CHANGELOG.md:15495-15497` (1.26.0.0): "Every gstack skill auto-loads what you actually did.", and the six skills "now declare what they want gbrain to surface in the preamble at every invocation" (`/investigate` was retired in #4110; five remain).

What I checked:

1. Callers. The steps below show every reference to the helper and to its off switch outside the changelog, tests and docs; none is a call. The `## Preamble (run first)` fence runs `bin/gstack-skill-start`, and neither that script nor any rendered `SKILL.md` or `sections/*` file names the helper. `context_queries` is read only by the helper and by `parseSkillManifest` in `lib/gstack-memory-helpers.ts`.
2. History. This does not look like a regression from moving the preamble into `bin/gstack-skill-start`. The v1.26.0.0 commit (`bf654871`, #1298) added the helper, the `gbrain:` blocks and `memory.md`, changed no file under `scripts/` or `hosts/`, and its test plan runs the helper by hand. Over the full history, `git log main -S'brain-context-load' -- . ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!test' ':!docs'` returns three commits: `bf654871` (adds the helper), `394db326` (adds the comment at `hosts/claude.ts:17`) and `b1485d88` (adds the test duration). This literal-string history shows no commit that adds a call.
3. What does run at skill start is different. `{{GBRAIN_CONTEXT_LOAD}}` (`scripts/resolvers/gbrain.ts:54-68`) renders a `## Brain Context Load` block that tells the model to run `gbrain search "<keywords>"` and read the top 3 results with `gbrain get`. It does not read `context_queries`, and `/design-shotgun` does not have it (that template has no `{{GBRAIN_CONTEXT_LOAD}}`). The closing comments on #2114 describe this block as the context-load mechanism ("skills load and save GBrain context through the generated {{GBRAIN_CONTEXT_LOAD}} resolver"). `bin/gstack-skill-start` also prints a "GBrain configured. Prefer `gbrain search`..." hint (`:404`), which is a third thing and not this helper.

Consequences I can see in the code:

- I found no automatic run that evaluates the 16 queries declared in five skills (`/office-hours` 4, `/plan-ceo-review` 3, `/design-shotgun` 3, `/design-consultation` 3, `/retro` 3). The `gbrain:` block still ships in every rendered `SKILL.md` of those skills, and `hosts/claude.ts:11-20` keeps it unstripped specifically because "bin/gstack-brain-context-load reads gbrain:".
- `setup-gbrain/memory.md:259` documents `gstack-config set gbrain_context_load off  # also disables retrieval`. Nothing on `main` reads `gbrain_context_load` (step 3 below). `gstack-config set gbrain_context_load off` succeeds silently, as it does for any unknown key, and `gstack-config get gbrain_context_load` then prints `off`, so the switch looks like it worked.
- Earlier reports describe the helper as part of every skill run: #1687 says its queries run "at skill startup", and #2883 reports "0 bytes of brain context in every skill". Each of #1559, #1687 and #2883 reproduces its bug by running the helper or its manifest parser by hand.

What I expected: either skill start runs the helper as the three places say, or those places, the `gbrain:` frontmatter and the off switch are corrected to match the `{{GBRAIN_CONTEXT_LOAD}}` block. Run by hand, the helper evaluates the four `/office-hours` queries and returns content (step 4), so what is missing is a caller, not the loader. I do not know which direction you want. If the prose block is the intended mechanism, `memory.md:262-286`, the helper's header (`:5`) and the `gbrain_context_load` line are stale, and the manifests are read only when someone runs the helper by hand. If the helper should run, `bin/gstack-skill-start` already has `--skill` and the repo slug, but I have not tried a call there or measured its cost against the 500 ms per-query cap.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gstack && cd gstack
git checkout 4414f4cc9377a9df06c7847433fe567ba6398aa8

# 1. No call site outside docs, tests and comments
git grep -n 'brain-context-load' -- . ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!test' ':!docs' ':!bin/gstack-brain-context-load.ts'
# hosts/claude.ts:17, lib/gstack-memory-helpers.ts:7, :462,
# scripts/free-test-durations.json:774, setup-gbrain/memory.md:265

# 2. Neither the preamble command nor any rendered skill or section names it
git grep -n -E 'brain-context-load' -- bin/gstack-skill-start ':(glob)*/SKILL.md' ':(glob)*/sections/*'
# (no output)

# 3. The documented off switch has no reader
git grep -n 'gbrain_context_load' -- . ':!CHANGELOG.md'

# 4. Run by hand, the helper evaluates the manifest (output on a real install; OK or SKIP and the durations depend on its data)
```

title: Close the stray about:blank tab in the browse handoff window (#4323)
body: ## Why (in your own words) Every `browse handoff` window opens with two tabs: the page I'm meant to sign in to, and an empty `about:blank` tab next to it. On Windows I hand the window over several times a day to sign in to local apps, and the extra tab gets in the way every time (and it's easy to click into by mistake). It comes from `launchPersistentContext()`, which opens a first tab of its own. `restoreState()` then opens a new page for each saved tab and never closes that first one. This change closes it at the end of `restoreState()`, but only a context page that browse doesn't track and that is still on `about:blank`. Tracked tabs, and any untracked page that has navigated somewhere, are left alone. Fixes #4323 ## Live evidence Real use, Windows 11, browse daemon rebuilt from this branch, then `browse stop` and (the internal app's name, title and port redacted as `<…>`): ``` $ browse goto http://localhost:/ Navigated to http://localhost:/ (200) $ browse handoff "" HANDOFF: Browser opened at http://localhost:/login?next=<…> $ browse tabs → [2] — http://localhost:/ ``` Before the fix the headed window showed that tab plus an `about:blank` tab that `browse tabs` doesn't list (it isn't tracked, which is also why no browse command can close it). After it, the window shows the one tab. The new test, with and without the fix, on current `main`: ``` $ bun test browse/test/handoff.test.ts -t "closes the blank tab" 1 pass 0 fail $ git stash push -- browse/src/browser-manager.ts # fix removed $ bun test browse/test/handoff.test.ts -t "closes the blank tab" (fail) restoreState > closes the blank tab a fresh persistent context opens on its own [243.92ms] 0 pass 1 fail ``` Whole file and the type gates on this branch: ``` $ bun test browse/test/handoff.test.ts 16 pass 9 skip 0 fail Ran 25 tests across 1 file. $ bun run typecheck # exit 0 $ bun run typecheck:test test typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new. ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** `BrowserManager.restoreState()` closes untracked `about:blank` pages after restoring the saved tabs (`browse/src/browser-manager.ts`). Adds one test case to `browse/test/handoff.test.ts` that mirrors `handoff()`: fresh tab maps plus a blank tab the context opened, then `restoreState()`. - **Verified live by:** handing off on Windows 11 to a local app several times and looking at the headed window's tab strip. - **Did NOT test:** macOS or Linux headed windows (the 9 Xvfb-dependent handoff tests skip on Windows). I also didn't test the `recreateContext()` paths beyond the existing round-trip test (a `newContext()` has no first tab, so the cleanup finds nothing there), or the extension and `connect` headed modes. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) Authenticated GitHub login checked with `gh api user --jq .login`: `Simba3696`. ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: #4323

title: Plan before build: let the owner answer a plan gate in the lane's own thread
body:
## What happened

crew/docs/captain.md (Plan before build) has the lane send its plan ask to the controller, which relays it and carries the owner's words back. Our owner sometimes opens the lane's thread and answers the gate right there. The lane then has the owner's exact words first-hand, but the doc gives it no way to use them: it either ignores a direct answer or asks the controller to relay words the owner already gave.

## What we did meanwhile

A crew-specific CREW.md rule, on the owner's word: when the owner answers a plan gate in the lane's thread, the lane answers the run with those words (`--by agent:<lane> --owner-reply "<words>"`), imports the approval and tells the controller in one line. The controller then checks the row against what it would have relayed.

## Suggestion

An option in Plan before build: "the owner may answer in the lane's thread; the lane records the words with `gstack-autoplan answer` and tells the controller, who checks the row the same way as a relayed one". The approval row could carry `relayed_by: none (owner in lane thread)`.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: /captain: no tool writes NOTES.md lines from the train records
body:
## What happened

captain/templates/NOTES.md defines the log's line shapes (READY, TRAIN built, verdict, MERGED, …) and captain/SKILL.md (The digest) says the digest is derived from it, but nothing produces those lines. A controller writes them from memory, so the log drifts or goes unwritten. The facts are already in `refs/notes/gstack-trains`, which `gstack-ship-queue ready`, `train build`, `verdict` and `land` write.

## What we did meanwhile

A script that reads `refs/notes/gstack-trains` and prints NOTES.md lines since a time, de-duplicated, plus a host script for lane events (started, done, archived) that only the host can see. On Capy, partial clones (blob:none) need the notes ref refetched without the filter first, or `git cat-file --batch` fetches each blob on its own and times out.

## Suggestion

`gstack-captain notes --since <iso>`: prints NOTES.md lines in the template's shapes from the train records, so a host only adds its own lane events. It should cope with partial clones.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: /captain: a doctor for a crew's drive
body:
## What happened

captain/SKILL.md (Setup) and crew/docs/captain.md (CREW.md: the lanes' contract) say the rules file is pointers plus parameters with rules 1 to 24 from the template, every Home path should exist, NOTES.md has fixed shapes, the digest is rewritten each turn and reports follow the template. Nothing checks any of it. Our Captains drifted from the template within days, and audits that found it were prose that drifted again.

## What we did meanwhile

A conformance script, run daily per Captain, with one row per check, each citing the gstack line it enforces: digest present and fresh, AGENTS.md and CREW.md size, CREW rules 1-24 equal to the installed template, parameters match `.gstack/ship-policy.json`, every Home path exists, the drive layout, NOTES line shapes, postmortems present, report shape, and `gstack-runaway scan`. A failed read is UNKNOWN, never PASS.

## Suggestion

`gstack-captain doctor --drive <dir> [--repo <dir>]`: the same rows, PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, each citing its home, so every crew gets the check by installing gstack.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: Nothing checks that a reverted or S1-fixed crew PR got its postmortem
body:
## What happened

crew/docs/captain.md (The lessons loop) and captain/templates/postmortem.md require reports/postmortem-<n>.md after any revert or S1 fix of a merged crew PR. Nothing notices when one is missing.

## What we did meanwhile

A row in our drive check: every revert or S1 fix merged in the last 14 days needs a postmortem file. Matching S1 from PR titles was too loose (one crew uses "S1" as a design-screen code), so we match labels or "S1 fix", "sev-1 hotfix" and "S1 incident" in titles.

## Suggestion

A row in the drive doctor (see the doctor issue), or a /ship check: a PR that reverts a merged commit, or carries a severity-1 label, refuses READY until its postmortem path is in the body.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: gstack-factory-scorecard: print the week's improvement goal
body:
## What happened

crew/docs/recommended-harness.md (The factory scorecard) gives each line a bar, and the scorecard prints the gap beside the number. It doesn't say which line to work on, so each week someone has to pick the worst line by hand, and it doesn't always happen.

## What we did meanwhile

A weekly script that reads the scorecard, picks the line that misses its bar by the most, and files or updates one "Scorecard goal: <line>" issue for the Captain.

## Suggestion

`gstack-factory-scorecard --goal`: print the one line that misses its bar by the most, with the bar and the number, so a crew can file it as its goal for the week.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: gstack-factory-scorecard: give "few" and similar bars a number
body:
## What happened

Some bars in recommended-harness.md's scorecard table are words, not numbers: "median 1 pass; few at the cap", "several merges a day". A tool can't tell whether a week meets a word, so automation that picks the worst line has to invent a threshold.

## What we did meanwhile

Our goal script reads "few" as 10% of PRs.

## Suggestion

Numeric bars in lib/factory-scorecard.ts for every line (for example, at most 10% of PRs at the pass cap), printed in the third column so the table and the tool agree.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: gstack-upgrade: list what changed for Captains since the last read
body:
## What happened

`gstack-upgrade` fast-forwards the checkout but says nothing about what changed. A Captain whose rules point at gstack docs needs to know when captain/, crew/, capy/ or docs/ changed, or its CREW.md and briefs go stale without anyone noticing.

## What we did meanwhile

One Captain runs a nightly reader for all of ours: it runs gstack-upgrade, lists commits under captain/, crew/, capy/ and docs/ since a recorded commit, judges which affect how Captains or lanes work, tells each affected Captain, and records the new commit.

## Suggestion

`gstack-upgrade --changes <since-sha>` (or a `gstack-changes` bin): after the fast-forward, print the commits touching those paths, with a one-line summary each, so any crew can follow gstack without a home-made reader.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: Capy: say when a Setup snapshot's gstack copy is stale
body:
## What happened

docs/capy-install.md recommends baking gstack into a Capy Setup snapshot. A snapshot keeps the gstack copy it was built with. The session check fast-forwards when it's behind, but every fresh machine pays that cost and nothing tells the owner the snapshot itself should be rebuilt.

## What we did meanwhile

A script, run on a machine freshly booted from the snapshot, that files a "Rebuild the Setup snapshot" issue when the snapshot's gstack copy misses a commit older than 7 days.

## Suggestion

A doctor row (or an install `--check` note) that reports the snapshot's gstack commit age and says `rebuild the snapshot` past a threshold.

Filed from Groom Club's Captains (checked against gstack 1.99.2.0, 4414f4cc). crew/docs/captain.md calls a rule that lives only in a crew's file a gap in gstack, so we're sending each of ours here, one issue per gap.

title: Finish before starting has no tool
body:
## What happened

crew/docs/captain.md (New threads join the crew) says the Captain starts no new fix thread while more than 10 finished PRs (green, reviewed, waiting only to merge) sit in the queue. The count is done by hand, so it's skipped.

## What we did meanwhile

Our brief renderer counts finished PRs before it renders a brief, and refuses past 10 unless the brief names a severe-hotfix exemption.

## Suggestion

`gstack-ship-queue finished --count` (and a refusal in whatever renders a brief): print the finished PRs and exit non-zero past the limit, with the hotfix exemptions as flags.

title: The digest on Capy: generate it from issues, don't hand-keep it
body:
## What happened

captain/SKILL.md (The digest) has the controller rewrite DIGEST.md every turn. On Capy the crew's real state lives in issues and threads, and a hand-kept digest drifts from them within a day: rows for archived threads, missing ages, asks already answered.

## What we did meanwhile

A host script generates DIGEST.md each wake from Capy's issues, threads and NOTES.md (Needs you, New, In progress, Stalls), never by hand, and prints how old it is. Our drive check fails when the digest is over 6 hours old while the crew was active.

## Suggestion

A note in crew/docs/captain.md, The digest: "on Capy, generate it from issues and NOTES.md each wake; never hand-keep it", and the freshness rule as a doctor row.

title: The gbrain source wireup and skill start follow GBRAIN_HOME, so the wireup writes to the right brain (GST-2621)
body:
The gbrain source wireup and skill start now read gbrain's config from `GBRAIN_HOME` when it is set, the same way gbrain does, so on a machine with two brains the wireup no longer registers and syncs gstack's source into the wrong one. This serves gstack's goal of running unattended alongside gbrain, where cron jobs and wrappers set `GBRAIN_HOME` and two brains on one box is a normal setup.

## What changed

![Before, the wireup always read ~/.gbrain/config.json. Now it reads the config gbrain uses under GBRAIN_HOME, and --check-target reports whether an earlier run hit the wrong brain without printing a URL.](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/VxD_Qca3KFCS3Hic4chLhv1zpSNMhp6t0-j4W0v61_o.png)

Before, the wireup always read ~/.gbrain/config.json. Now it reads the config gbrain uses under GBRAIN_HOME, and --check-target reports whether an earlier run hit the wrong brain without printing a URL.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Before, the wireup always read ~/.gbrain/config.json. Now it reads the config gbrain uses under GBRAIN_HOME, and --check-target reports whether an earlier run hit the wrong brain without printing a URL.</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ grep -n GBRAIN_CONFIG= bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup   # this branch
+62:GBRAIN_CONFIG=$(gstack_gbrain_config_path) || GBRAIN_HOME_VALID=0
-$ grep -n GBRAIN_CONFIG= bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup   # main 1d3c63c
-58:GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
 
 $ GBRAIN_HOME=/srv/named gstack-gbrain-source-wireup --check-target
+SOURCE_ID: (unknown)
+URL_ENV: GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL unset, DATABASE_URL unset (a run with either set used that URL before and after the fix)
+GBRAIN_HOME: set
+DEFAULT_CONFIG: ~/.gbrain/config.json (database_url set)
+GBRAIN_HOME_CONFIG: /srv/named/.gbrain/config.json (database_url set)
+TARGET: MISMATCH a run with GBRAIN_HOME set and no URL in its environment registered and synced this source in the brain named by DEFAULT_CONFIG, not GBRAIN_HOME_CONFIG; to confirm, run gbrain sources list with GBRAIN_HOME unset and look for SOURCE_ID
-Unknown flag: --check-target
 
~~~

</details>

## Why

Issue #4325: "the wireup writes to the wrong brain when GBRAIN_HOME is set." When no database URL was in the environment (the `/setup-gbrain` path, `gstack-brain-restore`, the daily advance), the wireup locked `~/.gbrain/config.json`'s `database_url`, so `sources add` and `sync` went to that brain instead of the one under `GBRAIN_HOME`, and skill start never showed its `/sync-gbrain` hint when the only config sat under `GBRAIN_HOME`. Both helpers now find the same config gbrain reads, and `--check-target` tells an operator whether an earlier run could have hit the wrong brain.

## Blast radius

The change touches two shell helpers, `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` and `bin/gstack-skill-start`, plus the new sourced file `bin/gstack-gbrain-home.sh`; nothing else calls `gstack_gbrain_config_path` (grep over bin/ and test/). With `GBRAIN_HOME` unset the resolved path is still `~/.gbrain/config.json`, so single-brain installs see no change; the negative-control test and QA capture 003 ran that path.

## Summary

People who run two brains, one named by `GBRAIN_HOME` and one in `~/.gbrain`, saw gstack's source registered and synced in the `~/.gbrain` brain. The fix resolves gbrain's config once, in `bin/gstack-gbrain-home.sh`, with gbrain's own rule: trim `GBRAIN_HOME`, append `.gbrain`, else use `~/.gbrain`, and refuse a relative path or one with a `..` segment instead of falling back to the wrong brain. The wireup exports `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` from that config, and its new read-only `--check-target` prints `TARGET: MATCH`, `MISMATCH` or `UNKNOWN` and never a URL. Review found that `--check-target` misreported the caller's URL settings, which is fixed with a test. The docs audit added the new flag and helper to `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md`.

**Security read.** `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL` is exported as before; only the file it is read from changed, and no new line logs it. The new warning names neither the URL nor the `GBRAIN_HOME` value, and `--check-target` keeps both URLs inside `python3` and prints only paths and status words. No file is written, no mode changes, no network calls and no new dependencies, workflows or install-script changes.

Thanks to @exGeni, whose #4326 found this. This PR rebuilds that change on current main and credits them as co-author.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage: each of the 3 changed runtime files has a changed test naming it.

Tests ran: targeted 88 (test/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup.test.ts, test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts; 88 pass, 0 fail at 39a9b77)
Tests ran: free 1665 files (carried from CI run 43468945578 at beee00b, tree 890a12520626)

The new cases failed on main 1d3c63c (12 fail, 1 pass: the negative control) and pass here. The `URL_ENV` assertion added in review failed against the pre-fix wireup and passes with the fix.

Pre-Landing Review: 3 issues — 3 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 4 noted

- [AUTO-FIXED] `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` `--check-target` printed the URL env after the startup lock had exported `GBRAIN_DATABASE_URL`, so it said a URL was set when the caller had none → record the caller's env before the lock and print that.
- [AUTO-FIXED] `test/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup.test.ts` never asserted `URL_ENV` → the MISMATCH test now does.
- [AUTO-FIXED] `bin/gstack-gbrain-home.sh` called `gbrainConfigDir()` its exact TypeScript twin, though that function neither trims nor refuses → the comment now says so.

Fix-check: NO FINDINGS. Native adversarial pass: 3 Low findings, none blocking, listed under Review notes. Outside review: unavailable (Codex CLI not installed; the review plan listed no outside voice for this code-class diff).

title: Health checks find gbrain's config under GBRAIN_HOME, trimmed the way gbrain does (GST-2625)
body:
gstack's health checks and gbrain helpers now look for gbrain's config where gbrain itself looks, so a machine that sets `GBRAIN_HOME` is judged by the brain it actually runs. This serves the goal of gstack and gbrain agreeing on which brain a machine uses, and finishes the work #4343 started for the shell helpers.

## What changed

![gstack-gbrain-detect with a GBRAIN_HOME gbrain refuses: it crashed at load before the fix and now reports no config](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/b_rELy0KHgwRRthPAcSKTY0CD-MgeXVCxVl5Fosm-jU.png)

gstack-gbrain-detect with a GBRAIN_HOME gbrain refuses: before the /ship fix in this PR it crashed at load, and now it reports no config and still prints its JSON.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: gstack-gbrain-detect with a GBRAIN_HOME gbrain refuses: it crashed at load before the fix and now reports no config</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ GBRAIN_HOME=relative/home gstack-gbrain-detect   # at c651444
+{
+    "gbrain_on_path": false,
+    "gbrain_version": null,

-$ GBRAIN_HOME=relative/home gstack-gbrain-detect   # at 3104ea6

- code: "ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE"
-
-      at /workspace/gstack/bin/gstack-gbrain-detect:66:23
-
 
~~~

</details>

## Why

When `GBRAIN_HOME` is set, which is gbrain's standard unattended setup, `lib/checks.ts` inspected `~/.gbrain/config.json` instead, so /health could pick or skip the gbrain probe based on a brain gbrain never uses. Now the TypeScript helper and the shell helper resolve `GBRAIN_HOME` exactly as gbrain's own `configDir()` does, and a value gbrain would refuse selects nothing instead of quietly falling back to `~/.gbrain`.

## Blast radius

`gbrainConfigDir()` now returns `null` for a relative or `..` `GBRAIN_HOME`, which every caller must handle, and all of them do. The typed callers are checked by `bun run typecheck`, and the one extensionless caller, `bin/gstack-gbrain-detect`, was fixed in c651444 after review reproduced its crash (QA captures 002 and 003, then 005 after the fix). Nothing changes when `GBRAIN_HOME` is unset; the parity test's unset negative controls pass.

## Summary

**One resolver rule, in shell and TypeScript.** `gbrainConfigDir()` in `lib/gbrain-exec.ts` follows gbrain's `configDir()`: `GBRAIN_HOME` trimmed with JavaScript `trim()`, `.gbrain` appended, unset or blank means `~/.gbrain`, and a relative value or one with a `..` segment returns `null`. Every caller (`buildGbrainEnv`, `gbrainChildCwd`, local status, MCP locality, memory helpers, memory ingest, brain context load, `gstack-gbrain-detect`) treats `null` as no config. `lib/checks.ts` health selection goes through it and names `$GBRAIN_HOME/.gbrain/config.json` in its source and reason text when `GBRAIN_HOME` is set.

**Unicode-blank `GBRAIN_HOME` in the shell helper.** `bin/gstack-gbrain-home.sh` trimmed with POSIX `[[:space:]]`, which misses the no-break space and the byte-order mark, so a `GBRAIN_HOME` made only of those was refused instead of meaning the default home. It now strips exactly the code points JavaScript `trim()` strips, spelled out as UTF-8 bytes so the result does not depend on the locale.

**Detect no longer crashes on a refused `GBRAIN_HOME`.** /ship's review found that `bin/gstack-gbrain-detect` still joined the helper's result at load time, so a relative or `..` `GBRAIN_HOME` threw a TypeError before any JSON. It now reads that as no config, and `test/gbrain-detect-shape.test.ts` covers it.

No line logs or writes a database URL; the tests use localhost fixture URLs. There are no new dependencies, workflows, network calls or file writes.

Still reading `~/.gbrain` directly, and left for after 11-21 because they only run once, during setup: `lib/gbrain-supabase-provision.ts:552`, `gstack-upgrade/migrations/v1.37.0.0.sh`, and the setup-gbrain brain-init and engine-remediation templates.

## Test Coverage

`test/gbrain-home-parity.test.ts` runs one table (unset, blank, every code point the runtime's `trim()` removes, NEL and zero-width space as not-whitespace controls, relative, `..`, trailing slashes, ordinary) against both resolvers, plus two-home tests for the health selection and `buildGbrainEnv`, each with a `GBRAIN_HOME`-unset negative control. On main 43c815be most of the table fails, and only the negative controls and ordinary cases hold; on this branch the whole file is green.

Coverage: 33% value-weighted (4 of 12 changed paths have a ★★★ test). The 8 gaps are the null short-circuits in downstream callers; the audit ran audit-only and proposed tests for the classifier, the local Postgres check and the child working directory.
Test value: 1 test written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 1 existing test extended, 0 paths weakly covered.
Regression proof — fails at HEAD: yes · passes at base: manual · passes after fix: yes (the new detect case; base control unavailable in a detached worktree because the bun shim cannot resolve a runtime under a temporary HOME, so the base run was done by hand).

Tests ran: focused 70

title: skill-start: a read cut off after 30 lines looks like a clean one, and the skill doesn't say to run it bare or inside the repo
body:
## What happened

I ran `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-skill-start --skill verify --model claude | head -30` for `/verify`, from a folder that isn't a git repo. The full output is 49 lines. Line 30 was `GSTACK_INSTRUCTION_BEGIN: upgrade-flow <session id>`. Its body, its `GSTACK_INSTRUCTION_END`, and a second block (`telemetry-prompt`, lines 33 to 49) were cut. The preamble text says "Treat an unterminated block as ending at end-of-output", so a cut block reads as an empty one and nothing tells the agent the read was short. The telemetry consent question never reached the user.

The same run printed `BRANCH: unknown` and `REPO_MODE: unknown` because the shell was in a non-git folder. The text doesn't say which directory to run it from.

Expected: the skill text tells the agent to run the script bare, from inside the repo the task is about, and to report a block whose END line is missing instead of treating it as empty.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a folder that isn't a git repo, run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-skill-start --skill verify --model claude | head -30`.
2. The last line shown is `GSTACK_INSTRUCTION_BEGIN: upgrade-flow ...` with no body and no END line.
3. Run it again inside a git repo. `BRANCH` and `REPO_MODE` are filled (I got `main` and `solo`).

title: Run Playwright specs that use a local fixtures file under playwright test, and let a repo send chosen tests to its own runner
body:
## Why (in your own words)

My app repo has vitest unit tests and Playwright specs in one package. Every spec takes `test` from its own fixtures file (`export const test = base.extend(…)`, then `import { expect, test } from './fixture'`), which is Playwright's documented fixtures pattern. pregate only marks a spec as Playwright when the spec itself imports `@playwright/test` (#3741). So a diff that touches only a spec, even one comment line, sends it to `vitest run <spec>`. Vitest finds no test files, the lane fails, and `/ship` cannot publish a record. This PR follows the modules a test takes `test` from. A unit test that imports some other Playwright-based helper keeps its unit runner.

Detection alone does not get my specs to pass. My harness has to build the native engine and the bundle before a spec can start, and the repo's entry point `pnpm run e2e -- <spec>` does that build, while a bare `playwright test` deliberately never builds. A repo can declare only one `runner` for every file today, so I add `runners` to `.gstack/pregate.json`. A rule is `{ when: [globs], runner, cwd? }`, and the selected files it matches go to that command ahead of `runner` and detection, first match wins. Every other file keeps today's plan. `gstack-checks` treats each rule as a command that needs consent, like `runner`.

## Live evidence

Same branch, where one commit changes one comment line in `app/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (later `editing-flag.spec.ts`). Command: `gstack-pregate run --stage tests --allow-repo-commands --base <base>`.

**Installed 1.99.2.0**, the spec goes to vitest:
```
    lanes: ran: (cd 'app' && pnpm exec vitest run 'e2e/smoke.spec.ts')
    lanes:   No test files found, exiting with code 1
    lanes:   include: src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, e2e/lib/**/*.test.ts
tests      lanes     fail               1823 ms  local lane exited 1 (? failed of ? ran; 1 files; pipefail) (PREGATE_LANE_FAILED)
```

**This branch, no `runners` rule**: the spec is now seen as Playwright. My harness then refuses to start on a stale bundle, which is why the second part exists:
```
    lanes: ran: (cd 'app' && pnpm exec playwright test --reporter=list '(?:^|/)e2e/smoke\.spec\.ts$')
    lanes:       Error: Harness kann nicht starten:
    lanes:       - Bundle nicht frisch (main älter als app/src, …) — `pnpm run e2e:rauch` baut es
tests      lanes     fail               6576 ms  local lane exited 1 (1 failed of 1 ran; 1 files; pipefail) (PREGATE_LANE_FAILED)
```

**This branch, base policy with** `"runners": [{ "when": ["app/e2e/*.spec.ts"], "runner": "pnpm run e2e -- {files}", "cwd": "app/e2e" }]`: the spec runs through the repo's entry point, which builds and then runs it:
```
PREGATE_TEST: 1/1 editing-flag.spec.ts pass 30.7
tests      lanes     requires-remote   31246 ms  1 tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0; 2 requires-remote obligation(s)
    lanes: ran: (cd 'app/e2e' && pnpm run e2e -- 'editing-flag.spec.ts')
    lanes:     ✓  1 [e2e] › e2e/editing-flag.spec.ts:16:7 › … (14.2s)
    lanes:     ✓  2 [e2e] › e2e/editing-flag.spec.ts:45:7 › … (12.3s)
    lanes:     2 passed (26.8s)
```
The two requires-remote obligations are the repo's Linux CI lanes, unchanged by this PR.

The four new tests were red before the fix:
```
(fail) … > a spec importing test from a local fixtures module that extends @playwright/test runs through playwright test
(fail) … > a runners rule sends its files to its command from its directory; the rest keep their plan
(fail) … > config: runners entries need globs, a {files} command and a contained directory
(fail) gstack-checks on a fixture repo > consent covers the runners rules
```
The first one was red because the specs went into the vitest group (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`, `e2e/deep.spec.ts` under `pnpm exec vitest run`). The consent test was red because a rule added on the base ran with exit 0 and no new consent.

To confirm the tests can fail, I broke the code on purpose:

| Sabotage | Test that went red |
|---|---|
| Spec detection back to the direct import only | the fixtures-module test |
| `runners` ignored (`planRuns` skips the rules) | the runners-rule test |
| `cwd` validation removed | the config test |

## Scope

- **Changed:**
  - `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts`:
    - `playwrightSpec` follows the modules a test takes `test` from, through `import { test }`, aliases, `export { test } from`, `index` modules and `.js` specifiers that name `.ts` sources, up to 8 hops and only inside the repo.
    - `planRuns` applies `runners` rules first. A matched file outside the rule's `cwd` is `unclaimed`, so the lane reads `incomplete`.

title: Stop /ship failing on test files under hidden folders like .github (GST-2640)
body:
/ship now runs test files that live under hidden folders such as `.github/scripts/`, instead of failing a passing test with `PREGATE_LANE_FAILED`. This keeps /ship usable for every repo that keeps tests next to its CI scripts; it was blocking gbrain PRs that touch `.github/scripts/` (gbrain#3965).

## What changed

Every place /ship builds a `bun test <files>` command now hands Bun explicit paths: the local lane (runner detected or declared), the remote-gate command a small machine records, the docs-only reader tests and the base-red check. One helper in `lib/test-paths.ts` adds `./` to a relative path unless it already starts with `./`, `../` or `/`. The CI carry's per-file command already did this and now shares the helper. Other runners such as vitest, jest and pytest get the same arguments as before. A runner written with Bun's own flags before `test`, like `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test {files}`, is recognized too.

Before and after on Bun 1.4.4, for a passing test at `.github/scripts/x.test.mjs`:

```text
before: bun test .github/scripts/x.test.mjs     -> exit 1 (no test files matched)
after:  bun test ./.github/scripts/x.test.mjs   -> 1 pass, 0 fail, exit 0
```

## Why

"PREGATE_LANE_FAILED on a green test": Bun reads a bare relative path as a name filter, and that search skips hidden folders, so the selected test never ran and Bun exited 1. Now the lane runs the test and judges its real result, and a failing test in a hidden folder still fails the lane.

## Blast radius

The change touches how five /ship commands spell test file paths for `bun test`. That is safe for existing setups because an explicit `./` path names the same file Bun already ran for non-hidden paths, and every non-bun runner keeps its arguments unchanged (the vitest control row in `test/pregate-hidden-folder-paths.test.ts`). The full free suite at 3ee7fd1 is green in CI run 43527019293, and the macOS and Windows jobs are green too.

## Summary

- Add a shared helper that gives `bun test` explicit test paths, and use it in the lanes check, the remote-gate command, the docs-only lane, base-red and the CI carry.
- Recognize bun runners that pass Bun flags before `test`.
- Tests: a fixture repo with a test under `.github/scripts/` runs the real lanes check (green passes, red still fails, a missing file never reaches Bun), plus direct checks of base-red's select, the CI carry's per-file command and the small-machine remote-gate command.

## Test Coverage

Value-weighted coverage is 67% (minimum 60, target 80), with 4 of 6 changed paths covered by a two-star test and none weakly covered. The /ship coverage audit wrote 3 tests over two generation passes (one was rejected for an incomplete value card and removed).

```text
[+] lib/test-paths.ts explicitPath / testFileArgs      ** tested
[+] lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts runOnce bun args        ** tested (green, red, missing-file lanes)
[+] lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts remoteObligation        ** tested (small-machine remote-gate command)
[+] lib/base-red.ts runAt select                        ** tested
[+] lib/ci-carry.ts perFileCommand                      ** tested
[+] lib/pregate/docs-only-lane.ts spawn args            GAP (proposed: a docs-only fixture with a hidden-folder reader test)
```

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue fixed in pass 1 (a runner with Bun flags before `test` still got bare paths), 3 below-floor notes in pass 2, 0 blocking. The notes are listed under Review notes below.

Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

## Exploratory QA

Smoke probes on Bun 1.4.4, both passed: a bare `bun test .github/scripts/x.test.mjs` exits 1 (the original failure), and the `./` form runs 1 test and passes. The focused lane of 7 test files ran 119 tests with 0 failures.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: run hidden-folder tests in /ship's lanes. Delivered: explicit bun test paths in every /ship bun test command, plus tests.

## Plan Completion

No plan: a bug fix, exempt from plan review.

## Issues

Refs GST-2640 and gbrain#3965.

## Verification Results

No plan-specific checks; the automatic checks are listed above.

## TODOS

No TODOS.md changes.

## Documentation
**Status:** current. No documentation needed a correction for this change.

**Scope:** base 6b033e79..head 3ee7fd1e (2 commits, 8 files): a new `lib/test-paths.ts` helper (`BUN_TEST`, `explicitPath`, `testFileArgs`) and its use in the pregate local lane, the remote-gate command, the docs-only reader tests, base-red `select` and the CI carry's `per_file` command, plus a new test and a changelog.d fragment. There were no staged, unstaged or untracked changes. I searched docs/pregate.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, docs/test-impact.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md for claims about test-path arguments.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/pregate.md: current (the `per_file` text already says paths are anchored with `./`)
- docs/ship-policy.md: current (nothing in it is wrong)
- README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, docs/test-impact.md: not affected

**Coverage debt:** `explicitPath` and `testFileArgs` are internal, so they have no public surface. Reference gaps, both optional: the pregate `runner` row and the ship-policy `base_red.select` description could each say that `bun test` file arguments now get `./` added, so test files under hidden folders such as `.github/` run.

**Diagram drift:** none.

- [x] `bun test ./test/pregate-hidden-folder-paths.test.ts` and the focused lane: 119 pass, 0 fail
- [x] Free suite in CI run 43527019293 at 3ee7fd1: green (1667 files carried)
- [x] macOS named regressions (run 43527019293) and Windows smoke (run 43527019447): green
- [x] `bun run typecheck`: clean

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/test-paths.ts:9` The widened BUN_TEST pattern only accepts a Bun flag that is glued to its value, as in `--config=/dev/null`. When the flag and value are separated by a space, as in `bun --config /dev/null test {files}` or `bun --preload ./setup.ts test {files}`, the pattern does not match. testFileArgs then passes bare `.github/...` paths, and the hidden-folder bug this change fixes comes back for that spelling. The new test covers only the `=` form and has no case for the space form or for commands that must stay unmatched, such as `bun run test`.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/test-paths.ts:9` The widened BUN_TEST regex backtracks exponentially when a command has many dash flags after `bun` and no `test`. `--?` followed by `[\w-]+` can split every `--flag` token two ways (`--`+`flag` or `-`+`-flag`), so a failed match tries about 2^n paths. On Bun 1.4.4 I measured `'bun' + ' --a'.repeat(n) + ' run x'` at 6 ms for 16 flags, 56 ms for 20, 625 ms for 24 and 1.2 s for 26, and each two more flags roughly doubles it. This regex runs synchronously on every runner and base-red `select` string, in testFileArgs (lanes.ts:370 and 464, base-red.ts:87) and as the progress adapter (supervise.ts:29 and 118, lanes.ts:570), so a long flag list in the repo's config stalls pregate before any test starts. The old `bun\s+test` had no such path. Normal runners with 2 or 3 flags stay under a millisecond, which is why this is informational.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/test-paths.ts:9` The trailing `test\b` also matches `test` when it is followed by `/` or `.`, so the flag form now treats a Bun script that lives under test/ as `bun test`. Examples are `bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null test/helpers/run-one.ts {files}` and `bun --watch test/x.ts {files}`. Both now return true, where the old regex returned false, and testFileArgs rewrites `.github/x.test.ts` to `./.github/x.test.ts`. The bun progress adapter is also chosen for them. `bun --filter=pkg test`, which runs the package.json `test` script, and `bun -e test` match too. The bare `bun test/x.ts` case already existed, but this change extends it to the `--no-env-file --config=/dev/null` prefix that AGENTS.md requires for every gstack Bun launch. A wrapper script that compares its arguments with git-relative paths would then get `./`-prefixed names that never match.

title: setup-browser-cookies: say the Windows Chrome/Edge/Brave limit before step 2, and name $B handoff
body:
**What happened:** On Windows, an agent invoked `setup-browser-cookies` to reuse a Chrome sign-in for a protected preview page. The skill's step 2 asks five questions (source browser, profile, domains, verification, storage reset) before anything runs. Only the last section, "Platform boundaries", says Windows supports DPAPI cookies but not App-Bound Encryption, with native extraction disabled, which rules out current Chrome, Edge and Brave. The agent read to the end and abandoned the skill. It never ran the Aside probe and never offered the documented alternative of signing in manually through `$B handoff` / `$B resume`, which is described only in BROWSER.md.
**Expected:** A Windows + Chromium-family source is caught before the questions, and the skill points straight to a source that works or to the headed manual sign-in handoff.
**Version:** gstack 1.61.0.0 · **OS:** Windows 11
**Screenshot:** none: nothing about this is visible

**Repro:**
1. On Windows with Chrome 136+, invoke `/setup-browser-cookies` asking to import a site's cookies from Chrome.
2. Read SKILL.md top to bottom: step 2 asks for browser/profile/domains; the Windows App-Bound limit appears only after step 5.

**Proposed fix:** Add a platform check at the start of step 2: on Windows with Chrome/Edge/Brave as the source, say in one line that native import is not supported there, and offer (a) a supported source browser, or (b) `$B handoff` for a manual sign-in followed by `$B resume`, naming those commands in SKILL.md itself.

**Notes:** Closed #765 asked for Windows support generally. This report is narrower: the skill's ordering spends the user's answers before saying the import cannot work.

title: Retry /ship's second-model review on Astra, then Gemini, when OpenAI refuses it as a cyber-security risk (GST-2649)
body:
When OpenAI refuses /ship's outside voice under its cyber-security policy (the error says `cyber_policy`), Capy's /ship now retries the review instead of losing the second-family read. This keeps cross-model review working on security-heavy PRs, which are the ones that need it most (rule R95). **A refusal is its own outcome.** `lib/outside-review-result.ts` classifies `cyber_policy` as `cyber_policy_refused`, a new reason in `lib/gate-outcomes.ts` with its own entry at [docs/troubleshooting.md#outside-review-cyber-policy](docs/troubleshooting.md). It reads Capy's host error for the reviewer (a new `providerError` input and `--provider-error` flag) and Codex's trailing `ERROR:` lines, never the whole stderr, so a prompt echo that quotes `cyber_policy` is not a refusal. Auth, quota, timeout and empty-reply outcomes are unchanged. **One retry per step, in R95's order.** When the outside voice ends failed with a `cyber_policy` host error, the pass program asks the new `gstack-review-dispatch retry`, which plans the next attempt in the manifest: GPT-6 Astra on a read-only correctness brief, then, only if Astra is refused too, Gemini 4 Carbon on the original brief, byte for byte. Each refused attempt is collected as unavailable coverage with its reason, so the ledger shows every attempt. Any other failure prints `RETRY: none` and keeps today's unavailable path, and nothing else retries. **The reworded brief is used only on the retry.** `READ_ONLY_RETRY` in `lib/review-brief.ts` is the one home for the new text: it drops "Think like an attacker and a chaos engineer" and "Be adversarial" from the section's outside prompt, and asks for file:line, the condition under which the code returns the wrong answer, and the smallest fix, with no exploit code or reproductions. If the section's wording changes, rendering fails loudly instead of sending a half-edited brief. The first brief every outside voice gets is unchanged. **A spent chain is a disclosed gap, not a pass.** Step 11's `OUTSIDE_RECORD` now names the last attempt and adds `outside_note`: either "second-family read by openai/gpt-6-astra on the read-only retry brief after cyber_policy refused openai/gpt-6.1-sol", or "second-family read missing: cyber_policy refused ...". As today, a missing outside voice doesn't block: the native voice still runs and the PR body lists the gap as missing coverage. Also: the diff-size ceiling now exempts every outside-voice reader by role, not just the one named `outside-voice`, so a retry reader slices its diff like the original instead of stopping the stage.

title: gstack-redact refuses any input over 16 MiB even with --max-bytes, and neither --help nor the error says so
body:
## What happens

`gstack-redact --from-file` refuses any file larger than 16 MiB (16,777,216 bytes) before the engine's size cap is consulted, so `--max-bytes` cannot raise the limit past it. The error is:

```
gstack-redact: input file too large (<n> bytes)
```

and the exit code is 3. Input on stdin has the same ceiling and prints `gstack-redact: stdin too large`, also exit 3.

Nothing a user can read says this. The header comment describes `--max-bytes N` as "Override the fail-closed size cap (default 1 MiB)", and `--help` lists `--max-bytes N` with no description at all. Neither names the 16 MiB ceiling, and neither error names it, the flag, or what to do. A user who sees "too large" and passes a bigger `--max-bytes` gets the same error again.

## Evidence

gstack 1.99.3.0 (`main`), `bin/gstack-redact`:

- Line 42: `const MAX_STDIN_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024; // hard ceiling before the engine cap`
- Lines 157-159: the `--from-file` check (`st.size > MAX_STDIN_BYTES`, then the error above, exit 3).
- Lines 180-181: the stdin check (`stdin too large`, exit 3).
- Line 24 (header comment) and lines 259-260 (`--help` text): the only mentions of `--max-bytes`; no ceiling.

## Reproduce

```bash
head -c 17000000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a' > big.txt
gstack-redact --from-file big.txt --max-bytes 20000000; echo "exit=$?"
```

Output:

```
gstack-redact: input file too large (17000000 bytes)
exit=3
```

A file of exactly 16,777,216 bytes is accepted with the same flag (exit 0), so the ceiling is the 16 MiB constant, not the value given to `--max-bytes`.

## Effect

The documented override looks unlimited, so a user who needs to scan a large file has no way to learn that the limit is fixed. Exit 3 is also the code for a HIGH finding, so a script or CI step that calls `gstack-redact` can read an oversize input as "credential found" with only the stderr line to tell the two apart.

## Suggested fix

- Name the ceiling where `--max-bytes` is described, in the header comment and in `--help`, for example: "`--max-bytes N` overrides the fail-closed size cap (default 1 MiB); input over 16 MiB is always refused, split it."
- Say it in both errors, for example: `input file too large (17000000 bytes; the limit is 16 MiB and --max-bytes cannot raise it). Split the input and scan the parts.`
- Optionally reject a `--max-bytes` above 16 MiB at argument parsing (the check near line 208 already validates the value), so the contradiction shows up before any file is read.

Related but not a duplicate: #1824 (invalid `--max-bytes` values) and #2304 (the pre-push hook's 1 MiB cap). Neither mentions the 16 MiB ceiling.

title: /ship reviewers state their blocker count in one line, and gstack checks it against their findings (GST-2495)
body:
/ship's reviewers now end their reply header with one machine-readable line, `REVIEW_VERDICT: blocking=`, and gstack checks that count against the findings it parsed from their prose. Why: the findings parser misread free-form review prose in both directions, so a "nothing blocks" summary could become a fake blocker and a real blocker could be lost. Nothing to do: a reply with no verdict line, or a malformed one, is read exactly as before, and review logs written before this change replay byte for byte.
Why, in detail The findings parser reads free-form review prose, so it fails in both directions. FOUN-298's native reviewer wrote "I found nothing that blocks. There are three Low findings, all FIXABLE", and the parser collected a CRITICAL from that sentence. CAPY-1's fix-check and red-team replies held no-defect summaries that collected as CRITICAL. The earlier prose-rule fix (#4301) tried to recognize "nothing blocks" sentences and failed open on phrasings like "nothing blocks, but the API key is logged". This change stops guessing from prose: the reader states the count, and the parser's own rows are checked against it. It serves the review loop's core goal: a blocker a reviewer reports must never vanish, and a reviewer's "nothing blocks" summary should not be turned into a fake blocker.
What changed - **The ask.** Every blocking reader (specialists, the batched specialist, the targeted reader, the Red Team, fix-check, the native adversarial reviewer and the second-model review) is asked, right after the REVIEWED_TREE step, for `REVIEW_VERDICT: blocking=` with optional `at=:` locations. Audit readers are not asked. The render records `verdict: 1` so collect and verify know the brief asked. - **Higher count than parsed:** collect adds a CRITICAL row for each declared location no parsed blocking row names, plus one row for the rest. A blocker written in a shape the parser misses now blocks anyway. - **Lower count than parsed:** nothing is lowered automatically. A row that blocks only because a sentence uses the word CRITICAL or P0 (no list item, heading, field, lead label, JSON or file:line, no `Blocks: yes`) becomes a summary candidate, which the lead may lower with a written reason. - **One automatic lowering:** with a valid line, the native adversarial reviewer's unanchored prose line with no CRITICAL, P0 or `Blocks: yes` keeps its own label instead of the FIXABLE raise. That is the FOUN-298 sentence. - **No line or a malformed line:** today's parse, recorded as such. - `collect` prints a `COLLECT_VERDICT:` line per reader and `verify` an informational `VERIFY_VERDICT:` line; the `VERIFY:` line is unchanged. - Docs: [docs/review-policy.md step 3a](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/review-policy.md#verdict-line). Preregistration: [docs/evals/verdict-line-replay-prereg.md](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/main/docs/evals/verdict-line-replay-prereg.md).
Blast radius Only /ship and /review reader output parsing changes. The one new behavior that can block is a reader declaring more blockers than the parser found, which adds CRITICAL rows instead of losing a blocker. Nothing is lowered automatically.
Tests - New test/review-verdict.test.ts (25 tests): the grammar, the ask on every blocking role and not on audit readers, negative controls (FOUN-298, #3901, both CAPY-1 shapes, the GSTA-521 probe lines) under no line, a malformed line, `blocking=0` and `blocking=1` on all seven roles and both review classes, synthetic rows, a ledger round trip and judge. - Failing first: on main the test file cannot load (no verdict module), and main's parser collects FOUN-298's reply as CRITICAL,Low,Low,Low and both CAPY-1 replies as INFORMATIONAL,CRITICAL on every role. - test/review-dispatch.test.ts and test/review-pass.test.ts: brief expectations updated for the ask only. - CI: Free Tests [pull_request run 43569056755](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/43569056755) and [dispatched free-tests run 43569554184](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/43569554184) at ac0d6b1 (tree 33892a4c5508) green, 37,300 tests. Every pull_request check at ac0d6b1 (Version Gate, Workflow Lint, Quality gate, Skill Docs Freshness, E2E Evals, Windows Scoped Tests, Windows Smoke, Plain title) green. CI at b5d0abe: all checks green. - Local checks at b5d0abe: typecheck clean; test typecheck ratchet "none new"; affected files 187 pass, 1 fail, where the failure is the review-dispatch "edited to look refused" case hitting bun's 5 s default timeout (it takes 8.8 s alone on main too, and passes with --timeout 30000); module-size, spawnSync tripwire, bun entry isolation and state-root ratchets pass; gen:skill-docs --host all leaves the tree unchanged (no template or SKILL.md change).

title: Exclude a data file from /ship's review when the base policy names it by file name (GST-2674)
body:
/ship can now leave a large results data file out of its reviewers' diff when the base branch's `review_exclude_paths` names that file by its exact file name, even when the name looks like tool config (`manifest.json`). Why: an eval results PR with a 1.42 MB manifest went past the 2 MB review limit and /ship refused it with no override, although the base policy already listed that manifest. Nothing to do: broader patterns (`data/**`, `**/*.json`) still keep config files in review, and a PR still can't exclude its own files, because the policy is read only from the base branch.
What changed One classification rule in `lib/review-exclude.ts`, with no other visible surface. A matched JSON, CSV, TSV or image file whose name gstack treats as config (`manifest.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, dotfiles) is now treated as data when a base-policy pattern ends in that file's exact name with no glob character. It is excluded from every reader's diff, and it no longer counts as code that names other files, so the receipts it lists stop being kept as `named-by-code`. Config files under broader patterns are still kept as `config`, and every earlier keep rule (gate paths, executables, links, secret lines, gate tags, `.gstack/` and `.github/`) still runs first. `docs/ship-policy.md` describes the new rule. It keeps big eval results PRs reviewable instead of stopping at the 2 MB reader ceiling, which serves gstack's goal of shipping reviewed work unattended.
Why, in detail "Their 1.42 MB results manifest then pushes /ship past the 2 MB reader ceiling, and /ship refuses with REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE, which has no override." The base policy already listed `docs/benchmarks/*/results*/**/manifest.json`, but gstack kept every `manifest.json` in review as config anyway, so readers got the 1.42 MB file and the run stopped. The kept manifest also counted as code that names files, so every receipt it listed stayed in review too.
Blast radius Only the `review_exclude_paths` selection changes, and only for files a pattern names by file name. Every other keep rule runs before the new check (`lib/review-exclude.ts:279-290`, read). QA checkpoint 002 ran `gstack-review-plan --json` on fixture repos to confirm the broad-glob, exact-path and glob-in-last-segment cases (script ran).
Tests - New case in `test/review-exclude.test.ts`, written first and failing on main: a manifest named by a pattern is excluded along with the receipts it lists; `data/manifest.json` and `data/package.json` under `data/**` stay kept as `config`; an unmatched `package.json` stays in every reader's diff. Every changed runtime file has a changed test naming it. - `test/review-exclude.test.ts` (49 pass), the other exclusion and receipt suites, typecheck, the test typecheck ratchet, module size, changelog fragment and spawn timeout checks pass locally. `bun test test/review-exclude.test.ts -t 'config-named data file'` passes (QA capture 001). - CI is the full run: `bun run test` green in [Free Tests run 43565161884](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/43565161884) at 076db4a (1,668 files).

Nothing in the review blocks: no finding would fail a test, break production or lose data or secrets. Every finding below stays open as a note for a follow-up. Second-model review: GPT-6.1 Sol (host subagent) completed, VERDICT: CLEAN. - INFORMATIONAL (security specialist) `lib/review-exclude.ts:372`: a base-policy pattern like `**/package.json` now drops every package.json from review, including a root one with install scripts (QA checkpoint 002 reproduced it). It needs an explicit base-branch entry. - INFORMATIONAL (Red Team) `lib/review-exclude.ts:372`: whether a file counts as named comes from the changed-file list, so an unchanged named `manifest.json` still counts as a consumer and keeps the changed receipts it lists. This fails closed, but a correction PR that leaves the manifest unchanged can still hit REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE. - Medium, Blocks: no (native adversarial) `lib/review-exclude.ts:372`: the same leading-`**` case as the first note, confirmed by a second reader. Suggested follow-up: also require a literal leading directory (`literalPrefix(q) !== ''`). - Low, Blocks: no (native adversarial) `lib/review-exclude.ts:410`: the selection digest changes across gstack versions for ranges where a named pattern matches a config-named file, and `REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEY_VERSION` did not move, so a receipt from one version checked by another refuses (fails closed). - Low, Blocks: no (native adversarial) `lib/review-exclude.ts:372`: a pattern skipped at `KEEP_ARG_MAX_BYTES` still marks its file as named, so a broader applied pattern can exclude it while the receipt lists the naming pattern as skipped.
