Differences from #4352: the limit comes from one constant (`MAX_STDIN_MIB`) instead of a hardcoded "16 MiB" in three places; the help sentence sits on its own lines; the exit line names the oversize case; #4352's test that `--max-bytes 67108864` scans small input was dropped because it doesn't test the ceiling.
- Security read: the diff changes only stderr strings, help text and a comment. `MAX_STDIN_BYTES` is still 16777216, both checks and `process.exit(3)` are unchanged, and the errors print only the byte count they printed before, never input content.

title: Explain in CONTRIBUTING how outside reports and PRs land (GST-2723)
body:
CONTRIBUTING.md now explains, in plain words, what happens to an outside issue or PR here and what makes one likely to land.
It answers an outside review that found most contributors see "Closed" with no explanation, and there is nothing for you to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

## Summary

- A new "Sending a report or a PR" section in CONTRIBUTING.md, written for outside contributors. It says AI agents working for the maintainer triage issues and PRs, rebuild good patches on current main and land them with the author credited, which is why commits read as the maintainer's. It lists three paths a PR can take. A docs-only PR for people (for example the README) can be merged as it is after every link, command and install step is checked; a plainly correct fix of about 40 lines or fewer is taken even when the gain is small, at most one a day; everything else is rebuilt on main when it has proof, a real consequence and matters to most users. It gives the 48-hour first-reply goal and the narrowed open-PR limit, which never applies to anyone with a PR taken in the last 90 days.
- The maintainer steps in "How a contributor's PR lands" now add a first reply within 48 hours, the docs-only merge step, the small-fix rule and the open-PR limit for repeat authors whose PRs mostly weren't taken.
- The old "Community PR triage (wave process)" section is gone, because it merged outside PRs on a collector branch, which the current rules don't allow. `docs/triage.md` and `docs/review-policy.md` now point at the new steps.
- The maintainer guide for AI teams (`crew/docs/captain.md`), its rules template, the harness comparison table and the `/captain` skill say the same thing.

## Why

"Outside PRs almost never merge directly ... contributors see 'closed, not merged' about 99% of the time," said an outside review of the project on 2026-11-15. The maintainer changed three rules that day. Docs-only PRs for people can merge as they are, small correct fixes are taken, and the open-PR limit no longer applies to anyone with a recent PR taken. Contributors can now read what will happen before they spend time on a PR.

## Blast radius

Documentation only, plus the regenerated `captain/SKILL.md` (one sentence). No code, script or test changed. The `/captain` skill and its rules template are read by agents, so their wording now allows a docs-only outside PR to merge after a text read; the change in `captain/SKILL.md.tmpl` and the generated file match (read at the head, and the skill-docs freshness check passed in CI).

</details>

title: Bring back the standalone /plan-eng-review command (GST-2726)
body:
`/plan-eng-review` is back as its own command on every host that had it before #4108, and architecture-review requests route to it again.
Why: many people run it on its own (Garry, 2026-11-15), and cutting it took that away; `/autoplan`'s eng phase is unchanged.
To do: nothing. If an earlier upgrade removed the command, your next `./setup` or upgrade puts it back.

<details>
<summary>What changed</summary>

- **Install.** `./setup` installs `/plan-eng-review` again on Claude Code, Codex and the other external hosts, and OpenClaw's default (hybrid) skill list includes it again. `/investigate` stays retired through the same mechanism.
- **Routing.** The router sends architecture and engineering-review requests to `/plan-eng-review` again, and its voice triggers ("tech review") are back. `/autoplan`'s description drops the "review the architecture" and "engineering review" phrases #4108 added, so the two skills no longer claim the same requests.
- **Docs and chaining.** AGENTS.md, README, docs/skills.md, CLAUDE.md, llms.txt and the OpenClaw and hosts docs list it again. The office-hours handoff, the CEO, design and devex review chaining, `/ship`'s review dashboard row and its over-200-lines hint name it again.
- **`/autoplan` is unchanged.** Its eng phase reads the same methodology. On external hosts that file still ships beside `gstack-autoplan/SKILL.md` as `plan-eng-review.md`, byte-identical to before on all 12 external hosts, so `/autoplan` works even if someone disables the standalone command. #4108's Kiro fix (copying that file into Kiro installs) and its ownership guards stay.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Not restored</summary>

The paid standalone test cases deleted after #4108 (`plan-eng-plan-mode`, `plan-eng-finding-floor`, `plan-eng-review-artifact-full`, `carve-section-loading-plan-eng-review`) stay deleted, and `plan-eng-multi-finding-batching` stays out of the weekly run. title: gstack-issue-links prints an empty commit id for issue mentions from older commits
body:
## What happened

`gstack-issue-links` labels each issue mention with the commit it came from. A mention from the newest commit on the branch gets that commit's id; a mention from any older commit prints `commit :` with an empty id:

```text
Refs #11
Refs #12
  reference #12 ← commit afb363788803: Refs #12 (promote: fix #12)
  reference #11 ← commit : Refs #11 (promote: fix #11)
```

The same empty label is in `--json` output (`"source":"commit : Refs #11"`). /ship's Step 19 ("Issue links", `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl:59-65`) asks the user about these `(promote: fix #N)` references, and for a mention in an older commit the user is not told which commit it is in.

Cause, at `main` 0326b144af36676d599dcf63a9fad9a870d22ed6 (same blob in 1.99.4.0), `bin/gstack-issue-links:144` and `:147-151`:

```ts
const log = git(['log', '--format=%H%n%B%x00', `origin/${base}..HEAD`], repoRoot) ?? git(['log', '--format=%H%n%B%x00', `${base}..HEAD`], repoRoot);
...
for (const entry of log.split('\0')) {
  const nl = entry.indexOf('\n');
  if (nl < 0) continue;
  mentions.push(...mentionsIn(entry.slice(nl + 1), `commit ${entry.slice(0, nl).trim().slice(0, 12)}`));
}
```

`git log --format` ends each commit's output with a newline after the format, so the bytes are `<hash>\n<body>\0\n<hash>\n<body>\0\n`. After `split('\0')` every entry except the first starts with that `\n`: `indexOf('\n')` is 0, the label's hash is the empty string, and the hash line is read as the first line of the message. No mention is lost or invented in our tests (a hash line has no `#`), only the label.

Expected: every candidate line names its own commit. Two ways that would do it: `git log -z --format=%H%n%B` (git then ends each commit with NUL and adds no newline; on the repro below the entries start `afb…`, `4ef…`, then an empty tail), or strip one leading `\n` from each entry before looking for the hash. With `-z`, both `git log` calls on line 144 need it (the `origin/<base>` one and its `<base>` fallback); the leading-`\n` strip sits in the loop and covers both. The CLI-level assertions in `test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts` (`:73`, `:186`) check only the `← commit ` prefix; a two-commit CLI test asserting each mention's own commit id would catch this.

Related: #4371 (another `gstack-issue-links` reading of commit messages).

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a scratch repository:
   ```bash
   git init -q -b main && git commit -q --allow-empty -m base && git switch -q -c feat
   git commit -q --allow-empty -m "first change" -m "Refs #11"
   git commit -q --allow-empty -m "second change" -m "Refs #12"
   ```
2. Run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-issue-links --base main --no-auto-links --repo acme-example/widget-co`.
3. The stderr line for `#12` names the newest commit; the line for `#11` reads `commit : Refs #11`.

## Readiness report

```text

ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: claude global current (1.99.4.0), agy global current (1.99.4.0), codex global current (1.99.4.0)

ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.160.1; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 1h ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 0)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.99.4.0 (81fb9008351d)

15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

title: /ship's existing-PR step does not ask the agent to check gstack-post's "kept" list, so a re-run can leave an earlier run's sections in the PR body
body:
## What happens

We re-ran /ship on an open PR after merging the base. Step 19 composed a fresh body, as `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl:73` says ("never reuse a prior run's body"), and posted it with the existing-PR command at `:281`, `gstack-post pr-body <pr-number> --body-file …`. It printed:

```text
gstack-post: pr-body merged by section: replaced leading text, Summary, Blast radius, Test Coverage, Pre-Landing Review, Review notes, Exploratory QA, Design Review, Eval Results, Scope Drift, Plan Completion, Verification Results, TODOS, Documentation, Test plan, Agent notes; kept Discrimination test, Tests; added Review bot comments
```

The two kept sections were in the PR body from before this run. We believe the earlier /ship run's agent wrote them (the template lists neither), but the merge cannot know that. They described the earlier head as if current: a regression check run against an older base commit, with that run's pass counts, under a body whose other sections now described the new head. The kept `## Tests` section ended with its own `🤖 Generated with …` line, so the body carried that line twice.

The post exited 0, and the run took the `**0** posted` branch (`:310`), which goes straight to removing the temporary files. At `main` 0326b144, neither `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` nor any `ship/sections/*.md.tmpl` mentions checking gstack-post's `kept` list.

`gstack-post` is doing what it documents: `lib/gstack-post.ts:9-16` keeps sections the file does not rewrite, and `docs/troubleshooting.md#gstack-post-pr-body-merge` says under **Fix.**: "Nothing, when the kept sections are wanted. … To drop a section, post the body with `--replace` or edit it on the host." That is how we repaired it: the same composed file, posted with `--replace`. It already carried the receipt, and nothing kept was wanted; a body with sections a person added would need those carried into the file first. So this is a request for /ship's handling, not a merge defect.

## What we expected

Either of these would have caught it:

- After an existing-PR post that reports `kept` sections, Step 19 has the agent decide each one: leave a section a person added; for one an earlier /ship run wrote, drop it (rewrite the file with the person-added sections carried over, then `--replace`, or edit on the host). That rewrite would be a deliberate exception to `:275` ("Never re-render the body: every retry sends the same files."), which is about retrying a failed post. The duplicate-title case keeps its own rule (`:322`: stop, a human picks the copy; never `--replace` on your own).
- New: /ship marks the sections it composes, so a later run's merge can tell an earlier run's sections from a person's and report or drop them. No marker covers the `## ` sections the agent composes (Summary, Test plan and the rest); the agent-notes marker and the receipt fence cover only the closing notes and the receipt.

Related: #3575 (closed: the merge kept a stale copy when a title appeared twice; here each title appears once).

## How to reproduce

1. /ship a branch to an open PR; in Step 19 the body includes a section the template does not list (for example `## Discrimination test`).
2. Merge the base into the branch and run /ship again; this run's body does not include that section.
3. Step 19 posts with `gstack-post pr-body <n> --body-file …`; stderr lists the old section under `kept`, the PR body still shows it with the first run's results, and the run continues on exit 0.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.309 on Linux 7.0.0 (container); gstack 1.99.4.0 (81fb9008351d), doctor 15 ok, 0 warn, 0 fail
- `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl`, `lib/gstack-post.ts`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` and every `ship/sections/*.md.tmpl` read at `main` 0326b144af36676d599dcf63a9fad9a870d22ed6 (`pr-body.md.tmpl` and `gstack-post.ts` are the same blobs as in 1.99.4.0)

title: Add guides for landing a fix in someone else's repo and running human playtests (GST-2757)
body:
Adds two short how-to guides: landing a fix in a repository you don't own, and running a human playtest. Why: both habits kept coming up in our own agent teams, and gstack had no page for either. Nothing to do as a reader; the pages are in `docs/` and change no skill or tool.
Agent notes **What's in it.** `docs/howto-land-a-fix-in-someone-elses-repo.md`: read their rules, search their main and open PRs for the same fix before designing, read the code's history, keep it small, run every guard their CI runs before opening, answer each review point in a new commit and rerun the proof. `docs/howto-run-human-playtests.md`: vendor-free; ask about moments and where people would stop, and never pick a winner by having people play two builds back to back, because the order played decided the pick. Plus a changelog fragment. **Evidence is thin, said plainly.** Guide 1 rests on one outside repository: the first PR there failed its first review on a CI guard that was never run locally, and a maintainer's much smaller fix merged over a far larger one. Guide 2 rests on one team's playtests, where the build played second won most back-to-back picks whichever build it was. Neither figure was re-checked for this PR. **Why add it, and how we'll know (ETHOS 9, Earn Its Place).** Stated reason: both lessons cost real review rounds and a wasted test series. Measure, as the follow-up: count review rounds on the next two outside PRs that use guide 1, and use guide 2 on the next playtest and record whether a decision came from quit points and moments rather than a pick. **Docs-only.** `bin/gstack-docs-only --base origin/main --head HEAD` prints `DOCS_ONLY: yes (3 file(s); ...)`. A README index row would make the PR non-docs-only (README.md is named by workflows and CLAUDE.md), so the index rows are left for a follow-up. ## Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 0 asked (0 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 1 noted REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=1 fixed=0 scope=frozen ledgers_read=1 Gate edits: none detected (0 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Review plan: class=docs, depth light, one pass on the whole diff, no dispatched readers (specialists, red team, adversarial and second-model review skipped by the plan for a docs-class change with no numbers). ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `README.md:270` The two new how-to guides are not listed in README.md's how-to table, so readers browsing the README won't find them. title: Add a write-up checklist to ETHOS and the READY template (GST-2755)
body:
Adds a three-item write-up checklist to ETHOS.md: a post's words match the page it links, every number, "green" and "ready" names its source and is read at the current head, and a fresh model reads it cold once. Why: posts that said more than their linked page, and numbers read from a stale tree, were the most common corrections in our own agent teams. The READY template now points to the second item; nothing else changes for users. **Status:** current. The docs audit for docs-4381-a1 found nothing to correct and made no edits. **Scope:** base 0326b144af36 to head c25b0eefc00a on `write-up-checklist`: two commits touching 3 committed Markdown files (ETHOS.md, captain/templates/READY.md, changelog.d/write-up-checklist.md). Nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. Also checked docs that reference these files: crew/docs/captain.md (READY contract section), captain/templates/CREW.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md and NOTICE.md (ETHOS anchors), README.md (ETHOS link), CLAUDE.md and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md (ETHOS edit policy). The repo keeps no banned-terms list. ``` Documentation health: ETHOS.md Current (new section 8 write-up checklist; section numbering and existing #8-explain-the-number / #9-earn-its-place anchors intact) captain/templates/READY.md Current (new sourcing paragraph; link ../../ETHOS.md#write-up-checklist resolves; the Unverified: line it cites exists) changelog.d/write-up-checklist.md Current (fragment matches the diff; not edited by this audit) crew/docs/captain.md Current (READY contract unaffected: no new required line, check or receipt) README.md Current (Builder Ethos row still links ETHOS.md) CHANGELOG.md Current (latest entry 1.99.5.0 matches VERSION) TODOS.md Skipped (out of scope for this audit) ``` **Coverage:** ``` Documentation coverage: [entity] [reference] [how-to] [tutorial] [explanation] Write-up checklist (ETHOS 8) ✅ ETHOS.md ✅ ETHOS.md (numbered steps) ❌ ✅ ETHOS.md READY sourcing rule ✅ captain/templates/READY.md ❌ ❌ ✅ via ETHOS link ``` ### Documentation Debt - ⚠️ READY sourcing rule: only the template states it. The summary of the READY contract in crew/docs/captain.md doesn't mention it (a reference gap). Not filled here because adding a rule to that doc is a narrative change for the author. **Diagram drift:** none. No diagrams reference the changed files.
Agent notes **What changed.** `ETHOS.md` section 8 (Explain the Number) gains a `### Write-up checklist` subsection (anchor `#write-up-checklist`, so a later second-reader skill can defer to item 3 for the cold read) and two anti-patterns. `captain/templates/READY.md` gains one paragraph: every number, "green" and "ready" in the block names its source and is read at the pinned head, and anything carried over goes under `Unverified:`. Plus a changelog fragment. No SKILL template changed, so no generated file moved (`bun run gen:skill-docs` left the tree clean). **Why ETHOS and not the shared preamble.** Section 8 already holds the write-up rules (takeaways first), and the shared every-host preamble is owned by other work. This PR is separate from the guides PR (#4380) because ETHOS and the captain templates are text agents load, so it keeps full CI. **Evidence, in general terms.** In our own agent teams: several readers of one post repeated a parity claim its linked page didn't make, and a draft said "as good as" where the page showed the other model ahead; and in two weeks agents corrected their own reports dozens of times, about a third of them retracting a number from a stale tree or a capped list. These figures come from our internal notes and were not re-checked for this PR. A separate claim, that several agents reported ready while the screen was red, was not checked by anyone and is not relied on here. **Why add it, and how we'll know (ETHOS 9, Earn Its Place).** Stated reason above. title: Load the never-print-secrets rule in every skill on every host, with the commands it missed (GST-2753)
body:
Every gstack skill, on every host, now tells the agent never to print a whole environment, git config or process table, and how to read the one value it needs instead.

Why: in our own agent teams, tokens leaked through exactly these commands, and the old rule loaded only in the Capy wrapper and missed `git config --list` and process listings.
Nothing to do: the next `./setup` or upgrade picks it up.

<details><summary>Summary, why and blast radius</summary>

## Summary

A new Ground Rules section in the shared preamble lists the commands that print a whole environment, git config or process table, with the safe form for each. It also says to wait on CI with one `gstack-pr-wait` call instead of a poll loop or `gh pr checks --watch`.

## Why

Run tokens leaked through these commands in real agent sessions. The old rule lived only in the Capy wrapper, so other hosts never saw it.

## Blast radius

Prompt text only. Every skill that loads the shared preamble gets about 600 more bytes. Seven skills with no shared preamble (careful, cso, deslop-shared-libs, freeze, gstack-upgrade, guard, unfreeze) are unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation audit</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed, because the branch already updated the affected doc.

**Scope:** The audit covered base 0326b144 to head 15d80aca on `never-print-secrets-shared-rule`, plus the unstaged change to `changelog.d/never-print-secrets-shared-rule.md`. The change adds a pinned shared-preamble piece, `ground-rules`, generated by `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts`. It tells every skill never to print a whole environment, git config or process table, and to wait on CI with one `gstack-pr-wait` call. The rest of the diff is the regenerated SKILL.md and preamble outputs, plus updated size guards and budgets.

**Documentation health**
- `docs/loadouts.md`: current. Its Pinned row and its Lite on Claude Opus 5.5 section name the Ground Rules, which matches `modules/loadouts.json` and `PREAMBLE_PIECES`.
- `changelog.d/never-print-secrets-shared-rule.md`: current. It is accurate against the generator and against `gstack-pr-wait --help`. I reviewed it but did not edit it, because changelog edits belong to the parent.
- `docs/capy-install.md`, `docs/state-root.md`, `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md` and `capy/skill/gstack/lane-card.md`: current. They agree with the new rule.
- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`: no change needed.

**Coverage debt:** The Ground Rules piece has reference coverage in docs/loadouts.md and explanation coverage in its generator docstring and the changelog fragment. It has no how-to or tutorial, which is acceptable for a guardrail rule. There are no critical gaps.

**Diagram drift:** None. No architecture diagram names preamble pieces.

</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

**Where the rule lives.** A new preamble piece, `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts`, renders a `## Ground Rules` section at every tier (`minTier: 1`). Tier 1 skills carry it inline; tier 2+ skills get it in the shared `sections/preamble.md` that `preamble-hoist.ts` writes for every host. `gen:skill-docs --host all` renders it for Claude Code, Codex, Factory, Kiro, OpenCode and the other hosts, so this is the one place every host loads. ETHOS.md is only pointed at, never loaded, so it was not the home. The piece is pinned in `modules/loadouts.json` so no model loadout drops it, and `docs/loadouts.md` lists it with the other pinned pieces.

**What it bans.** `env`; bare `printenv`, `set` and `export`, and an `export $(...)` that expands to a bare `export`; `export -p`/`-n`; `declare -p`/`-x`; `typeset -p`; `set -x`; `git config --list`/`-l` (it can print a proxy login header); any `ps` with full args (`ps aux`, `ps -ef`, `ps -o args`); `docker top ... args` and `docker inspect`'s Env block. The safe form: `git config --get <name>`, `[ -n "${NAME:-}" ] && echo set` for a variable, processes by name or pid. `printenv NAME` is not taught as the safe form: `test/launch-env-echo-ratchet.test.ts` bans `printenv` with a name in every skill fence, and printing a named secret still prints it.

**CI waits.** One line: wait on CI with one `gstack-pr-wait <n> --until green` call, never a poll loop or `gh pr checks --watch`. The first draft recommended `gh pr checks --watch`; review pointed out that it spends the shared GitHub GraphQL quota gstack moved off (GST-1713), so it now names gstack's REST-based watcher.

**Left alone.** The Capy wrapper's launch-file sentence (`capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md`) keeps its own short ban, because it loads before any workflow and explains the `export $(...)` trap specific to the launch file.

**Size guards.** +614 bytes per skill (+544 at b681106, +70 from the review fixes). Raised to measured, each with a comment: eight parity ratio caps and two tier 1 skeleton caps in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`, the runaway-stopper eager ceiling in `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` (that one value only; a full recapture would have moved 38 unrelated ceilings), and a /ship size-ledger entry. Ship goldens refreshed.

**Evidence and measurement.** A safety guard, so no eval is owed. Evidence of the leaks stays private. `test/ground-rules.test.ts` pins the byte budget, every banned command, the safe forms, the render in a tier 1 skill and the shared preamble, and the loadout pin.

**Checks run locally.** At 15d80ac: 148 focused tests (ground rules, parity, context budget, size ledger, host config, size guards, catalog budget), 0 fail; typecheck clean. At b681106: `bun run typecheck` clean; 1,023 tests across the parity suite, size guards, context budget, preamble compose and hoist, loadouts, launch-env ratchet, carve guards, generator, host config and conformance, agents digest and prose lint: 0 fail.

**Plan.** Plan: exempt: Garry-approved safety guard (A1), no plan review

**Paid coverage.** Paid coverage of the preamble change is left to the release gate; no paid evals at PR tier

**Review fixes.** Pass 1 red-team findings p1/red-team#1 (the CI-wait bullet named the GraphQL-spending watcher) and p1/red-team#2 (the banned list missed `ps aux`/`-ef`, `set -x`, `git config -l` and an empty `export $(...)`) were fixed in 15d80ac. The release note was narrowed to skills that load the shared preamble in c204cca.

**Review notes.**

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts:16` The CI-wait rule names gstack-pr-wait by its bare name; a standard install does not put gstack's bin/ on PATH, so the host-resolved path (~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-pr-wait, as land-and-deploy uses) would be more reliable.
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts:16` CI-wait rule names gstack-pr-wait bare; a standard install does not put gstack's bin/ on PATH (same as fix-check note).
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts:16` gstack-pr-wait blocks up to 60 minutes; the rule does not say to run it in the background or with a --timeout sized to the host shell limit, so a foreground run gets killed and rerun.
- INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/never-print-secrets-shared-rule.md:1` Changelog says every skill on every host; seven skills with no shared preamble (careful, cso, deslop-shared-libs, freeze, gstack-upgrade, guard, unfreeze) do not carry Ground Rules.

</details>

title: Ask each question once and check every handed-over file, in every skill that loads the shared preamble (GST-2756)
body:
Every skill that loads the shared preamble, on every host, now tells the agent to ask a question once and carry it as one waiting line, and to open every file it hands over and remove placeholders first.
Why: in our own agent teams, about a third of the questions agents sent their owner were repeats, and owners kept asking agents to check handed-over files for placeholders.

Nothing to do: the next `./setup` or upgrade picks it up.

## What changed

Before: the shared `## Ground Rules` section had two lines, one banning commands that print a whole environment and one about waiting on CI. After: it has two more. One says to ask each question once, after checking what you can yourself, and to list an unanswered question as one waiting line in later updates instead of asking again. The other says to open every file you hand over and remove placeholders first: TODO, `<fill in>`, lorem ipsum, broken links and images. The Capy factory page's item 11 now points at this shared rule instead of restating it.

## Why

Agents kept asking their owner the same question again and handing over files with placeholders still in them. The rule against repeat questions lived only on the Capy factory page, so skills on other hosts never saw it. Putting both habits in the shared preamble means every skill that loads it gets them.

## Blast radius

The change is prompt text only, made of two strings in `scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ground-rules.ts`, the regenerated SKILL.md and preamble copies, and size limits raised to the measured sizes. No runtime code changed. Skills that don't load the shared preamble (cso, careful, freeze, guard, unfreeze, gstack-upgrade, deslop-shared-libs) are unaffected. CI's free suite passed at this head (run 44074612324, 1,678 test files), and so did windows-smoke (run 44074612295).

<details><summary>Summary, documentation, tests and review</summary>

## Summary

Two Ground Rules lines join the shared preamble, raising its size limit from 850 to 900 bytes. The factory page's item 11 points at the shared rule, and `docs/loadouts.md` now lists all four Ground Rules. The changelog fragment says the rules reach every skill that loads the shared preamble. The per-skill size guards in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` were raised to the measured sizes, with a size-ledger entry, and the verify context-budget pin in `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` was raised to its measured 2922 after main's verify/SKILL.md grew.

title: Make /eval-plan check judges, zeros, failure counts and decisions before results count (GST-2754)
body:
`/eval-plan` now runs four checks before a result counts: a model judge has to agree with hand labels, a zero has to come from a counter that was shown to find a planted case, a failure count has to sit beside the answer-only count, and the plan has to say what each result changes before any money is spent. Why: in our own agent teams, a counter that never fired reported zero, and a reported rise in failures disappeared once the grader's own rule counted it. Nothing to do: preregistrations frozen before 2026-11-15 keep the rules they were frozen under.

title: gstack-runaway prices each wake and marks it cold or warm (GST-2770)
body:
`gstack-runaway` now says what a thread's quiet and wasted wakes cost, not just how many there were: each wake is marked cold or warm and priced, and the scan reports cold starts' and empty wakes' share of spend. Why: most of a busy coordinating agent's spend goes on wakes after the 5-minute prompt cache lapsed, and nothing showed that without a hand count. Nothing to do: the tool stays read-only, and no threshold changed.
Agent notes **What changed** - `lib/runaway.ts`: `wakes()` returns one record per wake (start, idle seconds, cold, calls, cold calls, empty, cost in warm calls). A cold call costs `COLD_CALL_PRICE` = 19.4 warm calls (Opus 5.5, measured 2026-11-08: $2.42 against $0.125 per million counted tokens). A wake is cold when it starts more than `CACHE_TTL_S` (300 s) after the thread's previous model call; any later call issued more than 300 s after the model call before it (the call after a long tool) is also priced cold, and a cold wake's first call is counted once. More than 300 s idle before a call inside a turn, less that call's own run time, starts a new wake (platform wakes leave no transcript item). - The RUNAWAY line adds `wakes cold_wakes empty_wakes cold_extra_spend empty_spend`; the empty-wake WARN adds the empty wakes' share of spend; `scan --wakes` prints a WAKE line per wake. - Behavior change: a `message_agent` send to another thread (it names a non-null `to`) is action even with state "working". Before, it counted as an empty wake, which put coordinating threads' empty share 4 to 12 points high. A report to the parent with an explicit `"to": null` stays a report. - `/runaway-stopper` fetch keeps each message's target (with a fallback on the item's target text when the input is cut short) and each call's run time. Its context-budget ceiling alone moves 3841 → 4328 (fresh capture value). **Measure: priced meter against the 2026-11-08 hand count**, four coordinating agent threads, 2026-11-03T20:45Z to 2026-11-08T14:01:54Z, read-only transcripts: | Thread | Wakes (meter/hand) | Cold share | Empty share | Old counter's empty share | Cold extra, % of spend | Empty wakes, % of spend | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | A | 828 / 821 | 40.0% / 41.0% | 34.9% / 34.1% | 46.1% | 76.5% / 75.2% | 22.4% / 22.0% | | B | 888 / 864 | 38.5% / 38.1% | 36.7% / 36.3% | 46.1% | 76.8% / 75.2% | 29.5% / 30.1% | | C | 1219 / 1189 | 21.2% / 21.6% | 41.8% / 43.1% | 52.8% | 63.5% / 60.9% | 21.7% / 21.7% | | D | 945 / 944 | 38.9% / 38.0% | 29.7% / 30.9% | 35.0% | 72.6% / 71.1% | 20.0% / 20.4% | Recounted with the meter as shipped at 97aa5e6; cold and empty shares within 1.3 points of the hand count. Residual: the hand count's own turn-splitting script isn't readable from here, so the last points are unexplained, not fixed. The hand count's spend shares were themselves modelled from the same ratio. **Checks run locally:** `bun test test/runaway.test.ts` (24 pass, 140 expect calls; the two changed tests fail on the pre-fix code), typecheck, test-typecheck ratchet, module-size ratchet, gen-skill-docs freshness, parity suite, context-budget ratchet, host-config goldens and the skill-size guards. **Plan:** lean /autoplan, one reviewer: 1 High (a wrong "9 to 12" figure, corrected to 4 to 12), 3 Medium and 4 Low, all fixed or documented; gate answered `rec`. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-8a52294c3a83). The full approval record stays private. Plan: approved (record r-787b1ecf5c01) Plan check: approved (record r-787b1ecf5c01) ## Pre-Landing Review Pass 1 at 1dc33b7 (full panel: batched testing/security/state-machines specialist, red-team, targeted money reader, Claude adversarial pass, second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol): 10 findings, 3 marked blocking by the second-model review, 0 by the others; the targeted money reader found nothing. One fix round (7c57510) fixed 4: a `"to": null` report counted as a send, cache expiry after a long tool charged to the wrong call, and a cold wake's first call counted twice. Pass 2 on the fix range (specialist, red-team, targeted money reader): 0 blocking, 2 notes. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=3 deferred=0 noted=6 fixed=4 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 dispatches=5 est_input_tokens=21036 Gate edits: none detected (5 listed, 3 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol): FINDINGS, 3 marked blocking; 2 fixed, 1 left open below. **Open note:** `lib/runaway.ts:81` sums the run times of an `execute` program's parallel calls, so overlapping calls can overstate run time and understate idle time (second-model review finding 2, also adversarial note 2). Left unfixed after the second round; the recount above at 97aa5e6 shows the published shares hold with it in place. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:123` a sleep inside an execute program past 300 s splits one turn and can add an empty wake - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:81` summing parallel call durations can push idle below zero and hide idle time - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:118` two inbound messages with no tool call between them share the first one's start and warm flag - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:78` the cut-short send fallback rests on an unconfirmed transcript text field for reports to the parent - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:78` the cut-short fallback in addressed() and its template copy can count a long report to the parent as a send - INFORMATIONAL `lib/runaway.ts:296` gstack-runaway --help still says a wake is cold after the thread's previous item; the code now measures from the previous model call ## Exploratory QA One functional probe on `bin/gstack-runaway scan --wakes` with a synthetic two-wake fixture: a wake after 600 s quiet reads `cache=cold cold_calls=1 cost=20.4` and the RUNAWAY line carries the wake and spend shares. Verdict: pass (1 capture). ## Documentation **Status:** updated, with one factual correction to `docs/skills.md` and no blockers. **Scope:** `18652ccc..7c57510` on `price-runaway-wakes` (4 commits, 7 files: `lib/runaway.ts`, `test/runaway.test.ts`, `runaway-stopper/SKILL.md(.tmpl)`, `docs/skills.md`, `changelog.d/price-runaway-wakes.md`, `test/fixtures/context-budget.json`). There were no uncommitted or new files. **Documentation health:** - `docs/skills.md`: Updated. `cold_extra_spend` and `empty_spend` are now described as shares of spend, and `cold_extra_spend` now includes calls made after a tool that ran past 5 minutes. - `runaway-stopper/SKILL.md.tmpl`: Current. It says only cold starts count toward `cold_extra_spend`. That is close enough, so I left it unedited. - `changelog.d/price-runaway-wakes.md`: Current. It matches the code and was not edited. - `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`: Current. The skill list is unchanged. **Coverage debt:** The new `scan --wakes` flag and the `WAKE:` line have reference coverage in `docs/skills.md`, the skill template and the CLI usage text, but no how-to example. `COLD_CALL_PRICE` is documented only in a code comment and the changelog. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Test plan - [x] `bun run test`: free suite at 97aa5e6 from CI run 44058599585 (1672 files); macOS named regressions from the same run, Windows smoke from run 44049762314.

title: TypeScript hooks start under a Windows home with an apostrophe, or with MSYS path conversion off
body:
## TypeScript hooks start under a Windows home with an apostrophe, or with MSYS path conversion off

### Root cause

Git Bash rewrites a `/c/x` argument to `C:/x` when it starts a native program. msys2-runtime skips that rewrite for any argument that contains `` ` `` `'` `*` `?` `[` `]` ([`winsup/cygwin/msys2_path_conv.cc`](https://github.com/msys2/msys2-runtime/blob/msys2-3.6.12/winsup/cygwin/msys2_path_conv.cc#L368-L375)). It skips every argument when `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*` is set.

Each TypeScript hook shim builds `HERE` with `pwd`, which gives `/c/x`, and runs `bun "$HERE/<hook>.ts"`. bun.exe cannot open `/c/x`: it reports `Module not found`, and `Bun.build` throws `EINVAL: failed to open root directory`. `gstack-hook-check` hands Bun its entries in the same `/c/x` spelling.

So under a home such as `C:\Users\O'Brien`:
- All 13 shims die before their entry runs. The `/autoplan` Read barrier returns its "Publication hook unavailable" deny on every Read.
- `gstack-hook-check` reports all 12 registered TypeScript hooks as `bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry`, so setup's hook-registration gate would refuse them (inferred from that gate's own tests; `./setup` itself was not run under an apostrophe home).

### Who is affected

Git Bash or MSYS2 users on Windows are affected in two cases:
- **The gstack path contains `'`, `` ` ``, `[`, `]` or `;`.** I tested each character by passing `/c/a<char>b/x` to bun.exe. Spaces, `( ) & # ! $ % @ { } = + ^ , ~ "` and the rest were all rewritten. Windows file names cannot contain `*` or `?`.
- **Path conversion is turned off** with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*`, which Docker users often set. This breaks every path, apostrophe or not: the unfixed checker failed all 12 hooks on a plain `C:\gsp-ctl` root.

Cygwin never rewrites arguments, so I expect it to fail on every path. I have not tested it.

### Fix

The fix is one mechanism, placed where each path is created:
- **Shims:** after `HERE` is set, each shim converts it with `cygpath -m`:
  ```sh
  case "${OSTYPE:-}" in msys*|cygwin*) if command -v cygpath >/dev/null 2>&1; then HERE="$(cygpath -m "$HERE")"; fi ;; esac
  ```
  This runs under the same `OSTYPE`/`cygpath` test that already sets `GSTACK_BUN_CONFIG`. It does nothing off a Windows bash or when `cygpath` is missing. `phase-publication-hook` uses the same line with its `_AUTOPLAN_HOOK_DIR`.
- **`bin/gstack-hook-check`:** passes `BUN_ENTRIES=$(cygpath -m $ENTRIES)` to Bun under the same test. `shellPath` already maps Bun's `C:/x` output back to the `/c/x` keys the checker looks up.

The line is written into each shim rather than kept in a shared helper. This follows `GSTACK_BUN_CONFIG`, which is also one fixed line per shim, and keeps hook-check self-contained so it can still check an extracted archive. Calling a helper would add a `uname` plus a `cygpath` process to every hook run, and these shims run on every prompt and tool call. The inline line adds a single `cygpath` (about 25 ms), and only on Windows.

`AGENTS.md` states the rule for new shims.

### Tests (`test/setup-hook-syntax-gate.test.ts`, already in the Windows lane)

- **`entries bundle in a root Git Bash does not convert`:** runs hook-check on a fixture root named `hook root o'brien`. On Windows it runs both as-is and with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`. On POSIX it runs in a simulated Windows bash: `OSTYPE=msys`, a fake `cygpath`, and a fake `bun` that rejects the unconverted spelling the way bun.exe does.
- **`every shim that runs TypeScript starts its entry …`:** copies every hook shim that runs a TypeScript entry into that root, 13 today (the registered ones plus `memorable-user-prompt-hook`). Each entry is replaced by a stub, and each shim must exit 0 and print `entry ran`. It uses the same real-or-simulated environment.

The space in the fixture root is needed on Windows. It makes Bun quote the path when it starts bash; without quotes, MSYS reads a bare `'` in its command line as a quote character (see "Not fixed here").

| run | without fix | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11, Git Bash, bun 1.4.4-canary, whole file, `--timeout 120000` | 15 pass, 5 fail | 17 pass, 3 fail |
| Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu), bun 1.4.4, whole file | 20 pass, 2 fail (the new tests) | 22 pass, 0 fail |

On Windows the two new tests are the only difference between the runs. The other 3 failures happen with and without the fix: the test harness writes `BUN_CMD='<bun path>'` in single quotes, and on the test machine the bun path itself contains an apostrophe. On Linux, the shell-caller ratchet in `test/bun-entry-isolation.test.ts` (run with `-t "shell callers|detector|config-definition"`) passes 4/4; the whole file gives 7 pass, 3 fail on the partial tree used here, identically with and without the fix, and `test/ceo-mode-handoff-hook.test.ts` (which runs the real shim) passes 4/4.

<details><summary>Before/after on a real install under a home with an apostrophe (Windows 11, Git Bash)</summary>

The test tree is gstack v1.91.101.0 with the upstream 0326b14 hook subsystem copied over it: setup, the 13 shims, the hook-check, and every TypeScript entry with its local imports. `<root>` stands for `/c/Users/<me>'/…/root`.

Upstream `bin/gstack-hook-check <root>` exits 1:
```
ok bin/gstack-session-update
fail hosts/claude/hooks/question-log-hook <root>/hosts/claude/hooks/question-log-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook <root>/…/question-preference-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/auq-error-fallback-hook <root>/…/auq-error-fallback-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook <root>/…/timeline-stop-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook <root>/…/skill-route-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/skill-contract-stop-hook <root>/…/skill-contract-stop-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/ceo-review-gate-stop <root>/…/ceo-review-gate.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/ceo-review-gate-subagent-stop <root>/…/ceo-review-gate.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/autoplan-stop-gate-stop <root>/…/autoplan-stop-gate.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail hosts/claude/hooks/autoplan-stop-gate-publish <root>/…/autoplan-stop-gate.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
fail autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook <root>/autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
ok careful/bin/check-careful.sh
ok freeze/bin/check-freeze.sh
fail plan-ceo-review/bin/mode-handoff-hook <root>/plan-ceo-review/bin/mode-handoff-hook.ts:1: bun could not bundle the TypeScript entry
```
The same bytes reached through a junction with no apostrophe (`C:\gsp-ctl`) give 15 `ok` and exit 0.

With the fix, the checker prints 15 `ok`, 0 `fail`, and exits 0. It does the same with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` and with `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*`. A TypeScript syntax error planted under that root is still caught: `fail plan-ceo-review/bin/mode-handoff-hook <root>/…/mode-handoff-hook.ts:35: Unexpected ;`.

Each shim was run through `/bin/sh -c '<root>/<shim>'` with hook JSON on stdin:
```
SHIM                                           BEFORE                                         AFTER
plan-ceo-review/bin/mode-handoff-hook          1  Module not found ".../mode-handoff-hook.ts"  0  {"systemMessage":"Auto-decided review mode → HOLD SCOPE (your preference). …"}
hosts/claude/hooks/question-log-hook           1  Module not found                             0
autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook            1  deny "Publication hook unavailable"           0  the .ts's own decision (identical through the no-apostrophe junction)
hosts/claude/hooks/auq-error-fallback-hook     1  Module not found                             0  {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PostToolUse"}}
hosts/claude/hooks/question-preference-hook    1  Module not found                             0
timeline-stop, memorable-user-prompt, skill-route, skill-contract-stop,
ceo-review-gate-stop, ceo-review-gate-subagent-stop,
autoplan-stop-gate-stop, autoplan-stop-gate-publish   0  Module not found (fail-open)  0  no error
```
After the fix, every row at the apostrophe root matches the same run through the junction.

Off Windows, the line does nothing. With `HERE=/home/o'brien/.claude/skills/gstack/plan-ceo-review/bin`, `HERE` is unchanged under `OSTYPE=linux-gnu` or `darwin23`, with or without `cygpath` on PATH, and under `OSTYPE=msys` or `cygwin` with no `cygpath`. It becomes `C:/…` only under `msys` or `cygwin` with `cygpath` present.
</details>

### Not fixed here (found while proving this)

1. **bun → bash argument passing.** When Bun starts a bash script through `lib/script-invocation.ts` (`runScriptSync`), the MSYS runtime parses bash's Windows command line and treats a bare `'` as a quote. Node and Bun only add quotes around an argument that has a space or a `"`. So `C:/Users/O'Brien/…/bin/gstack-question-log` plus its JSON argument reach bash as a single word, minus the apostrophe, and bash exits 127. With this fix, `question-log-hook` now runs, but this spawn still fails. `timeline-stop-hook` (`gstack-slug: exit 127`) and `memorable-user-prompt-hook` (`gstack-config get … failed`) fail at their own spawns, which looks like the same bug but I have not traced them.
2. **Shell bins that hand Bun a path.** Examples: `GSTACK_LIB_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib" bun -e …`, `bun "$BIN/…ts"`, and `bun run gen:skill-docs --out-dir "$RENDER_TMP"`. MSYS leaves environment values with an apostrophe unconverted too. Native Bun then resolves `/c/Users/O'Brien/x` as `C:\c\Users\O'Brien\x`. On the test machine, 406 files (skill renders `render/claude.tmp.<pid>` and `.brain-sync-status.json`) sit in `C:\c\Users\<me>'\.gstack`, which is where native Bun resolves `/c/Users/<me>'/.gstack`. They were all written before these test runs.
3. **Bun-shebang bins run by absolute path,** for example `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-decision-log --help`, fail with `Module not found "/c/Users/…"`. Running the same bin from its directory (`./gstack-decision-log`) works.
4. **`setup`'s own `bun "$SOURCE_GSTACK_DIR/…"` calls** pass the same `/c/x` paths. I have not run `setup` under such a home.

Each of these needs its own change, and items 1 and 3 need changes outside the shims.

### Not verified

- The full test suite: the network only allowed fetching single files through the GitHub API, so every run used a partial upstream tree of 162 files.
- macOS: the simulated-bash tests call `realpath` on their root because macOS `/var` is `/private/var`, but they have not run there.
- Cygwin.

title: Say when to use each gstack skill in Claude Code's skill list (GST-2774)
body:
Claude Code's skill list now says when to use each gstack skill, so Opus 5.5 loads /review on "review my changes" and /plan-eng-review on "plan this feature".
Before, each Claude Code description was cut to its first sentence, which said what a skill is but rarely when to load it; in a test, /review loaded 0 of 3 times and no planning skill loaded in 9 tries.
Nothing to do: the next `./setup` or upgrade picks it up. The list Claude Code loads every session grows by about 840 tokens.

<details><summary>Why, summary and blast radius</summary>

## Why

"Review my changes before I land them" loaded /review 0 of 3 times, because its Claude Code line read "Use when you review this PR's diff." and nothing said a local diff counts. Each line now ends with when to use the skill, so Opus 5.5 picks /review and /plan-eng-review on the plain requests people actually type.

## Summary

Claude Code reads one short line per skill to decide what to load, and gstack cut that line to the first sentence. Most first sentences say what a skill is, not when to use it, so plain requests slipped past /review and /plan-eng-review. The generator now appends a short when-to-use clause from each skill's own trigger phrases, /review and /plan-eng-review got first sentences that match how people ask, and the root router got a real description. "deploy this" left /ship's trigger list because deploying belongs to /land-and-deploy. Router lines for harnesses that reuse the Claude Code render (dots and the generic context block) still get the full 160-character trigger list instead of the shorter clause.

## Blast radius

Every generated Claude Code SKILL.md description changes, and the other hosts and `--catalog-mode=full` do not. That is safe because the generator check passes with every tracked output fresh, all 63 Claude descriptions parse as YAML under the 260-byte cap (script ran), and the catalog, trim, trigger and harness tests pass.

</details>

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

## What changed

- Each trimmed Claude Code description keeps a when-to-use clause of at most 64 characters after its first sentence: the skill's own `triggers:` list ("Use for: review my changes, look over my diff, review this pr."), or its "Use when" sentence when it has no list. A first sentence that already fills the line gets no clause.
- /review's first sentence no longer assumes a PR exists: "Use when you review a diff before it lands: local changes, a branch or a PR." Its full description is also shorter than before.
- /plan-eng-review says it plans a feature before you build it and gains a "plan a feature" trigger. Its full description is shorter than before, and its body is unchanged.
- The `gstack` router's line says what it does instead of "Router for the gstack skill suite."
- /ship's trigger list drops "deploy this", which belongs to /land-and-deploy; "push to main" stays.
- Harness router lines (dots, generic) keep using the full trigger list when the description's only trigger sentence is the new short clause, so those targets don't lose trigger phrases.
- `--catalog-mode=full` and the other hosts are unchanged. /autoplan's line ("Auto-review pipeline ...") still describes reviewing an existing plan, so it doesn't compete with /plan-eng-review.

Before and after, /review's Claude Code line:

```text
before: Use when you review this PR's diff. (gstack)
after:  Use when you review a diff before it lands: local changes, a branch or a PR. Use for: review my changes, look over my diff, review this pr. (gstack)
```

</details>

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

Opus 5.5 in Claude Code 2.1.312 at effort high, gstack from this branch installed with `./setup --host claude --no-browser`, 28 preregistered trials (3 per prompt, 1 per task), every trial reported:

| Prompt | Skill loaded (this branch) | Before (0326b14) |
|---|---|---|
| Review my changes before I land them | review 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 (built-in code-review once) |
| Plan this feature before we build it | plan-eng-review 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |
| Is this worth building? | office-hours 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| Run the checks and make it green | verify 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| Test the CLI and HTTP server, fix bugs | qa 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| Security audit before going live | cso 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
| 10 Terminal-Bench tasks no skill fits | none loaded, 0 of 10 | 0 of 10 |

Model spend for the run was $4.50. The run used the first commit (a52a2ac). Since then the only Claude Code line that changed is /ship's, which dropped "deploy this"; no trial prompt asks to ship or deploy.

</details>

<details><summary>Budgets</summary>

The catalog ceiling in `test/catalog-budget.test.ts` moves from 1,452 to 2,290 token-equivalents (measured 9,160 bytes), and 14 carved skills' skeleton and size-ratio caps in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` move to their measured sizes (each grew by its new description, 8 to 106 bytes). /ship's union size is recorded in its size ledger, the context-budget fixture is refreshed, and the per-host size pins for /review and /plan-eng-review go down. `/gstack-upgrade` sat 7 bytes under its 1.5x size budget, so its body drops a line that repeated its description.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

## Documentation
**Status:** current. The docs already match the branch, so no edits were made.

**Scope:** the committed diff 18652ccc..fdd9b44fd (83 files: the when-to-use clause in Claude Code's trimmed skill list, rewordings of the /review, /plan-eng-review and gstack router descriptions, and the catalog budget raised to 2,290). There was no staged, unstaged or new content.

**Documentation health:**
- CLAUDE.md: Current (the catalog budget of 2,290 matches the test)
- CONTRIBUTING.md: Current (the catalog-budget entry says 2,290)
- docs/voice-input.md: Current (it describes the when-to-use clause and the --catalog-mode=full exception)
- docs/proactive.md: Current
- docs/skills.md: Current
- docs/hosts.md: Current
- changelog.d/claude-skill-descriptions-say-when-to-use.md: Read only (it matches the diff)

**Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

<details><summary>Test plan</summary>

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/catalog-trim.test.ts`: 29 pass, 0 fail (the buildTrimmedDescription cases were written first and failed before the generator change)
- [x] `bun test test/skill-triggers.test.ts`: 9 pass, 0 fail (the new router-line case failed before its fix)
- [x] `bun run typecheck`: 0 errors
- [x] `bun run scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts --host all --dry-run`: every tracked output fresh
- [x] catalog-budget, skill-descriptions, catalog-mode-full, parity-suite, carve-guard-completeness, skill-size-budget, skill-md-size-guard, context-budget-ratchet, instruction-facts, shared-libs-rendering, proactive-core-set, host-config, gen-skill-docs, harness-register: pass
- [ ] `bun run test` (full free suite): runs in CI at the pushed head

</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

## Agent notes

Issue GST-2774. Diagnosis: GSTA-558 (Captain drive reports/GSTA-558.md). Acceptance preregistration, runner and every trial: Captain drive handoffs/GSTA-559/.

## Approvals

Plan check: exempt bug fix

### Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 8 issues — 2 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred; the other 6 are the advisory notes listed below

Gate edits: none detected (25 listed, 22 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=1 fixed=2 scope=frozen ledgers_read=4 fix_checks=1 dispatches=2 est_input_tokens=71270

Review depth full (63 runtime lines): batched specialist (testing, security, state-machines), Red Team, one fix-check (clean), native adversarial and outside voice (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, clean). Fixed: CONTRIBUTING.md said 2,294 instead of 2,290; dots/generic router lines took the 64-char clause instead of the full trigger list.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `docs/proactive.md:9` Non-core Claude catalog lines now carry trigger clauses, which docs/proactive.md's core-default rationale says they should not.
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts:370` buildTrimmedDescription caps by UTF-16 chars (230) while catalog-budget caps name+description at 260 bytes; multibyte leads could overflow; CI catches it.
- INFORMATIONAL `plan-eng-review/SKILL.md.tmpl:7` Hermes withTriggerLead drops the 'Use when...' first sentence that also carries what /plan-eng-review does.
- INFORMATIONAL `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl:7` /ship prose still says 'deploy this' while its triggers list dropped it; /land-and-deploy never gained it; hosts route it differently. Needs a routing decision.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-triggers.ts:68` routerLine cannot tell an authored 'Use for:' sentence from the generated clause; latent, no template has one.
- INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/claude-skill-descriptions-say-when-to-use.md:1` Changelog trial numbers have no raw run data in the repo; link the run ids in agent notes.
- Low `scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts:370` The clause cap counts characters while catalog-budget caps bytes; a multibyte lead could pass the generator and fail the test (CI catches it).
- Low `plan-eng-review/SKILL.md.tmpl:7` Hermes's trigger-first lead drops the "Use when..." sentence that also says what /plan-eng-review does.
- Low `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` /ship's description prose still says "deploy this" after its trigger list dropped it; /land-and-deploy has no such trigger. Needs a routing decision.
- Low `lib/skill-triggers.ts:68` routerLine can't tell an authored "Use for:" sentence from the generated clause (no template has one today).
- Low `changelog.d/claude-skill-descriptions-say-when-to-use.md` The trial numbers come from the run records under handoffs/GSTA-559/, not from this repository.

### Exploratory QA

Smoke and revalidation passed: generator dry-run fresh for every tracked file, 63 Claude frontmatters parse as YAML under the 260-byte cap, and the 5 descriptions without "(gstack)" were untagged on main too.

### TODOS

No additions or completions. #2118 (fold triggers into descriptions) is addressed for Claude Code only and stays open for the other hosts.

title: gstack-issue-links names the older commit of each issue mention (#4378)
body:
## Why (in your own words)

/ship's Issue links step lists each issue mention with the commit it came from, so the user can decide whether to promote a `Refs #N` to `Fixes #N`. Any mention outside the newest commit on the branch read `commit :` with an empty id, on stderr and in `--json` sources. The user was not told which commit a candidate came from. git log ends each commit's `--format` output with a newline, so after `split('\0')` every entry except the first starts with `\n` and the hash read as empty. Each entry now drops that one leading newline before the hash is read. The change covers both the `origin/<base>` log and its `<base>` fallback (fixes #4378).

## Live evidence

```
$ git log --format='%h %s' main..HEAD
d74c9a9 tidy again        # message body: Refs #12
46e5f05 tidy              # message body: Refs #11

# before (main 0326b14)
$ bun bin/gstack-issue-links --base main --no-auto-links
Refs #11
Refs #12
  reference #12 ← commit d74c9a9739e2: Refs #12 (promote: fix #12)
  reference #11 ← commit : Refs #11 (promote: fix #11)

# after (this branch)
$ bun bin/gstack-issue-links --base main --no-auto-links
Refs #11
Refs #12
  reference #12 ← commit d74c9a9739e2: Refs #12 (promote: fix #12)
  reference #11 ← commit 46e5f051452d: Refs #11 (promote: fix #11)

$ bun test test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts
 15 pass, 0 fail   # the new two-commit case fails on main: "commit : Refs #11"
$ bun run typecheck && bun run typecheck:test
test typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new.
$ bin/gstack-prose-lint changelog.d/fix-issue-links-older-commit.md --gate
PROSE_LINT: ok files=1
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `bin/gstack-issue-links` (3 lines), a two-commit CLI test in `test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts`, and a changelog fragment.
- **Verified live by:** Running `gstack-issue-links` on a throwaway two-commit repo before and after the change (output above), plus the issue-links test file.
- **Did NOT test:** A full `/ship` run, and the `--json` output; that output carries the same `source` string from the same code path. I did not run the full free suite.

title: gstack-issue-links skips /ship's Review-Finding trailers (#4371)
body:
## Why (in your own words)

/ship commits each review fix with one `Review-Finding: <ledger id> reader=<raised_by>` trailer. A ledger id such as `p1/red-team#3` matches the cross-repo `owner/repo#N` pattern, so `gstack-issue-links` printed `Refs p1/red-team#3` for each one. /ship pastes those lines under `## Issues` in the PR body, where they claim issues in repositories that do not exist. `mentionsIn` now skips `Review-Finding:` trailer lines, and the rest of the commit message is read as before (fixes #4371).

## Live evidence

```
$ git log -1 --format=%B
fix: pre-landing review fixes

Review-Finding: p1/red-team#3 reader=red-team
Review-Finding: p2/adversarial-native#3 reader=codex

# before (main 0326b14)
$ bun bin/gstack-issue-links --base main --no-auto-links
Refs p1/red-team#3
Refs p2/adversarial-native#3
  reference p1/red-team#3 ← commit e135c6ffb64e: Review-Finding: p1/red-team#3 reader=red-team
  reference p2/adversarial-native#3 ← commit e135c6ffb64e: Review-Finding: p2/adversarial-native#3 reader=codex

# after (this branch)
$ bun bin/gstack-issue-links --base main --no-auto-links
ISSUE_LINKS: none

$ bun test test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts test/gstack-ship-receipt.test.ts
 15 pass, 0 fail / 18 pass, 0 fail   # the new trailer case fails on main with both ledger ids
$ bun run typecheck && bun run typecheck:test
test typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new.
$ bin/gstack-prose-lint changelog.d/fix-issue-links-review-finding.md --gate
PROSE_LINT: ok files=1
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `lib/issue-links.ts` (one pattern and one `continue`), a pure test in `test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts` that keeps a real cross-repo reference and a bare `#N` beside the trailers, and a changelog fragment.
- **Verified live by:** Running `gstack-issue-links` on a throwaway repo whose commit carries two Review-Finding trailers, before and after (output above), plus the issue-links and ship-receipt test files.
- **Did NOT test:** A full `/ship` run. Trailers named anything other than `Review-Finding` are still read as before. I did not run the full free suite.

title: Release notes list every change with its pull request instead of "see CHANGELOG.md"
body:
GitHub release pages now list every change a release ships, one plain line each, linked to the pull request that made it, instead of one headline per version or "see CHANGELOG.md". Why: the release page is where people read what changed, and recent releases went out saying only "see CHANGELOG.md". Nothing to do: the next release uses it; a release with no CHANGELOG entry stops with `NOTES_MISSING` instead of publishing a stub.
What changed The old release notes took one sentence per CHANGELOG version, so a release that shipped 38 changes showed one of them, and entries written as bullets showed "see CHANGELOG.md". Each release page now lists every change in the versions it ships, grouped under What's new, Fixes and Changes for maintainers, each linked to its own pull request, then the compare link. Before and after, for the v1.100.0.0 release (rendered from the code at the base commit and on this branch; image unavailable because the version numbers trip the screenshot tool's address scanner): ```text BEFORE ## gstack v1.100.0.0 (regular release) 1 version since v1.99.5.0, one line each. Compare or read the full changelog. - **1.100.0.0** (2026-11-17): Sixteen in-repo documentation links reach their section again. ... AFTER ## gstack v1.100.0.0 ### What's new - Every skill that loads the shared preamble, on every host, now says to ask a question once and to check a file before handing it over. (#4383) - Claude Code's skill list now says when to use each gstack skill, so Opus loads /review and /plan-eng-review when a request fits. (#4387) - ... 38 lines in all, every one linked [Compare v1.99.5.0...v1.100.0.0] · [Full changelog] ``` - Each change links the pull request whose commit added the `changelog.d` fragment holding it, looked up in git history rather than guessed from the wording, and never a later pull request that reused the same file name. Release commits link nothing. - Notes past GitHub's 60,000-character limit keep the changes that fit and end with "N more changes are in the full changelog" instead of refusing. - A `## ` heading inside a fragment no longer cuts off the lines after it, and only parentheses made entirely of issue codes are dropped, so "(SHA-256 of the body)" stays. - A release whose version has no CHANGELOG entry, or an entry with nothing in it, stops with `NOTES_MISSING`; the daily check reports it only when a release is due. - The release harness guide and docs/releases.md describe the new notes.
Why "Releases v1.99.1.0 to v1.99.4.0 said only 'see CHANGELOG.md'." People read the release page, not the changelog, so each release now says what changed and where to read more.
Blast radius Only the stable release workflow (`.github/workflows/weekly-release.yml`, through `crew/scripts/release-cut.ts`) builds these notes; nothing else imports `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts` (read in the diff and `scripts/test-pr-profile.ts`). The links were checked against real history: for v1.100.0.0 the 34 linked pull requests equal, one for one, the pull requests that added each of the 34 fragments that release folded, found independently (script ran).
Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. The one changed file with no changed test naming it, `scripts/test-pr-profile.ts` (one new list entry), is covered by tests that loop over every entry: `test/paid-free-boundary.test.ts:73`, `:145` and `:209`. Coverage: 100% value-weighted (100% including 0 weakly covered paths) Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. Tests ran: release 55 Tests ran: test 1680 (files; 37,504 tests in CI run 44131909907)
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. A full review read the whole diff: a batched testing, security and state-machine review (no findings), an adversarial review, a red-team review, a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol (clean), and the parent checklist. Eight notes below the blocking floor are listed under Review notes and were not fixed in this PR; none produced a wrong pull request link. Two are from the first part of the review: a version whose fragments hold no prose would stop every later release with `NOTES_MISSING` until the CHANGELOG is edited (`crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:202`, not seen in history), and the issue-code stripper also drops parentheses such as "(UTF-8)" (`:114`).
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:190` Notes render each folded fragment as it read when it was folded, so an edit to a released CHANGELOG entry before the release is not published, and an added or removed bullet shifts the version's own-change slice. Not observed across five real release spans, and release commits link nothing for their own changes. - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:45` package.json and bun.lock count as neutral paths, so a dependency security bump with a test lands under Changes for maintainers (#4408 in the real v1.100.0.0 run). - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:114` The issue-code stripper drops (GPT-6), (UTF-8), (SHA-256)-only and (ISO-8601) parentheticals. Same as the core finding at :114. - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `changelog.d/release-notes-list-every-change.md:1` The fragment says v1.99.1.0 to v1.99.4.0 published stub notes; the reader says v1.99.5.0 also ran the old logic. Today's v1.99.5.0 and v1.99.4.0 pages show hand-written notes, so the original stub cannot be confirmed from the live page. - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:74` Lines inside a
block become change lines, and an @mention in a first sentence notifies on release creation. - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `crew/scripts/release-notes.ts:218` The cap loop re-renders per dropped line (quadratic); measured 72 ms for 900 changes in QA capture 003. ## Exploratory QA Functional, report-only, three checks within the five-minute budget, all passing on the reviewed tree: - Real release v1.99.5.0 to v1.100.0.0: notes build with 38 lines, every line linked, 6,488 characters. - The 34 linked pull requests equal the pull requests of the commits that added each fragment the v1.100.0.0 release commit deleted, found with plain `git log`, without the code under test. - 900 synthetic changes: the notes stop at 59,883 characters with "441 more changes are in the full changelog" and the full-changelog link, instead of refusing. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Review bot comments No review bot comments. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN Intent: release pages list every change with its pull request instead of a stub. Delivered: a new notes builder, its tests and docs, and the workflow path and test-profile entries it needs. ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). ## Verification Results No plan verification items (no plan file); the three exploratory checks above pass. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Status:** updated. One stale description of the GitHub release notes was corrected, with no blockers. **Scope:** the 11 committed files from base e0c4136d to head eebe8305 (release-notes.ts split out of release-cut.ts, release notes that list every change, NOTES_MISSING), with no staged, unstaged or new files. Every authored doc that mentions release notes, release-cut.ts or CHANGELOG headlines was audited. **Documentation health:** - `docs/releases.md`: current. The branch's Release notes section, the NOTES_MISSING row, the change-lines dry-run wording and the workflow path list match the code. - `changelog.d/README.md`: current. It links to #release-notes. - `crew/docs/recommended-harness.md`: updated. The stable-release paragraph said the notes carry one line per CHANGELOG version; it now says every change, one line each with its pull request, linked to docs/releases.md#release-notes. - `docs/CHANGELOG_STYLE.md`, `docs/writing-prs.md`, `ship/sections/changelog.md`: current, with nothing affected. **Coverage debt:** none new. docs/releases.md lists sample maintainer paths and fix words rather than the full sets in release-notes.ts. **Diagram drift:** none. ## Tests - [x] `bun test crew/test/release-cut.test.ts crew/test/release-cadence.test.ts test/weekly-release-workflow.test.ts`: 55 pass, 0 fail - [x] `bun run test` (CI free-tests run 44131909907 at f879a5a05a13): 1680 files, 37,504 tests, green - [x] `bun test test/paid-free-boundary.test.ts test/free-fixtures.test.ts`: 20 pass, 0 fail (coverage audit) - [x] `bun run typecheck`: no errors
Agent notes Review rounds: this is the PR's third full review round by hand count (GSTA-562 pass 1 with its fix round, GSTA-563 round 2 at 60b53e0, and this /ship at eebe830), run under the Captain's grant (GStack Minder, GSTA-36) with no fix round. The receipt history in this body counted no earlier round (PR_REVIEW_ROUTE: first), because the earlier rounds left no receipt rows here. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=0 fixed=0 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 dispatches=4 Gate edits: none detected (15 listed, 12 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Second-model review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol, completed, VERDICT: CLEAN. Lead judgment: the six Step 11 adversarial notes and two pass-1 notes were recorded as advisory below the blocking floor (each reader marked them Blocks: no; nothing fails a test, breaks production or loses data, and no wrong link was reproduced); judge kept every reader's stated severity. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch release-notes-list-every-change. title: A line that opens with an inline code span reads as a code fence, so the docs link check refuses valid links and gstack-prose-lint skips half of troubleshooting.md
body: ## What happened On main (0326b14), `unfenced()` in `lib/doc-links.ts` opens a fence on any line that starts with three or more backticks, and closes it on any later line that starts with the same character. `docs/troubleshooting.md:3098` starts with the inline code span ````` ````gstack-ship-receipt```` `````, so the checker reads lines 3098 to 3729 as fenced. The headings and `` anchors there vanish, and the links on those lines are not checked. A docs change that adds a correct link to one of those anchors is refused by `scripts/check-doc-links.ts` and by the docs lane's pregate (`lib/pregate/docs-only-lane.ts` calls the same `brokenLinks`): ``` $ git log -1 --format=%h 0326b14 $ printf '\nSee [Unattended runs and artifacts](troubleshooting.md#unattended-runs-and-artifacts) and [ROUTE_BOUNDED_REFUSED](troubleshooting.md#route-bounded-refused).\n' >> docs/unattended.md $ bun scripts/check-doc-links.ts --base HEAD docs/unattended.md docs/unattended.md:1045: troubleshooting.md#unattended-runs-and-artifacts: no heading or for #unattended-runs-and-artifacts; fix: correct the link or add the heading it names docs/unattended.md:1045: troubleshooting.md#route-bounded-refused: no heading or for #route-bounded-refused; fix: correct the link or add the heading it names DOC_LINKS: broken 2 exit=1 $ grep -n '^## Unattended runs and artifacts\|^ ``` Run over every tracked Markdown file on main, `brokenLinks` reports 23 missing anchors. Six are this false positive, on links main's docs already carry: - `docs/unattended.md:116` → `troubleshooting.md#unattended-runs-and-artifacts` - `docs/review-policy.md:785` → `troubleshooting.md#route-bounded-refused` - `docs/ship-policy.md:24` → `troubleshooting.md#queue-aware-ship-policy-restamp-tree-receipt-ship-receipt` - `docs/ship-policy.md:1964` → `troubleshooting.md#route-mechanical-refused` - `docs/ship-policy.md:2097` → `troubleshooting.md#route-sidecar-refused` - `docs/ship-policy.md:2619` → `troubleshooting.md#repo-commands-not-allowed` `lib/prose-lint.ts` has the same opening rule. On `docs/troubleshooting.md` (7,779 lines) it masks lines 3098 to 4054 as code, takes the bare fence at 4058 for an unclosed block and reads nothing after it. /ship runs it with `--base --gate` on the lines a branch adds, so a sentence added in the second half passes while the same sentence in the first half is flagged: ``` $ bin/gstack-prose-lint docs/troubleshooting.md | tail -2 PROSE: docs/troubleshooting.md:4058 unclosed-block "fence never closed" (close it; nothing after it was read) PROSE_LINT: found=23 files=1 # the same sentence added after lines 500 and 5000, as /ship lints a branch $ bin/gstack-prose-lint docs/troubleshooting.md --base HEAD --gate PROSE: docs/troubleshooting.md:501 mid-sentence-colon "says what changes: nothing at all" (end the sentence there, or join the halves with a plain conjunction) PROSE_LINT: found=1 files=1 ``` Read as CommonMark reads it, the file has 72 findings and no unclosed block. The link check's closing rule has a second problem: an example block opened with ````` ````markdown ````` ends at its first inner ````` ```mermaid ````` line, as in `docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md:17`. Expected: CommonMark's fence rules. A backtick fence's info string cannot contain a backtick, so line 3098 is text. Only a bare run of the same character, at least as long as the opening run, closes a block. #4193 carried a fence fix and was closed because the link-checker cases "don't change how gstack's workflows run today". The docs lane refusing valid links is the workflow effect its closing comment asked for. ## Steps to reproduce 1. In a checkout of main (0326b14), append a link to `troubleshooting.md#unattended-runs-and-artifacts` to `docs/unattended.md`. 2. Run `bun scripts/check-doc-links.ts --base HEAD docs/unattended.md`. It prints `DOC_LINKS: broken` and exits 1, though the heading is at `docs/troubleshooting.md:3171`. ## Readiness report Not collected: this was reproduced from a source checkout with `bun scripts/check-doc-links.ts`, with no installed skill involved. ## Environment - Host: none (source checkout, bun 1.4.4) - OS: Linux x64 A fix for both, with regression tests that fail on main, is on the `fix/doc-links-inline-code-fence` branch of Davmunrey/gstack.

title: docs: 16 in-repo links point to anchors that don't exist (skills.md index, review-policy.md's targeted-only read)
body: ## What happened On main (0326b14), `lib/doc-links.ts`'s `brokenLinks`, run over every tracked Markdown file, reports links whose anchor has no heading or ``. Apart from the troubleshooting.md false positives (a separate fence bug), these are real: **`docs/skills.md`: 13 links to 12 skills that have no section** (lines 8, 32, 37-40, 42-44, 48, 50, 57, 58): `#spec` (twice), `#document-generate`, `#plan-devex-review`, `#devex-review`, `#plan-tune`, `#context-save`, `#context-restore`, `#health`, `#landing-report`, `#benchmark-models`, `#setup-gbrain`, `#sync-gbrain`. The heading at line 542 is `### Targeted-only read after the loop (GST-1598)`, whose anchor is `#targeted-only-read-after-the-loop-gst-1598`. `troubleshooting.md`'s link to `ship-policy.md#approval-classes` is the same kind of defect and is already #4320.
