title: OpenClaw docs point to ClawHub skills still at the April 1.0.0 publish; the count says four, the list has three
body:
## What happened

`docs/hosts.md` and `docs/OPENCLAW.md` send OpenClaw users to the `gstack-openclaw-*` skills on ClawHub. Checked against `main` at 5dcd76b4 (`garrytan/gstack`):

1. **The docs say four skills and list three.**
   - `docs/hosts.md:122-126`: "Four methodology skills that work directly in your OpenClaw agent ... `clawhub install gstack-openclaw-office-hours gstack-openclaw-ceo-review gstack-openclaw-retro`"; the table at lines 129-133 has three rows.
   - `docs/OPENCLAW.md:178`: "Install the 4 native methodology skills"; lines 104-108 list three ("Published to ClawHub. Install with `clawhub install`").
   - The fourth, `gstack-openclaw-investigate`, was removed from `openclaw/skills/` by `ef99eb5a` ("feat: retire /investigate after a no-gain eval (GST-1717) (#4110)"). The docs were not updated for it.

2. **ClawHub still serves the first publish of every skill.** Each of the four has exactly one version, `1.0.0`, published 2026-04-05 between 16:57:28 and 16:57:41 UTC (ClawHub `latestVersion.createdAt`, `stats.versions: 1`). Meanwhile `openclaw/skills/` changed on 2026-04-16 (`b805aa01`), 2026-04-17 (`1211b6b4`), 2026-08-15 (`008dd65b`) and 2026-11-07 (`ef99eb5a`). For `gstack-openclaw-retro` I compared the ClawHub 1.0.0 `SKILL.md` with the repo file. (I compared only this skill's contents; for office-hours and ceo-review I verified the version and date, not the text.) Diff, `-` = repo `main`, `+` = ClawHub 1.0.0:

   ```diff
   -description: "Weekly engineering retrospective. ... engineering retrospective."
   +description: Weekly engineering retrospective. ... engineering retrospective.
   +version: 1.0.0
   +metadata: { "openclaw": { "emoji": "..." } }
   ...
   -git ls-files 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(\.test\.|\.spec\.|_test\.|_spec\.)' | wc -l
   +find . -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' -o -name '*_test.*' -o -name '*_spec.*' 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | wc -l
   ```

   The ClawHub file counts test files with `find ... | grep -v node_modules`, not `git ls-files`. A user who follows the docs gets a file that predates later fixes in the repo. `docs/OPENCLAW_PUBLISHING.md` says to republish with "the same `clawhub publish` command with a higher `--version`", but no later version exists.

3. **The retired skill is still published.** `openclaw skills search gstack` lists `@garrytan/gstack-openclaw-investigate` (1.0.0, same date) next to the other three. The docs no longer mention it, but a user who searches finds it.

4. **The install command does not work on one current OpenClaw version.** The docs say `clawhub install <bare slug>`. On OpenClaw 2026.11.3 there is no `clawhub` binary on PATH. `openclaw skills install --help` there says "ClawHub skill ref (@owner/slug or skills-sh:owner/repo/slug), git:<repo>, or local skill directory", so the working form is `openclaw skills install @garrytan/<slug>`. This is one version only: `docs/OPENCLAW_PUBLISHING.md` uses `clawhub publish`, so a separate `clawhub` CLI exists. The docs do not say which of the two a user should run.

5. **The ClawHub trio overlaps native registration, and the docs do not say which wins.** `./setup --host openclaw` registers the four task skills (review, qa, ship, plan-eng-review) plus one `gstack` router skill (`docs/OPENCLAW.md:182-189`, "Both can be installed together"). The generated router lists `office-hours`, `plan-ceo-review` and `retro` among the rest, with their full current `SKILL.md` files. `docs/OPENCLAW.md:212` says "No hand-ported coding skills (native registration copies the generated OpenClaw render)". An agent with both installed has two office-hours, two CEO reviews and two retros, one of each from April. Nothing says whether the ClawHub trio is still recommended once native registration is installed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read `docs/hosts.md` lines 120-135 and `docs/OPENCLAW.md` lines 104-111 and 178 on `main`.
2. `openclaw skills search gstack` shows the four `@garrytan/gstack-openclaw-*` skills.
3. `curl https://clawhub.ai/api/v1/skills/gstack-openclaw-retro` shows `latestVersion.version` 1.0.0 and a `createdAt` of 2026-04-05 16:57:41 UTC; the same call for the other three slugs shows 1.0.0 and 2026-04-05.
4. Compare the ClawHub `SKILL.md` with `openclaw/skills/gstack-openclaw-retro/SKILL.md` (diff above).

## Environment

- Host: OpenClaw 2026.11.3
- gstack 1.99.5.0 (docs verified again against `main` at 5dcd76b4)
- This is a docs and publishing issue; no install state is involved, so the doctor report does not apply.

## What I would ask

a. Republish the three skills from `openclaw/skills/`, or say in the docs that ClawHub lags the repo.
b. Change "four" / "4" to three, and unpublish or mark the retired `gstack-openclaw-investigate`.
c. Say whether the ClawHub trio is still recommended alongside `./setup --host openclaw`, whose router already carries the same three workflows, and which one wins when both are installed.
d. Give the install command for current OpenClaw (`openclaw skills install @garrytan/<slug>` or `clawhub install`, and for which versions).

title: Skill routing never matches prompts or triggers in a non-Latin script
body:
## What happened

The skill routing hook (`lib/skill-route.ts`) never produces a candidate for a prompt written in a non-Latin script, and it ignores triggers written in one. A Russian prompt gets no routing, and adding Russian triggers to a skill does not help. Prompts that mix in English trigger words do route, which hides the problem.

`bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "<prompt>"` is the documented dry run (`docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, "Dry run"). It injects nothing.

Installed 1.99.5.0, commit `0326b144af36676d599dcf63a9fad9a870d22ed6`. The file `lib/skill-route.ts` is byte-identical on `main` at `5dcd76b4eae6bb06f73460d3ab29cef8e33e8537`.

English prompts route:

```
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "run the checks and verify my change"
candidates:
  1.00  /verify  "verify my change" (2 words)
  0.50  /review  "check my diff" (1 words)
route: /verify

$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "test the site and find bugs"
candidates:
  1.00  /qa  "find bugs on site" (3 words)
  0.50  /verify  "make the tests pass" (1 words)
route: /qa
```

A Russian prompt that contains English trigger words routes, only because of those words:

```
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "сделай review этого PR"
candidates:
  1.00  /review  "review this pr" (2 words)
route: /review
```

Pure Russian prompts get no candidate at all (each prints `candidates:` followed by `(none)` and `route: none (below-threshold)`):

```
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "проверь мой дифф перед пушем"
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "протестируй сайт и найди баги"
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "прогони проверки и убедись что изменение работает"
```

## Steps to reproduce

Localized triggers do not help. Create a throwaway config directory with one skill named `review`:

```
<tmp>/cfg/skills/review/SKILL.md
---
name: review
description: Review a diff.
triggers:
  - review this pr
  - проверь мой дифф
  - сделай ревью изменений
---
# review
```

Then, with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<tmp>/cfg`, every run scans `1 skill`:

```
$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "review this pr"
  1.00  /review  "review this pr" (2 words)
route: /review

$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "проверь мой дифф"            # prompt equal to a trigger
candidates:
  (none)
route: none (below-threshold)

$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "сделай ревью изменений"      # prompt equal to a trigger
  (none) / route: none (below-threshold)

$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "проверь мой дифф перед пушем"   # contains a trigger word for word
  (none) / route: none (below-threshold)

$ bin/gstack-skill-route --explain "сделай ревью изменений в ветке" # contains a trigger word for word
  (none) / route: none (below-threshold)
```

So both rules fail: the whole-phrase rule (prompt equal to the trigger) and the content-word share rule.

## Cause

In `lib/skill-route.ts` at `0326b144`:

- Line 161: `const words = (text) => text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z]+)?/g) ?? [];`. This is the only tokenizer. `tokens()` (line 163) and `contentTokens()` (line 167) both build on it, so every character outside `[a-z0-9']` is dropped before scoring, in the prompt and in the trigger text alike.
- Line 190 in `scorePrompt` (line 182): a trigger whose `contentTokens()` is empty is skipped (`if (!content.length) continue;`). A Cyrillic trigger tokenizes to `[]`, so it is skipped before the whole-phrase check or the word-share check can run.
- Lines 145-148 (`STOPWORDS`), line 151 (`stem`) and line 174 (`SPECIFIC_WORD = /^...[a-z0-9]{5,}$/`) are English-only too. They would need a decision once the tokenizer accepts other scripts.

Confirmed directly against the module:

```
tokens("проверь мой дифф")           -> []
contentTokens("сделай ревью изменений") -> []
tokens("сделай review этого PR")     -> ["review","pr"]
```

`docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` does not say routing is English-only.

## Ask

One of:

1. Tokenize Unicode letters and digits (for example `/[\p{L}\p{N}]+(?:'[\p{L}]+)?/gu`), so triggers a user adds in any script match. Say whether localized triggers are in scope for the three routed skills (`review`, `qa`, `verify`), or how a user should add them. `ROUTED_SKILLS` and the shipped triggers are English, and the docs do not say how a non-English speaker is meant to get routing.
2. Or state in `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` that routing is English-only, and that triggers in other scripts are silently ignored.

If `--explain` printed a line when a trigger or prompt has no tokens (for example "prompt has no Latin words"), the failure would be visible instead of looking like an ordinary below-threshold miss.

Related, but about localizing skill content rather than the routing hook: #245 and #481 (both closed).

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.5.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: openclaw global current (1.99.5.0), codex global current (1.99.5.0), claude global current (1.99.5.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.169.0; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 1h ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 2)
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.99.5.0 (0326b144af36)
ok              claude code     2.1.311 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal no session journals for this project
ok              guard log       209 decisions (9 denied)
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

- OS: Linux

title: Skill routing routes messages from other agents and sessions as if a person asked
body:
## What happened

With `skill_routing` on, the UserPromptSubmit routing hook scores every text Claude Code hands it, including messages no person typed. In a Claude Code session, a message sent by another Claude Code session arrived as a user turn wrapped in a `<cross-session-message from-session="...">` block (about 6,000 characters, a read-only diagnosis report that mentions "contract tests"). The session received this hint:

```text
gstack skill routing (UserPromptSubmit hook; matched the installed /verify trigger "make the tests pass"; off: gstack-config set skill_routing off): this request fits /verify. Run /verify with the Skill tool before you start, and tell the user in one sentence that gstack routed this to /verify.
```

The routing log line was `event=routed skill=verify score=1 variant=name`. Nothing in that turn asked for a verify run; the text was a peer's report.

Earlier turns of the same kind in that session (subagent hand-back reports of 9,000 to 11,000 characters) were logged `event=no-route reason=prompt-too-long`. They escaped only through the 8,000-character cap, not because the hook knew they were not a person's request. A shorter hand-back would have been routed the same way.

## Steps to reproduce

The documented dry run, with a short synthetic report of my own (generic content, no real session):

```bash
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-skill-route --explain '<cross-session-message from-session="peer">Read-only report. The contract tests pass and nothing needs verifying. Nothing to do on your side.</cross-session-message>'
```

Output (exit 0):

```text
switch: skill_routing on (config skill_routing)
threshold: 0.66
skills: 60 scanned in ~/.claude/skills
candidates:
  1.00  /verify  "make the tests pass" (2 words)
  0.50  /qa  "qa test this" (1 words)
route: /verify
hint: gstack skill routing (UserPromptSubmit hook; matched the installed /verify trigger "make the tests pass"; off: gstack-config set skill_routing off): this request fits /verify. Run /verify with the Skill tool before you start, and tell the user in one sentence that gstack routed this to /verify.
```

The report says the tests already pass and nothing needs verifying, and it still routes to `/verify`. Reports that say "I reviewed my changes" route to `/review` the same way. The trigger match is on words, so a report that talks about tests, review or verification matches whatever the report is about.

## Cause (commit 5dcd76b4, upstream `main`; the two files below are byte-identical in my installed checkout at 0326b144)

- `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook.ts` lines 62-72: the hook parses the stdin JSON, takes `p.prompt` (line 69) and passes it straight to `routePrompt` (line 72). It reads `session_id` and nothing else from the payload, and it does not look at the text's wrapper.
- `lib/skill-route.ts` lines 215-222 (`routePrompt`): the only rules that skip a prompt are an empty prompt, a prompt starting with `/`, and a prompt over `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS = 8000` (line 24). Below the cap, any text that scores at or above the threshold is routed.
- `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` line 40 lists the same two skips ("start with `/`", "over 8,000 characters (pasted logs)").

## What the Claude Code docs say about the payload

The hooks reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, UserPromptSubmit) says these hooks "don't fire only on prompts you type", and that Claude Code also runs them on:

- a session-scoped scheduled task firing, including a `/loop` iteration;
- a background subagent reporting back to the session that started it;
- a message another session sends to your main conversation.

The documented UserPromptSubmit input is the common fields plus `prompt` (and `session_title` when the session has a custom title). I found no documented field that says whether the text was typed or injected. `agent_id` and `agent_type` are documented only for hooks that fire inside a subagent, and `prompt_id` is described as identifying "the user prompt currently being processed"; neither marks an injected message. So I do not see a payload field the hook could use today, and I may have missed one. The text itself does start with a recognizable wrapper in my case (`<cross-session-message from-session="...">`); I have not checked what wrapper a background-task notification or a subagent hand-back carries, so a wrapper rule would need that confirmed on a live session.

## The ask

Either of these would close it:

1. Skip prompts that are agent or session messages: by a payload field if Claude Code offers or adds one, otherwise by their wrapper (for example a leading `<cross-session-message`, `<task-notification>` or a subagent hand-back header), logged as a `no-route` reason of its own so the log shows why.
2. If skipping is not wanted, say in `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` that routing applies to every UserPromptSubmit text, not only typed prompts, and that the 8,000-character cap is the only length guard.

Cost in multi-agent setups: most messages between agents are English and full of the words the triggers use (tests, review, verify, qa). The routing hint tells the receiving agent to run a skill "before you start" and to tell the user that gstack routed it, so a peer's report can start an unrequested `/verify` or `/review` run and put a stray routing notice into the conversation. The 8,000-character cap hides this for long reports only.

## Readiness report

Output of `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-doctor` (version and summary lines only):

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.5.0
13 ok, 2 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host and version: Claude Code 2.1.311
- OS: Linux
- gstack: 1.99.5.0 (commit 0326b144), `skill_routing` on

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for skill routing with subagent, cross-session, task notification, agent message, UserPromptSubmit, GST-1088 and routing hook. I found no issue for this. #4422 (non-Latin scripts) is a different problem.

title: /ship test step fails on Linux when the unit suite has thousands of files (argument list too long)
body:
On Linux, `/ship`'s test step cannot run a large unit suite. It stops with `PREGATE: incomplete` before any test runs, so `/ship` cannot write a receipt.

## What happens

`gstack-ship-preflight --tests-only --base master --lanes serial --lane "unit=bun run test" --lane "serial=bun run test:serial"` on a repository with about 5,500 test files (gstack v1.99.5.0, 5dcd76b, Ubuntu x86_64, Bun 1.4.4):

```text
PREGATE: incomplete
PREGATE_DETAIL: gstack-pregate: lanes: the runner could not be launched (5567 files): E2BIG: argument list too long, posix_spawn 'bash'; fix: install the named tool on this machine (or put it on PATH), or run the lane remotely (--remote, or clear it with a run URL); the diff is not at fault (PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT)
STOP: pregate incomplete: fix what PREGATE_DETAIL names (gstack-pregate --allow-repo-commands), then rerun --tests-only
```

The serial files ran first, about 55 minutes of work. Then the launch of the unit group failed.

## Cause

`runOnce` in `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts` puts every unit file of a run group into one shell command string (`g.runner.replace('{files}', joined)`). `supervise.ts` then starts it as `bash -c <command>`. Here that string is about 250 KB.

Linux limits each single `execve` argument to `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 32 pages = 128 KiB, even though the total `ARG_MAX` is 2 MiB. So `posix_spawn` returns `E2BIG`. macOS has no per-argument limit (only `ARG_MAX` of about 1 MiB in total), so the same run works on a Mac. That is likely why the bug has not appeared before.

The fix text is also wrong: no tool is missing, so "install the named tool" sends the operator the wrong way.

## Proposed fix

- Split the unit files of a group into chunks that keep each command string below a safe size, for example 100 KB, and run the chunks one after another. `runLocal` already adds up the counts across runs.
- Or pass the file list some other way than the command string, for example as positional `"$@"` arguments, a list file or an environment file. Each argument then stays small.
- Classify `E2BIG` as its own cause (`argument list too long: split the selection`), not as `missing-binary`.
- Add a test with a file list longer than 128 KiB that passes on Linux.

## Workaround today

Run the lane remotely (`--remote`), or split the selection by hand.

title: test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts fails when the free suite runs as root
body:
## What happened

`bun run test` on main 5dcd76b, run as root in a Linux x64 container, fails 5 tests in `test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts` (the trailing serial shard). The rest of the free suite passes. `bun test test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts` alone gives the same result: 31 pass, 5 fail.

- pre-existing same-uid nondumpable host process is not an attempt writer: `expect(() => fs.readlinkSync(`/proc/${child.pid}/cwd`)).toThrow('EACCES')` does not throw (line 115).
- new process cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: expected false, received true (line 151).
- new denial cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: same assertion (line 151).
- different lifetime cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'data.uninspectable.find((native) => native.pid === child.pid).start = "0"')` (line 136), because no process is recorded as uninspectable.
- reusing a scope cannot baseline-exempt an unreadable process from its prior attempt: the promise resolves instead of rejecting (line 254).

All five rely on the same fact: a same-uid process that made itself nondumpable denies reading its `/proc/<pid>/cwd`. That denial goes through the ptrace access check, which root passes (CAP_SYS_PTRACE), so as root the process is readable and the "uninspectable process" paths never run. None of the three open PRs from me touch these files; I checked the same file on plain main before reporting.

Expected: the block is skipped where the denial cannot happen, as other tests in the suite do for permission-based simulations (`process.getuid?.() === 0` guards, or a functional probe like `test/helpers/fs-caps.ts`). For example `describe.skipIf(process.platform !== 'linux' || process.getuid?.() === 0)`, or a probe that starts a nondumpable child and checks that reading its `/proc/<pid>/cwd` fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. As root on Linux, check out main (5dcd76b) and run `bun install`.
2. Run `bun test test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts`.

title: Run large unit suites on Linux instead of failing with argument list too long (#4424)
body:
/ship's test step now runs a unit suite with thousands of files on Linux instead of stopping with `E2BIG: argument list too long` before any test runs. It keeps gstack's merge checks working on large repositories such as gbrain, which has 5,567 unit files.

## What changed

Before: a lane over Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit stopped with `the runner could not be launched (700 files): E2BIG: argument list too long, posix_spawn 'bash'`, and the fix text said to install a missing tool. After: the same lane passes with `700 tests ran in 700 file(s), exit 0`, and a launch that still hits the limit is reported as `arg-limit`, not as a missing tool.

## Why

gbrain's merge check stopped with `PREGATE: incomplete` and `E2BIG` on its 5,567 unit files (#4424). gstack put every unit file of a lane into one command argument, and Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB. A big file list now runs as several runner processes of about 96 KB each (24 KB on Windows), read back as one run, so any failing chunk still fails the lane.

## Blast radius

Only a unit group whose quoted file list passes the limit changes; a group that fits in one process runs the identical command, because `runOnce` returns its single part unchanged (read at lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:414). CI's free suite passed at 7eeef79 (run 44026832699, 1,672 test files), and the remote-gate path is untouched.

<details><summary>Summary, tests and review</summary>

## Summary

A team running /ship on gbrain hit `E2BIG` before a single test started, with advice to install a tool that was already installed. Lanes now split a large file list into byte-bounded chunks run one after another under the group's one deadline, add up their counts, and let the first unfinished or failing chunk decide the result. An `E2BIG` launch failure gets its own environment kind, `arg-limit`, whose fix says to report it as a gstack bug. The review round made the new test put its failing file in the last chunk, and the docs audit noted the Windows chunk size.

## Test Coverage

```

  argChunks()      [★★★] order, budget, oversized argument, empty list, one chunk
  runOnce() chunks [★★] single chunk unchanged; [★★★] 700 files over 128 KiB pass; [★★★] failing last chunk fails the lane
                   [GAP] a chunk that stalls or times out ends the group
                   [GAP] noBrowsers kept only when every chunk has it
                   [GAP] ran/failed become null when any chunk's summary is unparsed
lib/pregate/environment.ts
  [★★] E2BIG and "Argument list too long" classify as arg-limit
  [GAP] the launch path shows the arg-limit fix text
lib/pregate/types.ts  type only
COVERAGE: 8/12 paths (67%)
```

Tests ran: free 1672

## Pre-Landing Review

Pre-Landing Review: 8 issues — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked (0 fixed, 0 skipped), 0 deferred, 7 noted.

- [AUTO-FIXED] test/pregate-lanes-arg-limit.test.ts:56: the test was named for a failure in the last chunk, but sorting put the failing file first; the failing file now sorts last (3c1a808), and the fix-check read it clean.
- Second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol): completed with one finding, that adding counts across chunks hides a chunk that ran zero tests. Ruled below the blocking floor and kept as a note: the zero-run check is per runner process and a unit group was one process before this change, so a whole-group zero is still caught and no lane that failed before now passes.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:468` The PREGATE_INCOMPLETE timeout detail says --timeout applies to each runner process, but chunks of a split unit group now share one deadline, as docs/pregate.md says; the message names the wrong scope for a chunked group.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:502` The undeclared remote fallback (ubi-runner.sh run -- '<runner with every file>') still inlines the whole file list into one bash -c argument, so a huge selection routed remotely on a <8-core machine can still hit E2BIG; pre-existing, and the new arg-limit fix text suggests the remote route.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:417` Outside voice (stated High, Blocks: yes): summing ran across chunks lets a zero-test chunk pass beside a chunk that ran tests, so the ZERO-RUN guard does not see it. Lead judgment, below the floor: the guard is per runner process and a unit group was one process before this change, so an unsplit group whose files partly ran zero tests already summed to a positive count and passed; a whole-group zero still sums to 0 and is still caught. No test fails and no lane that failed before now passes; failing a zero-test chunk would make a split group stricter than the same files in one process (for example a chunk of win32-skipped files). Named for the owner in Review notes.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:468` Native voice 1 (Low): the timeout detail says --timeout applies to each runner process, but a split group's chunks share one deadline; macOS is also capped at 96 KiB though it has only the 1 MiB total limit, so a large macOS group now runs as several processes under one deadline. Same location as p1/specialist-batched#2.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:415` Native voice 2 (Low): bad prefers the first unfinished chunk, so a later chunk that fails to launch reports PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT even when an earlier chunk had counted test failures; the lane still fails (misattribution only).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:416` Native voice 3 (Low): noBrowsers survives aggregation only when every chunk has it, so a split Playwright group where one chunk shows no browser error reports PREGATE_LANE_FAILED instead of the missing-binary environment cause; the lane still fails.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/environment.ts:26` Native voice 4 (Low): the arg-limit rule also matches runner output printed before the first counted test (proof output), the same risk every output rule carries; investigate only if it shows up.

## Exploratory QA

Functional surface, smoke budget (5 minutes): 2 probes on fixture repositories, both pass. Probe 1: a 700-file unit group whose quoted list is over 128 KiB passes with 700 tests in 700 files. Probe 2: the failing file sorts last, so only the final chunk fails; the lane fails with `PREGATE_LANE_FAILED`, 1 failed of 700 ran. A first probe set was blocked by the probe's own inherited install-verdict environment and was rerun with it unset. title: test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts fails when the free suite runs as root
body:
## What happened

`bun run test` on main 5dcd76b, run as root in a Linux x64 container, fails 5 tests in `test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts` (the trailing serial shard). The rest of the free suite passes. `bun test test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts` alone gives the same result: 31 pass, 5 fail.

- pre-existing same-uid nondumpable host process is not an attempt writer: `expect(() => fs.readlinkSync(`/proc/${child.pid}/cwd`)).toThrow('EACCES')` does not throw (line 115).
- new process cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: expected false, received true (line 151).
- new denial cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: same assertion (line 151).
- different lifetime cannot inherit an unrelated process census exclusion: `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'data.uninspectable.find((native) => native.pid === child.pid).start = "0"')` (line 136), because no process is recorded as uninspectable.
- reusing a scope cannot baseline-exempt an unreadable process from its prior attempt: the promise resolves instead of rejecting (line 254).

All five rely on the same fact: a same-uid process that made itself nondumpable denies reading its `/proc/<pid>/cwd`. That denial goes through the ptrace access check, which root passes (CAP_SYS_PTRACE), so as root the process is readable and the "uninspectable process" paths never run. None of the three open PRs from me touch these files; I checked the same file on plain main before reporting.

Expected: the block is skipped where the denial cannot happen, as other tests in the suite do for permission-based simulations (`process.getuid?.() === 0` guards, or a functional probe like `test/helpers/fs-caps.ts`). For example `describe.skipIf(process.platform !== 'linux' || process.getuid?.() === 0)`, or a probe that starts a nondumpable child and checks that reading its `/proc/<pid>/cwd` fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. As root on Linux, check out main (5dcd76b) and run `bun install`.
2. Run `bun test test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts`.

## Readiness report

Not applicable: this is the contributor test suite in a source checkout, not an installed skill.

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: not applicable (source checkout, `bun test`).
- OS: Linux x64 container, running as root (uid 0).

title: Stop the optional Stop hook checking for a test after the last edit (GST-2811)
body:
The optional Stop hook (`./setup --skill-contracts`) no longer stops a run for missing a test after the last edit; /verify asks for that test in its own words instead. This keeps gstack to the steps that measurably help a model finish real work.

## What changed

![/verify now asks for the full check after the last edit and no longer forbids a changelog entry the repo expects](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/2Yi4KOWyUOpq2xdxo1K0RT6eGny3LDthiFeCN5njbe8.png)

/verify now asks for the full check after the last edit and no longer forbids a changelog entry the repo expects.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: /verify now asks for the full check after the last edit and no longer forbids a changelog entry the repo expects</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · verify/SKILL.md.tmpl § /verify — build, check, fix, repeat at 18652cc · source text
+++ After · verify/SKILL.md.tmpl § /verify — build, check, fix, repeat on this branch · source text
 # /verify — build, check, fix, repeat
 Use this while building, before /ship. It runs checks and fixes code. It never
+reviews, bumps a version, pushes, or opens a PR: that is /ship. A changelog entry
+the repo expects with a change is part of the change.
-reviews, bumps a version, edits CHANGELOG, pushes, or opens a PR: that is /ship.
 
 ## 1. See what will run
 
@@ ⋯ 33 unchanged ⋯ @@
   A `FAIL` whose own error says a service, secret or env var is missing is
   the same: report it, do not stub or skip it.
 - Rerun one check with `"$C" run --only <name>` while fixing it, then a full
+  `run` after your last edit, before you stop.
-  `run` before you stop.
 
 Never weaken, skip, delete or edit a test, a checker config or a package.json
 script to get green.
~~~

</details>

## Why

Garry approved cutting the hook's "run a test after your last edit" check because it showed no measured gain. With /verify loaded, Opus 5.5 ran that test in 96% of runs and GPT-6.1 Sol in 89% without the hook, and the hook added between -0.5 and +2 points, with every interval crossing zero (gstack-evals#356). The same eval found Sol, told to use /verify, wrote the changelog entry an upstream fix carried in 0 of 58 tasks against 32 of 58 plain, so /verify stops saying it never edits CHANGELOG.

## Blast radius

The change touches the contract checker, the "Done means" renderer, the routing doc and /verify. No shipped skill declares the removed item, because a repo-wide search at the base found it only in the checker, the renderer and the doc example. A custom skill that still lists it now reads as an invalid contract. A smoke run showed the hook letting the stop through with one line naming the file (script ran).

## Summary

People who turned on skill contracts got a block when a model skipped a test after its last edit, but models already run that test when /verify asks. The checker loses that item kind and the shell-write parser only it used. /verify keeps the rule as prose and now treats a changelog entry the repo expects as part of the change. The pre-merge check maps the deleted parser to the contract checker's test so it accepts the removal.

## Test Coverage

All changed code paths have test coverage: each of the 4 changed runtime files has a changed test that names it. The contract tests now assert that the removed kind is rejected as an unknown kind.

## Pre-Landing Review

No issues found.

Gate edits: 21 listed, 21 read, 0 findings. The two RH-1 hunks remove tests of the deleted check and parser, whose subject code this diff deletes under Garry's recorded approval.

Outside review: openai/gpt-6.1-sol, completed, clean.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-contract.ts:25` A custom contract that still lists the removed check_after_last_edit kind is invalid as a whole, so the optional Stop hook stops checking that skill's other items too, not only the removed one. The changelog entry now says so.
- INFORMATIONAL `verify/SKILL.md.tmpl:31` The new changelog sentence could lead a model to edit CHANGELOG.md directly in a repo that expects a fragment; the sentence already scopes it to what the repo expects.
- INFORMATIONAL `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md:79` The reader did not check the cited figures against gstack-evals#356; they match that PR's description (96.0%, 89.0%, -0.5 to +2.0 points).
- INFORMATIONAL `.gstack/pregate.json:19` The dependencies entry for the deleted lib/shell-writes.ts stays after the deletion lands, as the QM review script's entry did (#4279).

## Exploratory QA

Functional smoke on the `gstack-skill-contract` CLI and the Stop hook, 3 probes within the 300 s budget, all passing on the current tree:
- `check` on a contract skill that ended without its report: exit 1, only `debug-report` missing.
- `check` on a custom skill that lists `check_after_last_edit`: exit 5, `unknown kind "check_after_last_edit"` naming the SKILL.md.
- The Stop hook on that skill: exit 0, no block, one `SKILL_CONTRACT_STATE_ERROR` line naming the file.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No paid eval ran. The cut rests on gstack-evals#356; the changed /verify prose is covered by the free parity, prompt-size and freshness checks.

## TODOS

No TODO items completed in this PR.

## Documentation
**Status:** current — no documentation edits were needed for removing the Stop hook's check_after_last_edit item.

Scope: base 18652ccc..head e769afdc on remove-test-after-edit-stop-hook-check (14 committed files plus 1 unstaged changelog fragment), with a repo-wide search for the removed kind, shell-writes parser and example item ids.

title: /ship's test step says when it hits its time limit, and long test file lists no longer overflow the remote command (GST-2958)
body:
/ship's test step now says when it runs out of time and lets you set its budget, and the remote test command no longer packs every test file into one command-line argument, which Linux refuses past 128 KiB.
You don't need to do anything: the default budget is still one hour, and `--step-timeout <s>` on `gstack-ship-preflight` raises it.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

## What changed

- `gstack-ship-preflight --step-timeout <s>` (1 to 86400, default 3600) sets the budget for the whole test step. When a run hits it, the output says so and names the way out:

```text
PREGATE: time limit hit (Step 5's whole pregate ran past its 2 s budget, --step-timeout, and was stopped with exit 143; no verdict)
STOP: the tests are longer than this step's 2 s budget on this machine: push, let CI's full run at this tree carry them (gstack-ci-carry wait --base main, then rerun --tests-only; gbrain docs/ci-event-parity.md#ship-lanes), or rerun --tests-only with --step-timeout <s> above 2
```

(Captured on this branch with a 2-second budget in a throwaway clone. Before this change the same stop printed `PREGATE: unreadable (exit 143)`.)
- On a machine with fewer than 8 cores and a remote test backend, the command printed for gstack's Ubicloud runner now sends the selected test files in a small setup script instead of one long argument. The script is named by its content, so the same selection prints the same command every run.
- A selected test path that contains a newline keeps the old quoted command, so it can never end the file list early and run as shell on the test machine.
- docs/troubleshooting.md has an `arg-limit` entry, and docs/pregate.md describes both changes.

## Why

"PREGATE: unreadable (exit 143)" told nobody that the suite simply ran past the hour /ship gave it. Now the stop says it hit the time limit and how to get past it. Separately, a large selection made the remote test command too long for Linux to start, and now the command stays short however many files are selected.

## Blast radius

The changes stay inside `gstack-ship-preflight`'s test step and the command pregate prints for a remote test backend. Pregate never runs that command itself. The default budget is the same 3600 s as the old fixed limit, and a run that finishes in time takes the same path as before (lib/ship-preflight.ts, read). Bun's `spawnSync` sets `ETIMEDOUT` when the limit hits, and pregate's SIGTERM handler kills the test processes it supervises (walked failure path; QA probe 005 found no test process left behind).

## Summary

Long suites and big selections both failed in ways that hid the cause. The test step now has a budget you can set and a clear message when it runs out. The remote command passes its file list through a setup script. After review, odd file names fall back to the old quoted form.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths have test coverage: each of the 4 changed runtime files has a changed test that names it.
- test/ship-preflight.test.ts: a run past `--step-timeout` prints the time-limit line and the way out; bad values are usage errors.
- test/pregate-lanes-arg-limit.test.ts: 700 long file names give a command under 2 KB that still reaches all 700 files.
- test/pregate-remote.test.ts: the new command shape and its setup file, and a path with a newline that keeps the quoted inline form.
- The new tests fail on main, and the newline test fails without its fix.

Tests ran: test 1678 (files)

## Pre-Landing Review

Two rounds:
- **Round 1.** A batched reader for testing, security and state machines, a red-team reader, a native adversarial reader, and a second-model review (gpt-6.1-sol).
- **One blocker, fixed.** The second-model review found that a test path containing a newline could end the setup script's file list early and run the rest as shell on the test machine. It is fixed, with a test, in f0434305.
- **Round 2.** A full re-read of the fix found nothing blocking.
- **Skipped.** A round-1 test-gap note: the scratch fallback for an unwritable state root has no test. The fallback was read and is correct.

## Review notes

These are below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items). They are recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:521` Two pregate runs with the same selection rewrite the same content-named setup file without an atomic write. If the runner reads it mid-rewrite, it could see an empty list.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:528` The printed command now names a file on this machine, so it fails elsewhere or after the state root is cleaned. In the scratch fallback its path changes every run, so a later clear never matches.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:519` Old setup scripts are never pruned. Each is a few KB, one per distinct selection.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:578` The declared `remote_gate` route (`scripts/ubicloud/pregate-remote.sh`) has the same newline problem. That code predates this PR.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:518` On a very large selection that also holds an odd path, the quoted fallback can exceed the argument limit and fail loudly.

## Exploratory QA

Pass, 5 captures in a throwaway clone with its own state root:
- `--help` documents the option.
- `--step-timeout 0` and `86401` exit 2 with a usage message.
- A 2-second budget stops with the time-limit line and exit 3.
- No test process is left running afterwards.

Limits: the budget ran out during pregate's own checks, before the slow test started. The stop also took about 19 s of wall time for a 2-second budget, because pregate cleans up after SIGTERM.

The 3600 s preflight and `finish` wrapper deadline (P3) is narrowed to `finish`'s half. The preflight half is done in this PR.

**Scope:** This audit covered the committed changes in base 2af3822f..84c9e0da at reviewed tree 4486a9a9b0ba9de0c74ebdb2669580f7ff9d6fc9. The working tree had no staged, unstaged or new files.

**Result:** The docs were already current, so I edited nothing. docs/pregate.md covers the time limit in the `timeout_s` row, and TODOS.md has a matching note. The move of the remote file list into a setup script is covered in the remote gate section and the `arg-limit` row of docs/pregate.md, and docs/troubleshooting.md has a new `arg-limit` entry. Both anchors resolve. The eight-shard wording matches .github/workflows/windows-free-tests.yml and agrees with docs/support-tiers.md. No ship template or README mentions the preflight time budget or the old `PREGATE: unreadable (exit 143)` output, so no template needs to be regenerated. The banned-terms check found nothing because main has no .gstack/banned-terms.json.

**Debt:** None. The changelog fragment and the TODOS.md edit belong to the parent ship run, so I read them but did not change them.

title: Stop Ubicloud fan-outs overshooting the vCPU limit and owners deleting each other's VMs (GST-2852)
body:
Eval fan-outs on the shared Ubicloud project can no longer start more VMs than the room left, an unreadable usage now launches nothing, and two owners whose ids share their first 12 characters no longer delete each other's VMs. This serves the README's promise that heavy suites run on Ubicloud without starving merge checks and canaries.

## What changed

![The runner now books each VM's vCPUs under a lock, refuses when usage can't be read, and keeps the whole owner id](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/JFqjwC1KRvHxdpqNmiYYSnnMlGW5eBN8UI1kmp2296A.png)

The runner now books each VM's vCPUs under a lock, refuses when usage can't be read, and keeps the whole owner id.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The runner now books each VM's vCPUs under a lock, refuses when usage can't be read, and keeps the whole owner id</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
-# owner_id (before)
-217:  echo "${raw:0:12}"
+# owner_id (after)
+232:  [ ${#raw} -le 31 ] || die "UBI_OWNER is ${#raw} characters once lowercased to letters and digits ($raw), and a VM name has room for 31; use a shorter owne
 
-# quota_preflight when usage cannot be read (before)
-1250:        log "quota preflight: could not read the project's vCPU usage; the API's own answer decides"
+# quota_preflight when usage cannot be read (after)
+1361:        die "create refused before any request: $why, so the UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS=$QUOTA_MAX ceiling can't be checked and nothing was launched (UBI_QUOTA_UNREADABLE); rerun once the API answers, or se
 
-# check then create (before): every caller reads the same usage, nothing is booked
-1259:    [ $(( used + need )) -gt "$max" ] || return 0
+# check then book under one lock per machine (after)
+1345:      if [ $(( used + held + need )) -le "$QUOTA_MAX" ]; then
+1346:        echo "$name $need $$ $(date +%s)" >>"$QUOTA_LEDGER"
~~~

</details>

## Why

A second-model review found that shards started together all read the same usage, so at 448 of 464 vCPUs two of them could both pass and reach 480, and that the check let a create through when usage couldn't be read. Owner ids were also cut to 12 characters, so two owners sharing that prefix reaped each other's expired VMs (#3748). Now each machine books its VMs one at a time, a fan-out can ask how many more VMs fit, and VM names carry the whole owner id.

## Blast radius

Only scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh changes behavior; merge checks and canaries set no `UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS`, so they skip the preflight exactly as before (read at the `[ -n "$QUOTA_MAX" ] || return 0` early return in quota_preflight, and the cached-ceiling and no-ceiling creates are exercised in test/ubicloud-runner-verify-quota.test.ts). The copies in gbrain, harness-evals, gbrain-evals and the ubicloud skill keep the old behavior until they sync this file.

<details><summary>Summary, tests, review and docs</summary>

## Summary

Fan-outs could overshoot the 464-vCPU eval limit because the quota check and the create were not atomic, and a failed usage read let the create go ahead. `up` now reads usage and books its VM's vCPUs under one lock per machine (flock through python3, which also works on macOS, and which ends with the process); a booking counts until its create is answered, and bookings from dead processes or older than any create can take are dropped. `ubi-runner.sh room [-s SIZE]` prints how many more VMs fit, so a fan-out driver can size each batch to the room left. With `UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS` set and usage unreadable, the create is refused with `UBI_QUOTA_UNREADABLE`; a cached refusal maximum is the API's own limit, so there the API still decides. VM names carry the whole owner id (up to 31 characters, longer is refused with `UBI_OWNER_TOO_LONG`), `recover` accepts those ids, and a VM that an older runner copy named under the 12-character cut form still counts as the long owner's when this machine's VM record lists it in the old five-column form. New record rows carry a sixth column, `full`, so a current 12-character owner's VMs are never adopted by a longer owner sharing the prefix.

## Test Coverage

All new code paths named below have test coverage, against the fake Ubicloud API (no real VMs):
- Two `up`s started together at 448 of 464 vCPUs create one VM; the other is refused with the first one's booking named, and `room` reports 1, 0, then 1 after teardown.
- A dead-process booking and an aged booking are pruned; a create answered 503 and then found by lookup releases its booking.
- Unreadable usage is refused under `UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS` (with and without a wait), `room` says unknown, and a cached ceiling or no ceiling still creates.
- Owners `gstackminder1` and `gstackminder2` reap only their own VMs; the cut form is reaped only from an older copy's record row, never from a current 12-character owner's row; `recover` accepts a 13-character owner.
- Mutations (no lock, owner cut back to 12, cut form accepted without the record, the five-column check dropped) each fail a new case.

Not covered: the lock-busy path (quota_lock's 300-second timeout has no test knob).

Tests ran: ubicloud 37

## Pre-Landing Review

Pass 1 (one batched specialist reader) found 3 issues, all fixed: `recover` still rejected owners longer than 12 characters; a 13-character owner could adopt a current 12-character owner's VMs from the shared record; and booking-pruning paths had no tests. One fix-check found nothing blocking. A second-model adversarial read found nothing blocking and recommended shipping as is.

Gate edits: none detected (0 listed, 0 read; patterns: gate scan tagged 0 hunks)

## Review notes

Left open, all below the blocking floor:
- The quota lock is held through the whole usage read, and lock waits don't count against `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT`; under a slow API, late shards are refused rather than overshooting.
- A long owner no longer reaps old cut-name VMs that this machine didn't record; they run to their TTL with nobody reaping them, and an owner whose id is exactly that 12-character prefix can still reap them.
- `UBI_OWNER_TOO_LONG` is checked when the script loads, so it also blocks read-only commands for an owner longer than 31 characters.
- On a host without python's `fcntl` (Git Bash), the lock error says "could not take this machine's quota lock" instead of naming the missing module.
- When a create's outcome stays unknown, its booking is released before the script stops.
- `recover --owner <cut form>` writes a six-column row, so a recovered old-form VM isn't reaped by the long owner.
- docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md doesn't mention that only five-column record rows count for the cut form.

## Exploratory QA

Smoke checks were the focused fake-API tests above, plus a manual `recover` run with a 13-character owner (exit 0). No UI.

## Design Review

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Review bot comments

No review bot comments.

## Plan Completion

Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix (Plan: exempt).

## Issues

Fixes #3748

## Verification Results

No Step 8.1 obligations (no plan).

## TODOS

</details>

## Documentation
**Scope:** the diff from 18652ccc to the working tree on ubicloud-quota-booking-full-owner (ubi-runner.sh quota lock and booking, the new `room` command, `UBI_QUOTA_UNREADABLE`, full owner ids up to 31 characters), checked against the docs that describe the Ubicloud runner.

**Result:** docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md and the changelog.d fragment already cover the change. docs/skills.md now names `gstack-ubi room` in the /ubicloud summary. README.md and docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md are still accurate.

**Debt:** ubicloud/SKILL.md.tmpl (the agent-loaded skill) does not mention `room`, `UBI_QUOTA_UNREADABLE` or the 31-character owner limit. Updating it needs a template edit followed by gen:skill-docs, which this audit was not permitted to run.

title: Keep reviewer product challenges open on the approval page
body:
/autoplan's approval page no longer turns a reviewer's objection to a plan's scope, build order or direction into a default "keep your direction", because only lines the owner actually wrote now count as the owner's direction. The person approving a plan sees every reviewer's product challenge as a lettered choice instead of missing it.

<details><summary>What changed, why, review and tests</summary>

## What changed

Before: in the replayed GHome-shaped run, round 1's build-order (F4) and promise-scope (F18) challenges disappeared once round 2 stayed silent about them, and round 2's one-voice ordering challenge (d1) was recommended as "keep your direction", because the planning agent's own draft counted as the owner's direction. The page had 2 lettered items. After: F4, F18 and d1 are lettered proposals recommending the reviewer's change (a: take the change, b: keep the plan's draft), the day-one table is the first thing on the page, and the page has 7 lettered items.

- **Owner's words.** `lib/autoplan-owner-text.ts` parses `### Owner's words` (one quoted bullet each), `### Day one` and `### What it won't do yet`. Reviewers report `changes` on any finding that changes scope, cost, direction, packaging or ordering, at any severity, and `user_challenge` with `owner_quote: <n>` only when the change goes against quote n. Quotes feed the owner-words redaction index from every plan text the run kept, so a quote a later revision removed stays redacted in public exports.
- **Gate items** (`lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts`). A challenge to a quoted owner line keeps today's both-voices rule. A finding with `changes` against agent-written text becomes a `proposal` item; its `changes` is scope, cost or direction when any row names one, so its cost line reopens the phase. Declining a proposal behind a Critical or High finding keeps the plan's draft and carries the finding into the build as a blocking task. A plan with no Owner's words section keeps today's defaults plus one `confirm_direction` item. App plans get day-one and cut questions.
- **Open challenges carry across rounds.** An earlier round's challenge stays on the page until the owner answers it, a later challenge or settled row covers it, or the confirm round marks it `resolves`. A later round staying silent closes nothing.
- **Briefs and docs.** `render --captain` and the owner brief open with the day-one table, the cuts and the owner's words. `docs/unattended.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` and the Capy captain guide describe the new items.

## Why

"The approval page hid the reviewer's build-order and scope objections behind keep your direction." The planning agent's draft was treated as the owner's own direction, so a one-voice product challenge defaulted to no change and an earlier round's challenge vanished when the next round said nothing. Now only the owner's quoted words are direction, and every other recommended change reaches the owner as a choice.

## Blast radius

The change touches the /autoplan gate builder, its reviewer prompt (`autoplan/DRIVER.md`, regenerated), the confirm and revise paths, the captain and owner briefs, and public exports. A plan with no Owner's words section keeps today's defaults plus one auto item, which the replay controls show (script ran: lettered items on main 5b4fa9e vs this branch, below), and the redaction index was reproduced leaking before the fix and redacted after it (repro).

## Summary

Reviewers' product objections were being defaulted away on the approval page. The gate now separates the owner's quoted words from the agent's draft, turns any other recommended change into a lettered proposal whose cost line matches what revise does, keeps earlier rounds' challenges open until answered, and opens briefs with the day-one table. Review fixes in this PR keep removed owner quotes redacted, pick the strongest `changes` value for a proposal, and keep a declined High proposal as a blocking build task.

## Test Coverage

Every changed source file has changed tests that reference it (per-file map from the coverage step: for example `lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts` 2 changed tests, `lib/gate-list.ts` 4, `lib/headless-artifacts.ts` 2 of 119 referencing).

- `test/autoplan-day-one-gate.test.ts` (24 tests): a synthetic, public-safe replay (titles and fields only; no owner replies or real quotes) plus negative controls. Lettered items, same fixture on main 5b4fa9e → this branch: replay 2 → 7; (a) a challenge to a quoted owner line: 2 → 7, keeps "keep your direction"; (b) no Owner's words section: 2 → 8, today's default plus one confirm item; (c) a round-1 challenge resolved or answered: 2 → 5, does not resurface. The review fixes add an ordering-plus-scope proposal test, a declined-High-proposal test and a removed-quote redaction test; the pair and redaction tests fail when their fixes are reverted.
- Pre-existing failure: `autoplan-gate-judgment` "b, as-is, or a token reply…" hits Bun's 5 s default timeout on main 5b4fa9e too (same machine, same file set: 490 pass, 1 fail). The /ship lane runs with `--timeout=30000`, where it passes.

Tests ran: targeted 1665

## Pre-Landing Review

Full-depth review of a gate-class change: batched specialist and red team, a fix-check, the native adversarial voice and a cross-family outside voice, the targeted money reader, then two owner-granted scoped fix-checks (the review fixes, then the docs-audit edits). Six findings were fixed, both fix-checks were clean once two prose lines the collector misread as Critical were ruled false positives, and the outside voice ran on GPT-6.1 Sol because the Codex CLI is not installed.

### Known gaps

- On the two-voice challenge path (`lib/autoplan-gate.ts`, `n.changes ?? o.changes`, unchanged from main), an ordering plus scope pair answered b can settle a scope change without re-review. It gets fixed after this PR lands, in one small follow-up PR off main with a failing-first test.
- `ledgerWords` can mark a quote verified from another repo's approvals record when the branch names match (red-team #5, adversarial #3). It gets fixed in the same follow-up PR, with a failing-first test.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- The table path of `parseRecordFindings` (`lib/autoplan-reconcile.ts`) reads no `owner_quote` or `resolves` column, so hand-run records cannot carry them (red-team #4).
- A settled row's correlates can close a different open challenge in `openEarlier` (first fix-check #1).
- An owner item answered b is asked again in a later round; agent-invented owner quotes count as direction; generic quotes over-redact; owner items with no phase can be refused at revise (adversarial Lows).
- A High proposal answered b is proposed again when another item reopens its phase, because the blocking-task origin keeps it open (granted fix-check #1).
- A CEO-only run no longer records the auto-kept decision row for a High proposal in `decisions.jsonl` or the report's conservative choices; the finding still appears under Findings (granted fix-check #2).
- The declined-High test's `buildTasks` assertion holds with or without the fix; only its `settledIds` assertion depends on it (granted fix-check #4).

## Exploratory QA

Functional surface: the gate builder on synthetic run directories, 6 captures, verdict pass. A below-High `changes` finding in a plan with Owner's words becomes one lettered proposal; a Medium challenge with a bad owner quote, which reached the gate as nothing before the fix, is now a proposal; a round-2 Low row that only correlates with a round-1 challenge no longer closes it.

**Status:** updated. Three authored docs were stale against the new /autoplan approval page. Each now gets a small factual fix, and nothing is blocked.

**Scope:** base `5b4fa9ea3` to head `247b77fde` on `approval-page-keeps-reviewer-product-challenges-open`. That covers 19 committed files, one unstaged edit (the changelog.d fragment), and nothing staged or untracked. The owner and captain briefs now open with a day-one block, and public exports redact quotes from the plan's Owner's words. I found related docs by searching all tracked docs and templates. The gate step lists proposal, confirm-direction, day-one and cut items, plus earlier-round challenges that stay open. The agent-words rule lists every `uc` item kind. The public-copy "Whose words" bullet includes Owner's words quotes, removed ones included. The shadow `item_class` list has the five new classes. The owner brief opens with the day-one block.

title: Never let a later docs-audit line override an earlier blocked result (GST-2349)
body:
/ship's documentation audit no longer accepts a passing result when an earlier line from the same audit said "blocked". The blocked verdict now carries forward, and the audit gets one free chance to restate it.
What changed - **An earlier blocked line can't be overridden.** If one JSON line for an audit says "blocked" or lists a blocker, and a later JSON line for the same audit (the last line) drops that, `gstack-docs-candidate result` no longer accepts the last line. It prints `FORMAT_REPAIR:` and re-asks once without spending an attempt. The reply must stay blocked and keep every earlier blocker, though it may add more. - **This also covers a last line whose only fault is its format.** Before, that line could be repaired back to "current". Now it can't. - **A real content problem on the last line still spends an attempt**, as before. - **Wording now matches the code.** The docs-audit step no longer says it "parses only the LAST nonempty line". A new changelog entry corrects #4285's claim to what the parser checks: a later JSON line or a re-ask reply can't drop a blocked verdict, but a blocker written only in prose depends on the re-ask reading it.
Why The review of #4285 found that a blocked result line followed by an unfenced "current" JSON line as the very last line was accepted as current. Main behaved the same way before #4285, but #4285's changelog promised more than that. This closes the gap with the same one-way rule #4285 applies to its re-ask.
Blast radius Only the documentation audit's result parser (`lib/ship-docs-result.ts`), one sentence in `ship/sections/documentation.md`, the troubleshooting entry, and a new changelog entry that corrects #4285's claim (the landed entry is left as is). Output with a single result line behaves exactly as before.

A direct CLI probe shows the code does refuse a swapped blocker; only the test is missing. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:95` A child that prints a blocked line, fixes the blocker, then ends with a valid updated line is now refused and ends blocked (fails closed; product call). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:47` When the last line parses, the drop path ignores content problems on earlier lines and always returns repairable: true, unlike the text-follows path. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-docs-result.ts:41` A reworded earlier blocker now triggers the drop path (new friction); an earlier blocked result not on its own JSON line is not detected (older limit). ## Exploratory QA Smoke probes against `bin/gstack-docs-candidate result` at bc69621: current only → `DOCS_RESULT: ok`; blocked then current → refused; blocked then blocked with a swapped blocker → refused; blocked then the same blocked line → `DOCS_RESULT: ok status=blocked`. title: Let an owner ruling close only the finding and head it names, on full passes and Step 11 findings (GST-2273)
body:
An owner's ruling now closes a finding on a round-2 full pass and on a cross-model (Step 11) finding, as docs/review-policy.md already promises, and it closes only the finding and the head the owner named. This supersedes #4272, which a cross-family audit held because rulings there could close more than the owner ruled.

## Why

Before this change, only the narrow re-check after a fix read the owner's rulings. Crews parked #4248, #4266, #4257 and harness-evals#361 at the round cap with the owner's ruling recorded and nothing applying it. #4272 added that, but the audit of its head 36ce6ad (handoffs/GSTA-495/sol-audit-36ce6ad.md in the Captain's drive) showed three wrong closes. /ship's read-only review of the rebuilt head fa3e4a2 then found a fourth: a gate finding that only a dispatch ledger holds could be ruled. #4272 was at its review-round cap, so the fix ships here as a fresh PR with its own review.

## Summary

- **Full passes and Step 11 findings.** `gstack-review-read` applies each approved `gstack-approvals rule` made at the commit a review row read, so a round-2 full pass whose only blocker is ruled reads `CURRENT`. `gstack-review-scope summary` counts a ruled finding that no row records as `noted` instead of `unrecorded`.
- **Only the head the owner ruled.** A ruling at an earlier head closes nothing on a later row, even when that head lies inside the row's range.
- **Only the finding the owner named.** When two findings share a fingerprint (one line, one reviewer), a ruling by that fingerprint closes neither, so the owner rules each by its ledger id. A bare ledger id that repeats in every pass closes nothing.
- **Only /ship rows.** The summary takes rulings from the run's newest via:ship review row. A manual review row logged later can't choose them.
- **Gate findings are never ruled.** This now includes a gate finding only a dispatch ledger holds: `ledgerBlockers` carries `gate` and `gate_id` from the reader's line.

title: Say in the release docs that the stable cut also waits on commit statuses (GST-2252)
body:
The release docs now say that the stable release cut treats a failed commit status as red and a pending one as still going, not only check runs. This keeps docs/releases.md's definition of a green commit matching what the cut has done since #4257, so people reading the release rules see the real gate.
Details ## What changed One sentence in the "green" definition of docs/releases.md, plus its changelog entry. Before: "…count as red even though GitHub's default list hides them. A commit with a check run still going is skipped…" After: "…count as red even though GitHub's default list hides them. A failed commit status counts as red too, and a pending one counts as still going. A commit with a check run still going is skipped…" ## Why #4257's documentation audit found that the release docs described only check runs, while the stable cut also reads commit statuses. That gap was accepted at merge with a promised follow-up; this is it. Readers who rely on docs/releases.md to know why a commit was or wasn't cut now get the actual rule. ## Blast radius Documentation only: docs/releases.md and a changelog.d fragment. No code, prompt or test changes. The sentence was checked against the code by reading lib/ci-head-checks.ts (commit-status contexts map success to pass, pending to pending, anything else to fail) and crew/scripts/release-cut.ts gateVerdict (fail rows make the head red; pending rows return pending, so the cut moves to the next older commit). ## Summary The stable cut's green rule has counted commit statuses since #4257; the docs now say so. ## Test Coverage No runtime file changed, so no new tests. title: Accept a requested docs fix when the audit names the file with a line number
body:
/ship no longer refuses a small docs fix just because the documentation audit named the file with a line number, such as `docs/guide.md:8: wording`.
What changed - `finish --docs-requested ` checks that the audit's blockers or decisions name the file. The path may now be followed by `:` or `::` (for example `changelog.d/engine-parity-decisions.md:8: wording` or `...md:8:12 wording`). Before, only forms like `...md: line 8` were accepted. - A different file whose name starts with the same path, such as `docs/KEY_FILES.md.tmpl:8:` when the fix is to `docs/KEY_FILES.md`, still doesn't match.
Why Vorflux hit this. The audit asked for a one-line fix to a file and named it in the common `path:line` form, the fix was correct, and /ship still stopped with "is not named in the audit result's blockers or decisions".

title: Open pull requests with three plain lines and land each one as a single commit (GST-2737)
body:
/ship now opens pull requests with at most three plain lines, folds every other section, and every merge lands as one commit titled with the PR title. Why: people outside the project read PRs and the commit log to judge it, and long bodies full of in-house words hid what changed. Nothing to do: PRs opened before 2026-11-18 only get warnings; a repository without `.gstack/plain-titles.json` sees no refusals.
What changed - **Folded bodies.** `gstack-post` turns each `## ` section into a collapsed `
` section when it posts, and puts Agent notes last. `gstack-post fold --body-file F` prints the folded body without posting it (new `lib/pr-body-shape.ts`). - **A check on the opening.** In a repository with `.gstack/plain-titles.json`, `gstack-post`, `gstack-plain-title check --body-file` and the Plain title workflow refuse a body that shows more than three lines or 600 characters before its first fold, or uses a listed in-house word above Agent notes (`PLAIN_BODY_REFUSED`). Comments only get warnings. `body_since` keeps older PRs to warnings. - **One commit per merge.** Every `gstack-ship-queue land` path (direct, queued and stacked) passes the subject ` (#n)` and a body made of the PR's opening lines plus every distinct `Co-authored-by:` and other branch trailer (new `lib/squash-message.ts`). `--body-file` replaces the opening and `--dry-run` prints the message. Commits of a stacked parent that already landed are left out. A high-severity secret finding in the message refuses the land. - **Release and repair PRs** use the same shape. A release PR's commit body is its Release notes section, one plain line per change with its PR. - **Two policy settings**, both refused by older gstack: `history: no-rewrite` (squash only, `check-history --plan rebase` refused) and `land.merge_commit_paths` (keep a merge commit for PRs that touch those paths). - **/ship templates** write What changed, Tests and Agent notes instead of Summary and Test plan. New guide: `docs/writing-prs.md`. </details> <details><summary>Blast radius</summary> Every repository that ships with gstack gets the folded bodies and the commit message on land. Refusals apply only where `.gstack/plain-titles.json` exists. The two policy settings are opt-in and need `min_gstack_version` at the release that adds them. </details> <details><summary>Tests</summary> - New: `test/pr-body-shape.test.ts`, `test/squash-message.test.ts`. - Updated: gstack-post, plain-title, ship publication gates, prose-lint, the three merge paths, release body, ship-policy no-rewrite, policy floor tests. - Added during review: an older or exempt PR only gets warnings about its opening; Dependabot branches are exempt; a broken policy file still lets comments post; re-posting a folded body replaces each section once; file names in the body don't count as prose. Each of the last two tests failed before its fix. - The free test suite passed in CI at this head (Free Tests run 44084192476, 1681 files), with the macOS and Windows jobs green. `bun run typecheck` is clean. </details> <details><summary>Documentation</summary> **Status:** updated. Two factual fixes, no blockers. **Scope:** this branch's changes from e9f38d6 to 708fd45 (46 committed files, nothing staged, unstaged or untracked). It covers the new PR body shape (three plain lines, folded sections), the one-commit merge subject and body, `history: no-rewrite`, `land.merge_commit_paths`, and `gstack-post fold`. I checked the docs against lib/plain-title.ts, lib/pr-body-shape.ts, lib/gstack-post.ts, lib/ship-policy.ts, lib/squash-message.ts and bin/gstack-ship-queue. **Documentation health:** - `README.md`: current. The /ship row links to writing-prs.md. - `docs/writing-prs.md`: current. New page; its limits, word list, commands and settings match the code. - `docs/ship-policy.md`: current. The history, land and plain-title rows match the policy validator. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: updated. The prose-lint section now names `## What changed` instead of `## Summary`; PLAIN_BODY_REFUSED is current. - `docs/skills.md`: updated. The PR body section now describes three plain lines, folded sections and the What changed / Tests sections, and its prose-lint `--sections` example matches the template. - `changelog.d/plain-pr-bodies.md`: current. Read only, not edited. **Coverage debt:** `gstack-post fold` and the commit message that `land` writes have reference and how-to coverage in writing-prs.md, plus troubleshooting for PLAIN_BODY_REFUSED. There is no tutorial, which is a common gap, not a critical one. **Diagram drift:** none found. </details> <!-- gstack:agent-notes --> <details><summary>Agent notes</summary> Closes GST-2737. Captain go 2026-11-17 (GSTA-36); gate answers A1, B1, C1 to G1, H1, I1, J1. Policy key versions are set to 1.100.0.0 ahead of the release that ships them. Main merged in once under the Captain's rule-13 grant (8d949f6): the only conflict was the `lib/gstack-post.ts` import block after #4365 landed, resolved as the union of both import lists; this PR's own lines are unchanged. title: Keep checking custom skill contracts that still list the removed test-after-edit item (GST-2811)
body:
If you wrote your own skill whose contract still lists `check_after_last_edit`, the optional Stop hook now skips only that item and keeps checking the rest, where before the whole contract read as invalid. This keeps the #4428 removal from switching off a custom skill's other checks.

Nothing to do. Until you delete the item, the hook prints a `SKILL_CONTRACT_SKIPPED` line naming the file and the item.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `validateContract` (`lib/skill-contract.ts`) skips an item of the removed kind and records one warning for it. A contract whose only items use that kind is still invalid, because nothing would be left to check, so the hook lets the stop through and prints its usual error line.
- The Stop hook and `gstack-skill-contract check` print the warning on stderr each time they read such a contract.
- Tests: a parse test for a mixed contract, a Stop-hook test where a custom skill with both items still blocks on its missing report and prints the warning, and a `check` test that the warning prints once while the other items are still checked.
- The routing doc describes the new behavior. A new changelog entry corrects the unreleased #4428 entry, which says such a contract becomes invalid. That landed entry is left as it is, because landed entries are never edited.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes (below the blocking floor, not fixed here)</summary>

- `lib/skill-contract.ts:127` A skipped item's id is not counted when checking for duplicate ids, so a hand-written contract that repeats an id is accepted or rejected depending on item order. No check result is lost.
- `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-contract-stop-hook.ts:70` The warning repeats on every Stop and goes only to stderr, not to the hook log, so many users won't see it. The file's header comment still says the hook prints one stderr line only when it fails open.
- `bin/gstack-skill-contract:72` Two stderr writes end their template string with a literal line break instead of `\n`. The output is the same.
- `changelog.d/keep-custom-contracts-with-removed-item.md:1` The unreleased #4428 entry contradicts this one. The new entry now says it corrects it, so whoever writes the release notes can drop the older sentence.

</details>

<details><summary>Checks</summary>

- Full free suite: carried from CI at the pushed head (see the receipt).
- Focused: the contract, Stop-hook, descriptions and route suites; typecheck and the test typecheck ratchet; parity, module-size and `gen:skill-docs` freshness. A negative control showed the new `check` test fails when the warning loop is removed.
- Smoke, 3 probes on the current tree, all passing: the hook on a mixed custom skill (exit 0, blocks only on the missing report, one `SKILL_CONTRACT_SKIPPED` line); a contract made only of the removed kind (exit 0, lets the stop through, one `SKILL_CONTRACT_STATE_ERROR` line); `check` on the mixed skill (exit 1, only the report missing).

</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Follow-up to GST-2811 that Garry asked for. Thread GSTA-574 for Captain GStack Minder. gstack: ok 1.99.5.0 for=ship.

Review: two rounds on the final tree aa985f67. Round 1 (specialist, adversarial, second-model review from openai/gpt-6.1-sol) found nothing blocking; its one test-gap was fixed. Round 2 reran the specialist on the frozen tree because round 1's record was logged after its fix landed; it found the changelog contradiction above.

## Documentation
**Status:** current. No permitted doc needed a change. One wording problem in a CHANGELOG fragment is left to /ship because fragments are protected (see decisions).

**Scope:** `99256a86..34260f58` on `keep-custom-contracts-with-removed-item` (3 commits, 7 files) plus the unstaged edit to `changelog.d/keep-custom-contracts-with-removed-item.md`. Nothing is staged and there are no new files. Audited every doc that mentions skill contracts: `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, `docs/install.md`, `docs/skill-gates.md`, the contract block in `review/SKILL.md.tmpl`, and both related `changelog.d` fragments. Checked them against `lib/skill-contract.ts`, `bin/gstack-skill-contract`, `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-contract-stop-hook.ts` and `lib/changelog-fragments.ts`.
