title: Keep a pull request's review count intact when a posted description brings its own run history (GST-2707)
body:
When `/ship` posts a pull request's description, the count of earlier review rounds now always comes from the PR's real history. Before this fix, a description that brought extra history blocks of its own could make gstack count one round where there were three. Why: the per-PR round cap (R51) depends on that count, and it's the last gap before crews can stop counting rounds by hand. Nothing to do as a reader.
What changed ## What changed - `lib/gstack-post.ts` `keepRuns`: when a post brings its own Agent notes, every `gstack-receipt-runs` block the history reader would recognize is removed from them, not only the first one at a line start. The reader takes the first block it finds, so a second block placed before the receipt used to stand in for the real history. Exactly one block goes back: the live body's history (earlier runs, started stubs and the replaced receipt), right after the posted receipt. When the live body has no history, none goes back. - A post whose notes hold no receipt yet (the body between a review stub and the receipt write) now gets the live body's runs block in place of the first block it brings, so the PR's started stubs are kept. Review found that the first version of this change dropped them. - A post that brings no Agent notes is unchanged. - `docs/review-policy.md` says the posted body's own runs blocks are dropped.
Blast radius ## Blast radius Only `gstack-post pr-body` merges of a body that carries an Agent notes section. Reading history, writing receipts and stubs, and posts without Agent notes are untouched.
Documentation ## Documentation Scope: the diff from c5250ded to the branch head (lib/gstack-post.ts, test/pr-review-history.test.ts, docs/review-policy.md, changelog.d/strip-incoming-receipt-runs.md), plus related mentions of runs blocks and GST-2706 in docs/ship-policy.md and docs/troubleshooting.md. The worktree had no staged, unstaged or untracked changes. Result: current. docs/review-policy.md (rounds per pull request, step 1) already says that a /ship body post drops any runs block it brings, so only the live history is counted. The changelog fragment describes the same fix for users. No edits were needed. Debt: none found.
Tests ## Test plan - Two free tests in `test/pr-review-history.test.ts`. The first posts a body with two runs blocks before its receipt: it fails on main (c5250ded) and passes here. The second reposts a body whose notes hold only a started stub, with a forged runs block before it: it failed on the first head of this PR (2c95943) and passes now. - `test/pr-review-history.test.ts` and `test/gstack-post.test.ts`: 74 pass, 0 fail at 106e83d, after main was merged in. Typecheck and the module-size ratchet pass. - The full free suite ran in CI at 106e83d (run 44096565563, 37499 tests).

title: Approval page re-reviews two-reviewer scope changes and checks quotes only against this repository
body:
/autoplan's approval page now re-reviews a scope change both reviewers raise, asks a plan with no Owner's words to confirm its direction, and checks owner quotes only against this repository's approvals record. This keeps the rule that only the owner's own words set a plan's direction, and there is nothing for the reader to do.
What changed, why and blast radius ## What changed ![With a .gstack-project marker above the repository, the quote lookup now finds the owner's recorded words where the approvals record writes them](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/Z7XsEMqmdQowvwR77RF-a-_hWmods1PSHgH0Bf1_LJc.png) With a .gstack-project marker above the repository, the quote lookup now finds the owner's recorded words where the approvals record writes them.
Before/after as text: With a .gstack-project marker above the repository, the quote lookup now finds the owner's recorded words where the approvals record writes them ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ bun ledger-probe.ts marker # same fixture, after the fix -$ bun ledger-probe.ts marker # .gstack-project marker above the repo, before the fix { "scenario": "marker", "writer_slug": "this-repo", "record_slug": "this-repo", + "words": [ + "I want to remember what I promised people" + ] - "words": [] } ~~~
- **A pair that names a scope change is a scope change.** When both reviewers challenge the plan and one says build order while the other says scope, the item used to take the first reviewer's label, so taking it settled without another review. It now takes the heaviest change either reviewer names (scope, cost or direction before packaging or ordering). One-reviewer proposals already worked this way, and both paths now share `heaviestChanges`. - **No Owner's words means one confirm question for two-reviewer challenges too.** A one-reviewer challenge on a plan with no Owner's words section already added "confirm the plan's direction is yours". A two-reviewer challenge whose recommendation keeps the plan now adds it as well. A two-reviewer challenge that recommends the change adds nothing. - **Quotes are verified against this repository only.** The approvals reader used to scan every project folder for a record named after the current branch. It now reads only this repository's record. The slug comes from `GSTACK_PROJECT_SLUG`, cleaned the way the writer cleans it, or from the repository's slug cache entry. A `.gstack-project` marker no longer moves that lookup away from where the record is written. It never resolves the slug fresh, because that writes outside the run. With no known slug, a quote stays unverified. ## Why "Close the known gaps 1 to 3 that #4431 left on the approval page." A scope change two reviewers raise now goes back for review. A plan without the owner's words asks the owner to confirm its direction. A quote shows as verified only when this repository's own record holds it. ## Summary #4431 kept reviewer challenges open on the approval page but left three gaps. This change closes them. In review, the Red Team found that the new quote lookup missed records in projects with a `.gstack-project` marker, and that is fixed here too. ## Blast radius The change touches the approval page builder (`lib/autoplan-gate.ts`, `lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts`) and adds an optional `scope` argument to `readVersionedSlugCache` in `lib/bin-context.ts`. Every other caller passes no options and keeps reading the marker entry as before (verified by reading each caller and by the passing slug-parity and project-marker suites). The verified flag only changes a display label, never a recommendation (`gate-list.ts:171-172` read).
Tests, review and QA ## Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. Six new tests are in `test/autoplan-day-one-gate.test.ts`. Three failed on main at c5250ded before the fix (ordering plus scope pair, missing confirm item, another repository's record verifying a quote). One more fails on the pre-review code: the marker case read no record. The new confirm question appears in the shared small-plan fixture, so 17 existing expectations in five files list one more item and the matching counts. Tests ran: targeted 200 Tests ran: test 1679 (files, carried from CI run 44089136798) ## Pre-Landing Review Round 1 was a full review by a batched specialist (testing, security, state machines) and the Red Team. It found no blocking issues and 3 informational findings in the quote lookup, all fixed in 3e376907. A check of the fix found nothing. A second-model review (gpt-6.1-sol) on the final head was clean, and the targeted money reader found nothing. The native adversarial voice raised the notes below. None blocks. Gate edits: none detected (20 listed, 18 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts:46` quote can read as unverified when no repository slug cache entry exists on the gate-building machine (marker-only cache, mirror-only record, env-pinned writer, 'unknown' slug); display label only - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts:46` summary paragraph of the native voice (no blocking findings; four Low findings listed separately) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts:126` confirmDirectionItem doc comment still says a two-voice challenge adds no confirm item; autoplan-gate.ts:238 now adds one when the recommendation keeps the plan and there is no Owner's words section - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-gate.ts:238` runs that straddle the upgrade may get the confirm-direction question again (keptIds now includes two-reviewer ids), and an amendment recorded under the old native-first changes value keeps it - INFORMATIONAL `lib/approval-record.ts:99` pre-existing: the project-user drive mirror that locate() writes is never read by ledgerWords ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke on the quote lookup through a probe script with its own temporary fixtures. Before the fix, the marker case read no record; captures 002 and 004 replayed it. After the fix, all three contracts pass on the current source (captures 005 to 007): cache fallback, marker above the repository, and no known slug. Verdict: pass. ## Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped. ## Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped. ## Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). The plan is recorded under Approvals below. ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
## Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation needed changes for this branch. **Scope:** 10 committed files from ab114c53 to 3e376907d. There were no staged, unstaged or new files. Three source files changed internal behavior of the /autoplan approval page (`lib/autoplan-gate-items.ts`, `lib/autoplan-gate.ts`, `lib/bin-context.ts`). The other seven are six test files and one changelog.d fragment. The docs were checked by searching every authored .md and .tmpl file for the changed concepts and reading the matching passages, plus AGENTS.md and README.md. **Documentation health:** - AGENTS.md: current - README.md: current - autoplan/DRIVER.md.tmpl: current (the findings `changes` contract already ranks scope, cost and direction above packaging and ordering) - autoplan/DRIVER.md: current (generated) - docs/unattended.md: current **Coverage debt:** None. The change adds no new commands, flags, environment variables or skills. The new export `heaviestChanges` and the new `scope` option on `readVersionedSlugCache` are internal and have no user-facing documentation, which is expected for internal helpers. Quote checking is now scoped to this repository's approvals record. That is covered only by the changelog fragment, which is reference-only and adequate for a fix. **Diagram drift:** None. No touched component appears in an ASCII or Mermaid diagram. ## Test plan - [x] `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=30000` on the six autoplan test files plus the bin-context, slug-parity and project-marker suites: 200 pass, 0 fail - [x] Free Tests (CI run 44089136798 at 3e376907): green, carried as the full test run

title: Stop giving bug reports a special rule in gstack's router (GST-2873)
body:
gstack's router no longer gives bug reports a special check-the-cause, fix-it-test-first rule, and its description no longer lists debugging, so the model fixes a bug the way it would without gstack. This keeps gstack to the parts that measurably help, and on 26 hard real bugs the rule gave no clear gain.

Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `SKILL.md.tmpl` drops the bug-report routing line and its **Failures** block. `generateFailureRouting()` goes with them.
- The router's description (`SKILL.md.tmpl` and `ROUTER_DESCRIPTION` in `lib/harness-register.ts`) no longer lists debugging, so a bug report doesn't load the router and fall through to /qa.
- The two paid evals of the removed rule (`router-failure-verified-cause`, `router-failure-triage-resolves`), their fixture and arm tests, and their registry, host and duration entries are retired. A free test checks that the router has no bug-fix route.
- Docs: `docs/skills.md` says why, and that the bugs line in the optional CLAUDE.md routing block stays; `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` drops the retired router eval arm.

</details>

<details><summary>Why remove it instead of slimming it</summary>

On 26 real gbrain bugs that plain Opus 5.5 had failed once, gstack v1.99.3.0 with this rule fixed 3 and plain Opus fixed 2: +3.8 points, with a 95% interval of -11.5 to +19.2 (paired bootstrap over tasks, 10,000 resamples), 3 wins and 2 losses. The test could detect about 23 points. A slimmer rule would still be text with no measured gain, and Garry asked for bug fixes to run plain, so the route goes entirely. Planning, review, /verify, /qa and /ship are unchanged, and so is the bugs line gstack offers for your CLAUDE.md, which this test didn't measure.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes (below the blocking floor, not fixed here)</summary>

- Existing OpenClaw, Hermes and Dots registrations keep the old router description until the harness is registered again, because `lib/harness-register.ts` writes it only at registration. The old text just sends debugging requests to a router with no special rule.
- The published interval was recounted from the raw hard-tier data with the preregistered method and matches: +3.8 points, -11.5 to +19.2.

</details>

<details><summary>Checks</summary>

- Full free suite: carried from CI at the pushed head (see the receipt).
- Focused: skill-validation, codex-host, eng-finding-retry-budget, harness-register, parity, gen-skill-docs, touchfile and budget suites; typecheck and the test typecheck ratchet; `gen:skill-docs` fresh for both hosts.
- No paid eval ran. The eval selector falls back to every gate case because a shared resolver file changed, but the only rendered change is the router itself; CI's PR eval route ran no slices, and the release gate on main covers the rest.

</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Refs GST-2873. Thread GSTA-574 for Captain GStack Minder. gstack: ok 1.99.5.0 for=ship.

Review: full depth (the diff retires gate-tier eval cases). Pass 1 (specialist, red-team, coverage audit) found one below-floor gap, fixed in 61ac9eb1. title: /sync-gbrain's memory stage re-imports ceo-plans and design-docs when the artifacts source is registered at a host-side clone, because the skip guard matches only the worktree and state-root paths
body:
## What happened

On a machine that is also the brain host, the artifacts repo is registered in gbrain at a clone path, which is the shape of the hookup command gstack prints for a brain host. `/sync-gbrain`'s memory stage then does not recognise that source and does not exclude `ceo-plan` and `design-doc`, so it imports them a second time. That is the duplication the default guard was added to stop (#2922).

The guard `federatedCuratedSourceId()` finds the source only by path. Verified at `e8c8625bd65fdcc0f0650f982830649d326c4bf4` (main, VERSION 1.99.5.0):

- `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:241-245`: `federatedCuratedSourceId` keeps a federated row only when `isArtifactsSourceRow` accepts it.
- `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:248-262`: `isArtifactsSourceRow` accepts a `local_path` that is the worktree (`GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE`, default `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`) or the state root, and nothing else.
- `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:305-324`: with no `--sources` and no `GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_SOURCES`, no match means the selection excludes nothing, `ceo-plan` and `design-doc` included, so the selection carries no `--sources` filter, with the stage line `(default: no federated gstack source registered)` (`:1627`). (Transcripts have their own consent gate; this report is only about the two curated types.)
- `bin/gstack-artifacts-init:512-525` prints `gbrain sources add <id> --url <https> --federated` (or `--path ~/<id>` when the url form is off) "On the brain host", and `docs/gbrain-sync.md:46-49` describes step 5 the same way and says that on the same machine `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` "does the same wiring" (it registers the source with `--path "$WORKTREE"`, wireup `:336-350`). Neither form puts the clone at the default worktree path or the state root: `--path ~/<id>` names `~/<id>`, and with `--url` gbrain picks the clone location itself ("--url manages its own clone path", gbrain `src/commands/sources.ts:279`, master `280b5a87`). We did not trace where gbrain puts a `--url` clone; on our machine the registered path is a gbrain-side directory that is neither accepted path (see the live state below).
- `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` is the id override, and the wireup (`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:164-165`) and `brainSyncIndexVerdict` (`bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:274-275`) read it. `federatedCuratedSourceId` does not.

The help text promises the skip: `--sources` says the default is every type "except ceo-plan,design-doc when a federated gstack source already indexes them" (`bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts:521-525`), and `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl:56` says "types a federated gstack source already indexes are skipped". Neither says the source must sit at the worktree path. I read this as a defect in the detection (the promise holds for one registration form only), and the way to fix it as a proposal; see "What would help".

Live state on our machine, gstack 1.99.5.0 (the four files cited above have the same blob SHAs as at `e8c8625b`), gbrain 0.60.728.0, paths and ids shortened or renamed:

```text
$ gstack-gbrain-source-wireup --probe
source_id=acme-gstack-artifacts
worktree=~/.gstack-brain-worktree
worktree_status=absent
gbrain=ok (0.60.728.0)
source_status=registered (different path)

$ gbrain sources list --json        # the one row, trimmed
{"id":"acme-gstack-artifacts","local_path":"~/gbrain-sources/acme-gstack-artifacts","federated":true,"page_count":750}
```

`~/.gstack/.gbrain-sync-state.json` after `/sync-gbrain` lists all eight memory types in the memory stage's `memory_sources`, and its brain-sync row reads "no gbrain artifacts source on this machine, so indexing is not checked here". The artifacts clone has 15 files under `projects/*/ceo-plans/` and 12 `projects/*/*-design-*.md` files, and `gbrain get projects/<project>/<file> --source-id <artifacts source>` finds a page for each of the 27 (slug = path without `.md`, lower-cased). The ingest state (`~/.gstack/.transcript-ingest-state.json`) holds 15 `ceo-plan` and 12 `design-doc` entries with `source_id: default`, and `gbrain list --type ceo-plan --source-id default` returns 15 pages named `ceo-plans/<project>/<date>-<date>-<name>-<hash>` (and `--type design-doc` returns 12). So the same plans and design docs exist twice, in two sources.

## Steps to reproduce

In the style of `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts`: a fake `gbrain` on `PATH` reports one federated source, and only its `local_path` and the env change; the script clears the gstack variables it inherits and runs against a temporary `HOME`. It checks the detection and the selection the memory stage would pass, not the page writes (the duplicate pages are shown above from our live state). Nothing touches a real brain.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
GSTACK_ROOT="${GSTACK_ROOT:-$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack}"
unset GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_SOURCES GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID GSTACK_HOME
T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/shim" "$T/home"
cat > "$T/shim/gbrain" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "sources" ] && [ "$2" = "list" ]; then
  echo "{\"sources\":[{\"id\":\"acme-gstack-artifacts\",\"local_path\":\"$SRC_PATH\",\"federated\":true,\"page_count\":750}]}"
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
SH
chmod +x "$T/shim/gbrain"
cat > "$T/probe.ts" <<TS
const m = await import("$GSTACK_ROOT/bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts");
const sel = m.selectMemorySources(undefined, process.env, true);
console.log("  federatedCuratedSourceId:", m.federatedCuratedSourceId(process.env));
console.log("  --sources filter:", sel.sources ? sel.sources.join(",") : "(none)");
console.log("  why:", sel.why);
TS
run() { HOME="$T/home" PATH="$T/shim:$PATH" bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null "$T/probe.ts"; }
echo "A. federated source registered at a host-side clone"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= SRC_PATH=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts run
echo "B. same source at the wireup worktree path"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID= SRC_PATH="$T/home/.gstack-brain-worktree" run
echo "C. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID set"
GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID=acme-gstack-artifacts SRC_PATH=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts run
echo "D. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE set to the clone"
GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts SRC_PATH=/srv/brain/sources/acme-gstack-artifacts run
rm -rf "$T"
```

Output on gstack 1.99.5.0 (the script was run with `GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_SOURCES` set in the caller's environment, to show that it clears it):

```text
A. federated source registered at a host-side clone
  federatedCuratedSourceId: null
  --sources filter: (none)
  why: default: no federated gstack source registered
B. same source at the wireup worktree path
  federatedCuratedSourceId: acme-gstack-artifacts
  --sources filter: transcript,eureka,learning,timeline,retro,builder-profile-entry
  why: default: ceo-plan,design-doc already indexed by federated source acme-gstack-artifacts
C. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID set
  federatedCuratedSourceId: null
  --sources filter: (none)
  why: default: no federated gstack source registered
D. as A, with GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE set to the clone
  federatedCuratedSourceId: acme-gstack-artifacts
  --sources filter: transcript,eureka,learning,timeline,retro,builder-profile-entry
  why: default: ceo-plan,design-doc already indexed by federated source acme-gstack-artifacts
```

A is the gap, B is the case the guard handles, C shows the override is not read, D shows the one setting that makes the guard accept a clone.

## Readiness report

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.5.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: openclaw global current (1.99.5.0), codex global current (1.99.5.0), claude global current (1.99.5.0)
ok              rescue refs     none in ~/.claude/skills/gstack
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              codex           codex-cli 0.169.0; self-locate ok; model gpt-6.1-sol (source: GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL)
ok              codex probe     cached MODEL_OK, 11m ago (not re-run; --live probes now)
warn            artifacts sync  status error
                                fix: ~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync --status
ok              browse bundle   browse/dist built
ok              binaries        find-browse, design, pdf, gstack-global-discover launch (4 of 4)
ok              cso             native helper 1.99.5.0 (0326b144af36)
ok              claude code     2.1.311 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal largest of 2: 585.0 KiB
ok              guard log       232 decisions (10 denied)
ok              CLAUDE.md       no gstack section lists skills (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
14 ok, 1 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

The `artifacts sync` warning comes from `gstack-brain-sync --status` on this machine; we did not investigate it for this report.

## Environment

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.311, Linux 7.0.0-43-generic, one machine that runs gstack, gbrain 0.60.728.0 (managed brain) and its serve.
- gstack 1.99.5.0 installed; claims checked at main `e8c8625bd65fdcc0f0650f982830649d326c4bf4`.
- Related: #2922 (closed; introduced the guard and `GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_SOURCES`); #4327 and its pull request #4328 (open; the same same-host layout, where `gstack-decision-search --semantic` also finds the artifacts source only by worktree path and does not read `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID`); #4417 (open; curated imports into an unbound `default` source on the same machine); #4418 (open; the `brain-sync` row's "no gbrain artifacts source on this machine" text).

## What would help

1. Let `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` name the source for `federatedCuratedSourceId` too, with the precedence `brainSyncIndexVerdict` already uses (`:274-275`): when set, use the row whose id equals it; when unset, keep the path match. The guard should keep its `federated === true` requirement (`:243`), which `brainSyncIndexVerdict` does not have. The operator who sets the variable says which source holds the curated artifacts, and a machine that is also the brain host can say so without moving the clone. A test in the style of the repro above (case C) would pin it.
2. Optional, so that no setting is needed: also accept a federated row whose id is the one gstack's own commands use, `gstack-artifacts-${USER}` (`bin/gstack-artifacts-init:494`, the id in the hookup command it prints) or what `derive_source_id` yields from the artifacts repo's remote (`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup:160-178`). Both are heuristics (the second truncates to 32 characters), so an explicit `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` should win over them.
3. When the default finds no source and the machine has a `gbrain sources list` row whose id matches the derived id but whose path is not recognised, the stage line could name that row, for example "a source with the derived id exists at another path; set GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID to use it for the skip". Today the line says "no federated gstack source registered", which is false for that machine.

## Alternatives

- `GSTACK_MEMORY_INGEST_SOURCES=transcript,eureka,learning,timeline,retro,builder-profile-entry` (or `--sources`) works today and is what we use. Its cost is that the list is a copy of `MEMORY_INGEST_TYPES` minus the two curated types (`:180-189`, with `FEDERATED_CURATED_TYPES` at `:198`), so a memory type added later stays off until each machine edits its copy, and it is easy to keep after the artifacts source is removed.
- Re-register the source in the worktree form, which is the route `docs/gbrain-sync.md:47-48` gives a same-machine operator. We did not: the wireup's recreate path (`:346-350`) runs `gbrain sources remove "$id" --yes` and adds the source again, and we did not want to remove a 750-page source on a managed brain (`gbrain sources writer status --json` reports `"mode": "managed"`, whose documented cron line runs `gbrain sources git-reconcile` over every checkout, gbrain `skills/cron-scheduler/SKILL.md:106-113`) to put it under a detached worktree (`:194-203`). We have not tried that wiring and do not claim it fails.
- `GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE=<the clone's path>` makes the guard accept the clone (case D of the repro), so it is a workaround on a same-host install. It is a use the wireup header describes only as "override worktree path" (`:27`), and we have not traced what a full wireup run would do with gbrain's clone at that path, so we are not relying on it.
- Register the source at the state root (the form `gbrain sources add gstack --path ~/.gstack --federated` in gbrain's `docs/guides/multi-source-brains.md:24`, master `280b5a87`). The guard accepts it, but gstack commits into that repo itself, which we did not want a managed brain to reconcile. Not tried.

title: v1.100.0.0 release
body:
v1.100.0.0 ships 37 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- /autoplan's approval page no longer hides a reviewer's product objection behind "keep your direction". (#4431)
- Every skill that loads the shared preamble, on every host, now says to ask a question once and to check a file before handing it over. (#4383)
- The Captain manuals now name the `Failed or skipped:` and `Also changed:` lines that READY and lane reports carry. (#4432)
- gstack's shell locks hold again on Ubuntu 26.04, where `mkdir` reports success when another process won the race (GST-2247). (#4262)
- `test/gstack-lock-race.test.ts` runs the old pattern and the helper against a PATH shim that behaves like uutils 0.8.0 `mkdir`, so it runs on any runner image: the old pattern lets two of four racers win, the helper admits exactly one in each of 60 races and never overlaps across take, hold and release loops, and parallel `gstack-config` writers keep every key. (#4262)
- Windows Setup E2E now runs when `bin/gstack-lock.sh` changes. (#4433)
- Claude Code's skill list now says when to use each gstack skill, so Opus loads /review and /plan-eng-review when a request fits. (#4387)
- A pull request's merge head can no longer keep its `/ship` receipt without a full review. (#4365)
- `/ship` now counts review rounds per pull request, and the head that merges always gets a full review. (#4360)
- /ship's documentation audit no longer accepts a passing result when an earlier line from the same audit said "blocked". (#4434)
- /ship's documentation audit no longer spends an attempt when the audit child writes text after its result. (#4285)
- The README lists the two new guides, and the install doc counts its hooks right. (#4403)
- docs/releases.md now says the stable release cut treats a failed commit status as red and a pending one as still going, as it has since #4257. (#4436)
- /ship's `finish --docs-requested` now accepts a docs fix when the audit named the file with a line number. (#4437)
- Document the `.gstack/approval-classes.json` schema, `gstack-approval-classes` CLI commands, and owner approval citation format in `docs/ship-policy.md#approval-classes`. (#4355)
- `/eval-plan` now runs four result checks instead of leaving them to judgment. (#4384)
- The /review coverage-audit eval no longer fails a run that really read the source file when zsh stops a command line at an `echo ====` separator. (#4364)
- Sixteen in-repo documentation links reach their section again. (#4394)
- gstack agents now open every status report with what failed, what they didn't verify and what else they changed. (#4273)
- Two new short guides. (#4380)
- A skill you wrote whose contract still lists `check_after_last_edit` keeps the rest of its contract. (#4439)
- The ship policy guide now explains how to merge any pull request with `gstack-ship-queue land`, even in a repository with one maintainer. (#4377)
- /ship's test step runs a large unit suite on Linux. (#4426)
- Every skill that loads the shared preamble, on every host, now says never to print a whole environment, git config or process table. (#4382)
- Pull requests from /ship now open with at most three plain lines, and every merge lands as one commit titled with the PR title. (#4438)
- `gstack-pr-wait`, `gstack-ci-gate` and the release cut no longer call a commit green while a check on it failed. (#4257)
- `gstack-runaway` now says what a thread's cold and empty wakes cost, not just how many there were (GST-2770). (#4385)
- The optional Stop hook no longer checks for a test run after the last edit, and /verify asks for it in plain words instead. (#4428)
- /ship's test step says when it ran out of time, and you can set its budget. (#4429)
- The remote test command no longer puts every file on one command line. (#4429)
- The stable release no longer waits on the nightly Windows tests (GST-2815). (#4400)
- Ubicloud fan-outs can no longer overshoot the vCPU limit, and owners no longer delete each other's VMs. (#4430)
- hono is pinned to 4.13.16, which fixes five advisories the weekly OSV scan found in 4.13.13 (gstack#4406). (#4408)
- `package.json` overrides (#4408)
- `test/dependency-security.test.ts`: the lockfile floor check now covers `hono >= 4.13.16`. (#4408)
- The nightly Windows test run finishes again. (#4409)
- A short write-up checklist in ETHOS.md. (#4381)

</details>

title: brain-sync: a skill started with an empty project slug queues projects//timeline.jsonl, and that one path refuses every later artifacts sync of that repository
body:
## What happened

When a skill starts in a directory where `gstack-slug` resolves an empty slug (we reproduce it with the working directory `/`), `gstack-timeline-log` writes `~/.gstack/projects/timeline.jsonl` and spools the artifact path `projects//timeline.jsonl` (double slash). On the next drain, `gstack-brain-sync` stages the file as `projects/timeline.jsonl`, `gstack-brain-sync-index.py` sees a requested path that is not in the index, and the whole batch is refused. Every record in the spool is refused with it, so one bad record stops the artifacts sync for every project that shares that artifacts repository. A plain retry does not clear it.

Our part, stated first: two `/codex` runs that subagents of ours started outside any checkout wrote the records; starting skills there was our own choice. We did not record those runs' working directories (both timeline rows carry `"branch":"unknown"`, which does not by itself say which directory it was); `/` is the only directory where we could reproduce an empty slug, and it reproduces the whole chain below. We also did not set `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=unattended` for those runs; `docs/unattended.md:27-33` says `gstack-brain-enqueue` is a no-op in such a session (the gate is `bin/gstack-brain-enqueue:38`), which would have kept the record out of the spool. `GSTACK_PROJECT_SLUG` would also have given the run a slug. The report is about what gstack does when neither is set, not about whether to run there.

What we saw on 1.99.5.0 on 2026-11-17: two runs (11:53Z and 13:06Z) left two spool records with the path `projects//timeline.jsonl`. From 13:06Z, `gstack-brain-sync --status` showed `"status": "error"` with `staged artifact validation refused; index and queue preserved; inspect before retrying`, the queue depth grew (46), `gstack-doctor` warned `artifacts sync status error`, and `gstack-brain-sync --once` printed `BRAIN_SYNC: staged artifact validation refused: requested/index path mismatch; inspect exact path spellings and unrelated staged entries`. What cleared it: `gstack-brain-sync --drop-queue --yes`, unstaging and deleting the stray `projects/timeline.jsonl`, `--discover-new`, then `--once` (status ok, pushed after rebase).

Two separate gaps are in this, and they can be fixed independently:

1. An empty slug is not handled: nothing between `gstack-slug` and the writers refuses or replaces it, so a path with an empty component reaches the spool.
2. The refusal does not name the path, and the bad record is never dropped or held, so the status does not tell the user which record to remove and the sync stays refused.

## Steps to reproduce

Hermetic: a throwaway `GSTACK_HOME` with its own git repo, a local bare remote, a synthetic allowlist and the brain worktree pointed at an absent path inside the fixture; nothing touches a real `~/.gstack`. Run on `main` at 169eb9c8a59571b54e5205dd4a351a6f271941ea (VERSION 1.99.5.0, the same version as our install), and against the install, with the same result.

```bash
BIN=<a gstack tree>/bin
unset GSTACK_PROJECT_SLUG GSTACK_SESSION_KIND        # either would hide the problem
R=$(mktemp -d); git init -q --bare -b main "$R/remote.git"
H=$(mktemp -d); git -C "$H" init -q -b main
git -C "$H" config user.email a@b.c; git -C "$H" config user.name x
git -C "$H" remote add origin "$R/remote.git"
echo seed > "$H/.seed"; git -C "$H" add .seed; git -C "$H" commit -qm seed; git -C "$H" push -q origin main
printf 'projects/*/timeline.jsonl
projects/*/learnings.jsonl
' > "$H/.brain-allowlist"
export GSTACK_HOME=$H GSTACK_STATE_ROOT=$H GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE=$H/absent-worktree
"$BIN/gstack-config" set artifacts_sync_mode full

# one healthy record, then one skill start from /
mkdir -p "$H/projects/foo-bar"; echo '{"skill":"x"}' > "$H/projects/foo-bar/timeline.jsonl"
"$BIN/gstack-brain-enqueue" projects/foo-bar/timeline.jsonl
( cd / && "$BIN/gstack-slug"; "$BIN/gstack-timeline-log" '{"skill":"codex","event":"started","branch":"unknown"}' )
cat "$H"/.brain-queue.d/*
"$BIN/gstack-brain-sync" --once; "$BIN/gstack-brain-sync" --status
```

Output (trimmed):

```text
SLUG=
BRANCH=unknown
{"file":"projects/foo-bar/timeline.jsonl","ts":"..."}
{"file":"projects//timeline.jsonl","ts":"..."}
BRAIN_SYNC: staged artifact validation refused: requested/index path mismatch; inspect exact path spellings and unrelated staged entries
{"status": "error", ... "message": "staged artifact validation refused; index and queue preserved; inspect before retrying"}
{"queue_depth":2,"last_push":"never","mode":"full"}
```

A later healthy record (another project's `learnings.jsonl`, enqueued afterwards) is refused with the same message and the queue depth grows to 3. Without the seed commit the same input stops one step earlier with `index verification Git command failed`; that is a property of an empty throwaway repo, not part of this report.

## What the code does (all at 169eb9c8)

- `bin/gstack-slug:576`: `SLUG="${SLUG:-$(basename "$PROJECT_DIR" | tr -cd 'a-zA-Z0-9._-')}"`. For `/` the basename is `/`, and the character filter leaves an empty string. Nothing after it checks for an empty result (the marker branch at `:443-454` does reject `""`, `.` and `..`, but the main flow does not).
- `bin/gstack-timeline-log:20-24, 68, 74`: `eval "$(gstack-slug)"`, then `mkdir -p "$GSTACK_HOME/projects/$SLUG"`, the append to `projects/$SLUG/timeline.jsonl` and `gstack-brain-enqueue "projects/$SLUG/timeline.jsonl"`, with no check that `$SLUG` is non-empty. `bin/gstack-learnings-log:47,131,134` and `bin/gstack-review-log:34,154,172` have the same `projects/$SLUG` pattern (the review log takes its slug from `gstack-slug --get REPO_SLUG`, which is empty in the same case). `bin/gstack-skill-start:286, :722` and `:731` already use `${SLUG:-unknown}`, so a fallback name is an existing convention.
- `bin/gstack-brain-enqueue:32-33`: the only check on the path itself is that the argument is not empty.
- `bin/gstack-brain-sync-index.py:99-114`: `verify()` compares the requested paths with the index and refuses with `requested/index path mismatch; inspect exact path spellings and unrelated staged entries` when `requested - entries.keys()` is not empty (`:113-114`). The path is not named; the handler at `:155-157` prints only the colliding component names (empty here) and that sentence.
- `bin/gstack-brain-sync:1056-1059`: on that refusal it writes status `error` with `staged artifact validation refused; index and queue preserved; inspect before retrying` and prints the script's message to stderr. The queue is preserved by design, and the `error` row of `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md` says "the queue is kept and retried"; the retry hits the same record each time.

## Expected

1. A skill started where the slug is empty should not write or spool a `projects//...` path: either a fallback slug (`unknown`, as `gstack-skill-start` already uses) or no write at all.
2. A single malformed queue record should not stop the whole drain with a message that names nothing. Rejecting or holding such a path before staging (so it never reaches the index check), with a counted notice (the classification JSON already lists the paths) (as the `unmatched`/`invalid` classification at `bin/gstack-brain-sync:312-323` and `:462-474` already does for other bad records, and as `hold()` in the index script does for case collisions), would fit the existing design; the refusal for unexplained index differences can stay, since preserving the index there is deliberate. Naming the offending path in `--status` and in the `error` row would already let the user fix it without reading the script.

We do not know which of these you prefer, and a dropped record alone would not unstage Git's normalized entry, so the check has to happen before staging. (1) alone would stop this input; (2) would also cover any other path spelling the verifier cannot reconcile.

## Docs

The docs at 169eb9c8 do not cover this case. The `error` row at `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md:44` lists the causes as "a git index lock, a commit hook, a `git add` failure"; a refused path spelling is not named there (we do not claim the row is meant to be exhaustive), and `--drop-queue --yes` is documented there for the `blocked` row (`:42`) and for held files (`:80`), not for `error`. `docs/state-root.md` does not say what happens when the slug is empty.

## Related

We searched open and closed issues and PRs for `projects//timeline.jsonl`, `requested/index path mismatch`, `staged artifact validation refused`, empty slug and queue-stuck wording and found no report of this. Neighbours that are not the same defect: #3658 (case-collision check blocks a clone), #3220 and #3254 (case-colliding project paths, held instead of ok), #2549 (silent drop of unmatched queue entries), #4418 (an `idle` status after a failed push).

## Readiness report

`gstack-doctor` run after we recovered (the incident run showed `warn artifacts sync status error`):

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.5.0
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              hooks           15 hook(s) parse
ok              artifacts sync  status ok (mode full; queue 0)
ok              claude code     2.1.311 (Claude Code)
13 ok, 2 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

(Two unrelated warns omitted: codex project unregistered; CLAUDE.md skill list. The full output is trimmed to the lines that bear on this report.)

## Environment

- Host and version: Claude Code 2.1.311
- OS: Linux 7.0 (x86_64), Docker container
- gstack: installed 1.99.5.0 (`0326b144`); claims checked against `main` at 169eb9c8a59571b54e5205dd4a351a6f271941ea, also VERSION 1.99.5.0; the reproduction above ran against a `git archive` of that commit and against the install, with the same result
- `artifacts_sync_mode: full`

title: Let an owner's ruling close the one finding it names on a full review pass (GST-2273)
body:
An owner's ruling can now close a blocking finding on /ship's second full review pass and on the cross-model review step, and it closes only the one finding it names, at the head it names. This makes /ship do what docs/review-policy.md already promises, so a pass held open only by findings the owner accepted can finish (needed by #4248). Nothing to do: rulings recorded the old way by fingerprint keep working on the re-check after a fix and close nothing new.
What changed - `gstack-approvals rule --id / --head ` records a ruling for one finding by its ledger id. The record stores it as `id=` where the fingerprint goes, so an older gstack reads it and matches nothing. - `gstack-review-read` closes that finding on a /ship `review` or `adversarial-review` row only when the row's read started and ended at the ruled commit and the ruling was recorded after the read ended. The logger now stamps `start_commit` and `ended_at` on the review binding for this. - `gstack-review-scope summary` counts that finding as noted instead of unrecorded. A finding only a dispatch ledger holds counts only when the run's newest /ship row read the ruled head and the whole pass ran during that read. - Never closed: a fingerprint ruling, a bare id, an id two findings share, a ruling at another head or made before the read ended, rows logged before this change, and any gate finding. A row finding whose paired ledger line names a gate (`gate` or an RH tag) now keeps that gate in the summary. - The re-check after a fix (finish's fix-check path) ignores `--id` rulings and is otherwise unchanged.
Tests - New test/ship-ruled-full-pass.test.ts (20 cases): the #4248 and #4266/#4257 shapes, plus every wrong close two earlier second-model audits found (fingerprint fan-out, ruling at range_base or mid-range, a non-/ship row choosing rulings, shared-line voice findings, a ledger gate on a paired row finding, a fingerprint shared with a non-blocking finding, an old stop row ruling a later finding). Each negative case asserts main's result: the finding stays unrecorded or UNVERIFIED. - The second audit's own scratch test (3 cases): 3/3 pass on main e8c8625, 0/3 on #4435 at e34f9b5, 3/3 on this branch. - New test file on main: 3 pass / 17 fail (main has no id rulings); on e34f9b5: 1 pass / 19 fail; here 20/20. - A finish test shows an id ruling closes nothing on a fix-check. - Focused related suites: 511 pass, 0 fail across 16 files. typecheck clean; test typecheck ratchet: none new.
Agent notes Supersedes #4435 and #4272 (GST-2273). Narrower design per GStack Minder: one ruling closes one finding by id at one head, no fingerprint matching, no range walk. Dropped from #4435: the approval mirror read change, the fix-check holdsOpen and FIX_CHECK_OPEN changes, and the commit-time fallback for stopped reads. Known limit, inherited from main's binding: a read that resets HEAD away and back mid-read (no new commit) still binds as one tree.

title: Ubicloud pack no longer fails while git rewrites a ref, and the HOLD SCOPE eval stops requiring the mode name
body:
Packing a checkout for a Ubicloud run no longer fails when git running beside it is rewriting a ref, and the /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE eval no longer fails a review whose follow-up question doesn't repeat the mode name. Why: both made tests fail at random. The pack race failed Free Tests twice on 2026-11-17, and the HOLD check failed the weekly eval census on main. Nothing to do.
What changed ![Before, pack died with 'not our ref 0000…' when one ref was unreadable; now it skips that ref and ships the rest](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/voaiwkelHDUcYsp6kqUqsURDyoDOra6h6mRl_oR9v-w.png) Before, pack died with 'not our ref 0000…' when one ref was unreadable; now it skips that ref and ships the rest.
Agent notes Daily flaky-fix pass 2026-11-17 (GSTA-579, GST-2983). - Free: test/ubicloud-runner.test.ts "pack snapshots a plain checkout without reading its live .git…", Free Tests 44063454800 shard 10 (gst-2737-plain-pr-bodies @ aa3d27f5) and 44050883970 shard 7 (approval-page-keeps-reviewer-product-challenges-open @ 507827f2), both passed on serial retry. REPEAT of the 2026-10 entry fixed in #3697 (a different cause: cp of the live index). Mechanism repro on this machine: 1 failure in 746 fetches under ref churn; deterministic repro with an empty loose ref. - Paid (periodic census 43815320847, main 8c3c39b5): plan-ceo-mode-routing HOLD failed "decision is not current HOLD work". A local replay of that run's decision through the real judge after this fix still fails, because the judge rated the model's post-mode question (how to treat unverified premises) "uncertain" rather than a HOLD remedy. So this fix removes one false-fail path but would not have turned that run green; the rest is model variance in which question comes first after the mode. - No thresholds, trial counts or case kinds changed. No retries added.
Before/after as text: Before, pack died with 'not our ref 0000…' when one ref was unreadable; now it skips that ref and ships the rest ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output $ ubi-runner.sh pack checkout # one empty loose ref file, as when git beside it is mid-write +exit=0 +warning: ignoring broken ref refs/heads/broken +$ git for-each-ref --format=%(refname) # inside the snapshot +refs/heads/detached-20e414e45232 +refs/heads/main +refs/heads/side -exit=1 -fatal: git upload-pack: not our ref 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 -fatal: remote error: upload-pack: not our ref 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 -ubi-runner: pack: could not snapshot the refs of /s2 ~~~ Free Tests failed with `not our ref 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` while `ubi-runner.sh pack` copied a checkout that another git command was changing. Pack used to fetch `'+refs/*:refs/*'`, and git's upload-pack lists a ref it can't read (a loose ref file caught mid-write or mid-delete) with a null id, so the fetch asked for an object that doesn't exist. Pack now reads the refs once with `git for-each-ref`, which skips an unreadable ref with a warning, and fetches exactly those object ids. A new test holds that state still with an empty loose ref file. The /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE eval check required the decision question's "Project/branch/task" line to say "HOLD SCOPE". The skill never asks the model to repeat the mode there, and the decision is already tied to the HOLD answer by session and order. Now only a line that names another mode, or past or hypothetical work, fails, and a new test keeps those negative cases.
Why "not our ref 0000…" failed Free Tests runs 44063454800 and 44050883970 on 2026-11-17, and the HOLD check failed eval census run 43815320847 on main. Both were false failures, so a red run now means a real problem in these two places.
Blast radius `cmd_pack` is the only caller of the changed fetch, and every Ubicloud test and eval run goes through it. It stays safe because the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` (ubi-runner.sh:150), so a failing `for-each-ref` still stops the pack, and a script run on three test checkouts (normal, unreadable ref, no refs at all) shipped the right refs each time. The HOLD check change is in a test helper only.

Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh:1708` checked-out branch made unreadable mid-pack leaves the snapshot HEAD on an unborn branch instead of dying - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh:1708` empty ref list makes fetch --stdin fetch HEAD into a stray FETCH_HEAD
Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `ubi-runner.sh pack`, 3 probes, all pass: a normal checkout ships main, side and an annotated tag at the right ids with HEAD on main; a detached checkout with an empty loose ref ships every readable ref and skips the broken one; a detached checkout with no refs still ships a branch at HEAD. Not covered: live concurrent ref churn (the empty ref file holds that state still) and macOS git and tar.

title: gstack-ship-budget launch: the claude -p child gets no prompt, because the variadic --allowedTools reads it as one more tool
body:
## What happened

With a token cap on Claude Code (`/ship --token-cap 100M`), `gstack-ship-budget start --session <id>` printed `verdict=delegate` (`call=393522 call_floor=40000`) and `DELEGATE: Steps 1-22 go to a fresh child`. `handoff --from 1 --to 22` wrote the brief and `launch --in <brief>` printed `CHILD: session=... pid=...`. The child exited at once. Its log holds one line:

```text
Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
```

No return file appeared, and `reconcile --handoff <sha>` printed `RECONCILED: handoff=<sha> child=interrupted child_used=<n>` and a budget line ending `verdict=stop`, so that `/ship` run ended there. With Claude Code 2.1.311 and this launch command, a `/ship` that delegates stops at its first handoff.

Expected: the child runs the prompt `launch` builds ("Load gstack. ... Run /ship --continue <brief>: first gstack-ship-budget verify-handoff ...", lib/ship-handoff.ts:303), on the route docs/ship-budget.md:203-204 gives Claude Code: "`gstack-ship-budget launch --in <brief>`: a background `claude -p` (resolved through lib/claude-bin.ts) with explicit permission flags and the return file named".

Cause, read at main b79843c5 (VERSION 1.100.0.0; the same lines run in the 1.99.5.0 install here):

```ts
// lib/ship-handoff.ts:291
export const CHILD_PERMISSION_ARGS = ['--permission-mode', 'acceptEdits', '--allowedTools', 'Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob'];
// lib/ship-handoff.ts:307
const child = spawn(claude.command, [...claude.argsPrefix, '-p', '--session-id', session, ...CHILD_PERMISSION_ARGS, prompt], ...);
```

Claude Code 2.1.311 declares the option as variadic (`claude --help`: `--allowedTools, --allowed-tools <tools...>`), so the prompt right after it is read as one more tool name and `-p` has no input. The launch test cannot see this: test/ship-budget.test.ts:311 replaces `claude` with a script that prints its arguments, and :318 pins this same order.

## Steps to reproduce

No model call is made in step 1; it fails before any request.

1. `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools 'Bash,Read' 'Reply with the single word ok'` exits 1 with the error above.
2. `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools 'Bash,Read' --model haiku 'Reply with the single word ok'` exits 0 and prints `ok`: an option after the list ends it, and the prompt is read.
3. In a Claude Code session whose context is large (at start, 100k or more above the call floor delegates the whole `/ship`, docs/ship-budget.md:185-186), on a branch with changes: `/ship --token-cap 100M`. Once `start` or a `check` prints `verdict=delegate`, the child launched by `gstack-ship-budget launch` dies with the error above.

Possible fixes, not tried here: send the prompt on stdin, as lib/claude-code.ts:273 already does (`child.stdin?.end(options.prompt)`); pass the list as one argument (`--allowedTools=Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob`); or put the prompt before the permission flags. A launch test whose fake `claude` parses `--allowedTools` as variadic would catch a regression.

## Readiness report

Trimmed to the lines about this path; home paths shortened to `~`.

```text
gstack doctor 1.99.5.0
ok              install root    ~/.claude/skills/gstack: openclaw global current (1.99.5.0), codex global current (1.99.5.0), claude global current (1.99.5.0)
ok              state root      ~/.gstack durable=yes (selected by default)
ok              bun             1.4.4 at /usr/local/bin/bun (floor 1.3.3, tested 1.4.2)
ok              claude code     2.1.311 (Claude Code) at /usr/local/bin/claude
ok              session journal largest of 1: 3.0 MiB
15 ok, 0 warn, 0 not configured, 0 fail
```

## Environment

- Host (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) and its version: Claude Code 2.1.311
- OS: Linux 7.0.0
- gstack: 1.99.5.0 installed; code read at main b79843c5 (1.100.0.0), where lib/ship-handoff.ts:291 and :307 are unchanged.
- Related: none found in the tracker (searched the error text, `allowedTools`, `ship-budget launch`, `cmdLaunch`, `CHILD_PERMISSION_ARGS`, open and closed).

title: Stop /ship asking owners to approve its own review bookkeeping
body:
/ship no longer stops for an owner's approval in three cases where the stop came from its own bookkeeping: an approved extra review round now buys that round, a base merge that only changes base-side text is no longer a behavior change, and a reviewer's "nothing blocks" reply no longer turns into Critical findings.
Each of these cost a stopped run plus an owner ruling or a new PR (gstack#4272, #4383, #4431); every shortcut keeps a test showing a real change still stops.
Nothing for readers to do.

<details><summary>Round grants at the review cap (GST-2968)</summary>

- A run that starts past the two-round cap (the read-only final review) is now marked `read_only` in the PR body's runs block by `gstack-ship-receipt stub`.
- When a round grant applies at the head, `gstack-ship-receipt history` leaves those read-only passes out of `--prior-full`, so the grant buys the round the `PR_ROUND_CAP` stop names. Before, the read-only pass already counted as that round, so the next run was read-only again (gstack#4272: two grants bought nothing).
- The granted round keeps its fix round (its pass 2); nothing past it plans. A spent grant routes read-only again.
- A grant now applies across a base merge that leaves the PR's own added and removed lines byte-identical, in either direction, since preflight merges the base before the review (ghome#17: grant at 28b7968, reviewed e9ee170). A head that changes those lines needs a new grant.
- `lib/review-depth.ts` is repinned with a deterministic no-loss replay (`test/fixtures/review-pins/replays/GST-2968.json`): over 21,233,664 cases, the only step changes are 23,040 granted-round stops that now get their fix pass; no review step is removed.

</details>

<details><summary>Base-side text after a base merge (GST-2975)</summary>

- Path comparison now reads all four sides with the shared-preamble hash ids masked (both generated forms), so a main merge that only moved those ids in regenerated skill files is a base merge (#4383).
- A line that is the base's new line plus exactly the tokens the branch added to the reviewed line (both sides appended to one expected-value list, ghome#16) is base context, so finish sends it to the one scoped reader instead of stopping for an owner grant. Test paths whose own lines are unchanged are no longer gate-scanned on the base's edits.
- Negative controls: a resolution that drops, invents or rewrites anything on the branch's own lines still stops as a behavior change.

</details>

<details><summary>Reviewer replies that say nothing blocks (GST-2972)</summary>

- A file:line in a reviewer's prose no longer anchors a finding. Before, prose that confirmed code ("a High or Critical challenge… autoplan-revise.ts:103") became an anchored Critical that only an owner could clear (#4431, twice).
- A reply that says `NO FINDINGS` collects only structured finding lines: JSON, a lead severity label, a label heading, a numbered finding heading, a `Severity` or `Blocks: yes` field, or the native voice's FIXABLE/INVESTIGATE tag.
- A reply whose valid `REVIEW_VERDICT` says `blocking=0` still collects its prose rows, because a verdict line lowers nothing by itself (the existing negative controls in test/review-verdict.test.ts). Such a row is now a summary candidate the lead can lower with a reason, instead of an owner stop.
- The test replays both real #4431 replies; a structured Critical in a `blocking=0` or `NO FINDINGS` reply still collects as anchored and still disagrees with the verdict.

</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- Commits: d104e87 (GST-2968), 23b3073 (GST-2975), 3c2d982 and 18b6262 (GST-2972), 1ad188a (pre-landing review fixes for 3 blockers), 22bb3c1 (changelog fragment), 0a9459e (review-policy correction from the docs audit).
- Local runs: two tests fail with a 5 s timeout on this machine (`review-plan-targeted-delta` "the #225 shape", `review-dispatch` "edited to look refused") and the same way with the branch's lib and bin changes stashed, so they are machine speed, not this change. Seven local preflight/re-review test failures also occur at the untouched 18b6262 (environment). CI is the full run.
- Known gap: a read-only run that finishes with a receipt (no stop) is not marked `read_only`, so a grant at a later head still counts it.

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=3 deferred=0 noted=6 fixed=3 scope=frozen dispatches=8
Gate edits: none detected (7 listed, 2 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

Refs GST-2968 GST-2975 GST-2972

</details>

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![A file and line in a reviewer's 'nothing blocks' prose no longer becomes a Critical finding (GST-2972)](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/4Ir9BM34HKdjIg7-OQ4xeNm_FuYiENhnhjkJP-4wNbs.png)

A file and line in a reviewer's "nothing blocks" prose no longer becomes a Critical finding (GST-2972).

</details>

<details><summary>Before/after as text: A file and line in a reviewer's 'nothing blocks' prose no longer becomes a Critical finding (GST-2972)</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
    real blockers named in an exception clause ("No CRITICAL issues except the token leak in log.ts:3"); GSTA-167
    reverted that. A reply that says `NO FINDINGS` keeps only its structured findings (GST-2122). Those are JSON objects
    (malformed JSON included), lead labels, label headings, numbered finding headings, `Severity` fields, `Blocks: yes`,
+   the native voice's FIXABLE or INVESTIGATE tag, which still collect at their label. A file:line in its prose is the
+   reader confirming code, not a finding, so it no longer anchors one (GST-2972). Its other prose collects nothing. Outside such a reply prose collects as described above. A denial that a change
-   the native voice's FIXABLE or INVESTIGATE tag, and anything naming a file:line, which still collect at their label.
-   Its other prose collects nothing. Outside such a reply prose collects as described above. A denial that a change
 
~~~

**Extra review rounds an owner approves (GST-2968).** Owners hit "two grants bought nothing" (gstack#4272): a read-only final review already counted as the round a grant was meant to buy, so the next run was read-only again. A run that starts past the two-round cap is now marked `read_only` in the PR's run record, history leaves those passes out when a grant applies, and the granted round keeps its fix pass. A grant also survives a base merge that leaves the PR's own added and removed lines byte-identical (ghome#17). `lib/review-depth.ts` is repinned with a no-loss replay over 21,233,664 cases: the only step changes are 23,040 granted-round stops that now get their fix pass.

**Base-side text after a base merge (GST-2975).** A main merge that only moved shared-preamble hash ids in regenerated skill files read as a behavior change (#4383), and so did a line that was the base's new line plus exactly the tokens the branch added (ghome#16). Both now count as base context and go to the one scoped reader instead of an owner stop. A resolution that drops, invents or rewrites anything on the branch's own lines still stops.

**Reviewer replies that say nothing blocks (GST-2972).** A file:line in a reviewer's prose confirming code became an anchored Critical only an owner could clear (#4431, twice). A `NO FINDINGS` reply now collects only structured finding lines, and a `blocking=0` reply's prose rows stay lowerable with a reason. A structured Critical in either reply still collects and still blocks.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Two grants bought nothing" (gstack#4272), and two more runs stopped for an owner on text the branch never wrote (#4383, #4431). Owners now rule only on real changes; bookkeeping no longer asks them for anything.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

This touches the round count /ship's run history feeds into the review plan, finish's base-merge comparison, and the review collector every reader's reply goes through. Each shortcut has a negative control that a real change still stops (test/pr-round-cli.test.ts, test/ship-base-side-masks.test.ts, test/review-ledger-quiet-reply.test.ts, test/review-verdict.test.ts), and the full free suite passed in CI run 44123166003 at this tree (script ran).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two review passes. Pass 1 found 3 blockers, all fixed in 1ad188a with tests:
- `lib/ship-patch.ts:171`: a regenerated file whose only change was the shared-preamble id still compared as changed after masking, so finish stopped on the #4383 shape this PR targets.
- `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1096`: a granted run's stub recomputed read-only at its current head, so after the fix commit the granted passes were marked read-only and a later grant would subtract them.
- `lib/pr-review-history.ts:62`: recording the finished run dropped its read-only mark, so a later read-only stop plus grant still routed read-only (QA reproduced it before the fix and passed after).

Pass 2 on the fixed tree found no blockers. The money-path targeted reader returned NO FINDINGS on both passes, and one more read of the final head (asked for because the docs and changelog edits after review carry numbers) found one informational note, listed below.

Second-model review: ran in pass 1 and raised 2 of the 3 blockers above; pass 2 ran the specialist, red-team and targeted readers.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-patch.ts:209` splicedHunk compares the inserted token sequence, not its position, so a resolution that moves the branch's token counts as context (still goes to the scoped reader).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-ledger.ts:344` A NO FINDINGS reply's unstructured prose with a file:line now collects nothing (the intended GST-2972 trade-off).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-round-grant.ts:60` ownLinesSame uses a -U0 patch-id, so relocated but byte-identical own lines on an ancestor/descendant head inherit the grant.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-patch.ts:130` sideDiffs runs up to four git cat-file calls per compared path even when no side has a preamble id.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1085` The stub's new at-or-before grant fallback has only a positive test; no test checks a non-ancestor grant or another PR's grant leaves the stub read_only.

title: Run each driven /ship phase as one command, count its calls, and stop it at 100 minutes (GST-2984)
body:
A driven /ship now runs each ship/DRIVER.md phase as one command, shows how many calls the run made, and stops itself with a printed line at 100 minutes. Why: measured /ship runs made 121 to 308 calls where the driver plans 9 to 12, and 10 of 12 ran past the 100-minute stop while those limits were only prose. Nothing to do: older ship records without `calls=` still validate and print.
What changed Driven /ship runs kept making hundreds of tool calls and running long, because the one-call-per-phase rule and the 100-minute stop were only written down. They are now code. - **One command per phase.** `gstack-ship-phase run --dir --phase [--record ] -- ''...` runs a phase's commands in order, each in the background with its log under `/phases//`, and prints only result lines. A command still running after 200 s keeps running and the call returns `NEXT: rerun`; the same command picks the wait back up. A failed command prints `STOP:` (exit 3), and after the fix the same command starts at the failed step. If you change the command list while an old command is still running, the runner now stops that old process first, so its exit status can never be counted for the new command. - **One call per phase on Capy.** `gstack-ship-phase program` serves `lib/capy-ship-phase.js`, loaded like the review pass program. It reads the thread's cost counter for the commands, runs the phase, then the review pass or the closing budget note, then the next phase's section parts. When Capy reports `cost.dollars` but no `cost.credits` (as it does today), this program and the review pass program now use dollars × 1,000 instead of passing an empty reading that every budget note refused. - **Calls are counted.** `gstack-ship-budget note` records `calls=` since the previous note, and `BUDGET_TIMELINE:` shows them per phase. `gstack-ship-receipt write --budget-record ` (or `--calls `) puts the run's total in the record, and `SHIP_RECEIPT:` prints `calls=`. The field is optional. - **Printed 100-minute stop.** In observe mode, the first note or phase run past 100 minutes prints `STOP: past 100 minutes ...`, writes the head, review passes, next step and calls to `stop.json`, and keeps the run stopped until `gstack-ship-budget resume` restarts the clock. Admission mode has no clock. - **Waits priced by length** in ship/DRIVER.md and the Capy skill: a 200 s keep-alive for waits under about 80 minutes, one wait that ends the turn for longer ones, and no 10-15 minute polls.
Blast radius Only driven /ship runs (ship/DRIVER.md, observe mode) use the phase runner and the stop. Review requirements, the round cap and every check's verdict are unchanged, and the `calls` field is optional, so older records still validate (test/ship-phase.test.ts runs both shapes through write and placement; script ran). The credits fallback only fills a reading that was otherwise missing.
Calls in this PR's own /ship run This PR's own /ship run (on its final head 5f04632d) printed `calls=44` (`CALLS: source=log calls=37 ... keepalive_est=7 total_est=44`). The handoff's baseline was 121 to 308 parent turns across 12 measured conductor runs. That's one data point, not a measured saving: it ran on the branch that adds the runner, the call log counts only calls that ran a gstack command plus estimated keep-alives (the baseline counted every turn), and the run took two review passes and one CI wait.
Agent notes Tests: `test/ship-phase.test.ts` (12 cases, all free): runner resume after a failure, the 200 s return and reattach, result-line filtering, usage errors; the Capy program driving a real Phase 2 (`gstack-ship-budget start` plus `gstack-ship-preflight --audit`) on a fixture repo on a fake host whose shell is real, and handing a pass to the review pass program; the time stop by note and by phase run, resume restarting the clock, admit mode untouched; calls per note and in the timeline; receipt write with `--budget-record` and `--calls`; the schema field; carry of receipts with and without `calls`. `test/exercised-map.test.ts` gains a reviewed-superset row for `lib/ship-clock.ts`. Handoffs: org drive handoffs/fold-subagents-2026-11-17 (G2) and handoffs/ship-conductor-cost-2026-11-16.
Test Coverage Coverage: 22 of 30 changed paths have a test at two stars or better (73%); the other 8 are new-code edge paths with no test yet (an edited command list's journal cut, a killed command's `exit=lost`, the 60-line output cap, a bad `--calls` value, bad program input, a closing note without a thread id, the 32 KB return cap, next-phase parts). No regression test was needed: every changed behavior is new except the credits fallback, which has its own tests. Tests ran: phase 58 Tests ran: guards 8
Pre-Landing Review The full review panel ran on this change (two specialists, a red-team reader, a native adversarial reader, a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol, and a targeted money reader), then a second pass on the fix. One blocking finding, from the second-model review and confirmed by the adversarial reader, was fixed: a replaced command that was still running could write its exit status into the file its replacement is judged by, so a failing replacement could be recorded as passed. Nothing else met the blocking bar; the items below are recorded and not fixed here.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:87` the journal keys finished commands by their text only, so a same-text rerun after a fix shows the earlier results as done (test evidence is still rechecked at finish) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:34` liveness is judged by pid alone; a pid reused after a machine sleep keeps a killed command waiting until the 100-minute stop - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:75` no lock around the journal's read, start and write; two runners could start the same command twice - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:85` after SIGTERM only the group leader is checked, so a group member that handles SIGTERM can still write the shared log - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:80` a running entry whose command already wrote its exit file can be signalled if its pid was reused - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-phase.ts:83` on Windows the process-group kill throws, so a changed list with a running entry stops after 5 s instead of continuing - INFORMATIONAL `lib/capy-ship-phase.js:31` the credits fallback reads 0 when both cost.credits and cost.dollars are missing (same expression in `lib/capy-review-pass.js:91`) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/capy-ship-phase.js:45` a phase call with only a review pass dispatches readers without the run's stop check that `gstack-ship-phase run --record` makes - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:243` write fails hard when the budget record is missing, over a calls count that is only informational - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-clock.ts:32` the call count filters the shared call log by time only, so two runs on one state root count each other's calls - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-clock.ts:43` the next-step reader treats a bullet starting with a heading word as the next heading - INFORMATIONAL `docs/ship-budget.md:112` the long-wait advice names a long local preflight, but phase commands are detached processes with no Capy operation id, so a turn-ending wait lets the machine sleep and stop them - INFORMATIONAL `test/ship-phase.test.ts:107` the new replacement test gives the old command about 1 s of slack, so a heavily loaded runner could make it flake (the scope tool classed it a note)
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual correction, no blockers. **Scope:** the base b49ed6a0..193c1a95 on capy/run-each-driven-ship (5 commits, 19 files), with no staged, unstaged or new files. The changes add the `gstack-ship-phase` runner and its Capy program, the 100-minute clock stop (`lib/ship-clock.ts`), `calls=` in budget notes and receipts, and a fallback from `cost.dollars` to credits. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-budget.md: Updated. The Credits paragraph now covers the `cost.dollars` x 1,000 fallback. The new sections on the 100-minute stop, the phase runner and `calls=` match the code. - ship/DRIVER.md.tmpl and ship/DRIVER.md: Current. Both describe the phase runner, `--budget-record` and the 100-minute stop. - capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md: Current, with one note. It still names only `cost.credits` as the credits source. Agents load this file, so it was left for the parent. - changelog.d/capy-run-each-driven-ship.md: Current. Not edited, because it is a changelog fragment. - docs/troubleshooting.md: Current, with a gap. title: Token-capped /ship hands its child Claude Code session its prompt (#4448)
body:
A `/ship` with a token cap on Claude Code no longer stops at its first handoff: the child `claude -p` session now gets its prompt.
Why: `--allowedTools` takes every argument after it, so the prompt was read as one more tool name and the child exited at once. The launch now puts `--` before the prompt.
Nothing to do. Thanks to @exGeni for the report and diagnosis.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Claude Code 2.1.292 with the launch argv: before, the prompt is swallowed by --allowedTools; after, -- hands it over](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/wAHeS4URXJ5tVwcXmWcqsfzCclLxyc0kxwbIqcLIxJg.png)

Claude Code 2.1.292 with the launch argv: before, the prompt is swallowed by `--allowedTools`; after, `--` hands it over.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Claude Code 2.1.292 with the launch argv: before, the prompt is swallowed by --allowedTools; after, -- hands it over</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ claude -p --session-id <id> --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob -- <prompt>
+Invalid API key · Fix external API key
+(prompt accepted; stops at the deliberately fake key, so no model call)
-$ claude -p --session-id <id> --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob <prompt>
-Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print
-(exit 1)
 
~~~

</details>

A token-capped `/ship` that hands work to a fresh Claude Code session started that session and then stopped, because the child printed "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument" and exited. `gstack-ship-budget launch` now ends the options with `--`, so the child reads its prompt and the run carries on. The launch test now reads the child's arguments the way Claude Code does and requires exactly one prompt.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"The child exited with 'Input must be provided'" (#4448): the first handoff of a capped `/ship` killed the run. Now the child gets its instructions and the run continues past the handoff.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `cmdLaunch` in `lib/ship-handoff.ts` changes, and only the argument list it passes to `claude`. `--` is the standard end-of-options marker, and the real Claude Code 2.1.292 binary (the CI pin) accepted the prompt after it in a repro (script ran). The other place gstack starts Claude Code, `lib/claude-code.ts`, sends its prompt on stdin, so it never had this problem (file read).

</details>

All new code paths have test coverage: the one changed line is covered by the extended launch test in `test/ship-budget.test.ts` (★★★).

No issues found. One specialist reviewer (testing, security, state machines, red team) found nothing; the adversarial reviewer raised three low-severity notes, none blocking.

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- `test/ship-budget.test.ts:308`: the regression test checks a hand-written model of Claude Code's argument parser, not the real CLI, so a future change to how Claude Code reads `--` would not turn it red. The real-CLI repro above covers 2.1.292 today.
- `lib/ship-handoff.ts:307`: on Windows through WSL (`wsl claude ... -- <prompt>`), whether wsl.exe passes `--` through is unverified, and the prompt's unquoted paths go through the Linux shell (that part predates this change).

title: CI uploads test results with Trunk's uploader v2.1.8 (GST-2999)
body:
Free-tests CI now uploads test results to Trunk with analytics-uploader v2.1.8 and analytics-cli 0.17.0, up from v2.1.6 and 0.16.2.
Why: Trunk warned that uploader v2.1.6 may pick up analytics-cli 1.0.0 when it ships and then fail to upload; v2.1.8 never resolves a CLI above 0.x.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Trunk asked every repo on analytics-uploader v2.1.6 to move to v2.1.8 before analytics-cli 1.0.0 ships. The free-tests workflow's upload step now pins the action to commit 9886de74a788c450c793109577a4d97bfb3e799f, which `git ls-remote https://github.com/trunk-io/analytics-uploader refs/tags/v2.1.8` returns, and sets `cli-version` to 0.17.0, the default that v2.1.8's `src/constants.ts` falls back to and the latest analytics-cli release. The wiring test in `test/free-tests-workflow-wiring.test.ts` now checks the new pin and CLI version; it failed against the old workflow before the workflow changed.

This is the change Trunk proposed in #4411 by Tyler Beebe, rebuilt on current main and credited with Co-authored-by. Dependabot's #4416 bumps the same action without the CLI version or the test.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The flaky-test upload feeds Trunk's flaky-test detection for gstack's free suite. Keeping the uploader on a release that caps the CLI below 1.0 keeps that upload working through Trunk's 1.0 release.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the upload step of the trunk-flaky-tests job changes, and that job runs with `permissions: {}`, `continue-on-error`, and a gate on `TRUNK_ORG_API_TOKEN`, so nothing else in CI reads it. Between v2.1.6 and v2.1.8 the action's `action.yaml` only rewords two input descriptions and adds an optional `summary-output-file` input and output, so every input the step passes is still declared with the same default (file read at both tags). The step ran on this branch: Free Tests run 44128395249 shows the upload step succeeded with 37,495 tests reported and 0 failures.

</details>
