title: Keep skill_prefix after updates, retire the ClawHub install route, and stop misreading cross-repo issue refs (GST-2967)
body:
Three small fixes: `skill_prefix=true` now survives updates when gbrain is installed, the OpenClaw docs stop sending people to stale ClawHub skills, and `gstack-issue-links` no longer reads other repositories' issue numbers as gstack issues. Why: each one misleads users or /ship today (wrong skill names after every update, April 2026 skill builds, wrong `Refs #N` lines in PR bodies). Nothing to do as a reader. Thanks @fliaron (#4413) and @exGeni (#4421) for the detailed reports.
What changed - **`skill_prefix` after re-renders (#4413).** Three Claude render paths swapped a fresh render into the live render dir without running `gstack-patch-names`: the gbrain branch of `./setup`, `gstack-config gbrain-refresh`, and `gstack_claude_render_plain` in `bin/gstack-render-claude.sh`. Because `./setup` renders after its relink step, every update served unprefixed `name:` fields. Each path now patches the temp render before the swap, as `_render_install` already did. The plain render reads the saved `skill_prefix` through the `gstack-config` beside it. - **OpenClaw docs (#4421).** `docs/hosts.md` and `docs/OPENCLAW.md` no longer tell anyone to `clawhub install` the `gstack-openclaw-*` skills (the docs said four and listed three). Those were 1.0.0 builds from 2026-04-05 that were never updated, and the four gstack skills were removed from ClawHub on 2026-11-17 (each now returns 404). The docs now point to native registration (`./setup --host openclaw`), whose `gstack` router skill already serves the current /office-hours, /plan-ceo-review and /retro, and tell readers who installed them to remove them. `docs/OPENCLAW_PUBLISHING.md` says the route is retired. - **Cross-repo issue references (GST-2967).** A parenthesis citing several repositories, such as `(founderstar #837, harness-evals #393)`, used to fall through to the bare-`#N` rule and became this repository's `Refs #837` and `Refs #393` with fix-#N offers. Each named reference in a parenthesis is now a cross-repo reference to its own name. `owner/repo#N` naming the current repository is now its own issue, so `Fixes garrytan/gstack#N` closes it. Bare mentions (`mentions #12`, `(see #12, #13)`, `Fixes #14`) are unchanged.
Tests Each fix has a test written first that fails on main: - `test/user-render-out-dir-install.test.ts`: every render swap in `setup`, `bin/gstack-config` and `bin/gstack-render-claude.sh` comes after `gstack-patch-names` on the same temp dir, and the plain render serves `gstack-retro` with the prefix on and `retro` with it off. - `test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts`: the founderstar case, the bare-mention controls, and this repository's `owner/repo#N` (pure and through the bin). - [x] `bun test test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts test/user-render-out-dir-install.test.ts`: 27 pass, 0 fail at 066e283. - [x] `bun run test` (the full free suite): green in CI at 066e283, free-tests run 44132131782.
Blast radius Render paths: one extra `gstack-patch-names` call per Claude re-render, idempotent, and a failure there is treated as a failed render (the previous render stays). Issue links: only parenthesised named references and this repository's `owner/repo#N` change. A `name #N` written in prose outside parentheses is still read as this repository's issue, because the text can't tell `founderstar #837` from `mentions #12`. Docs: OpenClaw pages only. The ClawHub listings were removed separately, outside this PR.
Why People with `skill_prefix=true` saw their skills lose the `gstack-` prefix after every update, OpenClaw users were sent to skill builds from April that were never updated, and PR bodies linked unrelated gstack issues whenever a commit cited issues in other repositories. Each fix removes one of those surprises.
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. title: /sync-gbrain reports failed pushes and imports instead of OK, and one bad queued path no longer blocks artifacts sync
body:
/sync-gbrain now says when an artifacts push failed or memory pages failed to import, instead of printing OK and "pushed", and one malformed queued path (from a skill started where the project slug was empty) no longer stops artifacts sync for every project. Why: people trusted those rows and lost track of unsynced work; fixes #4445, #4418 and #4417. Nothing to do after upgrading: a stuck `projects//timeline.jsonl` record is dropped and reported on the next sync. Thanks to @exGeni for all three reports and their hermetic reproductions.
What changed - **Malformed queued paths (#4445).** `gstack-brain-enqueue` refuses a path with an empty, `.` or `..` component (exit 1, nothing queued). The drain classifies such a record as `invalid` before staging, so git never stages it under another spelling; the record is dropped, the rest of the queue syncs, and the status message, stderr and `~/.gstack/.brain-sync-drops.json` name it. The writers' own local write to `projects/timeline.jsonl` is unchanged (out of scope). - **Failed pushes stay failed (#4418).** Every drain that pushes nothing goes through one helper: with local commits still not on origin, `ok` and `idle` become `push_failed`; `held` and `collision` keep their code (their attention line names the files) and carry the unpushed count in the message. This covers the drained-queue and nothing-stageable branches the empty-queue path already handled. - **brain-sync row (#4418).** The orchestrator reads the status file `gstack-brain-sync --once` wrote in this run instead of trusting exit 0: `ok` says "curated artifacts pushed to git", `idle` says "nothing new to push", `held`/`collision` are WARN, and `push_failed`/`blocked`/`error` are ERR `artifacts not pushed (: )`. When no status was written (sync off, lock held) the row says nothing was pushed. The gbrain page-count check still runs on every non-failure row. - **memory row (#4417).** `gstack-memory-ingest` writes its written/failed counts to `GSTACK_INGEST_RESULT_FILE` when the orchestrator sets it. Any failed page makes the row WARN, failed pages with none imported make it ERR, and the row shows the count and the first failure's cause (the child's FAILED lines were never shown by /sync-gbrain). Per-page failures still exit 0 and retry next run. - **/sync-gbrain skill text** tells the agent to report each row as printed: "pushed" only on `curated artifacts pushed`, and WARN/ERR rows as concerns. `docs/gbrain-sync-errors.md` gains entries for the new brain-sync ERR row and the malformed-path drop.
Tests Each new test failed on main e0c4136 before the fix and passes after: - `test/brain-sync.test.ts`: enqueue refuses malformed paths; a malformed queued record is dropped and reported while the clean record syncs (main: whole batch refused); push_failed survives a drain of an unchanged queued file and of a file gone from disk (main: `idle`). - `test/gstack-gbrain-sync.test.ts`: end to end with a real artifacts repo, the brain-sync row says pushed after a push and `ERR artifacts not pushed (push_failed: ...)` after a rejected push and on the run after it (main: OK "pushed"). The A5 page-count test now expects the "nothing was pushed" lead, since sync is off in that fixture. - `test/gstack-gbrain-sync-transcript-mode.test.ts`: a fake gbrain refuses every import; the memory row is ERR `0 imported, N failed` with gbrain's cause (main: OK), and OK again once imports succeed.

title: Plan a trial of /ship without its separate conductor subagent (GST-3003)
body:
Adds the locked plan for a paid trial: does /ship cost less and catch as much when the pull request's own thread runs it, instead of a separate subagent?
Why: that subagent's own steps cost about $22 of a $35 /ship run, and the keep-or-drop decision is written down here before anything is spent.
Nothing to do: no code changes; paid runs start only after this merges and the budget is approved.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Catch rule (b) now credits a fix only when the sealed regression test passes, so a reworded but unfixed bug earns nothing](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/vE2lt30JgTbMlQEk0cJu1wn8RFHlNliQrr0lsCKUKTI.png)

Catch rule (b) now credits a fix only when the sealed regression test passes, so a reworded but unfixed bug earns nothing.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Catch rule (b) now credits a fix only when the sealed regression test passes, so a reworded but unfixed bug earns nothing</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md § Scoring at 0ee5914 · source text (new in this change)
+++ After · docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md § Scoring on this branch · source text
+## Scoring
+judge: gpt-6-astra
+labels: 48
+agreement: 0.6
+paired: yes
+interval: 95%
+mdd: about $7 a run on cost (20% of C's $35; estimated from the profile's 121 to 308 conductor steps, so a per-run spread near $8, and 3 trials a case), and about 35 percentage points on catch rate; the pilot's measured spread is printed beside these and the bars do not move
+
+**Catches, by rule (no judge).** A trial catches its planted bug when either (a) a finding in the run's findings
+record (`merged.jsonl`) or final report names the labelled path, a line within 3 of the labelled line, and at least
+one cause word; or (b) the sealed regression test for the plant (from the label file, run by the runner, never shown to
+the arm) passes at the run's final head, and one of the run's findings or commit messages names that file. A case's catch rate in an arm is its catches over 3 trials. The script that applies this
+rule is checked against the decoys below before any trial runs.
+
+**Real problems, by judge.** Every finding that is not the plant and that the run marked blocking, or that led to a
+fix, goes to GPT-6 Astra with the case diff. It answers two questions: does this meet the blocking floor (would fail
+a test, break production, or lose data or secrets), and which other findings name the same problem. A case's real
+problems are the union of judged-real problems across all arms and trials; each arm's catch rate on them uses the
+rule above, with the judge's grouping in place of the planted label. The judge sees findings as A, B and C, never an
+arm name, model or cost. It is checked first against 48 hand-checked labels: findings from merged gstack pull
+requests outside the case set, 24 that led to a fix and 24 dismissed below the floor, each read against its diff by
+the runner and frozen with a SHA-256 before the judge sees any. `gstack-eval-plan judge --check` must print
+`JUDGE_AGREEMENT: ok` (Cohen's kappa at least 0.6) before its numbers count.
+
+**Comparisons.** Every comparison is paired by case: the per-case difference of means (cost, wall time, `calls=`)
+or of catch rates, with a 95% t interval over the 10 cases. Every trial is reported; nothing is averaged away.
~~~

</details>

Today every /ship run on Capy starts a separate subagent just to drive /ship's phases, and a profile of 12 runs put that subagent's own steps at most of the run's cost. This plan fixes, before any money is spent, how we will test dropping it. It uses three arms on the same 10 real gstack pull requests (today's /ship, /ship run by the thread itself, and the same model with no gstack and a plain review prompt), 3 trials each, paired comparisons with 95% intervals, the decision for every outcome, and stop rules under a $3,250 cap. Review caught one real hole before freeze, because a reworded but unfixed planted bug could have counted as fixed. The scoring rule now requires the sealed regression test to pass.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Does /ship need its conductor subagent?" (GST-3003). Writing the bars, arms and decisions down first means the result decides the question instead of being read to fit it.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

One new Markdown file under docs/evals/ and one changelog fragment; no code, prompt or skill changes. `gstack-docs-only` classes the file as pinned results, so the full CI suites still run (script ran: `DOCS_ONLY: no … pinned results`), and `gstack-eval-plan prereg --check` prints `PREREG: ok present=8/8`.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Light review (docs class, 0 runtime lines). Pass 1: my checklist read plus a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol), which both found the same problem: catch rule (b) credited a reworded but unfixed planted bug, contradicting the cosmetic-edit decoy. The plan's author accepted it and the rule was amended (commit 70933db). Pass 2 checked the fix with a fresh reviewer and a red-team reader, and found nothing blocking. Six notes below the floor stay open for the author: the label file should list the sealed regression test so its posted hash covers it; real problems have no sealed test, so say they are scored by clause (a) only; no decoy exercises clause (b)'s credit path (add a test-passes decoy and require the runner to prove the test ran); and a source fix's own test may still sit in the arm's checkout.

title: Secrets check stops flagging three code shapes and catches concatenated and commented secrets (GST-3004)
body:
The secrets check no longer stops a push on three kinds of ordinary code that only look like secrets: TypeScript types with spaced generic arguments, Python arguments that read a settings constant, and camelCase dotted field paths.
It also catches two kinds of real secrets it used to miss, one built with `+` from short pieces and one written in a comment, so pushes are both quieter and safer.
Nothing to do; a secret in any of the loosened positions still fails the check.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People hit the secrets check on code that holds no secret: `session: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof launch>>;`, `aws_secret_access_key=settings.S3_SECRET_KEY,` and `KEY = "form.section.fieldName"` each stopped a push. Those three shapes now pass. Each exemption reads the value's shape, never the key's name, and each has tests that put a real-looking secret in the same position and expect it to report.

Two misses are closed too. `KEY = "form.x" + "<secret>"` is reported because the string pieces of a `+` chain are joined and checked, and `x = 1  # API_KEY = "<secret>"` is reported after `#`, `//`, `/*` or an HTML comment opener, while prose in comments is not.

The dotted field path exemption applies only in source files, and only when the rest of the line holds no secret literal. So `password = "form.section.fieldName" or "<secret>"` and the same path in a `.env` or YAML file still report.

Known limits, still reported and documented in docs/pregate.md (allowlist them by value): JS/TS template keys, arrays of names, and generic types with string-literal arguments.

</details>

<details><summary>How it was checked</summary>

- New tests: `test/redact-env-kv-code-shapes.test.ts` (the three loosenings, each paired with holds, plus the known limits and every audit bypass line, which must report) and `test/redact-env-kv-misses.test.ts` (the two misses and a linear-time check on 40 KB lines). At main 0ee5914 every pass and miss test fails and every hold, known-limit and benign test passes. One pregate end-to-end case in `test/pregate-secrets-source-context.test.ts`.
- Every tracked text file in gstack (5,080) and gbrain (15,363) was scanned with main's scanner and with this branch's: no finding is added in gstack and one in gbrain (a commented-out template line in a test file); 1 and 3 false positives go away. Scan time is within 5%.
- Focused suites before the narrowing: 24 redact and pregate secrets test files, 781 pass; one existing pregate case (GST-2047) timed out at its 5 s limit under load and passes alone in 3.6 s.

</details>

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Second-model audit (GPT-6.1 Sol), two rounds. Round 1 at 1d93c56, 3,621 probes: HOLD, four bypasses (a spaced password with symbols in a template, array element or literal type; a regex literal in a template slot) and a quadratic slowdown on long space runs from the comment lookbehind; fixed once in 6a464d6 and fbb4156. Round 2 at fbb4156, 6,639 probes: HOLD, random 20-character hex under 3.0 bits/char passing the template-key and name-array exemptions (19 of 1,500 samples) and a `String.fromCharCode` slot. Per the Captain's ruling the PR was narrowed in f84cfad, not fixed again: the template-key, name-array and literal-type exemptions are removed and their false positives documented as known limits. Long-line timing after the fix: main 5.8 ms, branch 6.0 ms worst case.
Outside PR #4309 (@atharva081106) was read as text only; its template exemption is not carried. Thanks to @atharva081106 and to @LimpingWolf for #4289's regression table.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The secrets check runs before every push, so a false alarm on ordinary code blocks real work and teaches people to allowlist by reflex. Fewer false alarms and two closed misses make the check something people can trust.

</details>

title: /ship stops asking owners to clear base-side merge text and reviewers' confirmation prose (GST-2975, GST-2972)
body:
/ship no longer stops for an owner's ruling when a base merge only changes base-side text, such as the preamble hash in regenerated SKILL.md files, and a reviewer's confirmation prose becomes a finding the lead can lower with a reason.
Why: each of these cost a stopped /ship and an owner ruling on recent PRs (#4383, ghome#16, #4431), which keeps unattended shipping from finishing.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Base-side merge text (GST-2975).** After a merge from main, /ship counted two base-side differences as "behavior changed since review": the shared-preamble hash id in every regenerated skill file the branch also touched, and an expected-value list where main's new entry landed next to the branch's own. `comparePath` in `lib/ship-patch.ts` now reads every side with the shared-preamble ids masked, so a file whose only change is that id compares as unchanged. A line that is the base's new line plus exactly the tokens the branch added counts as base context and goes to one scoped reader instead of a full review. `lib/ship-release.ts` keeps those base-context test files out of the test-gate edit check.
- **Confirmation prose (GST-2972).** In `lib/review-ledger.ts`, a file:line in prose no longer anchors a finding, and in a `NO FINDINGS` reply neither does a list item or the native voice's FIXABLE tag. Under a verdict that declares fewer blockers, such a row is a summary candidate the lead can lower with a reason; until then it still blocks, so "NO FINDINGS … except the token leak in log.ts:3" still blocks.
- Docs: docs/review-policy.md (collector paragraph and verdict table) and a paragraph in docs/ship-policy.md on base-side text. Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/capy-ship-base-side-and-confirmation-prose.md`.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Each one cost an owner ruling and a stopped /ship" (#4431, #4383, ghome#16). /ship now tells base-side noise and confirmation prose apart from real changes and real blockers, so those runs finish on their own.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change touches the after-review route in `gstack-ship-release finish` and the reply collector every reviewer goes through. Both fail safe: every new path in `comparePath` falls back to the old "changed" verdict or to the scoped reader, and a prose row still blocks until the lead lowers it with a written reason (file:line read and walked failure paths by five reviewers; the new tests fail at main and pass here).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

16 of 19 changed code paths have a strong test (84% value-weighted). Three narrow fallback paths in `sideDiffs` (a side missing the path, a hash-object failure, scratch directory cleanup) have no test; the hash-object failure is not reachable without a test seam.
Tests: 1801 → 1801 test files in this run (the two new test files landed earlier on this branch).
Test value: 0 tests written, 1 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered.
Tests ran: tests 1683

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues. Five reviewers read the final code (a batched testing, security and state-machine reviewer, a red team, an adversarial reviewer, a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol, and a money-path reader); every one declared zero blockers. Six notes, all below the blocking floor, are left for follow-up:
- `lib/ship-patch.ts:209` (also raised at :195): `splicedHunk` matches the tokens the branch inserted but not their position, so a resolution that moves the branch's token to other code on the base's rewritten line reads as base context instead of changed. It still goes to the scoped reader.
- `lib/ship-patch.ts:269`: the scoped reader's brief says the branch's added lines are unchanged, which is not true for a spliced line.
- `lib/review-targeted-delta.ts:42`: the targeted-reader delta treats a spliced path as unchanged while the final shipping record counts it as the PR's own change (traced by reading, not reproduced).
- `lib/review-ledger.ts:322`: the `parseLabelled` comment says a prose file:line stops anchoring only in `NO FINDINGS` replies; the code and docs/review-policy.md apply it to every reply.
- `lib/ship-patch.ts:146`: with `diff.noprefix` or `diff.mnemonicPrefix` set in git config, an id-only change falls back to context or changed (the safe direction).
Second-model review: completed, clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional smoke, 2 probes, both pass on the reviewed tree: the base-side masking tests (`test/ship-base-side-masks.test.ts`) and the collector tests (`test/review-ledger-quiet-reply.test.ts`, `review-ledger-verdict-line`, `review-ledger-invariant`). The moved-token splice case from the review notes was not probed separately.

</details>

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: stop base-side merge text and confirmation prose from stopping /ship (GST-2975, GST-2972), without the round-grant work from #4449. Delivered: exactly those two changes, their tests, a Windows-curation entry for the new test and docs.

**Scope:** the branch capy/ship-base-side-and-confirmation-prose against base 88da124d (committed changes only; nothing staged, unstaged or new): lib/ship-patch.ts, lib/ship-release.ts, lib/review-ledger.ts, docs/review-policy.md, scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts, two new tests and one changelog fragment.

title: Unattended /autoplan runs its configured second-model review in the foreground, and run ids no longer collide (GST-3015)
body:
Unattended `/autoplan --full` now runs the second-model review when `codex_reviews: enabled` is set, runs it in the foreground with a 9-minute limit, and records a timeout with the standard failure line instead of ending the session. Two runs started in the same second also get different run ids now. Why: in a planning test, Opus 5.5 skipped the second reviewer in 2 of 3 runs over consent the config had already given, and ended the third session while the review ran in the background. Nothing to do: an unset `codex_reviews` is handled as before, and `disabled` is still enforced by the runner.
What changed ![Unattended /autoplan now treats codex_reviews: enabled as consent and runs the second-model review in the foreground](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/RH9JXLzq7DtRn7-T7pFjVu2V-fCn3M2nt8XR4IUpx7A.png) Unattended /autoplan now treats `codex_reviews: enabled` as consent and runs the second-model review in the foreground. The same before/after as text is in the Agent notes at the end (it quotes the new driver line, which uses an in-house word). Someone who turned on second-model reviews and ran /autoplan without watching got a plan reviewed by one model, because the agent read its general consent rule as covering the second review, or started that review in the background and ended the session before it finished. `gstack-autoplan next` now prints `OUTSIDE_CONSENT: given by codex_reviews=enabled` beside the second-model attempt, and the driver text says that setting is the owner's consent, that the review runs in the foreground under a 9-minute limit, and which line to record when it fails. Run ids also include six random letters before the timestamp, so two runs in directories with the same name no longer share an id and a checkpoint folder.
Why "I'm waiting on Codex's CEO review now", written right before an unattended session ended with the review still running, is the failure this fixes. A plan reviewed unattended now gets the second-model review its owner turned on, or a recorded reason it didn't.
Blast radius The change touches the unattended autoplan runner's `next` output, the generated autoplan/DRIVER.md and unattended profile, and the run id format. The run id stays `-...-<14-digit timestamp>` with the timestamp last, so the approvals importer's timestamp exemption still matches it; `test/autoplan-run-id.test.ts` imports a minted id through `buildRow` (script ran). A disabled setting still refuses before any dispatch (CLI probe 002 ran).

body:
Lets the /ship conductor trial use pull requests whose revert conflicts with later code, by resolving those conflicts by hand in docs, tests and the planted file only.
Why: only 5 of the 10 needed cases (and no large one) reverted cleanly, so the trial could not start as planned.

title: /ship reuses CI's passing run when a base merge changed no file, and stops before long local test runs or an unknown base (GST-3019)
body:
/ship's preflight and its CI-run lookup now reuse a passing CI test run when a base merge left the files unchanged, stop instead of quietly starting an hour-long test suite on the local machine, and refuse a `--base` that names no commit instead of reporting an empty diff. Why: gbrain #9662 lost a green CI run to a no-op base merge, then ran a 50-minute suite on a 4-CPU box, and its audit read a commit sha as a branch and saw zero changed files. Nothing to do: `--run-uncarried-here` restores running an uncovered suite locally under `--tests-only`.
What changed A merge of the base branch that changed no file used to throw away the green CI run of the commit before it, so /ship fell back to running the whole free suite on a small machine. Now a verified CI run of an earlier commit counts when git reads that commit's file tree as identical to HEAD's (`git rev-parse ^{tree}`), under every existing rule: same workflow, event, jobs and command, newest attempt, freshness, and a `tree.json` naming that tree. Only HEAD's newest 20 ancestors are candidates, and a newer red or running run on any of them still blocks. The output names the commit and run it used (`CI_CARRY_FROM:`, and `from= (same tree as HEAD)` on the Step 5 line). `gstack-ship-preflight --tests-only` now checks every mapped test suite read-only before anything starts. If one has no passing CI run to reuse, it starts nothing and stops with `SHIP_LANE_NOT_CARRIED`, naming the CI workflow to dispatch; `--run-uncarried-here` runs it on this machine instead. `--audit --base ` now diffs against that commit, and a base that names no commit stops with `SHIP_BASE_UNKNOWN` instead of reporting zero changed files. The review found two problems, fixed in 6b83917 with tests written first: a docs-only CI run skipped at an earlier commit now counts only when HEAD itself is docs-only against the base, and the `--tests-only` stop no longer runs one suite's per-file leftovers before noticing another suite has no CI run.
Why CI is the one full test run for gstack. Reusing an identical tree's run and refusing to start long suites by surprise keeps /ship fast on small machines without weakening what counts as tested.
Blast radius The change touches the CI-run lookup that /ship's preflight, its evidence recorder and its local gate check all share, plus `gstack-ship-preflight --tests-only`. It stays safe because git, not the run's own record, decides tree identity, and every earlier rule still applies to the earlier commit. That was read in `treeTwins` and `newestVerified` and exercised by the negative controls in the three changed test files (104 targeted tests ran and passed).
Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage. Tests: 1801 → 1801 test files (the two review-fix tests went into existing files). Coverage: 100% value-weighted (100% including 0 weakly covered paths). Test value: 0 tests written, 1 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. Tests ran: test 1683
Pre-Landing Review Two blocking problems were found by the second-model review and fixed (see What changed). Everything else is below the blocking floor and listed in the Agent notes: stale `--tests-only` advice in the release helper and the /ship driver, a race where waiting can return an earlier commit's finished run, a date-ordered ancestor window, extra GitHub API calls per identical commit, tests that read git history, a hex-looking base resolving a local branch first, and the new read-only check ignoring test exceptions. Two in-diff notes were skipped as below the floor: the `SHIP_LANE_NOT_CARRIED` text says "nothing ran here" even when a per-file leftover ran, and the 20-commit ancestor window is ordered by commit date across both parents. Second-model review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): completed, 2 blocking findings, both fixed.

title: Find the tests of a monorepo app that imports through its own @/ alias
body:
The checks that run before a PR opens now find the tests of a monorepo app that imports through its own `@/` alias.

Why: only the repository root's tsconfig was read for `paths`, so every source file in such an app failed as having no test, even with a test right beside it.

Nothing to do: a repo whose only tsconfig is at the root resolves exactly as before.

## Why (in your own words)

Our monorepo has an Expo app at `apps/mobile` whose `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` to `./src/*`. Its tests import the code they cover as `@/media/close-bar`. `/ship` stopped on 14 touched files in that app with `PREGATE_NO_LANE`, because the import graph reads `paths` and `baseUrl` from the root tsconfig only and could not follow any `@/` import under `apps/mobile`. The `--explain` output even names the gap ("specifiers in test files that resolve to no repo file ... or report the resolver gap"). The only workaround was a `dependencies` entry per source file.

This change reads each file's aliases from the nearest tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json above it that declares `paths` or `baseUrl` (itself or through a relative `extends`). A nested config that declares neither defers to the next one up, and the root config governs everything else, so no file loses an alias it has today.

## Live evidence

`repro.sh` builds a throwaway repo: a policy with a `dependencies` key, `apps/mobile/tsconfig.json` with `"paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }`, `apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts`, and a test beside it that imports `@/media/close-bar`. A branch edits `close-bar.ts`, then it runs `gstack-pregate --base main --allow-repo-commands --stage tests --only lanes --explain`. Temp paths are shortened to `<tmp>`.

Before, on main at e1cfceae:

```
PREGATE: tests fail in 0.2s — lanes: 1 touched file(s) with no test lane: apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts
tests      lanes     fail                195 ms  1 touched file(s) with no test lane: apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts (PREGATE_NO_LANE)
    lanes: FAIL lanes — apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts has no test lane
PREGATE: fail tree=b368cdc6bf05 head=5edc0df21634 checks=1 of 8
--- explain ---
apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts: no lane; specifiers in test files that resolve to no repo file: apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.test.ts: '@/media/close-bar' [touched]
apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts: if a test covers it, declare the file under dependencies in .gstack/pregate.json, or report the resolver gap [touched]
exit=1
```

After, on this branch:

```
PREGATE: tests pass in 0.2s — lanes: 1 tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0
tests      lanes     pass                236 ms  1 tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0
    lanes: ran: bun test './apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.test.ts'
    lanes:    1 pass
    lanes:    0 fail
PREGATE: pass tree=b368cdc6bf05 head=e0dffb0e8b4f checks=1 of 8
--- explain ---
apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.test.ts ← apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts (import) [touched]
```

The three new tests in `test/pregate-import-graph-paths.test.ts` fail on main and pass here:

```
# main's lib/pregate/import-graph.ts with the new tests
(fail) import graph: nested tsconfig paths govern the files under them > an alias in a nested tsconfig maps a source file under it to the test that imports it
(fail) import graph: nested tsconfig paths govern the files under them > each app resolves the same alias through its own config; the root config still governs files outside them
(fail) import graph: nested tsconfig paths govern the files under them > a nested config takes paths through a relative extends, joined relative to the config that declares them
 16 pass
 3 fail

# this branch
 19 pass
 0 fail
```

The reproduction script:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# repro.sh <gstack checkout>
set -eu
GSTACK=$1
T=$(mktemp -d)
git init -q --bare "$T/origin.git"
git init -q -b main "$T/work" && cd "$T/work"
git config user.email repro@example.com && git config user.name repro && git config commit.gpgsign false
git remote add origin "$T/origin.git"
mkdir -p .gstack apps/mobile/src/media
echo '{ "runner": "bun test {files}", "dependencies": { "README.md": [] } }' > .gstack/pregate.json
echo '# repro' > README.md
echo '{ "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } } }' > apps/mobile/tsconfig.json
echo 'export const label = () => "Close";' > apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts
printf '%s\n' "import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';" "import { label } from '@/media/close-bar';" "test('label', () => expect(label()).toBe('Close'));" > apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.test.ts
git add -A && git commit -q -m base && git push -q -u origin main
git checkout -q -b change
echo 'export const label = () => "Close";  // edited' > apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.ts
git commit -q -am 'edit close-bar'
GSTACK_HOME="$T/home" "$GSTACK/bin/gstack-pregate" --base main --allow-repo-commands --stage tests --only lanes --explain 2>&1 || echo "exit=$?"
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts` (`readPathAliases` takes a directory; new `pathAliasResolver` picks the governing config per importing file; `buildGraph` uses it), three tests, one paragraph in `docs/pregate.md`, a changelog fragment.
- **Verified live by:** the reproduction above on macOS with Bun 1.3.13; `bun run typecheck`; `test/pregate-import-graph-paths.test.ts`; the six other test files that use the import graph, where no test fails here that does not also fail on main. It has also run in a private pnpm monorepo's `/ship` since 2026-11-11.
- **Did NOT test:** Windows; TypeScript project references; the full free suite (`bun run test`).

title: /office-hours keeps its founder resources out of the skill file (GST-3024)
body:
/office-hours no longer carries its 34 founder videos and essays in the skill file; the closing runs a new `gstack-founder-resources` command that prints the ones a user hasn't been shown yet.
Why: the skill was 9 bytes from its size cap, and the approved partner-session improvements need room. This frees about 8.6 KB.
Nothing to do as a reader.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

The skill file was full, so the next round of /office-hours improvements had nowhere to go. The resource list now lives in `lib/founder-resources.ts` (the 34 entries exactly as the prompt had them), and the closing section runs `bin/gstack-founder-resources`. The command prints the totals, then either `RESOURCES: exhausted` or every entry the user hasn't seen, under its category header, in the prompt's own form. It reads what was already shown from the builder profile, or from `--shown`. The opt-out check still runs first, and the selection rules and format are unchanged.

Small behavior changes: selection now sees only the unshown entries (before, it saw all 34 and skipped shown URLs itself); "all shown" counts pool URLs instead of any 34 logged URLs, which is the same today; and when the builder profile can't be read the command says `PROFILE_READ: failed` and offers everything, as the prompt did.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

It frees the bytes the approved content change for /office-hours needs, without raising the skill's size cap.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the /office-hours closing section calls the new command, and the generated section matches its template (gen:skill-docs reports no stale output). title: Pre-push test selection finds tests in monorepo apps that use their own @/ alias
body:
/ship's pre-push test selection now finds the tests of a monorepo app that imports through its own `@/` alias (for example `apps/mobile` mapping `@/*` to `./src/*`).
Why: only the root tsconfig was read, so every touched file in such an app failed with `PREGATE_NO_LANE` even with a test beside it. Rebuilt from #4462 by @dtoelke, who found and fixed it; thank you.
Nothing to do: a repo whose only tsconfig is at the root (gstack itself) resolves exactly as before.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![A monorepo app's own @/ alias now maps its source file to the test beside it](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/Mqh5_P6cVukrh-cbl2dgyQdF3C_cbTz58uwNTrqIiJE.png)

A monorepo app's own @/ alias now maps its source file to the test beside it.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: A monorepo app's own @/ alias now maps its source file to the test beside it</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 $ testsFor apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.tsx   # apps/mobile/tsconfig.json maps @/* to ./src/*
+tests: apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.test.tsx
-tests: (none) -> PREGATE_NO_LANE
 
~~~

</details>

"My app's tests sit right next to the file, but /ship says there is no test for it." Each JS/TS file now takes its `paths` and `baseUrl` from the nearest tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json above it that declares them, itself or through a relative `extends` inside the repository. A nested config that declares neither defers to the next one up, and the root config governs the rest. Config files are read only when they resolve inside the repository and are under 1 MB, so a tracked tsconfig that is a symlink to a file outside the repository, or to a device such as `/dev/zero`, is skipped instead of read.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Every touched file in apps/mobile failed with PREGATE_NO_LANE even though its test was right beside it" (#4462). Monorepos with per-app aliases now get their tests picked before the push, and gstack's own single-tsconfig layout is unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `buildGraph` in `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts` changes: its callers (test selection, the flaky-exception check, the policy draft and the test-impact cache key) take the same graph type, and `lib/test-impact/key.ts` already hashes every nested `tsconfig*.json`, so no stale cache can reuse an old graph (file:line read by two reviewers). Reading configs through the existing `readRepoFile` also applies to the root config, so a root tsconfig larger than 1 MB, or a symlink out of the repository, is now treated as unreadable (test run).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two full review passes and one focused re-check of the last fix found nothing left that blocks. One finding was fixed in each round. In the first pass, a test reached into an internal helper, so the helper is now private and the test checks only the graph. In the second-model review, nested config files were read without a size or location check. They are now read through the existing bounded, in-repository reader, and a new test that failed before the fix passes now. The re-check confirmed that fix and noted one narrower gap, listed below. Four smaller notes are listed under Review notes and are left as follow-ups.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:283` notes from every nested config are printed for every file with no test found (same as red-team#1)
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:293` root fallback can apply aliases TypeScript would not, including through an unfollowed package-name extends (same as red-team#2; not a regression)
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:284` a nested config with only baseUrl now governs its files, so root alias edges they had before (e.g. @repo/* to packages/*) disappear; matches TypeScript and fails closed with PREGATE_NO_LANE
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:216` an unparseable nested config drops its aliases with no note in the explanation printed when no test is found (root config always behaved this way)
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:83` `readRepoFile` checks containment only when the last path part is a symlink, so a relative `extends` through a tracked directory symlink can still read an outside file (size and file-type limits still apply; it already worked this way before this PR)
- INFORMATIONAL `test/pregate-import-graph-paths.test.ts` a nested config whose aliases come only through an unfollowed package-name `extends` falls back to the root aliases (identical on main; reproduced in QA)

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

A functional smoke test ran on a throwaway monorepo built outside the checkout, calling `buildGraph` and `testsFor`. In the success case, `apps/mobile/src/media/close-bar.tsx` maps to its `@/` test. In the riskiest edge, a nested config whose aliases come only through an unfollowed package-name `extends` falls back to the root aliases and names that config in the notes, as the docs describe. Both captures were rerun after the review fix and passed (2 probes, 4 captures, verdict pass). The jsconfig-only and deleted-file paths were not probed.

</details>

<details><summary>Design Review</summary>

No frontend files changed — design review skipped.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

</details>

No review bot comments.

Scope Check: CLEAN

No plan file, so there were no plan checks to run (0 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED, 0 NOT RUN).

</details>

<details><summary>TODOS</summary>

No TODO items completed in this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

title: Check each app build with an agent from another model family before its owner is asked to try it (GST-3025)
body:
Adds `gstack-first-use`: before an app build reaches its owner as "ready to try", an agent from another model family plays that exact build, does the plan's first five day-one actions with a screenshot or video of each, and checks every link. Only then does it print the "try this build" message. Why: a recent app build passed every review and its owner still found the first screen broken, because nothing tried the build the way the owner would. Nothing to do now; the first real use is that app's next build.
What changed - `gstack-first-use start` freezes the first five rows of the plan's day-one table (the `/autoplan` table or the one-page list, one format) and the build fingerprint (commit plus TestFlight build or deploy version) into a write-once manifest. It refuses a missing or malformed table, a table with fewer than five complete rows, a row still marked assumed, a play spec missing any of the ten play-instruction parts, and a checker from the builder's model family. - `brief` prints the only thing the checker gets: device, account, play text and the five actions, with the commands to record each. Every value from the play spec in those commands is shell-quoted, so an account name with a quote, `$` or backtick can't run anything. On Capy it plays on a cloud phone through the host's phone tools. - `record`, `predict` and `links` keep one write-once file per result (evidence copied in and hashed), the checker's predicted 1-10 score, and a dated check per link. Results and link checks are bound to the owner-equivalent account and the build's device class; any other audience is refused or ignored. - `check` and `message` pass only for the same build, unchanged day-one rows, a pass with intact evidence for every action, every link live within 15 minutes, and a predicted score. `message` prints the "try this build" text with all ten parts; it never shows the prediction. - `score` keeps the owner's score and exact words beside the prediction in the owner's private user-level Capy Drive folder, never in a repository. `show` prints the gap.
Docs `docs/first-use-check.md` (steps, the pinned table format, the play-message requirements, where the record lives), troubleshooting anchors for the six new result codes, a README how-to row, and a short section in the Capy Captain guide.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/first-use.test.ts`: 22 pass, 0 fail (made-up owner and app; pins the day-one table, every refusal including fewer than five rows and an empty cell, a spec whose values hold `"`, `$` and a backtick, and the CLI end to end under a temporary HOME and drive) - [x] CI free suite at this tree (run 44192453838): 1688 files, exit 0

title: Tests and scratch repositories can no longer write approval rows into a real Capy Drive (GST-3027)
body:
Tests and scratch repositories in the temp directory can no longer write approval rows into your real Capy Drive. When `gstack-approvals` runs under `bun test`, or its state root or repository sits in the temp directory, a Drive mirror that resolves outside the temp directory (links followed) is refused with `APPROVAL_RECORD_WRITE_FAILED`; the local row is kept.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `lib/approval-record.ts`: `locate()` detects a fixture run and refuses a mirror that resolves outside the temp root; `writeMirror` fails with the refusal and keeps the local row. Drive roots outside the temp root are not read in a fixture.
- `test/approval-record.test.ts`: a failing-first test covers a fixture repository, a fixture state root, an explicit mirror directory, a Drive symlinked out of the fixture, the `NODE_ENV=test` case, and a positive control inside the temp root (GST-3027).
- `docs/troubleshooting.md` and a `changelog.d` entry describe the refusal and its fixes.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A review probe on 2026-11-09 wrote three QA rows into a real project-user Drive. Fixtures must never touch the owner's real data.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only runs that look like fixtures change behavior. Normal runs (state root and repository outside the temp directory, no `NODE_ENV=test`) mirror exactly as before; a smoke probe confirmed it.

<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 1 auto-fixed (p1/red-team#1, changelog title), 0 asked, 0 deferred, 5 noted; 1 blocking finding closed by a ruled note.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/approval-record.ts:131` Read-only callers lose the Drive roots in a fixture with no diagnostic; a missing grant reads as never granted.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/approval-record.ts:128` Temp root is only os.tmpdir(); a scratch repo under a literal /tmp is missed when TMPDIR points elsewhere (macOS /private/tmp vs /var/folders).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/approval-record.ts:79` Check-at-locate, write-later TOCTOU and dangling-link components; only matters against a deliberate attacker, not the accidental writes the guard targets.

title: Check a question against the owner's earlier answers before asking it again (GST-3025)
body:
An agent can now check a draft question against the owner's earlier answers before sending it, so the owner isn't asked again about something they already said yes to.
Why: owners repeat "don't ask me, just do it" across threads, because each new session forgets earlier answers. In a four-day sample, about 1% of 444 asks were repeats this could skip, so a two-week pilot decides whether it's kept.
Nothing to do: the new command is opt-in, and no existing command, install output or factory rule changes.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

An owner who already said "yes, merge when green" gets asked again by the next thread, because that thread never saw the answer. `gstack-owner-answers` keeps those answers in one record outside every repository (on Capy, the owner's private Drive folder) and `screen --ask-file` proposes leaving out only the lines that a verified, current standing yes in the owner's own words covers exactly. Everything else stays in the ask, with related answers shown beside it.

- Each answer is one file, written once; a correction is a new row that replaces the old one, and a second replacement of the same row is refused.
- A row can be taken only when it is a standing yes in the owner's own words, with no limits, not replaced, and verified by a second actor who read the cited source.
- `screen` keeps autoplan gate items, untyped, compound and limited lines, every "always a fresh ask" class, and any line where a newer or narrower answer for the same action can't be taken.
- A damaged, conflicting or unreadable record keeps every ask. So does a record folder that is a link leading out of the owner's folder, and a write that fails removes its own file.
- File format, fresh-ask classes and the pilot: docs/owner-answers.md. The nine new result codes: docs/troubleshooting.md.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

New files only, plus nine new entries in the result-code table and its generated anchor map (bin/gstack-doctor-components.sh); no existing command reads the new module (checked by grepping every caller of lib/owner-answers.ts: only bin/gstack-owner-answers and its test).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Coverage: 74% of 23 new code paths had a test at review time (17 of 23); the gaps were CLI `check`, `list`, argument errors, revoke through the CLI, an unreadable rows folder and long-quote truncation. Review fixes added 6 tests since. Tests ran: owner-answers 26. Tests ran: result-codes 394.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Six findings were fixed: a target that isn't one lower-case token was accepted; a multi-line agent name could forge output lines; a newer or narrower "no" didn't stop an older blanket yes from being proposed; a second replacement of a row left the record unreadable; a record folder linked outside the owner's folder was written and read through; and a failed write left an empty row behind. Nothing blocking is open. The second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol) completed and raised the last two.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

title: /office-hours checks for a real user first and ends startup sessions with a dated test (GST-3024)
body:
/office-hours now opens every startup session with one reality-check question (a paying user, or someone who used it this week unasked) and sends founders with no outcome yet, or a new **Pivot** goal, to a one-page decision memo instead of a design doc. Every startup session ends with a dated KILL/CONTINUE or SUCCESS line, which the next session on that project brings back once the date passes.
Why: founders were getting a polished design doc before anyone had used or paid for what they were building.
Nothing to do. #4463, which this builds on, is already on main.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Founders kept getting a polished design doc before anyone had paid for or used what they were building. Now the first question asks for one real outcome. Without one, the session becomes a memo session. It brings a ceiling check for pivots, a conversation quota with the math, a payment test, and a memo with one action and a kill date. Memos are saved as `*-memo-*.md` (repo copy in `docs/memos/`), so the design-doc lookup and plan reviews never read one as a design, including on branches whose names contain "design" or "memo".

The approved KILL/CONTINUE or SUCCESS line is recorded, and `gstack-developer-profile --kill-check <slug>` brings it back at the start of the next startup session once its date has passed (local date; an empty slug is an error instead of "nothing due"). Customer names and prices stay in the private `~/.gstack` copy; repo copies and second-opinion summaries use roles or initials. Builder mode is unchanged. The competitor search moved into its own section, and a "pivot" goal joins the question registry and signals.

This head rewords a set of coaching lines in plainer, general terms and shortens ten of the new lines so the merged text fits the size cap. Each technique keeps its meaning. That covers the ceiling check, the evidence ladder, the conversation quota, the payment test, the smallest first version, delivering by hand first, the pivot questions, memo routing and the reality check's skip and weak-answer rules.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

title: Review planner sorts Swift and Xcode files by risk instead of sending every iOS PR to the full panel (GST-3041)
body:
/ship's review planner now sorts Swift and Xcode files by risk, so a plain iOS UI change gets the light review instead of the full five-reader panel. Why: `gstack-diff-scope` had no rule for `.swift`, so every all-Swift diff printed `SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched` and the planner failed closed. Reported from the GHome iOS app's PR review. Nothing to do: unknown file types still fail closed exactly as before.
How each Apple path is classified, and why Every rule mirrors what the classifier already does for the JS/TS or Dart equivalent. The depth policy, thresholds and round caps are untouched. The planner now gets real scope flags instead of an error, and the outbound-client line rule in `lib/review-risk.ts` adds the Swift networking APIs, so a Swift network client still gets the full panel the way a `fetch` client does. A replay of the planner on the last 200 main commits, before and after that addition, gave identical plans for all 200. | Paths | Scope flags | Mirrors | Planned depth | |---|---|---|---| | `*.swift` (except `Package.swift`) | FRONTEND + BACKEND | `.dart`: the extension can't tell a SwiftUI view from a network client, so both reviewers' scopes apply | light, unless a risk rule fires | | Swift lines that open a network connection (`URLSession`, `URLRequest(`, `NWConnection`, Alamofire) | risk class security | `fetch(`, `axios`, `requests.get(`: the existing outbound-client line rule in `lib/review-risk.ts` | full | | `*.storyboard`, `*.xib`, `*.strings`, `*.stringsdict`, `*.xcstrings`, `*.xcassets/*` | FRONTEND | `.tsx`/`.html`/stylesheets: UI only | light | | `Info.plist`, `*-Info.plist`, `*.entitlements`, `*.xcprivacy` | AUTH + CONFIG | the existing `*permission*` auth arm: these hold URL schemes, App Transport Security exceptions, usage strings, keychain/push/HealthKit capabilities and declared data use | gate class, full | | `Package.swift`, `Package.resolved`, `Podfile`(`.lock`), `Cartfile`(`.resolved`) | CONFIG, never FRONTEND | `package.json`, `Gemfile.lock`, `pubspec.lock` | same as a JS dependency change | | `*.pbxproj`, `*.xcconfig`, `*.xcscheme`, `*.xcworkspacedata`, `*.xctestplan`, other `*.plist` | CONFIG, never FRONTEND | build and CI config | same as JS build config | | Swift under an auth path (`App/Auth/…`) or a keychain path (`App/Keychain/…`) | AUTH / secret path, as today | the extension-agnostic auth and secret-path rules already in place | gate class, full | `isFrontendPath` (`lib/frontend-scope.ts`) mirrors the new UI arm, and `gstack-design-detect` skips Swift and Apple UI files the way it already skips Dart, since its engine only reads web sources.
Tests - `test/review-plan-cli.test.ts`: a ghome#32-like SwiftUI diff plans `REVIEW_DEPTH: light` with no `DEPTH_ERROR` (red on main: `scope error: unmatched`, 5 dispatches); adding an `Info.plist` plans gate class, full depth. - `test/diff-scope.test.ts`: the ghome#32 file list (red on main with `SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched`), one table row per Apple path class above, and a negative control: a Metal shader (`.metal`) still prints `SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched` and exits 2. - `test/frontend-scope.test.ts`: new samples, including the bash/TypeScript parity run. - `test/gstack-design-detect.test.ts`: a `.swift` file never reaches the web design scan. - `test/review-risk-routing.test.ts` and the review-pin replay `GST-3041`: a Swift `URLSession` client plans full with risk class security, and a SwiftUI view stays light.
Agent notes Issue GST-3041 (from GHOM-1's report on garrytan/ghome#32). Plan: exempt: bug fix (R40) Open notes (below the blocking floor, not fixed here): - launchd and ExportOptions plists read as plain config, not auth. - Swift test files named `*Tests.swift` outside a test directory are not recognised as tests (over-reviews). - `Package@swift-*.swift` reads as UI and app code, not config (over-reviews). - An asset catalog's `Contents.json` may plan at docs depth through the data-file rule. - `URLSessionWebSocketTask` or `URLSessionConfiguration` alone still plan light. - `.xcconfig` key assignments and Swift Keychain calls (`SecItemAdd` and the like) carry no secret risk class; the pregate credential scan still runs. Approvals: a-d62fbde31bce (Captain GStack Minder: one scoped fix-check after round 2), a-5f3f591b9783 (Captain GStack Minder: the review-policy.md security-list edit). ```gstack-ship-receipt { title: Let autoplan revise accept a plan without section headings, as next does (GST-3050)
body:
`gstack-autoplan revise` now accepts a revised plan whenever the first `next` accepted its shape, so a run no longer pays for a full review round and then refuses the owner's edit.
Why: a plan with no section headings is reviewed whole by `next`, but once the owner added one heading, `revise` stopped with `PLAN_SECTIONS_INVALID`.
Nothing to do: runs already in progress pick this up too.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A plan with no section headings is reviewed whole by `next`. When the owner later added one heading while editing (say a `## Review record` listing the accepted changes), `revise` stopped with `PLAN_SECTIONS_INVALID` after a paid review round and pointed at a `--scaffold` flag the first `next` never asked for. It hit all four sessions in the day-one eval's third smoke repeat.

- **revise adds the missing heading when next would have.** When the run's first plan had no section headings (read from the run's restore point, which holds that plan's exact bytes, so older runs are covered without a `run.json` change) or the run was scaffolded, a revision missing exactly one heading gets it added in the run's own copy, and `revise` prints `SCAFFOLDED: added "<heading>" (...; copy at <out>/plan-source.v<k>.md; <file> unchanged)`. The owner's file is never edited. Duplicate, reversed or empty sections still refuse, as before.
- **Runs that started with both headings keep both.** Dropping one there would fold the private Review record into reviewed text, so `revise` still refuses, now saying `this run's first plan had both headings, so its revisions keep both`.
- **A different plan file is allowed, never silent.** `revise --plan <other file>` used to move `run.json`'s `plan_input` quietly. It now prints `PLAN_INPUT: <old> -> <new> (drift checks and later revises read <new>; pass --plan <old> to go back)` and records `plan_input_from` on the `plan_revised` journal row.
- The troubleshooting entry for `PLAN_SECTIONS_INVALID` and the revise notes in `docs/unattended.md` now describe both lines.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"revise refused the plan the first next accepted, after we paid for the round." The other option was for `next` to refuse or add headings up front, but `next` can't know what shape the owner's later edit will take, and refusing bare plans would break the documented "a plan with no headings is reviewed whole" path. Adding one missing heading is unambiguous (the same rule `next --scaffold` uses), so `revise` accepting it is the cheap, safe fix.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `gstack-autoplan revise` changes: `revisionText` in `lib/autoplan-revise.ts` and its one other caller, `settleEvidence`, which now reads `.text` from the same function. The restore file it reads is written once at init and never rewritten by revise (`lib/autoplan-run.ts:113`, read), and an unreadable restore file makes `firstPlanBare` return false, so revise refuses exactly as before (walked failure path).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues found. One review pass ran: a batched specialist reader (testing, security, state machines, red team) found nothing, and an adversarial reader found four low-severity notes, listed below; none would fail a test, break a run or lose data, so none was fixed here.

</details>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/result-codes.ts:542` PLAN_SECTIONS_INVALID fix text still suggests --scaffold for a mid-run revise refusal

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-revise.ts:41` first-plan-bare is re-derived from restore.md instead of recorded in state; fails closed
- Documentation leftover: `autoplan/DRIVER.md:129` still points only at `next --scaffold` for `PLAN_SECTIONS_INVALID`; agents load that file, so the docs audit left it for a follow-up.

</details>

title: Second-model plan reviews in autoplan stop being reported unavailable; --help stops printing a fake refusal (GST-3051)
body:
A second-model plan review in `/autoplan` is no longer reported as unavailable when it actually ran, and `gstack-outside-voice --help` no longer prints a line that reads like a real consent refusal.
Why: sessions believed the false label and paid to re-run the review, or closed the plan phase without its second-model review.
Nothing to do: the command autoplan already runs now picks the right check by itself.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![gstack-outside-voice --help: the two status lines are now indented examples, so no help line reads like a real consent refusal, and --gate lists autoplan](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/ZJi1cOsUHY82HqO1qBsQG3qSrEhYc2vq_5iqdHeQoao.png)

The help text now shows the two status lines as indented examples, so no help line reads like a real refusal, and `--gate` lists `autoplan`.

Before and after as text:

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 gstack-outside-voice — one outside voice, three runners (docs/unattended.md)
 
   run --runner <r> --prompt <file> --out <file> [--model <id>] [--result <file>] [--native-model <id>]
+      [--fallback <r>] [--gate review|structured|spec|proposal|autoplan] [--timeout-ms N] [--max-tokens N] [--cwd <dir>] [--json]
-      [--fallback <r>] [--gate review|structured|spec|proposal] [--timeout-ms N] [--max-tokens N] [--cwd <dir>] [--json]
   runners [--model <id>] [--json]        the runner table: id, capabilities, available here
   family <model-id>                      print the model family (anthropic, openai, google, ...)
 
@@ ⋯ 2 unchanged ⋯ @@
 cross-family subagent the host ran; needs --model). --max-tokens caps the api runner's output
 (Anthropic default 16384; its default time limit grows with it); a response cut off at the limit
 is unavailable (truncated). --native-model enforces the same-family
+rule. GSTACK_OUTSIDE_RUNNER names the fallback when --fallback is absent. --gate defaults to
+autoplan (its INPUT receipt and gstack-findings fence) when the prompt carries gstack-autoplan's
+RESULT FORMAT, else review. Writes <out>.meta.json and prints a status line, for example
+    OUTSIDE_STATUS: <status> provider=<runner> model=<id> family=<f>
+codex_reviews=disabled (or an unreadable config) refuses every runner before it starts, exit 3,
+with the status line
+    OUTSIDE_STATUS: not_run reason=consent_missing
+Enable: gstack-config set codex_reviews enabled.
-rule. GSTACK_OUTSIDE_RUNNER names the fallback when --fallback is absent.
-Prints OUTSIDE_STATUS: <status> provider=<runner> model=<id> family=<f> and writes <out>.meta.json.
-codex_reviews=disabled (or an unreadable config) refuses every runner before it starts:
-OUTSIDE_STATUS: not_run reason=consent_missing, exit 3. Enable: gstack-config set codex_reviews enabled.
 Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 fail · 2 usage · 3 refused or needs a flag
 
~~~

A plan review that followed autoplan's own result format was judged by `/review`'s rule, which wants a `Recommendation: ... because ...` line that autoplan never asks for, so a finished review came back `VERDICT: unavailable`. Now a prompt that carries autoplan's result format is checked against that format, which needs its `INPUT: <phase> <sha256>` line and its `gstack-findings` block. Critical or High rows read as findings, Medium, Low or no rows read as clean, and a reply missing the line or the block, or an empty reply, is still unavailable. `--gate autoplan` asks for this check on any prompt, and every other prompt keeps the old check. The text autoplan sends to reviewers is byte-for-byte unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Sessions saw "unavailable" on reviews that had run and either paid to run them again or dropped them (the day-one eval at e671a531 showed it). After this change the label matches what happened.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only autoplan calls `gstack-outside-voice run`. `/review` and `/ship` call `lib/outside-review-result.ts` with an explicit check name (`scripts/resolvers/outside-voice.ts:146`, read), so the new default never reaches them. The shared parser's other callers (`lib/autoplan-run.ts`, `lib/autoplan-carry.ts`) still pass the expected phase and hash, and the new runtime file `lib/autoplan-reconcile.ts` imports only types, so the Claude Code copy list stays complete (file read, and the targeted tests ran).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Tests: 1809 → 1809 (+0 new in this review; the PR itself adds `test/outside-voice-autoplan-gate.test.ts`)
Coverage: 82% value-weighted (82% including 0 weakly covered paths)
Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered.
Two small gaps are left as proposals: a Critical row mapping to P0 and an Informational row mapping to nothing (only High and Medium rows are tested), and the `outside-review-result.ts --verdict autoplan` command form has no test. Both were checked by hand during review and behave correctly.
Tests ran: targeted 339
Tests ran: free 1691 (files, from CI run 44219378952)

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues found. One review round; three low-severity notes, listed below, are recorded and not fixed here.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- `bin/gstack-outside-voice:84`: the check is picked by a plain text match on the whole prompt, so a prompt that only quotes autoplan's format header would get autoplan's check. Only autoplan calls this command today, and `--gate review` overrides it.
- `lib/outside-review-result.ts:271`: the autoplan check accepts any phase and hash in the `INPUT:` line, so a stale result file reads as completed until autoplan's own submit step refuses it.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md:390`: the sentence could also say that an explicit `--gate review` on an autoplan prompt still gives the old message.
- One parsed item was a line from the reviewer's own summary of the tests, not a defect.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Smoke checks on the built command: `--help` prints no line starting with `OUTSIDE_STATUS:` or `VERDICT:`; a reply with a Critical row under `--gate autoplan` reads `VERDICT: findings`, `FINDINGS: P0`, status completed; `outside-review-result.ts --verdict autoplan` gives the same verdict. QA's method files were not loaded for this small CLI change.

</details>

title: Review planner sends Swift health, permission and on-device storage code to full review (GST-3052)
body:
/ship's review planner now sends Swift code that asks for a privacy permission, reads HealthKit or calendar data, or writes, deletes or protects users' files on the device to the full review panel. Why: since #4469, iOS changes that asked for microphone permission, wrote and deleted meeting transcript files, or read calendars got the light, one-reader review. Reported from the GHome iOS app's PR review. Nothing to do: plain SwiftUI views, UserDefaults settings and file reads still plan light.
Tests - `test/review-risk-routing.test.ts`: 9 permission lines are security, 24 storage and data lines are data, 17 ordinary SwiftUI, UserDefaults and read lines raise nothing, and the rules ignore non-Swift and XCTest paths. A product `HearingTest.swift` permission request is security, and three calls split across lines are data. The first cases were written first and failed on main. - `test/review-plan-cli.test.ts`: a synthetic change that creates and deletes spill files (shaped like ghome#10), and one that reads calendars through EventKit (shaped like ghome#31), each mixed with Markdown and tests, plan full. The control, a SwiftUI settings view plus a model that reads and writes UserDefaults, plans light. No GHome code is copied. - `test/review-risk-redos.test.ts`: the new patterns run in linear time on 100k-character hostile lines. - CI: free-tests run 44231984976 at 2855b5e passed; the focused tests passed locally (231).
No-loss replay Preregistered before any run. The planner ran at main 29e95022 and at the final rules (39009fa) on the last 200 gstack main commits and on all 34 merged Apple-platform PRs (garrytan/ghome 33, garrytan/imsg-reader 1). - gstack: 200 of 200 identical (129 full, 71 light). - Apple PRs: **0 lowered**, 3 raised from light to full, 31 unchanged, no risk class lost. The raised PRs are ghome#10 (spill files created, written and removed), ghome#14 (speech and microphone permission requests) and ghome#31 (`calendars(for: .event)`). Eight already-full PRs also gained the data class. - A read-only second-model review (gpt-6.2-sol, medium) labeled every matched line blind. All 3 raises are true positives, so the raised-PR noise rate is 0 of 3. Caveat: those three are the reported PRs the rules were drafted from, and no other PR was raised, so the replay has no independent raise to judge. At line level, 35 of 49 matched lines are true. The 14 noise lines are mostly setup next to a real access (an `import`, an `HKHealthStore()` or `EKEventStore()` init, opening a `FileHandle`), plus one config file's file protection. At PR level, 11 of 12 are true. Those setup-only lines could raise a PR by themselves, for example an `import HealthKit` with no query. - The first run, at bd4b96b, led to one change: test temp-file cleanup in Swift test targets matched (gstack's classifier reads `Tests/GHomeTests/*.swift` as code), and it counted a ninth already-full PR (ghome#17) gaining data. The rules now skip XCTest paths. The review's two fixes in 39009fa (product `*Test.swift` files and split calls) were replayed again, with the same result as the run before them.
What changed The rules read only `.swift` files outside XCTest targets (`Tests/`, `*Tests/`, `*Tests.swift`), so TypeScript, this module's own regexes and test temp-file cleanup never match. A product file named `*Test.swift` is read like any other product file. **Security (a privacy permission request, like a `consent` path today):** - `request…Authorization` (speech, HealthKit, photos, location, tracking, notifications), `requestAccess`, `requestFullAccessToEvents`, `requestWriteOnlyAccessToEvents` (EventKit, camera, contacts), and `requestRecordPermission` (AVAudioSession and AVAudioApplication). These are in because a request is where an app first touches the user's private data. Trailing-closure calls with no `(` match too. **Data (user data read, stored, deleted or kept on the device):** - HealthKit: `import HealthKit`, `HKHealthStore`, `HK…Query`. EventKit and Contacts: `import EventKit`/`Contacts`, `EKEventStore`, `CNContactStore`, `.events(matching:)`, `.calendars(for:)`, `predicateForEvents…`, `.fetchReminders(`. - Calls that write or delete files: `.write(to:)`, `.write(toFile:)`, `.write(contentsOf:)`, `.removeItem(at:/atPath:)`, `.trashItem(at:)`, `.createFile(atPath:)`, `.replaceItem…(`, `FileHandle(forWritingTo:/forUpdating:)`, `OutputStream(url:/toFileAtPath:)`. A call split across lines (`removeItem(` then `at: url)`) is read over the file's changed lines joined. `temporaryDirectory` by itself is not a rule, because it is also read-only. - Protection and placement: `NSFileProtection…`, `FileProtectionType`, `.completeFileProtection…`, `.protectionKey`, app group containers (`forSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier`, `UserDefaults(suiteName: "group.…")`), and `isExcludedFromBackup`. - Retention: a `let`/`var` whose name says how long data lives (`…Retention…`, `keepDays`, `maxAge`, `purge…`, `deleteAfter`, `ttl`), and `olderThan:`/`purgeBefore:`/`deleteBefore:` arguments. **Out, on purpose:** - UserDefaults reads and writes, and `@AppStorage`. These are settings, and flagging writes would send every settings toggle to the full panel. Calendar choices saved this way still plan full when the same change reads EventKit. - `authorizationStatus()` checks, `EKCalendar`/`EKEvent` type mentions in views, `Data(contentsOf:)` and other reads, and names like `expiresAt` (token expiry, not data retention). - `print(…, to: &log)` and `write(to: &stream)` (text streams, not files). - Objective-C (`.m`, `.mm`): there is none in the replay population, and its selector syntax would need its own patterns. `docs/review-policy.md` now describes these rules under Risk classes.
Why Once `.swift` stopped failing closed, iOS changes that touched private user data planned the light review. These rules only add the security and data classes, so they can raise a plan to full but never lower one.
Blast radius Only review planning changes: `lib/review-risk.ts` (`matchRisk`) and the `RISK_RULES` hash, which is repinned to the GST-3052 replay. Swift diffs that hit these rules now get the full review panel. Nothing else in /ship, the tests it runs or the merge checks changes.
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs match the Swift privacy and storage review-routing change, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** base 29e95022 to head b8837060 (6 commits) plus an unstaged edit to docs/review-policy.md. Changed files: lib/review-risk.ts, its tests and pins, and changelog.d/review-plan-swift-user-data.md. | File | Status | |------|--------| | docs/review-policy.md | Current: the Swift paragraph matches SWIFT_PATH, SWIFT_TEST_PATH, SWIFT_SECURITY_LINE and SWIFT_DATA_LINE | | changelog.d/review-plan-swift-user-data.md | Current | | README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/skills.md | Not affected | **Coverage debt:** the Swift risk rules have reference coverage only (docs/review-policy.md). The permission list there is illustrative and omits tracking, contacts and reminders. There is no diagram drift.
Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 4 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 4 noted (round 2; round 1's 2 findings were fixed in 39009fa) Gate edits: none detected (7 listed, 4 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Two full review rounds on the plan gstack printed (gate class, full depth): a batched specialist (testing, security, state-machines), the Red Team, an adversarial reviewer and a second-model review (gpt-6.1-sol, clean). No finding met the blocking floor. A docs paragraph added after review got one scoped read, which was clean. Below the blocking floor, recorded here and not fixed in this PR: - `lib/review-risk.ts:235`: the joined-lines check for permission requests can never add a hit, because none of those patterns spans a newline. It costs one extra scan per changed Swift file. - `lib/review-risk.ts:236`: the joined-lines check allows at most 20 whitespace characters after `(`, so a split call whose next line is indented 20 or more spaces still plans light. Split calls never matched before this PR. - `lib/review-risk.ts:235`: joining every changed line in a file can match across two separate hunks. That only sends more files to full review. - `lib/review-risk.ts:137`: a singular-named XCTest file outside a `*Tests/` folder is now read, so its temp-file cleanup can raise data. That only sends more files to full review.
Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `matchRisk`: a Swift permission request is security, an on-device delete is data, a SwiftUI setting and a TypeScript path raise nothing (pass). The Red Team's two cases (a product `HearingTest.swift`, a split `removeItem(`) raised nothing at 539e422 and raise security and data at b883706 (pass after the fix).
Issues Refs GST-3052
Agent notes ## Agent notes GST-3052, GSTA-604. Prereg: GStack Minder drive reports/GSTA-604-prereg.md (sha256 95d75d44…). Replay data, scripts and reader labels: handoffs/GSTA-604/ (final run: run3). Decision trail: reports/GSTA-604-decisions.tsv. Out of scope: Android and Kotlin, depth policy, round caps, the Swift test-path classifier gap in lib/review-depth.ts. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=1 fixed=2 scope=frozen dispatches=8 ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch review-planner-swift-privacy-storage.
