title: Reused CI runs that passed only after a re-run are now marked instead of shown as clean passes (GST-3054)
body:
When /ship reuses a CI run that passed only after its failed jobs were re-run, its CI line and its final summary line now add `rerun=<files> attempts=<list>`.
Why: gbrain's CI now records which test files passed on a re-run (gbrain#9690), and a pass on a re-run must read as flaky, never as clean.
Nothing to do: runs without that record print as before; a malformed record is refused with `CI_CARRY_RERUN_MALFORMED`.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A CI run that went green only because someone re-ran its failed jobs looked exactly like a clean first-attempt pass when /ship reused it, so a flaky test could ship unnoticed. Now, when a run's `tree.json` lists `rerun_files` and `attempts`, the reused-run line, the stored test record and the final summary line all say how many files passed on a re-run and which attempts ran. The run is still accepted. Each re-run file is counted once per run even when two checks read the same run, and a check that reuses the same run without the record no longer hides the marker.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change touches the reused-run reader (`lib/run-evidence.ts`), the stored test record (`bin/gstack-evidence`) and the summary line (`lib/ship-receipt.ts`). It is safe for existing runs because every new field is optional, and a `tree.json` without `rerun_files` prints byte-for-byte as before, which `test/ci-carry-rerun.test.ts` checks with and without an inventory (script ran). The existing line parsers match single tokens such as ` runs=(\S+)`, so the inserted marker does not break them (file:line read by two reviewers).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Coverage: 75% value-weighted (83% including 1 weakly covered path).
Test value: 1 test written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 1 path weakly covered.
Gaps left as proposed tests: the `attempts=unrecorded` branch (a re-run record with no attempts list) has no row of its own, and the stored test record write in record-ci is reachable only with a live CI run (end-to-end only).
Regression proof — fails at HEAD: yes (import of the new helper fails before the fix) · passes at base: unavailable (new helper) · passes after fix: yes
Tests ran: tests 1692 (files, CI run 44230473580)

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two review rounds plus one owner-approved check of a one-line test fix. Round 1 found that re-run counts could be overwritten or double-counted when two checks or two run profiles read the same CI run; that is fixed. Round 2 and that last check found nothing to change. Second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol) completed; its two findings were the counting bugs above, fixed.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-release.ts:727` The /ship summary clips the CI_CARRY line at 240 characters, which can drop the rerun marker on a long multi-run line; the stored check record keeps the full text.
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts:158` gstack's own tree.json writer does not write rerun_files, so gstack's own reused runs never show the marker.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:248` attempts is validated even without rerun_files, so a writer using attempts for something else is refused (fails closed).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:254` Re-run data is only shape-checked: paths outside files, attempts [1] with re-run files, and a corrupt stored rerun entry is dropped silently.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt.ts:216` Across checks that share a run, the summary merges re-run counts with the maximum, a lower bound that is display-only.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Smoke: `bun test test/ci-carry-rerun.test.ts test/evidence-reuse.test.ts` covers one success (a re-run record carries and is marked) and the riskiest failure (a malformed record is refused); 11 of 11 passed before the fix round and the re-run test passes 5 of 5 at the final head. No plan checks (bug fix, no plan).

</details>

<details><summary>TODOS</summary>

No TODO items completed in this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

Status: current. docs/ship-policy.md, docs/pregate.md and docs/troubleshooting.md already describe the marker and the new error code, so the audit made no edits. The full audit section is in the Agent notes.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test test/ci-carry-rerun.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bun test test/free-fixtures.test.ts test/ci-carry-rerun.test.ts test/evidence-reuse.test.ts`: 23 pass, 0 fail

title: /ship's push step ends with one line that says whether it pushed (GST-3053)
body:
/ship's push step now always ends with one line that says what happened: `PUSH: pushed …`, `PUSH: already_pushed …` or `PUSH: failed reason=`, with the remote, branch and full commit. Why: an eval grader looked for a `git push` call and counted 48 real /ship pushes as "no push"; scripts and graders can now match this one line instead. If a script of yours matched the old `PUSH: ALREADY_PUSHED ` or `PUSH: pushed to origin/` lines, update it; the exit status is unchanged.
What changed - `gstack-ship-release push` (/ship Step 17) ends with exactly one of `PUSH: pushed remote=origin ref= head=`, `PUSH: already_pushed remote=origin ref= head=` or `PUSH: failed reason=PUSH_REFUSED|PUSH_REJECTED|PUSH_GIT_FAILED`. - The three reason codes are registered in `lib/result-codes-release.ts`, each with a `docs/troubleshooting.md` entry. The format is documented at `docs/unattended.md#push-line`. - Step 17 in `ship/SKILL.md.tmpl` and `ship/DRIVER.md.tmpl` now names the line, trimmed to stay under the skill and driver size limits. Generated files and golden copies are regenerated, and a changelog entry is added.

Why Outside tools need a stable way to tell whether /ship pushed. An eval grader searched for a `git push` call, found none in 48 real runs that did push, and scored them all as "no push". One fixed line, always last, is something any script can match.
Test Coverage New tests in `test/ship-release.test.ts` failed 3 of 3 on main at 29e9502 and pass here. They cover a push, a rerun at the pushed head, and refused, rejected and failed pushes with their exit codes. Coverage of the changed paths is 9 of 11. The two paths without their own test both end in `PUSH_GIT_FAILED` when git cannot reach the remote, and the smoke check below exercises that case.

title: Let CSO prepare a monorepo component without changing the Git snapshot root
body:
**Reproduction** — On macOS arm64 with CSO 3.0.0, put a pinned `requirements.txt` under `api/` in a Git monorepo with an npm package under `frontend/`. Commit the identical Python manifest at the root of a separate Git repository as a control. Run `gstack-cso-launcher doctor --repo <path>` against the monorepo root, its `api/` directory, and the standalone control.

**Observed** — The monorepo root reports `static-snapshot: ready` and `application-preparation: missing` (`MISSING_METADATA`). Pointing to `api/` reverses those results. The standalone control reports both as `ready`. Docker was ready in all three runs.

**Requested behavior** — Allow an explicit repository-relative preparation directory such as `api/`, while keeping the snapshot anchored at the Git root. With that directory selected, `doctor` should report both checks as `ready` without moving the manifest.

title: Codex /ship renders Claude-only Agent calls and stops at the coverage audit
body:
## What happened

After registering gstack for Codex, a fresh Codex session discovers `$ship` and the installed section links resolve. Step 7 in the Codex-rendered `gstack-ship/sections/test-coverage.md` still asks for Claude Code's `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` and `run_in_background: false`. The Codex session exposes its own subagent lifecycle. It cannot make the documented call, so the required coverage audit stops before a ship receipt.

The same instruction is present in the [shared template on upstream main](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/33b1a965bacb9ae28ac9281a1a70cbd987e54c01/ship/sections/test-coverage.md.tmpl). The Codex host renderer for v1.100.0.0 leaves it in the generated output.

**Expected behavior.** Render the appropriate reviewer dispatch for the Codex host. Preserve the existing requirement to wait for a terminal result, validate review evidence, and refuse shipping when required evidence is missing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Check out gstack v1.100.0.0 and run `./setup --host codex --no-browser`.
2. Open a fresh local Codex session in a small Git test repo on a feature branch with a passing test and no existing PR. Confirm the session lists `$ship`.
3. Run `$ship` through Step 7. The installed Codex section requests the Claude-specific tool and arguments above, and the coverage audit cannot start as written.

A source-only repro is to render `bun run gen:skill-docs --host codex --out-dir <scratch-directory>` and inspect `gstack-ship/sections/test-coverage.md` in the output.

## Additional evidence

- In an isolated candidate, mapping dispatch and wait to Codex's native subagent lifecycle ran the coverage audit successfully.
- For ledger-backed reviews, the observed native rollout did not expose the exact dispatched brief as plaintext. The existing ledger correctly refused to count those runs as verified. An isolated app-server adapter that binds the echoed input and final output to the acknowledged thread and turn passed brief, output, and judgment verification.
- With those changes, the ordinary local Orca Codex session completed a synthetic no-PR ship run and produced a valid receipt against a local bare origin. A separate workspace-write/no-shell-network CLI smoke still could not start the nested review transport with model connectivity. That is a separate runtime limitation.

title: Stop killing a working test run as stalled when its workers run in their own session
body:
/ship no longer kills a working test run as stalled when the test command starts its workers in their own session.

Why: the stall check measured CPU in the command's process group only, so under pnpm 11 a busy but quiet Vitest run read as idle and was killed.

Nothing to do: a command whose workers stay in its process group is measured and killed exactly as before.

## Why (in your own words)

Our monorepo runs its tests through `pnpm exec vitest run`. With pnpm 11, `pnpm exec` starts Vitest in a new session, so the workers are outside the process group gstack creates for the command. One of our suites prints nothing for longer than the stall timeout while it works. `/ship` ended `PREGATE_STALLED` three times in a row at the same tree, and the same suite was green when run by hand. The stall check was reading CPU time from the process group alone, where only the idle `pnpm` wrapper was left.

This change sums CPU over the command's process tree: its group plus every descendant reached by parent links, whatever session it started. A stall or timeout kill now signals the group of each such descendant too, so the worker is not left running after the command is killed. After a normal exit only the command's own group is cleaned up, as today.

## Live evidence

`repro.sh` builds a throwaway repo whose test command starts one worker in a new session (a detached spawn, which is what `pnpm exec` does). The worker is busy and silent for 8 seconds, then the command prints its result and exits 0. It runs `gstack-pregate --base main --allow-repo-commands --stage tests --only lanes --stall-timeout 3`. Temp paths are shortened to `<tmp>`.

Before, on main at dd4266dc:

```
PREGATE: tests incomplete in 3.3s — lanes: no test output for 3 s and its process group used under a tenth of one CPU; process group killed; last file started: test/util.test.js
tests      lanes     incomplete         3349 ms  no test output for 3 s and its process group used under a tenth of one CPU; process group killed; last file started: test/util.test.js (PREGATE_STALLED)
    lanes: ran: node run-tests.js 'test/util.test.js'
PREGATE: incomplete tree=fd2289dee249 head=8e052a07c1ae checks=1 of 8
exit=1
```

After, on this branch:

```
PREGATE_TEST: 1/1 test/util.test.js start
PREGATE_TEST: 1/1 test/util.test.js pass 8.1
PREGATE: tests pass in 8.4s — lanes: count unavailable tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0
tests      lanes     pass               8357 ms  count unavailable tests ran in 1 file(s), exit 0
    lanes: ran: node run-tests.js 'test/util.test.js'
    lanes:   1 pass, 0 fail
PREGATE: pass tree=fd2289dee249 head=73f81a72a9a6 checks=1 of 8
```

The two new tests in `test/pregate-supervise.test.ts` fail on main's `lib/pregate/supervise.ts` and pass here:

```
# main's supervise.ts with the new tests
(fail) supervise: process group, log file, stall and deadline > a worker the runner starts in its own session counts toward CPU: busy and silent runs to the end, never-ending is killed with the runner at the deadline
(fail) supervise: process group, log file, stall and deadline > a tree whose runner and own-session worker both sit idle is killed as stalled, worker included

# this branch: both pass
```

The reproduction script:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# repro.sh <gstack checkout>
set -eu
GSTACK=$1
T=$(mktemp -d)
git init -q --bare "$T/origin.git"
git init -q -b main "$T/work" && cd "$T/work"
git config user.email repro@example.com && git config user.name repro && git config commit.gpgsign false
git remote add origin "$T/origin.git"
mkdir -p .gstack lib test
echo '{ "runner": "node run-tests.js {files}", "dependencies": { "README.md": [], "run-tests.js": [] } }' > .gstack/pregate.json
echo '# repro' > README.md
cat > run-tests.js <<'JS'
const { spawn } = require('node:child_process');
const busy = 'const end = Date.now() + 8000; while (Date.now() < end) {}';
const worker = spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', busy], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' });
worker.on('exit', code => { console.log('1 pass, 0 fail'); process.exit(code ?? 1); });
JS
echo 'exports.add = (a, b) => a + b;' > lib/util.js
echo "require('../lib/util.js');" > test/util.test.js
git add -A && git commit -q -m base && git push -q -u origin main
git checkout -q -b change
echo 'exports.add = (a, b) => b + a;' > lib/util.js
git commit -q -am 'edit util'
GSTACK_HOME="$T/home" "$GSTACK/bin/gstack-pregate" --base main --allow-repo-commands --stage tests --only lanes --stall-timeout 3 2>&1 || echo "exit=$?"
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `lib/pregate/supervise.ts` (a process table with parent links, `processTree`, `treeCpuMs` in place of `groupCpuMs`, `killTree` for stall and timeout kills), two tests, the wording "process group" to "process tree" where the stall is described (`bin/gstack-pregate` help and cancel line, `lib/result-codes.ts`, `lib/pregate/config.ts`, the guard and stall detail lines, `docs/pregate.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`), a changelog fragment.
- **Verified live by:** the reproduction above on macOS with Bun 1.3.13 (the `ps -S` path); `bun run typecheck`; `test/pregate-supervise.test.ts`, where five other tests fail here and fail the same way on main. It has also run in a private pnpm 11 monorepo's `/ship` since 2026-11-12.
- **Did NOT test:** Linux (the `/proc` path is changed the same way but I ran it only on macOS); Windows (no CPU reading there, unchanged); a worker reparented away from the tree by a double fork, which is still not measured; the full free suite (`bun run test`).

title: Stop flagging unrelated tests when a property such as limit changes its number
body:
/ship's changed-number check no longer flags unrelated tests when an ordinary property such as `limit` changes.

Why: lowering `limit: 120` to `30` reported every test that used the word "limit" and held the number 120, so /ship stopped on files that had nothing to do with the change.

Nothing to do: constants with uppercase names and one-character values are matched exactly as before.

## Why (in your own words)

We lowered a rate limit from 120 to 30 in one module and updated its test. `/ship` then failed `PREGATE_LITERALS` on 30 other test files. None of them touched the rate limiter: each one used the word "limit" somewhere and held the number 120 somewhere.

`docs/pregate.md` and the comment on `consumersOf` already say that a call-site name such as `attempts` or `limit` is an ordinary word, so a test counts only when it also names the changed module. The code applied that rule only to one-character values. This change applies it whatever the value's length. It is one condition in `consumersOf`.

## Live evidence

`repro.sh` builds a throwaway repo: `src/rate-limits.ts` with `{ limit: 120, ... }`, its own test, and two unrelated tests that use the word "limit" and the number 120. A branch lowers the limit to 30 and updates the module's own test, then it runs `gstack-pregate --base main --only literals`.

Before, on main at dd4266dc:

```
preflight  literals  fail                141 ms  2 test location(s) still carry an old literal (PREGATE_LITERALS)
    literals: tests/pagination.test.ts:2: limit still 120 (now 30 in src/rate-limits.ts)
    literals: tests/upload.test.ts:2: limit still 120 (now 30 in src/rate-limits.ts)
PREGATE: fail tree=42cc85e53e48 head=ac5717e1c320 checks=1 of 8
exit=1
```

After, on this branch:

```
preflight  literals  pass                137 ms  1 changed literal(s), no test still carries an old value (3 test-tree files scanned)
PREGATE: pass tree=42cc85e53e48 head=92e39621dab8 checks=1 of 8
```

The new test in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts` fails on main's `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts` and passes here:

```
# main's literals.ts with the new test
+   "tests/pagination.test.ts:2",
+   "tests/upload.test.ts:2",
(fail) literals (pure) > consumersOf: a longer call-site literal needs the changed module in the file too

# this branch
 7 pass
 0 fail
```

The reproduction script:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# repro.sh <gstack checkout>
set -eu
GSTACK=$1
T=$(mktemp -d)
git init -q --bare "$T/origin.git"
git init -q -b main "$T/work" && cd "$T/work"
git config user.email repro@example.com && git config user.name repro && git config commit.gpgsign false
git remote add origin "$T/origin.git"
mkdir -p src tests
echo '# repro' > README.md
echo 'export const SEND_RATE = { limit: 120, windowMs: 60_000 };' > src/rate-limits.ts
printf '%s\n' "import { SEND_RATE } from '../src/rate-limits';" "expect(SEND_RATE.limit).toBe(120);" > tests/rate-limits.test.ts
printf '%s\n' "const page = await list({ limit: 50 });" "expect(page.rows.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(120);" > tests/pagination.test.ts
printf '%s\n' "// the size limit is checked before the upload starts" "expect(chunk(120)).toHaveLength(3);" > tests/upload.test.ts
git add -A && git commit -q -m base && git push -q -u origin main
git checkout -q -b change
echo 'export const SEND_RATE = { limit: 30, windowMs: 60_000 };' > src/rate-limits.ts
printf '%s\n' "import { SEND_RATE } from '../src/rate-limits';" "expect(SEND_RATE.limit).toBe(30);" > tests/rate-limits.test.ts
git commit -q -am 'lower the send rate limit'
GSTACK_HOME="$T/home" "$GSTACK/bin/gstack-pregate" --base main --only literals 2>&1 || echo "exit=$?"
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** one condition in `consumersOf` (`lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts`) and its comment, one test, one sentence in `docs/pregate.md`, a changelog fragment.
- **Verified live by:** the reproduction above on macOS with Bun 1.3.13; `bun run typecheck`; the `consumersOf` tests in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts`. The same rule has run in a private monorepo's `/ship` since 2026-11-08.
- **Did NOT test:** Windows; the full free suite (`bun run test`).

title: A round grant at the review round cap buys the fix round it names (GST-2968)
body:
When /ship stops at a pull request's review round cap, a grant naming that stop now buys one scoped review of the fix, in the same run or the next, instead of another read-only full review. Before, a grant recorded after the read-only review, or between /ship runs, bought nothing, so teams paid for extra full reviews or second grants (ghome#40: $8.78 against about $3). Nothing to do: /ship prints the grant command when it stops.
What changed ![The troubleshooting steps for the review round cap, before and after this change](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/_z0ADnYrYw7ZxvFCM1IxNzygZOePfgw58DUPoXNXfes.png) The troubleshooting steps for the review round cap, before and after. A grant now names the stopped review and buys one short review of the fix. The text version is in the notes at the end. A /ship run that hit the review round cap used to leave the team with no good move. A grant recorded after the read-only review bought nothing, and a grant recorded between runs was ignored, so the next run paid for another full review. Now /ship writes the stop into the PR description, a grant names that stop, and the next run reviews only the fix made since the stop. Each grant is used once, by the first run that claims it, and a later run no longer tries to reuse a grant someone already used. A grant recorded before any review still covers its own fix round, even after /ship merges the base branch in.
Why "A round grant at the review round cap buys nothing" (GST-2968, ghome#40). Teams that recorded a grant after a stop still paid for a second read-only full review, about $8.78 against about $3 for the short review of the fix that the grant was meant to buy. With this change the grant buys exactly the review round it names, once.
Blast radius The change touches the review planner, the PR-description bookkeeping that counts review rounds, the release step that checks the review chain, and the review summary. Every new path runs only when a grant and a recorded stop both exist, and the preregistered replay of 9,830,400 planning cases showed every decision unchanged outside the granted-round case (script ran: test/fixtures/review-pins/replays/GST-2968.json).
Test Coverage The coverage audit (it wrote no tests) found tests for 15 of 18 changed paths (83%), or 78% weighted by value. The review's fix round then added tests for claiming an unknown grant, for a grant another run already used, and for the range checks after a stop. One path is still weakly covered: the help anchors for the three new error codes, which only have an existence check. Tests ran: focused 39
Pre-Landing Review Two full review passes and a second-model review found nothing that blocks merge. The first pass found 6 small issues, all fixed in 5b8fd5d: two runs could both claim one grant, a fresh run could reuse a grant another run had used, the re-plans after a granted review could not keep the stop, the error text told a run to repeat a step that refuses to run twice, the release step accepted a grant on the wrong part of the review chain, and three tests were missing. The second pass and the later readers left 7 notes below the blocking floor, listed in the notes at the end and not fixed here.
Exploratory QA Smoke only: the focused test files (39 tests) and one live reproduction of the planner's usage error after a stop, which a test now covers. The QA method files were not loaded and no other probes ran, so exploratory coverage beyond that smoke did not run.
Design Review No frontend files changed, so design review was skipped.

The existing X14 test covers only the positive match. No test shows that a fix-check grant whose stop head falls inside a link but is not that link's range_base is now left unmatched. Before this change such a grant was matched by any SHA in ask/scope inside the range. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1142` cmdClaim gained a re-read after posting the grant marker. It refuses with GRANT_SPENT when another run's marker comes first, and fails when the re-read itself fails. Neither branch has a test. The re-read also only narrows the race: if a losing run writes its whole body after the winner's re-read, both runs can still confirm their claims. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-review-plan:164` This commit relaxes --stop to accept a later --range-base for 'the post-review or targeted re-plan after the granted fix-check'. The targeted re-plan still can't dispatch, though. Later in this file, targetedDelta gets granted=!!grant, where grant is only --grant, which needs a review_loop_grant row. grantedStop (--stop/--round-grant) is never passed through. So when a granted fix-check round changes code in a targeted class (auth, secret, gate, money, the likeliest classes for a fix round), targetedDelta skips with 'not docs-only, so it takes the review loop'. Passing the round grant's id as --grant is refused, because a review_round_grant row doesn't contain 'review_loop_grant'. Meanwhile gstack-ship-receipt write refuses review_targeted, because a targeted class changed since the read (its usage text). pr-body.md.tmpl tells the lane to 'add its --grant' at that point. The lane is left with no path to a receipt unless the owner records a second, review_loop_grant-style grant. No test covers a targeted re-plan with --stop. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1144` The new re-read in cmdClaim treats 'no grant marker for this id at all' (first === undefined) the same as 'another run's marker came first'. It reports GRANT_SPENT ('claimed by run another run') and tells the lane to record a new grant. A missing marker means some other whole-body write (a concurrent run's stub, stop or receipt write, or a hand edit) clobbered this run's marker, and nobody spent the grant. The lane gets told to buy a grant it doesn't need. A rerun of claim would succeed, because no marker exists. - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1139` 1. **The claim race is narrowed, not closed** (bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1139-1144). The PR body is replaced whole on every `gh pr edit`, so the last write wins. The new re-read after posting catches one case: another run overwrote this run's marker before the re-read. It misses the reverse order. Run A reads, B reads, A writes, A re-reads and sees itself first, then B writes over the body and re-reads and also sees itself first. Both runs print `GRANT_CLAIMED`, and A's claim marker is erased from the record, so history afterwards shows only B. This only happens when two /ship runs on the same PR claim the same grant within a few seconds. The current lane rule of one /ship per head makes that unlikely, but the check reads as a guarantee it doesn't give. A real fix needs a compare-and-swap that GitHub PR edits don't offer: an exclusive lock (for example a lock comment or a git ref the claim pushes), or a second re-read after a short delay plus a rule that the lexically smallest run wins. INVESTIGATE. Severity: Low. Blocks: no - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-review-plan:164` 2. **`--range-base` after `--stop` isn't limited to the re-plan cases it was added for** (bin/gstack-review-plan:164). The new check only requires the stop to be an ancestor of the range base. It doesn't require `--post-review` / `--last fix-check` or `--targeted-ran`, even though the error message describes the relaxation as being for those cases. So a lane's first fix-check plan after a stop can pass `--stop S --round-grant G --range-base R`, with R after the fix commits, and get `grantedStop` history with a fix range of only R..HEAD. The fix commits between S and R would then not be in the planned fix-check. It fails closed further down: `fixChecked` in lib/ship-release.ts now binds a fix-check grant only when `fc.head` is the link's own `range_base`, and a link starting at R doesn't hold the reviewed tree. Finish therefore refuses, but only after a fix-check reader has been spent on the wrong range. The check also doesn't require the range base to be an ancestor of HEAD. Fix: allow `range-base ≠ stop` only with `--post-review --last fix-check` or `--targeted-ran`, and require `ancestor(range-base, HEAD)`. FIXABLE. Severity: Low. Blocks: no - INFORMATIONAL `docs/troubleshooting.md:7443` 3. **One docs line wasn't re-wrapped** (docs/troubleshooting.md:~7443). The line starting "`. It adds `--round-grant --stop `…" runs to about 120 characters inside a list that is otherwise wrapped at 80. It's cosmetic only, and I found no lint for it. FIXABLE. Severity: Low. The lane or Captain records that grant: `gstack-approvals round-grant --pr + --head --kind fix-check --stop-run --findings + --reason --by `. +3. Commit the fix on top of the stop's head. title: gstack-post flags the ship receipt's own run id as pii.phone.e164
body:
**gstack version:** 1.100.0.0 (Linux, Claude Code host)

**What happened:** At /ship Step 19, `gstack-ship-receipt write --pr <n> --run <SESSION_ID> ... --body <file>` appends the ```gstack-ship-receipt``` JSON block to the PR body. Then `gstack-post pr-body <n> --body-file <file>` refused with exit 2:

```
RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 192 PART: body
gstack-post: MEDIUM findings; nothing was posted. Ask the user about each finding; to post these exact bytes, rerun with --confirm <token>.
```

The only phone-shaped string in the body is the receipt's own run id: the `SESSION_ID` that `gstack-skill-start` echoes, in the form `<pid>-<epoch>-<8 hex>`, e.g.

```
  "run": "1234567-1794900000-0a1b2c3d",
```

A 7-digit pid followed by a 10-digit epoch reads as an E.164 number.

**Expected:** The receipt gstack writes itself should post without a PII confirmation. `receiptDigitTokens` in `lib/gstack-post.ts` already exempts the receipt's 12-digit `tree=`/`head=` shas and 11-digit CI run ids, but not the session-id `run` field.

**Repro:** Run /ship until Step 19 in a session whose `SESSION_ID` pid has 7 digits, and post the receipt-bearing body with `gstack-post pr-body`.

**Suggested fix:** Inside a ```gstack-ship-receipt``` fence, exempt the `"run"` value when it matches the skill-start session-id shape (`^\d+-\d{10}-[0-9a-f]{8}$`), the same way the receipt's tree and head shas are exempt.

**Workaround used:** confirmed the token with `--confirm` after checking that the match was the run id.

title: Unattended /autoplan on Claude Code says its phase guard is on, and a report hidden in reasoning gets a clear fix (GST-3062)
body:
An unattended /autoplan run on Claude Code now says its phase guard is on, instead of saying it is off while the guard blocks it. A phase report written only in reasoning now gets a denial that says so and names the exact command to send.
Why: in the day-one eval, two runs were blocked by a guard their own record called off, and one run ended blocked after four publish attempts whose report was invisible.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![An unattended /autoplan start on Claude Code now says the phase guard is on, because Claude Code runs the hook whatever the session kind](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/FsDZtGcG5T9KkhW70K3kw7UX6q_HHJYLOF8KOKWTRE4.png)

An unattended /autoplan start on Claude Code now says the phase guard is on, because Claude Code runs the hook whatever the session kind.

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output (base 33b1a965)
+++ After · after.txt · captured output (this branch)
-autoplan guard: not enforced by this host; publication order is unverified (GUARD_NOT_INSTALLED)
+autoplan guard: enforced by Claude Code's /autoplan hook at phase Reads and reviewer dispatch; publish each phase report as visible message text, not reasoning, before the next phase (GUARD_ENFORCED)
~~~

Runs were stopped by a guard that their own start line called off. The start line now follows the host. On Claude Code, with no other host active and the installed `autoplan/SKILL.md` declaring the hook, it prints `GUARD_ENFORCED`. Everywhere else it prints `GUARD_NOT_INSTALLED` as before. `gstack-artifact validate` accepts either line in an unattended run's record.

When a `true autoplan-published` message after the close packet Read has no visible text, the guard now denies with its own corrective code, `publication_not_visible`, instead of the generic `publication_missing`. Every publication denial names the exact command (for example `true autoplan-published dx`), the line the report must start with, and says reasoning does not count. The guard still denies when the report is really missing, and a saved report file still does not count.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"The guard blocked the run while the record said it was off." Unattended Claude Code runs now get a start line that matches what the host does, and a stuck run gets a denial that tells it the one next step instead of a generic retry.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change touches the autoplan start line in `bin/gstack-skill-start`, the `gstack-autoplan` run record (`lib/autoplan-run.ts`), the publication hook's denial path and the validator's guard-line check. The validator accepts the old `GUARD_NOT_INSTALLED` line unchanged, so existing records still validate (`lib/headless-artifacts.ts:552` read, covered by `test/headless-artifacts.test.ts`). The full free suite passed in CI at this head (Free Tests run 44266618870).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Test Coverage Audit: 12 new code paths, 9 covered (75% have any test, 75% have a two-star or better test). No tests generated (audit only).

Tests: 1811 → 1811 (+0 new from the audit; the branch itself adds test/autoplan-publication-visible.test.ts).

Leftover gaps, proposed as follow-up tests:
- Guard status with an autoplan/SKILL.md that lacks the hook, has it only in the body, or is missing should give `GUARD_NOT_INSTALLED` in both bash and TypeScript.
- `initRun` with `CLAUDECODE=1` (the fixture removes it today).
- Denial text for phases 2, 2.5 and 3 naming design, dx and eng.

Tests ran: free 1693 files (37778 tests), reused from CI run 44266618870 at this exact tree.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues found. One review round on the whole diff (a batched specialist reader for testing, security, state machines and red-team, plus a same-model adversarial reader). Three findings sit below the blocking floor and are left as notes below.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

- `lib/autoplan-run.ts:133`: the `gstack-autoplan` runner records `GUARD_ENFORCED` whenever `CLAUDECODE` is set. A Claude Code agent that drives the runner through autoplan/DRIVER.md, without starting /autoplan as a skill, has no hook registered, so its run record would wrongly say the guard was on. The record line is wrong, but no test, run or data breaks. Follow-up: keep the runner on `GUARD_NOT_INSTALLED`, or claim enforcement only when the skill is provably active.
- `lib/autoplan-guard-status.ts:8`: the header comment names `test/autoplan-guard-status.test.ts`, which does not exist. The bash and TypeScript parity check lives in `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts:403`.
- `autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts:479`: if a journal ever leaves out message ids, a publish message that did have text, just not a correct report, would be denied as `publication_not_visible` instead of `publication_missing`. It still denies, so the guard stays safe, but the fix it names would be the wrong one.

</details>

title: Let an owner rule a blocker from the final review below the bar, so the PR ships with it listed (GST-2273, GST-3005)
body:
When /ship's last allowed review finds a blocker that the owner rules below the bar, the PR can now ship with that finding listed as a note, instead of staying stuck. This makes the review limit work the way docs/review-policy.md says. Nothing to do. ## What changed Before, a ruling after a round-2 full review changed nothing, though the docs said it closed the finding. A PR past its two review rounds had no way to record an owner-accepted deferral from its read-only final review either. Now: - A ruling names one open finding of the stop /ship recorded, by its review id: `gstack-approvals rule --pr --stop-run --head --finding `. - `gstack-ship-receipt ruled-stop` lists every open finding of that stop and says whether each one is ruled. Gate findings and security-class blockers can't be ruled, and a later commit voids the rulings. - When /ship records the PR's review result, `--ruled-stop` runs the same check again and saves the deferral (`second_pass`, or `read_only` when the PR already had two full rounds before this run). - The review log and its summary still show a ruled finding as open. Only /ship's saved result and the PR body show it as deferred by the owner. Two loose ends from #4479 are closed too. The review planner and /ship's finish step now honor a grant for the fix round only after `history` has matched it to the stop record. The `--by` docs now say what the code refuses (a first word of "gstack"). ## Blast radius /ship's handling of a stop at the review limit, and the review result it saves when given `--ruled-stop` or a `read_only` exception. Runs without them, review depth and reviewer prompts are unchanged.

title: Pull requests that merged a release reuse their earlier test run when the release only regenerated a declared file (GST-3067)
body:
When a pull request merges a release whose only extra change is a generated file the repo lists under `release_outputs`, its earlier remote test run now counts for it, if the clear command gets `--allow-repo-commands`. Why: gbrain paid one extra full CI run for each such pull request, several a day. Without the flag nothing changes except that the refusal now says to pass it; a hand edit to the generated file, or any other changed file, is still refused.
Tests - [x] The two changed test files: 10 pass, 0 fail on this branch; 5 pass, 5 fail on main. - [x] CI free suite (run 44287738353) at 7abca341ccd5: green, 1696 test files. - [x] Pre-merge guards (typecheck, module size, conflict markers) passed.
What changed ![The five new tests fail on main and pass on this branch, because clear now accepts a regenerated release output when given --allow-repo-commands](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/qbFyX0YKsL_swJT2JX8YpLdk_QW_9vzK-wC_205lIuE.png) The five new tests fail on main and pass on this branch, because clear now accepts a regenerated release output when given --allow-repo-commands. The text version of this picture is in the Agent notes. A pull request that merged a release commit into its branch had its earlier remote test run refused, even though the only difference was a generated file the release tool rewrites. The clear command checked that file against the `stamp_files` list before the release-output rule, and it never reran the release tool the way the two-commit comparison already does. Now a `release_outputs` file is judged by the release-output rule. With `--allow-repo-commands` the clear reruns `release_tool` on the recorded head and accepts the file when it comes out byte for byte the same. The troubleshooting entry for the refusal now says when the tool reruns.
Why "gbrain paid one extra full CI run for each such pull request, several a day" (gbrain#9679). After this, a release merge that only regenerated a declared file reuses the test run it already has.
Blast radius The rule lives in the shared `classifyFile`, so the two-commit comparison, the merge-time recheck, the merge-batch verifier and review-depth sizing also let a `release_outputs` path past `stamp_files`. That is safe because such a file still counts as unchanged only for exact version rewrites or a byte-for-byte rerun of the base branch's own release tool on the recorded head. gstack's own policy also keeps its tests out of any such substitution through `stamp_sensitive_gates` (read in the shared classifier and in the clear command's substitution code, and walked by the four new clear tests).
Test Coverage The clear path is covered by four new fixture tests and the two-commit comparison change by one. All five fail on main and pass here, as the picture above shows. Tests: 1814 → 1814 (+0 new files; the branch adds 5 tests in one new and one extended file) Coverage: 73% value-weighted (73% including 0 weakly covered paths) Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered (weak = ★, gate-failing or unrated). Gaps left as proposed tests: the `--run` clear and the CI reuse path passing `--allow-repo-commands` through, the "head is not a commit at the recorded tree" refusal, and an added release output with `stamp_files` set. Tests ran: tests 1696 (files, reused from CI run 44287738353)
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. The full review panel read the final reviewed tree once. It had a batched specialist reader (testing, security, state machines), a red-team reader, a native adversarial reader and a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol), which found nothing. Seven informational notes came back, and none is fixed in this PR because none would fail a test, break production or lose data: - No test covers the CI reuse path or the `--run` clear passing the flag through. - The "release_tool not rerun: head is not a commit at tree" refusal is untested. - The `release_outputs` exemption reaches every `classifyFile` caller, and the `stamp_files` descriptions in the ship-policy key reference and the remote-gate docs still call it the only list. - Accepted bytes can differ from the tested bytes in repos without `stamp_sensitive_gates` (gstack sets it). - The refusal names the missing flag before the head check, so following it can hit a second refusal. - A killed clear can leave a stale temporary worktree from the release-tool rerun. Paths and line numbers for each note are in the Agent notes.
Exploratory QA Functional (CLI) smoke, one probe: the two changed test files run against throwaway fixture repos (capture 001) and pass, 10 of 10. Not probed: the head-not-at-tree refusal, the `--run` clear and the CI reuse path.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

Plan Completion No plan file. This is a bug fix (plan exempt), so plan completion was not audited.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.

The documentation audit covered docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md and made one factual edit to the troubleshooting page, which now says when the clear command reruns the release tool and that it needs `--allow-repo-commands`. No blockers. The audit's full section is in the Agent notes.
Agent notes - `classifyFile` (lib/tree-receipt.ts) judges a `release_outputs` path by the release-output rule instead of refusing it through the `stamp_files` allowlist first. It is still a stamp only if its hunks are version rewrites or `release_tool` regenerates it byte for byte. - The GST-1176 regenerate step moved out of `buildReceipt` into one helper, `regenerateReleaseOutputs`, which the tree receipt and `gstack-pregate clear` both call; the added-file case no longer requires a `stamp_files` match either. - `clear --receipt` (and the `--run` / `--from-run` substitutions, which share `treeSubstitution`) rerun the tool only under `--allow-repo-commands`, and only on pregate.json's head when that commit's tree is the recorded tree; otherwise the residual says why. - GSTA-610 for GStack Minder (GSTA-36), GST-3067, from GBRA-108 / gbrain#9679. Decision trail: reports/GSTA-610-decisions.tsv in the Captain drive. Refs GST-3067 ### Documentation audit (verbatim) **Status:** updated. One factual edit to docs/troubleshooting.md. No blockers. **Scope:** base 44170d67 to head 90920868, 9 committed files and nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. The change: gstack-pregate clear (with --receipt, --run or the CI carry) now treats a regenerated `release_outputs` file as a stamp under rule `release_tool` when the file is in `release_outputs` and rerunning `release_tool` with --allow-repo-commands writes it byte for byte. The tree receipt now lets `release_outputs` paths through even when they aren't in `stamp_files`. **Documentation health:** - docs/pregate.md: current (updated on the branch; describes the rule, the flag and the `release_tool` rule name) - docs/ship-policy.md: current (updated on the branch; covers the `stamp_files` exception and pregate clear) - docs/troubleshooting.md: updated (the PREGATE_RECEIPT_INVALID entry now lists `release_outputs` and the --allow-repo-commands refusal) - changelog.d/pregate-clear-accepts-regenerated-release-outputs.md: current - README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md: current (no change to the public surface they cover) **Coverage debt:** none new. The behavior has reference coverage in pregate.md and ship-policy.md and a fix path in troubleshooting.md. The gate-ahead example in pregate.md doesn't show the --allow-repo-commands variant (minor how-to gap). No diagrams were affected. ### Test commands - `bun test test/pregate-remote-release-output.test.ts test/tree-receipt-release-tool.test.ts`: 10 pass, 0 fail (head); 5 pass, 5 fail (main) - gstack-pregate guards: typecheck, module-size, conflict-markers passed ### Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/tree-receipt.ts:148` A remote gate receipt can clear a head whose regenerated release output differs from the tested tree; repos without stamp_sensitive_gates get the GST-1176 rule (gstack sets it, so unaffected). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/tree-receipt.ts:108` The release_outputs allowlist exemption reaches review-depth sizing (stampPathsSince); undocumented in changelog/docs. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/remote-receipt.ts:110` notRerun checks the missing flag before the head-commit check, so following the hint can hit a second refusal. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/index.ts:131` release_tool rerun can leave a stale git worktree under tmp if gstack-pregate is SIGKILLed mid-run. Informational notes with paths: lib/pregate/index.ts:131 (CI reuse and --run flag threading untested), lib/pregate/remote-receipt.ts:110 (head-not-at-tree refusal untested), lib/tree-receipt.ts:108 with lib/ship-policy.ts:224 and docs/pregate.md:639 (stamp_files described as the only stamp list).

title: Unattended /autoplan records the owner's relayed gate reply instead of refusing it (GST-3068)
body:
An unattended /autoplan run that's handed the owner's reply at the final gate now records it and finishes, the same way whichever instruction file the agent reads. Before, autoplan/SKILL.md said "never approve" while autoplan/DRIVER.md said to record the relayed reply, so the outcome depended on which file the model followed. Nothing to do; this fixes existing instructions and adds no new feature.
What changed - **One gate rule, rendered into both files.** `AUTOPLAN_UNATTENDED_GATE_RULE` (scripts/resolvers/autoplan-driver.ts) renders word for word into `autoplan/sections/unattended.md` and DRIVER.md step 4. It says three things: never approve on your own judgment; with no owner reply, the run stops at `status=gate_pending`; record a reply relayed from the owner yourself with `gstack-autoplan answer ... --by agent: --owner-reply-file `, and never hand the owner the command to run. DRIVER.md's old "You never approve the gate for the owner" line is gone, and its `--by human` note stays in step 4. - **SKILL.md's gate step points to that rule.** The unattended sentence at the end of the reply-parse paragraph used to say "end here with its GSTACK_RESULT line and never approve". It now says "Read `sections/unattended.md` and settle the gate by its gate rule instead." - **gstack-skill-start says the same.** Its unattended block tells every skill "never approve a gate; the only exception is the one named in your skill's record rule", but autoplan's record rule named no exception, so an unattended session still read an unconditional ban. Autoplan's record rule now names the relayed-reply exception. - **No change to gate code.** `answer --by agent --owner-reply[-file]` already existed and already binds the owner's words.
Evidence (GEVA-549, no new paid eval) GEVA-549's day-one eval (at e671a531, and the same text at a2a421ba and 798782ae) produced two outcomes from one relayed "rec": - An A session followed DRIVER.md: `answer --gate-rev 4 --reply "rec" --by agent:claude-opus-5-5 --owner-reply-file ...`, then APPROVED and status=complete. - An S-full session followed SKILL.md: it refused to record the relayed "rec", told the owner to run the command themselves, and stayed gate_pending. This PR changes no eval pins or arms.
Size: paid for inside autoplan's existing cap The rule adds 282 bytes to `sections/unattended.md`. Autoplan's parity cap (SKILL.md plus sections, 1.1804 × 101,979 bytes) had about 1 byte of room on main, so these cuts in `autoplan/SKILL.md` pay for it. The cap is not raised. | Cut | Bytes | Why it's safe | |---|---|---| | The "What Auto-Decide Means" paragraph "**Never auto-decide User Challenges:** ..." moved into Decision Classification's User Challenge entry | 225 | It repeated that entry. Its two extra points ("or a premise is clearly wrong", "never mid-run; the user has context models lack") now sit in the entry, and so do the phrases test/autoplan-phase-order.test.ts checks for. | | "At the final approval gate give the original direction, proposed change, reasoning, blind spots and cost of being wrong (Phase 4 gate item)" replaced by "each is a Phase 4 `uc` approval" | 11 net | The gate.json step already lists those fields for each `uc` item (`why` = you said / both recommend / why / blind spots / cost if wrong). | | The last line of Completion, "Suggest `/ship` when ready to create the PR." | 46 | Option A already says "write review logs, suggest /ship". | | The unattended gate sentence in the reply-parse paragraph, rewritten as a pointer | 12 | It's the old rule, replaced by the pointer. | That's 294 bytes cut against 282 added: the union is 120,360 bytes, 15 under main's 120,375. The 12 per-host SKILL.md size pins in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` go down to the new sizes (pins only go down).
Tests - New `test/autoplan-unattended-gate-rule.test.ts` checks five things: - the rule appears word for word in the rendered unattended.md and DRIVER.md; - rendered SKILL.md, unattended.md and DRIVER.md contain no "never approve" sentence without the own-judgment condition; - a negative control: the detector catches GEVA-549's two old sentences; - SKILL.md's gate step points to the rule; - every flag the rule names is one `bin/gstack-autoplan` parses. - `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts` checks that autoplan's unattended block names the exception and that no other skill's block mentions `--owner-reply`. - `test/host-conformance.test.ts` checks the new pointer text instead of the removed "end here". - Local run: typecheck clean; 51 files (every test that reads autoplan's SKILL.md, plus parity, size, freshness, context, catalog, module-size, changelog and tripwire guards): 1,573 pass, 1 fail. The failure was a 5,001 ms timeout in gstack-skill-start's "autoplan guard line" test under load. It passed alone at the same tree in 3,285 ms, so it's marked flaky.
Review notes (below the blocking floor, not fixed here) Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/autoplan-driver.ts:88` Gate rule's answer command omits --rec-hash; a copied `rec` reply after recommend is refused with GATE_REC_STALE, which names the hash (fails safe, one retry) - INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/sections/unattended.md.tmpl:9` 'Relayed to you' is prose-only; the CLI cannot verify the words came from the owner. DRIVER.md already allowed this before the PR; needs a policy call (narrow wording or a provenance field) - INFORMATIONAL `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl:403` Unattended branch defers to the gate rule, which does not mention APPLY:/amend_pending handling or owner-brief close; DRIVER.md step 4 covers APPLY: - INFORMATIONAL `docs/unattended.md:42` Human doc still says the skill never approves; humans only, nothing runs wrong
Documentation **Status:** updated (one factual correction, no blockers) **Scope:** base 44170d67 to head d36b3aea on `unattended-autoplan-records-relayed-owner-reply`, with 2 commits and 14 committed files, and no staged, unstaged or new files. The change gives unattended /autoplan one gate rule, rendered from `scripts/resolvers/autoplan-driver.ts` into `autoplan/sections/unattended.md` and `autoplan/DRIVER.md`: a session never approves on its own judgment, and it records an owner's relayed reply with `--owner-reply-file`. `gstack-skill-start` names the same exception. **Documentation health:** - `docs/unattended.md`: Updated. The terminal-line section no longer says /autoplan always ends `gate_pending`; it now says that happens only when there is no owner reply, and how a relayed reply is recorded. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Current. `owner-reply-required` already documents `--owner-reply-file`. - `autoplan/*.tmpl`: Current. These are the authored sources of the change. - `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/skills.md`: Current. No gate details there. **Coverage debt:** `AUTOPLAN_UNATTENDED_GATE` is an internal resolver. The relayed-reply path has reference coverage in `docs/unattended.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` and how-to coverage in `docs/unattended.md` step 4. It has no tutorial (a common gap, not critical). **Diagram drift:** none found.

title: /ship no longer reports zero blockers when the second-model review found one (GST-3075)
body:
When /ship stopped on a second-model review finding marked "Blocks: yes", the record it left on the PR said no blockers were found; now the finding is counted and /ship will not write that record until it is fixed or ruled. Why: `ready` and the merge step trust that record, so an undercount let a blocked PR look clean. Nothing to do: the next /ship run logs Step 11's findings and checks them before writing.
What changed - Step 11's review-log row is now written with `via: ship` and the findings it raised (`open` for a blocker, `noted` below the floor), so a run that stops after Step 11 still records them. - `gstack-review-scope summary` counts findings on that row toward `blocking_found`, `deferred`, `noted` and `fixed`. The row is never a pass or a round. It also lists blockers whose newest action is still `open` (gate findings keep their own draft-PR path). - `gstack-ship-receipt write` refuses with `RECEIPT_BLOCKER_OPEN` (docs/troubleshooting.md#receipt-blocker-open) while such a blocker remains and no owner ruled note covers it. `stub` still records rounds mid-run. - docs/review-policy.md's counter table now describes the new `review_loop.open` field.
Why The /ship record written where the run stopped counted zero blockers although the second-model review's blocking finding had stopped the run. Before this change only a later Step 9 row carried queued Step 11 findings, and a run that stops after Step 11 writes none.
Blast radius The /ship record's counts and its write step only. Two existing summary tests encoded the old behavior (a `via: ship` adversarial-review row's blocker was ignored); their expected counts now include it. Records with blockers whose fixes were never logged (`unrecorded`) are still written as before. Evidence rung: script ran (`test/ship-receipt-voice-blockers.test.ts` fails on main and passes here; CI free-tests run 44304511662 green at ec80a9c).
Pre-Landing Review Two full review passes, the second-model review and one follow-up check of the fix since the stop. Four blockers were found and fixed. One finding from that follow-up check is still open and ships as an owner-ruled disclosed note (listed below); two blockers in code this PR did not change are deferred. A scoped read of the post-review docs edit (docs/review-policy.md) came back clean. Second-model review: completed (openai/gpt-6.1-sol), one blocking finding, fixed.
Deferred findings Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues. - Deferred: CRITICAL `lib/review-scope.ts:435` a late defer without a fingerprint never closes the voice blocker (rowLocus ignores f.locus); reader stated Low, Blocks: no; judge kept the parsed CRITICAL - Deferred: CRITICAL `lib/review-scope.ts:349` a High or Blocks: yes voice finding logged without blocking:true is not counted (rowBlocks only ranks CRITICAL); reader stated Low, Blocks: no; judge kept the parsed CRITICAL
Review notes Open notes, recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - Open (owner-ruled disclosed note, fc1/fix-check#1): CRITICAL `lib/review-scope.ts:493` a reopened blocker is cleared only by a later review row, never by an earlier fix commit; the record fails closed (it refuses to write rather than writing a false count), and the documented /ship flow logs the clearing row - Open (fc1/fix-check#2): INFORMATIONAL `docs/troubleshooting.md:7303` still names a follow-up review check (`fix-check`) as a way out of the open-blocker refusal - INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-scope.ts:436` one finding recorded under both its reviewer id and its fingerprint counts twice and can stay open (fails closed) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt.ts:500` the guard trusts the loop file and runs only with --review-loop; malformed open entries are dropped - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-receipt.ts:503` onHead accepts a ruling from any ancestor head, looser than finish's range rule - INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-scope.ts:294` The open doc comment says a following `fix-check` clears a later open; the code clears it only through a Review-Finding trailer or a newer non-open row (fails closed)

title: Security findings no longer show their file, line or reason in PR bodies (GST-3076)
body:
A security finding that an owner ruled a note, dispositioned, or that review deferred now shows in a PR body only as an opaque id and "security finding, details recorded privately".
Why: on a public repository the old lines named the file, line and reason of a live exposure outside the PR's change.
Nothing to do: other findings print exactly as before, and the details stay in the private approval record.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `Ruled note:`, `Gate disposition:` and the deferred-findings and review-notes sections redact any finding whose category is security, auth, secret or red-team. The /ship record block in the PR body stores the same redacted form.
- The full approvals table that a private repository's PR body carries redacts a security ruling's row too, so /ship's own body check no longer refuses that body.
- /ship's final body check and `gstack-post` refuse text that names a raw `path:line:security` fingerprint, and both refusals link to docs/troubleshooting.md#security-finding-in-body.
- Redaction applies on every repository, whatever its visibility. These lines are compared word for word when /ship finishes and when the PR merges, so they can't depend on a visibility lookup that can fail or change. A private repository can also go public with its PR history.
- `gstack-approvals list` still shows the full ruling.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A PR body is world-readable on a public repository, so a ruled or deferred security finding printed there pointed readers at a live exposure in code the PR did not change.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only how security-class findings are printed in PR bodies, approvals tables and posts. Other findings, the private approval record and the review log are unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No issues found. The fix for the private-repository approvals table was read again by one reviewer, scoped to that change, who found nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

Paid evals were not run for this PR: CI's paid eval slices are skipped on pull requests, and the scheduled release gate on main covers the selected cases.

</details>

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Refs p1/red-team#1
Refs p1/specialist-batched#1

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] Free suite: carried from CI run 44305297353 at this exact tree (1696 test files, 0 failed).
- [x] `bun test test/security-finding-redaction.test.ts test/approval-record.test.ts test/approval-classes.test.ts`: all green, none failed.

</details>

title: The token-capped /ship child on Claude Code now starts its prompt with the typed /ship command (GST-3078)
body:
The /ship child that `gstack-ship-budget launch` starts on Claude Code now opens its prompt with `/ship --continue ` (or `/gstack-ship` under `skill_prefix`), so Claude Code expands the skill instead of hoping the model finds it. Why: Claude Code expands a skill only when the prompt starts with the typed command, and unattended Opus 5.5 found a skill from its description in 0 of 60 sessions (gstack-evals#366). Nothing to do: the rule for parents is now in docs/unattended.md.
What changed - `lib/ship-handoff.ts`: the child prompt starts with the typed command, then the session id and the verify-handoff, steps and return instructions. The `--` before the prompt (#4452) stays. The command name follows `skill_prefix` from the gstack config, because a typed name that isn't installed expands to nothing. - `docs/unattended.md`: new section "Starting a child agent: type the skill first". - `docs/ship-budget.md`: the `launch` step now says the child's prompt opens with the typed `/ship --continue ` and links to that section. - `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md`: the Claude Code launch line said "tell it to load gstack and name the intended workflow", which invites the same prose prompt; it now says to start with the typed `/` and points at the docs section. - `test/ship-budget.test.ts`: a new test launches the child through a fake `claude` and checks the prompt starts with `/ship --continue `, and with `/gstack-ship` when `skill_prefix: true`. It failed on main (the prompt started with "Load gstack.") and passes now. No paid probe.
Is the Skill tool needed in the child's allowed tools? No The child keeps `--allowedTools Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob`. Claude Code's Agent SDK docs ("Commands in Agent SDK sessions") say a command is sent by putting it in the prompt, that dispatch doesn't depend on the `skills` option, and that sending `/` runs a user-invocable skill even when the skills list omits it. The Skill tool is the model's own way to load a skill, which is the route that failed. gstack-evals#366's typed arms also delivered the skill text with no Skill call. /ship reads its section files by path with Read, so adding Skill would only widen the child beyond edits and the shell. The `claude` CLI isn't installed on the machine that made this change, so its `--help` wasn't read; the docs are the source.

title: gstack-post no longer reads /ship's own run ids and commit ids as phone numbers (#4480)
body:
Posting a /ship PR body no longer stops on a phone-number warning for the run id and commit ids that /ship writes into it. Why: most /ship runs hit this confirm (#4480, and #4474), which turned a privacy guard into noise people click past. Nothing to do: the next /ship post goes through without `--confirm`.
What changed `gstack-post` skips only exact values that /ship's own tools write: - In a ```gstack-ship-receipt``` block that /ship's writer rendered (closed, schema-valid and byte-identical to `renderReceiptBlock`): the `run` value when it has the session-id shape `--<8 hex>` that `gstack-skill-start` mints, and the 12-character commit prefixes inside the `pregate` value (`@ ( checks, current for )`) and the `requires_remote` values (`heads=`, `tree=`). - On a line outside any code block that opens with `SHIP_RECEIPT:`, `CI_CARRY:`, `PREGATE:` or `READY_RECEIPT:`: the commit-prefix lists after `heads=`, `head=`, `tree=`, `gated_tree=`, `predecessor=`, `carried_from=` and `base_red=`, and the run id in each `ci_carried=:/` item. The #4474 hit was the all-digit head prefix `229446506618` after `heads=` and in the `pregate` value; its `runs=44231639842/1` list was already exempt. Replaying #4474's live body through the new code posts it with no finding.
Why this shape, and not a wider exemption The secrets and privacy scan is a security guard, so the exemption reads positions and exact shapes, the way the existing GST-2047 run-id exemption does: - **Not the whole block.** Some of its fields hold free text (`thread`, `pregate`, job names). Skipping the whole block would hide a real phone number written into one of them, and the GST-2047 test already pins a phone number in `thread` as a finding. - **Not the scanner's phone rule.** `lib/redact-patterns.ts` also guards pushes, approval records and the decision log. This change lives in `lib/gstack-post.ts` only, so no other caller gets looser. - **A hand-written block skips nothing.** Only a block that passes the schema and matches the writer's rendering byte for byte counts, so pasting JSON into a fence opens no hole. Still a finding, each pinned as a negative control in the new test: a phone number in prose, in a `json` or plain code block, in `thread`, in `run` when it isn't a session id, a session id with no random suffix, `heads=` on a line without one of the four prefixes, a phone number elsewhere on such a line, a 10-digit `ci_carried` run, one of those prefixed lines inside a ```` ```text ```` or `~~~` code block, and a hand-written one-line block.
Tests - The new `test/gstack-post.test.ts` case was written first and failed on main `3ecd716` with three `pii.phone.e164` findings; it passes now. `test/gstack-post.test.ts` and `test/gstack-post-cli.test.ts`: 62 pass, 0 fail. - Review fix (20c3b02): lines with those four prefixes inside a fenced code block are no longer skipped; its two new negative controls failed first on 4574561. `test/gstack-post.test.ts`: 57 pass, 0 fail at 20c3b02. - `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun run typecheck:test` reports no new diagnostics. - `docs/troubleshooting.md#redact-run-id-as-phone` lists the new positions.
Agent notes Refs #4480 - Lane GSTA-617 for GST-3083. Issue #4480 is from an outside author: its suggested regex was read as text only, and the fix was written fresh on main. - Decision trail: GStack Minder drive, reports/GSTA-617-decisions.tsv. - Review (light depth, 2 rounds): round 1 at 4574561 ran the batched specialist (no findings), a native adversarial voice and a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol). The second-model review found one blocker: receipt-looking lines inside any code block were skipped. Fixed in 20c3b02; round 2 (scoped red team, fix-check, native adversarial) found no blocker. - Review notes (below the floor, not fixed here): fences inside blockquotes, list items indented 4+ spaces and indented code blocks are not tracked, so receipt lines there keep the skip; a line opening with inline triple-backtick code opens a phantom fence (fails closed: one extra confirm); the older `receiptDigitTokens` allowlist still skips 12-digit values after `head=`/`tree=`/`gated_tree=`/`predecessor=` everywhere; the session-id shape keeps the pid fallback `gstack-skill-start` uses. - Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) - Exploratory QA: pass, 3 smoke probes at 20c3b02 through `gstack-post pr-body` with a stub `gh`. - Documentation: current (read-only audit of docs/ and changelog.d/). - CI_CARRY: accepted ci-carry tree=f74842bb8f0c tests=37832 runs=44325026986/1 profiles=ci-reuse/free-tests heads=20c3b02f1024 - PREGATE: warn tree=f74842bb8f0c head=20c3b02f1024 checks=8 of 8 (secrets warn: 29 MEDIUM pii.phone.e164 hits, all synthetic session ids, sha prefixes and 555 numbers in the new test fixtures and docs examples) ```gstack-ship-receipt { "schema_version": 1, "pr": 4488, "head": "20c3b02f1024b4982427b8cf05c3602fc86d504c", "version": "1.100.0.0", "base": "main", "gate": { "dispositions": [] }, "ci_carried": [ { "lane": "tests", "run": 44325026986, "attempt": 1, "tree": "f74842bb8f0c7d62c1cfe2696a2368b6cca449f5" } ], "calls": 22, "session_kind": "unattended", "run": "ship-4488-4574561", "head_tree": "f74842bb8f0c7d62c1cfe2696a2368b6cca449f5", "product_patch_id": "df278f0e5eb55e5169280780c29b0996ad0b1e44", "gstack_version": "1.100.0.0", "review_depth": { "depth": "light", "class": "code", "runtime_lines": 66, "rules": "1afa38a4be3b5eef", "base": "3ecd7168b2323fc60899a351a18595d7dd108c21", "registry": "3ecd7168b2323fc60899a351a18595d7dd108c21", "gate_scan": { "tagged": 0, "head": "20c3b02f1024b4982427b8cf05c3602fc86d504c" }, "reasons": [ "runtime=66" ], "risk": [], "mode": "panel" }, "pregate": "warn @f74842bb8f0c (8 checks, current for 20c3b02f1024)", "issues": { "fixes": [], "refs": [ 4480 ], "flakes": [] }, "docs": { "status": "current", "scope": "docs/ and changelog.d/ (read-only audit, docs-4488-1)" }, "review_loop": { "passes": 2, "blocking_found": 2, "deferred": 0, "noted": 10, "fixed": 2, "scope": "frozen", "fix_checks": 1, "rounds": 3, "ledgers_read": 6, "dispatches": { "specialist": 1, "red-team": 1 } }, "gate_dispositions": [] } ``` ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch post-skips-ship-ids-as-phones. title: /ship on Codex starts its audits with Codex's own subagent tools, not Claude Code's (#4476)
body:
On Codex, /ship and the other skills now start audit and reviewer subagents with Codex's own `spawn_agent` and wait on `wait_agent`, instead of Claude Code's Agent tool, which Codex can't call.
Why: Codex's /ship stopped at the Step 7 coverage audit and never finished (#4476).
Codex users need `multi_agent = true` under `[features]` in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Codex users running /ship hit a dead end at the test coverage audit: the Codex version of the skill told Codex to start a subagent with Claude Code's Agent tool, `subagent_type` and `run_in_background`, none of which Codex has, so the run stopped there. Now every audit and reviewer subagent in the Codex skills starts with Codex's `spawn_agent` (with `fork_turns: "none"` where the shared dispatch sentence is used) and waits on `wait_agent` for a final status.

- One Codex dispatch sentence lives in `hosts/codex.ts` (setup loads `hosts/` without the resolvers). Resolver sites render it on Codex, and the template sentences that spell out Claude Code's Agent call, plus the shared foreground-dispatch note, are rewritten for Codex through `toolRewrites`, the mechanism Hermes and OpenClaw already use.
- Sites fixed on Codex: /ship's coverage, plan-completion, Greptile and docs audits and its same-model adversarial reviewer; /review's same-model reviewer; /document-release's doc review; /office-hours' second opinion, design sketch and spec review; the design reviewers; the /plan-ceo-review spec review; /autoplan's four phases; /context-restore's transcript readers.
- The plan reviews' timed fallback reviewer needs a read-only Plan subagent type and a stoppable timer. Codex has neither, so on Codex it takes the unavailable path without launching anything.
- Claude Code's render and every other host's are byte-identical to main. Five Codex SKILL.md files got smaller, so their size pins go down.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

gstack promises the same workflows on Codex as on Claude Code; a /ship that can't get past its own coverage audit breaks that promise for every Codex user.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the Codex render changes. The edits are host-gated in the resolvers or live in Codex's own `toolRewrites`, and no checked-in Claude SKILL.md changed in this diff while the Skill Docs Freshness check passed at this head (CI run 44329740543), so the Claude output is byte-identical to main. A new test renders every Codex skill and fails on any leftover Claude-only subagent call; it failed on main with 66 lines and passes here.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues. The batched specialist review (testing, security, state machines, red team) found nothing; the same-model adversarial reviewer raised five informational notes, listed below, none above the blocking floor.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `hosts/codex.ts:11` CODEX_SUBAGENT_CALL and the autoplan/context-restore rewrites omit fork_turns: "none", so on Codex V2 those subagents inherit the parent transcript
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/outside-voice-steps.ts:750` Codex doc-review dispatch says wait until final status, then bounds it at a 5-minute timeout without a stop instruction
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/spec-review.ts:161` Codex non-CEO spec review says 'both inputs' but lists one
- INFORMATIONAL `docs/hosts.md:230` docs say multi_agent must be turned on; Codex config reference lists it on by default
- INFORMATIONAL `hosts/codex.ts:11` On Codex V2 wait_agent returns a status summary, not the child's final message

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Smoke, 2 probes on the current head, both passed:
- Rendered every Codex skill (`bun run gen:skill-docs --host codex`): no rendered file names `subagent_type`, `run_in_background` or `TaskStop`, and 16 files name `spawn_agent`.
- Riskiest changed path, the reported failure: Codex's /ship `sections/test-coverage.md` now dispatches the Step 7 audit through `spawn_agent` then `wait_agent` (lines 7, 13 and 376 of the render). The working tree stayed clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

Not run. The selector picked 8 PR probes (plan-ceo-review-plan-mode, plan-eng-coverage-audit, plan-review-report, review-exploratory-small-cli, ship-exploratory-late-input, ship-exploratory-plan-checks, ship-exploratory-small-cli, ship-exploratory-unavailable) and no quality judges. All of them run on the Claude render, which this PR leaves byte-identical to main, so none reads a changed input.

</details>

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Fixes #4476

</details>

<details><summary>TODOS</summary>

No TODO items completed in this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The documentation already describes the change, so no edits were made.

**Scope:** base 3ecd7168 to head 43e94352 on `codex-ship-starts-audits-with-spawn-agent`: 11 committed files (hosts/codex.ts, three resolvers, docs/hosts.md, a changelog fragment and tests). Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked.

**Documentation health:**

- docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md: Current. The toolRewrites row is still accurate.

**Coverage debt:** none found. The hosts.md paragraph lists fewer affected skills than the changelog fragment, which is acceptable because the fragment carries the full list.

title: Two owner-answer adds at once no longer collide, and three flaky tests get real fixes (GST-3084)
body:
Recording the same owner answer from two processes at once no longer fails about one time in ten; the second add waits for the first to finish writing. Why: this was a daily flaky-test repair, and the owner-answers "two processes adding at once" failure turned out to be a real race, not a flaky test. Nothing to do: tests only change, except the 11 lines in `lib/owner-answers.ts`.
What changed - **`lib/owner-answers.ts`, two races in a concurrent add.** (1) The winner creates the row file with `O_EXCL` and then writes it, so the loser could read an empty file and report `OWNER_ANSWERS_CONFLICT`. The loser now waits up to 2 s for the file to hold JSON before comparing; a row file that stays empty is still a conflict (new negative-control test). (2) `storeEscape` called `realpath` and then `lstat`, so a folder created by the other add between the two calls was refused as "a link that cannot be resolved". It now checks the folder exists first and only then resolves it. Publishing through a hard link was ruled out because the Capy Drive mount, where the record lives, refuses hard links. - **`test/owner-answers.test.ts`.** The new "created but not yet written" test now waits for the writer process to say it has started before the timed add begins, so a slow Bun start on a busy runner can't use up the 2 s wait. - **`test/sealed-stream.test.ts`.** The copied pre-fix helper judged git by exit status only. Under load Bun reports status 0 with `error: ENOBUFS` and a truncated stdout when git exits before the overflow kill lands, so "a 4 KiB maxBuffer reproduces the refusal" stopped throwing. The helper now counts a spawn error as a failure. - **The two /ship record test files (named in Agent notes).** Both set `setDefaultTimeout(30_000)`, the same limit CI passes. Two cases run 3.0 to 3.4 s on a 4-core machine with plain git and 7 to 11.6 s through a wrapped git, so a bare local `bun test` timed them out at Bun's 5 s default.
Evidence - owner-answers: a CLI stress of the test's exact command failed 22 of 200 pairs on main and 0 of 300 on this branch; the new "created but not yet written" test fails on main and passes here. - sealed-stream: under CPU load on Bun 1.4.2 (CI's pin), 74 of 80 runs of the case failed on main and 0 of 40 on this branch. Why Two people or agents recording the same owner answer at the same moment should both succeed. Before this change about one pair in ten got a conflict error for an answer that was identical, and three tests failed intermittently on loaded CI runners.
Blast radius `addAnswer` is called only from the `gstack-owner-answers` command, so the blocking 2 s wait can't stall a long-running process (file read of every caller). A link that really can't be resolved is still refused, and a row with different words is still a conflict (unit tests, plus a 12-process concurrent add run on this branch: 1 written, 11 present, no conflict).
Pre-Landing Review One reviewer read the whole diff and found one test that could still flake: it raced the writer process's start against the 2 s wait. That test is fixed in this PR. A second reader looking for failure modes found three low-severity edge cases, all of which fail closed (an error, never a false success); they are listed below and left as notes. A second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol) found nothing.
