title: The Codex readiness check and the second-model review pick the same model for a custom Codex provider (GST-3089)
body:
With a custom Codex provider, `gstack-codex-probe role-ready` and `gstack-outside-voice run --runner codex-cli` now resolve the plan-review model the same way, so a session no longer skips a review that would have run. Why: the check refused a `config.toml` naming `gpt-6-astra` while the runner ran it, and a day-one eval session dropped the second-model review in every phase. Nothing to do: a custom provider naming the frontier catalog ID just works; any other name now says how to opt in.
What changed - One resolver: `resolveCodexPlanReviewModel` reads the Codex config model through the same function the runtime selection uses, and `resolvePlanReviewModel` decides tier membership for a custom provider. - `gstack-codex-probe select-model` takes `--role plan-review` (the same selection `role-ready` makes, without its auth, sandbox and probe checks). The codex-cli runner passes it for the `autoplan` and `spec` gates, the same gates whose generated skill invocations use the plan-review role. Other gates keep their current selection. - Every policy refusal prints `CODEX_MODEL_POLICY: `, so the probe's stderr and the runner's `meta.json` detail show the same reason code. - Side effect on the stock OpenAI provider. For `autoplan` and `spec` the runner now runs the plan-review tier's model, as `role-ready` already did, instead of whatever `config.toml` names. - Docs: `docs/model-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md#model-policy-provider`, and a changelog fragment.
Why The named model counts as the frontier plan-review model only when it is exactly the selected tier's catalog ID (`gpt-6-astra` for the default frontier tier). The refusal exists for two reasons in `docs/model-policy.md`: gstack must not guess that a public ID works at someone else's endpoint, and generic coding-model settings must not quietly pick a cheaper plan reviewer. A catalog frontier ID that the user already routes to their endpoint is neither a guess nor cheaper, so the probe was wrong to refuse it. Any other name (a smart-tier ID, a deployment alias) could be any model, so the outside-voice runner was wrong to run it as a plan review. Both now refuse it with `custom_provider_model_not_tier` and point at `model_frontier_openai`, `GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL` or `plan_review_tier host`. A custom provider with no model keeps `custom_provider_requires_model`.
Blast radius Codex model selection for plan reviews only. Users of a custom Codex provider whose `config.toml` names the frontier catalog ID now get the review. Users naming any other model get a refusal with repair steps instead of a review on an unknown model. Stock-provider users of `autoplan` and `spec` now get the plan-review tier's model, matching what `role-ready` already checked.
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match the change, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** base 782f459 to head 5b5d10a (2 commits, 8 files), plus the unstaged changelog.d fragment. This change makes the Codex readiness check and the second-model review pick the same plan-review model for a custom Codex provider. **Documentation health** - docs/model-policy.md: current. It covers the exact-tier-ID exception, the `custom_provider_model_not_tier` refusal, and the shared selection between role-ready and outside-voice. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. It lists both `CODEX_MODEL_POLICY:` refusal lines. - Skill sections that call `select-model exec`: current, because `--role` is optional. **Coverage debt:** `gstack-codex-probe select-model --role plan-review` is documented only in the probe's usage text (reference coverage only). No diagram drift was found.
Tests `test/codex-custom-provider-agreement.test.ts` (synthetic `CODEX_HOME/config.toml`, fake codex CLI, no paid calls) runs both tools on: a custom provider naming `gpt-6-astra` (both accept and run it), naming `gpt-6.1-sol` (both refuse, same reason code, nothing sent), naming no model (both refuse, same reason code), the smart tier accepting the smart ID, and a stock-provider control. The four agreement cases failed on 782f459 before the fix. The full free suite ran in CI (run 44346384986). Pre-Landing Review: 4 issues, 0 fixed, 0 deferred, 4 noted (all below the blocking floor). One full review round at tree e09a007e (reviewer: batched testing/security/state-machines/red-team checklist, NO FINDINGS; adversarial reader: three low notes). No second-model review: the review plan skips it for this code class. Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Coverage gate: 75% (9 of 12 changed paths have a test; target 80%). No test generation was authorized for this run, so the three small gaps are listed as proposed tests: - `selectionRepair` for a `native` source (`lib/model-policy.ts`): one row in `test/model-policy.test.ts`. - The runner leaves `--role plan-review` off for gates other than `autoplan` and `spec` (`lib/outside-voice-runner.ts`). - `role-ready` still rejects `--role`: one more row in the agreement test's bad-arguments loop. Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: make role-ready and the codex-cli runner pick the same plan-review model for a custom Codex provider. Delivered: one shared resolver, `select-model --role plan-review`, the shared reason code, docs and the agreement test.
Review notes - `lib/model-policy-cli.ts:328`: `gstack-models resolve` and `list` call `resolvePlanReviewModel` without the config.toml reader, so this diagnostic still reports `custom_provider_requires_model` for a custom provider naming the tier's catalog ID, while the check and the review accept it. - `scripts/resolve-codex-generation-model.ts`: under custom routing, a malformed or unreadable `config.toml` is still refused, but with a plain error and no `CODEX_MODEL_POLICY:` line. The changelog now says "each of these policy refusals". - `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:135`: with the stock provider, `autoplan` and `spec` now run the catalog plan-review model without the model probe `role-ready` runs, so an account that cannot use it sees the review fail at dispatch. Intended and documented above. - [ADVISORY] `lib/model-policy.ts:576`: policy errors join problem and cause with a bare space (unchanged from main).
Exploratory QA Status: pass (4 smoke probes on isolated fixtures, `bin/gstack-codex-probe` at 5b5d10a). A custom provider naming `gpt-6-astra` selects it for plan review (exit 0). One naming a deployment alias is refused with `CODEX_MODEL_POLICY: custom_provider_model_not_tier` and the three opt-in repairs (exit 1, nothing selected). `role-ready --role` is a usage error (exit 64). `select-model exec` without `--role` keeps the alias (exit 0). The runner path is covered by the agreement test, not probed here.

title: Commands that read cut-off output now fail instead of judging part of it (GST-3086)
body:
Commands that read large git or gh output, including the credential pre-push hook, the pre-merge secret and literal scans and the sealed-output guard, now fail when Bun cuts that output off, instead of judging the part they got.
Why: Bun can report exit status 0 together with ENOBUFS and partial stdout, so a push whose diff passed 64 MiB could get a credential past the pre-push hook.
Nothing to do: the failure names `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` and links its troubleshooting entry.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **`lib/spawn-sync.ts`** exports a `spawnSync` with Node's exact signature. When the result carries `error` and a non-null status, or the error is ENOBUFS, it returns `status: null`, keeps `error.code`, adds `(SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE)` to `error.message`, and appends a line naming the code and its troubleshooting entry to a captured stderr. It imports nothing from lib/, because the paid test runner's global import closure includes it. Everything else passes through unchanged, so a launch failure or timeout that already had status null keeps its message.
- **131 product files** in lib/, bin/, scripts/ and crew/scripts now import it instead of `node:child_process`. They are the files with a buffered `spawnSync` that reads output of unbounded size: an explicit `maxBuffer`, a generic `git`/`gh` wrapper taking arbitrary args, or a diff, show, log, cat-file, ls-files, ls-tree, grep, merge-file or api read. Every `status === 0` check there now fails closed with no call-site change.
- **Three reads needed more than the import:** `listRepoFiles` (test selection for the pre-merge checks) read stdout with no status check and now throws on a spawn error; `gstack-design-detect`'s `Bun.spawnSync` engine call now treats `exitedDueToMaxBuffer` as too large; the pre-push hook's `gitStrict` error now carries the reason code.
- **`SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE`** is in `lib/result-codes-release.ts` (lib/result-codes.ts is at the 800-line module cap) with a `docs/troubleshooting.md#spawn-output-incomplete` entry.
- Left alone: `execFileSync`/`execSync` (Bun throws ENOBUFS even at status 0; the one catch that reads `err.stdout`, gbrain doctor, JSON-parses it, so a cut-off read fails the parse), unbuffered calls, `Bun.spawnSync` without `maxBuffer` (no limit), small-output probes, browse/src (no unbounded buffered read; it bundles without lib/), and tests' own spawn helpers (out of scope, #4490).

</details>

<details><summary>Testing</summary>

- `test/spawn-sync.test.ts` (new): a Bun child that ignores SIGTERM and prints 200 KB under a 1 KiB `maxBuffer` gives raw `spawnSync` status 0 with ENOBUFS every time (the GSTA-618 finding), and the helper turns it into status null with the code, in string and Buffer mode; clean reads and plain non-zero exits pass through. The scanner case runs the real pre-push hook with a stub `git` whose diff prints about 90 MB before the real diff, ignores SIGTERM and exits 0. **On main the push carrying an AWS-format key exits 0 (allowed); on this branch it exits 1 with `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE`.** The shell-stub cases skip on Windows.
- Passed locally: `bun run typecheck`; module-size ratchet, spawnSync timeout tripwire, troubleshooting anchors, Bun entry isolation and state-root ratchet (428 pass); the redact pre-push, design-detect, import-graph, gbrain-exec and pre-merge secret-scan suites (336 tests, one pinned-wording failure fixed, then 56/56 on the hook file); 609 passing tests in the suites that exercise overflow paths, from a run cancelled before its summary line (its failures are listed next).
- Failed locally, and identically with this branch's edits stashed, so not counted against it: 12 CSO tests (`bin/gstack-cso-launcher` is not built in this checkout) and 2 `test/evidence.test.ts` cases hitting their 5 s limit under a concurrent run. CI is the full run.

</details>

<details><summary>Open review notes (none block)</summary>

- `lib/script-invocation.ts` (`runScriptSync`, `runBashSync`) still calls node's `spawnSync` directly, so the pre-merge test-selection manifest read and the /ship review-log read can still take cut-off output as complete; about 60 product files keep a raw import and nothing stops a new one. The changelog line's "the other gstack commands that read large git or gh output" is broader than this change. Follow-up: route `script-invocation.ts` with an overflow test and add an import ratchet, or narrow the release note.
- `browse/src/session-name.ts:90` reads `ps -A` under the 1 MiB default with no error check; left alone because browse bundles without lib/, an accepted risk rather than a bound.
- `test/spawn-sync.test.ts` finds git with `Bun.which('git')`; under a PATH-resolving git wrapper the stub recurses. CI and plain machines use real git.
- The new throw in `listRepoFiles` has no test of its own.
- The red-on-main claim was rerun independently by a second-model reviewer on Bun 1.4.4: the main hook exited 0 where the test expects 1, and this branch's hook blocked.

</details>

title: v1.101.0.0 release
body:
v1.101.0.0 ships 46 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- A test, or a scratch repository in the temp directory, can no longer write approval rows into your real Capy Drive (GST-3027). (#4466)
- An unattended /autoplan run on Claude Code no longer says the publication guard is off while it is on. (#4481)
- A phase report written only in reasoning now gets a denial that says so and names the fix. (#4481)
- `gstack-autoplan revise` no longer refuses a plan that the first `next` accepted. (#4470)
- `revise --plan` with a different file now says the run follows that file. (#4470)
- A second-model plan review in `/autoplan` is no longer reported as unavailable when it actually ran (GST-3051). (#4471)
- The /ship conductor trial plan now lets case reverts that conflict with later code be resolved by hand in docs, tests and the planted file, so large pull requests can be cases (GST-3003). (#4460)
- A locked plan for a trial of /ship without its separate conductor subagent (GST-3003). (#4456)
- A driven /ship now runs each phase as one command, counts its calls, and stops itself at 100 minutes. (#4451)
- /ship stops asking owners to clear two kinds of bookkeeping noise: base-side merge text and a reviewer's confirmation prose. (#4458)
- A base merge that only touched base-side text no longer stops `/ship` finish for an owner's grant. (#4458)
- A reviewer's confirmation prose no longer becomes a Critical finding that only an owner can clear. (#4458)
- A CI run that passed only after its failed jobs were re-run is now marked wherever gstack reuses it. (#4473)
- /ship reuses CI's passing test run when merging the base changed no file, and stops instead of quietly starting hour-long test runs or reviewing an empty diff (GST-3019). (#4461)
- /ship on Codex no longer stops at the test coverage audit. (#4489)
- A cold first-use check before an app build reaches its owner (GST-3025). (#4465)
- `skill_prefix=true` now survives updates when gbrain is installed. (#4454)
- The OpenClaw docs no longer send you to ClawHub, which held only April 2026 builds of office-hours, ceo-review and retro and no longer has gstack skills (the docs also said four skills while listing three). (#4454)
- `gstack-issue-links` no longer reads other repositories' issues as gstack's. (#4454)
- /ship's pre-gate finds the tests of a monorepo app that imports through its own `@/` alias. (#4464)
- /office-hours explains why it recommends a mode. (#4450)
- /office-hours keeps its 34 founder videos and essays out of the skill file. (#4463)
- Two `gstack-owner-answers add` runs for the same answer no longer collide. (#4490)
- A Captain can check an ask against the owner's earlier answers before sending it. (#4467)
- `gstack-post` stops reading /ship's own receipt identifiers as phone numbers, so posting a /ship PR body no longer needs a confirm. (#4488)
- GitHub release notes now list every change in plain words, with a link to its pull request. (#4390)
- gstack's router no longer gives bug reports a special rule, so the model fixes a bug the way it would without gstack. (#4442)
- /ship's review plan now sorts Swift and Xcode files by risk instead of sending every iOS PR to the full review panel (GST-3041). (#4469)
- /ship's review plan now sends Swift code that touches private user data to the full review panel (GST-3052). (#4472)
- A round grant at /ship's review round cap now buys the fix round it names, in the same run or the next (GST-2968). (#4479)
- The secrets check stops flagging three kinds of ordinary code as a secret, and catches two misses. (#4457)
- A security finding's location and reason no longer go into a PR body. (#4486)
- The token-capped /ship child on Claude Code now starts its prompt with the typed `/ship` command, so the skill actually loads. (#4487)
- A /ship receipt now counts the second-model review's blocking findings, and refuses to be written while one is still open. (#4485)
- A `/ship` with a token cap on Claude Code no longer stops at its first handoff. (#4452)
- /ship's push step now always ends with one line that says whether it pushed (GST-3053). (#4474)
- A PR's review-round count can no longer be overwritten by the body `/ship` posts. (#4440)
- One queued record with a malformed path no longer stops artifacts sync for every project. (#4455)
- A failed artifacts push stays reported until a push succeeds. (#4455)
- The /sync-gbrain memory row no longer says OK when pages failed to import. (#4455)
- CI now uploads free-suite test results to Trunk with analytics-uploader v2.1.8 and analytics-cli 0.17.0, up from v2.1.6 and 0.16.2. (#4453)
- Packing a checkout for a Ubicloud run no longer fails when git beside it is rewriting a ref. (#4447)
- The /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE eval no longer fails a review because its follow-up question didn't repeat the mode name. (#4447)
- Unattended /autoplan now records the owner's relayed gate reply instead of refusing it. (#4484)
- Unattended /autoplan now runs the second-model review you turned on, and waits for it instead of ending the session. (#4459)
- Two /autoplan runs started in the same second no longer share a run id. (#4459)

</details>

title: gstack-artifact validate now refuses a run.json that gstack-autoplan never wrote (GST-3090)
body:
`gstack-artifact validate` and `ack` now refuse a run.json that gstack-autoplan never wrote, so a hand-built run can no longer pass as a finished review. Why: a session skipped `gstack-autoplan next`, built run.json with a script copied from the reference fixture, and got ARTIFACT_VALID. Nothing to do unless you validate old or hand-made run directories: rerun those through gstack-autoplan.
What changed ![Before, a hand-built run.json from the reference fixture validated. After, the same file is refused (error lines shortened).](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/dYWOjd2clOD1vGL51Ar3gW_fGHUFAga4jL6oemVzyPc.png) A session that skipped the review built its own run.json from the reference fixture, and the completion check said it was fine. Once run.json parses against its schema, `validate` and `ack` now also check what gstack-autoplan writes on every run: - **`ARTIFACT_NOT_AUTOPLAN_RUN`**: `host` is not `gstack-autoplan`, one of the fields gstack-autoplan always writes is missing (`plan_input`, `plan_source`, `active_plan`, `restore`, `out`, `created_at`, `revision`, `attempt_counter`, `outside_enabled`, `phase_order`, `history`, `scope`), or there is no `attempts.jsonl` journal. - **`ARTIFACT_JOURNAL_MISMATCH`**: the journal has no `init` row for the run, a reviewer attempt was never journaled as dispatched, a completed review's output or hash differs from its `submitted` row, a bound review output changed after submit, or the run's checkpoint is ahead of run.json, disagrees on status or gate revision at the same revision, or holds a journal the live one no longer begins with. Both codes have troubleshooting entries (`docs/troubleshooting.md#artifact-not-autoplan-run`, `#artifact-journal-mismatch`) and are described in `docs/unattended.md`. Public copies (`validate --public`) are unchanged, and the library function `validateRun` stays the structural check; the new check is `validateAutoplanRun` in `lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts`. The reference fixture (`test/fixtures/multi-agent-wave/reference-run`) was hand-written before gstack-autoplan existed. It stays the structural fixture for `validateRun`, the CLI now refuses it, and its `generator` line, `docs/unattended.md` and `INCIDENTS.md` say so.
Why The validator is the completion check every unattended consumer trusts. If a script can produce a file that passes it, a skipped review looks like a finished one.
Blast radius Only `gstack-artifact validate ` and `gstack-artifact ack` call the new check; gstack-autoplan is the only writer of run.json (`lib/autoplan-run.ts:132` sets `host: 'gstack-autoplan'`), so real runs pass, which the CLI-written control test and the full free test suite in CI show. A run directory written by a gstack older than these fields is refused and has to be rerun; there is no migration for it.
Test Coverage 8 of the 14 paths in `lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts` have tests that would catch a regression. Untested branches: a wrong host on an otherwise real run, a field of the wrong type, a completed review missing its submit records, a status or gate-revision change at the same checkpoint revision, choosing the checkpoint after `resume --from`, and the guard that ignores outputs outside the run directory. None is a regression; they are proposed as follow-up tests. Tests ran: targeted 32 Tests ran: full 1699 files (CI)
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. The specialist review found nothing. The adversarial review raised four notes below the blocking floor, listed under Review notes.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/result-codes-autoplan.ts:17` check proves self-consistency, not authorship; docs/changelog wording promises provenance - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts:85` a cp -r copy of a run can be falsely refused as checkpoint-ahead when a checkpoint dir is set - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts:79` checkpoint comparison skips silently when no reference generation is found - INFORMATIONAL `lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts:20` runs begun on an older gstack lacking WRITER_FIELDS fail validate/ack after upgrade; migrate does not backfill
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual correction was made, and there are no blockers. **Scope:** 12 committed files from base 782f4595 to head 49d51781 on artifact-validate-refuses-hand-built-runs, with no staged, unstaged or new files. These docs were audited against lib/autoplan-writer-check.ts, lib/result-codes-autoplan.ts and bin/gstack-artifact: docs/unattended.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, the changelog.d fragment, test/fixtures/multi-agent-wave/INCIDENTS.md, autoplan/sections/unattended.md.tmpl and autoplan/DRIVER.md.tmpl. **Documentation health** - docs/troubleshooting.md: updated. The ARTIFACT_JOURNAL_MISMATCH entry now says the checkpoint must also agree on gate revision. - docs/unattended.md: current. The validate contract, the ack behavior, the public-copy exemption and the reference-run description match the code. - changelog.d/artifact-validate-refuses-hand-built-runs.md: current, not edited. - test/fixtures/multi-agent-wave/INCIDENTS.md: current. - autoplan/sections/unattended.md.tmpl and autoplan/DRIVER.md.tmpl: current. **Coverage debt:** none found. Both new result codes have troubleshooting anchors that match their result-code table entries. **Diagram drift:** none, because no diagrams are affected.

title: Keep a policy-floor test passing after gstack's version bump to 1.101
body:
A policy-floor test assumed gstack's own version stays below the next minor after the newest policy key. The v1.101 release (#4493) reaches that number, so its CI fails; the test now checks a floor above both. Why: this unblocks today's stable release, which carries a security fix (#4486) and four blocker fixes. Nothing to do as a reader.
What changed ![With VERSION at the release's number, the policy-floor test fails on main and passes on this branch](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/DEaaGr9jUb3gzFkVVT286a7agTGCl_POwavQph8IMsg.png) With VERSION at the release's number, the policy-floor test fails on main and passes on this branch.
Before/after as text: With VERSION at the release's number, the policy-floor test fails on main and passes on this branch ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ VERSION at the release bun test test/policy-floor-stable.test.ts # this branch (b036e5a) + 8 pass + 0 fail + 54 expect() calls +Ran 8 tests across 1 file. [7.42s] -$ VERSION at the release bun test test/policy-floor-stable.test.ts # main (fda9dea) - 7 pass - 1 fail - 53 expect() calls -Ran 8 tests across 1 file. [11.21s] ~~~
The release PR's free test suite failed in `test/policy-floor-stable.test.ts`. The test builds a floor that no running copy of gstack meets and expects it to be refused, and it built that floor as one minor above the newest policy key. Once VERSION itself reached that minor, the floor was met and the check passed instead of refusing. The test now builds the floor one minor above whichever is newer, VERSION or the newest policy key, so it stays out of reach on every release.
Why The v1.101 release PR (#4493) failed its free test suite on this one test, twice. The failure came from the test's own expectation, not from the product, so the release can go out once the test is fixed.
Blast radius Only the test file and a changelog fragment change; no product code moves. The floor check the test exercises, `validatePolicy` in `lib/ship-policy.ts`, is unchanged, and the repro shows the old test fails 1 of 8 with VERSION at the release number while the new one passes 8 of 8 (script ran).

title: Changed-number check stops flagging tests that only share a word like limit (#4478)
body:
/ship's changed-number check no longer stops on tests that only use the same word as a changed property: lowering `limit: 120` to `30` used to report every test that said "limit" and held 120. Why: `docs/pregate.md` already said a test counts for a word like `limit` only when it also names the changed module, but the code enforced that only for one-character values. Tests that import the module are still reported. Nothing to do. Thanks to @dtoelke, who reported this and sent the first fix in #4478.
What changed - **`lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts`, one condition in `consumersOf`.** A test file is read for the old value when it passes the existing name-or-module rule *and*, for a lowercase call-site name (`limit`, `attempts`, `timeout`), also names the changed module. Before, the second part applied only when the old value was one character long. Uppercase constants (`SEND_LIMIT`, `ARM_SHARDS`) are matched exactly as before. - **`docs/pregate.md`.** The call-site sentence now says the module rule holds whatever the old value's length. - **Test** in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts`: two files that only use the word, plus one that imports a sibling `rate-limits-v2`, are no longer reported; two files that import `src/rate-limits` still are.
Why "Lowering a rate limit from 120 to 30 flagged 30 unrelated test files" (#4478). The check now asks the same question for every call-site value that the docs already described, so a test is reported only when it can actually see the changed module.
Blast radius Only `consumersOf` changes, and only for a lowercase call-site name whose old value is two or more characters; constants and one-character values follow the same path as before (file:line read: `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:138`, both predicates walked branch by branch in review). A test reached only through a wrapper that never names the module's stem is no longer reported; the check is advisory, so such a test is caught only when a CI run includes it (a nightly-only test would surface after merge).
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. The full review panel (a batched specialist covering testing, security and state machines, a red team, a native adversarial reader and a second-model review on openai/gpt-6.1-sol) read the whole diff; the second-model verdict was CLEAN. Two low notes are listed below and were not fixed in this PR.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:138` A call-site literal reached only through a wrapper, subprocess or barrel that never names the module stem is no longer reported; intended and documented trade-off, advisory check, CI is the backstop - INFORMATIONAL `test/pregate-selection.test.ts:329` The SEND_LIMIT toEqual([]) assertion proves nothing because no fixture holds SEND_LIMIT; it does not show an uppercase name still counts alone
Exploratory QA Functional smoke on `consumersOf` with synthetic fixtures in an owned temporary directory (2 probes, 300 s budget), verdict pass: - Success: a call-site literal `limit` (old 120) is reported only in the test that imports the changed module. - Edge: an uppercase constant still counts by name alone, and a one-character call-site value still needs the module. Limit: smoke only; the full suite ran in CI.

title: /sync-gbrain's read check works when the first page is over 64 KB (#4396)
body:
/sync-gbrain's read check no longer reports `unknown` when the first page in your code source is over 64 KB.
Why: the check read the whole page to confirm its source and slug, and big pages (lockfiles) hit the 64 KiB output limit on every run.
Nothing to do: it now reads a 4 KB window of the page and still treats any cut-off output as `unknown`.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `bin/gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts` reads the page with `gbrain get <slug> --source <pin> --json --body window --max-bytes 4096`. The source and slug checks are unchanged.
- If that call fails (a gbrain older than 0.60.231.0 rejects the flags), the check falls back to the old whole-page read under the same 64 KiB limit, so small pages on older gbrain still read `ready`.
- A spawn error, including the `ENOBUFS` Node raises when output passes the limit, still fails closed through the existing `!result.error` and length checks. #4492's shared spawn helper (`lib/spawn-sync.ts`) merged after this branch was cut; it changes only this file's import line, so after merge the probe uses that helper as well. A trial merge with main at 0ab5657 is clean, and typecheck plus the 52 focused tests pass on it.
- Measured on a scratch gbrain 0.60.740.0 brain with a 317 KB page: the whole-page read returned 322,098 bytes and the check on main said `unknown`; the window read returned 5,254 bytes with `slug` and `source_id`, and the check said `ready`.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Every /sync-gbrain run in a repo whose first listed page is large reported its read capability as `unknown`, so the readiness verdict never reached ready even though reads worked.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the read check's page fetch changes. On an older gbrain a small first page costs one extra rejected call before the fallback. A page that is still too big, or any failed call, reports `unknown`, never `ready`.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Pre-Landing Review: 4 issues — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 3 noted

- Fixed: the paid readiness test `test/skill-e2e-sync-gbrain-readiness.test.ts` still expected only the old whole-page call; it now expects the windowed call, plus the fallback in its `unknown` case.
- Second-model review: clean, no findings.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- `bin/gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts:79`: the fallback assumes an older gbrain exits non-zero on the new flags. If one exits 0 with an error body, a small page reads `unknown` instead of `ready` (fails safe).
- `bin/gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts:80`: a timed-out windowed call starts the fallback, so the worst case waits about 20 s before `unknown`.
- `bin/gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts:84`: the windowed JSON shape (top-level `source_id` and `slug`) is checked against the repo's mock and the scratch brain above, not a test against a real gbrain.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional, fake gbrain on PATH, 3 probes, all pass: an 80 KB page reads `ready` through the window; an older gbrain that rejects the flags falls back and reads `ready`; an older gbrain with an 80 KB page reads `unknown`.

</details>

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Fixes #4396

</details>

No TODO items completed in this PR.

**Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed.

The change makes the /sync-gbrain read probe ask gbrain for a 4 KB window of the page (`--body window --max-bytes 4096`) and fall back to the whole-page read on older gbrain.

Documentation health:

- `docs/evals/detector-inventory.md` is current. Its line reference `:88` points to the `ready` status return.

title: v1.101.0.0 release
body:
v1.101.0.0 ships 48 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- A test, or a scratch repository in the temp directory, can no longer write approval rows into your real Capy Drive (GST-3027). (#4466)
- An unattended /autoplan run on Claude Code no longer says the publication guard is off while it is on. (#4481)
- A phase report written only in reasoning now gets a denial that says so and names the fix. (#4481)
- `gstack-autoplan revise` no longer refuses a plan that the first `next` accepted. (#4470)
- `revise --plan` with a different file now says the run follows that file. (#4470)
- A second-model plan review in `/autoplan` is no longer reported as unavailable when it actually ran (GST-3051). (#4471)
- The /ship conductor trial plan now lets case reverts that conflict with later code be resolved by hand in docs, tests and the planted file, so large pull requests can be cases (GST-3003). (#4460)
- A locked plan for a trial of /ship without its separate conductor subagent (GST-3003). (#4456)
- A driven /ship now runs each phase as one command, counts its calls, and stops itself at 100 minutes. (#4451)
- /ship stops asking owners to clear two kinds of bookkeeping noise: base-side merge text and a reviewer's confirmation prose. (#4458)
- A base merge that only touched base-side text no longer stops `/ship` finish for an owner's grant. (#4458)
- A reviewer's confirmation prose no longer becomes a Critical finding that only an owner can clear. (#4458)
- A CI run that passed only after its failed jobs were re-run is now marked wherever gstack reuses it. (#4473)
- /ship reuses CI's passing test run when merging the base changed no file, and stops instead of quietly starting hour-long test runs or reviewing an empty diff (GST-3019). (#4461)
- /ship on Codex no longer stops at the test coverage audit. (#4489)
- A cold first-use check before an app build reaches its owner (GST-3025). (#4465)
- `skill_prefix=true` now survives updates when gbrain is installed. (#4454)
- The OpenClaw docs no longer send you to ClawHub, which held only April 2026 builds of office-hours, ceo-review and retro and no longer has gstack skills (the docs also said four skills while listing three). (#4454)
- `gstack-issue-links` no longer reads other repositories' issues as gstack's. (#4454)
- /ship's pre-gate finds the tests of a monorepo app that imports through its own `@/` alias. (#4464)
- /office-hours explains why it recommends a mode. (#4450)
- /office-hours keeps its 34 founder videos and essays out of the skill file. (#4463)
- Two `gstack-owner-answers add` runs for the same answer no longer collide. (#4490)
- A Captain can check an ask against the owner's earlier answers before sending it. (#4467)
- `gstack-post` stops reading /ship's own receipt identifiers as phone numbers, so posting a /ship PR body no longer needs a confirm. (#4488)
- GitHub release notes now list every change in plain words, with a link to its pull request. (#4390)
- gstack's router no longer gives bug reports a special rule, so the model fixes a bug the way it would without gstack. (#4442)
- /ship's review plan now sorts Swift and Xcode files by risk instead of sending every iOS PR to the full review panel (GST-3041). (#4469)
- /ship's review plan now sends Swift code that touches private user data to the full review panel (GST-3052). (#4472)
- A round grant at /ship's review round cap now buys the fix round it names, in the same run or the next (GST-2968). (#4479)
- The secrets check stops flagging three kinds of ordinary code as a secret, and catches two misses. (#4457)
- A security finding's location and reason no longer go into a PR body. (#4486)
- The token-capped /ship child on Claude Code now starts its prompt with the typed `/ship` command, so the skill actually loads. (#4487)
- A /ship receipt now counts the second-model review's blocking findings, and refuses to be written while one is still open. (#4485)
- A `/ship` with a token cap on Claude Code no longer stops at its first handoff. (#4452)
- /ship's push step now always ends with one line that says whether it pushed (GST-3053). (#4474)
- A PR's review-round count can no longer be overwritten by the body `/ship` posts. (#4440)
- One queued record with a malformed path no longer stops artifacts sync for every project. (#4455)
- A failed artifacts push stays reported until a push succeeds. (#4455)
- The /sync-gbrain memory row no longer says OK when pages failed to import. (#4455)
- ### Tests (#4495)
- A policy-floor test no longer fails once gstack's own version reaches the minor after the newest policy key; it now checks a floor above both, so the v1.101.0.0 release can pass CI. (#4495)
- CI now uploads free-suite test results to Trunk with analytics-uploader v2.1.8 and analytics-cli 0.17.0, up from v2.1.6 and 0.16.2. (#4453)
- Packing a checkout for a Ubicloud run no longer fails when git beside it is rewriting a ref. (#4447)
- The /plan-ceo-review HOLD SCOPE eval no longer fails a review because its follow-up question didn't repeat the mode name. (#4447)
- Unattended /autoplan now records the owner's relayed gate reply instead of refusing it. (#4484)
- Unattended /autoplan now runs the second-model review you turned on, and waits for it instead of ending the session. (#4459)
- Two /autoplan runs started in the same second no longer share a run id. (#4459)

title: Fix GBrain reads and validation on Windows
body:

title: The router and the Claude overlay stop contradicting themselves and drop planning nudges
body:
The gstack router and the Claude overlay stop giving a model two opposite instructions, and stop telling it to plan the way it already does.

Why: a model that follows always-loaded prompt text to the letter, such as Claude Opus 5.5, has to pick one side when that text contradicts itself, and pays for nudges it does not need on every skill run.

Nothing to do: skills run the same way; only the prompt text changes.

## Why

Three spots in the always-loaded text pull a literal reader in two directions or push habits it already has:

- **Router contradiction.** With `PROACTIVE=all`, `SKILL.md` said "Do NOT answer directly when a skill exists for the task", while its own "When to invoke, and when not to" section says to answer a quick factual question directly.
- **Pressure text in the Claude overlay.** "Todo-list discipline" restates the todo tool's own contract, and "Think before heavy actions" asks the model to narrate a plan it already makes. Both land in every tier-2+ skill's preamble.
- **Duplicated or dead text.** Near-synonym voice triggers, a routing sentence that is only read after the skill is already running, and a branch-preference rule stated three times.

## What changed

- `SKILL.md.tmpl`: the `PROACTIVE=all` rule invokes the matching skill "subject to 'When to invoke, and when not to'" instead of forbidding direct answers. The /ship routing rule drops "deploy" and points at `/land-and-deploy`.
- `model-overlays/claude.md`: remove "Todo-list discipline" and "Think before heavy actions"; the dedicated-tools nudge stays. `test/model-overlays.test.ts` anchors the inheritance checks on that nudge.
- Voice triggers: collapse near-synonyms in `make-pdf`, `cso`, `devex-review` and `plan-devex-review`; phonetic aliases stay.
- `context-save`, `context-restore`: drop the "This is a gstack skill, not a Claude Code built-in" routing sentence. `context-restore` now states its current-branch-first ordering once.
- `codex`: the error table points at Step 0.4, and the web-search note drops the legacy-flag history.
- `open-gstack-browser`: Step 6 is one sentence instead of a feature tour.
- Regenerated with `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all` and `bun scripts/gen-ship-goldens.ts`; refreshed `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` with `bun test/helpers/capture-context-budget.ts`; recorded the ship size entry with `bun scripts/size-ledger.ts record ship`; added a `changelog.d` fragment. The shorter `plan-devex-review` output lowers its nine host pins in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` by 46 characters each. VERSION is not touched.

## Tests

Rebased onto main at d789dd965. Each file ran alone with `bun test <file> --timeout 60000`:

- Pass: `skill-md-size-guard`, `context-budget-ratchet`, `model-overlays`, `claude-overlay-models`, `proactive-core-set`, `safety-rule-registry`, `safety-none-arm`, `spec-template-invariants`, `catalog-budget`, `catalog-trim`, `catalog-mode-full`, `carve-guard-completeness`, `external-host-carve`, `gen-skill-docs-idempotency`, `gen-skill-docs-checks`, `host-config`, `parity-*`, `template-context-parity`, `size-ledger`, `skill-triggers`, `skill-validation`.
- `bun scripts/size-ledger.ts check ship`: ok. `gen:skill-docs --dry-run`: every file fresh. `bin/gstack-prose-lint changelog.d/*.md --gate`: ok.
- Not from this change: `test/first-use.test.ts` "where records live" expects `readdirSync` to list two folders in creation order. It fails on some machines and failed the same way on main's own push run for 45f879b53.

No eval was run. This is a prompt-text change, and only the structural tests above were run.

title: /ship, /spec and /review state their gates in plain prose, and /ship's description stops promising a deploy
body:
/ship, /spec and /review say their gates once, in plain sentences, and /ship's description no longer promises a deploy it never does.

Why: a model that reads instructions literally, such as Claude Opus 5.5, gives all-caps banners and repeated rules more weight than the steps they summarize, and takes "use when" phrases as promises.

Nothing to do: the skills do the same work; only the prompt text changes.

## Why

Some text in /ship, /spec, /review, /eval-plan and /design-shotgun says the same thing twice, asks the user to confirm the same thing twice, or promises something the skill never does.

## What changed

- `ship`: the description says "ship it", "push to main", "create a PR" or "open a pull request" and sends deploys to `/land-and-deploy`. /ship stops at a PR, so "deploy", "deploy this" and "get it deployed" promised work it never does. The triggers list is unchanged. The section self-check asks that each applicable section was Read before its step, without the "worked from memory, STOP" wording. Step 16's evidence rule stays word for word: it is a held safety rule whose wording changes only after its paid eval (`safety-ship-stale-evidence`) shows the new wording works.
- `spec`: one plain Phase 1 rule replaces the HARD GATE, the "STRICT" heading and rule 1's "NEVER produce an issue", which said the same thing three times. The rule is: start at Phase 1, and file nothing until the user confirms the Phase 4 draft. The self-check drops its STOP wording. `test/spec-template-invariants.test.ts` checks the rule's meaning instead of its capitals, and the carve guard in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` anchors on the new sentence.
- `review`: drop "Read the FULL diff", "Be terse" and "Only flag real problems", which the steps already cover.
- `eval-plan`: the unimplemented "Tier 3, after P7" roadmap moves from the skill body to `TODOS.md`.
- `design-shotgun`: Step 5 no longer asks the user to confirm feedback that the Step 4 loop already confirmed.
- Regenerated with `bun run gen:skill-docs --host all` and `bun scripts/gen-ship-goldens.ts`; refreshed `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` with `bun test/helpers/capture-context-budget.ts`; recorded the ship size entry with `bun scripts/size-ledger.ts record ship`; added a `changelog.d` fragment. title: gstack's script runner and merge-queue checks now refuse cut-off command output (GST-3104)
body:
The helper that runs gstack's own scripts and `bash -c` commands, and the merge queue's branch-ownership, stacked-test, release-version and merge-group record checks, now fail with `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` when Bun cuts a command's output off, instead of treating part of it as the whole answer. Why: #4492 added this for the scanners and gates but left these on Node's `spawnSync`, and its release note claimed wider coverage than it shipped. Nothing to do: a new test stops any new gstack command from calling Node's `spawnSync` directly.
What changed ![runBashSync on 200 KB of output under a 1 KiB limit that exits 0: main reports status 0 on cut-off output; this branch reports status null with SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/m2PcrlUQee7e4bEVY43sz9jzW-fIVpVLWxd7v5ZTGIg.png) On main, `runBashSync` returns status 0 when the child's output overflows the read limit and the child still exits 0, so a caller reads cut-off output as a finished answer. On this branch it returns status null with `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE`.
Testing - Failing first: two cases in `test/script-invocation.test.ts` run a bun-shebang script and a `bash -c` string that print 200 KB under a 1 KiB `maxBuffer`, ignore SIGTERM and exit 0. On main both return status 0; on this branch both return status null with ENOBUFS and `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` on stderr. The `bash -c` case skips on Windows. - The two tests #4492's review left out, in `test/spawn-sync.test.ts`: the pre-push stub now execs the git binary from `git --exec-path` instead of `Bun.which('git')`, with a case showing a PATH-resolving wrapper first on PATH is what `Bun.which` returns and is not what the stub uses; and `listRepoFiles` throws both when git cannot start and when a stub `git ls-files` prints past 64 MiB and exits 0. - Fixture copy lists that include `lib/script-invocation.ts` now also include `lib/spawn-sync.ts` (doctor fixture, PlanTune cathedral, timeline stop-hook slug). - Passed locally: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:test` (no new diagnostics), and the focused files above plus pr-dependencies (paid-runner closure), module-size ratchet, sync-spawn timeout tripwire, Bun entry isolation, docs-only and test-of-test ratchets. `bun run test:quick` failed only in browse tests that need a Playwright browser this machine does not have, and two `test/cso-witness.test.ts` cases that need the built CSO launcher; neither touches a changed file. CI is the full run.
Before/after as text ~~~diff --- Before (main at 36b349d) +++ After (this branch at e67b269) -{"status":0,"stdoutBytes":20480,"error":"ENOBUFS","stderrTail":""} +{"status":null,"stdoutBytes":16384,"error":"ENOBUFS","stderrTail":"bash: the output may be cut off (ENOBUFS, exit 0), so it was not used; see docs/troubleshooting.md#spawn-output-incomplete (SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE)"} ~~~ - **`lib/script-invocation.ts`** (`runScriptSync`, `runBashSync`, used by the pre-merge checks' test-selection manifest read, /ship's review-log read and many bins) now imports `spawnSync` from `lib/spawn-sync.ts`. - **Five merge-queue modules** in `crew/lib/` that read git or test output with a 64 MiB or 256 MiB limit do the same: `lane-ownership.ts`, `ship-queue-gate.ts`, `ship-queue-stack-tests.ts`, `version-gate-train.ts` and `ship-queue-train-record.ts` (the last already checked `r.error`; it moves so the list below shrinks). - **Import check** in `test/spawn-sync.test.ts`: no product file (code files and `bin/` scripts, tests excluded) may import `spawnSync` from `node:child_process` unless it is in `test/fixtures/spawn-sync-raw-importers.json`. That list has 68 files and may only shrink. - **Changelog:** a new fragment says what is covered now and that the earlier entry's claim was too broad.
Why The follow-up to #4492 (GST-3086) found that "every other gstack command that reads large git or gh output" was not covered: the script runner and five merge-queue modules still called Node's `spawnSync`, which reports status 0 on cut-off output when the child exits 0. These now fail closed like the pre-push hook and the pre-merge scans.
Blast radius Every caller of `runScriptSync` and `runBashSync` and the five merge-queue modules now gets status null instead of 0 only when output overflowed; normal output passes through unchanged (wrapper tests in `test/spawn-sync.test.ts`, a probe of `diffLane` on this branch's own diff returned all 14 files, and the full free suite passed in CI run 44362338523).
Test Coverage All new code paths have test coverage: 7 of 7 paths (two runner paths tested end to end with a real overflowing child, the five module imports held by the import check and the wrapper's own tests). Tests: 1819 → 1819 test files (+0 written in this step; the failing-first cases came with the change).
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. Five notes below the blocking floor, left for a follow-up: - The import check misses the combined form `import cp, { spawnSync } from 'child_process'`; no file in the repo uses it. - `lane-ownership.ts` drops git's stderr, so a cut-off read reports "git diff failed" without the reason; it still marks the branch unresolved. - `wtreeFingerprint` labels a cut-off read as "could not start"; it still refuses. - The cut-off notice is printed twice by `lib/ship-bin-common.ts`; the verdict is unaffected. - A caller that branches on a specific exit code sees null in the overflow case; no caller can reach it today. A second-model review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol) found nothing.
Exploratory QA Pass, 3 probes on this branch: `runBashSync` returns status 0 with full output on a small command; it returns status null, ENOBUFS and `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` when 200 KB overflows a 1 KiB limit and the child exits 0; `diffLane` reads this branch's diff normally (14 files).
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: send the script runner and the merge-queue modules through the cut-off-output wrapper and stop new raw imports. Delivered: exactly that, plus the fixture copy lists and the changelog fragment.
Documentation **Status:** current. The documentation already matches this branch, so no edits were made. **Scope:** base 36b349d6 to head e67b2692, branch script-runner-and-merge-queue-refuse-cut-off-output, with no staged, unstaged or new files. The change sends the script runner (lib/script-invocation.ts) and five merge-queue modules in crew/lib through lib/spawn-sync.ts, so cut-off output fails with `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE`. It also adds a guard test and a list of 68 files that still import spawnSync raw. **Documentation health:** - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. The `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` entry is generic and covers the new callers. - changelog.d/script-runner-and-merge-queue-refuse-cut-off-output.md: current. It matches the code, and its count of 68 matches the fixture. - README.md, AGENTS.md and docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: not affected. These modules are internal and no doc describes them. **Debt:** none in coverage and no diagram drift. The browser's process-list read is still not protected; the changelog fragment says so.
Tests - [x] Failing first: two cases in `test/script-invocation.test.ts` (a bun-shebang script and a `bash -c` string that print 200 KB under a 1 KiB limit, ignore SIGTERM and exit 0) return status 0 on main and status null with `SPAWN_OUTPUT_INCOMPLETE` here; the `bash -c` case skips on Windows. - [x] Focused local run at e67b269: `test/spawn-sync.test.ts`, `test/script-invocation.test.ts`, `test/free-fixtures.test.ts`, `test/plan-tune-cathedral.test.ts`, `test/timeline-stop-hook-slug.test.ts`, `test/gstack-doctor.test.ts`, `test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts`, `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts`, `crew/test/ship-queue-train-logic.test.ts`, `crew/test/train-backstop.test.ts`: 127 pass, 0 fail. - [x] Typecheck, module-size and conflict-marker checks before push: pass. - [x] Full free suite in CI on this exact tree: [run 44362338523](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/44362338523), green; macOS jobs green in the same run; Windows smoke green in [run 44357891103](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/44357891103).
Agent notes Follow-up to #4492 (GST-3086), GST-3104. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch script-runner-and-merge-queue-refuse-cut-off-output. title: Helper hooks are on by default, the destructive-command check runs as a hook, and prompt routing fires on long bug reports (GST-3110)
body:
Claude Code now gets gstack's prompt-routing, skill-contract and destructive-command hooks on by default, and new OpenClaw and Hermes registrations get the start hook. On 60 real bug reports, routing now matches a bug-fix skill on 40 (was 22), but gstack's own skills route 14 (was 17). Why: on Opus 5.5, unattended, a hook line naming a skill got it loaded in 58 of 60 sessions, and a skill relying on its description in 0 of 60 (gstack-evals#369). To opt out: `gstack-config set skill_routing off` (or `skill_contracts`, `destructive_guard`, `harness_start_hook`); an off you chose before is kept.
What changed: the defaults, before and after | Hook | Before | After | Turn it off | |---|---|---|---| | Prompt routing (UserPromptSubmit, one line naming the skill a prompt fits) | off | **on** | `gstack-config set skill_routing off` or `./setup --no-skill-routing` | | Skill contracts (Stop, holds /review once if its specialist reviewers never ran) | off | **on** | `gstack-config set skill_contracts off` or `./setup --no-skill-contracts` | | Destructive-command check (PreToolUse on Bash and PowerShell) | only while /careful or /guard was loaded | **on in every session**; in `claude -p` and other headless sessions it warns instead of asking | `gstack-config set destructive_guard off` or `./setup --no-destructive-guard` | | OpenClaw and Hermes start hook (a note on each turn to run a skill's start command) | off | **on for new registrations**; an existing off stays off on upgrade | `gstack-harness register openclaw --no-start-hook`, or `gstack-config set harness_start_hook off` | - **Upgrade path.** The first `./setup` or `/gstack-upgrade` after this lands registers each hook the person never turned off, prints one line per hook with its off switch, and once prints a notice listing what it turned on (marker `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/.hooks-on-by-default-notice`). An off set earlier by flag, `gstack-config` or the environment is read before the default and kept. For the start hook, every off a registration already has is kept, including a registration recorded before the start hook existed, so an upgrade never turns on a plugin that grants OpenClaw conversation access; the first refresh prints once `off, as before: gstack now turns it on only for new registrations; turn it on: gstack-harness register --start-hook`. The one off the default overrides is one gstack recorded because it had to refuse the hook (custom `--skills-dir`, foreign `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), so the hook comes on once that cause is gone. When the default turns the start hook on and the harness can't activate it yet, registration still succeeds (no exit 4); later refreshes retry. - **Destructive-command check as a hook.** `hosts/claude/hooks/destructive-guard-hook` runs `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` unchanged: ask for the destructive families, deny for a recursive delete of `/` or home and a force-push to the default branch. An ask's reason (the person reads it) adds the hook's name and off switch; a deny's reason (the model reads it) doesn't. The two deny messages no longer tell the model to "end the /careful session", which can't lift an every-session check. In a session nobody is watching (`claude -p`, which Claude Code marks `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli`, or a headless `gstack-session-kind`), an ask would wait forever, so the hook prints the reason as a warning and allows the command, the same as when the check is off; interactive sessions keep the ask and a deny stays a deny. About 0.13 s per Bash call. - **Windows.** The new hook registers the same way as the others (`bash` prefix on Windows, matcher `Bash|PowerShell`); no Windows-only path changed.
Prompt-routing matcher: what changed and the replay numbers The matcher now (1) scores a prompt longer than 5,000 characters on its first 4,000 and last 1,000 characters instead of skipping anything over 8,000; (2) reads defect words (error, exception, traceback, crash, fail/failure, broken, regression, incorrect, wrong, defect, and exception names like `ValueError`) as "bug"; (3) keeps paths and identifiers whole (`site-packages`, `src/review.ts`), so traceback paths stop matching trigger words; (4) prefers a whole-phrase match when two triggers of one skill tie. Replayed with no model calls on the 60 B1b bug prompts (`b1b routes` from garrytan/gstack-evals lanes/delivery-route at 6191ded's prompts; prompt hashes identical to the preregistered route-table.tsv): | | Before (main) | After | |---|---|---| | prove-it routable (score >= 0.66, with /prove-it installed and eligible), as GEVA-2 counts it | 22 of 60 (26 scored >= 0.66, 4 of those were over 8,000 characters) | **40 of 60** | | Of those, tasks from the benchmark's `_interface` split (mostly new-code asks; at least one reports a real bug) | 0 of 7 | 1 of 7 (aws__bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python-279_interface) | | Plain prompts that should route nowhere (new fixture `test/fixtures/skill-route-plain-prompts.txt`, 60 prompts: features, questions, docs, refactors, ops, data, and 6 that use error/exception/failed in feature requests) | 0 of 60 routed | **0 of 60 routed** | | Same 60 bug prompts with gstack's real routed skills only (/review, /qa, /verify) | 17 routed (12 /verify, 5 /qa) | 14 routed (11 /verify, 3 /qa) | Reading the remaining 20 misses by hand (not classified by the replay), most describe the defect only with "should", "instead" or "doesn't", or read like feature requests. Adding those words would route feature requests too. gstack's own routed list (/review, /qa, /verify) still has no bug-fix skill, so in a stock install a bug report routes to /verify, /qa or nowhere, and that stock routing fell from 17 to 14 of the 60 with this change; GEVA-2's measurement lists prove-it as B1b did.
Agent notes - Scope: GST-3110 A1 + B1, approved by Garry on 2026-11-18 ("do it"); /autoplan skipped per that approval. Out of scope and untouched: the CLAUDE.md routing block, "Load gstack. Run /X" docs, paid evals. - b1b routes caveat: its `routable_if_listed` column reads `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS`, which this change removes, so the "after" count is that column's other half (`best_score >= ROUTE_THRESHOLD`) from the same tool run. - Changes after the review cap, per Captain GStack Minder's ruling (decision A plus two scoped fixes): d3f19f2 makes the destructive-command hook warn instead of ask in headless sessions (tests "an interactive session (the claude CLI) gets the ask" and "claude -p and headless sessions get a warning and no decision, so nothing waits on an answer; a deny stays a deny" in test/destructive-guard-hook.test.ts); 21cc40d keeps an existing start-hook off on upgrade (test/harness-start-hook.test.ts "an off given by flag or env is kept by later runs; an off recorded before the default changed stays off and says once how to turn it on"). The read-only full review of 89ed42e (four readers, second-model review clean) found no blocker; the docs audit flagged four docs still describing the old opt-in defaults and a reader found that a record from before the start hook existed still turned it on. Per a second ruling, d5f4a63 fixes both (test "...or a record from before the start hook existed, stays off..." fails without the fix) under one scoped fix-check. That fix-check found that d5f4a63's other change, treating every Agent SDK entrypoint as headless, took the ask away from interactive Conductor sessions (also sdk-ts); b35ea46 reverts that part to the reviewed 89ed42e behaviour and adds the test "an interactive Agent SDK host (Conductor, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-ts) still gets the ask", under a second scoped fix-check (the Captain's third exception on this PR). finish then refused because gstack does not count a fix-check link that found an issue as review for the other files in its commit, so a third scoped fix-check, granted separately, read lib/harness-register.ts and test/harness-start-hook.test.ts over 89ed42e..b35ea46 and found nothing. - The first ruling's fix-check allowance was used as the read-only full review of 89ed42e; the three fix-check links above came from later, separate grants. - Open notes, left as is by that ruling: - On upgrade, only an off that came from a record without a saved choice prints the one-line "turn it on" hint. An off set through `GSTACK_HARNESS_START_HOOK` or `harness_start_hook` stays off silently, and the changelog's "prints one line" reads broader than that; the docs-only follow-up corrects the changelog wording, along with its "40 instead of 22" line and the exit-4 sentence in docs/hosts.md. - If bun is missing from the hook's PATH, the destructive-command hook fails open (allows) with no signal; it is an advisory guard documented as fail-open. - Upstream Claude Code: a hook "ask" may drop bypassPermissions mode for the rest of the session (anthropics/claude-code#37420, closed stale) and may act as "allow" in auto mode (#89561, open). Not checked against the current release; gstack's own upgrade and temp-dir cleanups can trip the ask. - Agent SDK runs (sdk-ts, sdk-py) still get the ask, because Conductor's interactive sessions use the same entrypoint. - The check (up to 8 s) plus the session lookup (up to 2 s) can exceed the 10 s hook timeout, and then the command runs unchecked. - lib/harness-register.ts:353's `startHook` comment still ends the order at "then the ledger". - The tokenizer keeps hyphenated words whole, so "code-review" no longer matches the two-word "code review" trigger, and "pre landing review" without the hyphen scores 0.5 against "pre-landing review". - Local checks at b35ea46: typecheck, the test typecheck ratchet, the destructive-guard-hook and changelog-fragments tests (22 pass; the Conductor test fails on d5f4a63's hook). At d5f4a63: gen:skill-docs freshness, the harness-start-hook, harness-register and hooks-windows-paths tests (101 pass with the guard tests), and seven docs-reading suites (556 pass). CI was green on every check at d5f4a63. Review-loop exception: accepted by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) 2026-11-18 via ruling of 2026-11-18 relayed by the lane (GSTA-627): one read-only full review of the final head 89ed42e, no fix round, per R51 and the ruling of 2026-11-18, then granted fix-checks of d5f4a63 (a-8354f1687fbd) and b35ea46 (a-4f7937d1e7ea) (fix-check at b35ea46a8649, 0 findings) - Fix-check chain: d5f4a63 (grant a-8354f1687fbd, one blocker found and reverted in b35ea46), b35ea46 (grant a-4f7937d1e7ea, no findings), and lib/harness-register.ts plus test/harness-start-hook.test.ts over 89ed42e..b35ea46 (grant a-be1c97dcc94b, no findings). Documentation: **Status:** blocked, shipped under a documentation exception. **Scope:** docs/, README.md and careful/SKILL.md.tmpl against base 2f57b07 at head b35ea46 (read-only audit docs-4503-b35ea46-2). Two lines in docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md are stale (line 18 and the Host support table); everything else this PR changed is current. Line 18 says an unreadable config turns 'both' hooks off, but it turns off three. The Host support table has no column for the destructive-command check. title: /ship's state-machine check accepts the header lines its reader is told to write (GST-3115)
body:
The state-machine check in /ship no longer stops a review because its reader opened the reply with the `REVIEWED_TREE` and `REVIEW_VERDICT` lines its instructions require.
Why: on yc-software/qm#3728 the check reported those two lines as gaps, so /ship stopped before its adversarial review step.
Nothing to do after merge.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![The state-machine check used to flag the reader's required header lines as gaps; it now reads them and reports ok](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/a22ste9Q_vnVEBbiJd0lSY5y6al9xTiBI3owqQuLFuc.png)

The state-machine check used to flag the reader's required header lines as gaps; it now reads them and reports ok.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The state-machine check used to flag the reader's required header lines as gaps; it now reads them and reports ok</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ gstack-state-matrix check reader-reply.txt   # this branch
+STATE_MATRIX_CHECK: ok machines=0
+exit 0
-$ gstack-state-matrix check reader-reply.txt   # gstack 1.101.0.0 (main)
-STATE_MATRIX_GAP: unparsed-line — REVIEWED_TREE: 225264fb303085455cdb4cffbfd1393470205b32 /workspace/gstack
-STATE_MATRIX_GAP: unparsed-line — REVIEW_VERDICT: blocking=0
-STATE_MATRIX_GAP: unparsed-line — NO FINDINGS
-STATE_MATRIX_CHECK: incomplete gaps=3 machines=0
-gstack-state-matrix check: the state-machines specialist output lacks a kind × owner action cell, maps a cell to a test that does not exist, or leaves an untested cell without a CRITICAL finding (3 gap(s)); fix: rerun the state-machines specialist on the same diff; its review coverage stays incomplete until gstack-state-matrix check passes (STATE_MATRIX_INCOMPLETE)
-exit 1
 
~~~

</details>

A reader that followed its brief got its review marked incomplete. Now the check skips a `REVIEWED_TREE` first line and a well-formed `REVIEW_VERDICT` line right under it, using `isReviewedTreeLine` (lib/review-brief.ts) and `parseVerdict` (lib/review-verdict.ts), the parsers the collector already uses, so there is no second list of header names. `NO FINDINGS` under the header counts as clean. Any other non-JSON line is still an `unparsed-line` gap: prose, the header repeated later, the two lines in the wrong order, or a malformed verdict such as `blocking=none`. The new test in test/state-matrix.test.ts builds the header from the brief itself and fails on main with the two gaps from the report.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"STATE_MATRIX_CHECK: incomplete gaps=2" on yc-software/qm#3728: the reader did what its brief says and /ship treated the review as missing. Reviews of proposal, hold and approval flows now reach the adversarial step instead of stopping.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`parseSpecialistOutput` is called by `checkStateMatrix` and by lib/review-scope.ts through the findings parse; both now see the same lines minus the header, and every other line keeps its old handling (lib/state-matrix.ts:70 read; 17 tests in test/state-matrix.test.ts ran, including the negative controls).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues found. One batched reader (testing, security, state machines, red team) found nothing; the adversarial reader found two low-severity notes, listed below; the second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol) was clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/state-matrix-check-accepts-reader-header.md:4` Changelog says the check and collector can't drift apart; they share parsers but not position rules (collector accepts a tree line anywhere, check only at the top)
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/state-matrix.ts:70` isReviewedTreeLine calls fs.realpathSync on the reader-written path; one filesystem read per reply

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

CLI smoke on `bin/gstack-state-matrix check`, 3 probes, all pass: this pass's real reader reply (header, then `NO FINDINGS`) checks ok with exit 0; a malformed verdict under the header stays an `unparsed-line` gap with exit 1; the same real reply on main 1.101.0.0 reports the header lines as gaps. Wrong-order and repeated-header cases are covered by the unit tests, not probed.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

No paid cases selected: the PR profile picked no probes or judges; review-army-state-matrix stays in scheduled release coverage.

</details>

<details><summary>Review bot comments</summary>

No review bot comments.

</details>

<details><summary>Scope Drift</summary>

Scope Check: CLEAN

</details>

<details><summary>TODOS</summary>

No TODO items completed in this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

Scope: the changes from base 2f57b07 to HEAD e06095b. They cover the state-matrix check skipping the reader's REVIEWED_TREE and REVIEW_VERDICT header lines (lib/state-matrix.ts), its tests, and a changelog.d fragment. The worktree had no uncommitted or new files. Docs that mention the state-matrix check were reviewed: docs/troubleshooting.md (STATE_MATRIX_INCOMPLETE), docs/review-policy.md (test-gap precedence) and docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md.

Result: current, with no edits. The fix makes the check behave the way those docs already describe, and the changelog fragment explains the change to users.

Debt: none.

</details>

title: The prompt-routing hook suggests skills you install, and stops sending bug reports to /qa (GST-3123)
body:
The prompt-routing hook can now suggest skills you installed yourself: any skill that lists `triggers:` in its SKILL.md, not only gstack's /review, /qa and /verify. It also stops sending ordinary bug reports to /qa.
Why: a bug-fix skill you install was never named (0 of 60 real bug reports); now it's named on 40 of 60, and /qa takes none of them instead of 3.
Nothing to do after merge.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![gstack-skill-route --explain on a bug report with a bug-fix skill installed: main names nothing, this branch names /prove-it](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/pACBXot_4-tUxC8cf4LnKNzMEdIaZVpZwWXN6-GrvIA.png)

gstack-skill-route --explain on a bug report with a bug-fix skill installed: main names nothing, this branch names /prove-it.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: gstack-skill-route --explain on a bug report with a bug-fix skill installed: main names nothing, this branch names /prove-it</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 switch: skill_routing on (default)
 threshold: 0.66
+skills: 4 scanned in ~/.claude/skills (evil: trigger text outside letters, digits, spaces and . , ' ? ! / -)
-skills: 4 scanned in ~/.claude/skills
 candidates:
+  1.00  /prove-it  "fix this bug" (2 words, installed: ~/.claude/skills/prove-it/SKILL.md)
+route: /prove-it
+hint: gstack skill routing (UserPromptSubmit hook; matched the installed /prove-it trigger "fix this bug"; off: gstack-config set skill_routing off): this request fits /prove-it. Run /prove-it with the Skill tool before you start, and tell the user in one sentence that gstack routed this to /prove-it.
-  (none)
-route: none (below-threshold)
 
~~~

</details>

You install a bug-fix skill with a "fix this bug" trigger, paste a traceback, and the hook never mentions it, because it only ever scored gstack's own /review, /qa and /verify. Now any installed skill that isn't gstack's own and lists triggers is scored the same way.

**Installed skills.** One hook line names at most two different skills ("this request fits /verify or /prove-it"), and at the same score gstack's skill comes first. gstack's other skills still never route. A skill is gstack's own when its folder holds `.gstack-owned`, its SKILL.md links into gstack's checkout, or its name is one gstack generates or one of setup's alias names (`_gstack-command`, `connect-chrome`). A skill built from a gstack-style template is not gstack's own and still routes.

**Limits on what a skill can put in the line.** A skill's triggers are used only when its name is letters, digits, `_ : -`, it has at most 12 triggers of at most 200 characters, and every trigger is letters, digits, spaces and `. , ' ? ! / -`. Otherwise the whole skill is skipped and reported. Trigger text therefore can't leave its quotes or add markup or shell characters, though the quoted words are still the skill author's own.

**/qa and bug reports.** A trigger only partly present needs one of its specific words (five letters or more, not the defect word). Short everyday words must sit within 8 words of each other. Before, "pip cannot find ... fails" matched "find bugs on site", and "call site" plus "regression tests" 1,500 characters later matched "test the site".

**Where to see it.** `gstack-skill-route --explain` lists each candidate's source (gstack, or the SKILL.md path) and both routed skills. The routing log adds `source=` and `also=`.

**Route counts on 60 real bug reports.** B1's 60 SWE-rebench tasks, with gstack's /review, /qa and /verify plus a bug-fix skill (/prove-it, triggers "fix this bug", "prove the fix", "reproduce the bug in a test") installed, scored with each commit's own `routePrompt`:

| first skill named | 3f1b82b (main) | 5554594 (qa fix) | 629a3cd | b46e91d | 2329ada (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /prove-it | 0 | 0 | 33 | 0 | 33 |
| /verify | 11 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 |
| /qa | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| nothing | 46 | 51 | 18 | 51 | 18 |
| /prove-it named at all | 0 | 0 | 40 | 0 | 40 |

The review fix in 1bf71b5 counted gstack's generated-file banner as ownership; a template-built /prove-it carries that banner, so at 1bf71b5 through b46e91d (which only changed docs and the release note) it was never named. 2329ada tells gstack's skills apart by name instead. The 60 plain prompts in `test/fixtures/skill-route-plain-prompts.txt` route nowhere at every commit, with /prove-it installed too.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"A bug-fix skill you install was never named": the hook dropped every skill but gstack's three before scoring, so a skill written for bug reports got 0 of 60. It's now named on 40 of 60, and /qa stops claiming bug reports on everyday words.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change is inside the prompt-routing hook (`lib/skill-route.ts`, `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook.ts`, `bin/gstack-skill-route`); `lib/skill-contract.ts` also calls `readFrontmatter` and `scanInstalledSkills`, and `readFrontmatter` is byte-identical to main (checked by the review of the fixes). The hook still always exits 0 and prints nothing on error, so the worst case is a missing or extra suggestion, never a blocked prompt (`test/skill-route.test.ts`, all 24 focused cases green).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Pre-Landing Review: 3 issues, all three resolved automatically; no approvals requested; 0 deferred, 6 noted.

- security finding, details recorded privately (fixed: wording).
- One line could name the same skill twice; `routePrompt` now names each skill once.
- security finding, details recorded privately (fixed in 1bf71b5, then replaced in 2329ada after it stopped a template-built third-party skill from routing; a second read of that range found nothing).

Second-model review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): no findings. Exploratory checks, the review readers and both re-reads of the fixes raised no blocker.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `changelog.d/qa-routing-skips-bug-reports.md:1` The 40-of-60 and 3-of-60 counts have no raw data in the checkout, and the /verify 9-of-60 result is left out. The release note no longer quotes them; the counts above were recounted from each commit's own lib.
- NOTE `lib/skill-route.ts:280` A third-party trigger that is one word claims every prompt containing that word, and a defect word (bug, error, fails, regression, an exception name) claims nearly every bug report: in a second-model check, a skill with the single trigger "error" was named on 40 of the 60 bug reports (first on 33) and 6 of the 60 plain prompts. "fix it" claimed none of either. A suggestion never blocks a prompt or outranks gstack at equal score. Skill authors should avoid bare generic words and defect synonyms, and prefer specific phrases of several words; the zero-route result covers only the triggers measured.
- NOTE `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook.ts:31` The opt-in pilot hint styles (`GSTACK_SKILL_ROUTE_HINT=step` or `contract`) quote the routed skill's own first step (at most 200 characters) or contract item text (no length cap) without the trigger character limit. The default style quotes only the checked name and trigger. `--explain` always shows the default style.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:146` Name-based ownership: a third-party skill named like a gstack template is logged source=gstack and wins ties.

Functional smoke on `gstack-skill-route --explain` against a scratch skills folder (5 probes): a bug report routes to an installed /prove-it and a skill with markup in a trigger is skipped and named (pass); an unmarked `_gstack-command` alias copy routed on any prompt naming gstack before the review fix and stopped after it (fail, then pass).
