title: /ship's review works when the shipped checkout isn't the project's default checkout (GST-3145)
body:
/ship's review pass now lets its readers start in a checkout of an unrelated repository, and refuses to start them in any other checkout that holds the review's diff base, such as a sibling worktree or a separate clone of the shipped repository.
Why: a project whose default checkout is another repository needed a fresh machine for every /ship review, while a worktree or clone of the same history could read the wrong diff with no error.
Nothing to do: the pass still stops before anything starts if the shipped checkout can't be reached.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

The review pass in `lib/capy-review-pass.js` runs one check from the directory readers start in. It runs `cd <checkout>` and reads that checkout's top level, and it asks whether the start directory's repository holds the pass's diff base commit (`git cat-file -e <base>^{commit}`). The pass stops with nothing started when the shipped checkout can't be reached, or when the start directory is another checkout holding that commit, which covers sibling worktrees and separate clones. A checkout of another history, a directory outside any checkout, and a directory with a broken `.git` dispatch. `test/review-pass.test.ts` adds a separate-clone case, which fails on the previous version, and pins the broken-`.git` dispatch. `docs/review-policy.md` and the changelog fragment describe the check.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Two teams hit `STOP: readers on the shared machine start in <dir>, not in <checkout>` when the checkout they shipped wasn't their machine's default one. The previous version of this PR stopped only for a sibling worktree, so a separate clone of the same repository still dispatched, and a reader command that skipped its `cd` would read that clone's diff silently.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the dispatch check of the review pass on a shared machine changes; reviewer briefs and collection are untouched. `bun test test/review-pass.test.ts` passes 80 tests at this head.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Scope:** the branch `fix-review-readers-in-another-checkout` against base 5afef04e. It changes the /ship review pass so it no longer stops when readers start in a different checkout. Changed files: `lib/capy-review-pass.js`, `docs/review-policy.md`, `changelog.d/review-readers-start-in-another-checkout.md` and `test/review-pass.test.ts`.

**Result:** the docs are current. The review-policy paragraph and the changelog fragment describe the new reach check accurately: readers may start in another checkout; the pass stops when the shipped checkout can't be reached, or when the start checkout holds the diff base, such as another worktree or a clone of the same history. A search of Markdown files and templates outside CHANGELOG.md found no remaining text that tells users to run /ship in the thread's own checkout.

**Debt:** none found.

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Coverage audit (audit only, no tests written): 8 of 9 changed code paths tested (89%, value-weighted 89%). The gap: every test uses one shared diff base, so the branch that also collects each active reader's own `diff_base` is never exercised. Proposed test: a row in the separate-clone test whose clone holds only a reader's own base.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No finding reached the blocking floor (a failing test, a production break, or lost data or secrets). This was the PR's read-only final review: it had two full review rounds on earlier heads, so this head got one full review with no fix round. Four review notes were raised and left unfixed. Second-model review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol): clean. The targeted reader and the red-team reader found nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `test/review-pass.test.ts:130` The new `unrelated()` helper sits between `repo()`'s doc comment and `repo()`, so that comment now attaches to `unrelated()`.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/capy-review-pass.js:193` A start directory whose git call fails with another error, such as dubious ownership, now dispatches without an early stop; a wrong-tree reply is still refused by the reviewed-tree check.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/capy-review-pass.js:193` In a partial clone that lacks the base commit, `git cat-file -e` can start a lazy network fetch, adding up to the 300 s timeout.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/capy-review-pass.js:194` The check's reply is split by line position; a shell that prints a preamble shifts the fields, and the pass stops with a confusing message rather than dispatching.

title: When Claude Code runs /verify before a commit, it now gets a quick check instead of the full fix loop (GST-3150)
body:
When Claude Code calls /verify on its own right before `git commit`, gstack now runs one quick check-only command that ends in a single `VERIFY PASS`, `VERIFY FAIL` or `VERIFY skipped: ` line; typing /verify still runs the full skill. Why: since Claude Code 2.1.286 any skill named `verify` is run before every commit, so gstack's fix loop, its first-run notices and a hard stop in repos with no remote landed on ordinary commits. Nothing to do; `gstack-config set verify_before_commit off` turns the check off.
What changed ![/verify now opens with a quick check-only section for the call Claude Code makes before each commit](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/ZfAUdhOQPABVjOMRlDSUA9hPlFsyTIg0g2MnZXzMwas.png) /verify now opens with a quick check-only section for the call Claude Code makes before each commit.
Measured on the real claude binary Claude Code 2.1.328, Opus 5.5, Anthropic key, prompt "add() in calc.py returns the wrong answer. Fix it and commit the fix.", toy repo with no remote and no pytest, fresh HOME per run, 3 runs per arm. Every run made the one-line fix and committed. | Arm | Turns | Seconds | Cost per commit | |---|---|---|---| | No gstack | 4, 4, 4 | 8.5, 9.6, 9.3 | $0.055, $0.057, $0.057 | | gstack main (5afef04) | 8, 8, 9 | 22.7, 22.9, 23.2 | $0.201, $0.142, $0.149 | | This branch | 8, 8, 8 | 17.2, 17.7, 16.7 | $0.130, $0.134, $0.132 | On this branch every run called /verify, ran `gstack-checks quick` once, got `VERIFY skipped: no origin/main to compare against … (POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE)` and committed, with no gstack notices in any answer (main showed them in 2 of 3 final answers). A typed `/verify` on this branch still ran the full skill (preamble, notices, detect). Against main the per-commit cost fell by about 20% and the time by about 25%; it is still about 2.4x the no-gstack run, mostly from loading verify's 12 KB SKILL.md and gstack's skill list on every turn. $0 stub-API capture: Claude Code's "Always run /verify right before the commit command" line is present with gstack on main and on this branch, and absent with no gstack (the skill keeps its name, as asked).
Before/after as text: /verify now opens with a quick check-only section for the call Claude Code makes before each commit ~~~diff --- Before · verify/SKILL.md.tmpl § Right before a commit: the quick pass at 5afef04 · source text (section not present before) +++ After · verify/SKILL.md.tmpl § Right before a commit: the quick pass on this branch · source text +## Right before a commit: the quick pass +Use only this section when you started /verify yourself because you are about +to run `git commit` (Claude Code asks for /verify before every commit), and the +user has not typed /verify or asked you to verify or run the checks in this +conversation. The arguments `quick` or `pre-commit` mean the same. When the +user typed /verify, skip this section and run the full skill below. + +Skip the preamble and everything after this section: edit nothing, add no +tests, ask nothing. Run one command with a Bash timeout of 10 minutes: + +```bash +"{{RUNTIME_ROOT}}/bin/gstack-checks" quick +``` + +It ends with one line. `VERIFY PASS: …` or `VERIFY skipped: `: go on +with the commit, and mention /verify only by quoting that line. `VERIFY FAIL: +…` (exit 1): don't commit over it; quote the line and the failing output to +the user and ask whether to fix it first or commit anyway. + +{{PREAMBLE}} ~~~ People committing with Claude Code saw gstack's whole build-and-fix loop start on every ordinary commit, notices and all, and in a repo with no remote it stopped hard. Now that pre-commit call runs one command, `gstack-checks quick`: the repo's existing checks and the tests /ship would pick, with no edits, no new tests and no questions. A repo with untrusted check commands, no `origin` base, or nothing declared gets `VERIFY skipped: ` and the commit goes ahead; a real failure prints the failing output and `VERIFY FAIL`, and the skill tells the model to ask before committing over it. Typed /verify is unchanged. The new `verify_before_commit` setting turns the pass off; `gstack-config` now rejects a mistyped value for it and shows it in `list` and `defaults`.

title: Claude Code skills run their start step as they load, so it can't be skipped (GST-3157)
body:
In Claude Code, every gstack skill now runs its start command and loads the shared preamble while the skill loads, so the model starts with their output instead of an instruction it can skip.
Why: in test runs, loaded skills' steps were followed in only 45% to 62% of sessions, and /autoplan's start command never ran in 5 of 10.
Nothing to do: other hosts keep today's instructions, and if Claude Code can't run the step, the skill says so and the model runs it as before.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People running a gstack skill in Claude Code saw the model skip its start step. The instruction to run it sat in the skill text, and in test runs it was followed in only 45% to 62% of sessions. Now Claude Code runs the step itself while the skill loads, so the model starts with the step's output already in front of it.

- Claude Code runs a skill's `!\`command\`` lines while it loads the skill and puts their output into the skill text. Each Claude Code skill now has two such lines: one prints the shared preamble file (`sections/preamble.md`), the other runs `gstack-skill-start`. The plain start command stays right below as the fallback.
- Both lines run a new helper, `bin/gstack-skill-load`. Claude Code aborts the whole skill load when an injected command exits non-zero, so the helper always exits 0. It stops the start after 15 seconds (`GSTACK_SKILL_LOAD_TIMEOUT`), killing everything the start launched, keeps any output the start printed before the limit, and turns any failure into one line that tells the model to run the start itself. It closes stdin and sends the start's output to a temp file, so nothing left running can hold Claude Code's pipe open. It runs nothing beyond what `gstack-skill-start` already does, network included.
- The preamble line prints the file only when its first line is the preamble header (`# gstack shared preamble <id>`), so it can't be pointed at another file. This works for every install layout, including installs served from a render directory.
- In plan mode, a bare `Bash` in `allowed-tools` doesn't let an injected command run. The classifier or a prompt decides, and anything short of "allow" aborts the load. So each Claude Code skill's `allowed-tools` also names the helper (`Bash(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-skill-load:*)`), which Claude Code allows in every mode.
- Each injected line is one plain command with no variables or fallbacks, which worktree-isolated sessions require (#2763).
- /plan-eng-review and /plan-design-review still run their start command after their scope question, so only their shared preamble loads early.
- The instruction-block rule now trusts blocks in the start output shown in the skill, or in the tool result when the model ran the start itself.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Loaded skills' steps were followed in only 45% to 62% of sessions, and /autoplan's start command never ran in 5 of 10." Running the start step at load means the model can't skip it, so every Claude Code skill begins with its session state, settings and preamble in context.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only Claude Code skill files change, and the other hosts' generated skills are byte-identical, and of the four ship goldens only the Claude one changed (script ran: `gen:skill-docs` for every host plus the golden tests). The new helper can't break a load by exiting non-zero, because every path through `bin/gstack-skill-load` ends in `exit 0` (walked failure path, covered by `test/gstack-skill-load.test.ts`).

</details>

<details><summary>Which hosts get which</summary>

- Claude Code: load-time lines, with the old instruction kept below each one as the fallback.
- Codex, Factory, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Kiro, OpenClaw, Hermes, gbrain, Slate and agy: unchanged instruction text.
- Claude Code with `disableSkillShellExecution` on, or any agent that reads a Claude skill file directly (Capy, for example): it sees the command or Claude Code's placeholder, and the text tells it to run the start command and read the preamble itself, as before.

</details>

<details><summary>Known limits, queued for a follow-up</summary>

- A missing helper, or a deny rule on Bash or on `bin/gstack-skill-load`, makes Claude Code abort the skill load instead of falling back to the plain instruction.
- Paid end-to-end tests that look for a `gstack-skill-start` Bash call may miss the start, because it now runs at load and makes no tool call.

</details>

<details><summary>Proof on the real claude binary ($0, local stub API)</summary>

The real `claude` binary ran `/autoplan` against a local stub that logs each request body, with this branch installed in a fresh HOME. In every run below, the first request already held the shared preamble (`# gstack shared preamble d8804c5ab6bf`) and the start's STATUS lines (`SESSION_ID:` and the rest), with no tool call.

| Claude Code | Mode | Preamble inlined | Start output inlined | Tool calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.292 (pinned) | default | yes | yes | 0 |
| 2.1.292 | plan | yes | yes | 0 |
| 2.1.292 | auto | yes | yes | 0 |
| 2.1.328 (latest) | default | yes | yes | 0 |
| 2.1.328 | plan | yes | yes | 0 |
| 2.1.292, start missing | default | yes | one `SKILL_START: failed at load (exit 127)` line; the skill still loaded | 0 |
| 2.1.292, `disableSkillShellExecution` | default | placeholder | placeholder; the fallback text applies | 0 |

Probes with a dummy skill showed why the helper and the grant are needed. On both versions, a non-zero exit, a missing command or a deny rule aborted the skill load with no API call. In plan mode, a bare `Bash` grant aborted the load, and a specific `Bash(<path>:*)` grant ran the command. A PreToolUse hook's "allow" did not help.

</details>

<details><summary>Size caps raised (Garry, 2026-11-19, "Do it" on I1 (GST-3157))</summary>

Each Claude Code skill file grows by about 380 to 400 bytes, plus one 58-byte frontmatter line. Each cap is set to the value measured on this tree:

- Always-on context budget, `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` alwaysOnTotal: 8,647 to 9,498 tokens. The counter includes every skill's whole frontmatter, so the grant line costs about 399 tokens there. Claude Code's skill list shows only names and descriptions.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`: 15 skeleton caps and 9 size-ratio caps (design-html gets its own ratio in place of the 1.05 default).
- `test/size-ledger/ship`: one +378-byte entry.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues. The final full review of this head found nothing that would fail a test, break production or lose data; its six notes are listed below and none is fixed here. Second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol): clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/load-injection.ts:27` 1. **A missing or uncallable helper now stops the skill from loading at all** (`scripts/resolvers/load-injection.ts:27`, `generate-preamble-bash.ts`). The module's own header says a non-zero `!` command aborts the whole skill load. The rendered line calls the helper at a fixed path, `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-skill-load`, or an install-root rewrite of it. When that file is absent, the shell exits 127 and the skill no longer loads. That happens when an install outside the default path falls back to the committed render, for example when its first per-install render fails (setup keeps t
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/resolvers/load-injection.ts:14` 2. **Sessions that deny Bash can no longer load any gstack skill** (`load-injection.ts:14-16`, the `addLoadGrant` grant). The docstring says a `!` line whose permission check fails aborts the load. In Claude Code a deny rule outranks a skill's `allowed-tools` grant. So a managed-settings deny on Bash, or `--disallowedTools Bash`, now turns every gstack skill into a load failure instead of a skill whose start step the model can't run. The changelog covers `disableSkillShellExecution` but not deny rules. I did not run Claude Code to confirm this; the precedence is inferred from Claude Code's doc
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-load:57` 3. **The 15-second limit can kill the start mid-way through its daily brain pull and sync** (`bin/gstack-skill-load:57-75`). `gstack-skill-start` runs a daily `git fetch` plus `merge --ff-only` in `$GSTACK_HOME` and `gstack-brain-sync --once`. Both are network-bound (the low-speed limit alone allows 5 s of stall), and both are now inside the TERM-then-KILL of the whole process group. The brain lock clears locks whose pid is dead, and the drain treats an old `.git/index.lock` as abandoned, so I found no lasting corruption. The cost is a killed fetch on slow networks, no record of the pull, a 15-second
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-load:77` 4. **When the start fails at load, its own error message is dropped** (`bin/gstack-skill-load:77-80`). On a non-zero exit the helper prints only `failed at load (exit N)` and throws away `$OUT`, which holds the actionable text (for example "cannot resolve the gstack state root… reinstall with ./setup"). The model recovers by running the start again, but that costs a step. FIXABLE: print `$OUT`, or its last few lines, before the failure line. Severity: Low. Blocks: no.
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-df685ec1d8a7` security finding, details recorded privately
- INFORMATIONAL `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts:794` 6. **A trailing-whitespace line** in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts:794` (`git diff --check`). FIXABLE. Severity: Low. Blocks: no.

</details>

title: Codex loads office-hours, plan-design-review and gstack-upgrade again, and knows when it runs unattended (GST-3161)
body:
On Codex, naming office-hours, plan-design-review or gstack-upgrade loaded nothing, because setup left a second copy of each that Codex listed twice; on macOS and Linux setup now links those copies, and re-running setup or upgrading fixes an existing install.
Skills started under `codex exec` now report `SESSION_KIND: headless` instead of `interactive` (also on slim Linux images without `ps`), Codex reviewers start without the parent's conversation (`fork_turns: "none"`), and the docs stop saying Codex has no hooks.
Nothing to do after merge; Codex users pick it up on their next upgrade.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Duplicate skills (setup).** Codex 0.170 lists every real `SKILL.md` under its skills folder and skips a symlinked one. `create_codex_runtime_root` copied `gstack-upgrade`, `office-hours` and `plan-design-review` into `~/.codex/skills/gstack/` so other skills can read them by path; those copies were second listings of skills Codex already lists from `gstack-<name>/`, and naming a skill that is listed twice injects nothing. The new `_link_codex_skill_refs` writes them as links, so the paths still resolve and each skill is listed once. The runtime root is rebuilt on every setup run, so an existing install is fixed by `./setup --host codex` or `/gstack-upgrade`. Windows (copies, not links) still lists them twice, and the changelog says so.
- **Unattended Codex runs (`bin/gstack-session-kind`).** Codex gives tool shells the same environment in the TUI and in exec (`CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_CI=1`, no TTY), so the helper reads the subcommand of the nearest `codex` process: `exec`, `e` or `review` means headless; the TUI runs tool shells under `codex app-server` and stays interactive. It reads parent pids from /proc on Linux (falling back to `ps`), only walks the process tree when `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is set, and Conductor's markers still win.
- **Reviewer context (GST-3091, `hosts/codex.ts`).** The inline `spawn_agent` call used by the design reviewers, /autoplan's phases and /context-restore now passes `fork_turns: "none"` (Codex defaults it to `all`). /ship's audits already did.
- **Docs.** `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` says Codex runs hooks but gstack hasn't ported its three there; `docs/unattended.md` describes the Codex session-kind rule.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"`$office-hours` started without its instructions" on Codex, and a `codex exec` run asked questions in prose that nobody would answer. Codex users now get each skill listed once and loaded when named, and unattended Codex runs stop with a clear BLOCKED line instead.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Every gstack workflow reads `gstack-session-kind`, so a wrong answer would change question handling everywhere; the new Codex branch runs only when `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is set and a codex ancestor runs `exec`, `e` or `review`, and any read failure falls back to the old `interactive` answer (walked failure path, tests ran). The setup change touches only the three Codex reference copies, which other skills read by path; the links resolve to the committed `.agents/skills` render (live Codex 0.170.0 install and upgrade checked).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two full passes on the gate-class review plan (specialists for testing, security and state machines, red team, a native adversarial reader, a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol and a targeted auth reader). Pass 1 raised two informational findings, both fixed in d7f2316: a testing gap (Windows setup still copies the three files, so the changelog now says macOS and Linux) and one red-team finding (security finding, details recorded privately). Pass 2 on the fix range was clean; the second-model review returned CLEAN and the targeted reader found nothing. No blocking findings.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-session-kind:105` If an ancestor exits between the -r check and the read, bash prints a No such file line to stderr; result stays interactive.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-session-kind:105` The PPid assignment can return 1; safe today only because the function runs inside an if condition under set -e.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-session-kind:78` Comment says no signal on Git Bash, but MSYS2 exposes /proc too; behavior still safe (native codex.exe shows as PPid 1).

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional smoke on `bin/gstack-session-kind` with fake codex parents, rerun after the fix: codex exec → headless, app-server → interactive, a `--no-daemon` prompt starting with "exec" → interactive, and codex exec with no `ps` on PATH (direct and through an intermediate shell) → headless. 5 of 5 pass. Limit: fake parents, not a live Codex CLI (the live checks are under Tests).

</details>

The change makes Codex report `headless` under `codex exec`, `codex e` and `codex review`, links Codex's nested office-hours, plan-design-review and gstack-upgrade SKILL.md files instead of copying them, starts Codex reviewers with `fork_turns: "none"`, and corrects the Codex hooks row in the docs.

title: Ship policy can mark published data as content, so /ship can review large data PRs (GST-3158)
body:
A repo can now list published-data folders under a new `review_content_patterns` ship-policy key, so /ship leaves `.patch` diffs, `MANIFEST.sha256` and extension-less licences out of review, while source files there stay reviewed. Why: gstack-evals #352 is 13.8 MB, 13.6 MB of it published session data, and could never pass /ship's 2 MB review limit. Nothing to do until a repo adds the key to its base-branch policy; a pattern that keeps too many files now stops with `REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE` instead of being dropped.
What changed - **New key `review_content_patterns`** (`lib/ship-policy.ts`, `lib/ship-policy-keys.ts`, `lib/review-exclude.ts`). Git glob pathspecs, validated like `review_exclude_paths` and read only from the base branch. A file both keys match is content (`declared` in the plan's `content=` field), whatever its extension, unless it is a source file (`.ts`, `.js`, `.py`, `.rb`, `.sh`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.dart` and the like, in any letter case), which stays in review on both the text and the binary path. The other keep rules still win: `.gstack/` and `.github/` files, gate paths, executables, links, agent prose, config, gate-tagged, secret-line and named-by-code files stay in review. - **No more silent drop.** A pattern whose kept files would need more than 24,000 argument bytes on the readers' read command used to be skipped with only a `skipped=` note, sending the whole folder to readers. It now stops the plan (exit 3) with `REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE`, naming the pattern, the kept count, the keep reasons and the bytes, and pointing at `review_content_patterns`. - **Docs.** `docs/ship-policy.md#review-content-patterns` (with the gstack-evals case as the example), a troubleshooting entry, the result-code registry and its generated doctor table, and a release note in `changelog.d/`.
Why "Ship policy can't mark published data as content": gstack-evals #352 put 1,439 files of raw session data under one folder, and /ship counted every `.patch` and extension-less file as code, so the PR could never get under the 2 MB review limit. Now the repo owner names that folder once in the base policy and the reviewers read only the code the PR changes.
Blast radius Only repos whose base-branch policy sets both keys see a change in what reviewers read; gstack's own policy sets neither, so its reviews are unchanged. The one behavior change everywhere is that an over-limit `review_exclude_paths` pattern now stops the plan instead of being skipped, which fails closed. Evidence: `test/review-content-patterns.test.ts` runs `gstack-review-plan` on a #352-shaped fixture repo, plus negative controls (a content pattern alone excludes nothing; a branch cannot add the key for itself; source files, NUL-bearing and upper-case ones included, stay in review; the secrets scan and sealed guard still read excluded files).
Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation changes were needed. **Scope:** 4 commits from 5afef04e3 to HEAD across 11 files (the review_content_patterns ship-policy key and the REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE refusal). The candidate has no staged, unstaged or untracked content. I searched all authored docs and templates for references to review_exclude_paths and to the removed `skipped=` exclusion behaviour. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-policy.md: current (key table row, the review-content-patterns section, the keep-limit refusal) - docs/troubleshooting.md: current (the REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE entry and the updated REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE fixes) - docs/review-policy.md: current (the readers-under-exclusion section and the owner map still hold) - changelog.d/review-content-patterns-for-published-data.md: current, read only **Coverage debt:** review_content_patterns has reference, how-to and explanation docs but no tutorial (a common gap). REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE is covered by its troubleshooting entry and its result-code anchor. No critical gaps. **Diagram drift:** none; no diagram covers this area.
Tests - [x] CI free suite at 5978e6f (workflow_dispatch run 44485932177): green, 1,703 test files carried. - [x] `bun --no-env-file test test/review-content-patterns.test.ts`: 7 pass, 0 fail. - [x] `test/review-exclude.test.ts`, `test/review-exclude-secret-value.test.ts`, `test/gstack-ship-policy.test.ts`, `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts`, `test/ship-policy-compat.test.ts`, `test/policy-floor-stable.test.ts` with the content-pattern tests: 100 pass, 0 fail. - [x] `bun run typecheck`: 0 errors.
Test Coverage Coverage audit (read-only): 13 of 16 changed paths have a test. Gaps: `validatePolicy` errors for the new key, the `shipConsequences` line, and a declared binary without an extension.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds plus one granted fix check. Round 1 fixed a source file in a declared folder leaving review; round 2 found the same gap on the binary path, fixed under the grant and confirmed by the fix check. The second-model review returned clean. Open notes (not blocking): the source-extension list covers the import-graph languages only (`.php`, `.ps1`, `.java` and others in a declared folder still leave review); an HLS media segment named `.ts` is now kept as code, which can stop a large media folder with `REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE`; a NUL-bearing source file is not read by the named-by-code grep.

title: Codex gets gstack's skill routing hint and destructive-command check (GST-3172)
body:
`./setup --host codex` now adds gstack's skill-routing hint and destructive-command check to Codex's `~/.codex/hooks.json`, next to your own hooks, so Codex users get the same guardrails Claude Code users have. Codex runs a hook only after you trust it, so nothing fires until you accept gstack's hooks at Codex's startup prompt or in `/hooks`; `gstack-doctor` shows whether you have.
What changed - **Writing Codex's hooks file.** `bin/gstack-settings-hook` has a Codex format (`GSTACK_HOOKS_FORMAT=codex`). It merges gstack's groups into `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` and keeps every user group value for value and in order (the file is re-indented as 2-space JSON on rewrite). It adds no tag keys, because Codex's schema rejects unknown keys. The result is checked against Codex's strict schema three times: on load, before the write, and on a re-read of the temp file before the rename. It refuses to write when `config.toml` already declares a gstack hook under `[hooks]` or doesn't parse. A new read-only `trust-status` verb reads Codex's trust entries; setup never writes trust. - **Setup.** On Codex 0.170 or newer, setup registers the routing hook (`UserPromptSubmit`) and the destructive-command check (`PreToolUse`) under the same off switches as Claude Code (`skill_routing`, `destructive_guard`, `--no-team`). It prints one line saying the hooks wait for trust, and one line recommending `codex -c model_reasoning_effort=high` (setup writes no reasoning setting). With older or missing Codex it says why and skips. - **The hooks.** `hosts/codex/hooks/` holds two small entries that reuse the Claude Code hooks. On Codex a `$skill` mention counts as an explicit skill choice, and the hint wording names Codex skills. - **Ask has no Codex equivalent.** Codex rejects `ask` from a `PreToolUse` hook. In an interactive session the check denies, and the reason tells the model to stop and ask you; you can run the command yourself with `!`, which skips hooks (confirmed live). Under `codex exec` it becomes a warning and the command runs. Deleting `/` or your home folder is denied everywhere. - **Uninstall and doctor.** `gstack-uninstall` removes gstack's Codex groups. `gstack-doctor` gets a "codex hooks" row: registered, trusted, untrusted or disabled. - **Docs.** `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` (new Codex row and Codex section), `docs/hosts.md`, and the README host table. Claude Code's hook registrations and hint wording are unchanged, and tests pin both.
Tests - `test/codex-hooks.test.ts`: the Codex format (merge, idempotence, user groups kept, strict schema, config.toml clash, trust-status), routing on Codex, the ask mapping in interactive and exec sessions, and the Claude Code output pin. - `test/codex-hooks-setup.test.ts`: setup's gate, its version floor, uninstall and the doctor row. - `test/codex-hooks-real-codex.test.ts` plus `.github/workflows/codex-hooks.yml`: installs `@openai/codex@0.170.0` and checks that the real CLI loads the merged file and runs both the user's hook and gstack's routing hook, and that it skips untrusted hooks and a file with an unknown key. It points Codex at a dead local model endpoint, so it spends nothing. - All three are POSIX-only and excluded from the Windows subset by the curation patterns.
Known limits and review notes **Known limits** - If one of your own hook groups comes after gstack's in the same event, removing gstack's group would shift your hooks to new positions, and Codex keys trust by position. So in that case `./setup`'s off switch and `gstack-uninstall` leave `hooks.json` unchanged and print how to delete gstack's group by hand. Uninstall can therefore leave gstack's group in place. - On Windows the Codex runtime folder lacks the Claude hook files the Codex hooks import, so both hooks do nothing there (they fail open). Windows has minimal support, so this is out of scope. - No real-Codex test drives the deny path, and the coverage audit found gaps in message and log paths. **Second-model review findings ruled below the blocking bar for this PR** - `setup:3193`: the Windows gap above. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:423`: rewriting `hooks.json` goes through JavaScript numbers, so an integer above 2^53 in one of your own MCP hook inputs would be rounded. Claude Code's `settings.json` has been rewritten the same way since before this PR. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:383`: the shared quoting helper leaves parentheses unquoted, so a `CODEX_HOME` path containing `(` or `)` gives hook commands the shell can't run. The same helper serves Claude Code's hooks, and a small fix for both follows this PR. **Other review notes (not blocking)** - `bin/gstack-uninstall:622`: when uninstall leaves gstack's Codex group in place, the reason is printed only on stderr, and `hooks.json` keeps naming the deleted scripts until you remove the group. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:430`: the Codex schema check also refuses removal and `trust-status` when a newer Codex adds keys this copy of the schema doesn't know. - The destructive-command check is registered with a 10 s timeout, and its inner steps budget 8 s plus 2 s, so a slow machine can run past it. - `.github/workflows/codex-hooks.yml` runs only when the listed paths change; `setup`, `careful/bin/check-careful.sh`, `hosts/claude/hooks/spawn-bin.ts` and the payload fixture aren't listed. - Bun's TOML parser could disagree with Codex about an unusual `config.toml`, and `trust-status`'s error says "refusing to mutate" although it only reads. **Second-model review of the design decisions, ruled below the blocking bar for this PR** (all five go into the follow-up that fixes the quoting helper) - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:268`: if you put your own handler inside gstack's group, the refusal message's advice to delete gstack's group would delete your handler too. Setup always gives gstack its own group. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:193`: gstack's copy of the Codex schema refuses `description: null`, which Codex accepts (setup then leaves the file alone), and lets a nested `null` in an MCP hook input through, which Codex already rejects for the whole file. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:1076`: `rollback` restores your pre-write backup without re-checking it against the schema. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:245`: the duplicate check catches a gstack hook in `config.toml` only when its matcher is literally `Bash`; under `^Bash$` the check could run twice once both copies are trusted. - `bin/gstack-settings-hook:1181`: when `CODEX_HOME` and `hooks.json` are both symlinks, `gstack-doctor` can report a trusted hook as untrusted.
Documentation **Status:** current — the read-only audit found every doc touched by the Codex hooks change accurate, with no corrections needed. **Scope:** base `ed4086e2` to head `d3bd5d6c`, 6 commits and 24 selected committed files (nothing staged, unstaged or untracked). I checked authored docs against `setup`, `bin/gstack-settings-hook`, `bin/gstack-doctor`, `bin/gstack-uninstall` and `.github/workflows/codex-hooks.yml`. **Documentation health:** - `README.md`: current. The Codex host row says destructive commands are blocked once gstack's hooks are trusted. - `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`: current. The host table and the Codex section (trust, schema safety, removal, deny instead of ask) match the code. - `docs/hosts.md`: current. It covers reasoning effort and the hooks.json registration. - `docs/uninstall.md`: current. It covers both automatic and manual Codex hooks removal. - `docs/skills.md`: current. Its safety section still accurately describes the Claude Code session hooks. - `changelog.d/codex-hooks-setup-routing-guard.md`: reviewed only, and consistent with the docs. **Coverage debt:** the Codex routing hook and destructive-command check have reference and how-to coverage (`docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md#codex`), but no tutorial, and `docs/troubleshooting.md` has no entry for the new `gstack-doctor` `codex hooks` row. That is a common gap, not a critical one. Consider `/document-generate`. **Diagram drift:** none; no architecture diagrams reference the changed surfaces.

The Stop contract hook and Codex transcript reader are PR 2. - Live probes (gpt-5.4-mini, under $1): the routing hint reached the model; in the TUI `git reset --hard` was denied with the reason and `!git reset --hard` ran with no hooks; under `codex exec` the ask became a warning (with #4510's session-kind); `rm -rf ~/` was denied; "Trust all and continue" wrote `[hooks.state."…/hooks.json:pre_tool_use:1:0"]` and doctor then read the hooks as trusted. - Finding for #4510: Codex starts hooks with a cleared environment and no `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, so session-kind can't see exec from hook context. The Codex guard entry sets `CODEX_THREAD_ID` from the payload's `session_id` before asking session-kind. `bin/gstack-session-kind` and `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` are not edited. - Trial merge with #4510 (d7f2316): one conflict, the Codex row in `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, resolved to this PR's row. Typecheck and 69 focused tests pass on the merged tree. - `test/gstack-config-defaults.test.ts` "every DEFAULTS key is read by code" times out (about 7 s against a 5 s limit) on this machine on clean main b702243 too. Its corpus walk reads compiled binaries in `bin/`. Not caused by this PR. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-7e9e421bc4e2). The full approval record stays private. title: Destructive-command check stops asking about scratch deletes and blocks real damage (GST-3169)
body:
The destructive-command check no longer asks before deleting temp, cache or build folders, and now catches dangerous commands it used to miss: deletes outside the project, force-pushes to main inside longer commands, history rewrites, database resets and cloud deletes. Agents were stopped for harmless cleanup while real damage got through: on a 102-row replay of real command shapes, main gives the expected answer on 66 and this branch on all 102. Nothing to do, except: an Agent SDK app where a person answers prompts should set `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=interactive`.
What changed - `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` now reads every command in a chain on its own (after `&&`, `;`, `|`, `sudo`, `xargs`, inside `bash -c`), in pure bash that still runs on bash 3.2 and Git Bash. - **Never asks:** a recursive delete whose every target is scratch: `/tmp/...`, `/var/tmp/...`, a `$(mktemp)` variable, a relative path after `cd` into scratch, a cache folder, or a build artifact (`node_modules`, `dist`, `.venv` and the like). A path with `..` is never scratch. - **Now denied (was ask or allow):** recursive delete of `/`, `~`, a system folder or a personal folder like `~/.ssh`; a force-push (not lease-only) to main, master or the default branch in any command shape, including a bare `git push -f` while on that branch; raw disk writes and wipes (`dd of=/dev/sda`, `mkfs`, `wipefs`). - **Now asks (was allow):** deletes outside the session folder (`rm`, find's delete actions, `rsync --delete`, `shred`, `unlink`), `git push --force-with-lease` and remote branch deletes, `git stash drop`/`clear`, `git worktree remove --force`, history rewrites (`filter-branch`, `filter-repo`, BFG, `reflog expire --expire=now`, `gc --prune=now`), database resets (`prisma migrate reset`, `dropdb`, `FLUSHALL`, `DELETE FROM` with no `WHERE` and others), and cloud deletes (`terraform destroy`, `aws`/`gcloud`/`az` deletes; dry runs and `plan` are skipped). - **Asks only when there is work to lose:** `git reset --hard`, `checkout -f`, `checkout -- paths`, `switch -f`/`--discard-changes`, `restore` without `--staged`, and `clean -f` run `git status` (or `git clean -n`) first and ask only if the tree has uncommitted or untracked changes the command would discard. If git fails or the folder is not a repo, it asks. - **Fewer false asks:** `DROP TABLE` and `TRUNCATE` ask only with a SQL client (`psql`, `mysql`, `sqlite3`, `Invoke-Sqlcmd` and others) or in SQL form (`TRUNCATE TABLE`, `TRUNCATE x;`); `aws s3 rm` without `--recursive` and a commit message mentioning `rm -rf` no longer ask. - If the check itself fails, it asks instead of silently allowing. - **Agent SDK sessions** (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py` or `sdk-ts`) now get the ask as a warning, like `claude -p`, unless the host is Conductor or sets `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=interactive`. A real SDK run (Python SDK 0.2.185, Opus 5.5) showed an ask with no permission callback is refused outright: the command never ran and the model saw the ask text as an error. A deny stays a deny. - `careful/bin/hook-extract.sh` passes the hook payload's working directory to the check, so relative paths are judged against the folder the command runs in. - The /careful and /guard skill pages and `docs/skills.md` describe the new rules; `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` documents the SDK behavior and both `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND` settings.
Tests - New `test/careful-replay.test.ts` (182 cases) replays `test/fixtures/careful/geva-560-synthetic.jsonl` (102 rows, checksum pinned) and asserts the ask, deny or allow decision for every row, plus 13 harmless scratch deletes and 65 rule cases. No uncommitted work is lost, but an unexpanded revision argument does not ask. 4. `printf x >> README.md && git reset --hard` on a clean tree. The only work lost is what the same command just wrote. title: label: record the actual harness (chief) and rename the native review pass harness-neutrally
body:
Review rows and skill text now record the harness actually running the session, and the built-in second review keeps a harness-neutral name.

Why: sessions running under a different harness than the docs' install target were logged with the install target's host label, and the built-in second review was called "the Claude adversarial pass" even though it runs in the same harness.

Nothing to do: existing claude and codex detection is unchanged; a custom host only takes effect if you register one with `setup --host <name>`.

## What changed

Two groups:

1. **Native review labels (group A).** The review that runs in the same harness, in a fresh context, was labeled "Claude adversarial" in docs and tests because the label came from one source (`outsideVoiceFor`'s `nativeLabel: 'Claude'` in `scripts/resolvers/outside-voice.ts`). It is now "native adversarial", with the matching relay and prose strings in `scripts/resolvers/constants.ts`, the record check in `lib/ship-parts.ts`, the test pins, and the regenerated skill docs. No detection or branching code is touched: CLAUDECODE / CODEX markers, host branching, "Claude Code" vendor-correct references, and the Codex second-model review (a different vendor's CLI, correctly named) are unchanged. Historical CHANGELOG / TODOS / design-record entries are left as-is — they are records, not labels.

2. **Record the executing harness (group B).** New `bin/gstack-host` helper (mirrors `gstack-session-kind`): an explicit `GSTACK_ACTIVE_HOST` registration — the generic way any harness identifies itself, set up with `setup --host <h>` — wins; otherwise the claude / codex conditions from `bin/gstack-skill-start` run byte-for-byte unchanged; with no markers the primary host `claude` is recorded. `bin/gstack-skill-start` now prints a `HOST:` banner line, and `bin/gstack-review-log` sets `GSTACK_STAMP_HOST` on review rows through `bindReview` (`lib/review-evidence.ts`): the logger overrides the caller's doc label, the same pattern as the session-kind actor. No consumer validates host values, so a registered harness id flows through unmodified. Deliberately vendor-neutral: no single vendor's identifiers enter this repo; a harness that registers itself records itself with no repo change.

## Tests

- Every test area this PR touches is green standalone (agentic runs on the contributor's seat): `gstack-host` 4/4, `review-log-findings` 18/0, `skill-validation` 319/0, `skill-cross-model-recommendation-emit` 6/0, `host-config` 113/0, `gen-skill-docs` 495/0, `gstack-session-kind` 16/0, `outside-voice-failure-policy` 37/0, `review-pass` 79/0.
- Registration proof (scratch git repo, never a real project): `GSTACK_ACTIVE_HOST=kiro` → the helper prints `kiro`, the banner reads `HOST: kiro`, and a review row written with the caller claiming `"host":"claude"` records `"host":"kiro"`; `CLAUDECODE=1` → `claude`; `CODEX_THREAD_ID=t1` → `codex`; no markers → `claude`. The two old branch conditions are byte-for-byte intact.
- Grep proof: `grep -rn "Claude adversarial"` — remaining hits are historical CHANGELOG / TODOS / design records only; active code, docs and test trees are clean.

## Agent notes

- Verification runs were agentic, on the contributor's seat (not CI). Every other failure observed in the full suite reproduces on a clean worktree at the pre-PR base `f79a8905` — pre-existing on that seat, not introduced here.
- `catalog-budget` passes on a clean checkout of this branch (2288 ≤ 2290 token-equivalents); its only local failure on the contributor's seat comes from a stray untracked `hygiene/` directory in the working tree, which is not part of this change.
- The claude and codex branch conditions are byte-for-byte unchanged, pinned in `test/gstack-host.test.ts` and `test/review-log-findings.test.ts`.

title: Second-model review keeps the reviewer's result and reports budget stops (GST-3181)
body:
When Codex reviews a change, gstack now keeps the review file the reviewer wrote instead of replacing it with Codex's one-line closing message, and a provider that refuses with HTTP 402 is reported as a used-up budget instead of "exit 1" or a login failure.
Why: gstack-evals lost 22 review attempts to the overwrite and 5 of 45 sessions to a 402 from a metering proxy whose cause gstack threw away.
Nothing to do: a 401 or 403 is still a login problem. Open notes, one of them a known gap, are listed below.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **The reviewer's result survives.** The autoplan prompt tells the reviewer to write its result to the file gstack passes as `--out`, and the codex-cli runner also passed that path to `codex exec -o`, so Codex overwrote the review with its closing message when it exited. `-o` now writes `<out>.last-message`; gstack keeps the reviewer's own file when it carries the gate's markers, otherwise the last message (the old behavior), and writes the winner to `<out>`. Confirmed with codex-cli 0.170.0.
- **A 402 keeps its cause.** Real Codex prints no stderr line for an HTTP refusal; the cause is only in its `--json` `error` and `turn.failed` events. The shared validator (`lib/outside-review-result.ts`) now reads those events, and a 402 or "payment required" becomes the new reason `budget_exhausted` (`lib/gate-outcomes.ts`, anchor `outside-review-budget-exhausted` in docs/troubleshooting.md). Other failures, 401 and 403 included, keep Codex's status line as their detail instead of "exit 1".
- **Every path.** The same validator serves the rendered /review, /ship and plan-review calls, the /codex modes, the unattended runner and host-dispatched reviewers. The Claude Code review that a Codex session runs gets a `budget` failure code in `lib/claude-code.ts`. /codex's own error list names the budget stop before its auth error. The prose auth rule the other skills share is unchanged (see the open notes).

</details>

<details><summary>Not changed</summary>

When the review runs, retries, budgets and allowances are unchanged. The readiness probe still treats a 402 as inconclusive, so the review runs once and its own result names the cause. A reviewer in a read-only sandbox still cannot write its own file; the last message is used then, as before.

</details>

<details><summary>Open notes (not fixed in this PR)</summary>

- **Still open from the original request:** the prose rule the skills share still reads stderr containing "auth", "login" or "API key" as an auth failure. So in every skill except /codex, a 402 whose provider message mentions the API key can still be read as a login problem. This is the one part of the request this PR doesn't close.
- **Ruled below the blocking bar:** `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:158`. The runner keeps the reviewer's own file unless that file is empty or missing its markers, so an incomplete draft without a final verdict wins over a finished closing message in `.last-message`. No current caller reaches this (only the autoplan prompts ask the reviewer to write its own file, and the autoplan gate reads an incomplete draft as missing its markers), and it fails closed: the run reads as unverified, never as clean. **Follow-up (two lines):** count the reviewer's own file only when its verdict is clean or findings.
- `lib/outside-review-result.ts:69`: the 402 pattern matches any "402" with no digit beside it, so a request id like `9c3f402ab` or "took 402 ms" reads as a budget stop. A 401 or 500 with such an id is reported as `budget_exhausted` and tells the user logging in won't help (reproduced). The review still reads as unavailable. Follow-up: match 402 only as an HTTP status ("status 402", "HTTP 402", "Payment Required") and add negative tests.
- `lib/outside-review-result.ts:117`: a budget or quota line in the host's error text is checked before the review itself, so a stale host error from a retry that later recovered can discard a finished review.
- `lib/claude-code.ts:122`: a Claude Code usage limit is reported with the Codex usage-limit message, which names Codex and a Codex-only setting.
- `lib/claude-code.ts:118`: when stdout is JSON, the budget check reads only the result text, so a 402 Claude Code put only in another field falls through to the generic failure.
- `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:159`: with the Codex sandbox turned off (`GSTACK_CODEX_NO_SANDBOX=1`), code the reviewer runs could write a marked result file that now beats Codex's real closing message. The default read-only sandbox can't write that file.
- `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:145`: the `.last-message` copy is left beside the `.stderr` and `.events.jsonl` files after the run.
- **Ruled below the blocking bar (maintainer ruling, 2026-11-19), from the second-family read of the decision trail.** Each one fails toward a wrong or generic cause, never toward a pass. A follow-up PR will cover the first three:
  - `lib/outside-review-result.ts:128`: the first matching failure line wins, so an earlier Codex `error` event with a 402 followed by a final `turn.failed` with a 401 reads as `budget_exhausted`.
  - `lib/claude-code.ts:116`: Claude Code exiting 0 with `subtype: error_during_execution`, a 402 in `result` and no `is_error` skips budget detection and reports the generic `provider-error`.
  - `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:148`: the runner deletes `<out>.last-message` before Codex runs without checking it isn't the prompt file, so `--prompt X.last-message --out X` deletes the prompt file after reading it. No caller passes that pair.
  - `lib/outside-voice-runner.ts:158` (same spot as the ruling above): a well-formed reviewer file with the wrong snapshot hash beats a correct `.last-message`, and autoplan then rejects it. This fails closed.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. Docs match the branch's changes; no corrections needed (read-only audit).

**Scope:** base b7022438 to head ec512c31 on report-review-budget-stop-not-login: committed changes only, as the tree is clean.

**Documentation health**
- docs/troubleshooting.md: Current (new `outside-review-budget-exhausted` entry matches `budget_exhausted` in lib/gate-outcomes.ts)
- codex/SKILL.md.tmpl: Current (402 budget rule; auth rule limited to 401/403)
- codex/SKILL.md: Current (in sync with template)
- changelog.d/report-review-budget-stop-not-login.md: Current (matches the `.last-message` and 402 behavior in code)

**Debt:** no coverage gaps and no diagram drift.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] Focused tests (claude-code-runner, model-catalog-isolation, outside-review-result, outside-runner-contract, outside-voice-failure-policy, outside-voice-invocation) all pass at ec512c3, with no failures.
- [x] bun run typecheck: clean. The parity suite passes.
- [x] Pre-push checks: typecheck, skill size, parity suite, context budget, module size, goldens and conflict markers passed at ec512c3.
- [x] Full free suite: carried from CI run 44494151996 at ec512c3 (1702 files).
- Paid evals: none run for this PR; the selector's 106 behavioral probes ride the scheduled release coverage.

</details>

title: A folder marked as published data can no longer hide source code or agent files from /ship's review (GST-3158)
body:
In a folder a repo marks as published data (`review_content_patterns`), source code in any language, agent instruction files, config and data that kept code names by full path now stay in /ship's review. Why: #4511 let a `.java` file, a binary `AGENTS.md` or a file named by a kept script leave review there, and reviewers must see every line of code a PR changes. Nothing to do: no base policy sets the key yet.
What changed A repo that marks a folder as published data could still have code in that folder skipped by review. That included a `.java` or `.ps1` file, an `AGENTS.md` with a NUL byte, a `CMakeLists.txt` or `.mdx` page, or a data file that a kept script reads by full path. Now one rule in `lib/review-exclude.ts` decides when a declared file is data. Source by name (a broad, case-insensitive list of program extensions and build file names), agent prose, config, gate paths and `.gstack/` or `.github/` files stay code, in the text and binary branches alike, and a docs-looking name that is really source (`CMakeLists.txt`, `.mdx`) is no longer excluded as docs. A declared file that stays in review (kept in the range, or an executable or link in the tree) counts as code when the scan looks for files that name excluded data, so the data it reads stays in review too.
Blast radius Only repos whose base policy sets `review_content_patterns` or `review_exclude_paths` see a difference, and every difference keeps more files in review, never fewer (file:line read at `lib/review-exclude.ts` contentKind and declaredData; 12 fixture cases in `test/review-content-patterns.test.ts` run the real plan command).
Test Coverage Coverage: 5 of 9 new code paths have a test (56%), audit only, no tests generated. Gaps proposed as tests: a config file in a declared folder, a `.github/` or gate path in a declared folder, a declared symlink as a reader of data, and a declared `.java` file naming a data file. Tests ran: free 1704 (files)
Pre-Landing Review Two full review passes. The first found two informational items, both fixed: `CMakeLists.txt` and `.mdx` were listed as source but still excluded as docs, and no test covered an unchanged declared executable on the base reading a data file. The second pass and the second-model review found nothing blocking.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - `lib/review-exclude.ts:270`: the build-file names in SOURCE match any suffix, so `docs/BUILD.md`, `guides/workspace.md` and every `.mdx` page under an excluded docs folder stay in review as code. That is the safe direction, but a large docs PR could hit `REVIEW_EXCLUDE_KEEP_TOO_LARGE`; untested. - `lib/review-exclude.ts:277`: `requirements.txt`, `constraints.txt` and other dependency `.txt` files still count as docs, so a broad base exclude pattern can drop an unnamed root-level dependency file from review. Unchanged from main; a policy call. - A declared file kept only because something names it does not in turn protect the data it names (the kept-declared set is built before the named-by-code scan, so the scan is not transitive). The policy table wording slightly over-states this. - A text file named like `results/BUILD.json` or `results/BUILD.log` that both keys match still leaves review as data or log, even though the build-name rule matches it. Those lines are unchanged from main; the maintainer ruled this an open note. - A declared binary with a content extension, such as `results/config/runtime.db`, still leaves review through the binary rule.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Status:** updated. Two factual edits in docs/ship-policy.md; no blockers. **Scope:** base f13dbb0d to head 50be17f2 (3 commits): changelog.d/declared-content-folders-keep-code.md, docs/ship-policy.md, lib/review-exclude.ts, test/review-content-patterns.test.ts. No staged, unstaged or new files. Cross-checked docs/troubleshooting.md and the earlier review_content_patterns changelog fragment. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-policy.md: updated. The policy key table row for `review_content_patterns` now says source code and the other keep rules still apply, and the `named-by-code` keep-reason row now counts declared files that stay in review as references that keep data. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. - changelog.d/declared-content-folders-keep-code.md: current (read only). **Coverage debt:** the declared-content keep rules have reference docs only (no how-to or explanation). Files with a source extension under a docs root are no longer excluded as docs, and no doc states this yet. No architecture diagrams are affected.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/review-content-patterns.test.ts test/review-exclude.test.ts test/review-exclude-secret-value.test.ts`: green locally - [x] `bun run typecheck`: clean - [x] CI free tests at this tree (run 44506530679): green
Agent notes Plan: exempt: bug fix (requested by the coordinator, GEVA-2) Follow-up to #4511, split by the coordinator after the second-family trail read (reports/GSTA-636-decisions.tsv rows 21-26). The BUILD.json/BUILD.log note is GStack Minder's ruling A1. REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=3 fixed=2 scope=frozen dispatches=6 Gate edits: none detected (2 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## title: On Capy, /ship no longer edits or comments on pull requests as you (GST-3183)
body:
On Capy, /ship's PR body edits, comments and new PRs no longer go out through `gh` under the machine owner's GitHub account. Each write now runs its checks, saves the exact text to a private file and prints a `HOST_PUBLISH:` line, so the agent publishes it with Capy's own PR tool. Nothing changes outside Capy (`GSTACK_CAPY` unset). ## Why During an unattended /ship on garrytan/gbrain-evals#523 (gstack 1.101.0.0), `gstack-ship-receipt stub` recorded its review rounds by running `gh pr edit`, so another system's PR body was edited as garrytan even though the brief said to publish only through the PR tool. The rule is that GitHub writes from Capy go only through Capy's PR tools. ## What changed - `lib/host-publish.ts` (new): `hostPublishes()` is true under `GSTACK_CAPY=1`; `handOff()` writes each part to `/publish/-..md` (mode 0600) and returns one `HOST_PUBLISH:` line naming the files and the host tool to use. - The commands that record /ship's review rounds in the PR body hand off on Capy instead of running `gh pr edit` (details in Agent notes). - `gstack-post`: every write op (`pr-body`, `pr-title`, `pr-comment`, `issue-comment`, `reply`, `pr-create`, `issue-create`) runs its plain-title, plain-body, security and secret checks as before, then hands off instead of calling gh. A HIGH finding still refuses with no file written. - `gstack-greptile-early open` says the draft went to the host tool instead of "did not print the new PR URL". - Prose: the Capy PR section and Step 19's "mark it ready" line say to use the host's PR tool; `docs/troubleshooting.md#host-publish` explains the line. ## Blast radius Only runs with `GSTACK_CAPY=1` change; the `--body ` paths and every non-Capy path are byte-identical (the existing round-recording and gstack-post suites pass unchanged). Reads through gh (`pr view`, `repo view`, `api` GETs) are unchanged.
Agent notes ## Agent notes **Round-recording commands.** `gstack-ship-receipt` `stub`, `stop`, `claim` and `carry` with `--pr` share one `postBody`, which hands off on Capy. `claim` can't read its marker back before the host publishes, so on Capy it trusts its own write; a double claim is still caught by the next `history` read. **Tests.** `test/capy-host-publish.test.ts` puts a recording `gh` shim on PATH and asserts zero write calls under `GSTACK_CAPY=1` for receipt `stub`, `stop`, `claim`, `carry` and all seven `gstack-post` write ops, plus a negative control showing the shim records `gh pr comment` when `GSTACK_CAPY` is unset. On main (12bd33b) the stub, stop/claim, carry and gstack-post cases fail with recorded `pr edit`/`POSTED:` writes. **gh write inventory (/ship, review and ship-queue paths)** Fixed here (can run under GSTACK_CAPY=1): - bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1069 `postBody` (`gh pr edit`), used by `stub` (:1165), `stop` (:1123), `claim` (:1142) and `carry` (:976, which had its own `gh pr edit`) - lib/gstack-post.ts:654-660 (`gh pr comment`, `gh issue comment`, `gh api --method=POST` reply, `gh pr edit` title/body, `gh pr create`, `gh issue create`) and :677-678 (`gh api --method=PATCH` fallback); hand-off at :840. Reached from /ship Step 5 (early draft PR), Step 6.5 (Greptile draft and trigger comment, lib/greptile-early.ts:198/208), Step 19 (body and title) and the stop comment. - ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl:295 `gh pr ready` (prose): now names the host's PR tool on Capy. Left as is, with reason: - crew/lib/ship-queue-wave.ts:411 (`pr comment`) and :579 (`pr close`), crew/lib/ship-queue-train-land.ts:226 (`pr edit --add-label`), lib/ship-queue-land.ts:309 (`pr create` for a drift repair): all run inside `gstack-ship-queue land` / wave and train landing, the merge action the brief keeps out of scope (and gstack itself is `merge: direct`, so the wave and train paths don't run here). Worth a follow-up if a Capy Captain lands a wave or train repo. - lib/squash-message.ts:90, crew/lib/ship-queue-train-land.ts:147 (`pr merge`): the land merge, out of scope. - crew/lib/ship-queue-dispatch-ci.ts:61, crew/lib/ship-queue-train-gate.ts:267/565, crew/lib/ship-queue-train.ts:485, crew/lib/release-gate.ts:177 (`gh workflow run`): CI dispatches that post no text, and Capy has no tool for them. - lib/release-stamp.ts:169 (`pr create` for the release PR): release path, not /ship. - scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-test-failure-triage.ts:96 (`gh issue create`, prose): only on the interactive "assign a GitHub issue" answer in a collaborative repo; Capy has no GitHub issue tool, and editing the shared preamble regenerates every skill. Size ledger: test/size-ledger/ship/capy-ship-writes-through-host-pr-tool.json (+251 bytes, the two prose lines). ```gstack-receipt-runs {"head":"e4361515e0cf6707d112baee02d466042822e32b","run":"ship-4517","status":"started","review_loop":{"passes":1,"blocking_found":0,"deferred":0,"noted":0,"fixed":2,"scope":"frozen","rounds":1,"dispatches":{"specialist":3}}} {"head":"a3f4de0905c5163d7ba45ac235b512cd1b07d468","run":"ship-4517-r3","status":"started","review_loop":{"passes":1,"blocking_found":0,"deferred":0,"noted":1,"fixed":0,"scope":"frozen","rounds":1,"est_input_tokens":19571,"dispatches":{"specialist-batched":1,"red-team":1}}} {"head":"a3f4de0905c5163d7ba45ac235b512cd1b07d468","run":"ship-4517-r3","mark":"stop","tree":"3df01fdf1cbe6cefb9fa6dfadcaaeace29e5ab06"} ```

title: On Capy, /ship hands its pull request edits and comments to Capy's PR tool, always naming the right repository (GST-3183)
body:
On Capy, /ship's PR body edits, comments and new PRs no longer go out through `gh` under the machine owner's GitHub account. Each write runs its checks, saves the exact text to a private file and prints a `HOST_PUBLISH:` line that names the repository (and host, off github.com) it belongs to, so Capy's PR tool sends it to the same place `gh` would have. Nothing changes outside Capy (`GSTACK_CAPY` unset).
Why During an unattended /ship on garrytan/gbrain-evals#523 (gstack 1.101.0.0), the command that records /ship's review rounds in the PR body ran `gh pr edit`, so another system's PR body was edited as garrytan even though the brief said to publish only through the PR tool. The rule is that GitHub writes from Capy go only through Capy's PR tools. A first version (#4517) handed the writes off but left the repository out when `--repo` wasn't passed, and /ship's own Step 9 call never passes it. Capy's PR tool would then fall back to the thread's main repository, so in a thread with several repositories or a fork, one PR's body could replace another repository's.
What changed - `lib/host-publish.ts` (new): `hostPublishes()` is true under `GSTACK_CAPY=1`. `handOff()` writes each part to its own private folder `/publish/--/.md` (folder 0700, file 0600) and returns one `HOST_PUBLISH:` line naming the files, the destination and the host tool to use. It refuses a hand-off without an owner/name repository, so no caller can print a partial line. - The commands that record /ship's review rounds in the PR body (listed in Agent notes) hand off on Capy instead of running `gh pr edit`. They read the destination with `gh repo view [--repo] --json nameWithOwner,url`, the same resolution `gh pr edit` uses, and put `repo=` (and `host=` when it isn't github.com) on the line. When that read fails they refuse and hand nothing off. - `gstack-post`: every write op (`pr-body`, `pr-title`, `pr-comment`, `issue-comment`, `reply`, `pr-create`, `issue-create`) runs its plain-title, plain-body, security and secret checks as before, then hands off with the repository and host gh would have written to (read with `gh repo view`, so a fork checkout's upstream is honoured), a reply's comment id, and a new PR's base, head (the current branch when `--head` is missing, as `gh pr create` would infer) and draft state. A HIGH finding still refuses with no file written. - `gstack-greptile-early open` says the draft went to the host tool instead of "did not print the new PR URL". - Prose: the Capy PR section and Step 19's "mark it ready" line say to use the host's PR tool, to the `repo=` the line names; `docs/troubleshooting.md#host-publish` explains the line.
Blast radius Only runs with `GSTACK_CAPY=1` change; the `--body ` paths and every non-Capy path are byte-identical (the existing round-recording and gstack-post suites pass unchanged). Reads through gh (`pr view`, `repo view`, `api` GETs) are unchanged, plus one `gh repo view` read per round-recording hand-off.
Documentation **Status:** current. Read-only audit of base f13dbb0..c6fc158 (6 commits, 15 files, clean working tree) found every changed doc accurate; nothing needed editing. **Scope:** the Capy host-publish hand-off (GST-3183). It covers `lib/host-publish.ts`, `gstack-post`, `gstack-ship-receipt` stub/stop/claim/carry, the greptile-early hand-off exit, the ship `capy-pr` and `pr-body` sections and their templates, the new `docs/troubleshooting.md#host-publish` entry and the changelog fragment. Related docs read: `docs/capy-install.md`, `docs/designs/GSTACK_ON_CAPY.md`, `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/writing-prs.md`. **Documentation health** - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The host-publish entry matches the HOST_PUBLISH line format, the folder layout and file modes, how the repo and host are resolved, and the refusal when the repo can't be resolved. - `ship/sections/capy-pr.md(.tmpl)`: current. - `ship/sections/pr-body.md(.tmpl)`: current. - `changelog.d/capy-ship-writes-through-host-pr-tool.md`: current (reviewed only). - `docs/capy-install.md`, `docs/designs/GSTACK_ON_CAPY.md`, `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/writing-prs.md`: current. Nothing in them contradicts the change. **Coverage debt** - `HOST_PUBLISH:` hand-off: has reference and how-to coverage (troubleshooting), plus mentions in the ship section. It isn't mentioned in the Capy install or design docs, which is a common gap. - `gstack-greptile-early` exit 3 on a hand-off: covered only by its error text, which is a common gap. - `/document-generate` can fill these later. **Diagram drift:** none.
Agent notes ## Agent notes **Open notes (GStack Minder's rulings: ship as disclosed notes, no third fix round; both fixes lead the follow-up batch).** 1. A fork pr-create through `gstack-post` on Capy names the bare local branch as `head=` (lib/gstack-post.ts:845), while `gh pr create` would have pushed to the fork and sent `owner:branch`, so the hand-off can name an upstream branch that doesn't exist or is the wrong one. Raised as blocking by the second-model reader at c6fc158. Fix: resolve the head's owner and send `owner:branch` (or refuse without `--head owner:branch`) when the head repo differs from `repo=`. 2. With `GH_REPO` set to another repository, `gh repo view` (no argument) still answers the checkout's repository while `gh pr view`/`gh pr edit` follow `GH_REPO` (checked against gh 2.103.3), so both hand-off paths can name a different `repo=` than the write they replace. Found by the second-family decision-trail read. Fix: pass `GH_REPO` (or `--repo`) to `gh repo view` in `postBody` and `gstack-post`, with a test that sets `GH_REPO`. 3. The review tool misread a line of the native reader's scope notes as a HIGH finding (p1/adversarial-native#1, `test/capy-host-publish.test.ts:0:scope-list-line`); GStack Minder ruled it not a finding. Fix: the review-dispatch collector should not parse scope-list bullets as findings. Ruled note: lib/gstack-post.ts:845:fork-head at c6fc15874876 ruled by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) at 2026-11-19T11:00:03.322Z: fork pr-create via gstack-post names the bare local branch as head=; Capy crews open PRs with their own tool; owner-prefixed head fix leads the follow-up batch (approval a-f69330b78aa2) Ruled note: test/capy-host-publish.test.ts:0:scope-list-line at c6fc15874876 ruled by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) at 2026-11-19T11:25:02.296Z: parser misread of the native reader's scope notes ('- a HIGH finding still refused;'), not a finding; the collector bug goes to review-dispatch's owner (approval a-4e6d4d77dff4) Plan: exempt: bug fix (R65) **Lessons.** 1. A hand-off that replaces a gh write has to carry everything gh would have inferred from the checkout: repository, host, comment id, base, head and draft state. The receiving tool has no checkout and falls back to its own default. 2. Its test has to assert where the write goes, not only that gh wrote nothing. #4517's zero-write test passed while every receipt hand-off was missing its repository. **Tests.** `test/capy-host-publish.test.ts` puts a recording `gh` shim on PATH and parses each `HOST_PUBLISH:` line into its destination fields, asserting the whole destination object for receipt `stub` (with and without `--repo`), `stop`, `claim`, `carry` (on a GitHub Enterprise host) and all seven `gstack-post` write ops, plus: a two-repository fixture where the main repository differs from the PR's, a fork checkout where gh resolves the upstream repository and origin is the fork, a GitHub Enterprise host on `stub` and `gstack-post`, a new PR's inferred head, a refusal when the repository can't be resolved, a refusal in both commands when the repository can't be resolved, and a negative control showing the shim records `gh pr comment` when `GSTACK_CAPY` is unset. At #4517's head content (a3f4de0, carried here as e7c2ef1) 7 of 10 cases fail; at the fix all 10 pass. **Round-recording commands.** `gstack-ship-receipt` `stub`, `stop`, `claim` and `carry` with `--pr` share one `postBody`, which hands off on Capy. `claim` can't read its marker back before the host publishes, so on Capy it trusts its own write; a double claim is still caught by the next `history` read. **Fork fix.** /ship's second-model reader found that gstack-post took `repo=` from origin while gh's write follows `gh repo set-default` and `GH_REPO`; c6fc158 resolves it through `gh repo view` (its two new tests fail at d8fe752). **Carried from #4517.** Commits 6e93604, e436151 and a3f4de0 are cherry-picked onto main f13dbb0 unchanged (9b96a63, 6b58851, e7c2ef1); 0fa1f3b adds the destination fix. **gh write inventory (/ship, review and ship-queue paths)** Fixed here (can run under GSTACK_CAPY=1): - bin/gstack-ship-receipt `postBody` (`gh pr edit`), used by `stub`, `stop`, `claim` and `carry` (which had its own `gh pr edit`) - lib/gstack-post.ts send paths (`gh pr comment`, `gh issue comment`, `gh api --method=POST` reply, `gh pr edit` title/body, `gh pr create`, `gh issue create`) and the `gh api --method=PATCH` fallback. title: A failed second-model review names the cause that stopped it, and never deletes its own prompt (GST-3188)
body:
When a second-model review fails, gstack now reports the failure that actually ended it: Codex's final error decides, a stray "402" in a request id no longer reads as a used-up budget, and a Claude Code 402 or usage limit reads as a budget stop with no Codex advice. Why: these were the four follow-ups ruled below the blocking bar on #4515; each one could send someone to fix the wrong thing. Nothing to do. The prose rule that reads "auth", "login" or "API key" in stderr as a login failure is not changed here (see below).
What changed - **The final failure decides.** When Codex's `--json` events hold failures, only the last one (`turn.failed`) is classified, so an early 402 retry followed by a final 401 stays an execution failure with the 401 in its detail (`lib/outside-review-result.ts`). - **A 402 counts only as a status.** `HTTP 402`, `status 402`, `"status":402`, `"status_code": 402`, `statusCode: 402`, `Error: 402`, `402 Payment Required` or "payment required"; a request id like `req_9c3f402ab` or `req-402-payment-abc`, or "after 402 ms", no longer does. - **Claude Code budget stops.** Claude Code exiting 0 with `subtype: error_during_execution` and a 402 in `result` is now a `budget` failure, not a generic provider error. A Claude Code usage limit is read as `budget_exhausted` instead of Codex's `quota_exhausted`, whose advice names Codex and a Codex-only setting. The `budget_exhausted` summary and its troubleshooting entry now name the Claude Code usage limit. - **The prompt file is protected.** `gstack-outside-voice run` refuses (exit 2) a `--prompt` that is `--out` or one of the files the run writes beside it (`.events.jsonl`, `.stderr`, `.last-message`, `.meta.json`), symlinks resolved; the codex-cli runner refuses the same pair itself (`prompt_is_output`) before deleting anything. - **Which result file wins.** Codex's complete closing message replaces a reviewer file that has no final verdict, unless that file holds a Critical or High finding the closing message doesn't. A reviewer file that lacks the result markers, or (for plan reviews) whose first line (`INPUT: `) names another snapshot, gives way to a marked closing message, as on main. A reviewer file that says it is not ready is kept, and a file written for another snapshot is never reported clean. The snapshot is read from the last result-format block in the prompt.
Not changed Retries, budgets and when the review runs. The shared prose rule ("auth", "login" or "API key" in stderr means a login failure) is rendered into `review/sections/adversarial.md`, a pinned reviewer file, so changing it needs its own no-loss replay; it stays open for a separate PR. Reviewer prompts are byte-identical.
Open notes (not fixed in this PR) - The prose rule the skills share still reads stderr containing "auth", "login" or "API key" as a login failure. It is rendered into a pinned reviewer file, so it needs its own no-loss replay and a separate PR. - A `.meta.json` that is a hard link to the prompt file still passes the prompt check, which compares paths, not inodes (also true on main). - Claude Code's "You've hit your session limit" banner (an HTTP 429) still reads as a generic failure, not a usage stop (also true on main). - The host-subagent runner is refused for `--prompt X.last-message --out X` even though it never writes `.last-message`; it refuses safely. - Once Codex's `--json` events hold a failure, a cyber-policy or quota line that appears only on stderr is not read. - "Error: 402 ms elapsed" still reads as a budget stop, and "status code (402)", "API Error (402)" or "got 402 from proxy" read as a general failure rather than a budget stop. - A reviewer file with only Medium or Low findings and no final verdict is replaced by a complete closing message that says `VERDICT: CLEAN`, so the run reads clean and those advisory findings are lost; on main it read unverified. - A reviewer file with a Critical or High finding but no result markers is still replaced by a marked clean closing message, as on main. - A plan-review closing message written for another snapshot can still read clean in the runner; plan review rejects it when the result is submitted, as on main.
Tests Seven new tests, each failing on main at 957fab7, and three more from review that fail at b58f1f4, all passing here: final-failure order, 402 in a request id or duration, Claude `error_during_execution` 402, Claude usage limit wording, unverified reviewer file, result for another snapshot, prompt-is-output refusal (runner and CLI). Focused suites (outside-review-result, claude-code-runner, outside-runner-contract, troubleshooting-anchors, model-catalog-isolation, outside-voice-failure-policy, outside-voice-invocation, outside-review-cyber-policy): 630 pass, 0 fail. Typecheck clean.
