title: A second review round reviews a gate-class fix instead of reporting done (GST-3187)
body:
/ship's second review round now reviews a fix that touched a gate-class path, instead of reporting done with nothing read.
A plan told "nothing was fixed" while the branch has new commits since the reviewed head now refuses with `review_required_no_readers` rather than printing done.
Nothing to do: the next /ship picks it up.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Gate-class fix counts as a fix.** After a full pass, `gstack-review-plan --last full --touched-gate` with no other fix flag planned done ("the step applied no edits"). The full-pass loop now counts `--touched-gate` as a fix, as the light review loop and the step after a follow-up check already did, so it plans a full pass on the range (or the owner stop at the round cap).
- **Fail closed on unreviewed commits.** With `--last full`, no fix flag, and a readable `--range-base` range holding the PR's own new commits, the plan exits 3 with the `review_required_no_readers` outcome (new row in `lib/gate-outcomes.ts`, section in `docs/troubleshooting.md`). `gstack-review-dispatch pass` stops on it before creating any reader. Exempt: `--post-review` and the `--targeted-ran` read, which plan their own post-loop edits.
- **Dispatch reads only its own flags.** `gstack-review-dispatch` read its flags across the whole argument list, including the review-plan flags after `--`. A pass with no `--pass` of its own took the plan's `--pass 1` as its pass id, and a plan flag such as `--audit-only` switched dispatch's mode. Its flags now come only from before `--`, for every subcommand (`pass` and `render` are the two that take a `--` tail).

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A round-2 /ship on garrytan/gbrain#9799 (gstack 1.101.0.0) passed `--pass 1 --last full --touched-gate` and got `PASS: none next=done`. It was first reported as dispatch eating the plan's `--pass`. That run's own debug call shows the planner did receive `--pass 1`; the `pass=0` lines came from calling the planner directly with `--pass=1`, which it doesn't parse. The collision is real but did not cause that run, so both are fixed here.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/review-round2-plan.test.ts` (new): the exact round-2 shape the Capy pass program builds, with and without `--range-base` over a committed gate fix; dispatch never taking its flags from after `--`; the `review_required_no_readers` refusal from the plan and from dispatch; negative controls (no commit since the reviewed head is still done; a flagged fix still plans its review). 5 of 6 fail on main f13dbb0, and the negative control passes on both.
- Review-depth no-loss replay `GST-3187`: the GST-967 1,440-case grid and the GST-972 grid keep main's hashes with the 30 changed cells read back as main's plan. Every changed cell is `last=full` with `--touched-gate` as the only fix flag, and each moves from done to a review step or the owner stop (20 full passes, 9 owner stops, and 1 run of the adversarial and second-model reviewers before its stop). `lib/review-depth.ts` is repinned under that replay.

</details>

title: Destructive-command check closes the command-parsing gaps found after the last release (GST-3190)
body:
The destructive-command check now blocks force-pushes to main written with `--repo=`, after a `cd`, or with `--all`, and asks again for the other shapes that slipped past it after #4513. It also stops over-blocking dry runs, `wipefs` on image files, and greps for SQL text, and `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=interactive` keeps the ask under `CI=1`. Nothing to do: the check runs in every session already.
What changed, by shape Steps back from main, fixed first: - `git push --repo=origin +refs/heads/main` and `git push --repo=origin --force main` are denied. With `--repo`, every operand is read as a possible refspec (git itself reads the first one as the repository, so this is the cautious reading). - A `cd` inside a pipeline (`cd /tmp | true && rm -rf dir`) no longer counts as moving into scratch: bash runs each pipeline part in a subshell. A subshell now gives back the exact outer state, so `cd /tmp && (pwd) && rm -rf dir` no longer asks. - `git reset --hard "$REV"` asks again. - `printf x >> f && git reset --hard` on a clean tree stays allowed: the only work it can lose is what the same command wrote. `git stash pop` earlier in the same command does make a later discard ask, because pop drops the stash, the same loss `stash drop` always asks about. Gaps in the catches #4513 added: - `git clean -q` / `--quiet` no longer hides the dry-run listing. - `--work-tree`, `--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR=` and `GIT_WORK_TREE=` forms of `checkout -f`, `switch -f` and `clean -f` ask. - `find -L -delete` (leading find options) is read correctly. - `rm dir -rf` with flags at the end asks when `rm` is the command; `docker rm web -f` and `aws s3 rm` stay those tools' subcommands. - A `mktemp` variable assigned again in the same command is no longer scratch. - `..` beats the `/proc` and `/dev` exemptions, a `cd` through `..` is never scratch, and `rm -rf ../build` no longer rides the build-output allow. - A cloud delete's dry run counts only from the delete itself to the end of its statement, so a dry run on the line before (or before `;` with no space) never excuses it, and `plan` counts only as a whole word. - `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=interactive` outranks `CI=1` in the every-session guard hook (`claude -p` stays headless). Over-catches removed: - `git push -nf` is a dry run (letters after `o` in a short-option group are a push-option value, not flags). - `wipefs -a` stays blocked unless every target has a disk-image suffix (`.img`, `.iso`, `.raw`, `.qcow2`, `.vhd`, `.vhdx`, `.vmdk`, `.dmg`) outside `/dev/`; the values of `-t`, `-o` and `-O` are not targets. - The bare SQL shape (`TRUNCATE x;`) is ignored inside grep, rg, ag, ack and `git grep`, and in `echo`/`printf` text when nothing after it pipes or redirects (`||` is not a pipe); `./psql/` in a path is a folder, not a client. Force-pushes that only asked: - `cd . && git push -f origin` on main is denied: git now reads the folder a `cd` chain leads to for the force-push lookups (discard checks still ask after any `cd`). - `git push --force --all`, `--branches` and `--mirror` are denied when main, master or the default branch exists locally. Speed: the statement loop no longer indexes a bash array, which is linear per read on bash 3.2. A 200 KB command takes 1.3 s instead of 4.3 s on bash 3.2.57 and 0.9 s instead of 1.1 s on bash 5.2. Everyday commands are unchanged: p50 73.4 ms vs 73.2 ms at 55aaa6c on bash 5.2 (n=400 each, same machine, interleaved), with 9 ms of drift between repeat passes.
Tests `test/careful-replay.test.ts` gains 48 rows (`PARSER_CASES`), one or more per shape above; 26 fail at 55aaa6c, 10 more (from review) fail at e20997b, 5 fail at e74219a, and the rest are controls or the pinned `printf` decision. Non-main test trees now also hold a local `main` branch, as a feature checkout does. `test/destructive-guard-hook.test.ts` gains the `CI=1` case, which fails at 55aaa6c. The 102-row GEVA-560 replay stays green on bash 5.2.21 and 3.2.57. Not in this PR (outside its scope, none a step back from main): a quoted scratch path with a space, denying a literal home path, a failure while reading input before the safety trap, and a backtick revision in `reset --hard`. Open notes found in review, left for a follow-up: the SQL-text exemption still allows `grep 'truncate users;' a.sql | sh` and `echo "$(dbtool exec 'TRUNCATE TABLE users')"`; quoted parentheses can restore an earlier `cd` into scratch; `echo cd /tmp` still counts as a `cd`; `LC_ALL=C cd /tmp && rm -rf dir` and printed SQL text followed by a pipe in a later statement ask; and `grep 'a; truncate demo;'` still asks.
Agent notes - Follow-up to #4513 (55aaa6c4a5dff86e02d9bf9bfc7557c491f98a37), GST-3190. Decision trail: captain drive reports/GSTA-647-decisions.tsv. - Local checks: 10 test files that load the check or the hook, 619 pass on bash 5.2; on bash 3.2.57 one unrelated failure (freeze-owned-lifecycle, fails identically at 55aaa6c on 3.2). Typecheck, module-size ratchet, changelog-fragments green. 1,500 fuzz commands, 0 crashes on both bashes. ```gstack-receipt-runs {"head":"e74219a82144c18753450f36c6fc697d207cf76c","run":"ship-4521-e74219a","mark":"stop","tree":"549c381c3b257cf96c2c5e14128d4f95bd6f91a4"} {"head":"f7dd58d837dfca81122e7db83215521861060959","run":"ship-4521-f7dd58d","mark":"stop","tree":"3b2e64b797cc9adaa1fb6713f0b330794a1557c7"} ```

title: Codex now holds /review to its checklist before a session can end (GST-3173)
body:
On Codex, gstack's /review can no longer end a session with a required step skipped: the end-of-session check reads Codex's own session log and sends the agent back to finish, as it already does on Claude Code. Why: Codex users got routing and the destructive-command check in #4512, but not the /review checklist, so a review could stop after the diff read with no second-model pass. To use it: run `./setup` again and trust the new hook in Codex (`/hooks`); turn it off with `GSTACK_SKILL_CONTRACTS=off`.
What changed - **Reads Codex session logs.** New `lib/codex-rollout.ts` turns a Codex rollout file into the same events the checklist checker uses for Claude Code transcripts: skill loads (from the skill input or a shell read of `skills/gstack-*/SKILL.md`), shell commands, and subagent starts. A subagent start counts only when Codex reports an agent id, so a failed spawn is not a second-model pass. - **Same checklist, one item fewer.** On Codex the checklist comes from gstack's own `review/SKILL.md`. The "selected specialists dispatched" item is skipped there, because Codex has no specialist dispatch. The block message uses Codex wording in a Codex-only branch; Claude Code's message is unchanged and pinned by a test. - **Stop hook on Codex.** `hosts/codex/hooks/codex-skill-contract-stop-hook` wraps the existing hook. `./setup` registers it in `~/.codex/hooks.json` with PR 1's registration code, at a 10-second timeout, inert until you trust it. A Codex subagent's own session is never checked. `gstack-skill-contract check` accepts a Codex rollout too. - **Docs.** `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` explains contracts on Codex; a changelog fragment is in `changelog.d/`.
Tests - New `test/skill-contract-codex.test.ts` (24 tests) over six trimmed real Codex 0.170 session logs, including negative controls (failed spawn, `ls` of a skill path, a subagent's log). - `test/codex-hooks-setup.test.ts` and `test/codex-hooks-real-codex.test.ts` now expect the Stop group. - Live run with real Codex 0.170 through the new hook: blocked on the missing second-model pass, then passed after the agent ran it.
Agent notes Plan: GST-3173 (parent GST-3162), approved plan items A1, B1, C1, D1, E2, F1. Rebased onto main 944b41e with the controller's grant. Decision trail: reports/GSTA-641-decisions.tsv in the controller drive. /ship receipt follows at the final head. **Open notes (ruled to ship as disclosed notes by the controller, 2026-11-19):** - A shell line where an earlier command fails before the `cat` still counts as a skill read, so the hook can block once. - Shell lines are split on `;` without respecting quotes, so `sed -n '1,200p;201q' …/SKILL.md` is not seen as a read and the review goes unchecked (fails open). - A user turn holding only an image does not end the run, so a re-read in that turn is credited to the earlier review. - `cat A/SKILL.md || cat B/SKILL.md` with the first read failing loads nothing. - The SKILL.md path match in read-error lines has no end anchor, so an `ls …/SKILL.md.bak` error drops a good read. - PowerShell's "Cannot find path" is not recognised as a read error (Windows only). - Pasted `` markup at the start of a user message counts as an injected load. - A Codex agent is never treated as still running, so a stop during the adversarial pass blocks instead of deferring. - Exit codes are parsed only from exec_command output. - Windows setup copies `hosts/codex/hooks` but not `hosts/claude/hooks`, so Codex hooks fail open there (shared with the two hooks already on main). ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-f015602d9cee). title: Codex skill suggestions name each skill the way Codex lists it (GST-3195)
body:
On Codex, gstack's routing hint now names each skill by the `name:` in its installed SKILL.md (`review`), the name Codex lists, so `$review` loads the suggested skill. Before, the hint said `gstack-review` (the folder name), which Codex doesn't list, so mentioning it loaded nothing. Nothing to do: the next `./setup --host codex` picks it up. Claude Code's hint is unchanged.
What changed - `scanCodexSkills` keeps the front-matter name that `scanInstalledSkills` already read, and falls back to the folder name only when that name is missing or not a valid skill name. The matcher and Claude Code's wording are untouched. - Tests: a fixture whose folder (`gstack-review`) and `name:` (`review`) differ, a prefixed name (`gstack-review`), and missing or unusable names. A new real-Codex test runs Codex 0.170 against a local stub model (no API key): the name in the hint is the one Codex lists, `$` loads the skill body, and `$gstack-review` does not. - Docs: docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md#codex.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:375` codexHintLine's doc comment still gives gstack-review as the Codex name; the name is now the SKILL.md name (review). - Open, non-blocking (second-model read of the decision trail, GPT-6.2 Sol): when a user's own Codex skill is also named `review`, Codex 0.170 reportedly skips a bare `$review` mention, so neither skill loads. This is no worse than before (944b41e2). - Open, non-blocking: a `gstack-` folder whose `name:` was renamed to something outside ROUTED_SKILLS no longer routes. - Open, non-blocking: the real-Codex `$gstack-review` negative control would also pass if Codex sent zero requests. - Open and out of scope. Nine skill templates' `codex_default_prompt` still say `$gstack-` (Codex render work). - Skipped: lib/skill-route.ts:225, a user's own Codex skill with the same name as a gstack skill makes the hint ambiguous. The suggested fix (keep the folder name on a clash) brings back the bug this PR fixes, and Codex's own skill list already shows both names.
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match this change, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** base 944b41e to head 74f97db, one commit and six files (changelog fragment, docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md, the Codex routing hook, lib/skill-route.ts and two test files), with no staged, unstaged or new files. I searched every authored doc and template for the old Codex routing-hint wording and found no stale copies. **Documentation health:** - docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md: current. The Codex section says the hint uses each skill's SKILL.md `name:` (`review`, mentioned as `$review`) and falls back to the folder name. - changelog.d/codex-routing-hint-uses-codex-skill-names.md: current, and not modified. - README.md: reviewed and not modified. Its Codex host row still says 'ask for `gstack-office-hours`'; that is a possible follow-up. **Coverage debt:** the new Codex naming rule has reference and explanation coverage in skill-routing-and-contracts.md, but no how-to coverage. Nine skill templates still put `$gstack-` in `codex_default_prompt`, while installed Codex copies are named without the prefix; a separate change should check and fix that, then regenerate. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Codex picker prompts and docs name skills the way Codex lists them (GST-3196)
body:
On Codex, the suggested prompts for nine gstack skills and the README now say `$office-hours`, `$review` and so on, which load the skill; `$gstack-office-hours` loaded nothing. Why: Codex lists each skill by the `name:` in its SKILL.md, not the `gstack-` folder, and skill_prefix never changes that name on Codex. Nothing to do: the next `./setup --host codex` picks it up.
What changed - `codex_default_prompt` in autoplan, land-and-deploy, modernize, office-hours, qa, review, runaway-stopper, ship and write-skill: `$gstack-` becomes `$`. Only the Codex `agents/openai.yaml` reads this key, so every tracked Claude SKILL.md is byte-identical. - README's Codex row: first invocation is `$office-hours`. - docs/skills.md and docs/hosts.md: the Claude second-opinion skill on Codex is `$claude-code`. - docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md: `codex exec '$review ...'` injects the skill; only a folder-name mention is plain text (the example #4522 added). - New test in test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts scans every file in the Codex render plus README.md and the five Codex-facing docs (hosts, skills, skill-routing-and-contracts, troubleshooting) for `$gstack-` mentions that are not a listed skill name, and checks the README Codex row. It fails at be83949 (nine openai.yaml files, and the README row on its own).
How it was checked - Keyless probe, codex-cli 0.170.0 against a local stub model with this branch's rendered skills: `Use $office-hours ...` injects one skill block (`office-hours`, the rendered SKILL.md); `Use $gstack-office-hours ...` injects none. - `./setup --host codex --prefix` into a throwaway HOME: skill_prefix=true, and Codex's office-hours SKILL.md still says `name: office-hours`. - parity-suite, catalog and context budgets, module-size ratchet, spawnSync tripwire, gen-skill-docs freshness and size: green; no size pin moved.

title: Destructive-command check closes the parsing gaps found after #4513 and blocks wipefs -a in every spelling (GST-3190)
body:
The destructive-command check now blocks force-pushes to main written with `--repo=`, after a `cd`, or with `--all`, and asks again for the other shapes that slipped past it after #4513. `wipefs -a` is blocked in every spelling, including targets fed by `xargs`; only existing image files it names outside `/dev` are exempt. Dry runs and greps for SQL text stop over-blocking. Nothing to do: the check runs in every session already.
What changed, by shape Steps back from main, fixed first: - `git push --repo=origin +refs/heads/main` and `git push --repo=origin --force main` are denied. With `--repo`, every operand is read as a possible refspec (git itself reads the first one as the repository, so this is the cautious reading). - A `cd` inside a pipeline (`cd /tmp | true && rm -rf dir`) no longer counts as moving into scratch: bash runs each pipeline part in a subshell. A subshell now gives back the exact outer state, so `cd /tmp && (pwd) && rm -rf dir` no longer asks. - `git reset --hard "$REV"` asks again. - `printf x >> f && git reset --hard` on a clean tree stays allowed: the only work it can lose is what the same command wrote. `git stash pop` earlier in the same command does make a later discard ask, because pop drops the stash, the same loss `stash drop` always asks about. Gaps in the catches #4513 added: - `git clean -q` / `--quiet` no longer hides the dry-run listing. - `--work-tree`, `--git-dir`, `GIT_DIR=` and `GIT_WORK_TREE=` forms of `checkout -f`, `switch -f` and `clean -f` ask. - `find -L -delete` (leading find options) is read correctly. - `rm dir -rf` with flags at the end asks when `rm` is the command; `docker rm web -f` and `aws s3 rm` stay those tools' subcommands. - A `mktemp` variable assigned again in the same command is no longer scratch. - `..` beats the `/proc` and `/dev` exemptions, a `cd` through `..` is never scratch, and `rm -rf ../build` no longer rides the build-output allow. - A cloud delete's dry run counts only from the delete itself to the end of its statement, so a dry run on the line before never excuses it, and `plan` counts only as a whole word. - A `cd` after `if`, `while`, `until` or `time` still counts, so `if cd B; then git clean -fdx; fi` asks. - `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND=interactive` outranks `CI=1` in the every-session guard hook (`claude -p` stays headless). wipefs: - `wipefs` is back in the whole-command disk-wipe deny for `-a`, any short-option group holding `a` (`-fa`), and the abbreviations `--a` and `--al` that getopt accepts for `--all`. That deny sees targets the word scan cannot: `ls /dev/sd* | xargs wipefs -a` and `echo /dev/sdb | xargs wipefs --all` are denied again. - The one exemption sits on top of that deny: every statement in the command must be a `wipefs` that leads its statement (after `sudo` or `NAME=value`), and every target, with options read the way getopt reads them, must be a plain literal path outside `/dev` with a disk-image suffix (`.img`, `.iso`, `.raw`, `.qcow2`, `.vhd`, `.vhdx`, `.vmdk`, `.dmg`) that already exists as a regular file, not a symlink, in a folder the check knows. A redirect into `/dev` other than `/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout` or `/dev/stderr` breaks the exemption. A short group stops at `t`, `o` or `O`, whose value is the rest of the word, or the next word when nothing follows, so `wipefs -a -tvfat /dev/sdb` no longer hides its device. `wipefs -a demo.img`, `wipefs -t ext4 -a demo.img` and `wipefs --all disk.qcow2 build/b.iso` are allowed. - Still denied, on purpose: `ls *.img | xargs wipefs -a` (targets not spelled out), `ln -sf /dev/sdb d.img; wipefs -a d.img` and a symlinked `alias.img`, `wipefs -a demo.img > /dev/mmcblk0`, `wipefs -a demo.img; wi''pefs -a /dev/sdb`, an image created earlier in the same command, a `wipefs` beside any other statement or inside `bash -c '…'`, `wipefs -tvfat /dev/sdb` without `-a` (the deny reads the `a` in `vfat`), and quoted image names with spaces. Other over-catches removed: - `git push -nf` is a dry run (letters after `o` in a short-option group are a push-option value, not flags). - The bare SQL shape (`TRUNCATE x;`) is ignored inside grep, rg, ag, ack and `git grep`, and in `echo`/`printf` text when nothing after it pipes or redirects (`||` is not a pipe); `./psql/` in a path is a folder, not a client. Force-pushes that only asked: - `cd . && git push -f origin` on main is denied: git now reads the folder a `cd` chain leads to for the force-push lookups (discard checks still ask after any `cd`). - `git push --force --all`, `--branches` and `--mirror` are denied when main, master or the default branch exists locally. Speed: the statement loop no longer indexes a bash array, which is linear per read on bash 3.2, so a 200 KB command takes about a third of the time on bash 3.2. Everyday commands against 55aaa6c on the same machine (interleaved, the 102 GEVA-560 commands in turn, n=400 each): bash 5.2 p50 99.6 ms vs 95.1 ms, bash 3.2.57 p50 94.3 ms vs 90.6 ms; p90 is lower on the branch in both. Process start dominates, and the base p50 itself moved by 20 ms between passes on this machine, so the 4 ms gap is within run-to-run drift.
Tests `test/careful-replay.test.ts` gains 63 rows (`PARSER_CASES`), one or more per shape above. The 8 wipefs rows (xargs, stdin, `--a`, `--al`, an attached `-t` value alone and in a group, `--al` on `/dev/sdb.img`, image names from `xargs`) each fail at f7dd58d and are denied at 944b41e. 4 more (a symlinked image, a symlink made in the same command, a redirect into `/dev/mmcblk0`, a quoted spelling) fail at 05b36ee; three are controls. The test trees now hold real `demo.img`, `disk.qcow2` and `build/b.iso` files and an `alias.img` symlink. `test/destructive-guard-hook.test.ts` gains the `CI=1` case. Replay plus hook tests: 270 pass, 0 fail on bash 5.2.21 and on bash 3.2.57. Not in this PR (outside its scope, none a step back from main): a quoted scratch path with a space, denying a literal home path, a failure while reading input before the safety trap, a backtick revision in `reset --hard`, and the extra `/tmp` asks GEVA-560 measured (a relative `rm -rf` after a second `cd`, a subshell, a loop or an unresolved `$VAR`). Open notes from #4521's review, left for a follow-up: - The SQL-text exemption still allows `grep 'truncate users;' a.sql | sh`, the same through `<( )` process substitution and `git grep -O`, and `echo "$(dbtool exec 'TRUNCATE TABLE users')"`. - `LC_ALL=C cd /tmp && rm -rf dir` asks, and printed SQL text followed by a pipe in a later statement asks. - Quoted parentheses can restore an earlier `cd` into scratch, and `echo cd /tmp` still counts as a `cd`. - `grep 'a; truncate demo;'` (a quoted `;`) still asks, and `sudo -u root rm dir -rf` is still allowed, as on main. Open notes from this PR's second-model review, ruled not to block because each needs quote tricks or contradictory flags and main already allows an equivalent shape: - `wipefs -a demo.img >'/dev'/sdb`: a quoted `/dev` redirect target isn't seen as `/dev` (main already allows `echo hi >'/dev'/sdb`). - `wipefs -a demo.img" #" /dev/sda`: a quoted `#` is read as a comment, so the later target is never seen (it only reaches the disk if a file named `demo.img #` exists). - `git push -fn --no-dry-run origin main`: `--no-dry-run` after an `n` in a short group isn't read as undoing the dry run (main already allows `git push --force -n --no-dry-run origin main`). - `git push --mirror` in a checkout without a local default branch still only asks, as on main. - `git grep -h 'TRUNCATE TABLE' | dbwrap prod`: search output piped to an unlisted client, the same class as the SQL-text note above. - A folder that is already a symlink into `/dev` can get a redirect past the image exemption (`wipefs -a demo.img > d/sdb` with `d -> /dev`): the `/dev` checks read the path as text. Main already allows `echo hi > d/sdb` through the same folder. - Over-catch: `_RX_WIPEFS` also matches a longer word, so `echo wipefs-archive` now denies.

title: Codex /review with gpt-6.1-sol counts the second-model pass it already ran (GEVA-562)
body:
On Codex with gpt-6.1-sol, /review is no longer blocked at session end for a missing second-model pass that it ran.
Why: with Sol, Codex starts subagents through its `collaboration` tools and names a started agent by `task_name`, not `agent_id`, so the checklist reader missed it; this blocks gstack-evals' Codex pin.
Nothing to do: the fix ships with the next gstack release.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `lib/codex-rollout.ts` counts a started call to Codex's own `spawn_agent`: an `agent_id` result from the `multi_agent_v1` namespace, or a `task_name` result from the `collaboration` namespace (`multi_agents_v2`). A call with no namespace may hold either. A failed spawn still doesn't count, and a same-named tool from any other namespace never counts.
- New fixture `test/fixtures/skill-contract/codex/exec-sol-spawn-met.jsonl`: a keyless Codex 0.170 run with `-m gpt-6.1-sol` against a local stub endpoint, trimmed like the other fixtures.
- Docs: the dispatch rule in `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, and a changelog fragment.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/skill-contract-codex.test.ts`: the Sol run's adversarial pass is met at the first stop (fails at b0f865c0); a collaboration spawn whose result has no `task_name` (empty, error text, nickname only) is not a dispatch, and neither is a `spawn_agent` from another namespace.
- Full free suite: CI run 44530390627 attempt 2 at the reviewed head e0060272 (1709 files, green), and CI run 44535570812 at the merged head 2c3ee550, green.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The end-of-session contract check reads the Codex rollout to see whether /review ran its adversarial pass. Its fixtures came from gpt-5.4-mini, where a started agent answers with `agent_id`. Sol answers with `task_name`, so a session that did the work was held once for a pass it had already run.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the Codex rollout reader behind the skill contract check changes. Claude Code sessions and other hosts are untouched. A Codex release that renames the namespace would make the check hold a session once, which is the same failure this fixes, not data loss.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The docs already match the change, so nothing was edited.

**Scope:** the diff from base b0f865c00c50 to head e0060272 on codex-sol-spawn-dispatch, which counts a Codex `spawn_agent` call in the `collaboration` namespace as started when its result names a `task_name`. The diff touches lib/codex-rollout.ts, a new Sol fixture and its test, the codex fixture README, docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md and a changelog.d fragment. There were no staged, unstaged or untracked changes.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md: Current. Its dispatch definition already covers `agent_id` and `task_name`, failed spawns and tools of the same name from other namespaces.
- test/fixtures/skill-contract/codex/README.md: Current. The new fixture's row describes how it was captured and what it shows.
- changelog.d/codex-sol-spawn-dispatch.md: Current (read only).
- docs/hosts.md: Current. Its Codex subagents paragraph doesn't depend on the result shape.
- CHANGELOG.md: Current. It has no stale claim.

**Coverage debt:** none. **Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

title: Pre-commit /verify fails on a timeout, and the review collector stops reading reviewers' scope lists as findings (GST-3201)
body:
Pre-commit /verify now fails a check that times out and runs its checks on one time budget; a reviewer's scope-list bullets no longer need an owner ruling to clear; stack tests fail when git can't list a PR's tests.
Why: each let a result read clean with nothing proving it, or block on nothing (#4518, #4519). Goal: gates never pass on missing evidence.
Nothing to do; `gstack-checks quick --timeout` is now one budget the checks share (540 s default).

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A pre-commit check that ran out of time was listed as "not run", so the commit still got `VERIFY PASS` with nothing proving it. A reviewer that declared no blockers still had its own list of what the tests cover collected as HIGH or P0 blockers (#4518, #4519), so the run waited on an owner ruling for nothing. A merge-queue slot whose test list git could not read passed as if it added no tests.

</details>

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Pre-commit /verify (`gstack-checks quick`).** A check that times out is now a red: `VERIFY FAIL: <check> TIMEOUT`, exit 1. Before, it was listed as "not run" and the commit still got `VERIFY PASS`. The checks share one deadline, so each gets the time that is left, and a check that cannot start before it is a TIMEOUT. Before, each check got its own 600 seconds. The test stage starts with the time left, but its runner can still run past it, so a very slow test run can still outlast a 10-minute Bash call; carrying the deadline into lib/pregate is a follow-up. `gstack-checks run` is unchanged.
- **Review collector (`lib/review-ledger.ts`).** When a reviewer's own `REVIEW_VERDICT` line declares `blocking=0`, a single-line bullet with no file:line, no Severity or Blocks field, no lead label and no severity except ones naming findings as a kind ("a HIGH finding still refused", "can't occur alongside P0 or P1 findings") keeps its label and becomes a summary candidate, which the /ship lead may lower in judgment with a reason instead of needing an owner ruling. It still blocks until judged, so a bullet like "Two P0 findings remain unfixed" is never lost. Everything else parses exactly as before.
- **Stack tests (`crew/lib/ship-queue-stack-tests.ts`).** A git failure listing a PR's added test files fails the slot with git's error, instead of reading as "no new test files".
- **spawnSync import ratchet (`test/spawn-sync.test.ts`).** The scanner now sees `import cp, { spawnSync }` and a default import beside a named or namespace one. No file in the repo uses those forms today, so the baseline is unchanged.
- **Docs.** docs/skills.md, docs/review-policy.md, docs/ship-policy.md and docs/troubleshooting.md describe the three changes, and the changelog fragment matches them.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The collector change only adds a summary-candidate mark to rows that already collected; a marked row still blocks until the lead lowers it with a reason, so no row that blocked before can pass silently (read at `lib/review-ledger.ts:356-358` and covered by the negative controls in `test/review-ledger-scope-bullets.test.ts`). `gstack-checks run` and `status` pass no deadline, so only the pre-commit quick pass changes (lib/checks.ts:308-311, fixture test in test/gstack-checks.test.ts).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Step 7 audit: 9 of 11 changed paths have a two-star or better test (82%). Gaps, proposed and not written: no test reads quick's 540-second default, and no merge-queue batch test reaches the new `QUEUE_TRAIN_STACK_RED` wording for a slot whose files git could not list.
Tests: 1831 → 1831 (+0 new in this run; the branch's own new tests are listed under Tests)
Tests ran: targeted 26

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Full review of 21cd505 (specialists, red team, native adversarial, a second-model review on GPT-6.2 Sol, targeted reader): two findings. The collector's first version relabelled a bullet that asserts an open blocker, and the quick-pass wording promised more than the test runner keeps. Both were fixed in one granted fix round (04dbf60, docs in 2c67625); the follow-up check of that fix and the targeted reader on 2c67625 found nothing. Second-model review: completed, two findings, both fixed. Noted, not fixed: the `QUEUE_TRAIN_STACK_RED` fix hint still suggests fixing or reordering tests when the real cause is a git listing failure (crew/lib/ship-queue-train.ts:579, Low).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Scope:** 3 commits from 45e6d549e to 2c6762501, 14 files: the /verify quick-pass timeout budget, the review collector's scope-list rule and the stack-test listing failure (GST-3201). No staged, unstaged or new files.

title: gstack's Codex hooks keep working with unusual folder paths and after uninstall (GST-3197)
body:
gstack's Codex hooks no longer block every prompt when your Codex folder's path has a `(` or `&`, and uninstall keeps your own Codex hooks trusted.
Why: both broke Codex sessions; setup also now matches Codex's hook rules, and the /review checklist on Codex reads shell commands more carefully.
Nothing to do: plain paths keep the exact hook command they had, so Codex asks for no new trust.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Path quoting** (`bin/gstack-settings-hook`): a hook command whose path holds any character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]` (or non-ASCII) is quoted for Claude Code and Codex. Before, `(` or `&` made a shell syntax error, which Codex reads as "block".
- **Uninstall keeps your hooks' trust positions**: removing gstack's group (uninstall, prune-stale, turning a hook off) leaves `{"hooks": []}` where gstack's group sat, so groups after it keep the index Codex trusts them by. When your handler is inside gstack's group, gstack leaves the file alone and names the one handler to delete. `gstack-uninstall` prints a warning when gstack's Codex hooks are still in place.
- **Setup matches Codex's own rules**: `description: null` is accepted, MCP hook input carrying a null is refused, `rollback` won't restore a backup Codex would skip, a gstack hook already declared in `config.toml` under any matcher that covers Bash is caught (Rust's leading `(?i)`/`(?m)`/`(?s)`, `\A` and `\z` are translated; anything JS still can't compile is refused), and trust status keys on the same path Codex uses when `CODEX_HOME` is a symlink.
- **Windows**: setup also copies `hosts/claude/hooks` into Codex's gstack folder, because the three Codex shims import it. Native Windows Codex starts hooks through `cmd.exe`, which can't run these Bash scripts, so this alone doesn't make them run there (see Known limits).
- **/review checklist on Codex** (`lib/codex-rollout.ts`): quote-aware command splitting; every read-error line still drops the read unless it provably names another file (another read's path, longer path winning, or a path that is no SKILL.md); PowerShell's "Cannot find path" counts as a failed read, a last command that reads one file and exits non-zero isn't a load, a `||` fallback isn't a load, and an image-only user message starts a new turn.
- Docs: the Codex paragraph in `docs/uninstall.md` (delete a trailing group only when it holds nothing but gstack's handlers); a changelog fragment.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- New and rewritten tests in `test/codex-hooks.test.ts`, `test/codex-hooks-setup.test.ts` (Windows copy, uninstall slot and warning), `test/skill-contract-codex.test.ts` and `test/codex-hooks-real-codex.test.ts` (real codex-cli 0.170 `hooks/list` shows your group keeps its trusted key after gstack's is removed, and the hooks run from a `hooks(2)` path).
- Each new or changed test fails against main's `bin/`, `setup` and `lib/codex-rollout.ts`, and passes here; typecheck clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Known limits</summary>

- A read in the middle of an `&&` chain (`cd /nope && cat X && echo`) still counts as a load, and so does a quoted `echo` that contains `cat …SKILL.md`.
- Other hook options (`timeout`, `statusMessage`) stay stricter than Codex's own parser, except that `rollback` accepts a backup with `"timeout": 1.0`, which Codex rejects; such a backup is the user's own earlier file.
- Native Windows Codex runs hook commands through `cmd.exe`, so gstack's Bash hooks don't start there.
- A read inside a pipeline under `pipefail` is judged by the call's exit status.
- A successful SKILL.md read is dropped when the skill's own text has a read-error phrase with no slash in it (such as "can't read"); no skill with a contract has such a line today.
- Named risk (accepted in review): a Rust-only matcher class in `config.toml` (`\pL` without the u flag, `[[:alpha:]]`) reads as no clash, so a gstack hook also declared there under such a matcher would run twice.
- Rewriting `hooks.json` round-trips it through JSON, so an integer above 2^53 in a hook's input would change; this already held for every write before this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** updated. One stale Codex hooks paragraph corrected; no blockers.

**Scope:** base 18e24a2..1c91b66 on `codex-hooks-hardening` (10 committed files, nothing staged, unstaged or new). I audited docs that mention Codex `hooks.json` or `hosts/codex/hooks`: `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, `docs/uninstall.md`, `docs/hosts.md` and `changelog.d/codex-hooks-hardening.md`.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`: Updated. Uninstall and `--no-team` now leave an empty group so your own hooks keep their Codex trust positions; gstack refuses only when your handler sits inside gstack's group. Added that native Windows Codex can't run the hooks yet.
- `docs/uninstall.md`: Current (updated on the branch).
- `docs/hosts.md`: Current.
- `changelog.d/codex-hooks-hardening.md`: Current (reviewed only).

**Coverage debt:** none. The changed hook behavior is covered by the reference docs and the uninstall how-to. Path quoting is described in the changelog only; it's internal hardening with no user setting.

**Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

title: READY prints real trial merges and the second-model trail read, plus six small ship-tool fixes (GST-3200)
body:
READY now prints each open PR's trial-merge result and the reader of the second-model trail read, or a loud MISSING line, instead of lines left to fill in. Why: agents dropped those lines as noise and skipped the trail read on three gate-class PRs. Six more small ship-tool bugs from 2026-11-19 reports are fixed here too. Nothing to do: pass `--trail ` to `gstack-ship-queue ready` on risk-class PRs.
What changed - **READY tail.** `gstack-ship-queue ready` lists the open PRs into the base that change a file this PR changes. It prints one `TRIAL_MERGES:` line for each, built from `git merge-tree` at both heads: clean with its tree, or the conflicting files. With `--trail`, the Attention line of a PR whose review is gate or risk class names the reader from the trail's newest `trail-read` row. Without one it prints `MISSING: cross-family trail read`. gh or fetch failures print MISSING too. - **Plan line.** `Plan: exempt:` accepts bug-fix wording ("bug fix with failing-first tests", "bugfix", "bug-fix: ..."). `/ship` finish `--plan` now records the line it resolved, and ready uses that record when the PR body has no Plan line. The READY note marks it `from: finish`, so land accepts it. - **Round grants.** `gstack-approvals round-grant` and its reader refuse only gstack's own names ("gstack", "gstack no-stop default (K1)"), matched whole. "gstack-evals Captain" can now record a grant. - **Hand-off destination.** Both HOST_PUBLISH paths pass `GH_REPO` to `gh repo view`, which doesn't read it on its own. A fork `pr-create` hand-off names its head as `owner:branch`, and it refuses when the fork is on another host. - **Targeted patch id.** `targetedPatchId()` hashes the diff with `core.quotePath=false`, like the check that compares against it. A read on a non-ASCII path now carries across a docs-only change. - **Relayed rulings.** While a /ship run is open, `gstack-approvals rule` takes `--owner-ref :` with the owner's `--by` and `--words`. The approval row, the /ship record in the PR body and the Ruled note line are marked as relayed from that message. Without the flag, the refusal now has its own code, `APPROVAL_RULING_RUN_OPEN`, with accurate text. - **Red-team redaction.** `rule --not-security` is the owner's call that a red-team finding isn't a security finding. Its line then shows `: (red-team, ruled not security class)` and the reason. Security, auth and secret findings can't take it, and every other red-team line stays redacted.
Tests Each item has a test that fails at main 45e6d549 and passes on this branch: pr-round-cli, review-round-grant, review-plan-targeted-delta, plan-record, the READY tail unit test, gstack-ship-queue, capy-host-publish (one test drives real gh against a fake API on a unix socket), security-finding-redaction, ship-finish-ruled-notes. Typecheck, typecheck:test, generated-file freshness, troubleshooting anchors, module-size ratchet, spawnSync tripwire, bun entry isolation, free-shard curation and the credential scan pass locally.
Known limits The second-model review of the final head raised five issues. The maintainer chose to ship them as open notes: 1. `bin/gstack-approvals:213`: self-attested --owner-ref relay by design: the source is checkable, nothing verifies it automatically. 2. `lib/plan-record.ts:249`: finish's fallback copies raw --plan text into the public notes ref; an approved: line naming a local path would publish it. 3. `lib/gstack-post.ts:834`: the MEDIUM confirm token binds origin, not the GH_REPO destination. 4. `lib/gstack-post.ts:859`: the PR-URL check compares owner/repo, not the host. 5. `lib/ship-queue.ts:386`: TRIAL_MERGES misses a rename's old path and treats the 200-PR list as complete (advisory line). Another small gstack bug seen while shipping this PR, not changed here: `gstack-ship-queue ready` prints its own template line `` under Attention instead of the flags.

title: Free-suite CI survives a slow Ubuntu mirror, and four flaky tests and eval checks stop failing (GST-3206)
body:
Free-suite CI stops failing before any test runs when archive.ubuntu.com is slow, and four tests that failed and then passed in the last day are fixed at their cause. Why: 27 setup failures and 5 flaky reds on 2026-11-19 cost reruns and blocked READY checks across PRs and main. Nothing to do: the first run on each runner image fills the new package cache.
What changed - **CI package cache** (`.github/workflows/free-tests.yml`, free-suite and quick-bun-default). Playwright's `--with-deps` downloads about 38 MB of system packages every run. On 2026-11-19 the mirror served some runners at 85 to 280 kB/s: 17 of 456 first install attempts hit the 5-minute limit, and the retry then died in about 6 s on the dpkg lock that the killed attempt's apt-get still held (run 44485949701, job 135438838194). 5 more jobs failed in the Xvfb/gate-tools apt step on fetch errors. Now apt waits up to 240 s for its lock and keeps what it downloads; those .deb files are cached under a key built from a hash of the runner's installed package list and the Playwright version. A later run with the same key installs them with `dpkg -i`, runs `playwright install chromium` without `--with-deps`, and the Xvfb step finds everything installed. A failed offline install falls back to today's path. Step timeouts and the single retry are unchanged. - **first-use** (`lib/first-use.ts`). Several user drives were listed in `readdirSync` order in the refusal text; now sorted. Failed on main and on #4497 and #4517. - **gstack-lease test** (`test/gstack-lease.test.ts`). The test read the lock's owner file as soon as it existed, but `gstack_lock_take` creates it with O_EXCL and writes the line after, so it could read "" (main run 44512215095). The test now waits for a complete line, and its shell hook holds the write open for 0.3 s so the window is hit every run. - **Read-only command grammar** (`test/helpers/read-only-commands.ts`). A backslash-quote inside double quotes is a literal quote in bash and zsh; the tokenizer refused it and failed ship-docsync-failure on census 44321344888. Only that escape is admitted; `\$`, backtick and `\\` stay refused. - **Coverage audit** (`test/helpers/coverage-audit-evidence.ts`). Claude Code keeps a Bash call's final cwd. The checker now tracks a proved session cwd, so `cd /review; ls ...` then `cd .. && cat -n src/billing.ts && ...` counts (review-coverage-audit, census 44351657692). The cwd becomes unknown after a failed call, any unrecognized command shape, a subagent's Bash call or overlapping Bash calls; the absolute-cwd rule is unchanged.
How it was tested - New first-use test spies `readdirSync` into reverse order: fails on main with the CI symptom, passes with the sort. 23/23. - gstack-lease: the hardened test fails on the old wait with `Received: ""` (the CI symptom) and passes with the new wait; whole file 40/40. - Workflow wiring test updated for the new steps and extended with the cache contract; 25/25 with the sandbox test. actionlint 1.7.11 clean. - Paid checker repairs: free replays of the captured census events are red on main with the recorded symptom and green after; 6 new regressions fail without the helper changes, with 40 negative controls that stay red. 204 + 202 + 148 pass. No paid runs. - Typecheck clean; test typecheck ratchet: none new.
Agent notes Daily flaky-fix pass GSTA-654 (GST-3206). Ledger: handoffs/flaky-ledger.md in the GStack Minder drive. ship-docsync-current (census 44432023197) stays Open: the child omitted documentation_section under clear instructions and the fixture does not declare the repair-prompt / result --repair-of commands documentation.md asks for, so the parent stopped as blocked; that repair needs a paid proof. Plan: exempt: flaky **Review** (one pass on fa1bc25, tree 7681981, no fix round): plan class=gate, 5 readers (specialist batch, red team, adversarial, second-model review on gpt-6.1-sol, targeted gate reader). Pre-Landing Review: 2 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 2 asked (0 fixed, 2 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted. Gate edits: 23 listed, 11 read, 0 findings — 0 kept, 0 restored, 0 open (the two RH-14 hunks are the new continue-on-error offline install steps; the next step reads their outcome). **Open notes (none blocks):** 1. A partly failed offline `dpkg -i` can leave packages unconfigured, so the `--with-deps` fallback's apt-get may refuse (specialist, adversarial). 2. A cache entry whose debs fail to install is never re-saved, so that image silently takes the network path (red team). 3. The offline step has no `timeout-minutes` and no `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` (adversarial). 4. The 240 s apt lock wait uses most of the retry's 5 minutes (adversarial). 5. Resolved: "27 jobs failed" was recounted from raw job data (22 in the Playwright retry step, 5 in the Xvfb step, across 5 runs); "17 of 456" is first-attempt timeouts in a 40-run sample. Both stand. **Exploratory QA:** pass (cache_key output in both jobs; `--with-deps` fallback for every apt_offline outcome other than success). **Tests:** targeted lane 646 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail; full free suite carried from CI run 44549845101 at tree 7d7baac2115c. **Documentation:** Scope: the diff from 17303862 to 558673eb, which changes the free-tests workflow (apt/dpkg caching for Playwright packages), a sorted drive listing in lib/first-use.ts, and several test helpers and fixtures. Result: current. The changelog fragment already covers every user-visible effect, and no README, guide or reference doc describes the changed behavior. Debt: I grepped Markdown for free-tests.yml and listed nine referencing files, but read only the changelog fragment in full. I did not read CONTRIBUTING.md or docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md in full, so a stale description of the workflow's apt steps there is unchecked. title: Destructive-command check stops asking about harmless /tmp work and written deploy hooks (GST-3207)
body:
The destructive-command check no longer asks about relative deletes in `/tmp` work folders after a second `cd`, a subshell or a loop, or about deploy hooks a command only writes to a file.
It blocks `wipefs -a` on every target and catches disk redirects written with quotes or through a link to `/dev`, so nothing a user runs gets less protection.
Nothing to do: the check runs in every session already.

<details><summary>What changed, by shape</summary>

Over-asks removed, each as a proven exemption on top of the existing ask:
- A relative `cd` from `/tmp` scratch keeps scratch when the command makes no links (`ln`) and no part of the path below scratch is a symlink on disk (`cd /tmp/w && cd sub && rm -rf out`).
- A statement after `;` inside a subshell, `$( )`, backticks or a `for`/`while`/`until`/`if`/`select`/`{ }` body starts from the state the group was entered with, while no `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` ran inside it (`cd /tmp/w && (make; rm -rf out)`).
- A `for` loop variable over plain literal words is a scratch target inside its own `do ... done` body: `/tmp` words anywhere, relative words after a `cd` into scratch. A use before or after the loop, a nested loop, a single quote, backslash or backtick in the body, any other assignment, `read`, `local`, `eval` and the like, a glob, `~`, `..` or a path after the variable keeps the ask.
- `cd "$W"` reads `W` when `W=...` is the command's first statement and no single quote or backslash follows it, so `W=/tmp/w && cd "$W" && rm -rf out` is scratch. A relative `cd` with `CDPATH` set or named is never scratch.
- A quoted target with a space (`rm -rf "/tmp/scratch demo"`) is one word when its closing quote ends a word; `rm "a b"c -r ~/x` is read word by word as before. The root deny still reads each piece.
- A heredoc written with `cat > F <<'EOF'` or `tee F <<'EOF'` is data: discards inside it don't ask. An unquoted end word counts only when the body has no `$` or backtick, since bash runs those while writing. Deletes and force-pushes inside it still count, and the whole body is read as commands again when the command runs `F` (as a command, through a quoted path, or after `bash`, `sh`, `source`, `.`, `exec`, `eval` or `xargs`, `sh < F` included), pipes anything into a shell, pipes the heredoc on, or, for a file under `hooks/`, runs `git push`.
- SQL `TRUNCATE` text printed by `echo` no longer asks because a later, separate statement has a pipe, a quoted `;` inside a grep pattern no longer splits it, and text sent to `/dev/null` is text. A copy to another descriptor (`>&3`, `1>&2`) still asks.

Gaps closed:
- `wipefs -a` is denied on every target. The image-file exemption is gone: GEVA-560's 254,322 commands hold no `wipefs -a` at all (its 13 denies are force-pushes and deletes), so it never fired and every fact it had to prove was a way past the deny.
- A redirect into a disk is denied with its quotes removed (`>'/dev'/sdb`, `> "/dev/mmcblk0"`) and through a folder whose real path is `/dev` (`> d/sdb` with `d -> /dev`); `mmcblk` and `rdisk` join the redirect names.
- A `#` inside quotes is no longer read as a comment, so `rm -rf "a #" ~` is denied.
- `git push -fn --no-dry-run` is a real force-push (the last flag wins).
- `\wipefs`, `wipefs''` and doubled quotes are caught; `echo wipefs-archive` is not (the deny needs `wipefs` as a word of its own).
- SQL text asks again when a grep's output is piped to anything but a viewer (`| sh`), goes through `$( )`, backticks, `<( )` or `>( )`, or comes from `git grep -O` / `--open-files-in-pager`. Statements are cut where bash cuts them, outside quotes.

Kept on purpose:
- `printf x >> f && git reset --hard` on a clean tree stays allowed (G7). The hook runs before the command, so the only work that can be lost is what the same command writes; asking on every compound command that ends in a discard would bring back the false asks the clean-tree probe removed.
- `LC_ALL=C cd /tmp && rm -rf dir` was already allowed at 17303862; a row pins it.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests and measurements</summary>

`test/careful-replay.test.ts` gains 95 `FOLLOWUP_CASES` rows, a `REVIEW_CASES` table from the review rounds, and a symlink test with a real `/tmp` folder; five wipefs rows move from allow to deny. Run against 17303862's check, 39 of the first 67 new or changed rows fail and the rest are controls; 19 of the 23 rows added after a second-model read of the first commit ask or deny where that commit allowed, and 4 of the 5 added after a second read of the fix ask where the fix allowed. Replay plus hook tests: 390 pass, 0 fail on bash 5.2.21 and on bash 3.2.57. Adjacent checks (hook scripts, setup hook syntax, state-root ratchet, Codex hooks, module size, spawnSync tripwire, bun entry isolation): 349 pass. Typecheck and the test typecheck ratchet are clean. 1,600 random command mixes at the first commit and 1,600 at the final one: no crash or fallback ask on either bash.

Corpus replays (feeding commands to the hook, nothing run): GEVA-560's 2,831 commands that main flagged and 55aaa6c4 allowed give the same decision at this head except 5 harmless deploy-hook heredocs that now allow, on both bashes. Of GEVA-560's 538 changed rows (cut text), 25 harmless discard rows (9 commands) now allow and all 16 destructive rows that 17303862 asks about still ask. GEVA-560's 102 incident rows keep every expected decision.

Latency, same machine, interleaved with 17303862 over the 102 incident rows (n=408 each), two passes: bash 5.2 p50 149.5 vs 151.2 ms and 133.9 vs 130.4 ms; bash 3.2 p50 195.6 vs 195.2 ms and 137.4 vs 132.6 ms. At the final head: bash 5.2 128.2 vs 124.8 ms, bash 3.2 130.6 vs 126.8 ms. Base p50 moved by up to 63 ms between passes, so the gaps are within run-to-run drift.

</details>

<details><summary>Open notes</summary>

- **Open blocker, so this PR is parked:** a `<<` after an unquoted `#` (`cat > f # <<EOF`, `ls # ; cat > f <<EOF`) is read as a heredoc. Bash treats it as a comment and runs the lines that follow, so a `git reset --hard` there is allowed here but asked on main. The fix is to cut each line at its first unquoted `#` before looking for `<<`.
- Any discard after a `cd` still asks, as on main, `cd $VAR && git reset -q --hard` included: a profile function or alias between the two can move the folder, and the hook can't see the profile.
- `cd $VAR` and `rm -rf "$VAR"` with `VAR` from the environment still ask: trusting the hook's environment for the Bash tool's shell is a design call.
- A `cd` inside a group followed by `;` (`(cd sub; rm -rf out)`) still asks, even when both folders are scratch.
- Statements are still cut at a quoted `;` for deletes and git (`rm -rf "x;" ~` asks rather than denies), and `echo cd /tmp` still counts as a `cd`, as on main.
- `wipefs --no-act` still denies (the `a` in `act`).
- GEVA-2's 104 `delete_outside` asks were not changed: none could be proven harmless from the files this PR could read.
- A `/tmp` folder that is itself a symlink still counts as scratch, as on main: `cd /tmp/L && cd p && rm -rf s` removes the same path main already allows as `cd /tmp/L && rm -rf p/s`.
- `wi''pefs -a` and `w"ipe"fs -a` (quotes inside the word) are allowed here and on main.
- A heredoc written to a file and then run by another program (`make`, `find -exec`) is not detected; only shells, `source`, `exec`, `eval`, `xargs`, a pipe into a shell and running the file by name are.
- A loop operand given to another delete tool (`for f in a b; do find $f -delete; done`) allows exactly when its spelled-out form (`find a -delete; find b -delete`) allows on main.

</details>

title: Syncing a second repo no longer makes GBrain ask the first repo to sync again (GST-3212)
body:
Once you synced a second repo, every repo synced before it showed a false "run /sync-gbrain" prompt at session start. The read check now uses the per-repo sync record `/sync-gbrain` already keeps. Why: people who work across several repos saw this on every session. Nothing to do after upgrading.
What changed `bin/gstack-gbrain-read-capability.ts` used to accept only the machine-wide latest code stage, so a sibling repo's sync made this repo look unsynced. Now: - If the latest code stage is for this repo's pinned source, it decides, exactly as before (a failed or unverified stage still says unknown, even when an older record says synced). - Otherwise the check reads `code_sources[].path` from the sync state, which `gstack-gbrain-sync` writes only after a successful code sync whose path matched. - A latest failed code stage that names no source still says unknown. - The record path must resolve to this worktree, then the same live source, list and page reads run before anything says ready. A state with no `code_sources` (older format), a non-object map, a null record, or a record with a missing or non-string path behaves as before: unknown, ask for a sync.
Tests `test/gbrain-read-capability.test.ts` adds two repos synced in either order (the sibling-last order failed on main), plus 12 controls that must stay unknown with no brain calls: a repo that never synced, an older state with no records, a record pointing at another worktree, a record whose folder is gone, malformed records, a record beside this repo's latest failed or unverified sync, and a latest failure with no source. A skipped code stage keeps the earlier record.
Credit and scope Reported, with the first version of this fix, by @SatriaSuriaAriffin in #4499. Rewritten on current main; their commit is credited with a Co-authored-by trailer. The rest of #4499 is not included. No network, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies change.
Known limit If this repo's own latest sync failed and another repo synced after it, the check falls back to this repo's older successful record and can report ready on the older pages. The live page read still has to succeed first, so nothing reads as ready when it can't be read. Closing this needs `/sync-gbrain` to keep each repo's last result next to its record; that is left for a follow-up.

title: Test runs whose workers start in their own session are no longer killed as stalled (GST-3213)
body:
/ship's test check no longer kills a quiet, working test run as stalled when the test command starts its workers in their own session, as pnpm 11's `pnpm exec` does for Vitest. Why: the stall check read CPU time from the command's process group only, where just the idle launcher was left; it now counts every process descended from the command. Nothing to do: a truly hung run is still killed at the same stall timeout, and every threshold is unchanged.
What changed - **Stall check counts the whole process tree** (the test supervisor): CPU is summed over the command's process group plus every descendant reached by parent links, whatever session or group it moved to. The busy share (a tenth of one CPU), the 1 s sample, the stall timeout and the deadline are unchanged. A descendant reparented away from the tree (a double-forked daemon) no longer counts. - **Stall and timeout kills reach those workers**: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace period, goes to the group of every tree member, so a worker in its own session is no longer left running after the kill. On main it kept running (and a busy one kept burning CPU) after its runner was killed. After a normal exit only the command's own group is cleaned up, as before. The kill never signals pid 1's group, gstack's own process or its own group. - Wording: the `PREGATE_STALLED` detail, the guard line, the result-code summary, `docs/pregate.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` say "process tree" where they described this check; a changelog fragment.
Proof On main at 9610ba4, a throwaway repo whose test command starts one worker in a new session, run through /ship's local test check with a 3 s stall timeout: | worker | main | this branch | |---|---|---| | busy and silent for 8 s | `incomplete` in 3.4 s, `PREGATE_STALLED`, worker still running afterwards | `pass` in 8.4 s, exit 0 | | idle forever (a real hang) | `incomplete` in 3.4 s, `PREGATE_STALLED`, worker still running afterwards | `incomplete` in 3.2 s, `PREGATE_STALLED`, worker gone | New tests in the supervisor's test file (three of them fail on main and pass here): a busy own-session worker runs to the end; a worker that never stops is killed at the deadline with its runner; an idle tree is killed as stalled at the stall timeout, worker included; and a pure test of which processes make up the tree.
Security notes This changes which processes gstack signals. The added targets are only process groups of descendants of the test command gstack itself launched, found through `/proc` (Linux) or `ps -A -S -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,time=` (macOS and other BSDs; the same `ps` call as before with three more columns). No network, secrets, workflows, install scripts or dependencies are touched. Windows is unchanged (`taskkill /T /F`).
Why pnpm 11 starts Vitest's workers in their own session, so the old check saw only an idle launcher and killed a run that was still working, which made /ship's local test check unusable on such projects (reported in #4477). A run that really hangs still fails at the same stall timeout.
Blast radius Only /ship's local test check and its housekeeping checks run through this supervisor (`lib/pregate/supervise.ts`, called from `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts` and `guards.ts`); CI's shard runner does not. The new kill targets are limited to process groups of descendants of the command gstack itself started, and never pid 1's group or gstack's own (read at `killTree`, exercised by the new tests).
Test Coverage Four new tests in `test/pregate-supervise.test.ts` were written before /ship ran; the coverage audit added none. Coverage: 75% of changed code paths (9 of 12). The three uncovered paths are the macOS `ps` fallback (needs real macOS output), the pid-1 and own-group guard in `killTree` (testing it would signal real groups inside the test runner) and SIGKILL escalation to an own-session worker that ignores SIGTERM.
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues found. Five readers ran on the whole diff: a combined testing, security and state-machine reader, an attack-focused reader, a Claude adversarial reader and a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol), which returned clean. The Claude adversarial reader raised five low-severity notes, listed below; none is fixed in this PR.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/supervise.ts:243` Stale group ids from the SIGTERM snapshot get the SIGKILL 5 s later; a reused pid could be a new unrelated group of the same user - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/supervise.ts:250` After a normal exit only the runner's group is killed, so an own-session worker can outlive the check (same as main; documented) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/supervise.ts:265` A busy own-session helper parented to a hung test keeps the run alive until --timeout instead of the stall timeout (documented trade-off) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/supervise.ts:242` A worker that starts a new session after the SIGTERM snapshot and whose parent dies before the SIGKILL snapshot escapes the kill - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/supervise.ts:82` cancelActive runs killTree per active run in the signal handler; on macOS each runs ps synchronously with a 15 s timeout
Exploratory QA No separate probe ran. The smoke evidence is `bun test test/pregate-supervise.test.ts` at the reviewed tree (22 pass, 0 fail, run by the coverage and adversarial readers), which covers one success (a busy own-session worker runs to the end) and the riskiest edges (an idle tree killed as stalled with its worker; a runaway worker killed at the deadline). The before/after repro is in Proof above.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed, so evals were skipped.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation Scope: the stall-check change (process tree instead of process group) on branch stall-check-counts-own-session-workers, base 9610ba43 to head a9e47181. Result: docs/pregate.md and docs/troubleshooting.md and the PREGATE_STALLED summary already describe the process-tree behavior, including the kill semantics, and a changelog fragment exists. A grep of README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/unattended.md and docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md found no stale mention. No edits made. Debt: none found.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/pregate-supervise.test.ts test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts test/ship-publication-gates.test.ts`: 33 pass - [x] `bun run typecheck`: clean - [x] CI free suite at this tree (run 44565670131): 1712 files, green; macOS and Windows jobs green (runs 44565670131, 44565670154)

title: Destructive-command check blocks four more ways past its disk-wipe and force-push checks (GST-3207)
body:
The destructive-command check now blocks `wipefs -a` on every target, disk redirects written with quotes or through a link to `/dev`, and `git push -fn --no-dry-run`.
It only gets stricter: replaying 3,471 recorded agent commands against the previous check moves 0 decisions toward allow.
Nothing to do: the check runs in every session already.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `wipefs -a` (any spelling getopt accepts) is denied on every target. The image-file exemption is gone: GEVA-560's 254,322 commands hold no `wipefs -a`, so it never fired, and each fact it had to prove was a way past the deny. `\wipefs` and doubled quotes (`wipefs''`) are caught too.
- A redirect into a disk is denied with its quotes removed (`>'/dev'/sdb`, `> "/dev/mmcblk0"`) and through a folder whose real path is `/dev` (`> d/sdb` with `d -> /dev`, resolved on disk). `mmcblk` and `rdisk` join the redirect names.
- `git push --no-dry-run` undoes an earlier `-n` (the last flag wins), so `git push -fn --no-dry-run` is a force-push.
- A disk redirect is found however many other redirects come before it: every `/dev/` redirect is scanned, and past 64 disk lookups the check asks.
- The wipefs scan skips redirects and their targets, so `wipefs > -- -$'a' /dev/sdb` is read as a wipe, as at 17303862.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests and measurements</summary>

`test/careful-replay.test.ts` gains a `STRICT_CASES` table (20 rows) and a `/dev` link fixture, and five wipefs-on-an-image rows move from allow to deny. Run against 17303862's check, 15 rows fail and the rest are controls. Replay plus hook tests: 291 pass, 0 fail on bash 5.2.21 and on bash 3.2.57 at 4c30630; at the final head 2acaf4e, 292 pass, 0 fail on bash 3.2.57, and CI is green. Typecheck is clean.

Replays against 17303862 (commands fed to the hook, nothing run), on bash 5.2 and 3.2 at 4c30630, gave the same results on both; the three recorded sets were replayed again at 2acaf4e with the same result:

| Set | Rows | Toward allow | Toward ask or deny |
|---|---|---|---|

title: v1.102.0.0 release
body:
v1.102.0.0 ships 46 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- `gstack-artifact validate` no longer passes a run.json that gstack-autoplan never wrote. (#4494)
- /ship's changed-number check no longer stops on tests that only share a word with the change (#4478). (#4496)
- On Capy, /ship no longer edits or comments on pull requests as you. (#4518)
- The destructive-command check stops asking about scratch deletes and catches the real damage it used to miss. (#4513)
- The destructive-command check reads commands more carefully, closing gaps found after the last release. (#4525)
- The Codex readiness check and the second-model review now pick the same model for a custom Codex provider (GST-3089). (#4491)
- gstack's Codex hooks work when your Codex folder's path has a `(`, `&` or other shell character in it. (#4528)
- Uninstalling gstack keeps your own Codex hooks trusted. (#4528)
- Codex hook setup matches Codex more closely. (#4528)
- On Windows, setup copies the Claude Code hook code that gstack's Codex hooks import (#4528)
- /review's checklist on Codex reads shell commands more carefully. (#4528)
- On Codex, gstack now suggests the right skill for a prompt and stops destructive commands before they run. (#4512)
- On Codex, /review is now held once when it tries to finish without its adversarial pass or its report, as it already is on Claude Code. (#4522)
- On Codex, gstack's skill suggestion now names the skill the way Codex lists it. (#4523)
- On Codex, gstack's suggested prompts and docs now name skills the way Codex lists them. (#4524)
- /review on Codex with gpt-6.1-sol is no longer held back for a second-model pass it already ran. (#4526)
- On Codex, office-hours, plan-design-review and gstack-upgrade work again when you name them. (#4510)
- gstack knows when Codex is running unattended. (#4510)
- Codex reviewers start with a clean context. (#4510)
- Docs no longer say Codex has no hook support. (#4510)
- A command whose output was cut off no longer counts as a finished read. (#4492)
- A folder marked as published data can no longer hide source code or agent files from /ship's review. (#4516)
- Correction to the on-by-default helper hooks entry: the hook still routes only to /review, /qa and /verify, so skills you've installed yourself aren't suggested yet. With gstack's skills it routes 14 of 60 real bug reports (was 17), and long prompts are no longer skipped. (#4505)
- /sync-gbrain's read check now works when the first page in your code source is over 64 KB. (#4497)
- Free-suite CI no longer fails before any test runs when Ubuntu's package mirror is slow. (#4530)
- Syncing a second repo no longer makes the first one ask for /sync-gbrain again. (#4532)
- gstack's helper hooks are now on by default in Claude Code, OpenClaw and Hermes, and the prompt-routing hook fires on real bug reports. (#4503)
- `gstack-pregate clear --receipt` accepts a remote gate run from before a merged release when the release only regenerated a declared release output. (#4483)
- The second-model review now keeps the reviewer's own result, and reports a used-up budget as a budget stop. (#4515)
- When the reviewer wrote its review to the result file it was asked for, Codex then replaced that file with its short closing message ("Done, I wrote the review"), so the review was thrown away and reported as missing its markers. (#4515)
- When the provider refuses the call with HTTP 402 Payment Required (usually a metering proxy that hit its allowance, or an account out of credits or quota), gstack used to record only "exit 1". (#4515)
- The pre-commit /verify check now fails a check that times out, and its checks share one time budget (GST-3201). (#4527)
- /ship's review collector no longer reads a reviewer's own scope list or list of passed checks as findings (GST-3201). (#4527)
- Merge-queue stack tests fail when git cannot list a PR's added test files (GST-3201). (#4527)
- /ship can now review results PRs that publish raw session data. (#4511)
- /ship's review pass works when the checkout you ship isn't the project's default checkout. (#4507)
- A second review round no longer reports done when nothing was reviewed. (#4520)
- The prompt-routing hook now suggests skills you install yourself, and no longer sends ordinary bug reports to /qa (GST-3123). (#4506)
- gstack's script runner and merge-queue checks now also refuse cut-off output. (#4502)
- A failed second-model review reports the cause that actually stopped it, and the runner never deletes its own prompt. (#4519)
- `gstack-ship-queue ready` now fills in the trial merges and the second-model trail read instead of printing lines to fill. (#4529)
- Five small ship-tool fixes. (#4529)
- A ruling the owner gives while a `/ship` run is open can be relayed. (#4529)
- /ship no longer kills a working test run as stalled when the test command starts its workers in their own session. (#4533)
- /ship no longer stops a review because the state-machine reader started its reply the way its instructions say. (#4504)
- When Claude Code runs /verify right before a commit, it now gets a quick check instead of the full fix loop (GST-3150). (#4508)

</details>
