title: A green CI run still counts when the repository's artifact storage is full (GST-3231)
body:
When a private repository's GitHub Actions artifact storage is full, a green run uploads no `tree.json`, so /ship and the merge checks could not reuse it and refused it as `artifact_missing`. A run profile can now set `tree_log_step`, and gstack reads `tree.json` from the one `GSTACK_TREE_JSON` line that step printed in the job log, only when the run has no artifact and only when GitHub's own log timestamp puts the line inside that step. To use it, add the one-line workflow step described under `tree_log_step` in the docs, and raise `min_gstack_version` to the release that ships this.
What changed - `lib/run-evidence.ts`: `ghRunDeps().artifact` throws `NoArtifactError` when the run has no unexpired artifact by that name. `verifyRun` then reads the profile jobs' logs at the attempt that ran (`gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos//actions/jobs//logs`, new `RunDeps.jobLog`), and only for a profile with `tree_log_step`. An artifact always wins. - Exactly one line matching `^\S+Z GSTACK_TREE_JSON (\S+) ([A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2})\r?$` that names the profile's artifact must exist across those jobs. Zero, or two or more, refuse as `artifact_missing` with the count. - The line is bound by the timestamp GitHub's runner stamps on it, which a step's output cannot set. It must fall between the named step's start and finish, at least one second after every earlier step that ran ended and one second before every later step started, because the jobs API gives step times only to the second (the step runs `sleep 1` before the line and `sleep 2` after it). The job and the step must both have succeeded. A line a test prints, even a well-formed one, is either a second line or falls outside the step, so it refuses: `tree_log_unbound` / `CI_CARRY_TREE_LOG_UNBOUND`. - The decoded `tree.json` is capped at 8 MiB, must be canonical base64 that decodes to JSON, and then goes through every existing `tree.json` check unchanged. - Every line that reports a reused run now says `tree_source=job-log` when `tree.json` came from the log, and so does the saved CI record. /ship's final record stores it in its `ci_carried` entry, checked by its schema. - Docs: a new `tree_log_step` section with the workflow step to add, the key in the `run_profiles` key list, and a troubleshooting entry for `CI_CARRY_TREE_LOG_UNBOUND`. Changelog fragment marked `important: blocker`.
Tests - [x] `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=30000 test/run-evidence-job-log.test.ts`: 15 pass, 0 fail - [x] `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=120000 test/ship-ci-carry.test.ts -t HARN-118`: 2 pass, 0 fail - [x] Free Tests run 44602104679 (workflow_dispatch) at e78389509d84: green, 1713 files, 38387 tests - [x] macOS and Windows jobs at e78389509d84: cso-macos-launcher and macos-named-regressions (run 44602104679), windows-smoke (run 44600251339), all green
Why A private repository's upload step failed with "Artifact storage quota has been hit", so its green CI run left no `tree.json` and every check that reuses CI results refused it. Those repositories can now opt in to reading the same record from the job log, bound to one step by GitHub's own timestamps, so a full artifact quota no longer forces the whole test suite to run again on the agent's machine.
Blast radius The change touches the shared CI-run reader that the merge checks, `accept`, `record-ci` and /ship use, and the output lines and saved records that report a reused run. It is safe because the log is read only for a profile that sets `tree_log_step` and only when the run holds zero artifacts by that name; every other path returns the same refusal as before (`lib/run-evidence.ts` verifyRun, read at file:line, and the no-key test in `test/run-evidence-job-log.test.ts`, script ran).
Test Coverage Coverage: 87% value-weighted (13 of 15 new code paths; no weakly covered paths). Tests: 1832 → 1832 files tracked before this branch's new file (+0 written by this audit). Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. Remaining gaps, proposed but not added (below the value bar): the dry-run "would reuse" line in `lib/ship-preflight.ts` naming a job-log source is not asserted; the safe-integer job-id guard in `ghRunDeps.jobLog` has no test (job ids come from the API as numbers). Tests ran: test 1713 (files, from CI run 44602104679 at e78389509d84)
Pre-Landing Review No issues found by the checklist, specialist (testing, security, state-machines), red-team or second-model reviews. The adversarial review raised five low findings, all below the blocking floor and listed under Review notes; each one makes the run refuse and the tests run locally, and none lets a run count that should not.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:469` a rerun whose earlier attempt uploaded the artifact never falls back to the log; refuses as artifact_missing - INFORMATIONAL `docs/pregate.md:858` docs do not say the upload step must not fail the job (continue-on-error) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:301` an ~11 MiB single log line may be split by the runner; would refuse - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:496` serial log reads across many shard jobs can pass ci_record_timeout_s; the tests then run locally - INFORMATIONAL `lib/run-evidence.ts:496` old gh without --allow-escape-sequences refuses with a generic log-read message
Exploratory QA Functional smoke, two probes, verdict pass: `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=30000 test/run-evidence-job-log.test.ts` (15 pass) and `bun --no-env-file test --timeout=120000 test/ship-ci-carry.test.ts -t HARN-118` (2 pass, 53 filtered). Not probed: a live GitHub run with a full artifact quota, and gh's `--allow-escape-sequences` against the real API.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: count a green CI run whose artifact upload hit the storage quota (GST-3231). Delivered: an opt-in job-log fallback bound by runner timestamps, with its refusal code, docs and tests.
Verification Results No plan file: 0 plan-specific checks. Automatic diff-scoped QA above.

No architecture-diagram drift.

Out of scope: release assets, and any change to how artifacts are uploaded. title: Telemetry backend only accepts writes through its own endpoint, and tests stop sending to it (GST-3234)
body:
The telemetry backend now takes writes only through its validated endpoint, signed-in Supabase users can read or write nothing, and gstack's tests can no longer send telemetry to the live project. Why: a signed-in prober read two views on 2026-11-19, probes wrote about 2,000 junk rows through the open insert policy, and 41% of all skill-run rows were test-suite traffic. Nothing changes for users until the migrations and edge functions are deployed; the deploy order is under Deploy.
What changed - **Lockdown (005, 008):** migration 005 mirrors the 2026-11-19 live revoke from `authenticated` and makes both old views `security_invoker`. Migration 008 drops the anon insert and update policies and revokes everything from anon, and `telemetry-ingest` switches to the service role key, so the edge functions become the only write path. Clients older than v0.11.16.0 (March 2026) stop landing: 245 events from 23 installs and 163 update checks in the last 30 days. - **Tests never reach the live project:** `test-setup.ts` sets `GSTACK_TEST_BLOCK_LIVE_TELEMETRY`, and `supabase/config.sh` then yields no endpoint. `test/state-root-one-variable.test.ts`, which was still leaking (20,054 rows), now uses a fixture endpoint. The new tripwire is `test/telemetry-no-live-endpoint.test.ts`. - **Real use separated from test traffic (006):** a `source` column that ingest now stores, a `telemetry_live_events` view (live source, real version, gstack-shaped session id), `crash_clusters` rebuilt on it, and `community_pulse_summary()`. community-pulse now counts every live row of the week in SQL instead of the first 1,000, and its `weekly_active` is distinct community-tier installs rather than update-check rows. - **Ingest:** keeps `source` and accepts `attack_attempt` with validated prompt-injection fields (migration 004, now idempotent, was never applied live). The funnel events were already allowed in the repo; the live function predates that. - **007:** drops seven unused `installations` columns that no migration defined (`email`, `user_id`, snapshots, backups). It refuses if any row holds a value; on 2026-11-19 all 37,566 rows were empty. - **verify-rls.sh:** checks that the public key and a signed-in user (a JWT given, or minted from `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`) are denied every read, insert, update and the pulse function. It writes nothing.
Deploy (out of scope here) 1. Apply 004, 005, 006 and 007. 006 builds an index on about 1.8M rows, which takes seconds. 2. Deploy `telemetry-ingest` and `community-pulse`. 3. Before 008, confirm that one ingest event lands in `telemetry_events` and updates its install, that an update-check ping lands in `update_checks`, and that community-pulse returns `weekly_update_checks`. 4. Apply 008. Running it before step 2 refuses every new event. To undo it, re-grant anon's table privileges and recreate the policies it drops (created in 001 and 003). 5. Run `bash supabase/verify-rls.sh` with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` set. **Undo 008 (incident only)** ```sql BEGIN; GRANT INSERT ON telemetry_events, installations, update_checks TO anon; GRANT UPDATE (last_seen, gstack_version, os) ON installations TO anon; -- 003's column-only grant CREATE POLICY "anon_insert_only" ON telemetry_events FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true); -- from 001 CREATE POLICY "anon_insert_only" ON installations FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true); -- from 001 CREATE POLICY "anon_insert_only" ON update_checks FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true); -- from 001 CREATE POLICY "anon_update_tracking" ON installations FOR UPDATE USING (true) WITH CHECK (true); -- from 003 COMMIT; ``` Before 008, legacy clients' installations updates and upserts already matched no rows, because 002 removed anon's SELECT policy. Only the inserts hold data.

title: gstack tells you what it's adding before it installs a background job or extension (GST-3239)
body:
gstack now tells you in one line what it's about to add, where you'll see it and how to remove it, before anything that keeps running or shows up goes onto your machine. This follows the standing rule that nothing gets added to Garry's devices without that line and a name he'd recognize. Nothing to do: behavior of the jobs themselves is unchanged.
Every path checked A repo-wide search for launchd plists, `launchctl`, systemd user units, crontab, login items (`SMAppService`), browser extensions and device installs found these: | Path | What it adds | Status | |---|---|---| | `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl` (and the guidance block it writes into CLAUDE.md) | tells the agent to run `gbrain autopilot --install`, which adds launch agent `com.gbrain.autopilot` (systemd `gbrain-autopilot.service` or a crontab line on Linux) | **Fixed**: the agent says the line above first. gbrain's own uninstall removes the plist, unit or crontab line. | | `bin/gstack-extension` | walks you through loading the gstack browse extension into your regular Chrome | **Fixed**: prints the notice before it opens chrome://extensions. | | `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` | names `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.gstack.brain-sync.plist` | **Already fine**: no gstack version writes this plist; the script only deletes it on `--uninstall`. The new test pins that. | | `open-gstack-browser/SKILL.md.tmpl` | fallback "Load unpacked" step | Not an addition: it loads gstack browse into gstack's own browser window that you just opened, not your regular Chrome. | | `ios-qa/daemon/src/devicectl.ts` `installApp()` | would install an app on an iPhone | Not an addition: no caller, and it would install your own app under test. | | `lib/gbrain-guards.ts` | mentions `gbrain autopilot --install` | Not an addition: a refusal message naming an existing install. | The browse, design and iOS daemons run only while you use them and stop on idle; nothing registers them to start again.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/background-job-notice.test.ts test/parity-suite.test.ts test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts`: 10 tests pass at 7ca81be. - [x] Free test suite in CI, run 44612696281 at 7ca81be: green (1713 files). - [x] macOS named regressions (run 44612696281) and Windows smoke (run 44611480307) at 7ca81be: green.
What changed ![gstack-extension now says what it is adding, where you will see it and how to remove it, before it opens chrome://extensions](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/OjZPHsN8aIrAbZORfc_u8BZnON7M56znHQDRJOXDR24.png) gstack-extension now says what it is adding, where you will see it and how to remove it, before it opens chrome://extensions.
Before/after as text: gstack-extension now says what it is adding, where you will see it and how to remove it, before it opens chrome://extensions ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output Manual install (for your regular Chrome): + Adding a Chrome extension called gstack browse that adds the gstack side panel to your regular Chrome. You'll see it as the gstack browse icon in Chrome's toolbar and on chrome://extensions. Remove it with: chrome://extensions → gstack browse → Remove + 1. Opening chrome://extensions now... Could not open Chrome. Navigate to chrome://extensions manually. 2. Toggle 'Developer mode' ON (top-right) ~~~ Before this, gstack could walk you into adding a background job or a browser extension without saying so. Now the /sync-gbrain guidance (and the block it writes into CLAUDE.md) has the agent say "Adding a background job called com.gbrain.autopilot that keeps gbrain's index of your repos fresh on a schedule. You'll see it under System Settings → General → Login Items on a Mac, or as gbrain-autopilot.service in `systemctl --user` on Linux. Remove it with: gbrain autopilot --uninstall" before it runs `gbrain autopilot --install`, and `gstack-extension` prints the same kind of line for the gstack browse Chrome extension.
Why Garry's rule on 2026-11-19: "before adding anything that keeps running or shows up on my devices, tell me in one line what I'll see, why and how to remove it." Now every gstack path that adds such a thing says so first, and a test fails if a new one is added without that line.
Blast radius Only two printed or spoken lines change. One is the sync-gbrain guidance text (template, generated SKILL.md and the CLAUDE.md block) and the other is one `echo` in `bin/gstack-extension`, and neither changes what gets installed. Script ran: `bin/gstack-extension` prints the notice before opening chrome://extensions both with and without a browser opener on PATH, and the gbrain names match gbrain's own `src/core/autopilot-paths.ts` and `src/commands/autopilot.ts`.
Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 0 noted - [AUTO-FIXED] test/background-job-notice.test.ts:33 The exemptions for files that only mention an install step skipped the whole file, so a real install step added to one later would go unflagged → each exemption now names its exact line, a stale exemption fails its own test, and the `devicectl.ts` exemption (which matched no line) is gone. Commit 7ca81be. The second review pass and the adversarial read of the fix found nothing.
Exploratory QA Two smoke runs of `bin/gstack-extension`: with stubbed browser openers and with none on PATH. Both exit 0 and print the notice before chrome://extensions opens and before "Load unpacked". Verdict: pass. Limit: without `pbcopy` the script exits 127 before printing anything; that is older behavior outside this change.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: tell users before gstack adds a background job or extension. Delivered: the notice in the sync-gbrain guidance, CLAUDE.md and gstack-extension, plus a test that guards every install step.
Eval Results No paid evals selected: `bun run eval:select` picked 0 behavioral probes and 0 quality judges for this diff.
Documentation Scope: the six committed files from ab6a38b7 to 7ca81be3 (CLAUDE.md, sync-gbrain template and generated SKILL.md, bin/gstack-extension, a changelog.d fragment and a new test), plus every repo doc that mentions `gbrain autopilot --install` or `gstack-extension`. Result: current. CLAUDE.md and the sync-gbrain template already hold the new one-line notice before the autopilot install, and they match each other. BROWSER.md's line describing gstack-extension is still accurate. No other doc describes these install steps, so nothing needed editing. Debt: none found.

title: The prompt-routing hook names your installed bug-fix skill on bug reports, and never puts /verify first (GST-3237)
body:
On a bug report, the routing hook now names the installed bug-fix skill (prove-it, or any skill whose triggers claim bug fixing) alone, so /verify is never ranked ahead of it. Why: in B1d, Opus 5.5 loaded prove-it in 29 of 33 sessions when the hook named it alone and 0 of 20 when it didn't; the old matcher named it on only 40 of B1's 60 prompts. Nothing to do: the hook line's wording is unchanged.
What changed Bug reports were getting /verify first, or no bug-fix skill at all, so the model often skipped the skill built for fixing bugs. Now a prompt that reads as a bug report names the installed bug-fix skill alone. - **Bug reports go to the bug-fix skill** (`lib/skill-route.ts`). A prompt reads as a bug report on one strong sign (a symptom word such as crash, hang, leak or wrong; an exception name; the verb fix; "expected behavior", "steps to reproduce"; "fails", "doesn't work"; a "should X, not Y" correction) or two different weak ones (error or exception used as a noun, a negated verb such as "can't", "should", "instead of"). gstack's own routed skills (/review, /qa, /verify) only check work, so they never claim one. With no bug-fix skill installed, routing is as before. - **Only a generic fixer claims bug reports.** A trigger claims them when it names the defect and fixing it and nothing else ("fix this bug", "reproduce the bug in a test"). A fixer with its own target, such as "fix lint errors" or "fix postgres bugs", no longer takes every bug report. - **Asking for a review or QA pass still gets one.** A prompt that holds the whole phrase of a /review or /qa trigger ("review this PR for bugs", "find bugs on site") and asks for no fix keeps that skill. "The checkout page crashes… find the cause and fix it" still goes to the bug-fix skill. - **Another installed skill's trigger needs two content words** (GST-3142). "error", "the crash" or "fix it" are skipped and named in the routing log and `--explain`; the skill keeps its other triggers. - **`GSTACK_SKILL_ROUTE_HINT=step` and `=contract` quote only gstack's own skills** (GST-3142). Another skill gets the default line. - **Router text** (its own commit, ideas from #4500 and #4501 by @lubosxyz, rebuilt on main). `PROACTIVE=all` no longer says "Do NOT answer directly when a skill exists", which contradicted "When to invoke, and when not to". /ship's router rule and description drop "deploy"; deploying is /land-and-deploy. - The trace line adds `bug_report=true`, and `gstack-skill-route --explain` says when a route came from a bug report.
Why The routing hook exists to put the right skill in front of the model. On bug reports it was naming /verify first or nothing, and in B1d that decided whether the model used the bug-fix skill at all (29 of 33 sessions with it named alone, 0 of 20 without).
Blast radius The change is inside the routing hook's matcher (`routePrompt` and its helpers), read by the Claude hook and `gstack-skill-route` only; both callers were updated and nothing else calls it (grep of `routePrompt(`). The hook only adds a hint line, so a misroute costs a wrong suggestion, never a failed command (`test/skill-route.test.ts`, 29 tests, and the full free suite in CI run 44617369574).

title: /cso audits repositories that track symlinks
body:
`/cso` can now audit a repository that tracks symlinks, such as a `CLAUDE.md` that links to `AGENTS.md`. Today one such link stops every run. A link that stays inside the repository is now listed as an exclusion in coverage and never followed, and its target is audited under its own path. Users need no new flag or setting.

## What this fixes

`gstack-cso start` fails with `UNSAFE_PATH "Symlink or special source file"` whenever the checkout tracks a symlink, even a relative link to another file in the same repository. Many repositories link `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md` so that every agent reads one instruction file.

`--paths` doesn't help either. The special-file walk in `rejectSpecialFiles` covers the whole checkout whatever the scope, and the capture loop refuses a symlink outside `--paths` with `Special source input`.

## Why the refusal looks unintended

No comment, doc or commit explains why a contained link is refused. The tests cover only links that escape the repository (`/etc/passwd`, an outside directory) or are broken. The rest of the codebase already treats contained links as safe:

- `treeManifest(..., allowContainedSymlinks)` in `lib/cso/preparation-executor.ts` accepts a relative link whose target stays inside the tree, and `test/cso-preparation-adversarial.test.ts` pins it.
- #3303 recorded nested repositories as `excluded:` snapshot entries instead of failing the run. This PR uses the same shape.

## What changed

**In-repository links** (`fix(cso): record in-repository symlinks as explicit snapshot exclusions`)

- A link is accepted only when its target is relative and resolves, lexically and through every intermediate link (`realpath`), to a regular file or directory inside the repository.
- It gets one manifest entry: `originalHash: not-read`, transformation `IN_REPOSITORY_LINK` (`excluded: ...`). So it appears under snapshot-inputs exclusions, not as a gap. Nothing is followed or copied; the target is captured under its own path.
- When nothing at the target is audited, the link is `withheld` and coverage counts it as a gap. That covers a target the snapshot doesn't capture (an ignored file, `.git/config`) and, under `--paths`, a target outside the scope.
- `assertEntriesStable` re-checks the link's inode, its target and the repository path it resolves to. A link that is retargeted, replaced or deleted during capture, or whose intermediate links come to resolve elsewhere, fails with `SNAPSHOT_RACE`. The target is read twice, so a link that reuses the inode between the two `lstat` calls is caught too.
- The Git blob hash of a link is the hash of its target string, so base comparison stays exact. An unchanged link is not a changed path; a retargeted link, or a file replaced by a link, is.
- A link inside a host dependency tree such as `node_modules` is excluded like the rest of that tree, and a link outside `--paths` is listed as out of scope. Both are bound by identity without resolving their target, so a dangling `node_modules/.bin` link does not block the run.
- A `--paths` entry that is itself a symlink is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, naming the path it points to; otherwise the scope would audit only the link.
- Still refused: absolute targets, `../` escapes, broken or looping links, links that resolve to a FIFO or device, and chains that escape through an ignored link.

A link's target is not part of the snapshot's original identity. That matches every other not-read entry, since the link is never followed.

**Scope** (`fix(cso): a special file outside --paths no longer blocks the audit`)

- The special-file walk covers only the `--paths` scope and its ancestors. It compares names without case, so a directory whose on-disk case differs from Git's spelling is still walked.
- So an escaping link or an untracked FIFO outside the scope no longer blocks the run. The link is recorded as out of scope without resolving its target, and a change during capture still fails.
- Inside the scope, an escaping, broken or special link is still refused, and so is a tracked path outside the scope that has been replaced on disk by a FIFO.

This is a separate commit, so it can be dropped if you'd rather keep the walk repository-wide. The first commit stands on its own; the changelog's last clause about an untracked FIFO or a symlink outside `--paths` would go with it.

## Tests

New cases in `test/cso-ordinary-repos.test.ts`, next to the nested-repository ones:

- `start` on a repository with a tracked file link and an untracked directory link succeeds. Both links are listed as exclusions, there are no gaps, and the snapshot holds the targets but not the links.
- A link that points up out of its directory (`web/README.md -> ../README.md`) is accepted and is not a changed path against a base that already had it.
- A retargeted link, and a file replaced by a link with the same bytes, are changed paths against the base.
- A link to an ignored file and a link to `.git/config` are gaps, and the ignored target is not in the snapshot.
- A broken link in an unignored `node_modules` is excluded, not refused.
- Negative controls: absolute, escaping, broken, self-looping, a link to an ignored FIFO, and an in-repo link whose chain escapes through an ignored link. All are refused with `UNSAFE_PATH`.
- A link retargeted to another contained file, or deleted, just before the final stability check fails with `SNAPSHOT_RACE`.
- Under `--paths`: a link entry is refused, an in-scope link to an out-of-scope target is a gap, an out-of-scope link is listed as out of scope, and an entry deleted from disk is recorded as a deletion.
- Second commit: an escaping link and a FIFO outside the scope are withheld; widening the scope refuses each of them.

Existing symlink tests in `test/cso-snapshot-state.test.ts` and `test/cso-ordinary-repos.test.ts` pass unchanged.

## Checks (macOS)

- `bun run typecheck`: no errors. `bun run typecheck:test`: no new diagnostics.
- `bun run format:cso:check`: clean.
- `test/cso-ordinary-repos.test.ts` and `test/cso-snapshot-state.test.ts`: all pass at each commit.
- All 58 `test/cso-*.test.ts` files: 836 pass, 35 skip, 3 fail. The same 3 fail on `main` on this machine: the archive-cache lease recovery, the forged TAP summary witness and the Python runner import order.
- On the repository that hit this, `gstack-cso start --scope auth --offline` now starts, and its links are listed as `excluded: symlink to a file or directory inside this repository`. Before the fix, the same command failed with `UNSAFE_PATH`.

title: round-grant --kind fix-check cannot be recorded: the ship run id trips the pii.phone.e164 scanner
body:
## What happens

After `/ship` stops at `PR_ROUND_CAP` (a blocker was fixed in a PR's last full review round), the documented way forward is a fix round recorded with `gstack-approvals round-grant --kind fix-check --stop-run <run> --findings <ids>`. That command cannot succeed:

- With `--stop-run`, the secret scanner refuses the row because the ship run id (`<pid>-<epoch>-<hex>`) matches `pii.phone.e164` (`APPROVAL_RECORD_SECRET`).
- Without `--stop-run`, the row is refused as incomplete (`APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID`: "round-grant --kind fix-check needs --stop-run …").

So a PR that fixes a blocker in its last round can never be granted its fix round, and `/ship` cannot reach the receipt or publish.

## Reproduce (current main, b0f865c)

In an empty repository:

```bash
git init -q && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init
gstack-approvals round-grant --pr 1 --head HEAD --kind fix-check \
  --stop-run 12345-1795085644-abcd1234 --findings p1/reader#1 \
  --reason "fix the open blocker" --by owner
# → APPROVAL_RECORD_SECRET (field scope: pii.phone.e164)

gstack-approvals round-grant --pr 1 --head HEAD --kind fix-check \
  --findings p1/reader#1 --reason "fix the open blocker" --by owner
# → APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID (needs --stop-run)
```

The run ids come from `gstack-skill-start` (`SESSION_ID`), so every real run id has this shape.

## Expected

The run id is an identifier gstack itself generated, so it should not be scanned as personal data: either exempt the `stop_run` field (and other gstack-generated ids) from the PII scan, or add the run-id shape to the false-positive exceptions in `lib/redact-patterns.ts`, beside the ones already there for timestamps and hashes.

## Consequence

Any repository whose `/ship` runs use `review_scope: frozen` and fix a blocker in the last round is stuck: the owner's grant cannot be recorded, so the PR has to be finished by hand without a receipt.

title: Telemetry records why skill runs end, which host and model ran them, and how upgrades went (GST-3234)
body:
gstack's anonymous usage telemetry now records nine more fields: the host and model family, how a skill was started, why it ended, whether checks passed, how skill routing is set up, a random per-session id, and for upgrades the version left and any error. This tells us where skills stop working and which setups break upgrades, which the current outcome-only data can't show. Deploy in order after merge: apply migration 009, deploy the telemetry-ingest function, then release the client; apply migration 007 after that.
What each new field holds | Field | Values | Set by | |---|---|---| | `host` | claude_code, codex, cursor, openclaw, hermes, other, unknown | detected by gstack-skill-end | | `model_family` | claude_opus, claude_sonnet, claude_haiku, claude_other, gpt, gemini, other | the agent, at skill end | | `invoked` | user, model, chained | the agent | | `exit_reason` | completed, user_stopped, blocked, tool_error, test_failed, context_limit, gave_up | the agent | | `checks` | passed, failed, not_run | the agent | | `routing` | none, block, hooks, both | detected from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md and settings.json | | `harness_session_id` | 16 hex characters, random per agent session, never reused | stored in the existing session marker | | `from_version` | the version an upgrade started from | gstack-upgrade | | `upgrade_error` | none, refused_dirty, busy, fetch_failed, setup_failed, other | gstack-upgrade | An empty value is stored as null and a value outside the list as `unknown`, on both the client and the server, so a wrong guess from a model can't add new categories. The session id is sent on both the community and anonymous tiers; the consent text now says so: "Anonymous mode sends the same usage with no device ID; a random id per agent session that is never reused." docs/privacy.md lists every field.
Other fixes in this change - Runs started by evals or CI are now labelled `eval` or `ci` instead of `live` (an explicit flag still wins, then GSTACK_TELEMETRY_SOURCE). - The server keeps the raw outcome in `outcome_raw` and maps known spellings to the four standard outcomes. - A skill run with no start time records an empty duration instead of 0. - Migration 007 now drops the three old row-level policies first and counts only non-zero `backup_version` values, so it can be applied cleanly after this merges. - Migration 009 grants the new view and columns to the service role only and revokes them from public, anon and authenticated. - The added prompt lines are byte-neutral: the telemetry step was reworded so every generated skill stays exactly its previous size.
Deploy steps and notes from the live project 1. Apply `supabase/migrations/009_next_telemetry_fields.sql`. 2. Deploy `supabase/functions/telemetry-ingest` (verify_jwt off, as today). 3. Release the client (gstack-skill-end, gstack-telemetry-log, gstack-upgrade). 4. Apply migration 007. The previous change (#4537) is already deployed. While deploying it we also deleted the unused community-benchmarks and community-recommendations functions; their sources are saved and both now return 404. Two things seen on the live project, left as they are: default privileges set by supabase_admin in the public schema still grant anon and authenticated, because the postgres role can't change them; and a handful of rows arrived with source "other" after the deploy.
Known limits left open - Deploy order matters: the new telemetry-ingest must not go live before migration 009, or every insert fails until 009 lands (clients keep their events and retry). - Some upgrades are mislabelled: an upgrade through `--ff-only-no-reinstall` (how Capy sessions upgrade) reports success before the install check runs, and `/gstack-upgrade` goes through gstack-ff-update, which sends no upgrade event. - Routing detection reads CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in the current directory only. - People who already opted in don't see the new consent text. - Pending events written before this change have no `source` and count as live. - `outcome_raw` keeps the raw outcome cut to 20 characters. - The migration tests check the SQL text only; nothing applies it to a database. - Smaller review notes: `gstack-skill-end --help` lists `--checks none`, which is sent as `unknown`; an outcome spelled like a built-in object key (`constructor`) can fail an ingest batch; two skill ends racing on an empty session marker can split one session's id; migration 009 adds CHECK columns and an index without CONCURRENTLY, so inserts wait while it runs; an upload batch over 45,000 bytes is not tested past the first POST.

title: The paid auto-decide check counts a start step that ran while the skill loaded
body:
Since #4509, Claude Code skills run their start step as they load, so the paid /plan-ceo-review auto-decide check could miss a run that really did auto-decide. It now accepts the start output in the loaded skill text. Why: one of the five passing runs captured for that check was credited only through the session journal, and that path needed a start command in the tool calls. Nothing to do: this changes test code and the journal reader the tests use; no skill text changes.
What changed ![The journal reader now keeps the skill text Claude Code loaded, so the check can find a start that ran at load](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/XKW62uAY5qOFoQo5htk8EKFGshVLxJvetpazQD4Kxo0.png) The journal reader now keeps the skill text Claude Code loaded, so the check can find a start that ran at load.
Before/after as text: The journal reader now keeps the skill text Claude Code loaded, so the check can find a start that ran at load ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ readPlanCountTranscript on the same journal (this branch, da098f2) +{"status":"ready","skills":["plan-ceo-review"],"sessions":["s1"]} -$ readPlanCountTranscript on a journal whose skill ran its start at load (base 7f9c1bc) -{"status":"ready","skills":[],"sessions":[]} ~~~
A /plan-ceo-review run that auto-decided its review mode could still fail the paid check, because the check looked for the start step only among Bash tool calls, and since #4509 the start runs while the skill loads. The check now also reads the start output that Claude Code put into the loaded skill text, and still requires exactly one start per session. - `lib/claude-public-transcript.ts`: the journal reader also keeps the skill text Claude Code loaded for a slash command or the Skill tool (`skillLoads`). It keeps only records in the run's own session and folder, with a timestamp, marked as loaded text, and starting with `Base directory for this skill:`. - `test/helpers/native-auto-decide.ts`: the check reads the start output between the "Preamble (run first)" heading and the "If the line above is not the start output" sentence. Together with start commands run through Bash, the session must still have exactly one start. - `test/helpers/touchfiles-data.ts`: the plan-mode and auto-decide paid cases also run when `bin/gstack-skill-load` or `scripts/resolvers/load-injection.ts` changes.
Why "The paid auto-decide check could never find a start Bash call" after skills began running their start at load. Without this, a real auto-decided run can be scored as a failure, so the paid gate case reports a regression that isn't there.
Blast radius The new `skillLoads` field is optional and only the auto-decide test helper reads it; every other caller of `readPlanCountTranscript` ignores it, and the full free suite passed at this exact commit (CI run 44625475053, 1717 test files). No skill text, setup or runtime path changes.
Pre-Landing Review No issues at or above the blocking floor. One reviewer pass (testing, security, state-machine and red-team checklists) found nothing; the adversarial pass found one low-severity note, listed below.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `test/helpers/native-auto-decide.ts:338` A load whose start timed out (partial start output followed by 'SKILL_START: timed out ... at load') is credited as the session's one start; the changelog says failed loads are refused
Exploratory QA Three bounded functional probes of the journal reader (synthetic journals, owned temp folders): an owned skill load is kept with its skill and session (pass); a base directory with a trailing slash still names the skill (pass); a Windows-style base directory is not split, so a Windows load would not be credited (observation only; the paid check runs on Linux).
Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped.
Eval Results The selector picked three paid probes (auq-format-gate, office-hours-auto-mode, plan-ceo-review-plan-mode); none ran in this review because paid runs were out of scope. plan-ceo-review-plan-mode passed earlier at dd98bcca (see Agent notes).
Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Scope:** The diff from 7f9c1bc touches 6 files, all test and helper code: the transcript reader now records the skill text Claude Code loaded, the auto-decide check accepts a start step that ran while the skill loaded, and the touchfiles were updated. There is one changelog.d fragment. There are no uncommitted changes. **Result:** The docs are current. docs/TEST_PORTFOLIO.md and docs/hosts.md mention the touched area and are still accurate. No user-facing docs needed an edit. **Debt:** None.

Agent notes Follow-up to GST-3157, asked for by the crew's merge owner after #4509's READY. A real plan-mode run of `plan-ceo-review-plan-mode` at dd98bcca (run gsta634-smoke-1, $0.57) passed with the start output in the first request and no start tool call; that gate case already covers plan mode, so no new paid case was added. lib/skill-route.ts is untouched. title: Review plan gives a preregistration with only its plain data the write-up review, and stops counting data rows as code (GST-3238)
body:
A preregistration whose diff is only its write-up, text and data files now plans as a write-up (one reviewer, one round); scoring, judge, guard and gate edits keep their full review, and CI is unchanged.
Results rows no longer count as runtime code, and a fix after an approved review stop that changes only a data file now gets its follow-up review instead of stopping.
Nothing to do for readers; this follows Garry's rule that preregistrations without scoring code get one review round, and fixes a stop reported by Founderstar.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![A fix that touches only data files used to read as an unrecognised change and stop the follow-up review; now it is recognised and exits 0](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/qyJWR2KcsSmJYK9dI5qLQFXJb1oD1M6GIt8rXpPH22M.png)

A fix that touches only data files used to read as an unrecognised change and stop the follow-up review; now it is recognised and exits 0.

~~~diff
--- Before · gstack-diff-scope main on a range of wiki/labels.json and results/rows.tsv
+++ After
@@ ⋯ 7 unchanged ⋯ @@
 SCOPE_MIGRATIONS=false
 SCOPE_API=false
 SCOPE_AUTH=false
+exit=0
-SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched
-# unmatched: results/rows.tsv
-# unmatched: wiki/labels.json
-exit=2
~~~

People writing an eval plan saw a preregistration that only holds its write-up and its data get the full four-reader review, because a test reads one of its data files. Now:

- **Preregistrations.** A data file under a path segment named `prereg` or `preregistration` (gstack-evals' `wiki/plans/<id>-prereg/`, harness-evals' `prereg-harbor.json`, `lanes/<x>/prereg.md`) counts as docs even when code reads it, so a preregistration-only diff is docs class at light depth. The gate scan and the risk classes still read that data (a tagged hunk, a missing scan or a secret makes it full). A scorer, judge, grader or rubric beside it keeps the eval risk class (full), and a gate path keeps gate class (full). Documented in docs/review-policy.md#preregistrations.
- **Data rows.** JSONL, NDJSON, CSV and TSV lines, and JSON lines under a docs, wiki, results, reports or preregistration folder, no longer count as runtime lines; the files keep their class, so readers still read them. A JSON file code reads anywhere else keeps counting, because it can be a guard's config.
- **Data-only fix range.** `gstack-diff-scope` printed `SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched` for a range of data files alone, so the review plan stopped with "no fix to read" even with an approved follow-up review and a committed fix. A data file is now recognised (no category, never unmatched); an unknown file beside it still fails closed.
- **Platform review skip.** The skip that lets a matching platform review stand in for readers now refuses every preregistration spelling the new rule accepts (`prereg2.json`, a `preregs/` folder), not only the plain `prereg` name. Found in review; see Pre-Landing Review.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Review depth should follow risk. A preregistration with no scoring or guard code is a write-up and gets one reviewer and one round, and results tables are data, not code. A results PR (harness-evals#432) planned 17,773 runtime lines, of which 147 were code.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the review plan's depth and reader choice change, in `lib/review-depth.ts` and `bin/gstack-diff-scope`. CI, the gate scan, secret and risk checks are unchanged. A planner replay over 460 real main commits (gstack-evals 200, harness-evals 60, gstack 200) kept the same depth on all 460; class, risk and readers changed on 2, and 34 others only lost data-row runtime lines. The replay predates the platform-skip fix and was not rerun; that fix only adds a catch, so it can only add readers.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

One blocker was found and fixed: with platform review on, a numbered or plural preregistration name (`lanes/x/prereg2.json`) could take the platform skip with zero readers, because the skip checked a narrower path pattern than the new rule. Fixed in 984066c with a planner regression that fails without it. The second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol) found it; the pass on the fix range was clean.

Below-floor notes, not fixed (none would fail a test, break production or lose data or secrets):

- security finding, details recorded privately (2 notes from the specialist review, about the preregistration path rule and data-only ranges planning lighter review).
- The preregistration path rule matches a `prereg` segment anywhere, not only under plans or results folders (`lib/review-depth.ts:75`).
- Row files (JSONL, NDJSON, CSV, TSV) never count as runtime lines, even when a guard reads them (`lib/review-depth.ts:73`).
- A data-only whole-PR range no longer raises `SCOPE_ERROR` for other callers (`bin/gstack-diff-scope:475`).
- The harness-evals#432 figure (17,773 runtime lines, 147 code) was not recounted by a reader; no reader found it wrong.
- The results-folder match applies at any depth, so consumed JSON under `src/reports/` stops counting runtime lines (`lib/review-depth.ts:268`).
- The changelog entry names "docs, results or preregistration" folders for JSON rows, while the code also covers wiki and reports folders.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional CLI smoke, 3 probes, rerun at 984066c after the fix: a data-only range exits 0 with every flag false; data beside an unknown file still exits 2 with `SCOPE_ERROR=unmatched` naming only the unknown file; a preregistration folder with only markdown and data plans docs at light depth. All pass. Limit: the consumed-preregistration branch and the platform skip are covered by tests, not probes.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The docs already match this change, so nothing was edited.

**Scope:** 6 commits (ab6a38b7..984066cc), 10 committed files, with nothing staged, unstaged or new. I checked docs/review-policy.md against lib/review-depth.ts, lib/review-risk.ts and bin/gstack-diff-scope, and searched docs/ship-policy.md, docs/captain.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md for stale preregistration or scope text.

**Documentation health**
- docs/review-policy.md: current. The data-rows and preregistration paragraphs, the light-depth table row and the platform-skip exclusion all match the code.
- docs/ship-policy.md: current. The platform skip already excludes preregistration claims.
- AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/captain.md, docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: current, with no affected text.

**Coverage debt:** the exit-0 behaviour of gstack-diff-scope for a data-only range is described only in script comments and the changelog fragment, with no reference doc entry (a common gap).

**Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test test/review-depth.test.ts test/review-depth-lean.test.ts test/diff-scope.test.ts test/round-cap-granted-stop.test.ts`: 381 tests pass, 0 fail at 984066c.
- [x] `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:test`: clean, no new diagnostics.
- [x] Full free suite: CI run 44633715797 (free-tests.yml at 984066c), green; carried at tree 91e07c68dec4.
- [x] macOS named regressions (run 44633715797) and windows-smoke (run 44632669462) green at 984066c.

</details>

title: A clean follow-up review of a fix now clears the findings it was approved for, plus three other /ship approval fixes (GST-3246)
body:
/ship stops needing a manual owner ruling in four cases: an approved follow-up review that finds the fix clean now clears the findings it was approved for, a stopped /ship run can record that approval itself, a leftover marker from a finished run no longer blocks approvals, and run ids like `507-7192673` are no longer mistaken for phone numbers. Why: each case forced a manual ruling or a workaround on 2026-11-19 (gstack #4537, harness-evals #507 and #508). Nothing to do: when a /ship run takes that approval, it now prints the two extra fields its follow-up review records.
Agent notes **What changed** - **Granted fix-check closes its findings** (`lib/review-scope.ts`, `bin/gstack-review-scope`): the loop summary reads the branch's fix-check round grants. A `review-fix-check` row that is complete, has `range_base` at the grant's stop head, lists every grant finding in `covers`, holds no unfixed blocker of its own, and was logged after the row that left the finding open marks exactly those findings `fixed`. A row covering fewer findings, finding a blocker, reading another range or predating the stop closes nothing, so `RECEIPT_BLOCKER_OPEN` still fires. `gstack-ship-receipt claim` prints a `FIX_CHECK_ROW:` line with both fields when a run claims a fix-check grant. The reviewer-pinned `ship/sections/review-army.md` is unchanged (a first version edited it and CI's no-loss pin test refused it). - **Stale marker and stopped runs** (`lib/ruled-notes.ts`, `bin/gstack-approvals`): `openShipRun` counts a `.git/gstack-ship-run` marker only while `gstack-lease open` says its run is open, as gate dispositions already did; a lease check that cannot run keeps the marker open. Inside an open run, `round-grant` still refuses everything except `--kind fix-check --stop-run `, which is what `gstack-ship-receipt stop`'s NEXT line tells the lane to record. - **Run ids are not phone numbers** (`lib/redact-patterns.ts`): a position exemption for a span inside a fix-check grant scope's `stop=` token. The same digits in the reason, the words or anywhere else still report. - **`--by "GStack Minder (GSTA-36)"`** (`lib/ruled-notes.ts` and its readers): the `/^gstack\b/i` catch stays, with an exemption on top for `GStack `. It was a pattern mistake, not a deliberate guard: the code's own comment already called `GStack Minder` "a person's crew, not gstack", and `round-grant` was fixed that way in #4529 while `rule`, `gate` and `lane-exception` (and the readers of their rows) kept the prefix match. gstack writes its own names in lower case only, so the exemption admits none of them. **Tests.** Failing first on main: 7 new cases failed before the fix. The refusal controls (fix-check with a blocker, covers fewer, other range, no covers, before the stop, extra-round inside the open run, phone in free text, gstack's own names) pass before and after. Four existing fixtures that simulated an open run with a marker alone now also open the run's lease, as `test/ship-gate-dispositions.test.ts` already did; their assertions are unchanged. Lane GSTA-665 for GStack Minder (GSTA-36), issue GST-3246. gstack: ok 1.102.0.0 for=ship. **Trail-read fix round** (Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36), 2026-11-19: one fix round for trail-read rows 1, 2, 3, 6, 8; R51 past two rounds). A cross-family read of the decision trail (openai/gpt-6.2-sol, reports/GSTA-665-decisions.tsv) found gaps, fixed in one commit, each with a test that failed at 81eb28a: - Row 1: a fix-check clears findings only when its derived status is not issues_found or issues_open and no unresolved or critical finding exists in any findings source it logged (inline findings or a findings file). - Row 2: the stop head comes from the logger's own record (a fix-range row's `fix_base`, else the commit of the bound Step 9 row the fix-check follows), and the copied `range_base` must agree; the copy alone never counts. - Row 3: a blocker that carries a ledger id closes only by that id, never by a fingerprint another blocker shares. - Row 6 (and 7): `gstack-lease open --any-age` keeps a run open past 120 minutes while its holder lives and exits 2 when a lease file cannot be read; `openShipRun` drops a marker only on exit 1 (released, or holder gone). Gate dispositions and preflight keep their current lease reads. - Row 8: the phone-number exemption moved out of the shared scanner into `buildRow`, for a fix-check grant row's `scope` field only; a grant-shaped excerpt in `--reason` or `--words` is scanned as before. **Open notes** (trail-read rows 4 and 5, below the blocking floor, not fixed by the Captain's ruling): - Row 4: the loop summary does not check a fix-check grant's PR, its stop record or whether another run claimed it; the approval record is per branch, and the fix-check route only runs after `history` (grantedStop) and `claim` check the stop. - Row 5: inside an open run, a fix-check grant whose `--stop-run` matches the open run records even for an unrelated head; `history` rejects it later, but `claim` and the review plan do not check the recorded stop. - Residual: `gstack-lease touch` still prunes lease files older than 120 minutes, so another session's touch on the same checkout can delete a live long run's lease, which then reads as released. **Pre-Landing Review** (/ship run ship-4546; full panel, 2 rounds) Pre-Landing Review: 9 issues — 2 auto-fixed, 3 asked (0 fixed, 3 skipped), 0 deferred, 4 noted REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=2 deferred=0 noted=4 fixed=2 scope=frozen dispatches=8 Gate edits: none detected (7 listed, 1 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) - Pass 1 at 5085521: batched specialist (testing, security, state-machines), red team, native adversarial and second-model review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol). title: skill_routing: let users add triggers (per language) and don't route a bare skill-name mention
body:
**Context.** gstack 1.101.0.0 turns `skill_routing` on by default (`lib/skill-route.ts`, `SWITCH_DEFAULT.skill_routing: 'on'`). On one day of real use by a Spanish-speaking user, `skill-route.log` shows 78 prompts: 72 `no-route reason=below-threshold`, and 4 `routed` events, all `variant=name`.

**Problem 1: triggers are English-only and not user-extensible.** Triggers live in each gstack `SKILL.md`. Editing them is overwritten on upgrade, and a user skill with `triggers:` routes to itself, not to `/review` or `/ship`. A non-English user effectively gets no routing.

**Problem 2: a bare mention of a skill name routes.** A prompt that discusses `/review` ("I agree we should use /review for small changes") got "this request fits /review. Run /review…". The user was talking about the skill, not asking to run it.

**Requests.**
1. A user trigger file outside the checkout (for example `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/skill-triggers.yaml`) that adds triggers to installed skills, gstack's own included, and survives upgrades. The same validation rules as `SKILL.md` triggers would apply.
2. Optionally, per-language trigger sets shipped by gstack.
3. Don't route on `variant=name` when the name appears inside a sentence about the skill, or lower its score below the threshold unless the prompt starts with it.

Related: #4423 (routing messages from other agents).

And a team named "GStack …" can record rulings, gate answers and test exceptions. Both caused avoidable stops in unattended /ship runs. What changed Unattended /ship runs stopped twice for no good reason. title: gstack-flaky reports green when a quarantined test is skipped
body:
## What happened

I ran a CI-style Bun test command through `gstack-flaky` with an active quarantine entry. Bun reported the quarantined test as skipped and exited 0. `gstack-flaky` also exited 0, reported `quarantined=0 verdict=pass`, and wrote no ledger entry.

I saw a related result when an ordinary failure triggered a whole-command retry. The quarantined test passed on the first run and was skipped on the retry. The wrapper stayed green and recorded `quarantined-pass` with attempts `pass,skip`. The quarantine report then counted it toward the clean streak (`recent=pass clean_streak=1`).

The [quarantine policy](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/1bd86d9a4547ed8df0c5da37380c838e61a91b9b/docs/flaky.md#quarantine) says a quarantined test still runs. I expected exit 1 and a visible `quarantined-fail` with the actual skip recorded. An ordinary skip should still follow the runner's verdict.

## Steps to reproduce

Run from a gstack checkout at `1bd86d9a4547ed8df0c5da37380c838e61a91b9b` with Bun 1.4.2. This creates a temporary Git project and uses placeholder evidence URLs.

```bash
# Run from the gstack checkout you want to test, with Bun 1.4.2 on PATH.
(
  set -eu
  checkout=$(pwd -P)
  cd "$(mktemp -d)"
  git init -q

  cat > cases.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
const active = process.env.GSTACK_SMOKE_SKIP ? test.skip : test;
active('quarantined case', () => expect(true).toBe(true));
test('ordinary case', () => expect(true).toBe(true));
EOF

  flaky() { bun "$checkout/bin/gstack-flaky" "$@"; }
  bun test --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=seed.xml
  id=$(flaky ids --runner bun --junit seed.xml | sed -n '/::quarantined case$/p')
  flaky quarantine add "$id" --owner smoke-test --class timing \
    --ledger https://example.org/fixture-ledger --evidence https://example.org/fixture-run \
    --reason 'Local synthetic reproduction' --junit seed.xml

  status=0
  GSTACK_SMOKE_SKIP=1 flaky run --runner bun --junit report.xml --ledger flaky.jsonl -- \
    bun test --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=report.xml || status=$?
  printf 'exit=%s\n' "$status"
)
```

FLAKY_RESULT: tests=2 failed=0 flaky=0 quarantined=0 reruns=0 command_exit=0 verdict=pass ledger=none

title: Fix #4550: a quarantined test skipped on the final attempt is a quarantined-fail
body:
A quarantined test that is skipped instead of running is now reported as a failure, so a skipped test can no longer look green.

Why: the quarantine rule is that a quarantined test still runs, but a skipped one was left out of the results entirely and the run stayed green.

Nothing to do.

## What changed

`gstack-flaky` left a quarantined test out of the results when it never ran, so the run exited 0 with `quarantined=0` and no written record. The same happened when a whole-command retry skipped it after a first-run pass, and the quarantine report then counted that run toward the clean streak.

The verdict now follows the test's final attempt: a skip on the final attempt is a `quarantined-fail`, and the run is red. A test that failed every attempt is still a hard break. A test skipped first but passing on the retry still counts as a pass, because it ran and passed on the attempt that decided the run. An ordinary skipped test still follows the runner's verdict.

`docs/flaky.md` now states the rule in one sentence.

## Tests

Four new tests cover the fix, two of which failed on the code before this change. The two affected test files pass (74 tests), the strict type check reports zero errors, and the test-code type check reports no new diagnostics. The full free suite was not run: the change touches only the flaky-run verdict path.

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Closes #4550.

Base: `main` @ `1bd86d9a4547ed8df0c5da37380c838e61a91b9b`, Bun 1.4.4.

Repro from #4550, before:

```text
(skip) quarantined case
(pass) ordinary case
FLAKY_RESULT: tests=2 failed=0 flaky=0 quarantined=0 reruns=0 command_exit=0 verdict=pass ledger=none
exit=0
```

After:

```text
FLAKY: quarantined-fail cases.test.ts::::quarantined case attempts=skip (quarantined, and skipped on the final attempt instead of running)
FLAKY_RESULT: tests=2 failed=1 flaky=0 quarantined=1 reruns=0 command_exit=0 verdict=fail ledger=flaky.jsonl
exit=1
```

Retry case, after:

```text
FLAKY: flaky-pass cases.test.ts::::ordinary case attempts=fail,pass
FLAKY: quarantined-fail cases.test.ts::::quarantined case attempts=pass,skip (quarantined, and skipped on the final attempt instead of running)
FLAKY_RESULT: tests=2 failed=1 flaky=1 quarantined=1 reruns=1 command_exit=1 verdict=fail ledger=flaky.jsonl
exit=1
```

The ledger records `{"kind":"quarantined-fail","id":"cases.test.ts::::quarantined case","attempts":["pass","skip"]}`, so `quarantine report` shows it as a fail and the clean streak resets.

Checks run: `bun test test/quarantine.test.ts test/flaky-run.test.ts` (74 pass), `bun run typecheck` (zero errors), `bun run typecheck:test` (812 known diagnostics, none new), `bun test test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts` (6 pass).

Scope: `lib/flaky-run.ts`, `test/quarantine.test.ts`, `test/flaky-run.test.ts`, `docs/flaky.md`. No change to `lib/quarantine.ts`: the report already treats a `quarantined-fail` ledger line as a fail.

</details>

title: Review read names the findings that owner rulings leave open (GST-3267)
body:
When owner rulings don't clear a stopped review, `gstack-review-read` now names each finding still missing a ruling (a `noted` CRITICAL included), and for a gate finding the `gate_id` its gate disposition needs. Why: on harness-evals#498 all 22 rulings applied, yet both rows stayed unverified because 7 duplicates were logged `noted` at CRITICAL, and nothing said so. Nothing to do: the review rules are unchanged; only the reason text gets more specific.
What changed ![The unverified reason now names the findings still waiting on an owner ruling, and the gate disposition a gate finding needs](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/T4vXob1HP2Pm24YUtj5VJRi0k66_2roo5LWabg3yk3Q.png) The unverified reason now names the findings still waiting on an owner ruling, and the gate disposition a gate finding needs. - `lib/review-evidence.ts`: new `rulingGap` explains a completed, stopped pass on unchanged content. It lists each finding that still holds the row open with no ruling, as ` (, )`, ten at most, or says the findings list fewer issues than the row claims. A gate finding also names its `gate_id` and says it needs a gate disposition, because a ruling never closes one. The ruling test is now one shared helper, so the listing and the clearing can't drift apart. - `bin/gstack-review-read`: appends that text to an UNVERIFIED reason. `reviewFreshness` and finish's `FIX_CHECK` lines are unchanged. - Docs: `docs/ship-policy.md#ruled-notes` and the open-findings entry in `docs/troubleshooting.md` say where the list appears, that a note never closes a CRITICAL, and what a gate finding needs.
Why A stopped review that the owner's rulings did not clear said only "incomplete/nonconverged pass", so whoever was shipping could not tell which findings still needed a ruling. On harness-evals#498 that cost a round of guessing: the seven noted CRITICAL duplicates were invisible.
Blast radius One reason string printed by `gstack-review-read`. No code compares that string, binding and refusal rules are unchanged, and only rows that already read UNVERIFIED get the longer text.
Test Coverage Coverage audit (audit only): 7 of 10 changed paths have a test. Open gaps, below the blocking floor: a gate finding the owner already dispositioned, unfingerprinted or malformed labels, and the row-shape guards (fix-range, a moved tree, `converged:true`).

Exploratory QA Four probes of `rulingGap` on owned fixtures: an unruled noted CRITICAL is named (pass), and a ruled gate finding is named with its `gate_id` (failed before the fix, passes after). The CLI path is covered by the tests, not probed separately.

title: Browse daemon skips port 10080, which Chromium refuses, and a process-census test stops flaking
body:
The browse daemon no longer picks port 10080, which Chromium refuses to open, so its welcome page can't fail with `net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT`. This fixes two flaky free tests at their cause: the xvfb welcome test and the paid-shard retention check. Nothing for the reader to do.
What changed - `browse/src/port-allocator.ts`: a random draw that lands on a port Chromium blocks (`CHROMIUM_UNSAFE_PORTS`, from `kRestrictedPorts` in Chromium's `net/base/port_util.cc`; 10080 is the only one inside 10000-49151) is drawn again. Explicit `BROWSE_PORT` values are unchanged. - `test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts`: a new test covers a same-user process that denies its fd table and exits during the census. It fails against main's helper and passes here. - `ARCHITECTURE.md`: the port-selection paragraph says a draw on 10080 is redrawn. - `changelog.d/flaky-fix-2026-11-20-port-and-census.md`: the release-note fragment. - `test/helpers/bootstrap-retention.ts`: when the process census at scope creation gets `EACCES`/`EPERM` on a same-user process and that process has already exited, it skips it instead of throwing. A live uninspectable process is still recorded as before, and every other error still throws. Skipping can only shorten the tolerated list, so the later quiet check is as strict as before.
Evidence - Free Tests 44539190714 (main 17303862), `browse/test/xvfb.test.ts` "welcome: startup settles welcome before publishing daemon readiness": the daemon log tail printed `Failed to navigate to welcome page: goto: net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT at http://127.0.0.1:10080/welcome`. The new allocator test is red on main (`Expected: not 10080`) and green here. - Free Tests 44548125960 (PR #4527 @ 2c676250), `test/bootstrap-retention-shard.test.ts` "ack-failure preserves the real attempt through runner cleanup": the controller exited 1 with `EACCES: permission denied, readlink '/proc/60805/cwd'` at `createBootstrapRetentionScope` (bootstrap-retention.ts:158). Stress repro (8 loops forking children that call `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` and exit, while creating 3,000 scopes): main 9 of 3,000 failed (4 readlink cwd, 5 scandir fd); this branch 0 of 3,000. - Focused: `terminal-agent-port-range` + `findport` 16/16; `bootstrap-retention` + `bootstrap-retention-shard` 40/40; typecheck clean.

The doc-sync eval fixture now allows /ship's one free format repair, so `ship-docsync-current` no longer fails when the audit child drops one field from its result line. This fixes a flaky paid eval at its cause: the fixture's command list was missing the two commands /ship's documentation step uses for that repair. Nothing to do.
What changed The `ship-docsync-current` eval sometimes went red with "completion fields: missing documentation_section". The audit child had done its job, but its last line dropped one field. /ship answers that with a free format repair (`gstack-docs-candidate repair-prompt`, then `result --repair-of`), and the eval's fixture refused both commands, so the parent correctly stopped. The fixture now allows exactly those two command shapes, and the eval accepts a repaired line only after `result --repair-of` printed `FORMAT_REPAIR: applied` for that dispatch's own audit id. The repair agent is not counted as another writer dispatch.
Evidence - E2E Evals gate/full census 44432023197 paid-slice-4-a1 (main f79a8905), `ship-docsync-current` red on `completion fields: missing documentation_section; extra none`, in-run rerun green. The child audited correctly (docs current), but its last line had no `documentation_section`; `result` printed `FORMAT_REPAIR: format-only`, and the parent stopped blocked because the fixture did not allow `repair-prompt` (its own report says so). - `test/fixtures/docsync-format-repair-public.json` replays that capture: the recorded red reproduces, the product classes it as repairable (`checkDocsResult`), and a reply `checkDocsRepair` accepts stands for the attempt. Negative controls stay red: no `result --repair-of`, a refused repair, an applied line from a plain `result`, a repair before its result, and a repair after a second dispatch. A repair prompt quoting `document-release/SKILL.md` is still not a dispatch. - Grammar: 4 admitted shapes, 15 refused (missing or reordered flags, repo or skills paths, relative paths, duplicate flags, extra flags, tilde path). Both new tests are red with main's observer and contract and green here. - The interface text change reaches every doc-sync paid case; this PR's E2E Evals run is their paid proof.
Why The paid gate should fail only on real regressions. This case was red on census 44432023197 and green on its in-run rerun, so it was a fixture gap, not a product bug.
Blast radius Only test code changes. That is the doc-sync fixture interface, its command observer and the eval's contract helper, which are used by the 13 `ship-docsync-*` paid cases and two free test files. No product code, prompt, threshold, trial count or case kind changed (read in `git diff origin/main`; the free tests below ran).
Pre-Landing Review Two findings, both fixed. A testing reader noted that the repair check did not tie an applied repair to its own dispatch, so it now requires the result call's audit id to match that dispatch. A second-model reader then found that this check kept shell quotes on the audit id, so a quoted id would make a real repair look not applied. The check now splits arguments the way the fixture's command grammar does, and a quoted case was added. A narrower second read of those two fixes found nothing more.

It holds committed changes only, with nothing staged, unstaged or new. Its line citations for the ship-docsync cases still match the code. - `docs/TEST_PORTFOLIO.md`: current. No docsync case or file was renamed. - `docs/pregate.md`: current. It has no reference to the changed behavior. - `changelog.d/docsync-eval-format-repair.md`: current. It matches the diff. **Coverage debt:** none. title: Review reads only the tagged lines of data files the gate scan flags by content (GST-3273)
body:
Results PRs that commit captured agent sessions can now be reviewed: when the gate scan tags a data file only because a session quotes a lint pragma, an env check or a `--no-verify` push, readers get those lines with context instead of the whole file. Why: harness-evals#494 stopped at the 2 MB review limit because 25 such transcripts (11.4 MB) went to readers whole, and the only fix printed was "split the PR". Nothing to do: code files, files tagged by their path and files whose tag spans lines still go whole, and the gate review still runs.
What changed - `gstack-review-plan` reads which tagged files have every tag on a single added line outside the gate floor (`gateScanPaths`), and `lib/review-exclude.ts` excerpts a kept `gate-tagged` file when it is row data, results or preregistration JSON, a `.log` or declared data, kept for no other reason, not renamed and not named by code. Its keep reason, the record's `gate_tagged` list and the review class are unchanged. - The excerpt (`lib/review-secret-excerpt.ts`) adds every line `lineTags` (new in `lib/gate-diff/tags.ts`, the floor-free half of `tagHunk`) tags, under its own "Gate-tagged data excerpts" heading that names the tags; secret-line files render byte for byte as before. A file with no tagged line found, or a long tagged line with no span to show, goes whole. - `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE` gains a `files=` field and its "split the PR" fix names the largest files. - Docs: ship-policy.md#gate-tagged-data-excerpts, review-policy.md, troubleshooting.md; changelog fragment.
Tests `test/review-gate-excerpt.test.ts`, written first and red on main bd04289 (`REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE` at 3,150,647 bytes): twelve synthetic 230 KB sessions with three tagged lines each now fit, every tagged line reaches the excerpt, and a `.ts` file with the same pragma, a path-tagged snapshot and a log whose tag spans two lines stay whole. A second case checks the over-limit error names its largest files; a unit case covers `gateScanPaths`. All synthetic data.

title: browse: `eval <file>` path sandbox is not in browse/SKILL.md (only in BROWSER.md)
body:
**gstack version:** v1.102.0.0 (main bd042897)

## What happened

`browse/SKILL.md` (line 244) advertises `$B eval <file>` as the way to run multi-line JS. It does not say that the file must live under the system temp dir or the daemon's working directory. A helper script kept in a persistent location (for example a per-project scripts folder under `~/.gstack/projects/...`) fails with:

```
Path must be within: /private/tmp, /var/folders/.../T, <daemon cwd>
```

The message is accurate, but a wrapper that cuts the output (`$B eval f.js | tail -1`) shows only the daemon's "N consecutive failures" notice and an empty result, so the cause is easy to miss. The rule is documented in `BROWSER.md` (lines 501 and 1585: "path under /tmp or cwd") but agents read `browse/SKILL.md`, not `BROWSER.md`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `echo 'document.title' > ~/some-persistent-dir/t.js`
2. `$B eval ~/some-persistent-dir/t.js`
3. Output: `Path must be within: ...` (see above). Copying the file to `/tmp` makes the same call work.

## Suggested fix

One line next to the `eval` row in `browse/SKILL.md.tmpl`: "`eval` reads only files under the system temp directory or the daemon's cwd (`Path must be within: ...`); copy persistent scripts to a temp path first."

title: browse: running `$B` from a different directory silently starts a second daemon without the session
body:
**gstack version:** v1.102.0.0 (main bd042897)

## What happened

The daemon is selected by the git root of the current directory (`browse/src/config.ts:72`, `projectDir = getGitRoot() || process.cwd()`; state in `<project>/.gstack/browse.json`). This is described in `BROWSER.md` ("Multi-workspace isolation") but not in `browse/SKILL.md`, and nothing warns at runtime. Two ways to lose a logged-in session without noticing:

1. A helper script is started with `cd <some other dir> && bash script.sh`. `$B` prints `[browse] Starting server...`, opens a fresh headless browser on `about:blank`, and every later call runs against an empty page (`sessionId is not defined`, JSON parse errors). The same script run from the repo directory works.
2. In the middle of a session the working directory is moved into a nested repository (for example `cd vendor/<pkg>` for a grep; that folder has its own `.git`). The next `$B` call starts a new daemon, the PID changes, the URL is `about:blank`, and the logged-in tab is gone. It showed up only later as `Ext is not defined` in the page.

In both cases the only signal is one line on stderr that is easy to lose in a longer script.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In repo A: `$B goto https://example.com`, then `$B status` (note the PID).
2. `cd /some/other/repo-or-non-repo && $B status`
3. A new server is started (`[browse] Starting server...`), PID and URL differ; repo A's daemon and tab are untouched but no longer addressed.

## Suggested fix (any of these, smallest first)

- Docs: in `browse/SKILL.md` "Find the $B binary"/browser fallback, add: "The daemon is bound to the git root of the current directory. Run scripts that call `$B` from the project directory (absolute script path, no `cd`). `[browse] Starting server...` in the middle of a session means the session is gone."
- Runtime: when a command other than `goto`/`status`/`stop` auto-starts a server and another daemon of the same user is alive in a different project root, print a one-line warning naming that root.
- `$B status` could print the project root it resolved, so a PID or root change is visible.

title: `/context-restore` transcript fallback ignores `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; head check misses work outside the checkout's own repo
body:
**gstack version:** v1.102.0.0 (main bd042897)

## What happened

**1. Transcript fallback only looks under `$HOME/.claude`.** `context-restore/sections/transcripts.md` (Step T1) builds the directory as

```bash
TRANSCRIPT_DIR="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(printf '%s' "$PROJECT_ROOT" | sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g')"
```

(also the table row on line 16). With a second Claude profile started with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work`, Claude Code writes transcripts to `~/.claude-work/projects/<slug>/`. The fallback then prints `TRANSCRIPTS: none (... is missing; this workspace has no Claude Code transcripts)` although the transcripts exist, and Step T3 continues with git alone. `bin/gstack-claude-root.sh` already resolves `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}`; this file does not use it.

**2. The post-save check only sees commits of one repo.** The `HEAD_MOVED`/`HEAD_UNTRACKED` check (`context-restore/SKILL.md.tmpl`, "Check whether the branch moved since the save") compares the saved `head:` with the current repo. Work done after the save is missed when:

- the checkpoint has no `head:` because the project root is not a git repo (a monorepo root that holds many independent clones) - the skill prints `HEAD_UNTRACKED` and every Remaining Work item stays "Next steps";
- `branch:`/`worktree:` names a different repo than the one the restore runs in;
- the work was recorded in files listed under `files_modified:` (a plan document, notes) rather than in a commit.

In a real case, items listed as open in a checkpoint had been finished and committed in several sibling clones the next day; the restore presented them as still to do.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Claude with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a non-default directory, work in a project, then `/clear`.
2. In a project with no checkpoint: `/context-restore`. Step T1 prints `TRANSCRIPTS: none (~/.claude/projects/<slug> is missing ...)` although `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl` exists.
3. For item 2: save a checkpoint in a non-git folder, commit in a nested clone, then `/context-restore`: `HEAD_UNTRACKED`, no hint of the later commits.

## Suggested fix

1. `TRANSCRIPT_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/..."` (and the table row); ideally also check `$HOME/.claude` as a second candidate.
2. Small and cheap: report a `files_modified:` entry whose mtime is newer than the checkpoint as "changed after the save" and list those items under Verify first; when `branch:`/`worktree:` points to another repo, run the head check there.
