title: `gstack-checks detect` / `/verify`: PHP repos with PHPUnit/Pest tests report "CHECKS: none ... nothing to run" (also for packages inside a monorepo)
body:
**gstack version:** v1.102.0.0 (main bd042897; first seen on v1.99.2.0, Claude Code host, `~/.claude/skills/gstack`)

## What happened

In a PHP repository with `phpunit.xml`, `composer.json` requiring `pestphp/pest`, and test files under `tests/`, `gstack-checks detect` (used by `/verify` step 1) prints:

```
CHECKS: none (no gstack:verify: line, Health Stack section, manifest check, pregate policy or test file); nothing to run
```

and exits 0. `gstack-checks run` exits 3 with the same line. The tests exist and pass or fail when run by hand, so `/verify` never runs them. In my case a test for the changed class was red; only a manual run found it. The message says there is no "test file", which is wrong here: it reports a detector gap as "nothing to run".

Two variants of the same gap:

1. **Plain PHP repo** (repro below).
2. **Package clone inside a monorepo.** Each package is its own git repo; the folder above holds `vendor/bin/pest` and `phpunit.xml` and has no `.git`. `detect` runs at the package's git root (`bin/gstack-checks:40`, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and `CLAUDE.md` is read only from that root (`lib/checks.ts:125`). Result: `CHECKS: none`, even when the diff adds a new `tests/.../FooTest.php`. Same in a git worktree of such a package. A "none" here says something about the search radius, not about the tests.

Related: #4346 / PR #4358 improve the wording of the `CHECKS: none` report; this issue is about detection itself, so that line should not be reached for PHP projects.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir php-demo && cd php-demo && git init -q -b main
cat > composer.json <<'JSON'
{ "require-dev": { "pestphp/pest": "^1.23" } }
JSON
cat > phpunit.xml <<'XML'
<phpunit bootstrap="tests/Pest.php"><testsuites><testsuite name="all"><directory>tests</directory></testsuite></testsuites></phpunit>
XML
mkdir -p tests/Unit src
echo '<?php' > tests/Pest.php
echo '<?php test("example", fn () => expect(true)->toBeTrue());' > tests/Unit/ExampleTest.php
echo '<?php class Foo {}' > src/Foo.php
git add -A && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.com commit -qm init
git clone -q --bare . ../php-demo.git && git remote add origin ../php-demo.git \
  && git fetch -q origin && git remote set-head origin main   # detect needs a resolvable origin/main
echo '// change' >> src/Foo.php
~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-checks detect
```

**Expected:** a PHP test check is detected (`vendor/bin/pest` or `vendor/bin/phpunit`), or at least the output says "tests exist but no runner was recognised".

**Actual:** the `CHECKS: none (...) nothing to run` line above.

Monorepo variant: move the repo to `mono/pkg/`, put `phpunit.xml` (and a `vendor/bin/pest`) in `mono/` without a `.git`, add a new `tests/BarTest.php` to the diff, run `detect` in `mono/pkg`: still `CHECKS: none`.

## Cause (from reading the source at main bd042897)

- `bin/gstack-checks:93-94`: `nothingToRun(l)` true -> prints the `NONE` line.
- `lib/checks.ts:297-299`: `nothingToRun` is true when there are no checks, no pregate policy and `selectLanes(l.ctx).localTests` is empty.
- `lib/checks.ts:95-122` (`manifestChecks`): reads `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml` and `go.mod`. No `composer.json` / `phpunit.xml` branch.
- `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:34` (`TEST_FILE_RE`): no PHP pattern; `tests/Unit/ExampleTest.php` matches nothing, so pregate selects zero tests.
- `lib/checks.ts:149` (`/health` detection via `healthStack`) has the same shape: no PHP entry.
- `lib/checks.ts:125`: `CLAUDE.md` is read only from the detected repo root, never from a parent folder.

## Suggested fix

1. Detect `phpunit.xml` / `phpunit.xml.dist` plus `vendor/bin/pest` (if `pestphp/pest` is in `composer.json`) or `vendor/bin/phpunit`, as a `test` check in `manifestChecks` (and in `/health`).
2. Add `*Test.php` under `tests/` to the test-file pattern, so pregate can select tests for changed PHP files.
3. When a repo has files that look like tests (`tests/**`, `*Test.php`) but detect finds no runner, print something like `CHECKS: none (tests found under tests/ but no runner recognised; declare one with a gstack:verify: line)` instead of "nothing to run". Absence of a recognised runner is not absence of tests.
4. Many PHP projects run tests inside a container (`docker exec ... vendor/bin/pest`). The existing `gstack:verify:` declaration covers that; the NONE message could point to it.
5. Monorepo packages: when `detect` finds nothing in a repo root that has no `gstack:verify:` line, also read `CLAUDE.md` (and look for `phpunit.xml`) in parent folders and report the commands as `SOURCE claude-md` (untrusted until confirmed, like today). Alternative: document a `.gstack/pregate.json` per package clone that points at the parent's runner.

## Workaround

A line in the repo-root `CLAUDE.md` (`lib/checks.ts:54`, `declaredVerify`), for example:

```
gstack:verify: vendor/bin/pest --configuration phpunit.xml
```

(or in a container: `gstack:verify: docker exec -w /app mycontainer vendor/bin/pest`), then `gstack-checks trust` once. With this line `detect` prints `CHECK verify ... (CLAUDE.md gstack:verify:)` instead of the NONE line. In the monorepo case the line has to be repeated in every package clone.

title: `/gstack-upgrade` "Not now": snooze is keyed by version on a four-field `UPGRADE_AVAILABLE` line, so the prompt returns
body:
**gstack version:** v1.102.0.0 (main bd042897)

## What happened

`UPGRADE_AVAILABLE 1.102.0.0 1.102.0.0+2 bd04289` (four fields, main moved without a VERSION bump). The skill's "Not now" snippet (`gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md.tmpl:55-72`) writes `"$_REMOTE_VER $_NEW_LEVEL $(date +%s)"` with `_REMOTE_VER="{new}"`; the instruction to use the SHA (fourth field) for `{new}` is one prose sentence under the snippet. The snoozing session used the third field, and `~/.gstack/update-snoozed` contained `1.102.0.0+2 1 <ts>`. `bin/gstack-update-check` derives its key with `_snooze_key` (line 137: `NF >= 4 ? $4 : $3`) and compares it with the first column, so it never matched, and the upgrade question came back about 2 hours after "Not now" (snooze is 24 h at level 1).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Get a four-field `UPGRADE_AVAILABLE <old> <old>+<n> <sha>` line (main ahead of the last release).
2. Answer "Not now" and let the agent fill `{new}` from the line (it can pick field 2, 3 or 4).
3. Next skill start: the prompt reappears although the snooze file exists.

## Suggested fix

The writer should not re-derive the key from prose; the reader already has the logic. Add a verb that does both, for example `gstack-update-check --snooze "<UPGRADE_AVAILABLE line>"` (or `gstack-config snooze ...`), which calls `_snooze_key`, bumps the level (1 -> 2 -> 3) and writes the file. The skill then runs one command instead of the shell block. Until then, in the snippet replace `{new}` with a shell derivation from the raw line (`echo "$LINE" | awk '{print (NF>=4 ? $4 : $3)}'`).

title: `/gstack-upgrade` Step 5: `rm -f "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT"/...` is rejected by Claude Code's safety check when bundled in a shell wrapper
body:
**gstack version:** v1.99.5.0 -> v1.102.0.0 (template unchanged at main bd042897, `gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md.tmpl:361-363`)

## What happened

Steps 4.5 to 5 of the skill were run as one `/bin/bash -c '...'` call (a wrapper to avoid zsh differences). Step 5 contains

```bash
GSTACK_STATE_ROOT=$(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-paths --get GSTACK_STATE_ROOT); ...
rm -f "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT"/last-update-check
rm -f "$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT"/update-snoozed
```

Claude Code's built-in command safety check cannot inspect an `rm` inside a `-c` script and treats a variable target as a possible recursive delete of the root, so it refused the whole call. In auto mode no prompt reached the user and the entire block (including the migrations in it) did not run. The same step issued as its own call with literal paths (`rm -f ~/.gstack/last-update-check ...` spelled out as an absolute path) ran without objection.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `/gstack-upgrade` on a Claude Code host and bundle the shell blocks of Steps 4.5-5 into one `/bin/bash -c '...'` call.
2. The call is refused at the `rm` with a variable path.

## Suggested fix

- Add a helper so no `rm` with a variable path is needed in the skill, for example `gstack-config clear-update-cache` (removes `last-update-check` and `update-snoozed` under the state root and writes `just-upgraded-from`).
- Or document in Step 5: resolve `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT` first (read-only call), then run the deletion as a separate call with the literal path, not inside a wrapper.

title: `/gstack-upgrade`: `./setup --refresh-registered` registers new hooks in one settings.json only; the summary reports all installs as updated
body:
**gstack version:** v1.99.5.0 -> v1.102.0.0 (hooks default on in 1.102.0.0)

## What happened

Two Claude profiles are in use: `~/.claude` (default) and a second one started with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work`. Both have a registered gstack install (`~/.claude/skills` global and `~/.claude-work/skills`). 1.102.0.0 turns three helper hooks on by default (skill routing / `UserPromptSubmit`, skill contracts / `Stop`, destructive guard / `PreToolUse` Bash). `./setup --refresh-registered` listed both installs as `updated` in the Upgrade summary, but wrote the three hook entries (and the `settings.json.bak.<ts>` backups) only to `~/.claude/settings.json`. `~/.claude-work/settings.json` stayed unchanged, so that profile ran without the hooks and the summary gave no hint.

Reading the source: `bin/gstack-settings-hook:88` picks `SETTINGS_FILE=${GSTACK_SETTINGS_FILE:-${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json}` from the environment of the running setup, so one run edits one profile's file, while `--refresh-registered` refreshes every registered install. A later `gstack-config set <hook> off` presumably removes the entry in the same single file only (not tested).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have two profiles, each with a registered gstack install (`installs.tsv` lists both).
2. From the default profile: `/gstack-upgrade` to a version that adds default-on hooks.
3. Compare `~/.claude/settings.json` and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json` of the second profile: only the first has the new `_gstack_source` entries. The summary says both installs were updated.

## Suggested fix

- In the `Upgrade summary`, add per Claude install the settings file whose hooks were registered, and `hooks: not registered here` for installs whose profile dir differs from the one setup used (with the retry command `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> ./setup --refresh-registered`).
- Or loop over the registered Claude installs and register hooks in each profile's settings file, since the install already knows its profile dir.
- Do not mirror silently: hook registration should stay an explicit, opt-out step per profile.

title: Stop the prompt-routing hook from routing on words inside backticks
body: The prompt-routing hook no longer routes a prompt because of words inside backticks or code blocks; only the prose around them can match a trigger. Why: a tool that wakes a session with "Run ` … check …`" got a /verify hint on every message, and "Run `gh pr review 123`" got a /review hint. Nothing to do: "run the checks", "verify my change" and other prose requests route as before, on Claude Code and Codex. ## Why (in your own words) I run Claude Code sessions as workers under a coordinator. The coordinator wakes a session by typing one line into it, for example: ``` You have 1 orchestration message. Run ` orchestration check --run run_ --terminal term_`. ``` With `skill_routing` on (the default since 1.101), every one of these lines got `this request fits /verify. Run /verify with the Skill tool before you start`. In a coordinator session that happens dozens of times a day, and the model has to decide each time to ignore an instruction from gstack. Nothing in the line asks for checks. "run" comes from the prose, and "check" is a subcommand inside the code span, so the two content words of the `/verify` trigger "run the checks" are both "present" and the trigger scores 1.0. Related, but a separate cause: #4423 (messages from other sessions routed as if a person asked). This PR doesn't detect injected messages. It fixes the narrower rule that applies to typed prompts too: a command quoted in backticks is not a request in words. ## Live evidence Same prompt, same installed skills (`~/.claude/skills`), dry run with `gstack-skill-route --explain`: **Installed 1.102.0.0:** ``` candidates: 1.00 /verify "run the checks" (2 words, gstack) 0.50 /review "check my diff" (1 words, gstack) route: /verify hint: gstack skill routing (UserPromptSubmit hook; matched the installed /verify trigger "run the checks"; ...): this request fits /verify. Run /verify with the Skill tool before you start, ... ``` **This branch:** ``` candidates: (none) route: none (below-threshold) ``` Counter-checks on this branch: `run the checks` → `route: /verify`; ``verify my change in `src/app.ts` `` → `route: /verify`; ``Run `gh pr review 123 --approve` once CI is done.`` → `route: none` (on 1.102: `/review` via "review this pr"). The new test was red before the fix, on the first prompt: ``` (fail) scorer > words inside inline code or a fenced code block never match a trigger; the prose around them still routes - [], + [ + "verify", + ], ``` Every negative case routed before the fix, checked one by one against the real `/review`, `/qa` and `/verify` triggers: ``` "You have 1 orchestration message. Run ` orchestration check --run …`." -> verify (run the checks) "Run `gh pr review 123 --approve` once CI is done." -> review (review this pr) "Run ``tool lint check --fix`` and paste the output." -> verify (run the checks) "Pasted from CI:\n```\n$ make check\nall tests pass\n```\nWhat does this output mean?" -> verify (make the tests pass) ``` ## Scope - **Changed:** - `lib/skill-route.ts`: - A new function, `proseText`, blanks out Markdown code as CommonMark reads it. That covers fenced blocks (``` or ~~~, closed by a fence of the same character that is at least as long; an unclosed fence runs to the end) and inline code spans (a backtick run closed by a run of the same length; an unmatched backtick stays text). - `scorePrompt` and the find-bugs phrase check in `routePrompt` score `promptWindow(proseText(prompt))`. - `bugReport` still reads the raw prompt, because an exception name in backticks (`` `ValueError` ``) is evidence of a bug report. - Codex: `hosts/codex/hooks/codex-skill-route-hook.ts` calls the same `routePrompt`, so it gets the fix with no change. The test asserts both hosts. - `test/skill-route.test.ts`: one test with four prompts that must not route (the wake-up line, `gh pr review` in a span, a double-backtick span, a fenced CI paste) and six that must still route to /verify (plain prose, prose next to code, an unclosed backtick). - `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`: one bullet on the rule. - `changelog.d/fix-skill-route-ignores-code-spans.md`: the changelog fragment. - **Verified live by:** the `--explain` runs above on macOS (Apple Silicon, Bun 1.4.4). `bun test test/skill-route.test.ts test/codex-hooks.test.ts` has 56 passing tests. That includes the 60 plain prompts and the B1 in-sample set, unchanged. `bun run typecheck` is clean, and `bun run typecheck:test` reports none new. - **Full free suite:** `bun run test` exits 1 on this machine both on this branch and on an untouched `upstream/main` checkout (bd0428974): 92 test files red on the branch, 101 on main. That's shared-HOME and concurrency noise across the pre-PR checks, cso, update-check and other suites, and no skill-route file is among them. Two files were red only on the branch run, `shard-engine-equivalence` and `strict-output-formats`. Run alone, they pass on the branch and fail on main, so they're flaky here. CI is the judge for the full suite. - **Did NOT test:** - The paid evals (`skill-routing-e2e`). The hint text is unchanged; only which prompts get it. - Linux and Windows. - **Known limit:** a bare shell command with no backticks ("Run tool check now") still matches. Without Markdown there is no reliable line between a command and prose, so that case belongs with #4423's question of telling injected messages apart. ## Liveness proof (required for external contributors) ## Checklist - [x] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is `@garrytan` (owner exemption) - [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated) - [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references - [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A) - [x] Linked issue or reproduction: reproduction above; related #4423 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: /ship stops instead of running the whole test suite here when CI's run can't be reused (GST-3277)
body:
`gstack-ship-preflight` now stops with `SHIP_LANE_NOT_CARRIED` whenever a test suite mapped to CI has no reusable CI run, in a full preflight as well as `--tests-only`; `--run-uncarried-here` still runs it here. Why: a full preflight on gbrain-evals#547 ran the whole suite locally for 7 minutes after CI's run went stale, and the stop told an outside-author PR to dispatch a workflow that has no `workflow_dispatch` trigger. Nothing to do: a workflow that can't be dispatched now gets "merge the base and push it, or ask the author to" instead. ## What changed A /ship run on gbrain-evals#547 spent 7 minutes running the whole test suite on a small machine because CI's run no longer matched the tree, and the stop it printed suggested a `gh workflow run` the workflow could not accept. Now every preflight, full or `--tests-only`, stops before any test suite mapped to CI runs when CI's run can't be reused, whatever the reason. The stop names a route that works. It says to dispatch the workflow when it takes `workflow_dispatch`, and otherwise to merge the base and push it (or ask the pull request's author to). After a full preflight, the stop says to rerun with `--tests-only`, because rerunning the same full command with `--run` would stop on its own open run. `--run-uncarried-here` is accepted in both modes and still runs the suite here. ## Why Running the full suite locally can take most of an hour on a 4-CPU machine, and CI already runs it. The stop keeps that work in CI and gives advice that works on outside pull requests. ## Blast radius The change touches `gstack-ship-preflight`'s test step, the CI-reuse fix text in `lib/run-evidence.ts` and the CI-reuse lookup, and `gstack-pregate clear`'s run check. The dispatch check only reads workflow files from git and changes advice text, never whether a CI run is reused (lib/pregate/workflows.ts:231 read; both new tests and test/ship-ci-carry.test.ts ran). ## Test Coverage Coverage: 9 of 13 new paths covered (69%), every covered path at two stars or better. Tests: 1838 → 1838 (+0 new by the audit; the PR adds one new test file for this stop). Regression proof: fails at HEAD: yes (2 of 2 assertion failures on pre-fix code) · passes at base: unavailable (the test is new) · passes after fix: yes. Gaps, as proposed tests: no_tests wording on a profile that can't be dispatched; `gstack-pregate clear`'s dispatch wiring; mixed dispatchable and push-only profiles in one stop; a test suite that isn't mapped to CI still runs in a full preflight. Tests ran: test 1719 (files; 38505 tests) from CI run 44768253420. ## Pre-Landing Review One fix: a full preflight's stop said "rerun this command", which with `--run` stops again on the run's own open marker. It now points to the `--tests-only` rerun (41e5602). A scoped re-review of the fix found nothing blocking. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL CI-reuse lookup (line 84) The dispatch check runs once per candidate run inside the loop. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/workflows.ts:231` An unreadable ref or workflow reads as not dispatchable; a reusable workflow whose caller takes `workflow_dispatch` gets push-only advice. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-preflight.ts:238` The push-only NEXT line drops "commit this tree". - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-preflight.ts:310` A full preflight no longer falls back to running the suite here; profiles that accept only `pull_request` on a fast-moving base rely on `--run-uncarried-here`. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-preflight.ts:236` The `--tests-only` rerun hint names the base and the test-suite flags but not `--policy-from`, `--timeout`, `--step-timeout` or the concurrency flag. - INFORMATIONAL The new test (line 84): the push-only NEXT line is asserted only under `--tests-only`. - INFORMATIONAL `ship/sections/tests.md.tmpl:34` The skill text says to rerun with `--run-uncarried-here` without naming `--tests-only`. ## Exploratory QA Functional smoke, 2 probes, both pass: `bin/gstack-ship-preflight --help` documents the full-preflight stop and flag; the read-only CI-reuse lookup on this repo accepted CI run 44757538558 at the first head. The stop paths are covered by the new tests rather than a live probe, since a live refused preflight with a test suite could start the suite on the QA machine. ## Eval Results No PR evals selected: the selector maps the changed libraries to scheduled and release coverage, and CI's eval route skipped eval slices. ## Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN ## TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR. ## Documentation **Scope:** The audit covered the GST-3277 branch diff against base bd04289 at tree eff71ef40bd209fc458fdde0055d99ecdd93f710. The working tree was clean, with no staged, unstaged or new files. The diff changes how `gstack-ship-preflight` behaves: a full preflight now stops with SHIP_LANE_NOT_CARRIED, gives advice when a run can't be dispatched, and suggests rerunning with `--tests-only`. I checked docs/pregate.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and ship/sections/tests.md (and its .tmpl) against lib/ship-preflight.ts, lib/pregate/workflows.ts and the preflight help text. **Result:** Current. Every doc the code change touches already matches it, so I edited no files. A search across the whole repo found no leftover description of the old full-preflight behavior. title: Prompt-routing hook ignores words inside backticks (#4564)
body:
The prompt-routing hook no longer acts on words inside backticks or code blocks, so a prompt that quotes a command (`Run `mycli check` now`) stops getting a wrong "run /verify" or "run /review" line.
Why: routing is on by default, so any session that quotes commands got these hints; this fixes the report in #4564 by @vilano93, rebuilt on current main.
Nothing to do: plain requests ("run the checks", "review this pr", bug reports in words) route as before.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Before: a prompt that only quotes a command in backticks was told to run /verify. After: it routes nowhere.](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/OfpFBn7hBprCn4yAQ9Hjt0J7nv7oPR1N8jU6uo8fOsY.png)

Before: a prompt that only quotes a command in backticks was told to run /verify. After: it routes nowhere.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun --no-env-file test test/skill-route.test.ts`: 31 pass, 0 fail, 331 expect() calls
- [x] `bun run typecheck`: clean
- [x] Full free suite in CI (free-tests run 44776960088 at this tree): green, 1718 test files

</details>

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Before: a prompt that only quotes a command in backticks was told to run /verify. After: it routes nowhere.</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
@@ ⋯ 1 unchanged ⋯ @@
 threshold: 0.66
 skills: 65 scanned in /home/user/.claude/skills
 candidates:
+  (none)
+route: none (below-threshold)
-  1.00  /verify  "run the checks" (2 words, gstack)
-  0.50  /review  "check my diff" (1 words, gstack)
-route: /verify
-hint: gstack skill routing (UserPromptSubmit hook; matched the installed /verify trigger "run the checks"; off: gstack-config set skill_routing off): this request fits /verify. Run /verify with the Skill tool before you start, and tell the user in one sentence that gstack routed this to /verify.
 
~~~

People quote commands in backticks all the time, and the routing hook read those words as a request: "Run `gh pr review 123`" was told to run /review, and a `--fix` flag or the word broken in a pasted log made a prompt look like a bug report. The hook now splits a prompt into prose and Markdown code the way CommonMark reads it (inline code spans, fenced blocks with backticks or tildes) and matches triggers and bug-report signs on the prose only. One sign still reads the code, since an exception name such as `KeyError` or a pasted traceback still marks a bug report. The split takes a single pass over the prompt, so even a prompt near the hook's 256 KB input limit that is full of stray backticks is handled in milliseconds, well inside the hook's 1.5 second deadline. Claude Code and Codex share the same code, and the docs and changelog say what changed.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Run `mycli check` now" should not be told to run /verify (#4564). With routing on by default, every session that quotes a command could get a wrong skill hint; now only the words around the code decide where a prompt goes.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `lib/skill-route.ts` changed in product code; its callers are the Claude Code and Codex routing hooks and `gstack-skill-route --explain`, which all read the same `routePrompt` result shape. That is safe because a prompt without backticks or fences takes the same path as before (repro: the full routing test file passes on both hosts, and the new single-pass split matched the earlier regex on 500,000 random strings in two separate fuzz runs).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two findings in the first review, both below the blocking floor and fixed in 5760b4d: a reviewer finding whose details are recorded privately, and a test gap (no test for a traceback inside a fenced block, and none showing a helper name such as `handleError` in code is not a bug report), now covered. A follow-up read of the fix found nothing. A second-model adversarial read of the final tree raised four low notes, none blocking; they are listed below.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:272` CRLF prompts: FENCE and PARAGRAPH_BREAK do not see \r\n line endings, so a stray backtick can pair across paragraphs and leave prose out of routing (the hint fails open).
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:290` An unclosed fence or a ~~~~~~~~ separator line sends the rest of the prompt to code; matches CommonMark and the documented behavior.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:297` A backslash-escaped backtick opens a code span here, while CommonMark treats it as a literal backtick; a few prose words can be left out of routing.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:355` splitCode runs over the whole prompt three times per route (scorePrompt, bugReport, routePrompt); bounded by the 256 KB stdin cap, about 53 ms on 100 KB worst case.

title: /cso audits repositories that track symlinks, without following them (#4540)
body:
`/cso` no longer stops on a repository that tracks a symlink, such as gstack's own `connect-chrome` or `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md`: each link is listed in the report by its target string, or as withheld when the target matches a secret pattern, and it is never followed. Why: a security audit that refuses ordinary repositories audits nothing, and following a link would let it point the scanner at `/etc/passwd` or out through `..`. Nothing to do. FIFOs, sockets and devices are still refused, and `--paths` now limits that check to the audited directories.
What changed Running `/cso` on almost any real repository used to fail with `UNSAFE_PATH` the moment it met one symlink; 5 of 8 mid-size open-source repositories we measured stopped there. Now `lib/cso/snapshot.ts` reads each tracked or nonignored link with `lstat` and `readlink` only, binds it by device, inode, mode and target bytes, and records it as an exclusion that names its target and says, from the text alone, whether it is absolute, escapes the repository, or names a path inside it. Nothing stats, resolves or opens through a link, so a link to `/etc/passwd`, `/dev/null`, a `..` escape, a loop or a dangling link is reported and never read, and links never enter the execution snapshot. A target that matches any secret pattern, whole or in any path segment, is withheld and no path derived from it is shown. A comparison base hashes a link as Git does (mode `120000`, blob of the target), so `--diff` sees a retargeted link. A link changed during capture fails as `SNAPSHOT_RACE`. The special-file walk now descends only into the `--paths` scope. The troubleshooting page, the changelog entry and TODOS.md describe the new behavior; thanks to @nathanshox for the report and first fix (#4540).
Why record instead of resolving inside the root The outside PR (#4540) resolved each link with `realpath` and `stat` and admitted it when the result stayed inside the repository. That is safe only if the resolution itself is: it follows every hop on the live filesystem, can touch an automounter or FUSE target while deciding, and leaves a window between the check and any later use. Recording the target string needs no resolution at all, so its safety does not depend on getting containment right, and it loses nothing an audit needs: Git stores a symlink as exactly that string, and a target inside the repository is audited under its own path anyway.
Tests - [x] bun test --timeout=30000 test/cso-ordinary-repos.test.ts test/cso-snapshot-state.test.ts: 106 pass, 0 fail - [x] Free Tests run 44785903660 at c0bd62d5: green, 1718 files carried - [x] typecheck, module-size and conflict-marker guards: pass
Security notes No network, secrets, permissions, workflows, install scripts or dependencies change. The link target string is new text in report.json and the report: it passes through `redact()` and `JSON.stringify`, is bounded by the OS path limit, and sits in the same byte-bounded coverage lists as file paths, which can already hold arbitrary names.
Agent notes
Blast radius The change stays inside `/cso` capture. It touches the new link branch in `capture()`, the text `symlinkTransformation` writes, and the scoped special-file walk. The manifest consumers in `lib/cso/cli.ts` match transformations by their `excluded:` prefix and recheck link entries by target bytes, so they need no change (read in review, and the 106 focused tests and CI's free suite at this head pass).
Pre-Landing Review Four review rounds ran on this security-sensitive change (specialists, red team, an in-house adversarial reader and a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol). They found three secret-exposure problems in how link targets were printed, each fixed with a regression test: the in-repository path was printed unredacted, a key=value secret after a slash slipped past the redactor, and redacting per path segment hid URL passwords. The final check of the last fix found nothing. Eight lower-severity notes stay open below.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-3df546269d55` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `sf-fd631400a8d9` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL security finding, details recorded privately (final review, red team, 2 items) - INFORMATIONAL security finding, details recorded privately (final review, adversarial reader, 4 items)
Exploratory QA A fixture repository with links to `/etc/passwd`, `README.md` and a synthetic token was audited with `gstack-cso start --offline` at each fixed head. Before the first fix one run file held the raw token; at the final head the run exits 0, no run file holds the token, and none holds `/etc/passwd` content. A synthetic postgres URL with a password is withheld at the final head. Smoke only: races, FIFOs and sockets are covered by the tests, not by probes.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed, so no evals were selected (the selector deferred the three /cso evals to release coverage).

The auditor's own proposed clause was then applied to all three.

title: Owner rulings close a stopped review whose findings were logged in a findings file (GST-3296)
body:
When /ship's final review is logged with `--findings `, or the native reader's row lists no findings, the owner's `gstack-approvals rule` rows now close those rows at Step 11.5. Why: harness-evals#515 had all 12 rulings recorded and green CI, yet /ship stopped at Step 11.5 because the rulings had nothing to match. Nothing to do: rows that already work read the same, and an unruled blocker, a noted CRITICAL or an unfinished pass still refuses.

title: ship-queue ready --fixes-base-red still can't name a Vitest case with a comma or >, and it now blocks a fixer train (reopen of #4233)
body:
Follow-up to #4233, which was closed as won't-fix with an invitation to reopen if it blocks a train we depend on. This integration can't reopen or comment there, so I'm filing it here.

Reopening as invited: this now blocks a train we depend on (groom-club/member-web, gstack a26529a / 1.102.0.0).

Main went red on 3 Vitest cases from a date-dependent test. The fixer is member-web#1038. Its READY used `gstack-ship-queue ready --pr 1038 --fixes-base-red '<3 cases>'`, and each case name contains a comma (for example "..., and the create saves before the cancel writes"), so the flag value split into 5 entries. T0's recorded red ids are also XML-escaped (>, ') while the declaration was plain.

- Train: gate.train-d3009decdc1e-7096db4f3c9f-432f8f
- T0 run 44793443250: RED on exactly the 3 cases
- T1 run 44793638882: GREEN
- Verdict: RED-ON-MAIN, landable=0/1

The code paths are unchanged from this issue's report at a26529a and origin/HEAD (crew/lib/ship-queue-train-cli.ts:186, crew/lib/ship-queue-train-gate.ts:100/114/149). A name with a comma has no workaround, so the fixer has to land outside the train, which is the path base-red trains exist to avoid. The proposed fix above still fits: a repeatable flag or a file form, entity decoding in parseTestRecord, and a READY-time check against the base's red set.

title: Free Tests plans its shards beside the reuse and docs checks (GST-3303)
body:
Free Tests on a pull request now starts its test shards after one round of small GitHub-hosted jobs instead of two, because the planner no longer waits for the reuse and docs-only checks. Why: faster PR feedback on the required `free-tests` check. Nothing to do: no check is renamed, and the same tests run.
What changed Every Free Tests run on a pull request used to wait for a GitHub runner twice before any test ran. The first wait was for the reuse and docs-only checks, and the second was for the planner that sat behind them. The planner now runs at the same time as those two checks, so the shards start after a single round. - `free-plan` has no `needs` and no condition, so it runs beside `reuse` and `docs-scope`. - `free-suite` now needs `free-plan`, `reuse` and `docs-scope`, and skips on a verified reuse or a docs-only pull request, as `free-plan` used to make it do. The `free-tests` aggregate is unchanged. - A reused main push now uploads the `free-plan` artifact, so `reuseChecker` (scripts/lib/ci-history.ts) treats a run whose only artifact is `free-plan` as one that may have reused, and checks its `reuse` job as before. The flake counts in `test:health` and the factory scorecard still leave reused pushes out. - Because `free-plan` now runs on docs-only pull requests too, it leaves the `skippable` list of the `ci-reuse/free-tests` run profile in `.gstack/pregate.json`, so /ship can still reuse a docs-only run's CI result instead of asking for tests that were never owed. A new wiring test checks that every job on that list waits for `docs-scope` and skips on a docs-only change. - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md now says a reused main push uploads only the planner's artifact.
Why Before, over 11-06 to 11-20: in 213 sampled first-attempt pull request runs, the time from the reuse and docs-only checks finishing to the first shard job being created was 21 s at the median, 192 s at p90 and 363 s at p95; in 244 sampled runs (every sampled run that ran shards), the time from the run being created to the first shard job being created was 45 s at the median, 297 s at p90 and 850 s at p95. After, on that second measure: this PR's two Free Tests runs took 29 s and 43 s, and #4572's run on the same afternoon without this change took 51 s. Three runs are too few to show a difference at p95, so the real measure is a window of pull request runs after this lands.
Blast radius The change touches the required Free Tests workflow, the CI-reuse run profile in `.gstack/pregate.json` and the flake-count reuse check. Every shard still waits for `reuse` and `docs-scope` and skips on either (read at .github/workflows/free-tests.yml:595-596, and covered by the new wiring tests). The run profile takes effect only once it lands on main, because /ship reads main's copy. This PR's own CI result was accepted at its final head (run 44803532677).
Test Coverage The coverage audit (audit only, no tests written by it) rated 8 of 9 changed paths covered, 89% value-weighted. The one gap: a run whose only artifact is `free-plan` and whose `reuse` job did not succeed should still count as a real run; the fixture's job listing always reports a green `reuse` job. Tests ran: test 1719 (files, from the CI run at this head)
Pre-Landing Review The first full review found one blocker, now fixed: the run profile still listed `free-plan` as skippable, so after this change /ship could never reuse a docs-only run's CI result. A second full review of the fix and a second-model review found nothing blocking.
Review notes Below the blocking floor, recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/lib/ci-history.ts:284` The reuse check treats a run whose only artifact is `free-plan` and whose `reuse` job succeeded as reused; a real main run whose shards uploaded nothing would drop out of flake counts. - INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/free-tests.yml:217` `free-plan` now also runs on reused and docs-only runs; if it fails there, the run concludes failure while the `free-tests` check stays green, and /ship can't reuse any CI result for that head. - INFORMATIONAL `test/ci-reuse-workflow-wiring.test.ts:184` The new test checks one direction only: it would not catch a docs-gated profile job left out of the skippable list, and its string match does not check which way the condition points.
Exploratory QA No runnable surface: this is a CI workflow and run-profile change. Smoke checks were the focused tests below, plus a control run showing the new wiring test fails against the pre-fix run profile.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

title: Redactor hides key=value secrets that follow a slash, so /cso history stops printing them (GST-3297)
body:
gstack's redactor now hides `password=…`, `api_key=…` and `token=…` values that come after a `/`, such as a symlink target `../password=…`, `cfg/api_key=…` or a Markdown link to such a path.
Why: `/cso`'s retained Git history went through this redactor and kept those values, so `gstack-cso history` printed them; review packets, telemetry and ship logs use the same redactor.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `env.kv` in `lib/redact-patterns.ts` may start a name right after a `/`, in addition to the line start, a diff marker or a comment marker. The name class excludes `/`, so each attempt stops at the next separator and the scan stays linear.
- The comment-text exemption (`isCommentText`) now applies only when a comment marker really precedes the name, so `a/token=…` is checked like a line-start match. A comment marker that opens a quoted string still counts as a comment.
- New exemption `isRegexLiteralBody`: a `/` after an operator or opening bracket starts a regex literal only when the text before the closing `/` holds regex syntax (an escape, a character class, a group or a `{n,m}` quantifier). Code such as `content.match(/authtoken:\s*(.+)/)` stays clean, while a Markdown link or a YAML value whose path holds a secret still reports.

Every exemption that existed before is unchanged for the matches it already handled; this PR adds a catch and narrows only the new over-catches.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

`gstack-cso history` printed key=value secrets that sat after a slash in a symlink target, a link that only exists in history, or ordinary file content. Keeping secrets out of what gstack prints and stores is the point of the shared redactor.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Every caller of the shared redactor: `/cso` history and snapshots, review packets, telemetry, ship logs and the pre-push credential scan. A scan of every tracked file in this repository finds the same 212 `env.kv` matches before and after the review fix, so the repository's own checks are unaffected.

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Test Coverage Audit: 8 new code paths, 7 covered before review (88% any test, 88% value-weighted). The one gap (a regex literal after `return`) got a test row in the review fix. Tests: 1838 → 1839 (+1 new file).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Pre-Landing Review: 4 issues — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 2 noted, 1 ruled note
Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none)

- Round 1 (full panel): the red-team reader found that the first regex-literal exemption also hid secrets in Markdown links, YAML values and single-slash URLs. Fixed in 060832a with four new leak rows and a `return /…/` control.
- Round 2 (full panel on the fix): no findings from the specialists or the red team. The second-model review and the adversarial reader raised the notes below.

title: Every flaky pass in Free Tests is now recorded in Trunk or the flaky-test log (GST-3303)
body:
Free Tests now records every test that failed and then passed on its retry: dispatched runs upload their test results to Trunk, and the quick tier keeps its flaky-test log. Why: a retried flake must always leave a record. Of the 13 retried flakes since Trunk uploads began (11-09), Trunk saw 11; one missing was on a dispatched run, the other on a main push from before the uploader reached main. The quick tier's flaky-test log was never uploaded at all. Nothing to do: no check, test or retry rule changes.
What changed ![Dispatched Free Tests runs now upload to Trunk, and the quick tier keeps its flaky-test log](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/sUJJgL0D5-mncum2Cjm-MpbU85dtom51dNjqEkArowg.png) Dispatched Free Tests runs now upload to Trunk, and the quick tier keeps its flaky-test log.
Before/after as text: Dispatched Free Tests runs now upload to Trunk, and the quick tier keeps its flaky-test log ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output # trunk-flaky-tests runs on if: always() && needs.free-suite.result != 'skipped' && ((github.event_name == 'push' && g +ithub.ref == 'refs/heads/main') || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.eve +nt_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repos +itory)) -ithub.ref == 'refs/heads/main') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pu -ll_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository)) # quick-bun-default steps after the quick tier +- Upload the quick tier's flake ledger -> artifact flake-ledger-quick (always, 90 days) -(none: flake-ledger.jsonl written, never uploaded) ~~~
- `trunk-flaky-tests` also runs on `workflow_dispatch`. Only someone with write access can dispatch, and the job still checks out and runs nothing from the branch, and is the only job that sees the token. - `quick-bun-default` uploads its flaky-test log as `flake-ledger-quick` (always, ignored when empty, kept 90 days), so the run's flaky-pass summary and `test:health` count it. It keeps no JUnit report, so its retries reach that log, not Trunk. docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md says so in its sections on Trunk and the flaky-test log. - The wiring test pins both, and it fails on the old workflow.
Why A test that fails and then passes on its retry is green but not fixed, so it has to leave a record somewhere. A dispatched run on test/spawn-sync.test.ts (run 44494151996) left none in Trunk, and every flaky pass in the quick tier was thrown away. Now both are kept.
Blast radius Only the Trunk upload job's trigger and one new upload step in the quick tier change. The upload job is fail-open at step and job level (`continue-on-error: true`), nothing needs it, and it has `permissions: {}`. A dispatch run already needs write access and runs that branch's own workflow file, so it gives nobody a new way to reach the token (free-tests.yml:899-930 read). Every reader of `flake-ledger-*` matches on the name prefix (scripts/lib/ci-history.ts:345, lib/factory-scorecard.ts:340), and the run summary reads a `flake-ledger-quick` folder correctly (script ran).
How the gap was found Every `flake-ledger-*` log since 11-09 03:25Z (13 entries) was matched to its test in Trunk collection 7yDVXXE3 and to that run's test runs. 11 show a failure and a success in the same run, and Trunk's Pass on Retry monitor flagged them. Run 44494151996 (dispatch, test/spawn-sync.test.ts) has no Trunk runs, because the uploader skipped dispatch events. Run 42560717406 (main push, 11-09 04:14Z) predates the uploader on main.
Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted. Four readers checked the final change: a batched specialist (testing, security, state machines) found nothing, and a second-model review found nothing. Two notes stay open, neither blocking: - [ADVISORY] A quick-tier flake now counts toward a main run's flaky files, so files in the quick subset get two chances per main run to reach the 5% flaky-file rule. The rule counts each run once per file, so one run can't count twice. Skipped: it is intended, and a one-line docs note can follow. - [Low] Runner-sizing dispatch runs (`free_runner`, `free_shards` or `free_jobs` set) now upload to Trunk too, which can add timing noise to a detection-only collection. Noted for a follow-up that narrows the condition to dispatches with empty sizing inputs.
Exploratory QA Smoke check: `flake-summary` over a folder holding a `flake-ledger-quick` log beside a shard log lists both files, the quick one under shard `quick` (pass). No plan checks: this is a bug fix with no plan file.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. The four changed files, plus the docs audit's one clause, match the stated fix.
Plan Completion No plan file: bug fixes need no plan review.
Verification Results No plan obligations. Smoke check: 1 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED, 0 NOT RUN.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Tests - [x] Free Tests (CI run 44804207423 at 66441e5): 1719 test files passed, 0 failed, including the macOS and Windows launcher and named-regression jobs. - [x] Before CI: 51 test files that read free-tests.yml or flaky-test logs, 869 pass, 0 fail; actionlint clean; the new wiring assertion fails on the old workflow. - [x] Trial merge with #4570 (also edits free-tests.yml and its wiring test): merged cleanly; free-tests-workflow-wiring, ci-reuse-workflow-wiring, docs-only-workflow and test-health-report tests 62 pass, 0 fail; actionlint clean.
Agent notes Refs GST-3303 (follow-up on audit change 6: the retry stays under R9). ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch ci/trunk-flaky-dispatch. Plan: exempt: bug fix, no plan review needed (R4) Plan check: exempt bug fix REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=2 fixed=0 scope=frozen dispatches=2 est_input_tokens=5651 Gate edits: none detected (3 listed, 2 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ## Documentation **Status:** updated. Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. Docs that mention the flake ledger or Trunk were checked against the workflow. **Documentation health:** - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: Updated. The Flake ledger section now names the quick tier's `flake-ledger-quick` artifact next to the per-shard and Windows ledgers. The Trunk section already covered dispatch runs and the quick tier. - CONTRIBUTING.md: Current. Its flake-ledger summary is still accurate. - docs/flaky.md: Current. It covers gstack-flaky, which this change doesn't touch. - changelog.d/ci-flaky-passes-always-recorded.md: Read only. It matches the workflow change. **Coverage debt:** No new public commands, flags or settings. The CI behavior change (Trunk upload on workflow_dispatch, plus the quick-tier ledger artifact) is described in docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md. No gaps. **Diagram drift:** None. title: v1.102.1.0 release
body:
v1.102.1.0 ships 21 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- Two /ship approval records stop needing workarounds. (#4549)
- For contributors: the paid auto-decide check counts a start step that ran while the skill loaded. (#4543)
- The destructive-command check closes three ways past its disk-wipe and force-push blocks. (#4534)
- A green CI run still counts when the repository's artifact storage is full. (#4536)
- `/cso` now audits repositories that track symlinks. (#4567)
- A doc-sync eval stops failing when the audit child drops one field from its result line. (#4555)
- The browse daemon no longer picks port 10080, which Chromium refuses to open. (#4554)
- Opted-in telemetry now says why a skill run ended, which coding agent and model family ran it, and whether an upgrade worked. (#4542)
- A preregistration with only its write-up and plain data now gets the write-up review: one reviewer, one round. (#4544)
- When owner rulings don't clear a stopped review, `gstack-review-read` now says which findings are left. (#4553)
- The prompt-routing hook now names your installed bug-fix skill on bug reports, alone, and never puts /verify ahead of it. (#4539)
- Owner rulings now close a stopped review whose findings were logged in a findings file. (#4568)
- /ship can finish after the owner accepts a stopped review's findings as open notes. (#4552)
- /ship no longer starts the full test suite on your machine when CI's earlier run can't be reused (GST-3277). (#4565)
- The prompt-routing hook no longer acts on words inside backticks. (#4566)
- In Claude Code, a gstack skill's start step now runs when the skill loads, so the model can't skip it. (#4509)
- gstack's telemetry backend only accepts writes through its own validated endpoint, and the community dashboard now counts real use. (#4537)
- gstack now says what it's adding before it adds a background job or a browser extension. (#4538)
- For contributors: every flaky pass in Free Tests is now recorded. (#4572)
- For contributors: Free Tests on pull requests starts its test shards one round of small jobs sooner. (#4570)
- Secret values written as `name=value` at the end of a path are now hidden. (#4571)

</details>

title: Results PRs with large agent transcripts can be reviewed again (GST-3273)
body:
Results PRs that commit captured agent sessions no longer stop at the 2 MB review limit: a data file kept in review only because a session quotes a lint pragma, an env check or a `--no-verify` push now reaches readers as those lines with context. Why: harness-evals#494 (25 transcripts, 11.3 MB) could not be reviewed at all. Only a strict set of files is cut, so anything in doubt still goes to readers whole. Nothing to do: the gate review still runs, and the change follows the review policy you already have.
What is cut, and what stays whole A gate-tagged file is cut to its tagged lines only when all of these hold: 1. It is a `.jsonl`, `.ndjson`, `.csv`, `.tsv` or `.log` file, or a `.json` under a docs, results or reports tree. A `review_content_patterns` declaration alone never qualifies a file. 2. No gate floor covers its path (test, CI, config, snapshot or golden), and it was not renamed. 3. It is kept for no other reason. 4. Every tag instance is one added line's own tag: the multi-line empty-catch rule finds nothing, and the untagged lines, scanned together, tag nothing. The review plan and the record /ship writes before merge compute this from the same input, so they build the same selection. Tests cover each case that stays whole: code with the same words, a snapshot, a multi-line catch alone, a multi-line catch next to a one-line tag, a declared `.out` session, a declared `.patch` under `test/`, a `.jsonl` under `test/`, and a code file renamed to `.jsonl`.
Also fixed - `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE` now names the largest files (`files=` and the fix text), and a name holding a space, a comma or a colon is quoted rather than cut at the first space. - The gate scan stored a path holding a space with the tab git appends after such names, so the tagged file matched nothing and was dropped from review without being read. The tab is now stripped.
Evidence - The new tests in `test/review-gate-excerpt.test.ts`: 9 pass on this branch. On main a529769, 7 fail; the #494-shape test stops with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE bytes=3151306`. - No-loss replay (deterministic, no paid runs), same reader selection on main and on this branch: harness-evals 60 commits, gstack-evals 200 and gstack 200 are all the same. On harness-evals#494, 25 transcripts are cut, 46 tagged or credential lines are checked and 0 are missing. `gstack-review-dispatch pass` on #494 exits 0 with a 107,802-byte excerpt. Record: `test/fixtures/review-pins/replays/GST-3273.json`. - Targeted and adjacent tests: 586 pass and 2 fail. The 2 failures time out at 5 s, and both fail the same way on main a529769 on the same machine. CI is the full run.
Agent notes Replaces #4556, which was closed after five reviews because every tag-matching inference was beaten by files that mixed tag instances. This is the allowlist rebuild GStack Minder asked for, carrying over the #494 test, the agreement tests, the largest-files fix and the replay script. No grants apply to this PR. The two local 5 s timeouts (review-dispatch "an output event edited to look refused…", review-plan-targeted-delta "the #225 shape") reproduce on main locally. ### /ship record (head 1571ea5, run ship-1571ea5) REVIEW_LOOP: passes=1 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=5 fixed=0 scope=frozen dispatches=4 **Pre-Landing Review:** 5 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 5 noted. None blocks: no test fails, nothing breaks in production, no data or secret is lost. Review plan: class=gate depth=full, one full pass (specialists testing/security/state-machines, Red Team, native adversarial, second-model review on openai/gpt-6.1-sol, targeted gate reader). title: Windows Setup E2E runs its long cases on parallel runners (GST-3303)
body:
Pull requests that touch install files get their Windows Setup E2E result about 3 minutes sooner: its long cases now run on parallel Windows runners instead of one after another. This goes toward PR feedback in minutes: Windows Setup E2E was the last check to finish on 77 of the 234 pull request heads it ran on. Nothing to do: every case still runs on every in-scope pull request, and no required check changes.
What changed | Job | Cases | Before | |---|---|---| | windows-setup | ./setup, setup.ps1, bun run build and the rest of the install checks | also ran the false-positive recovery and both forced-CSO failures | | windows-setup-recovery (new) | the false-positive recovery (#3088, #3100) | in windows-setup | | windows-setup-cso (new) | forced CSO failure is fatal under strict build; forced publish failure still completes setup (#3071) | in windows-setup | | held-install-journey | clean and already-unmerged installs | also ran dirty, trial, go-back and later-release | | held-install-trial (new) | dirty-conflicting recovery, then trial and go-back | in held-install-journey | | held-install-later-release (new) | dirty-conflicting recovery, then the later release | in held-install-journey | The held-install fixture that the three held jobs share moved out of the workflow into `scripts/windows-held-install-fixture.sh`, unchanged apart from a header comment and the shell settings the repository's script guards require, and that file joins the install paths list. Each job's closing step checks its own case list. The trial and later-release jobs each repeat the dirty-conflicting recovery, because both start from the install it leaves. The testing docs' table of observed CI jobs now lists all six jobs.
Why Windows Setup E2E finished last on 77 of the 234 pull request heads it ran on, because each of its two jobs ran every case one after another. With the long cases on their own runners, an install change waits for the slowest single case chain instead of the whole list.
Blast radius The change touches only the Windows Setup E2E workflow, the fixture script it runs, three tests that pin the workflow's job list and one docs table. None of the six jobs is a required check, so a red or skipped job cannot hold up a merge, and all six passed at this head in run 44814828573.
Numbers Before, from the last two weeks of pull request runs: held-install-journey ran 458 s at the median (525 s p95) and windows-setup 368 s (417 s p95). The slowest steps were Install with ./setup 170 s, the dirty step 145 s, clean plus unmerged 123 s, trial and go-back 102 s, later release 87 s, false-positive recovery 84 s and the CSO publish failure 38 s. The expected wall after the split is about 4.5 to 5 minutes.
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual correction in the documentation of Trunk's observed CI jobs. **Scope:** branch ci/windows-setup-e2e-parallel compared with base 6a64c49 (head bce0192): the workflow `.github/workflows/windows-setup-e2e.yml` (split into parallel jobs), the new fixture script `scripts/windows-held-install-fixture.sh`, three test pins and one changelog.d fragment. Staged and unstaged changes: none before the audit. **Documentation health** - `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md`: updated. The observed-jobs table row for `windows-setup-e2e.yml` now lists all six job ids (`windows-setup`, `windows-setup-recovery`, `windows-setup-cso`, `held-install-journey`, `held-install-trial`, `held-install-later-release`), matching the workflow and `test/trunk-dynamic-ci-observers.test.ts`. - `docs/pregate.md`: current. The `windows-setup` job it names still exists. - `changelog.d/ci-windows-setup-e2e-parallel.md`: current. Reviewed, not edited. **Coverage debt:** no prose doc describes the new held-install fixture script; the workflow comments and the changelog fragment cover it. No diagrams are affected.
Pre-Landing Review One full review pass at bce0192 (batched specialists, red team, native adversarial, a reviewer from a second model family and the targeted gate reader) found nothing that blocks. Nothing was fixed; the items below are recorded and left for later. The stale Trunk observer table the red team and native reviewer both named was corrected by the documentation audit in 432b259. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-a6a2df8b105d` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/windows-setup-e2e.yml:758` The later-release updater no longer runs after the trial and go-back forms, so updating after a trial plus go-back is no longer exercised. - INFORMATIONAL `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md:1729` The Trunk observer table and the workflow comment at line 107 still name only the old two jobs. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/windows-held-install-fixture.sh:12` Three held-install jobs now each fetch the pinned release commit, tripling the chance of a fetch flake. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/windows-held-install-fixture.sh:66` The generated lib.sh install_state removes HOME's gstack install; moved unchanged from the inline step, only reachable by sourcing the CI fixture by hand with RUNNER_TEMP set.
Exploratory QA Three captures on Linux, verdict pass: the moved fixture script builds the held-install fixture from this head (bare origin at this tree on top of v1.91.101.0, fix-branch with the trial marker, a valid lib.sh, an empty case list), and its body matches the old inline step apart from the strict-mode line. The first capture was superseded: the local clone was shallow and lacked the pinned release commit. Windows behaviour is covered by the Windows Setup E2E run, not by these probes.

title: Telemetry can count gstack's own use on Capy, opt-in and kept out of public numbers (GST-3311)
body:
Agent-driven Capy sessions still send no telemetry. If the owner's `preferences.yaml` holds `telemetry_capy: anonymous`, each skill run sends one anonymous row labelled `source=capy`, or `source=gt` from Garry's own machines.
Why: we couldn't see our own gstack use on Capy, and if we had sent it, it would have been counted as real use.
Nothing to do yet: nothing changes until the owner adds that line, and the ingest change ships in a separate deploy.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Before this, gstack runs on Capy sent no telemetry at all, so we could not see how much gstack is used there, and if they had sent, those runs would have been counted as real use. Now the owner can turn it on with one line in the preferences file, and those rows go out anonymous and labelled so the public numbers leave them out.

- `bin/gstack-telemetry-tier` (new) is the one place that reads the opt-in. It accepts only `anonymous`: `community` would send `installation_id`, a device id reused across sessions, which the consent rules out. A missing file or line, two such lines, another value, or a file over 4 KB all mean off.
- `gstack-skill-end`: an unattended session stays silent unless the Capy opt-in is on. When it is on, it sends the telemetry row but still writes no usage log line, so the batch it sends holds exactly one event.
- `gstack-telemetry-log` and `gstack-telemetry-sync` read their tier through the helper, so a Capy machine set to `community` still sends `anonymous` under the opt-in.
- Source label order: flag > `GSTACK_TELEMETRY_SOURCE` > eval > CI > `capy`/`gt` (`GSTACK_CAPY=1`) > live. Eval runs on Capy stay `eval`. `telemetry_capy_source: gt` gives `gt`; any other value, or none, gives `capy`.
- The ingest function accepts `capy` and `gt` (before this, it would have stored them as `other`).
- `lib/agent-model.ts` no longer warns about either telemetry key in the preferences file. Docs: privacy, unattended, model-policy and the Capy install guide.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

We could not see our own gstack use on Capy. If we had sent it, it would have been counted as real use. This counts it separately, only when the owner opts in, and keeps it out of the public numbers.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

This touches the telemetry scripts every skill run calls, the preferences reader and the ingest function. Without the opt-in line nothing changes, because the helper falls back to the machine's own setting (read at bin/gstack-telemetry-tier, and checked by four isolated smoke runs and 84 targeted tests). The public views count only `source = 'live'` (read in supabase/migrations 006 and 009), so `capy` and `gt` rows stay out of them.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two reviewers read the whole diff: one combined testing, security, state-machine and red-team reader, and one adversarial reader. Nothing blocks. One testing note was skipped and six notes were recorded.

- Skipped: `lib/agent-model.ts:119`: the preferences reader does not warn about a malformed `telemetry_capy` line. The helper already reads such a line as off, which is the safe default, and adding new session-start warnings is outside this change.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-telemetry-sync:42` Parallel opted-in Capy sessions sharing a state root can pass the 5-minute rate check together and post the same batch twice; capy/gt counts inflate, live numbers untouched.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-telemetry-log:152` Stale-marker sweep rows have no source, so ingest files them as live; reachable only when a non-unattended session left a marker on a Capy state root.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-start:265` TELEMETRY_WRITE: skipped (unattended session) still prints for an opted-in Capy session whose skill-end then sends a row.
- INFORMATIONAL `supabase/migrations/001_telemetry.sql:77` Internal skill_sequences view reads raw telemetry_events, so it now counts capy/gt rows (already mixed eval and CI; not public).
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-telemetry-tier:23` One owner opt-in covers every repo a Capy agent works in; rows include the existing redacted error_message and free-text failed_step.
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-end:126` Background sync throttled to 5 minutes can lose unsent capy rows when a Capy machine sleeps; undercount only.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Four smoke runs of `bin/gstack-telemetry-tier` against isolated fixture files, all passing: an opt-in file gives `anonymous` and `gt`; a duplicated opt-in line reads as off; a byte-order mark, Windows line endings, quotes and a comment still opt in, and an unlisted label falls back to `capy`; outside Capy the file is ignored. `gstack-telemetry-log` and the sync were not run live, so no row could reach the real endpoint; the targeted tests cover them against a fixture URL.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

No prompt, template or judge changed, so evals were skipped. The selector listed every behavior only because the ingest function has no mapped dependency; those stay in scheduled release coverage.

</details>

title: Step 11.5 keeps a reviewed head current across base-only merges (GST-3308)
body:
When main is merged into a pull request after its code review, /ship no longer throws that review away. If every commit since the review is a clean merge of the base branch and the pull request's own changes are byte-identical, `gstack-review-read` now reports the review as current, so /ship finishes without another review round. Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `gstack-review-read` passes a new check, `baseMergeOnly` in `lib/ship-receipt-patch.ts`, to `reviewFreshness`. It runs only when the current content differs from what a review row read, and accepts the head only when all of these hold:
  - every first-parent commit after the reviewed one is a two-parent merge whose second parent `origin/<base>` holds;
  - each merge's tree is exactly what `git merge-tree --write-tree` writes for its parents (no conflict resolution, no edit inside the merge);
  - the working tree is HEAD's;
  - the branch's product patch-id against the base (the same helper /ship already uses to keep a review across a rebuilt head) and its patch-id over every path are unchanged, so tests, release metadata and gate paths stay covered.
- A CURRENT reason from this route names the reviewed base to pass as finish's `--reviewed-base`. A STALE reason now says which condition failed.
- The patch-id helpers (`patchId`, `productRules`, `productSpec`, `productPatchAgainstBase`, `verifiedOutputs`) moved verbatim out of `bin/gstack-ship-receipt` into `lib/ship-receipt-patch.ts` so both callers share them. Their behavior does not change.
- `docs/ship-policy.md` and `docs/skills.md` describe the new CURRENT case.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

harness-evals#515 read CURRENT at 630a9903. Main was then merged in cleanly (deed041c) to make 2d3ab19d, and Step 11.5 read both review rows STALE because it compared whole trees, so the run could not finish without a new review. On those real commits, `baseMergeOnly` returns ok with one clean merge, product patch-id a548b6b4 and reviewed base 9d1b1c83.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The only behavior change is a row that used to read STALE on other content; every other row returns what it returned before, and finish's own read of post-review fixes passes no base-merge check, so it is unchanged (`lib/ship-release.ts`, read). Eight cases in `test/ship-finish-ruled-notes.test.ts` reuse the #515 fixture: a clean merge reads CURRENT and `finish --reviewed-base` binds with `behavior=0`; an own edit, a conflict resolution, an edit inside the merge, base context moved beside the branch's product or test hunk, uncommitted changes, a merge of a branch main does not hold, and a rebase all stay STALE (script ran: 8 pass, 0 fail).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Coverage: 12 new code paths, 8 tested before review (67%). Review added 2 tests for the side-branch merge and rebase refusals, so 10 of 12 are now tested. Still untested: a review row whose commit is missing or holds other content, and the import-failure fallback in `gstack-review-read` (both read STALE).
Tests: 1839 → 1839 files (+0 new files; 2 new cases in an existing file).

</details>

title: Free Tests splits the suite from freshly recorded test times (GST-3303)
body:
Free Tests should report about 45 seconds sooner. It splits the suite into shards using a record of how long each test file takes, and that record was eleven days old and missing 67 files, so some shards got far more real work than others. The times are now re-recorded for every file, so the shards should finish close together and the slowest one sets the result less often. Nothing to do: every test still runs, and no check name changes.
What changed - `scripts/free-test-durations.json` is re-recorded for all 1,727 free-suite files with the documented recorder, on the same Ubicloud size the weekly recording uses. No file failed while recording. - The 67 files added since 11-09 used to count as 54-second files each (the planner's guess for a file it has no time for). That was about 3,560 seconds of load that doesn't exist, on a suite that really runs about 5,870 seconds. - Six files now run past the 60-second limit for a single file. Each is added to `scripts/free-test-seed-allowlist.json` with its time and a follow-up to split it, the same way the 11-09 refresh admitted its long files. - The runner-size trial input on manual Free Tests runs also accepts `ubicloud-standard-16`, for paired trials of a bigger runner. Pull request runs don't change size.
Numbers Before, from the 215 pull request runs between 11-06 and 11-20 where all 11 shards passed: from the first shard starting to the last one finishing took 274 s at the median and 346 s at p90, and the slowest shard's test step took 220 s at the median and 262 s at p90. Inside one run, the slowest and fastest of shards 1 to 10 were 75 s apart at the median. In the latest run, each shard's four parallel groups ranged from 77 to 106 s for the fastest group up to 167 to 218 s for the slowest. Replaying that run's per-file times through the planner: the old record gives a slowest shard of 246 s, the new one 177 s. After, on this branch with the same runner, three runs of the same tree: first shard start to last shard end took 234, 227 and 220 s, and the slowest shard's test step took 186, 192 and 184 s. The shards finished 37 to 44 s apart. That is about 45 s off the shard phase at the median, from three runs; 22% of the earlier runs already had a slowest test step of 192 s or less, so read it as a shift of the typical run, not a guarantee for every run. A bigger runner isn't worth it yet. One run on ubicloud-standard-16, with twice as many parallel groups per shard, brought the slowest shard to 170 s: 16 to 22 s more for twice the cores. Its slowest group was a single file, test/review-pass.test.ts, which takes about 4.4 minutes alone. Splitting that file is the next step before more cores pay off, so the default runner stays as it is.

title: Trunk flaky-test upload runs after Free Tests, off the pull request's checks (GST-3303)
body:
Pull requests no longer wait on the upload that sends Free Tests results to Trunk. It now runs on its own after Free Tests finishes. The quick test tier's flaky passes now reach Trunk too, so a test that fails once and passes on its retry shows up there wherever it ran. Nothing to do: no required check changes, and the upload still never affects whether a check passes.
What changed - The Trunk upload moves out of `free-tests.yml` into its own workflow, `trunk-flaky-tests.yml`, which runs when a Free Tests run completes. It covers the same runs as before (pull requests from this repository, pushes to main and manual runs), skips pull requests from forks, checks out nothing and runs no shell. Its GitHub token can only read the finished run's files. - The quick tier on the install-default Bun now keeps its JUnit reports (`bun run test:quick --junit-dir ` is new) and saves them as `quick-junit`. The new workflow uploads them as a separate `bun-default` variant, because the same files also run on the pinned Bun. - The tests that pin the workflows' shape, and the testing docs, follow the move.
Why Pull requests waited on the Trunk upload. In 61 of 223 pull request runs it was the last job to finish, and in the slowest twentieth of those it held the checks for about three more minutes. Now the checks finish when the tests do, and the quick tier's flaky passes reach Trunk as well.
Blast radius It touches the Free Tests workflow, the new Trunk Flaky Tests workflow, the shard runner's `--junit-dir` flag and the tests that pin those workflows. It is safe because nothing reads the new workflow's result and both JUnit uploads in Free Tests are fail-open; the workflow wiring test checks this (18 pass at 77954d0), and the full Free Tests run at d07496a passed (run 44836203825).
Numbers Before, from 223 pull request Free Tests runs between 11-09 and 11-20 that had the upload job: the upload job finished after every other Free Tests job in 61 runs (27%). When it did, it was 7 s later at the median, 175 s later at p95 and 380 s at most. Waiting for a GitHub runner explains most of that gap in 13 of the 61 runs. So this saves almost nothing on a typical run and about 3 minutes on the slowest twentieth of them. It runs for 12 s once it starts.
How to check it after merge A workflow that runs after another workflow always uses the copy on main, so the new upload can't run on this pull request. After merge, the first push to main and the next pull request should each show a Trunk Flaky Tests run, and Trunk should show test runs for that commit, including `bun-default` ones from the quick tier.
Test Coverage 10 of 13 changed paths have tests that would catch a regression (77%). Two gaps are end-to-end only and can be checked after merge: the new workflow firing after Free Tests and downloading the other run's files, and a flaky quick-tier pass reaching Trunk as `bun-default`. One unit gap: no test runs the full quick tier with `--junit-dir`; the quick-tier job's own `quick-junit` file (894,943 bytes at 9ef148b) shows it works. Tests: 1840 → 1840 (+0 new) Coverage: 77% value-weighted (77% including 0 weakly covered paths) Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered (weak = ★, gate-failing or unrated). Tests ran: free 1721
