title: Add a weekly report of the wrong edits gstack's tests fail to catch (GST-3386)
body:
A new weekly Mutation report plants small wrong edits in the five `lib/` files with the most landings in the last 30 days and lists the edits no test caught.
Why: agents write most of our code and tests, and a green suite only means something if the tests reject plausible wrong code; this trial measures where they don't.
Nothing to do: it runs Saturdays on main, is never a required check, and never blocks a merge.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![The testing guide's Mutation report section now describes 30-day landings, file replacement, the baseline-and-message control and the shared 55-minute budget](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/5s0KYH0quMBX4dbNH3wBUzEeQybYqKjtwXoyHfQgmgo.png)

The testing guide's Mutation report section says what the weekly job does and how to run it locally.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The testing guide's Mutation report section now describes 30-day landings, file replacement, the baseline-and-message control and the shared 55-minute budget</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md § Mutation report at 69ad103 · source text (section not present before)
+++ After · docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md § Mutation report on this branch · source text
+## Mutation report
+A weekly, report-only trial of mutation testing. It checks whether gstack's tests reject plausible wrong code in the files agents change most. `.github/workflows/mutation-report.yml` runs every Saturday at 06:00 UTC, or on demand through workflow_dispatch, on `ubicloud-standard-16`. It is not a required check, never runs on pull requests, and never blocks a merge.
+
+`scripts/mutation-report.ts` does the work:
+
+1. It picks the five `lib/**/*.ts` files (not tests) with the most landings on main in the last 30 days (`git log --first-parent`), from the job's full-history checkout. A file that no test imports is listed as `no tests`, and a file Stryker finds nothing to mutate in (a data-only file) as `no mutants`; in both cases the next file takes its place.
+2. For each file it selects the test files that import it directly. If none do, it falls back to the transitive importers from `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts`. At most 20 run, and the report shows "20 of N" when it caps them.
+3. **Positive control.** The selected tests must first pass on the unedited file; if they don't, the file is reported as `failed`. Then the script prepends `throw new Error('mutation-report positive control')` to the file and runs the same tests, which must fail with that message. If they don't, the tests reach the file only through a spawned process, and every mutant would be a false survivor. The file is then reported as `control survived` and not mutated.
+4. It runs StrykerJS with the community Bun runner, using per-test coverage and `ignoreStatic`, within a 55-minute budget per file that also covers the two test runs before it (at most 10 minutes each). Stryker runs under `timeout`, which kills its whole process group at the budget, and the script then restores the tree with `git checkout -- .`. A file that runs out of budget is reported as `unfinished`. The report is rewritten after every file, so a job that hits its own limit still leaves the finished files.
+5. It writes a table (killed, survived, no coverage, timeout, mutation score) and up to 15 survivors per file, each with its line, mutator and replacement. The table goes to the step summary, and the Markdown, JSON and per-file Stryker reports go to the `mutation-report` artifact.
+
+Stryker (`@stryker-mutator/core`) and `@hughescr/stryker-bun-runner` are both Apache-2.0. They are installed at the exact versions in `STRYKER_PACKAGES` into the runner's temp directory with `--ignore-scripts`, so `package.json` and `bun.lock` don't change. Their own dependencies aren't locked.
+
+Stryker has to edit files in place, because its sandbox copy fails on this repo's symlinked directories (`EISDIR` on `connect-chrome`). The script therefore refuses a dirty tree, requires `--throwaway-checkout`, and must never run in a checkout you work in. If a run is killed, it can leave a mutated file behind: run `git checkout -- .` and remove `.stryker-tmp`. To run it locally, use a scratch worktree:
+
+```bash
+git worktree add /tmp/mut origin/main && cd /tmp/mut && bun install
+npm install --prefix /tmp/stryker --no-save --ignore-scripts @stryker-mutator/core@10.1.1 @hughescr/stryker-bun-runner@1.6.0
+bun --no-env-file --config=/dev/null scripts/mutation-report.ts --throwaway-checkout --files 1 \
+  --stryker-dir /tmp/stryker --out-dir /tmp/mutation-out
+```
~~~

</details>

We had no way to tell whether a passing suite would notice a plausible wrong edit in the code agents touch most. Now a weekly job answers that:

- It ranks `lib/` files by first-parent landings on main over the last 30 days. A file no test imports is listed as "no tests", and a data-only file Stryker finds nothing to mutate in is listed as "no mutants"; in both cases the next file takes its place, so five files get scored.
- Before mutating a file, the selected tests must pass on the unedited file, then fail with the planted message once a throw is added at the top. A file whose tests don't fail that way is reported as "control survived" instead of filling the report with false survivors.
- One 55-minute budget per file covers both control runs (at most 10 minutes each) and Stryker, which runs under `timeout --kill-after=60` so its whole process group stops at the budget. The tree is restored with git after every file, and the report is rewritten after every file, so a job that hits its own limit still leaves the finished files. The table shows "20 of N" when a file's tests are capped.
- The workflow runs on a schedule or by hand only, with a read-only token that is not kept, no secrets and pinned actions. Stryker 10.1.1 and its Bun runner 1.6.0 install at exact versions outside the checkout, so package.json and bun.lock don't change.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"A green suite only means something if the tests reject plausible wrong code." This report-only trial shows where gstack's tests miss wrong edits in the files agents change most, and its results decide whether mutation testing earns a permanent place.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Nothing that runs today changes, because the workflow has no pull request trigger and is not a required check, and the only edit to existing code is one entry in the list of workflow files that need only the free tests (`scripts/test-pr-profile.ts:282`, read), which the full free test run on this branch passed (run 44981232966 at this commit, 38,792 tests).

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

The new helpers (churn ranking, the planted throw, scoring, Markdown escaping, the exact version pins), the refusal without `--throwaway-checkout` and the workflow's trigger and permission shape have unit tests. The other refusals (dirty tree, output folder inside the checkout, bad numbers, unknown `--only` file), test selection and the control and Stryker outcome branches have no unit test; the refusals and the control were checked by hand below, and the Stryker branches by the earlier end-to-end runs.

Tests: 1860 → 1860 (+0 new)
Coverage: 44% value-weighted (44% including 0 weakly covered paths)
Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered (weak = ★, gate-failing or unrated).
Tests ran: focused 46

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues. A final full review of this commit ran once with no fix round, because the change already had two full review rounds: the specialist, red-team and workflow-gate readers, a native adversarial reader and a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol). The second-model review marked two findings as blocking: the positive control can be satisfied by a test that echoes a spawned child's stderr (`scripts/mutation-report.ts:132`), and the planted throw above a `#!` line makes shebang files read as "control survived" (`scripts/mutation-report.ts:56`). Both are below the blocking floor (a test that would fail, a production break, or lost data or secrets), because the weekly report never runs on pull requests and fails no test; they ship as ruled notes and get fixed in the next mutation report change. The other readers raised the same two issues as non-blocking, and every remaining finding repeats one of the notes below.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:161` Ignored static mutants may count, so a data-only file could be scored instead of no mutants (refuted for lib/result-codes-release.ts by the earlier end-to-end run, which reported no mutants)
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:143` 14 workers share one GSTACK_HOME; cross-talk failures and Timeout-as-detected could inflate scores
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:128` Planted throw above a #! line makes a syntax error, so shebang files are misreported as control survived
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:132` A test that echoes a spawned child's stderr could satisfy the control message check
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:152` OOM exit 137 reported as budget exhaustion
- INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/mutation-report.yml:36` Replacement files can push total time to the 330-minute job limit; summary appended only at the end
- INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/mutation-report.yml:4` Workflow header says 90-day commits; changelog says every edit no test failed on but report lists Survived only, up to 15
- INFORMATIONAL `.github/workflows/mutation-report.yml:51` Stryker transitive dependencies are not locked (already documented)
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:154` When Stryker crashes, the row's detail is its last output line, which for a Node crash is the Node version line rather than the error
- INFORMATIONAL `scripts/mutation-report.ts:208` Files reported as "no mutants" still spend both test runs and a Stryker start, with no cap on how many the job tries

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Status: pass. Five command runs in a throwaway worktree at this commit, within a 5-minute smoke budget:

- A run on a lib file no test imports (`--only lib/model-policy-freshness-parser-worker.ts`) listed it as "no tests", wrote mutation-report.md and .json outside the checkout, exited 0 and left the tree clean.
- A missing `--throwaway-checkout`, an output folder inside the checkout, `--files 0` and an `--only` file that hasn't landed in the window were each refused with exit 1 and a message naming the problem.

Stryker itself was not run here; the earlier end-to-end runs stand for it (`--only lib/sanitize-echo.ts`: 89 mutants, 70 caught, 15 survived, 4 not covered, controls passing). The dirty-tree refusal was not rechecked in this run.

</details>

<details><summary>Scope Drift</summary>

Scope Check: CLEAN
Intent: a weekly, report-only mutation trial over the most-changed lib files (part A of the plan).
Delivered: the workflow, the script and its tests, a docs section, a changelog fragment and the free-tests list entry with its harness pin.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** blocked, shipped under an exception. One stale workflow comment needs a correction that a read-only audit does not allow.

**Scope:** docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md against the committed changes from 6484fd58 to cc9b831 (7 files). Nothing staged, unstaged or untracked.

- `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md`: current. The Mutation report section matches the script and the workflow on every checked claim, and the workflow's #mutation-report anchor resolves.
- `changelog.d/mutation-report.md`: current.
- `.github/workflows/mutation-report.yml` header comment: stale. It says files are picked by commits in the last 90 days, but the script uses landings in the last 30 days.

The exception, accepted by the maintainers on 2026-11-22, is recorded word for word in the Agent notes below.

title: Keep secret files and keys out of /autoplan's quick plan review (GST-1164)
body:
/autoplan's quick plan review no longer sends secret files or keys from your draft code to the model that reviews it. Why: that draft goes to a model provider, so a committed `.envrc` or a key pasted into an ordinary file could leave your machine. Nothing to do.
What changed Before, the quick review's draft skipped only untracked files named like secrets, so a tracked or edited `.env` file, or a key inside an ordinary source file, went to the reviewer as-is. Now a file named like a secret is never read, tracked or untracked, under both names when git sees it renamed or copied, and inside a changed submodule even when your git config inlines submodule diffs. Every other patch goes through gstack's redact engine, so a key in an ordinary file reaches the reviewer as ``, and a patch it can't redact safely is left out with a note.
Why The draft of your code is shown to a model provider during planning, and nobody should have to remember to scrub `.envrc` first. This keeps secrets on your machine by default.
Blast radius Only `captureDraft` in `lib/autoplan-lean.ts` changed, and only the quick (lean) review calls it; the full review and every other skill are untouched. Proof reached the repro rung: `test/autoplan-lean.test.ts` passes 38 of 38 locally, the new submodule case fails without the fix, and CI's free suite passed at the reviewed code (run 44970463020).
Pre-Landing Review Two full review passes, each with a batched specialist (testing, security, state machines) and a second reader looking for gaps, then a same-model adversarial read and a second-model review (GPT-6.1 Sol). Pass 1 found one security finding (details recorded privately), fixed with a failing-first test, and one test gap, fixed with two new tests. Pass 2, the adversarial read and the second-model review found nothing.
Exploratory QA Five captures of `captureDraft` against a scratch repo with a tracked `.envrc`, a key in a source file and a submodule holding its own secret file. The default-config success case passed; the security edge failed before the fix (captures 002 and 003) and passed after it (004), and the success case passed again on the fixed code (005). The evidence tool rates the set inconclusive because the pre-fix captures were rerun under new output directories rather than byte-identical commands.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed, so evals were skipped.
Review bot comments No PR existed during review, so there were no bot comments to triage.
Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix, exempt from plan review.
Issues Linked to #3914 (the original pull request for this fix).
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation Scope: diff from base 071ae248 (docs/unattended.md, lib/autoplan-lean.ts, test/autoplan-lean.test.ts) plus the untracked changelog.d fragment; also checked autoplan/DRIVER.md.tmpl and the docs that mention lean drafts. Result: current, no files changed. docs/unattended.md matches how the lean draft now skips files named like secrets (tracked or untracked), leaves out both sides of a detected rename or copy, and redacts every other patch. Debt: docs/unattended.md does not mention the --submodule=short guard the changelog fragment describes, and its list of secret patterns omits .pypirc, *.pfx, *.keystore, *.jks and id_*_sk; this is security prose, so it was left unedited.

title: A stopped or crashed /ship run no longer blocks the next run or its granted fix round (GST-3260)
body:
A /ship run that stopped or crashed no longer blocks the next run or the fix round it stopped for, and a run that is still working past two hours stays protected. Why: a leftover "run in progress" note blocked fix-round grants on four PRs, and the old 2-hour timer could mark a live run as finished. Nothing for readers to do; a run that really died is ended with `gstack-ship-run abandon`.
What changed - The bare `.git/gstack-ship-run` note becomes a small record with a state (open, stopped, finished, abandoned) that only gstack's own commands change, under a lock, as a compare-and-swap. A record that can't be read blocks, as before. - Preflight, stop, claim, finish and gstack-skill-end move it through those states, and review logging refreshes its heartbeat, with or without a token cap. Liveness no longer reads the 120-minute lease file (the lease stays for the upgrade guard). - A stopped run may record only the fix-round grant for its own stop, once per run. Extra rounds, a second fix round, `--not-security` rulings and test exceptions stay refused until the run has finished or been abandoned. Relayed rulings (`--owner-ref`) still work. - A preflight with no `--run` stops on a stopped record instead of merging the base under it. - New `gstack-ship-run status` and `abandon` (refused within 60 minutes of the last heartbeat; an unreadable record is ended by its file digest; abandon also leaves an entry in the PR body). - A stop raised after a follow-up check or a second-model review now records its stop instead of failing to bind (seen on #4591). - Review-round history counts a run id reused at different heads as separate rounds (seen on gstack-evals#406); preflight refuses a run id that already finished.
Behavior changes - lib/ship-preflight.ts, lib/gate-dispositions.ts: a run parked before finish used to stop counting after 120 minutes; now it counts until it is stopped, finished or abandoned. - bin/gstack-approvals: a stopped run's checkout can record the fix-round grant for its own stop (previously refused); every refusal names the state, heartbeat age and the abandon command. - lib/pr-review-history.ts: entries sharing a run id at different heads each count as a round.
Why A run that stopped or died left a note that blocked the very grant its stop asked for, and the 2-hour lease could be pruned by another run while the first was still working, so preflight could merge the base under live reviewers. This gives every /ship run one record with a plain state, so nothing ends a run except gstack's own commands.
Blast radius /ship preflight, `gstack-approvals` round grants, rulings and test-coverage exceptions, gate dispositions, `gstack-ship-receipt` stop, claim and history, finish, and `gstack-skill-end`. A run parked before finish used to stop counting after 120 minutes; now it counts until it is stopped, finished or abandoned. The upgrade guard's lease file is unchanged.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds (gate-class panel: specialists, red team, second-model native and outside reviews, targeted reader), one fix round, no blocker. Round 1 fixed five informational findings (a stopped run granting itself repeated fix rounds, two untested transitions, a preflight with no run id merging under a stopped record, and heartbeats dropped under a token cap); two were left as notes. Round 2 and the second-model reviews found nothing at the blocking floor; their notes are listed below and are not fixed in this PR. - Note: when the claim write itself fails, the once-per-run limit is not enforced on that run (the PR-body grant marker still stops a grant being spent twice). - Note: a grant relayed from a maintainer also uses up the run's own fix round, and the refusal names it as the run's own. - Note: a run can record more than one self-grant for the same stop before it claims one. - Note: the stop message a preflight with no run id prints for a stopped record still says to let that run finish. - Note: review logging from any session on the checkout refreshes the run's heartbeat. - INFORMATIONAL security finding, details recorded privately (2 such notes). Exploratory QA: 5 functional probes of `gstack-ship-run` status and abandon, pass, rerun after the fix.
Documentation **Status:** updated. The audit made two factual terminology fixes and found no blockers. **Scope:** branch ship-run-record-replaces-stale-marker against base dd611038, using candidate docs2-pre.json (head dca87ed9, 28 selected files, plus unstaged edits to docs/review-policy.md, docs/ship-policy.md and docs/troubleshooting.md). Authored .md and .tmpl docs were searched for references to the old run marker and the 120-minute lease. **Documentation health:** - docs/ship-policy.md: Updated. The rule and test-coverage exception guards now say they read the run record, not the old marker, and link to the what-ends-a-run section. - docs/review-policy.md: Current. The stopped run's own follow-up grant (once per run) matches bin/gstack-approvals. - docs/troubleshooting.md: Current. The preflight-run-open, gate, STOP_UNBOUND, SHIP_RUN_ABANDON_REFUSED and SHIP_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE entries match the code. - docs/capy-install.md: Current. Its 120-minute text describes the separate workflow lease. **Debt:** no coverage gaps or diagram drift found. No generated output needs regenerating.

title: Skip the second Free Tests run when a PR lands onto a moved main (GST-3303)
body:
When the land tool merges a PR whose base moved, it has already run Free Tests on the exact merged tree. Main's push run now reuses that run instead of running the whole suite again, and still runs it whenever main moved again before the merge or the newest land run wasn't green. This also fixes the outdated `QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS` row in the maintainers' land guide. Nothing to do: the next stale-base land shows `REUSE: accepted run …` on main's push run.
How it decides, and why it's safe - `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts find` (main-push path): when the merged PR's head tree differs from the pushed tree, the only candidate is the newest `workflow_dispatch` run of `free-tests.yml` on `gstack-land/`. It's reused only when `verifyRun` accepts it under `ci-reuse/free-tests` and its `tested-tree` record names the pushed tree. - Only the newest land run counts, so a red retry on the same tree can't hide behind an older green one. A land run on another tree (main moved before the merge), an in-progress run, a `pull_request` run, another branch, or a profile without dispatch all fall back to the full suite. - No byte-identical check on the reuse files is needed here, unlike the pull-request consumer: the dispatch run executed the workflow from its own commit, whose tree is the tree now on main, so the rules it ran under are main's own, whoever dispatched it. - `landBranch()` in `lib/run-evidence.ts` is now the one source of the `gstack-land/` name for land and for reuse. - Docs: `docs/pregate.md#ci-reuse`, `docs/ship-policy.md#land-direct`, the `free-tests.yml` header, and the `QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS` row in the land guide (the hold-and-inspect case for files the checks changed, and the red `merged_ci` run).
Not verified live No `gstack-land/*` run exists yet. Two GitHub reads are untested against a deleted scratch branch: listing runs by `?branch=gstack-land/` and reading the scratch commit's tree. If either fails, the reuse job refuses and the push run tests the tree itself, as today.

title: Stop /sync-gbrain from importing plans and design docs twice when GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID names the artifacts source (#4443)
body:
`/sync-gbrain` no longer imports plans and design docs a second time on a machine that is also the brain host, once `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` names the artifacts source.
Why: the memory stage could not find a federated artifacts source registered at a gbrain clone path, so the duplication #2922 fixed came back on that layout.
Nothing to do unless gbrain registered your artifacts source at its own clone path; then set `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` to that source's id.

## Root cause

`federatedCuratedSourceId()` in `bin/gstack-gbrain-sync.ts` found the federated source only through `isArtifactsSourceRow()`, which accepts a `local_path` equal to the artifacts worktree (`GSTACK_BRAIN_WORKTREE`, default `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`) or the state root and nothing else. On a brain host, `gbrain sources add --url` or `--path ~/<id>` puts the clone somewhere else, so no source matched, `selectMemorySources()` passed no `--sources` filter, and `ceo-plan` and `design-doc` were imported again into the default source. The id override `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` was already read by `bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` and `brainSyncIndexVerdict()`, but not by this guard.

## Fix

When `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` is non empty after trimming, `federatedCuratedSourceId()` returns only a source with that exact id whose `federated` is `true`. An unknown or non federated id returns `null` with no fallback to the path match, so an explicit setting is never overridden by a guess, and the function writes one `[sync]` line to stderr naming the id and the consequence (the warning is skipped when `gbrain sources list` itself failed). When the variable is unset, empty or only spaces, the existing path match runs unchanged, still requiring `federated === true`. `brainSyncIndexVerdict()` now trims the variable the same way, so the memory stage and the brain sync page check pick the same source. `docs/gbrain-sync.md` gets one paragraph after the hookup step, and `changelog.d/fix-issue-4443-federated-source-id.md` carries the entry. `sync-gbrain/SKILL.md.tmpl` is unchanged: its sentence on skipped types stays true. Closes #4443.

## Tests

A new block in `test/gstack-gbrain-sync.test.ts` covers six cases against a fake `gbrain` on `PATH`, a bun script with a `gbrain.cmd` wrapper on Windows as in `test/helpers/sync-gbrain-readiness-fixture.ts`, with an env holding only a temp `HOME`, `GSTACK_HOME` and `PATH`. A source at an external clone without the variable gives `null` and no filter; a source at the default worktree is found by path and the curated types are skipped; the variable naming a source at an external clone skips them too; a non federated source named by the variable gives `null`; an unknown id gives `null` without falling back to a valid federated source at the worktree, and the warning goes to stderr and not stdout; a value of spaces only falls back to the path match. Every case checks that the fake was called, so a `null` cannot come from a fake that failed to start. With the source change stashed, the external clone with id case and the unknown id case fail, which shows the block guards this fix.

On Windows 11 with bun 1.4.5, the six cases pass, `bun run typecheck` reports no error and `bun run typecheck:test` reports no new diagnostic. `test/gstack-gbrain-sync.test.ts` and `test/regression-2922-memory-ingest-sources.test.ts` together give 51 pass, 12 skip and 13 fail; the 13 failures are the same tests by name on untouched main, all using the existing `#!/bin/sh` shims that cannot run on Windows.

The full free suite (`bun run test`) was started on that Windows machine but was stopped partway because the machine ran low on memory, so it gives no result for this change. Before it stopped, every failure it reported came from files this PR does not touch, most of them suites built on bash or macOS tools, and those were not rerun on main. The full validation of this PR relies on the Linux CI in `free-tests.yml`.

## Out of scope

`bin/gstack-gbrain-source-wireup` still tests `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` without trimming it, so a value with surrounding spaces is used as is there. `brainSyncIndexVerdict()` still accepts a source named by the variable even when it is not federated, while the memory stage guard requires `federated === true`; the two functions answer different questions (page count versus skip), so changing that rule is left to a separate decision.

title: Installing gstack for the docs step no longer stops /ship from running (#3561)
body:
When /ship's documentation step installs gstack for `document-release` on the same machine, /ship keeps permission to run instead of losing it mid-run.
This keeps the install-then-ship flow on shared Capy machines working end to end (the README's one-command install goal).
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A machine that ran `install.sh --for ship` and then `install.sh --for document-release` (which /ship's docs step does) ended up with an install record that only covered the docs workflow, so /ship refused to continue (`INSTALL_UNVERIFIED`). Now an install at the same checkout, project, gstack revision and Bun adds its workflow to the existing record instead of replacing it: `for` becomes `ship,document-release`, the list of checked components becomes the union of both runs, and pins count as skipped only when both runs skipped them. The installer prints `the install verdict at <file> keeps for=ship and adds document-release (for=ship,document-release)`. A failing install, a new revision, another Bun or a review-voice record still replace the record as before.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"An install for one workflow keeps the other current" (#3561): a second install on a shared machine silently took /ship's permission away halfway through a run. Now each install keeps what the earlier one proved, as long as the checkout, revision and Bun are the same.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `record_verdict` in `bin/gstack-capy-install` changes; it now reads the existing record before writing. Every reader of `for` either prints it or compares it to the `review-voice` profile name, and a merged list never equals that name because the merge is skipped for profile records (read at `lib/install-verdict.ts:112,181` and `bin/gstack-install-verdict.sh:139-149`). Admission itself checks `required`, which only grows. The new test and the 59 existing installer tests pass (`test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts`, 60 tests).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

One informational finding, fixed: the new code comment and docs said each install also writes a separate per-workflow record (`<verdict>.for/<workflow>.json`), but nothing writes that file, so those claims and an empty test comment were removed. A follow-up check of that fix found nothing. A separate adversarial read raised four notes below the blocking floor, listed under Review notes; none was changed in this PR.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- CRITICAL `bin/gstack-capy-install:452` A planning-workflow run that prints SKIP pins (planning-only; repo pins differ) at the same HEAD and Bun inherits pins_planning_only=false from an earlier ship verdict, so /ship stays admitted although the newest check saw a repo pin mismatch (before this change the narrower verdict refused /ship).
- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-capy-install:448` --check for a narrow workflow carries forward earlier required ids it did not re-check.
- CRITICAL `bin/gstack-capy-install:447` The read-merge-write of the shared verdict has no lock, so two overlapping installs for different workflows can drop one workflow from for/required; a rerun fixes it.
- CRITICAL `bin/gstack-capy-install:453` A --require run (FOR empty) merges its required ids silently: for keeps the old value and no 'adds' line prints.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional smoke on the post-fix tree: `bun test test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts -t 'keeps both'` (1 pass) and the whole installer test file (60 pass). Not probed: a later install for another workflow that fails or resolves another Bun after a /ship install; that path still replaces the record, as before this change.

</details>

A new HEAD still replaces both.

title: Installing gstack for a second workflow no longer drops the first one (#3561)
body:
When gstack is installed for /ship and then again for its documentation step on the same machine, the install record now keeps both workflows instead of replacing the first.
Why: /ship lost permission to run halfway through when its docs step reinstalled gstack for a narrower workflow.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![record_verdict now merges an earlier ok verdict at the same HEAD and Bun instead of replacing it](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/dMnx0UQSzQVdloSx5CTrOpz_6XDawOFrdOT9xbRDhEk.png)

record_verdict now merges an earlier ok verdict at the same HEAD and Bun instead of replacing it.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: record_verdict now merges an earlier ok verdict at the same HEAD and Bun instead of replacing it</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
 record_verdict() { # TRAILER OK — --check keeps the recorded resolution (drift is reported, never re-recorded)
+  local v_for="${FOR:-}" v_req v_plan e_for id
   if verdict_kept; then
     say "kept the install verdict for=$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" for) at $VERDICT (it covers more than $FOR; the trailer below is this check's)"
     return 0
   fi
   if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 1 ] && [ -n "$REC_BUN" ]; then set -- "$1" "$2" "$REC_BUN" "$REC_VER" "$REC_RULE" "$REC_BUN_INSTALL"
   else set -- "$1" "$2" "$RES_BIN" "$RES_VER" "$RES_RULE" "${BUN_INSTALL:-}"; fi
+  v_req=$(printf '%s\n' "${OUT:-}" | sed -n 's/^required: //p' | head -1)
+  v_plan=$(printf '%s\n' "${OUT:-}" | grep -q '^SKIP pins (planning-only' && echo 1 || echo 0)
+  if [ "$2" = 1 ] && [ "$PROFILE" -eq 0 ] && [ -f "$VERDICT" ] && [ "$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" ok)" = true ] \
+     && [ "$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" head)" = "$HEAD_SHA" ] && [ "$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" checkout)" = "$ROOT_REAL" ] \
+     && [ "$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" bun_path)" = "$3" ] && e_for=$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" for) \
+     && ! gstack_doctor_install_profile "$e_for"; then
+    for id in $(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" required); do
+      case " $v_req " in *" $id "*) ;; *) v_req="$v_req $id" ;; esac
+    done
+    [ "$(gstack_install_verdict_field "$VERDICT" pins_planning_only)" = true ] || v_plan=0
+    case ",$e_for," in *",$v_for,"*) v_for="$e_for" ;; *) v_for="${e_for:+$e_for${v_for:+,}}$v_for" ;; esac
+    [ "$v_for" = "$e_for" ] || [ -z "$e_for" ] || say "the install verdict at $VERDICT keeps for=$e_for and adds ${FOR:-$REQUIRE} (for=$v_for)"
+  fi
+  gstack_install_verdict_write "$VERDICT" "$ROOT_REAL" "$HEAD_SHA" "$v_for" "$v_req" "$v_plan" "$2" "$1" "${MIN_REVISION:-}" "$LAUNCH_DIR" \
-  gstack_install_verdict_write "$VERDICT" "$ROOT_REAL" "$HEAD_SHA" "${FOR:-}" "$(printf '%s\n' "${OUT:-}" | sed -n 's/^required: //p' | head -1)" \
-    "$(printf '%s\n' "${OUT:-}" | grep -q '^SKIP pins (planning-only' && echo 1 || echo 0)" "$2" "$1" "${MIN_REVISION:-}" "$LAUNCH_DIR" \
     "$PROJECT_REAL" "$PIN_EXACT" "$3" "$4" "$5" "$6" "$NODE_BIN" "$NODE_VER" "$NODE_RULE" \
     || say "could not write the install verdict $VERDICT"
 }
~~~

</details>

A /ship run on a shared machine installs gstack `--for ship`, and its documentation step later installs `--for document-release`. The second install wrote a narrower verdict over the first, so /ship was refused for the rest of its run. Now an ok install at the same checkout, project, gstack revision and Bun keeps what the earlier ok install certified. The required components become the union, pins count as planning-only only when both runs skipped them, and the verdict's `for` lists both workflows (`for=ship,document-release`). The installer prints one line when it does this. A failing install, a new revision or another Bun still replaces the verdict.

The docs in `docs/capy-install.md` and the verdict header in `bin/gstack-install-verdict.sh` describe the merged verdict. A new test runs `--for ship` then `--for document-release`, checks both workflows stay admitted, and checks that a new revision replaces the merged verdict.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"/ship's docs step reinstalls gstack for document-release and /ship then gets INSTALL_UNVERIFIED" (#3561). One machine now stays admitted for both workflows when both installs pass on the same revision and Bun.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `record_verdict` in `bin/gstack-capy-install` changed behavior; it merges only when the new run passed, the old verdict is ok, and checkout, HEAD and Bun all match, so every other path writes exactly what it wrote before. Admission reads `required`, not the `for` text (lib/install-verdict.ts:175-185, read), and a comma-separated `for` never equals a read-only profile name, so profile checks are unchanged (file:line read; 60 installer tests passed locally and CI carried the full free suite).

</details>

Nothing in this tree writes that record, and a probe confirmed a failed docs install still drops /ship's admission, so the claim was removed rather than kept as a promise. A second-model review and a reread of the fixed lines found nothing blocking; their notes are below.

title: Nightly Windows tests stop timing out: shards pack by Windows test times (GST-3440)
body:
The nightly Windows test run no longer cancels a shard at its 15-minute limit: files without a Windows time use their Linux time instead of a 161 s guess, and the plan adds shards past eight until no shard holds more than 12 minutes.
Why: one shard on #4646's tree held 946 s of Windows work against a 900 s job and was cancelled twice (run 44971202453); any PR adding test files could trip it.
Nothing to do: the Windows run is nightly-only and this changes no test selection, timeout or retry.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

The nightly Windows run kept losing a shard to its 15-minute job limit. Files that the Windows timing record didn't list were packed as if each took 161 s, so packing balanced made-up load and some shards ended up with more real work than the job allows. Now a file missing from the Windows record uses its Linux time, and the Windows plan adds shards beyond eight (up to sixteen) until no shard is predicted past 720 s. If even sixteen shards can't fit, the plan fails and says to refresh the Windows timing record.

- `scripts/test-free-shards.ts`: `--windows-only --ci-plan` reads `free-test-durations-windows.json` over `free-test-durations.json` per file. The new `--shard-budget-seconds` flag, passed only by `windows-free-tests.yml` with 720 (80% of the job), makes `createWindowsCiPlan` grow the shard count from `--shards` up to twice that. The scoped Windows check's single-shard listing plan takes no budget and is unchanged.
- `windows-free-tests.yml`: the plan step drops its `GSTACK_FREE_TEST_DURATIONS` override, since the planner now reads the Windows record itself.
- `scripts/test-pr-profile.ts`: an edit to `scripts/free-test-durations-windows.json` no longer selects paid test cases, because only the free Windows plan reads it (harness pin updated, non-behavioral).

On the committed timing records, main 7abc194 plans 8 shards with shards 1 and 7 at 835 s and 832 s; this branch plans 10 shards, the heaviest at 650 s. Replayed on #4646's tree b6d4150: the old plan's shard 3 held 946 s; the new plan has 9 shards, the heaviest at 670 s.

</details>

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

- The old plan already read the Windows seed (run 44971202453's plan log names 27 unseeded files, the Windows seed's count). The defect was the 161 s Windows 99th-percentile estimate for those files: packing balanced that phantom load, so shards with fewer unseeded files carried more real work.
- New test in `test/windows-native-workflows.test.ts` runs the workflow's own plan step on the real seeds and fails if any shard's recorded Windows time (Linux fallback) or prediction passes 720 s. On main 7abc194 it fails with shards 1 and 7 at 835 s and 832 s; with the fix it passes (10 shards, heaviest 650 s).
- Replayed on #4646's tree b6d4150: old plan shard 3 at 946 s; new plan 9 shards, heaviest 670 s.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"One shard on #4646's tree held 946 s of Windows work against a 900 s job and was cancelled twice (run 44971202453)." The nightly Windows result now completes instead of losing a shard whenever a PR adds test files.

</details>

Only plans built with `--windows-only --ci-plan` read the Windows record, and only the nightly workflow passes the budget, so the Linux plan, the scoped Windows check (`--shards 1`) and every PR check are unchanged. title: browse: `--session` before the command is read as the command, Windows gets no automatic session, and subagents share one
body:
gstack 1.102.2.0 (5db285c1). `browse/src/cli.ts`, `browse/src/session-name.ts`, and `BROWSER.md` are byte-identical to `main` at 69ad103 (checked with `curl` of the raw files and `cmp`). Claude Code 2.1.330, Windows 11, Git Bash.

During a review, four agents drove one browse daemon in parallel. Each was told to use its own session name and its own origin. Three problems came up.

## 1. `--session` placed before the command fails

The help lists `--session <name> | BROWSE_SESSION=<name>` under Tabs without saying where the flag goes. One agent ran `browse --session inventory <command>` and got `Unknown command: '--session'`. The flag works after the command, and `BROWSE_SESSION=inventory` works.

Cause: in `main()`, `extractGlobalFlags` (cli.ts line 1392) strips only `--force-restart`, `--proxy`, and `--headed`. Then `const command = args[0]` (line 1896) takes the first remaining word. `extractSession` runs later, inside `sendCommand` (line 1100), and only sees the arguments after the command. A leading `--session` therefore becomes the command name, and the server answers with the unknown-command message from commands.ts line 278.

Suggestion: strip `--session <name>` in `extractGlobalFlags` too, so it works in any position the way `--headed` and `--proxy` do, and pass it on to `sendCommand`. If it should stay a command-level flag, say "after the command" in the help line and in BROWSER.md.

## 2. Windows never gets an automatic session, but the docs say agents get one

BROWSER.md ("Sessions keep parallel agents on their own tabs") says a call from a known agent harness gets a session named after that agent process, and the help says "agents get one per agent process." On Windows that can't happen. `systemProcLookup()` in session-name.ts reads `/proc` on Linux and `ps` on macOS, and returns `() => null` on every other platform (line 85), so `autoSessionName` never finds a harness. Every agent on a Windows machine shares the active tab unless it sets `BROWSE_SESSION` or `--session` itself. I found this by reading the source; I didn't run a separate Windows test of the automatic path.

Suggestion: add a Windows process-table lookup, or state the platform limit in BROWSER.md and the help line so Windows users know to set a session per agent.

## 3. Subagents in one harness process share one automatic session

Claude Code subagents run inside the parent's process. As far as I can tell from `harnessOf`, every subagent's shell resolves to the same harness pid and gets the same automatic session, even where the lookup works. The documentation-debt list in #3773 already names this gap (no how-to for parallel subagents that share one agent process). In our run the agents set their own names, which kept the tabs apart, but two other things leaked:

- Sessions isolate tabs, not cookies or storage (BROWSER.md says so), so agents testing the same origin would share IndexedDB. We gave each agent its own origin to avoid that.
- Two agents wrote helper scripts with the same file name into one shared scratch folder. One overwrote the other, and two of one agent's commands ran in the other agent's session. They were read-only commands, so nothing was damaged.

Suggestion: add a short "several agents at once" how-to to BROWSER.md and the browse skill. Set `BROWSE_SESSION` per agent (or put the flag after the command). Give each agent its own origin or port when the app keeps client-side storage. Keep any helper script that names a session in that agent's own folder, never in a shared scratch folder.

## Principle

When parallel agents share one stateful tool, isolation has to cover everything that carries the session identity: the flag or variable, the storage origin, and any helper file that hard-codes it. A flag should also work where the help shows it.

Related: #1961 and #3773 (per-agent session tabs, which this builds on), and #4558 (a second daemon started from a different directory, which has a different cause).

title: The merge queue checks a pull request against the branch it targets, not the default branch (GST-3445)
body:
`gstack-ship-queue ready` now checks a pull request against the branch it targets, so a PR into a branch other than main is no longer refused when its /ship review was done against that branch.
Why: Founderstar #1024 targets `garrytan/v0.2-plan-wip`, and ready refused its correct /ship review record because it compared that record against main.
Nothing to do: until this lands, passing `--base <the PR's base>` to ready works around it.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- Without `--base`, `ready` reads the base of the PR that `--pr` names (`gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName`). Before, it used origin/HEAD first, which is the default branch. If gh can't answer, it falls back to the old lookup.
- `ready` then reads the PR's base a second time, in the same `gh pr view` call that checks the PR's state, and refuses with QUEUE_NOT_READY ("#N targets X, not Y") when that base differs from the one it checks against or can't be read. So a failed first lookup, or a base name that starts with `origin/`, ends in a refusal instead of a wrong READY.
- `ready` refuses an explicit `--base` that isn't the PR's base. Before, `--base main` on a PR into another branch would accept a review record made against main.
- `land` keeps using the default branch unless `--base` names another, so it still refuses a stacked PR instead of merging it into its parent branch.
- A review record made against any branch other than the PR's base is still refused.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

New test file `test/ship-queue-ready-pr-base.test.ts`. Its fixture has origin/HEAD set to main and a PR into `garrytan/v0.2-plan-wip`. These cases fail on main 69ad103:
- With no `--base`, the case fails with Founderstar's exact refusal. A review record for the PR's base is now accepted, and one for main is still refused.
- With `--base main`, main printed READY. It now refuses with QUEUE_NOT_READY.

One more case in the same file checks the second base read in `ready`. Both parts printed READY (exit 0) at c531eb9 and now refuse with exit 3:
- (a) the first base lookup fails, so `ready` falls back to main for a PR into another branch;
- (b) the PR's base is named `origin/foo`.

`test/ship-queue-land-direct.test.ts` adds one case: `land --pin` with no `--base` refuses a stacked PR shipped against its parent branch and merges nothing.

The new test file spawns shell fixtures, so it gets a Windows curation entry like test/ship-queue-ready-fresh-base.test.ts.

</details>

**Scope:** branch `ship-queue-uses-the-pr-base` against base `69ad1031` (head `ef08d775`): `gstack-ship-queue ready` defaults `--base` to the base of the PR that `--pr` names, refuses a mismatched explicit `--base`, and `lib/ship-queue.ts` refuses a PR whose base is not the queue's base. `land` still defaults to the main branch.

title: A granted fix round that a follow-up check reads clean now closes the findings it fixed (GST-3260)
body:
/ship now closes a review finding when its fix round was granted and a follow-up check read the fix clean, or when the fix commit names the finding and a later full review reads it clean. Before, someone had to write a ruling by hand. Why: since this was missing, PRs whose findings were already fixed and checked stalled at the round limit (#4537, harness-evals#508, #4597, harness-evals#504, #4612). Nothing to do.
What changed - `lib/fix-check-clearing.ts` is now the only place that decides whether a granted follow-up check closes findings. Both `finish` and the PR's /ship record writer call it. A fix round closes only the findings its grant names, and only when all of these hold: - the grant belongs to this PR and this run, and the grant hasn't been used yet; - the PR body records the stop the grant answers; - the follow-up check's review-log row covers the same range and the same hunks digest; - nothing else is left open. When any of these is missing, it prints a `FIX_CHECK_CLEAR:` line saying why. - A finding whose fix commit carries its `Review-Finding:` trailer also closes once a later full review round reads it clean (#4597). - `finish` counts a granted follow-up check from the stop its grant names, not from the newest reviewed tree (#4612). - The review plan sends a follow-up check grant that answers a stop raised after an earlier follow-up check to its single follow-up check (harness-evals#504). Reviewer prompts, packets and review depth are unchanged: `lib/review-depth.ts` is byte-identical to the parent branch. - Copy installs on other hosts keep working, because the new code imports nothing from `scripts/`.
Tests New file `test/fix-check-clearing.test.ts` with 23 tests. Of the first 21, 18 failed on the parent branch: - Negative cases, one per gap the closed #4546 had: another PR's grant, no stop record, another run's claim, a grant already used, another range, two findings with the same fingerprint, an open critical, an inline low finding left open, a newer review on a dirty tree, and a grant id that names nothing. - Positive replays shaped like #4537, harness-evals#508, #4597, harness-evals#504 and #4612. - A byte-equality check on the follow-up check's reviewer prompt. The only existing test files changed are fixtures: one exercised-map entry, one Windows curation entry and one module-size entry.
Issues Refs #4591 Refs #4597 Refs #4612
Agent notes - Approved plan: GST-3260 plan-v2, PR 2 plus amendments A, B, D, E, H, I and the item 10 dedupe. It was stacked on #4654, which merged as e8e75547; the branch is now based on main. - Commits: 1eb2332 (grant clearing, #4612, #504 routing), eff9e4e (trailer route, #4597), 301feb7 (reverted an edit to the byte-pinned `lib/review-depth.ts`; kept `lib/` free of `scripts/` imports for copy installs), 79a0671 (review pass 1 fixes), b2d3ab4 (rebuilt on main after #4654 merged; this PR's own lines byte-identical to 79a0671), c74e8ca (test-only fixture fix under fix-check grant a-3d9a27629e31, ruled by GSTA-36), 942b581 (changelog), ac9163d (docs/review-policy.md receipt table). - Checks at ac9163d: CI is the full run. Free-tests run 44992209844 is green (38,834 tests), and the macOS and Windows checks are green. `fix_checks: 1` counts the follow-up check that ran; finish didn't count it (`FIX_CHECK: not counted`, because its row names no range_base). The two pass-2 findings are closed by the review-loop exception below, not by that check. - Open notes from the cross-family trail read, ruled by Captain GStack Minder (GSTA-36) as a split: "Split: flag 2 needs a full review that finished with nothing open but didn't converge; flag 3 needs a fingerprint-only security closure, which /ship never produces. Both fixed first in PR 3." PR 3's first commit fixes all three, with failing-first tests. 1. `lib/fix-check-clearing.ts:71`: an unreadable dispatch ledger reads as empty, because `readLedger` swallows the error, so the "ledger unreadable" refusal never fires. 2. `lib/fix-check-clearing.ts:130-134`: the trailer route accepts a completed full review with an `incomplete` binding and never checks `converged`. 3. `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:322-323,408,439-445`: closure ids are added after the body's security scan, so a fingerprint-only security closure would be unredacted. ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-07c3938e7165). title: Review leaves out copied open-source files that match their upstream byte for byte (GST-3298)
body:
Files a repo copies unchanged from an allowlisted open-source project, and that gstack verifies byte for byte against the pinned upstream commit, can now be left out of `/ship`'s review under `review_exclude_paths`.
Why: verified upstream code doesn't need a reviewer, so its bytes no longer count toward the 2 MB reader limit, while every other keep rule still applies.
Nothing to do for repos without `review_vendored`: their review selection is unchanged (216 of 216 replayed commits identical).

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Repos that copy whole open-source test suites hit the 2 MB reader limit, because review had to read every copied file as if the repo had written it. Now a file that a `review_exclude_paths` pattern matches, and that `review_vendored` verifies byte for byte against an allowlisted upstream at the pinned commit, counts as vendored content and can leave the reviewers' diff.

- Agent prose, config, executables, links, `.github/` and `.gstack/`, gate paths, credential lines and gate tags still keep a file. A gate-tagged upstream test file stays in review whole.
- A verified vendored file still counts as code when review looks for files that name excluded content, so a file it names by full path stays in review exactly as it did before.
- A file the branch drops from the manifest but keeps and changes stays in review. Only a file the branch deletes is checked against the old pin.
- When a pattern matches a manifest the branch changes, nothing counts as verified and the plan prints `REVIEW_VENDORED: unavailable`.
- `gstack-review-plan` fetches the upstreams and prints what verified and what didn't. The review dispatch and the final ship check read the same cache without the network, and the verified list is part of the selection the final ship check binds.
- When unverified vendored files make a pattern keep too many files, the refusal names them and points at `gstack-vendored-verify`, which also stops trusting a cached copy of an upstream branch that was deleted.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change is inside `reviewExclude` and only runs when the base branch declares `review_vendored`; gstack itself does not, and the no-loss replay over 216 first-parent commits in gstack, harness-evals and gstack-evals produced identical selections (replay fixture read and test run). The plan's JSON now carries the vendored check as `vendored_selection`; its only readers are the review dispatch, which reads the numeric count, and this PR's tests (callers read).

</details>

<details><summary>What this does not fix</summary>

harness-evals#504 still goes over the 2 MB reader limit: 161 gate-tagged upstream test files (5.83 MB, mostly skip markers) stay in review whole by design (5 more gate-tagged files, pyproject.toml, are shown as excerpts), so that PR needs a separate change.

</details>

<details><summary>Known limit</summary>

A machine whose vendored cache is empty verifies nothing, so the final ship check there refuses until `gstack-vendored-verify --base <base>` fills it.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

This commit got one final full review with no fix round, because the PR had already been through two review rounds. The targeted reader for the gate path found nothing, and the second-model review completed. Seven findings were raised at blocking severity; none of them fails a test, breaks production or loses data or secrets. Each one either refuses to run instead of running wrongly, or says something wrong in a message, and only in repos that set `review_vendored` (none does today). Each is listed under Agent notes as a ruled note, and a follow-up PR closes them. Two missing tests are ruled notes too.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `sf-73eeaff8b633` security finding, details recorded privately
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-949e084a49a4` security finding, details recorded privately
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-vendored.ts:119` The head's manifest chooses local and upstream prefixes, so verified upstream files such as conftest.py can land in directories where they run; a trust-model question.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Two command-line checks on owned local fixtures passed: `gstack-review-plan --base main` on gstack itself (no `review_vendored`) exits 0 and prints no vendored lines, and a vendored file one byte off its pin stays in review as code and is named as `REVIEW_VENDORED_KEPT`. The live fetch from real upstreams, a machine with an empty cache and lock timeouts were not probed.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

Scope: a read-only audit of `review-skips-verified-vendored-files` against `main` (head 184a50a), covering committed changes plus a check for staged, unstaged and new files (none found). It read the branch's doc edits (docs/vendored-code.md, docs/ship-policy.md, the changelog.d fragment) and searched the repository for related or stale mentions of `review_vendored` and `REVIEW_VENDORED`. Result: current. The new "What review leaves out" section and the updated `review_vendored` policy row match the code in lib/review-vendored.ts, lib/review-exclude.ts and bin/gstack-review-plan. The old "a later release lets" wording is gone, and docs/troubleshooting.md is still accurate. Debt: none found.

</details>

title: Free test shards stop failing when a test's browser exits during the cleanup check (GST-3447)
body:
Free test shards no longer fail with "native process identity unavailable" when a browser a test started exits while the runner is checking it, and the Free Tests planning job gets 10 minutes instead of 5. Why: these were the two causes left of main's flapping Free Tests runs; the other four flaps from 11-18 and 11-19 were fixed earlier by #4490 and #4530. Nothing to do.
What changed Free test shards were failing with no failing test: "shard 8/8 shard cleanup or home containment failed: native process identity unavailable" (quick-bun-default, run 44850005025 at 41729a02). The shard's browser cleanup tracker checks each browser process it owns by reading its start time with `ps -o lstart=`. When that browser exited on its own during the check, the tracker counted it as an ownership failure and failed the whole shard. Now a process that is provably gone just ends that round of checking, and the next round sees it gone. A failed check of a process that is still alive, a process whose identity was replaced, and every ownership mismatch still fail the shard, and a real error is reported ahead of an exit seen in the same round. A new test mode, `identity-probe-exit`, uses a stand-in `ps` that kills the recorded Chromium child during its first check; it fails before the fix with the exact CI message and passes after. The Free Tests planning job (`free-plan`) now has 10 minutes instead of 5: its "Set up job" step alone ran 5m18s on run 44980222821 and the job was cancelled, while the job normally takes 13 to 26 seconds.
Why "Free Tests on main keeps going red with no failing test." These two causes were the last ones behind main's flapping Free Tests runs, so after this a red Free Tests run should point at a real test failure.
Blast radius The change touches only the free test runner's browser cleanup tracker (`scripts/test-free-shards.ts`), its test helper and one workflow timeout. The tracker still reports every live-process, replaced-identity and ownership failure: the replaced-pid, replaced-start, stale-child-start and unavailable-environment settlement modes were rerun on this head and pass (script ran), and CI's full free suite passed at this head (run 44993690417).
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. The review panel (batched specialist, red team, targeted gate reader, a second-model review on GPT-6.1 Sol and an adversarial reader) found nothing that blocks. The one gate change, the planning job's longer timeout, was reviewed and kept by the owner with the measurement above.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/test-free-shards.ts:1419` error-handling - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/test-free-shards.ts:1345` observability - INFORMATIONAL `test/helpers/free-owned-browser-settlement.ts:167` test-isolation - INFORMATIONAL `test/test-free-shards-settlement-lifecycle.test.ts:1` flaky-test
Exploratory QA Pass. Capture 001: `identity-probe-exit` passes (1 pass, 0 fail). Capture 002: unavailable-environment, replaced-pid, replaced-start, stale-child-start, cancel-cold-probes and settle-cold-probes pass (6 pass, 0 fail). The probe stand-in modes are Linux-only, so macOS and Windows coverage comes from CI.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Scope:** branch `free-tests-browser-exit-during-identity-check` against base 6484fd58. It changes the Free Tests workflow (free-plan timeout raised from 5 to 10 minutes), the shard browser cleanup tracker in `scripts/test-free-shards.ts` (a browser that exits during its identity check now ends the check instead of failing the shard), its test helper, and one changelog.d fragment. **Result:** current. I searched README, CONTRIBUTING, docs/ and skill Markdown. `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` and `docs/pregate.md` name the `free-plan` job and artifact but describe neither its timeout nor the tracker's identity-check behavior, so nothing became stale. The changelog fragment matches the code change. **Debt:** none found. The tracker's identity-check rules are documented only in code and in the changelog fragment.

title: Publish the /ship conductor trial results (GST-3003)
body:
Adds the results of the preregistered trial of /ship with and without its conductor subagent: running /ship in the pull request's own thread showed no clear difference in cost or bugs caught over 30 paired runs. The verdict hangs on one scoring ruling made after seeing data, so it goes to the owner with both readings; nothing in /ship changes in this PR. Nothing to do but read [docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-results.md](docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-results.md).
What the numbers say - Cost a run, folded minus conductor: +$0.07 (-$1.42 to +$1.57). Planted bugs: 22 of 30 against 21 of 30. Real problems, after removing restatements of the planted bug: -0.03 (-0.37 to +0.32) over 6 cases. No structural loss. - Reader fidelity: 30 of 30 under the ruling, 29 of 30 read literally, which flips the plan's decision. - The no-gstack arm caught 16 of 30 planted bugs at $0.83 a run; its gap to /ship's better arm only just reaches zero, so /ship's review panel gets a "Why null?" check under G3.

title: Merge queue ready fetches missing pull request heads in one go, says so, and stops after 60 seconds (GST-3460)
body:
`gstack-ship-queue ready` no longer goes silent for minutes on a long merge queue: it fetches every missing pull request head in one `git fetch`, prints a progress line first, and stops after 60 seconds. Why: on gbrain #10011 ready printed nothing for minutes, so nobody could tell a slow fetch from a hang. Nothing to do; `GSTACK_TRIAL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` changes the limit.
What was happening A trace of the stuck run showed one pass, not a loop. Ready checks the PR against every open PR that touches the same files by merging the two heads in memory. Any head missing from the clone was fetched with its own `git fetch origin refs/pull//head`, one at a time, and each fetch could take up to 120 s. Ready prints its whole report at the end, so nothing appeared until every fetch was done. The trace ended inside `git fetch origin refs/pull/9946/head`, 26 s into that one fetch.
What changed Ready's trial merges against other open pull requests used to fetch each missing head on its own, one after another, allowing 120 s per fetch, and said nothing until the end. Now the missing heads come down in one `git fetch` (one at a time only if that fails), all inside one 60 s limit, and ready prints a line to stderr before it starts: ``` gstack-ship-queue ready: TRIAL_MERGES: fetching 12 PR head(s) from origin (time limit 60 s): refs/pull/2/head ... (+7 more) ``` When the limit runs out, ready refuses with `QUEUE_NOT_READY` and names each `refs/pull//head` it was waiting on, instead of printing READY with that trial merge missing.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/ship-queue-trial-fetch.test.ts test/ship-queue-ready-tail.test.ts test/ship-queue-ready-fresh-base.test.ts test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts`: 40 pass, 0 fail - [x] `bun run test`: carried from CI run 44989710296 at this tree (38,819 tests)
Why "ready printed nothing for minutes" (gbrain #10011). The wait is now bounded and announced, and a fetch that cannot finish stops ready instead of slipping through.
Blast radius Only `ready` (and the batched landing path, which calls `ready()`) runs the trial merges; `git()` in crew/lib/ship-queue-gate.ts gains an optional timeout whose default stays 120 s, so its other callers are unchanged (file:line read). The new stderr line cannot break a caller, because nothing parses ready's stderr (read across the source tree by the reviewers).
Test Coverage Tests: 1863 → 1864 (+1 new). The new file test/ship-queue-trial-fetch.test.ts has 4 cases: one combined fetch for twelve missing heads with the progress line first; a fast-failing combined fetch falling back to one fetch per ref and still trial-merging the rest; a stalled fetch stopping at the limit; and ready refusing `QUEUE_NOT_READY` naming the ref. Left untested: the fallback loop running out of time partway through. Tests ran: focused 40
Pre-Landing Review One full review pass (testing, security and state-machine checklists, red team), one follow-up read of the fix, a Claude adversarial pass and a second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol). Pass 1 found one test gap (the fallback path), fixed in 51cac14; the follow-up read found nothing. The second-model review raised two findings it marked blocking: presence checks can fetch lazily on a partial clone outside the 60 s limit, and ready finds a stall by matching a sentence in its own output. The maintainer accepted both as open notes (see Agent notes): the first is unchanged old behaviour, and the second can only cause a refusal, never a wrong READY.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - A negative, fractional or infinite `GSTACK_TRIAL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` makes `spawnSync` throw instead of giving a coded refusal (lib/ship-queue.ts:315). - A null exit status also covers a failed spawn or another signal, which is reported as a stall (lib/ship-queue.ts:321). - The combined fetch gets the full limit although the clock started before the presence checks (lib/ship-queue.ts:321). - A timed-out `git fetch`'s transport child processes are not killed; Bun's `spawnSync` still returns at the limit (crew/lib/ship-queue-gate.ts:51).
Exploratory QA Functional smoke, report-only, on owned fixture repositories: the combined fetch, stall and refusal cases passed (`bun test test/ship-queue-trial-fetch.test.ts`, 3 of 3), and a probe with one sibling ref missing from origin showed the fallback recovering the other three heads (5 fetches, plain MISSING line, no stall). One probe was a test-runner selector error and was rerun. Revalidated after the fix: 4 of 4 pass. Not probed: the fallback running out of time partway through.
Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.
Review bot comments Review bot triage: not run in this /ship invocation.
Issues Refs #10011 Refs p1/specialist-batched#1
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Scope:** This audit covers the trial-merge fetch change on tree 43511a407711020f5a2d7d76756e2ebce178a530, run in ship-owned edit mode (Steps 1, 1.5, 2-4 and 6 only). I reviewed changelog.d/ready-finishes-fast-on-a-long-queue.md, crew/lib/ship-queue-gate.ts, lib/ship-queue.ts, scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts, test/ship-queue-trial-fetch.test.ts, docs/unattended.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and docs/ship-policy.md. **Result:** I updated two docs and left the edits uncommitted. - docs/unattended.md: the TRIAL_MERGES paragraph now covers the fetch. Missing heads are fetched in one go, with a 60 s limit you can change with `GSTACK_TRIAL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`. ready prints a progress line first and refuses with `QUEUE_NOT_READY` when the limit runs out. - docs/troubleshooting.md: the `QUEUE_NOT_READY` entry now lists the fetch timeout as a cause and gives its fix. - docs/ship-policy.md: current. Line 875 mentions the sibling trial merge only in passing and does not describe fetch behavior. - changelog.d fragment: reviewed but not edited, because it already describes the change accurately. - Every other doc in the candidate list: no reference to this change. No templates or generated files changed, so nothing needs regenerating. The banned-terms check reported none (the repo has no .gstack/banned-terms.json). **Debt:** There are no blockers and no documentation debt. title: /ship keeps a PR's review after a main merge that only updates a shared harness pin, and warns when reviewers ran unlogged (GST-3463)
body:
A pull request no longer needs a fresh /ship when merging main only updates a harness pin file it shares with another PR, and /ship's review summary now warns when reviewers produced output that the run never logged.
Why: #4652 paid for a full new review after such a merge, and a harness-evals run lost its granted follow-up review because nothing was logged.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A sibling PR that touched the same pinned harness file used to lose its saved review after a main merge and pay for a whole new review, even though the only change was a pin file recording the new contents of a file that was already compared. Now a harness pin file counts as generated output when, before and after the merge, it records exactly the pinned file's contents with the same reason, and the harness version and patterns did not change. The pinned file itself is still compared, so any real change still needs a new review.

The review summary also prints a warning line when a run's reviewers wrote output that no review-log row of the run records, so a run that skipped logging hears about it before the follow-up review it was granted fails to bind. Each review pass and each follow-up review is checked against its own kind of row, so a logged row of another kind no longer hides a missing one. The warning never changes the exit code. The Capy skill now says never to run a reviewer by hand, and the review policy lists the new warning.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

#4652 paid for a fresh review after a main merge that only re-recorded a shared harness pin, and harness-evals#507 lost its granted follow-up review because the run's reviewers were never logged.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The pin rule runs only when /ship decides whether a saved review still covers the new head (lib/ship-receipt-patch.ts productSpec) and fails closed: a missing or malformed harness manifest, a pin that is not an object, a changed reason or a moved harness version all count as a real change, as the four new tests show (one keeps the review, three refuse). The warning is stderr only in bin/gstack-review-scope summary; exit codes and the summary JSON are unchanged, which a negative-control test and the existing review-scope suites (129 tests) confirm.

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

Coverage: 9 of 13 new code paths tested (69%). Gaps, all in fail-closed or diagnostic paths: manifest patterns changed at the same version, a missing or malformed pin or manifest, a rewritten-history re-pin, and a review row of another pass number beside first-pass reviewer output.
Tests ran: test 1745 (files, CI run 44997575097)

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

A final full review of this head ran read-only (no fix round): a batched testing, security and state-machines read, a red-team read, a money-focused read, an adversarial read and a second-model review. The second-model review repeated one finding: a harness pin turned into a symlink whose link text is the pin's JSON could pass the re-pin check, because the pin is read with `git show` and its file mode is not compared. It was ruled below the blocking floor (see Agent notes); a file-mode check follows in a second PR. Everything else is below the floor and listed under Review notes.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- The new warning also counts review passes that a later pass replaced, so it can contradict the existing "abandoned pass" line.
- The warning only fires when the summary reads the run's reviewer records, which happens at the final summary, not when a review stops or before finish.
- The warning does not check unlogged second-model or adversarial reviewers once a review pass is logged.
- The harness-version test also changes the pin's `since` field, so it cannot prove the manifest version check on its own.
- The re-pin check compares a pin's other fields between the reviewed head and the new head, not against main's side of the merge.
- A pin with no `blob` field for a file absent at both heads passes the blob comparison (other fields must still match).

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Two smoke checks on this head: the two new test files pass, and `gstack-review-scope summary` on this run's own records prints the new warning naming the unlogged pass before its row was logged. Verdict: pass. Evidence: ~/.capy/work/gstack/ship-4669-r4/qa/functional (checkpoint 002).

</details>

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: keep a review record across a base merge that only re-pins a shared harness file, and warn about unlogged reviewers. Delivered: exactly that, plus the policy rows for both.

</details>
