title: /ship runs in the pull request's own thread, with no helper agent (GST-3466)
body:
On Capy, /ship now runs in the thread that owns the pull request, starting its reviewers as that thread's own subagents, instead of handing the whole run to a separate helper agent.
Why: a 30-run trial found no clear difference in cost or bugs caught, so the extra agent layer goes; the project owner chose this.
Nothing to do: /ship's review plan, review rounds, final sign-off and checks are unchanged.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

"Make the in-thread way the default and only documented way to run /ship." Every place that told an agent to hand /ship to a helper agent, sleep, and then stop that helper now tells the thread that owns the pull request to run /ship itself, phase by phase, with its reviewers as its own subagents. The old instructions are removed, not kept beside the new ones.

![The thread that owns the pull request now runs /ship itself, instead of handing it to a helper agent and sleeping](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/zp2wWwFFa72wyhKB7W115YKdwDztBbKN-4elSb_CHnI.png)

The thread that owns the pull request now runs /ship itself, instead of handing it to a helper agent and sleeping.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The thread that owns the pull request now runs /ship itself, instead of handing it to a helper agent and sleeping</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md § Plan, approve, ship at c2b4f0d · source text
+++ After · capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md § Plan, approve, ship on this branch · source text
@@ ⋯ 3 unchanged ⋯ @@
 - **Plan first.** Run `/autoplan` on new functionality right after the install check. The lean run (the Capy default) is one reviewer over plan and draft code; `--full` adds every phase.
 - **ELI5, then the word.** Send the plan and gate to the person, or the Captain, in plain language: `gstack-owner-brief render --captain --out <run dir> --captain-name "<Captain name>"`, its choices as lettered lines in the ask format (`crew/docs/captain.md`) and "do it" taking every recommendation at full scope. Build only after their word is answered into the run and it reports `APPROVED`; then `gstack-approvals import --autoplan <run dir> --by "<owner>"`.
 - **/ship before ready.** Run /ship at the final pushed head before a PR is called ready; `SHIP_RECEIPT: pr=<n> head=<head>` must name that head, and a later push needs a new /ship. The review inside /ship, like the autoplan, is sized to the change.
+- **Run /ship yourself, then keep the PR.** The thread that owns the PR runs /ship phase by phase (`ship/DRIVER.md`), with its reviewers as its own subagents. Once /ship prints its receipt, the thread reads the PR's checks and comments once, runs `gstack-ship-queue ready` and owns the PR thereafter: slot stamp, re-READY, receipt carry (`crew/docs/captain.md`, the lane's /ship sequence).
-- **Sleep while /ship runs, then stop it.** After dispatching /ship the parent ends its turn with no PR watch until /ship completes (a re-READY drops a held watch first). On that wake it subscribes to the PR (renewed on expiry, cancelled at merge or close), reads its checks and comments once, stops the subagent, runs `gstack-ship-queue ready` and owns the PR thereafter: slot stamp, re-READY, receipt carry (`crew/docs/captain.md`, the lane's /ship sequence). A stopped /ship subagent woken by a check, review or merge notice, not its parent, reports what woke it, its pin and the PR head (`gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid`) in one line and ends the turn without acting, even if the head moved. A message from its parent is an instruction it carries out.
 - **No merge without the owner's word.** A thread never merges on its own; under a Captain the controller merges on a recorded standing approval, and a thread with no Captain asks the person.
 
 Exempt from the plan step: read-only work, the daily flaky pass's repairs, slot stamps, CHANGELOG-only resolves, cap re-pins under a written grant, S1 emergencies (a broken install or upgrade, a red main, a security bug) and fixes from an already-diagnosed, audited problem list. Other bug fixes skip plan review (`--kind fix`, R65) but carry a repro on current main or a failing test written first; features get the lean run (`--kind feature`).
~~~

</details>

One code change keeps /ship's spending guard: a /ship run that reads its own thread's token counter (`--reading-from own`, or no reading flag on a non-tree meter) still gets the 50M default token cap that the helper agent used to get. Without it, moving /ship into the calling thread would have silently dropped the default cap.

What the trial found (#4667): ten cases, three runs each way, on Claude Opus 5.5. Arm C handed /ship to one fresh helper agent (the old way); arm F ran /ship in the calling thread.

- Cost a run, F minus C: +$0.07 (95% interval -$1.42 to +$1.57); mean $11.47 for C, $11.54 for F.
- Planted bugs caught: 22 of 30 for F, 21 of 30 for C (F minus C +0.03, -0.18 to +0.24). No case was a structural loss.
- Real problems found: F minus C -0.003 (-0.21 to +0.20).
- Wall time F minus C: -1.9 minutes (-8.1 to +4.4).
- Only 9 of 60 runs reached /ship's final sign-off (4 C, 5 F), so this compares the review and fix phases, not the release steps after them.

The verdict depends on a scoring ruling made after seeing data. One F run (F7t3) stopped at /ship's own round cap before the step where its two named second-model reviewers run. Counting a named reviewer only if /ship reached its step, reader fidelity is 30 of 30 and every bar passes; read literally, it is 29 of 30 and the plan's decision would keep the helper agent with one fix cycle. The results page reports both readings; the owner chose the first.

Files changed:

- `ship/DRIVER.md.tmpl`, `ship/DRIVER.md`: /ship runs in the pull request's own thread, never in a subagent.
- `ship/sections/budget-handoff.md.tmpl`, `ship/sections/budget-handoff.md`: the token reading is the thread that runs /ship, reviewers included.
- `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md`, `capy/skill/gstack/lane-card.md`, `capy/skill/gstack/captain.md`: run /ship yourself, then keep the PR; no helper-agent titles or task-row metering.
- `crew/docs/captain.md`, `captain/templates/brief.md`: the steps before a PR is ready no longer start, sleep on, or stop a /ship helper.
- `runaway-stopper/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `runaway-stopper/SKILL.md`, `runaway-stopper/templates/successor-brief.md`: "/ship runs in the PR's own thread"; the mid-run stop hold names /ship's reviewers.
- `docs/ship-budget.md`, `docs/skills.md`: the same rule; the default cap is described by its flag.
- `lib/ship-budget-cli.ts`, `lib/ship-budget.ts`: the 50M default cap also applies to a run reading its own counter, and its note says so.
- `test/ship-budget-meter-scope.test.ts`: checks the skill has the thread read its own counter and start no /ship helper, and checks the default cap for own-counter runs.
- `test/size-ledger/ship/ship-runs-in-the-calling-thread.json`, `changelog.d/ship-runs-in-the-calling-thread.md`: size record and release note.

Not changed: `docs/ship-policy.md` (no helper-agent text in it). The `--reading-from task` and `--subagent` budget flags stay in code for older runs.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"The extra agent layer costs a whole context and buys nothing we could measure." The trial in #4667 found no clear difference in cost, bugs caught or wall time between handing /ship to a helper agent and running it in the calling thread, so agents now run /ship where the pull request lives, which is simpler to follow and to resume.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

This touches the agent-facing instructions every thread loads (the Capy skill, its start card, the team manual, /runaway-stopper and the /ship driver) and one budget default in `lib/ship-budget-cli.ts:254`. It is safe because /ship's review plan, rounds, final sign-off and checks code are unchanged, and the default-cap change only widens which observe runs get the existing 50M cap: `test/ship-budget-meter-scope.test.ts` covers both the instructions and the cap, and the full free suite passed in CI at 452f845 (script ran).

title: Local checks reuse every green CI run at your code, not only the first (GST-3381)
body:
Local checks before opening a PR now reuse the newest verified CI run per eligible profile at your exact code, so files an end-to-end run already passed beside the test run no longer run again on your machine. Before, only the first matching profile's run counted; a failed run, a run of different code, or a run that changes while it is being read still counts for nothing. Nothing to do: this changes what runs locally, not what CI runs.
What changed - The local check that reuses CI results now keeps the newest verified run of each eligible profile at your exact code, verifies each one on its own, reads them all again once they are collected, and counts the test files any of them ran. - A failed run, a run of different code, or a run that moves to a new attempt while the others are read adds nothing (the last case refuses the reuse, so every selected test runs locally). - A new test reproduces the bug with a Test run and an E2E run (it fails on main and passes here), with a failed E2E run and an E2E run of other code as negative controls.
Agent notes ## Agent notes ### Files - `lib/pregate/index.ts`: the CI carry keeps every run profile that verified at HEAD's tree (`ctx.fromRun.runs`) instead of stopping at the first; the remote-gate clear uses the run under the gate's profile. - `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts`: `fromRun` verifies each kept run under its own profile and unions their `tree.json` files. - `lib/pregate/types.ts`, `docs/pregate.md`, `changelog.d/` fragment, `test/pregate-ci-carry-profiles.test.ts`. Commit 14c3760de points the test's state root at its fixture home, so it no longer writes the runner's real `~/.gstack/security/egress.jsonl` (CI's free suite refused shard 9 for that at 92dc2e99d). - Commit 860fe6080 (cross-family trail read blocker, owner grant a-9f7bcc32d32c): `fromRun` rereads every kept run with `runChanged` once the union is built, as `findCarry` does, and refuses the reuse on any change; `docs/pregate.md` says a `remote_gate_runs` naming two profiles is refused by the carry; a new case flips the Test run to a red attempt while the E2E run is read. One scoped fix-check on 14c3760de..860fe6080: clean, one informational note (the reread runs only when two or more runs verified; `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:745`). ### Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 13 issues — 0 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 1 deferred, 7 noted, 4 skipped (informational, below the blocking floor), 1 ruled note Gate edits: none detected (GATE_SCAN tagged=0 at 14c3760de) Scope Check: CLEAN Coverage: 7/9 paths (78%); gaps: which carried run feeds the gate clear, and the skipped count across runs Exploratory QA: no server or browser surface; smoke covered by the targeted test lane (494 tests) including the red-run and other-tree negative controls Pass 1 (full panel plus second-model review) raised the findings below; pass 2 read the test-only fix range and found nothing. #### Deferred findings Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues. - Deferred: CRITICAL `lib/pregate/index.ts:136` 1. **Multi-profile remote gates never auto-clear.** `lib/pregate/index.ts:136` passes only `ctx.fromRun.ref` to `clearByRuns`, which requires exactly one distinct run per `remote_gate_runs` profile. If two declared runs are green and jointly cover the gate inventory, but a gate-only file leaves a remote obligation, pregate still refuses with `got 1`. Small-machine shipping stays blocked until someone clears the gate manually. Pass the verified runs for the configured gate profiles to `clearByRuns`. Severity: High. Blocks: yes. #### Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:747` 1. **Duplicate run in the receipt** (lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts:747). Say two base profiles share a workflow and OS but list different jobs. They can resolve to the same run id, and then the receipt shows `runs=123/1,123/1` and counts `tests=` twice. The union of files is still correct; only the receipt number is wrong. Fix: dedupe `ok` by `run_id/run_attempt` before summing and before calling `runReceiptFields`. FIXABLE. Severity: Low. Blocks: no. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/index.ts:136` 2. **Remote gate gets one run even though all runs are now known** (lib/pregate/index.ts:136, with :87). `carryGate` still passes only `[ctx.fromRun.ref]` to `clearByRuns`. So a base whose `remote_gate_runs` names two profiles is always refused with "exactly 2 run(s)", even though `ctx.fromRun.runs` now holds both verified runs. title: Review and shipping tools: seven small fixes to exclusions, issue links, PR description checks, build outputs, known-red tests and telemetry (GST-3464)
body:
Fixes seven small bugs in the review and shipping tools: bad exclusion keys now refuse, `Review-Finding:` lines are no longer issue references, older commits' issue mentions name their commit, and wording checks skip the PR's short opening lines.
A native binary the checkout builds at a path its committed `.gitignore` names is no longer flagged as a download; the grouped-merge test gate can read the list of tests already failing on main from a file; and telemetry no longer logs a duplicate onboarding event when a run crosses midnight.
Nothing to do; each fix has a test that fails on main.

## What changed

- **Review exclusions** (`lib/ship-policy.ts`): the key filter used an unanchored pattern, so a key such as `review_exclude_paths[0]` was set aside instead of refusing. It now matches `review_exclude_paths` and `review_content_patterns` exactly.
- **Issue links** (`lib/issue-links.ts`, #4371): a `Review-Finding:` trailer line is skipped when collecting issue references, so a finding that quotes `#123` no longer links that issue. This supersedes outside PR #4389, which fixed the same thing.
- **Issue mentions in older commits** (`bin/gstack-issue-links`, #4378): the commit log is read with `git log -z`, so each mention's label names its own commit instead of `commit :`. Reported and first fixed by @Davmunrey in #4388; rebuilt here with credit.
- **PR description checks** (`lib/ship-receipt-prose.ts`): the claim checks skip the plain opening above the first `<details>` fold (for example a result the PR is about) when that opening fits the 3-line, 600-character limit, measured the way the body shape check measures it. A body with no fold, or a longer opening, is still checked whole.
- **Build outputs in the fetch sweep** (`lib/review-sweep.ts`): a new large file is exempt only when it is an ELF, Mach-O or PE executable inside the checkout at a path the committed, unmodified root `.gitignore` names exactly (for example `bin/gstack-cso-core`). A build output that already existed when a stage started is not counted when the stage ends. Everything else, including a large file that replaces a test fixture folder, is still a download.
- **Tests already failing on main** (`crew/lib/ship-queue-train-*.ts`, #4569): `--fixes-base-red-file <file>` reads the case list from a file, and JUnit attributes are entity-decoded so a case name with `&` matches.
- **Telemetry midnight race** (`bin/gstack-telemetry-log`): only onboarding markers dated before today are deleted, so a run that crosses midnight no longer logs a third event.

## Why

Each item is a bug someone hit while shipping. They caused false refusals from the PR description check, wrong issue links in PR bodies, a review stopped because the repo built its own binary, and test case names with commas or escaped characters that the merge gate could not match.

## Blast radius

Only gstack's own review and shipping tools and the telemetry logger change. The fetch sweep's new exemption is narrow and sits on top of the existing check; every other large new file still stops the review. No defaults, settings or stored data change.

## Pre-Landing Review

Two full review passes and one approved follow-up check, all on this PR.

- Pass 1 (whole diff): 4 findings. Fixed: a build output seen at a stage's start could be counted as a download at its end; the opening skip had no length limit. Skipped with reasons: the notes-push retry hint joins gate case names on commas (rare path that fails safe), and the PE header check reads only its first two bytes (a reader could write a full header just as easily).
- Pass 2 (fixes only): 1 blocker fixed, the opening was measured differently from the body shape check. Second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol) raised 2 blockers: the start-of-stage skip also excused test fixture folders, and code blocks in the opening were measured collapsed. Both fixed and read again in the approved follow-up check, which found nothing new.
- Review notes: three Low findings from the native second reader (the skipped region can run past the measured opening when text sits between the Agent notes marker and the first fold; fenced openings), the last two fixed by the follow-up check.
- Exploratory checks: 10 probes, all passing on the final code.

title: /eval-plan checks follow the plan's own dates and models, and plans name their grader (GST-3464)
body:
`/eval-plan dry-run --prereg <file>` now reads the plan's frozen date and Models section, so plans frozen before the model-generation rule, and competitor vendor defaults, pass as the rule allows; priced families refuse unpriced older generations; and a new `grader:` line is required for plans frozen from 2026-11-23.
Nothing to do for readers; plans frozen before 2026-11-23 need no `grader:` line.

## What changed

Eval authors hit refusals the rule never meant: `dry-run` refused a competitor arm the plan declared as a vendor default, and arms in plans frozen before the model-generation rule, because it never read the plan. Unpriced older models of a priced family (`claude-opus-4-5`, `gpt-4.1`, `o1`, `gemini-2.0-flash`) slipped through.

- **dry-run reads the preregistration** (`bin/gstack-eval-plan`, `lib/eval-plan-checks.ts`): `--prereg <file>` passes the plan's Models lines and `frozen:` date to the generation check and prints each exception or `MODEL_GENERATION: exempt`; `pilot start` re-checks with the same record. The frozen date counts only when the plan's `## Arms` names every dry-run arm, and pilot start applies it only to arms the dry run checked. A malformed `vendor-default:` line, or an old reader or simulator, is named in the failure instead of "an arm". /eval-plan step 2 passes `--prereg`.
- **Older generations** (`lib/pricing.ts`): `currentReplacement` refuses an unpriced older generation of a priced family instead of letting it through.
- **Grader line** (`lib/eval-plan-checks.ts`): Held-out exposure needs a `grader:` line, or `grader: none`, for plans frozen on or after 2026-11-23.
- **Docs**: the `EVAL_MODEL_OLD_GENERATION` troubleshooting entry names unpriced older generations and `dry-run --prereg`.

## Why

Eval plans keep the model rules they were frozen under, and declared vendor defaults are allowed exceptions; the checks now follow the plan instead of refusing it, while still refusing old models a plan does not name.

## Blast radius

Only `gstack-eval-plan` (prereg check, dry-run, pilot start) and `lib/pricing.ts` callers of `currentReplacement` change. Every change refuses the same or more except the plan-backed exemptions, which need `--prereg` and a plan that names the arms; the 7 changed eval-plan and pricing test files pass (133 tests including the module-size ratchet).

## Pre-Landing Review

Round 2 (a check of the fixed lines plus the money reader): nothing blocking. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pricing.ts:171` gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro and gpt-5.3-codex are now refused as older than gpt-6 (matches R116; a plan using one now fails)

title: Prompt router names your bug-fix skill first and stops sending feature requests to it (GST-3462)
body:
gstack's prompt hook now recognizes more bug reports and names your installed bug-fix skill first. Why: in our Codex run the model loaded whichever skill the hook named first, and on 7 bug tasks that was /verify, never prove-it. Nothing to do: the change is in the hook's scoring, with no setting or install change.
What changed - **Order.** When the installed bug-fix skill (a non-gstack skill with a trigger like "fix this bug") reaches the threshold beside a gstack skill, it is named first. - **More bug reports recognized.** New strong signs: "should X, but Y", "Expected:"/"Actual:", regressions ("started with 0.19", "used to work", "no longer"), security holes, lost data. New weak signs: "never", "must", and words for an unwanted outcome (lost, ignored, dropped, twice, truncated). - **Messages no person typed are skipped (#4423).** Claude Code runs the hook on a message from another session (``) and on a background agent's hand-back (``) too, and its payload has no field that marks them, so the hook skips text that starts with either wrapper and logs `reason=agent-message`. Closes #4423. - **/qa or /review for a reported defect only on their own phrase.** A prompt that reports a defect goes to /review or /qa only when it holds one of their trigger phrases in order, with only small words such as "my" added ("find bugs on my site", "review this PR for bugs"), and never asks for a fix; a report that just shares their words ("the site crashes during the smoke test") goes to your bug-fix skill, or with none installed is not named to /review or /qa. "Test the site and fix what you find" reports no defect and keeps /qa. - **Feature-titled requests are unchanged.** A rule that stopped treating feature requests (titles starting with Add, Support, [Feature] and the like) as bug reports moves to a follow-up pull request; here they route as they do on main.
Evidence All on the synthetic prompts in `test/fixtures/`; the first-draft set is held in (the rules were written after reading it). | Set | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | First-draft bug reports naming prove-it alone | 32 of 46 | 42 of 46 | | First-draft bug reports naming /verify first | 1 | 0 | | First-draft feature requests routed | 1 of 14 | 1 of 14 (same prompt) | | Long bug reports sent to /qa with no bug-fix skill | 3 of 4 | 0 of 4 | | Current fixture: bug reports naming prove-it alone | 46 of 46 | 46 of 46 | Known misses kept in the test so they can only shrink: synthetic-bug-21, -27, -36, -43. Four new tests fail on main and pass here, including #4423's dry-run prompt.

title: Secrets check flags keys in Rust let, const and static bindings and stops flagging Rust type annotations (GST-3474)
body:
The secrets check now catches a key written as `let token = "<key>";` (or `let mut`, `const`, `static`) in a Rust file, and no longer flags Rust type annotations like `token: Option<&str>,` or match arms like `Token::Char(c) =>`.
Why: a real key in that Rust form passed the check, while every Rust change needed allowlist entries for type annotations (seen on garrytan/gbrain#10028).
Nothing to do: files in other languages are checked as before.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A Rust project hit two problems with the secrets check. A real key written as `let token = "<key>";` passed it, and ordinary struct fields such as `token: Option<&str>,` failed it, so every Rust change needed allowlist entries. Now the key reports and the field passes.

- **New rule `env.kv.rust`** (MEDIUM, secret, so it blocks like `env.kv`): a `let`, `let mut`, `const`, `static` or `static mut` binding, optionally `pub`/`pub(..)` and typed, whose value is a string, raw or byte literal, directly or as the first argument of `Some`, `String::from`, `Box::new` or `Cow::Borrowed`/`Cow::Owned`. It uses the same name, placeholder and entropy checks as `env.kv`, and it also reads after `//`, `///`, `//!` and `/*`.
- **A scan with no file path now also reports the declaration form** (`let`/`const`/`static NAME = "<key>"`) as `env.kv.rust`. With a file path the rule reports only in `.rs` files. The pre-push hook scans Dart and Python files without a path, so a Dart `const token = "<key>";` now gets an `env.kv.rust` warning there.
- **Rust type annotations stop reporting**, through an exemption added on top of the existing `env.kv` checks. It applies only in a `.rs` file, to a line-start `name:` whose value is type-shaped (a primitive such as `u32` or `str`, a path, or a CamelCase name) and ends in a closing comma; a match arm needs no comma. A literal, an `=`, a second field, a random-looking name, a lowercase or all-caps word, or a line with no comma still reports. That keeps a `token: <value>` line inside a Rust string or comment reporting, because the check sees a `.rs` file's added lines without the string around them.
- Docs: the secrets check's code-shapes section names the known limit (a line inside a string that reads exactly like a field annotation passes) and the pre-push behavior.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Every Rust landing needs allowlist entries, and `let token = \"...\"` sails through" (garrytan/gbrain#10028). Rust keys in bindings now fail the check, and struct fields and match arms pass it, without hiding anything the check flags today outside Rust type annotations.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the secrets scanner's pattern list changes. Every line the new exemption skips was also skipped at the first review's head, and each extra condition only adds a reason to report. Checked by a base-vs-head replay of every tracked file, by scanner probes at main, the first head and this head (script ran), and by CI's full free test run at this head.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The first full review found that the type-annotation exemption also skipped credential lines inside Rust strings and comments and struct-literal values, which main reports. The exemption was tightened to need a type-shaped value and a closing comma, with tests for each case. The second review of the fix found no blockers. The second-model review raised three lines that now report as they do on main (a comma-less last field, `std::ffi::c_char`, a match-arm body that uses its binding); none lets a secret through, and the maintainer ruled them disclosed notes. A missing test-fixture-label exemption for the new rule in Rust test files was left as is.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/redact-patterns.ts:1172` No test pins the new depth-0 `;` rejection in isRustTypeAnnotation.
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-543d8477ef9f` security finding, details recorded privately

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Scanner probes through `scan()` (functional surface, 7 captures): a Rust binding reports and a type annotation passes; a credential line inside a raw string and inside a normal multi-line string reported nothing at the first head (reproduced and replayed) and reports `env.kv` after the fix. Verdict: pass on current inputs.

title: Plan a test of whether /ship's reviewers beat two plain reads (GST-3467)
body:
Adds the plan for a test of whether /ship's review panel finds more planted bugs than two plain review reads plus its second-model reviewer, on Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol. It settles the open question from the last trial, where a single plain read came close to the panel at a fraction of the cost, before anything in /ship changes. Nothing to do but read [docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md](docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md); no paid run starts until this merges.
What changed ![The decision rules now say which result wins when two bars pass, and the panel and second-model reviewer commands are pinned in full](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/vHVb7jGTYq2UzRA-xtR7KKbvWnIgxfCmjI2MCcfjDis.png) The decision rules now say which result wins when two bars pass, and the panel and second-model reviewer commands are pinned in full.
Before/after as text: The decision rules now say which result wins when two bars pass, and the panel and second-model reviewer commands are pinned in full ~~~diff --- Before · docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md § Decisions at c2b4f0d · source text (new in this change) +++ After · docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md § Decisions on this branch · source text +## Decisions +Each model's result decides for the /ship host that runs that model (Claude Code runs Opus, Codex runs Sol). +- if N2V is no worse than P and P is not better (the N2V minus P lower bound is at or above −0.10 and the P minus N2V interval does not lie entirely above 0): /ship's first-pass panel on that host is a candidate to replace with two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer; that change is its own /ship plan, through /autoplan and Garry's approval, and nothing changes from this result alone +- if P is better than N2V (the P minus N2V interval lies entirely above 0, whether or not the no-worse bound also passes): the panel stays on that host, and G3 merges only the readers that find nothing alone (today, the targeted reader) +- if neither: the panel stays on that host, the null is published with this run's smallest detectable difference, and G3's panel question closes on that host +- if the run stops incomplete (spend cap, a harness stop, a scorer below its bar): no decision is taken, the panel stays, and every finished trial is reported ~~~
The last trial left one question open: does /ship's review panel catch more bugs because of how its readers are built, or only because it reads the code more often? This plan fixes the answer in advance. It runs 30 paired cases (the last trial's 10 plus 20 new ones), 3 trials each, on both models. It compares the panel's first pass with two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer, and counts "no worse" as a 95% interval whose lower bound is at or above −0.10 on planted bugs caught. It takes one look at 15 cases, with fixed stop bounds, and costs about $1,200, capped at $1,500. Review before merge tightened the plan: - It gives the exact commands for the panel and the standalone second-model reviewer. - The panel runs without the second-model reviewer on cases where gstack's own plan leaves it out. - The repository's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are removed from every case checkout, so the plain reads load no gstack guidance. - When both bars pass, the "panel is better" result wins. - If the judge misses its label check, the results check allows exactly one known issue.
Why "Merging two of the existing plain reads would have caught about 70%, close to the panel, at a fraction of its reader spend." That lead came out of the last trial's follow-up check. Before /ship's review panel changes on either host, this test measures whether two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer really match it.
Blast radius The change adds two Markdown files, the plan and its changelog fragment. No code, prompt or skill reads them except `gstack-eval-plan prereg --check`, which passes at this head (script ran).
Pre-Landing Review The second-model reviewer (GPT-6.2 Sol) found five problems that would have stopped the paid run or skewed its result, and one broken link. All six are fixed in this PR. They were: commands that could not run as written; a panel arm that assumed a reviewer gstack sometimes leaves out; plain reads that could load the repository's own instructions; a fallback that the results check would refuse; and two decision rules that could both apply to one result. A scoped re-check of the fixes found no blockers.
Review notes - Open (not fixed; below the blocking bar, and the review round limit is used up): a case whose own change touches the root AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md keeps that file. The new audit rule would then score every plain read on that case as zero. That favours the panel. The re-check counted 1 of 50 recent main commits touching those paths. Raised by the reviewer that re-checked the fixes, at docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md:188; a second reviewer raised the same point. - Noted: the results check also flags a 0 in any results table column unless a Diagnostics counter declares it, so the results page has to keep such zeros out of its tables or declare them (docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md:299).
Exploratory QA Smoke checks on the plan file: `gstack-eval-plan prereg --check` prints `PREREG: ok present=10/10 stack=loaded no_gstack_arm=ok interim_look=required` at this head. A link check found the one relative link that didn't resolve; it is fixed. Nothing was blocked or left unrun.
Eval Results No prompts, templates, judges or eval harness changed, so no evals ran.
Review bot comments No review bot comments.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Status:** current. The documentation audit found nothing that needed an edit. **Scope:** base c2b4f0d2 to head b8c7a071 on `plan-a-test-of-ship-reviewers-against-plain-reads`, with 2 committed files and no staged, unstaged or new files. The audit read the changelog fragment, the new preregistration `docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md`, the fragment rules in `changelog.d/README.md` and the linked preregistration `docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md`. **Documentation health:** - `changelog.d/plan-a-test-of-ship-reviewers-against-plain-reads.md`: current. It follows the fragment format and points to the right path. - `docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md`: current. It is a new authored doc, its internal link resolves, and the results page it names is described as arriving later. **Coverage debt:** none. This change adds no public commands, flags, skills or configuration. The preregistration is its own reference doc, and like earlier preregistrations it is not listed in an index. **Diagram drift:** none. The diff contains no diagrams and changes nothing that a diagram shows.
Tests - [x] Free Tests (the full free suite, run 44993304715 at this head): green, 1,743 test files. - [x] `gstack-eval-plan prereg --check docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-prereg.md`: `PREREG: ok present=10/10`. - [x] Push checks at this head: secrets scan pass, guards pass, sealed files clear.

title: Docs link check stops hiding sections after inline code, /learn prune checks every learning, /retro counts Godot test runners
body:
Four small fixes from outside reports: the docs link and prose checks no longer treat a line that starts with inline code as a code block, /learn prune reads every learning instead of the first 100, /retro counts a test runner in `tests/` and skips game-engine sidecar files, and five tests that cannot work as root now skip there. Why: each one was reproduced on main and gave a wrong answer (refused valid links, skipped stale learnings, a test total of 0, red tests as root). Nothing to do after merge.
Security read No CI, install, dependency, network, auth or process-spawning change. The outside PRs were read as text only and rebuilt on main; `gstack-learnings-search --all` only lifts an output limit on a local file the user already reads.
What changed People hit four wrong answers. A valid docs link was refused, /learn prune quietly skipped old learnings on bigger projects, /retro reported zero test files on a Godot repo, and the free suite went red when run as root. Each now gives the right answer. | Report | Repro on main (c2b4f0d) | Fix | |---|---|---| | #4391 / PR #4393 (@Davmunrey) | Adding a correct link to `troubleshooting.md#unattended-runs-and-artifacts` fails `scripts/check-doc-links.ts` with `DOC_LINKS: broken 2`. Over all tracked Markdown, 6 false broken links. | `lib/doc-links.ts` and `lib/prose-lint.ts` read fences as CommonMark does: a backtick fence's info string has no backtick, and only a bare run at least as long as the opener closes it. All tracked Markdown: 185 → 179 broken links, 0 newly reported. | | #4215 (@exGeni) | 111 learnings, prune's `--limit 100` list omits the one stale entry, and the summary gives no sign of the cut. | `gstack-learnings-search --all`; the prune row uses it. The query-only "more matched" notice is unchanged. | | PR #4306 (@huongtran84) | Godot fixture: `TEST_FILES_TOTAL: 0`, `TEST_FILES_CHANGED: 2` (the `.uid` sidecar). | When no file follows a test naming convention, count code files under a test folder; `.uid`, `.import` and `.meta` never count as tests. | | #4425 (@Davmunrey) | As root: `bun test test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts` gives 32 pass, 5 fail. | Those five cases skip as root (root passes the ptrace check they depend on). As root: 32 pass, 5 skip; as a normal user: 37 pass. |
Why "Adding a correct link fails the docs check" (#4391), "prune never sees my oldest learnings" (#4215), "/retro says I have no tests" (#4306) and "the free tests fail as root" (#4425). After this change the link check, prune, the test census and the root run all report what is actually there.
Blast radius The fence change also alters how the prose check masks code in every Markdown file. A second-model review diffed the old and new parser over every tracked `.md` file. Only 5 files parse differently, each a nested four-backtick fence the old parser closed too early, and the link check passes on all 5 (script ran). `--all` is a new flag; `--limit 0` is still refused, so no existing caller changes (repro).
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues. The main review found one test-coverage note (the root check uses the user id where the real condition is the ptrace capability, so a root container without that capability skips cases it could run; CI runs as a normal user, so CI coverage is unchanged). It was left as a note. A second-model adversarial review recommended shipping as-is and raised four low-severity notes, listed below.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/doc-links.ts:22` unclosed fence silently masks later links; prose-lint reports it, doc-links does not - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-retro-metrics:401` no-convention fallback counts fixture data, snapshots and .gitkeep under tests/ as test files - INFORMATIONAL `learn/SKILL.md.tmpl:40` prune reads an unbounded list into context on very large stores - INFORMATIONAL `test/bootstrap-retention.test.ts:113` uid check is a proxy for CAP_SYS_PTRACE (duplicate of specialist-batched#1)
Exploratory QA Functional smoke, 4 probes on isolated fixtures, all pass: /retro on a Godot fixture reports 1 test file, 1 changed, 1 inserted line; the link check on a fixture with an inline-code line and a tilde fence whose info string holds backticks reports only the truly broken anchor; `gstack-learnings-search --limit 0` still exits 2; on a 12-entry store `--all` prints 12 and the default prints 10. Not probed: the /learn prune agent flow and the root-only skips (the latter needs a root shell; the repro above covers it).
Eval Results The eval selector (profile pr) picked no quality judges. It listed behavioral cases that depend on `lib/doc-links.ts` and `lib/prose-lint.ts`; the selector marks those as scheduled release coverage, not PR runs, so no paid eval ran for this PR.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: fix the four outside reports. Delivered: those four fixes, their tests and one changelog fragment.
Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches). This is a bug fix with repros in the table above.
Verification Results No plan-specific checks (bug fix, no plan file). The exploratory smoke above is the verification: 4 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 BLOCKED, 0 NOT RUN.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Issues Refs #4391 Refs #4393 Refs #4215 Refs #4306 Refs #4425
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match the change, so nothing was edited. **Scope:** 12 committed files on fix/outside-docs-lint-retro-learn, compared with c2b4f0d2adfa. Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. The changes are the CommonMark fence fix in lib/doc-links.ts and lib/prose-lint.ts, the new `--all` option for `gstack-learnings-search` (now used by /learn prune), the /retro test-file fallback and the engine-sidecar exclusion, and the bootstrap-retention skips when the suite runs as root. **Documentation health:** - learn/SKILL.md.tmpl and learn/SKILL.md: current. The prune row uses `--all`. - retro/SKILL.md.tmpl and retro/sections/report-format.md.tmpl: current. They still describe `TEST_FILES_TOTAL` correctly. - CONTRIBUTING.md: current. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. - README.md: current. Nothing in it is affected. **Debt:** There is no coverage debt and no diagram drift. The `--all` option is documented in the binary's `--help` and in the /learn table.

title: Defaults name current models, and review stops reading "the HIGH branch" as a HIGH finding (GST-3462)
body:
Three defaults gstack picks now name current models, and a reviewer's mention of a code name like "the HIGH branch" no longer becomes a HIGH finding. Why: our rule is no older-generation model in a role we choose, and the review parser forced a ruling on two notes that only quoted code. Nothing to do: no settings change; overrides work as before.
What changed ![Review parser labels before and after: code names like the HIGH branch no longer count as HIGH findings, and CRITICAL keeps its label](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/BFF5O6NwwEcjsCnuLj1_UM5AOvjVBRxi6ddHkjC3Ts4.png) Review parser labels before and after. Code names like "the HIGH branch" no longer count as HIGH findings, and CRITICAL keeps its label.
Evidence `test/r116-model-defaults.test.ts` (3 tests) and `test/review-ledger-name-use.test.ts` (2 tests, with the captured reply from #4612's review) fail on main and pass here. The existing review-parser suites, including the never-weaker-than-main invariant and the "reaches the CRITICAL write path" control, pass.
Before/after as text: Review parser labels before and after: code names like the HIGH branch no longer count as HIGH findings, and CRITICAL keeps its label ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +INFORMATIONAL In the redact-doc HIGH and scanner-failure branches, the size check runs before the scan. +INFORMATIONAL The cleanup runs after the HIGH branch has already removed the file. -HIGH In the redact-doc HIGH and scanner-failure branches, the size check runs before the scan. -HIGH The cleanup runs after the HIGH branch has already removed the file. CRITICAL the HIGH and CRITICAL write paths drop the auth check (store.ts:40) HIGH HIGH: auth.ts:9 skips the token check. ~~~ A reviewer who wrote "the redact-doc HIGH and scanner-failure branches" about redact-doc's HIGH exit path got that line collected as a HIGH finding nobody could lower. Now a capitalized HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW used as the name of something in the code ("the HIGH branch", "the MEDIUM and LOW tiers") collects at INFORMATIONAL when it is the line's only label, so the reviewer's own Severity fields decide. CRITICAL is never read as a name, even in "the HIGH and CRITICAL write paths", and a word that rates a finding ("the HIGH finding", "the HIGH vulnerability") keeps its label. The design prototype script sent gpt-4o, which cannot drive the image tool's current model. It now builds its request with the design binary's own helper, so it takes the binary's models and stops with the binary's fix-it message on a pairing OpenAI would reject. A Gemini run whose CLI reports no model is labelled and priced as Gemini 4 Argon instead of Gemini 2.5 Pro, and `gstack-context-bill --exact` counts tokens with Claude Opus 5.5 instead of Opus 4.5. The judge model is unchanged, because it moves only with a recalibration run.
Why "No gpt-4o or older-generation model sits in a role we choose." Three defaults still did. Separately, a review of #4612 collected two notes that only quoted code as HIGH findings, and the lead had to rule on them by hand.
Blast radius The parser change touches every /ship and /review reply the review parser collects. It can only lower HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW on a line with no Severity field, and `blockingRow` counts only rank 4 (CRITICAL or P0), so no blocker can drop (lib/review-ledger.ts read; the 31 test files that import the parser pass, 516 tests). The model defaults touch a dev-only script, a test adapter's fallback label and one CLI default.
Pre-Landing Review Two rounds. Round 1 found that the first version of the parser change read "the HIGH and CRITICAL write paths" as a code name and dropped a CRITICAL to INFORMATIONAL; two reviewers found it independently, and it is fixed with controls. Round 1 also moved the prototype onto the design binary's request helper. Round 2 found nothing at the blocking floor. Second-model review (GPT-6.2 Astra): completed.
Deferred findings Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues. - Deferred: CRITICAL `test/helpers/providers/gemini.ts:167` run() passes only opts.model to resultFromGeminiStream, so a model requested through extraArgs is labelled with the unreported-model fallback when the stream omits it. Pre-existing; line 167 is unchanged by this PR.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/context-bill.ts:66` Divisor header should say which tokenizer a refit uses. - INFORMATIONAL `test/helpers/providers/gemini.ts:79` Unreported-model label is a guess recorded as if reported. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-9864856e2e60` security finding, details recorded privately
Exploratory QA Three probes on the changed code, all pass: a code-name line collects INFORMATIONAL while a real HIGH lead stays HIGH; CRITICAL, `Blocks: yes` and a rating noun keep CRITICAL, CRITICAL and HIGH; the prototype bundles with its new import (no live API call).
Eval Results No prompt, template or judge changed, so paid evals were not run. The selector lists behavior probes only because they import the review parser.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual addition to the review collection policy. **Scope:** base c2b4f0d to HEAD dea7de7 (3 commits, 8 files: design/prototype.ts, lib/context-bill.ts, lib/review-ledger.ts, test/helpers/providers/gemini.ts, a changelog.d fragment and tests). There were no staged, unstaged or new files outside that set. **Documentation health:** - docs/review-policy.md: Updated. It now says that a capitalized HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW that names something in the code ("the HIGH branch") collects at INFORMATIONAL, while CRITICAL and `Blocks: yes` keep blocking (GSTA-711). - docs/standalone-binaries.md: Current. The `gstack-context-bill --exact` description names no model. - docs/designs/DESIGN_TOOLS_V1.md: Current (historical design record). Its gpt-4o snippets record the original design, not live reference. - changelog.d/fix-model-defaults-and-review-log-severity.md: Current. It describes every user-visible change. **Coverage debt:** The `--exact-model` default (now claude-opus-5-5) is documented only in the CLI usage text. The Gemini fallback model (gemini-4-argon) lives only in a test helper and needs no user documentation. design/prototype.ts is an internal script with no docs. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Test selection finds tests for NodeNext .js imports and Rails specs
body:
In TypeScript repos that import `./x.js` for `x.ts` (NodeNext) and in Rails repos, touched source files now get their tests instead of none.
Why: `/verify` and `/ship` found no tests for these files even though tests covered the files (#4398, #4211).
Nothing to do: a Rails file maps only when its spec exists at the conventional path.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts`: an import written as `./x.js` (or `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`) resolves to its TypeScript source first (`x.ts`, then `x.tsx`; `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`), as tsc does, then to the path as written. Path string literals keep naming the file as written.
- Same file: an RSpec spec at `[<root>/]spec/<path>_spec.rb` selects `[<root>/]app/<path>.rb` or `[<root>/]<path>.rb` when that file exists, at the repo root or under an engine's root.
- Tests in `test/pregate-import-graph-paths.test.ts` and the new `test/pregate-rspec-convention.test.ts`; `docs/pregate.md` documents both rules.
</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Test selection found no tests for these files, so the checks stopped or asked for hand-written mappings (#4398). Rebuilt on current main from #4401 by @mikhailsal and #4211 by @ikraamg, credited as co-authors.
</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only test selection changes, and almost always more files map to tests. One narrow loss: when a committed `x.js` sits beside its `x.ts` source, a plain-JS file that imports `./x.js` now maps to `x.ts`, so a test that reaches `x.js` only through that file is no longer selected locally for a change to `x.js` (CI still runs it). A repo whose declared runner cannot run Ruby treats a mapped spec as not run and not counted, as it does for Python today; with no remote check configured, nothing then runs that spec before CI. The docs' note that request and system specs are not mapped holds only because no `app/requests/` or `app/system/` source normally exists; the rule itself does not exclude them.
</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

Scope: the branch diff against c2b4f0d2. It changes the test selector in `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts`, adds two tests, and adds a changelog.d fragment. The working tree had no staged, unstaged or untracked changes. Result: `docs/pregate.md` (test selection) now lists RSpec's spec/<path>_spec.rb to app/<path>.rb or <path>.rb convention, including engine roots, and says request and system specs are not mapped. It also documents that NodeNext emitted-extension imports (./x.js for x.ts or x.tsx, .jsx to .tsx, .mjs to .mts, .cjs to .cts) resolve to their TypeScript source first, before the path as written. The changelog.d fragment was already accurate. Debt: none found; no other doc describes selector resolution.
</details>

title: Publish the /ship conductor trial results (GST-3003)
body:
Adds the results of the preregistered trial of /ship with and without its conductor subagent: running /ship in the pull request's own thread showed no clear difference in cost or bugs caught over 30 paired runs of the review and fix phases.
The verdict hangs on one scoring ruling made after seeing data, so the page gives both readings; nothing in /ship changes here. This replaces #4667, closed after a correction of its own.
Nothing to do but read [docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-results.md](docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-results.md).

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

This adds two Markdown files, the results page for the preregistered trial (docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-results.md) and its changelog fragment. No code, prompt, skill or test changes.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The trial's preregistration (docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md) decides whether /ship keeps its conductor subagent, and that decision needs its result on the record, with both readings of the scoring ruling.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Nothing loads or runs these two files, so nothing changes at run time. Readers of the page are the audience.

</details>

<details><summary>What the numbers say</summary>

- Cost a run, folded minus conductor: +$0.07 (-$1.42 to +$1.57). Planted bugs: 22 of 30 against 21 of 30. Real problems, after removing restatements of the planted bug: -0.03 (-0.37 to +0.32) over 6 cases. No structural loss.
- Reader fidelity: 30 of 30 under the ruling, 29 of 30 read literally, which flips the plan's decision.
- The no-gstack arm caught 16 of 30 planted bugs at $0.83 a run; its gap to /ship's better arm only just reaches zero.

</details>

<details><summary>Why it replaces #4667</summary>

#4667 carried the same page through review. Reviews there found and corrected a stop breakdown, restatements of the planted bug counted as real problems, and the interval width for the 6 cases left with a real problem; its last check found a mislabelled critical value in the correction text itself, and the PR was closed rather than given another round. This PR carries the page from #4667's branch with that line fixed and every interval rechecked against the raw analysis.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

The full free test suite passed in CI at this head (run 44992581120, started on the branch after the pull request's own run 44990793131 passed against an older main). `gstack-eval-plan results --check` on this head: `RESULTS: ok no_gstack_rows=1/1 rows=3/3`, `JUDGE_AGREEMENT: ok judge=gpt-6-astra n=71/48 kappa=0.73 bar=0.6` (with the private hand labels; without them it prints EVAL_JUDGE_UNCHECKED, as expected).

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

title: Review and ship tools: read Codex numbered severities, check Remote Control sessions, see every worktree
body:
Five fixes from outside reports. The too-large-diff fix line now suggests only folders the policy can exclude, Codex findings written as `### 1. High` keep their severity, /autoplan's report check runs in Remote Control sessions, /ship's version picker sees all worktrees, and PR before/after images use the real base. Why: each reproduced on main with a failing test and gave a wrong answer. Nothing to do after merge.
What changed, per report | Report | Repro on main (c2b4f0d) | Fix | |---|---|---| | PR #4231, part 2 (@larsonthune) | `### 1. High — title` and `## 2. Critical — …` give no severity: 3 of 4 new cases fail. | `lib/outside-review-result.ts`: a label may start with a heading and then a bullet or number. A "high-level" prose control stays unlabelled. | | #4298 (@exGeni) | A journal whose root is a `system`/`bridge_status` record gets `unrecognized_shape:preamble:system:bridge_status` and enforcement is skipped. | `lib/claude-journal-records.ts` accepts that one record (null parent, no message) above the first turn, like a SessionStart attachment. A second null-parent prompt next to it still denies as `competing_root`. | | PR #4196 (@vilano93) | A worktree at `../elsewhere/wt1` holding a higher VERSION: `siblings: []`. | `bin/gstack-next-version` adds `git worktree list --porcelain` to the workspace_root scan, compares real paths, and skips its own top level. `workspace_root: null` still disables it. | | #4369 (@exGeni) | A 2.38 MB reader diff (2.03 MB of code in `src/`, 0.35 MB of docs) prints "land `src/**`"; after that policy lands, it excludes 0 files and the line asks for `src/**` again. | `suggest()` in `lib/review-exclude.ts` ranks folders by the bytes of files a policy could exclude, judged by path (data, logs, docs, binary assets; never code or tests), and suggests nothing when those cannot reach the ceiling, so the line says split the PR. Patterns already in the base policy are never suggested again. | | PR #4141 / #3733 (@szsunyuan) | With `origin/HEAD` → `feature`, the default base is the feature head, so before and after match. | `lib/pr-shots.ts` uses the shared default-base resolver, then falls back to main, then master. | Not taken from PR #4231: part 1, which lets a quoted declaration inside the publication no-op stand in for the phase report. It loosens a check that exists to prove the report was written, so it needs its own decision.

title: Windows hooks start under unconverted paths, and six more setup and install fixes from outside reports
body:
Seven install and setup bugs reported by outside contributors are fixed, each with a test that fails on main: Windows hooks under an apostrophe home or with path conversion off, two misleading `./setup --status` rows, owner-only files in Bun's shared cache, a leftover `/connect-chrome` alias, a doctor false alarm, and harness installs ignoring `disabled_skills`.
Nothing to do after merge; the next `./setup` or upgrade picks it up.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People on Windows reported that every TypeScript hook died with "Module not found" when their home folder held an apostrophe or they had `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` set. Each hook shim and `gstack-hook-check` now hand Bun a `C:/…` path, and `./setup` turns Git Bash's path conversion back on for the programs it starts.

| Report | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| #4386 (abyss-node) | On Git Bash, a path holding `'` (or any path with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`) reaches native Bun as `/c/x`, so every TypeScript hook failed and `gstack-hook-check` refused all of them | Each hook shim and the checker pass Bun a `cygpath -m` path on Windows, and the checker reads those paths literally; `./setup` unsets `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` and `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` for what it starts |
| #4164 / #4190 (NekoCCN, ElNeMeR70) | `./setup --status` failed every `--prefix` install on `../qa/sections/…` | The checker also tries the prefixed sibling `../gstack-qa/…` |
| #4420 (exGeni) | A gone row said "the next setup drops this row" (only `--refresh-registered` does); the checkout's own Codex render showed as an unregistered project install | Text names the real command; that render is skipped |
| #4288 (exGeni) | `bun install` and the Playwright install ran under setup's `umask 077`, leaving 0600 files in Bun's shared cache | Those installs run under `umask 022`; setup itself keeps 077 |
| #4308 / #4319 (dipbazz, szsunyuan) | Disabling `/open-gstack-browser` left `/connect-chrome` registered | `gstack-relink` removes the alias's generated SKILL.md through the ownership check; an edited one is backed up and the user's other files stay |
| #4324 (alexanderhaire) | `gstack-doctor` inside a gstack checkout flagged gstack's own CLAUDE.md as a pasted skill list | That file is skipped and named in the row |
| #4548 (stevewandler) | OpenClaw, Hermes and Dots registrations carried skills turned off with `disabled_skills` | The payload drops them |

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Every TypeScript hook dies with Module not found" (#4386) and six smaller reports: install and setup should work for everyone who installs gstack, including Windows users and people who turn skills off.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Install scripts and hook launchers. The `cygpath` lines run only when `OSTYPE` is msys or cygwin and `cygpath` exists, so Linux and macOS behaviour is unchanged (script ran: the destructive guard still denies `rm -rf /` on Linux). The umask change applies only inside the two install subshells (test asserts setup's umask is still 0077 afterwards). Alias cleanup removes only gstack's generated file (tested with a user's file in the folder and an edited SKILL.md).

</details>

<details><summary>Security read</summary>

Touches install scripts and hook launchers, so each was read for spawn and permission effects. No new dependencies, network calls or CI changes. Outside branches were read as text only and rebuilt on main.

</details>

<details><summary>Not fixed here</summary>

`./setup` under a home folder holding an apostrophe still hands Bun unconverted `/c/…` paths at several call sites (the Codex preflight at `setup:1414` is the first), and #4386 lists further failures past that point. Those need changes we can't verify without a Windows machine with such a home, so this PR fixes the hooks and the `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` case only.

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

12 of 14 changed paths have a test (86%); value-weighted 11 of 14 (79%). Tests: 1862 → 1862 files (+0 new files; 2 tests added in existing files during review). Gaps left as proposals: a non-checkout `.agents/skills/gstack` registry row, and `disabled_skills` naming `gstack` or `gstack-upgrade`. Weak: the Playwright umask is a source check.
Tests ran: targeted 197 (2 skipped: they need a real Hermes source and a real OpenClaw binary).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two rounds. The first full pass found three blockers from the second-model review: two were fixed in this PR (the alias cleanup could delete a whole alias folder; hook paths were glob-expanded before Bun saw them), each with a test that fails without the fix, and one is in unchanged code (below). The second, scoped pass over the fix found nothing blocking.

</details>

<details><summary>Deferred findings</summary>

Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues.

- Deferred: CRITICAL `setup:1414` under a checkout path holding an apostrophe, Git Bash leaves the Codex preflight's script path unconverted and native Bun exits; setup:7's unset does not cover that case (unchanged code at 1414-1417, same on main)

</details>

title: Changed-constant check stops flagging unrelated tests for one- and two-digit numbers
body:
Changing a small constant such as `MAX_ITEMS = 10` no longer flags every test that mentions its module and holds a `10` somewhere; only lines that use something taken from the module, or name the constant, count. Why: one-line raises of two-digit constants were blocked by dozens of false matches (#4312); on gstack itself, changing `RECEIPT_RUNS_KEPT` (30) flagged 20 test files and now flags 4. Nothing to do. Three-digit and longer values keep the old rule, and a test that imports the module and asserts the old value is still caught.
What changed Raising a one- or two-digit constant used to trip the changed-constant check on every test file that mentioned the constant's module and happened to hold the same small number anywhere, even in a comment or an unrelated timestamp. Now a one- or two-digit old value found through the module counts only on a statement that names the constant or a binding the test takes from the module. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts`: for a one- or two-digit integer old value (sign not counted, so `-10` is included), a test file found only through the module counts a line only when its statement names the constant or a binding the file takes from the module: a JS/TS import of it (named, aliased, default, namespace or multi-line; type-only imports excluded) or a variable that a line naming the module declares (`const out = run('scripts/arms.ts')`, `const { a } = require(...)`). One-character values keep needing the constant's name. - The GST-820 test now runs its fixtures twice. At 120 -> 180 every original module match still counts, and at the incident's own 12 -> 18 importers and kept results still count and comment-only, type-only and unbound mentions do not. - A new test covers unrelated importers, comments, type-only imports, multi-line, namespace and require bindings, `-10`, and a three-digit control. Both tests fail on main and pass here. - `docs/pregate.md` states the new rule in the `literals` entry. Known trade-off: some tests that really do use a changed one- or two-digit value are no longer reported early. That covers a test that runs the module without taking a binding from it, a typed or array-destructured declaration, and a test that imports the module but asserts through another module's function. Three-digit values still use the old rule, and the full test run still runs every such test. Rebuilt on current main from #4354 by @ElNeMeR70 (co-author), using the narrower rule @Davmunrey proposed in review so GST-820's two-digit importer case stays covered. Closes #4312.
Security read Pure text matching over test files the check already reads. Nothing new spawns a process, reads new files, touches the network, auth, CI, install scripts or dependencies. The outside diff was read as text only; no outside branch was fetched or run.
Blast radius Only the changed-constant check's choice of which test files to warn about moves; it reads the same files as before and starts no process. A warning it no longer gives is still caught when the test itself runs, locally and in the full CI run (confirmed by reading `consumersOf` in `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts` and by base-vs-head probes over gstack's own test tree).
Pre-Landing Review One read-only full review of the final head by four readers: a batched specialist, a red team, a same-family adversarial reader and a second-model review. None found a defect that fails a test, breaks production or loses data. The second-model review marked two early-warning gaps as blocking (listed below); they were ruled notes because the stale assertion still fails when the test runs.
Review notes - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:149` (testing): a one- or two-digit value asserted on a statement that names the module inline, with no binding in the file, is no longer reported early. - Red-team note: details recorded privately. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:203` (adversarial): typed, array-destructured, defaulted and multi-variable declarations are not followed as bindings, and the look-back stays at three lines. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:149` (adversarial): a code line naming both the module and the old value no longer counts without a binding. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:196` (adversarial): binding chains stop after four rounds, and statements are built from text with comment lines removed. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:181` (second-model review, ruled note): a test that imports the module but asserts through another module's function (for example `test/design-lint-fifth-cycle.test.ts:112` for `WAIVER_MIN_REASON`) is no longer reported early. - `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts:203` (second-model review, ruled note): `const items: string[] = listItems()` is not followed as a binding.
Exploratory QA Smoke: the targeted tests (`test/pregate-selection.test.ts`, `test/spawnsync-timeout-tripwire.test.ts`) passed, 60 tests, and the readers ran base-vs-head `consumersOf` probes on synthetic files and on gstack's own test tree; the probe for `WAIVER_MIN_REASON` 24 -> 25 was rerun independently (base flags `test/design-lint-fifth-cycle.test.ts:112`, head does not). No plan checks apply (bug fix). No separate browser or QA charter ran.
Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed in this read-only audit. **Scope:** branch `fix/constant-check-short-numbers` at `ed2dd06` against base `c2b4f0d2`: 4 committed files (`lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts`, `test/pregate-selection.test.ts`, `docs/pregate.md`, `changelog.d/pregate-literals-short-numbers.md`). Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. **Documentation health:** - `docs/pregate.md`: current. The `literals` section already describes the new rule for one- and two-digit integers: they count only in statements that name the constant or a binding taken from the module, type-only imports are excluded, and local helpers are not followed. This matches the code. - `docs/troubleshooting.md` (`PREGATE_LITERALS`): current. Its general wording is unaffected. - `changelog.d/pregate-literals-short-numbers.md`: reviewed only, since the release owner owns changelog content. Its file counts were not re-measured. **Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none, because no diagrams cover this check.

title: browse --session before the command, Gemini AQ. keys, /verify trust across worktrees, and two more fixes from outside reports
body:
Five bugs reported by outside contributors are fixed, each with a test that fails on main: `browse --session` before the command, a stray blank tab in the handoff window, new Gemini keys refused by `$D setup`, `/verify` asking for trust again in every worktree, and `/context-restore` missing a second Claude profile's transcripts. Nothing to do after merge.
What changed, item by item | Report | What was wrong | Fix | |---|---|---| | #4662 part 1 (TayTaySwizzle) | `browse --session x goto …` failed with `Unknown command: '--session'`; help and BROWSER.md promised an automatic per-agent session that Windows never gets | A leading `--session ` moves right after the command, where it is read, and `chain` still reads its flow from stdin; help and BROWSER.md say Windows needs `BROWSE_SESSION` per agent | | #4330 for #4323 (Simba3696) | The headed handoff window kept the blank tab its new browser context opened, which no browse command could see or close | `restoreState` closes the new window's own startup tab if it is still untracked and on `about:blank` | | #4239 / #4283 (slamtanna, Lockyer228) | Google AI Studio now issues Gemini keys starting with `AQ.`; `$D setup` refused them and auto-detection called them OpenAI keys | `AQ.` is accepted and detected as Gemini; gstack's secret scan, browse's cookie masks and the live check's log redaction recognize it too | | #4407 (kylewludwig) | `gstack-checks` trust was keyed by the checkout folder, so each new git worktree was untrusted | Trust is shared by every folder git lists as a worktree of the repository; the command-set hash must still match, and rows written before this still count | | #4559 part 1 (tomg65) | The transcript fallback looked only in `~/.claude` | It reads `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}` (and `${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}` for Codex) |
Security read The /verify trust change widens one grant to the folders `git worktree list` names for that repository (a planted `.git` file does not qualify, and GIT_DIR, GIT_COMMON_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE are cleared for the lookup), and only for an identical command set: the hash covers every check command, package.json script and runner input, so a worktree that declares different commands is still untrusted (tested). Anyone who can add a worktree can already edit the trusted checkout. The new `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` call has a 10 s timeout and falls back to the folder key. The Gemini change only widens a prefix check on a key the user types; the key still goes only to Google's endpoint, and the shared redaction pattern `google.api_key` (MEDIUM, warns at pre-push) and browse's cookie masks now match `AQ.` keys. No new dependencies, network calls or CI changes. Outside branches were read as text only and rebuilt on main.
Left out #4662's third point (subagents in one harness process share a session) needs a design choice; #4559's second point (spotting work done after a checkpoint in other repositories) is a new feature.
Linked reports Refs #4662 Refs #4330 Refs #4239 Refs #4407 Refs #4559

Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match this branch's changes and nothing was edited. **Scope:** 19 files changed on `fix/outside-browse-design` against c2b4f0d (3 commits), plus one unstaged edit to the changelog fragment. Changes covered: `browse --session` before the command, the stray blank tab in the handoff window, `AQ.` Gemini keys in `$D setup` / redaction / cookie masking, `/verify` trust shared across a repository's worktrees, and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`CODEX_HOME` transcript lookup in /context-restore. I searched the repo's Markdown and template docs for key prefixes, transcript paths, session flags and trust keying. **Documentation health:** - BROWSER.md: current. It already documents `--session` before or after the command and the Windows note. - context-restore/sections/transcripts.md: current. It already matches the resolver change. - docs/CONTRIBUTOR_REFERENCE.md: current. The `AIza` example is still accurate, and `AQ.` is optional (redaction prose, so I left it alone). - docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md, docs/hosts.md, docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/BROWSER_INTERNALS.md, README.md: current. Nothing in them contradicts the change. **Coverage debt:** `/verify`'s worktree-shared trust appears only in the changelog fragment; no reference doc covers how /verify keys trust (a common gap, reference-only). `AQ.` Gemini keys appear only in the `$D setup` usage text and the changelog. title: gbrain memory lookups find the artifacts source, product pages and newest timeline rows
body:
`/sync-gbrain` and `gstack-decision-search --semantic` now find a brain host's artifacts source through `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID`, planning skills read their product and brand digests from current gbrain, and the brain gets each sync's newest artifacts and timeline rows. Why: five outside reports (#4443, #4327, #4265, #4179, #4362), each reproduced on main by a test that fails before this change and passes after it. Nothing to do unless your artifacts source lives outside `~/.gstack-brain-worktree`; then set `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` to its id.
What changed, item by item | Report | Before | After | Test | |---|---|---|---| | #4443 (rebuilt from #4656 by @Barack-zero-to-one) | `/sync-gbrain`'s guard found the federated artifacts source only at the worktree path or state root, so a brain host whose source is a gbrain clone re-imported every plan and design doc into the default source | `federatedCuratedSourceId` takes the id `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` names (still required to be federated, with no fallback to the path match), as `brainSyncIndexVerdict` and the wireup already did | `test/regression-2922-memory-ingest-sources.test.ts` | | #4327 (rebuilt from #4328 by @exGeni) | `--semantic` found the memory source only by a path ending in `.gstack-brain-worktree` | the named source wins when registered; an unregistered name gives the file results only, never the worktree or an unscoped search | `test/gstack-decision-semantic.test.ts` | | #4265 (narrowed from #4316 by @atharva081106, reported by @stevotcp) | `gstack-brain-cache` read `page.body`, which current gbrain's `get --json` uses for the read-mode name, and asked for the mixed-case slug gbrain never stores, so every product, brand and persona digest missed | reads `compiled_truth` (`content` for a streamed page) under the lowercased slug | `test/brain-cache-page-read.test.ts` | | #4179 (rebuilt from the PR by @extremenelson) | the drain advanced the brain worktree at its start, before its own commit, and at most once a day, so gbrain served artifacts up to a day old | the advance runs in the drain's exit trap after the commit, on every drain; a failed or refused advance holds retries for 24h; INT/TERM skip it | `test/gbrain-source-worktree-advance.test.ts` (its old test pinned the daily window and is replaced) | | #4362 (rebuilt narrower from the PR by @DanCanadian) | an artifact over 200,000 characters kept its first 200,000, so a long timeline, learnings or eureka log lost its newest rows and ended mid-row | an oversized `.jsonl` log keeps its newest complete rows; markdown keeps its start as before; the cap is unchanged | `test/memory-artifact-body.test.ts` | Left out on purpose: #4316's not-found versus unreachable message and markdown fallback for gbrain 0.46; #4179's `glab auth status` move; #4362's 24 MiB ceiling, `--project` scoped repair and readback changes.
Security read No CI, install script, dependency, auth or new network path changes. `gstack-brain-sync`'s advance calls the same `gstack-gbrain-source-wireup --advance-only` as before (no force-remove, refuses dirty or foreign worktrees) from the exit trap while the drain lock is still held; INT/TERM disarm it. `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` only selects among sources `gbrain sources list` already reports and scopes reads to it; it never widens a search.
Issues Fixes #4179 Fixes #4265 Fixes #4327 Fixes #4362 Fixes #4443
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match this branch's changes, so nothing was edited. **Scope:** committed changes from c2b4f0d2 to HEAD on gbrain-memory-lookups-find-their-pages (nothing staged, unstaged or untracked). That covers the `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` source selection, the brain worktree advance on every sync, the gbrain page-text fix and the newest-rows rule for jsonl logs. **Documentation health** - `docs/gbrain-sync.md`: current. It documents `GSTACK_BRAIN_SOURCE_ID` and the advance on every sync with a 24-hour wait after a failure. - `USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md`: current. The `--advance-only` flag row is unchanged and still accurate. - `changelog.d/gbrain-memory-lookups-find-their-pages.md`: current. It matches the code. **Coverage debt:** none. **Diagram drift:** none.
