title: Fix eight problems users reported in skill instructions
body:
Fixes eight user-reported problems in skill text agents follow: Aside asks you to open the app when it's closed, /test-audit finds your branch's test plan, and /codex reads your repo's own `agents/` folder. Goal: gstack skills do what their docs promise.
Nothing to do as a user; it arrives with the next gstack update.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **#4366, from #4367 by @thehashrocket:** the browser setup check now reports `ASIDE_NOT_RUNNING` when the Aside CLI exits 1 with "isn't running", so the agent asks you to open Aside instead of falling back to the headless browser. A new test fixture copies the real CLI (exit 1, real wording).
- **#4216, from #4315 by @atharva081106:** `/test-audit` Step 1 sets `BRANCH` the way the plan writer does before looking up the eng-review test plan.
- **#4346, from #4358 by @ElNeMeR70:** `/verify` says what `CHECKS: none` means (`READY_FOR_SHIP` never follows) and offers a `gstack:verify:` line.
- **#4379:** after updating an open PR, `/ship` checks the sections `gstack-post` kept. To drop one an earlier run wrote for an older head, it starts from the live PR body (which keeps the PR's review history), reads the body again just before posting, and stops if someone changed it in between.
- **#4616:** `/spec --execute` points the spec archive at the spawned branch, so `/ship` can link and close the issue.
- **#4618:** `/design-shotgun` passes `--reason` to `gstack-taste-update`, naming only the taste dimensions your feedback speaks to, so taste memory fills in without recording opinions you never gave.
- **#3924:** /codex's filesystem boundary named every `agents/` folder, so Codex could skip a repo's own agent code. See "The /codex boundary" below.
- **#4296, from #4397 by @szsunyuan:** the guide for running a coordinating agent on Capy, and its `AGENTS.md` template, now say worker threads read `CREW.md`, not the coordinator's own `AGENTS.md`.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Each report was a case where an agent following gstack's own instructions did the wrong thing. It fell back to a worse browser, missed a test plan, stalled on a repo with no checks, left a stale PR section, lost a spec link, learned nothing from a design pick, skipped code it was asked to review, or put rules where worker threads never read them. Every fix was reproduced on main c2b4f0d first (a failing test for #4366 and #4216, a command repro for the rest).

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Skill text and the generated SKILL.md files, the codex host's boundary line and the shared Aside readiness probe that every browser skill renders. The probe change adds one shell `case` arm on output it already captured; `test/aside-probe-shell.test.ts` runs the real probe under bash and zsh against a fake CLI that prints the real exit-1 message (script ran). Everything else is prose, pinned by `test/skill-text-user-reports.test.ts` and the regenerated goldens.

</details>

<details><summary>The /codex boundary (#3924)</summary>

This narrows /codex's own safety boundary on purpose. /codex told Codex not to read "~/.claude/, ~/.agents/, .claude/skills/, or agents/". A bare `agents/` also covers a repository's own `agents/` folder, which is code under review, so Codex skipped it in consult mode. /codex's copies (the skill, its consult, challenge and review modes, and the codex host's boundary line) now say "... .claude/skills/, .agents/, or any agents/openai.yaml" and that other files in the repository `agents/` folder are code to review. Installed skills and every `agents/openai.yaml` stay protected by name, and `.agents/` is now named explicitly.

The same sentence in the second-model review that /ship, /review and the plan reviews run (`CODEX_BOUNDARY`) is unchanged: it's part of a reviewer brief pinned at no-loss-tested bytes, so it changes only after a no-loss replay. That stays open on #3924.

</details>

<details><summary>Security read</summary>

No CI, install script, dependency, network, auth or process-spawning code changes. The Aside probe change is a shell `case` glob on output already captured; it never prints that output. Outside PR branches were read as text only and rebuilt on main.

</details>

<details><summary>Size growth</summary>

The Aside probe arm (about +90 bytes in every skill that runs the browser check) raises 30 SKILL.md size pins, 8 skeleton caps, 8 size-ratio caps, the /verify context ceiling (3231 to 3282 tokens) and /ship's recorded size total, each to its measured value. The review fixes add 60 bytes to /ship's recorded size total (419 to 479) and raise the /design-shotgun skeleton cap from 36,278 to 36,335 bytes, both measured.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two full review passes and one follow-up check on the final head, plus a native adversarial pass and a second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol). Three blocking problems were found and fixed, all in text this PR adds: one in the /ship body cleanup (details recorded privately), the cleanup overwriting a PR body someone edited between the read and the post, and /design-shotgun's reason claiming all four taste dimensions. One blocking item sits in unchanged lines and is listed under Deferred findings; nine notes below the bar are listed under Review notes.

</details>

<details><summary>Deferred findings</summary>

Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues.

- Deferred: CRITICAL `test-audit/SKILL.md.tmpl:61` /test-audit can select another branch's eng-review test plan by suffix match

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl:316` Re-run read-modify-write with --replace can overwrite PR body edits made between fetch and replace

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional smoke on the gstack-post body merge and the new tests (4 captures, report-only). The success probe passed; the riskiest changed edge (the --replace repost) reproduced the first review finding (run history dropped), and after the fix the same replay kept the history and removed the stale section. Captures run on the final text: pass. Limits: no live GitHub round trip; Aside, Codex and the other fixes rely on CI's full test run and the targeted tests.

</details>

<details><summary>Design Review</summary>

No frontend files changed, so design review was skipped.

</details>

title: Skills load their declared gbrain context at start, and harness status says unknown when its list fails
body:
`/office-hours`, `/plan-ceo-review`, `/design-shotgun`, `/design-consultation` and `/retro` now load the brain context they declare when they start, skill start stops telling a read-only repo to run a sync that can't help, and `gstack-harness status` says `unknown` when a harness's skill list fails. Why: three outside reports (#4329, #4419, #4412), each reproduced on main by a test that fails before this change and passes after it. Nothing to do; `gstack-config set gbrain_context_load off` turns the context load off.
What changed | Report | Before | After | Test | |---|---|---|---| | #4329 (reported by @exGeni) | nothing ran `gstack-brain-context-load`, though its header, `setup-gbrain/memory.md` and the 1.26.0.0 notes said every skill start did; the 16 declared queries never ran and `gbrain_context_load off` had no reader | `gstack-skill-start` runs the loader for a skill whose `SKILL.md` declares `gbrain.context_queries`, only when gbrain is configured, never in a `deny` repo, and not when `gbrain_context_load` is `off`; output goes through the same `_sanitize` as learnings and keeps the loader's data envelope | `test/skill-start-gbrain-context.test.ts` | | #4419 (reported by @exGeni) | in a read-only repo the unpinned hint said to run `/sync-gbrain --full`, which skips code ingest by policy and never pins, so the hint came back every start | read-only gets a line saying code isn't indexed there and how to change the tier; deny gets no gbrain hint | same file | | #4412 (reported by @exGeni) | `harnessSees` searched OpenClaw's `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` error text for skill names and reported every registered skill missing | a failed or erroring list command is `unknown` with its first error line; a completed list still reports what is missing; `docs/hosts.md` notes `--agent ` | `test/harness-sees-failed-list.test.ts` |
Why Each report described a skill start or status line that said one thing and did another, so people saw hints they could not act on or missing skills that were really there.
Blast radius Only the five skills that declare queries run the loader; the generic fallback the loader has for other skills stays unwired. Each run is bounded by the loader's 500 ms per gbrain query, and a repo policy that can't be read counts as deny, so a broken store never turns brain access on (file read and test run: `test/skill-start-gbrain-context.test.ts`). The policy lookup reads the existing `gbrain-repo-policy.json` store with `get --batch`, which never moves a corrupt store aside.
Security read Process spawning: skill start now spawns `gstack-gbrain-repo-policy get --batch` and, for the five skills, `bun gstack-brain-context-load.ts` with the Bun isolation flags; the skill name is checked against `^[a-z0-9-]{1,60}$` before it forms a path, and the SKILL.md path is inside the gstack checkout. Brain content reaching the model is wrapped in the loader's `USER_TRANSCRIPT_DATA do-not-interpret-as-instructions` envelope and passed through `_sanitize`, which strips forged `GSTACK_INSTRUCTION` and `SESSION_ID:` lines. A `deny` repo gets no gbrain call. No CI, install, dependency, auth or network change beyond the gbrain queries the loader already makes.
Test Coverage Coverage: 83% value-weighted (83% including 0 weakly covered paths). Test value: 0 tests written, 0 rejected by the authoring gate, 0 existing tests extended, 0 paths weakly covered. Two small gaps stay open: the `gstack-harness status` line printing the error text, and a test that passes a bad skill name. Tests ran: targeted 204
Pre-Landing Review No blocking issues found in the final read-only review of this head. Earlier rounds fixed one blocker (skill start read the policy store with plain `get`, which could turn a corrupt store into "no policy"). Four second-model findings were ruled notes by the owner, listed in the agent notes.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-7f377291dcec` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-start:417` pinned deny repo still gets the gbrain search hint (Low, Blocks: no) - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-start:411` without jq every repo reads as deny, silently (Low, Blocks: no) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/harness-register.ts:741` non-zero list exit reads unknown even with a valid list (Low, Blocks: no) - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-harness:130` first stderr line printed raw into status output (Low, Blocks: no)
Issues Fixes #4329 Fixes #4412 Fixes #4419
Exploratory QA No separate probe ran on this head. The final review's readers ran the two new test files (5 pass) and six neighbouring files (53 pass), and CI's full free suite passed at this tree.
Documentation Scope: the committed diff on skill-start-gbrain-context-and-harness-status against main, which covers loading gbrain context at skill start for skills that declare context_queries, the read-only and deny repo-policy hints, and gstack-harness status reporting unknown with the harness error. The worktree had no staged, unstaged or new files. Result: current. docs/hosts.md and setup-gbrain/memory.md were already updated in this branch and match the code. The five skills that declare context_queries match the skills the docs name, and the gbrain_context_load off switch is documented. No doc edits were needed. Debt: historical CHANGELOG.md entries still say context load runs at every invocation. They were left as written because they are past release notes.

title: /cso keeps going when a .env-style file cannot be read, and reports it as unread
body:
/cso's `start` no longer aborts when a tracked secret-like file (`.env.example` and the like) cannot be read because of a sandbox deny rule or file permissions; the file is listed as unread and the run's source coverage reads partial. Why: with Claude Code's sandbox and a `Read(**/.env*)` deny rule, /cso could not run at all on any repo tracking such a file. Nothing to do after merge.
Repro and fix Repro on main (c2b4f0d), as a normal user: a repo tracking `.env.example` with mode 000 gives `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNSAFE_PATH","message":"Source could not be opened as a regular file: .env.example"}}`. When the sandbox also denies `lstat` (the reported case), the raw `EPERM` escapes and `start` prints the generic `INVALID_SCHEMA`. Both are tests in `test/cso-unreadable-secret-file.test.ts` that fail on main. Fix, all in `lib/cso/snapshot.ts`: - A permission error (`EACCES`/`EPERM`) on `lstat` or `open` of a path that `exclusion()` already keeps out of `snapshot/` records an entry with `originalHash: not-read` and `withheld: … unreadable (EACCES); its payload was not assessed`. It has no `excluded:` prefix on purpose, so coverage counts it as an in-scope gap rather than a clean exclusion. - The special-file walk skips such a path without opening it, and the end-of-capture stability check requires a path whose `lstat` was denied to stay denied. - Any other unreadable file still fails with `UNSAFE_PATH` and the same message as before. Five tests in `test/cso-unreadable-secret-file.test.ts` cover this: the two repros above, an ordinary unreadable file that still refuses, an ordinary file whose `lstat` is denied that still refuses, and a denied secret file that becomes readable during capture, which raises `SNAPSHOT_RACE`. After the fix, `start` on the repro repo runs and reports `snapshot-inputs: partial` with that line. Not changed: an old run whose `readable/` folder already holds a copy of such a file can still fail retention cleanup under the same deny rule, and the generic `INVALID_SCHEMA` message does not yet name the errno.
Security read This touches /cso's capture boundary, so the read was about what can now get past it. The only new path is: a file whose name /cso already treats as a credential (the `exclusion()` list) and which the OS refuses to let us read. Such a file is never opened, copied, redacted or handed to a scanner; it is reported as an unread gap, so the report cannot claim it was checked. A non-excluded unreadable file, a FIFO, a symlink or a hard link keeps today's refusal. No CI, install, dependency, network, auth or process-spawning change.
Review notes (4, all below the blocking floor) Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/snapshot.ts:901` With --paths plus --base, an out-of-scope secret-like file that can be lstat'd but not opened still aborts start: gitBlobStable -> readStableWith throws UnreadableSource uncaught. Not a regression (same abort as main). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/snapshot.ts:837` An lstat-denied secret-like file outside --paths is labelled 'withheld: unreadable' instead of OUTSIDE_AUDIT_PATHS, so coverage counts it as an in-scope unread gap. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/snapshot.ts:305` exclusion() also matches omittedPath() (agent config under .claude/, .agents/, .codex/, .cursor/, .github/agents/), so unreadable files there are withheld too; still reported as a coverage gap. The changelog's 'any other unreadable file still stops the run' overstates strictness. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/snapshot.ts:1088` Withheld entries set no gitHashes/gitModes, so under --base they always count as changed; safe default, adds noise to diff-scoped reports.
Documentation **Status:** current. Audited the release docs for this branch and found none stale, so nothing was edited. **Scope:** base c2b4f0d2 to head 7356635 (4 commits): `lib/cso/snapshot.ts`, `test/cso-unreadable-secret-file.test.ts`, `changelog.d/fix-cso-unreadable-secret-files.md`. Nothing was staged, unstaged or untracked. I checked the /cso docs: `cso/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `docs/cso-scanners.md`, and the /cso entries in `docs/troubleshooting.md`. **Documentation health:** - `cso/SKILL.md.tmpl`: Current (its partial-coverage reporting rules already cover an unread input) - `docs/cso-scanners.md`: Current (unaffected) - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: Current (nothing documented the old abort) - `changelog.d/fix-cso-unreadable-secret-files.md`: Current (describes the fix accurately; not edited) **Coverage debt:** when /cso hits an unreadable secret-like file, it now records the file as withheld and reports source coverage as partial. That behavior is documented only in the changelog fragment, with no troubleshooting entry next to `#cso-capacity` (reference-only gap). **Diagram drift:** none; no diagrams reference the snapshot capture path.

title: /ship can clear its test gate from CI on a branch stacked on another branch (GST-3381)
body:
When a branch is stacked on another branch, /ship can now clear its test gate from a green CI run instead of refusing with `base_mismatch`.
Teams that ship stacked branches were stuck: the record named the stacked base, but the check read run profiles from the default branch.
Nothing to do: branches based on main behave exactly as before.

## What changed

- `gstack-pregate clear --run` reads run profiles from the base branch the gate record was made against, not from `origin/HEAD`. A new optional `clear --base <branch>` names it explicitly; a `--base` that differs from the record is refused with `base_mismatch` before any evidence is read, for every clear route.
- The CI reuse inside `gstack-pregate --base <branch>` (what `gstack-ship-release accept --base` runs) clears the gate against that same base.
- Accepting a run of a version-bump-only parent commit keeps the default branch's rule on purpose (docs/pregate.md#remote-gate-stamp-only).
- docs/pregate.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and the CLI help say where run profiles come from.

## Why

"REUSE: refused reason=base_mismatch" blocked /ship on every branch stacked on a base other than main, even with green CI at the head. The record already names its base, so the clear now trusts the same base the gate run trusted.

## Blast radius

Only `gstack-pregate clear` and the CI reuse inside `gstack-pregate --base`. Records made against main resolve to the same base as before, so their behavior is unchanged (bin/gstack-pregate:274 read; the existing clear tests in test/pregate-clear-runs.test.ts still pass). Rung: script ran (494 targeted tests).

## Pre-Landing Review

REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=2 deferred=0 noted=5 fixed=2 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 dispatches=8
Gate edits: none detected (GATE_SCAN tagged=0 at e660b0bb9)

Fixed in this PR: a `--base` that differed from the record could let the bundle option skip run verification (second-model review), and a programmatic clear with no base got the wrong fix hint.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. GSTA-724, GSTA-725 and GSTA-726 reported the refusal.

- `bin/gstack-pregate:274` The record's base now chooses run_profiles; no consumer binds the record base to the PR base (red team and adversarial review; the ruled note in Agent notes covers the same gap).
- `lib/pregate/index.ts:389` Accepting a version-bump-only parent run on a stacked base refuses with advice to rerun against main.
- `bin/gstack-pregate:276` The early base_mismatch refusal also covers the run-URL and saved-result routes; the test covers only the run-ID and bundle routes.

## Documentation
**Status:** updated — one factual correction, no blockers.

**Scope:** commits 6acb93a8a..e660b0bb9 against base c2b4f0d2 (bin/gstack-pregate, lib/pregate/index.ts, docs/pregate.md, test/pregate-clear-stacked-base.test.ts, changelog.d/pregate-clear-reads-record-base.md); nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. Audited docs/pregate.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/ship-policy.md, the ship templates that mention `gstack-pregate clear`, and docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/pregate.md: current (the branch updated run evidence for the record's base and `clear --base`)
- docs/troubleshooting.md: updated (the `PREGATE_RECEIPT_INVALID` entry now says run profiles come from the base pregate.json was recorded against, and that `--base` naming another branch refuses `base_mismatch`)
- docs/ship-policy.md, ship/sections/tests.md.tmpl, ship/DRIVER.md.tmpl, ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl: current (they don't describe where profiles come from)
- docs/evals/ship-conductor-fold-prereg.md: not edited (frozen preregistration; describes earlier behavior)

**Coverage debt:** `gstack-pregate clear --base <branch>` has reference coverage (CLI help, docs/pregate.md#run-evidence, troubleshooting) but no how-to for clearing on a stacked branch. That is a common gap.

**Diagram drift:** none.

title: Review keeps a file that a branch swaps from our own code to upstream bytes (GST-3298)
body:
A branch that replaces your own file, or drops a local patch, so the file now matches an upstream copy byte for byte no longer leaves review: a changed file counts as vendored only if it was already vendored and verified at the merge base, or is new on the branch. This closes the gap the second-model review of #4665 found, so readers always see your own lines leave. Nothing to do for repos without `review_vendored`, which is every repo today.
What changed The second-model review of #4665 found that a branch could swap a file it owned for the upstream's bytes, list it in the vendored manifest, and have review skip the change. Now a changed vendored file is left out of review only when the merge base already pinned it and its copy there matched the upstream too. Otherwise review keeps it as your code and says why. - **Modified vendored files** (`lib/review-vendored.ts`, `vendoredSelection`): a head manifest entry the merge base already has is checked at the merge base too. If the base manifests did not pin it, or its base copy does not verify, it stays in review with `REVIEW_VENDORED_KEPT: mismatched (...)` naming why. New files and re-pins of files that were already vendored are unchanged. - **`gstack-vendored-verify`** also checks the merge base's pins for the files a branch changes or deletes and prints `VENDORED_BASE: checked=N verified=M`. That line never fails the run, and when the check itself errors it prints `VENDORED_BASE: unavailable (...)` and the head verdict stands. - **Failed fetches** fail their own run and no longer wipe good cached pin records. `gstack-vendored-verify --offline` still answers from them, while review keeps that pin's files until a fetch succeeds, so the review plan and the later offline check /ship runs before landing pick the same files. - **Wording**: the keep-too-large refusal no longer points at lines a refused plan never prints, and says plainly when the vendored check could not run. The line reviewers get no longer claims the manifest is in their diff. - Docs: `docs/vendored-code.md`; changelog fragment.
Why "A file the branch swaps from our own code to upstream bytes leaves review" was a finding the second-model review of #4665 raised. Now that removal of your own code always reaches the readers.
Blast radius Only repos whose base policy sets `review_vendored` see any change, and none do today. For everyone else the plan is byte for byte what it was, and the selection only ever keeps more files in review than before (read in `vendoredSelection`; covered by the "without review_vendored nothing changes" test and the no-loss replay fixture for repos without the key).
Pre-Landing Review The full review panel ran on this change, plus one fix round. The second-model reviewer found two problems in the first version, both fixed with tests that failed before the fix. First, after a failed fetch the review plan and the later offline check /ship runs before landing could pick different files. Second, the merge-base check in `gstack-vendored-verify` could fail the run when it errored. Six smaller notes stay open below the bar for a fix: a large re-pin whose base copies don't verify now keeps every file and can refuse to plan, and five wording or diagnostics points in the plan and verify output. Two further findings from the security reader: security finding, details recorded privately.
Exploratory QA Two smoke probes on a local fixture (a base that owns `up/lib/tests/a.py`, a branch that swaps it for upstream bytes and adds a new vendored file), run on the final code: the plan keeps the swapped file as code and leaves the new verified file out of review, and `gstack-vendored-verify --base main` passes with exit 0. Status: pass.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. The change closes the ruled findings from #4665 and the two blockers its own review found, nothing else.
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already match the branch, so nothing was edited. **Scope:** base 9cfbbb94 to head 8ae55030 on `vendored-modified-files-stay-ours`: 3 commits, 7 files, nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. Docs reviewed: `docs/vendored-code.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` (the vendored upstream files section), `docs/ship-policy.md` (the `review_vendored` row), plus the changelog fragment and the changed code in `bin/gstack-vendored-verify`, `lib/review-vendored.ts` and `lib/review-exclude.ts`. **Documentation health** - `docs/vendored-code.md`: current. This branch already updated it to explain that review keeps a file when a branch swaps your own code for upstream bytes, what the `VENDORED_BASE:` line means, and that a failed fetch keeps earlier good cache answers. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The `VENDORED_FETCH_FAILED` entry is still accurate. - `docs/ship-policy.md`: current. The `review_vendored` row is high-level and still true. **Coverage debt:** two minor gaps, nothing critical. Troubleshooting has no entry explaining the new `REVIEW_VENDORED_KEPT` details ("replaces our own code" and "the latest fetch failed"). The `VENDORED_BASE:` output line is documented only in `docs/vendored-code.md`. **Diagram drift:** none.
Tests - [x] `bun run typecheck`: exit 0. - [x] `bun test test/review-exclude-vendored.test.ts test/review-vendored.test.ts test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts`: 40 pass, 0 fail. - [x] Free test suite on CI at this tree (free-tests.yml run 44999154884): green, 38,835 tests. - [x] macOS named regressions (run 44999154884) and Windows smoke (run 44995451943): green.

title: A granted follow-up check that confirmed its blockers fixed now counts once the rest are ruled (GST-3501)
body:
/ship's finish now accepts a granted follow-up check that confirmed its blocking findings fixed (or auto-fixed), once the findings left over have been ruled.
Why: gbrain#10036 stalled at the review limit with every finding either fixed or ruled, because finish kept printing "FIX_CHECK: not counted".
Nothing to do. A stuck PR reruns finish at the same head after upgrading gstack; no new review round is needed.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![The new test fails on main and passes on this branch: a ruled follow-up check with fixed or auto-fixed blockers now reads CURRENT](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/AYQOKvsXitF5_l6q_m-I_DEq_llMaRnaSI0hyVuwyz8.png)

The new test fails on main and passes on this branch. A ruled follow-up check with fixed or auto-fixed blockers now reads CURRENT.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The new test fails on main and passes on this branch: a ruled follow-up check with fixed or auto-fixed blockers now reads CURRENT</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+(pass) a fixed blocker no longer holds a ruled fix-check row open (GST-3501) > GBRA-732's fix-check row reads CURRENT once its two deferred blockers are ruled [0.57ms]
+(pass) a fixed blocker no longer holds a ruled fix-check row open (GST-3501) > an unruled deferred blocker still holds the row open, and an open or skipped blocker still needs a ruling [0.14ms]
+ 2 pass
+ 0 fail
-(fail) a fixed blocker no longer holds a ruled fix-check row open (GST-3501) > GBRA-732's fix-check row reads CURRENT once its two deferred blockers are ruled [3.91ms]
-(fail) a fixed blocker no longer holds a ruled fix-check row open (GST-3501) > an unruled deferred blocker still holds the row open, and an open or skipped blocker still needs a ruling [1.30ms]
- 0 pass
- 2 fail
 
~~~

</details>

A PR whose follow-up check fixed its blockers and whose owner ruled the rest still could not finish, because finish said the check had unresolved findings. Owner rulings can clear a follow-up check's row, but the rule for what a ruling must cover counted every finding the reviewer had marked blocking, whatever its action, including the fixed ones. A fixed finding can't be ruled, so the row never cleared. Now `holdsOpen` in `lib/review-evidence.ts` skips a blocking finding recorded `fixed` or `auto-fixed`, the two actions the rest of the code already treats as resolved. Blocking findings that are open, deferred, noted or skipped still need a ruling. The policy docs (`docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`) now say the same.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"FIX_CHECK: not counted (review has unresolved findings or did not finish clean)" kept printing on gbrain#10036 after every finding was fixed or ruled, so the PR sat at the review limit with nothing left to do. A row with no rulings already reads a fixed finding as resolved; rows with rulings now agree.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`holdsOpen` has three callers: `withoutRuledNotes` and `rulingGap` in `lib/review-evidence.ts`, and the rulable list in `lib/ship-release.ts:360`, which checks `RULABLE` first and so is unchanged (file:line read). Gate findings are unaffected because `stampGateFindings` never leaves a gate finding `fixed`; the 154 focused tests and the full CI run pass.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

One finding, below the blocking floor: the first version exempted only `fixed`, but `auto-fixed` deadlocked the same way (reproduced with a probe). Fixed in f2b1a70, and the follow-up check of that fix found nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Functional smoke on `holdsOpen` and `reviewFreshness`: the success path passed; the `auto-fixed` edge failed before the fix and passed after. Verdict: pass.

</details>

title: /cso finish no longer closes an audit after a refused submit (GST-3504)
body:
When the /cso helper refuses a submission, `finish` now keeps the audit open and asks for a corrected submit, instead of closing it and losing the evidence. Why: an eval session hit `exclusions must be an array`, ran `finish` in the same command, and its corrected resubmit was then refused because the audit had closed. Nothing to do for users; `finish` still closes the audit once the audit deadline passes.
What changed - `submit` writes `submission-refused.json` in the run directory when the helper refuses input for a running audit before its deadline. A later accepted submit removes it. - `finish` refuses with `PREREQUISITE` while that marker exists and the deadline has not passed, and names the refused message. After the deadline it closes the audit and adds the gap "A refused submission was never resubmitted: ". - New test in `test/cso-cli.test.ts` drives the compiled launcher: refused submit, blocked finish, `inspect` still reports `remainingSeconds`, corrected submit, finish; then a second audit whose deadline has passed finishes with the gap. It fails on main at the blocked-finish step.
Why A refused submit followed by `finish` closed the audit, so the corrected resubmit had nowhere to land and the evidence was lost. Keeping the audit open until a submit is accepted, or until the deadline, keeps that evidence.
Blast radius Only the /cso helper's `submit` and `finish` commands (`lib/cso/cli.ts`). Audits with no refused submit behave as before. An audit whose last submit was refused now needs one accepted submit, or the deadline, before `finish` closes it.
Documentation Scope: the diff from ef72e414 to fix/cso-finish-after-refused-submit (lib/cso/cli.ts, test/cso-cli.test.ts and the new changelog fragment), plus the /cso docs that mention submit or finish (cso/SKILL.md.tmpl, cso/SKILL.md, docs/cso-scanners.md, docs/cso-release-qualification.md). No staged, unstaged or untracked changes were present. Result: docs are current. The changelog fragment matches the new behaviour: `finish` refuses to close an audit whose last submit was refused until the deadline passes, then closes it and records the refused submission as a gap. No other doc contradicts this, and no files were edited. Debt: cso/SKILL.md.tmpl line 98 ('make one correction, then finish partial') doesn't say that `finish` waits for the deadline if that correction is also refused. Clarifying it is a small, optional follow-up that needs a template edit and regeneration.
Tests - Focused tests `cso` (`bun test test/cso-cli.test.ts test/cso-cli-lifecycle.test.ts`): pass, tests_ran=35, at 54ddf89. - The new test fails on main at the blocked-finish step and passes on this branch. - CI runs the full suite.
Exploratory QA Five probes against the compiled launcher on a throwaway fixture repo. Required checks pass: a refused submit is recorded, and `finish` then refuses and leaves the audit running. Optional probe 005 shows that an empty `{}` submit clears the marker and lets `finish` close before the deadline; that is review note `lib/cso/cli.ts:1530` below, under the blocking floor. The QA tool's overall verdict is fail because of that probe.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/cli.ts:1543` resume after the deadline marks the run interrupted, so finish skips the refused-submission marker and closes without the gap - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/cli.ts:1402` recordRefusedSubmission swallows a lease failure; a submit refused for a busy lease leaves no marker - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/cli.ts:1530` any accepted submit, even {}, clears the refused marker (duplicate of specialist-batched#1) - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/cli.ts:1394` pre-lock JSON-shape refusal can race a concurrent valid submit and leave a stale marker; a resubmit clears it - INFORMATIONAL `lib/cso/cli.ts:1563` marker file is left in the run directory after finish (redacted, 0600, unread once finished)
Agent notes
Agent notes - Second report in GST-3504 (`inspect` omitting `remainingSeconds`) does not reproduce on main: a daily run with `--budget 600` returns `remainingSeconds` from `inspect` (539 at the first call), and the existing run-clock test pins it. The new test also checks it after a refused submit. The eval's session transcripts were not available to compare. - Local: `bun test test/cso-cli.test.ts` 32 pass, `test/cso-cli-lifecycle.test.ts` 3 pass, `format:cso:check` and typecheck clean. - Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: /cso finish must not close an audit after a refused submit. Delivered: refused-submit marker, finish refusal before the deadline, gap after it, one failing-first test, one changelog fragment. - Review: specialist-batched (testing, security, state-machines, red-team) and adversarial-native, one full pass at 54ddf89. Fix-First skipped specialist-batched#1 (any accepted submit clears the marker; below the floor, a design choice). Five adversarial findings, all Low and Blocks: no, recorded as notes above. ## Approvals Plan: exempt: bug fix with a failing-first test (GST-3504) Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 0 auto-fixed, 1 asked (0 fixed, 1 skipped), 0 deferred, 0 noted Gate edits: none detected (1 listed, 0 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) ```gstack-ship-receipt { "schema_version": 1, "pr": 4692, "head": "d0cdbaf76e57e1816e92b4d1baf198fe9aea68ca", "version": "1.102.2.0", "base": "main", "gate": { "cso": { "pass": 35, "fail": 0, "skip": 0 } }, "calls": 21, "session_kind": "unattended", "run": "ship-4692-r1", "head_tree": "baeeeb95d1fa541b373c6e93a092b1fef89016c1", "product_patch_id": "1a5e104b985aa07a7febaf94c0b2bf0a2fb113ff", "gstack_version": "1.102.2.0", "review_depth": { "depth": "light", "class": "code", "runtime_lines": 37, "rules": "630fd3101899e28e", "base": "0b4f0ceeec19fef62480db6c8eb00c4015380a39", "registry": "0b4f0ceeec19fef62480db6c8eb00c4015380a39", "gate_scan": { "tagged": 0, "head": "d0cdbaf76e57e1816e92b4d1baf198fe9aea68ca" }, "reasons": [ "runtime=37" ], "risk": [], "mode": "panel" }, "pregate": "requires-remote cleared @baeeeb95d1fa (8 checks, current for d0cdbaf76e57)", "requires_remote": [ "pregate.json/remote_gate: remote-gate tree=baeeeb95d1fa tests=38833 runs=44996806817/1 profiles=ci-reuse/free-tests heads=d0cdbaf76e57 verified=2026-11-22T07:25:06.125Z" ], "issues": { "fixes": [], "refs": [], "flakes": [] }, "docs": { "status": "current", "scope": "README.md, cso/ and docs/ (/cso docs that mention submit or finish), plus the changelog.d fragment" }, "review_loop": { "passes": 1, "blocking_found": 0, "deferred": 0, "noted": 5, "fixed": 0, "scope": "frozen", "rounds": 1, "dispatches": { "specialist": 1 } }, "gate_dispositions": [] } ```

title: /ship can finish after a docs audit stopped before saving its snapshot (GST-3502)
body:
/ship no longer gets stuck when its docs audit edits a left-out docs file and then stops: the second audit can now include the first audit's edits, so /ship can record its result and finish.
Why: a gbrain release was blocked with no supported way forward.
Nothing to do: `gstack-docs-candidate snapshot` gains one optional flag for this case, and /ship's Blocked recovery step names it.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `gstack-docs-candidate snapshot` takes a new flag, named in the Agent notes, that records, in the second audit's after-edit snapshot, the files a stopped audit edited: what changed between the stopped audit's Prepare snapshot and the second audit's Prepare snapshot, at the same commit. It needs `--pre` and `--run`, and refuses an after-edit snapshot or one taken at another commit.
- Run ids that name the same record file by two spellings (`a/../b.md` and `b.md`) now count as the same run, in the docs candidate, in the check that keeps an earlier audit's edits, and in the review depth check.
- ship/sections/documentation.md's Blocked recovery step 2 names the flag.
- New test test/review-exclude-stopped-audit.test.ts reproduces the stopped-audit case and fails on main.
</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

The new flag is `--carry-stopped <stopped audit's Prepare snapshot>`.

Reported by GBRA-732 on gbrain at 8e0159ab (audits ship2-docs-1, blocked, and ship2-docs-2): `gstack-ship-receipt write` refused RECEIPT_INVALID on review_exclude because the re-audit's post snapshot could not carry the stopped audit.

title: Prompt router stops sending feature requests to your bug-fix skill
body:
The prompt hook no longer treats a feature request as a bug report just because its body mentions an error, so your bug-fix skill isn't named for "Add …", "Support …" or "[Feature]: …" requests. Why: in our eval runs, 13 of 27 feature-titled tasks were routed to the bug-fix skill, so the model started a bug-fix workflow on a feature. Nothing to do: the change is in the hook's scoring. This builds on #4674 and should land after it.
What changed - A request whose title (its first line, or the first line inside its first tag such as ``) starts with a word that asks for something new is not a bug report, unless the title itself names a defect (any strong or weak sign, the verb fix, or an error status such as "returns 404"), the body asks for a fix, or the body follows an issue template (steps to reproduce, expected or actual behavior). - A title where the feature word leads a noun phrase and a verb that says what happens ("Support page shows a blank screen", "New users see a blank dashboard", "Add to cart button does nothing") describes a symptom, so it stays a bug report. - An exception name in a fenced code block outside a `` tag counts as a defect when deciding whether the first line inside the tag is a feature title. - An exception name in backticks in the title (`ValueError`) still counts as a defect, curly apostrophes are read as straight ones, and "Add-to-cart …" is not read as the word "Add". - Outside a bug report, the word "bug" in a trigger no longer exempts it from the 8-word proximity rule, so a wrapper's "STATUS: FIXED" plus a distant "error" doesn't score "fix this bug".
How it was checked A probe set of 34 synthetic prompts (`test/fixtures/skill-route-feature-title-probes.json`) was written and committed before the rule: 16 feature requests (14 with a feature-word title and 2 plain controls) and 18 bug reports (15 with a feature-word title and 3 plain controls), including every edge case reviewers found on #4674. | | feature requests not routed to the bug-fix skill | bug reports routed to it first | |---|---|---| | main | 4 of 16 | 16 of 18 | | #4674 | 3 of 16 | 18 of 18 | | this PR | 15 of 16 | 18 of 18 | The one miss is listed in the test: a feature title that says "no longer", which already counts as a regression sign. On the 46 held-in first-draft bug reports the hook still names the bug-fix skill alone on 42.
Agent notes Follow-up split out of #4674 (GSTA-794; eval finding GEVA-558), per GStack Minder's ruling. Misroutes a reviewer finds that route the same as on #4674 or main are notes, not blockers, per that ruling. Correction (2026-11-22): the probe table first published 14 feature requests and 20 bug reports; the fixture holds 16 and 18 (c04 and c05 are feature requests). Recounted from the fixture with the test's own routing. ## Issues Refs #4423 ### Documentation **Scope:** The diff from base c1f16c5 touches 6 files, and the working tree had no uncommitted changes. I reviewed `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`, `changelog.d/feature-titled-requests-not-bug-reports.md`, `lib/skill-route.ts`, `test/fixtures/skill-route-feature-title-probes.json`, `test/skill-route.test.ts`, `test/helpers/free-fixtures-data.ts` and `docs/skill-gates.md`. **Result:** The docs are current, so no files were edited. `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` already describes the new feature-title rule and the changed defect-word "everyday" rule. Both match `lib/skill-route.ts`: `FEATURE_TITLE`, `NOUN_LED`, `ERROR_STATUS`, `TEMPLATE_SIGN`, and `everyday` now depending on `reported`. The changelog fragment is present. CHANGELOG.md, TODOS and VERSION were left alone, as the brief requires. `docs/skill-gates.md` mentions the router but needs no change. The new `keep` parameter on `splitCode` is internal and needs no user-facing doc. **Debt:** The probe fixture has 34 entries, which matches the doc and the changelog fragment. The probes were not re-run, so the 15/16 and 18/18 rates are the branch's own figures and have not been checked here. ### Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 1 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 0 deferred, 1 noted (round 1, light depth); fix-check 1: 1 noted; Step 11 (Opus adversarial, GPT-6.2 Astra second-model review): 9 findings, 5 fixed in a granted fix-check (grant a-d9217bf878c4, Captain GStack Minder), 4 ruled notes; fix-check 2: 2 noted. title: A skipped CI run no longer blocks reusing a passing run on the same commit (GST-3514)
body:
When one commit gets two runs of the same workflow and the newer one skipped every job, the passing run can now be reused, and the CI wait no longer reports that commit red. gbrain hit this when a pull request run that skipped all its jobs, created in the same second as a passing manual run, blocked that passing run. Nothing to do: a newer failed, cancelled or still-running run still blocks reuse exactly as before. ## What changed - The newer-run check in `verifyRun` (lib/run-evidence.ts) now ignores a newer run whose conclusion is `skipped`, just as it already ignored a newer green run. A skipped run ran no job, so it says nothing about the commit's tree. - `waitForRun` (lib/ci-carry.ts), which `gstack-ci-carry wait` and `gstack-ship-release accept` use, now passes over a newer skipped run and waits on the run before it. When every run on the commit was skipped, it still reports red, as before. - docs/pregate.md says which newer runs block reuse and which don't, and the changelog entry covers both commands. ## Why A run that never ran a job isn't evidence against the tree, but it was treated like a failure. A newer red or running run of any event still blocks reuse, including the documented case where a red pull request run blocks reusing a manual run (docs/pregate.md, the CI tree reuse section). ## Blast radius Only the CI reuse check and the CI wait read the change. Both still refuse a commit whose newer run failed, was cancelled or is still running, so a red run can't be reused. ## Pre-Landing Review One review pass on the whole change: a combined specialist reader (testing, security, state machines, red team) and a second adversarial reader. The specialist reader found that the CI wait still read a newer skipped run as red, so `accept` would have stopped in the same case this PR fixes. That is fixed with a test that failed first, and a second read of just the fix found nothing. The adversarial reader found nothing blocking; its three notes are below. ## Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ci-carry.ts:179` When every run on the head is skipped, waitForRun still returns red with an empty failing list (pre-existing; the fallback keeps it). - INFORMATIONAL [ADVISORY] `docs/pregate.md:907` The docs and changelog describe only verifyRun's veto; the wait now passes over a skipped newest run to an older run, which they don't mention. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ci-carry.ts:78` findCarry cuts HEAD's runs to CANDIDATES before skipped runs are dropped, so a burst of skipped runs could push the green run out of the window (pre-existing). ## Documentation **Scope:** base `0b4f0ceee` to head `0fbc61d89` on branch `ci-reuse-skipped-run-no-veto` (3 commits, 6 files), with no staged, unstaged or untracked changes. I ran Steps 1, 1.5, 2–4 and 6. The banned-terms check returned `none` because main keeps no list. **Result:** the docs are current and I made no edits. The branch stops a newer skipped run from triggering `newer_run_vetoes` in `lib/run-evidence.ts`, and `waitForRun` in `lib/ci-carry.ts` now passes over completed skipped runs when it picks the newest run. - `docs/pregate.md` §run evidence (~l.907) already says newer skipped runs don't veto, which matches the code. - The same-tree-commits paragraph (~l.1158) says "a newer red or running run vetoes", which is still accurate. - The `newer_run` text at l.1752 belongs to the flaky-exception check in `lib/pregate/flaky-exception.ts`, which the branch doesn't touch, so it isn't stale. - The verdict-reuse section of `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` describes a different mechanism and isn't affected. - The changelog fragment is accurate and stays unchanged, as the brief requires. **Debt:** none found. ## Tests - [x] New case in test/run-evidence.test.ts: a same-second skipped pull request run and a skipped manual run no longer block reuse. Negative controls: a newer failed or running manual run still does. The case failed with `newer_run_vetoes` before the fix. - [x] New case in test/ci-carry.test.ts: the wait passes over a newer skipped run to the green run before it, a newer skipped run beside a failed one is still red, and a lone skipped run is still red. It failed before the fix. - [x] test/run-evidence, test/ci-carry, test/ci-tree-reuse and test/ship-ci-carry: 130 pass, 0 fail. The full free suite ran in CI (Free Tests run 45003784713), green at this head.

The second clause of the issue, about a run whose event the profile doesn't accept never blocking reuse, was dropped by GStack Minder's ruling, because it would undo the documented red pull_request veto in scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts. ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch ci-reuse-skipped-run-no-veto. title: A granted fix round now ends with one full review of the final head, and fixed findings close only on a finished review (GST-3260)
body:
After a granted fix round changes code, /ship now runs one read-only full review of the final head, and a fix commit's trailer closes its finding only after a full review that finished with the fix in range. Why: a scoped re-check of only what changed never stands in for a PR's last full review, and three closure paths could close a finding too easily. Nothing to do. This PR is stacked on #4664 and lands after it.
What changed - **Final full review after a granted fix round.** `gstack-review-plan` used to stop after a granted follow-up check ("never a new full review"). When that check reads the fix clean and the fix changed runtime code, the plan is now one read-only full review of the final head: no fix round, and a blocker stops the run for the PR's owner to decide (`PR_ROUND_CAP`). A fix that only touches docs or tests still finishes after the check. The /ship step that runs the check asks the plan again afterwards. - **Trailer closures need a finished review.** A `Review-Finding:` trailer closes its finding only after a full review that converged, is bound to its committed tree and has the fix commit inside its range. Before, a completed pass that had made its own fixes, or whose range began after the fix, could close it. - **Security findings never close by location.** A security finding known only by its raw `path:line:category` fingerprint never closes by grant or trailer, so its location can't reach the PR body. - **A missing reviewer record closes nothing.** A granted check whose record of what its reader raised can't be read no longer passes the check that it dealt with every finding. - **Fix lists with markup.** A fix list that writes an id as `**p1/x#1**` or `[p1/x#1]` now names that id, so the granted check can close it. - **New files in the check's diff.** The follow-up check's diff now includes files the fix created but hasn't committed (`git add -N`, then `git diff`). With no new files, the diff is byte-identical to before.
Tests and replay Every new case fails on #4664's head first. - `test/fix-check-clearing.test.ts`: trailer closure refused for a pass that didn't converge or whose range starts at the fix; a security fingerprint closes nothing, while a plain fingerprint still closes; a missing reviewer record closes nothing; bracketed and bolded fix-list ids. - `test/fix-check-hunks-untracked.test.ts`: the documented hunks command includes a new untracked file and is byte-identical when there is none. - `test/round-cap-granted-stop.test.ts` and `test/r51-final-review-replay.test.ts`: the new plan through the CLI, and the preregistered no-loss replay (`docs/evals/r51-final-review-after-grant-prereg.md`). The replay compares main's planner with this one on 2,596 recorded test histories and 1,658,880 grid histories. Every step main plans still runs; the only addition is one read-only full review after a clean granted check that changed runtime lines; no fix round or check is added. It's deterministic and makes no model calls.

The first commit (efa87de) fixes the three open notes from #4664's cross-family trail read (flags 1–3); later commits fix #4664's deferred notes p2/outside-voice#1 (fix-list markup) and p2/red-team#1 (untracked files in the check's hunks), and add the R51 final review. - Review pins: `test/fixtures/review-pins` repins `lib/review-depth.ts` and `ship/sections/review-army.md` under replay GST-3260. Reviewer brief bodies and goldens are unchanged. - The #4663, #4664 and gbrain#10036 replay shapes are modelled from their PR bodies, not taken from recorded logs. - Local: typecheck clean; targeted planner and CLI files 588/589. The failure is GST-1607 "#271 shape" at the 5 s per-test timeout, which fails the same way with the changes stashed. ```gstack-receipt-runs {"head":"ef58d375717997e2bb30d163ded119bfbd0ba4fa","run":"ship-4696b","mark":"stop","tree":"d1b1b338d17ec36eb18484226e2f6463eb9ff127","at":"2026-11-22T10:15:21.088Z"} {"head":"ef58d375717997e2bb30d163ded119bfbd0ba4fa","run":"ship-4696b","mark":"grant","grant":"a-5a39bc5f25d0","at":"2026-11-22T10:25:56.708Z"} {"head":"e3a087bd1671a6659f66a7af646ecad6f6ab26e1","run":"ship-4696b","mark":"stop","tree":"c2e700e5158d469aa9231c0cf6ac5a3b80c2ef13","at":"2026-11-22T10:28:40.338Z"} {"head":"e3a087bd1671a6659f66a7af646ecad6f6ab26e1","run":"ship-4696b","mark":"abandoned","by":"GSTA-36","reason":"Captain GSTA-36 granted an extra-round read-only final review; it runs in ship-4696c"} {"head":"e3a087bd1671a6659f66a7af646ecad6f6ab26e1","run":"ship-4696c","mark":"stop","tree":"c2e700e5158d469aa9231c0cf6ac5a3b80c2ef13","at":"2026-11-22T11:51:43.229Z"} ```

title: Secrets check flags keys in JavaScript and TypeScript const, let, var and class fields (GST-3500)
body:
The secrets check now catches a key written as `const token = "<key>";` (or `let`, `var`, `export const`, a typed declaration, or a class field like `private apiKey = "<key>";`) in JavaScript and TypeScript files.
Why: before this, a real key in that form passed the check, and JavaScript and TypeScript are the most common languages in projects that use gstack.
Nothing to do, but a test that builds a fake key from pieces (`const token = 'ghp_' + '…'`) now fails the check when that line is edited; build it with `[...].join('')` instead.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **New rule `env.kv.js`** (MEDIUM, blocks like `env.kv`). It reads a declaration with one to four of `declare`, `public`, `private`, `protected`, `static`, `readonly`, `override`, `accessor`, `const`, `let` or `var` (optionally after `export`), then a secret-named name, an optional `?`/`!` and type, and a quoted or template literal. It also reads after `//` and `/*`.
- It reports only in `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts` and `.cts` files. A scan with no file path is unchanged, because the Rust rule already reads `let` and `const` there.
- It is a separate pattern, so every existing `env.kv` match is unchanged and no line reports twice. A name with no keyword, including a bare `#secret = "<key>"` line, is still `env.kv`'s.
- The value gets `env.kv`'s checks: a credential-shaped name, no placeholder, 3.0 bits of entropy and the test-file fixture-label exemption. A key split across a `+` chain of quoted pieces reports.
- These stay clean: key-naming text (`'agent_model'`, `'terminalFontSize'`), lowercase paths or ids (`'test/skill-e2e-bws.test.ts'`), environment-variable names (`const API_KEY = "MY_SERVICE_API_KEY"`), and a template whose text beside its `${…}` slots holds no secret. A type stops at `;`, so `let session: string; const mode = "BILLING_DASHBOARD";` gives nothing. UUIDs, hex, digit segments and mixed-case random text still report.
- docs/pregate.md lists what this rule does not read: a fallback after an environment read, a declaration that does not start its line, a value on the next line, `.vue` and `.svelte` files, letters-only passphrases, a space inside a `${ }` slot, and a `+` chain whose first piece is a template.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A real key bound by a JavaScript or TypeScript declaration passed the check that runs before every push. The tests were written first and failed on main; the negative controls (types, destructuring, imports, calls, environment reads, placeholders, other file types) passed there and still pass.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only added lines in JavaScript and TypeScript files are read by the new rule, so nothing that passed before fails unless it is edited. A replay over every tracked file, comparing main 75410da with this branch at a0763dc, lost 0 findings and added 41, all secret-shaped literals in test files (fake `sk-` keys, UUID tokens, random strings).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The documentation already matches this change; no edits were needed.

**Scope:** 6 committed files from 75410da7 to a0763dc3 (the secrets check reads JS/TS declarations as `env.kv.js`): `changelog.d/secrets-check-reads-js-declarations.md`, `docs/pregate.md`, `lib/redact-patterns.ts` and three tests. There were no staged, unstaged or new files. Cross-doc reads covered the redaction sections of CLAUDE.md, docs/CONTRIBUTOR_REFERENCE.md and spec/sections/gate-and-file.md.tmpl.

**Coverage:** `env.kv.js` has reference coverage (docs/pregate.md secrets section), how-to coverage (allowlisting by finding id in the same doc) and explanation coverage (why each shape is or is not read, with known limits). No critical or common gaps.

title: /ship counts a clean recheck of granted fixes even when its brief was written just before the review started (GST-3523)
body:
When an owner grants one recheck of a fix and it reads the fix clean, /ship now counts it, even when the review pass wrote the recheck's brief a moment before it took the review's start token.
Why: /ship only accepted the record of what the reviewer read if it was written after that start, so a clean recheck was not counted and the PR needed an owner's exception to finish (gbrain#10057).
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- The review pass writes the recheck's brief, which records the hunks the reader gets, and then takes the recheck's review start token. When `gstack-review-dispatch mark --log-start` records that start, it now re-dates the brief's hunks record, but only while the record's digest still matches the hunks file. So a record for hunks the reader never got is never attached.
- It prints `FIX_CHECK_HUNKS: restamped` or `not restamped` so the pass shows what happened. An unreadable hunks file prints `not restamped (hunks file unreadable)` and still records the start instead of failing.
- The record's fix list also keeps approval ids (`a-…`). It used to keep only reader finding ids and `path:line:category` fingerprints, so a grant naming ruled notes recorded an empty fix list and closed nothing (gbrain#10063).

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Two runs on gbrain hit this: gbrain#10057, where the brief was written about two seconds before the start token, and gbrain#10063, where the same timing plus the dropped approval ids left a granted recheck closing nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the recheck's hunks record in `lib/review-evidence.ts` and the start-recording step in `bin/gstack-review-dispatch`. A record is re-dated only when its digest matches the hunks file at the moment the start is recorded; a clearing still needs the grant, the fix list and exactly one open blocker to agree on the same id, so approval ids can't close anything a grant didn't name.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

`test/fix-check-hunks-restamp.test.ts` (new; Windows-curated like the other dispatch-bin tests):
- A record written before the start is not attached on main, and after the fix it is attached with its digest and fix list.
- Hunks edited after the render, a repeated start and a start for another kind of review re-date nothing.
- A missing hunks file still records the start and says why nothing was re-dated.
- The fix list keeps approval ids beside reader finding ids and fingerprints, and nothing extra.

Each case fails without its fix. CI's full free suite passed at this tree (run 45024757519).

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `sf-7060f709df5f` security finding, details recorded privately
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-a45a04086dfe` security finding, details recorded privately

</details>

title: Review exclusions stay in place when the repo's own policy test pins an excluded path (GST-3512)
body:
An excluded data file no longer comes back into review just because the repo's own test for `review_exclude_paths` pins that exact path in its pattern list.
Results PRs that exclude a single data file and pin the list in a test now stay under the reader limit; code that reads the file, and example paths the test checks against the patterns, still keep it in review.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `lib/review-exclude.ts`: a test file that names `review_exclude_paths` no longer keeps a path as named-by-code when the path is itself one of the base policy's `review_exclude_paths` patterns and every mention of it in that file is a whole quoted array entry (`'p'`, `"p"` or a backtick string). The bracket scan now reads forward and skips other strings and comments (`#` comments too in `.py` files), so a bracket inside a comment or string no longer changes the answer.
- Everything else still keeps the file. That covers code that reads it, other tests, a quoted path passed to a call, held in an object or constant, joined or prefixed, and any array of paths that are not literal patterns (hit and near-miss examples, `test.each` tables, `for…of` lists).
- `docs/ship-policy.md`: the named-by-code row says the same. Changelog fragment added.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A results PR (GEVA-569) stayed at about 4.8 MB in review because its policy test pinned `PATTERNS`, which lists the literal path of a large `sessions.jsonl`. That one quoted pin kept the excluded file in every reader's diff.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the named-by-code keep rule in `lib/review-exclude.ts` changes, and only for test files that name `review_exclude_paths`; every other file and keep reason reads as before. The new tests fail against the previous rule and pass now, and the negative-control test (code, another test, call argument, object value, joined path) keeps all six files (`test/review-exclude-contract-test.test.ts`, run in CI at this head).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two review passes and one granted follow-up read of the fix. title: A fix closes its review finding only after a finished full review, and a security finding never closes this way (GST-3260)
body:
A commit that says it fixes a review finding now closes that finding only after a full review that finished, made no fixes of its own, and read the fix. A security finding never closes this way, so its file and line can't reach the public PR body.
Why: three gaps on main let a finding close too easily: a review that was still fixing things, a security finding's location, and a follow-up check whose record of what it read was missing.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- A `Review-Finding:` trailer closes its finding only after a later full review that converged, was bound as verified, and whose range holds the fix commit. A first pass reads the whole pull request, so it still closes the finding.
- Security findings never close by trailer or by grant, with or without a line number in their fingerprint, so no closure line puts their location in the PR body.
- A granted follow-up check whose record of its readers' findings can't be read closes nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

These three gaps came from the second-model trail read of #4664, and #4696's last review found two more in the first fixes: a first pass's empty range was read as leaving the fix out, and a security fingerprint with no line slipped past the filter. Both are fixed here.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only how /ship decides that a review finding is closed (`lib/fix-check-clearing.ts`). Every change makes closing stricter or keeps it the same, except a first pass with an empty range, which closes a committed fix the way it did before #4664's follow-up work.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

`test/fix-check-clearing.test.ts`:
- A round that hadn't converged, or whose binding was incomplete, closes nothing.
- A range that starts after the fix closes nothing.
- A pass 1 with `range_base: null` still closes.
- A security fingerprint, with or without a line, closes nothing by trailer or by grant, while the same fingerprint with a plain category closes.
- A missing findings record closes nothing.

All four changed tests fail on main's `lib/fix-check-clearing.ts`. CI's full free suite passed at this tree (run 45021799133).

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

title: Secrets check reads files whose names hold a space or an accent (GST-3528)
body:
The secrets check now reads a file whose name holds a space, an accent, a quote or a backslash, such as `src/clé.rs` or `src/my file.rs`. Why: git writes those names quoted or with a trailing tab, so the file reached the scanner with no type and a key in it passed; the push check also listed it as an unknown file. Nothing to do.
What changed - New `diffHeaderPath` in lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts reads a `+++ ` header the way git writes it: a C-quoted name (`"b/src/cl\303\251.rs"`, octal UTF-8 bytes and `\t`-style escapes) is unquoted, and the tab git adds after an unquoted name holding a space is dropped. - The secrets check's three diff parsers (added lines, added line numbers, postimages) and the push check's parser all use it, so they can't drift. - The old reading stays: a name git quoted or tab-ended is also scanned the way main read it (as a file with no type), so every rule main applied to it still runs. Its findings are now listed under the decoded name, so an allowlist entry scoped to that path can match them where main's nameless findings matched none. - A decoded name too long to write as a scratch file falls back to `added` plus its extension instead of stopping the check. - A file name holding control, C1 or bidi-override characters is printed quoted on allowlist and scanner-error lines, so it can't rewrite the terminal. - The secrets check's docs and a changelog fragment say what changed.
Tests and replay - Failing first (773c5bb4): on main, a Rust key in `src/clé.rs` or `src/my file.rs` passed the secrets check, and the push check named the first `(unknown file)` and dropped the second. The parser unit test read both names wrong. - Negative control: a quoted `.ts` name still reports at least what main reported. - Replay of the secrets check's parsers over a diff of every tracked file (main vs this branch, at 47982a88): 5,321 files each, 0 lost, 0 changed; this repo has no quoted names.
Agent notes Thread GSTA-800 for GST-3528, found by the second-model review on #4697. lib/pregate/index.ts is not touched. Other `+++` parsers with the same raw read, left out of scope: lib/banned-terms.ts, lib/no-stop.ts, lib/sealed-guard.ts, bin/gstack-brain-secret-scan.py (lib/gate-diff/git.ts already drops the tab). ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-b892276d528e). title: Deleted tests still check the files that list them, and Playwright fixture specs run under Playwright
body:
Deleting or renaming a test now runs the tests of files that still list it even when another test already covers it, and Playwright specs that take `test` from a local fixtures file run under `playwright test`. Why: a deleted test could pass the local checks while a stale curation list failed after merge (#3536), and fixture-based Playwright specs went to the unit runner and failed (#4347). Nothing to do. A repo whose specs import `@playwright/test` directly sees no change.
What changed - `lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts`: the "files naming it" check for a removed test (deleted, or a rename's old name) now also runs when the removed test already maps to a test through a `dependencies` entry or a remaining test that names its path. Those files' tests run, and a naming file with no test fails closed. A mention does not count when it sits under another directory's path (`packages/b/util.test.js` for a deleted `test/util.test.js`), and `.gstack/pregate.json` does not count when its only mentions are `dependencies` keys, listed tests beside another test that still exists, or another directory's test. A mention spelling the test's own directory always counts. - `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts`: a JS/TS spec counts as a Playwright spec when it takes `test` from a repo module built on `@playwright/test` (`base.extend(…)`, `mergeTests(…)`), directly, aliased, through named or `export *` re-exports, `index` modules or a `.js` specifier naming a `.ts` source, up to 8 modules deep. A module that takes `test` from vitest, `@jest/globals`, `bun:test` or `node:test` keeps the unit runner even when it also uses Playwright APIs, and nothing outside the repo is read. - `docs/pregate.md` describes both rules. Tests: #3536 cases, fail-closed and control rows in `test/pregate-removed-paths.test.ts`, and #4347 plan rows (fixtures, `export *`, `mergeTests`, vitest-fixture and outside-the-repo controls) in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts`. Rebuilt on current main from #4158 by @szsunyuan and the detection half of #4347 by @vilano93, both credited as co-authors. The `runners` setting proposed in #4347 is new configuration and is not included. Closes #3536.
Known limits - When a `dependencies` list holds the deleted test next to an existing non-test file, `.gstack/pregate.json` is not treated as still naming the deleted test, so the deletion is not refused. A later edit to that source fails only if nothing else covers it. A one-line fix follows separately. - A vitest fixture that also imports a Playwright API and takes `test` from another local vitest module, or a barrel that re-exports vitest's `test` next to `export *` of a Playwright helper, can be planned under `playwright test`, which then fails loudly with no tests found. - `export { appTest as test }` is not followed, so that spec keeps the unit runner, as before this change. - Directory matching compares path suffixes: `packages/b/test/x` counts as a mention of `test/x` (fails closed), and an unnormalized `a/src/../test/x` mention is missed. A one-line fix follows separately.
Security read The test-selection change reads the repo's own `.gstack/pregate.json` with a JSON parse in a try/catch and reuses the existing `git grep`; no new process starts. The Playwright detection reads repo files through `readRepoFile`, which refuses symlinks that leave the repo, follows only relative specifiers that stay inside it, and stops after 8 levels. No network, auth, CI, install script or dependency change. The outside diffs were read as text only; no outside branch was fetched or run.
Issues Refs #3536 Refs #4158 Refs #4347
Agent notes Lane GSTA-805 for GStack Minder (GSTA-36), issue GST-3487, PR C of three. Repro on c2b4f0d2a: a deleted `test/util.test.js` mapped by `dependencies` to `test/retry.test.js` while `scripts/curation.js` still listed it exited 0 running only retry.test.js; a spec importing `test` from `./fixture` planned as `npx vitest run`. `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts` is at 800 lines, the module-size limit.
Documentation audit **Status:** current. The branch's own docs changes are accurate; no edits needed. **Scope:** 6 committed files from base 7530280 to head fb4fc554 (pregate lane selection and Playwright runner detection, their tests, one changelog.d fragment, docs/pregate.md). Nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. Searched docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, AGENTS.md and docs/ship-policy.md for related claims. **Documentation health:** - docs/pregate.md: Current (the branch already describes the expanded checks on files that still name a deleted test, from #3536, and Playwright fixtures-module detection, from #4347; both checked against the code) - changelog.d/fix-removed-test-namers-and-playwright-fixtures.md: Current (fragment owned by the parent; read only) - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: Current (no affected claims) - CONTRIBUTING.md: Current (no affected claims) **Coverage debt:** none. No new command, flag or setting; both changes are behavior fixes covered in the docs/pregate.md reference. No diagram drift.

title: /ship keeps its review count and grant claims honest, and a symlinked harness pin needs a fresh review (GST-3463)
body:
/ship now keeps a PR's earlier runs when it rewrites the PR description, so later runs count review rounds correctly, and it refuses to start reviewers when it could not save a granted round's claim.
Why: both slips let a PR get more review rounds than the two-round limit allows, without anyone seeing it.
Nothing to do: the fixes apply on the next /ship run.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

The problem: a PR could go past its two review rounds without anyone noticing. When Step 19 wrote a fresh description, the published body kept only the newest run, so the next run counted fewer rounds than the PR had. When the run record could not save a granted round's claim, `gstack-ship-receipt claim` still printed `GRANT_CLAIMED`, so a run could stop and grant itself the same round twice.

- **Rewritten descriptions keep earlier runs.** `gstack-ship-receipt write --pr`, given a description file with no record or run history, reads the live PR description's earlier record and runs into it. If the live description can't be read, write says so with a `RECEIPT_RUNS:` line and keeps only this run.
- **A claim that wasn't saved fails.** `claim` exits non-zero and says not to start reviewers when the run record exists but could not save the claim, and says to rerun with the same run id, because a new id would find the round already spent.
- **Shared harness pins.** A pin that a main merge only re-recorded counts as already reviewed only when it is a regular file at both commits and both pinned files resolve. A pin turned into a symlink now needs a fresh review.
- **Docs audit wording.** The docs audit steps say a re-audit names each earlier audit by its post snapshot, or with `--carry-stopped` and its Prepare snapshot when it stopped first. The review and ship policy docs describe the claim failure and the pin rule.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Make the pin mode check the first commit of PR 2", then items 1 and 4 of GST-3463: a claim that fails open and a description rewrite that undercounts rounds. Both are gaps in the check that limits each PR to two review rounds.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The changes touch `gstack-ship-receipt claim` and `write`, the harness-pin rule in `lib/ship-receipt-patch.ts`, and the /ship docs audit steps. Each change only adds a refusal or reads more history. The new live read runs only when the description file has no record and no runs, and a failed read warns and writes what it wrote before. Each new test fails on main, and CI's free suite passed at 49be1d4.

</details>

<details><summary>Test Coverage</summary>

The coverage audit read 10 changed paths. 7 have tests rated two or three stars and 3 have none (audit only, no tests generated):
- A pinned file missing at one commit, when the pin has no blob field.
- `claim` when no run record exists (it still claims and prints a `RUN_RECORD:` note).
- `write` when the body already holds a record or runs, a live body with runs but no record, and `--repo` passed through to the read.

Tests: 1883 → 1883 test files (the three new test files were written before /ship). Coverage: 70% (7 of 10 paths).
Tests ran: tests reused from CI, run 45027568836 (1764 files, 39095 tests).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Round 1 (full panel) found three notes and fixed two: the claim error now says to rerun with the same run id, and the docs audit wording no longer says `--carry-stopped` replaces `--carry`. The third, making `write` fail when the live description can't be read, was skipped: it is no regression, and failing would stop every write made without GitHub access. Round 2 (full, on the fix range) and the second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol) found only notes. A scoped reader read the docs audit's two policy edits clean.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- `ship/sections/documentation.md.tmpl:106`: the prose says `--carry` for each earlier audit and `--carry-stopped` for each stopped one, but the snapshot takes each flag once. The two-attempt limit means a re-audit has one earlier audit, and a repeat flag fails loudly.
- No test runs `--carry` and `--carry-stopped` together in one snapshot.
- `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:1072`: on Capy, where the description is handed to the host to publish, "the PR body already holds the claim" may not be true yet. Rerunning with the same run id is still right.

</details>

<details><summary>Exploratory QA</summary>

Smoke: the three new test files ran on the reviewed tree (10 pass, 0 fail). No plan checks; this is a bug fix with no plan.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

No paid evals ran here. The PR screen selects 25 end-to-end cases (mostly /ship's own docs-audit cases) and no judges; they are not verified on this PR and run in main's paid gate after merge.

</details>

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: GST-3463 items 1 and 4, the pin mode check and the docs lines deferred from #4693. Delivered: those, plus two test fixes CI found (a `gh` stub and a bin path).

**Scope:** the committed diff from 25bf93c4 to 49be1d47 on ship-claim-and-rerun-history, plus the unstaged changelog fragment. It covers the harness-pin rule (when a re-recorded pin counts as reviewed), the claim failure when the run record can't save it, write --pr keeping earlier runs, and the `--carry-stopped` wording in the docs audit steps.

**Documentation health:**
