title: gstack-upgrade refuses to run after setup applies disabled_skills (SKILL.md marked as changed)
body:
gstack-upgrade refuses to run after its own setup has applied `disabled_skills`.

Steps (gstack at origin/main of 22 Nov 2026, Linux and macOS):
1. `gstack-config set disabled_skills qa-only,careful` (any non-empty list), then run `./setup`.
2. Setup (gen-skill-docs / gstack-relink) rewrites the tracked root `SKILL.md`, adding "Disabled on this install (never invoke or suggest them): ..." and dropping the disabled routing rules.
3. Run `bin/gstack-upgrade`.

Expected: the upgrade proceeds, since the only change is the one gstack made itself.
Actual: `gstack-upgrade: tracked files changed: SKILL.md; nothing was changed; fix: commit or move those changes`. Every scheduled upgrade fails until someone runs `git checkout -- SKILL.md`; after a successful upgrade, setup rewrites the file again, so the next upgrade fails the same way.

Possible fix: have the dirty check in `bin/gstack-upgrade` ignore the router `SKILL.md` when its only change is the generated disabled-skills block (or write the per-install router outside the git tree).

title: The recommendation judge's calibration test checks two real captured questions (GST-3447)
body:
The recommendation judge's calibration test now checks two real captured questions, one on each side of the pass line, so a judge-model change can't silently change what the AskUserQuestion format eval passes. Why: after the judge moved to Haiku 5.5, the format eval started failing on recommendations the old judge passed, and no calibration case covered that boundary. Nothing to do.
What changed and the evidence - `test/llm-judge-recommendation.test.ts` + `test/fixtures/judge-recommendation/`: two captured questions from the runs after #4630. 44962016350's reason names the tradeoff against adding scope and must score at least 4 (Haiku 5.5: 15/15 samples at 4 or 5; Sonnet 5.5: 10/10 at 5). 44955253712's reason rests on the plan's category and must score below 4 (Haiku 5.5: 25/25 at 3; Sonnet 5.5: 9/10). With the old Haiku 4.5 judge swapped back in, the test fails on the second one (it scores it 5). - `test/helpers/touchfiles-data.ts`: the calibration case reruns when its fixtures change. - The format eval itself is unchanged and still scores one judge sample. An earlier commit on this branch moved it to the median of three samples; more samples showed that makes it slightly more likely to fail on the question that motivated it (run 44952328945: Haiku 5.5 scores it 3 in 25 of 41 draws), so that change was dropped. The fix for those failures is a wording change in plan-ceo-review (GST-3536).

title: /ship reruns the test gate when its record was taken against a different base branch (GST-3493)
body:
/ship no longer accepts a test-gate record taken against a different base branch: it reruns the gate against the base it ships to.
Why: a record cleared while a pull request was stacked on another branch still verified after the pull request was retargeted at main with the same code, though it used the other branch's policy and CI run profiles.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `gstack-pregate verify --base <branch>` refuses a record whose base names another branch (`PREGATE_STALE`). Without `--base` it behaves as before, and a record with no base still verifies.
- /ship's finish step passes its base to that verify, so a mismatched record reruns the gate on the stamped tree instead of passing.
- `gstack-ship-queue ready` and the step that writes /ship's sign-off record for the final head make the same check, so a stale record can't reach the merge queue or the sign-off either.
- `gstack-pregate clear` refuses a base that already contains the recorded head (`BASE_CONTAINS_HEAD`), on a branch or a detached checkout, before it reads that base's policy.
- `docs/pregate.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` describe the new refusal and its fix.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

GST-3381 (#4689) found that a test-gate record taken while a pull request was stacked on another branch kept verifying after the pull request moved to main. That record's checks used the stacked branch's policy and CI run profiles, so the merge checks could pass on evidence gathered for a different base.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the test-gate record's verify and clear paths in `bin/gstack-pregate` and `lib/pregate/index.ts`, and the three callers that now pass a base (/ship's finish step, the merge-queue check and the sign-off writer). A record whose base matches, or that names no base, verifies exactly as before; the only new outcome is a refusal that sends /ship back to rerun the gate.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/pregate-verify-base.test.ts` (new): a record cleared under a stacked base verifies with `--base stack` and is refused with `--base main`; a record with no base still verifies under `--base`; `clear` refuses once the stacked base holds the head, on a branch or detached, and leaves the record uncleared.
- `test/ship-release.test.ts`: finish passes `verify ok` on a matching record and reruns the gate once the record's base names another branch.
- `test/ship-queue-ready-pr-base.test.ts`: `ready` refuses a record from another base.

Each new case fails without its fix. CI's full free suite passed at this tree (run 45030602055).

</details>

</details>

- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-ship-receipt:586` no test covers the base comparison in receipt write and carry; carry without --base skips it
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-632487ab67ea` security finding, details recorded privately
- INFORMATIONAL `sf-bf570b47ca0b` security finding, details recorded privately

</details>

GST-3493, follow-up to GST-3381 (#4689), ruled ship-as-note by GSTA-36 on finding outside-voice#2, with the clear-side BASE_CONTAINS_HEAD scope added from #4689's cross-family trail read. Round 1's second-model review raised two blockers (ready and receipt write still accepted a record from another base; the clear guard read HEAD, which is null on a detached checkout); both are fixed in ce772771. Round 2 found no blockers. Evals: none affected (no prompt, template or judge change).

Documentation (Step 14.5 audit docs-4706a-1, inserted unchanged):

**Scope.** The audit covered the committed diff from main (f528f5ba) to the head (91efe35c). The working tree was clean. The diff adds `gstack-pregate verify --base`, which refuses a test-gate record taken against another base branch. It also makes `gstack-pregate clear` refuse with `BASE_CONTAINS_HEAD`, and makes `gstack-ship-receipt` and `gstack-ship-queue ready` check the base. The changelog.d fragment already describes the change.

**Result.** Two docs were updated with small additions:
- `docs/pregate.md`: `verify --base <branch>` now refuses a record taken against another base branch (`PREGATE_STALE`).
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: the `PREGATE_STALE` entry now explains the base-mismatch cause and its fix (rerun `gstack-pregate --base <real base>`). The `BASE_CONTAINS_HEAD` entry now says that `gstack-pregate clear` refuses even on a detached checkout.

**Debt.** None found. CHANGELOG.md, TODOS.md and VERSION were not touched, and no generated files changed.

title: Prompt router stops naming your bug-fix skill on bug reports, and CLAUDE.md drops the failing-test-first step
body:
gstack's prompt hook no longer names an installed bug-fix skill (prove-it and the like) on bug reports, and the CLAUDE.md bug line drops "a focused failing test first". Why: in gstack-evals#426, on 183 real Python bugs, naming that skill got its steps followed in 80% of sessions against 3%, but fixed no more bugs (-1.5 points, 95% interval -3.8 to +0.9). Nothing to do: /review, /qa and /verify route exactly as before.
What changed Until now, when a prompt read like a bug report and you had a bug-fix skill installed, the hook told the model to run that skill, alone, and named it first even beside /verify. The hook now names no skill for that reason. A third-party trigger that names only a bug and fixing it ("fix this bug", "reproduce the bug in a test") no longer routes at all, so the skill is not named through its own triggers either; a trigger with its own target ("fix lint errors", "fix postgres bugs") still routes. The CLAUDE.md bug line now reads "fix them directly: one read-only check of the cause, then fix it", in this repo's CLAUDE.md and in the test copy of the routing section older projects still have. Two pieces stay. The bug-report signs added in #4674 and the feature-title rule from #4694 still decide whether a prompt reads as a bug report. That reading no longer names a skill, but it still keeps a reported defect away from /review and /qa unless it asks for them in their own trigger words, and it decides whether a defect word counts as an everyday word when scoring. Removing either would change how gstack's own skills route, so both stay, with their fixtures; their tests now check the classification directly. The guard against routing messages from other agents (#4423) is unchanged.
Why gstack-evals#426 (B2) compared the bug-fix skill named by the hook against plain gstack on Opus 5.5, GPT-6.2 Sol and particle-1. The steps were followed (80% against 3%) but passes moved -1.5 points [-3.8, +0.9] and passes with a regression test +1.6 [-1.0, +4.3]. Garry cut both pieces on 2026-11-22. B1f (gstack-evals#432) found the hook is the only reliable route to its other skills, so the rest of it stays.
Blast radius Only the routing hook, `gstack-skill-route --explain` and the CLAUDE.md line change. A before/after replay of all 222 prompts in the router's fixtures (60 synthetic, 60 first-draft, 8 QA-overlap, 34 feature-title probes, 60 plain), on Claude and Codex, with and without prove-it installed (888 decisions), ran the real `routePrompt` on main (f528f5ba) and this branch: with gstack's skills alone, 0 of 444 decisions change; with prove-it installed, 234 change, every one from naming prove-it to exactly what main routes without it (224 to no skill, 10 to /verify). prove-it is named on 0 prompts, and `bugReport()` gives the same answer on all 222. `--explain --json` no longer prints `bug_report`, and the routing log no longer writes `bug_report=true`; nothing in this repository reads either.
Pre-Landing Review Light depth, one full pass (specialists, then a Claude adversarial reader and a second-model review on GPT-6.2 Sol). The two specialist notes were fixed in the docs and changelog. The second-model review raised two findings it called blocking. One, a generic crash report reaching a narrower repair skill on a repair verb alone, is how main already routes when no generic bug-fix skill is installed (code this PR does not change), so it is deferred below. The other, that "test" counts as a generic word so a test-diagnostics trigger such as "debug failing tests" no longer routes, was skipped: main already treated exactly those triggers as a bug-fix skill's and named that skill alone on every bug report, which is the behavior this change cuts. Neither would fail a test, break production or lose data. The docs/skills.md note below was fixed by the documentation audit.
Deferred findings Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues. - Deferred: CRITICAL `lib/skill-route.ts:395` a generic crash report can route to a scoped repair skill on a repair verb alone
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:554` claimsBugReports also drops triggers that name tests or a crash as their target - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:554` a skill whose triggers are all dropped is silent in --explain - INFORMATIONAL `docs/skills.md:665` docs/skills.md still describes the failing-test-first clause in the CLAUDE.md routing block - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-skill-route:49` bug_report key removed from --json and the routing log - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:424` reproducing stems to reproduc, so that spelling of a generic trigger is not suppressed
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual fix; no blockers. **Scope:** 12 committed files on `stop-naming-bug-fix-skill` (base f528f5ba, head dc6555df), plus every authored doc grepped for stale bug-report routing claims (`bug_report`, the bug-fix skill named first, a failing test first). Staged, unstaged and untracked content were empty. **Documentation health:** - `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md`: Current. The branch already updated it: the bug-report rule is gone, and the `--json` and routing-log mentions of `bug_report` were removed. - `CLAUDE.md`: Current. The bugs line was updated in the branch. - `docs/skills.md`: Updated. The /investigate section no longer says the CLAUDE.md routing block keeps a failing-test-first step. - `changelog.d/stop-naming-bug-fix-skill.md`: Current. Not edited, because it is protected. - README.md, docs/install.md, docs/proactive.md: Current. They only link to the routing doc. **Coverage debt:** `gstack-skill-route --json` no longer prints `bug_report`. That change is covered in reference docs (the routing doc and the changelog); no how-to is needed. No new public surface. **Diagram drift:** none. No diagrams reference the router.

title: /ship can finish when its docs audit fixes a reviewed doc after the last review round (GST-3532)
body:
/ship no longer gets stuck when its last-step docs audit corrects a line in a doc the review read, after the PR's last allowed review round.
Why: gbrain#10059 had to skip its /ship record to land, because the only fix /ship offered was a third review round, which the two-round limit forbids.
Nothing to do: the next /ship run asks for one small read of the audit's change on its own.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- When the docs audit (Step 14.5) edits, after the review, a doc that the review kept for reviewers to read, and the audit's snapshots show that edit is the only change to what the review read, `gstack-ship-receipt write` now stops with `RECEIPT_DOCS_AUDIT_READ` and writes a short packet of just that change. This works even when the PR has used both review rounds.
- One scoped reader reads the packet. It is not a review round and needs no grant. A clean read, passed back with `--docs-audit-read <record.json>`, is bound into the record as `docs_audit_read`. A reader's finding still refuses and goes to the owner. A stale record means rerunning the reader on the current packet. title: pregate lanes: let a policy keep a server-backed e2e tree out of the local lane (not only test/, tests/, spec/, __tests__/)
body:
## What happens

In a pnpm monorepo whose Playwright suite lives at `apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, any diff that selects one of those specs makes `lanes` read `fail` on a green tree. Every other group passes: on gstack 1.102.2.0 the `node --test` root group was 1233 of 1233 and every vitest workspace group passed.

The cause is a chain:
- `lanes` routes the spec to `pnpm exec playwright test --reporter=list` (the `importsPlaywright` path).
- `runOnce` sets `CI: env.CI ?? '1'`.
- The repo's `playwright.config.ts` starts its API and web dev servers through `webServer` only when `CI` is unset. In CI, the e2e job starts them as workflow steps.

So no server is running, and the suite's `globalSetup` fails before any spec runs:

```
TimeoutError: apiRequestContext.post: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
  - → POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/sign-in/email
   at global-setup.ts:97
```

It is not `PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT`: Playwright's browsers are installed, so the missing-browser check does not match, and the run is graded as the diff's failure.

## Why the repo can't fix it alone

- Starting the servers inside the pre-gate isn't safe here. Several /ship sessions run in parallel worktrees on one machine, and each would start dev servers on the same fixed ports (3000, 5173) against the same dev database.
- `dependencies: { "<glob>": [] }` keeps a tree out of the local lane only for a folder inside `test/`, `tests/`, `spec/` or `__tests__/`. `apps/web/e2e/` is none of those.
- Adding any `dependencies` key also makes the policy declare lanes, which changes every other lane verdict.

## Ask

Either of these would work:
1. Let a policy name a declared test tree by any glob, for example a `local_skip: ["apps/web/e2e/**"]` key, or `dependencies` `[]` honored on a glob the repo marks as a test tier. It would print the same `declared test tree <glob>: N test file(s) not run in the local lane` line and leave remote obligations unchanged.
2. Or grade a Playwright group whose every test is unstarted because `globalSetup` threw as `PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT` ("the diff is not at fault"), the way the missing-browser case is graded.

Option 1 is the more general one. It matches how the existing `[]` test-tree exemption already works.

Related: #4586 (the `node:test` routing fix this report follows).

title: Four tests and two tools stop failing at random: gate-ahead worktrees and the gbrain MCP probe (GST-3543)
body:
Two gate-ahead preparations for one PR no longer fail each other, and `gstack-gbrain-mcp-verify` no longer misreads a valid SSE reply as broken.
Both turned up in the daily flaky-test pass from CI runs that failed once and passed on retry. Two test fixtures that raced on timing are fixed too.
Nothing to do for users; the version is written at merge.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Gate-ahead and version-stamping worktrees take one lock per repository** (`lib/git-worktree-lock.ts`). While git adds a worktree it reads every sibling's `commondir`, and a concurrent add leaves its own empty for an instant, so the other add died with `failed to read .git/worktrees/worktree/commondir: Success` (Trunk e3ed3abf, Free Tests 44999855570; the 4th time since 2026-10-29). Plain git failed 1 of 480 concurrent adds with that exact message, and 0 of 480 failed through the lock. The lock is best effort. When it can't be taken (a filesystem without hard links, an unwritable git directory, or six minutes of waiting), the command runs unlocked, as it does on main today, instead of failing.
- **`gstack-gbrain-mcp-verify` reads the SSE reply without early-exit pipes.** Under `pipefail`, `echo | head -1 | grep -q` fails with SIGPIPE when the reader exits first. A valid SSE body was then parsed as plain JSON, and jq's exit 5 ended the probe (Trunk 1afdd260). Locally 7 of 400 runs failed before the fix and 0 of 400 after. A new test with a reply larger than a pipe buffer fails 5 of 5 on main and passes with the fix.
- **The git fixture template test turns off auto-maintenance.** `git commit` and the receiving end of `git push` start a detached `git maintenance run --auto`, which created and deleted `objects/maintenance.lock` while the template was being copied (ENOENT in cpSync, Trunk 3a4e1509). A new test traces the build and fails on main.
- **The late-SDK-completion overlay test gives both arms 250 ms to start** instead of 15 ms. A 20 ms stall in the first trial's setup reproduces the CI failure (Expected 3, Received 2, Trunk 5a3199f2).

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Each of these failed a CI run at random and cost a rerun. Two of them are real bugs that users of `/ship`'s merge queue and `/setup-gbrain` could hit, not just test noise.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The lock wraps only the worktree add and remove calls in `lib/restamp.ts` and `crew/lib/ship-queue-gate.ts`. When it can't be taken, those calls behave exactly as on main (8 lock tests, including the unlocked fallback, which is red on the version that threw). The verify script's output classes and JSON are unchanged (its existing test file plus the new large-body test). The other two changes touch tests only.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The full review panel and a second-model review ran on this PR. Every finding was fixed except two edge cases in the new lock, which ship as notes: a takeover that stalls for more than 10 seconds, or a killed parent whose git child is still running, can let two worktree commands overlap. Both are no worse than main, which has no lock at all. A third second-model finding, that a lock error could fail a command main ran fine, is fixed by making the lock best effort, and a scoped re-check of that fix found nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The docs already match this branch, so nothing was edited and nothing is blocked.

**Scope audited:** `a88cc7c1..dfb1a663` on `flaky-fixes-2026-11-22`: 9 committed files (`bin/gstack-gbrain-mcp-verify`, `crew/lib/ship-queue-gate.ts`, `lib/git-worktree-lock.ts`, `lib/restamp.ts`, a changelog fragment and 4 test files), with nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. All 157 candidate docs were checked for the changed surfaces, and every doc that mentions them was read at the affected sections.

  CLAUDE.md                                 Current (changelog-fragment pointer still accurate)
  docs/ship-policy.md                       Current (staging and gate-ahead worktree descriptions still hold; the new lock is internal and falls back to running unlocked)
  docs/troubleshooting.md                   Current (RESTAMP_* and gate-ahead entries unchanged by this diff)

title: Code review reads the design checklist and your repo's agents/ folder (#3924)
body:
Code review now checks frontend changes against the design checklist, and the second-model review now reads code in a repository's own `agents/` folder.
Before, the design reviewer was pointed at a file that doesn't exist, and the second-model review skipped every `agents/` folder (#4410, #3924).
Nothing to do as a user; it arrives with the next gstack update.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People reported two blind spots in code review. For a frontend diff, /ship and /review sent the design reviewer to `review/specialists/design.md`, a file that doesn't exist, so the design checklist was never read (#4410, reported by @nfitzsimmons). One resolver in `lib/review-pass.ts` now maps the design reviewer to the real `review/design-checklist.md`, for the staged review and for `gstack-review-dispatch render` alike, and an unknown checklist name now stops the render instead of pointing at a missing file.

The second-model review told the reviewer not to read any `agents/` folder, so code in a repository's own `agents/` folder went unreviewed (#3924, reported by @kolla23). It now keeps the reviewer out of installed skill folders only (`~/.claude/`, `~/.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/`) and any `agents/openai.yaml`, and says the rest of a repository's `agents/` folder is code to review: the same words #4686 gave /codex.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Code review should read everything a change touches. Both bugs silently skipped part of the review, and nobody saw a warning.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The boundary sentence is one shared constant, so the fix reaches every prompt that uses it: /ship's and /review's second-model review, the plan-ceo, plan-eng and plan-devex reviews, the /office-hours second opinion and the /document-release review. No other prompt text changed. A replay of the existing review test panel found no lost blockers with the new wording (details in the notes below).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The batched specialist found nothing. The two second-model readers raised five notes, none fixed here: one is about code this PR didn't change and four are below the blocking bar (both listed below). The outside reviewer's verdict was FINDINGS, with one blocker that this review deferred. Its claim is that an installed gstack points readers at checklists outside the checkout they review. That holds for every checklist since the workspace rule was added; this PR moves the design path to the same root the others already use.

</details>

<details><summary>Deferred findings</summary>

Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues.

- Deferred: CRITICAL `lib/review-brief.ts:238` The design checklist path comes from the gstack install root, but every brief asks readers to read only paths under the checkout under review, so an installed gstack reviewing another project points readers outside their workspace. Lead judgment: the defect lives in workspaceParagraph (lib/review-brief.ts:238), unchanged by this PR; main's pass and render CLI already join every checklist (testing, security, red-team, targeted) to the same install root, so this PR moves the design path to that same root and adds no new out-of-workspace read.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-pass.ts:229` review/design-checklist.md prescribes its own clean reply ('Design Review: No issues found.') and AUTO-FIX prose; a batched reader that follows it instead of the outer brief's NO FINDINGS marker is not a clean reply.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-pass.ts:204` The design checklist was written for the lead /review agent (AUTO-FIX, detector probes, its own output format); a specialist reader could follow those instructions.
- INFORMATIONAL `crew/scripts/review-dispatch-compare.ts:42` The dispatch cost-comparison script sizes the design specialist from review/specialists/design.md, which does not exist, so it counts the design reader as free.
- INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-pass.ts:229` checklistFile throws mid-loop in renderStage, leaving earlier readers rendered and logged but the manifest unsaved; only a hand-edited manifest can reach it.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Scope:** The audit covered base 5962f0d4..HEAD dee6154 (5 commits, 22 files) on reviewed tree 386a2a9b5424476448364cdd3f02c756cd0d3813, with nothing staged, unstaged or untracked. **Result:** The docs are current, so I made no edits. `docs/skills.md:636`, `ARCHITECTURE.md:371`, `CLAUDE.md:124`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:114,831` and `docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md:30,54` already point at `review/design-checklist.md`. title: A crashed merge no longer blocks every other merge, and a one-call count of PRs waiting to merge (GST-3549)
body:
When `gstack-ship-queue land --pin` dies in the middle of a merge, the next merge now takes over its lock by itself (the process has exited, its machine restarted, or 90 minutes passed) and logs it; a merge that is still running is never interrupted. New `gstack-ship-queue count` says how many finished PRs are waiting to merge, and the docs now say how to drain that queue and how to time a revert drill. Nothing to do: the next `land --pin` uses the new lock on its own.
What changed On 2026-11-22 one merge died while it held the land lock, and every later merge refused for hours while about 15 green PRs waited. The lock had no way to tell a dead merge from a live one, so the only way out was a person passing `--break-lock`. A direct merge's lock now records the process holding it (machine boot, process namespace, process group, start time) and an expiry 90 minutes after its last step. The next merge refuses a lock whose merge still runs, `--break-lock` included, and takes over one whose merge is gone or that expired, printing `LOCK_TAKEOVER:`. If a merge stops while the repository's own post-merge checks run (they can outlive it), it leaves a deliberate hold on that machine, which a person releases with the command the refusal prints. Takeovers write under an exact lease on the lock they judged, so a slow takeover never replaces a newer lock. `gstack-ship-queue count` reads open PRs with one GitHub call and counts the finished ones (ours, on the base, not draft, not conflicting, green at the head). It prints a `DRAIN` line when more than 6 wait or one has waited a day. The coordinator docs (`crew/docs/captain.md#drain-the-queue`, factory.md point 16) say to run it at every wake and how to merge a backlog, and `docs/ship-policy.md` gains `#land-lock` and `#revert-drill`.
Blast radius Only `land --pin` writes these process-scoped locks; locks from the older per-PR `land` and from `train land` keep their rules, and an older lock with no process record expires 90 minutes after its last step (crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts, read and covered by crew/test/ship-queue-land-lock.test.ts). A reproduction against the stuck lock from 2026-11-22 refuses forever on main and is taken over after expiry with this change.
Why Finished PRs that sit unmerged go stale, because the base moves under them and conflicts appear. A merge lock that can go stale turns one crashed process into a stopped queue, so the lock has to clear itself, and the queue has to be counted before it piles up.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds and one owner-granted check of the second round's fixes. The second-model review found six problems in how the post-merge hold was set and judged; five were fixed in this PR and the check of those fixes found nothing blocking. The sixth is in code this PR did not change and is listed under Deferred findings. Remaining notes are below the blocking floor.
Deferred findings - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:187`: a rerun of an already-merged PR runs the post-merge checks before it reads the lock. This code predates this PR; left for a follow-up.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:277`: no land-direct test drives the post-merge hold end to end. - `crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts:84`: a rerun wrapped in a command substitution from the dead merge's own script now reads its wrapper as a running merge and refuses (the safe direction). - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:142`: when the post-merge hold cannot be written, the suggested rerun takes the already-merged path, which runs the checks unheld (the deferred finding above). - `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts:195`: an already-merged rerun with `--allow-repo-commands` against a deliberate hold refuses each time without naming the release command. - `crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts:246`: `--break-lock` can still take a hold whose checks changed the checkout's git directory; only the advice changed. - `crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts:248`: releasing a deliberate hold prints the generic takeover line, not that a hold was released. - Plus earlier informational notes from round one and the in-house adversarial read, and one security note whose details are recorded privately.
Documentation **Status:** updated — one factual fix; the branch already documents its own changes. **Scope:** 4 commits from 5962f0d to d732e9c (12 files: land-lock takeover in crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts and lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts, new `gstack-ship-queue count`); no staged, unstaged or new files. **Documentation health:** - docs/troubleshooting.md — Updated (the QUEUE_LAND_LOCKED fix now covers the merge: direct automatic takeover and its three refusals) - docs/ship-policy.md — Current (land-lock and revert-drill sections added on this branch) - crew/docs/captain.md — Current (Drain the queue section and QUEUE_LAND_LOCKED row added on this branch) - capy/skill/gstack/factory.md — Current (item 16) - changelog.d/land-lock-cannot-go-stale.md — Current (not edited by policy) **Coverage debt:** `gstack-ship-queue count` has reference docs (help text, captain.md) and a how-to (Drain the queue) but no tutorial; land-lock takeover has reference and explanation docs (ship-policy.md#land-lock). No critical gaps. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: CI reuse: a neutral run no longer blocks a passing one, and workflow_call checks clear only at the exact commit (GST-3554)
body:
A newer CI run that concluded `neutral` no longer blocks reusing a passing run on the same commit, and a check that only runs inside another workflow (`workflow_call`) now clears only from a run that tested your exact commit.
Why: gbrain kept hitting `newer_run_vetoes` on passing runs (#9827, #10058, #10021), and a calling workflow's green run from any commit could clear such a check.
Nothing to do: gbrain's skipped-run case was already fixed on main by #4695; this adds `neutral`, the exact-commit rule and regression tests built from gbrain's real runs.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- A newer `neutral` run is passed over like a `skipped` one, both when a passing run is reused and when the CI wait picks the commit's result. A newer failed, cancelled, timed-out, startup-failed or unfinished run still blocks reuse.
- A check that only runs through `workflow_call` takes its caller's run only when that run was at the recorded commit, was not a pull request run (those test GitHub's merge commit, not your commit), and that commit's files match what was recorded. A run of the check's own workflow is checked as before.

title: /verify is now /build-check, so Claude Code's built-in /verify works again (#4593)
body:
gstack's build-and-check skill is renamed from `/verify` to `/build-check`, so typing `/verify` opens Claude Code's own built-in skill again and Claude Code stops running gstack's skill before every commit. Why: Claude Code ships a skill named `verify`, and gstack's skill with the same name hid it. Fixes #4593. What you do: use `/build-check` from now on. If your gstack config has `disabled_skills: verify`, change it to `build-check`. Upgrading removes gstack's old `verify` entry but never a `verify` skill of your own.
What changed - The skill folder, template and `name:` are now `build-check` on every host. `/build-check quick` keeps the check-only pass. - `verify` joins gstack's list of retired skill names. `./setup`, `gstack-relink` and `gstack-upgrade` remove gstack's own `verify` and `gstack-verify` entries and leave a user's own skill alone. An edited copy of gstack's old skill moves to the backup folder instead of being deleted. - The `verify_before_commit` setting is retired. Setting it prints a note and changes nothing, and a config file that still has it keeps working. - The prompt router, docs, the AGENTS.md skill table, tests and fixtures use the new name.
Why Since Claude Code 2.1.286, the skill name `verify` alone told the agent to run gstack's skill before each commit, and gstack's entry also hid Claude Code's built-in `/verify`. Renaming the skill fixes both problems. Garry chose the rename on #4593.
Blast radius The rename touches every host's generated skill files, the install and relink scripts, and the prompt router. Cleanup only removes entries that gstack generated or linked, and `test/retired-skills.test.ts` covers both a user's own `verify` skill and an edited gstack copy. CI's full free suite passed at this head.
Documentation **Status:** current. Every authored doc already matches the /verify to /build-check rename, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** the diff from base 00a6b7a3 to head 76bfe24 (4 commits, 43 files) plus the unstaged changelog.d/verify-is-now-build-check.md. I searched all tracked .md, .tmpl and .txt files for leftover skill names (/verify, verify_before_commit, gstack-verify, skills/verify). **Documentation health:** - AGENTS.md: Current (skill table lists /build-check) - README.md: Current (skill table row renamed) - SKILL.md.tmpl: Current (routing rule names /build-check) - build-check/SKILL.md.tmpl: Current - docs/skills.md: Current (/build-check section, rename note, verify_before_commit retirement, disabled_skills migration) - docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md: Current (examples use /build-check) - docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md: Current (build-check/ directory) - docs/state-root.md: Current - gstack/llms.txt: Current - changelog.d/verify-is-now-build-check.md: Current (the unstaged edit only splits a sentence) **Coverage debt:** none. /build-check has reference coverage (AGENTS.md, README, llms.txt) and how-to coverage (docs/skills.md). The retired verify_before_commit setting and the disabled_skills migration are both documented. **Diagram drift:** none. The tree in docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md shows build-check/.
Tests - [x] `bun run test` (the full free suite, CI run 45059936334 at 55dd73c): 1770 test files passed, 0 failed. - [x] macOS and Windows jobs at the same head passed: macos-named-regressions, cso-macos-launcher and windows-smoke.
Pre-Landing Review The first full review found a test that still named the old skill folder. It's fixed: `test/skill-descriptions.test.ts` now uses `build-check`. A second-model review then found that cleanup could delete a user's edited copy of the old skill. That's fixed too: the copy now moves to the backup folder, and a new test covers it. A read-only full review of that fix left three open notes, each with a recorded reason: - Two upgrades of separate installs in the same second could pick the same backup path. This already happens on main, and a follow-up PR makes the backup path unique per run. - A `disabled_skills: verify` entry no longer turns off `build-check`. It switches the skill back on and loses no data. The release note tells users to change the entry, and the follow-up PR maps the old name automatically. - `/build-check quick` runs the skill's startup line before it skips the full pass. This line is identical on main. The last commit only adds comments to `test/retired-skills.test.ts`, marking test inputs that a release check had misread as stale. A scoped check of that commit found nothing.

title: After a pull request's second review round, an approved extra check now leads to a /ship sign-off (GST-3546)
body:
After a pull request's two review rounds, an approved extra check of the fixes now ends in a /ship sign-off instead of a dead end. Why: three projects (gbrain #10068, gskills #23–#25, gstack #4712) had no way to finish after a ruling at the round limit and skipped the sign-off or bent their records. Nothing to do: the next /ship uses it.
What changed - **One kind of approval.** The review planner, `gstack-ship-receipt claim` and `write` now accept both ways of recording the approval for one more scoped check after the round limit. - **A ruling at the limit can finish.** The approval no longer needs a stop record, so an edit made after review (such as a docs-audit edit) can get one, and a clean scoped check closes the open blockers it was asked to read. A blocker nothing covers still refuses. - **A malformed check no longer uses up the approval.** A check row that didn't finish or doesn't match the diff is ignored, so the run can log a correct one. A check that found issues still uses it, so the approval buys one round of fixes, as before. gstack now builds the diff the checker reads, from the approved commit to HEAD. - **Long reasons fit.** A reason longer than the 300-character limit is shortened in the summary, with the full words kept. - **Finished runs stop blocking upgrades.** A /ship run that finished, was abandoned, or whose process is gone no longer holds gstack upgrades on that machine. A stopped run still holds them, since it may resume. - Docs: `docs/review-policy.md#one-grant-path` and `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
Tests New `test/round-cap-ruling-path.test.ts` has 13 cases, one per reported failure plus the review findings. Run against main at 2ab2aad, all 9 original cases that can load there fail; the upgrade-hold cases need the new module. Each review fix added a case that fails on the code before it (3 of 3 after round 1, 3 of 3 after the extra check). Focused suites at the final code: 118 tests pass. CI's full free run at 2b11ffa passed.
Approvals ## Approvals Approved: yes (record r-23f8f6209764). The full approval record stays private. Plan: exempt: bug fix (GST-3546); bug fixes need no plan approval (R4) Plan check: exempt bug fix
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-run-record.ts:62` thisRunOwner now returns null when the ancestor walk reaches a wrapper process (a shell or similar) whose parent is init (ppid<=1). Before this change it returned that orphaned wrapper as the owner. With no owner, ownerGone cannot prove the run ended, so the run keeps holding gstack upgrades and aba - INFORMATIONAL `sf-784e06c66d90` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `sf-d5ee1d766831` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-approvals:255` (targeted reader): the add guard's spelling gap, fixed in the extra check by matching any `review_loop_grant` mention. - INFORMATIONAL `test/round-cap-ruling-path.test.ts` (second-model review): the add guard's refusal had no negative test; the extra check added the spellings. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-release.ts:308` (second-model review): after a spent grant, release's fix-check chain and receipt clearing can print different lines; the receipt still refuses. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/ship-run-live.ts:37` (second-model review): a budget ledger rebuilt by `resume --rebuild-from-record` keeps holding upgrades until it closes or ages out (fails safe). - INFORMATIONAL `lib/fix-check-clearing.ts:107` (targeted reader on the final head): a legacy `review_loop_grant` row that an older run already spent through `gstack-review-plan --grant` (which wrote no claim) could be claimed again by a later run; a follow-up should check `grantSpent` at claim for legacy rows.
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual fix, no blockers. Scope: base 2ab2aad7 to head 06ccb4b (3 commits, 23 files; nothing staged, unstaged or new). The branch's own docs (review-policy.md #one-grant-path, troubleshooting.md, the changelog.d fragment) were checked against the code and are accurate. Documentation health: - docs/review-policy.md: Current (the new one-grant-path section matches the code) - docs/troubleshooting.md: Current (UPGRADE_BUSY, STOP_UNBOUND, abandon, GRANT_SPENT and GRANT_UNKNOWN updated in the branch) - docs/ship-policy.md: Updated (#what-ends-a-run now says abandon takes a run at any age once its harness process is provably gone) Coverage debt: `gstack-ship-run live` has reference-only coverage (its --help text and troubleshooting.md). No critical gaps. No diagram drift.
Agent notes Lane GSTA-815 for GStack Minder (GSTA-36). Grant kinds unified in `lib/review-round-grant.ts` (legacy `review_loop_grant ` rows parse as fix-check grants with pr 0); `clearByGrant` answers a no-stop grant through this run's claim and reads only the first counted row (a counted read that found issues spends the grant); `gstack-approvals add` refuses a self-recorded `review_loop_grant` row inside an open /ship run unless it carries `--owner-ref` and `--words`; `grantSpent` counts only counted rows; `claimedFixCheckHunks` builds the fix-check packet; `lib/ship-run-live.ts` plus `gstack-ship-run live` replace the Capy installer's file-age-only open-run check; `abandonRefusal` skips the 60-minute wait when the owner is provably gone. title: gstack-approvals rule: a refused --owner-ref does not say which check failed or what the thread code must look like, and its fix line names `add`'s flags
body:
## What happened

During /ship, the owner ruled a review finding a disclosed note, so I recorded the ruling with `gstack-approvals rule ... --owner-ref <ref>` (an open /ship run on the checkout requires `--owner-ref`). The first two refs I tried were refused, and the third was accepted:

- `ship-D1:2026-11-22T18:40:00Z`: refused
- `SHIPD1:2026-11-22T18:41:00Z`: refused
- `SHIP-161:2026-11-22T18:42:14Z`: accepted

Each refusal printed the same line (reproduced below with synthetic values in a throwaway repo, exit 2):

```text
gstack-approvals rule: an approval row is missing a required field, holds a value outside its enum, or exceeds a length cap (--owner-ref relays the owner's ruling: <thread code>:<message id or timestamp> (GSTA-36:2026-11-19T12:29:59Z), with --by <the owner> and --words <their exact words>); fix: rerun gstack-approvals add with every required flag (--ask, --words, --scope, --by) inside the caps it names; nothing was written (APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID)
```

Three things make this hard to act on:

1. The thread code has to match `OWNER_REF = /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[1-9]\d*:[A-Za-z0-9][\w.:+-]*$/` (`lib/ruled-notes.ts:32`): an uppercase prefix, a dash, and a number from 1 up. The message only shows one example, `GSTA-36:…`. `--help` (`bin/gstack-approvals:46`, `:64`) and `docs/ship-policy.md:1847` only say `<thread code>:<message id or timestamp>`, and the `approval-record-invalid` entry in `docs/troubleshooting.md` does not mention `--owner-ref`. None of them states the shape, so a lowercase or dash-less code fails with no hint why. The shape matches a Capy thread code, so the pattern looks deliberate; `gstack-archive-check` already says so for its own `--thread` ("a thread code such as GSTA-462", `bin/gstack-archive-check:51`).
2. One message covers three different checks (`bin/gstack-approvals:219`): a ref that does not match `OWNER_REF`, a missing `--words`, and a missing `--by`. Whichever one failed, the output is the same.
3. The `fix:` part comes from the result-code table (`lib/result-codes-capy.ts:16`). It says "rerun gstack-approvals add with every required flag (--ask, --words, --scope, --by)", but `rule` takes `--finding`, `--head`, `--reason`, `--words` and `--by`, so the fix line points at a different subcommand. Every `APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID` refusal of `round-grant` (`bin/gstack-approvals:178`–`196`), `lane-exception` (`:197`–`209`), `rule` (`:210`–`226`) and `gate` (from `:227`) goes through the same `fail()` (`:116`–`117`), so each prints that one `fix:` line naming `add`'s flags.

Expected: the refusal names the check that failed, and for `--owner-ref` it states the accepted shape (for example "the thread code is uppercase letters or digits after a leading letter, a dash, then a number from 1, e.g. GSTA-36"). The `fix:` line names the subcommand that was run and its own flags. I am not asking to loosen `OWNER_REF`; only to say what it requires and which check failed.

Checked against `main` at 20ab591412c27a76ef0e037b431aadd00baa7252. The installed version is 1.102.2.0. Related: #4541 (another `APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID` refusal of `round-grant`, closed). It is a different cause, and I found no open issue on this message.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `git init -q /tmp/r && cd /tmp/r && git commit -q --allow-empty -m init`
2. `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-approvals rule --finding a.txt:1:docs --head HEAD --reason synthetic --words A --by owner --owner-ref ship-161:2026-11-22T18:40:00Z`
3. Exit 2 with the line above. `--owner-ref SHIP-161:2026-11-22T18:40:00Z` passes the same check.

title: A disabled_skills verify entry keeps /build-check off, and gstack stops claiming verify prompts (#4593)
body:
A `disabled_skills: verify` entry now turns off `/build-check`, and gstack's router and skill description no longer claim prompts that say "verify my change". Why: this finishes the #4593 rename, so Claude Code's built-in `/verify` gets those prompts and an old opt-out keeps working. What you do: nothing.
What changed - setup, `gstack-relink`, the install code and `gstack-config set` read a `verify` entry in `disabled_skills` as `build-check`. The retired-skills list keeps the old name, so `build-check` stays on when nothing disables it. - `/build-check`'s trigger list and the prompt router drop "verify my change" and add no replacement trigger. - Each setup or relink run that moves an edited skill file aside gets its own backup folder (`mktemp -d`), so two runs in the same second can't overwrite each other's backups. - docs/skills.md says a `disabled_skills: verify` entry now turns off `build-check`.
Why #4714 renamed the skill and shipped with three open notes. This PR fixes two of them, the disabled_skills mapping and the shared backup folder. It also removes the trigger wording that still pulled "verify" prompts toward gstack.
Blast radius The change touches the install scripts, `gstack-config` and the router text. The rename map applies only to a user's own `disabled_skills` value, so the retired `verify` name never turns off `build-check` by itself, and `test/retired-skills.test.ts` covers both cases plus the same-second backups. CI's full free suite ran at this head.
Documentation **Status:** updated. One stale factual line was corrected; there are no blockers. **Scope:** 16 committed files from 9d758432 to e7960384 (the router template, the build-check skill template, gstack-config, the install registry, relink, setup, discover/modules-install scripts, harness-register and 3 test files), plus the docs that mention disabled_skills or /verify. **Documentation health** | File | Status | |---|---| | docs/skills.md | Updated: the /build-check section now says a `disabled_skills` entry of `verify` is read as `build-check` | | docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md | Current: the branch already updated the --explain example | | docs/troubleshooting.md | Current | | docs/loadouts.md | Current | | README.md | Current | | SKILL.md.tmpl / build-check/SKILL.md.tmpl | Current: "verify my change" was removed on the branch | **Coverage debt:** the verify→build-check alias for disabled_skills now has a reference in docs/skills.md and the changelog fragment. It has no how-to coverage in the troubleshooting entry for disabled_skills, which is minor. No architecture diagrams are affected.
Tests - [x] `bun run test` (the full free suite, CI run 45066264421 at 256a1ad): 1771 test files passed, 0 failed. - [x] The macOS and Windows jobs at the same head passed: macos-named-regressions, cso-macos-launcher, windows-smoke and windows-setup.
Pre-Landing Review Two full reviews and a second-model review ran. - **Fixed in this PR:** - `gstack-config set` refused the old `verify` name. It now stores `build-check`. - `gstack-config` could exit silently when the install registry file was missing. - The new "check my change" trigger matched unrelated prompts, so it was removed with no replacement. - **Dropped:** a proposed change to the release check for stale test values, which weakened that check. It's left out of this PR. - **Open notes, each with a recorded reason:** - Turning off a skill deletes the folder gstack created for it. That's the same as on main, and keeping a user's own files there is a separate fix. - One sample output line in docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md shows an older runner-up trigger. That line predates this PR.

title: gstack-approvals says which --owner-ref check failed and stops pointing every refusal at add (#4718)
body:
`gstack-approvals rule` and `round-grant` now say which `--owner-ref` check failed and what shape the ref needs.
Why: one shared sentence covered a bad ref, a missing `--words` and a missing `--by`, and its fix line pointed at `gstack-approvals add`.
Nothing to do; refs that were accepted before are still accepted, and every refusal still exits 2.

## Root cause

In `bin/gstack-approvals`, `rule` tested the `OWNER_REF` match, a non empty `--words` and a non empty `--by` in one condition and printed one sentence for all three, and `round-grant` did the same for the ref and `--words`. Neither sentence stated the shape `OWNER_REF` in `lib/ruled-notes.ts` requires, so `ship-161:…` or `SHIPD1:…` failed with no hint why. Every `APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID` line also ends with the one `fix` clause of `lib/result-codes-capy.ts`, which named `add` and its flags (`--ask`, `--words`, `--scope`, `--by`), so `rule`, `round-grant`, `lane-exception`, `gate` and the `locate()` refusals of the read commands all sent the user to a different subcommand.

## Fix

`lib/ruled-notes.ts` exports `OWNER_REF_SHAPE`, the regex in words next to it. `rule` now runs three checks in order. A ref outside `OWNER_REF` is refused with the ref quoted and `OWNER_REF_SHAPE`, then a missing `--words` and a missing `--by` each get a line naming only that flag; `round-grant` gets the same shape check and its own `--words` check. The help states the shape through the same constant. The `fix` clause of `APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID` is now neutral. It says to rerun the command the line names with the flag its detail names, and `gstack-approvals --help` lists each command's flags. `OWNER_REF`, exit codes, the anchor, `resultLine` and `fail()` are unchanged. `docs/troubleshooting.md#approval-record-invalid` describes the two `--owner-ref` refusals, and `changelog.d/fix-issue-4718-owner-ref-refusal.md` carries the entry. Closes #4718.

## Tests

Five tests at the end of `test/approval-record.test.ts` split stderr at `; fix: ` so the refusal and the fix clause are checked apart. They cover the issue's own command (the ref is quoted, the shape is stated, neither `--words` nor `--by` is named, and `SHIP-161:…` still records), a missing `--words`, a missing `--by`, a bad `round-grant` ref, and a fix clause free of `add`, `--ask` and `--scope` on `rule`, `round-grant`, `lane-exception` and `gate`. All five failed on the old code for those reasons before the source changed.

On Windows 11 with bun 1.4.5, `test/approval-record.test.ts` gives 41 pass and 13 fail; the 13 are the same tests by name on untouched main, all using a fake `gh` shell script or symlinks. `test/troubleshooting-anchors.test.ts`, `round-cap-granted-stop`, `ship-finish-ruled-notes`, `ship-run-record`, `security-finding-redaction` and `fix-check-clearing` give the same failures by name as main, except two anchor walks that timed out at 5 seconds under load and pass when the file runs alone (423 pass, twice). `bun run typecheck` reports no error, `bun run typecheck:test` no new diagnostic, and the doc link check, the credential scan and prose lint on the added lines pass. The full free suite was not run on this Windows machine, so full validation relies on the Linux CI in `free-tests.yml`.

## Out of scope

`docs/ship-policy.md` and `docs/review-policy.md` still give the ref only as `<thread code>:<message id or timestamp>`; the refusal, the help and the troubleshooting entry now state the shape.

title: Learnings (.jsonl) are not indexed by gbrain, so they are not searchable in the brain
body:
`gstack-learnings-log` writes learnings as `.jsonl`. When the gstack artifacts are synced into a gbrain source, gbrain's sync strategy skips `.jsonl` files, so the learnings are never indexed and `search` / `query` cannot find them.

**Proposal** (any of):
- an optional markdown export of learnings (one page per learning or per day, with frontmatter `type`), written next to the `.jsonl`;
- or a note in the gbrain setup / sync skill that learnings are not searchable in the brain, so users don't assume they are.

title: A used review grant can no longer be claimed again, plus two /ship finish fixes (GST-3560)
body:
A grant for one follow-up review of a fix can no longer be claimed again once that review ran, so one grant still buys one round. /ship finish no longer calls the docs audit stale for a file a clean follow-up review read, and the CI-record timeout no longer counts local test runs. Nothing to do: the merge checks only get stricter, and the timeout setting keeps its name and default.
What changed - `gstack-ship-receipt claim` reads the review log before it writes a claim. For a grant for a follow-up review, if a counted follow-up review already read under that grant (a row that names the grant, or an unstamped row logged after the grant was recorded), claim refuses with `GRANT_SPENT`. A row stamped with a different grant never spends this one. This closes the gap where a read planned through `gstack-review-plan --grant` left no claim in the PR body, so the same grant (an owner's `review_loop_grant` row or a round grant) could be claimed for a second read. A run that already holds the claim can still claim again, and a malformed row still spends nothing. - `gstack-ship-release finish`: a path the follow-up review read, and that is byte-identical since that review, no longer stales the Step 14.5 docs audit. `DOCS: fresh` lists it as `fix_checked=`. Before, `DOCS: stale ()` stopped finish after a clean follow-up review at the current head, and no documented recovery applied. - `ci_record_timeout_s` now bounds only finding and verifying the CI run. `record-ci` prints `CI_RECORD_PHASE: local` before it runs CI-skipped files or an exception preflight here, and from that marker the caller allows up to an hour more. Before, harness-evals #538's 445 remainder tests took about 880 s against a 900 s bound. A failure to start `record-ci` still returns `record_failed`. - Docs: troubleshooting `GRANT_SPENT`, review-policy (claim, and the docs check for reviewed paths), ship-policy and the merge-check reference page on `ci_record_timeout_s`, and a changelog fragment.
Tests Each fix has a test that fails on main and passes here: `test/round-cap-ruling-path.test.ts` (claim refuses a spent legacy grant and a spent round grant; negative controls for an unspent grant, a row stamped with another grant, a malformed row and a re-claim by the same run), `test/ship-finish-fixed-links.test.ts` (a path the follow-up review read counts as reviewed; an unread or later-changed path still refuses), and `test/ship-record-ci-reuse.test.ts` (local runs past the bound still count the CI run; a CI phase past the bound stops and runs nothing here). Focused run: 18 files, 466 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` and `typecheck:test` clean. CI is the full run.

title: The stale-test-value check matches tests by resolved import, not file name (GST-3563)
body:
The check that flags tests still holding a changed constant's old value now matches tests by the import that resolves to the changed file, not by file name. Why: when two files share a name (two `config.ts`), it flagged tests of the wrong file and a JSON golden nobody could waive, and a list that only gained an item flagged every test still naming the kept item. What you do: nothing.
What changed gbrain changed `DEFAULT_SESSION_TOKEN_BUDGET` from 2000 to 8000 in `src/core/skills/resolver/config.ts`, and the check flagged 17 tests that import the other `src/core/config.ts` and contain an unrelated `2000` (`since: '2000-01-01'`, `lockWaitMs: 2000`). It also flagged an exports golden where `"2000"` belongs to `LONG_PAGE_DEADLINE_MS`, and JSON can't hold a waiver comment. Separately, when `GSTACK_RETIRED_SKILLS` went from `"investigate"` to `"investigate verify"`, every test line that creates an `investigate` folder needed a waiver (13 of them, in #4714). Now: - **Same-named files.** When another file in the repository has the changed file's name, a test counts only if one of its imports or paths resolves to the changed file. That covers relative imports, tsconfig/jsconfig `paths` and `baseUrl`, quoted repository paths and `join()` segments, through the same resolver that picks which tests a change runs. An alias import also counts when the name is unique. Run as text over gbrain's main (5f989a1e) for that change, the old rule flags 17 files by file name alone (16 unrelated, plus `test/skill-resolver.test.ts`, matched only through an unrelated `'../config'` string); the new rule flags none. - **JSON files.** An old value counts only where the JSON ties it to the constant: the value of a key with the constant's name, or anything inside a record whose string value is the name (`{ "name": "LIMIT_MS", "signature": ["2000"] }`). A golden that pins the changed constant still fails. A JSON file that doesn't parse counts only on lines that name the constant. Call-site names (`timeout`, `limit`) still need the module named in the file, as they do for other files. - **A one-item list that only gained items.** Lines that use the kept item (paths, fixtures, `toContain`) no longer count. A line still counts when it asserts the whole old value: `toBe`/`toEqual`/`===`, an assert call, an assignment, or a statement using the constant or a binding from it, such as an alias `modes`. Multi-item lists and prose keep the old rule. The 13 waivers in `test/retired-skills.test.ts` are gone. **What this does not catch:** a test that reaches the constant only through another module (a barrel or a caller), without naming the constant, isn't flagged. Such a stale value now shows up only when that test runs in CI, not as an early warning from this check. gbrain's one real consumer is like this: `test/skill-resolver.test.ts` imports `resolver/index.ts`, and the old check found it only through an unrelated `'../config'` string. Following every import transitively instead would make 6,606 gbrain files (6,284 of them tests) depend on that one config file.
Blast radius Only the stale-value check in `lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts` changes; `pathAliasResolver` is now exported from `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts` and otherwise unchanged. When no other file shares the module's name and no alias is configured, matching for code and shell tests is the same as on main (JSON files and grown one-item lists follow the new rules above), and the existing 25 literals tests in `test/pregate-selection.test.ts` pass unchanged (CI run 45082536135).
Test Coverage New `test/pregate-literals-consumers.test.ts` (4 tests) fails at main and passes here: two `config.ts` files with a test of each (only the real consumer flagged, through a relative import, a `@/` alias and an exact alias), JSON goldens (tied, keyed, unrelated, sibling, unparseable, and a call-site key without the module), and the grown list (member uses, membership checks, whole-value assertions, alias and derived bindings, prose and multi-item lists). Negative control: putting `toBe('investigate')` back into `test/retired-skills.test.ts` is flagged again at line 27. Coverage audit: 9 of 12 paths at first; two of the three gaps (unparseable JSON, unique-name alias) got tests in the review fix. The third is that no test drives `run()` itself with a twin.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds plus a second-model review. - **Fixed in this PR:** JSON files had dropped the module requirement for call-site names, so an unrelated fixture with `"attempts": 3` would have failed the check with no way to waive it. A folder sharing the module's name (`config/README.md`) no longer counts as a same-named file. - **Open notes, ruled to ship as notes:** a JSON golden that never names its source module isn't flagged when a call-site value changes (same as main). A same-named folder module (`src/x/config/index.ts`) isn't treated as a same-named file, so its importers can still be flagged by name (same as main, waivable; a one-line follow-up can add it).
Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already describe the new stale-test-value check behavior, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** the diff from 50cc2967 to 61bf71f8 (3 commits, 7 files), plus staged, unstaged and new files (none). I read docs/pregate.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and the changelog.d fragment in full against lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts and lib/pregate/import-graph.ts. **Documentation health:** - docs/pregate.md: current. It explains how name twins are resolved through imports, aliases and paths, how JSON values tied to a constant count, and how a one-item list that only gained items is handled. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. The PREGATE_LITERALS fix text explains that a JSON file cannot hold a waiver marker. - changelog.d/stale-test-value-check-resolves-imports.md: current (reviewed, not edited). **Coverage debt:** the PREGATE_LITERALS behavior has reference coverage in pregate.md and how-to coverage in troubleshooting.md, which is enough for an internal check. There are no gaps to fill. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: The merge queue's bisect accepts a red judge case whose name holds a space (#3580)
body:
`gstack-ship-queue train bisect` now bisects a red judge case whose name holds a space, such as `setup-browser-cookies/SKILL.md workflow`.
Why: bisect refused that case as outside the gate's plan, though the gate's panels held it and the CI route accepts the same id.
Nothing to do; ids bisect accepted before are still accepted.

## Root cause

`bisectInputs()` in `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-verdict.ts` checked each red case against `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,128}$`, which has no space. A judge case id is `<skill>/SKILL.md workflow`, so the check failed before the panel lookup and bisect stopped with `QUEUE_TRAIN_PREFIX_INVALID`. The two other checks of the same ids already allowed the space: `CASE_ID` in `crew/lib/release-gate.ts` (release bisect) and in `crew/scripts/train-gate.ts` (the route `evals.yml` runs, which splits the `cases` input on commas only, so a space survives and the comma the pattern leaves out stays the separator).

## Fix

`CASE_ID` is now defined once, in `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-record.ts`, which the verdict and the release gate already import and whose types the CI route already reads; the record module imports none of the three, so no cycle appears. The red case check moves into an exported pure function, `redCasesOutsidePlan()`, which uses `CASE_ID` and keeps the same message; `bisectInputs()` calls it. The release gate and the CI route drop their copies and import the shared one. No message, exit code or accepted id outside the space changes. `changelog.d/fix-issue-3580-bisect-case-id-space.md` carries the entry. Closes #3580.

## Tests

Three pure tests in `crew/test/ship-queue-train-logic.test.ts` call `redCasesOutsidePlan()` directly. They accept a red judge panel whose id holds a space, refuse ids the dispatch input cannot pass even when a panel holds them (empty, a comma, a newline, 129 characters), and refuse a red id no panel holds. After the extraction and before the pattern changed, only the space test failed, with the refusal from the issue; the file now gives 26 pass.

On Windows 11 with bun 1.4.5, `crew/test/train-gate.test.ts`, `crew/test/release-gate.test.ts` and `crew/test/ship-queue-train-bisect.test.ts` fail 21 tests on this branch, all of them among the 23 that fail on untouched main; they come from the fixtures' `#!/bin/sh` fake `gh` and their git pushes, which do not run on Windows. The shell integration tests in those files therefore rely on the Linux CI in `free-tests.yml`. `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts`, `test/crew-move-layout.test.ts` and `test/evals-train-workflow.test.ts` pass, `bun run typecheck` reports no error, `bun run typecheck:test` no new diagnostic, and the doc link check, the credential scan and prose lint pass.

## Out of scope

The CI route trims each case it splits from the input, so an id that starts or ends with a space would not match its panel there; no gate case is named that way today. A bisect integration test with a judge case red would need a judge panel in the shared merge queue fixture, so this PR keeps the regression at the pure function.

title: gstack-post holds the PR body on the receipt's own run id in the gstack-receipt-runs fence (pii.phone.e164)
body:
## What happened

`/ship` Step 19 composes the PR body, runs `gstack-ship-receipt write --pr <n> ... --body <file>`, then reposts it with `gstack-post pr-body <n> --body-file <file>`. The repost stopped with exit 2 and `RULE: pii.phone.e164` on a line of the tool-written receipt. The only route the message offers is to ask the user to `--confirm`.

The match is the ship run id (`<pid>-<epoch>-<hex>`, e.g. `3454314-1795338725-c32255b8`). Its epoch part is a 10-digit Unix timestamp, which reads as a phone number. The receipt writes that run id twice:

- inside the ```` ```gstack-ship-receipt ```` JSON block (`"run": "..."`). `gstack-post` no longer flags this one, presumably since #4198.
- inside the ```` ```gstack-receipt-runs ```` one-line JSON block (`{"head":...,"run":"...",...}`). `gstack-post` still flags this one.

Plain `gstack-redact --from-file` flags both, at the `"run"` value. So the exemption covers the first fence but not the second, and every `/ship` that writes a receipt into a PR body hits a false MEDIUM hold. #4221 is the same symptom for the `SHIP_RECEIPT:` summary line's `ci_carried=` ids. This is the receipt's own `run` field in its second fence.

This is a false hold, not a leak: the value is machine-written by gstack and contains no personal data. It happened on a private repo, gstack 1.102.2.0.

A possible fix is to give the `gstack-receipt-runs` fence the same treatment as the `gstack-ship-receipt` fence, or to recognise the exact `"run":"<digits>-<10 digits>-<hex>"` shape in either fence. A phone number anywhere else in the body would still report.

## Steps to reproduce

In a scratch git repo whose `origin` is an unreachable GitHub URL, with synthetic values:

1. Write `body.md`:
   ````text
   Body.

   ```gstack-receipt-runs
   {"head":"abc123abc123abc123abc123abc123abc123abcd","version":"1.0.0.0","run":"4242424-1700000000-deadbeef"}
   ```
   ````
2. Run `gstack-post pr-comment 1 --repo-visibility private --body-file body.md`.

Result, exit 2:

```text
RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 4 PART: body
gstack-post: MEDIUM findings; nothing was posted. Ask the user about each finding; to post these exact bytes, rerun with --confirm <token>. Any edit needs a new scan.
```

Expected: the scan passes, and the post then fails at `gh` on the unreachable remote.

title: A version bump can no longer rename or reorder released CHANGELOG sections (#3588)
body:
A CHANGELOG change that renames, swaps or re-heads a released section no longer passes as part of a version bump when gstack compares a tested commit with its bumped successor.
Why: such a change hid an edit to published history inside the bump, so test results could be reused for a tree whose CHANGELOG rewrote a release.
Nothing to do; a normal bump, which moves the branch's own entry to the top under the new version, is accepted as before.

## Root cause

`classifyFile()` in `lib/tree-receipt.ts` accepted a CHANGELOG change as a version bump whenever `normalizeChangelog(foldIntoUnreleased(before, folded))` equalled `normalizeChangelog(after)`. `normalizeChangelog()` in `lib/changelog-check.ts` replaces every section heading with `## <version>` and sorts the sections, so a renamed release heading, two swapped releases and a release moved to the top under the new version all compared equal to a real bump. The only change a bump makes is the one `reheadChangelog()` writes. It moves the `[Unreleased]` section, or the branch's own top section when there is none, to the top under the new heading with its text unchanged, and leaves every other section as it was.

## Fix

`lib/changelog-check.ts` exports a pure `reheadOnly(before, after)`. It returns null when the header above the first section is unchanged, the moved section (`[Unreleased]` when there is one, else the top section, the one `reheadChangelog` takes) keeps its text under `after`'s top heading, and every other section, headings included, is equal line for line and in the same order; trailing empty lines are ignored, as `reheadChangelog` trims them. Otherwise it returns a reason that names the heading, which was renamed (old and new heading), moved, removed, added or edited, or a top section that is not the moved one re-headed. `classifyFile()` keeps the normalized comparison and, on the path without folded fragments (rule `changelog-heading`), also requires `reheadOnly(before, after) === null`; a refusal comes back `changed` with rule `changelog` and that reason.

`reheadOnly` does not run when changelog fragments are folded (rule `changelog-fragments`). On that path the release check (`classifyRelease` in `lib/release-stamp.ts`) and the merge queue's version check (`stampMismatch` in `crew/lib/ship-queue-train-stamp.ts`) already compare the released sections and name the rewritten release. The first commit ran `reheadOnly` there too, so those refusals came earlier with a vaguer message, and the refused CHANGELOG also marked the deleted fragments as not folded; the second commit limits it to the plain re-heading the issue names. `normalizeChangelog()` is unchanged, because `crew/scripts/train-gate.ts` and the version bump tools use it for other comparisons. The CHANGELOG clause of `docs/ship-policy.md` now states the rule, and `changelog.d/fix-issue-3588-changelog-restamp-headers.md` holds the entry. Closes #3588.

## Tests

Five tests at the end of `test/tree-receipt-stamp-sensitive.test.ts` call `classifyFile()` on a temporary two commit git repository, without the shell based fixture. A `reheadChangelog` of `[Unreleased]` to the new version and a second bump of the branch's own section are still accepted with rule `changelog-heading`. A renamed released heading, two swapped released sections, and a released section moved to the top under the new version with `[Unreleased]` left below come back `changed`, and each reason names the heading. The three refusal tests failed on the old code, which accepted all three with rule `changelog-heading`.

Linux CI on the first commit failed two tests on the fragment path, `crew/test/ship-queue-train-stamp.test.ts` "a tampered earlier version or a product change in S_i is refused" and `test/release-stamp.test.ts` "refuse a release head where two released sections swap their entries", which expect those checks' own messages. Both failed the same way on Windows before the second commit and pass after it; the two files give 29 of 29, as on main.

On Windows 11 with bun 1.4.5, the three `test/tree-receipt-*.test.ts` files, `test/gstack-restamp-queue.test.ts` and `test/gstack-version-bump.test.ts` fail the same tests here as on main, apart from runs that hit the 5 second limit, which changes from run to run on this machine. With `--timeout 60000`, `test/tree-receipt-release-tool.test.ts` and `test/gstack-restamp-queue.test.ts` give the same 31 pass and 6 fail by name on this branch and on main. Those remaining failures come from the fixtures' `#!/bin/sh` fake `gh` and their bins, so the shell fixture integration tests rely on the Linux CI in `free-tests.yml`. `test/changelog-fragments.test.ts`, `test/changelog-merge-damage.test.ts`, `test/pregate-remote-stamp-only.test.ts`, `test/restamp-foreign-version.test.ts` and `test/stamp-templates.test.ts` pass (34 of 34), including the fragment fold that must still be accepted. `bun run typecheck` reports no error, `bun run typecheck:test` no new diagnostic, `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts` passes, and the doc link check, the credential scan and prose lint pass.

## Out of scope

A fragment fold compared outside those two checks keeps the normalized comparison, which accepts the same entries in any order. `normalizeChangelog()` still blanks headings for its other callers, and this check does not compare the moved section's new heading with the version file, which the version file rule and the merge queue's own checks cover.

title: land: hand worktree removal to the owning session after a PR lands (no worktree GC today; 516 worktrees accumulated)
body:
## Problem

In a repo where many agent sessions each work in their own linked worktree (one worktree per task or PR), nothing in gstack ever removes a worktree after its PR lands. `/land-and-deploy` and `gstack-ship-queue land` merge the PR, but the lane's worktree stays registered and on disk.

Measured on one Windows host: **516 registered worktrees** had piled up. A manual pass (snapshot each tree, archive its non-regenerable ignored files, then `git worktree remove`) cleared 273 of them. Every local cleanup we had was a dry-run report, a manual script or an unregistered hook, so none of them ever removed anything. gstack, gbrain and gbrain-evals docs contain no worktree lifecycle or GC step.

## Proposal

Tie cleanup to the event that proves the work is finished: a landed PR.

1. After `land` confirms the PR is `MERGED` and the landed tree is verified, `land` marks the lane's worktree as **releasable**. It writes a small record: path, branch, head SHA, PR, merge SHA.
2. The **session that owns the worktree** removes it with a plain `git worktree remove`, never `--force`, once it has released the tree. That happens at session end, or on its next start when it sees the record. The coordinator never deletes another session's checkout, because work can continue in a tree after a merge.
3. If the tree is dirty, nothing is removed. The record says why, so a person or a periodic sweep can handle it.

A periodic sweep would still be needed for abandoned and unfinished trees. That part needs stricter rules:
- skip locked trees, trees with recent activity and trees with live processes;
- skip trees containing nested repos, symlinks or junctions;
- before any `--force`, take a full snapshot (not a partial one) and archive the ignored files;
- cap the number of removals per run.

Most of the sprawl, though, is trees whose PR already landed, and the land hand-off above removes those.

## Pitfalls seen in practice

- In squash-merge repos, a merged branch whose remote head was deleted looks like it has unpushed commits by ancestry. The merged PR's head SHA has to be the test.
- On Windows, Git for Windows unlinks symlinked shared directories (`node_modules`, `.next`, `.venv`) rather than following them, which is the behaviour you want. A Linux venv symlink created from WSL makes `git worktree remove` fail with "Function not implemented" and leaves a half-deleted tree.
- Copied `.env` files that differ from the main checkout's mean the tree has to be kept. Compare them byte for byte; never read them.

Happy to test a prototype on the Windows multi-worktree setup.
