title: A green CI run now counts for your branch when only main moved under it (GST-3567)
body:
/ship's final CI check (`gstack-ship-release accept`) now accepts a green pull request run that tested your branch merged onto a newer main, when main changed none of your lines.
Why: before, it refused that run and you had to merge main and rerun CI, which never settles on a busy repo (harness-evals #576, gstack #4722).
Nothing to do. Repos with a land step still re-check the merged tree; repos with `land: null` get no merged-tree check.

## What changed

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- `onlyBaseMoved` in `lib/pregate/run-check.ts` counts a pull request run for your head when GitHub's merge commit is a commit on main plus your pushed head, and your own added and removed lines in that merge are byte-identical to your head's at the same places. It uses `ownLinesSame`, the rule a base-only merge of a reviewed head already meets. Main may change other files, or other parts of your files, but none of your lines and none next to one.
- When that merge used a main commit newer than your checkout's `origin/main`, the check fetches main once before it refuses.
- Every check that reuses a CI run for a test command uses it: `accept`, `gstack-evidence record-ci`, `gstack-ci-carry`, and `gstack-pregate`'s own reuse, `--from-run` and `clear --run`. Land's merged-tree CI (`lib/land-merged-ci.ts`) never does.
- The accepted line adds `base_moved=<main commit>`. A refusal keeps its old line and adds a `CARRY_DIAGNOSIS:` line that says why.
- Docs: docs/ship-policy.md#ci-carry-base-moved, docs/pregate.md#base-moved-carry, docs/troubleshooting.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
</details>

## Why

<details><summary>Details</summary>

GitHub tests a pull request by merging it onto main as main was when the run started. Once main moved past your fork point, that merge's tree was not your head's tree, so `accept` refused the run with `tree_mismatch`. The only way out was to merge main and run CI again, and on a busy repo main moves again before that run finishes.
</details>

## Blast radius

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Only checks that reuse a CI run change, and they now accept one more case. Landing is unchanged: a repo with a land step checks the tree that lands with `land.merged_ci`, so a change that only passed on the older merge is still caught there. A repo whose `land` is `null`, such as harness-evals, gets no merged-tree check before landing, just as before this change.
</details>

## Tests

<details><summary>Details</summary>

`test/ship-accept-base-moved.test.ts` rebuilds harness-evals #576's run 45058890128: a pull request run at the head that tested a merge with a newer main. `accept` takes the test result and its final check from that run, with nothing run locally. A main edit to another part of the branch's own file (gstack #4722's run 45089670503) still counts, and a main commit newer than the checkout's `origin/main` is fetched, then counts. These refuse: an edited merge, a main edit next to the branch's line, a merge of an earlier commit, a red run, a base commit not on main, and `verifyRun` without the opt-in, which is land's path. `test/pregate-carry-gate.test.ts` covers `clear --run`. On this PR's own final head, `bin/gstack-ci-carry find` from this branch counted pull request run 45104696756 with `base_moved=dd1b610a3a52`.
</details>

## Issues

Refs #4722

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Lane GSTA-817 for GStack Minder (GST-3567).

Documentation audit (Step 14.5, docs-a2-gsta817):

**Status:** updated. One factual fix in CONTRIBUTING.md; the branch's own docs already cover the change.

**Scope:** 12 committed files against base ccd80de8 (no staged, unstaged or new files): the rule that a green pull_request run carries when only main moved (GST-3567), `CARRY_DIAGNOSIS:` output and the `base_moved=` receipt field.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/pregate.md: current (branch adds #base-moved-carry)
- docs/ship-policy.md: current (branch adds #ci-carry-base-moved)
- docs/troubleshooting.md: current
- CONTRIBUTING.md: updated. The "Which command do I run?" CI carry row now says a branch behind main dispatches Free Tests only when `CARRY_DIAGNOSIS:` says its run does not count.
- changelog.d fragment: reviewed, not edited (owned by the parent)

**Coverage debt:** none. The new behavior has a reference (pregate.md), an explanation (ship-policy.md) and a how-to (troubleshooting.md, CONTRIBUTING.md). **Diagram drift:** none.

## Approvals

title: fix(post): stop flagging ship run ids in history blocks as phone numbers (#4725)
body:
## Why (in your own words)

When `/ship` updates a PR body that carries prior run history, `gstack-post` exempts the `<pid>-<10-digit-epoch>-<hex>` session id inside the closed `gstack-ship-receipt` block from `pii.phone.e164`, but `receiptIdSpans()` in `lib/gstack-post.ts` did not inspect the adjacent `gstack-receipt-runs` block. As a result, `gstack-post` falsely held the post with exit 2 (`RULE: pii.phone.e164`) on the tool-written `"run"` value in `gstack-receipt-runs`.

This change extends `receiptIdSpans()` to exempt only the exact column span of the top-level `"run"` value when it matches `SESSION_ID` inside a closed `gstack-receipt-runs` block whose line is canonical single-line JSON (`JSON.stringify(entry) === raw`) with a non-empty string `head`. Real phone numbers in any other field on the same line, a phone or truncated id in `"run"`, non-canonical JSON, lines missing `head`, and unclosed blocks still trigger `pii.phone.e164`.

## Live evidence

Before fix (from `test/gstack-post.test.ts` reproducing #4725):
```text
RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 4 PART: body
EXIT=2
```

After fix (running `bin/gstack-post pr-comment 1 --repo-visibility private --body-file body.md` in a scratch repo with an unreachable GitHub origin):
```text
REPO_VISIBILITY: private
gstack-post: gh failed (exit 1); nothing more was sent.
GraphQL: Could not resolve to a Repository with the name 'example/unreachable-repo'. (repository)
EXIT=3
```

Typecheck and unit tests:
```text
$ bun run typecheck
$ tsc -p tsconfig.json
$ bun run typecheck:test
test typecheck ratchet: 812 known diagnostics, none new.
$ bun test test/gstack-post.test.ts test/ship-receipt-runs.test.ts test/pr-review-history.test.ts
 85 pass
 0 fail
 637 expect() calls
```

## Scope

- **Changed:** `lib/gstack-post.ts` (handle closed `gstack-receipt-runs` blocks in `receiptIdSpans`), `test/gstack-post.test.ts` (positive and negative regression tests for `gstack-receipt-runs` session ids).
- **Verified live by:** Reproducing the exact #4725 `gstack-post pr-comment` CLI scenario in a scratch git repo and running `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:test`, and 85 tests across `test/gstack-post.test.ts`, `test/ship-receipt-runs.test.ts`, and `test/pr-review-history.test.ts`.
- **Did NOT test:** Live `gh` write against a real GitHub PR (verified up to the `gh` invocation boundary).

## Checklist

- [ ] Liveness screenshot attached (`GSTACK PR` typed live into a real surface) or PR author is @garrytan (owner exemption)
- [x] This is not a generated-file-only diff (I edited the source/template and regenerated)
- [x] No ETHOS.md edits, and no changes to voice / founder perspective / YC references
- [x] New public command / external service / host adapter has an accepted issue linked (or N/A)
- [x] Linked issue or reproduction: Fixes #4725

title: /plan-ceo-review explains its mode recommendation by what that mode does that the closest other mode wouldn't (GST-3536)
body:
`/plan-ceo-review` now explains its review-mode recommendation by naming a fact from your plan and what the recommended mode does with it that the closest other mode wouldn't, instead of by the plan's category. Why: category-only reasons ("the plan fits no clear category") scored 3 of 5 on the recommendation-substance check, so the AskUserQuestion format eval failed about 3 runs in 10 and could block release cuts. Nothing to do.
What changed and the measurement - `plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl` § 0E step 2 (and the generated SKILL.md): the `because` clause must name a plan fact and what this mode does with it that the nearest other mode would not, and never rests on a count or category alone. The "categories overlap or are unclear" rule no longer says "explain why", which is what produced category-led reasons. The skill ends up 27 bytes smaller than before (61,119 bytes, under the 61,146-byte size cap). - Measurement, 10 trials each of the auq-format-gate eval (Claude Code 2.1.292, the repo's default eval model and judge), with the repo's single-case measurement runner: - main at ccd80de: 7/10 pass. Substance scores 4,4,4,4,4,4,4 and 3,3,3 (the three 3s are category-led reasons such as "lists no files and isn't clearly a new feature"). Recommended mode: 7 HOLD SCOPE, 3 SELECTIVE EXPANSION. - this branch: 10/10 pass, which meets the 9-of-10 bar. Substance scores 5 in 8 trials and 4 in 2. Recommended mode: 5 HOLD SCOPE, 5 SELECTIVE EXPANSION. - The mode mix moved from 7/3 to 5/5. With 10 trials per side, that's within chance (Fisher's exact test, two-sided p ≈ 0.65), but it's the one thing to watch: the change is meant to affect how the pick is explained, not which mode gets picked.
Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation changes were needed for this release. **Scope:** 3 commits since ccd80de8 changed 4 files: `plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl`, the generated `plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md`, the changelog fragment and `test/skill-ceo-section-ordering.test.ts`. The working tree was clean. I searched every tracked Markdown file and template for the mode-recommendation wording and for HOLD SCOPE. **Documentation health:** - `docs/skills.md`: Current. The four-modes description doesn't describe how the recommendation is justified. - `README.md`: Current. The skill table row is unaffected. - `plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl`: Current. It holds the changed rule, and the generated SKILL.md matches it. **Coverage debt:** The rule that the because clause must name a plan fact and what the chosen mode does that the nearest other mode wouldn't is documented only in the skill itself, so it has reference coverage only. That's a minor, internal detail and needs no new page. **Diagram drift:** None. No diagrams reference this behavior.
Agent notes ## Approvals No approvals recorded for branch plan-ceo-review-recommendation-names-the-tradeoff. Plan: exempt: bug fix (R65) Plan check: exempt bug fix Review: one full round (code class, light depth): the batched specialist (testing, security, state machines, red team) found nothing; the native adversarial reader raised two notes below the floor. (1) Medium, Blocks: no: the changelog's "7 of 10 before" was credited to the substance check without per-trial proof. title: Release check's docs-audit tests accept /ship's step for a stopped docs audit (GST-3569)
body:
The release check's three ship doc-sync tests pass again when the model follows /ship's instruction for a docs audit that stopped before its snapshot. Why: these tests have held the stable release since main 5962f0d4; the test fixture left out the `--run` record /ship always passes, and its command checker didn't know the new snapshot flag. Nothing to do: test-harness change only; product code is unchanged.
What changed The release check went red on ship-docsync-recovery, -stale-before and -stale-after, so stable couldn't move. /ship's docs steps now tell the model to record a docs audit that stopped before its post snapshot with a new snapshot flag, and every trial that followed that instruction failed inside the test fixture, not in /ship. Two fixture gaps caused it. The fixture's own audit snapshot left out `--run `, which /ship's Prepare line always passes and the new flag requires, so the model's post snapshot was refused and it stopped as blocked. And the fixture's command checker didn't know the flag, so it called the command "outside declared docs observation interface". The fixture now passes `--run` like /ship does, and the checker accepts the flag with the same private-file rule as `--pre`. A new free test replays the two commands captured from the failing release check and a real snapshot sequence.
Why A red release check blocks the stable channel, and main holds a security fix and several blockers that should already be on stable.
Blast radius Only the paid ship doc-sync fixture and its free tests. All 13 doc-sync cases share the fixture; the added `--run` puts a `run_id` in their audit records, which /ship's own Prepare already does (ship/sections/documentation.md, Prepare step 3, read). Nine paid trials of the three red cases passed at the fix, all of them using the new flag.
Test Coverage No new product code paths: the diff changes only test helpers, one new test, the Windows exclusion list and a release-note fragment. Tests: 1893 → 1894 (+1 new file). The new test's captured-command and replay checks fail on main's helpers (2 of 3 tests) and pass after the fix. Tests ran: test 1774 (files, from CI)
Pre-Landing Review No issues found. The second-model review was skipped by the review plan (code change with no numeric claims).
Exploratory QA Smoke, 2 of 2 passed: the new regression test at HEAD, and the checker's refusal controls (relative, in-repo, non-JSON, skills-folder and /etc paths, missing value, misspelled flag). No plan checks are bound.
Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped.
Eval Results Paid proof, planned before launch: 3 trials each of ship-docsync-recovery, ship-docsync-stale-before and ship-docsync-stale-after at 8f97c23, which has the same fixture bytes as this head. Result: 9 of 9 passed, about $4. Before the fix, every trial of these cases at main 17afb68 or later in the release check's bisect failed.
Review bot comments No review bot comments.
Plan Completion Plan completion audit: not run (no plan is bound to this branch and no docs/designs/ file matches).
Verification Results No Step 8.1 obligations: no plan is bound.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.

These are the docs-sync test fixtures (`test/helpers/docsync-repo.ts`, `docsync-observer.ts`, `docsync-fault-actor.ts`), a new regression test `test/docsync-stopped-audit-snapshot.test.ts`, a `KNOWN_WINDOWS_INCOMPATIBLE` entry in `scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts` and a changelog.d fragment. **Documentation health:** - AGENTS.md: current (no new commands or skills) - CLAUDE.md: current - CONTRIBUTING.md: current - README.md: current - docs/TEST_PORTFOLIO.md: current (the docs-sync row lists example tests, not every one) - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: current (the Windows-skip instructions match the new entry) - ship/sections/documentation.md.tmpl: current (it already describes `--carry-stopped`) **Coverage debt:** none, because nothing user-facing changed. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Publish the test of /ship's review panel against two plain reads (GST-3467)
body:
Adds the results of the preregistered test: on Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol, two plain reads plus /ship's second-model reviewer were not shown to catch as many planted bugs as /ship's first review pass, and they cost as much per run. /ship keeps its panel on both Claude Code and Codex. This answers the open question from the earlier /ship trial (#4680) about whether the panel's readers earn their cost. Nothing in /ship changes. Nothing to do but read docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-results.md.
What changed ![Every arm on both models: the panel led on Opus and Sol; two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer came close but missed the no-worse bar](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/d0JGU1XNdwRz-czlx5ixq5A6nsz9ol30VHuEtiuT-4M.png) Every arm on both models. The panel led on Opus and Sol, and two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer came close but missed the no-worse bar.
Before/after as text: Every arm on both models: the panel led on Opus and Sol; two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer came close but missed the no-worse bar ~~~diff --- Before · docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-results.md § Results at dd1b610 · source text (new in this change) +++ After · docs/evals/ship-panel-plain-reads-results.md § Results on this branch · source text +## Results +Every arm, on both models, 30 cases and 3 trials per case. "Caught" counts trials whose pooled findings named the planted bug under the frozen `catch.py` rule (a). "Real problems" is the secondary judge measure (Scoring). + +| Arm | Model | Reads | Caught (of 90) | Catch rate | Minus the panel (95.2%) | Cost per run | Cost per catch | Real problems found (judge, secondary) | +|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| +| `claude-opus-5-5#ship-panel` | Claude Opus 5.5 | /ship first pass (second-model reviewer on Sol) | 71 | 78.9% | reference | $1.60 | $2.03 | unscored | +| `claude-opus-5-5#no-gstack` | Claude Opus 5.5 | one plain read | 38 | 42.2% | −36.7 (−48.7 to −24.6) | $0.66 | $1.55 | unscored | +| `claude-opus-5-5#no-gstack-x2` | Claude Opus 5.5 | two plain reads | 54 | 60.0% | −18.9 (−30.7 to −7.1) | $1.30 | $2.16 | unscored | +| `claude-opus-5-5#plain-x2-voice` | Claude Opus 5.5 | two plain reads + second-model reviewer on Sol | 67 | 74.4% | −4.4 (−14.8 to +5.9) | $1.61 | $2.16 | unscored | +| `gpt-6.2-sol#ship-panel` | GPT-6.2 Sol | /ship first pass (second-model reviewer on Opus) | 58 | 64.4% | reference | $1.19 | $1.85 | unscored | +| `gpt-6.2-sol#no-gstack` | GPT-6.2 Sol | one plain read | 46 | 51.1% | −13.3 (−28.7 to +2.0) | $0.50 | $0.98 | unscored | +| `gpt-6.2-sol#no-gstack-x2` | GPT-6.2 Sol | two plain reads | 47 | 52.2% | −12.2 (−28.2 to +3.8) | $1.00 | $1.92 | unscored | +| `gpt-6.2-sol#plain-x2-voice` | GPT-6.2 Sol | two plain reads + second-model reviewer on Opus | 56 | 62.2% | −2.2 (−20.0 to +15.6) | $1.41 | $2.26 | unscored | + +Secondary contrasts, paired, no bar. The plain arms are nested, so on Opus a pooled arm never scores below the arm inside it. On Sol the network rule zeroes a whole pooled arm when any of its runs fetched GitHub, so N2 lost the one catch N1 had made in trial 3 of N3. The Sol N2 minus N1 interval therefore reflects both the second read and that rule: 2 cases gained a catch and 1 case lost one. + +| Contrast | Claude Opus 5.5 | GPT-6.2 Sol | +|---|---|---| +| second read: N2 minus N1 | +17.8 (+9.9 to +25.7) | +1.1 (−2.9 to +5.1) | +| second-model reviewer: N2V minus N2 | +14.4 (+5.9 to +23.0) | +10.0 (+1.8 to +18.2) | +| one plain read: N1 minus P | −36.7 (−48.7 to −24.6) | −13.3 (−28.7 to +2.0) | + +Sensitivity analyses for N2V minus P. The first two are preregistered; the third is not: + +| View | Claude Opus 5.5 | GPT-6.2 Sol | +|---|---|---| +| primary, all 30 cases | −4.4 (−14.8 to +5.9) | −2.2 (−20.0 to +15.6) | +| without G2, the case that keeps its instruction file (29 cases) | −4.6 (−15.3 to +6.1) | ±0.0 (−17.8 to +17.8) | +| without the panel trials flagged by the exposure audit | −5.3 (−19.6 to +9.0), 62 trials in 25 cases | +5.1 (−14.8 to +25.0), 64 trials in 26 cases | +| unplanned: GitHub fetches not zeroed | unchanged (Opus fetched nothing) | +11.1 (−1.4 to +23.6) | + +Inside the panel (G3's count), counting by reader output file: + +| Panel reader | Opus: ran / named the plant / only one to name it | Sol: ran / named the plant / only one to name it | +|---|---|---| +| first-pass reader (adversarial-native) | 90 / 52 / 7 | 89 / 46 / 16 | +| specialist batch | 90 / 39 / 3 | 90 / 16 / 1 | +| red team | 60 / 20 / 2 | 59 / 7 / 1 | +| second-model reviewer | 75 / 45 / 3 | 74 / 33 / 8 | +| targeted reader | 21 / none / none | 20 / 5 / none | + +The targeted reader again never named a plant that no other reader named. ~~~
The page publishes catch rates for all 8 arms on 30 planted-bug cases with 3 trials each. The no-worse bar for two plain reads plus the second-model reviewer (a lower bound at or above −10 points against the panel) missed on both models: Opus −4.4 (−14.8 to +5.9), Sol −2.2 (−20.0 to +15.6). The panel was not shown to be better either, so the preregistered decision is "neither" and the panel stays. Adding the second-model reviewer to two plain reads raised catches by 14.4 points on Opus and 10.0 on Sol, both intervals above zero. The real-problem judge missed its label check (kappa 0.51 against a 0.6 bar), so its numbers are unscored, as the preregistration allows. Every departure from the plan is listed on the page.
Why The earlier trial asked whether /ship's panel catches more because of how its readers are built or because it reads the code more times. This run gives that question a preregistered answer on both frontier models, so /ship's review stays as it is unless a later, larger test shows otherwise.
Blast radius The change adds one Markdown page under docs/evals/ and one changelog fragment. No code, prompt, skill or test changes. The results check (`gstack-eval-plan results --check`) passes with its one allowed issue, and every number on the page was recounted from the frozen scoring file (script ran: 38 of 38 match).

Frozen, and already names this results path. - `changelog.d/plan-a-test-of-ship-reviewers-against-plain-reads.md`: Current. Points to the preregistration. **Coverage debt:** none. The diff adds only an eval results page, so there is no new public command, flag, skill or setting to document. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Every fix browse suggests for a daemon with other proxy settings can now be followed (#3455)
body:
When `browse` refuses a running daemon because its proxy settings differ, every fix it suggests can now be followed.
Why: four pairings told the user to change a setting that `--proxy` or `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` overrides, or left a set variable that refused the next run.
Nothing to do; the first suggestion, `browse stop`, is unchanged.

## Root cause

`proxyMismatchLines()` in `browse/src/cli.ts` builds the refusal for a daemon whose proxy differs from the session's. Its guard let a `--proxy` session through to the variable based lines whenever the daemon had `proxyDirect`, so it was told to set `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct`, which `--proxy` outranks. Each `unset` suggestion named one variable, although `HTTPS_PROXY`, `https_proxy` and the other `STANDARD_PROXY_VARS` all resolve a proxy, so following it led to a second refusal for the next one. A session with `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` meeting a daemon that took its proxy from `HTTPS_PROXY` was told to run with the daemon's `HTTPS_PROXY`, which its own opt out overrides. A `connect` daemon is headed, and headed mode is part of the config hash, so a plain session always fails the headed test at the top of the function and gets the generic "pass the same flags" refusal from `ensureServer()`, which never named the variable even when the proxy settings differed as well.

## Fix

`proxyMismatchLines()` returns null for a `--proxy` session against a daemon without a proxy, including one with `proxyDirect`, so `ensureServer()` prints its `--proxy` refusal. The two `unset` suggestions list every variable set in `env` among `BROWSE_PROXY_URL` and `STANDARD_PROXY_VARS`, falling back to the single variable named today when none is set. An opted out session meeting a daemon whose proxy came from a standard variable is told `unset BROWSE_PROXY_URL and run this session with the daemon's <variable>`. A new pure export, `headedDaemonProxyLine(flags, state, env)`, returns one line naming the variable when the headed mode and the proxy settings both differ (proxy, bypass or the direct opt out) and a variable is part of the difference; `ensureServer()` prints it after the generic refusal. The descriptions of both sides and the choice of variable move into one internal helper that both functions share. `BROWSER.md` says what a `connect` daemon now prints, and `changelog.d/fix-issue-3455-proxy-mismatch-remedies.md` holds the entry. Closes #3455.

## Tests

Four tests in `browse/test/proxy-env.test.ts`, one per point of the issue, call `proxyMismatchLines()` and `headedDaemonProxyLine()` directly and check the flags and variable names in the fix line. All four failed on the old code for the reasons above, and the file now gives 37 pass, with the 33 existing tests unchanged. The 23 other test files in `browse/test/` that mention a proxy or `BROWSER.md` give the same result on this branch as on main on Windows 11 with bun 1.4.5 (292 pass, 36 skip, and one failure, an Opera cookie import case that fails on main too). The daemon integration tests in `browse/test/proxy-env-daemon.test.ts` skip on Windows, so they rely on the Linux CI in `free-tests.yml`. `bun run typecheck` reports no error, `bun run typecheck:test` no new diagnostic, `test/module-size-ratchet.test.ts` passes, and the doc link check, the credential scan and prose lint pass.

## Out of scope

A `--proxy` session against a daemon whose proxy came from a variable still gets the variable based lines, whose second suggestion `--proxy` overrides; the issue does not list that pairing. The comments around the refusal for a daemon without a config hash, and the three names the direct opt out travels under (`explicitDirect`, `direct`, `proxyDirect`), are unchanged.

title: v1.103.0.0 Release v1.103.0.0: /verify becomes /build-check, plus security and /ship fixes
body:
Releases gstack v1.103.0.0: security fixes to the destructive-command check, the secrets check and the merge tool, the /ship fixes that were stopping pull requests from finishing, and the /verify to /build-check rename.
Why: these fixes are on main but not yet on the stable channel most installs follow.
To do: anyone with `disabled_skills: verify` changes it to `build-check` after upgrading.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People on the stable channel are still on v1.102.2.0, which lacks the security and blocker fixes that landed on main since. This pull request moves the version to 1.103.0.0 and folds the 74 pending change notes into CHANGELOG.md, so the next daily release run can tag it and move stable. The release notes below are the ones that go on the GitHub release.

### Action needed: `/verify` is now `/build-check`

- `/verify` is now `/build-check`, so typing `/verify` opens Claude Code's built-in `/verify` again. Use `/build-check` for gstack's build-and-check loop and `/build-check quick` for the check-only pass. (#4714)
- If you turned the skill off with `disabled_skills: verify`, change that entry to `build-check`. Until you do, gstack reads `verify` as `build-check`, so the skill stays off after you upgrade. (#4719)
- gstack no longer runs the check pass before every commit on its own, so the `verify_before_commit` setting is retired. Setting it prints a note and changes nothing, and a config file that still has it keeps working. (#4714)
- Prompts about verifying a change now go to Claude Code's own skill, because gstack's prompt router and `/build-check`'s description no longer claim them. (#4719)
- Upgrading removes gstack's old `verify` skill entry (and `gstack-verify` on other hosts or with `--prefix`), but never a `verify` skill of your own. (#4714)

### Security

- The destructive-command check behind `/careful` and `/guard` now blocks force pushes to main hidden behind an abbreviated `--no-dry-run`, a `-n` that is really a push-option value, or a flag group with a digit (`-f4`), and asks before a relative delete after `cd` into a system folder or a delete of a device under `/dev`. (#4604)
- The same check no longer asks about a quoted path that is safe unquoted, or about the quoted title or body of a `gh issue` or `gh pr` command. (#4604)
- `gstack-ship-queue land` now runs a repository's merged-tree checks in a throwaway clone, and refuses to go on if a check changed the git or gh configuration, hooks or binaries its later git and gh calls would use. Every git call it makes runs with hooks turned off. (#4649)
- The secrets check now flags keys written as Rust `let`, `const` and `static` bindings, and stops flagging Rust type annotations and match arms. (#4675)
- The secrets check now reads files whose names hold a space, an accent or another character git quotes; a key in `src/clé.rs` used to pass. (#4701)
- gstack's secrets check and browse's cookie masking recognize the Gemini keys Google AI Studio now issues, which start with `AQ.`. (#4684)
- New gstack installs no longer contain 63 prompts copied from real SWE-rebench benchmark tasks: the router tests use synthetic prompts, and a test fails if a benchmark task id appears again. Older commits still hold the prompts, so an install with full git history can still reach them through `git log`. (#4642)
- A review finding on security code that names only a file never closes automatically, so its location can't reach the public pull request body. (#4700)

### Fixes for /ship and merging

- An approved extra review check after the two-round limit can be used once; a second claim is refused with `GRANT_SPENT`. (#4722)
- /ship's finish no longer reports the docs audit stale for a file that a clean follow-up check read and nothing changed since. (#4722)
- An owner's approval for one more check after a pull request's second review round now lets /ship finish, whichever command recorded it. (#4717)
- The stale-test-value check no longer flags tests of a different file that shares the changed file's name; a test counts only when one of its imports resolves to that file. (#4723)
- /ship on a branch stacked on another branch can clear its remote test gate from a green CI run. (#4689)
- /ship's final CI check accepts a green run that tested your branch merged onto a newer main when main changed none of your lines or the lines next to them, so busy repositories stop rerunning CI. (#4728)
- A crashed `gstack-ship-queue land --pin` no longer blocks every later merge, because its lock now expires 90 minutes after its last step and a lock whose process is gone is taken over. (#4712)
- A /ship run that stopped or died no longer blocks the next /ship, and the new `gstack-ship-run` command shows a run's state and ends one that stopped working. (#4654)
- A base branch whose `review_exclude_paths` list breaks the policy schema no longer stops every /ship: review covers every file and prints a warning, so the fixing pull request can land. (#4637)
- A skipped or neutral CI run no longer blocks reuse of a passing run on the same commit. (#4695, #4713)
- A CI job that runs only through a reusable workflow now counts only from a caller run that tested your exact commit. (#4713)
- The local test gate reuses every green CI run at your exact code, not only the first one it checks. (#4671)
- /ship no longer accepts a test-gate record taken against a different base branch. (#4706)
- `gstack-ship-queue ready` checks a pull request against the branch it targets, not the repository's default branch. (#4663)
- `gstack-ship-queue ready` fetches missing pull request heads in one go, prints progress and stops after 60 seconds instead of going silent for minutes. (#4668)
- /ship can finish when its docs audit corrects a reviewed doc after the last review round. (#4708)
- /ship can finish after a docs audit that stopped before saving its snapshot. (#4693)
- /ship can finish when the docs audit ran before a merge from the base branch. (#4648)
- /ship keeps a pull request's finished review after a base merge that only re-records a shared harness pin, and /ship warns when its reviewers ran without a logged review. (#4669)
- A follow-up check that confirmed its blockers fixed now counts once the remaining findings are ruled. (#4691)
- A follow-up check that reads an approved fix round clean now closes the findings that round fixed. (#4664)
- A clean recheck of approved fixes counts even when its brief was written just before the review started. (#4698)
- A fix commit's `Review-Finding:` trailer closes its finding only after a full review that finished with the fix in its range. (#4700)
- /ship's bookkeeping holds up in three more cases: a harness pin turned into a symlink needs a fresh review, a claim that could not be saved says so, and earlier runs stay counted after a new description. (#4703)
- /ship's review plan finishes on repositories with very large data or trial files, and `GSTACK_REVIEW_CONSUMER_SCAN_CAP` raises the data-file scan limit. (#4651, #4643)
- `GSTACK_REVIEW_PLAN_TIMEOUT_MS` now raises the review-plan time limit at every step of /ship, so large repositories can finish. (#4632)
- A repository's own test for `review_exclude_paths` no longer pulls excluded files back into review. (#4699)
- Code review now reads the design checklist for frontend changes (it pointed at a missing file before), and the second-model review now reads code in your repository's own `agents/` folder. (#4711)
- /ship's review no longer reads a code name like "the HIGH branch" as a HIGH finding. (#4678)
- Codex review findings written as numbered headings keep their severity. (#4681)
- Seven small fixes to /ship's helper tools, including issue links that no longer turn `Review-Finding:` trailers into `Refs` lines. (#4672)

### Other fixes

- /cso keeps an audit open after a refused submit, so a corrected resubmit is accepted. (#4692)
- /cso no longer aborts when a secret-like file such as `.env.example` can't be read; it lists the file as unread and goes on. (#4688)
- Defaults gstack picks for you now name current models in the design prototype script, Gemini cost labels and `gstack-context-bill --exact`. (#4678)
- `browse --session <name> <command>` works with the flag before the command. (#4684)
- The `browse handoff` window no longer opens with a stray blank tab. (#4684)
- `$D setup` accepts Gemini keys that start with `AQ.`. (#4684)
- `/build-check` trusts a repository's checks in every git worktree of it, so agent apps that start each session in a fresh worktree stop asking again. (#4684)
- `/context-restore` finds Claude Code transcripts under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and Codex sessions under `CODEX_HOME`. (#4684)
- TypeScript hooks start on Windows when Git Bash leaves a path unconverted, such as a home folder with an apostrophe. (#4682)
- `./setup --status` passes on a `--prefix` install and names the command that clears each row it reports. (#4682)
- `./setup` no longer leaves owner-only files in Bun's shared package cache. (#4682)
- Disabling `/open-gstack-browser` also removes its `/connect-chrome` alias. (#4682)
- `gstack-doctor` no longer flags gstack's own CLAUDE.md as a pasted skill list. (#4682)
- OpenClaw, Hermes and Dots registrations leave out skills turned off with `disabled_skills`. (#4682)
- /autoplan's phase-report check works in sessions where Remote Control was on from the start. (#4681)
- /ship sees every git worktree of a repository when it picks a version, so two worktrees can't take the same one. (#4681)
- `gstack-pr-shots --path` compares against the real base branch when `origin/HEAD` points at the feature branch. (#4681)
- When a reviewer's diff is too large, the suggested fix names only folders that review can actually leave out. (#4681)
- The docs link check and prose check no longer read a line that starts with inline code as the start of a code block. (#4677)
- /learn prune checks every learning, not just the first 100. (#4677)
- /retro counts a test runner in `tests/` with no test-style name and stops counting Godot and Unity sidecar files as tests. (#4677)
- Deleting or renaming a test now checks the files that still list it, even when another test covers it. (#4702)
- Playwright specs that take `test` from a local fixtures file run under `playwright test`. (#4702)
- The changed-constant check no longer floods on one- and two-digit numbers. (#4683)
- `gstack-gbrain-mcp-verify` no longer misreads a large or slow server-sent-events reply as broken. (#4710)
- gbrain memory lookups find their pages again. A cloned brain host no longer imports plans twice and gets its "Related from memory" hits, and oversized logs keep their newest rows. (#4685)
- Eight skill fixes reported by users, including the Aside check asking you to open Aside, `/test-audit` finding the eng-review test plan, and `/design-shotgun` passing the reason for each pick. (#4686)

### What's new

- The prompt-routing hook no longer names your bug-fix skill on bug reports, because a preregistered test on 183 real Python bugs found that naming it got the skill's steps followed but fixed no more bugs. It still routes /review and /qa, and never routes a message from another Claude Code session or a background agent's hand-back. (#4707, #4674, #4694)
- Review can leave out copied open-source files that `gstack-vendored-verify` proves byte-for-byte equal to a pinned upstream commit; list the upstreams in `review_vendored`. (#4646, #4665, #4690)
- `gstack-ship-queue land` can run full CI on the merged tree before it lands a pull request whose base moved (`land.merged_ci`), and main's push run reuses that result instead of testing again. (#4649, #4655)
- `gstack-ship-queue count` prints how many finished pull requests are waiting to merge. (#4712)
- On Capy, the second-model review in `/ship` and `/review` defaults to GPT-6.2 Sol. (#4636)
- On Capy, `/ship` runs in the pull request's own thread and starts its reviewers as subagents, with no separate helper agent. (#4670)
- `/eval-plan` refuses gpt-4o and older-generation models in every role a plan chooses, and plans frozen on or after 2026-11-22 check a model judge against 100 hand labels. (#4630)
- `/eval-plan`'s dry run follows the plan's own dates and declared vendor models, and new plans name how their grader treats the agent's repository. (#4673)
- `/plan-ceo-review` explains its review-mode recommendation by what that mode does that the next-closest mode wouldn't. (#4730)
- Skills that declare gbrain context queries load them at start; `gstack-config set gbrain_context_load off` turns it off. (#4687)
- `gstack-harness status` reports `unknown` with the error when a harness's skill list fails, instead of listing every skill as missing. (#4687)
- Test selection follows TypeScript NodeNext `.js` imports to their `.ts` source and maps Rails `app/` and `lib/` files to their specs. (#4679)
- Published the results of two tests of /ship: running it in the pull request's own thread made no clear difference in cost or bugs caught (#4680), and its review panel beat two plain review reads, so it stays (#4676, #4732).

### Changes for maintainers

- Every gstack pull request gets a Test changes summary of deleted or skipped tests, loosened limits and edits to its own checks, as a two-week trial that never fails a pull request. (#4645)
- A weekly Mutation report lists small wrong edits gstack's tests fail to catch. (#4652)
- Free test shards survive a browser that exits during cleanup (#4666), nightly Windows shards stay under their time limit (#4661), weekly test health passes again (#4633), and two git worktree races no longer fail each other (#4710).
- Release-check fixes: the recommendation judge's calibration includes two real questions (#4705), the /autoplan guard test keeps its Claude Haiku 4.5 actor (#4639), and the docs-audit tests accept /ship's step for a stopped audit (#4731).
- The bootstrap retention tests skip five cases that can't happen when the suite runs as root. (#4677)
- Removed a sentence the revert drill added to its own docs. (#4716)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/blob/v1.103.0.0/CHANGELOG.md · **Compare:** https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/compare/v1.102.2.0...v1.103.0.0

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Stable has been 28 hours behind main while main holds security fixes and fixes for problems that stopped people's /ship runs. Releasing them within a day of passing the release check keeps the stable channel safe to follow.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The diff is the version in VERSION, package.json and the agents digest header, the new CHANGELOG section, the deletion of the 74 folded change notes, and one constant: `REVIEW_VENDORED_KEY_VERSION` moves from the provisional 1.102.3.0 to 1.103.0.0, the release that ships the `review_vendored` key. That is safe because gstack's own policy does not use the key and a code search found no other repository that declares it (search run during review). Every required CI check passed at this head (Free Tests run 45110327753); jobs that only run on other triggers were skipped.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No issues block this release. The second-model review asked whether moving the provisional version of `review_vendored` could reject a policy written against an unreleased main build; no such policy exists and stable never had the key, so it ships as a disclosed note. Two wording notes about the generated CHANGELOG lines (the old `/verify` name and two prompt-router lines that the later change supersedes) are fixed in the release notes above; the CHANGELOG itself has to match the change notes byte for byte.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current: the v1.103.0.0 release commit needs no documentation changes.

**Scope:** release/1.103.0.0 against main (base 261f3800, head 43f19ce0). This is a read-only audit of one release commit with 79 files changed: VERSION, package.json, the agents digest header, CHANGELOG (74 changelog.d fragments folded in) and REVIEW_VENDORED_KEY_VERSION in lib/ship-policy-keys.ts. The working tree is clean.

**Documentation health**
- CHANGELOG.md: current (the 1.103.0.0 entry is release metadata, not changed)
- agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md: current (version header matches)
- docs/vendored-code.md: current (the CI example already pins v1.103.0.0, which matches the new review_vendored key version)
- docs/troubleshooting.md: current (the release reference is still accurate)

**Debt:** None. No tracked or new file outside CHANGELOG still mentions 1.102.2 or 1.102.3, and no architecture diagram is affected.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] Free Tests at this head (run 45110327753): 1,775 test files passed in CI, 0 failed.
- [x] `bun test test/gstack-ship-policy.test.ts`: 22 pass, 0 fail (the check that failed on the first attempt at this release).

title: Write up a failed or shelved attempt before closing it (GST-3576)
body:
gstack now asks for a short write-up before any attempt is closed as failed, shelved, cut, null or not now, and the close links to it.
Why: a failed attempt is paid-for knowledge; without a page of notes the next person repeats it or never learns which part worked.
To do: nothing. Workflows that close an attempt now point at the new template, docs/shelved-attempt.md.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

When an experiment, an eval arm or a prototype didn't work out, gstack had no default for what to keep, so a dead attempt often closed with a one-line reason and its numbers stayed in a thread nobody reopens. Now there's one short template and every place that closes an attempt points at it.

- **New template, `docs/shelved-attempt.md`:** takeaways, what we tried and why, what worked, what didn't (with numbers and how far each was checked), why it's shelved, what would reopen it, where the data and scripts are, what wasn't done, what went wrong on our side, and cost.
- **The default, stated where gstack keeps its rules:** point 17 on the factory page every Capy session reads, and a new "Write it up before you shelve it" section in the multi-thread lead manual, whose rule for closing a PR as dropped now asks for the link too.

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The archive check is the one gstack step that sees a thread's closed PRs, but it can't read the close comment, and many closed PRs were superseded, not shelved. A refusal there would block every archive that holds a superseded PR, and /ship is being simplified to drop refusals without stated reasons, so this adds a reminder at the last moment the thread's context still exists. title: /ship reviews fixes with full rounds instead of narrow re-checks (GST-3562)
body:
/ship no longer plans a narrow re-check after a fix: a fix after round 1 gets a full round 2, and a fix in round 2 gets one read-only full review of the final code, so fixed code never ships unread.
A new test also stops /ship from gaining refusals without a stated reason.
Part 1 of 3 of the /ship simplification Garry approved; nothing for readers to do, and approvals recorded before this change keep working for one release.

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- **Review loop (lib/review-depth.ts).** `nextStep` plans no new fix-check. A fixed blocker, a gate-class edit or a below-floor fix after round 1 gets a full pass on the fix range as round 2 (a light diff whose below-floor fixes touch no runtime lines still ships them as notes, and a lean round 2 adds the second-model review when numbers changed). A fix applied in round 2 gets one read-only full review of the whole PR diff with no fix round; a fix after that stops for the owner instead of offering a grant. A round that replaces a fix-check, and the read-only review, keep one full-effort reader: the Red Team reader is added when nothing else runs at full effort (a docs-only round 2 under `review.panel off` or `risk` otherwise had none). The per-PR cap (R51) works the same way across /ship runs. Round 2 still reads the fix range, not the whole head, as it does today.
- **Old fix-checks, one release.** A grant no longer buys a fix-check at the round-2 stop. Fix-check rows recorded before this change still verify, and a grant still answers the stop that follows one of them. Part 3 removes both.
- **Round-cap message (lib/ship-release.ts).** finish's behavior STOP now says the planner at the round cap plans one read-only full review of the final head, not a grant.
- **Refusal ratchet.** test/ship-refusal-code-ratchet.test.ts lists the 131 refusal codes /ship's review, receipt, pregate and queue code raise today; a new one needs an "R56:" reason in test/fixtures/ship-refusal-codes.json, and a removed one must leave the list.
- **Docs.** docs/review-policy.md's transitions table and docs/ship-policy.md's round-cap paragraph describe the new behavior. The skill prose follows in part 2.

**Why it is safe.**
The change was checked against main's transition table frozen at 0408128 (test/fixtures/review-depth-main/next-step-0408128.ts) over 3,932,160 review histories: 2,757,344 plan the same step with the same reason. Every other case either replaces a fix-check with a full pass (133,120), rewords a stop, voices or done reason (897,760), stops after a read-only review instead of running a fix-check (74,880), reviews a below-floor fix main shipped unread (46,976), or gives a fixed blocker at the cap a read-only full review instead of a stop (22,080). None drops a read of changed code, and none drops a reader: each replaced fix-check must keep a full-effort reader that excludes nothing the fix-check read, plus main's other readers. The grid tests read each changed case back as main's plan through test/helpers/gst3562-replay.ts and assert these kinds; the review-depth pin moves to replay GST-3562-A.


GSTA-820, GST-3562 letters A and Q. Letter M (green PR CI standing in for requires-remote clears) is set aside: the Windows and macOS remote lanes run on schedule or dispatch, not as PR checks, so green PR CI does not cover them (crew/test/ship-queue-train-ops.test.ts caught it). The plan's other part-1 items (receipt records made optional, the identical-tree rule for base merges) follow in a second code PR before the prose PR. Letter B (folding the targeted reader into the second-model reviewer) failed its pilot and is out. Rule-15 ruling: approval a-6ec01c09edf8. /ship receipt follows.

title: /ship reports GitHub GH007 email-privacy rejection as a non-fast-forward error
body:
**gstack:** 1.102.2.0 (stable channel), Claude Code, macOS

**What happened**
During `/ship`, GitHub rejected the push with GH007: "Your push would publish a private email address" / "push declined due to email privacy restrictions". The commit's author email was a private address, and the account has GitHub's "Block command line pushes that expose my email" setting on.

`/ship` reported this as a non-fast-forward rejection instead. That points to pulling or rebasing, which doesn't fix it.

**Expected**
`/ship` recognizes GH007 (or "push declined due to email privacy restrictions") and says what fixes it: set `user.email` to the GitHub no-reply address and amend the commit.

**To reproduce**
1. On GitHub: Settings → Emails → turn on "Block command line pushes that expose my email".
2. Make a commit whose author email is that private address.
3. Run `/ship`.

title: /cso reports every security finding the code supports instead of dropping most of them (GST-3588)
body:
/cso now reports every security finding the code supports, with a confidence level, and keeps low-confidence ones as labeled hypotheses instead of dropping them.
Why: on 52 real GitHub security advisories, Opus 5.5 with /cso named the published flaw in 3 of 51 audits, against 12 of 51 for a plain audit request (gstack-evals#443).
Nothing to do: the next `/cso` run uses it; the before-and-after rerun on the same 52 advisories is planned separately.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Findings with doubt are kept.** The skill told daily runs to keep only findings with impact proven inside the repository, and the helper refused anything else, which drops almost every library bug. Now a finding is supported when code traces attacker-controlled input to it and nothing inspected blocks it, and a library's public API counts as an entry point. A finding with one open question is submitted at low confidence as a hypothesis and listed under **Hypotheses (unconfirmed)** in the audit's reply. It is dropped only when code disproves it. The helper now accepts hypotheses in a daily run and saves them in `report.json`; `report.md` still lists them only for comprehensive runs.
- **The run ID and file list can't be cut off.** One audit started but lost its run ID to `start | tail -80`. The skill now saves `start` and `inspect` output to private files, reads the ID with `jq -r .runId`, lists every file with `jq -r '.manifest.entries[].path'`, and tells the model to read every attacker-reachable file in full rather than narrowing by file name.
- **A refused start is retried.** The skill said "never call `start` again", so a refused start ended the audit. A refused start holds no run, so the skill now applies the correction it names and starts again, with at most 32 `--paths` prefixes (1024 characters) when the 64 MiB source cap refuses.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

- **Never started (all 12 such Opus sessions):** the helper at the eval's pinned build refused any source holding a symlink, and `--paths` retries hit the same refusal or the 32-prefix limit. That was already fixed on main by #4567 and #4592: 10 of those 12 repositories now start with no flags, and the other 2 are over the 64 MiB cap. This PR only removes the skill's "never retry" rule.
- **Started but lost its run ID (1 session):** `tail` cut the ID off. Fixed by the `jq` instruction above.
- **Started but never reached the vulnerable file (3 sessions):** one helper read per file inside the 600-second budget. This PR doesn't fix that; a whole-snapshot search command with a hard time limit follows in a separate PR.
- **Found but dropped:** the daily "supported only" rule and the helper's refusal of daily hypotheses. Fixed above.
- The 64 MiB cap and `inspect`'s file list sitting past the first 30,000 characters caused none of the recorded sessions; they show up only in a replay of the 52 repositories.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the /cso skill text and one helper check change. The helper no longer refuses a low-confidence hypothesis in a daily run (two deleted lines in `lib/cso/cli.ts`); hypotheses still can't be verified, reproduced or counted as supported, because `verify` and `record-review` require supported evidence (read at `lib/cso/cli.ts`, and confirmed by the review). `lib/cso/contracts.ts`, the launcher, setup and the runtime images are unchanged, so every existing safety rule (helper-only reads, redaction, private control files, proof labels) still holds and the existing /cso tests pass.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The final review of this head (specialists with the red-team checklist, a native adversarial pass and a second-model review) found no blocking issue in my judgment or the native reviewers'. The second-model review marked five items as blocking; the owner ruled all five below the floor and they ship as notes, listed in the Agent notes. Notes kept for the follow-up: daily `report.md` lists only supported findings while `report.json` keeps the hypotheses; the `jq` file list prints in one shell result; each `read` re-checks the whole snapshot. An earlier head carried a whole-snapshot search command that could stall on a long line; it was removed from this change and moves to a follow-up with a hard time limit.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed.

**Scope:** 5 committed files from 8143a918 to ae964eab (`cso/SKILL.md.tmpl`, generated `cso/SKILL.md`, `lib/cso/cli.ts`, `test/cso-recall.test.ts`, `changelog.d/cso-reports-every-supported-finding.md`). No staged, unstaged or new candidate files. I reviewed the /cso docs: README.md, docs/skills.md, docs/cso-release-qualification.md, docs/cso-scanners.md and cso/sections/audit-phases.md.tmpl.

**Documentation health:**
- README.md: current. The /cso row is still accurate.
- docs/skills.md: current. The /cso section and its example are still accurate.
- docs/cso-release-qualification.md: current. Hypotheses already count in neither term of the daily precision gate.
- docs/cso-scanners.md: current. No change touches it.
- cso/SKILL.md.tmpl and cso/SKILL.md: these are the changed sources themselves. The generated file matches its template.

**Coverage debt:** Two behaviors are covered only in cso/SKILL.md: daily runs now keep low-confidence hypotheses in a separate **Hypotheses (unconfirmed)** table, and a library's public API now counts as an attacker entry point. The user-facing /cso summaries in README.md and docs/skills.md do not mention either one. This is a common gap with no how-to or explanation, and filling it would be a security-prose edit for a human to approve.

**Diagram drift:** none. No diagram references the changed code.

</details>

title: Add a test that stops /ship from gaining refusals without a stated reason (GST-3562)
body:
A new test lists the 131 ways /ship can refuse to continue today and fails when a new one appears without a written reason.
Why: about a third of gstack's recent PRs were gstack repairing its own gates, and new refusals are how that work grows.
Nothing for readers to do; it changes no /ship behavior.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

test/ship-refusal-code-ratchet.test.ts scans /ship's review, release-check and merge-queue code for refusal codes (`code: 'X'` and `refused('X')`-style calls) and compares them with test/fixtures/ship-refusal-codes.json. The 131 codes raised today form a baseline that may only shrink. A new code needs an entry under `codes` whose reason starts with "R56:" and names its evidence or measurement plan, and a code that leaves the source must leave the list.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"25 of 67 merged gstack PRs on 2026-11-22 were gstack repairing its own gates." Each new refusal is a new way for /ship to stop someone's work, so this test makes every new one state why it earns its place.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

It touches only a test and its fixture, with no product code, skill prose or reviewer prompt changes, so no /ship run behaves differently. The test reads source files and runs nothing (file read: test/ship-refusal-code-ratchet.test.ts; it passed on main and in CI at e17fb72).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Scope:** I reviewed tree 2a583355f7e31ae0532b03beb9a810ee75c4d7af. The change is 4 committed files (e17fb72 over base 8143a91), and nothing is staged, unstaged or untracked. It's all test infrastructure plus one changelog fragment.

**Result:** The docs are current, so I made no edits. The fragment's "131 ways" matches the fixture: the baseline has 131 codes and `BASELINE_MAX` is 131. docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md describes `FREE_FIXTURES` in general terms, and the new entry fits that description. No doc lists refusal codes or per-test ratchets, and the banned-terms check found nothing.

**Debt:** The refusal-code ratchet has no prose docs. It's explained only in the fixture's `_comment` and in the test's own failure messages. Filling that gap means writing new content, so I'm reporting it as debt instead of writing it.

</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

- **Known limits, from review.** It does not see refusals emitted only through `resultLine(...)` (for example STOP_UNBOUND, GRANT_SPENT), its baseline check is by length (a retired baseline name could be swapped for a new one), and it has no planted positive or negative control. These are follow-ups, not regressions: nothing checked this before.
- **Origin.** GST-3562 letter Q, split out of #4737 by the Captain's ruling (GSTA-36, 2026-11-23): "A: split. Ship Q alone as a new PR from main with one review round." Letter A is being rebuilt as its own PR.

title: /ship reviews fixes with full rounds instead of narrow re-checks (GST-3562)
body:
/ship no longer plans a narrow re-check after a fix: a fix after round 1 gets a full round 2, and a fix in round 2 gets one read-only full review of the whole PR, so fixed code never ships unread.
Why: the narrow re-check read only the fixed lines, and each round now keeps at least one full-effort reviewer, the one the re-check was.
Part 1 of the /ship simplification Garry approved, rebuilt after #4737; nothing for readers to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

lib/review-depth.ts plans no new narrow re-check. A fixed blocker, a gate-class edit or a below-floor fix after round 1 gets a full pass on the fix range as round 2; a light diff whose below-floor fixes touch no runtime lines still ships them as notes. A fix in round 2 gets one read-only full review, and a fix after that review stops for the PR's owner. The per-PR round cap counts the same way across /ship runs.

Each planned step that replaces a re-check, and the read-only final review, carries a structured `keepReader` flag, and both dispatchers add the Red Team reader at full effort when no full-effort reader that excludes nothing is planned. A lean round on a docs or tests change also keeps the targeted reader main runs. The read-only final review carries a `readOnly` flag: bin/gstack-review-dispatch stages it on the PR's merge base whatever `--diff-base` it is given and prints `READ_ONLY:`, and Step 3's edit guard in ship/sections/review-army.md applies no fix on such a pass. The bot-review skip (`review.platform on`) applies only to a run's first review.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A narrow re-check read only the lines a fix changed, so a fix could break code next to it and ship unread. Full rounds read the whole range again with the same readers, which is what the two-round cap (R51) already assumes.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

It changes how /ship plans review after a fix, on every repo. Re-check rows and grants recorded before this change still verify for one release; part 3 removes them. A replay of main's planner against this branch over 3,932,160 review histories found no case that drops a read of changed code (test/review-depth-lean.test.ts, test/helpers/gst3562-replay.ts).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** updated. Two authored docs got factual corrections so they describe GST-3562 A (full rounds instead of fix-checks, plus the read-only final review at the cap).

**Scope:** the diff from af6deb99 to c51a6abe on branch ship-full-rounds: 33 committed files and no staged, unstaged or new files. Docs audited: docs/review-policy.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md (PR_ROUND_CAP), docs/model-policy.md, the changelog.d fragment and ship/sections/review-army.md.tmpl.

**Documentation health**
- docs/review-policy.md: updated. Items 3–5 of the per-PR round rules now say that a fix in round 2 or at the cap gets one read-only full review, and that a fix after that review stops for the PR's owner.
- docs/troubleshooting.md: updated. The `PR_ROUND_CAP` meaning no longer says a below-floor fix finishes with notes.
- docs/ship-policy.md: current. It was already updated in this branch.
- ship/sections/review-army.md.tmpl: current. The `READ_ONLY:` cap rule is documented.
- docs/model-policy.md: current. It is still accurate for grandfathered fix-checks.
- changelog.d/ship-full-rounds-instead-of-fix-checks.md: current (not edited).

**Coverage debt:** the new `READ_ONLY:` dispatch line and `planReviewAt` have reference coverage only, in review-policy and the review-army template; there is no how-to. The K1 `scoped-fix-check` table row, the `--fix-checks` paragraph and the scoped-pass dispatch text may be stale after GST-3562 A and need a policy decision before anyone edits them.

**Diagram drift:** none. No diagram names the changed review-depth entities.
---

</details>

title: /cso searches the whole repository in one call with a hard time limit (GST-3588)
body:
/cso can now search every file in a repository with one helper call, which stops at a hard time limit, and a daily report.md lists its low-confidence hypotheses.
Why: audits that started never reached the vulnerable file because each file took its own helper call inside a 10-minute budget (gstack-evals#443).
Nothing to do: the next `/cso` run uses it.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **`gstack-cso search <run> <regex> [--seconds N]`.** It checks the snapshot once and runs one regular expression over every readable file. It prints `path:line:text` with the text around the match. It reads only the helper's redacted copy and skips paths outside `--paths`. The pattern is capped at 512 characters and the output at 96 KiB.
- **A hard time limit.** Matching runs in a worker, one 4 KiB window of a line at a time, so a long minified line stays fast. The limit (60 seconds, or `--seconds` from 1 to 60) starts before any file is read; the snapshot check before the first file cannot be interrupted, and the 64 MiB snapshot cap bounds it. The helper stops the worker at the limit, even inside one runaway match, keeps the hits it has received (including earlier hits in the file it was on; one still in flight at the limit can be lost), and lists the files it did not finish: the first 50 by name, then a count.
- **Honest gaps.** Files over 1 MiB or unreadable are listed as a coverage gap. Files the snapshot deliberately left out (dependencies, nested repositories, binaries, symlinks) go on a separate count line that points to `inspect`, so they no longer look like a gap. Files with lines over 4096 characters are named, because `^`, `$`, lookbehind and matches over 256 characters are approximate there.
- **Paged file list.** The skill reads the `jq` file list 500 paths at a time instead of in one shell result, and its source-access rule now names `search` beside `inspect`, `read` and `history`.
- **Daily hypotheses in report.md.** `report.md` now lists a daily run's hypotheses under "Hypotheses (unconfirmed)", the section the shared renderer already writes for comprehensive runs. Text such as `$'` in a hypothesis is copied literally. `lib/cso/contracts.ts` is unchanged, so the runtime images need no requalification.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `test/cso-recall.test.ts`: 6 pass. Its search tests cover hits, a hostile file name that is never run, an over-1-MiB file listed as unsearched, a dependency file kept off the gap line, a match past column 300, the long-line note, no matches, an invalid pattern and a bad `--seconds`. A one-line 1 MiB file finishes a quadratic pattern, and a runaway pattern stops at its 2-second limit with the hit before it in the same file kept. The daily-report test checks the hypotheses section with `$'` and `$&` in a title.
- [x] The tests added in the review round fail on the first head (ba138f2cc) and pass here; the first head's new tests failed on main.
- [x] Free test suite in CI at this tree (run 45181717166): 1776 test files, 0 failures. The macOS and Windows launcher jobs, macos-named-regressions and windows-smoke pass at this head.
- [x] typecheck, typecheck:test, format:cso:check, /cso helper suites, skill validation, parity, size and budget guards: pass

</details>

<details><summary>Review</summary>

Two full rounds ran (specialists, red team, a native adversarial pass and a second-model review). In the second round the second-model reply was collected by hand after a resend, so its record is incomplete; see the Agent notes. The first round's 14 findings were all fixed. The second round found no defect that fails a test, breaks production or loses data or secrets. Its seven items marked blocking were ruled below that bar and ship as notes, listed in the Agent notes: the time limit cannot interrupt snapshot validation (bounded by the 64 MiB cap), the unfinished list names 50 files then a count, CRLF and trailing-newline line handling and `\b` at window edges, and the worker posting hits after the output budget is full. Other notes kept: a stop notice can be cut off when a pipe reader stalls for seconds; hits queued just before the limit can be dropped while the file is still listed as unsearched; `"${@:3}"` in the build script passed the macOS CI job; two further red-team notes are recorded privately.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed.

**Scope:** base af6deb99 to HEAD ca1222f8 on `cso-search-with-a-time-limit`, 9 selected files (the `gstack-cso search` command, its search worker, daily hypotheses in report.md, the build script, tests, the /cso skill template and its generated SKILL.md, and a changelog fragment), plus an unstaged edit to the changelog fragment.

**Documentation health:**
- `cso/SKILL.md.tmpl`: current. It covers search, the 60-second limit, the 500-path paging and the hypotheses line.
- `cso/SKILL.md`: current and matches the template.
- `changelog.d/cso-search-with-a-time-limit.md`: current; it matches the 50-path listing in the code. This audit doesn't edit changelog files.
- `docs/skills.md`: current. The /cso section doesn't list helper subcommands.

**Coverage debt:** `gstack-cso search` has reference coverage only (SKILL.md and the CLI usage text). Nothing explains how to use it or why it exists, which is a common gap. The hypotheses section in daily report.md has the same reference-only coverage.

**Diagram drift:** none. No diagrams reference the changed modules.

title: gstack-upgrade works again after you disable skills (#4704)
body:
If you turned off skills with `gstack-config set disabled_skills ...`, every `gstack-upgrade` stopped with "tracked files changed: SKILL.md". It now upgrades, and your skills stay off afterwards. Why: gstack has to keep itself up to date without a person cleaning up after its own setup. Nothing to do. ## What changed Setup rewrites the router file `SKILL.md` in the gstack checkout to leave out skills you disabled (or the plan-mode preamble, with `plan_mode_preamble off`). The upgrade's safety check saw that rewrite as your own edit and refused. Now `bin/gstack-upgrade` renders the router fresh for your current settings and compares. Only when `SKILL.md` is the one changed file, its file mode is unchanged, and its bytes match that fresh render exactly, does the upgrade treat it as gstack's own. It checks the bytes again under the setup lock, puts the committed file back for the fast-forward, and renders the router again right after, so the disabled skills stay off. Anything else still refuses exactly as before. That includes an edit on top of the rendered router, a router rendered for an old setting, a staged or mode-changed `SKILL.md`, or any other changed tracked file. If the fast-forward fails, the router is rendered again only if it wasn't edited after the restore (a sub-second race remains; see Review notes). If the render after the update fails, the upgrade prints a fix and leaves the reinstall pending. ## Why The bug report (#4704) showed every scheduled upgrade failing for anyone who disables a skill, and the next setup making the file dirty again. Two fixes were possible. One was to teach the upgrade's dirty check to recognise the generated router. The other was to move the per-install router out of the git checkout. The first is much smaller and keeps the safety check in force, because the exception is narrow (one file, exact bytes from the same generator and settings relink uses) and fails closed on any mismatch. Moving the router would touch setup, relink and every host's install layout, which this fix does not need. ## Blast radius Only `bin/gstack-upgrade` changes behaviour, and only when `SKILL.md` is the sole changed tracked file. For everyone else the dirty check runs exactly as before. `setup`, `gstack-relink` and `gstack-config` are unchanged. The check runs Bun and the router generator from the checkout, only after confirming every other tracked file is clean. ## Test Coverage New `test/gstack-upgrade-rendered-router.test.ts` (9 cases, skipped on Windows), written first and failing on main 45e33b5e (2 of its first 6 cases failed with "tracked files changed: SKILL.md"). It builds a throwaway gstack remote and clone in a temp folder, sets `disabled_skills` through the real `gstack-config` and `gstack-relink`, then upgrades. It covers the upgrade passing and the router staying rendered (plain and `--ff-only-no-reinstall`), `plan_mode_preamble off`, a failed fast-forward, and five refusals: a user edit on the rendered router, an edit with nothing disabled, a mode change, another tracked edit, and a router rendered for an older setting. ## Documentation **Status:** current. The docs match the change, so no edits were needed. **Scope:** the committed diff against base 45e33b5e (bin/gstack-upgrade, docs/troubleshooting.md, changelog.d/upgrade-works-with-disabled-skills.md, test/gstack-upgrade-rendered-router.test.ts), plus a search of the authored docs and templates for gstack-upgrade, disabled_skills and "tracked files changed". **Documentation health** - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. The UPGRADE_REFUSED entry (#upgrade-refused) already explains the rendered router SKILL.md exemption. - changelog.d/upgrade-works-with-disabled-skills.md: current (read only; changelog files are owned by the parent). **Coverage debt:** bin/gstack-upgrade has a new stderr warning ("could not render the router for disabled_skills again ...") that no troubleshooting entry covers. No diagram drift. ## Tests - [x] `bun test test/gstack-upgrade-rendered-router.test.ts test/gstack-upgrade-bin.test.ts test/relink-disabled-router.test.ts test/bun-entry-isolation.test.ts test/gstack-config-defaults.test.ts`: 67 pass, 0 fail at b48d1fa - [x] `bun run typecheck:test`: no new diagnostics - [x] Full free test suite in CI at b48d1fa: green (run 45194763944). title: Refresh this week's recorded test times so the free test suite splits its shards evenly
body:
This copies this week's recorded test durations into the free test suite's seed files, unchanged from the weekly recording.
The suite uses these times to split tests into evenly sized shards, and the recording bot's own pull request (#4736) cannot land on its own.
Nothing to do as a reader: data only, no code changes.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

The weekly recording on 2026-11-22 measured how long each free test file takes, but those numbers sat in a bot pull request that cannot be merged as built, so the shard planner kept packing tests by last week's times. This pull request carries the same three data files, byte for byte, so the planner splits by current times again.

- `scripts/free-test-durations.json` (Linux) and `scripts/free-test-durations-windows.json` (Windows) hold the durations from run https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/45110767670 on 261f3800.
- `scripts/free-test-seed-allowlist.json` drops eight files that now run under 60 seconds from the slow-file allowlist, so the 60-second ceiling covers them again.
- A changelog fragment and one TODOS line record that `test/setup-codex-scope.test.ts` left the allowlist at 58 seconds.

There is no visible surface to picture, because the change is three JSON data files.

</details>

"Land this week's duration seed refresh." Stale durations make shards uneven, and three unmerged weekly refreshes once left the free suite red on three Mondays in a row.

title: Fix three intermittent test failures: large developer profiles, a docs-audit fixture and an error-review fixture
body:
`gstack-developer-profile --vibe` no longer fails once a profile grows past 64 KB, and two paid test fixtures stop giving the model contradictory instructions.
These were the repeat failures in this week's test runs; fixing them keeps the release checks green without retries.
Nothing to do as a reader.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

People with long session histories hit a failing `gstack-developer-profile --vibe`, and three paid checks kept going red for reasons in the test fixtures rather than the product. Now:

- **`bin/gstack-developer-profile --vibe`** piped the profile into a `bun -e` script that never read its input and passed the same profile again as an environment variable. A profile over 64 KB made `cat` die of SIGPIPE (exit 141, the CI symptom in run 45100410843); one over 128 KB failed to start at all (exit 126, "Argument list too long"). It now reads standard input like the other subcommands. A new test covers both sizes; it fails on main (141) and passes here.
- **Docs-audit fixture** (`test/helpers/docsync-interface.ts`): #4678 added a `gstack-banned-terms` step to /document-release, which the fixture's closed command list does not allow. One trial probed it with `--help` and the observer failed the run (census 45091322954). The interface now says to skip such a step and record it, never probe it.
- **Error-review fixture** (`test/fixtures/dx-error-contract-case.ts`): the example meant to need no findings left gaps the review rubric counts (what a crash leaves behind, a fix once network retries run out, versions and exit codes on the crash path), so reviewers flagged it in census 45122546426 and again here. The example now meets every rubric item on its network and crash failures; the pass bars are unchanged.

There is no visible surface to picture, because the change is one CLI input path and two test fixtures.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"These were the repeat failures in this week's test runs." Each one cost a retry or a red check, and the profile bug also breaks the command for real users with large histories.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`--vibe` keeps its flags and output; only its input path moved, matching the stdin pattern the other subcommands in the same script already use. The two fixture edits change only what the paid tests show the model, and the paid runs below passed on them.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Scope:** the diff from a3ecfd53 to a6296db2 plus the unstaged changelog fragment: bin/gstack-developer-profile, changelog.d/flaky-fixes-2026-11-23.md, and four test files and fixtures. Nothing is staged and there are no new files.
