title: Blocker: free-suite duration seed PR closed unmerged
body:
Seed PR #4736 was closed without merging, so scripts/free-test-durations.json still lacks every free test file added since its last recording. Unseeded files are packed at the seed's 99th percentile, which unbalances shards and stretches every Free Tests job toward its 90-minute cap.

Fix: dispatch a fresh recording on main (`gh workflow run free-durations-record.yml --ref main`) and merge the seed PR it opens, or record with `bun run test:ubicloud --record-durations` and land the seed in a PR. This issue closes when a seed PR from the recorder merges; close it by hand if the seed lands another way. See docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md#free-suite-duration-seed.

title: Stop false phone-number holds on /ship run ids and name interactive /autoplan runs
body:
Posting a PR body that lists earlier /ship runs no longer stops for a "phone number" that is really a run id, and an interactive /autoplan approval is imported under its own run id instead of `autoplan`.
Every /ship that rewrote a body holding earlier runs waited for a confirmation (#4725; about 1 in 10 run ids also reads as a card number and still asks, fixed in a follow-up), and interactive /autoplan runs could not be cited by run id (#4402).
Nothing to do after merge.

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Fixes #4402
Refs #4725 (partly fixed: run ids no longer read as phone numbers; a run id that also reads as a card number still asks for confirmation until the follow-up PR)

Refs #4729 (outside PR by @thomsjack; its idea is rebuilt here on current main, with credit)

</details>

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **`gstack-post` skips /ship's run ids in the run history block.** In each closed run history block that /ship writes into a PR body, a line that is a JSON object byte-identical to its `JSON.stringify` rendering, with a 40-hex `head` and a `run` shaped like a /ship session id (`<pid>-<epoch>-<8 hex or digits>`), has the column span of that top-level `run` value skipped for `pii.phone.e164` only. Repro on main c4cfe6d1: the reporter's body exits 2 with `RULE: pii.phone.e164 LINE: 4`; on this branch it scans clean.
- **`gstack-approvals import --autoplan` uses the run id written on its gate rows.** With no `run.json` (an interactive run), the import takes the newest `run` written on its `decisions.jsonl` rows and only that run's rows, instead of the folder name `autoplan`. A `Plan: approved: <folder>` line resolves the same way.
- **Interactive /autoplan run ids read cleanly.** The id was `<branch>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>`; on a branch like `fix-4402` the privacy check read `4402-20261122-093321` as a phone and card number, so the import was refused and a `Plan:` line citing it would be held. The id is now `<branch>-autoplan-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>`, which scans clean in the import and in a PR body. No scanner exemption was widened for this; the restore file name is unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Security read</summary>

This adds an exemption to a privacy check, so it is additive only: the existing catch is unchanged, and the new code only adds skip spans.

- Only the top-level `run` value is skipped, only for `pii.phone.e164` (a card-number or any other finding there still reports), only inside a closed fence whose opening line is exactly the run history block's fence line, only on a canonical JSON line with a 40-hex head, and only when the value matches the session-id shape the PR body's other /ship record already uses.
- Commit ids were checked and need no exemption: 40-hex commit fields, including all-digit ones, raise no finding.
- Negative controls in the new test, each still held: a phone number in `reason` on the same line as a valid run; a phone number as the `run`; a truncated id; a session id under another key (`grant`) and nested under `review_loop`; non-canonical spacing; a duplicated `run` key; a missing head; a non-sha head; an unclosed block; the same id in prose after the block; the same line in a `json` block.
- The /autoplan change touches no exemption: an imported run id still goes through the full scan.

</details>

- `test/approval-record.test.ts`: the new numbered-branch test fails on main's `autoplan/SKILL.md.tmpl` and passes here; the interactive import tests and the plan-record path test pass.

title: Clearer errors for GitHub email-privacy pushes, approval refusals and bisect case names
body:
/ship now tells you to fix your commit email when GitHub refuses a push with GH007, instead of sending you into a pointless merge; `gstack-approvals` says which `--owner-ref` check failed; and the merge queue's bisect accepts a red judge case whose name has a space.
Why: three small, plainly correct fixes from outside reports (#4738, #4718 with #4720, #4724 for #3580), taken as one batch.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **GH007 push refusal (#4738).** "/ship reports GitHub GH007 email-privacy rejection as a non-fast-forward error." `gstack-ship-release push` read any push output containing "rejected" as a non-fast-forward. Now GH007 gets its own stop line (set `user.email` to your GitHub noreply address and rewrite the commits), any other remote refusal (a protected branch, a hook) quotes the remote's reason after passing it through the secret scanner, and only git's own non-fast-forward status line gets the fetch-and-merge route. Matching uses git's remote-error and ref-status lines, so a branch name containing those words can't pick the wrong advice. The `PUSH: failed reason=PUSH_REJECTED` line is unchanged. Reported by @raymondllee.
- **Approval refusals (#4718).** `gstack-approvals rule` and `round-grant` checked the ref shape, `--words` and `--by` in one condition and printed one sentence. Each check now has its own line, the shape refusal says what a valid ref looks like without repeating the rejected value, and the shared fix clause no longer points every command at `add`'s flags. Accepted inputs and exit codes are unchanged. Rebuilt on main from #4720 by @Barack-zero-to-one.
- **Bisect case ids (#3580).** The merge queue's bisect left the space out of its case id check, which the release bisect and the CI route already allow, so a red `<skill>/SKILL.md workflow` judge case was refused. The three now share one `CASE_ID` rule. Rebuilt on main from #4724 by @Barack-zero-to-one.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"/ship reported this as a non-fast-forward rejection instead. That points to pulling or rebasing, which doesn't fix it." (#4738). Users with GitHub's email privacy setting on now get the one change that works, approval refusals name the flag to fix, and a red judge case can be bisected.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`lib/ship-release.ts` changes only which stop line a failed `git push` prints; the push, its guards and the `PUSH:` reason codes are unchanged (file:line read at lib/ship-release.ts:836-842, and the push tests drive a real bare origin with a declining pre-receive hook). `crew/scripts/train-gate.ts` (run by `evals.yml`) now imports the same `CASE_ID` regex it defined before, so its accepted ids don't change; the full free suite passed in CI run 45231787731.

</details>

The quoted remote reason passes through the secret scanner and is withheld when it can't be redacted. Its test adds a pre-receive hook to its own temp bare origin. | ours, plus the full review panel |
| Approval refusals | PR #4720 | rebuilt with Co-authored-by credit; outside branch never fetched | Message text in `bin/gstack-approvals` only; its tests add a fixed-argument `git commit` with a timeout. The second-model read caught that the outside version echoed the rejected ref into stderr; this rebuild does not. | ours + GPT-6.2 Sol |
| Bisect case ids | PR #4724 | rebuilt with Co-authored-by credit; outside branch never fetched | Yes: `crew/scripts/train-gate.ts` runs in `evals.yml`. Its accepted ids do not change; the merge queue's bisect now accepts the space the other two already did. | ours + GPT-6.2 Sol |

Each fix has a test that failed on main first: the GH007, protected-branch, redacted-reason and plain-decline cases in `test/ship-release.test.ts`; four `--owner-ref` refusal tests in `test/approval-record.test.ts`; three `redCasesOutsidePlan` tests in `crew/test/ship-queue-train-logic.test.ts`.

title: Run Free Tests shards on 8-core runners again to cut CI cost
body:
Free Tests goes back to running its shards on 8-core runners with four sub-shards each, the setup it used before #4600.
The 16-core runners made each shard faster but a whole run only about 0.4 minutes faster, while the median run cost about a third more.
Nothing to do as a reader: the same tests run in the same shards.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Free Tests got more expensive this week without getting noticeably faster: #4600 doubled each shard's cores, but the macOS jobs and the final check still decide when a run finishes. This puts the shards back on `ubicloud-standard-8`, so a run costs about what it did before.

- `.github/workflows/free-tests.yml`: `FREE_SUITE_RUNNER` goes back to `ubicloud-standard-8` and `FREE_SUITE_JOBS` to `'4'`, two vCPUs per sub-shard as before. `FREE_SUITE_SHARDS` stays `'10'`; no job is renamed or split, so the required check names are unchanged.
- `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` records the move back, the audit numbers and which runner size each belongs to.
- A changelog fragment describes it.

There is no visible surface to picture, because the change is two workflow constants.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The 2026-11-23 weekly CI audit found that on 16 cores shard jobs took 2.6 min p50 against 4.4 on 8 cores, but a whole run only went from 6.2 to 5.8 min p50, while a run's Ubicloud cost went from $0.23 to $0.31 p50. The audit puts that at roughly $80 a week at current volume, an estimate from the median gap at list price; the mean gap in its sample was smaller ($0.240 on 16 cores, n=27, against $0.230 on 8 cores, n=71).

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the free-suite shard jobs change runner size. Each shard's job timeout is computed from `FREE_SUITE_JOBS` and the recorded durations, so the slower shards get matching timeouts, and the wiring tests pass on this tree. Free Tests on this pull request ran on the new setting.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The documentation already matches the change, and no edits were needed.

**Scope:** 3 committed files from cb06a6de to 9baea905 (`.github/workflows/free-tests.yml`, `changelog.d/free-tests-runner-8-core.md`, `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md`), with no staged, unstaged or new files. I searched the authored docs for stale references to the free-suite runner size and sub-shard count.

**Documentation health:**
- `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md`: current. The Free Tests sizing paragraph and the duration-recorder note both say `ubicloud-standard-8` at k = 4, which matches `FREE_SUITE_RUNNER` and `FREE_SUITE_JOBS`.
- `changelog.d/free-tests-runner-8-core.md`: current. It agrees with the workflow and the testing doc.

title: ship-queue: support a trusted local test lane for repos without hosted CI
body:
A PR with a current ship receipt and a passing local pregate is refused by `gstack-ship-queue ready` when its head has no GitHub checks (`QUEUE_NOT_READY`: CI at that exact head is not green). This is a repo with GitHub PRs but no hosted CI (Actions unavailable), so no head ever has checks.

Please add an opt-in lane configured by the base branch's ship policy:
- accept a trusted local test receipt bound to the exact head and tree, or a named commit-status context from a configured GitHub App / login;
- keep refusing missing, stale, failed, pending or unreadable evidence;
- test the lane in a fixture repo with no Actions workflows.

Today the only paths are the interactive `NO_CHECKS` confirmation in /land-and-deploy, or posting a commit status from a local runner and relying on `ready` counting status contexts, which any account with write access can also post under the same name.

Related: #3991 (local repos with no PR and no CI; this one has PRs).

title: Stop false card-number holds on /ship run ids in PR bodies
body:
Posting a PR body that lists earlier /ship runs, or the /ship result record, no longer stops for a "card number" that is really a /ship run id.
About 1 in 10 run ids passes the card-number checksum, so those bodies still waited for a confirmation after #4747's phone-number fix (#4725).
Nothing to do after merge.

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Fixes #4725

</details>

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **`gstack-post` skips the card-number check on /ship's own session ids.** The two places that already skip the phone check for a session id, the `run` of a well-formed line in the earlier-runs block and the `run` of the /ship result record, now also skip `pii.cc`, but only when the whole card-shaped digit run starts and ends inside that run value. Every other skipped span (run ids, shas, Approvals table) still clears the phone check only.
- Measured before the fix: 10 of 100 consecutive session ids (`<pid>-1795338725-c32255b8`, pid 4242400 to 4242499) raised `pii.cc`; `99999-1795338725-12345678` is one.

</details>

<details><summary>Security read</summary>

This adds an exemption to a privacy check, on top of the existing catch: no finding main reports outside those two exact run values is dropped.

- The skip needs the run value to match the session-id shape (`<pid>-<10-digit epoch>-<8 hex or digits>`), so a card number written as the run (`4111111111111111` or `4111 1111 1111 1111`) never qualifies.
- Negative controls in the new test, each still held for `pii.cc`: a card number in `reason` on a line with a valid run; a card number as a runs line's run, plain and spaced; a card number as the result record's run; the same session id in prose after the block and in a `json` block.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/gstack-post.test.ts`: the new card-number test fails on main's `lib/gstack-post.ts` and passes here; the existing earlier-runs and result-record tests pass unchanged.
- Targeted: gstack-post, spawnsync tripwire, module-size ratchet; `bun run typecheck` clean. CI is the full run.
- No paid eval ran: no prompt, template, judge or eval code changed.

</details>

title: gbrain-refresh no longer deletes a healthy brain-aware render when python3 is the Windows Store alias (#1967)
body:
`gstack-config gbrain-refresh` now reads the gbrain detection file with the first of `python3` and `python` that runs, then grep, so a healthy gbrain is no longer reported as not detected and its brain-aware render is no longer deleted.
Why: on Windows `python3` is often the Microsoft Store alias, which exits 49 and stays on PATH next to a python.org install, including during the refresh run after each auto-update.
Nothing to do; where `python3` works, nothing changes.

## Root cause

In `bin/gstack-config`, `gbrain-refresh` chose its interpreter with `command -v python3 || command -v python` and never checked that it runs. The Store alias prints its hint on stderr and exits 49, so both parses fell to `|| echo unknown`, and the grep fallback stayed unreachable because `PYTHON_CMD` was set. The `*)` branch then printed "gbrain not detected (local-status: unknown)" and, with a global install present, removed `$RENDER_DIR` through `gstack_claude_render_action "$RENDER_DIR" absent`, although `gbrain-detection.json` said `ok`. `bin/gstack-session-update` runs this refresh silently after every pull, so a Windows team-mode install loses its brain-aware skills on each update. #3025 fixed the MSYS path half of #1967 by passing the file on stdin. The reporter of #1967 also had `python3` under `WindowsApps`, and this cause survives that fix.

## Fix

The parse now tries `python3`, then `python`, keeps a result only when both reads exit 0, and otherwise uses the existing grep fallback. Before this change that fallback ran only on a machine with no Python at all, and under `set -euo pipefail` a field grep could not find ended the run with exit 1 and no output. The `no-cli` record written when detection fails has no `gbrain_version`, so that case is common once the fallback is reachable; both greps now end with `|| true`. Production change: 29 lines in `bin/gstack-config`.

## Tests

`test/gstack-config-gbrain-refresh.test.ts` gains a stub that behaves like the Store alias (hint on stderr, exit 49) and four cases. With the alias under both names, the grep fallback reports `Detected gbrain v0.35.8.0 (local-status: ok).` With the alias only as `python3`, `python` parses the file, and the stub records that it ran twice before grep. With a fake global install and an existing render, a failed render step leaves the render file intact instead of printing "Removed the brain-aware render". A failed detection is reported as `local-status: no-cli` with exit 0. All four fail on main; the existing two cases still pass unchanged.

Run on Windows 11 with Git Bash and bun 1.4.5: the file passes 6 of 6, and `test/gbrain-refresh-install-render.test.ts` and `test/plan-mode-preamble-render.test.ts` pass. `test/claude-overlay-setup-lifecycle.test.ts` and `test/claude-overlay-setup-recovery.test.ts` skip on win32, so these integration tests rely on the Linux `free-tests.yml` run of this PR.

## Reproduction

On a Windows machine where `command -v python3` prints `.../Microsoft/WindowsApps/python3`, copy `bin/` to a temp root, stub `gstack-gbrain-detect` to print `{"gbrain_on_path":true,"gbrain_version":"0.9.1","gbrain_local_status":"ok"}`, create `$HOME/.claude/skills/gstack` with `VERSION` and `package.json` and a file under `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/render/claude`, then run `gstack-config gbrain-refresh`. main prints "gbrain not detected (local-status: unknown)" and deletes the render. This branch prints "Detected gbrain v0.9.1 (local-status: ok)" and keeps it.

title: The /cso release check accepts the low-confidence hypotheses /cso now reports (GST-3624)
body:
The release gate's /cso diff-mode check now accepts the low-confidence hypotheses /cso reports since #4739, which turns the gate green again so the stable release can go out.
Why: the check still required every finding in a daily report to be confirmed, so it failed every run (release gate 45216872389, twice at the same line).
Nothing to do: this changes tests only.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `test/helpers/cso-e2e-report.ts` (new) holds the fixture and report checks the three /cso eval cases share. A daily finding may now be a hypothesis, but only at low confidence, and `report.md` must list hypotheses under "Hypotheses (unconfirmed)".
- Each case still requires its main finding to be confirmed: the webhook's missing authentication (diff mode, named in the title or root cause), the cross-tenant read (full audit) and the comment-to-token workflow (infra scope).
- `test/cso-e2e-report-contract.test.ts` (new, free) replays the failed run's two captured submissions through the real `gstack-cso` helper. It fails on the old check with the gate's exact error (Expected "supported", Received "hypothesis") and passes now. Its negative controls still reject a medium-confidence hypothesis, the main finding downgraded to a hypothesis, and a finding outside the diff.
- Fixture git commits ignore the host's global and system Git configuration, so commit signing or hooks on a developer machine can't break them.
</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

#4739 (af6deb99) made /cso keep an unconfirmed candidate as a low-confidence hypothesis instead of dropping it, and removed the helper's rule that daily reports hold confirmed findings only. In release gate 45216872389 (main @ c4cfe6d1) /cso did exactly that: it found the webhook forgery as High and confirmed, plus two more confirmed issues and one hypothesis (hard-coded session tokens). The e2e check at `test/skill-e2e-cso.test.ts:77` still asserted that every finding was confirmed, so cso-diff-mode failed in attempt 1 and in its one rerun. That red holds the stable release, which owes users the upgrade fix #4743.
</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Tests only. The three /cso paid cases share the new helper; cso-full-audit and cso-infra-scope would have failed the same way on their next periodic run. The diff-mode check is slightly stricter than before: the webhook-authentication finding must name the defect in its title or root cause, so a supported side finding that only mentions it in its impact text no longer counts.
</details>

title: /ship counts a clean base merge as reviewed (GST-3562)
body:
When you merge main into a reviewed branch and your own lines, file modes and symlink targets come through byte-identical, /ship now treats the head as reviewed and lets CI check it, instead of asking for another reader.
Why: these routine merges cost a reader stop on almost every PR that sat a day, and the reader only ever re-read lines that had not changed.
Part of the /ship simplification Garry approved (items G and H); nothing for readers to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- /ship now tells merge shapes apart. If main only changed lines near your unchanged code, the head counts as reviewed at the final check and when the review record moves to the merged head, and the record says CI on that head checked it.
- If main replaced the very lines one of your changes replaces and the merge kept both, or main added lines at the exact spot where you inserted lines (so the merge had to choose their order), one scoped reader still reads those lines. The 200-line limit for that read now applies only to these cases.
- A file mode that differs between the reviewed and current heads, or a diff git prints with bytes that are not UTF-8, now counts as a real change and gets a full review (one exception: the pathspec-name gap under Deferred findings).
- /ship's record of a finished run is accepted without the docs, review-loop, issue or budget entries; a new test confirms that, and that older records with those entries are still accepted.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The old rule sent every merge that touched nearby lines to a reader, even when none of your lines moved, so most PRs paid for a read that could not find anything new. The cases that can change what your code does, a splice into your own lines or a merge that orders your insertion against new lines, keep their reader.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only /ship's final check and the step that moves a review record to a merged head. Merges that change your own lines, file modes or symlink targets still stop for review as before, with one known gap listed under Deferred findings: a file whose name starts with git pathspec magic (for example `:(`) can hide a mode flip that comes from main. CI at the merged head remains a required check before anything lands.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- New no-loss cases: a merge that keeps your own lines, an executable script and a symlink exactly as reviewed passes with no reader; a file-mode flip (in the merge or from main), a symlink retarget, a conflict resolution inside your own line, and bytes that are not UTF-8 each count as changed; insertions whose order against main's new lines the merge chose are sent to the scoped reader in either order.
- The earlier fixtures for moved lines (GST-384, GST-442, GST-1226, GST-2229, qm#3457, founderstar#563, #4383) stay as acceptance cases for the new rule, and every scoped-reader check (record validation, an unwritable packet directory, the dry run that writes nothing, the 200-line limit) moved to a spliced fixture so it still runs.
- CI at 18290d5a: every check green, including free-tests (run 45259819295, 39,272 tests across Linux, macOS and Windows).

</details>

title: Show the weekly benchmark in every stable release plan, ready to hold a measured drop (GST-3606)
body:
Every stable release plan now prints the weekly benchmark's result: whether this week's gstack measurably fixes more or fewer bugs than the current stable release. Why: about 30 PRs land a week and this is the first number that says whether agents using gstack got better or worse; a measured drop should not reach every stable install. Nothing to do: holding is off for the first two weekly records, so this only reports for now.
What changed ![The stable release docs gain a Weekly benchmark section, and every cut plan prints the weekly result, report only for now](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/QuLcfsU36dVkd0WBuGnItnrZSZR9IWc5c7rS8akW4bk.png) The stable release docs gain a Weekly benchmark section, and every cut plan prints the weekly result, report only for now. Garry asked "Is Gstack this week significantly better than last week?" gstack-evals now answers that every Saturday and publishes a `weekly.json` record. Until now the stable release never looked at it. The release tool now reads those records and prints one `BENCHMARK:` line on every cut plan, dry runs included, using the same rule gstack-evals uses to decide which record counts. The code to hold a regular cut on a measured drop is in place and tested, but it stays switched off until two weekly records have arrived on time; security, data-loss and regression fixes always ship. A hand-run cut can pass a hold with a new `benchmark_waiver` input, which is written into the release tag so a retried cut is not held again. A malformed record reads as unreadable instead of stopping the cut, and text from the records is cleaned before it reaches the job log.
Why "Is Gstack this week significantly better than last week?" (Garry, 2026-11-21). The weekly benchmark now measures that, and the stable release is where a measured drop would reach everyone, so the cut has to see the number before it can ever hold on it.
Blast radius Only the stable release tool and its workflow change: `crew/scripts/release-cut.ts` gains one benchmark block after its existing plan, and `planRelease`, `gateVerdict` and `readTrainNotes` are untouched, so gstack-evals' resolver shim still loads the module (its export test passes). With `BENCHMARK.hold` false the gate always passes, which the report-only test and a live read against garrytan/gstack-evals (`BENCHMARK: none (no weekly record published yet) (report only)`) confirm.
Pre-Landing Review Two review rounds at full depth (a gate-class change: specialists, red-team, a second native reader and a second-model review on GPT-6.2 Sol). - Round 1 found one blocker: a malformed weekly record could crash every cut, report-only included (security finding, details recorded privately). It was reproduced, fixed in b6b6322 and covered by a regression test. Three smaller findings were fixed in the same commit, including a test that a waiver written into the tag is read back. - Round 2 found two follow-on hardening gaps in that fix (security findings, details recorded privately). The second-model review marked them blocking. The repository owner's agent ruled them below the blocking floor, because both need release-write access on garrytan/gstack-evals and holding is off, so they ship as disclosed notes and the fix lands in a follow-up PR before holding is switched on.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-d93a26797613` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `sf-15b3e575a938` security finding, details recorded privately
Exploratory QA Functional smoke (CLI, report only). Before the fix: a live read of garrytan/gstack-evals passed; a record with a null no-gstack comparison crashed the status line (reproduced twice); record text with a newline could start a workflow-command line. After the fix, all three reran on the fixed tree and passed. Not run: the hold-on paths through the CLI, since holding is a constant that is off; they are covered by unit tests of the gate.
Design Review No frontend files changed — design review skipped.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN
Plan Completion Every item in the approved plan is delivered: the record reader and resolver rule, the `BENCHMARK:` line on every cut plan, the hold table with the switch off, the waiver input, the tests and the Weekly benchmark docs.
Verification Results The plan's checks: 1 PASS (the real fetch against garrytan/gstack-evals, run locally on this tree), 0 FAIL. The `Dry run against main` CI job currently refuses before any new code runs because main's own release gate is red; the same refusal reproduces with main's own code.
TODOS No TODO items completed in this PR.
Documentation **Status:** updated. docs/releases.md now matches the weekly benchmark code after b6b6322; two small factual edits, no blockers. **Scope:** the release diff b5eb401e..b6b6322a (crew/lib/release-benchmark.ts, crew/scripts/release-cut.ts, .github/workflows/weekly-release.yml, changelog.d fragment, tests, docs/releases.md), plus the docs that reference the stable release tooling (crew/docs/recommended-harness.md, README.md channel notes). No staged, unstaged or untracked content. **Doc diff:** - docs/releases.md (Weekly benchmark): added that a `vs_none` with a missing or non-numeric number is left out of the BENCHMARK line instead of making the record unreadable (b6b6322). - docs/releases.md (Dry runs): added `crew/lib/release-benchmark.ts` to the files whose PR runs the dry run against main, matching the workflow's `pull_request.paths`. ``` Documentation health: docs/releases.md Updated (vs_none drop sentence; dry-run trigger file list) crew/docs/recommended-harness.md Current (defers release details to docs/releases.md) README.md Current (channel description unaffected) CONTRIBUTING.md Current (not affected by this diff) CHANGELOG.md Skipped (protected; changelog.d fragment matches the code) TODOS.md Skipped (protected; out of scope) ``` **Coverage:** ``` Documentation coverage: [entity] [reference] [how-to] [tutorial] [explanation] BENCHMARK: line / gate ✅ releases ✅ releases ❌ ✅ releases benchmark_waiver input ✅ releases ✅ releases ❌ ✅ releases --benchmark-waiver flag ✅ release-cut usage ❌ ❌ ❌ ``` Debt: `--benchmark-waiver` is documented only in release-cut.ts's usage line and through the workflow input (common gap, reference-only). crew/docs/recommended-harness.md's stable-release summary doesn't mention the weekly benchmark (it links to docs/releases.md). body:
Bumps the production-dependencies group with 4 updates in the / directory: [@ngrok/ngrok](https://github.com/ngrok/ngrok-javascript), [marked](https://github.com/markedjs/marked), [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) and [socks](https://github.com/JoshGlazebrook/socks). Updates `@ngrok/ngrok` from 1.7.0 to 1.8.0
Changelog

Sourced from @​ngrok/ngrok's changelog.

1.8.0

  • Change how a session waits between reconnect attempts after it loses its connection, for every session: the wait starts at 50 ms and doubles up to 30 s, each wait scaled by a random factor in [0, 1). Before, the wait grew 50-fold per attempt with no cap and no random factor: about 2 minutes before the fourth attempt and 1 h 44 min before the fifth.
  • Add SessionBuilder.reconnectBackoff(initialMs, maxMs), which sets the first wait between reconnect attempts and the cap the doubling waits stop at, and SessionBuilder.reconnectJitter(enabled), which turns off or on the random scaling of each wait. The defaults are 50 ms, 30 s and jitter on. reconnectBackoff refuses a value that is not a whole number of milliseconds, such as a fraction, NaN or Infinity, with an error naming the argument.
  • Add SessionBuilder.reconnectMaxAttempts(attempts), which stops a session reconnecting after that many failed attempts in one outage; every listener then stops forwarding, and its forward() and join() reject with the last attempt's error. listenAndServe, ngrok.listen and net.Server.listen(listener) log that error with console.error and leave the process running. It refuses anything but a whole number from 1 to 4294967295. By default a session never stops reconnecting on its own.

Updates `ossf/scorecard-action` from 2.5.0 to 2.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from ossf/scorecard-action's releases.

v2.6.0

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.7.0, built with Go 1.27.4. For changes to checks and results, and the security fixes in this Scorecard release, see the Scorecard v5.7.0 release notes.

Getting started

This is the first release with ready-to-use workflows in this repository. To add Scorecard to a repository, copy one into .github/workflows/scorecard.yml:

  • examples/scorecard.yml for public repositories. It publishes results to the Scorecard API, which enables the badge and the REST API, and fails the step if the API rejects them.
  • examples/scorecard-private.yml for private repositories. It doesn't publish.

Both pin every action to a full commit SHA, set cache-mode: none, and upload results even when an earlier step fails. CI lints them with zizmor, actionlint and yamllint. If your linter reports cache-mode as unknown, see Workflow Linters.

Copy the examples from main, which pins this release. A tagged commit can't pin its own SHA, so the copies at the v2.6.0 tag still name v2.5.0.

To add the workflow to many repositories at once, the installer opens a pull request in each one. See docs/installer.md.

What's Changed

  • New fail_on_publish_error input (default false): when set, the step fails if the Scorecard API rejects the results. Network errors and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx stay warnings. New outputs results_published and publication_status report whether publishing worked, and the job summary says so. A rejected (4xx) publish is now sent once instead of three times, and the publish error and warning show as annotations. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1721
  • Example workflows for public and private repositories in examples/, with every action pinned to a full SHA. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1722
  • The examples set cache-mode: none and upload results even when an earlier step fails. The README's new Workflow Linters section lists which linter versions recognize cache-mode. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1727
  • The installer (cmd/installer) adds the generated example workflow with the repository's default branch, and no longer needs a starter-workflows checkout. Usage is in docs/installer.md. by @​justaugustus in ossf/scorecard-action#1728

Other

title: First versions open with the owner's own words, and the try-it check follows his exact steps (GST-3608)
body:
When we hand someone the first version of something, the approval page and the try-it message now open with their own quoted requests, each marked "does it" or a lettered choice.
Before they're asked to try it, gstack-first-use has an agent from another model family follow the exact numbered steps on their real setup, and holds the message until no step is broken, wrong or needs a lookup.
Nothing to do: this changes /autoplan's first-version gate, gstack-first-use and the guides that point to it.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![The new guide shows how a first version's plan quotes the owner, and how an agent from another model family runs his exact try-it steps before he is asked.](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/g_kpBLMdpVZYD3nmoxcOTBijgGYnhWskO28MeJZIhsw.png)

The new guide shows how a first version's plan quotes the owner, and how an agent from another model family runs his exact try-it steps before he is asked.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The first-use check guide: a first version's plan quotes the owner, and an agent from another model family runs his exact try-it steps before he is asked</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · docs/first-use-check.md § The owner's words and the day-one table at 100e109 · source text (section not present before)
+++ After · docs/first-use-check.md § The owner's words and the day-one table on this branch · source text
+## The owner's words and the day-one table
+A plan is a first version when it has a `Day one` section or the run passes `--first-version` (on `gstack-autoplan next` or in the plan's scope marker). Both kinds of plan use the same two sections: the plan `/autoplan` puts on its approval page, and the one-page list of the first five things the owner does on day one.
+
+```markdown
+### Owner's words
+
+- Ada Example, 2026-11-18 09:12Z: "I keep forgetting which plant needs water" → does it
+- Ada Example, 2026-11-18 09:14Z: "and tell my partner when I'm away" → choice; size: two days; leave out: needs a second account
+```
+
+Each bullet is who, when, the words in quotes, then an arrow (`→` or `->`) and the line:
+
+| Line | Meaning | At the gate |
+|---|---|---|
+| `does it` | this version does what the words ask | a reviewer who finds it does less files a `narrows_quote` finding, and the gate asks |
+| `choice` | this version doesn't fully do it yet | one lettered choice quoting the words: a) build it in this version, b) leave it out. It recommends a, unless the line says `leave out: <reason>`, shown on the choice. `size: <n>` is shown as the cost |
+
+A cut under `### What it won't do yet` that drops a quoted line becomes that quote's choice and leaves the list. On a first version every other cut gets its own letter. The owner brief shows the quotes and their lines first, then the day-one table, then the remaining cuts.
+
+The day-one table needs a heading named `Day one` (any level; `Day-one page` also works) followed by a table with these seven columns, in any order:
+
+| action | frequency | source | feature | route | first build | check |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| sees which plant needs water today | daily | owner words 1 | Today list | root screen | build 1 | the plant due today is at the top, marked due |
+
+The table needs at least five rows, and every cell of the first five needs a value; the check freezes those five in table order. Each of the five cites a quote with `owner words <n>`. A row whose source starts with `assumed` must be confirmed with the owner first; once he confirms it, add his answer to Owner's words and cite it. `test/first-use.test.ts` pins this format, so a change to the parser fails that test instead of quietly changing what gets checked.
~~~

</details>

- **Owner's words drive the page.** Each `### Owner's words` bullet carries a line after an arrow: `does it`, or `choice` (optionally with a size and a reason to leave it out). The gate shows the quotes first; a cut that drops a quote becomes a lettered choice beside it that recommends building it, never a bullet under "What it won't do yet".
- **The first five day-one rows cite a quote** (`owner words <n>`), and gstack-first-use refuses to freeze a plan that has no Owner's words or a quote with no time or line.
- **gstack-first-use runs the real steps.** The play spec gains numbered steps and a target (the real setup or a realistic copy). Each step gets useful, thin, wrong or broken plus one line; the message waits on any broken, wrong or needs-a-lookup step, and names thin steps, notices and the known bugs in the build the owner holds now. A stored result with any other verdict refuses, as it did before this change. New platforms: macos and server.
- **The owner's quotes stay out of public exports**, whatever their script, and a bullet whose attribution holds an arrow or quote marks reads its quote exactly as before.
- **Discovery.** factory.md, the short card every build thread reads, the coordinator guide, /autoplan's plan format and /ship's TestFlight step now point at gstack-first-use.
- **Not in this change: the owner's own "ruled out" line.** A bullet ending `→ ruled out <date>: "<ruling>"` reads as it did before lines existed: one quote running to the last quote mark, still redacted from exports. Letting a ruling outrank a reviewer's finding needs a product decision first, so it comes in a separate change.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Every first version drew a complaint first." Six first versions reached the owner between Nov 14 and 23; in at least four the gap was written down before he touched it, and in none did anyone run the exact steps we asked him to take on his real setup. Now the plan starts from his words and the steps are run before he sees them. The plan was approved on 2026-11-23.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The parser change reaches every /autoplan plan with an Owner's words section, not just first versions. That is safe because a 64-row table test requires every bullet shape to read the same quote and attribution as the merge-base parser (test ran, 0 differ), and the first-use verdict check is back to refusing anything but a known passing verdict, as on main (test ran: 'pass', 'great' and a missing verdict all refuse).

</details>

One full review of the final head, read-only with no fix round: four reviewers plus a second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol), and a coverage audit that found no gaps. Every finding above the floor was decided by the maintainer as a disclosed note (listed in the notes below). Open notes, none blocking:

- **Short owner quotes in public gate items.** A quote under three words can appear in a public export's gate item title; replies that short were never redacted before this change either. Fixed in the follow-up change.
- **TestFlight-only builds.** The checker brief asks for a TestFlight build number, but the cloud phone installs only a build the build service made, so a TestFlight-only check refuses instead of running. It fails closed. Fixed in the follow-up change.
- The try-it message shows the gate's wording for a choice ("a lettered choice below"), which points at choices the message doesn't have.
- A plan that is not a first version but has an arrow after a quote now reports its Owner's words as malformed in an advisory line.
- Answering "leave it out" to a High narrowing finding keeps that question open until the plan changes.
- The try-it text check compares a hash stored beside the text, so it catches accidental edits only.
- A `~~~` inside an owner quote would close the fence around the try-it text in the checker's brief.
- `predict --why` checks for emptiness before stripping markup, and one usage line in `bin/gstack-first-use` lists fewer device classes than the code accepts.
- Two further notes from the security-minded reviewer are recorded privately.

title: Landing a PR reuses an earlier CI run on the same merged code instead of starting another (GST-3634)
body:
When main has moved, `gstack-ship-queue land --pin` now reuses an earlier CI run on the same merged code: it lands at once on a green run, waits on one still queued and refuses on a red one, instead of starting a new run on every try. Why: GitHub's macOS runner queue has been slower than land's 45-minute wait, so lands kept timing out while the run they started finished green unused. Nothing to do. Rerunning a timed-out land now waits on the run it named.
What changed A land onto a moved main kept getting refused with `QUEUE_NOT_READY`. Each try built a new merged commit, dispatched a new Free Tests run and gave up after 45 minutes, and the next try ignored the run that had since passed and joined the same queue again. #4753 was refused twice this way on the same base and the same merged tree. Before it dispatches, land now lists the workflow's `workflow_dispatch` runs on `gstack-land/` and at the merged commit, and keeps those whose head commit has the merged tree. It matches on the tree, never the commit. Cancelled runs are skipped and the newest remaining run decides. A green run still has to pass `lib/run-evidence.ts`'s `verifyRun`, and one that no longer proves the tree (its artifact expired, or it is too old) gets a fresh dispatch. A timeout names the run the next land will wait on. For a flaky red run, the fix line says to rerun that run (`gh run rerun `), because rerunning land alone finds the same red run. GitHub keeps a run going after its branch is deleted. Run 45249277829's macOS jobs started after the branch was deleted and passed, and the deleted branch's commit can still be fetched by sha. So land still deletes the scratch branch every time.
Blast radius The one caller is `landMergedCi` in `lib/ship-queue-land-direct.ts`. When no earlier run matches, the old push, dispatch and wait path runs unchanged (the existing tests still pass). A read-only probe against GitHub with #4753's real runs, with push and dispatch stubbed out, adopted green run 45249277829 through the real `verifyRun` and pushed nothing.
Test Coverage The test was written first: commit aced15f has 6 new cases failing against main's code. They now pass, plus 3 more added during review (16 in `test/land-merged-ci.test.ts`). The cases cover green, still-running, red, tree rather than commit matching, skipping cancelled runs, an unprovable green run falling through, a run at the merged commit, an adopted run that can't be proved, and timeouts on both a dispatched run and an adopted one. Not covered by tests: `landMergedCi`'s fix-line wording, and the live `runsOn` API call (exercised by the probe above).
Pre-Landing Review The specialist pass found 2 test gaps, both fixed (a test fake whose lookup used up scripted polls, and two untested outcomes at `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:77`). The second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol) and the native adversarial pass raised three findings recorded as blocking. Each was ruled below the blocking floor and ships as an open note: - A, `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:77`: the choice to dispatch fresh reads the run-list snapshot, not what land saw while polling. If a green run is rerun between listing and polling, a red or timed-out rerun is ignored and land dispatches again (worst case about 90 minutes). It never lands on a red or unproven run. A follow-up PR fixes it. - B, `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:47`: reuse is keyed on the tree, not on base plus pin, and Free Tests' seed ratchet reads the merge base. This only matters if main returns to an identical merged tree. Tree matching is what the issue asked for. - C, `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:63`: a red run on a tree never expires, and `gh run rerun` stops working after 30 days. This needs a merged tree unchanged for 30 days.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:47` 4. `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:47` — Land skips cancelled or wrong-tree runs before choosing a candidate, but the post-merge Free Tests consumer chooses the newest scratch-branch run before checking its status or tree (`scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts:80–87`). In the new test’s older-green/newer-cancelled case, land passes without dispatching but main rejects the cancelled run and queues the entire suite agai - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:77` The worst-case CI wait goes from 45 to 90 minutes, which equals `DIRECT_LOCK_TTL_MS` (90 minutes, `crew/lib/ship-queue-land-lock.ts:37`) before `merged_checks` time is even added. Another machine could then take over an expired lock while this land is still running. It's also a small correctness slip, because a red result for that tree gets dropped. The fix is to have `settle` mark the one case th - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:77` 2. **INVESTIGATE: a red run now stays red for its tree until someone reruns it by hand.** Any conclusion other than `success` or `cancelled` refuses with `QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS`, as a red run: `timed_out`, `startup_failure`, `action_required` and `stale` included (`settle`, line 63). Every later land on that tree finds the same run, and the only way out is `gh run rerun `. That isn't always - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:77` 3. **INVESTIGATE: reuse matches on the tree, not the parent commits.** Two merged commits can have the same tree and different parents. For example, main moves to B and then a revert C returns it to A's tree. A run on the old merged commit is then accepted for the new one. Anything in the free suite that reads git history (diffs against `HEAD^1` or the merge base, checks on changelog fragments or - INFORMATIONAL `lib/land-merged-ci.ts:106` 4. **FIXABLE: the branch run listing is capped at 20 runs.** `runsOn` asks for `per_page=20` with no paging (`lib/land-merged-ci.ts:106`). A PR whose `gstack-land/` branch has more than 20 newer dispatch runs on other trees won't find an older run on the matching tree, and dispatches a duplicate. That only wastes CI time; it never lands a wrong tree. Severity: Low. Blocks: no.
Exploratory QA Pass. Probe 001: PR #4753's real runs on the deleted `gstack-land/4753` with merged tree 6a3569f1 adopted green run 45249277829, checked by the real `verifyRun`, with no push or dispatch. Probe 002: the same branch with a tree no run tested adopted nothing and went on to push. Limits: a real dispatch and wait were stubbed out. The timeout and in-progress adoption are covered by unit tests only.
Scope Drift Scope Check: CLEAN. The 45-minute timeout, the required jobs and the 7 required checks are unchanged.

Documentation **Status:** current. The docs already describe the new merged-tree CI reuse, so the audit made no edits. **Scope:** the branch `land-reuses-merged-tree-ci-run` against base `a256d153`, covering committed and working-tree content. The diff touches `docs/ship-policy.md` (the `land` policy row and the land --pin section), `docs/troubleshooting.md` (QUEUE_NOT_READY and QUEUE_LAND_MERGED_CHECKS), `crew/docs/captain.md` (the refusal table) and the changelog fragment. Each was checked against `lib/land-merged-ci.ts`, `lib/land-merged-checks.ts` and `lib/run-evidence.ts`. **Documentation health** - `docs/ship-policy.md`: current. It covers reuse by tree, the newest run that wasn't cancelled deciding, the 45-minute wait, red runs refusing, and the `gh run rerun` advice. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: current. The timeout and red-run fixes match the CLI's fix text. - `crew/docs/captain.md`: current. The rerun guidance for a red run matches. - `changelog.d/land-reuses-merged-tree-ci-run.md`: current. The fragment matches the behavior. **Coverage debt:** none found. **Diagram drift:** none, because no diagrams cover this path.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/land-merged-ci.test.ts`: 16 pass, 0 fail - [x] `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:test`: clean, no new diagnostics - [x] Adjacent files (changelog-fragments, ci-tree-reuse, gstack-ship-policy, module-size-ratchet, run-evidence, ship-policy-compat, ship-queue-land-direct, troubleshooting-anchors, land-direct-recovery-isolation): 632 pass, 0 fail - [x] Full free suite: CI on this head

title: make-pdf: quotes in alt text, titles and raw HTML can no longer add script handlers (GST-3641)
body:
Quotes in image alt text, link titles and raw HTML attributes now stay inside their attribute, so a Markdown file can no longer add an `onerror`, `onload` or `javascript:` link that runs in make-pdf's print browser. Why: the print browser runs page scripts, and on main a crafted image caption made it send the document's own text to another address. Nothing to do: ordinary Markdown prints the same (609 of gstack's own Markdown files render identically).
What changed - **Quote entities are read only in text.** `render()` used to turn `"`, `'`, `'` and `'` back into straight quotes across the whole page after the sanitizer had run, so an image caption such as `x"/onerror="alert(1)` printed as a live handler. That pass is gone. Smartypants now reads those entities as quotes inside its text runs only, and every quote in a text run comes out curly, so an entity can never become attribute or tag syntax. Tags, code and URLs keep their entities, which the browser shows as the same characters. - **Handlers and `javascript:` links after `/` or a closing quote.** The browser starts an attribute after whitespace, a `/` or a closing quote. The sanitizer only looked after whitespace, so inside a raw HTML block ``, ``, `
Security notes **Does the print browser run page scripts? Yes, on both engines.** Both open the staged HTML over a loopback server at `http://127.0.0.1://document.html` with JavaScript on: the Aside path injects its error hook with `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` and both paths poll page expressions, so script is required there, and nothing sets a Content Security Policy or intercepts requests. Checked on this branch's base (a256d15) with gstack's own browser (headless Chromium 158): a raw-HTML `
Tests - `bun test make-pdf/test/`: 317 tests ran, 0 failed (final check at e1f0632). `typecheck` clean; `typecheck:test` 812 known, none new. - Render diff of all 609 tracked Markdown files, main vs this branch: 0 differ.
Why make-pdf prints Markdown that often comes from somewhere else: a README, a report an agent fetched, a document a user was sent. The sanitizer is what stands between that text and a browser that runs scripts, and both bypasses let script run with access to the document being printed and to the network.
Blast radius `make-pdf/src/render.ts` (sanitizer and render pipeline) and `make-pdf/src/smartypants.ts`. Rendered all 609 tracked Markdown files with main and with this branch, reading quote entities as characters: 0 differ. Handler-looking text such as `/onload=x` is now removed wherever it appears, URLs and code included; the same was already true after whitespace.
Test Coverage New tests in `make-pdf/test/render.test.ts` check what the browser's tokenizer would see, not exact strings: an `onerror` from an image alt, an `onload` from an image title (which must not swallow the next paragraph), a second `href` from a link title, a `javascript:` href from a raw-HTML title, single-quote entities ending a raw attribute, handlers or `javascript:` links after `/` or a closing quote, handler values starting with `<` or a quote (including an HTML comment opener followed by an encoded newline), handler text in a code span that must not eat ``, and a positive control. Two smartypants tests pin the contract. On base, with only the tests applied, 7 of the first 10 fail; the image-title test passes on base and guards a regression this change would otherwise cause.
Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 10 issues — 3 auto-fixed, 0 asked, 1 deferred, 4 noted, 2 open as ruled notes.
Deferred findings - Deferred: CRITICAL, in code this PR did not change: the NUL-character bypass described under Security notes. It predates this PR and goes in the next PR.
Review notes - Informational: the offline-posture rules still need whitespace before the attribute (see Security notes). - Informational: quoted handler values can still eat an enclosing attribute's closing quote on crafted input; `/on…=` in URLs and code is removed; the `javascript:` rewrite can flip quote parity on crafted input. None runs script; all are covered by the structure-preserving rewrite in the next PR.
Exploratory QA Functional, `make-pdf generate` through gstack's own browser on owned fixtures. Status: pass. An ordinary document with quotes printed (exit 0, 16,699-byte PDF), and the encoded-quote `onload` caption plus a raw `
Documentation **Status:** current. No documentation changes were needed for this branch. **Scope:** the committed diff a256d1530dad..e1f0632 (make-pdf/src/render.ts, make-pdf/src/smartypants.ts, make-pdf/test/render.test.ts, changelog.d/make-pdf-quote-entities-stay-in-attributes.md). There were no staged, unstaged or new files. The change is an internal security fix: quote entities stay inside attributes and the sanitizer is stricter. No flag, command or output format changed. **Documentation health:** - make-pdf/SKILL.md.tmpl and make-pdf/SKILL.md: current. Neither mentions sanitizer or quote handling. - docs/skills.md (/make-pdf section): current. - README.md (/make-pdf rows): current. - docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md: current. - changelog.d/make-pdf-quote-entities-stay-in-attributes.md: matches the diff (read only). **Coverage debt:** no user doc describes how make-pdf sanitizes raw HTML. This audit leaves that gap as it is and does not fill it. **Diagram drift:** none.
Agent notes Found in GEVA-584's Opus 5.5 runs on main b5eb401e (control agent gstack-c); its blind verifier spotted the `onerror` bypass. The handoff patch kept entities in tags by splitting on `<[^>]*>`, which still decodes them wherever that split disagrees with the browser, so this PR moves the decode into smartypants' curly-only text pass instead. The opening-quote and SVG `stroke-width` fixes from the same handoff touch other functions and follow in a separate PR. `gstack-issue-links` read ` ` and `'` in commit messages as issue references #10 and #39; they are not, so no issue links are listed. title: A land that waits on an earlier CI run decides on what that run did, and main's reuse skips cancelled runs (GST-3634)
body:
A land that waits on an earlier CI run now goes by that run's real result, and main's Free Tests run skips a cancelled run when it looks for a land's run. Why: a green run rerun at the moment land picked it up could have its red result ignored, and a cancelled run made main rerun the whole suite. Nothing to do.
What changed This follows up #4760. Land used to decide whether to start a fresh run from the run list it read before waiting. If a green run was rerun at that moment and the rerun went red or ran past the wait, land threw the result away and dispatched again. Now it decides on what it saw while polling. A red rerun refuses as red, a slow one times out naming the run, and only a run that was already finished green and no longer proves the tree gets a fresh dispatch. `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts`, which lets main's own Free Tests run reuse the run a land already did, now passes over cancelled runs on `gstack-land/`, as land does. In #4753's case, an older green run and a newer cancelled one, main now reuses the green run instead of running the suite again.
Blast radius The change touches only `runMergedCi`'s decision to fall through and one filter in `findReuse`. Every existing case in `test/land-merged-ci.test.ts` and `test/ci-tree-reuse.test.ts` still passes. A read-only probe with #4753's real runs still adopts green run 45249277829 with no dispatch.
Test Coverage Tests first: bebcfc78 adds two cases that fail against main's code (a rerun that goes red or stays running, and a cancelled land run ahead of a green one). They pass with the fix, 48 in the two files.
Pre-Landing Review The specialist pass found nothing. The adversarial pass found two low-severity notes, recorded below and not fixed.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts:82` It's hard to reach. A green-and-provable A on the same tree means land wouldn't have started B, so you'd also need a passing verify failure (an `api_error`) when B was started. Land itself already skips cancelled runs, so nothing it already merges changes. FIXABLE: in both places, skip a cancelled run only when `run_attempt === 1`. | Severity: Low | Blocks: no - INFORMATIONAL `scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts:82` **Finding 2: a cancelled run at the same head commit still blocks reuse, so the changelog promise doesn't always hold** (`scripts/ci-tree-reuse.ts:82` together with `lib/run-evidence.ts:186,237`). `verifyRun` counts any newer run at the same head commit that didn't end in success, skipped or neutral as a veto. title: No loop for reading production errors and usage back into planning
body:
## What happened

gstack covers shipping (/ship, /land-and-deploy, /canary, /retro), but nothing reads production signals back into planning: error tracking (Sentry) and product analytics (PostHog). /canary is a short watch right after a deploy, and /retro measures shipping, not what users hit. So a team has no gstack-shaped way to turn production errors and usage into /spec input, triage or plan items.

## What we did meanwhile

A nightly read-only signals check in the Captain's automation, plus a /spec with the owner on the real loop.

## Suggestion

A documented loop that says who reads production error and usage data and how often, how a finding becomes a /spec or a bug with a failing test, and what an agent may read versus what stays private, since analytics holds user data.

title: A first version's public copy keeps out the owner's short quotes, and phone first-use checks install a build the phone can run (GST-3646)
body:
A first version's public export now keeps out the owner's short quotes and his reasons to leave something out, and a phone first-use check installs a build the cloud phone can actually run. Why: a one- or two-word quote or a leave-out reason could reach the public copy through the gate's choice titles, and the phone check named a TestFlight build the cloud phone can't install. Phone checks now need `--phone-build ` on `gstack-first-use start`; phone runs started before this change must be started again.
What changed - **Public export.** `gstack-autoplan export --public` redacts each plan quote wherever it appears directly inside quote marks, whatever its length, and each quote's leave-out reason after `leave out:`, `leave it out for now:` or `reason to leave it out:`, in any case. `validate --public` refuses a copy where either was written back. A bare, unquoted mention of a short quote's words stays, so ordinary prose isn't blanked out. - **Phone first-use check.** `gstack-first-use start` for iOS or Android refuses to start without `--phone-build`, the 26-character id of the mobile build service's build of `--commit`. The checker's brief tells it to install that build, and to record step 1 as broken if it won't install. A phone run started before this change is refused with a note to start a new one. gstack can't prove that build is the same code TestFlight ships; the builder names it, as the docs say. - Docs: docs/first-use-check.md, docs/unattended.md (the public copy) and two entries in docs/troubleshooting.md.
Tests - CI at 4cee03a2 carries the full free suite: 1,779 test files, 0 failed (Free Tests run 45317161759), plus the macOS and Windows jobs. - New: a table of 4 quote shapes by 10 line shapes through the whole-export check, with every key the plan parser accepts in mixed case (`Does It`, `Choice; Size:`, `Leave Out:`, `Recommend Leave Out:`), plus `validate --public` catching quoted re-insertions while passing plain mentions. It fails on main and without the case fix. - New: a phone start without `--phone-build` is refused, an older phone run is refused on read, and the iOS and Android briefs name the build to install. Each fails without its fix.
Pre-Landing Review Two review rounds. Round 1 found that an older phone run would brief an install of "undefined", fixed here. Round 2 found that a capitalized `Leave out:` key still leaked its reason, fixed here with the same check for every key the parser accepts. The final head then got one read-only full review (no findings) and a second review of the whole diff. Open notes, none blocking: - A short quote written with spaces just inside its quote marks (`" water alerts "`) is still not redacted, so it can reach the public copy. Before this change every short quote did. - A one- or two-word quote that also appears in quotes inside a code block in plan.md makes `export --public` refuse until the plan is edited. It fails closed. - `--phone-build` is accepted and ignored on web, Mac and server builds. - A phone run that finished before this change can no longer print its owner message; it has to be run again. - Nothing ties the phone build id to `--commit`; the builder vouches for it.

title: pregate on Windows: a lane command over 8,186 characters is cut by Git Bash and the lane exits 2 with no output
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `gstack-checks quick` fails with

```
VERIFY FAIL: tests local lane exited 2 (? failed of 0 ran; 204 files; pipefail)
```

when the selected test files make the runner command longer than 8,186 characters. The log shows the `$ npx vitest run ...` line and then nothing: no runner output and no error.

The runner never starts. Git Bash keeps only the first 8,186 characters of the `bash -c` argument, the command ends inside a quoted file name, and bash exits 2 on the syntax error.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Git for Windows 2.53.0.windows.1, `GNU bash, version 5.2.37(1)-release (x86_64-pc-msys)`
- bash resolved to `C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe` (same result with `usr/bin/bash.exe`)
- Checker run under bun

## Cause

`lib/pregate/supervise.ts` runs each lane command as one argument:

```ts
const inv = bashCommandInvocation(`set -o pipefail; ${o.command}`);
child = spawn(inv.cmd, inv.argv, { ..., stdio: ['ignore', fd, fd] });
```

`argBudget()` in `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts` splits the file list on Windows only above 24 KiB:

```ts
const cap = platform === 'win32' ? 24 * 1024 : ...
```

Its comment says Windows caps a whole command line at 32,767 characters. That is the CreateProcess limit. On the setup above, bash itself receives no more than 8,186 characters of the `-c` string, so any command between 8,187 and about 24,000 characters is sent whole and arrives cut.

## Reproduce

Save as `probe.js` and run with `node probe.js` or `bun probe.js`:

```js
const { spawnSync } = require('node:child_process');
const bash = 'C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe';
for (const n of [4000, 8000, 8185, 8188, 8300, 16000, 24000]) {
  const head = 'echo "seen=${#BASH_EXECUTION_STRING}" #';
  const cmd = head + 'x'.repeat(n - head.length);
  const r = spawnSync(bash, ['-c', cmd], { encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true });
  console.log(`sent=${cmd.length} exit=${r.status} ${r.stdout.trim()}`);
}
```

Output here, the same from node and from bun:

```
sent=4000 exit=0 seen=4000
sent=8000 exit=0 seen=8000
sent=8185 exit=0 seen=8185
sent=8188 exit=0 seen=8186
sent=8300 exit=0 seen=8186
sent=16000 exit=0 seen=8186
sent=24000 exit=0 seen=8186
```

## Seen in a real run

A branch that selected 172 vitest files produced a command of 8,244 characters (with the `set -o pipefail; ` prefix). Replayed outside the checker with the same spawn call:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| The full 8,244 characters | exit 2, 0 bytes written to the log |
| The same with three files dropped (8,123 characters) | exit 0, 169 files and 1,932 tests passed |

What bash kept of the full command ended with `... 'src/schem`, inside a quoted path.

Spawned from node with the same stdio, bash writes `unexpected EOF while looking for matching` to the log. Spawned from bun, the log stays empty. I did not find out why.

## Expected

The file list is split so that every `bash -c` argument fits, or the list does not travel in the argument at all.

## Suggested fix

Either of these:

1. Lower the Windows cap in `argBudget()` to fit 8,186 characters for the whole string, and count the `set -o pipefail; ` prefix that `supervise` adds, which the budget does not include today.
2. Write the command to a script file and run `bash <file>`, as `backendCommand()` already does for the remote runner's file list. This removes the limit on every platform.

A check that the lane's output is empty and the exit is 2 could also report "the shell rejected the command" in place of a test failure.

## Not checked

- Where the 8,186 limit comes from in Git for Windows, and whether other Git versions have it.
- Runners other than vitest. The cut happens before the runner starts, so the runner should not matter.

title: /ship catches a file-mode change from main on files whose names start with a colon
body:
/ship's file-mode check now reads file names literally, so a name like `:!tool.sh` or `:(top)tool.sh` can no longer hide a mode change that a merge brought in from main.
Why: this was the one open finding on #4754 that could let a changed head count as reviewed. Nothing for readers to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `comparePath` (`lib/ship-patch.ts`) asks `git --literal-pathspecs ls-tree` for each head's file mode. A lookup that fails now counts as a change that needs review, instead of two failures comparing as equal.
- `baseHolds` uses the same literal lookup, so `:(top)tool.sh` no longer reads the mode of the root `tool.sh`.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only /ship's check of whether a merged head still matches what was reviewed. Normal file names behave exactly as before. A name starting with git pathspec magic now gets a full review whenever its mode moved.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/ship-base-side-masks.test.ts`: a base exec-bit flip on `:!tool.sh`, `:(glob)tool.sh` and `:(top)tool.sh` is changed, and the same merge without the flip is still context. `baseHolds` does not hold a reviewed mode change the base dropped on `:(top)tool.sh`, and does hold it when the base took the mode. Skipped on Windows, where those names are not legal.
- With the flags removed, the new test fails (checked locally).
- Focused: 9 pass, 0 fail. CI free-tests at this tree: run 45317295418, 39389 tests.

</details>

title: /ship is hidden by Claude Code's built-in /ship (same clash as /verify, #4593)
body:
## What happens

On Claude Code 2.1.331 with gstack v1.103.0.0 (short names, `skill_prefix: false`), gstack's `/ship` never loads. Claude Code now has its own built-in `/ship`, and the built-in takes the name.

- When the model calls the skill, the harness answers: "A custom /ship isn't loaded, because Claude Code has a built-in command of that name. To use the custom one, rename it. The built-in /ship starts only from a line that you type."
- gstack's skill is installed (`~/.claude/skills/ship`, `~/.claude/skills/gstack/ship`) but is absent from the session's skill list; only the built-in is listed.

## Why it matters

Any repo whose instructions route "ship / create PR" to gstack's `/ship` can no longer reach it, by typing or through the model. `gstack-ship-budget launch` also opens its child prompt with a typed `/ship --continue …`, which would now hit the built-in.

## Precedent

v1.103.0.0 renamed `/verify` to `/build-check` for the same reason (#4593).

## Workaround today

`./setup --prefix` gives `/gstack-ship`, but it renames every skill, so each repo's routing rules need editing.

## Ask

Rename gstack's `/ship` the way `/verify` was renamed, with the upgrade removing the old entry.

title: A first version's public copy keeps out a short owner quote padded with spaces inside its quote marks
body:
A first version's public export now also redacts a short owner quote written with spaces just inside its quote marks, like `" water alerts "`. Why: those words reached the public copy and `validate --public` passed it; this closes the gap left open on #4772. Nothing to do: the change is one pattern in lib/autoplan-owner-words.ts.

title: /cso: application preparation fails on npm lockfiles with bundled dependencies (inBundle entries have no resolved URL)
body:
## What happens

On a Next.js project that uses Tailwind CSS 4, `/cso --doctor` reports `application-preparation: missing` with:

```
{"code":"UNPINNED_ARCHIVE","message":"A public registry archive URL is required.","path":"package-lock.json"}
```

`qualified-runtimes` then stays missing, and `--comprehensive` can never prepare the app.

## Why

npm writes bundled dependencies into `package-lock.json` (v3) with `"inBundle": true` and no `resolved` or `integrity`, since their files ship inside the parent package's tarball. Tailwind 4 pulls in the optional `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi`, which bundles six packages:

```
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/@emnapi/core          inBundle=true optional=true
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/@emnapi/runtime       inBundle=true optional=true
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/@emnapi/wasi-threads  inBundle=true optional=true
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/@napi-rs/wasm-runtime inBundle=true optional=true
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/@tybys/wasm-util      inBundle=true optional=true
node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi/node_modules/tslib                 inBundle=true optional=true
```

The other 449 entries all have `resolved` URLs on registry.npmjs.org. The npm loop in `lib/cso/preparation.ts` treats every `node_modules/` entry that isn't a `link` as a public archive and calls `publicUrl(raw.resolved, ...)`, which fails when `resolved` is undefined. The loop never looks at `inBundle`.

## Environment

- gstack 1.103.0.0 (main at 84b4eab), macOS 26 on Apple silicon, Docker 29.5.2 through Colima
- npm 11.20.0, lockfileVersion 3
- Static `/cso` works, and all six scanners show ready after setup preloads them. Application preparation is the only check that fails.

## Possible fix

Untested suggestion: in the npm loop in `lib/cso/preparation.ts` (around the `plan.inputs.push({ kind: 'public', ... url: publicUrl(raw.resolved, ...) })` block), skip entries where `raw.inBundle === true` before building a public input. They have nothing to download on their own. Their files come inside the parent's tarball, whose `resolved` and `integrity` are already checked. If the plan needs to list them, they could be recorded as bundled inputs tied to the nearest non-bundled `node_modules/` ancestor instead of as public archives. A lockfile fixture with one bundled entry would cover this in the preparation tests.

#3185 is a different `/cso` failure (already closed), related only by area.

title: A first version's public copy catches a short owner quote whose padding or quote marks are encoded
body:
A first version's public export now catches a short owner quote when its padding or quote marks are encoded, such as ` `, a zero-width space, `"` or a JSON `\"`. Why: those spellings kept the owner's words in the public copy and `validate --public` passed them; short quotes are now matched on the same decoded text the long-quote scan reads. Nothing to do: the redaction still replaces only the original characters of the quote.
What changed - lib/autoplan-owner-words.ts: short plan quotes are also matched on the decoded view of each file (entities, JSON escapes and invisible characters decoded, in both the raw and the rendered view), with offsets mapped back to the original text, the way the long-quote scan already works. Spaces between a short quote's words match any run of whitespace, so an encoded or doubled space between them is caught too. The raw-text match stays, so a quote whose own text holds an entity is still caught. - Docs: the public-copy rule in docs/unattended.md and the ARTIFACT_OWNER_WORDS entry in docs/troubleshooting.md.
Tests - CI at 853fecc5 carries the full free suite: 1,779 test files, 0 failed (Free Tests run 45335081640), plus the macOS and Windows jobs. - test/autoplan-owner-words.test.ts: one case per encoded form (` ` padding, zero-width padding, `"` marks, ` ` inside the quote, JSON-escaped marks) and encoded or doubled spaces between a quote's words; each leaks without the fix. The same test pins today's over-redaction of a bare mention framed by two neighboring quoted strings, and keeps a plain mention and a longer quoted sentence unchanged. - test/autoplan-public-owner-words.test.ts: `validate --public` catches a quote padded with ` ` or a zero-width space written back (fails on main); the whole-export table gets entity-padded and zero-width-padded plan quotes (these already pass on main and guard the plan side).
Pre-Landing Review Two review rounds. Round 1 found that a short quote whose words were separated by an encoded or doubled space still leaked; fixed here. Round 2, a full pass, found nothing. A second-model review left three low notes, none blocking: - A zero-width character used as the only separator between a quote's words (`"ship​it"`) is not caught. - Markdown emphasis inside the quote marks (`"**ship it**"`) still hides a short quote. This was true before this change. - ` ` padding and quoted link targets can redact a little more than the quote itself; that fails safe.
Agent notes Follow-up to #4776 (adversarial-native#1 at 29557a3d), shipped apart from GST-3646 item 3 on the maintainer's ruling. title: /ship instructions match the new review rules (GST-3562)
body:
/ship's instructions, docs and the Capy skill now describe the review rules that already shipped: a change after the first review round gets a full second round, the old extra-reviewer permission slips are retired, and a clean merge from main counts as reviewed.
Why: agents follow these instructions, and they still taught the retired steps. Part of the /ship simplification Garry approved; nothing for readers to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `ship/DRIVER.md`, `ship/SKILL.md` and the review, adversarial, documentation and PR-body sections: a code change after round 1 gets a full round 2; a PR past its two rounds whose code changed gets one read-only full review of its final head, with no fix round. Narrow re-checks and the permission records that bought them are marked deprecated; one already recorded is still claimed before its reader runs.
- Unattended /ship skips the coverage reader, plus the scope, exploratory, TODOS, metrics and nudge steps. A run with a bound plan keeps the plan-completion and plan-verification steps; only a run with no plan skips them.
- The documentation audit edits only `README.md`, `docs/` and `bench/README.md`.
- `lib/review-depth.ts`: a read-only review is now read-only across separate /ship runs too, not only inside one run.
- `docs/review-policy.md`, `docs/ship-policy.md`, `docs/unattended.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/skills.md`, `crew/docs/captain.md` and the Capy skill say the same thing.
- The starter `.gstack/pregate.json` gstack prints links its schema at a GitHub URL that resolves.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Instructions agents read during /ship and review, plus one guard in `lib/review-depth.ts` that can only make a review stricter. No command, flag or file format changes. The deprecated permission records still parse and still work until the next release removes them.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `test/review-pass.test.ts`: a read-only review stays read-only when the next /ship run starts.
- `test/ship-driver.test.ts` and `test/ship-control-flow.test.ts`: the driver's skipped steps, including plan-bound runs keeping Step 8.
