title: Codex model resolver: add gpt-6.2-astra (cheaper than the gpt-6-astra default)
body:
## Summary

gstack's Codex model resolver doesn't know about **`gpt-6.2-astra`** yet, and its default is still `gpt-6-astra`. OpenAI's pricing page lists 6.2 Astra as cheaper on every token class, with a much cheaper cached-input rate. Codex review traffic is mostly cached input, so this matters for anyone running Codex outside passes regularly.

## What I see (gstack 1.102.1.0)

- `scripts/resolve-codex-generation-model.ts:16`: `const CODEX_DEFAULT_MODEL: Model = 'gpt-6-astra';`
- `scripts/models.ts`: the model list has `gpt-6-astra` (line 27, plus the `^gpt-6-astra(-|$)` normaliser at line 82) but no `gpt-6.2-astra` entry.
- `bin/gstack-codex-probe select-model exec` prints `CODEX_SEL: gpt-6-astra`.

## OpenAI list prices (per 1M tokens, standard tier, from https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)

| Model | Input | Cached input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-6-astra | $10.00 | $1.00 | $50.00 |
| gpt-6.2-astra | $8.00 | $0.40 | $40.00 |

## Why it matters

In our own outside-review usage, about 85% of Codex input tokens are cached reads. Re-pricing a month of real review traffic at 6.2 rates comes to roughly a third less spend for the same reviews.

## Ask

1. Add `gpt-6.2-astra` to the known model list, with whatever normalisation/profile handling the other IDs get, so `GSTACK_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6.2-astra` resolves cleanly rather than falling into a generic profile.
2. Consider making it the default for Codex outside passes once you're happy with its review quality.

We haven't yet run a review on 6.2 through the Codex CLI. We'll report back here if it fails or behaves differently.

title: skill-route.log: routed events do not record the matched trigger or prompt length
body:
## What happened

I could not tell which of my `routed` events were false routes, because a `routed` line in `hooks/skill-route.log` does not say what matched or what kind of prompt it was. I was trying to audit about 140 routed events across 14 sessions in five days on gstack 1.101.0.0.

A `routed` line:

```text
2026-11-24T17:13:59.427Z session=<id> event=routed skill=review score=1 variant=name
```

A `no-route` line from the same log:

```text
2026-11-24T16:40:59.778Z session=<id> event=no-route reason=below-threshold chars=374 top=review:0.5
```

So `no-route` records the prompt length and the best candidate, but `routed` records neither the length nor the trigger phrase that matched. The hint text the model sees does name the trigger (`matched the installed /review trigger "look over my diff"`), but that lives only in the session transcript, not in the log. To judge a route afterwards I had to open each transcript and read the turn before the hint.

The docs say the log never holds prompt text, and I am not asking for that.

## The ask

Add fields that carry no prompt text to the `routed` line, matching what `no-route` already has:

- `chars=<prompt length>`
- `trigger="<matched trigger phrase>"`: this is gstack's own trigger string, not the person's words
- a coarse kind for the prompt, for example `kind=typed|agent-message|task-notification|other`, set from the wrapper check that already exists

With these, a reader could find routes of agent messages, or routes whose trigger matched a short prompt, from the log alone. It would also make reports like #4801 and #4802 checkable without sharing a transcript.

## Environment

- gstack 1.101.0.0, Claude Code 2.1.331, macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

title: /autoplan stops asking the owner again for changes his "do it" already approved (GST-3753)
body:
When the review rounds run out and the only plan edit is the recommendations the owner already took in his own words, /autoplan now finishes instead of raising another approval gate, and leaves one note saying no reviewer read that last revision. Why: a run answered "do it" twice still got a third gate of 63 items, three of them "accept the unreviewed changes" once per review phase, which only the owner could answer. Nothing to do: `gstack-autoplan rule` closes the note when someone wants it closed.
What changed - **No gate for approved changes at the round cap.** A revise at the cap that only incorporates recommendations the owner approved in his own words (each decision approved as recommended, none in an agent's own words) is accepted. The phases' changes are recorded as accepted with the reason "applied owner-approved recommendations at the round cap", the journal gets `unreviewed_at_cap`, and the revise prints one `UNREVIEWED:` line, then `APPROVED:`. - **A ruling closes that note.** `gstack-autoplan rule --out --revision --by --reason "" [--owner-ref :]` records the ruling (`unreviewed_ruled`), the way a ruled note closes a /ship finding after round two. gstack itself can't rule. - **Anything else still goes to the owner, once.** An override, an agent's own words or an edit with no accepted change still raises a gate, now with one item naming every phase that hit the cap instead of one per phase; its "reopen" option grants each of those phases a round. A phase that does review the revision (one newly in scope) still raises its findings. - **Cuts keep their answer by a stable id.** Each cut under "What it won't do yet" gets an id (`c1`, `c2`, ...) saved as `cut_ids` on `gate.json`; the next gate matches cuts by id (same words, or at least half their words shared), so renaming a command inside a cut no longer makes it a new question.
Tests New `test/autoplan-do-it-at-cap.test.ts` replays the reported run's shape: two "do it" answers then the cap give no third gate; the ruling closes the note; an override at the cap gives one item and an agent's own words on it still exit 3; a phase newly in scope still raises its finding; a renamed cut keeps its id and answer. All six fail on main. Existing delta-check tests now set up the case that still needs the check (an override), and the two round-cap tests expect one item for both phases.
Agent notes Repro: GSKI-1's run autoplan-embftp-20261124162738 (gstack v1.103.1.0), gate_rev 3, Captain answer exited 3 with OWNER_REPLY_REQUIRED on uc20-uc22 (per-phase cap items) and uc39 (renamed cut). Out of scope: gate letters past Z (#4798), the reviewer packet's 40,000-character limit.

title: gstack-pr-wait counts a cancelled check run that a newer run of the same check replaced as a failure, while gstack-ship-queue ready reads the same head as green
/autoplan stops asking the owner again for changes his "do it" already approved (GST-3753)
body:
When the review rounds run out and the only plan edit is the recommendations the owner already took in his own words, /autoplan now finishes instead of raising another approval gate, and leaves one note saying no reviewer read that last revision. Why: a run answered "do it" twice still got a third gate of 63 items, three of them "accept the unreviewed changes" once per review phase, which only the owner could answer. Nothing to do: `gstack-autoplan status` shows the note as open until `gstack-autoplan rule` closes it.
What changed - **No gate for approved changes at the round cap.** A revise at the cap whose incorporated and settled decisions were all approved as recommended in the owner's own words (none in an agent's own words, none carried unseen) is accepted. The phases' changes are recorded as accepted with the reason "applied owner-approved recommendations at the round cap", the journal gets `unreviewed_at_cap`, and the revise prints one `UNREVIEWED:` line, then `APPROVED:`. - **A ruling closes that note.** `gstack-autoplan rule --out --revision --by --reason "" [--owner-ref :]` records the ruling (`unreviewed_ruled`), the way a ruled note closes a /ship finding after round two. gstack itself can't rule. `gstack-autoplan status` marks each such change `unreviewed open` or `unreviewed ruled by `. - **Anything else still goes to the owner, once.** An override, an agent's own words or an edit with no accepted change still raises a gate, now with one item naming every phase that hit the cap instead of one per phase; its "reopen" option grants each of those phases a round, and the gate's cost line counts all of them. A phase that does review the revision (one newly in scope) still raises its findings. - **Cuts keep their answer by a stable id.** Each cut under "What it won't do yet" gets an id (`c1`, `c2`, ...) saved as `cut_ids` on `gate.json`. A cut keeps its id only when its words are unchanged or differ only in command names (a backticked name, `gstack-*`, `--flag`, `/command`), so renaming a command no longer makes it a new question, while a changed hyphenated word, number or version does. A dropped id is never handed to another cut.

title: /autoplan stops asking the owner again for changes his "do it" already approved (GST-3753)
body:
When the review rounds run out and every decision in the last revision is a recommendation the owner already took in his own words, /autoplan now finishes instead of raising another approval gate, and leaves one note saying no reviewer read that last revision.
Why: a run answered "do it" twice still got a third gate of 63 items, three of them "accept the unreviewed changes" once per review phase, which only the owner could answer.
Nothing to do: `gstack-autoplan status` shows the note as open until `gstack-autoplan rule` closes it.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![At the round cap, owner-approved recommendations finish with one UNREVIEWED note instead of a third gate](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/u-rkaNAXXfL-bhxZirLOKDkVNLGzoc-vWqrL3gn7ubo.png)

At the round cap, owner-approved recommendations finish with one UNREVIEWED note instead of a third gate.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: At the round cap, owner-approved recommendations finish with one UNREVIEWED note instead of a third gate</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · docs/unattended.md § Carry-forward at beca1d6 · source text
+++ After · docs/unattended.md § Carry-forward on this branch · source text
@@ ⋯ 29 unchanged ⋯ @@
   decision row gets `carried_under: do it`, the output prints
   `CARRIED_UNDER_DO_IT:` per item, and the approval record lists them as
   "taken under "do it", not seen by the owner". `rec` carries no new item.
+- **Unreviewed post-cap delta.** A "plan changed after the <phases> cap" item
+  (one per revise, naming every capped phase) recommending `a` (accept) is read by one reviewer before it carries. `CARRY_CHECK:` names the attempt and
-- **Unreviewed post-cap delta.** A "plan changed after <phase> cap" item
-  recommending `a` (accept) is read by one reviewer before it carries. `CARRY_CHECK:` names the attempt and
   the prompt (the delta against `plan-at-gate.r<m>.md`, the accepted changes,
   the full plan); the run reserves the estimate in `spend.json` and refuses
   when it is over `--carry-check-cap <usd>` (default 5) or the run's cap.
@@ ⋯ 6 unchanged ⋯ @@
   check is void, its reservation released and the gate left for the owner,
   when the owner answers the gate, the plan is revised, a new gate is
   written, or the delta changed after dispatch.
+
+At the round cap, a `revise` that only incorporates recommendations the owner
+took in his own words (each decision approved as recommended, none in an
+agent's own words) raises no gate at all: the owner already approved exactly
+those changes. The capped phases' deltas are recorded `accepted` with
+`basis: applied owner-approved recommendations at the round cap`, the journal
+gets `unreviewed_at_cap`, and `revise` prints one `UNREVIEWED:` line naming
+the revision, the phases that never read it, the decisions and the owner's
+words, then `APPROVED:`. That line is an open note, as a finding /ship ships
+with after round two is: `gstack-autoplan rule --out <dir> --revision <k> --by
+<ruler> --reason "<why>" [--owner-ref <thread>:<message>]` records a Captain's
+or the owner's ruling on it (`unreviewed_ruled`; gstack cannot rule on its
+own note, an agent rules only by relaying one with `--owner-ref`, and a
+ruling stands once recorded; a retry of the same ruling is safe). The exported
+record names who ruled and the owner ref, never the reason text. `gstack-autoplan status` shows each such
+change as `unreviewed open` or `unreviewed ruled by <who>`. A phase that does review the revision (one newly in scope) still
+raises its findings at a gate, and a revise that takes anything else (an
+override, an agent's own words, an edit with no `--incorporates`) keeps the
+one cap item above.
+
+A cut under `### What it won't do yet` carries its answer to the next gate only
+while its words are unchanged (case and punctuation aside). Any reworded cut, a
+renamed command included, is a new item and the owner is asked about it once:
+a wrong carry would hide a scope cut from him, while a re-ask costs one question.
 
 Carried rows keep `answered_by: agent:gstack-autoplan` and name their source
 (`carried_gate_from`, `carried_gate_rev`, `carried_answered_by`);
~~~

</details>

- **No gate for approved changes at the round cap.** A revise at the cap whose incorporated and settled decisions were all approved as recommended in the owner's own words (none in an agent's own words, none taken unseen) is accepted. The phases' changes are recorded as accepted with the reason "applied owner-approved recommendations at the round cap", the journal gets `unreviewed_at_cap`, and the revise prints one `UNREVIEWED:` line, then `APPROVED:`.
- **A ruling closes that note.** `gstack-autoplan rule --out <dir> --revision <k> --by <ruler> --reason "<why>" [--owner-ref <thread>:<message>]` records the ruling (`unreviewed_ruled`), the way a ruled note closes a /ship finding after round two. gstack itself can't rule, an agent rules only by relaying one with `--owner-ref`, a ruling stands once recorded, and retrying the same ruling after an interruption is safe. `gstack-autoplan status` marks each such change `unreviewed open` or `unreviewed ruled by <who>`. The exported record and the public copy name who ruled and the owner ref, never the reason text.
- **Anything else still goes to the owner, once.** An override, an agent's own words or an edit with no accepted change still raises a gate, now with one item naming every phase that hit the cap instead of one per phase; its "reopen" option grants each of those phases a round, and the gate's cost line counts all of them. A gate written before this change, with one item per phase, still settles each phase on its own. A phase that does review the revision (one newly in scope) still raises its findings.
- **Cuts are unchanged:** an earlier answer to a cut is reused only while its words are unchanged, so a renamed command is asked once. Reusing an answer for a different cut would hide a scope decision from the owner; asking again costs one question.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A run answered "do it" twice still stopped at a third gate of 63 items, three of them "accept the unreviewed changes" once per review phase, and only the owner could answer it. Now the owner's "do it" finishes the plan at the round cap, and the one revision nobody re-read stays visible as an open note until someone rules on it.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change is limited to `gstack-autoplan` and its libraries (revise, gate, budget, export, status), plus the docs that describe them. A revise that takes anything other than owner-approved recommendations still raises the same gate as before, which the existing round-cap and delta-check tests cover with updated expectations (test/autoplan-carry.test.ts, test/autoplan-budget.test.ts); this rung is script ran: the new and adjacent tests pass and CI is green at this head.

</details>

One more round-one finding, that a revision taken at the cap stays unreviewed until someone rules on it, is by design and was ruled a note. Round two found no blocking issues. Its two notes: no test yet covers a settled change recorded beside an incorporated one, and three comments still say the decisions list holds only incorporated changes (lib/autoplan-state.ts:34, lib/autoplan-budget.ts:208, docs/unattended.md:842). title: /ship's docs check updates your project's doc templates again (GST-3740)
body:
/ship's documentation check edits the docs it finds in your project again, including docs written as templates such as `handbook/*.md.tmpl`, and still never edits `SKILL.md` or `SKILL.md.tmpl`.
Why: a recent change limited the check to gstack's own doc folders, so in other projects it stopped and asked instead of fixing a stale page; that turned main's paid release check red and is holding the next stable release.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

If your project keeps its docs somewhere other than `README.md`, `docs/` or `bench/README.md`, for example as `handbook/reference/*.md.tmpl` sources, /ship's Step 14.5 docs check found the stale page and then refused to touch it. It reported "Documentation: blocked" and asked for a decision. #4779 caused this when it added one line telling the check to edit only gstack's own three doc locations. The check now edits the docs roots, sources and generated outputs it discovers in your project, as it did before #4779. It still treats `SKILL.md` and `SKILL.md.tmpl` edits after review as code, because those cost another review round. The driver summary in `ship/DRIVER.md` says the same thing.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

This touches only the Step 14.5 instructions in `ship/sections/documentation.md(.tmpl)` and `ship/DRIVER.md(.tmpl)`, plus a changelog fragment. No code or test changed. Both generated files match their templates (`gen:skill-docs` reports them fresh). The paid gate case that went red, ship-docsync-completion, passes at this head; that is a live run of the real behavior, not a prose check.

</details>

<details><summary>Deferred findings</summary>

Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues.

- Deferred: CRITICAL `bin/gstack-docs-candidate:267` The SKILL.md exclusion is prose only; snapshot and compare do not enforce it.

title: gstack picks the newest Opus, Fable, Sol and Astra everywhere (GST-3760)
body:
gstack now uses the newest model of each family it picks from: the Codex second-model review defaults to `gpt-6.2-astra`, plan-review tiers move to `claude-fable-5-2` and `gpt-6.2-sol`, and eval judges to `claude-fable-5-2`.
Why: Garry's rule that gstack always uses the latest Astra, Sol, Fable or Opus; one table now holds each family's newest model, so the next release is a one-line change.
Nothing to do: models you pinned in your own config keep working.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

gstack named its models in dozens of places, so each new release of Opus, Fable, Sol or Astra left some of them on the old one. Now `lib/model-families.ts` holds the newest model of each family, and the tier catalog, the eval capture and judge defaults, the Codex default, the read-only Astra retry after a cyber-policy refusal, the census arms, the eval frontier lists and a new `{{NEWEST_MODEL:<family>}}` skill placeholder all read it. Setup, install, doctor, the codex and eval-plan skills and the docs name the newest ids, and `claude-fable-5-2` gets its price row ($8 in, $40 out, $0.20 cache reads per million tokens).

A new test fails when runtime code or skill text names an older Opus, Fable, Sol or Astra. History (tests, CHANGELOG, design and eval records) is exempt, and each file that must still recognize an older id (prompt-profile names, pricing, frozen-plan text) is listed with its reason.

Three things stay put on purpose. The arm benchmark keeps the `claude-fable-5-1` judge its frozen plan and calibration name. Every GPT-6 Astra release maps to the existing Astra prompt profile, so generated Codex skills keep the same profile. Which family speaks as the second voice is unchanged (Astra).

The model freshness check now hashes both files that define the catalog, read at one commit, and eval selection treats a change to the family table like a change to the eval model file.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The README promises gstack runs on frontier models, and Garry asked on 2026-11-24 that gstack "should always be using latest astra, sol, fable or opus".

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Every caller that used to hard-code a model id now reads the same table, so the risk is a caller that still names an old id or reads the table wrong. The new guard test scans runtime code and skill text for older ids (script ran: it failed on main with 78 offenders and passes here), and the Codex overlay test confirms the newest Astra still resolves to a prompt profile.

</details>

<details><summary>Eval Results</summary>

- Every other paid case is deferred to the next release gate on main.

title: browse: no supported way to keep untrusted page loads off loopback and private addresses (proxy bypass always includes loopback)
body:
## What happens

An agent drives `browse` to read untrusted pages (social posts, vendor pages). We want those page loads unable to reach the host's own services or its private network. browse allows loopback and RFC 1918 on purpose (`browse/src/url-validation.ts`: "Localhost and private IPs are allowed"), which is right for QA of local dev servers. But there is no supported way to turn that off for an untrusted-reading session:

- `browse goto http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` navigates to a local service.
- A filtering egress proxy can't close the gap. With `BROWSE_PROXY_URL` set, `resolveProxy` always appends `localhost,127.0.0.1,[::1]` to the Chromium bypass list (`withLoopbackBypass`, `browse/src/proxy-config.ts`), and the CLI forwards that as `BROWSE_PROXY_BYPASS` to the daemon (`proxyServerEnv`, `browse/src/cli.ts`). Loopback navigations therefore always go direct, and a user-set `BROWSE_PROXY_BYPASS` is overwritten.
- On a root container where user namespaces are unavailable, Chromium also runs with `--no-sandbox` (`browser-manager.ts`). That is expected, but it raises the cost of a page reaching local services.

Checked on gstack 8b684985 (Linux container, root, headless).

## Ask

Either of these would do:

1. A public-only navigation mode, for example `BROWSE_PUBLIC_ONLY=1`. It would extend the existing `classifyAddress` checks (literal, DNS answers, redirects, page-driven navigations) to refuse loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT 100.64/10 and the other non-public ranges for top-level and subresource requests.
2. Or a switch that leaves loopback off the Chromium bypass list, so a filtering proxy sees every request. For example, honour a user-set `BROWSE_PROXY_BYPASS`, or add `BROWSE_PROXY_LOOPBACK=proxy`.

Prior art: #17 (closed) covered SSRF generally. This issue asks for an opt-in mode, not a change to the default.

title: Docs: you don't need to cut back on MCP servers for accuracy, up to about 300 tools
body:
The gbrain guide now answers "Do you need to cut back on MCP servers?": not for accuracy up to about 300 tools, as long as Claude Code's tool search stays on, with each agent's numbers from a November 2026 test.
Why: people trim MCP servers expecting better tool picks; the test found accuracy held, while turning tool search off cost Claude Code accuracy and doubled its cost.
Nothing to do as a reader. If you use gbrain with Codex or OpenClaw, register it with `gbrain serve --surface full`.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **USING_GBRAIN_WITH_GSTACK.md** gets a new section under "MCP registration for Claude Code". Claude Code with tool search on: 94.6% right at 30 tools, 92.9% at 300; with it off, 85.4% at 300 and $0.240 per request against $0.117. Codex (97.5% to 95.4%) and OpenClaw (98.3% to 98.8%) held up too, but rarely used tools that gbrain unlocked through `request_tools` (13 of 131 and 0 of 131 trials), so the section tells their gbrain users to serve the full tool set. Hermes and Pi held up as well.
- It keeps the reasons that still apply, labelled as such: cost (Claude Code $0.076 per request at 30 tools, $0.117 at 300) and security (each server sees what the agent sends it).
- **BROWSER.md**'s "Why CLI over MCP" now says its reasons are cost, speed and reliability, not accuracy, and links to the new section.
- A changelog.d entry.

No skill, template or prompt text gave pruning advice before this, so no skill changed and `bun run gen:skill-docs` produced no diff.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

gstack had no advice on how many MCP tools is too many. The numbers come from our November 2026 MCP-at-scale benchmark across five agent harnesses, and every number in the guide was checked against its published results. The guide carries the numbers itself.

title: ship preflight: DEPS_MISSING hint 'npm ci' fails under npm 12 for git dependencies (EALLOWGIT)
body:
## What happens

`gstack-ship-preflight --tests-only` in a fresh worktree stops with `DEPS_MISSING` and names `npm ci` as the fix (`lib/ship-preflight.ts`, `depsInstall()`: `package-lock.json` maps to `npm ci`).

With npm 12 that command fails when `package.json` has a git dependency (here a `git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#<full sha>` pin):

```
npm error code EALLOWGIT
npm error Fetching packages of type "git" have been disabled
npm error Refusing to fetch "<pkg>@git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#<sha>"
```

npm 12 defaults `allow-git` to off. `npm ci --allow-git=all` installs, and the preflight then runs.

## Expected

When the lockfile has a git-resolved package and npm is 12 or later, the hint names a command that works, e.g. `npm ci --allow-git=all`, or the stop message says the git dependency needs `allow-git`.

## Environment

gstack 1.103.1.0 (8b684985), npm 12.2.0, Node 24, Linux.

title: v1.103.3.0 release
body:
v1.103.3.0 ships 14 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each.

It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.

<details><summary>Release notes</summary>

- ### Fixed (#4786)
- Screenshots, PDFs and page dumps taken in the Aside browser are no longer lost before you can see them. (#4786)
- ### Fixed (#4787)
- `/cso --comprehensive` can now prepare npm apps whose lockfile lists bundled dependencies, such as Next.js apps on Tailwind CSS 4. (#4787)
- A first version's ruled-out line now counts only against the one reply it cites. (#4800)
- A first version's plan can say the owner ruled something out, and that line now counts only when he actually said it. (#4789)
- /ship's documentation check updates your repo's own docs again, including docs written as templates. (#4810)
- ### Fixed (#4798)
- /autoplan approval asks with more than 26 choices now label them AA, AB and so on instead of punctuation. (#4798)
- /land-and-deploy no longer leaves an auto-merge request behind or deletes `main`. (#4795)
- When the branch you push moved on the remote since your last fetch, the pre-push credential guard now tells you to run `git fetch` instead of failing with ENOBUFS or telling you to rotate a credential that is already on the remote. (#4794)
- ### Fixed (#4796)
- The pre-merge secrets check now scans an added file over 16 MiB instead of failing it unread. (#4796)
- On Windows, an update no longer deletes your brain-aware skills when `python3` is the Microsoft Store alias. (#4793)

</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

Release stamp for v1.103.3.0, made by `gstack-release-stamp open` (`gstack-restamp --release`) on origin/main 69a1644c20fa: VERSION, the package.json version, the CHANGELOG and the release outputs.

Folds: changelog.d/aside-screenshots-survive-the-script.md, changelog.d/cso-npm-bundled-dependencies.md, changelog.d/first-versions-bind-owner-ruling-to-one-reply.md, changelog.d/first-versions-check-ruled-out-line-against-owner-replies.md, changelog.d/fix-ship-docs-audit-edits-authored-doc-templates.md, changelog.d/gate-choice-labels-past-z.md, changelog.d/land-and-deploy-never-arms-auto-merge.md, changelog.d/prepush-guard-scans-only-pushed-commits.md, changelog.d/secrets-check-reads-large-added-files-in-parts-gst-3665.md, changelog.d/windows-python3-stub-and-long-test-commands.md

Land it with `gstack-ship-queue land --pr <this PR> --pin 662f2737e84d6376d93c1b860b62fee1ab14555c` once its checks are green. land checks that this head is exactly the release stamp of its merge base (RELEASE_STAMP_INVALID otherwise), so a release PR needs no /ship receipt.

</details>

title: Next release's notes list each change once, with no stray headings
body:
The next release's notes now show 11 plain lines, one per change, instead of 14 lines with four stray "### Fixed" entries. The CHANGELOG no longer repeats "### Fixed" four times.

Four changelog entries began with their own heading, and one Windows entry held two separate changes, so the notes miscounted. This edits only those five entries. Nothing for readers to do.

## What changed

- The Aside screenshot, /cso bundled-dependency, /autoplan choice-label and large-file secrets-check entries drop their `### Fixed` heading and leading bullet, matching the other six entries.
- The Windows entry from #4793 is split in two: the Store `python3` fix and the Git Bash long test command fix (issue #4773) each get their own line. Both still name #4793, the pull request that made them.

## Tests

The release-notes and CHANGELOG code from main ran on this branch: 11 lines, each with its pull request, and no headings in the new CHANGELOG section. The changelog fragment, release notes and docs-only tests passed (82 tests).

## Documentation

Scope: the 5 changelog.d release-note fragments changed between 69a1644c and a2ab25d7 (heading and bullet wrapping removed so each change is one plain line, and the Windows entry split into two lines, one per change). Result: current. No README, docs/, SKILL.md or template references these fragments' wording, so no other doc needed an update, and no files were edited. Debt: none found.

title: Let an owner's ruling ship a small edit made after /ship's final review (GST-3775)
body:
An owner can now rule that a small edit made after /ship's read-only final review ships as a disclosed note, and finish accepts exactly that file at exactly the ruled bytes instead of forcing a whole new /ship.
This unblocks teams that hit "behavior, tests or build inputs changed since review" over a one-line test change (garrytan/gbrain#10256), while keeping the review stop for every other edit.
Nothing to do on merge; the changelog fragment is in changelog.d/edit-ruling-fixes.md.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- `gstack-approvals rule --finding edit:<path> --head <stop head>` records the owner's ruling for one edited path.
- `gstack-ship-release finish` routes a ruled path as `RULED_EDIT:` only when the ruled head is HEAD or an ancestor of it, the file's mode and bytes in the tree finish routes equal the ruled head's, and no later first-parent commit touches it. Anything else prints `RULED_EDIT_REFUSED: <path> (<why>)` and finish still stops.
- Both `git ls-tree` lookups check their exit status and must name exactly the routed path. An unreadable path, a missing file, and any spelling that holds a replacement character (U+FFFD, which a non-UTF-8 filename turns into) are refused, so a ruling can never clear an edit to a different file.
- An edit ruling that cleared nothing prints `RULED_NOTE: … (no RULED_EDIT at this head; not applied)`.
- The `gstack-review-plan --post-review` stop prints one paste-safe, shell-quoted command per path the PR itself edited since the final review, and names deletions and whitespace paths apart.
- docs/ship-policy.md#ruled-edits documents the rule, and docs/review-policy.md names it in its transitions table.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

GBRA-795 hit this on garrytan/gbrain#10256. After the final review, the owner ruled "ship it with the note" for a one-line test timeout change, but no command recorded that ruling in a form finish read, so the only way forward was a whole fresh /ship.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only /ship's finish route and the post-review stop text change: without an `edit:` ruling, finish takes exactly the path it took before, because the new block runs only over rulings whose finding starts with `edit:` (lib/ship-release.ts route, read and covered by test/ship-finish-edit-ruling.test.ts, which fails on main). The full free suite passed in CI at 91106aa (run 45521890768, 39514 tests).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. The documentation audit found the branch's docs accurate and made no edits.

**Scope:** the committed diff afb68ac..91106aa on `edit-ruling-fixes` (9 commits, 9 files). There were no staged, unstaged or new files. The audit read docs/ship-policy.md, docs/review-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md and changelog.d/edit-ruling-fixes.md, and checked them against bin/gstack-approvals, bin/gstack-review-plan and lib/ship-release.ts.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/ship-policy.md: current. The new `#ruled-edits` section matches finish's RULED_EDIT and RULED_EDIT_REFUSED routing.
- docs/review-policy.md: current. The transitions row names `gstack-approvals rule --finding edit:<path>` and links the ruled-edits anchor.
- docs/troubleshooting.md: current, but it has no entry for the new refusal line (see the gap below).
- changelog.d/edit-ruling-fixes.md: reviewed only. It is owned by the parent.

**Coverage gaps and diagram drift:** `edit:<path>` rulings are documented as reference (ship-policy, review-policy, the approvals help text) and as a how-to (the ship-policy command block and the printed stop line). The common gap: `RULED_EDIT_REFUSED:` has no docs/troubleshooting.md entry, and its message points to ship-policy.md#ruled-edits instead. There was no diagram drift.

</details>

title: Install gstack's shipping skill as /gstack-ship so Claude Code's own /ship stops hiding it (#4775)
body:
gstack's shipping skill now installs as `/gstack-ship`, because Claude Code keeps the name `/ship` for its own built-in and silently drops gstack's. Upgrading removes gstack's old `ship` entry and leaves your own `ship` skill alone. The resume command and most recovery messages now say `/gstack-ship`; nothing to do but upgrade. This replaces #4813, which ran out of budget before its last fixes.
What changed - The skill's installed name is `gstack-ship` in both prefix modes and on every host. Its folder (`ship/`), its internal id, its saved records, state folders, `--for ship` and the `gstack-ship-*` commands keep their names, and `disabled_skills: ship` still turns it off. - Printed recovery and next-step lines (resume, budget handoff, merge-queue next steps, result-code fixes, the early Greptile PR body, gate-disposition messages), OpenClaw's injected pipeline text and `llms.txt` say `/gstack-ship`. A few review-limit and ruled-edit messages still say `/ship` and are listed under Follow-ups. - `gstack-relink` and `setup` no longer serve a shared cached `ship` render made by an older gstack version (it still says `/ship`); they serve the checkout's copy until this version renders again. A per-install render that fails to refresh keeps its old name, and setup warns about it. - Because QA keeps its short name (`qa`) in a short-name install, the shipping skill's QA step reads `../gstack-qa/…` only when that file exists and otherwise `../qa/…`. - `gstack-relink` now says so when its install registry file is missing, no longer reports a user's own `ship` skill as skipped, and reports old `ship` copies it moves aside on upgrade as gstack's old entries.
Why Claude Code 2.1.331 drops any user skill named `ship` at startup ("Not loaded: a custom /ship"), so typing `/ship` ran Claude Code's version and gstack's never loaded (#4775).
Blast radius Install and upgrade paths for every host: `setup`, `gstack-relink`, the Claude render cache and the skill-name helpers. Anyone who typed `/ship` for gstack's skill now types `/gstack-ship`; Claude Code's own `/ship` is untouched.
Issues Refs #4775
Follow-ups Known gaps left for a follow-up, each below the blocking floor: 1. A per-install render kept after a failed re-render still says `name: ship` and `/ship --resume` until setup succeeds (`bin/gstack-skill-name.sh:41`, `setup:1285` warns). Same as today's stale-cache behavior. 2. The short-name upgrade's cleanup of the old `ship/` folder (`bin/gstack-relink:445`) also removes a symlink a user added there if it points into gstack's checkout. It is the existing cleanup helper main already uses for retired skills; the link's target stays. 3. Recovery text that still says `/ship`: `lib/ship-release.ts:471`, `bin/gstack-review-plan:315`, `lib/review-depth.ts:464` and `:477` (a pinned reviewer source, so it needs a no-loss replay), `lib/ship-preflight.ts:72` and `:77`, `lib/result-codes-release.ts:193`, `runaway-stopper/templates/successor-brief.md:11`, `ship/sections/review-army.md.tmpl` lines 17, 80 and 263, help text in `gstack-approvals`, `gstack-base-red` and `gstack-capy-session`, and `capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md` lines 41 and 57. 4. `test/helpers/native-auto-decide.ts:165` still matches only the old "/review then /ship" notice wording. 5. After a short-name upgrade on render or Windows installs, an empty `~/.claude/skills/ship/sections/` folder can be left behind. 6. In short-name mode, removing the old `ship/` entry depends on `gstack-relink` succeeding; `setup` only warns when it fails. 7. If a user has their own `gstack-qa` skill with `sections/exploratory.md` in a short-name install, the shipping skill's QA step reads it instead of `../qa` (`scripts/resolvers/qa.ts:17`). gstack's own leftover `gstack-qa` is removed by setup. 8. `crew/docs/captain.md:128` links to shipping headings that no longer exist. 9. On a Windows copy install in short-name mode, migrating the old `ship/` entry leaves its copied asset folders behind with no SKILL.md; Claude Code ignores them. 10. The dots harness (`lib/harness-register.ts:99`) installs into its own skills folder, not Claude Code's, so Claude Code's reserved `/ship` does not apply there and nothing changed for it.

title: make-pdf: bold Swiss-style layout by default, --style plain keeps the old look (GST-3770)
body:
make-pdf now prints in a bold Swiss-style layout by default: black bars for section headings, small red sub-headings in a left column beside the text, a large cover title, and a shorter, easier line. Generated documents should look designed, not default; Garry picked this look over today's in two rounds of blind comparisons. Nothing to do: pass `--style plain` to get exactly the PDF you got before. Word output always uses the plain look.
What changed ![The same CONTRIBUTING.md page with --style plain (left, unchanged) and the new swiss default (right)](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/hCmmveuUfQQOaw-hEDHDUvdxmimDkFrAHGnK6Da17Gs.png) The same CONTRIBUTING.md page, plain on the left (byte-for-byte today's look) and the new default on the right: the section heading becomes a black bar, the sub-heading moves into the left column, and the text column holds about 70 characters a line instead of about 83. - New `--style swiss|plain` flag on `generate` and `preview`, with swiss as the default. A bad or missing value exits 1 with a clear message, and the value is case-insensitive. - Swiss layout: h2 headings are full-width black bars; h3 sub-headings sit in a 1.9in left column next to the text they introduce and stay on the same page as it; body text is capped at about 5.1in; tables, code, figures and wide images span the full width; the cover is a black title block sized to the title and to the real page size and margins. - Margins default to 0.7in / 0.75in / 0.85in / 0.75in under swiss and stay 1in under plain; `--margins` and the per-side flags still win. - Sub-headings inside raw HTML, quotes or lists stay in normal flow, so they never jump out of their section. - `--to docx` always renders with plain, so Word output is unchanged. - `--style plain` CSS is pinned byte for byte against golden files captured from main.
Why Garry asked for "even more graphic design forward designs" after rejecting a wider-margin draft. In blind pairs he chose this layout over today's every time, and he saw no difference between a 1.6in and a 1.9in left column, so the tested 1.9in ships.
Blast radius Only make-pdf's own render path changes: `printCss`/`render` have no other callers in the repo (grep read), plain output is pinned by golden-file tests, and the generated HTML body for CONTRIBUTING, skills, howto and ETHOS is byte-identical before and after the last fix round (script ran). Word output is forced to plain and its document.xml is identical with or without swiss (test ran).
Pre-Landing Review Three review passes on this PR. Round 1 and round 2 found and fixed: sub-headings inside quotes, lists or raw HTML being pulled to the top of the page; image paragraphs losing full width; long one-word sub-headings overprinting; covers spilling to page 2 on small page boxes; Word output picking up the swiss cover size. Each fix has a test that failed before it. The final read-only review found the open items below, which ship as notes and get a follow-up PR right after this lands. Second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol): completed, findings listed below.
Deferred findings Blocking findings in code this PR did not change (review scope: frozen). They stay on this PR and are not filed as issues. - Deferred: CRITICAL `make-pdf/src/render.ts:156` HTML export has no viewport meta, so the 48em one-column rule never fires on phones
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `make-pdf/src/print-css.ts:126` a multi-value --margins becomes invalid per-side CSS under swiss - INFORMATIONAL `make-pdf/src/style-swiss.ts:57` an h3 above a landscape-promoted image stays floated on the portrait page
Known open issues (follow-up PR) - A `###` sub-heading directly before a mermaid or excalidraw diagram pairs the diagram into the left-column wrapper, so the diagram renders about 5.1in wide and offset (and a landscape-promoted diagram lands inside the wrapper). - A sub-heading with explicit `
` line breaks reserves one line, so it can overprint the next heading. - A paragraph with text and one inline image is treated as image-only and goes full width. - Screen (`--to html`) body text is 11pt.
Design Review Design Review: static (no preview declared). Two blind A/B rounds with Garry chose the layout and the field width; no model ranked anything.
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed in a way the selector gates; no paid evals ran.
Documentation **Status:** updated. One factual edit, no blockers. **Scope:** 5 commits and 25 files since 2eb3e5ad (the make-pdf Swiss default style, the `--style swiss|plain` flag, new swiss margin defaults, plain-style golden CSS fixtures, .gitattributes), plus an unstaged edit to the changelog fragment. Reviewed README.md, docs/skills.md, docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md, docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/why-gstack.md, docs/install.md and make-pdf/SKILL.md.tmpl. **Documentation health** - docs/skills.md: Updated. The /make-pdf section now describes the Swiss default look, `--style plain`, and that Word output always uses plain. - README.md: Current - docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md: Current - make-pdf/SKILL.md.tmpl: Current (already updated on the branch) - docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md: Current **Coverage debt:** `--style` is documented in the skill reference (SKILL.md.tmpl, the CLI help) and in a summary sentence in docs/skills.md. It is not mentioned in the README skill table or in the how-to guide. These are common gaps, with no critical gaps. **Diagram drift:** none found.

title: Stop three gstack tests from failing at random in CI (GST-3655)
body:
Three of gstack's own tests failed now and then on unchanged code. They now pass on every run, so a red check means something really broke.
Why: a contributor should only see a failed check when their change caused it.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Contributors kept seeing red checks on PRs that never touched these areas. Each failure had its own cause:

- **QA handoff re-read check.** The exploratory QA test counted a re-read of HANDOFF.md as a partial read when the agent asked for it from line 1 with no line limit. That request reads the whole file, so it now counts as a full read. The real captured run that failed is kept as a passing replay next to the existing captures that should still fail, and reads that start later, set a limit or pass the line as text are still flagged.
- **QA-only browser cleanup.** A headless browser started its terminal helper only on its first 60-second check. When the test cleaned up before that, there was no record of the helper yet, so cleanup could not prove the browser was gone. Cleanup now finds unrecorded helpers by their launch flag and working folder, fails with a clear message when it can't tell, and starts over if the record appears while it is cleaning up.
- **Office Hours abort test.** After killing the process group, the test now waits up to 2 seconds for the killed processes to leave the process table before it checks.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Rerun a failed test once and mark it flaky; flaky tests get fixed in a daily pass." These three were the worst open entries on the list of flaky tests we track, as of 2026-11-24, and two of them had failed more than once.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only test code and test fixtures change, plus one changelog fragment, so nothing that ships to users is touched. The QA cleanup helper is used only by the QA-only tests (file read: test/helpers/qa-only-cleanup.ts callers), and its new branches each have a test that failed on the old helper and passes now (script ran).

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation needed an update for this branch.

**Scope:** base 719b1f59 to head 51967373 on flaky-fixes-2026-11-24, with no staged, unstaged or untracked files. The branch changes 7 files: 6 test files and a changelog.d fragment. They cover the qa-callers HANDOFF.md re-read with `offset: 1`, the QA-only browser cleanup that runs before the terminal agent has started, and the Office Hours abort test's wait for the killed process.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: current. Its test-only timing knobs are unchanged.
- docs/TEST_PORTFOLIO.md: current. The qa-exploratory-callers row still matches.
- docs/BROWSER_INTERNALS.md: current. Only the test helper changed, not how the daemon owns its terminal agent.
- docs/evals/headroom-diagnosis-2026-10.md: current. Its census replay reference is still valid.

**Coverage debt:** none, because there is no new public surface. **Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test --timeout=30000 test/qa-exploratory-callers.test.ts test/office-hours-attempt.test.ts`: exit 0, 174 tests ran.
- [x] `bun test --timeout=30000 test/qa-only-cleanup.test.ts -t 'unconfirmed|owned state'`: exit 0, 10 tests ran.
- [x] New QA cleanup tests (`unrecorded-terminal`, `unlisted-agents`, and the headless daemon cases `no-terminal` and `published-mid-cleanup`) failed on the old helper and pass with the fix.
- [x] The new passing-replay test for the HANDOFF.md read failed on main's helper and passes with the fix.
- [ ] The Office Hours failure did not reproduce locally (0 of 40 runs, and 0 of 25 under load), so that repair is plausible but not proven. CI and the daily pass will show whether it recurs.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking bar (informational or test-gap items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- `test/helpers/qa-only-cleanup.ts:58`: no test covers a terminal reservation that stays at pid 0; cleanup would retry until its deadline and report the generic deadline message.
- `test/helpers/qa-only-cleanup.ts:80`: no test covers "terminal agent <pid> has no readable working directory"; a live agent owned by another user now makes cleanup fail closed.
- Two informational security notes (`sf-7ea0b43f3db5`, `sf-5fbb09b9ce39`), details recorded privately.

title: Run newer Claude Code and Codex in CI, and read the Astra model from the registry (GST-3801)
body:
CI now runs Claude Code 2.1.326 and Codex 0.172.0, which know gstack's newest default models, and the Capy installer reads its Codex model from `lib/model-families.ts`. Why: the old pins priced the default judge as an older Fable and had no GPT-6.2 metadata, and the installer named the Astra id by hand. Heads-up: the test harness's version moves to 8, so every paid case starts a new pass-rate series.
What changed CI's Claude Code didn't know claude-fable-5-2, the default eval judge, and CI's Codex had no metadata for gpt-6.2-sol or gpt-6.2-astra. The image now installs Claude Code 2.1.326 (npm `stable`) and Codex 0.172.0 (latest, and above the 0.170.0 floor gstack's Codex hooks need). Both binaries include those model ids, and Codex 0.172.0 answered on both GPT-6.2 models in a smoke call. The Codex boundary case now reads its expected version from the Dockerfile, so the case and the image can't drift apart. The test harness needed three fixes to run on Claude Code 2.1.326, all found by this PR's first paid screen (run 45574111261, 7 cases red 2/2): - 2.1.326 asks before using an `--add-dir` folder it hasn't seen, and the prompt defaults to exit. The seeded PTY config now pre-trusts the harness's own disposable run directory. This fixes the four plan-review timeouts, and it is why the harness version moves to 8. - 2.1.326's own startup Git calls add `core.alternateRefsCommand` and `diff.autoRefreshIndex`. The shared-code read-only check now recognizes those calls as Claude's, using argv captured from the screen, so it no longer counts them as the skill's. - The 2.1.326 binary is 371 MB, past the bootstrap check's 256 MiB limit. That limit is now 1 GiB. `bin/gstack-capy-install` reads the Codex setup model from the astra row of `lib/model-families.ts`. A checkout without that file (an older revision) keeps setup's own default, and a file whose astra row can't be read fails setup before either host runs. `docs/capy-install.md` describes both cases. The default judge's move to claude-fable-5-2 was checked against the labelled controls next to its callers: 18 inputs all agreed with their labels (plan-decision 4, DX peer-comparison 3, redaction semantic pass 11, which also agreed on 5.1 as a pair). The record, and the callers that still have no labelled outputs, are in `test/fixtures/judge-calibration/README.md`. The arm benchmark keeps its pinned 5.1 judge.
Why These are the three follow-ups from the newest-model bump in #4811: the CLI pins lagged the models gstack now defaults to, the judge change needed a check against labelled outputs, and the installer was the last place naming the Astra id by hand.
Blast radius The pins change only the CI image, so every paid case runs on the new CLIs. The harness fixes change only test helpers, and on Claude Code 2.1.292 they change nothing (that version never asked about `--add-dir` folders). The harness version bump resets every case's pass-rate series. The installer change affects Capy machines running `install.sh`; `test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts` covers the registry read, a relative root, a checkout without the registry and an unreadable registry.
Pre-Landing Review Four rounds on this PR: two full rounds, a read-only final review of 0ad9359, and, after the screen failed and the harness fixes landed, one read-only full review of the final head bb58933 (specialist, Red Team, native adversarial, the targeted reader and GPT-6.2 Astra). The second-model review found four blockers in round 1, all fixed: the Codex boundary case still expected 0.160.0, the registry read broke under a relative root, an older revision without the registry failed setup, and the calibration count overstated what ran on 5.2. The final review found no blockers.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - `autoplan/bin/phase-publication-hook.ts:62` keeps `CHECKED_CLAUDE_CODE = '2.1.292'`, so in CI the autoplan guard treats 2.1.326 as an unseen version (an unverified allow) until its Agent payload fixture is recaptured on the new pin. `scripts/resolvers/load-injection.ts:10`'s comment has the same drift. - The installer's registry read matches the astra row's exact format, so a reformat fails setup loudly. The default install test copies the live file, so a reformat fails CI first. - `test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts`'s relative `--root` case checks setup's arguments, not the launch file's PATH; a relative root still breaks the installer's other root-relative paths (pre-existing; the real caller passes an absolute path). - `.github/workflows/codex-hooks.yml` still tests hooks on Codex 0.170.0. - `setup:2079`'s source label still names gpt-6.2-astra by hand (display only). - The registry fallback keys on the file's presence, so a future rename would drop `--model` quietly.
Documentation **Status:** `current`. The documentation audit found nothing stale and made no edits. **Scope:** base `789e9bad` to head `bb58933d` on `newer-cli-pins-and-judge-check`: 56 committed files and no staged, unstaged or new files. The audit covered 157 candidate docs, the authored templates and the nested docs, and checked changed claims against `.github/docker/Dockerfile.ci` (Claude Code 2.1.326, Codex 0.172.0), `bin/gstack-capy-install` (the Codex setup model now comes from the astra row of `lib/model-families.ts`), `lib/eval-model.ts`, harness version 8 and the test-helper changes. **Documentation health:** - `docs/capy-install.md`: Current (this branch already updated step 3 for the astra model and the fail-setup path; both match the installer) - `test/fixtures/judge-calibration/README.md`: Current (the new `claude-fable-5-2` check record matches `ARM_JUDGE_MODEL`, #4811 and the cited fixtures) - `CONTRIBUTING.md`: Current (the judge default `claude-fable-5-2` and the Codex default `gpt-6.2-astra` are still right) - `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md`: Current (the CI CLI pin is described without version numbers) - `docs/autoplan-guard-troubleshooting.md`: Current (its 2.1.292 note describes that version's behavior and is still true) - `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`: Current (none of them names a changed part) - `CHANGELOG.md`, `TODOS.md`, `changelog.d/`: not changed by this audit (owned by the release step) **Coverage:** - CI image pins (Claude Code 2.1.326, Codex 0.172.0): explained in the Dockerfile comments and the changelog fragment. `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` covers the claude pin in general terms but doesn't mention that the Codex CLI is pinned exactly too (common gap, older than this branch). - The installer reading the astra model from the registry: documented in `docs/capy-install.md`. - The default judge on `claude-fable-5-2`: documented in the judge-calibration README and CONTRIBUTING. - The test-harness changes for 2.1.326 (pre-trusted PTY dirs, the Git probe match, the larger bootstrap size limit): internal, recorded in code comments and the changelog fragment. No user doc is needed. **Diagram drift:** none.

title: Stop the QA-only cleanup test from failing at random on a fast terminal-agent exit (GST-3830)
body:
The QA-only cleanup test's missing-terminal case now waits for the terminal agent to publish its port before it deletes the agent's record, so it no longer fails at random in CI.
Why: a red test should mean something broke, and this race turned the merged-tree check for #4803 red twice in a row.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Before: the race made cleanup time out instead of refusing. After: the case refuses as intended even when the agent has already exited.](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/BgmrcKEHBAFqshM6Kz0xv53rjVDP75LTTdbsMP_2oCE.png)

Before: the race made cleanup time out instead of refusing. After: the case refuses as intended even when the agent has already exited.

</details>

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Before: the race made cleanup time out instead of refusing. After: the case refuses as intended even when the agent has already exited.</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ bun test test/qa-only-cleanup.test.ts -t missing-terminal   # this branch, agent already exited before cleanup runs
+(pass) cleanup refuses unconfirmed settlement: missing-terminal [262.44ms]
-$ bun test test/qa-only-cleanup.test.ts -t missing-terminal   # main, agent held at its publish barrier while the record is removed
-Received message: "QA-only browser cleanup: owned process settlement deadline exceeded (daemon 10003, Chromium 10006); retaining fixture"
-(fail) cleanup refuses unconfirmed settlement: missing-terminal [1073.18ms]
 
~~~

The missing-terminal case removed the terminal agent's record right after starting the agent, but starting returns before the agent has opened its port. When the record vanished after the agent's startup check and before it wrote `terminal-port`, the agent stopped with "record was replaced before bind" and left no port file. Since #4821, cleanup treats "no record, no port file and no running agent" as a daemon that never started a terminal, so it tried to stop the fixture daemon, which ignores SIGINT, and ran out of time instead of refusing with `terminal identity is unavailable`.

The test now waits for `terminal-port` before removing the record, and its expected error names `terminal-port present`. The cleanup helper is unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

"Run 45564247467 failed both in shard 3/4 and the serial retry" on #4803's merged tree, in this test's missing-terminal case, on code that did not touch it. With the wait in place the case checks the one thing it is meant to check every time, which is that cleanup refuses when a terminal's record is gone but its port file is left behind.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only this test changes. It stays reliable because the agent's exit path deletes `terminal-port` only while the record is still its own (`browse/src/terminal-agent.ts`, the `cleanup` guard `readAgentRecord(dir)?.gen === CURRENT_GEN`, file:line read), so once the record is gone the port file survives the 25 ms owner watchdog. A variant that waits for the agent to exit before cleanup passed 3 of 3 (script ran).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No issues found. One testing reader read the whole diff and returned no findings.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current — no documentation changes needed.

**Scope:** base 789e9bad..adc74fd on `fix-qa-cleanup-missing-terminal-race`: one committed test-only change (`test/qa-only-cleanup.test.ts`: the missing-terminal case now waits for the terminal port before removing the agent record) plus the untracked changelog fragment. Searched every authored doc and template for references to the changed test, scenario and error message; read `docs/reference-qa-deadlines.md` and the QA mentions in `docs/flaky.md`.

- `changelog.d/fix-qa-cleanup-missing-terminal-race.md`: matches the diff (owned by the parent)

title: Eval plans can check a code judge against a third model's labels, with frozen anchors (GST-3833)
body:
`/eval-plan` now accepts labels made blind by a third-family model (Gemini 4 Neon by default) for a judge that grades code, but only when the plan freezes known-answer anchors with a pass line the labeller must meet first. Why: Garry ruled that a third model replaces people for code labels, and anchors catch a labeller that agrees on what it answers while dodging the rest. Nothing to do for existing plans; judges of anything other than code still need people's or construction labels.
What changed - `## Scoring` takes `labels-by:` (people when absent, or `construction`, `rule`, or a `/`). A model there needs `label-kind: code`, `blind: yes`, `anchors: `, `anchor-pass: ` and `anchors-digest: `, and a family that neither the judge nor any arm shares. `google/gemini-4-neon` is the labeller unless Gemini is the judge or an arm, or a `labeller-fallback:` line names the run where Neon missed its anchors. - New `gstack-eval-plan anchors --hash ` prints the digest of the frozen `{"id", "expected"}` anchor rows, which the plan records as `anchors-digest:`. - `judge --check` and `results --check` take `--anchors ` (`{"id", "expected", "label"}` rows). The labeller's labels count only when its anchors hash to the frozen digest, number exactly `anchors:`, and at least `anchor-pass:` are answered right; a "can't tell" is a miss and an anchor that is also a label row is refused. It prints `JUDGE_ANCHORS:`, `labels_by=` on `JUDGE_AGREEMENT:` and the `JUDGE_RESULTS_LINE:` to paste. - `results --check` refuses results from a model-labelled judge that don't say "judge checked against , a third model, not against people" (`EVAL_REPORT_THIRD_MODEL_UNNAMED`). - The label count (100) and kappa bar (0.6) are unchanged.
Why R126 (Garry, 2026-11-25: "Nah let's just use Gemini neon as another model here and don't use humans"). On the /cso check, Neon said yes on only 1 to 2 of 12 oracle anchors and "can't tell" on 25 to 32 of 104 reports while agreeing on the reports it answered: agreement alone hid the failure and the anchors caught it. gstack-evals made the same change to its wiki check in #453, #454 and #456.
Blast radius Only `gstack-eval-plan` prereg, judge, results and the new anchors command. A plan with no `labels-by:` line, or with people, construction or rule, behaves exactly as before. The eval-plan skill's context ceiling moves from 7057 to 7804 tokens for the added text.
Pre-Landing Review REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=0 deferred=0 noted=8 fixed=2 scope=frozen ledgers_read=3 dispatches=2 Round 1 (batched specialist) found that anchor answers were scored against expected values supplied in the same file, and that several refusal paths had no test; both were fixed (the `anchors-digest:` binding and its tests). The read-only final review and the native adversarial reader found nothing blocking; their notes are below.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `sf-b68560a54203` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `sf-d193903529fb` security finding, details recorded privately - INFORMATIONAL `lib/eval-plan-checks.ts:328` model labeller's can't-tell rows can be dropped from the labels file; no abstention count is required - INFORMATIONAL `lib/eval-plan-checks.ts:306` anchor answers compared as exact strings; digest coerces value types with String() - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-eval-plan:168` --anchors is silently ignored when the plan has no model labeller - INFORMATIONAL `lib/eval-plan-checks.ts:294` anchors --hash accepts an empty file - INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-eval-plan:196` anchors --hash parse failure reports EVAL_JUDGE_UNCHECKED - INFORMATIONAL `lib/eval-plan-checks.ts:244` label-kind and blind are taken on the plan's word
Documentation **Status:** current. Docs already match the change, and this audit edited nothing. **Scope:** the committed diff from base 47b464a0 to head 549ef51a on eval-plan-third-model-labels-for-code-judges (13 files; nothing staged, unstaged or untracked). Docs were checked against lib/eval-plan-checks.ts and bin/gstack-eval-plan. **Documentation health** - docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md: current. The result-checks table and the new third-model labels section cover labels-by, label-kind, blind, anchors, anchor-pass, anchors-digest and labeller-fallback. - docs/troubleshooting.md: current. EVAL_JUDGE_UNCHECKED covers the anchor refusals, and the new EVAL_REPORT_THIRD_MODEL_UNNAMED entry is linked from the table. - eval-plan/SKILL.md.tmpl and eval-plan/SKILL.md: current. Generated output matches the template. - bin/gstack-eval-plan help: current. It documents --anchors and anchors --hash. - changelog.d fragment: present, and it matches the behavior. **Coverage debt:** none found. test/eval-plan-result-checks.test.ts covers the new checks. **Diagram drift:** none. title: Skill authoring audit: suggested fixes for 55 skills
body:
An audit of the installed gstack skills against Anthropic's Agent Skills authoring best practices (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices); suggestions only.

Skill size is already tracked in #3505, so this list covers the other findings.

### Fixes that repeat across skills

- **Put the skill's own steps first.** In most skills the shared preamble (voice, writing style, question format, telemetry) comes before the skill's own workflow. Move the workflow to the top and load the shared preamble from one linked file. Cut preamble sections that a with/without-skill run shows have no effect. Applies to: autoplan, benchmark, benchmark-models, browse, canary, codex, context-restore, context-save, cso, design-consultation, design-html, design-review, design-shotgun, devex-review, diagram, document-generate, document-release, gstack, health, investigate, ios-clean, ios-design-review, ios-fix, ios-qa, ios-sync, land-and-deploy, landing-report, learn, make-pdf, office-hours, open-gstack-browser, pair-agent, plan-ceo-review, plan-design-review, plan-devex-review, plan-eng-review, plan-tune, qa, qa-only, retro, review, scrape, second-opinion, setup-browser-cookies, setup-deploy, setup-gbrain, ship, skillify, spec, sync-gbrain.
- **Add a progress checklist.** Add a copyable `- [ ]` checklist of the phases, with an "if this check fails, go back to step N" line. Applies to: autoplan, benchmark, benchmark-models, context-save, cso, design-consultation, design-html, design-review, devex-review, diagram, document-generate, document-release, gstack-upgrade, health, investigate, ios-clean, ios-design-review, ios-fix, ios-qa, ios-sync, landing-report, office-hours, pair-agent, plan-ceo-review, plan-design-review, plan-devex-review, plan-eng-review, plan-tune, qa, qa-only, retro, review, scrape, setup-deploy, setup-gbrain, ship, skillify, sync-gbrain.
- **Enforce hard rules with hooks.** Where a rule must always hold (for example, no writes in plan mode), use a frontmatter `PreToolUse` hook with matcher `Edit|Write|Bash`, and keep judgment rules in prose. Applies to: autoplan, design-review, devex-review, ios-qa, ios-sync, skillify, sync-gbrain, browse, canary, design-shotgun, land-and-deploy, spec, design-html, benchmark.
- **End telemetry with a Stop hook** instead of a prose instruction at the end of the skill. Applies to: diagram, document-release, health, ios-design-review, landing-report, learn, office-hours, plan-devex-review, plan-eng-review, review.
- **Add evals.** Add `evals/evals.json` with 3 realistic prompts, plus notes from a baseline run without the skill. Applies to all skills in this list except qa and ship.

### Skill-specific fixes

- **benchmark**: in the checklist, add "if the regression check fails, return to step N".
- **benchmark-models**: add a PreToolUse Bash hook before cost-incurring runs, or reword that rule as judgment. Add a go-back line after the judge step.
- **codex**: end the description with "Use when the user asks for a codex review, challenge or second opinion." Add a PreToolUse hook on `ExitPlanMode` that runs the gate check.
- **context-restore**: add a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks git write commands while restoring.
- **cso**: enforce the launcher-only rule with a PreToolUse Bash hook that rejects other commands.
- **design-consultation**: add a loop: render the preview, compare it to the proposal, fix, and repeat until it matches.
- **design-html**: give each of Steps 0-5 a "done when" line. Move the no-git-mutation rule into a PreToolUse Bash hook.
- **design-shotgun**, **open-gstack-browser**, **diagram**: write the description in the third person ("Generates multiple design variants... Use when...", "Launches GStack Browser...").
- **document-generate**, **document-release**: add "if the coverage map shows gaps, return to step 1".
- **gstack-upgrade**: add a PreToolUse Bash hook that denies `rm` on the gstack backup directories.
- **health**: add "if a tool fails to run, return to step 1".
- **ios-clean**: add "if a Phase 3 check fails, return to Phase 2 for the missed item, then rerun Phase 3". Add a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks `git push --force` and `git commit --amend`.
- **ios-design-review**: add "if a screen fails to load, return to Connection".
- **ios-fix**: enforce the Iron Law with a PreToolUse Edit hook that requires a reproduced bug record.
- **landing-report**: add "if the queue query fails, return to step 1".
- **office-hours**: add "if the premises fail, return to Phase 2".
- **plan-eng-review**: move the scope gate to a UserPromptSubmit hook and the exit-plan gate to a PreToolUse hook on `ExitPlanMode`.
- **qa**: add "if verify fails, return to fix". Use a PreToolUse Bash hook for the git rules.
- **qa-only**: add a PreToolUse `Edit|Write` hook that allows only the report path. Add "if a check is inconclusive, return to Select Surfaces".
- **second-opinion**: in spawned sessions, enforce the no-AskUserQuestion rule with a PreToolUse hook (matcher `AskUserQuestion`).
- **ship**: add "if tests fail, fix and return to step N". Add a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks force-push and direct pushes to main.

title: /gstack-ship drops bought extra review rounds and the second-model trail check (GST-3829)
body:
/gstack-ship no longer lets anyone buy an extra review round or a narrow re-check. After two review rounds, a blocking finding ships only as an owner's recorded ruling, or the PR waits.
Why: these paths were switched off last release and kept breaking; four PRs in one day tried to repair them. This is part 4 of the approved /gstack-ship simplification.
Nothing to do: each removed flag now refuses with a message that names what replaced it.

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

## What changed

- **Grants and fix-checks are gone.** The removed commands and flags are `gstack-approvals round-grant`, `gstack-ship-receipt claim`, and `gstack-review-plan --grant`, `--round-grant`, `--stop`, `--fix-checks`, `--fix-check-prompt` and `--last fix-check`. `write` and `finish` refuse `--review-loop-exception`, and `gstack-no-stop` no longer records a scoped fix-check. The fix-check stamping goes too, along with finish's fix-check counting and chain, the grant closure in receipt write and the grant-offer text in every stop message. `gstack-ship-receipt history` now prints only the round counts. The approval record refuses new grant rows; old rows still render.
- **Old receipts with a review-loop exception are refused.** Land and carry refuse a receipt that still records one, and the `QUEUE_RECEIPT_EXCEPTION_INVALID` fix text and the release note say to run /gstack-ship again for a fresh receipt.
- **No cross-family trail read.** `gstack-ship-queue ready` drops `--trail`, and the READY's Attention section opens with the receipt's risk class. `gstack-decision-trail` stays, because autoplan uses it.
- The driver records the budget at start and close only, no longer after every program. The review pass's own note keeps the spend-cap check.
- **A stop before any PR exists works** (HARN-138). `gstack-ship-receipt stop` without `--pr` records the run's stop and prints `pr=none`. When the run record refuses that write, it exits 1 and prints no `STOP_RECORD:`, and a `--pr` or `--body` with no value is a usage error.
- **Receipt checks treat file names literally.** `git ls-tree` in the receipt's patch and depth checks gets `--literal-pathspecs`, so a path with `*` or `?` in its name is read as that one file.
- **Docs and prompts updated to match:** review-policy, ship-policy, troubleshooting (the old anchors stay and say what replaced them), unattended.md, the driver, review-army, pr-body and the Captain doc. The driver also tells a run to write a plan agreed only in conversation to `.gstack/plans/<branch>.md`, so the audit doesn't read it as `plan=none`.

## Why

Grants, fix-checks and the review-loop exception were deprecated last release, when full second rounds replaced narrow re-checks, and they kept failing in ways that cost whole CI cycles. Removing them leaves one rule a person can follow. After two review rounds, a blocker ships as a ruled note or the PR parks.

## Blast radius

Only /gstack-ship's review, receipt and queue tooling changes. A script that still passes a removed flag gets a refusal that names the replacement. A PR whose existing receipt records a review-loop exception must run /gstack-ship again before it lands.

## Tests

Tests for removed behavior were deleted or rewritten to check the refusal. The no-loss replays (`test/helpers/gst3562-replay.ts`) gain a kind h for history the branch can no longer be given, such as a fix-check as the last step or a grant. Main's plan is read back for those cases, and every other case keeps its earlier kind and checks. Replay record: `test/fixtures/review-pins/replays/GST-3562-part-4.json`. `lib/review-depth.ts` and `ship/sections/review-army.md` are repinned, and the reviewer brief bodies are unchanged. New tests cover the refused pre-PR stop, a valueless `--pr`, and the legacy-exception refusal and its fix text.

Tests ran: tests 1782

## Pre-Landing Review

Two full rounds, then one read-only full review of the final head. The second round's second-model review raised three blockers. The owner ruled two as notes (below); the third, a pre-PR stop that reported success when nothing recorded it, is fixed with a test. The final review found nothing blocking; its informational items are listed under Review notes.

## Documentation

**Status:** current — no doc edits needed; the docs this PR touches already describe the removal.

**Scope:** docs touched by the PR diff (docs/review-policy.md, docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/unattended.md, crew/docs/captain.md, ship/DRIVER and ship/sections templates, the changelog.d fragment), plus a search of docs/*.md for the removed grant, fix-check, review-loop exception and trail-check paths. Steps 1–4 and 6 only.

**Documentation health:**
- docs/review-policy.md — current; the GST-1702 post-review paragraph (lines 109–121) states grants are gone. Possible debt: line 822 still says a granted fix-check clears a blocker (`cleared_by_grant`), which conflicts with line 111.
- docs/ship-policy.md — current; `review_loop_exception` stays in the receipt field list because the schema still accepts it on readback.
- docs/model-policy.md — current; fix-check effort is described as history.
- docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/unattended.md, crew/docs/captain.md — current, already updated by this PR.

**Coverage debt / diagram drift:** none found beyond the line 822 wording.

## Plan Completion

10 of 15 plan items done, 2 partial, 1 not done, 1 changed, 1 unverifiable. Not in this PR, as planned: F (run the docs audit before review) and the rest of G and H (the receipt carry's scoped reader and slimming the receipt). Both change finish's docs-freshness and receipt contracts, so they go in their own PR. Partial: J's carry machinery and the record fields `docs_audit_read`, `review_targeted` and `carry`, which stay because the frozen 0408128 replay and receipts in flight read them. Changed: `gstack-decision-trail` is kept for autoplan. GST-2204 (a carry letting a weakened test merge) is not addressed here and stays open: the receipt carry still accepts a head whose product diff is unchanged, so a test-only change after review can carry.

## Review notes

Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `test/review-pass-program-steps.test.ts:17` Unused legacyGrantFlags test helper builds flags review-plan now refuses
