title: careful: deletes inside a git worktree of the session's repo ask every time
body:
Since the destructive-command check became an always-on hook (1.102), every `rm` with an absolute path into a linked worktree of the same repo prompts, even in bypass mode.

Setup: session starts in `~/Projects/app` (main), feature work happens in `git worktree add ../app-192`. A cleanup like

    rm /Users/me/Projects/app-192/src/__tests__/e2e/debug.spec.ts

gets "Destructive: deletes files outside this session's folder". `_careful_outside` in `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` only treats paths under the session cwd as inside, so a sibling worktree of the same repo counts as foreign.

Suggestion: treat paths under any entry of `git worktree list --porcelain` for the session's repo as inside. The worktree is the same repo the session already owns, and `git worktree remove --force` keeps its own separate ask.

Workaround today: `cd ../app-192 && rm src/...` passes, since relative paths after a tracked `cd` are resolved and allowed.

title: make-pdf: diagrams after a sub-heading keep the full width, and HTML export fits phones (GST-3846)
body:
make-pdf's new layout no longer squeezes a diagram that follows a `###` sub-heading into the text column, and a sub-heading with `
` line breaks no longer prints over the next heading. `--to html` output now declares a phone-width viewport, so its one-column phone layout actually switches on. Nothing to do: `--style plain` PDFs and CSS and Word output are unchanged.
What changed - A mermaid or excalidraw diagram right after a `###` sub-heading stays a top-level block, so it spans the full width with the sub-heading above it, the same as code, tables and images. - When that diagram (or an image) is moved to its own sideways page, the sub-heading goes to that page with it instead of being left alone at the foot of the page before. - A sub-heading's reserved height counts each `
` as a new line, so a multi-line sub-heading clears the next block. - `--to html` (both styles) adds ``. The HTML used to print PDFs is unchanged.
Why These were the open notes from #4820, which made the swiss layout the default.
Tests - New fixture `make-pdf/test/fixtures/swiss-after-h3.md` puts a sub-heading before every block type: paragraph, both lists, quote, code, table, image, text with an inline image, mermaid, excalidraw, a diagram on a sideways page, rule, raw HTML, another sub-heading, and a six-line `
` sub-heading. - Unit tests in `make-pdf/test/style-swiss.test.ts` (which blocks pair with a sub-heading, diagram and sideways-page placement, `
` height, viewport in both styles) failed before each fix and pass after. - The new end-to-end test in `make-pdf/test/e2e/swiss-gate.test.ts` failed on main (diagram labels started in the text column), then on the `
` overprint, then on the stranded heading, and passes with all three fixes. - Local: `bun test make-pdf/test` 381 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail; typecheck clean; test typecheck has no new diagnostics. CI free suite green at 7088776 (run 45629741831).
Blast radius Only make-pdf's swiss render path and its HTML export change. `--style plain` CSS still matches its golden files byte for byte and Word output is unchanged (tests ran). CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/skills.md and docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md render to the same PDF text layout as main, and to the same HTML apart from the viewport line (script ran).
Pre-Landing Review Pre-Landing Review: 1 issue — 1 fixed, 0 deferred, 3 noted. Gate edits: none detected (6 listed, 2 read; patterns: RH-1,RH-3,RH-4,RH-12,RH-13,RH-14,RH-15,RH-16; unlisted idioms: none) Round 1 (testing, security, state-machine and red-team checklists, a second Opus read, and a second-model review on GPT-6.2 Sol): the second-model review found that a sub-heading before a diagram moved to a sideways page printed alone on the page before it. Reproduced in the new end-to-end test (heading on page 2, diagram on page 3) and fixed. Round 2 read the whole final diff and found nothing that blocks.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `make-pdf/src/style-swiss.ts:65` an explicit `page=landscape` fence on a near-square diagram, plus its sub-heading, can be taller than the sideways page, so the diagram moves on and leaves the heading behind. Automatic promotion only picks diagrams at least 1.8 times wider than tall, which leaves room. - INFORMATIONAL `make-pdf/src/render.ts:442` a sub-heading that ends in `
` reserves one extra blank line. - Not fixed from #4820's notes: a paragraph with text and one inline image still goes full width (needs a new marker on image-only paragraphs and a CSS change), a multi-value `--margins` is not supported in either style (the flag takes one length), and screen body text stays 11pt (a design call).
Documentation **Status:** current. Nothing in the docs became wrong. **Scope:** base 80fd754 to head 7088776, 8 files under make-pdf/ and changelog.d/. Reviewed docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md, make-pdf/SKILL.md.tmpl, and the make-pdf rows in README.md and docs/skills.md. **Held back:** the audit suggested one more clause in docs/howto-diagrams-and-formats.md (that `--to html` output carries a phone-width viewport). It is accurate, but this fix is limited to make-pdf/, its tests and changelog.d/, so it is left for a docs pass. **Coverage debt:** none new; the three fixes change rendering only and add no flags or commands.

title: /gstack-ship honours ruled edits after the final review and records second-model stops (GST-3814)
body:
/gstack-ship no longer asks for every reviewer again after an edit the owner already ruled a note, and a stop on a second-model reviewer's blocker now records instead of failing with STOP_UNBOUND.
Why: both forced hand-written workarounds after the final review (#4819, yc-software/qm#3973, gskills#45 and #46).
Nothing to do: the fixes apply on the next /gstack-ship run.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

After the final review, an owner could rule a late edit "a note, not a fix", and finish accepted that ruling. The review plan didn't read it, so it still asked for every reviewer again on the same bytes. The plan now reads the ruling with the same check finish uses. When every edited path is ruled at its exact bytes, the plan says no more review is owed. An unruled path, or a path edited after its ruling, still stops.

A second-model reviewer that found a blocker used to leave a review row with no start token. Recording that stop then failed with STOP_UNBOUND. Each reviewer row in that step now gets its own start token, so the stop records.

Smaller cleanups left over from #4826: recovery messages now say /gstack-ship instead of /ship, two broken doc links are fixed, a retired stop kind is refused everywhere, and stale wording is removed.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

/gstack-ship's job is to get a reviewed PR to ready without hand-edits around its own checks. Both bugs made people write workarounds after the final review.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The review plan, the Step 11 review program, the check for stops that don't need an owner, and some message text. Finish's ruling check moved into one shared function that the plan also calls, so the two can't drift. Focused tests cover each path, and the full CI suite passed at this head.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test test/review-plan-cli.test.ts test/no-stop.test.ts test/ship-finish-edit-ruling.test.ts`: 51 pass, 0 fail
- [x] Full free suite in CI at c4b7c52 (run 45649623643): green, carried as the full test run

</details>

<!-- gstack:agent-notes -->
<details><summary>Agent notes</summary>

## Agent notes

- `gstack-review-plan --range-base` reads `edit:<path>` rulings with the same check finish uses (now one shared `ruledEdits` in `lib/ruled-notes.ts`). When every path in the fix range is ruled at its exact bytes, the range plans as no fix: `FIX_RANGE: runtime_lines=0 … ruled=N`, `RULED_EDIT:` lines and `NEXT: done` (or `NEXT: targeted` when no targeted record covers the ruled bytes). An unruled path, or one edited after its ruling (`RULED_EDIT_REFUSED:`), still stops (GST-3814).
- Step 11's pass program, with no `logStart`, starts one `adversarial-review` token per voice row it logs (native adversarial and second-model reader), so the second-model row binds to its tree and `gstack-ship-receipt stop` can record the stop.
- `checkNoStop` refuses the retired `scoped-fix-check` (as `gstack-no-stop` already did); its dead docs-only path is gone. The receipt's `--no-stop` help no longer offers it.
- Recovery messages say `/gstack-ship` and "one scoped reader (not a review round)". `crew/docs/captain.md` heading links fixed; stale `cleared_by_grant` and GST-1702 wording removed from `docs/review-policy.md`; unused `legacyGrantFlags` test helper removed.
- Failing-first tests: `test/review-plan-cli.test.ts` (GST-3814 describe), `test/review-pass-program-steps.test.ts` (no-logStart voices), `test/no-stop.test.ts` (scoped-fix-check retired) each failed on main ec5d7e6 before the fix. The two round-2 tests (targeted NEXT, skip-ci stop) were written with their fix and have no failing-first run.
- `lib/review-depth.ts` changed two reason strings only; repinned under replay GSTA-861.
- Docs audit d1 (after review) edited docs/ship-policy.md and docs/review-policy.md; one scoped reader read them clean (not a review round).
- Not done: carrying pre-PR stop rounds into PR history needs a rounds field in the run record (new schema), so it is left as a note.
- GEVA-2 (R12 recount after a read-only final review): no non-deferral ruling kind clears a fixed blocker from `review_loop.open`; that needs a new ruling kind, so it is a design note, not a change here.
- Refs GST-3814

title: Stop six gstack tests from failing at random in CI (GST-3852)
body:
Six gstack tests that failed at random in CI now pass reliably, so a red check on a pull request means a real problem again.
Why: random failures cost reruns and hide real breakage, and the project's goal is a test suite people can trust.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Under heavy load the retention test failed every run on main; with the longer deadline it passes every run](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/xOJc11piZI-cZq61243qmeQxEcgRjBp71gUcqQmnz7E.png)

Under heavy load the retention test failed every run on main; with the longer deadline it passes every run.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

CI's logs show each failure. The plan review check failed with an unterminated JSON string in two runs, the QA caller check was stopped for `cat` of the hand-off file, and the retention test ran out its deadline twice in the free tests. Each fix was checked against a repro that fails on main and passes on this branch.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only test files, one test helper and a changelog fragment change; no shipped skill, command or binary does. The plan review judge change runs only inside that test (test/helpers/plan-floor-review.ts), two fake judges that stand in for it now answer in the same format, and a paid run of that case passed with the final judge on the pinned Claude Code CLI (script ran).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The first review round found two problems in the first version of the fix: the judge treated any exit code 1 as a finished answer, and the retention test's retry budget did not fit its outer limit. Both were fixed and the second round found no issues. A final full review of the last version found no blocking problems in the code it changed; its two blocking-rated notes were ruled to ship as notes (listed in Agent notes), and the remaining low notes are listed there too.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation changes were needed.

**Scope:** the committed diff ec5d7e6..0e1f33f on flaky-fixes-2026-11-25: 9 commits, 11 files, all test files and test helpers plus one changelog fragment. No files were staged, unstaged or new. I searched every doc and template in the candidate list for references to the changed files.

**Documentation health:**
- changelog.d/flaky-fixes-2026-11-25.md: current. It matches the diff.
- docs/evals/detector-inventory.md: current. It is a dated inventory, so its line citations into plan-floor-review.ts were left as recorded.
- Every other doc: not affected, because the change is test-only.

**Coverage debt:** none was introduced. **Diagram drift:** none.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test test/plan-floor-review.test.ts test/plan-ceo-floor-interactive-boundary.test.ts test/plan-floor-permission.test.ts test/plan-floor-target.test.ts test/helpers/claude-pty-runner.runners.unit.test.ts`: 197 tests ran, all passed
- [x] `bun test test/qa-exploratory-callers.test.ts`: 115 tests ran, all passed
- [x] `bun test test/bootstrap-retention-shard.test.ts test/docsync-fault-interface.test.ts test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts`: 64 tests ran, all passed
- [x] Load repros: retention test failed 5 of 5 on main and passed 5 of 5 here under 8 processes holding 50,000 open files each; the three slow tests failed 3 of 3 on main and passed 3 of 3 here under 8 CPU spinners
- [x] Paid, on the final judge: `plan-ceo-finding-floor`, `auq-format-gate`, `office-hours-auto-mode` and `plan-ceo-review-plan-mode` each passed once; the five QA caller probes passed at b5e50ce, whose inputs are unchanged since
- [x] CI free tests at this tree passed (run 45662874566), including the macOS named regressions job
- [x] typecheck clean; test type-debt ratchet has no new diagnostics

</details>

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Under heavy load the retention test failed every run on main; with the longer deadline it passes every run</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ bun test test/bootstrap-retention-shard.test.ts   # this branch, same load
+run 1  success preserves  (pass)  [17200ms]
+run 2  success preserves  (pass)  [17258ms]
+run 3  success preserves  (pass)  [16576ms]
+run 4  success preserves  (pass)  [16106ms]
+run 5  success preserves  (pass)  [18121ms]
+5 of 5 runs passed
-$ bun test test/bootstrap-retention-shard.test.ts   # origin/main, 8 processes x 50000 open files + CPU spin
-run 1  success preserves  (fail)  [12630ms]  shard failed, exit 1
-run 2  success preserves  (fail)  [11469ms]  shard failed, exit 1
-run 3  success preserves  (fail)  [12575ms]  shard failed, exit 1
-run 4  success preserves  (fail)  [17609ms]
-run 5  success preserves  (fail)  [18759ms]
-5 of 5 runs failed
 
~~~

CI kept turning red on tests that had nothing to do with the change under test. Each one now has a fix for its real cause:

- **Plan review finding check.** The small judge model that grades a plan review sometimes cut its JSON answer off mid-string, so the check failed with a parse error even when the review was fine. The judge now answers through Claude Code's schema-checked structured output with no built-in or MCP tools, the check reads the first answer the schema accepted, and the test log keeps only that answer instead of the whole session. The prompt is unchanged, and a run that uses its whole turn budget is accepted only when the stream says so.
- **QA caller check for a small CLI.** The agent under test kept reading the hand-off file with `cat`, which the test's fixture does not allow. The fixture's instructions now say to read hand-off files with the Read tool and never `cat`.
- **Bootstrap retention test.** Its 5 second deadline was too short on a busy runner, where counting open files is slow. The deadline and the outer time limits are longer.
- **Three slow tests** (docs sync fault check, skill start guard line, QA caller budget check) hit Bun's 5 second default when run directly with `bun test` on a loaded machine. They now have time limits that fit, and the QA caller test file has a 30 second default. CI already runs tests with a 30 second default, so the docs sync limit only helps local and focused runs; the skill start and QA caller budget limits are longer than CI's too.

</details>

title: Skill routing no longer fires on subagent hand-backs or passing mentions of a trigger
body:
Skill routing now ignores subagent reports that Claude Code delivers in an `` block, and routes a noun-phrase trigger such as "code review" only when the sentence asks for the work. Each `routed` log line now records the prompt's length, the matched trigger and the prompt's kind, so a false route can be checked from the log alone. Reported by @sohampatwardhan. Nothing to do.
What changed ![A subagent hand-back and a sentence that only mentions code review no longer route to /review; a real ask still does](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/AQ42G2f2ppctqHoVacQryG-wJnvsRoROL4SAuSTdcQM.png) A subagent hand-back and a sentence that only mentions code review no longer route to /review; a real ask still does.
Why gstack's routing hint should help a person reach the right skill. These false routes started work nobody asked for in every Claude Code session that uses subagents, which is how most heavy users work.
Blast radius Only the skill-routing hook on Claude Code and Codex (`lib/skill-route.ts` and `hosts/claude/hooks/skill-route-hook.ts`). The hook only adds a hint and always exits 0, so the worst case of a wrong decision is a missed or extra hint; the existing plain-prompt, bug-report and synthetic fixture tests in `test/skill-route.test.ts` pass unchanged. Anyone who parses `hooks/skill-route.log` sees the new fields at the end of existing ones.
Tests - [x] `bun test test/skill-route.test.ts test/codex-hooks.test.ts`: 66 pass, 0 fail (the three new tests failed first on main: 37 pass, 3 fail) - [x] Adjacent routing and hook suites (12 files): 814 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck`: clean - [x] CI free suite at 814a628: run 45656153546, 1784 test files
Before/after as text: A subagent hand-back and a sentence that only mentions code review no longer route to /review; a real ask still does ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output $ gstack-skill-route --explain ">" +route: none (agent-message) -route: /review $ gstack-skill-route --explain "even mentioning code review triggers it without me invoking the skill" +route: none (mention) -route: /review $ gstack-skill-route --explain "can you do a code review of this?" route: /review ~~~ A person using subagents in Claude Code saw their subagents' reports start /review and /build-check runs nobody asked for, followed by a Stop block on a review they never wanted. Those reports arrive under the line `Another Claude session sent a message:` in an `` block, which the hook did not recognize. Now it treats them like the other agent wrappers and never routes them (#4801). A sentence that only talked about code review ("even mentioning code review triggers it") routed the same as a request for one. Now a trigger that is only a noun phrase ("code review", "pre-landing review"), or a trigger's words side by side in another order ("pr review" for "review this pr"), routes only when a sentence that holds it asks for the work: please, "can you", "let's", "I need", a request verb first ("do a code review", not "do not run a code review"), the trigger first as a command ("fix lint errors in src"), or nothing else ("code review"). Another trigger of the same skill that the prompt does ask for still routes. Triggers that start with a verb and hold a common word ("review my changes", "look over my diff") route as before (#4802). The routing log could not tell a false route from a real one. `routed` lines now include `trigger=""`, `chars=` and `kind=typed|agent-message|cross-session-message|task-notification`, and `no-route` lines include `kind=` and the new `reason=mention`. No prompt text is logged (#4805). `docs/skill-routing-and-contracts.md` describes all three.
Pre-Landing Review Two review rounds and a second-reader pass found no blockers. Round 1 found that a mention-only trigger could hide another trigger of the same skill that the prompt did ask for, and that a negated request verb ("Do not run a code review") counted as an ask; both are fixed with tests. The remaining findings are below the blocking floor and listed under Review notes.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:568` The n't branch of the request-verb lookahead can never match, so the "Don't do a code review yet." test case already passed at the base; only the "Do not" case is new protection. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:574` A third-party verb-first trigger with no common words ("fix lint errors") is read as a noun phrase, so "fix the lint errors in src" no longer routes to that skill. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:576` An ask word anywhere in the sentence counts, so "Once the code review is done, can you merge it?" still routes to /review. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:582` Requests like "Code review: look at src/x.ts" and "pr review for #123" now route nowhere; a path or issue number fails the says-nothing-else test. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/skill-route.ts:608` Each flagged skill re-tokenizes the prompt once per trigger; with hundreds of third-party skills a 5,000-character prompt nears the hook's 1.5 s deadline (it fails closed).

title: gstack-pr-wait ignores cancelled checks a newer pass replaced, and the npm git-dependency hint names allow-git
body:
`gstack-pr-wait` no longer blocks on a cancelled check that a newer run of the same check replaced, and the `DEPS_MISSING` stop names npm 12's `allow-git` setting when the lockfile installs a package from git.
The docs audit that /gstack-ship launches also starts after a reviewer's install, and a refused launch no longer uses up its one retry.
Nothing for you to do. Fixes #4807 and #4815; thanks to exGeni for both reports and the repro.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **`gstack-pr-wait` and replaced cancels (#4807).** A cancelled run is left out only when the newest run of the same check (same app and name) passed or is still running, which is how `gstack-ship-queue ready` and `gh pr checks` already read it. The check then reads as that newer run, so it is green when that run passed and pending while it runs. A failed run beside a newer pass, a cancel that is the newest run, and another app's pass all still block. `docs/ship-policy.md` and `docs/troubleshooting.md` name this one narrowing.
- **npm git dependencies (#4815).** When `npm-shrinkwrap.json` or `package-lock.json` resolves a package from git, the `DEPS_MISSING` hint still says `npm ci` and adds that npm 12 and later need `allow-git`, naming `--allow-git=all` for a source you trust. It is not made the default.
- **Docs audit start.** When a reviewer's `--for review-voice` install has rewritten the shared install verdict, the start check (both the TypeScript and Bash versions) now also tries /gstack-ship's own install record. That record is checked in full for the workflow: checkout, HEAD, project, pins, components and Bun.
- **Docs audit retry.** `gstack-docs-candidate attempt` no longer counts a launch whose start check refused it when the child reports that as a `blocked` result with no file reviewed or updated.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

Each bug gave wrong advice to someone shipping with gstack. pr-wait reported a false `PR_WAIT_BLOCKED` on a head the merge queue called green. The npm hint suggested a command that fails with `EALLOWGIT`. And in a real /gstack-ship run (yc-software/qm#3974), the docs audit was refused at start and the refusal still spent the PR's one retry.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`gstack-pr-wait` (and /land-and-deploy Step 3, which runs it), the `DEPS_MISSING` stop in `gstack-ship-preflight`, workflow start checks on Capy machines after a review-voice install, and Step 14.5's attempt counter. The merge queue's own CI verdict is unchanged.

</details>

title: Remove the /cso security audit skill, since a plain audit request finds more
body:
/cso is gone: the skill, its native helper programs, scanner images, CI jobs, docs and the rest of its tests. Upgrading removes gstack's own `/cso` entries and old helper files, and leaves a skill of your own named `cso` alone.
Why: on 52 real security advisories, plainly asking the agent to audit the code caught more than /cso (13 vs 7 on particle-1; 12 vs 8 of 51 on Claude Opus 5.5, within the margin of error).
To do: nothing. Optional cleanup of old scanner images and reports is in the changelog entry.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **Removed:** `cso/`, `lib/cso/`, the native helper build (`scripts/build-cso.sh`, `build-cso-windows.ps1`) and the remaining `scripts/cso-*` files, the `build:cso` and `format:cso` scripts (and prettier, which only `format:cso` used), the C toolchain probe in `./setup` and `Dockerfile.ci`, the doctor's /cso row, the /cso routing line, the `windows-setup-cso` job and the CI steps that built the helper, and every test, eval case and doc still covering only /cso. The first half (the /cso-only tests, workflows and docs pages) landed in #4837.
- **Upgrade cleanup:** `cso` joins the retired-skill list in `scripts/discover-skills.ts` and `bin/gstack-install-registry.sh`, the same path /investigate took. `./setup` removes exactly the files and staging folders the old /cso build wrote in `bin/` and the two built `lib/cso/images` helpers; a locked file on Windows leaves a warning instead of failing setup. Tests cover the cleanup, that a file of your own with a different name under the same prefix stays, and that a `lib/cso` holding anything else is kept.
- **Shared tests kept, re-pointed:** tests that used /cso as an example of something general now use another skill (/qa, /health, /retro, /benchmark, /deslop-shared-libs). The paid-report census fixtures move their /cso shard onto `skill-e2e-shared-libs-periodic` and `skill-e2e-retro`, so every census behavior keeps its test.
- **Provider adapters:** the /cso producer mode (sandboxed Claude stream, producer env) is removed from `test/helpers/providers/*`.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

A plain security audit request outperformed /cso on frontier models, so the skill and everything it needed to run go (GST-3920).

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Anyone who used /cso loses it; a plain "audit this code for security problems" request or /review replaces it. Setup and relink delete only gstack's own /cso entries and the old build outputs by exact name. No required check names a removed job.

</details>

<details><summary>Issues</summary>

Fixes #3091

Closes #3091. Thank you for the report. Rather than fixing it, we removed /cso (see above); a plain security audit request replaces it.

</details>

Two rounds. Round 1 found one blocker from the second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol): setup's cleanup deleted anything matching `bin/gstack-cso-*`. It was fixed by naming the exact files, with a test. The second-model review raised one more: the staging-folder pattern `bin/.gstack-cso-stage.??????` would also remove a folder of your own given exactly that name. title: /careful no longer asks before deleting a file inside another worktree of the same repo (#4827)
body:
/careful no longer asks before every plain `rm` of a file inside another `git worktree` of the same repository, so people who run several worktrees side by side stop clicking through a prompt on each cleanup.
It keeps the safety check quiet only where it was wrong (gstack's goal: guards that stop real mistakes, not routine work), and every other delete still asks.
Nothing to do.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

A session started in `~/Projects/app` that ran `rm /Users/me/Projects/app-192/src/debug.spec.ts`, a file in a sibling worktree of the same repository, got "deletes files outside this session's folder" on every delete, even in bypass mode (#4827). Now a plain `rm` or `unlink` counts as inside when the path, resolved on disk, sits strictly inside a worktree that `git worktree list` reports for the session's own repository, and every statement in the command is such a delete. The same holds for a path elsewhere in the session's own worktree.

Everything else asks as before. That covers a worktree's root or a folder that holds one, `.git` and the git folder, `..`, symlinks, globs, other repositories, `rm` with any option other than `-f`, `-i`, `-I`, `-v` or `-d` (so `rm -r` and `rm --recursive` still ask), `find`, `rsync --delete`, `shred`, a command that runs anything before the delete, and `git worktree remove --force`.

On main, `rm /path/to/sibling-worktree/src/debug.spec.ts` asks. On this branch it runs without asking, and `rm -r /path/to/sibling-worktree/src` still asks.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The check exists to catch deletes that reach outside the project. A sibling worktree is the same project checked out in another folder, so asking there trained people to approve deletes without reading, which is the opposite of what the check is for.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` changes behavior, and only by adding an allow path on top of the existing check. A replay of 21,904 commands through main's hook and this branch's hook found 783 that now pass and 0 that became stricter, with all 125 denials unchanged, and an independent checker found no wrongly allowed command (script ran). If `git` is missing or older than 2.36, the exemption never applies and the old prompt comes back (walked failure path).

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The final full review of this head found no issues. An adversarial review found nothing blocking and left four notes, listed below.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

- A repository whose own git folder was hand-edited to list another repository as one of its worktrees would make that other repository count as a worktree. Writing there already takes control of the repository, so this was left as a note; a follow-up could compare each worktree's common git folder with the session's.
- A path elsewhere in the session's own worktree, outside the folder the session started in, is also exempt. The changelog entry now says so.
- With `git` older than 2.36 the exemption silently does nothing, which keeps the old, stricter behavior.
- Process note: the change was checked as additive against main's hook, as the guard rules require.

</details>

Fixes #4827

</details>

title: setup: --refresh-registered reinstalls Codex globally from the checkout's own .agents render
body:
Every upgrade puts gstack back into `~/.codex/skills`, even when `~/.gstack/installs.tsv` has only a `claude` row. Deleting `~/.codex/skills/gstack` doesn't stick, because the next upgrade brings it back.

Setup: global Claude install at `~/.claude/skills/gstack`, with `./setup --host codex` run once months ago, so `.gstack-installed-hosts` still lists `codex`.

The loop:

1. With `codex` in `.gstack-installed-hosts`, setup renders `.agents/skills/` inside the checkout, the `.agents/skills/gstack` sidecar included.
2. The upgrade runs `cd "$ROOT" && ./setup --refresh-registered`. `gstack_install_known_roots` takes `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` as the project, which here is the checkout itself, and emits `codex project <checkout>/.agents/skills/gstack`. `_gstack_install_source` resolves that sidecar to the checkout, so the refresh adds it as a pre-registry Codex install.
3. The refresh child gets `--host codex` without `--global` (only global rows get it). The checkout lives in `~/.claude/skills`, so `CODEX_REPO_LOCAL` stays 0 and it installs into `~/.codex/skills`, writes a `codex global` row and adds `codex` back to `.gstack-installed-hosts`.

Result on 1.103.1.0: `codex  experimental  global  installed` in the summary of every upgrade. Still the same on main (959df8c), `bin/gstack-install-registry.sh:263-267`.

Suggestion: skip the project rows in `gstack_install_known_roots` when the toplevel is the source checkout, since its `.agents/` is a render, not an install.

Workaround: `rm -r <checkout>/.agents`, drop `codex` from `.gstack-installed-hosts` and `installs.tsv`, remove `~/.codex/skills/gstack*`.

body:

Why: #4833 deletes those jobs along with /cso, so its own CI could never match the list main still holds. This lands first, then #4833 merges main and its CI counts.
Nothing to do: the jobs still run on main until #4833 lands, and the free-tests job still requires all three to pass.

The profile is always read from main, so the fix has to land on main first. The three names leave the profile's `jobs` and `skippable.jobs` lists, and nothing else changes.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

It unblocks the removal of /cso (GST-3920), which a plain security audit request outperformed on frontier models.

title: Drop release notes that later changes in this release made outdated (GST-3965)
body:
The notes for the next release no longer say /cso still works, no longer promise a /gstack-ship message fix that already shipped, and state the /cso test result on Opus without overstating it.
Why: someone reading the v1.104.0.0 notes should get one consistent, accurate account of what changed.
Nothing to do: only files under `changelog.d/` change.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

Three notes written for this release were overtaken by later changes in the same release, so the notes contradicted each other. The note from the first half of the /cso removal (#4837) said "The /cso skill still works until the next change removes it", but #4833 removed /cso in this release, so that note is deleted. The internal CI step on the way to #4833 (#4836) ended "Nothing changes for anyone using gstack" and is deleted too; the /cso removal note already says its CI jobs are gone.

The /gstack-ship rename note promised that "a few review-limit and ruled-edit messages still say `/ship`; a follow-up fixes them". That follow-up, #4829, is in this release, so the parenthetical is gone. The /cso removal note said that on Opus "/cso was at best no better", but the measured 95% interval (−19.6 to +2.0 points, gstack-evals#462) still allows /cso to be slightly better, so the note now just says the gap is within the margin of error.

A note already on main can't be edited in place (the release refuses that), so both corrections delete the old file and add the text under a new name, as docs/ship-policy.md says. A short contributor note records the cleanup.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the next release's CHANGELOG section and release notes change. A dry run of the release step on this branch folded all 19 notes into 1.104.0.0 with each heading once and no outdated sentence left (script ran). The two renamed notes will link this PR instead of #4833 and #4775 in the generated release notes, because the release-notes script credits the commit that added each file.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

The core checklist found no issues. The second-model review (GPT-6.2 Sol) raised two findings. First, if the v1.104.0.0 release were cut before this PR landed, the two renamed notes would be added again to the following release; that is ruled a disclosed note, because this PR lands before that release is cut or closes unmerged. Second, the renamed notes credit this PR in the generated release notes, as Blast radius says; that is a low, non-blocking note.

title: v1.104.0.0 release
body:
v1.104.0.0 ships 30 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each. It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.
Release notes - gstack now picks the newest Opus, Fable, Sol and Astra everywhere it chooses a model. (#4811) - /autoplan no longer asks the owner a third time for changes his "do it" already approved. (#4809) - The destructive-command check no longer asks before deleting a file inside another `git worktree` of the same repository, or elsewhere in the session's own worktree. (#4834) - New guide section: you don't need to cut back on MCP servers for accuracy, up to about 300 tools, as long as Claude Code's tool search stays on. (#4814) - This release's notes no longer contradict each other. (#4839) - An owner can now let a small edit made after the final review ship as a disclosed note, and /ship honours it. (#4818) - `/eval-plan` lets a judge that grades code be checked against a third model's labels instead of people's (R126). (#4824) - `gstack-pr-wait` no longer blocks on a cancelled check that a newer passing run of the same check replaced. (#4832) - The `DEPS_MISSING` stop names npm's `allow-git` setting when the lockfile installs a package from git. (#4832) - The docs audit /gstack-ship launches starts after a reviewer's install replaced the shared install verdict. (#4832) - `gstack-ship-receipt write` leaves a retired `scoped-fix-check` row out of `--no-stop`, (#4832) - The QA-only cleanup test no longer fails at random in CI. (#4823) - Three tests that failed at random now pass reliably. (#4821) - Six tests that failed at random now pass reliably. (#4830) - /gstack-ship honours a ruled edit after the final review, and a stop on a second-model blocker records. (#4829) - `/ship` is now `/gstack-ship`, so Claude Code loads gstack's shipping skill again (#4775). (#4839) - make-pdf's new layout handles three more cases. (#4828) - make-pdf has a bold new default look, and `--style plain` keeps the old one. (#4820) - The CI image now runs Claude Code 2.1.326 and Codex 0.172.0, versions that know gstack's newest default models. (#4822) - `bin/gstack-capy-install` reads the Codex setup model from the astra row of `lib/model-families.ts` instead of naming it, so the next Astra release is still a one-line change. (#4822) - The default judge's move to claude-fable-5-2 is checked against the labelled controls next to its callers (plan-decision and DX peer-comparison calibrations, the redaction semantic pass): every item agreed with its label. (#4822) - The test harness keeps working on Claude Code 2.1.326. (#4822) - A release no longer rewrites version numbers inside changelog entries, counts subsection headings as changes, or prints a subsection heading twice. (#4803) - The /cso security audit skill is gone, because a plain request for a security audit now finds more real problems. (#4839) - /gstack-ship no longer has round grants, fix-check grants or the review-loop exception: after two review rounds a blocker ships only as an owner's ruled note, or the PR parks. (#4826) - `gstack-ship-queue ready` no longer asks for a cross-family read of the decision trail. (#4826) - `gstack-ship-receipt stop` works before a PR exists. (#4826) - Receipt checks read a path with `*` or `?` in its name as that file. (#4826) - The /gstack-ship driver records spend at start and close only, (#4826) - Skill routing no longer fires on subagent hand-backs or on a passing mention of "code review". (#4831)

title: C:/Program Files/Git/codex challenge and consult trip destructive_guard on every run (unguarded $PROMPT_FILE in rm)
body:
## What happens

Every `/codex challenge` and `/codex consult` run stops at the gstack destructive-command hook:

```
[careful] Destructive: deletes files outside this session's folder, or through a variable that may be empty.
```

The trigger is the cleanup line at the end of the bash block:

- `codex/sections/challenge-mode.md.tmpl`: `rm -f "$TMPRESP" "$TMPRESP.events" "$PROMPT_FILE"`
- `codex/sections/consult-mode.md.tmpl`: `rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"`

`$TMPRESP` comes from `mktemp`, so `check-careful.sh` already treats it as scratch. `PROMPT_FILE="$_REPO_ROOT/.gstack/tmp/..."` has a `$` in its value, so `_careful_resolve` can't resolve it and flags it as an unguarded variable. The hook is right to be careful here; the skill's own command is what trips it.

## Fix

Guard the variable, so an empty value makes the shell abort instead of running `rm`:

```diff
-rm -f "$TMPRESP" "$TMPRESP.events" "$PROMPT_FILE"
+rm -f "$TMPRESP" "$TMPRESP.events" "${PROMPT_FILE:?}"
```
```diff
-rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"
+rm -f "${PROMPT_FILE:?}"
```

(plus the regenerated `.md` files)

## Checked

Feeding `check-careful.sh` the challenge-mode command:

```
rm -f "$TMPRESP" "$TMPRESP.events" "$PROMPT_FILE"        → permissionDecision: ask
rm -f "$TMPRESP" "$TMPRESP.events" "${PROMPT_FILE:?}"    → {}
```

Same result for the consult-mode line. Seen at 1145e80a.

title: plan-eng-review/plan-ceo-review: Codex outside voice can't run in Claude Code plan mode — prompt file is written to $TMPDIR with the Write tool, which plan mode refuses
body:
## What happened

`/plan-eng-review` (same text in `/plan-ceo-review`) could not run its Codex outside voice while Claude Code was in **plan mode**. Codex was never launched; the skill fell back to the native reviewer.

The outside-voice step (generated by `scripts/resolvers/outside-voice.ts` around line 181, rendered into `plan-eng-review/sections/review-sections.md` and `plan-ceo-review/sections/review-sections.md`) says:

> Create a private prompt file: run `umask 077; mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gstack-plan-prompt.XXXXXXXX"` in Bash and keep the returned path. Use Write to put the complete prompt and context ... in that file

From the session transcript (`permissionMode: "plan"`):

1. Bash `mktemp` **succeeded** and created an empty file under `$TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/.../T/gstack-plan-prompt.h7XtYt9m`).
2. The Write tool on that path was **refused**:
   ```
   Cannot edit files outside allowed directories (<workspace>). Attempted to edit: /var/folders/<...>/T/gstack-plan-prompt.h7XtYt9m
   ```
3. Following the skill ("if a write fails or is refused, do not send"), no Codex process started → native fallback.

In plan mode, Claude Code's Write/Edit tools are limited to the working directory (plus the plan file), while `$TMPDIR` is outside it. So the step as written cannot succeed in plan mode, which is exactly where plan reviews usually run. Expected: the Codex outside voice runs during plan mode.

## Suggested fix

Create the prompt file inside the working tree, in a gitignored scratch dir the skills already use with the Write tool (e.g. `.gstack/tmp/`, as the question-preference step does with `.gstack/tmp/qt.txt`):

```bash
mkdir -p .gstack/tmp && umask 077 && mktemp ".gstack/tmp/gstack-plan-prompt.XXXXXXXX"
```

and delete it after the run. (Alternatively, fall back to the in-workspace path only when the `$TMPDIR` Write is refused.) The hermetic test in `test/autoplan-dual-voice-fixture.test.ts` builds this same mktemp command, so it would need to change too.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In Claude Code, enter plan mode (Shift+Tab) in any git repo, with Codex installed and authenticated.
2. Run `/plan-eng-review` on a plan, accept the outside voice (Codex).
3. The Write to `$TMPDIR/gstack-plan-prompt.*` is refused; Codex never runs.

title: /careful: heredoc bodies are scanned as shell commands
body:
Since 1.103 made the destructive-command check a default hook, I get approval prompts in auto mode for commands that don't delete anything. Almost all of them have the same cause: the check reads the body of a heredoc as if it were shell.

#1060 fixed this for `git commit -m "..."` and for `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`. Any other heredoc still goes through the statement scan, which splits the body at newlines and backticks and checks each line as a command.

### Repro

1.103.1.0 on Windows 11 with Git Bash. I sent each of these as `tool_input.command` to `careful/bin/check-careful.sh`:

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
t = "the script runs rm -rf on the staging lib folder"
print(t)
EOF
```

```bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
staging: rm -rf the lib folder before copying
EOF
```

Both come back with:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"[careful] Destructive: recursive delete (rm -r). This permanently removes files."}}
```

The same message through `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"` returns `{}`, and so does the Python heredoc once the string no longer says `rm`.

Agents write heredocs like these all day, for small Python edits and for commit messages, and the text tends to describe the change. The one that made me look was a script rewriting a changelog line about a build step that clears a folder.

### What I'd expect

With a quoted delimiter (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`, `<<\EOF`) the body is literal, so it could be skipped the same way the commit message is. With an unquoted delimiter, `$(...)` and backticks in the body still run, so those parts would still need the scan.

### Windows temp folders

A smaller thing. A recursive delete only counts as scratch under `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` (`_RX_TMP`). Git Bash maps `/tmp` to `%TEMP%`, but the same folder written as `C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Temp/<dir>` still asks, and that's the spelling my agent's scratch folder has. Treating the resolved `%TEMP%` path like `/tmp` would cover it.

For now I've turned the guard off with `gstack-config set destructive_guard off`. That works, but I'd rather have it on.

title: Setup works on Windows when the home folder name has an apostrophe (#4386)
body:
`./setup` on Windows now installs when your home folder has an apostrophe in its name, such as `C:\Users\O'Brien`. Git Bash turns `/c/...` paths into `C:/...` before starting Bun, but skips any path holding an apostrophe, so setup stopped with `Module not found`. Nothing to do: re-run `./setup` after upgrading.
What changed ![Setup on a Windows runner with an apostrophe in the home folder: Bun could not find the script before; setup now finishes](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/WQuzRuMzeqNwW5dnzEw8Q1Ocb0gOY2tJNrUqlDp3D1k.png) Setup on a Windows runner with an apostrophe in the home folder: Bun could not find the script before; setup now finishes. Before/after as text: ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output +$ HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/o'brien/smoke-home" ./setup --host claude # Windows runner, this branch (run 45842245130) +gstack ready (claude) +/ship, /review, /qa-only, /browse: SKILL_START_PROTO: 1 +/browse chain from an unrelated directory: gstack-windows-smoke-ok -$ HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/o'brien/smoke-home" ./setup --host claude # Windows runner, main (run 45840283430) -+ bun --no-env-file --config=NUL '/d/a/_temp/o'\''brien/smoke-home/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/preflight-codex-overlap.ts' ... -error: Module not found "/d/a/_temp/o'brien/smoke-home/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/preflight-codex-overlap.ts" -##[error]Process completed with exit code 1. ~~~ A Windows user whose home folder name has an apostrophe could not install gstack: `./setup` handed Bun a `/c/Users/O'Brien/...` path, which Git Bash leaves unconverted, and Bun stopped with `Module not found`. Setup now converts every path it passes to Bun itself, through a small `_bun_path` helper that uses `cygpath -m` under Git Bash and does nothing elsewhere. That covers the Codex overlap preflight (script, `--source`, `--namespace`, `--relocation`), `gstack-harness` refresh and register, the skill-route default lookup and the skill-gate hook timeout. A new test pins those call sites and checks the helper on any OS. The proof is a one-off `windows-smoke` dispatch from a scratch branch, not a new required check. It cloned gstack into `$RUNNER_TEMP/o'brien/smoke-home/.claude/skills/gstack` and ran setup there: [run 45840283430](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/45840283430) failed on main, and [run 45842245130](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/45842245130) passed setup, the core skills start and the `/browse` chain flow.
Why "`./setup` still passes Bun unconverted paths under a home folder with an apostrophe" was the gap left open on #4386 after #4682. Windows users with such a name can now install gstack at all.
Blast radius Only Git Bash and Cygwin behave differently. Off Windows `_bun_path` prints its argument unchanged, which `test/setup-bun-path-apostrophe.test.ts` checks (script ran), and the full free suite passed on this head. No dependencies, network, permissions or workflows change.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds and a second-model adversarial read. Round 1 found one gap (the `--relocation` path was unconverted), fixed in this PR. The final review of the whole diff found nothing blocking. The adversarial read raised four notes below the blocking floor, listed next; all four were already broken before this PR and lose no data.
Review notes Below the blocking floor (advisory, informational, test-gap or wording items); recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `setup:2054` bun_cmd start of gstack-migrate-claude-code still passes unconverted paths; under an apostrophe home the legacy wrapper migration fails quietly (pre-existing, no data loss). - INFORMATIONAL `setup:4474` gbrain render passes unconverted --out-dir/--link-root paths; render keeps the previous output under an apostrophe home (pre-existing). - INFORMATIONAL `setup:4426` gstack-gbrain-detect (Bun shebang) may hit the same conversion skip; needs a Windows run with gbrain installed. - INFORMATIONAL `setup:5013` SKILL_ROUTE_BIN assignment would abort setup under set -e if cygpath -m failed (theoretical).
Eval Results No prompt-related files changed, so evals were skipped.

title: The release gate's live /autoplan guard test runs on Haiku 5.5 (GST-3441)
body:
The live /autoplan guard test in the release gate now runs its scripted actor on Claude Haiku 5.5 instead of Haiku 4.5.
On Haiku 5.5 the actor used to act before the background reviewer finished, so the test failed 8 of 8 release gate attempts; the test now waits on the reviewer's hand-back itself, whatever the model's speed.
Nothing to do; it passed one paid run on Claude Code 2.1.326.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![The live guard test now sees the actor's next steps after the reviewer hands back, and passes on Haiku 5.5](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/mLrMEWqbZGxRiJ8mDQXnyEeCe-gCTlunYdCEf1Bru40.png)

The live guard test now sees the actor's next steps after the reviewer hands back, and passes on Haiku 5.5.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: The live guard test now sees the actor's next steps after the reviewer hands back, and passes on Haiku 5.5</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ live autoplan guard test, Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.326 (paid run 5, at 129e1c4)
-$ live autoplan guard test, Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.326 (paid run 4, before the evidence fix)
 guard decisions: allow, allow, allow, allow   permission cards: 0
 reviewer hand-back waits: 2
+steps seen after the reviewer's hand-back:
+  Read .../autoplan-ceo-*/close-packet.md
+  Bash true autoplan-published ceo
+  Read .../autoplan/sections/design-phase.md
+  Agent Design review
+(pass) autoplan publication guard live PTY > autoplan-guard-pty [489379ms]
+ 1 pass
+ 0 fail
-steps seen after the reviewer's hand-back: (none)
-error: expect(received).toBe(expected)  Expected: true  Received: false
-(fail) autoplan publication guard live PTY > autoplan-guard-pty [489160ms]
- 0 pass
- 1 fail
 
~~~

</details>

- **Relay wait** (`test/helpers/autoplan-guard-pty.ts`): after the actor's background CEO reviewer dispatch, the test's local API relay answers the actor with an end-of-turn message until that reviewer's report comes back, and it also counts a report that arrives in the same request as the launch result. It recognises both forms of the notice: `<task-notification>` naming the call, and the `<agent-message from="<agentId>">` hand-back that Claude Code 2.1.326 actually sends in the request.
- **Evidence**: the test's journal reader takes the earlier of the task-notification record and the hand-back as the start of the notice turn, reads hand-backs whether the request stores them as plain strings or as text blocks, and the test prints the journal whenever that evidence is missing.
- **Launch**: the test sets `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0`. Behind a local relay, Claude Code's auto-mode billing notice otherwise holds the reviewer's first checked action waiting for Enter (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-classifier-billing).
- **Model**: `claude-haiku-5-5`, with an assertion that the relay wait ran or the report came back with the launch result.
- Free regression tests from the captured request shapes; they fail on the previous relay and journal reader.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

The release gate's live guard test failed 8 of 8 attempts once its actor moved to Haiku 5.5, because the faster model read the close packet before the background reviewer had handed back. The relay now holds the actor until the hand-back arrives, so the test checks the guard instead of the model's timing.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

Only the live guard test and its helper change; no product code, skill or prompt is touched. The helper's new exports are used by that test and its free fixture test alone (read in test/skill-e2e-autoplan-guard-pty.test.ts and test/autoplan-guard-pty-fixture.test.ts), and the full free suite passed in CI at this head.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Two review rounds. In round one the second-model review found two blockers: a reviewer report that arrived in the same request as the launch result left the wait counter at zero, and hand-backs stored as text blocks were missed by the journal reader. Both are fixed, each with a free test that fails without the fix. Round two found nothing.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. This audit found no documentation corrections and made no edits.

**Scope:** 4 committed files from base e6dd5673 to head f012176 on autoplan-guard-runs-on-haiku-5-5, with no staged, unstaged or new files. The change is test-only: the live /autoplan guard test now runs its actor on Claude Haiku 5.5, its relay holds the actor until the reviewer hands back, and the test sets CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0. The branch also adds one changelog.d note.

title: Let /gstack-ship handle very large results PRs (GST-4003)
body:
`/gstack-ship` now works on results PRs with tens of thousands of files and hundreds of megabytes of diff: more exclusion patterns, a secrets check with no size limit, a faster review plan and docs check, and bulleted ruled notes. Why: two 16,000-file results PRs hit each of these limits in real runs. Nothing to do: existing policies keep working unchanged.
What changed - **More exclusion patterns.** `review_exclude_paths` takes up to 256 patterns (was 64). A list longer than 64 must also fit its exclude pathspecs in 24,000 argument bytes together, because every reviewer's single `git diff` includes all of them. Every list the old cap accepted still validates. An older gstack reads a longer list as invalid and reviews every file, which is safe. - **Better fix advice when a reviewer's diff is too big.** The suggestion never offers to hide `docs/` (a results report is what the reviewer needs to read) and counts only data, log and binary bytes. When the suggested folders would push the base list past the cap or the byte budget, it prints no JSON and asks for the existing patterns to be merged instead of printing a policy gstack would refuse. - **Secrets check with no size limit.** The pre-merge secrets check and `gstack-banned-terms` used to read the whole diff through a 256 MiB pipe. git now writes it to a private file that is read back in whole-file parts (`lib/diff-parts.ts`), so each parser sees exactly what it saw before. A 361.8 MB diff now reads in 4 parts in 3.9 s. - **Faster review plan.** Matching the exclusion patterns now takes one `git diff` plus a cheap match per pattern instead of one diff per pattern. The search for code that names excluded files hands `git grep` each path's extension instead of all 16,165 paths (37 s down to 0.4 s for that grep) and finds the exact paths in each file it reads. On a real 16,165-file PR the plan went from 180 s to 100 s on 4 cores, with byte-identical output. - **Faster docs check.** The docs-only check finds which files name each changed doc with one `git grep -f -` instead of one grep per file: 5.6 s and one grep on the same PR. - **Bulleted ruled notes.** A PR body may list each `Ruled note: …` line as a `- ` or `* ` list item. The rest of the line must still match word for word.
Not in this PR A reviewer diff that is still over 2 MB after exclusions still stops with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`. Splitting it into several bounded reviewer slices changes how a review pass records and checks its reviewers, so it comes in a follow-up PR.
Testing New focused tests: `test/diff-parts.test.ts`, `test/docs-only-batched.test.ts`, `test/review-exclude-match.test.ts`, `test/review-exclude-pattern-cap.test.ts` and `test/ruled-note-bullets.test.ts`. They cover a file that replaces a folder of the same name, bracket and backslash patterns (a folder literally named `res/[0-9]*`), a consumer file git reads from the index (assume-unchanged), and 64 long multibyte patterns that the old cap accepted. The 64-pattern fallback tests now use 257 patterns. 336 tests in the review-exclude, docs-only, secrets, diff-parts, ship-policy and module-size suites pass locally, along with `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:test`. CI runs the full suite.
Documentation **Status:** updated (one factual doc correction, no blockers) **Scope:** the 21 selected files from fd81a04 to b8c6f60 (committed only; nothing staged, unstaged or untracked), checked against docs/ship-policy.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/review-policy.md and docs/pregate.md. **Documentation health** - docs/ship-policy.md: current. It already documents the 256-pattern and 24,000-byte limits for review_exclude_paths, the 257-pattern fallback example and Ruled note bullets. - docs/troubleshooting.md: updated. The POLICY_INVALID fallback example now names 256 patterns for review_exclude_paths and 64 for review_content_patterns. The suggested-fix and Ruled note bullet wording was already current. - docs/review-policy.md: current. Its 256 MB consumer-scan limit is unchanged by this branch. - docs/pregate.md: current. Its 64-per-list limit applies to pregate.json. - changelog.d/large-results-prs-ship-scaling.md: matches the code (not edited). **Coverage debt:** no dedicated doc says that the pre-merge secrets check and gstack-banned-terms now read large diffs in parts, or that the docs-only reference search is now batched. Both are internal speed and robustness changes, and the changelog fragment covers them. No diagrams are affected.
Review notes Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/review-exclude-match.ts:48`: the per-pattern fallback has no test that forces it. - INFORMATIONAL `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts:200`: the 256 MiB full-context cutoff has no test that forces it. - Low `lib/diff-parts.ts:31`: git's stderr keeps the 1 MiB default buffer, so very chatty warnings could fail the diff (it fails closed). - Low `lib/docs-only.ts:180`: the batched reference read can use more memory than the old grep on very large consumer files (it fails closed). - Low `lib/ship-policy-keys.ts:59`: lists of 65 to 256 patterns have no version floor, so an older gstack sets them aside and reviews every file. - Low `lib/ship-policy-keys.ts:65`: the comment's command-line budget leaves out the keep literals and `forbid_paths` specs.
Agent notes GST-4003, reported from harness-evals#616 and #619. The real-PR timings come from a local clone of #616 (base 26ca0095, head 98d30986) on a 4-core cloud machine. title: make-pdf blocks javascript: links written with tabs or entity letters, plus four small fixes (GST-3641)
body:
make-pdf now removes `javascript:` links in untrusted Markdown even when the scheme is split by a tab or line break or written with entity letters, and it fixes curly quotes at the start of a paragraph, SVG sizing, one learnings crash and one lost timeline event.
Why: these spellings still produced live links in the HTML make-pdf prints, and the other four bugs were verified on main by an independent check.
Nothing for readers to do; ordinary Markdown prints the same apart from opening quotes, which now curl the right way.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

- **make-pdf sanitizer.** Each URL attribute value (`href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`, `xlink:href`) is decoded the way the browser decodes it, with tabs and line breaks removed. If it still starts with `javascript:`, a `#` goes in front, which makes the whole value a harmless fragment. The existing rules are unchanged, so this only adds catches. A click handler whose quoted value contains `>` is now removed with its value when it starts an attribute of its tag; inside another attribute's value only its name goes, as before. A numeric reference such as `Ϋ` that only starts like a colon no longer rewrites an ordinary link.
- **make-pdf typography.** A quote right after a block tag (paragraph, heading, list item, table cell) opens. Inline tags such as `<em>` are read through, and images, code and unknown tags count as a word, so `--flag` and the quotes after a placeholder stay as they were.
- **SVG size.** `stroke-width` and `data-height` are no longer read as the width or height, so a wide diagram moves to a sideways page again.
- **Learnings.** A row whose `files` is a string or whose `ts` is a number no longer breaks every later search; the log stores a single path as a list; another project's learning never replaces this project's own.
- **Timeline.** Every event is stored as one line, and a numeric `ts` no longer stops `gstack-timeline-read`.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

make-pdf prints Markdown that often comes from somewhere else, and its print browser runs page scripts, so a `javascript:` link that survives the sanitizer is live. The other four fixes are bugs an independent check reproduced on main. They caused wrong quote direction in most documents that open with a quote, left wide diagrams on upright pages, let one bad learnings row silence every later search, and skipped pretty-printed timeline events without a word.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

`make-pdf/src/render.ts`, `make-pdf/src/smartypants.ts`, `make-pdf/src/image-size.ts`, `bin/gstack-learnings-log`, `bin/gstack-learnings-search`, `bin/gstack-timeline-log`, `bin/gstack-timeline-read`. No settings, defaults, dependencies, network, permissions or install changes. Rendering all 599 tracked Markdown files with main and with this branch changes only quote direction: 450 quote characters, every one from closing to opening at the start of a block, and nothing else.

</details>

<details><summary>Security notes</summary>

- Attack replay over 8,090 generated cases (handlers, `javascript:` spellings with tabs, line breaks, entity letters, padding past 2,048 characters, attributes right after a closing quote), parsed with htmlparser2 with tabs and line breaks stripped from URLs the way browsers do: main leaves 1,530 live, this branch 0.
- Still open, older than this PR: SVG animation attributes (`<animate>`/`<set>` with `attributeName=href`), `data:` and `vbscript:` schemes, and a remote `href` inside an unclosed `<svg>` after a `>` in an earlier quoted attribute.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

Pre-Landing Review: 13 issues — 4 fixed, 0 asked, 1 deferred, 6 noted, 0 open. Four review rounds: two full rounds, then two read-only full reviews of later heads; the last one, at 3d90c13, came back with no blocking findings.

</details>

<details><summary>Deferred findings</summary>

- Deferred: CRITICAL `make-pdf/src/render.ts:368` The tab and entity `javascript:` catch also rewrites `href=java	script:` text that sits inside another URL's path. Main already rewrites the plain `href=javascript:` spelling there the same way, so this is the existing fail-closed over-catch, not a new class.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

- Informational: one crafted tag with thousands of quoted `on…=` values holding `>` is slow to sanitize (128 KB took about 16 s; main 3 ms), because each handler rescans its tag. Ordinary documents are unaffected.
- Informational: a quote opening the text of `details`, `summary` or `label` still curls as closing, as on main.
- Informational: this project's own learning now wins over another project's with the same key even when its confidence has decayed; that is the intended rule.
- Informational: timeline events with their own `ts` are now re-serialized, so duplicate keys collapse to the last value.

</details>

<details><summary>Documentation</summary>

**Status:** current. No documentation edits were needed for this release.

**Scope:** 13 committed files (base fd81a04b to head eef1c541): make-pdf's untrusted-HTML sanitizer (javascript: links with tabs, line breaks or entity letters; click-handler values containing `>`; colon-like numeric entities), smartypants quote context at block starts, SVG width parsing, and fixes to gstack-learnings-search, gstack-learnings-log, gstack-timeline-log and gstack-timeline-read. No staged, unstaged or new files.

**Documentation health:**

**Coverage debt:** None critical. All changes are bug fixes with no new public surface. The minor reference gap is that the learn skill does not say this project's own learnings win over other projects' learnings with the same key.

title: Make the plan-review test judge reject failed sessions and steady two flaky tests
body:
The plan-review test judge now fails a Claude Code session whose final result reports an error, even when the process exits 0, so a broken session can no longer pass a quality check. Two tests that failed at random are steadier, and one of them now says why when it fails. Nothing to do.
What changed ![test/plan-floor-review.test.ts with the old judge helper (left) and this branch's (right): the three judge tests fail before and pass after](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/l28qZutxe68JIjLLSx7arl536Lrtlo4-BlRnlzIvvRM.png) test/plan-floor-review.test.ts with the old judge helper and with this branch's: the three judge tests fail before and pass after.
Before/after as text: test/plan-floor-review.test.ts with the old judge helper (left) and this branch's (right): the three judge tests fail before and pass after ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output + 84 pass + 0 fail -(fail) replacement judge retains the original CLI model, a tool-free schema session, measured cap and absolute case deadline [5.98ms] -(fail) an exit 0 whose result event reports an error is no assessment, even after an accepted call [1.88ms] -(fail) a CLI notice line is skipped, but a broken JSON event still fails the assessment [0.19ms] - 81 pass - 3 fail ~~~
A second-model review of the plan-review judge found that it trusted an answer from a session that ended in an error: when Claude Code exits 0 but its last result event says `is_error: true`, the judge used the assessment it had seen earlier. The judge (`test/helpers/plan-floor-review.ts`) now rejects that session. It also runs Claude Code with slash commands and hooks turned off, like gstack's other Claude Code calls, and skips a plain notice line in the output while still failing on a broken JSON event. The question-log Bun-config test (`test/bun-config-shell-bins.test.ts`) failed twice in CI with one leftover record written a few milliseconds before the failing test began. Each `gstack-question-log` write starts a background developer-profile update that keeps writing into the test's state folder after the test returns; the test now turns that update off with `GSTACK_QUESTION_LOG_NO_DERIVE=1`. This is the probable cause, not a reproduced one: 48 stress runs of the real test and 300 tight-loop trials never failed. title: Upgrading from inside the gstack checkout no longer reinstalls Codex you removed (#4835)
body:
Running `./setup --refresh-registered` (what `/gstack-upgrade` runs) from inside the gstack checkout no longer puts Codex skills back into `~/.codex/skills` after you removed them.
Why: upgrades should refresh only the installs you have. Reported by @schubter. Fixes #4835.
Nothing to do: the next upgrade refreshes only the installs you actually have.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![Inside the gstack checkout, the checkout's own Codex render is no longer listed as a project install](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/pxdrVdBg1oxO7jf5MkcG57-iks2ta2xs7q7Zq_FuIEM.png)

Inside the gstack checkout, the checkout's own Codex render is no longer listed as a project install.

</details>

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- [x] `bun test test/setup-install-registry.test.ts`: 19 pass, 0 fail, including the three new #4835 cases, which failed on main (8982588) before the fix
- [x] Adjacent install tests (host-renders, host-conformance, claude-overlay-setup-installs, gstack-upgrade-bin, spawnsync-timeout-tripwire, six setup-codex-scope files): 181 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:test`: clean
- [x] CI free suite at 8145261: green (run 45858357140, 1723 files)

</details>

<details><summary>Before/after as text: Inside the gstack checkout, the checkout's own Codex render is no longer listed as a project install</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ cd ~/.local/share/gstack && gstack_install_known_roots | grep project   # after
-$ cd ~/.local/share/gstack && gstack_install_known_roots | grep project   # before
 claude	project	~/.local/share/gstack/.claude/skills	~/.local/share/gstack/.claude/skills/gstack
-codex	project	~/.local/share/gstack/.agents/skills	~/.local/share/gstack/.agents/skills/gstack
 
~~~

A user with only a Claude install removed `~/.codex/skills/gstack`, ran the upgrade from inside their gstack checkout, and got Codex reinstalled globally. The checkout keeps its own Codex skill render at `.agents/skills/gstack`, and the upgrade's search for older installs treated that folder as a Codex install inside a project. Since the checkout lives under `~/.claude/skills`, setup then installed Codex globally and added it back to the checkout's installed hosts.

The list of places setup checks for older installs (`gstack_install_known_roots` in `bin/gstack-install-registry.sh`) now leaves out the project Codex folder when it resolves, with symlinks followed, to the same checkout as the project root. A separate project that keeps its own gstack copy at `.agents/skills/gstack` is still found and refreshed. `./setup --status` had its own copy of this check, which is removed now that the shared list does it.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

gstack's install rules say an upgrade refreshes exactly the installs you registered and never brings back one you removed (docs/ADDING_A_HOST.md, rule 3). This bug broke that rule for anyone who upgrades from inside their checkout.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The list feeds three callers, which are the upgrade's discovery of older installs (`setup`), `./setup --status`, and the first record of a checkout's installed hosts (`gstack_render_hosts_seed` in `bin/gstack-host-renders.sh`). All three now ignore only a folder that resolves to the checkout it sits in, which was already what `--status` did; the new tests run the real `./setup` for both the checkout case and the vendored-project case, and the existing install, host-render and Codex-scope tests pass unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Pre-Landing Review</summary>

No blocking issues. The second reviewer noted one low-severity side effect, listed below and not fixed here.

</details>

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Below the blocking floor; recorded here and not fixed in this PR.

- INFORMATIONAL `bin/gstack-install-registry.sh`: a checkout that has no installed-hosts record yet, and no Codex install anywhere, no longer counts its own `.agents` render as Codex being used, so setup's host-render cleanup moves that render to a backup on the first run. `./setup --host codex` brings it back. This is the behavior #4835 asks for.

</details>

**Status:** current. The docs already match this change, so nothing was edited.

**Scope:** the diff from base 89825888 to HEAD 81452615 (bin/gstack-install-registry.sh, the changelog fragment and test/setup-install-registry.test.ts), with no staged, unstaged or new files. I searched the docs for `--refresh-registered`, `.agents/skills/gstack` and install-registry discovery.

**Documentation health:**

- docs/troubleshooting.md: Current. Its Quick answers still describe project installs at `.agents/skills/gstack` correctly.
- docs/hosts.md: Current.
- docs/capy-install.md: Current.
- changelog.d/setup-refresh-skips-checkout-codex-render.md: Current. It is accurate and plain; CHANGELOG.md is not touched.

title: /codex cleanup stops asking for /careful approval, and plan-mode Codex reviews start again
body:
`/codex challenge` and `/codex consult` no longer stop for a /careful delete warning on every run, and the Codex second-model review in `/plan-eng-review` and `/plan-ceo-review` works in Claude Code plan mode again.
Why: both broke a core review path on every use; the reports came from @dmfrede and @mcp10.
Nothing to do after merge.

<details><summary>What changed</summary>

![/careful no longer asks about the /codex cleanup, and the plan-review prompt file moves into the project](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/oZyQfdnpz_APCkVgBELUYM8HkHR-LrZ40a_Jw_d1ul4.png)

/careful no longer asks about the /codex cleanup, and the plan-review prompt file moves into the project.

<details><summary>Before/after as text: /careful no longer asks about the /codex cleanup, and the plan-review prompt file moves into the project</summary>

~~~diff
--- Before · before.txt · captured output
+++ After · after.txt · captured output
+$ /codex consult cleanup, as the /careful hook sees it (this PR)
-$ /codex consult cleanup, as the /careful hook sees it (main)
 PROMPT_FILE="$_REPO_ROOT/.gstack/tmp/codex-prompt.AbC123"
+rm -f "${PROMPT_FILE:?}"
-rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"
 
 /careful:
+{}
+(allowed, no prompt)
-ask: [careful] Destructive: deletes files outside this session's folder, or through a variable that may be empty.
 
+$ plan review prompt file (this PR)
+[ ! -L .gstack -a ! -L .gstack/tmp ] && mkdir -p -m700 .gstack/tmp && mktemp "$PWD/.gstack/tmp/gstack-plan-prompt.XXXXXX"
+the file lands inside the project, where plan mode lets Write reach it
-$ plan review prompt file (main)
-umask 077; mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gstack-plan-prompt.XXXXXXXX"
-Claude Code plan mode: Write to $TMPDIR is refused, so Codex never starts
 
~~~

</details>

"Every /codex challenge run stops for a /careful approval at cleanup" (#4841): the cleanup deleted the prompt with `rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"`, a variable /careful cannot resolve, so it asked every time. The cleanup now reads `"${PROMPT_FILE:?}"`, which /careful already accepts as guarded. The hook itself is unchanged.

"The Codex outside voice fails in plan mode" (#4842): the plan reviews created the prompt under `$TMPDIR`, where plan mode refuses Write, so Codex never ran. The prompt now goes to `.gstack/tmp/` inside the project (folder mode 700, file mode 600). The command refuses a `.gstack` or `.gstack/tmp` that is a symlink, so a cloned repo cannot redirect the prompt. Cleanup is a plain `rm -- '<path>'`, which /careful allows.

</details>

<details><summary>Why</summary>

People reported that /codex stopped for approval on every run and that the plan-review second opinion never started in plan mode. Now /codex runs straight through under /careful, and plan-mode reviews get their second-model review again.

</details>

<details><summary>Blast radius</summary>

The change touches the generated /codex, /plan-eng-review and /plan-ceo-review skill files for every host, and nothing else reads these lines. The /careful hook is unchanged: the new test feeds the generated lines to `careful/bin/check-careful.sh` and runs the generated create and cleanup commands in a scratch repo (script ran).
