title: The destructive-command check no longer asks about text inside quoted heredocs (#4843)
body:
Commit messages sent with `git commit -F - <<'EOF'`, `gh` bodies sent with `--body-file -` and a bare `cat <<'EOF'` no longer trigger an approval prompt because their text mentions `rm -rf` or `git push -f`. Bash never expands a body with a quoted delimiter, so it is text; a body read by a shell, `ssh`, `eval`, `python` or a SQL client, an editor or exec option, an unquoted delimiter, a pipe, and every command outside the body are still checked. Fixes #4843, reported by @nghorbani. Nothing to do after merging.
What changed - New `careful/bin/mask-heredoc.awk`, run by `check-careful.sh` only when a Bash command contains `<<`. It follows bash's quoting, comments and heredoc rules, and blanks only the body lines of a heredoc whose delimiter is quoted (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`, `<<\EOF`, and the `<<-` forms). The header line and closing delimiter are kept, so anything chained on them is still read. The hook change is 23 added lines; every existing check reads the masked command, as it already does for `git commit -m` messages (#1060). - Readers whose body counts as text: `git [-C dir] commit -F -` / `--file -` with only `-a`, `-q`, `-s`, `--allow-empty`, `--amend`, `--no-edit` or `--cleanup=` beside it; `gh issue|pr create|comment|edit -F -` / `--body-file -` with title, base, head, repo, label, assignee, reviewer, milestone and draft options only; and a bare `cat`. - Nothing is masked when the command has an unclosed heredoc, an unquoted delimiter, `$( )`, `${ }`, backticks, a pipe, an output redirect to a file, process substitution, a command named by a path or variable, or a shell or interpreter name inside any word (`sh`, `bash`, `ssh`, `eval`, `xargs`, `python`, `node` and others, so `-c core.editor=bash` and `--exec 'bash m'` count). PowerShell commands are never masked. - `python - <<'EOF'` still asks when its body mentions a destructive command: python runs its program, and no text check can show a program never starts a process. The first repro in #4843 therefore still asks; the commit-message repro no longer does. - One existing expectation in `test/hook-scripts.test.ts` recorded the bug (`git commit -F - <<'EOF'\ndocs: rm -rf src\nEOF` asks). It now expects no prompt, and its place in the "stays unmasked" table is taken by the unquoted twin, which still asks. - The Windows `%TEMP%` spelling mentioned at the end of #4843 is not part of this change: Windows has minimal support, and `/tmp` already covers Git Bash's scratch folder.
Tests - `test/careful-replay.test.ts`: 68 new rows. 12 fix rows (each asked or denied on main) and 56 controls that keep main's decision: `bash`/`sh`/`sh -s`/`zsh`/`dash`/`sudo bash`/`env bash`/`ssh host sh`/`ssh host` reading the body, `source`/`.` of stdin, `eval`, a read loop, here-strings, `git -c core.editor=bash`, `git commit -e`, `GIT_EDITOR=bash`, a later amend or `rebase --exec`, `gh --editor`, unquoted and unclosed delimiters, an indented delimiter without `<<-`, a CRLF delimiter, deletes chained with `&&`, `;`, `||` and `|` on the header line or after the closing line, a heredoc marker in a comment or in quotes, several heredocs on one line, every python heredoc, cat writing a script that a later command runs, and `psql`. Plus a 200 KB message timing test. - Main-vs-head replay over every payload the careful test files send: counts are in the agent notes.
Agent notes

title: Review diffs over the 2 MB ceiling in slices instead of stopping (GST-4019)
body:
`/gstack-ship` now reviews a reviewer diff over the 2,000,000-byte ceiling in up to 8 slices that share no file and together cover every file, instead of stopping with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`. Why: large results PRs (harness-evals#619 is 2.27 MB after exclusions) and large pure-deletion PRs (#4837, #4833) could not be reviewed at all. Nothing to do: diffs at or under the ceiling are reviewed exactly as before, byte for byte.
What changed ![A reviewer diff over 2 MB now goes to up to 8 slice reviewers instead of stopping the review](https://api.capy.ai/pr-assets/lPONu8lluFJBnOy1-I5IFwQuJ3_nHgn6wCnoQKX-0UA.png) A reviewer diff over 2 MB now goes to up to 8 slice reviewers instead of stopping the review.
Tests - `test/review-slices.test.ts` (19 cases): planner packing and refusals, a 5 MB three-folder diff whose brief commands git runs to prove disjoint full coverage, verify refusing missing, uncollected, overlapping and dropping slice sets, 92 deleted files, odd-character paths, `review_exclude_paths` with kept files, the under-ceiling control, one start per voice, the stage guard, the sliced targeted record, `--slice` usage errors, quarantine of a slice reviewer, and the native slice's fixture summary. - Targeted local run: 200 pass, 0 fail across 10 review test files; typecheck clean; test typecheck reports no new diagnostics. - CI at fcb14fc: every check green, free suite 1,730 files (run 45886312671).
Before/after as text: A reviewer diff over 2 MB now goes to up to 8 slice reviewers instead of stopping the review ~~~diff --- Before · before.txt · captured output +++ After · after.txt · captured output Independently of the key, no reader is handed more than 2,000,000 bytes of +diff. When one reader's kept diff is bigger than that, `gstack-review-dispatch pass` +reviews it in slices instead of cutting it (`lib/review-slices.ts`): -diff: `gstack-review-dispatch` stops with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE` before it writes -anything, instead of a review of the part a reader happened to see. +1. **Plan once.** From the diff it already read, pass packs the reader's files into + at most 8 slices of at most 2,000,000 bytes each. It keeps each top-level folder + in one slice when the folder fits, and otherwise splits the folder by its + subfolders and files in sorted path order. Both sides of a rename stay in one + slice, and so does a file beside the folder that replaces it. +2. **Each slice is a reader.** Reader `R` becomes `R#1/k` … `R#k/k` in the manifest. + Every `git diff` command in a slice's brief names that slice's paths as + `:(top,literal)` items next to the reader's exclude items (a folder whose every + file is in the slice is named once), kept files under the base policy's patterns + come back through the slice's own keep command, and the brief says it is slice + `i` of `k`. A native reader's fixture summary lists only that slice's test, + fixture and spec files. Collect and sent take `--slice i/k`. +3. **Coverage is checked twice.** Before anything is written, pass asks git for each + slice's file list and refuses unless the lists share no file, together equal the + reader's whole kept-file list, and each slice's diff is at or under the ceiling. + The manifest and each slice's ledger render record the sha256 of the kept-file + list and of the slice's list. `verify` recomputes them with git at the reviewed + tree and prints one `SLICE ` row: `MATCH` only when every slice 1..k was + rendered from one plan on one tree and collected, no two slices share a file and + no kept file is in no slice. `MISSING`, `NOT_COLLECTED`, `MIXED`, `CHANGED`, + `OVERLAP`, `DROPPED`, `OVER` or `UNREADABLE` makes it `VERIFY: dirty`, so the + pass binds no review row and no receipt. A `stage` whose tree moved after pass + planned the slices refuses before rendering them. +4. **One reviewer.** A sliced reader is still one reviewer: one plan entry, one + review-log row and one start token (Step 11 takes one `adversarial-review` + start for a native voice however many slices it has), and one R51 round. Its + findings are collected under each slice's key and judged together. -## What readers may fetch +What still stops with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`: one file (one diff section) over +2,000,000 bytes by itself (`slices=refused(file=…)` names it), a diff that needs +more than 8 slices (`slices=refused(needs=N cap=8)`), and a slice whose paths +would take more than the 24,000 argument bytes one command may carry. A standalone +`render` never slices; its refusal says how many slices the pass would use. The +outside voice is not sliced: it keeps its single embedded diff, cut at the ceiling -Every reader brief closes with the fetch rule, before the workspace paragraph: -review only this checkout and its local git history (the diff base is already -local), and never clone, fetch, pull or download another repository, dataset or -archive. The rule names each forbidden shape from one table in -`lib/review-fetch.ts`: `git clone`, `fetch`, `pull`, `ls-remote` or `submodule ~~~ A PR whose reviewer diff passed 2 MB used to stop with `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE`, and the only advice was to split the PR. Now `gstack-review-dispatch pass` packs that reviewer's files into at most 8 slices of at most 2 MB each, keeping each top-level folder together when it fits, then subfolders, then files in path order. Both sides of a rename stay together. Each slice becomes its own reviewer whose every `git diff` command names only that slice's paths, and its brief says it is slice i of k. Before anything is written, git confirms the slices share no file and together cover every file the reviewer would have read. `verify` checks the same thing again at the reviewed tree and refuses a missing, uncollected, overlapping or dropping slice set, so a sliced review cannot silently skip a file. A sliced reviewer still counts as one reviewer and one review round. What still stops: one file over 2 MB by itself, a diff that needs more than 8 slices, or a slice that names more paths than one command can hold. A single flat folder of thousands of small files can hit that last limit. The second-model review is not sliced; it keeps its single cut diff.
Why "harness-evals#619 is 2.27 MB after exclusions and can't be reviewed" (GST-4019). Big results PRs and big cleanup PRs now get a full review instead of a dead end.
Blast radius The change touches the review dispatcher, brief rendering, the review record and the Capy pass program, but only for a reviewer diff over the ceiling. Every reviewer at or under it renders the same bytes as on main. A replay of three fixtures at main be64b10 and at this branch compared 12 briefs and 27 artifacts with 0 differences (script ran), and `test/review-slices.test.ts` checks that a normal pass gains no slice reader or slice text.
Pre-Landing Review Two full review rounds. Round 1 (6d4da13) found test gaps, fixed with three tests. Its final review and the second-model review found that the fetch-rule quarantine ignored slice reviewers and that a native slice's fixture summary read the whole slice; both are fixed in b4ef1a0 with failing-first tests. Round 2 (b4ef1a0) found nothing at the blocking floor from the specialists, red team, native or targeted reviewers. The second-model review marked 5 items blocking; the maintainers ruled all 5 disclosed notes because each fails closed, predates this PR, or is still caught before a review can bind (listed in Agent notes). Review notes, not fixed in this PR: - No test checks the `slices=fits=N` refusal text, or the MIXED, OVER and UNREADABLE slice statuses. - A flat folder of many small files can exceed the 24,000-byte path limit and still refuse. - A slice reviewer's changed-file list shows only its own slice. - The pass plans slices from the working tree while verify checks the committed tree, so an uncommitted edit makes verify fail late. - The token-cap check prices one reviewer per role before slicing multiplies them. Gate edits: none detected (3 listed, 1 read; one test fixture enlarged so each session is still over the ceiling by itself).
Documentation **Status:** updated. Two small factual corrections; no blockers. **Scope:** be64b10..4e94b30 on review-large-diffs-in-slices (diffs over the 2 MB review ceiling are now reviewed in slices). The working tree was clean before the audit. Docs checked against `lib/review-slices.ts`, `lib/review-exclude.ts` and `bin/gstack-review-dispatch`. **Documentation health:** - `docs/review-policy.md`: current. The new review-ceiling section matches the code. - `docs/ship-policy.md`: updated. The review-ceiling stop reasons now include the 24,000-byte argument limit for a slice's paths. - `docs/troubleshooting.md`: updated. The `REVIEW_DIFF_TOO_LARGE` fix list now covers `slices=fits=`: run the reader through the pass, or start a fresh pass. - `docs/vendored-code.md`: current. It records a past measurement. - `changelog.d/review-large-diffs-in-slices.md`: reviewed only; not edited, by scope. **Coverage debt:** `gstack-review-dispatch pass` slicing and the `--slice i/k` flag have reference docs (review-policy, ship-policy, troubleshooting) but no how-to example. The `SLICE` verify row and its statuses are documented only in review-policy.md. No diagram drift found.

title: v1.104.1.0 release
body:
v1.104.1.0 ships 17 user-visible changes, listed one per line under Release notes with the pull request that made each. It changes only the version, the CHANGELOG and the files generated from them, so it needs no review: merge it once its checks are green.
Release notes - The release gate's live /autoplan guard test runs its scripted actor on Claude Haiku 5.5. (#4846) - `/codex challenge` and `/codex consult` no longer stop for a /careful delete warning at the end of every run. (#4851) - The Codex second-model review in `/plan-eng-review` and `/plan-ceo-review` works in Claude Code plan mode again. (#4851) - Upgrading now removes the old `ship` and `cso` skill folders that 1.104.0.0 left behind. (#4844) - `./setup` on Windows now works when your home folder has an apostrophe in its name, such as `C:\Users\O'Brien`. (#4845) - The plan-review test judge no longer accepts an answer from a session that reported an error. (#4849) - The `gstack-question-log` Bun-config test no longer sees a record left by the test before it. (#4849) - A brain-sync merge test that failed at random now shows the sync status message when it fails, (#4849) - `/gstack-ship` now handles very large results PRs. (#4847) - make-pdf removes `javascript:` links spelled with tabs, line breaks or entity letters. (#4848) - Quotes at the start of a paragraph, heading, list item or table cell now curl the right way in make-pdf. (#4848) - Wide SVG diagrams are printed on a sideways page again. (#4848) - One malformed learning no longer breaks every later `gstack-learnings-search`. (#4848) - Cross-project learnings add to this project's own and never replace them. (#4848) - A pretty-printed timeline event that already has a timestamp is saved as one line (#4848) - `/gstack-ship` now reviews a diff over the 2 MB review ceiling in slices instead of stopping. (#4853) - `./setup --refresh-registered` run from inside the gstack checkout no longer reinstalls Codex after you removed it. (#4850)
